reviews.comment: great teacher for a difficult class, but if you miss one lecture you'll be lost until you catch up. poll everywhere is done by location so you have to go to get attendance credit
Hard class, grade teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The class is very well organized, with plenty of help available when needed. Office hours are especially useful for clarifying material. The professor lectures clearly, though the course can be challenging without prior experience in proofs. Homework and exams are demanding but help reinforce key concepts and prepare you well.

The lectures are good, but the textbook is infinitely better (note: there's a slight difference between the lectures and the textbook with NFAs and Thompson's construction, because the textbook doesn't allow NFAs to have lambda transitions but the lectures do). The grading is also very pedantic.

anke is a fantastic cs2800 professor, definitely take it with her. lectures were extremely well prepared and interesting. the hw and prelims are definitely challenging, but they help you understand material at a deeper level and are still fairly manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: ANKE MY GOAT!! Discrete math isn't easy but her lectures were very good at explaining difficult concepts -- I even ended up enjoying the subject! Tests are very fair/doable and we got a lot of good resources to prepare. The hw she writes also significantly improved my understanding. If you must take CS2800 take it with Anke.

Yes the class it hard but Anke makes it bearable. Nobody wants to take 2800 but she genuinely cares for her students and made the lectures very informative. I will say that the final was very hard. Honestly, if I had to take the class again, I would take it with Anke.

I have taken two classes with her and have not enjoyed either of them. She has an incredible ability to make content more confusing and boring at the same time. Her exams and homework are moderately difficult, but combined with the complete lack of support and poor lectures they become very hard. I would stay away from any of her future classes.
My favorite professor at Cornell, if you have the chance to take her courses, you should

Anke is an incredible lecturer who has an excellent grasp of the material and really challenges you to think during her lectures. I would definitely recommend going to class as much as possible if you have her.

This class was fairly difficult but Anke was a great professor and really helped to explain the material. Her lectures were very engaging and clear. The homework and tests were a bit hard but the class as a whole was a very positive experience largely due to Anke.

My advice, use the textbook, lecture slides were made off the textbook. Anke was enthusiastic and caring, but sometimes skimmed through topics. The key is to visit office hours, as long as you do HW well, you are set for the exam. Discrete math may require some creativity but once you notice the patterns its manageable. Poll for attendance.

Class is so hard but it's one of the hardest CS classes notoriously so I don't know what else you'd expect there. As a person, she's wonderful. Amazing lecturer and explains well. She cares deeply about her students as well and is absolutely lovely. You may not get an amazing grade in this class but it is a fair class overall.

Retaliates if a student knows more than her.
She is not as savvy as they portray her.

I took Algo with Professor Anke in FA23. Her lectures were easy to understand yet fascinating, delivered with humor, and provoked further exploration of topics through the textbook and other sources. The homework was hard, but really grinding it ensured success on exams. Her teaching has inspired me to continue studying algorithms more in-depth.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took this class cause I had to. I was lowkey depressed juggling the workload of this class and other classes. Word of advice, find a really good TA and religiously go to their OH for the PSETs. She is a good lecturer, but the tests are extremely hard. Think around 55% on each test. Also, don't cheat for any hw, she puts up fake answers online.

This class is the definition of artificial difficulty. PSET problems are intentionally detached from the actual material we learn in class solely to make them more difficult. I would learn far more with completion-based PSET grading rather than flushing my time down the toilet. Camping office hours should never be required to do well on homework.

Anke van Zuylen is a passionate lecture who makes discrete much more interesting than daunting. Psets are typically very doable, and are graded rather fairly. Office hours are super extensive, and certain TAs are just as passionate and good at explaining the material as Anke is. Office hours are incredibly well structured, class is interesting.

Anke van Zuylen is a passionate lecturer who makes a daunting subject interesting. Problem Sets can be difficult, but are intellectually stimulating. Office Hours are hosted by TAs who are just as passionate as Anke about the subject, so they are a great source of additional help, and are very structured.

Lectures are generally done well and the material is presented in an engaging way, but the material does not always carry over to the assignments. It is very possible to attend all the lectures, understand the material, and still pull C's on exams because of harsh grading.
Was incredibly misled by past reviews. In class lectures are superficial and do not carry over well to HWs and exams.
Good prof, but I am straight up not having a good time.
Wouldnt take unless absolutely necessary or have a background in PROOF BASED math. Dont be fooled by the high ratings, not a bad professor but incredibly overhyped. Exams and psets are challenging.
The psets and exams were so difficult I considered dropping out multiple times.
I highly recommend if you can wait a semester to take it with a different professor if they have easier hws/prelims her prelims and hws were both really hard

One of the best professors I have ever encountered. I love how she is open to hearing any of the ideas we have and truly cares about each of the students.
Suggestions for taking Anke's course: listen carefully and follow tight in lecture, clear up questions right after the lecture. And you are in good shape!
good

Anke's lectures were probably the best I've ever attended at Cornell. She wrote them out on blank slides every class, allowing us to go through content at a reasonable pace. Also very willing to discuss questions. The textbook, although not strictly necessary, was highly useful in doing well. Definitely recommend!!!

Anke's lectures were incredibly well put together and went through every detail of course content in excellent detail. Homework was sometimes lengthy, but definitely worth it in improving understanding.

Anke was one of the best professors I've had. She was proficient at teaching the course material and consistently motivated ideas. She also clearly cares about the mental health of her students, as she decreased the difficulty of the class halfway through. That said, this was also one of the hardest courses I've taken, which is normal for algo.

Anke is very sympathetic and cares about her students. She is an engaging professor and conveys the information well. It is difficult to find good STEM professors, but she is one of them. I have heard amazing things from other classes she teaches as well. Highly recommend taking a course taught by her.

Prof. Basu teaches very good lectures, and his slides are easy to read. If you study, you get good grades. He wants students to succeed in his class, so the exams are open-book. Attendance is not mandatory. TAKE THIS CLASS, and attend the lecture if you have time...
He was amazing, 10 out of 10 would recommend.

Cracks a good joke once in a while, but otherwise monotonous. He's so relaxed about everything and does not gaf, which is exciting at first. However, the fact that he does not gaf will be reflected on your first prelim score. He overcomplicates the entire instruction of econ. Got a good grade but learned very little, which sums up his class.
I felt like I didn't learn much. 😕 I know he's trying his best to teach, but it was really hard to understand him. The prelims and final were open book, but most students just used AI

By far the funniest professor I've had, half the time I was wondering if I signed up for a comedy show instead of office hours. Which he would just cancel if he didnt feel like it lol. Somehow managed to roast us, teach us, and make us think, all in one breath. Actually cared, helped, and made every lecture worth showing up for. I loved his class!!
Helped me out a lot and was one of the most forgiving teachers I've ever had. Very good guy.

His lecture style is pretty dry but once you get used to it he's kinda a funny guy. Says things like "this is boring im falling asleep" and "eh this is easy teach it to yourselves at home". Class seems confusing at first but if you go to lectures and write down everything he says (open note test) its not too hard at all.

I feel like he is pretty good at explaining key concepts, but his lecture slides aren't clear. Transparent about what will be on the exams. The quizzes are straightforward, and the tests are fairly easy, with a good curve

Basu has no passion to teach so his lectures were absolute hell and super boring. However, he also wants the best for his students so he made exams open-note which really helped boost my grade. Just take really good notes and you will do fine in his class.

teaches things that aren't on the internet, hard to understand lecture and lecture slides are super difficult to understand, I took macro in high school so I thought I'd be fine in this class regardless, but he teaches things you cant even Google. some prelim questions, even AI can't understand how I get them wrong and neither does the LSC center

He is a chill dude. He is not the best lecturer, and he knows that. But he curves the exams and he gives different ways to weigh your prelims and final, so he wants everyone to end up with a decent grade.

I think Basu is an okay professor, but he's certainly not for everyone. You really need to read the textbook AND PRACTICE to do well in this course. His lectures helped clarify the content and he literally tells you what you need to know for exams. While not the most excited to teach undergrads, Basu does want students to get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Basu is not a bad guy, don't get me wrong, but he definitely isn't made for teaching. His lecture style is pretty dry (and a little repetitive) so it's hard to pay attention in class. Partly because of this, paying attention pays dividends on prelims, which are curved. The class is moooostly easy, but do study extensively for exams.

Basu is an absolute baller. My guy understands students' pain and actively tries to condense material to reduce frustration. He'll flat out cancel lectures if he or the class isn't feeling it. I loved his dry, deadpan lecture style. Literally just show up to class and you'll do well on the prelims. Quizzes were free and helped a ton on prelims.

Basu doesn't teach the best, even he acknowledges that, however: open book exams (canvas, lecture notes, notes),  ALL MCQ, weekly quizzes, 3 grading schemes to give you the best grade. Discussions were super helpful, lectures not so much. Compared to the other prof teaching econ, I'd take easy exams over teaching quality for this intro couse

Basu is a nice guy, but his class is just insufferable. One of the most boring and unhelpful lecturers I've ever had. Doesn't teach material well and the weekly quizzes don't match up to the topics learned in class. Not necessarily a bad class, just a pain in the butt. He does curve grades, but take another professor if you can.
I wasn't sure about Econ 1120 until I realized that my professor was Arnab Basu. The median was graded to an A- and more importantly, he gets us.
He is very nice with grading. Fun dude, would take again.

Basu is a pretty boring lecturer however he makes the lecture materials accessible and the textbook is very informative. Lectures are not super helpful because he tends to rant a bit and oftentimes ends class early as hell. I think this class is very passable and comprehensible with a little extra effort. I would recommend skipping lecture!

Intermittently throughout lectures, Arnab would emit an exhausted, deflated sigh. I'd say that is an accurate summary of my sentiments toward the class. It is very obvious he despises teaching and is here only for his research funding. Sometimes, he'd end class an hour early. Just a bad professor. Thank the dyson curve.

The most unorganized professor I have ever had. I took AP Macro in high school and figured it wouldn't matter what 1120 section I enrolled in since I knew the material, but he only confused me. His slides cannot be understood, he makes up material that's not even on the internet. Taught me the professor is pertinent to the quality of the class.

Personally I enjoyed his class, he seemed like a decent enough guy and lecturer. 

Criticism is that some slides in his lectures were hard to decipher.
not an engaging course at all

One of the worst professors I've had in my life. Tests and quizzes were very tough, I don't even know where half the questions come from. Very boring, almost never went to lecture. Had to switch to pass/fail so I wouldn't have a B- on my transcript.

Despite other ratings, I liked Basu. His exams were online and open note, and he uses 3 different grading schemes to then select the highest as your total grade in the class. He clearly wants his students to succeed, and he even tells us exactly what chapters/problems to study for exams. I especially enjoyed how he let us leave class early often

Honestly not a blast. Seemed to not like teaching which was weird since he is a professor? Huh. 
Ended class early, read off of lecture slides that he did not make, etc. Learned basically nothing.

Professor Basu was honestly one of the worst professors I have ever taken. Almost nothing that he taught made sense and the online quizzes, especially Prelim 2 and the Final were downright impossible. Half of the time he showed up late to class, ended class very early, and at the end of the year he didn't even care whether the lights were on.

Professor Basu was honestly one of the worst professors I have ever taken. Almost nothing that he taught made sense and the online quizzes, especially Prelim 2 and the Final were downright impossible. Half of the time he showed up late to class, ended class very early, and at the end of the year he didn't even care whether the lights were on.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Even though my grade may not reflect it, this class was an utmost horror. I was very disturbed by the way the class was run: disorganized lectures, no engagement with students, no lights, and very poor TAs. Just don't take this class guys, it was so bad.
I emailed Prof. Basu to set up a meeting to discuss Prelim 2, and he simply didn't show up to the meeting. He was so unhelpful, don't take this class!
If I could give Prof. Basu a 0, I would. Made this class difficult for no reason, and I was shocked with how he basically came up with his own facts!

I'm sorry but what teacher gives a Prelim with an average in the 70s for an Introductory Economics course and doesn't give the answer key to the test. He is so absent and never there to help students. Never take this class.

This was the worst class I have ever taken at Cornell! The class is so disorganized, and the lectures are taught way too fast and don't correspond to what's on the test. Moreover, Professor Basu made Prelim 2 way too hard and caused so many students to fail. I wish I knew not to take this class. Plus, the class is basically taught in the darkness!

Prof. Basu is the worst lecturer I have had in my time at Cornell. He is impossible to pay attention to and his Prelim 2 was impossible. Never take this class unless your life depends on it. This was my biggest mistake at Cornell so far.

He went AWOL after the final exam and did not respond to emails. His lectures were boring and too fast. He did not seem like he cared about teaching the subject and did not seem to care that students did not understand the lessons.
Basu is the man. Great professor, you wont regret taking this class at all.

Basu is amazing. Good at teaching, extremely flexible grading criteria to get you the best grade possible, and a great guy. Tests are moderate and he pretty much tells you what will be on them. You don't have to do work or show up if you don't want to , but I would recommend doing it.

Very smart and engaging lecturer. Really cares about his students and always makes sure that everyone understands the topics. Homework is somewhat challenging but going to office hours is super helpful. Tests were relatively easier and the final project is super interesting! Great professor, great class!

Very solid professor. Posts every previous exam online and tells you exactly what will be on the exams. Provides different grading criteria based on what will be most beneficial for you. Not a very interesting course, but worth taking nonetheless.
He seems nice and smart, but his lectures are quite boring and his accent is hard to understand. However, as mentioned in previous comments, he gives multiple grade criteria which is AWESOME
One of the best lecturers I've come across. Gives thorough motivation and insight for theorems and what we're learning. Homeworks are pretty easy.
Fantastic lectures, explains hard concepts very clearly.
Decent lecturer and friendly person. However, is not accessible outside of class (like, at all) and doesn't really seem to care about the class.
Not accessible at all. Does not follow the textbook or post lecture notes. Disappointing
Lectures have little relation to homework. Gets sidetracked

One of the very few algebra professors at Cornell who can clearly explain the historical and pedagogical motivation for algebraic objects using concrete examples. That alone is worth a 5. (It is also surprising that most other algebra professors don't even care/know how to explain things like that...)

Prof. Knutson makes his lectures and homework pretty fun and engaging, you can feel his genuine love for abstract algebra :) Office Hours are very helpful and he tailors his answers based on the level of the student. Nevertheless, the presentation of the material in class is sometimes not very well-structured, so make sure you read the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Knutson is great! He really cares about his students and explains the concepts very, very well. His lectures are some of the best I have experienced at Cornell from a pedagogical perspective.

He's a brilliant lecturer. He explains things in ways you've never thought of, and figures out what students are confused about even before they finish asking their questions. His lectures (and his runic shirt/rainbow pants combo) are unforgettable. His classes are generally hard though; you'll have trouble if you're not interested in the content.
great lecturer. this class in particular is very hard. a lot of homework. very interesting material. cares about his students. grades fairly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He is brilliant, but his lectures are not quite relevant to textbook. Homework are just easy questions from book, and exams are doable if you do understand the materials well. Take his class if you are good at math and you will learn a lot. Try to avoid his classes, especially 3000+ if you just want to find an easy class.

Confusing lectures weren't related to the material on the exams at all. After the first 20 minutes of the class, he would go off on long tangents doing proofs we didn't need to know. If you love theory, you'll do great, but he didn't teach practical material. Had to learn almost entirely from the textbook and homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Could not understand any of his lectures. Even if you did the reading beforehand, it felt as if nothing connected to what we were being taught. Would absolutely NOT take again.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Terrible. Exams aren't representative of what you learn in class. Homeworks are too easy so you aren't sufficiently prepared for the material. The Professor is nearly incomprehensible sometimes because he keeps rambling on and doesn't connect topics.

Dr. Knutson is a brilliant mathematician, but it sometimes seems as though he forgets how even the easy things can be difficult for a beginner. He encourages questions but moves through the lecture material quite quickly, leaving some of us wondering what we *should* have asked. Unfortunately, he does not seem to welcome questions on old material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Really good lecturer with a sense of humor. Classes are always engaging. He doesn't really follow the text book in the second half of both 2230 and 2240, but this gives him the option of introducing us on different but related and interesting aspects. Homework is often hard, but very fruitful.

Outstanding professor: clear, entertaining lectures (sometime with juggling), useful problem sets, fair tests, quirky humor, and Jedi-level patience.   His ability to explain concepts and predict (and resolve) areas of confusion is almost supernatural.
If you ask for help, he will explain until you understand, but you must ask. His juggling skills are mind-blowing.

This guy apparently went to MIT and Princeton but can't explain anything well.  Makes things a lot harder than they actually are.  I took this class out of interest during my last semester at Cornell and found it a nightmare.  I wouldn't have cared even if I failed his class, but I think he made it hard...definitely doesn't belong there teaching
No one seems to understand what he is lecturing about and I found his discussion of Klein bottles to be unrelated to the material.  It confused me more and he looks ridiculous.  Don't take his class

ABSOLUTE GOAT OF A PROFESSOR!! Genuinely, idk what the other past ratings were on about. Walden really cares about his students; his class is extremely engaging, and he truly wants to see every one of his students improve. His feedback is not arbitrary but incredibly reasonable, leaving room for constant improvement. HANDS DOWN BEST DYSON PROF!!

Don't be intimidated by what you may have heard, he's genuinely chill with grading. Just read the rubric and ask clarifying questions if needed. He wants to connect with students and is fun to talk to (especially about film!). Definitely helped me improve my public speaking!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Was great!

One of the best teachers I've had! Don't hesitate to reach out as he's eager to help. Class is engaging and enjoyable (movie quizzes are a fun way to start class!). He's kind, caring, and wants students to succeed. Grading is generous with extra credit too!

Fun lectures, we always did a guess the movie game in class. Easy to get good grades as long as you listen in class and follow the rubric. Participation is super important. Super nice guy, he gave us personalized film recs at the end of the semester!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Walden makes it very difficult to succeed in his class by making achieving A's in assignments virtually impossible and having arbitrary rubrics. I must admit having him as a prof forced me to improve my public speaking overnight (literally, I pulled an all-nighter for this class). He's also very rigid & gives no flexibility.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Avoid. The class itself is not hard but his grading is so harsh. He takes points off and provides feedback which can be arguable. Even if your work is solid, if it's not done exactly the way he wants, you'll lose so much points. Seems nice but is actually not helpful at all.

Worst professor/teacher I've ever had. If you don't complete assignments EXACTLY how he wants (and he does not make the instructions clear), you will be docked many points. Switch to another teacher for ManComm. Stay away from Walden if you want a fair grade for the effort you put into the class.
I agree with the other low ratings. Switch to another prof for business writing if you can.

Professor Walden does not care about his students at all. Teaches you absolutely nothing throughout the course. Assignments are ambiguous and hard because he literally does not teach anything. Downgrades you heavily for missing class. Rude person. Worst professor I have had at Cornell.

He comes off as calm and nice but in reality is VERY unaccommodating and difficult to work with. The class is easy but he grades unnecessarily difficult and takes himself too seriously. Content is extremely basic and dull and his way of teaching doesn't make it much better. You have to complete every assignment EXACTLY how he wants it

This was a solid class. Definitely not my favorite at Cornell, but not as bad as people on here are saying. He is a pretty easy grader. This stuff about him being a hard grader is more about penalizing bad behavior and not accepting late work than about grading an average student's assignments. I would take another one with him.

Worst teacher I've had so far at Cornell (if you can even call him a teacher, given that he doesn't teach anything in his class). The material is so basic and his lectures are horribly boring. If you're in the Hotel School, take 1650 with absolutely anybody other than Walden. The class still sucks but at least you'll have a decent teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Walden teaches nothing in class. I learned absolutely nothing during this semester. He is wasting our class time by giving meaningless lectures or asking us questions. He seldom grades our projects, and gives limited feedback. I don't think he is qualified to be a professor. I will never take his class again.

He gives little work at the beginning of the semester but super busy work at the end of the semester. In class, he basically teaches nothing and attendance is required. Although he grades pretty generously, don't take his class if you actually want to learn something.

Walden is an awful teacher. His lectures are boring and dull, and he lacks basic communications skills. During the coronavirus pandemic, he made little effort to ensure our wellbeing or communicate updates to the course. He also never gives feedback yet grades harshly. He makes us call him professor, which is weird, seeing he's only a lecturer...

One of the worst profs I've ever had! Walden teaches material that most of us learned in middle school like we've never seen it before. He gives a TON of busywork and he never returned most of our writing assignments, so we had no way to know what to change/improve. Takes off lots of points if he sees you on your phone or if you miss class. AVOID!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: Nope
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Very good professor! I highly recommend taking his class, his lecture slides are very clear and his office hours are super helpful.

He is such a kind person and an amazing lecturer. He writes the most thorough and neat notes ever and includes plenty of practice in class which makes it so much easier to learn admittedly difficult concepts. He is my absolute favorite professor!

Lowkey a goated prof, cares about students, explains concepts very well, passionate. Exams were all fair, basically no HW, u needed to just study yourself. Exams includes proofs, some were chill, some were harder.

*math 2930

Makes sure students understands the material and grading system reduces work on future exams. Explains concepts very clearly
YES THE BEST
great prof but I fumbled a bit too much on exams

One of the most wonderful and caring professors I've had at Cornell. His lecture slides were amazing for learning all of the content necessary. The class was very hard because of the lack of a curve and very proof-heavy exams, but completely doable if you put in the effort to do the problem sets.

Very cool lecturer, has GOAT potential imo, but for a class called "Linear Algebra for Engineers", he really expects you to learn the material as if you were an upcoming mathmatician in the 1600s. Extremely proof heavy, prelims containted T/F sections but also sections where you prove theorems you learned in class.
Very hard semester overall. The course was much harder than it was last semester from what I've heard. You do need to prepare and go to office hours.
The MATH 2940 curve was harsh on a lot of people this semester. The class was harder than it needed to be, and the curve didn't help anyone. Much harder than Lin Alg from previous semesters.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Mosunov actively wants you to succeed. His lectures are great and the iclicker questions are actually really helpful for learning (shocking I know). The hw was easy altho there were optional problem sets that better prepared you for the exams and quizzes but they aren't necessary. Pay attention early and you will be rewarded.
Nice guy and cares about his students but made the class a million times more difficult than it had to be
THE BEST PROFESSOR TO EVER EXIST! Anton is such a mush and should be celebrated! TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HIM! Very good at lecturing!!!!
Prof mosunov is the gooooaaattt!!!!
he is the best! so wholesome and cares so much about his students. his lectures are fantastic and the notes are really easy to follow afterwards. i will actually miss bro
Anton is kind of the goat. Lectures are extremely detailed and basically hold your hand through learning new concepts, and his slides are like the best thing I've ever seen.
anton mosunov is the goat

There is a tacit understanding that your race and gender play a significant factor in determining your success. Ask any student who took his class, and unless they benefitted from his deep rooted biases, they are likely to say the same. Most don't blow the whistle on his appalling behavior in fear of retaliation in another required core class.

Quag is so full of crap. his lectures are so rehearsed and he does not know how to apply communication skills outside of that. So when you ask him for help outside of the classroom, he gaslights you into believing his mistakes. He will never admit he is wrong. He is a clear example of "if you can't do something, teach it." Absolute joke

You will learn a lot from Professor Quagliata but need to put in the effort to do so. Always available for help and for feedback. Lengthy assignments, but truly beneficial if you are planning to enter the workforce.

This guy is the worst professor at Cornell. He entire class is designed to create pretty slides that he thinks adds value but in reality most corporations have their own template and format that you will be required to follow. His approach to writing as well is rather academic and has not adapted to the changes on technology. Steer clear.

Professor Quagliata is one of best professors I have ever had. He is kind and understanding, but also extremely helpful. I learned a lot and gained so much from his class. I wouldn't say it's an easy A, but if you work hard, you will get an A. And you will learn along the way.

If you are Asian, you basically start off with a C in the class. After receiving a D for an assignment, I visited his office hour, but was cut off in the middle as he only allocated 10 minutes of his time. When I revisited him, he told me that the reason was because English was not my first language. The truth is, English is my first language.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: final module for ILRGL 2350. he's a very nice guy and cares about his students but the final was too much work for what it was

Had him as the final professor for Work Labor Capital. Very passionate about labor in Latin America and is funny. Good lectures but the final was way too much work. Two multi paragraph essays and two short responses that were a page each and only 75 minutes to do them meant that tons of people were barely able to finish or couldn't finish at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: (ILRGL2350) He is very knowledgeable in his subject and he brings a lot to the table. Even if it isn't required he will want you to participate and he wants students to be engaged. He is smart and very kind. His office hours are very helpful and he is very open to meeting with students
(ILRGL2350) Good prof. He explains everything clearly and provides interesting informational content. Take good notes and pay attention and you will do well.

One of the most caring professors that I have had at the ILR School that takes the time to know each of his students. Extremely personable and always has so many availabilities open for office hours. Classes are all discussion based, and he is super passionate about Latin American history and politics.

Prof. Anria is one of the best profs at ILR. The class is based on a final paper which is subdivided into drafts and outlines which make up a considerable percent of the grade. Prof. Anria is very fair and offers a lot of feedback throughout the process. He really cares about his students and makes sure that everyone is included and does well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Brad will push you to deepen your analysis and ground it in textual evidence and close-reading. He's not always super clear with his feedback but gives plenty of room for improvement. He rambles a bit in class but is a good professor overall and has very flexible deadlines. He will definitely push you to improve your writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Brad is hands down the GOAT. Class will improve how you write and think. Do anything you can to snag a spot in pre-enroll.

Brad is the professor I recommend to anyone needing to take an FWS. He is an amazing storyteller and seems to know so much about everything! He was pretty flexible with deadlines especially if you have a lot going on. He is always available for office hours and will work around your schedule, so take advantage of that. Your grade will thank you!!

Brad always knows what's going on and allows rewrites for almost all the papers. Unlike other writing professors, he is not only good at writing but also knows physics and math, has easy grading, and is the best professor

One of the best prof at Cornell. Write whatever ideas that into your brain, Brad is always neutral and will be 100% respectful to them, and he likes us to come up with 'special ideas'. Great and deep lectures, great and deep feedback on the paper. You will have revision chances for each paper, and you can show him the draft for each paper.

If you just wanna gain a S grade in FWS , this course is your best choice. Pro. Brad put the whole grading and workload pretty little and the estimated time spending per week is 5 hrs or less. But he is willing to listen to your advice and if you want to dive in deep topics, you can still talk with him in person.

Do not take this class if you don't like scientific writing. All he grades you on is the accuracy of your thoughts and not your writing. Class is also boring and he overcomplicates ideas for no reason. Grade is made up of 5 essays with no homework but you have 20+ page readings before class. If you want a fun and easy FWS, this is not for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Take his class.
Great professor. Some of the topics can be confusing at times. He is super helpful outside of class. The only thing is that the subject was too philosophical for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Gives a lot of useful comments. Don't be scared by the philosophical words! Flexible deadlines.

Take his FWS. Interesting, sometimes confusing concepts, but he cares a lot about his students and will review drafts and devote many hours to helping his students. Compared to other FWS, this class is not a lot of work.

Professor Bush is deeply committed to ensuring his students enjoy the learning process. He is very accommodating and often shares stories about his home life and family, which shows that he genuinely values building meaningful connections with his students. While the material can be complex at times, just continue to ask questions and participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great professor. Makes the content very interesting and gives a lot of useful feedback.
You can tell he really cares about his students and is very passionate about the content he teaches.

Professor Bush is a great person; he is super kind and clearly cares about his students. From providing feedback and his fair grading, Bush wants his students to succeed. He brings a joyous and fun class environment. Take his FWS classes

One of my favorite professors at Cornell. Super super chill and, especially for an FWS, there is not a lot of work and there is no attendance. Four three-page papers throughout the semester and then quite a long paper at the end but he guides you through most of the writing. Wants students to succeed and it super into the class he teaches.

Lectures were confusing and there was no textbook so if you did not understand them it was tough luck and you had to hope you could figure out the slides. Tons of homework that took a while to do. Grading was super easy though and there were tons of opportunities for extra credit and retakes for quizzes. She was nice when speaking one on one.

Really hard teacher but if you get to know her super funny and helpful. Lots of homework and strict grading for sure, but if you go to office hours you'll do great. Also generous with curving and extra credit. I'm not that strong of a math/cs student and I got a good grade in the class.

The professor is clearly very knowledgeable in OR. GO TO LECTURE, you will only learn the material in lecture. Lots of office hours and TAs are great. Quizzes almost every week, and attendance is based on you turning them in/picking up. Canvas is organized abysmally. Generous curve in the class, if you try a little you will be perfectly fine.

Brenda is sometimes condescending (fair enough, she was the VP of IBM so her huge ego is justifiable). Lots of tedious homework, but grading is fair and there is a lot of opportunity for extra credit. Tests are challenging & take a long time but not all questions need to be attempted, so it's manageable. An A-/A is the average grade of the class.

Prof. Brenda's lecture arent really gonna help you learning the material but her office hours will. The class is really nice and gives you a lot of opportunities to get your grades up even if you bomb homeworks or prelims.

Homeworks and exams often felt sloppy and were tedious. It was rather easy to get a good grade, however. Lectures were rather dense and were hard to follow, though certain slides were useful in studying.

homework is really heavy and varies a lot week to week, be prepared to spend a lot of time doing it. lectures are good, definitely teach useful skills for later classes even if you're not an ORIE major. tests are very fair to the content, and extra credit opportunities can boost your grade

Professor Dietrich makes an effort to know your name and care about you as a student. The homework's kinda suck and are graded harshly, but the professor and TA's are super accessible for office hours. The tests are very straightforward and she won't throw surprises at you. If you put in the effort, you can easily do very well in this class.

Prepare the course content in advance, including teaching materials, handouts, and demonstrations. She will ensure that the classroom content is organized and coherent.She pays attention to students' progress. She will pay attention to the learning progress of the class and provide necessary guidance and support.
her class is not hard if you put in effort and she is always available for office hours and stuff
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The other reviewers had a different professor than me. The only complaint about this class is frequent algebraic mistakes on slides. The workload is relatively steep for 3 credits, but it is made up for by light grading and quality office hours. Take this class if you have any interest in ORIE ever.

Professor Dietrich is awesome! She does go over lectures a bit quick but as long as you pay adequate attention lectures are not too hard to comprehend. She hosts a lot of office hours and is always accessible. Tests are easy as long as you review quizzes, homework, and practice prelim.

Her class has a heavy workload and can be fast-paced. However, she is very accessible outside of class and is always willing to help her students. One thing to note is that she tends to give low scores at the beginning of the semester, but she is generous with her curve. Overall, while the class may be challenging, it is also very rewarding.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lecture is very heavy and move through slides very fast. There are 11 homework through the semester. Each homework is a 20 pages & coding. I took four classes this semester, and the time I spent on her class is more than the sum of the time I spend on all other classes. I am regretful everyday for not dropping this class before the deadline.

Worst professor at Cornell. Lecture slides are extremely messy, some homework questions make no sense, homework takes forever to complete, a quiz at the end of the lecture that asks questions about the material that was just taught! Exams are long as hell. Don't take her class if you are a slow writer

She goes through the lecture slides way too fast, but records and posts them after class every day so you can go back and review them which is nice. Homework is an absurd amount of work and is harshly graded, but if you go to her office hours she is very helpful and will make sure you understand it. Attendance is important, since she gives quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Her lecture doesn't make any sense because of all the algebraic mistakes on the slides and she skim through the concept really quickly because she had been teaching the same topic for so many years. Lots of homework and harshly graded.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Absolutely horrible. Literally the worst professor I had at Cornell ever. Will never take a class with her again.

Her lecture slides are very very messy. Full of small texts and no single picture included. What is worse, she basically reads all those text word by word during the lecture. Not informative at all. Avoid this class.

She is clearly brilliant, lectures on high level topics, and interesting, relevant content. First ORIE class in which I feel things are well applied to industry. However I don't think I would enjoy the course as much, if it weren't for the grading scale being lax (mostly participation and homework completion grades) as I was free to make mistakes.

She is actually the worst teacher I have ever had. Her lectures are uninformative, so you have to figure everything out yourself. She makes the homeworks impossible and super time consuming. The Prelims and Finals are copy and pasted from the practice exams, but there is no enough time to finish, ever. NEVER taking a class taught by Brenda, EVER.

You can probably get by without going to lecture, but be prepared to read the course packet because the uploaded lecture notes are vague--and even then, she doesn't follow the course packet that well. The homework assignments have contradictory, ambiguous directions, and sometimes unrelated to lecture content; they basically set you up for failure.

Prof. Brenner is super passionate about this topic! You can tell from her lectures that she loves what she does, and she is always respectful and considerate in regards to her students. My only complaint is that the assignments are sometimes vague, but overall a great beginner course for those interested in policy!

Professor Brenner is the nicest, most caring professor ever, and her lectures in this class were always really great. Attendance is mandatory on the sign-in sheet. Graded by three very easy comparative reflections on different policies, and then two group projects. Grading was done exactly by the provided rubric, so it's super clear and simple.

Super easy class, for freshmen if they don't know if they want to do Public Policy as a major or minor. Graded by 4 reflections and 2 group projects. Pretty lecture-heavy, but fun activities sprinkled in about every other class. Participation matters in the final grade but overall very easy. Super hard to get below an 95, if you actually try
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Brenner was a really great professor. She was kind, caring, and passionate about the subject matter which really made a difference. The subject matter can be dense at times but she is very open to explaining things further either in lecture or in office hours. Overall just a really good person which translated to a really good professor.

She is nice and the class is pretty easy. The grading was lenient but sometimes nitpicky. This was her first year teaching this class so it had some issues but she was very open to feedback and was overall a caring professor.
Not ever give a ref, though work hard in his lab and courses.

Great class. The work is kinda tedious but you will get a good grade if you can motivate yourself to do it. I've never met Professor Richards but he loves writing Canvas announcements. Like my little penpal who's super interested in Life Cycle Sustainability Assessments
Professor Richards is extremely helpful during office hours. The expectations are clear and the course is very organized!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Taken online but doesn't matter bc this class has no lectures! SD is a great class where all you do is a weekly assignment for a long-term project of your choosing. If you simply do all the work by the rubrics and the EC you will get an A+. The prof is helpful in office hours if you need. Highly recommend this class!
It was a fantastic class.
It was an amazing class!

Engaging content in the lectures. Overall a fun course. Was pretty chill, we were allowed cheat sheets for exams. People in previous years seemed to give negative reviews, but they likely did not go to class/did not pay attention. Asking questions during lectures will help you understand a lot, and the professor gives pretty detailed responses.

He really stepped it up since last spring because most (all?) of the issues are irrelevant now. Clear grading, fair exams, strong support system in OH and after lectures, assignments are well spread out throughout the semester. The syllabus is also refreshed now to include more recent topics like NeRFs, transformers, semantic segmentation, etc.

This isn't the worst course I've ever taken, but it's definitely up there. The material is interesting, but the course is so disorganized that it makes it hard to care about the material. Almost all of our assignments were shoved into the last month of the course. Lectures are boring, slide decks are not organized, and staff support is non-existent
boring lecture. I feel like I barely learned from this course, even though I did well

Seriously disorganized class. Gives us about 2 assignments in the first 90% of the semester and then drops 4 towards the last 2 weeks of class. Review material has no answers, frequently canceled office hours, and no help on ed discussion.  Terrible grading scale as well which was final despite half the class doing not as well as he expected.

This may have been one of the most disorganized classes I have taken. The TAs in this course were useless and assignments were graded extremely late. It feels like the relaxed grading scale was used to make up for the faults of the course. Luckily Bharath is a somewhat decent lecturer.
Get ready for a few out of syllabus questions.

Very hard prelim and final exams with unfair marking scheme (no partial marks, though assignments and prelim had). Did not look at my regrade requests or provide finals solution sheet. Almost 300 students per class with high level of cheating on untimed take home exam. Very bad student support almost nil interaction with professor in crucial times.
Great professor, knows the content super well. Very nice and approachable after class. Gives good suggestions on research/professional-related questions.
Great professor, the course covers a good amount. Explained things really well. Projects were fun to do.
Excellent professor and can explain topics very clearly. Could answer any question any student has instantly, and explain the answer very well.

The class wasn't much work, and the written homeworks and exams were very relevant. However, the projects were more programming-focused, so many hours were spent debugging code that I would rather have spent learning new concepts. Most of the class is dedicated to classical computer vision, and the last few weeks are spent on ML topics.
What kind of professor leaves most of the work ungraded, provides little to no lecture notes, and drops us in the deep end for exams? A very bad one.
A very very bad class.
Lectures were messy, half of the assignments were not graded, little to no feedback or prep. Avoid.
Ive never taken such a disorganized course.
Good teacher and explains material well. Decent slides and tests are pretty fair. However, assignments can be pretty confusing.

Unclear and sparse slides, virtually no exam preparation materials, unresponsive course staff, messy handwriting, unclear and bug -ridden programming assignments, changing syllabus, unfair grading guidelines, dry material.

Despite what the comments below say, Bharath cares a lot about all his students and tries to make the content as understandable as possible. This semester new projects were tried out and though the documentation was bad, he cleared up any misconceptions about the projects. Great to talk to and very approachable
Terribly managed course.
Projects and assignments widely out of sync with lectures. Incomprehensible lectures. Terse slides.

Lectures are well planned, and most of the learning is visual. Lecture notes are enough for a good understanding of the material and, most of the homework can be solved by just relying on it. Since the course projects are research-oriented, he grades them by looking at the amount of effort you put in and what you have learned from it.

He's really straightforward and funny in lectures, makes it very engaging. He also had more in-lecture polling questions than Dr.Helmann and Dr.Pesciotta, and that helped me understand and engage with the topic more. Generally a really fun bio class, especially if you have a bit of background (e.g. IB HL Biology). Loved his martial art shirts.
1440 made bio feel like one big, weirdly logical story, and Buchon explains it super clearly (with just enough humor) that I actually looked forward to lecture.

Professor Buchon is excellent! BIOG 1440 was challenging, but it's remarkable how far we dove into physiology for an intro class. His clear explanations and enthusiasm made the complexity fascinating and rewarding.

I thought he was a pretty good prof, but his lectures were the most difficult for me to understand out of the 3 profs. His were so extremely content-dense that it was nearly impossible to actually memorize everything. Though the material was extremely interesting, and I thoroughly enjoyed learning it all, even though it took a lot of work to do so.

I had the pleasure of being in Professor Buchon's class this semester, and I must say it was an absolutely enriching experience. I highly recommend their class for anyone interested in physiology, especially if you plan on taking the MCAT
I really liked his style of teaching. He mixes clear explanations, with physiological problem sets and I really got a sense I learned a lot. A must have for premeds

Taking Professor Buchon's physiology class was super cool! He made it easy for us to get what he wwas talking about. He really cared about us doing well and was always there to help out, whether it's explaining stuff after class or using fun ways to teach. I'd totally recommend his class to anyone who wants to learn about how their body works!

Great professor who cracks a lot of jokes. he deals with the most complicated lectures in class but make them very accessible. Follow in class. This helps a lot! Accessible professor outside of class.
Very good professor that made complicated concepts pretty clear. Very accessible outside of class, supportive and quite funny.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: really nice professor

Really funny professor, wrote the easiest out of the four prelims. I thought his lectures were the most entertaining and very clear. Very heavy french accent but still not hard to understand. His prelim was not too detailed oriented. Loml

Dr. Buchon is, in my opinion, the best 1440 instructor! His slides are very clear. His lecture was thorough and his explanations was extremely clear. He takes hard physiology concepts and explains it in a way that's really easy to understand. He's very accessible outside of class and holds extra office hours before exams so we get the help we need.

His videos were helpful, but it is a little hard to understand his French accent. His lectures were pretty engaging and thorough. The class is moderately difficult. There's lecture videos, readings, and mandatory quizzes twice a week, 4 prelims, optional final, and attendance is not mandatory. Prelims are tricky. Don't take if not required.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: best 1440 lecturer, with very clear presentations, slides, and grading criteria. organizes and explains things very well and grades super fairly. the only problem I've ever heard from people about him is his accent, but I never had any issue (it's french, if anyone is wondering) wish he taught the entire semester!

From the three instructors in BioG1440, Pr. Buchon was the most interesting and clear.
Easy to talk to and mentions in class what the test will be on.
Lectures are content heavy, but complex concepts are well explained.

Prof Buchon's slides and lectures were by far the most clear and easy to understand. I felt like the topics he taught were some of the more difficult ones, but his explanations and heavy use of in-class practice questions helped a lot. He also pushed back a prelim when he knew the students were stressed about other emergency matters.

The ability to watch the recorded lectures is what carries this class. All the information you need for the exams are in the recorded lectures, and the three professors that teach this class have plenty of office hour times to help with understanding the lectures. The discussion sections are great fun, with great experiments. JOIN BIOG1044! GL

An interesting class where you will learn a lot about physiology. Contrary to what is said in the syllabus, it is heavy in human physiology and not so much focused on other organisms. Pr. Buchon really explained well complicated concepts.
Intelligent and thoughtful professor with interactive lectures. Explains topics well. The way the class is curved is annoying.

I really loved the lectures of Pr. Buchon, they were very structured and the problems were well explained. I took AP biology so have seen some of that content before, but this was way more structured.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: I loved the lecture of Professor Buchon on how microbes influence physiology. Coolest lecture ever. It made me think a lot.

I actually loved BioG1440 and especially the section taught by Buchon. The exams were very fair, you really just have to listen to what he says in class. The other instructors were a bit less clear, but overall a good class. Exams come one day apart from chem, this was tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Took BIOG1440 with Buchon, Shapleigh, and Selveraj in FA 2020. Class had both synchronous and asynchronous lecture components. Buchon's slides and lectures were by far the most comprehensive and he emphasized topics that were likely to be tested. Compared to the other two professors Buchon was by far the best.
The course itself is difficult but Buchon explains things in a very clear and understandable way. He does have an accent that can be heavy at times, but his way of teaching is great
There were 3 instructors for this class and they were really uneven. The body physiology is really the coolest part. Advice: go to office hours!
I am very thankful for this professor's time. He hold something like 10 extra office hours sessions before prelim and these really help.

Professor Buchon had very good powerpoints, but his thick French accent sometimes made it difficult to understand him. BIOG 1440 itself is difficult and very memorization heavy, but I think he explained concepts well.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Fantastic professor. He made some complicated subjects feel quite simple!

Dr Buchon was very helpful during the semester. I started with a bad score during my first prelim, but thanks to TAs and Professors' office hours, I kept increasing my score. Dr Buchon advices were really helpful
Dr Buchon explained everything we needed to know very clearly and plainly. I was glad to get to study from him

Dr. Buchon is a great professor and really cares about his students and the subject material. Very easy to understand and available for extra help during office hours. I went every week. He is passionate about physiology and you will learn a lot from him. I wish I could take more courses with him!
Great teacher. Loved it!

Great introduction to physiology. Has been recommended to me by my academic mentor as a premed. This course is very time-consuming course but also very rewarding and practical to understand human physiology.

The material is difficult but presented very clearly. Exams are fair; but you better go to review sessions. This professor is very accessible, he will spend time with you until you understand things. There is a lot of information so better study from the start. Thankfully the final is not cumulative.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: This professor really helped me organize to study for my exams. In addition, he took ample time to explain the material even after exams, or to explain what I was missing in my exam. This class is my last requirement and this helped a lot!

He's amazing! If you put your all into his classes you will be rewarded. Yes it will be the hardest class of your life but you will not regret a single moment- be sure to take advantage of office hours and ask questions!
The lectures are amazing. I consider changing major and taking more biology because of this class.
He was sooo helpful during review sessions!!!
Fantastic professor. He makes everything clear !
I loved that class. But it was clearly the toughest since I started at Cornell !
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I took that class as an external student. The content was very interesting, and challenging. I really appreciated the feedback from the Professor, who answered all my questions quickly.
Great class. But the curving really makes it difficult to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class is quite interesting but tough on non bio majors. The course goes quite in depth which requires a lot of memorization. Overall a very interesting class for premeds.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: A very solid class for physiology
This class was terrible- so disorganized, the material was not presented in a clear way and it was very unclear what we were meant to learn. Class objectives were not meant

He gives the study guide beforehand, so it's easy to study in advance for the first two prelims. Final is a take-home with 3 short answers and 1 long essay question. Relatively easy, but grading varies by your TA. 3 short op-eds throughout the semester, but the rubric is odd, and TA feedback didn't help me much. Prof. Young is a great prof though!

There are 3 short essays throughout the semester and2 prelims and 1 final with a long-essay question. The 2 prelims come with study guide, so you can prepare before. Everything is basically graded by your Grad TA with the help of Professor Young. Does not take attendance frequently and is more spontaneous so you'll never really know when he will
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is very easy. Lecture is late at night and they occasionally do random attendance checks at lecture, so try to go. Dr. Young is very approachable. Your grade is based on 3 opinion based memos, 2 prelims & a final (great study guide posted for prelims), and section/lecture attendance. He posts slides that correlate with assigned readings.

Had him this year, and he is literally the sweetest guy ever. His lectures were pretty entertaining, and he always makes good jokes during class. The tests were not that hard because he gives a good study guide, but the grade is based on basically 3 tests. Highly recommend!

Young's super chill. Lectures could be understood by a middle schooler--if you really understand something, you can explain it to a 5-year-old. Young can do that. He delivers lectures in a casual and unpretentious manner. Study guides available w/ all possible questions for the prelims. Papers: ez opinion pieces. Actually riveting content!!!

I took 2 classes with Professor Young back in 2023 and 2024. Great guy, extremely accessible & down-to-earth. 
If you are struggling in his classes, you are clearly doing something wrong because the professor posts a list of possible questions. While some of the topics we discussed were a little outdated, the topics were generally very interesting.

This class is tough to succeed in since your entire grade comes from just two exams. The grading is super unclear; we never really know what he's looking for in answers. Overall, it seems like the professor puts in minimal effort, and I wouldn't recommend this class if you care about your GPA or want a clear learning experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Your grade will mostly depend on two exams. He never specify what he really want to see on the exams, like graphs, examples, etc. The exams are not very relevant to the lectures. Avoid him if possible.

One of my favorite teachers of all time. Extremely good public speaker with great lecture slides. Incredibly honest tests with extensive reviews done with TA's. Grading was very fair and even open to debate once we got tests back. Memos were easy. Young is a funny teacher, loves to answer students question. He reminds me of Cam from Modern Family.

Young doesn't deserve all the bad reviews, but he could approve a lot. He was very monotone and wouldn't post lectures, which was frustrating. His views are questionable but he often had a variety of views. He gave us prelim questions in advance. His class structure was fair: 3 small papers, 2 prelims & a final. My TA was great, fairly easy A.

A pretty average gov class. Even though its "controversies about inequality", we only really talked about wealth based disparities. Prelim questions were released beforehand which was nice, you can skip some of the readings if you go to lecture. Memo grading wasn't clear and is dependent on TA. Prof is very monotone but lots of guest speakers

Don't listen to bad reviews, definitely recommend this class for an easy A. Mostly read off slides which made classes boring at times but easy to follow. 75% of the grade is based on 3 tests--he posts a list of potential questions before the prelims so you know exactly what will be on it. Lots of guest speakers which was cool. Reading manageable.

This Professor openly praises elon musk and other billionaires and remarks how "poverty is motivating" and "blue states have caused the housing crisis." He hates welfare, housing subsidy, & minimum wage,. Test was just regurgitating right-wing propaganda from lectures. Uses his own works as sources for the class. All data cited is 20-60 years old.

Tedious and disconnected. Dude has never met a single nonrich human, and lacks fundamental empathy. A penchant for social darwinism. For all that his research allegedly critiques the rich, he basically worships wealth.

Did not care at all about the class, and it showed. Tests had ultra specific, rigid criteria for written responses that didn't always make sense. Topics didn't even always relate to inequality. Professor essentially made the class buy his book and put it on an exam when it didn't really connect to the class as a whole. Massive disappointment.

Professor Haskins taught the class, and she was an amazing lecturer. Unfortunately, she left, and he is now teaching it. He reads off the PowerPoint word for word in a monotone, and he leaves everything to the TAs, who didn't know what the test would be like 3 days before the exam. As long as you do the readings, you will be fine, but his lecs suck

The class itself and the professor are a little dry. You cover new topics every class and speed through lecture slides. The class itself is very easy, especially if you put a good amount of effort into it. As long as you know the key takeaway from each lecture you are good for the test. If you want an easy class to pass this is it.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The TAs would literally say how little the professor cared about the class. He was a very uninspiring lecturer, often not even practicing. It was the first time running the class for him, and the rubric they graded with used bulletpoints for each question that you had to mention. Of course, the TAs failed to mention this in the leadup to the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very clear grade breakdown. Interesting subjects covered but because there's nearly a new topic every week - each warranting their own class, it's pretty surface level.

Hes a super friendly guy. The class is supposed to focus on CONTROVERSIES about inequalities not inequalities 101. Rude students interrupt his lecture for not discussing the basics of inequalities, but thats not what his class is supposed to be. Its a capstone course, if you dont know racial inequality is a thing, what are you doing here.

Prof. Young is readily approachable. Great personality. He tries to make the everything as fun as possible during class meeting time, and he's very good at keep students engaged. I recommend going to his class just because it's really interesting. It's half lecture and half casual conversations, pretty chill. The workload is also very light as well

Cristobal just came from Stanford and he really has that California chill vibes. The workload is very manageable - several readings and one short memo for each week. He doesn't take attendance, but if you go you will get high participation grade. The class is more like a conversation than a lecture, so it can be really fun. Would strongly recommend
good teacher, prelims are exactly what is on the lecture. Nothing surprising about this class. Be prepared to spend your entire sundays before prelims studying.

such a sweet prof and seems passionate ab what he does. the exams were very reflective of lecture slides and the lectures were basically just the profs reading off the slides which was great imo since it was relatively easy to study for. (just memorize all the slides fully).

Just a chill guy who loves cells. His lectures are kinda boring but they get to the point. Hardly any homework for this class and you do not need to read the textbook. 2-3 days prior to exams study super hard and you should be fine, for the rest just do the 1 weekly homework. If you do well enough on the 4 prelims, you can skip the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Fromme is very knowledgable, passionate about biology, and enjoys teaching and coming to class each day. He's easy going and very accessible either after class or during his office hours. He explains concepts well and calculates your class grade 1 of 3 ways in order to give you the best score possible.

Fromme's lectures were extremely boring and consisted of him reading from the slides; what made this class hard was the exams bc there is so much info and the tests are literally designed to trick you and make you not do well; don't need to attend lecture, but you should read the textbook and go to office hours; pick a diff. bio class if you can
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: first off you don't need to read the textbook even if he heavily encourages it. He's a cool guy who just wants everybody to learn about cells. It's structured in a very understandable way that builds in a way where the pieces fit together. Lots of options for grading so don't worry about failing a prelim. Exams just memorize big ideas from slides.

Fromme is a fantastic person and professor. He genuinely cares about the course and students and is clearly very passionate about the subject matter. Do at least some of the readings and study and you will do well in this course.

Such a great lecturer although he speaks fast at times. Content is very manageable. 1350 as a class overall is hard but he made it super enjoyable. He is one of the lecturers in combination with Kelly Liu, and he was definitively missed once his part of the course was over.

I already miss Fromme. Probably my favorite professor at Cornell. Prof. Fromme cares about his students and tests us on what we know instead of what we don't know like some other classes at Cornell. He genuinely cares about our learning and engages with us, even if it's nerdy/cheesy jokes (my favorite). The class is test heavy but if very do-able!
understandable lectures, but can't always help when the material is tough. he clearly enjoys teaching tho and is pretty helpful and engaging

I think he's a great lecturer, really clear on his explanations. However, he was not helpful in person sometimes. He did not have office hours and was inaccessible many times. Tests are becoming harder every year, but still pretty manageable. But overall nice guy. (Second part of the class makes me miss him)
Very funny and moves quickly through the material. He's very energetic and genuinely interested in your learning. One of my favorite professors.

She's really great. There are times where she explains something in class which isn't completely clear, but the Canvas resources compensate for this. And that's only a fraction of the time– the rest of the time, she provides clear explanations, engaging demonstrations, and a fascinating look into developmental biology. Would take again

Cora was very kind and helpful, especially during office hours. She explains difficult concepts clearly and is patient with questions. Exams were very fair, everything came straight from the lectures, with a lot of memorization. If you attend class and review the slides, you'll do well. Don't be afraid to ask her questions.
Cora is very kind and cares a lot about the students. She is passionate about developmental biology and teaching in general.

Class was not hard to do well in but lectures were very boring. Professor Whitmore lectured very blandly and did not add much to the material beyond the slides. The class itself was pretty straightforward and memorization heavy.

Cora is an excellent professor, and I surprisingly found her Developmental bio the more interesting half of the course. Lectures are similarly engaging yet even more fast-paced, so make sure you're a fast writer. Grading is extremely fair - TAs are wonderful and genuinely care about students. BIOMG1350 is my favorite class I've taken this semester.

Prof. Whitmore is super nice and always willing to chat during OH! Lectures are clear and the slides mostly contain everything she covers, so nice to not have to sit through the recording to catch up. Always engages with students and exams are very straightforward MCQs during class time. 1350 is a great and easy class!
Wonderful professor for such a difficult class. A ton of content to memorize for prelims/final, but overall Dr. Whitmore did a great job of lecturing the second half of the class.

Cora is such a sweet professor who seems genuinely passionate about biology. Her lectures are clear and more engaging than the molecular biology section. Yes, there's a lot of memorization in this class, so be prepared to spend time processing the content and memorizing it. But it's definitely doable to get an A.
Average all around. Pretty nice though. More interesting than the other professor.

This was Cora's first time teaching this class, but honestly no one would know based on how knowledgable and confident she was with the material. She's very passionate about the subject and a lot of the lectures are about really interesting developmental mechanisms. I highly recommend taking BIOMG 1350 with her!

Cora is very nice and accessible. 1350 is a grind but the prelims were very easy (all MCQ + during class time) and you are able to drop up to two of them. Homework is easy and course is run well– plenty of resources to do well, including practice prelims and other practice questions. Just memorize the slides and you're guaranteed an A

Jeff is a very caring and patient professor. He is very accommodating for my extension requests when I'm experiencing technical difficulties, and when I wanted to request regrade, he is very open to discussion and super flexible. Learned a lot and would definitely take his class again.
Patient and caring professor that is really flexible in everything. Would definitely take his class again
Best professor at Cornell. Very patient and supportive. You can learn a lot from his class
professor christen is very helpful and responsive. just get things done following the requirement.
Best Info class i've taken.

Easy A class but super useful for BI, couple of in-class open-note quizzes but most answers are in lecture slides, homeworks are just walkthroughs of BI concepts that he tells you how to do step by step and final project and presentation is a breeze if you follow the homeworks properly. Prof is also extremely nice and accommodating

The most helpful professor I've ever met at Cornell. He hosts additional office hours before project milestone to help students debug individually. This is a learning heavy class, with lots of new concepts. Grading is fair and the project is rewarding.

Greatest professor I've ever had at Cornell. Such an understanding guy and really looks to accommodate his students. Isn't as focused on grading as he is understanding concepts. Provided tons of added resources for the class when students were struggling. 10/10, can tell he knows a lot and cares a ton about subject matter.

NO test, a few quizzes, and a project with 3 milestones. Assignments are time-consuming but worth it since you will learn a lot of new stuff. Jeff is one of the best professor I've met at cornell. Always responsive and available to help you out. I don't see any reasons not taking this class with jeff if you are interested in data.
Professor Canuedo is very cobfusing and the TAs are not very competent too. Hard and confusing tests, I really dislike the way that this class is run

This course is not particularly difficult, but there are many issues with the way it's run and taught. It's clear that the course is lazily-structured: the homeworks and exams are written badly and are very unclear with what they're asking, and the professor lacks the ability to explain topics. From my experience, I would not recommend.

She is not a great lecturer. She goes really fast during lectures and jumps from topic to topic so be ready to take notes and lock in the whole time, or just self study. She also has an accent which can be hard to pick up sometimes. The workload was alright with group problem sets and mostly just exams.
The teaching was bad. I wouldn't recommend it.
CURVED DOWN EVERYONE'S GRADES BY A HALF-LETTER. Does not follow her own grading rubric. Reads directly off of slides in thick accent. Homeworks not related to lecture material. Do not recommend.
rushes through slides in class despite TAs asking her to slow down and struggles to answer questions clearly, leaving the TAs to carry the class.
This course gave me foundational knowledge about markets, inflation, unemployment, interest rates. Very applicable things that have a lot of value. A must to understand the real world
Professor Caunedo is inspirational. She is teaching tough material and I liked her style of bringing it down to real world examples.

I have learnt a ton for this course. The professor was available to answer questions outside class and always clear when asked for clarification. My letter grade was wrong and was freaking out because of internship applications but she fixed it by the morning after.

Enraged by Econ 3040. Lectures are unclear, and grading is arbitrary and inconsistent between exams. Content unclear throughout. The stats are concerning, but prof said it's normal.
