Unresponsive before final. Got sick (102° fever), but makeup would mean "I" on the transcript. Never been so frustrated with a course.
Terrible clarity in class and absolutely did not follow syllabus grading. Never take a class with her.
Terrible professor. Doesn't know what she's teaching. Grading couldn't be more random. Doesn't stick to her own syllabus. Managed to curve grades down. Never take her class.

Professor Caunedo disregarded syllabus grading and gave much lower grades for many students than was outlined in the provided syllabus. The lectures were difficult to follow, yet the content was easy to digest once reviewed outside of class. Highly recommend taking a different professor for 3040 if possible
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor really funny. She let you to drop a prelim and replaced by a higher final score, deeply cares about the growth of students. I would definitely recommend this. One of the most caring professors I have at Cornell so far

Professor and nice and really funny, keeps lectures lighthearted. Homeworks and exams start hard, but it seems to all click around the final few weeks. 

Attendance not mandatory, but save yourself confusion and extra hours studying by going.

Highly enjoyed 3040 with Caunedo! Learning curve was tough, but she lets you replace prelims with your final if it's higher, so there's chance for a comeback. Cracks jokes in class and asks questions during lecture - I struggle with focus but she was able to keep me engaged. I liked her "MBA-flavor" (as she put it) - would recommend her for 3040.

her class is a learning curve. I started out doing so bad but ended up with good grade once I got used to her exam style and her lecture style. Homework is graded sorta harshly but seems like she curved the class generously
She cares about the students. Lectures are dense, but I feel I learnt a bunch.
Don't recommand. Most boring class ever. She reads through the slide. Heavy accent. Exams aren't really hard though. She's not awful, she just can't catch anybody's attention.

Macroeconomics is very dry material but was delivered very-well in an MBA setting, I really liked that the material was tied to the current economy. Her lectures are intense, maybe the models could be simplified a little so things are better understood, but I like that she facilitated discussions that came up in class instead of shutting them down.

Professor Julieta, while bright, doesn't seem to understand that many MBA students do not have a background in economics. She never manages to finish what she planned for a lecture in just ONE lecture, and crams an absurd amount of information in every sentence she says. With her heavy accent as well, classes become impossible to understand.
Really bad class organization Never able to finish class material as planned Discussion always went out of the way Speak too fast mostly mumbling with heavy accent

Caunedo is knowledgeable but really bad at teaching. Struggles to explain basic concepts, skips important points and rambles a lot. Has a heavy accent, if you are not good at deciphering accents, go with another professor.

Nice but relatively new -- slides still had some errors, but she corrected them in class. Does a pretty good job explaining in lecture. Discussion helps too.   Practice prelim/finals from previous semesters weren't very exemplary of the actual prelims/final, especially the 2014 ones.   HW was easy (1-2 hrs/pset). Tests were easy, uncurved.
very nice

She sometimes made mistakes on the slides, but was quick to clarify. This might be because it was her first year teaching though. She's generally very helpful and as long as you understood the lecture slide deck, the problem sets were not too challenging.
New professor. Not super comfortable in front of the class. Would constantly change her mind on statements of theorems when questioned. Extremely nice and willing to help if asked though.

Nice teacher, but first year teaching. Understands concepts, but can't really teach students. She doesn't follow a book, so you have to go to lecture. A lot of students have trouble understanding. Would recommend taking other ECON3040.   Bottom line: she can't teach, but her tests are fair.

Amazing professor. Take a class with her if you get the chance! Not an easy class by any means - lots of reading but not bad at all if you're interested in the subject matter and can always skim if you have lots of other work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Best lecturer I've ever had at Cornell. Never a dull moment in the class, she presents interesting aspects of the law and even manages to make the more boring aspects engaging. Grade is based on 3 writing assignments so those are each super important but she prepares you well for them if you go to lecture and do the readings.
Great professor but TAs very rarely give out higher than an A- and the TA who grades your assignments changes each time, making it difficult to get tangible feedback in order to raise your grade

Best prof. I've had so far. Such a great experience to be in the Law School, and Prof. Chutkow makes the class feel like you're an actual student in it. Not hard to do well at all, but you need to take solid notes in lecture.
I loved Dawn. She is so charismatic and funny. Also, mostly very engaging lectures that would make me want to go to class.

Such an interesting lecturer omg. The problem sets were long but super fun, and there were only three of them. The feedback you'll receive is super thorough as well I improved so much from my first problem set. If you're a government major or looking to fill some distribution requirements Chutkow should be at the top of your list.

Loved this class. As someone with very little law/govt background, I found this class to be very easy to understand; prof. Chutkow explained things very well and provided great examples. You dont really need to do readings to do well in the class. Very important to take good notes and go to lecture, as problem sets rely on stuff she says outloud.

As many commenters have said, take thoroughly detailed notes during lectures. This will significantly help you complete the problem sets. Professor Chutkow is very knowledgeable in the law, and she made everything we needed to know super clear. I highly recommend taking one of their classes if you're interested in law school.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: GO TO LECTURE AND TAKE DETAILED NOTES!!!!! graded based on 3 problem sets that are more like essays analyzing a case she makes up. office hours are closed while problem sets are open so its important to go to OH right away if you have questions (slides are just outlines). Lectures are great. Due dates are firm but she is understanding and kind.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Chutkow was one of the best professors I have ever had at Cornell. The class lectures were very interesting and very relevant to current day affairs. There are 3 problem sets and all are manageable as they directly connect to lecture notes and readings. Would 100 percent recommend this class and professor to anyone. Easy A- class!

awesome prof, awesome class. lectures are super relevant and engaging. material is not too difficult as long as you do the readings and problem sets are fun to write. absolutely recommend and would totally take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Chutkow is such an amazing and engaging lecturer, and taking her class(es) solidified my desire to attend law school after completing undergrad. I learned so much and really got to stretch my intellectual skills. Love her so much! She is accessible outside of class.

AMST 3821 is my favorite class taken in college. The material is complex but so interesting. I tried to rearrange my schedule to take another class of Professor Chutkow's. Truly amazing and so engaging.

Professor Chutkow is wonderful! She has super engaging lectures that make you want to come to class even though attendance is not mandatory. If you have any interest in constitutional law then take this class. I will say it's difficult to get above an A- on the problem sets, but it's also lowkey hard to get below an A- on the problem sets

Her lectures are very engaging and interesting and she spends a lot of time making sure she explains everything in a clear way. No discussion (instead we have a small section during class time three times throughout the semester). Grade is based on 3 papers that are relatively straightforward. Grading is a little unclear but fair, she grades not ta

Amazing class and a great professor. If you are interested in SCOTUS, take this class. Just three writing assignments which are very hard but if you take notes in class, you are all set. Skim the homework readings. She has so much enthusiasm and is a great person overall. Learned a lot and enjoyed this course. Ask questions and be engaged!!

Professor Chutkow is probably the best professor I've had at Cornell. She is fantastic to listen to and is very interactive with her students within lectures. Grading scheme of only writing 3 papers throughout the year is amazing--but make sure you show up to lecture, you'll need the information.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Chutkow gives really interesting lectures and makes the cases memorable with her stories. The readings are all very interesting and worth doing.

Engaging lecturer. Assignments are interesting, lots of time to get them done. Feedback is detailed and helpful. It's ok to skip the hw readings. Chutkow really cares about her students. And the best part, no tests!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Chutkow completely lacks any semblance of human empathy. You will be denied any and all requested accommodations, regardless of medical condition or extraneous situation. If you wish to be helplessly thrust into grueling problem sets with little to no formal guidance, Professor Chutkow is the one for you!
Phenomenal professor. Witty, knowledgeable, and makes lectures engaging. Grade is dependent on three essays and participation in section (only meets a couple times a semester). Would take again.
Very tough to get past an A-, but a really interesting class. Would recommend for anyone remotely interested in Constitutional Law
Best professor I have had at Cornell so far. She is great and gives engaging lectures. I looked forward to attending her class each week.

Very good law professor - unbiased, engaging, detailed. Funny & explains concepts well. Difficult to get passed an A- in the class - grading done by harsh TAs, and criteria is not well explained. Attendance & good lecture notes critical for the problem sets. Overall solid but have to work very hard to get a good grade on the few assignments

Lecture was online/asynchronous for SP21, with 4 live sessions with a TA. Still, lectures were engaging and topics were easy to grasp. 2 problem sets and 1 final that were fun to write and helped me grasp the concepts. You can't go to TAs for help on assignments so make sure to meet with them early if needed. Would take another class with her
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Excellent professor. Very knowledgeable. Favorite characteristic was her level-headed, fair approach to explaining issues. Never got on a soapbox and preached, just presented the facts. Refreshing in the study of government. Only complaint, lecture was recorded, almost no live interaction with the professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She's honestly just majestic. I don't know what else to say. Literally amazing. Extremely smart, helpful, and engaging.
She actually wants you to do well. Very interesting lectures. THIS IS HOW PROFESSORS SHOULD TEACH.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Chutkow is an icon. I loved her class so much that I took another class by her this semester (even though it is all online, I love her lectures). She is so so engaging and her assignments really help you learn the law and actually apply it, which I appreciate. The only thing is, the highest grade I have ever heard in her class was an A-

Chutkow is amazing. Manages to make even the dryest of subjects interesting and is so fun to be in a class with. Class is definitely hard and you have to work to get a good grade but it's by no means impossible to do so. If you're even thinking about entering law definitely take this

Prof Chutkow is an intelligent and well-spoken professor. She doesn't cold call. She is very understanding and makes sure students learn and challenge their assumptions about the law. The class is pretty hard. Midterm was incredibly difficult. But overall, great class. Make sure you ask questions after class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She is a good lecturer, but the slides on their own are useless. Grading is extremely unclear but not arbitrary. The final is hard and the essays take a lot of time. cool class if you want to enter law though

Lectures are engaging and you will learn a lot, but there are two big writing assignments for which you really need to understand the material. Pay attention and do the readings. Grading depends on the TA but is typically tough.

Lots of reading (20-50 pages a night) but as long as you do the reading, you will be fine on the papers and the exams. Her lectures are super passionate and she is hilarious, she always makes sure the class is engaged with the material.

Chutkow knows everything there is to know about constitutional law. She's funny and her lectures are engaging. I learned a lot, and even though law is not my path, the class was interesting. Definitely read the cases- it makes the essays doable and following along in class much easier.

Prof. Chutkow is an extremely lucid lecturer, she makes you want to hear and understand Law. I loved this class so much that I am taking another class with her next semester and am probably going to venture the career path of Pre-Law as an undergraduate (and continue later on).
Prof. Chutkow is an amazing lecturer! Do the readings for class and you will enjoy it!
Enjoyed her class and she's a good professor, but wouldn't say she's incredible.  I've taken better courses in the GOVT Department.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Amazing! I absolutely loved this class. Her class was pretty much the only one I made sure to attend all the time because she's such a great lecturer. It's not that hard of a class but you need to do the readings and think hard about the papers. Luckily I thought the readings and assignments were very interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Chutkow is a phenomenal lecturer and instructor. I enjoyed each lecture, which were all engaging and clear. Professor Chutkow made complicated legal jargon feel familiar and has guided me toward a career option I never would have thought existed. An excellent class.
I LOVED Chutkow... but you have to work for a good grade.  You need to be willing to carefully look over your essays and analyze key points.  If you put in the time and effort, you will do well.

You have to work to do well, but she is straight up the best professor. She is so clear and organized. Her lectures are always timed perfectly and she never uses an extraneous word. If you are interested in law at all, this is a must take.

Professor chutkow is very engaging, likes to interact with the class. incredibly upbeat, lively and funny. really likes the material and wants students to as well. papers are pretty straightforward and she gives you two weeks between when she gives you the essay prompt and when its due. good law class though the lectures are a bit too simplified

Excellent professor who's very knowledgeable about the subject matter, answers students' questions, and presents the material clearly and in a straight forward manner.  Tests are difficult but fair.  Though lecture isn't mandatory, it is extremely useful.  Overall, excellent class and professor. 9/10 would take again.

Great professor, no doubt about it, just a few qualms about the class format (frustratingly broad paper topics, etc.) Still totally worth taking the course and getting to know her. She is the classiest prof I've ever had.

Probably my favorite professor so far at Cornell, and by far my favorite class. She is a great lecturer and puts very interesting readings on the syllabus. The only problem is that her classes tend to be early in the morning (8:40am).

Great Prof. One of the best i have had at Cornell. Really interesting subject matter and she tries to connect with all of her students. Every class and section is technically optional, however you wouldn't learn anything without them. Class is a must if you enjoy  politics, current events, or law.
She is really really smart and is able to connect all of the disparate constitutional issues together well so that even if you don't read all the cases, they still all make sense

Nice guy and lectures were easy to follow, but grading on the assignments and exams was a bit harsh, with not that much partial credit. Still learned a lot though and helpful for future CS and coding stuff

Heavy workload with little practical value. Clarkson often directly shamed students who were struggling to their face. While the content is deceivingly easy, the class is made to be stressful and discouraging. Exams are graded harshly, rubric is always weird. At least the grade bounds are lenient though. Overall, a waste of time and energy.

Kindest professor known to man. He prepares so much for lectures and its obvious he cares. If you show up to every class, take notes, and do the practice problems in the textbook as they are assigned you will get an A in the class easy.

Lectures were clear and well-organized. Assignment structure slightly varies from semester to semester; this semester, we only had 4 assignments so the workload was very manageable. Exams were generally fair. While he is good at explaining and definitely knows what he's talking about, Prof. Clarkson can have a tendency to be pedantic and snarky.

I still remember walking in the first day with KPDH music playing and it was amazing. I will say I did not like how he added Interpreters at the end since he has never taught that before and the TA's did not know it at all so you could barely get help on it. Otherwise, he explains what I thought would be a mid language really well.

His lectures were good but he was just a rude jerk sometimes for no reason. He would be nice to certain people and then randomly he would just choose someone to be completely rude and mean to for no reason. I remember a girl asking a normal question and he framed it like she asked a completely braindead question.

His lectures were pretty good, but outside of class he was rude. He held a review session and told everyone who asked a question to just look at his lecture slides, and refused to walk through problems. I think he would probably be better for higher level cs courses not for someone who has never coded before. lots of assignments and tough grader.

As someone that has never touched code in their life, I have learnt a lot from his lectures. His slides are really easy to understand and the way he explains everything is very concise and understandable. The assignments are pretty heavy in content but they are useful to your understanding.

Cannot teach at all and never knows what he's talking about. Tries to be funny but comes off as condescending. It's very clear he thinks he is smarter than everyone else when he actually knows nothing. Truly the worst person possible to teach CS and I would never recommend him or his classes to anyone else if they care about their mental health.

Clarkson was great in 3110. He wrote the textbook, and is so good at explaining things. He dresses up for Halloween and calls us his little class. Learnt a new language, learned so much about functional programming, and had a great time. Weekly programming assignments, one final group project, 90 minute in class exams. 10/10

Raw professor, Walker White if he was young and taught Ocaml. The workload is not the worst, only 1-2 of the assignments were actually a problem interms of time-commitment, the exams are some-what easier if not comparable to 2110 exams under mulburger, but unlike burger the median is higher, B+ > B, the lecture content is all available online, goat

I feel like a much better programmer after this class, but with an assignment/exam every week and the final project looming a class that should be enjoyable is not. I don't really like Clarkson's energy. The only classes I've experiences noise problems in are his. Attention should be earned, make the lectures invaluable and people will shut up.

Silly guy, but he cares a TON about the classes he teaches. It's clear a lot of effort goes into every assignment and making sure everything is fair.

That commitment to fairness can, in my opinion, go too far sometimes. He won't be lenient

I dont understand the hype around clarkson. He is not a great lecturer and I think he is trying to make CS 3110 more of a weed out class for the major. This semester there were 3 prelims all in an 8 week period lol. Course was very unforgiving with drops for assignments with required lecture attendance. Way too involved.

Professor Clarkson is an engaging lecturer. Discussions and lectures are both mandatory. Absurd workload for no reason 8-10 hours per week.

When students ask for help he is egotistical showing little care for them. His approach to assistance is him focusing on enforcing requirements rather than fostering a deeper understanding.

Professor Clarkson is a great lecturer. Each class was interesting and engaging. However, there was a lack of compassion for students. He wasn't very open to all kinds of questions, which was discouraging to many students. He has very high expectations, and was not understanding towards students who reached out for help.

Entitled, no idea why widely-liked. Boring lectures, useless language, repetitive concepts taught in previous core classes (that are also required!). What a waste of time, and we only live once. In the future I will surely reflect sadly upon all the time I spent on this class that I could have spent elsewhere pursuing knowledge and happiness.
Great professor, one of the best, if not the best, in the cs department. fair tests and homeworks, very knowledgable about the industry. His textbook is also great and easy to read.

Greatest CS professor I've ever had. Coming out of Muhlberger, who I liked in some ways and disliked in others, Clarkson was a breath of fresh air. IDK if I'll ever use functional programming in my job, but there's no denying how I've gone from memorizing code to actually understanding it. Take this class if you'll ever use any CS anywhere.
Michael Clarkson is a ball of glowing radiant sunshine.
Clarkson in cs == Messi in football
nn

Very clear, engaging, and informative lectures. Professor cares about students' long-term goals, pushes you to think like a high-level software engineer rather than just a programmer
Also a fun guy to be around
Really enjoyed his lectures although he didn't do too many along with the exam study guides which I believe he made. No complaints. Cares so much about the course and students.

It just simply does not get better than Prof. Clarkson. The man really cares about his students. Course is well-put together and grading is fair, especially on exams (no surprises). Take a class with him if you can.

Tests were hardest they have been for the past few years, the lectures didn't match the 'hard' questions, consultants CARRIED the class though. The co prof was just as mid. I believe Clarkson is just a mid prof, nothing special about him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Clarkson is a phenomenal CS lecturer who deeply cares about his students. His CS 3110 class will singlehandedly transform the way you look at programming fundamentally. Overall, an amazing class taught by a passionate, lovable, and unforgettable lecturer.
They were not joking when they said taking this class with Clarkson would change the way you think about programming.

His class is difficult for no reason. He makes his exams ridiculously hard this semester, with medians averaging in the 50s. He brags about how hard he makes his tests. Overall, I think he's an overrated lecturer, and that attending his lecture can be entertaining sometimes, but for the most part, you'll end up reading the textbook.
Clarkson is a legend who makes the class as approachable as possible, all in all, phenomenal.

Professor Clarkson is a great lecturer and easy to pay attention to. He explains concepts very well and is clearly very passionate. However the tests for CS 2110 cover a lot of content and are super obscure, so the average is very low in the 70-80s.

Amazing, personable lecturer. His exams are fair, projects are slightly on the difficult side. But he is very accommodating and cares for his students a lot. Also, is obsessed with camels and Taylor Swift.
Great professor
goat

Clarkson is the only professor I've ever rated a 5 and easily my favorite at Cornell by far. Not only is he so accommodating, but he also gives engaging lectures and ensures that help is always available. CS3110 has been my most difficult yet rewarding class.

Honestly, the best prof I've ever had. Prof. Clarkson truly and genuinely cares about his students, and he loves OCaml. I'd take 3110 over and over again if I could because it's such an incredible class.
Really great professor! Would love to take his class again (this semester 3110)

Awesome prof. Actually goated. Made online learning not only doable but also enjoyable. He's also genuinely passionate about functional programming and now I feel like I understand it's strengths and pitfalls exceptionally well. You can't skip this class anyway if you're a CS major but to allay your fears about him, he's a great prof

Phenomenal professor and phenomenal class. Clarkson made online learning so much fun. Every part of the course was so well done. The lectures, assignments, and projects were all extremely interesting and extremely educational. So much respect for Clarkson.

Very clear and easy to understand lectures. Funny and nerdy. Very understanding and sympathetic in COVID times. In my experience (and in the experience of a couple of friends), can come across curt in emails (not as much in Campuswire posts, but increasingly so as the semester goes on). Textbook used but necessity is arguable.
Professor Clarkson is very knowledgable, but his classes are pretty difficult.
Great professor and learned a lot from his lectures. Was also very accomodating when we transitioned online.

Attendance isn't exactly mandatory but I found going to lecture helpful. Class was medium difficulty for me because while assignments are easy, I consistently perform below the mean on exams (final is now mandatory btw). Clarkson is extremely clear, easy to understand, friendly, and nerdy (like D&D kind of nerdy).
He is so great!

Prof. Clarkson is very intelligent and humorous. The assignments are great and fun and are of acceptable difficulty. I learned so much in his class, although I have to admit that I sometimes felt sleepy during the lecture:) Also, it's extremely hard to get an A... even if you are above the median of A range.
I learned so much from his course, it blew my mind. I didn't appreciate the difference between just knowing how to code and actually understanding the principles of cs before taking this course.

Michael Clarkson is the best professor I've had at Cornell. He knows OCaml like the back of his hand, and unlike several other professors, he can explain the material in a very straightforward and interesting way. I highly recommend taking this class with Clarkson.
Simply not the best.
He's the best professor I've ever had. In my entire life. Like, seriously. You have /no/ idea.
Great lecturer.
HE IS THE BEST
The material is very well structured and very, very detailed. The workload is heavy, but this has been my favorite class so far in Cornell.

Great lecturer with a passion for functional programming and even more so for teaching.  Plays a different song related to the class topic each day, and then made a playlist available on spotify at the end of the year.  Some lectures he comes dressed in costumes and makes the lectures very fun and engaging, as well as very easy to follow.
Material is taught very well, he is very easy to contact for help, and testing was done to actually test material you learned rather than trip you up. He wants you to succeed.

Professor Zywina backs up each new theorem and concept with varied and relevant examples. He can go off on tangents when proving theorems but if you lose focus its fine as he specifies what is "extra information". Tests are clear and fair but they do require thorough understanding of concepts. Patient and accessible outside of class as well.
The GOAT.
The BEST! You can't bear to waste any single second in his class being distracted. Legend.
Great lecturer, very approachable. Homework wasn't too bad if you start early. Tests were fair.

Excellent professor. He did a great job of lecturing, making things clear almost to a fault. We had homework once a month: problem sets were great. 6 fairly hard problems but nothing too insane. I rarely even needed to reference notes, let along a textbook.

Proofs in assignments are graded somewhat harshly but class is curved at the end. Assignments are much, much harder than exams (exams are primarily computational). Grading: 55% assignments, 15% prelim, 30% final exam. Zywina posts lecture notes online. Textbook helps but is not necessary. TAs are helpful.

Great teacher, makes challenging concepts very clear. Tends to spend alot of time proving concepts, but balances it out with alot of examples that help apply the concepts. Homeworks are very tough compared to the exams and in-class material, and they make up a large portion of your grade. But, the exams are very easy. All in all a balanced class.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--Would take again

reviews.comment: Great guy. Had a kid in class. His wife, not him

Cool dude. Mixed feelings about the class. Lectures were very good. Homework was unnecessarily hard. TA discussion sections were mediocre and revolved around complicated proofs for the unnecessarily hard homework problems. Prelims and exams fair but decently hard.

Overall great guy. Gives good lectures and stays on task the whole time. HW assigned is not too much and tests are not bad either. Never felt like a waste of time going to lecture. However, occasionally he'll make a minor mistake on the board that is easily fixed. Nothing terrible.
Amazing lectures. Explains in full detail. Does not go off topic. Teaches you what you need to know. Great textbook examples in class.

Loved taking Professor Yang's Labor Relations class. As long as you go to class and pay attention you will do well. She and the TA want you to succeed, and the grading is pretty fair. She's an inspiring prof and had some guest lecturers in class.

She's very nice and wholesome, and the course content is digestible and easily understood. Attendance counts, but exams are straightforward and generally graded leniently. Duanyi is super genuine and nice and helpful.
I love her class. She's nice, and I'm a pretty bad student so, I'd say that's a good way to judge a prof

Prof Yang is wonderful and I would recommend her to any student looking to take Labor Relations. The Collective Bargaining Simulation is one of the most fun group activities I have ever participated in. The class is super manageable and you learn a whole lot. Great class, even better professor!

Yang is great! I am currently in her class for Labor Relations and thoroughly enjoy it. You can tell that she wants her students to succeed and is passionate about the course. Will happily answer any questions you have about the material too. Recommend taking Labor Relations with her!

I enjoyed Labor Relations, and she made lectures as engaging as possible with guest lectures and class discussions. She provides study guides for quizzes and sets clear expectations for class assignments and quizzes. She wants everyone to succeed; take her if you can!

I would definitely recommend taking labor relations with Professor Yang!  She cares about students and gives good lectures.  The class was very straightforward with reasonable expectations.  Participation is important but there are many ways to earn credit.  She also provides study guides for all exams.  The group projects are not too difficult.
Nice professor, no outside assignments besides the final and some prep for a project
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Yang is one of the best choices you can pick for 2050. She's extremely caring and knowledgeable. The class was pretty easy. Lectures are usually just what was in the textbook. My only complaint was the class was at 8am.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Caring

reviews.comment: I'm so traumatized by this professor that I've come back ten years later to share my experience. In fall 2016, I was extremely depressed, and she took that personally. She would often call me into her office and berate me like she was my mother. I always left sobbing. I wish I could go back and stand up for myself. It's just a class.

Someone else said this and I agree (took last semester): "A very eccentric professor, wants the class to be free and open but grades harshly when you do not specifically respond to the ridiculous questions that occur to her when reading your writing. I'm not sure how I feel about her she's okay but I would not recommend taking a class with her."
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Cecilia is a very odd instructor and it was obvious that very few in our class trusted her. She does the bare minimum and never provides any feedback but gets upset if you ask about grades. Quite obvious to everyone that she just wants to come to class without being prepared for the lecture. I'd rate her teaching skills as very poor.

A very eccentric professor, wants the class to be free and open but grades harshly when you do not specifically respond to the ridiculous questions that occur to her when reading your writing. I'm not sure how I feel about her she's okay but I would not recommend taking a class with her. Also she never gave grades so my final grade was a surprise.

One of my favorite teachers/professors ever! It felt less like a formal student-teacher relationship, and more like a relationship of mutual respect. She's happy to meet with you for office hours, which you might need, since she's picky about thesis. She is very eccentric, but it creates an incredibly lively and entertaining in-class environment.

I will agree that she is very scatterbrained, but she keeps class very entertaining and is passionate about what she teaches. Does say some very odd comments but she was not racist in MY class (I have seen some comments saying she was in theirs, which I don't doubt). Lots and lots of work, but easy grading. Brought homemade bread on last day!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: No African American would ever claim another African person's lived experience with racial microagressions to be untruthful. This is all I will say about the comment below.

She is chaotic but her energy is infectious and if you put in effort she responds really well in her grading. 

I had no problem as an African American student. I obviously am concerned by the comments on this site but I asked other former students about their feelings and they were all super positive.
Why did this site remove the comment where i said she asked me why I, as an African, looked and acted differently from the other African she had met???
Avoid at all costs. Extremely disorganized and if you are a student color, prepare to be intimidated.

I agree with past comments that she's all over the place. Her class is literally a chaotic mess. Also, shes had a few "problematic" comments to say about peope of color. I dont recommend taking any class with her.

Like some of the other comments mentioned, she is a bit eccentric and her instructions are often unclear. However, the class was a genuinely enriching experience and fostered an intimate, introspective environment. She can be intimidating and does call on people at random, but sincerely cares about students. My Spanish noticeably improved.

Genuinely cares about students and takes time to meet with them outside of class. Passionate about her subject. Somewhat disorganized and gives instructions that are often confusing. Can be hard to figure out what she expects from students on the assignments.

Great professor! She is kooky in a good way. Her class is structured like an AP English class but with Spanish literature and of course only using Spanish! There's a lot of reading and a lot of writing. But that's about it---no tests! She's very easy to plan a meeting with and will give you feedback. She also gives a lot of extra credit opportunit
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She's nice and flexible about deadlines, and her grading isn't bad. The papers themselves are short and easy, but there is a lot of reading for a "writing workshop." Her instructions are often confusing/unclear, and it feels like she imposes her own perspective of the readings onto us, so any conclusions we make about them are heavily guided.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: She's really wacky and amazing. I love her. She does grade a lot of papers like you'll get homework every day but it's super easy to follow and she offers lots of extra credit.

This lady is bomb. Many people can't handle the class and thats understandable but if you are ready to be challenged and learn Cecelia is the ideal prof. She makes you work for your grade but the classes she teachers are wildly different from the rest at Cornell and it's a very fun break from the norm

I am seeing a lot of negative comments below, but Cecilia Lawless is one of the best professors at Cornell. She definitely pushed me beyond what I thought my limit was and this class perfected my Spanish writing. Yes, perhaps she would forget some deadlines, but as long as you check your email, all of her instructions are there. She is the best.

She's amazing teacher. I was quite competent and spanish and still needed a tutor for her essays from time to time. I ended up with an A in the class (i was actually aiming for an A+ since i went to soooo many extra credits) so I am happy. She is incredibly sweet, interesting, and fascinating!!!! I was forced to take the class b/c of the rquirement
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: My Spanish really improved in Cecilia's class.  For introductory level courses, I'd imagine she's a bit overwhelming, but if you're a Spanish Major/Minor, you already have a passion for the language and would enjoy her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The class can be a little unorganized and homework-heavy, but she's very approachable and definitely cares about you if you show you're trying. A

Cecilia cares most about the quality of effort you put into the class. The essays are not too long, and she makes sure your writing and speaking improves over the semester. The reading material, discussions, and assignments are interesting and relevant. If you participate, don't miss class, and care, you will do well. Fair grader. Highly respected.

Absolutely incredible. She definitely makes you work for the class, but she often allows late work, gives extra credit, and gives meaningful feedback. Plus, she's always enthusiastic about class discussion, she'll genuinely care about you (if you put effort in), and her assignments are very open and thought-provoking. I wish she taught above 2180!!

I absolutely loved having Cecilia as a professor.  She is quite scatterbrained but she is so passionate about what she is teaching and she really does care about students.  My writing improved incredibly this semester, not just in Spanish but in English too.  I'm hoping to take a class of hers next semester, too.
Prof. Lawless changed my life; I will never forget her.

No, she doesn't know what time it is and yes, she is eccentric, but Cecilia is a passionate, articulate professor and I will be forever grateful I signed up for a class with her. She cares personally about students and is incredibly encouraging if you put in the work. Take the time to go to her office hours, even if it's just to chat!

she's an amazingly passionate teacher who really knows her stuff. sure she's disorganized but the assignments are super open ended so you can literally write about anything. she's a pretty interesting lady who will genuinely care about you and how much you learn. EASY EASY EASY GRADER. if you show genuine interest you'll get at least an A

She takes a bit of getting used to. She is a bit disorganized and never knows what time it is, and her assignment directions can be a bit confusing. However, she is very goodhearted and genuinely tries to help students if they tell her they are having trouble. She is passionate about Spanish and indigenous peoples. Class helped my Spanish so much!!

She is a little bit "loca."  Often arrives to class in a fluster and is somewhat disorganized.  Sometimes her assignment directions make no sense.  However, she is a thoughtful professor who is willing to extend deadlines if needed.  She also cares deeply about her students and is always willing to help.  She's worth putting up with.

Cecilia is a professor for people who really care about spanish. She knows who's serious and who's just filling a requirement. I've taken several of her classes. She's a bit confusing in terms of assignments and her style is a bit peculiar, but if you want to have legitimate skill and experience w/ the Spanish language, and you work hard, shes 4 u

Horribly disorganized & unable to properly communicate. Gets angry with class when we can't figure out what's supposed to be happening. Assignments are somewhat bogus & a lot a of work. Discussion is repetitive & focuses on irrelevant details which we are expected to find & understand.   I love the Spanish language but can't stand this class.
I would not take another class with her even if I had to switch to French.

My Spanish improved by leaps and bounds in this class; my writing is now more or less automatic, and my speaking is more fluid.  Of the 2 professors teaching this course, Sra. Lawless the more laid-back one.  All assignments and exams are written, and the focus is more on analyzing Spanish lit. and films than filling out grammar worksheets.

I really liked Spanish before I took this class, and she's not horrible or anything, but I just didn't feel I learned very much.  She seems disorganized and though she starts out with a syllabus, it quickly becomes modified-again and again. We didn't use text books so much--more in class discussion.  Homework regularly
Pretty bad, avoid at all costs.
Ridiculous essays. A bunch of psychobable and pseudo-philosophy. Horrid accent.

At first she may seem a little bit distant or above her students. But if you do the readings and truly participate she absolutely has a lot to offer, though her arguments can be complex sometimes, especially if you have not done the readings!

A really enthusiastic educator....watch out for her distinctive smell, you'll start to notice that all your Spanish notebooks smell like her. She's not good with technology or emails so make sure that you get on her class list serve.
You have to try in her class, as long as you do, you will be ok. A's are rare in her class, but it's pretty easy to get B's. Just go to class and participate every now and then.

Though not an easy class, Cecilia tries very hard to get you interested. Some students may say that she is tough, but how else are you going to learn Spanish? Overall, I really like her teaching style.
No Comments

I REALLY liked Cecilia. After my first spanish instructor left on pregnancy leave with only 4 weeks left in class, Cecilia came in and blew us all away. Thought extremely eccentric, she is a great teacher. She really pushes you to speak spanish which only helps you. She obviously cares about making you learn and not just get though the class.
An excellent teacher who instills analytical strategies into her students while challenging them to develop their own unique voice to nurture.
Horrible teacher!  Unorganized and even ****.  I would not advise anyone to take her EVER!  It's a shame she is still teaching.
HORRIBLE, HORRIBLE, HORRIBLE!
Very unorganized(ie never came to class with a watch, never even brought pens!). During office hours she does not help at all, and only seems to want to leave.
Very kind professor.  Extremely helpful if you approach her.
His slides seem very low-effort. Content is not too bad, and sometimes can be interesting. Overall, not a bad person, though.

He never seems very prepared for class, saying that many of his lecture ideas came the morning of. And although ethics is never cut and dry, the lectures are often unsatisfying and lack takeaways because Doris often avoids picking sides or tries too hard be contrarian. He also says he encourages free thought, but sometimes shoots valid ideas down.
just awful. so difficult. useless boring class. exams suck and so harshly graded.

Prof Doris' class was enjoyable mainly due to the discussions he had in class with students. One of the few classes I've taken where opposing views are respected. The class is very easy and you don't need to go to lecture to do well, but I found the lectures enjoyable and learned a decent amount
Dude blows, does not respond to emails and teaches a terrible course, get a grip.

Interesting lecturer (a bit fast) and the content is interesting, exams are straight memorization focused on very specific information in the slides. Cheat all you want I guess - he doesn't care. Wow, I hated this class.

The class is interesting but really easy to get an A in if you go, take notes. I never study for the exams and I get As because its really straight forward. Dont need to read/textbook stuff but I would go to class. Extra credit if you do business simulation. Also really easy homeworks every week. Participation pollevs and stuff so go to class.

The lectures aren't bad at all, and there was no homework, but the grading scheme is way too skewed towards quizzes/tests, when there was only 1 prelim, a final, and 2/3 quizzes. Goldberg is very well spoken, and definitely extremely knowledgeable, but at times seems to go too in depth. He's much more suited for higher level courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures and discussions were mandatory with no drops. Lectures are written only in chalk and it takes at least a week to upload notes from lectures. Next to no partial credit on answers, if you make a small mistake you can easily lose over half of the points on a question. Grading takes a long time
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This prof spends more time making 6 versions of the exam and writing down every student's netid instead of grading the quizzes/exams on time. His handwriting is like deciphering hieroglyphics every class added with the sprinkling of old age dust from previous classes he doesn't remove because he forgets his bucket all the time. dont take this class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: one of the worst courses i've taken. boring required lectures w/ participation (you can teach yourself everything from the lecture notes), but grade determined mainly by quizzes and exams, all graded poorly (month turnaround for a quiz) and nothing like practice problems (despite his only advice for studying being to do all of them). do not take.

Genuinely the worst professor ever. Office hours are online, and TAs don't completely understand how to do problems and don't understand concepts. Tests/Quizzes are worth 85% of your grade. Minimal partial credit. Practice problems are not similar to test questions. Takes forever to grade and post lecture notes/practice problems. Don't take

Worst prof I've ever had. Nearly no partial, 2 quizzes + one prelim/final make up 85% of your grade (3-5 q with no parts a b c). No HW-have to practice on your own time. exams took forever to grade. Lec's are mandatory, required you take notes and turn in every class. Set up in very unhelpful way to learn and very difficult to do well. Do not take!

worst class i have taken at cornell. exams poorly formatted grading very slow; quiz 1 took almost a month. no partial credit -- you either get it fully right or 0. grade based on exams; mandatory participation no drops. quizzes don't match practice exams. do not take this class. he wants us to fail.

questions are either full credit or a 0, and there's very few questions per exam/quiz. grades also come back slow. lectures are a waste of time b/c his handwriting is unreadable and he can't explain concepts

Worst professor ever. Even the TAs don't know how to do some problems, and use AI (ChatGPT) to try to help us figure them out. Exams/Quizzes are worht 85% of your grade. Exam questions are nothing like the practice problems. Lectures are very unorganized, he has very bad handwriting, and writes on the chalkboard.

Worst class taken at Cornell. He said quizzes were going to be like practice problems. I did all the practice problems at least twice, but I only knew how to do one question. Takes forever to grade. Very unorganized, lecture notes are posted weeks after the content is covered in class. He wants us to fail, barely any partial credit on prelim.

Optional quiz that can decide our final grade, but we don't even have the past quiz grades, which is supposed to inform our decision to take it. No one has any idea what we are doing until he posts the notes after the entire unit.  Exams are limited partial credit and very few questions, so if you do not get a 100 you are getting
he wants us to fail.

No lecture/discussion drops, missed classes get averaged into your final. Hard to follow lectures, illegible handwriting even from the front. Poor scheduling meant 3 quizzes became 2, with a last-minute optional cumulative quiz that could lower your grade (have not received any other quiz grade to help make the decision).

Insufficient lecture notes for prelim. There was only one prelim and was behind schedule for quizzes so your grade suffered. He provided a lot of practice questions from the packets and textbook. would not recommend this class to anyone, try to take it another semester with a different teacher.

Messy handwriting and unclear lectures. Requires a participation every single class and had an extensive procedure to distribute tests/quizzes that went over the typical time required for the exam. Stuff in lecture is scaled to a disproportionate difficulty during exam. Provides sufficient textbook questions and resources to understand material.

Just extremely unprepared for lecture and doesn't know how to run a class. Exams were chaos (he insisted on handing out tests student by student and usually ended up starting 15-30 minutes late). Discussions were okay and participation grades made it easier to get a good grade, since grades are reliant only on participation and exams/quizzes
Prof. Goldberg must be one of the most patient professors at Cornell. His grasp of technical concepts is so strong that he can answer any question that you may and will ever have!

Teaching Style - Lectures were problems or proofs that would highlight key theories that were prevalent within that chapter. 

Very fair, intuitive approach to statistics. 

I would hunt down this profs courses.

Truly the greatest of his kind. Robby was a solid 5 stars through and through. Genuinely cared for the students. He speaks a bit like a cartoon character but you get used to it. 
-signed Robby's #1 fan
Tries to act like he's nice and understanding but nothing he said was that helpful when you went to him for help. Also tries to make grading clear however I was curved down at the end.

A little funny but he clearly doesn't want to teach. He's definitely not a terrible person but I found him very inaccessible towards the end of the semester which was frankly aggravating. 

Lectures were just textbook but he sometimes helped clarify some details. Maybe I should've just skipped class and watched youtube videos on the subject.

He is a pretty good lecturer but his exams were the complete opposite of the practice problems he provided. the previous year's exams that he gave were 10x easier than our exams and the material taught during lecture was not reflective of exam materials at all. he is very knowledgeable of the material and kind, but the exams were way too difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a great guy who cares about his students and makes the time to help people, but his tests are pretty difficult and does not provide enough materials to prepare for those caliber of questions. Lectures are straight from the textbook and I would recommend reading the textbook, especially parts you're having trouble with. Great dude, mid teacher.
Curve sucks. Lectures are uninspired, straight from the textbook. Exams are too hard for it to be curved so poorly.

DiStasio is a great professor. The material comes directly from the textbook and is easy to follow. The exams are straightforward and there are many opportunities to improve your grade. He is very open to feedback and meeting with students one on one. Genuinely one of the easiest classes at Cornell just read the textbook and do the practice.

He's actually such a sweetheart. People dislike the class because it's hard but thats not this professor's fault. Such a breath of fresh air compared to my other prof's he was so great, always encouraging and willing to help.
Good lecturer! Exams were super tough, but the curve was generous. Average on one exam was a 26%

DiStasio is a good lecturer and I found it easier to attend class when I read the material- even skimmed for ten minutes - before coming because he's organized with the topics. Go to office hours to go over back of the book questions/conceptual (!!!) understanding - heavy on concepts - and don't fall back on lab grades, it can seriously hurt
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Didn't like it. Lecture material versus test material didn't match too well.

CHEM 2080 was a very difficult class for me. I didn't love how his questions were worded - left me very annoyed when I could solve something but simply didnt understand what the question wanted. But the DiStasio is a great person - ever-willing to help, stay extra time, etc. His prelims are TOUGH but the curves usually compensated. Best of luck!

Professor DiStasio makes the content interesting and funny, so I'd recommend attending lecture. Material is straight from the textbook. Discussion sections weren't helpful, but their problems were good practice. Prelims were hard but well-curved; good preparation with the textbook, practice problems, and practice prelims will help you succeed.
no
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I liked his lectures. He definitely gives you everything you need to succeed in his class, given you put in the effort. One thing I didn't like was how difficult the prelims were, but that meant the curves were really helpful. Just do EVERY textbook problem and you'll be fine.

Dr. DiStasio cares deeply about his students. This was a difficult semester for me and he was more than understanding. I recommend going to office hours. It's an 800-student class, but only seven or eight people go to his office hours. He went over my exams with me and helped me understand course material in a one-on-one environment.
Distasio is THE MAN! His exams come directly from lecture and his explanations are extremely clear. Go to class, do practice problems, and attend sections and you're good!

Robert is great. As others have said he really cares about making sure you learn the material. Lectures not required but I highly recommend- he's always telling some funny story or analogy. Exams are very fair just do the practice tests. 2080 labs SUCK but not Robert's juristiction so can't blame him
He really likes chemistry and wants his students to as well. You can tell he genuinely cares about his students and just wants us to appreciate chemistry like he does. He's a funny bloke also.

DiStasio was helpful in making a hard class more fair; he let students have one-on-one meetings with him and even gave me points back for two of my exams, he listens to student feedback and is easy to talk to; the class itself is difficult but I felt a lot more comfortable having him as a professor!
Good professor, exams were mostly fair, genuinely wanted us to succeed.

Robert is a beautiful soul. People say humans make mistakes, but rob doesn't. He is the closest thing to perfect a human can be. His kindness and caring nature has almost brought me to tears. His class was actually very good, difficult but since Rob is so amazing he got us through it, unlike in chem 2070. He also frequents goldies often, so pu.

I genuinely adore Prof DiStasio-- I haven't had such a lovely chem professor since high school. His lectures are well-paced, engaging, understandable, and informative, and he makes it obvious how much he cares about our success and well-being. Exams are fair and he regularly asks our opinions about the length and difficulty. Overall lovely guy.

Professor DiStasio is a great! He's accessible outside of class & cares for the students. Curves the exams(actually tries to benefit as many people as possible). The exams are fair and similar to PS problems. The lab for this course sucks it's not in sync with the lecture and you have to make up your own procedure. Only responsible for lec though.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: heavily relied on the textbook, but lectures were well organized and easy to follow. tests were fair. if you go to lecture, follow the textbook, and do the practice problems and homework, you should have no problems with the class. definitely learn a lot and dr. Distasio was great!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures come straight from the textbook and are recorded (very easy to watch in 2x speed). Discussion sections were pointless since they would go over the easy questions. Problem sets were a must do before every exam. Basically understand how to do every problem on the PS and the class is cake. Lab depends on TA, some good and some very bad.

He's kind of boring during lectures and basically rewords the textbook. He was very behind on content and that kind of messed with the lab portion of the course. Exams are at a reasonable difficulty if you do practice problems from the textbook + discussion sets, but a bit too many questions in my opinion (have to rush to finish them).

Dr. DiStasio is not a bad professor, but he's just very boring. His lectures are live readings of the textbook and aren't very engaging. However, he pulls straight from the textbook problems for prelims so if you do a lot of the problems from the end of chapter, you'll be fine. Gives lots of opportunities for grade improvement through mini prelims.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor DiStassio was a great teacher and I would highly recommend taking a class from him. Very kind and caring toward his students and you could tell he genuinely cares about student success. 2080 is a hard class but DiStassio was always available to work through difficult concepts in-office hours. The grading breakdown was also quite fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. DiStasio loves chemistry, and it shows in the way he speaks during lectures. He makes content interesting, easy to understand, and is accessible for 1:1 meetings with any student upon request. After the horror that was CHEM 2070, 2080 was a breath of fresh air that made me realize why I'm passionate about chemistry.

So surprised to see the comments about the exams being difficult--the questions were based on the problems in the textbook! If you studied and did all the problems in the chapters/back of the book, you wouldn't be confused at all. All the DPSs were prelim level problems. Oh, and Kinsland runs the labs/TAs, not DiStasio. Truly one of the best Profs!

Professor DiStasio is understanding and caring. Doesn't try to harm you with grading but grading could be tough due to the difficulty of the content taught. Tests are reasonable, but challenging. Professor DiStasio makes himself clear and available. Lab portions are hard. lectures are strictly followed by a textbook. Overall good professor.
Nice-ish guy but does not give enough practice problems to prep for exams. Lab portion is unreasonably difficult. Do not take this course if you don't absolutely have to

Sweet man who loves his students. However, prepare to be confused and struggle on those exams. A lot of 2080 is assumption based, so if you're like me and prefer things to be exact, you will find this class difficult. If you don't need to take this class, don't. Not too many resources but use the book, but exams are harder than the examples given.

The content in this course was relatively easy, but the lab portion was unreasonably difficult. Professor Distasio gave clear lectures, however he went slow and we did not finish the course material. He is a very nice and engaging man, you would be lucky to have him as a gen chem professor.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a very good lecturer and cares about his students. Solid professor

Lectures are awesome and he closely follows the textbook which is good because you always know where to reference information. Wasn't a fan of how tough he graded the class considering that the material was less difficult compared to 3890. Super accessible outside of class and always willing to help during office hours.

You'd think this man has a pizza place in Brooklyn, not a PhD from Berkeley in Quantum Mechanics. Crazy hard tests, but he made them shorter so that he can get out of campus earlier to his hot date (aka wife). Take this class, you will not be disappointed (except with your grade).

Tests are very specific, and test questions may be based on a two-sentence comment made in class. Take precise notes on what is said in class. Roberts is, by far, the most qualified teacher in Nolan, having led revenue management in Marriott for years. The ~2 guest speakers were very prestigious, and brought more light to his stellar character.
Model professor that cares about his students.

Incredible professor and person. His class is a model for every college course and is the benchmark for which I will base all future classes. 

Everyone I've ever met reveres Professor Roberts.

Cheerful, kind, and highly respected in the hotel industry, with genuine love for it that shines in his teaching. The class is not that tough but exam kinda hard. His slides have blanks you fill in during lecture, so pay close attention in class. Very lecture heavy. Exams (2 prelims, 1 final) are all open note and computer-based.
Love this man. If you try to pretend to be remotely interested in what he is talking about by speaking up in class (which usually the material is interesting already), then he will like you.

Really nice and understanding professor. But course material could be explained more, plus more practice time in class. Exams are open note which is really nice but sometimes I feel like I don't actually understand the content.
The best! Maturing is realizing Professor Roberts himself has a wealth of knowledge and is the best part about the course by far.

Really nice guy. This class is exactly what ppl are thinking of when they imagine an easy hotelie class. Tests are open note and not hard at all if you ACTUALLY take notes. He likes people who participate and go to his office hours! Not a very interesting course but definitely chill.

Fun and intriguing professor. Exams can be a bit tough (even though they are open note) so listen in class and make a good study guide. He wants you to succeed and really is passionate about the class

Great professor. I didn't know anything about the hospitality industry, but I walked away with learning a lot more than I expected. One of my best things to do is participate in class and go to office hours (he usually has a small treat there) to show participation and build a relationship with him.

Professor Roberts is one of the most approachable and respected professors at Cornell. His exams are open note but they are graded very toughly by the TAs. His lectures are very tedious and he uses his own terms a lot that you will not use in the industry. Students don't do as well as they would think in his class.

Mr. Roberts is an amazing teacher and person. He is very well respected among the Cornell Community. Make sure to pay attention and take notes and you'll do just fine in this course. Make sure to also go to his office hours. He will talk about anything and he has incredible insight.

Prof. Roberts is incredibly organized and clearly demonstrates his knowledge and excitement for the course. He is very accommodating and an all-'round nice person. Exams are open-note, and he releases his slide decks (just cmd-F). Befriend him and send him pictures and anything you think he'd like.  He's the nicest professor in Statler Hall.

Professor Roberts is truly an amazing professor. Though I am not interested in Hotel Operations, I have enjoyed being in his class this semester. My biggest tip is to try and pay attention even though he sometimes gets very excited and speaks super fast. If you participate and try your hardest he will see that and reward it.
Such an amazing person and professor!!
Amazing guy. He is super nice and really understanding of all different kinds of issues or scenarios.

Professor Roberts is easily the best professor at the hotel school. While the class itself may not be the best, Professor Roberts is. Being able to pick his brain was one of my most favorite things to do.
Absolutely incredible professor

Dave Roberts is far and away the best professor at Cornell. He puts in a ton of effort to make sure his students enjoy the class and get as much as possible out of it. He is one of the nicest people around and really cares about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Might be the nicest dude Ive ever met. One of few professors who truly cares about his students and will go out of his way for you. Certainly a nice break from other professors *cough CG*
The best professor ever! Such a kind guy.

Professor Roberts is the BEST. He genuinely wants all of his students to do well and does not want his class to be stressful; there is hardly any outside work for this class and exams are open note. HADM1350 is so interesting, and Roberts has so much experience from his time at Marriott that he is the perfect person to teach it.
So kind and awesome! Always make you feel engaged and never makes it boring. One of my favorite professors to date.

Profesor Roberts is both the most knowledgeable, kind and considerate professor. Not only does he have an insane amount of industry experience but he doesn't act like a god in the classroom, he takes questions and makes time to connect and talk with students both about his class and about the industry at large.

The class is hard and psets require a lot of work. Please do the homework carefully. TA review sessions and their practice questions SAVED my grade. Ezra's lectures themselves are quite difficult to follow, so seek out outside resources when you are confused. Exams were quite hard, but if you studied a lot, they are DOABLE.

If you want to know what taking a class from Helen Keller is like, take Ezra's class. He will fully look at you and ignore you if you have a question. He can't explain anything for the life of him yet has the audacity to give you heinous exams and psets. I am not exaggerating when I say I would rather be run over by a semi than take his class.
Best professor!

Prof. Ezra is a good professor and Pchem is a tough class. He does teach you everything you need to know in his lectures. PSETS are very hard without going to office hours. When you go to office hours he will make you work through the solutions on the chalkboard with his guidance, which can be annoying but in the end will help you learn.

Prof. Ezra is a really good lecturer - super clear and great handwriting. Prelims are easier than problem sets. If you understand the problem sets, prelims shouldn't feel too difficult. The final was very hard, but if you do well on the prelims, the final shouldn't matter too much.

Undergrad TA OH are super helpful too.

Very smart prof with a passion for the subject.
He has high standards - I did not reach them, but I learned so much. Psets are darn-near impossible for us mere mortals. Prelims graded very fairly and give so much feedback. You can get sub-30 on a prelim and still get a B.
The mathematica nightmares will go away, but your knowledge won't.
Take 3890.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Solid Prof, good lecturer. Lecture is integral in understanding material, you wont pass if you don't go. Chem 3890 is a conceptually challenging class for most, and Ezra's tests are quite difficult so be ready to study. Also, be prepared to do a lot of math, 3890 is basically a math class. (some diff eq, multi, linear algebra, etc..)

While I do think that Professor Ezra is a kind person, his class was incredibly disorganized and difficult. Homework assignments took forever and were nearly impossible to complete without going to office hours. Exams were difficult and very little partial credit was given. Lectures were disorganized and if you missed a day, you were screwed.
He was not an accommodating professor, and rude when speaking with him 1-on-1.
The course material is hard as it is, and Dr. Ezra has relatively good lectures. The problem is the exams. They are very difficult and you only get 90 minutes..
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: His longwinded lectures are exclusively given live in a dim room with chalk, his handwriting is small, and he fights tooth-and-nail against accommodating sick students. The PSets are extremely conceptual and usually can only be completed with info from poorly timed OH. Ezra has almost no sympathy for the many students who struggle with PChem.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Makes exams unfathomably hard. Assigns lots of work. Not lenient with grading. Not a great or clear lecturer. He's nice enough, but he's not very helpful. All in all, an extremely difficult professor.
The most articulate professor I ever had at Cornell. Tests are difficult and he might not be that friendly, but he is helpful. Every professor should aspire to lecture like Prof. Ezra.

The best lecturer I have had after 4 semesters. Never missed a word he said, I was utterly captivated. Class was very challenging and I didn't think I would like quantum. I now am considering following it to grad school.

If you just show up and follow along on the spreadsheet during class, you'll understand how to do the homework and prelims. Willing to answer questions during class. If she says class isn't mandatory, I'd recommend going.

Mrs. Haegar was dedicated to ensuring her students not only learned Excel but also enjoyed the process. This year placed a strong emphasis on AI, and her enthusiasm for what the technology is capable of made it clear how passionate she is about teaching. I recommend introducing yourself to her and the TAs who help make this course such a success.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Originally, I was nervous about this class after reading the reviews. However, she is very kind, caring, and willing to explain any questions you have about the course. Her prelims were fair and a clear representation of what was taught in class. As long as you respect class time and are on top of your work, you will do fine.
Grade is based off whether or not you have a good TA. Some are stricter than others. Prelims are unorganized, but manageable if you watch her videos.

She is nice to students during lectures, and also like to help students on their HW. The HWs can be a little hard since they aren't always exactly the same as in the demos, and the HW instructions can be unclear. The beginning of the semester was a bit confusing, and the prelims are a little hard and very time consuming. She teaches very fast.
Great class for folks trying to explore the waters of excel. Assignment are easy to complete as long as you just follow along with the videos and understand how and when to use what functions.

Does the bare minimum for her students, will not accommodate for anything (I'm not talking about late submissions) unless "required by the university". Disrespectful to students and clearly does not enjoy teaching. Beware.
Forcing students to watch those low-quality videos is torturous. Plus the class policy is so weird. Not a fan.

The class is very accuracy-based. The prelims are a lot like the practice ones, and she does not necessarily make anything confusing; everything is stuff we have seen in the past. She is very kind and genuinely seems to want to help her students.
While the class is easy, Haeger is often rude to students unnecessarily.

As was mentioned before by some other rating, she is notorious at Cornell for being by far the most disrespectful towards students. Constant patronizing and passive aggression towards students and an extremely tough grader when it comes to the most minute details. All incoming Dyson students should be aware of this.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would argue that this is the worst professor at Cornell. The teacher puts on the facade of a supposedly nice person, but during one-to-one interactions, she completely changes. Whoever is applying or attending Cornell should think twice about the school because of this class. Notorious at Cornell for her disrespect towards students!!

Lectures and videos provide precisely what you need to know to complete the assignment. TAs were also nice with helping during class and office hours. I would say that grading could be harsh at times, and the cutoff for an A in this class was surprisingly high (95%). Someone that pays a little bit of attention to detail will have no problem.

Great professor, very clear, easy-to-follow lectures with helpful videos. 2 hw assignments/week align very closely w/ lectures. Prelims are almost exactly like the homework, so you'll know exactly what to prepare for. No final exam, just a final group project which isn't too much work. Just note that cutoff for A this sem was 95%

Course content is really useful. Nice prof but she is strict with deadlines. As long as you watch her video tutorials, attend her lectures, and do your homework, you should have the prelim part completely covered. Make use of Thursday lab sessions and OHs to get full credit for assignments (if not you will always lose a point here and there).

The class is pretty easy and it was primarily asynchronous this past semester. Professor Haeger was always attentive and accommodating to students, but she was often not present on Thursday classes with the TAs to take questions. Prelims are a large portion of the grade, so review the activities and cases before taking these exams.
Not a hard class, but I've never seen a professor be so rude to her students. Especially for one that just teaches excel at an ivy league.

I oved Professor Haeger's class and as an instructor, she did a good job. What I vehemently disliked was the disrespect towards students. I had her for an early class period, so students often would arrive a little late. Each time she would stop the whole class to essentially berate the student in front of their peers. It was absolutely unnecessary
One of the most useful classes in the major. Learned a lot without the class being overly difficult. Probably could add some concepts but overall great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Easy class, but not a great professor. She's super disrespectful to her students and very arrogant.

Can be nit picky and corky, but overall if you come to class youll be fine. Videos of the lecture are online. The TAs are easily accessible. The first class will be a demo of what youre doing, next class you will do it yourself, then a case due outside of class. Demos can be different from your other activity. Study activities for tests!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: VERY easy course. Assignments and tests are easy, and you learn a lot. She is nice but she seemed unnecessarily harsh about academic integrity. There were several kids who had hearings but nothing ever came from it. The course is set up well, but a lot of learning is TA dependent. The final project is long but good experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She is not a great professor, but if you watch the video tutorial on blackboard you will do well. Pick a good group for final project because it is a lot of work. Average grade in class is A+
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS
