reviews.comment: It was my first time learning Excel, and all the assignments and prelims were very easy. However, the month-long final group project was extremely hard. Be sure to have someone who really understands Excel in your group, then you'll be fine. And do NOT procrastinate on the project.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: She is an amazing professor and very kind. Oral exams felt like a regular conversation; she makes them stress-free. I took up to AP French in high school and felt like the course was a review of everything up to that point. My only critique is that the grading is strange; some grades are letter grades, while others are numeric. Loved her class tho.

FREN 1210*. Prof. Epperson is very effective at teaching a foreign language and I feel like I learned a lot in one semester. She is caring, accessible, and gives good feedback. Assignments are very manageable. Quizzes are easy as long as you actively participate/complete homework and do a little review.
Good teacher
Great teacher, kind and helpful

Professor Epperson is a fantastic teacher who really understands how to teach a foreign language to students so that they really understand the concepts. Took both 1210 and 1220 with her and the classes are not particularly hard but they are a lot of fun. Oral exams, short writing prompts and quizzes but that can be expected for any language class.

not that engaging lectures. compared to other engineering classes i would say courseload is reasonable and difficulty of prelims is slightly easier. lectures can just be rlly boring and he spends a lot of time writing stuff down on his slides. i honestly find michael xing, who he sometimes has lecture, more interesting. nice guy though

Good lecturer and accessible outside of the lecture. Prelim and final are interchangeable compared to the practice exams, which were very helpful. However, assignments towards the end of the semester have no consideration for students' workload and can take upwards of 15-20 hours. Grading for assignments is harsh as well.

Eichhorn is super disorganized in his lectures and I can barely understand his handwriting. No curve in the class and the assignments are SUPER hard to do good in. TAs in office hours DO NOT help AT ALL. Walker was much better so please lower your expectations for Matt.

The class is well organized and structured for student success. Expectations and grading criteria are clearly outlined for assignments and exams. There is plenty of practice material, along with helpful exam reviews and accessible office hours. Overall, the learning environment is supportive and comfortable.
goated teacher
Matt is fun and he is patient, but I just hate CS 2110 material .......

Really good lectures and knows data structures really well. Tests were very straightforward and clearly based on the practice materials. Assignments got reworked for FA25 and were long but not entirely useful.

Great lecturer and writes excellent lecture notes. Very responsive and helpful on Ed. HW can be tedious/annoying but not difficult to get high grades if you put in some time. Exams are very fair, and practice exams are extremely similar to actual ones. Overall course grading is very transparent.

Overall a good lecturer and very available outside of class. I really appreciate how he has good notes/exercises for each lesson. Generous grading/grade weighting. However the hw takes hours/days and requires you to camp on Edstem because he expects something that wasn't in the assignment handout and the only way to know is to see his Ed posts.

Great lectures and great lecture notes. Really supportive professor who is very willing to help outside of class. Provides practice prelims very similar to real ones. However, homework assignments are long and very harshly graded.

He makes really hard assignments especially the last few, which can take up to 15-20 hours. He also teaches certain topics in a very theoretical way. For example, instead of applying data structures to solve problems, he asks you to create the methods of the data structure yourself. Overall good class and doable prelims, but hard assignments.

Prelims were pretty difficult and the homework is such a pain, but Matt's lectures made the class bearable as they were very engaging and interesting. He also is always helping and answering questions on Ed and making sure you understand the material
Great professor and amazing communicator!
Really caring and nice professor. GOAT. Not an easy class content-wise but everything he does and the organization of his class makes everything feel feasible.

Prof. Eichhorn is really one of the most caring and inspirational professors at Cornell. He genuinely cares about his students and wants each and every one of you to succeed. The content moves fast and can be a bit difficult at times, but he is always available during OH or reachable by email. GO TO OFFICE HOURS!

Most empathetic professor I've had at Cornell! Cares very much about students being able to digest course material. Tests were fair and similar to practice exams. Very passionate about math and breaks down difficult concepts in a way that makes them digestible. Class attendance and participation matters.
great professor!
matthew my beloved
matthew saved my marriage

Matt is the best CS professor I've had so far. He's awesome, super caring, and is able to explain difficult topics in lectures super well. This class has hard psets and exams, but that's how it is regardless of the professor. He is a great professor and person.

Easily one of my most interesting classes at Cornell, and Matt's ability to lecture really contributed to that. He's a genuinely great person and I can tell how much he cares about his students. Homeworks can be graded pretty harshly/nitpicky

such a goated prof, one of the kindest, most caring faculty here who's clearly loves his job. genuinely feel like bros lectures are a shot of expresso to my MWFs. problem sets do requires a lot of attention to detail as simple mistakes can dock u -1/-0.5, which is basically -4% since they're always out of 25 points. TA's are R&D

Matt is by far one of the smartest and most capable faculty members in the CS department. He is kind, caring, and genuinely cares about his students. His course is really satisfying to take because he is so passionate and good at explaining things.
Matt is the goat and makes 2800 an actually good class

good lectures & organization but strict grader, no partial credit, and hard exams. on an Ed post he refused to give ANY credit for a question that a TA gave misinformation to a student on, saying it was the student's fault for believing wrong info from a TA. but isnt that literally the TA's job??? very odd, felt weirdly like victim blaming.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lectures included a lot of tangents and maybe not so much the actual content, which can all be learned through the slides. Fairly easy class, and some pop quizzes which were very simple about the material during that class (I think he drops a couple). Nothing was cumulative, and final had a cheat sheet

Professor Lewis was a bit unorganized, with some lectures just being him talking through current events or material irrelevant to class. Other than that, he was incredible, always looking to help out students, by making a large portion of our tests online.

I think many of the reviews are harsh. I think Lewis is very accommodating when it comes to students. His tests are fair, and everything is from lectures or involves adding a little critical thinking. Many people skip his lectures, and I think it can be difficult to catch up. Nice guy, although I will agree he doesn't respond to a lot of emails.

Lewis is professional and respectful in the classroom and always maintains a formal and serious teaching style. However, responsiveness to student emails is limited, which can make it difficult to seek clarification outside of class. Moreover, the exams do not always closely align with the material covered during lectures.

Eric Lewis is the worst professor I ever met in my life. He never pay attention to his students on the class and just want to go through everything he have to say. And don't care about whether students able to digest knowledge or not. But the other aspect make him become the worse professor is he NEVER reply to students email.

One of the best professors at Cornell. Has very good life stories that flow through to in-class topics, very friendly and kind to all the students who come to class, and is very knowledgable about both accounting info systems and advanced financial accounting. Exams are very fair, just show up to class. His exam content shows up directly on the CPA

Professor Lewis is a fair professor who teaches his coursework enthusiastically and keeps students engaged by including many of his stories about his life that are very entertaining. Additionally, his exams are fair and are similar to the practice prelim so students usually do not end up too surprised at the content covered during the prelims.
I really enjoyed listening to this professor lecture and exams were very straightforward.

Ignore all comments discussing the difficulty of his classes. Had him for ~3 classes and unless you either have room temperature IQ or no agency (going to OH) you will get a guaranteed A in any course he teaches. Subject matter expert and one of the funniest professors at Cornell.
Lewis can not teach and makes concepts more difficult than it seems. I would not recommend and he yaps too much about his own life into everything on this course. He needs to retire.

Very very bad lecturer who does not cover all of the material needed for tests. The content is very easy but it is taught so poorly that it makes the class very confusing. Homeworks are long and tedious
He does not teach he only likes to share his mid-aged crisis life in the class. No practice exam and the questions he asked during the exam are not understandable.

I would say he is the worst prof in Cornell accounting program. As an accounting professor, Eric doesnot even have a CPA. He talks a lot during class but not related to the book materials or exam. Go to his class is a waste of time. He doesnot respond to emails and he does not trust his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is nice to talk to sometimes, but talks too much around circles and about personal stories. Most disorganized course structure ive ever seen and he never goes by the syllabus. He makes up assignments and exams on the fly. His lectures lack any useful content for assignments or professionally, so you don't learn much. I skipped most lectures.
Vague instructions on projects and inefficient lecturing

Not a tough course just nothing was ever made clear.  No specific grading criteria, no assignment dates, and no exam dates. Project instructions were super vague as if he made them up randomly. Told students at the end of the semester that there will be a final project when there was also a final exam coming up. Never engaged in lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice guy and I like how course-load is little. Good class if you want to chill and not learn much.
Tough grader, beware of pop quizzes, graded by few things.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing professor, really cares about his students and passionate about teaching. Weaves real-world examples and funny stories into lecture to keeps things interesting. Was definitely not a fan of how much weight the tests were given (95/105). But maybe that's a policy thing that's out of his control, because the class is combined grad/undergrad
So engaging even though I find accounting SO boring.

Prof. Lewis was an outstanding teacher. Clear and engaging, even in otherwise boring and tedious subject matter. Students who dont attend class beware: you will not achieve an A if you arent there. Most of his testing material will also be heavily reviewed in class only, so if you attend you will be well prepared.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Lewis's systems class was great for about half of it. Learned a good amount about Tableau, which is super useful. Unfortunately there are only a few grades that contribute to your final grade, but he does not tell students how they have done on past assignments, so it is difficult to know where you stand in the class. Also doesn't email.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: Got upset because people weren't showing up to class, so he added material to the final that wasn't on the course syllabus. Generally had an attitude regarding class attendance, but he wasn't engaging and his lectures weren't interesting so it's unfair to expect participation.

Solid class. Can be dry but accounting is dry. Professor Lewis is super nice and helpful for students who come to class, but if you dont come to class the tests can be challenging. Put in the work and you'll get the grade you want.
Great class that teaches a lot about accounting. Not difficult if you come to class. Lots of example and practice problems given before exams so you know what to expect.

Professor Lewis (was in ithaca college before Cornell) is great. Very good with following up with emails and very reasonable. Provides you a lot of resources and happy to answer any of our questions. Would recommend taking his class. But not an easy A, you have to earn it. The workload is average.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: A lot of the reviews on Entner are really harsh. He is a really poor lecturer but all of the tests are very easy and the class is an easy A. All prelims and the final are open note and there is also an extra credit opportunity. Lectures are attendance optional and the final replaces your lowest prelim grade.

THE WORST PROFESSOR AT CORNELL. He can not teach. Grading is very generous but if you haven't taken Stats prior look elsewhere because you won't learn. I'm about to drop because there are better stats classes out there. Trust me.
Extremely boring lectures. His antics are very unnecessary and the course setup doesn't make sense at all. Don't recommend.

Go to lectures even though he isn't the most amazing lecturer; missing them will make a difference based on how much you'll recognize the content on the test. Tests are not difficult, but you need to be meticulous to his standards on the discussion HWs. Unlimited attempt lecture quizzes, HW, and pre-discussion quizzes make up ~50%. of final grade.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The lectures honestly made the content more confusing to understand and I stopped going after 2 weeks of class. Exams are ridiculously easy becasue they are open note and are honestly easier than AP stats. One of the easiest classes to get an A+ in but Entner's teaching ability leaves much to be desired.

Go to class and understand the lectures, then do discussion and hw. Attendance isn't mandatory but you should go to understand what's going on. He tries to make it accessible for all students no matter your background. He writes his own notes and gives a copy. TAs were mostly nice and helpful

Funny and makes the exams pretty easy, but not good at teaching. Overcomplicated most topics to the point of confusing people who understood them beforehand. I learned all of the concepts myself by reviewing the notes he gave us. Exams were open note and many of the questions basically tested your ability to find the right page in the packet.
legit the worst professor I have ever had. truly not a good guy. counting down the days to never have to be near him again.

Other reviews pretty much sum it up. Lectures are unbearably boring; Entner rambles and over-explains simple concepts. His assignments, while minimal, are mindless and unhelpful. Avoid if possible. Entner is a super weird guy and his class is generally a waste of your time.

I've seen a lot of poor reviews of this professor so I was worried when I began to take his class. After going through it, the reviews are absolutely true. This professor should not be teaching at Cornell.
Horrid lecturer but if you've already taken AP stats this class is a free A+ and the guy is so hilarious when he lectures.
Don't take his class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: honestly this was an easy A without any high school stats and some coding background. Stopped going to lectures because they were boring - make sure you do the discussions and lecture quizzes and you should be okay. The exams were not like the quizzes or lectures more so random general knowledge so be prepared for that. Felt like I learned nothing.

The course mainly covers linear regression and different kinds of ways of building models. Exams are fair and professor Entner overall is okay. I do think the course is helpful if you wanna pursue some careers relate to biostatistics.
Jeremy is notoriously one of the absolute worst professors at cornell. The only B I have received so far at cornell was a B- in his class. STAY FAR AWAY.

Lectures felt very long and hard to get through. He would over-explain simple topics and ramble. Tests were open note, but notes aren't uploaded online. Half of the things he writes down don't make any sense. Had to watch videos online when I didn't understand a topic, and realized the topic was extremely simple when explained well.

Probably one of the most work I've gotten in terms of time spent per week in my 3 years so far. Not all hard, but all tedious and boring. Don't take unless you need it to fill a req

There was a girl after time expired on one of the exams that didn't finish transferring her answers into the bubbles and he didn't let her finish. That kind of prof.

To be honest, this is a super useful class with a okay professor. Yes he is a weird guy but he is pretty generous when writing the prelims. Everything that's on the quiz can be found in your note, which is allowed to take to prelim room. He also drops 1 out of the 2 prelims if your final exam grade is better than the prelim grade.

I have nothing good to say about Entner. He made lectures boring and long, spent a lot of time on topics that were easy but breezed through hard ones, and has easy assignments that were not reflective on tests. I would turn back time if i could to take this class with a different professor. escape while u can

TAKE WITH ANYONE ELSE IF YOU CAN. Intro stats is not hard, he made it hard as possible. Notes are extremely confusing and he doesn't publish what he does in class. You can get a better grade in this class by not showing up and teaching yourself the material. HWs are worded so confusing and have nothing to do with lectures. How is this man a teacher

Jeremy, oh Jeremy. Lectures are useless: he explains topics in a dull and un-mathematical manner that goes in one ear and out the other. He once went up to my peer and asked her, "Are you crying yet?" He's in his own head and will go out of his way to waste time yelling at someone leaving lecture early, etc. The notes are as confusing as possible.

Not a great teacher but people are exaggerating on these reviews. He isn't really that bad. The labs are awful and take way too long but exams are open note. I think it's helpful going to lecture but you don't have to. Exams only make up 50% of your grade which is nice and they are multiple choice. No practice exam though. Not great, not awful.

Not a bad dude; lectures can be very boring, but is very responsive to students' questions. Class itself is not difficult if you're willing to show up and put in the bare minimum amount of work, and you do learn a lot regarding the material listed in the syllabus.

Genuinely the most confusing lecturer I've met at Cornell—including all of the upper level engineering classes I've taken. Attendance is not mandatory so just study on your own (do go to discussions though for the R sections) and rely on youtube videos. Haven't been to lecture after the first month so I don't know if he's mean or whatever
Overall an extremely inflexible person who's hard to deal with

It sucks that he is the only teacher teaching stats. the lectures are useless, not engaging. He also over complicates things when he could just say things in simple terms. 

I got a better grade on my second prelim than I did on my first and I didn't attend a single lecture and watched youtube videos to explain concepts.
The biggest piece of _ ever.

Wow. This Professor is the absolute worst at actually teaching ideas simply. He will take a simple concept and explain it in the most confusing way possible (im a physics major).He seems to think his students are "afraid of math" so tries to substitute w/ words. Math is a language of its own. Stick to engineering/math dept classes.

Just an actual piece of work. Makes jokes about how he doesn't want to pay child support and picks on students asking them if his tests makes them cry. Like what is up with you man. His class is ridiculously easy if you don't go and just study on your own/run through the notes, a lot of people are failing and you really should have no excuse to.

TONS of work, normally 3 short quizzes per week but infinite tries at least, allowed to have class notes for the test which makes it rly easy to pass but the discussion hw is insanely difficult and unneccessary and just truly ridiculous, but I took ap stats in high school so the notes and a 4 hour study session was enough to get a 90
the sun of a beach. He is mentally challenged.

I think Prof Entner is a nice guy who is largely misunderstood at Cornell. His classes are hard. He is not the best at explaining material, and can sometimes come across as rude/dismissive to students, but I don't believe it's intentional. I probably wouldn't take him again. I didn't learn much about stats, but learned a lot about R programming.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Discussion work is worded confusingly. He gave students zeros on an assignment if they were absent the Friday before Spring Break (attendance is usually not mandatory)! His lectures are extremely repetitive yet he somehow still fails to show us how equations are applied (which you need to teach yourself for the exams). There is so much busy work.
It feels like he wants you to do worse. Nobody goes to lecture because they're so useless and no material is covered during the lecture.

Negative reviews here are true. Like others, I was told things that made no sense. The exams didn't reflect the material well. Not allowed to have his written notes, not allowed to retake quizzes for practice before exams, told to bum them off others. Directions for open notes are contradicting. Forced to use trash calculators. Get with the times!!
horrible professor. whats on the exam does not line up with what is taught in class. if you can take a different stats class do it. dropped it after the first exam because it was so horrible
he is just too mean

AVOID AT ALL COSTS. Lies about what materials students will have available to study for exams, refuses to help students and mocks them when they ask for help, constantly makes uncomfortable jokes about students, does everything in his power to ensure students fail. The day he retires will be a national holiday.
First day of class but this fire

Unfunny. The material is not difficult, but he is an incredibly rude man, made inappropriate jokes in class, and replied to emails in three days with one word. 
Just watch videos on youtube and ask your TAs for help, bc jeremy will not help anyone ever

This man is insufferable. I'm serious. Easy A course but I didn't even go to lectures because he's so irritating and inappropriate. Do not even try to email him because he will respond to you in a very rude and dismissive manner, usually with just one line which is rage-inducing. Worst professor I've ever had and I'm a senior.

Professor Entner is blunt and unkind. He often targets individuals in class, and while trying to be funny, it is an uncomfortable environment. He is not understanding or empathetic. There was an exam timing issue that affected many students. I emailed him, and he sent a rude response, making me feel disrespected. Easy class, bad professor.

I wouldn't worry about the exams, but the lectures are boring and unhelpful. You're better off finding youtube videos and teaching yourself the content. Also, you will not get an A+ in this class because the syllabus says that you need higher than a 99.8% to achieve that and he's very particular about the details.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: honestly if you just go to class and have notes on top of his you will be fine, exams are open note and you can figure it out even if you didnt go to class (make sure you know where everything is) hes pretty chill in office hours, sometimes makes stupid jokes but not out of harm. lectures get boring but hes nice as long as youre respectful in class
He was not a good lecturer in any regard it was very much a self taught class. He is not an understanding person at all.

As a person he can be a little rude. He's not super responsive or accessible. Aside from that, lectures are fine, prelims are open note MC, homeworks are not too hard to do well on. The class can be annoying- he makes a lot of random errors that can make things confusing, but it's fine overall and he doesn't make it too hard to do well.

This guy was actually the worst. His exams made no sense, his discussions were useless and annoying, and his lectures. His lectures were such a bore and he thought he was so funny making what he thought were clever jokes but they weren't. He got mad when he saw people leaving the lecture hall but tbh I don't blame them.

Avoid him at all costs! During class he often waists time by telling insensitive and inappropriate jokes. He tends to skip over important material and ends up putting it on the test. He reads over his notes and the little work that he does is not applicable to anything. He does not post practice material for exams causing mass confusion.

Very, very bad lecturer. Lectures are confusing and convoluted...he is also completely unreachable and you will have to go to your TAs with questions. Couldn't handle listening to him, so I stopped going to lecture halfway through the semester.

The lectures in the first month of class were fine, but once the content became more complex, it became evident there was no reason to attend lectures. This is one of those 'teach yourself' kind of classes, so I used online sources to teach me the content since the lectures did nothing. Generous grade weight distributions so easy to pass.

Actually the worst. So horrendous at teaching i'm not sure how he even got the job and I'm convinced he wants his students to do bad in the class. I would've never taken this class if I knew how bad he was. Made us code in statistics for some reason which makes no sense either. Never obtained a single piece of information from lecture.
Do not take if you struggle with math he is so confusing, does not explain concepts well and is overall a rude person.

He is a terrible lecturer, his tests are written extremely poorly to the point of being nearly undecipherable, and he has an army of undergrad TAs who are not good section leaders. My TA told me to use ChatGPT to figure out the problem I was working on because they could not figure it out. Avoid him at all costs, he will just confuse you more.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Yeah he's a bit weird but if you do the work, take good notes, and have friends in the class to work on the labs with, easy A.

I don't really get why he's a professor it never felt like he liked teaching. His lectures were so boring and honestly made me more confused about lots of subjects than before (just watch YouTube videos). He was not just rude to the students but I also noticed him being rude to his TAs. The exams were just kind of weird logic puzzles.

Lectures are extremely boring and he is disrespectful and insufferable to be around. Makes distasteful jokes commenting on people's ethnicities and appearances. Does weird crowd control during lecture by calling people out which makes everyone uncomfortable. Doesn't respond to emails, no rounding, prelims unrelated to notes, makes stats too hard

avoid him at all costs, especially if stats is not your major. labs and exams are COMPLETELY unrelated to the lecture content and graded at an unreasonable standard. the class is very unforgiving and will suck the soul out of you.

Most of reviews are overly critical. That said, he is an odd ball and not a great lecturer. Simple concepts can be confusing. Rude emails. Dumb grading system. Rules won't bend. Late by just 1 second = 0, no excuses. If you just do work on time you should be fine. I recommend taking a different stats such as 2150.

Jeremy Entner will make it his personal mission to ensure you do not understand statistics. Genuinely one of the most confusing professors I have ever had, and the TAs were sophomores and juniors who had no idea what was going on in the course. Avoid at all costs.

The R class was great with him, super boring, but doable workload. He dropped our prelims, and 85% of grading came from problem sets and labs that you can work with others on. He gets distracted easily and does not accept late work for any reason. If you need to ask questions because you were talking he'll harass you instead of answering.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I suggest taking the class because it is Easy to do well but the teacher is such an a-h0le so don't expect to like him. Rude emails and no leniency. 50% of the class should be an automatic 100% though because of the weekly assignments.

Pretty poor teacher. His lectures are a real snore and you often end up just having to self-study in the end. Prelims vary a lot in difficulty. Without AP Stats already under my belt, there is no way I would have gotten the grade I did.

Honestly, the class itself wasn't hard but the lectures are unbearable. He tries to be funny and engage with the class but it honestly isn't that great. I didn't feel like I learned a lot in the lectures but more so in the discussions which attendance is mandatory. but whether the discussion is good or not really depends on your TA so goodluck.

Entner's teaching style sucks. The videos he posts are way better. Lab and exam questions are not clear and sometimes make no sense. No curve at all, I literally had an 89.99% and still didn't get an A-. Learning R is fun if you have a good TA and you can take the lecture quizzes as many times as you need to get a 100% before they close.

Very bad at teaching, give ambiguous exam questions and instructions, is mostly condescending, never reply emails, and seems annoyed when students ask him questions (sometimes judgemental). if not like teaching why become an instructor??? just avoid him

My second semester with Entner and he's sure one of a kind. It's hard to do poorly and isn't too much work and you learn an ok amount, particularly using R and regression, but it's always typos or questions on labs or exams that are very ambiguous. The open notes tests and recorded lectures are what make Entner and the course bearable.

Nice guy but you need to watch the videos in addition to lecture. Course material is extremely bland, but Entner tries his best and  any other professor would get 1/5 reviews. Biggest complaint is zero curve at all.
He is ok. His tests will have things you could never have expected or planned to study for. He will not round your grade at all.

Not the "easy A" class everyone says it is. Concepts are explained poorly/confusingly. Can use a cheat sheet on exams, but only basic calculators allowed despite stat software used in section. Easy to get full section/quiz points, making up 50% of grade. But to do well on other 50% (exams), expect to teach yourself. I barely made the A threshold.

Professor Entner was pretty good in lectures but material was simply enough to be learned outside of class as well. Tests were pretty reasonable as you are allowed a cheat-sheet and other assignments helped boost overall grade. Would highly recommend class, especially for non-stem majors as material is not too complicated.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good lecturer and a funny guy. Made a very foreign concept interesting/enjoyable through his unconventional sense of humor (he can be out of pocket). Tests are not very hard (cheat sheet allowed). Only work was textbook readings, weekly quizzes (unlimited attempts), and section activities (time limit). Overall, great experience and a good class!
Don't make the same mistake I made.

This guy is the worst. Actually the worst class Ive ever taken at cornell. He teaches NOTHING, seems like he knows nothing either. His tests have the WORST formats, and everything he does is so extra and not helpful. Never replied to ANY emails that are sent to him over the semester. All around USELESS. 0/10.

3010 was an unpleasant experience. Jeremy is not an engaging lecturer, and most people did not attend them. There is no textbook, and the class relies on a notes document Jeremy provides. The tests could be annoying and tricky but were open note, which I appreciated. Late assignments are not accepted and Jeremy would be condescending about it.

He seems like a nice guy,  but he is a TERRIBLE teacher. The discussions are led by other students who don't know what is going on. All the tests are on things barely mentioned in class. He literally is useless, there is no way to contact him, no guide to what is on the exams, and literally no access to any forms of help or practice for this class.
open note tests. that says it all.

Ok so most people dislike him but he's really not that bad. Tests are open note for 3010 and only count for 50% of your grade. Now his test questions are a bit weird but if you pay any amount of attention to the lectures you can figure out how to do them with the notes. This is the major complaint most people have.
He's ok.

His lectures were kind of useless, but I found him to be quite funny. He always wears this backwards camera wherever he goes. I did everything in my dorm (read through the Google slides myself), never went to class etc and still got an A.
skipped the lecture because they were long and boring and didn't want to hear his lame joke. lecture vids posted were lifesavers

Best, easiest college class ever. The material was basic, the tests were exactly like the questions done in discussion section, and the grading scheme emphasized homework, quizzes, and discussions as much as exams. It's totally possible to skip class and still get an A (unfortunately doesn't give A+). He's a quirky guy but I found it entertaining.
Tests are fair if you just listen to the lectures, and he uploads everything online. Multiple attempts allowed for quizzes to get a good grade.

Definitely the least engaging professor I've every had, which explains why 80% of the class didn't attend his lectures. He never replies to emails and his lectures were pretty painful to sit through. I appreciated his leniency with weekly quizzes, but he worded tests so badly that many students without a stats background were destined to fail.

I took his 3010 and 3020. lectures are kind of dry and there are so many trivial details of stat models / R code that you must pay attention to later in 3020. He uploads all lecture videos to Canvas, but his lectures are generally better (at least 60% students never go to lectures). His OH is helpful and he answers individual questions pretty well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took STSCI 2100 this semmester and I absolutely hated it. I had taken a previous into to stats college class that I got a 100 average in and while the homework and discussions were easy. He doesn't word the test well. He is never responsive to emails and the ta I had didn't know anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Sometimes students can be a little hyperbolic when they say "oh my god, this professor is the worst." Jeremy Entner lives up to the hype. He is easily the worst teacher I have ever had. Like, in my entire academic history from preschool to college. I would choose my daycare teacher from when I was 3 over Jeremy Enter to teach me statistics. Awful.

Professor Entner does his best to make the lectures fun and enjoyable. Despite it being a 4-credit course, the work was lighter than any other course that I've taken. Lectures weren't mandatory, and he recorded videos for the people who didn't want to show up to the lectures. Definitely take Professor Entner's class for intro stats!

Lectures were extremely dry to the point that they made me hate the content that was being covered and really made me not want to become a stats major. There is no extra credit which is terrible because the class isn't curved and the median is low. The workload is fine but there are no practice prelims or a textbook to get help from.

Entner is one of the more down to earth and funny professors I have had. Always cracks jokes and really tries not to overcomplicate lectures and exams. One wrinkle is that the discussion sections mainly use software not available on the exams, leading to exams that students have not been adequately prepared for. Overall kind and willing to help.
Stats prelims are worded oddly. He makes basic concepts (ie graphs/ p value) more difficult by poorly explaining them. You might be better off in Bio stats.
Just cannot understand him for some reason. I have taken stats class with another prof and found it interesting; however, he pushed me away from learning more stats.

The class was super easy, even with no stats or R background. Lectures got pretty boring and some of the exam questions were a little mysterious, but labs, homework, and quizzes were essentially a guaranteed 100 as long as you put in a tiny bit of effort.

This class was not that hard if you have stats experience and the labs on R were very helpful. The only issues with this prof are that some of the questions on his tests are unclear and he is sometimes mean to students in lecture. He does give extra credit and is generally responsive. This class is easy enough that you can get by just with your TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Lectures are useless and irrelevant to exams.
Lecture and lecture quizzes pretty much irrelevant to exam.

Stats and R both aren't my thing but Jeremy made them both pretty easy to understand as a non-math person. All content is covered in lecture, and he makes it easy to take good notes. The class overall is pretty light, not a ton of work.

This class is not too conceptually challenging, but it does take up a lot of time. First of all, don't even think about skipping lecture, since everything covered will come up later. Aside from that, the weekly labs have a lot of questions, and are also ambiguously worded to the point that many people need clarification in office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Haha 89.68, what do you want? No curve, no extra credit, you know how much time I have spent on the course? Every weekend, I slept at 3 to finish the lab. Ended up with a B+ but I got A+ on my last stats class.

He is the type of guy who does not round up 89.5 to 90 in the final grade. His exam is also weirdly worded. It was very confusing when you cannot understand what he is trying to test in his exam. Trust me: AVOID him anyway.
Don't get close to statistic here or you will be miserable
very entitled and arrogant person. strange because of how incompetent he is.
Jeremy, why are your tests like this? The wording makes the test more about solving a lexicon puzzle instead of the actual content.

The class is not difficult if you go to lecture and lab. Stats isn't really my thing so I didn't find the material very engaging, but if you keep up with the workload you will get a good grade. The professor gives extra credit if the prelim medians aren't where he wants them to be, and you can tell he wants students to succeed in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Jeremy is, well, goofy. He has this interesting wit that I truly thought was funny. However, his tests were literally out of left field; they were much harder than class material. His explanation of R is a joke. Does give extra credit. ILR stats way less work and easier, take that instead if you can.

The class content was not difficult, however, grading was biased and arbitrary. His exam q's felt like they were testing your understanding of his psyche rather than the material. His behavior in lecture was also immature. He constantly made people uncomfortable by calling students out and mocking them, even for things like going to the bathroom.

Jeremy, oh Jeremy, what a man. While he was a really quirky teacher, and some people didn't like that, he truly knew his stuff when it came to statistics. The class was relatively easy and enjoyable, with little homework, but his tests weren't a good reflection of that we were learning. Notes were helpful, and was always responsive, ready to help!

Lecture feels more like bad stand up than actual class. Not extremely enjoyable and the prof uses strange analogies instead of actually explaining why things work the way they do. Clicker quizzes aren't hard. There is no curve but the grading is somewhat generous.
Very engaging teaching style. Gave extra credit and wanted students to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Jeremy is one of the rudest, least professional professors I have ever had. Not only is his teaching style odd, distracting and unprofessional, he seems to hate students who bring up anything to do with grades. His tests are also extremely irrelevant to actually using statistics - they are more like decoding double negative T/F questions
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Very rude. You learn very little. He doesn't explain most things well. Instead of learning why statistics work, you plug numbers into the equations from your notes that he lets you use on everything. Assumes everyone is lazy. I missed one lecture and went to office hours, and he shamed me about how I would've known the material if I went to lecture
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: His lectures are awkward, and he is always picking on students. Beware of sitting in the front. He spends more time trying to be an awkward SNL character than a nice prof. He is also super rude.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: As a near the end of my senior year, I just wanted to come back around and acknowledge Prof. Foster. She is an exemplary human being and brings so much to the table as a Cornell English grad herself. I didn't love the course material since I'm not a Victorianist, but I will treasure having known her during my time here!

Her class was an absolute breeze work wise, and the content (I took No Spoilers!) was interesting. The workload never exceeds a fairly sized essay and she is genuinely one of the kindest people on earth. She's extremely lenient/understanding which was really helpful during tough times, & cares about her students. TAKE A CLASS WITH HER SHES AMAZING

Dr. Foster was excellent, and I would highly recommend taking any of her classes. All classwork and reading is super manageable and interesting. I feel as though my writing genuinely improved throughout the FWS. She gives great, specific feedback on all writing.

Great Prof for my FWS; super kind and understanding of people's other responsibilities outside of his class. Her feedback is really helpful, and the classwork is very light. Overall, great prof, and would definitely take her class again!

ENGL 3747 was a breath of fresh air! Grade is based on participation (attendance and speaking), 3 short book reports, mid-term, final essay, and a presentation. The assignments were manageable, fun, and included many options for us to choose from. Foster was charming and engaging, making the plethora of readings worthwhile! A must-take at Cornell.

Took ENGL3747. Dr. Foster is hands down the best professor at Cornell. This was my favorite class! It is not burdensome at all, but there is a lot of reading (super fun though) so don't fall behind. The class is pretty discussion heavy and you're technically graded on it. Highly recommend to anyone remotely interested in crime fiction in any form.
One of the most kind and caring profs at Cornell and very knowledgable too. Crime fiction class is insightful and gives you a lot of flexibility. Recommend to anyone.

One of the nicest professors. She taught the FWS Rom Coms course. She works with you to set up flexible deadlines around other exams and makes reading and analyzing Shakespeare fun. Just apply yourself and put real thought into your papers and you'll be fine. Only 3 complete papers and some other minor things. She also gives amazing feedback.

Professor Foster makes class really enjoyable and interesting. She gives great feedback and helped me take my research paper ideas to the next level. I would take any class with her regardless of the subject honestly.

She taught my FWS on Shakespeare and Rom Coms. She was engaging and the class was discussion based. We had really interesting conversation and she was great at encouraging ideas. Only homework was to read Shakespeare, write, and watch the occasional film. Fair grading with helpful feedback. She connects well with students. This was a great class!

This course was super fun and enjoyable. I loved how Professor Foster focused on content that was interesting to us. Professor foster brought a lot of energy to class, graded in a timely manner (a couple days), and made herself available with office hours and one-on-one meeting.

Eshan's lectures were straightforward and his exams were difficult but fair. Much of the lecture material is covered in the textbook, but attending and participating in lecture helped to gain a deeper understanding of the concepts.
Cares more about research than teaching the class. Don't bother going to lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lectures, especially ones with proofs, lacked depth. Textbook was much more thorough. I would have hoped at least for pointers or intuition. Nothing of the sort. Attended less than a quarter of the lectures, found it more worthwhile to read the textbook thoroughly. Exams were graded fairly, and generously. Read the textbook. Spend time on homework.
Not the best at explaining things. Algo is a tough class in general but can't say that having him as a prof made it better.

Can't explain intuitively, most students rely on AI to explain concepts. Topics are not useful (it's a theory class, so completely fine of course), but also not fun. 
Over-focused on NP reductions. Overall least favorite class I've taken at Cornell.
Made a difficult class better than it could have been
CS 4820 was probably one of the easiest classes I've taken here thanks to him, what an amazing Professor, learned so much from this class, if he's teaching definitely recommend taking it with him!
I LOVE ESHAN!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
pretty chill guy, workload was reasonable, course was organized, nothing to complain about
He is a great professor. Extremely based and goated.

Lectures are very well-presented. Professor is very nice and takes care to ensure what he teaches is relatively easy. Homework needs some construction but generally manageable. Exams are straightforward and does not include hard questions that require creative thinking. A pretty routine algorithm course that is well taught and not too hard.
good professor

Friedman got review bombed because  the ILRID 1530 exam was cruel. However, I was in that class and have since taken others with him, and he is a great professor otherwise. Engaging lectures, readings aren't bad, and you will actually learn stuff if you listen. 

The one exam (which was bad) doesn't reflect what your experience will be.

Professor Friedman's ratings on this site are unfair. He is an amazing professor! The people who complain are those who want to have every single test question spoon-fed to them. He is one of the few professors that doesn't read word for word off his notes, but actually lectures and tells stories about the content making it easier to memorize.
terrible professor, lied to all of us to what the test was going to be on. avoid!

Professor Friedman is the biggest yapper teacher I've ever had. Not only did he extensively talk about unimportant topics during lecture and did not reflect the important information into his powerpoints, having 4 slides of 3 bullet points at most for a 50 minute class. His quizzes was very reasonable but his final exam was A JOKE. 0/10
The grade on the final was literally a D, but he did not curve it. Very unclear instructions for every essay with no fair rubric and pretty subjective grading as well.

Friedman's class was very fair other than the final. You're seeing all these bad reviews because he'd created an unconventional final exam, but overall he wasn't bad. He was a good lecturer, and was one of the few that explained and never read off the slides. If you did well on the papers, and ace the prelim (easy), there's no reason to complain

One of the worst professors I've ever had. Lectures are not helpful at all, especially for an impossible final with a 68% average and no curve. Maybe spend more time on the classes you're teaching than joining the encampment that's supporting terrorism.
No rubrics for his papers, boring lectures with minimal information on slides, and is inconsiderate to students. However, if you pay attention and study for the final, you will do well.
No no no.

Had Friedman for ICL 2350 and ILRID 1530. Made a super hard final for 1530 and one that seemed easy for 2350, but was graded very harshly. Barley puts anything on the slides so hard to follow along. Don't take!

Ok until the end of semester -- created an incredibly detail heavy final that was only 15 questions long 3 days before the final -- scheduled a test review at 10pm the day before the final and EXPLICITLY told students that the exam was 'not about any specific details in the readings' -- the final ONLY tested on obscure parts of the class. Awful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor told his TAs to not give too many As on the papers because he didn't want the class median to be high and then he made the final impossible 10/15 avg. He lied about curving the final. All this to not mention the fact that his lectures were dull and unengaging, at times it felt like he hadn't even looked at his slides before lectures.

Prof Friedman did nothing to engage us with his very boring lectures. At least pose a question or two to the class, instead of yapping about material that will not be on the final exam. 

The final exam was multiple choice, some questions ranged from A-H. Even the current professor of the course pointed out where he went wrong, not a good look....
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: MISERABLE POS GAVE IMPOSSIBLE EXAM QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS TO PURPOSEFULLY THROW OFF STUDENTS
Implemented an arbitrary negative curve to the first half of graded papers when students scored too highly on the first paper. Final was made on purpose to trick students and even TA's were stunned.

Awful. His lectures have 3 words and when the test comes around he wont give you any notes. All the questions on the final were different than the review session, and 75% of the questions about random statistics in 1 reading that we never discussed. The average for the final was a 65; he refused to curve and didn't release final grades for months.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His structure of the course was completely unreasonable with a final exam that doesn't represent anything relevant from the course. Both TA's and students were blindsided by Friedman's choices and left everyone in an unfair state.

He gave an impossible test that covered specific statistics which were irrelevant to the broader concepts of the course. The average of the exam was a 68% which he decided not to curve, citing the class average of a B+ to somehow justify the final. The people who did well guessed and the people who knew the content likely failed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Friedman's made it incredibly difficult to do well in his class - the slides have few words and difficult-to-understand concepts are never fully explained or reinforced during lecture. No detailed rubric is provided for either writing assignment. The final exam was 15 vaguely-worded multiple choice questions with up to 8 answer choices.

Got mad everyone did well on the first paper and added in a criteria AFTER we submitted so no one could get 100. Made the final the most insanely hard exam anyone has ever seen in their whole lives. Finalized it the night before too we took it. The median average for my section's final was 10.4/15!! 69%. Petty.

Although Friedman was unpopular because of the final, I thought he was great. Very interesting material and great lectures (you have to really listen though because the slides are pretty blank). Essays were really fun and midterm was extremely easy. The final wasn't great but not as bad as people say. I disagree that he's rude/unprofessional

He is an intelligent professor who not only has detailed lectures and cares about his students, but works with them if they are struggling so they can succeed too. Although I liked him and his lectures, it was a bit difficult to study for exams and write essays because his slides were somewhat general, and he did not provide his TAs with rubrics.

Multiple choice final that goes up to option H thats worth a quarter of our grade is absurd. This guy is also very disrespectful to students to the extent that he doesn't even acknowledge our presence when we simply say hi to him. Tests involve material he didnt teach

He knows what he's talking about but is probably better for higher level courses. He clearly did not care about this class and made no efforts to connect with students. He seems to want students to fail and he through very hard working TAs under the bus.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Friedman is an unnecessarily disrespectful professor. He is arrogant and rude to students. His exam reviews do not prepare you for his tests. He has intentionally made exams different from what he tells you to review for just to bring grades down. He should not be teaching intro classes.

Professor Friedman repeatedly showed the lack of effort he put into this course. His lecture slides were very lazy and hard to follow. He did not give TAs rubrics for essays until after they were due, harming students who sought help. With only 15 questions, the final exam focused on minute details from lecture slides and readings.

Was not my teaching style, had no words on the slide and gave no rubrics when grading essays so we had no idea what he wanted us to write about. Also the final exam was 15 questions (25% or grade) all with 5-8 answer choices on things we did not talk about in lecture. I was very prepared for the exam based on lectures but I think I failed.

Never before today have I been moved to write a negative review here. Professor Friedman purposefully wrote an incredibly confusing final. On top of his reputation for being rude and unprofessional, he failed to plan ahead to create a fair grade average in the class. To artificially lower the average, he wrote the final incredibly poorly.

His lectures gave me chills and I found his module the most compelling and easiest of the 4 (though I don't know my grade on the last one yet). Lecture is not mandatory but go, well worth your time and his slides are only a few short bullet points and a some pictures for an an hour and 15 minute lecture.

Very knowledgeable about Chinese affairs and an amazing lecturer. Attendance is not mandatory but you should show up to class since his slides are very simple (sometimes only pictures). You will also learn a lot more if you participate in discussions on the readings and current Chinese affairs, but in-class participation is not graded.

I absolutely loved Friedman's lectures, but outside of class, I thought he was a bit of a jerk. He acted like he was above everyone. He also had a really unfair late policy for the take-home where he took 2% off regardless of when you turned it in and marked people later who submitted exactly on time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Have to be in person for the lectures to do well on the module exam but it's worth it. He is a very compelling lecturer and one of the best professors in the class. Ties lectures to present day current events making it even more interesting. Also, the module exam wasn't too hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor, knowledgeable, you will learn a lot
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Best class I've taken at Cornell - you'll learn so much. Engaging lectures, take lots of notes & do all the readings. 2 reading quizzes and one final paper, very manageable to do well. Mandatory attendance & participating. Great teacher & researcher, presents information in an engaging & accessible way. Take this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Taken online. The prof is a smart guy but lecture is pretty boring. There isn't any work except for a few short reflections and a final paper. A bit hard to follow if you don't know anything about China but you can still get by. This class won't blow you away but there's nothing to hate about it. Grading seemed pretty lenient.

Shame for Cornell to have such a professor who cannot think logically nor incorporate any quantitative data into the context, but rather only good at blaming China to appease to his masters for grants.
such a cool guy and brings a really interesting perspective. Ive taken two classes with him and one of the best/ most relatable profs in ILR

Took Friedman for a writing seminar and loved it. By far, the brightest prof I've had in ILR , and a cool guy too. Really knows his stuff. Serious on attendance and participation, read the material and give thoughtful answers. He's a fair grader, not harsh but not easy, go to his office hours and get feedback. I would absolutely take him again!
Amazing professor, very clear, informative, and engaging. Every lecture is well presented. I wouldn't pass up an opportunity to take a class with him. I've learned so much.

Very into his own research work, but is also too pompous in that regard. The grading is too harsh and he does not really understand East Asian labor at all. He thinks he's rather superior to his students and the people he studies

Chinese labor.  Very informed guy that has done research in China about workers and speaks the language too.  Need to do readings and had 3 quizzes with a final research paper. Class attendance is required (signin sheet) and participate and ask THOUGHTFUL question.  I think he has a good BS meter, and it might hurt you.  Very knowledgeable!

I really liked the course content, but the professor ruined it. She is so picky with wording and leaves the craziest revision comments on essays. She also does not tolerate even being a little late and expects you to put down your phone the moment she starts talking. She will call you out in class if you do something that bothers her.

She is extremely up-tight and allows no room for creativity. She will take off points if you come in a second late and will ridicule you in front of the entire class. Her expectations are at times unclear and the assignments themselves are largely unrelated to the class.
The class is easy but the professor will make you regret it. You've got to be on her favorites list to get by easily.

Does not "believe" in giving 100s. Soft spoken, but speaks audaciously to children, students, and all. Very strict classroom rules. No leeway for attendance. Thought the class content was okay and easy, but disliked it purely because of her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class was easy content wise. She has a bunch of nonsense rules on classroom behavior. If you enter the classroom before class time with earbuds in you will be reprimanded. You are not allowed to use the bathroom during class either, does not realize that we are adults. She is also very confrontational.

I came into class not knowing a single word of Polish and had a terrific experience. Ewa is super fair and thoughtful on grading, and is extremely supportive. There are straightforward rules in the class... you need to be willing to follow and respect them. Polish is a unique course that I highly recommend versus more traditional language courses.

Professor Bachminska is an exceptional instructor! I took POLSH 2034: Intermediate Polish II with her and there was never a time when I did not feel supported, heard, or respected. I highly recommend taking any class with her :)

In the Polish class, I liked the best the trip to Cornell museum. I also really enjoyed the movie about Walesa. Ewa even brought Polish sweets for us and we learned how to order food in Polish at a restaurant. I recommend taking her class.

Simply one of the best language courses I have ever taken. Professor Bachminska is very engaging and makes learning Polish a truly wholesome experience of Polish culture, film, art and history. Taking this course made me visit Poland. I would like to take more Polish courses as long as she teaches. She is very dedicated and excellent in her craft.

Very poor instructions on assignments followed by grading on criteria that was never stated. English is not her first language and it clearly shows when your paper is read. Forces you to limit your writing. Its not too hard to get an A if you try and guess what she wants, but it could get frustrating.

This guy rocks. I don't like Econ generally, but I loved this class. In-class debate and controversy common, any ILRie should love this class. Structured for each topic to have 2 competing sides. You read different scholarly takes on the higher ed policy, then debate and hash it out in class, with Riehl clearly providing both sides objectively.
Professor Riehl has been my favorite teacher at Cornell and his class has been excellent. Must take for all ILRies, Inequality in higher education. Tough class but very worth it.

The material was presented in an understandable way. Lectures were interesting and group debates were incredibly engaging. He is a fair grader and offers ample feedback to do better next time. He is also incredibly understanding and approachable, so be sure to go to him if you need help. Could not recommend more.
Professor Riehl is a great professor--definitely the best teaching ILRLE 2400. His lectures are generally clear and understandable, and he is very accessible outside of class. Highly recommend!

The best option for labor econ. Super clear lectures; basically all you need to study for his tests is to copy down his notes verbatim and study them later. Lots of availability outside of class, where he is very helpful both with problem sets and with test prep. Problem sets are pretty straightforward for the most part. Tests really aren't bad.

Professor Riehl is super nice and caring. His lectures are great, so I never read the textbook. He basically solves the homework problems for you during his office hours, and practice questions are really good prep for his exams
lectures were good and nicely organized. workload very reasonable. he is not very approachable though, it felt like his fight or flight response activated when I approached him for a regrade.

Not an approachable teacher nor a fair grader. After going to his OH after a bad grade, he didnt offer any advice and just said that I was unlucky and do better on the next test. Also on one homework he agreed my answer was right but since it was not what the key said he gave no points back. He also lacked any empathy or understanding.

Probably one of the best professors in the Econ department, If not THE best. Evan is a great lecturer and class discussions are great too. The problem sets are very interesting and not overly difficult, and the paper assignment is as well. Fair grader. Very engaged/ passionate/ accessible, overall a great guy. Highly recommend this professor.

Professor Riehl is very nice. His lectures are organized and engaging. The workload is very manageable and his tests are easy as long as you can answer the questions on his slides. 100% strongly recommended.

Professor Riehl assigned very interesting readings that you will want to complete. His lectures were also always provocative and engaging. The problem sets were all fun challenges. Bonuses offered for some of the problem sets.
Professor Riehl is super nice!

Great class, super interesting content. Professor Frank is clearly very knowledgeable and passionate. However, he would frequently get distracted by questions or go on a tangent and not get to significant amounts of material. Lots of reading, need to be good with timed essays. Class is based on 3 tests and participation in section(run by grad TA).

He was fine but would sometimes take a long time getting through material. Honestly the main problem was other students asking long, complicated, and unrelated questions. Not his fault at all, but still feel like he could be more concise with things.
Lectures were great; he's a fantastic speaker, and he broke down the readings well. Readings were somewhat substantial, but not too bad. Always happy to answer a question, too.

I liked Frank's class on American Political Thought, though I felt like he did not follow the syllabus as well as he should have. We would do A LOT more reading outside of class because Frank wouldn't be able to finish his main point at the end of each lecture. Still, he is a fantastic lecturer and is clearly passionate about he teaches.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great class with interesting readings and a professor that clearly knows what he is talking about. However he will spend most of lecture discussing things that are only tangentially related to the readings. Grading feels tough during the semester but isn't actually that bad by the end. Would recommend.
Great professor and super nice guy. The readings for this class are heavy and the work is very theoretical. Would take again.

Extraordinarily knowledgeable and gives very passionate lectures. Not afraid to challenge students with difficult, controversial, but phenomenal texts! Go to lectures, and you will be fine. Only downside is that he is so popular, and it's hard to get time during his office hours, especially in a big class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's passionate but it doesn't make political theory more interesting. Grading is based on 2 papers worth 25% each, section participation worth 25%, and an essay final worth 25%. Tons of reading - we're averaging a book or so every week. Seems like a great guy and an intellectual. Just not for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Take his class!!!! One of the best lecturers you will encounter at Cornell! Jason Frank is absolutely brilliant and the class wasn't that difficult. The median was an A-, so as long as you read the material and listen to the lectures you are fine.

average professor who seems good because of passion and delivery. grading is based 3 papers and discussion. lectures generally have little to do with the actual paper prompts. if ur a good writer and can understand the readings well and incorporate that into ur essays u can get an A
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Jason Frank is an Intellectual, listen and learn
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: He is so far my favorite professor at Cornell. The reading material is quite difficult, but his lectures magically conveys the ideas in those texts in a clear and in-depth way. He is extremely passionate about the topic and he interacts with students in his lectures actively. All these aspects adds to the attractiveness of his personality.
best
BEST and HOTTEST professor ever. Smart. Eloquent. Passionate. Helpful. Great lecturer. Nough said.

Very interesting material and fascinating lectures you won't want to miss. Also, you shouldn't miss them, because you will struggle with the papers if you don't go to lecture. Material is hard, but getting an A is not overly difficult
He is a great professor, and actually peaked my interest in Theory. Don't miss lecture though, because he does have a lot to say.

He was just ok. Very passionate about the subject, but his lectures were wandering and sometimes lacked focus. It was his first time teaching the large lecture course, so perhaps he's better in smaller settings...

Professor Frank is outstanding.  He has the unique ability to direct discussion to bring out the most interesting and thought-provoking elements of American political theory.  Any class with him is highly recommended.  If you work hard, you will do very well.

He expects a lot, stimulates interest, and makes you think critically about American political thought -- and this was a writing seminar.  If you want to learn, and you're willing to do some work, take any class he teaches.
My favorite professor at Cornell! He's very knowledgable and is a great teacher.. He makes class very interesting especially through the discussions. I liked the final project too.
A very helpful course for your data science and AI career. I got some questions in my recent job interview that were so close to the homework problems. Thank you Professor!!!
Like his courses! Rich and useful content. Fair grading. Very supportive.
I would give between 4and 5 but most people gave 5 so I follow. He is in demand as others said.
A very popular professor. I am so glad to get into his class again this semester

Ed Discussion was excellent.
Lecture content preparation and delivery with high quality.
Excellent course. Very useful of operations and with wide variety of application to multiple domains.
Overall the course was well structured and organized. The seminars were especially interesting in terms of the topics and research covered.
I appreciated how the lecture notes displayed and explained the practical applications of particular optimization techniques in industry. Grading is fair and reasonable.
Professor You is a good lecturer and speaker overall and he has a very unique teaching style that is highly respected and adequately engaging to students. He is also very knowledge and an expert.
Interesting course on digital agriculture. There are diverse speakers and there expertise on the work
I like the flexibility offered by the professor. The topics are interesting. A great experience overall!
Interesting topics. Fair and reasonable grading
I learned a lot from the course. The professor seems an easy and fair grader.
Great course and interesting topics. Many emerging ones are covered.
Lectures are clear and organized. Very understanding about end-of-semester stress. Dropping HW at the end really helps with the workload. Would definitely recommend!
Nice professor and very DL- friendly. Super responsive in responding to my questions
Five star professor! Very responsive and accommodating.
As a distance learning student, I was impressed with how well the course was adapted. The asynchronous format worked great for my schedule, and the material didn't feel watered down at all.

Took the course last fall as a distance learner. The extra office hours during late evenings, on weekends and also on need basis helped significantly in getting the required support and I am thankful to Prof. You and the TAs for the same.

Not an easy course, but you will learn a lot. Professor is very supportive, and grading is quite fair with reasonable workload. I'm so happy with taking both courses with him and earn the data science certificate as part of my Cornell Master's degree.

Very knowledge professor and TAs. Great outside class support. Exercises very applicable. Homework not overwhelming. Easy grader. If you get the chance to take a class with him, take a class with him!

Professor You executed the class with high quality. His course content was highly organized. The content in the lectures directly supported the concepts being taught and the homework assignments related directly to the lectures and discussions.
Even though I am a distance learner, I felt engaged in the classes which helped understanding the content.

Ed Discussion was excellent.
Lecture content preparation and delivery with high quality.
Optimization Wiki was very helpful.

Prof. You is a knowledgeable and supportive instructor. Took initiative to ensure students' enjoyment. Assignments and projects were valuable; unstuck AI was a helpful study tool. Reasonable workload, easy-to-follow content.
I liked the learning through application, I felt like I learned a lot better by doing assignments and a challenging, creative project than by preparing for exams in other classes
An easy A course. Intelligent, well-spoken instructor (Prof. You); he took initiative to ensure that all students were enjoying class; Use of projects, instead of exams
The availability for office hours and the promptness of the professor in providing a schedule for office hours each week was extremely valuable.

The content is very inspiring, I could learn a lot from it. Instructors are very very helpful. Also, I learned how to do some application with what I learned in this class and got some basic understanding of the use of the machine learning methods.
This course was a perfect blend of theory and applications that no other machine learning course at Cornell could provide. Learnt a lot. Look forward to another course with Dr. You in the fall
Homeworks were very useful and You was a generous grader. The best teaching professor at Cornell SE!!
Excellent curriculum for non computer science background people to transition into Machine Learning.
Very interested topics and very timely. It covered ChatGPT and many LLMs.
I really value Dr. You for the flexibility that he extended to students like me, Distance Learners, in the office hours and deadlines.
This my favoriate class I've taken at Cornell and hope it never changes. TA Akshay was amazingly helpful throughout this course.

The balance of the course was very enjoyable. The lectures covered a wide variety of concepts in the field,
and the assignments/OH provided more of a hands on application of the material.
Good course and supportive instructor and TAs. I will take his deep learning course in the fall to learn more. Very exciting!
Easy A professor. A truue gem in Cornell system engineering
Good course. Learn a lot about AI and machine learning. Highly recommended by my LM co-workers. I am glad I took it this semester.

A wonderful machine learning course! I did not take 5800 in the fall, but the professor made an exception for me to try it out this term as he may leave Cornell next year. Super DL-friendly course! The best one in Cornell System Engineering. I hope other DL students could benefit from Professor You's classes while still here

Great Professor. He is very much concerned about how you will be able to perform in the outside world when people know you have taken his class. I learned more in this class than any other SYSEN class that I had taken.
Nice professor. Always grant permissions for reasonable requests.

Great course, great professor, great TAs! Many office hours. The professor is highly experienced in teaching distance learning students and very accommodating. I plan to take his another course in the fall.

The professor is very accessible, accommodating and knowledgeable on data science. He always teaches in the classroom even when there were very few students there. The TA Yvonne is unfamiliar with the subject. TA Bryan is much more knowledgeable about machine learning than Y. A great course but hopefully the TA would be better next time!
Nice professor and useful course. Take it if you could! I heard You will be on sabbatical leave next spring. Not sure if he will still teach in the fall.
Nothing more can be expected from an excellent course. Professor You is the best!! Take his course(s) if you can when you (and he) are at Cornell.
Nice professor and easy ML course with no exam. Attendance not mandatory. Very effective use of electronic platform like Ed Discussion and Canvas. I like it!

I am so confused why so many ppl are commenting so positively at the beginning of the course without even knowing what is going on in the lecture. Professor is teaching online for this semester even the university no longer accepts hybrid instruction mode. No Python instruction for the heavy project assignments (30 pages required.)
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: It's just been a few weeks, but I really like this course. Professor makes it very FLEXIBLE! No exam, no mandatory attendance! There are timely support and replies on Ed Discussion on various issues. No wonder the class is so popular and hard to get in. I appreciate the Professor sent me a quick email when a slot was opened to sign up.

Another great course by Professor You! The recent Fukushima nuclear disaster example is very inspiring. It looks like the workload this semester is actually lighter than the previous course (less homework and assignments). Look forward to the exciting weeks in the rest of this semester to come!
Professor Fenggi is simply awesome. Tkae his class if you can!
