We spent half of every lecture on review, and though that boosted our test scores, it meant that there was no point in going to class. If you're solely here to pass the class, just read the course pack before tests. You'll thrive. However, you will miss his fantastic shirt collection and jolly attitude--he is genuinely a delightful person.
amazing. take linalg with him if you can
Really nice professor. I did poorly because of my own lack of studying, but he was super nice and great at explaining things.
Great professor, interesting lecture, helpful afterclass, a rare in the ORIE department

Frans is really chill, and the class is slow-paced. The first half of the semester covered materials less than expected, so he had to rush through all SVD, but overall Frans is a really good professor! Take 2940 with him if you can!

frans is a good lecturer but lecture did move slow at times. in general his lectures will give you a better understanding than just reading the textbook though. the class is structured very fairly and many resources such as discussion section worksheets were posted (for all sections) to use as practice before exams.

he's a genuinely passionate and kind professor who wants his students to succeed. this class made me switch my major to ORIE. he designed his course pack well and he's friendly and responsive on edstem + office hours. homework can be tricky but exams are fair. his high rating is so deserved. going to try to take his classes in the future

He's pretty chill, and the exams were very fair in my opinion. The mean for the first exam was higher than a 90. Sometimes the lectures can be slow, especially whenever he does proofs, but you can tell he doesn't really want to do them either lol.
Lectures were not mandatory as the course could be covered by just the coursepack. Very friendly and lenient when it comes to homework and exam grading.
Fantastic professor and interesting material

What more can I say... Frans is so passionate about the content, his enthusiasm and jovial nature never fails to rub off on students during lecture. He explains things very well and the weekly labs and homework push your understanding of the concepts even further. I wish he would teach all my classes.

He's an amazing professor! The lectures are engaging and funny, and he explains everything in an intuitive way instead of making concepts complicated. The psets can take time but it's not too difficult to figure it out + it's fun once you get the hang of it. Tests were straightforward and on the easier side. This class made me consider orie.
Enjoyed his lectures, he is also generous with a 90% and up counted as an 100% for homeworks. Definitely recommend this class

Frans is a great guy, really cares about the stuff he teaches. The workload is not too bad and the class is setup in order to give you the best grade possible (weighting shifts depending on what you do well on). The HW sometimes is really hard but just work in groups and you can figure it out. Overall a great teacher and a fun guy

He was an amazing professor! made the class fun and engaging and cared about the students. All of the work is really helpful to understanding the content and its not too hard. He wants the students to succeed.
Amazing professor; would take another class with him again

This class was fine but tests were hard. Unfortunately many randos who arent engineering majors that mess up the curve bc this is their hardest class. The medians were 80's which is great but also means everyone is super sweaty so you absolutely cannot be excited when your raw score is 85 like you would in any other exam ever in engineering math
Funny guy but talks kind of slow. Lecture wasn't worth showing up to because we barely covered anything. Better off reading the textbook on your own.

Frans is funny and genuinely good lecturer. I enjoyed attending his lectures despite attendance not being mandatory. He posts the lecture slides on Canvas right after. The weekly quizzes in discussion were usually a randomly chosen HW question from the week's prior PSET. exams were VERY fair!! you will do well in this class if you pay attention!

amazing professor!! really tries to make sure that you understand the content from the class when sitting in lecture. is super receptive to questions and is a generally fun and caring guy to be around. one of my favorite professors at cornell, hands down!

Prof. Schalekamp was a very engaging lecturer. Super friendly guy overall. His office hours were extremely helpful (especially on tough p-sets). He's great at answering questions and he always has a funny line in lecture.
Super funny lectures and made the content very interesting! 10/10 prof who turned ENGRI 1101 into my favorite class~

Love this man, great professor! I didn't know what Linear Algebra was before this class but I feel really confident in the material now. The lectures follow the textbook, so it's really easy to get ahead on the material by reading through before lecture. Homework is very straightforward. Exams and weekly quizzes are very fair. Highly Recommend!

Frans is the best professor I have had so far at Cornell and inspired me to pursue ORIE as a major! He is truly passionate about ORIE and his lectures are sometimes hard to understand as topics get harder but he is really good at answering questions. I will definitely try to take one of his classes again in the future.

The teaching assistant randomly deducts points from your assignments. She might say, "Grades don't matter for your career," but when you spend 6-8 hours on a single individual assignment only to lose 20% of the points due to "lack of creativity" or "clarity" you'll lose motivation to continue studying in this field. It's really demoralizing.

Grading is somewhat random, where graders take off points that do not align with the rubric. Feedback is not informative enough to make corrections. Although this is an important concept, the class does not align to what you are expected to do in industry and seems to be more related to research purposes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The grading in this class is SO subjective and makes no sense.  It is super demotivating because why should we even try on the assignments if lots of effort is rewarded with low grades?  If you are a more technical major like Computer Science, RUN.  This professor + class will cause more pain than algo or discrete.

Grading criteria are vague, inconsistent, leaving students guessing about expectations. Instead of fostering an atmosphere of support, she communicates in a curt and unapproachable manner that discourages engagement. The class feels less like a space for learning and more like a test of endurance against unclear standards and unnecessary hostility.
Mean teacher, meaningless homework, the way some TAs give grades are just as mean as the Gilly. The worst thing I did in Cornell was taking this class.
The amount of meaningless homework was overwhelming. It felt like we were just doing busy work instead of actually learning or engaging with the material.

All her homework wastes a lot of time and is completely meaningless. There is never a clear scoring standard. She and the TAs never listen to students' advice.She never cares about students subjective design and forced everyone to follow her ideas, otherwise she would be deducted a lot of points. Don't take her class, the worst prof you could meet.
way too much unnecessary work and heavy workload. There is def a better way to learn this interesting topic in HCI than doing this much meaningless homework.
There are many assignments that feel pointless and time-consuming. She doesn't take student feedback into account and forces projects to follow her own ideas.
too much meaningless work
Her class wastes a lot of students' time and energy to do meaningless homework. Her lecture level is also very bad. Don't take her class.

Course operates at a kindergarten level with arbitrary grading criteria. Professor is rude and seems completely unsympathetic to students — ironic for a class about human interactions. 

This course could have been really interesting given a different structure. Do not take expecting it to be “easy”; class is not easy but mind-numbingly pointless.

Gilly is extremely unaccommodating. She never adopts students' feedback. TA's grading criteria is also very confusing. They always deduct points on assignments somehow. There is a lot of outside class work that is time-consuming but you won't learn anything in the end. Never take the class with Gilly. The worst professor I have ever had at Cornell.
mean
I've never had a professor be more unaccommodating than gilly. good luck if you are required to take her class

As ux in info sci, this class has been by far the worst I've taken in my 3 yrs here. The class is worse than cs2110 or cs1110 w walker white or 1300 with kyle harms. gilly brushes off feedback and is unwilling to accommodate students. the late policy is awful too, she takes off 1.5% per hour late, encouraging students to stay up late finishing hw
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Strong skills as an instructor but course was largely bs. A lot of unnecessary busy work and participation. Seemingly arbitrary grading and benchmarks. Painful group work. A LOT /deliverables culminating in very few lessons that actually stick. The entire class can be (and has been) summarized into a well-written 1-page article on a tech journal.

I took human computer interaction design. The class is a lot of work, but if you do what is asked you certainly get a good grade. I had a good team, but I know that other classes were struggling with lazy team members who did not take this class seriously or were overwhelmed with Cornell. 

I am amazed how Gilly made this huge class personal!

I go back and forth about how I feel about this class. It was interesting and the projects make sense, but the grading is beyond opaque with no rubric given. In my experience, this has led to subjective, unfair grading between TAs which could not be logically explained as to how points were deducted. Her attitude makes it difficult to ask for help

All projects  make your final grade. Not difficult but tedious work. Course concept is good but not "inspirational." Prof has a reputation. Quite nice in person but different on Piazza. Vague grading criteria make student furiously frustrated. Info UX major? No choice + take it, save time for later projects,move on. COMM major just looking? Hmm.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class is so project-heavy but in the end you don't learn anything. The assignment instructions are never not vague and the grading is never consistent. She is also extremely unreceptive to student feedback, whenever someone proposes a suggestion or comment she's just like "sorry can't help, this is how things are done." DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS

This course is extremely intensive for very little payoff. The assignment instructions are somehow simultaneously long and incredibly vague, and grading is incredibly inconsistent across TA's. I really hope that the coordinators for this class take a good long look at the way they've set the class up.

Blurry grading rubrics and inconsistent grading standard across different TAs. The lecture is like a readout from textbook. This class should be inspiring since its about HCI and design; but its the opposite. You need to play by her rules and no room to be creative.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Each class has an attendance activity. Show up, mess around on your laptop, and it. No need to pay attention to the lecture. Rubrics were very ambiguous and vague and it was common for her to take points off for stuff that wasn't clearly mentioned in the rubric. You'll work for your grade in the class, but its rewarding to have a completed project.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Listen. It's whatever you personally want to get out of it. She is basically a kindergarten teacher who encourages young adults to remember the imagination that many have left behind. The class is absolutely huge. You'll be afraid to speak up because all eyes will be on you. So if you do not participate, it is your loss. Nut up or shut up.

Lectures are boring, but since there is an attendance grade, just show up and do other work on your laptop. She's fairly nice, but not the best lecturer, if only because the material is boring and straightforward. Work on the assignments and group project and you'll be fine.

INFO 3450 is a great and rewarding class but warning, it is time consuming. You will have to put in lots of effort, but in the end you should have a project  you can talk about in job interviews.   Gilly is a great, respectable prof. You can tell she puts in a lot of time and attention to her lectures which are always easy to read later on.
The professor tried to control students a lot. No phone and no laptop during the speech (are we elementary students?) The grading criteria is also confusing and doesn't reflect our efforts.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Lectures were uninformative, straight from the textbook, and nobody paid attention. Group activities took up half of lecture and were not helpful at all. Grading "rubrics" were ambiguous at best. Grading is done by TAs. Some gave straight 100s while other students were failing assignments for comparable work. Poorly organized class.

The worst class and professor I have ever had here at Cornell in my three years.  No grading rubrics makes the class extremely confusing.  Takes points off on assignments for items not even mentioned in instructions.  TA's don't even know what is going on in the class or assignments.  This class was terrible. DO NOT TAKE IF YOU DON'T HAVE TO!
This class was horrible.
Lectures were deadly and the course was not structured coherently

Professor Leshed does a good job with the Online Communities Course.  Be forewarned it is fairly repetitive of other Info/Comm classes.  Graded assignments are often blog/blackboard posts re: weekly readings.  The other portion of your grade come from large scale group assignments.  If you do not like group work, this is NOT the class for you.
Professor Leshed does a really good job to make lectures interesting and mixes it up every class. She's not bad looking either.

Very knowledgeable lecturer with dry humor during lectures. Some of the grading schemes for weekly assignments were somewhat harsh and some of the readings were felt unmotivated / unnecessary. Overall, interesting course content and the weekly assignments were mentally stimulating and interesting.

Professor Giannella was an okay lecturer, important to pay full attention and take good notes in class. Readings are not too bad to go through, however it is important to memorize key facts and cases. I would not recommend this class to anyone who is not interested in Ancient Roman terminology and society.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very chill professor. A large portion of your grade comes from doing the readings where you have to make your annotations and respond to others. These are helpful for the prelims where you have to memorize individual cases and respond to hypothetical scenarios. The class wasn't too difficult as long as you actively do the readings and come to class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Giannella was great. She really pushed us to think about the texts and about different kinds of domination and slavery. I hope my professors later are like her
Amazing professor. Really cares about his students' well-being and future. Of my past three and a half years here, Field Bio has been my favorite class and certainly the most memorable one.

My favorite professor I've had by a long shot. He is funny and really cares about his students. Very disorganized which can get annoying but he makes up for it. The weekend trips to Arnot and Oneida were really fun and it was a great way to get closer to people in the class than you normally would. Lot of time but it is not difficult.
My favorite class ever. Marc is amazing. If you have to take a field class, you want to take his class.
Genuinely the best professor I have ever had.

Marc is the best professor I've had at Cornell, hands down. Although the class is quite time consuming (2 labs and a lab lecture weekly), the labs are always new and tend to be interesting. Marc also makes a genuine effort to get to know his students (he will know your name within the first week). Take his class if you can you won't regret it!!

Great professor, and so much fun. If you already know a lot about the environment, you may be bored (because content and identification skills are mostly basic), but there's still fun field components

Marc is extraordinary, and his class ranks highly among those that I've taken at Cornell. It's basically just guided frolicking in nature in labs and on field trips, and I learned so much about identification that I think about it at some point on almost every day

Such an awesome class and teacher. There are guest lecturers each week, and while they can get a little boring sometimes, the labs make up for it. While there is a good portion of writing, almost all of the labs are outside and interesting. Marc keeps you on your toes and is a great professor who really cares. Beware his driving though :).

Best academic experience I've had to date; Marc maintains high standards with high support. Not a single kid in our class regretted taking it despite the courseload. Our time was respected, as were we. A fun, adept teacher. Drives fast, is supportive of extenuating circumstances without leaving you out. Chose his TAs super well to form a community.

Dr. Goebel is inspirational, kind, and fair. Maintaining a 100% would-take-again ratio on RMP with a very work-heavy course is a testament to his capabilities. He drives fast, walks quickly, laughs heartily, and makes you feel like you're on the Magic Schoolbus. Yes, there's a decent workload. No, you will not regret it.

Marc is my favorite professor at Cornell so far.  I loved this class because I was excited to hear what he had to say.  He is engaging and inspirational, he makes education in natural resources etc feel so important.  A lot of work- if you do it, you will get a good grade. Take this class with him and it will change your life and be so much fun.
marc is more like a friend than a professor but try not to miss lab as much as u can bc that is where you learn everything for the course basically .

Marc is caring and has sincere dedication to the class, but put your seatbelt on because he rips it in the vans. The course does require two weekend field trips. Marc himself is very humorous, often yelling "hutt hutt" and other German words at us in the field. Research project and species memorization takes a bit of time, but it is not difficult.

Marc is everything you could ever want in a professor. He is always there for his students and willing to lend a hand or listen to whatever is happening in your life. His class teaches you so much and manages to be the most fun you will ever have at Cornell at the same time. Take a class with him. Change your perspective. Love your education.

While I didn't take his course, I interned for him over the summer one year and he was a great boss. He was very hands-off and helped us fight the pencil-pushers for money that was promised at the outset of the job.

Marc is truly a gem. Easygoing, funny, and a great teacher--he seriously cares about his students and their success. In terms of lab, you definitely get out of it what you put into it, but Marc makes them fun and informative! Overall: great guy, great class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Favorite professor at Cornell. He loves to laugh and really loves engaging his students. In my entire time here, I've never met a professor so dedicated to his students and leaving them with field knowledge that will never, ever leave them. I freaking love this guy

Marc is like a German god. He would give his life for his students, but he would rather spend time in the soil than in the classroom. He's the sort of guy that will drop you at your door in Collegetown after a field trip if you ask (or for an ice-cream stop for that matter). Drives like its the Autobahn though, buckle up!
He's really good at lecturing, super well respected in his field, and I learned a lot.

One of the best psych classes I've taken at Cornell. Attendance not mandatory but his lectures are always super interesting and I agree with others that say he has the best fits. Tests did include a lot of specific facts from readings/lecture, but nothing too unmanageable.

PSYCH 2800 was a really interesting course. Lecture is definitely super important - he would include niche comments from lecture on tests. Top 3 class I've taken at Cornell. If you are interested in the class content, the grades will follow. Would not recommend taking it as a non-psych major for fun/distribution, unless S/U. His outfits also eat!

Would not take this class unless it's required - big mistake as someone who's not a psych major and just thought the subject matter would be interesting. He's a good lecturer but the grade is 80% based on tests, so makes it very hard to do well if you're not a strong test taker.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not an easy class, and I wouldn't recommend taking it just for fun. The material is interesting, especially if you have an interest in the social sciences, but the class structure is a bit strict and most of your grade is from exams that are quite difficult. I've taken several Psych/HD courses, and this was definitely one of the hardest ones.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't take this class unless you have to. Grade is 80% made up of prelims + final, and the exams are very difficult. Hopefully class is curved. Content is interesting but not worth the trouble
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is funny and tries to be engaging although some of what he says can be offensive. Class is made up of only two exams, a final, and a paper. People usually do very poorly but the class is curved and there is extra credit. I would try to find other options and avoid this class if you care about getting high grades, otherwise might be interesting.

As a lecturer, Prof. Gilovich is pretty good! He includes anecdotes and videos to keep everyone entertained, but sometimes there were charts involved alongside other material that was not very well explained and it became confusing. The two in-class prelims and the final were definitely challenging, but the class is curved thankfully (life saver)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tough exams with questions I've never seen before. The lowest grade I've ever got in the field of Psych.
It is tough to get an A in the class and lectures are quite boring

Super engaging lectures. Go to them please. Use of videos, film clips, pop culture references and stories was phenomenal. Do the outside readings because he will ask super specific questions on tests about them.

Professor Gilovich is simply an amazing lecturer. The lectures are super engaging, fun, and very informational. He is also a great actor. However, you will have a hard time in Pysch 2800 if you don't go to lecture. There are no assignments and only a few supplemental readings, so the GO TO LECTURES! Would 100% take his class again.

The material itself is NOT HARD, however the average grade is a 70%. The tests are insane and he attempts to incorporate horrible "real-world examples", which force you to guess even if you know the material. He also teaches borderline race science with his obsession with the East-West difference, and defends it by saying he is "just the messenger"
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I am paying 80k in tuition with some of it going towards a class where the average is a failing grade. Even though this professor is chill during class and about attendance, I have never felt stupider. He returns grades almost a month later and is the harshest grader I have had. Do not take this class unless you want a WF on your transcript.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As a psych major, found this course relatively straightforward. Extra credit and office hours really helped me get the A. Extremely interesting and relevant course material that I talk about them to people outside of class. Don't focus on the minute details, but sit back and listen to understand the concepts, and ask a lot of questions!

PowerPoints are so vague, if you miss lecture, all you will see are pictures on the slides with no notes to help you out. He wrote the textbook, so expect to read a lot. Prelim questions are so specific, which is not ideal for an introductory course. Passionate about his field, but VERY politically bias in how he presents materials.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prelims are very difficult, but the papers are graded easy. Hard to do really well but if you do the readings and go to to class you should be in decent shape. He's not very accessible, the times I asked for help I didn't get it. Personally I'd avoid this class specifically, it was too much work for an elective.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Gives extremely convoluted explanations on topics. Not the best lecturer. Least favorite class at Cornell so far. Does not really care about logistics. Do not take it if you are not a psych major. I have taken several classes that covered some experiments taught in this class and still find it quite hard to follow. Tests are unfair and hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The best professor I have ever had. Class is interesting and thought-provoking; tests are very fair and doable if you do the readings. 10/10 would recommend!!!

Professor Gilovich was perhaps the greatest lecturer I have ever had while in school. He made each class interesting and applicable while crafting lectures to interest his audience. My only regret is that I didnt take a course with him sooner to allow me to take more courses that he teaches. Highly recommend

Tests you on ridiculously minute details, oftentimes mentioned in passing during lecture or readings. ALWAYS go to class, do the readings beforehand, study, and you will do fine. Slack off and those tests will kill you.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Captivating professor. He posts lecture slides, but I found that I could have taken better in-class notes. He includes questions directly from the textbook on the prelims and final, so read the textbook. He doesn't return prelims but lets you see them during OH, and he reuses several questions on the final. Final40% Prelims20% Paper10%

The best professor I've ever had. Interesting, intelligent and incredibly talented at explaining concepts during lecture. Go to lecture and do the readings and you'll be fine. Pre-lims are slightly difficult but fair. Lecture is always interesting. Term paper is easy but make sure to incorporate a lot of your own ideas

The lectures are fine. The problem is the material. You learn little about social psychology. Instead, you memorize experiments. Take the class if you are a psych major. Otherwise, stay far away.  He also claimed that psych majors know more about economics than econ majors, so I guess his brain just works differently than everybody else. Ironic.

Gilovich is a great professor. He is smart and his lectures are incredibly interesting. He is quite a rockstar in psych and he exudes knowledge about the subject. The tests are straightforward though they require a very thorough reading of the textbook

Terrible class. Gilovich clearly cares and knows his stuff, but the class is very poorly organized. It's a large lecture for a topic that NEEDS to be taught through discussion, so lectures end up being him rambling about random topics in psychology. Grading is unfair, super harsh, and nitpicky. Unless you're a psych. major, DON'T take this class.

Professor Gilovich is one of my favorite professors. He really knows his stuff and shares it with you in a really interesting way. I really enjoyed his lectures. That said, his tests can be hard, even when you study; there's a lot of nitpicky details from the books. Overall, definitely take the class. You learn a TON of interesting things!

Loved this class, so many interesting ideas applicable to everyday life. He is a fantastic lecturer and he also offered a review session before every test that I would recommend. This class is hard however. Make sure that you do the readings because his exams can be tricky. One of my favorite classes at Cornell.

My favorite class at Cornell, definitely take it. So interesting and applicable to daily life. Gilovich is a rock star in the psych world and he knows all the material by heart + wrote the textbook. Both prelims and the final are horribly specific. Read the textbook word for word. Attendance not required but will definitely help you on the test
Psych 2800 is a great class, the tests are a little tricky but overall everything was good. Make sure to do the readings!

Really great lecturer. Tests are a little hard and readings can make or break you on exams. He is a little scattered sometimes but overall I had a great experience with him as a lecturer! He also held review sessions before tests, which were nice.
A great professor! His lectures were fun and interesting every time, and he played cool music and videos. Very understanding and helpful.
While psych 2800 requires a little bit of work, it is worth it.  Very interesting and a must-take for psych majors and a great class for non psych majors.

I took him for Social Psych and the class was fantastic! He's a really great lecturer and the material was really interesting. His prelims were really hard though; he's REALLY into nitpicky details from the book that you could overlook. Despite the hard tests though, it's a great class!

Goes on ad nauseum about the smallest details and typically goes off on a tangent during his lectures. I am a psych major, and even I have difficulty finding interest in his lectures. At least the TA is bearable.

Professor Gilovich is a great guy, but this class was SO hard. The prelims were ridiculous and borderline unfair. He packed so much info into his lectures that it was nearly impossible to stay awake and keep good notes. I tried really hard in this class, and it still didn't pay off. Only take this class if you love psych more than anything.

I took writing section (WIM), so experience was different. But Tom is a great researcher and speaker. Lectures do trail off in liveliness towards end of 75 minutes, partly because he throws out so many experiments. I didn’t study, of course, but when he went over prelims, I was grateful I took WIM — MC are hard! I Recommend WIM, TA was very chill.

Very good lecturer. Engaging, never very dull, and very clear explanations. However, exams are very tough (means in  low 60s usually). The class is also a lot of work, as there are mandatory and often lengthy readings. It's also a little annoying that he expects you memorize multiple experiments. Overall, class is good, but definitely demanding!
Tom is a chill professor. His explanations are very clear.

Gilovich is by far one of the most captivating lecturers at Cornell. Fascinating subject and he makes it fun and interesting. His class was tough, but if you attend classes and do the reading you will be fun. Definitely take this before you leave Cornell!

I was a little surprised about how boring I found this class, especially with all the comments on this site. He was my least engaging teacher, and would throw a TON of experiments at you for each topic. The tests were graded unnecessarily harsh, too. He curves, though, so don't worry. And I recommend taking notes on the slides as you go.

Probably the best prof. I've had at Cornell. Very enthusiastic about the material. Also knows the stuff well, since he wrote the textbook and conducted a lot of experiments presented in class. Each lecture contains a lot of information, so make sure you stay focused through out. Tests are hard, but they are well designed and fair. TAKE THIS CLASS!

Incredible, incredible speaker-- never even went close to nodding off during his class. The way he presents material is incredible. (Tests are hard, not going to lie, but if you do the reading and really remember the experiments it talks about, you'll do well. Another plus-- he helped write the book, so all the lecture stuff is covered.)

He is probably the best prof I've had at cornell. He's extremely interesting and a fantastic lecturer. He uses the book he wrote for the class and the readings were almost enjoyable to do. The prelims were pretty hard but they're curved so it doesn't matter too much. Not the easiest course in the world but not a lot of work definitely worth it!
fun class
GREAT PROF.  GREAT CLASS.  tough grader

Good professor and interesting lectures, but made tests intentionally hard, and would go over prelim answers extremely quickly so you couldn't really understand why you got certain questions wrong. One of those professors who will pick out small details from textbook that are often looked over to test you on. Read CAREFULLY. Otherwise, OK class.

Interesting lectures, but incredibly unclear and tangential.  Designs tests to be intentionally difficult and low-scoring.  Irrational requisite for attention to detail.  Requires much more work than the average course in the department.  Only advised for students who have a profound interest in the subject matter.

Tests are incredibly difficult multiple choice questions, often confusing and contradictory ten times.  Tries to make class hard.  In all, it was doable if you put the extra effort in, but not sure it was worth the time. Means on exams were low, but lectures were (sometimes to rarely) interesting
Great lecturer!! good class
good lecturer and interesting material but tests were unreasonably hard for a class that most took for an elective

This class was great! material is fascinating and gilovich is a great lecturer. Regan talks waaaay too fast, but they both give outlines for each lecture which makes it easier. Pay attention to experiments and do the reading. Take this class if you can!!
He's a great professor, and a great speaker. When I'm trying to do a presentation for another class, I try to speak like Professor Gilovich, and the presentation goes well.

Not only is Gilovich brilliant, but his lectures are interesting and even humorous. Sometimes his lectures are identical to the reading, but that's because he co-wrote the textbook. Tests are tricky, but if you go to class, do the reading, and study, you will do fine.

Take this class! Gilovich and Regan give you lecture outlines, which means that instead of frantically scribbling notes for 75 minutes straight, you can listen to the (mostly entertaining) lectures. Gilovich throws in a lot of fun material, and is clearly passionate about psychology. The textbook he co-wrote is sometimes even-- gasp!-- fun to read.

Neat guy. Knows the subject intimately; he's really well-known in the social psychology world. Heck, he was one of the co-authors of the brand new (and very useful) textbook. Good sense of humor, too. But yeah, prelims are pretty hard. Take good notes (or get TakeNote) and do all of the readings carefully, especially in the textbook!
Very knowledgable and a good lecturer. Tests are very difficult though.

Probably the best professor I had at Cornell. His lectures are incredibly interesting and very practical. Difficult class but if you study the material and read the book, its not too bad. This class is definitely worth it. Gilovich rocks!

Gilovich is the greatest! He's very intelligent and extremely amusing. The subject is interesting, but Gilovich makes it intriguing. I signed up for 350 next semester cause I thought Gilovich was teaching it, but it turns out he's not, and I am really sad. Oh well. Definitely take 280!

Gilovich is the man!  He and Regan have very different styles, but I found both to be effective lecturers and I don't even think it's fair to compare.  Gilovich is "flashier", I guess - powerpoints, videos, funny stories.  The class is tough, tests especially, but well worth it.  I loved it!
Very hard class (tests are brutal). Very nice and helpful guy (I found him a bit less helpful than Regan). Lectures are very interesting and good.  Great class

A pretty good, entertaining lecturer. BTW, I strongly disagree with the person who perferred Gilovitch over Regan. They’re both good profs - Gilovitch might be more charming, but I think Regan actually has the edge on explaining things and caring about students. Good class overall if you're into it.
Loved his class.  If you think he's overrated, know it isn't so: I read his book as an undergrad, and now 10 years later I have to read it again for a law school class.
this guy is awesome! the best teacher i had at cornell!
No Comments
Gilovich is awesome.  He is very intelligent and always clear.  I wish it was just Gilovich teaching this class (rather than him and Regan).

Knows his stuff, but he speaks in a monotone, after a while it gets boring. He has no facial expression!  This guy makes psych more boring than it has to be.  His questions are tricky on exams, esp for 280.
im naming my first son after him!
Great professor, funny and helpful, but sometimes not quite clear.
really good lecturer, inserted a good amount of fun material into class. made all the topics interesting, even when describing the details of an experiment. take psych 280

Good prof, tries hard to makes class interesting. He uses good examples and makes points clear.  Have to say though, tests are short, so pressured to do well on so few questions and his questions on tests are ambiguous.
This is the most boring class I ever took at Cornell. More boring than Chem 207.
Awesome professor. Why can't more instructors be like him?
No Comments
He's like the nicest guy ever! Plus, he rides his bike to class! Awesome teacher!
Really hot, cute, i love him, i want to have his children, he is so passionate... about psychology... =D
He has clear expectations of students and understands their needs well, and is very flexible with scheduling of assignments and in some cases exams.

Godwin is a great professor. He explains everything so clearly and you can tell he really cares about his students. He even holds extra office hours late at night on days before exams. It's refreshing how much he cares.
The Best Professor in Dyson! He does an amazing job explaining all of the content and truly cares about his students' growth in the class.

The class itself is difficult, given the nature of financial accounting, however, Professor Godwin is one of the BEST professors in Dyson. He is extremely knowledgeable of the material and is so caring and always willing to help. Extremely grateful I was able to take this class with Godwin!!!

Godwin is the GOAT. He genuinely cares about your success and says that often–he means it. He is so hospitable and accommodating, if you need anything, ask. He gives great feedback and creates fair exams and assignments. This course is totally manageable as long as you do the homework and practice. Do the practice exams and assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very passionate about what he teaches, so I found his lectures enjoyable. Cancelled class leading up to break, offered lots of office hours, helpful review sessions before exams, great guy

Professor Godwin is hands down one of the best professors in Dyson. He's always going the extra mile for his students, even hosting late-night office hours before exams. He's approachable, easy to talk to, and makes accounting fun by tying in current news with class topics. You can tell that he genuinely cares and wants you to succeed.

Professor Godwin is my favorite professor this semester. The class is a lot of work, but he is passionate about the material and always willing to help and talk during office hours. He responds to emails quickly too.
Amazing Professor.

Great professors are professors who can still be viewed as respected teaching hard subjects. Godwin is a great professor and is constantly looking out for us. The class has a heavy amount of workload but is definitely manageable by attending lectures and asking him questions. He is very fast with his teachings but overall an amazing professor
This is gonna be a tough class just because of the subject. That being said, I can't imagine taking the class with a better professor. He is a great professor and any rating outside of a 5 is wrong

Honestly one of my favorite professors within Dyson. Weekly homework and quizzes, but work load is manageable. Super responsive and understanding with any issues/confusion. One answered one of my emails past 10pm. Recommend going to class to get best understanding of concepts.

One of my favorite professors I've had so far. Teaches with a passion. Weekly homework activity and take-home quiz. If you go to lecture and pay attention, you will succeed. Just stay on top because he goes very fast. Exams were very similar to homeworks.  Great professor overall, would definitely recommend.

Great class, show up and participate and you will do well. Fun to talk to people you wouldn't otherwise and you can see the tangible change the material facilitates within both yourself and your peers.

If you need to take this for your ILR diversity requirement just wait for the other diversity ethics course. this class is graded so unnecessarily harsh for no reason, one of my hardest courses for this semester and you really just don't know what they are looking for in those reflection papers. Participating in class session is easy.

I took the course and then became a facilitator after. Yes, it can get tedious to read so many papers and write the weekly essays so it's supposed to not feel easy -- it's supposed to challenge students' critical thinking and reflections. The payoff is so worth it and is truly a unique experience for students from all backgrounds.
This is the worst class ever

I absolutely hate this class. I have gotten C's on half of the papers. They don't care about how well you write or how deeply you incorporate the class materials -- they care about how much discrimination you face. The same 3 topics are discussed every class for 3 hours. You can't miss a section. A diversity credit should be an easy A. Do not take.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: I thought this was a chill class. Show up, do the work (write papers, reading comments, and talk in class) and you're guaranteed an A. With a little effort, it's not hard to get an A+. Was kinda cool to talk to kids who you normally wouldn't have overlapping social circles with so I would take it if you need an A or a requirement.

The curriculum is tedious since you have to write a paper essentially every week on top on doing the readings. The papers were graded inconsistently depending on who graded it. The feedback was circular and just kept recommending writing resources on campus. I feel like my writing was not the problem, but rather the dry prompts that lacked depth.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: EDUC 2610 is an annoying and tedious class. Much of the curriculum and content in every 3 hour class period is pretty much spent on discussing how good and valuable the class and program (Intergroup Dialogue Project) is. There's lots of talk of changing society through education, but this class does nothing for that goal. Lots of work and it sucks.

An aimless class with no goals or meaningful takeaways whatsoever. Weekly sessions are led by student "facilitators" and 3 hours long -- but still accomplish nothing. Tons of reading that serves no purpose b/c irrelevant or repetitive. Strict grading criteria for annoying papers. Can't discuss grades over email as they claim it's "against FERPA."
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: EDUC 2610 is the worst class I have taken at Cornell. 25 students have a pointless discussion for 3 straight hours. The content is useless and you spend the first 8 weeks covering common sense topics like respect. I got a B on my first paper, and I only got an A after I started making up stories about discrimination (that's what they want to hear).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She presented the lecture material in an engaging way and clearly put a lot of effort into her lectures. The class was very well organized but the final project was a little vague and it was hard to tell what to do. She was generally available outside of class and was helpful.

What did she do to those BEE2510 students?!? CHEME 2027 class consensus: shes the best! She filled in for a professor our semester. She provided LOTS of resources (cheat sheets, ect). Focuses on learning and comprehension. Super accommodating. Puts in lots of effort. Taking an elective class by her this sem. Top 2 prof for me. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!

Has a weird savior complex where she will drown you in work all semester only to magically give you a good grade at the end. No indication of curve before that. Additionally, OH are a waste of time where you may get insulted/berated for not knowing concepts. Avoid if you can.

As one would expect, given the courses name, Professor Goldfarb's BEE 2510 course was all about sustainability. Specifically, Professor Goldfarb outlined how a single unsustainable aspect of a system could ruin the system as a whole: that single aspect being BEE 2510 and the system as a whole being a student's academic life.

Avoid Prof Goldfarb.

Tough class, felt confused most of the time but thats my normal. I appreciated her focus on environmental justice and social responsibility. PSETS and exams were tough, but not abnormally so. She was aware of diff learning styles and tried to accommodate them in the final thru diff question types. It is definitely a wild ride but hang in there.

Professor Goldfarb has a caustic attitude and can be extremely insensitive to her students. She makes the class unnecessarily difficult to boost her ego. She is also insensitive of disabilities and makes snarky comments about people needing accommodations. Avoids her and her class.

She is the worst professor I have ever had. This class made me
question whether or not I still wanted to be an Environmental Engineer, but thank
goodness I made it past this roadblock because I love the major. If you cannot avoid
her, hang in there and do not let her ruin your ambitions.
Just avoid this professor. Honestly the entire class was confused with what was going on most of the semester. Way too much work for 3 credits!

I really liked this class during the first week. She spoke clearly and the course content was something that interested me a lot. Unfortunately, thats the only positive things I can say about this course. She is condescending, negative, and a difficult grader. As a CivE I wish I would have taken CEE 4725, avoid this course at all costs.

One of the few things more detrimental to a student's life than a sulfuric acid spill directly into their drinking water is this professor's caustic attitude. She will go to great lengths to deny that she is wrong even when she demonstrably is. Never be the one to tell her: she will only target you from then on. Avoid the class or just avoid her.

This is by far the worst professor I have had at Cornell. She is an extremely tough grader for silly things and a poor lecturer. I understand very little in class and she comes across as very condescending when answering questions. She has the potential to be a good professor but continually chooses a different path. Shame as it is a great subject.

The class was right up my alley but she managed to almost make me hate it. Had unnecessarily strict exam rules during covid that only added to the stress of taking online exams. She lectures in a conceding high-pitched voice and reads everything off slides or a textbook. Lecture sounds like a really bad audiobook. Avoid her if you can.

I had high expectations for both Professor Goldfarb and this class, but unfortunately this was the worst class I've taken at Cornell. She is not great at explaining things, and the homework, prelims, and projects rarely reflect what we learned. Lectures also felt like a waste. Honestly it was a shame, since the subject matter was interesting.
interesting, manageable (if you do the readings), and curves the class median to a A- at the end.

fav class at cornell by far. make sure u do all of the textbook readings as they will help you conceptualize topics and will allow u to spend less time studying for the 2 prelims since you already have a good understanding of everything. super easy class, profs are very engaging and lectures are lots of fun. Poll evs for class, section attendance!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very very interesting class. Professor Hans will sometimes drone on for a while and ask intuitive questions that are hard to answer because she already answers her question when asking it.

One of the most interesting classes Ive taken at Cornell. It is essential that you thoroughly do all reading homework because she cold calls students in class. This can be stressful at first but is honestly not a huge deal. I honestly never felt bored, and as long as you show up to every class (attendance is huge) and take good notes you'll do well

Really an amazing class!! Prof. Hans is an accredited expert on Juries and brings a lot of her interesting research into class. However, the assignments were graded a bit tough by the TAs. Also, they did law school style cold calls, so be prepared!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Lectures and demonstrations were clear and engaging. I used to dislike physics in high school but I enjoyed his class. The content can be hard to process, but there is also a lot of opportunities to attend office hours or ask questions after class. Gave me a solid foundation in physics.
Honestly you don't learn physics well from this class at all. I was lucky to have taken physics in high school and completely relied on that knowledge. Incredibly poorly organized and taught class.

Very poorly organized and failed to properly support his students. Office hours were incredibly full, to the point where it could take hours to get a single question answered. Answer keys for discussions and practice exams didn't exist. Heard him use a mocking voice to answer a student who asked a question he thought was easy to answer.

Very eccentric guy, makes a lot of mistakes working out problems during lecture. Gives vague answers to students' questions in class. Extremely poorly written tests and no answer guys given for everything but homeworks.

Phys 2207 has one of the most awful course structure. I paid to learn and they give you a online resources instead of teaching in class and call is "flipped class." Also they don't provide answers to practice exams. Which does not make any sense since they are meant for "practice," but how can I practice without knowing if I am doing things right.

This is the poorest taught class I have ever taken. There are no real lectures, you watch videos recorded by another professor years ago, which are super unclear. He doesn't put the effort into providing practice exams, review, or exam statistics. It's not terribly difficult to do well, I got an A but I still don't understand a thing about physics.

Glenn really cares about his students. Grading scheme is somewhat unclear but has a nice policy that allows a good final exam score to replace one or both prelim scores. Stay up to date with lecture content because it's easy to fall behind.

Professor Case was super accessible outside of class, and never makes you feel dumb at office hours. Having never taken physics, this was a tough class, but still feasible if you thoroughly understand lecture material. Also not calculus heavy, just know basic differentiation and integrals.
Best prof. I've had at cornell so far

Prof made lectures as fun and engaging as he could. Clear he cares about his students and enjoys teaching. Overall the workload was very manageable compared to the prior physics course I had taken but labs were a little long and felt a bit more tedious. The content was interesting if you enjoy physics.
Very engaging lecturer. Also willing to help if needed and always excited to discuss tangential physics topics. Very forgiving grading policy.
Hard class and a lot of assignments per week, but good prof who is passionate about physics and wants you to learn and succeed in the course.

Professor Case was a good lecturer, although the lectures were very slow-paced and pretty boring - very monotone. Thankfully they were pre-recorded and posted so you can speed them up. The material itself is challenging, but Professor Case presented in helpful ways. Exams were fair. Overall an okay class.

Professor Case is kind and passionate about his work. Admittedly, I would get pretty frustrated with the difficulty of the homework, as sometimes the questions were not covered in lecture or instead required a lot of conceptual thinking. However, he is ready to invest time with you at his office hours and he loves student feedback. Grades fairly

Extremely caring professor, incredibly fair and accommodating towards students. Lectures are clear and organized, although the content itself can be difficult and abstract. Exams are very fair if you've put in the effort. Grading policy is extremely generous (several drops allowed for homeworks and quizzes).

Amazing professor, clear lectures, answers questions extremely well. His class is hard, but you will do well if you put in the effort. I never took physics in high school but you don't have to in order to succeed in his class.

Glenn Case is an incredibly fair teacher. The tests and quizzes are derived from his powerpoints. If you can truly understand what is going on in the powerpoint the prelims and finals should be very doable. Clear lecturer but ppt are not simple to understand so make sure to review ppt at your own time
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Why Glenn was downgraded so much. Each time I had a last min question on hw and straightly broke into his office, he would stop to help even sometimes he was having lunch. He was this patient to everyone in our section as I can tell. Even when he couldn't answer a question, he still sincerely tried to inspire you and ask you to teach him back.

Professor Case is a competent lecturer and he places extreme emphasis on understanding. However, he also offers few (and often poor) review materials so preparing for exams was quite challenging, particularly because his exams covered several niche topics while leaving much of the important course material untouched.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Glenn was my professor and my section TA as well. I can say that he is very knowledgable and cares about students learning. I worked extremely hard in this class and I really enjoyed E&M because of him. I don't know why people are complaining about him when half of them don't even show up to lecture.

Terrible professor. Does not cover necessary material in class. Lecture was complete waste of time. Pretends to care but is actually rooting for your demise. Talks a lot about integrity but does not follow through. This class made me despise physics and I would advise anyone debating on taking this class to run away.

Lectures were not clear. Difficult to study for tests as never taught how to solve problems in class and never presented test-type questions. Teaches a lot of irrelevant theory using equations that are difficult to understand. Would not recommend, take auto-tutorial course to save time and stress.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: AWFUL PROFESSOR AND AWFUL COURSE. Glenn was extremely into explaining the theory behind concepts, yet never covered test level questions in class. Tests were super difficult and hard to prepare for adequately owing to the fact that half of the tests were student-created questions. Problem sets were impossible without help. Incompetent lecturer. BAD
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Lectures were very ambiguous. Did not learn much from coming to lecture, although I do realize it was difficult to cover as much material as this class presents. I just feel his lectures could have been more productive, and that he was not very helpful, more exam-like questions should have been provided in homeworks and in clicker questions.
Really helpful if you talk to him. Not the greatest lecturer but one on one he's very good at explaining concepts.

Very clear and useful lectures. Tests are challenging. There are questions relating to labs and very specific concepts, which are given large point values. If you forget one of many concepts, you will lose significant points on the exam.  There is no curve, but a fair grading scale (class average will be a B). Prelims are optional with him.

Glenn is a nice guy, and is passionate about physics.  He seems like a dry lecturer, but that his actually his dry sense of humor.  The class is hard though, you have to really work for it, since there is no curve.

Glenn presents things clearly in a well prepared lecture, and really cares about students. Lectures may be a bit dry, but do make an effort to know him outside of lecture. He is way more engaging and caring then he may let on from lecture. Really amazing command and passion for physics.
Very clear in lectures, and very eager to clarify and help students understand the materials. Very nice prof, would definitely recommend.

Professor Hirsh is a fair guy who genuinely cares about his students. The lecture are not the most engaging, but he takes time to explain things clearly, provides a decent amount of material for prelims, and is usually available to answer questions.
Very caring and approachable- no technology allowed in lectures but it actually ended up helping me pay attention better. The class itself has some problems material-wise but that's beyond Prof Hirsh

Extremely boring lecturer and repeats himself a lot BUT nice, fair, considerate guy and he'll take the time to give you really thorough and detailed answers to questions you have. Class and material are not hard if you pay attention (go to OH), exams are easy if you memorize his slides (no surprises).

Interesting material, great test review but hard exams, and a high though non-problematic level of disorganization. This class won't suck away too much time, too. At times when coursework is particularly heavy, Hirsh will give what amounts to a several-day extension on homework, and he provides many high-quality answers on Piazza.

I took Prof Hirsh's class when the Covid-19 situation first started and he was very caring and thoughtful of the struggles students would be going through. He cancelled both the midterm and the final and replaced them with manageable weekly quizzes. Additionally, his lectures were very interesting and greatly increased my interest in AI.

CS 4700 has historically gotten a bad rep at Cornell. I think a lot of things changed for the Spring 2020 semester. I was surprised at the good lectures, clear slides, accessibility of the staff, improvement in HW quality and understanding that I was able to gain from this class. Haym has also been an extremely caring professor during the crisis.

CS4700 was probably the worst class I took at Cornell. Everyone describes AI as an "Easy A" because the topics are simple, but the class is so unorganized and inconsistent that it is frustrating to prepare for it. Prof Hirsh seemed unprepared for class and his slides/problem sets had many errors. To learn similar content, take CS 2110 and CS 4780.

Most unorganized class I've ever taken. Prof promised weekly hws, have gotten 3 (12/15 weeks into semester). Office hours a mess because he doesn't provide TAs with intelligible HW solutions. Grade based on 2 tests (practice exams not helpful), and HWs which are hard to seek help for. Very apparent prof doesn't care about the course; stay away!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The homeworks (there are about 6) are pretty helpful in understanding the material. There were also some good example problems provided before the exams last semester. Overall, the class was a lot better than what I'd previously heard. The curriculum/course structure has changed for the better, and Hirsh cares a lot about helping students learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Poor lecturer, very disorganized. Tells class a homework will be released that night and then takes another 6 days to actually release it. Class itself is a joke, you won't learn anything but you will get an easy A. If you're a CS major, don't bother. If you're just looking to fulfill a requirement, I still wouldn't tbh.

I didn't go to lecture that much, but still did well on exams and homeworks. All you need to really do is study the powerpoint slides and notes from old CS 4700 websites to pass + go to exam reviews. Prof. Hirsh is a nice guy and good teacher, but the material in this course is pretty scarce so he ends up spending alot of time on simple topics.

Comparing Strandford or Berkeley, this course is a shame. Probably one of the worst CS courses at Cornell. Extremely unorganized. Professor was too busy to take care of the class. Spending a month on DFS and BFS (Remember this is a 4000level course). It only covers 1/5 or fewer materials than Berkeley. Don't take it if you are a CS major.
Was quite flexible regarding the projects, easy assignments, boring lecture, lots of extra credits activities. He was very unorganized and the exams were vague and quite difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Never seen any other professor is as responsible and patient as Prof. Hirsh.  His recitations and replies on piazza are super helpful. He is really a nice guy.

Good professor. May be his first time teaching AI in Cornell but he led the class pretty well. HWs are not so heavy and everyone could easily get full credit. Exams are a large portion of your grade, so do prepare. Usually the test questions are harder than HW, or tricker.   Professor is nice and spent a lot of time of Piazza :)

Her grading is inconsistent and based on personal bias rather than the exam scores outlined in the syllabus. A student with higher exam scores can receive a lower final grade than someone with lower scores simply because she favors the other student. And she never responds to emails asking about grades.

She is by far the worst professor in CBE. Her grading is unclear, and she is not responsive if you ask about it. There are tons of grammar errors and typos in her handouts and HWs. Topics are scattered around and her monotone voice is not encouraging. She has no innovation in her teaching style. Attend TA to learn and you might get a good grade.

Pretends to be encouraging and positive but it's not. Her grading method is very unreasonable, giving you a low final grade without you knowing the final project grade. The worst professor in the CBE department. Avoid if you can.

Very nice and caring professor. Grading is evenly spread out amongst exams, quizzes and homework. Workload is fairly light, quizzes are pretty long (1hr) and tests are slightly less than twice the length of a quiz. Highly recommend going to OH and working on HW with friends.

unprofessional She skipped half of her classes and asked students to read her lecture notes Spent class time trying to bribe students with bonus marks to attend the talks she organized and write nice comments for her in the evaluations In her last attempt to honeypot the students she got the beer and pizza in a makeup session while she was teaching
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Worst professor in the CBE department.
1. Skipped most of the course contents
2. The graded assignments/exams were not distributed, like ever
3. Extremely petty, bribes students with "bonus marks" for writing her a good feedback 
4. Almost always makes a typo in the prelims that throws the students off
5. Pretends to be empathetic but is not
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Harsh grader and answered questions in a condescending manner. Grade is entirely based on prelims and final, so even if you get 100s on homeworks, it will have virtually no impact.

He definitely cares a lot about the material. Lots of homework, each assignment takes a long time, but he is gracious with deadlines. Hard tests that he grades very harshly, final is worth almost half of the grade. Definitely meet with him if you need help during the course.

I was initially dissuaded by the harsh reviews, but found him to be a real sweetheart and very passionate about logic. Generous with extensions, and the course material is very doable if you put the time in. Has a tendency to get off topic sometimes, but will answer homework questions in class.

He has a supreme understanding of the subject and a genuine purpose for it. Immense knowledge to offer If you want to learn set theory, he is the best. I did find it difficult to adapt to his teaching style at first. It can seem like unorganized nonsense. There is a method to his madness, you just have to be willing to take the L a lot. Kind man

Literally changed the course of my life. Took this class 15 years ago in the spring semester of my senior year and realized I made a mistake studying the humanities. Took a hard right turn after graduating and became an engineer. Do the work and Hodes is great. Don't and suffer.

Harold Hodes is intelligent and passionate about his material. Introductory classes are quite fun. Difficulty and course rigor increases with more depth. Expects diligence and to "hit the mental gym". He is always willing to meet outside of class one on one to do more problems. He accepts resubmissions on incorrect hw. Very fair grader and person.
Very disorganized, capricious when writing/grading exams, harsh when answering questions for no reason, difficult to learn from, difficult to work with, brilliant.
Grades harshly, but still is the GOAT
Hodes is iconically bad. Lectures are horrible. He's condescending whenever a question is asked. Huge mismatch between lectures and homework. Would only recommend it for the memes.

I don't know how he is for philosophy but don't take any of his math classes, he nitpicks a ton when grading proofs and won't give any credit unless everything is done his way (even if the logic is spot on). He's also quite arrogant and condescending (you'd think someone who can barely operate zoom would be a bit more humble.)

One of my favorite professors at Cornell. I have taken two classes with him so far. Brilliant and extremely clear. A logician indeed. Not to mention he is the most chilled professor I've had when it comes to deadlines. I don't know why most ratings are negative about him. Maybe if they took one of his smaller classes, they'd appreciate him more.
He came to class late without a sense of apology. Very disorganized, ill-prepared and irresponsible. Trite and glib. Doesn't seem to enjoy teaching or enthusiastic about the subject.

Prof. Hodes is one of the worst and most disorganized professors I've had. Lectures jump all over the place, handwriting is terrible, grading criteria is vague, grading is overly harsh, and gives assignments (like papers) on the fly with no advance notice or proper timing. Totally advise against taking a class with him.
no

Lectures were a little on the dull side, but you can tell Hodes loves logic. The proofs were interesting and homework was very simple. Exams were reasonable and based entirely on proofs done in class.

Don't take previous comments too seriously. Hodes is good at the subject and he is suuuuuper cute!!! You won't see many old nice guys around the campus. The course is hard though and worth taking only if you like to analyze boring sentences. Homeworks are hard compared with prelims and finals.

Hodes is a brilliant man, but is tragically condescending. He'll openly bash you in class for having faulty reasoning or poor grasp of the English language. The subject material is focused more on fundamentals, so it's a bit different from normal logic classes. He's usually one to stammer because the material is dense at times.

A real sweetheart, but at times confusing, and not a very kind grader. Not to be recommended if you don't have a keen interest in the subject material. The stuff we covered in class was difficult, but accessible with persistence. All that said, he's a hilarious dude with a moustache that will make you crack up. Go see him during office hours.
Hodes is (a) awesome, and (b) too cute for words. What a mensch!!!

An excellent Professor for students who accept, even though they are "Ivy League", that they are often wrong and unaware that they are wrong.  Many people like him even though they are not doing well grade-wise.  Often these are people who don't do the homework.  This material isn't difficult if you do the homework.  Do it!  Hodes rules.

As interesting a teacher as you are in the material. Those that found him boring found the material boring, while I thought both were pretty interesting. No question he wants you to do well, makes himself available outside of class, and gave us last year's tests to study by. I'd take his advanced calss next year. The text book he chose was great.

Professor Hodes is a nice guy who wants to help his students.  However, unless you are exceptionally good at things like math and logic, it is impossible to get an A.  I am very hardworking and have never had a grade below A, but in this class, despite working 10-20 hours/week, the best grade I got was a B.  He moves at his own pace, not students.

Prof Hodes is the funniest entity in the world. His bushy moustache just makes me wanna scratch it. That being said, he is an utter horror of a professor. He goes at his own speed, not the student's. And he is far too cruel to ask questions. He WILL humilliate you. Expect to see 'rewrite' next to 90% of your papers. That being said, he's too funny.
Most people dislike the class, not him. He is an excellent teacher who happens to enjoy a very difficult field. He loves what he does and makes for an interesting, if not useful course.

I really like him personally. He does try hard to be available to give outside help. But I had done well in logic with other professors and in this class I was utterly lost. I didn't understand his questions and he didn't understand my assignments, and it was all just a very unhappy experience.
He's not as bad as everyone says.  Still, he is a bit dull.

He's really not that bad. Absent-minded and yes he did assign impossible problems on the prelim and final. But his presentation in class is decent and the textbook is excellent. Exams are fair, he doesn't ask things you haven't learned. Make sure you check your prelim grades though -- he messed up mine 2 times. Do all the homework, best way 2 learn

On both one prelim and our final, he gave literally impossible questions. He announced that he messed up the prelim after the test, and realized his mistake in the last 10 mins of the final. Despite this, he didn't offer any type of compensation for the time people wasted trying to solve his impossible questions. Overall, a very unreasonable guy.
this guy makes the class harder than it is. he never helps you out on the smallestof issues & makes you feel dumb for asking something on the topic your LEARNING!!!

Prelim 1: Spent 30 min on one problem that was actually unsolvable because Hodes made a mistake writing it.  And, for my efforts in noting that on my test, I got an extra "+" next to my grade.  Meaning I got a "D-+", i.e. a D- with a gold star next to it.  Really makes me feel much better about having to drop this and take 20 credits next semester.
Cool class, terrible professor. Good Prof--but grades unfairly.

He definitely puts a lot of time and effort into his job.  He'll usually try hard to answer your questions.  Just keep a positive attitude and don't be intimidated.  And he's a bit hard of hearing, so speak up!

A GPA BUSTER! Yes he is definitly clear on what he wants you to do, that is, unless you ask a question-for if you do beware of an unprecedented tongue-lashing! Take this class with a different professor, and you may actually learn something, and may potentially make above the HODES-stipulated mean:C
completely unapproachable.  makes you feel like an idiot for asking a question.  grading seems very subjective.  avoid him.  other profs teach this class

Actually a very interesting course, but Hodes is the absolute worst.  He has a bad rep with other profs too.  His grading is not understandable (he doesn't give A's unless "you know the material as well as [he] does." AVOID LIKE THE PLAGUE.

It's like you're calling him out whenever you ask a question... and he knows what you're getting at, you can see it in hi eyes, but he'll pick apart the grammar of your sentence... like a needle under your cuticle

Professor Hodes is amazing. He's one of my favorite professors so far. If you're interested in the material and you are willing to put in the time, he'll be there for you. He is one of the professors that I am asking to write a recommendation for me.
Underrated as a funny professor, not because he makes jokes, but because I just cant stop laughing when I'm around him.
HODES!!!! HODES!!!! HODES!!!! HODES!!!! HODES!!!! HODES!!!! HODES!!!! HODES!!!! HODES!!!!
Oh man, this was the worst class in the world.  Hodes! is now a rallying cry of frustration amongst many people I know.
Absolutely Intolerable. Avoid. Avoid. Avoid.
Not a fun class
This man is a nightmare.  He is not only incompetent, but he is an intolerable person as well.  He will make a seemingly interesting course into torture.  Do not take any course taught by this man.

Had her for ECE2300 and ECE4160, this review is about the 4160 experience. This class is SO MUCH WORK, but the payoff is tremendous and Prof Helbling tries her absolute hardest to make it all make sense. She respects her students and tries to be very flexible, but refuses to compromise on the underlying course content (a good thing).
Good lecturer. Only thing were her replies on ed discussion or in office hours which were not helpful or sarcastic , otherwise a good professor
Terrible professor. Terrible labs and HW. Condescending on Ed discussion

Lectures were alright, overall organized but could have been made clearer. The first prelim was overkill for the reduced time limit, but she managed to get it right on the second prelim and final exam, which were much more fair. However, she is often condescending and snarky on Ed Discussion, which is rather disappointing to see.

Generally good lectures, however some feel very rushed and lack of organization (VM lecture). The first prelim was challenging. Her second prelim was much fairer for the reduced time constraint. The problems sets are lighter than other ECE ENGRDS. Lab are long, but they help immensely with concept mastery. But, she's incredibly unhelpful on EDStem.

She has so many unorthodox teaching methods that are annoying for the sake of being annoying. She didn't post second prelim solutions because she didn't want it to be easy? She also isn't releasing practice finals for god knows what reason. I swear she makes this class much harder than it has to be so that she feels smarter than her students.

I took this class thinking Albonesi would be teaching, not knowing he was on sabbatical. Terrible idea. She refuses to give solutions to practice prelims as it'd be 'too easy', includes lengthy exam questions on content barely gone over in lecture, regurgitates words from 5-year-old slides, and seems to WANT her students to fail & have a hard time.

Professor Helbling is one of those professors who is a nice person and very knowledgeable but shouldn't be teaching in the classroom. The content is hard, and she makes it even harder by answering questions vaguely and not providing the practice prelim solutions to students. If you can, try to take this class in a semester she's not teaching.

Echoing what others have said, only take this class if you have to. She gives open-ended/unclear responses on ED and refuses to provide solutions for practice prelim 2. The class itself requires heavy thinking and often concepts get confusing. Not providing the solutions to us for practice prelims only worsens this. Terrible & stressful class.

Only take this class if you really have to. The professor makes the labs and exams hard as hell, refuses to provide answers to practice prelims because "cause you need to practice the problems". Her responses on ED are completely unhelpful and the class is frankly carried by a small group of overworked TAs at this point.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Honestly trying to study for this prelim has been a total nightmare. The professor refuses to give us the solutions to the practice prelims so we are practically guessing and checking whether our solutions are correct. The professor does not helpful advice on ED, and sounds condescending. If you don't have to take this class, please don't.

Honestly very deceitful as a professor. Promised to release extra practice for a subject in prelim 2 and walked it back. Also refused to give solutions to practice prelims. Every part of this class seems designed to inflict as much suffering as possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The professor refused to release answers for practice prelim 2 when it would make a difference for some of us who would like to learn from the answers. If the professor released the answers I would give a higher rating.
