Zero chill regarding workload - get ready to be pounded by homework, prelabs, lab, and report. Doesn't realize that her class isn't the only class students are taking smh. 

I came in interested in hardware and left hating the subject.

Kinda sadistic as she purposely makes homework and exams difficult.

These past few labs have honestly been insane in their difficulty and length. Honestly makes you wonder what the purpose of a lab section is when chances are you are going to be spending office hours trying to finish one. Don't even get me started on the terrible lab reports - they are honestly so tedious.
Labs are very long, frustrating, and confusing. The homeworks are also relentless. Ignore the people who say that the class isn't hard; most people in the class are honestly struggling.

Do not take this class if you think you can just do nothing and get a free A+, this class is not time-consuming if you actually pay attention during her lectures and understand the materials because all the pre-labs and labs are based on the materials you learned, if you do not understand the logic behind each of the labs then you going to struggle
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Class feels awful in general. The only saving grace are some amazing TAs that actually care and want to help. Prelabs and labs take up sooo much time and the prelims aren't fair. For our first prelim we got 1 additional question and 30 min less time compared to a practice prelim. Prof. Helbling is a decent lecturer, but that ends there.

The labs are incredibly time consuming, expect to spend several more hours in office hours debugging the code that you already spent hours in actual Labs trying to write. The prelabs are also very long and complicated. The grader also makes things due at the most random times, such as making prelabs due at 12 pm on mondays.

She is a decent lecturerer but the first prelim was honestly insane. It was longer than the practice prelims and we had less time to do it (this year prelims were 90 minutes compared to 2 hours for previous years). Labs are also an insane time sink: be prepared to spend hours on pre-labs and lab reports.

The Lectures are okay but the exams are extremely difficulty. She added more questions to the first prelim and decreased the allotted time compared to previous years. The Labs are also extremely time consuming (spending hours on prelabs and lab reports).
Decent lecturer but the difficulty of her exams are mind-blowing. Workload is a intense especially with prelabs, labs, and psets taking up a huge amount of time. Brutal class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Exam was pretty difficult to complete in time. In previous year, the exam was 2 hrs long with 5-6 questions. She added more questions to the exam and shrunk the time duration down to 90 mins. The exam questions were like pset problems, these questions take sometime to think in order to come up with the proper approach
Lectures are good but the exams are extremely difficult (time crunch and many topics covered). The prelabs and lab reports are also very time consuming. Homework is consistently substantial.

One of my favorite classes so far. The professor was very understanding of special circumstances. I struggled in the last (Assembly) lab but everything else was very doable and she conveyed the content very clearly.

Although it was her first time teaching the class, she presented the information in a very accessible way. As a result, I was easily able to follow many of her slides. The exams were on the more difficult side, however that could be due to the first time teaching it. The exams just required a bit more thinking than the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She has an amazing personality, however, it was her first time teaching the class and this was reflected back on the students in return. She made herself accessible, however, even though I was able to do all the homeworks, the prelims and finals was nothing representative of the homework, if you have to take her, I wouldn't say not to but get ready

One of the best professors and classes I have taken at Cornell; I wish I weren't graduating so that I could take more courses with her. She meets you at your level of knowledge of the NT, and she's capable of answering any questions you may have. Very engaging, kind, and accommodating. She genuinely cares that her students learn in her course.

Dr. Haines-Eitzen has been one of my favorite professors at Cornell. For her christian literature class, you would read a gospel, and she would analyze each line with so much depth. It was quite fascinating. Grading is easy, just pay attention to her lectures and particpate.

I was in Desert Monasticism. Workload is fair. Weekly discussion posts and a capstone project. A lot of reading but discussions are led in an insightful way and Haines-Eitzen changed what we did each week (not boring). She is approachable and kind. Her own research is super interesting too. One of my favs from RELST.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: She was well-prepared, kind, personable, and very knowledgeable on the subject. She also delivered very sensitive content without controversy.
Her class was very interesting and I looked forward to it every week. I learned a lot and the coursework was not too bad.
One of the most interesting classes I've taken so far. She teaches the material in a way that makes it really interesting. Essays are not too long or frequent, and she's very generous in her grading.

Very nice, understanding, and supportive of students. As long as you are engaged with the material and the class, she'll like you. Was flexible about how you approached weekly reading responses. Grading was based on participation, reading responses, and midterm and final essays, no exams. It was a relatively easy class, but I also learned a lot.
Fantastic teacher.  Really cares about her students and about the material.  Teaches a potentially very volatile class in a really sensitive manner. Wish Cornell had more teachers like her.
She is a great teacher and lecturer. Everyone likes her, the TA and the class. I would highly recommend her and her religious survey class, Islam, Judaism and Christianity (RELST 2651).
The prof knows her stuff.  Nice to watch, too.
Prof. Haines-Eitzen is an excellent lecturer who really highlights the historical context of everything I thought I "knew."  Great class!  One of my best experiences at Cornell.
not as wonderful as many think..she's sorta fake

i agree that this prof is overrated. i liked the subject, so i learned alot from readings, but the instructor wasn't all that helpful. she's sorta has a fake personality too..she might seem nice to many people tho'. i'd take the class if it interests u, but otherwise i wouldn't want to take another class from this lady
lame class..subject material/readings are interesting however.. professor is hugely overrated..
Excellent teacher, and very dedicated to her students!
One of the best teachers at Cornell.  Very helpful.  Fairly easy classes (they are intro).  Take any of the intro classes with her.  She makes a relatively boring subject fairly interesting.
wonderful wonderful woman...

Very good professor. Nice, clear, and relatively easy. One of those professors who will actually teach you stuff that you will remember, not like those other people who develop their own stupid philosophies about things that you really don't care about.
She knows her stuff and how to teach it ^^.
Very nice and helpful. One of the better professors I have had.
Great professor, one of my favorites...good use of videos and music to enhance class.
She is just excellent!  She always did really cool demos in class and kept everyone interested.  There was a lot of reading but the grading was really fair.
This was the best class I had at Cornell.  A lot of fun and very informative.
Excellent lecturer, very energetic and interested in the course material, really cares about students, fair exams and grading, and good reggae music.  An overall great class and professor!
great class

He might be good at researching, but he is absolutely not good at lecturing and breaking things down. If you take his class, be ready to learn on your own for more than 80% of the time. Even many CS lovers on YouTube outperform him in terms of teaching DB stuff.

This class is relatively interesting, but takes SO MUCH time. Only take it if you have a significant interest in getting started with DB design. You will need equally committed partners.
If you choose to take it take advantage of opportunities to fix and ask for regrades. Additionally, make sure to rigorously test.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Class is eh. People are right that it is 'easy', the hard part is parsing the content out of the lecture material. Slides are very long, while what is important is not always evident. Exams have a strong emphasis on SQL which for a DB class I think is good, but I found them difficult. SQL is covered but not enforced to the degree which is tested.

He's lowkey just a chill guy, he is def passionate about the material and it shows when you ask him questions. This is the easiest CS class you can take at this school, like, its easier then 1110. The material is also pretty useful for industry, though I don't think ill ever use a where not where not exist sql negation irl.

Loved his lectures. He answers questions if you have any (even though only few people asked). Homeworks are very representative of the exams and also gives enough practice exams. Not hard to get a good grade in this class. Office hours are also good.
Great Prof, great content

Might as well not even be there. Course staff never answers Ed posts. There's no syllabus, and he would flip flop on the late policy to whatever he feels like. Normal DB is just boring, but the practicum is an unreal amount of work. Infuriating how absent he would be from what should be easy questions on Ed.

Despite his looks and how he speaks, Dr. Trummer is actually a very smart guy. Otherwise, our department wouldn't hire him as a new faculty member.

His lectures are very difficult to understand, and the TA I interacted with is not helpful at all. I dropped the course during the first month. I ain't wasting my time here.

Good luck.

This class was terrible. Legit could win an award for how badly he teaches. The content isn't necessarily hard, but his extreme lack of explanation and his terribly worded problem sets make it unnecessarily difficult. To top it off, the course staff he hires for this class have absolutely no idea what they are doing and mess up when they help.

This is a very demanding class. It felt more like a 4 credit class than a 2 credit one. The 5 projects were difficult and built off of each other, so if you implemented something wrong it has to be resolved before your next project (and you do not get access to solutions or the test cases that TAs run). You have to be a strong Java developer.

Because of COVID this class was graded only on 6 homeworks (no exams) and it ended up being very easy. Trummer is a clear & effective lecturer and made concepts easy to understand with examples and visualizations in his slides. Homeworks were straightforward and followed directly from the lectures. There was a textbook but I did not use it.
The content of the course is really useful. However, his lecture is hard to understand even with the video recordings from past semester.
His lecture was somewhat hard to follow!

Lectures were super dry, but they were posted online so you could work through them at your own pace. Made the requirements clear and assignments+exams were manageable. Grading was very slow. Material somewhat interesting.
Ambiguous Assignment with unrefined score judgement. Accent is 'tuple' or 'Lets get started!"
Learning from Trummer was the highlight of my college career.
Very good course
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Extremely good professor. Enjoyed the lectures. Highly recommend the course.
Trummer was a below average professor. His lectures were tough to understand. MANY people dropped.

He's super knowledgable and a good guy to talk to but his content in WLC tends to be all over the place without as much cohesiveness as other lecturers. In regards to the exam def the toughest to prepare for b/c you have to cite readings in a closed-book exam. Exam Qs were rough but grading seemed more lenient relative to other profs

Had him as the second professor for Work Labor Capital. He mixed lectures with documentaries which I enjoyed. Provided a list of all of the readings on the final which was useful as we were required to quote from them during the short answer section. Final was much harder than Boyer's so beware of the difficulty spike. A decent prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He mixed lectures with documentaries which was interesting but the test was hard. Short essay and short answers, a couple people weren't able to finish. DO THE READINGS and take notes.

Great professor. Readings were insightful and informative. He expertly covers a plethora of interesting topics, including workplace cultures and discrimination. Papers are really easy (just have to reflect on the readings), and tests were graded fairly. I enjoyed the lectures, but if you aren't interested in the topics they may be boring. Gives EC.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The entire class is based off of readings, most of which I found interesting, but long. The class has no clear theme and is very disjointed. Lectures are useless, but mandatory. The actual grading is entirely done by your TA and it matters which one. I like the content and idea of the class but it was poorly executed.

Class itself was not that difficult just incredibly boring and required you to do an obnoxious amount of reading which was NEVER talked about in class so you had to infer meanings on the tests. Tests are mostly short answers and discussions were useless. He seemed like he did not want to teach the class and word-for-word read off the slides.

God, he is the absolute worst. He literally just chats, like no content comes out of his mouth, he just says words. I personally think his class is the biggest waste of time, but attendance is mandatory!!!

For a 1.5 credit class, the amount of readings and work given seemed unnecessary. Professor Ivory used an index card system that made lecture attendance mandatory. They improved after the first prelim, but the lectures were generally pretty useless and did little to help me understand the incredibly dense and long readings for the week.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: unnecessarily strict with his attendance/deadline policies and is unsympathetic to needing flexibility. he basically reads off of his slides, so going to lecture feels pointless, and rather than discussing the incredibly dense readings, he just puts "discussion questions" up on the board and reads them to the class. he doesn't even answer them.
Seems like a nice guy, but I couldn't hear a single thing. Talks into his neck. Tests were dumb. Like high school. Did not enjoy. Some readings were interesting though. Lectures were just not good.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class is based on readings which are never discussed meaningfully in class, useless lectures, attendance is mandatory with mini flashcard assignments about readings, he doesn't seem like he wants to be there, must study hard, some TAs make class much easier than others, overall would not recommend class unless you have to take it as an ILRie
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very boring and useless lectures. He just reads off from the slides every day. And attendance is mandatory. Extremely heavy readings with few explanations in class lectures. Would not take it again.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: she can't distinguish what's AI and what's not iykwk
The content was super interesting, reading was reasonable, grade was nice and feedback were constructive. Would recommend!
Not too difficult to get an A. Assigns a decent amount of reading. Writing quantity is probably at the average for an FWS.

Prof Rivera is genuinely so awesome!! One of my favorite english classes I've taken, she's super enthusiastic about teaching and really facilitates a fun + collaborative environment in class that helped me get to know a lot of my classmates. Feedback on essays is really good and all of them are peer-reviewed, readings for homework aren't too bad

I love Professor Rivera. She is intelligent and witty, and covers so many different and interesting concepts. Spans from disabilities in love to BDSM to Plato to online dating. Readings for homework are mandatory for discussion but never too long. Peer reviews for most essays, and Profs feedback is good. Such a good class, would recommend.

You will get at least a B if you just turn in the assignments (that's what she says). She covers interesting and fun topics, but I don't think the class is an easy A. Not a lot of instructions on the essay. Also, you don't know what your grade is until she releases the final grade. She's very understanding with deadlines though.

It is a good FWS and has interesting topics. Final essay lets you express your interest and the first essay is very fun to write. Some cool topics are in this course, such as gender and cultures influence on food. I like her she is very engaging and it is an easy A if you go to class, participate and try your best for your essays.

Wide range of class topics introduced through a variety of means and interesting discussions make her FWS a joy to be in. She focuses on writing structure and grammar but also allows students to write in their own styles and express their personalities through writing. Wonderful professor and wonderful class!

The professor is very considerate and understandable. Class is interesting. I appreciated the work that was put into it. There are readings for hw, but they are usually short and interesting. This class was not work heavy at all.

Standard FWS class interesting topics covered, but not necessarily focused on love as originally intended. Zero feedback on papers other than "good" and "okay" on certain paragraphs, but I got an A so can't complain. Final Paper and Presentation. Overall easy though.

Easily my favorite professor of the semester. So funny and caring. Really fun content between books and movies and you get to choose your own topic for the final paper. Essays every 2-3 weeks with a rewrite allowed each time. So fun, low stress :)

My favorite class this semester by far. Readings and movies were carefully picked and captivating. You can tell she cares about what she teaches and about her students. Very understanding of the difficulties learning in a pandemic, and flexible if you explain your situation. Participation is vital to your grade and makes the class more enjoyable.

Participation and attendance are required, but the discussions are never boring. She picks a wide variety of readings and movies, almost all of which are quite interesting. She is very approachable, and she understands conflicts for assignments, and is willing to work with you for extensions. Her class is not an easy A, but she wants you to succeed

Great lecturer who is super engaging with the class. I recommend any class with her. She always finds interesting films, books, and short readings which are engaging. Discussions can be slow at times if you do not have a well-read class. She is a tough but fair grader.

Interesting readings and movies picked for class. You can tell that she was very interested in the topics that we discussed. Sometimes I was so entertained by the discussions we had in class that I forgot that it was a writing seminar. It is easy to do well in the class, but she will make you work in order to get an A.

INCREDIBLE professor + WARM person. My favorite prof. last semester (and yet @ college). I was reading pieces of literature that I did not know existed (!), and it is so clear that her passion shines through. chill class w/ super reasonable amount of work + readings. commit yourself to the work + participate and you'll leave w/ much more than an A.

I took her writing seminar on Queer Hispanisms. Simply amazing. She assigns a very reasonable amount of readings and she will make sure that they are NOT boring. Her lectures are interesting and very clear. She has a great personality and she is very REAL. Understands the lives of college students very well, so she's flexible on deadlines.
Prof. Bazarov is a great person and really teaches the content with passion. It is genuinely fun to be in his class, with his small jokes and puns.

Amazing, clear lectures with excellent posted notes (still worth attending in person). Original problem sets are a reasonable length and surprisingly enjoyable. Exams are challenging, but plenty of practice problems are provided, and the curve helps. Difficult but rewarding content.

Professor Bazarov is an excellent lecturer with an amazing sense of intuition for physics that makes you appreciate the subject all the more. It's obvious he cares about students' well-being and success, and his lectures are definitely the easiest way to understand the material. Would highly recommend taking any course he teaches!
Not knowing what he is doing.
Incompetent of physics

Professor Bazarov is a great lecturer - he knows when to balance rigorous derivations with intuitive arguments and usually presents material in a very engaging way. He's not particularly heavy on homework, but get ready to spend time reading because his lectures are paced fast and usually have a few not-so-obvious parts.

EM is a historically tough class. Set up/organization for the class was weaker but overall the professor was fine! My suggestion would be to go to LSC office hours instead of TA ones. Clear grading criteria though and his flipped classroom model helped give very immediate feedback.

This class was extremely difficult and the lectures were okay. I am not really a fan of flipped lectures though. The best part about this class were the TAs. There is so much help available and the TAs are truly excellent.

Bazarov didnt teach us anything, and his answers to our questions just made us more confused. Each class was spent in breakout rooms, working on problems with other students, which proved to be useless. Homework was extremely hard, way above the level of lecture videos. Also grade inflation (on some assignments, a 70% becomes 100%).

Bazarov is one of the worst professors ive ever had. He never actually gave one ounce of instruction, just assigned a billion things per week including lecture videos that were taught way below the academic level of the class, every lecture is spent in breakout rooms and most of the class is pretty convinced he doesn't know anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Hard class. You gotta work for it...
Great Professor. Although the class was very hard, he helped me and basically saved my semester.
Great Professor, hard class. I like how he records lectures online.
Expects you to do ridiculous problems that you've never worked through. He seems more interested in weird niche applications of the stuff than teaching it coherently.

Engaging, unconventional, and very endearing. He assigned us interesting and dare I say it, fun, Matlab projects and illuminating seminar presentations in place of prelims. A very fair grader. Approachable, and his office hours were very helpful. Overall, I had a great experience in a class that I really did not expect to enjoy.

I still have nightmares from her statics and diff eq classes two years later. After graduating Cornell I can confidently say "she" was by far the most unpleasant professor I ever had the displeasure of attempting to learn from. Genuinely mean in the heart, or at least loathes students.

Prof Ritz is absolutely fantastic for statics. She has great intuition and extremely helpful in office hours. Statics is a tough course, but she is really fantastic. Be proactive and she will be super helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Learning outcome system initially seems nice, but makes the last quiz and final exam very stressful. Problems on exams are more difficult than homeworks, especially on second tries of an LO. She's rude when responding to questions in class and on ed discussion. Her lectures aren't the worst but they're not good - I learned everything on my own.
The grading system makes no sense. Really hard to catch up if you fall behind by the first quiz. Good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's pretty polarizing but her notes were very helpful. Also the LO system can be both a blessing and a curse, it was very good if you did well early on and mostly only got 2s and 3s on the quizzes, but falling behind on the quizzes early could set you up to not do very well in the class. The quizzes were fair but some exam questions were not.

The Learning Outcome grading system is not as bad as it seems based on the other reviews. It's easy to know whether you have a solid understanding of each LO from the problem sets. And if you don't, go to office hours. Simple as that. You'll get a good grade. Also go to lectures, I hate the textbook.

In defense of the LO system: This system ensures that if you actually have a strong conceptual understanding of the class, you will be fine. You can revise algebraic/integration mistakes, and can discuss revisions in office hours. You will do well if you consistently put in effort, which is very manageable when spread throughout the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: worst professor I have had at cornell

The teaching and learning approach often proves ineffective, frequently resulting in numerous issues escalating into a single preliminary or final assessment. The checkpoint mastery grading method appears unnecessary, and no credit is awarded for work already completed.

The whole semester felt redundant losing points over small mistakes in math and overcomplicating simple topics. Too much theory for a class that only tests examples. The mastery system is not good and it needs to be taken away immediately.

First time reviewing a professor here, worst experience ever. The problem with the LO system is that it emphasizes perfection for a course that does require a lot of algebra. The lecture and the textbook aren't great either.
By far, the worst experience with a professor at Cornell.

Grading is completely unreasonable and often unrepresentative of your understanding in the class. Furthermore, she does not foster an environment for asking genuine questions, leaving many students on their own to learn material.

Professor Ritz shows little care for her students, and this applies to her Math 2930 class as well. In the ed discussion, she scolds students for asking questions, saying that they are wasting the staff's time. Both big and small things about how she runs the class make me believe that she does not think from the students' perspectives.
She genuinely grades like a madman. She does not care about your mental health or wellbeing. Always rude and creates the most undoable exams and quizzes.

Like the other reviews are saying, the grading system is.. interesting. Nevertheless, it's not hard to do good in this course ONLY IF you don't fall behind. It's not easy to catch up if you do. Put in the work early in the course, knock out as many learning outcomes as you can on your first try, don't slack off on PDEs, and you'll end up with an A.
don't learn anything in lecture. grading system is very unforgiving towards the end.
GARBAGE TEACHER. LIKE MY RATING IF YOU WANT HER FIRED
Ritz is a mediocre lecturer who is able to semi-clearly explain topics. The grading system makes the class needlessly stressful, and punishes you for making mistakes early.

Ritz is a good lecturer but the grading system penalizes students pretty early on for falling behind. The learning outcomes are checked only on quizzes and prelims and the questions for the learning outcomes tend to be difficult and unlike examples in homework and lecture. The course is more difficult than necessary due to the grading system.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Grading system is not great: not standardized and regrade requests are not taken politely. She does not teach intuition, she just regurgitates the textbook but worse. Cornell has really got to step up its hiring game. Students pay so much to get a good education to be the top students in the country to get this. Way to go Cornell, do better.
Absolutely horrendous at teaching. Very unfortunate.

Love the grading system of this course. It's an easy A if you put in the bare minimum. Go to class, take notes, that's it. Honestly. I didn't even do a single textbook problem set until we started PDEs.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very clear that she absolutely hates her students. A very discouraging environment
The course itself should not be this hard, but somehow the exam questions are impossible to do that it's impossible to do.

Really clear lectures with helpful lecture notes. Not too much homework. The "outcome-based" grading system (look it up) is innovative and really rewards student effort. This professor got a bad reputation a few years ago, but has improved a ton since then. I would highly recommend taking math with them.

Lectures are decent but she gets passive aggressive when no one participates. Homeworks are very long but exams are easier even though they are still slightly difficult. Decent class but work load was on the heavier side

She is an okay lecturer but I despise the way her classes are graded. For statics, homeworks are tedious to the point where they are not useful for learning the content. Prelims have the opposite problem and are far too easy but you will lose an absurd amount of points for barely doing anything wrong. The checkpoint system for Diffeq is also dumb.

Ritz is genuinely the worst professor I have ever had. Statics is an interesting topic and should be a fairly engaging class, but the grading system is insanely punitive and demotivating. A ridiculous amount of points get taken off for the tiniest mistakes, even the TA's complain about her, and the time commitment is much more than 4 credits worth.

She was genuinely a wonderful professor for statics. Very caring and took effort to learn all of our names in a large lecture. Homework was tedious and difficult but her office hours are incredibly helpful and accessible. Prelims difficulty was very reasonable given what was covered in lecture and homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She's great at explaining things and doesn't move too fast in lectures. The homeworks are really long though, so go to office hours. She's sometimes quite blunt when answering questions but she's helpful.

I'm not sure why she has such a bad rating, maybe she's just better with Statics than with DiffEQ, but I think she's a great teacher, takes the time to learn student's names. Homework is difficult, but it makes Prelims so much easier. I also think the prelim grading is quite generous as I don't deserve a lot of the points I get on them.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Ritz is probably a good lecturer, like I'm sure she teaches fine. However, her disgusting attitude overwhelmed any redeeming qualities she has. By far the rudest and most uncaring professor I have ever encountered. Severely lacks empathy.
Never take this course if you see that she's teaching. Honestly, Ritz made me question what Cornell looks for when it hires professors.

I heard lots of things about Dr. Ritz before coming to the class, but to be honest throughout the class she was very generous with grading and such. She's pretty funny and makes an effort to be fair and reasonable. Although the course structure is a little strange, overall it's more helpful than it is hurtful.

Ritz made DiffEq a great experience for me. I looked forward to class and enjoyed learning the content. The content itself can feel disconnected and a bit abstract at times but Ritz made it easy to learn. She made her expectations clear, had good, thorough notes, and was very efficient and effective during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ritz got a bad rep a few years ago, but I think she is great.  She is organized, and will ask for feedback consistently. I was terrified of participating in class, but I still got a lot out of lectures. Her exams are fair, but you definitely need to study. Problem sets are hard, but help is accessible.

If you understand the grading system from the beginning - then it's your average engineering class. I Lecture's were also great. Not a lot of review material available to practice, so join an AEW, do webworks, optional textbook questions, textbook readings, lecture readings.

P-sets are optional, WeBWorks are easy. The Learning Outcome system is still really weird. It's hard to know what your standing is in the course until the very end. Ritz's lectures are solid and, in my opinion, better than the textbook. The final was graded very lightly to fit a normal engineering grade distro, so final grading was not an issue.

Professor Ritz gives really great lectures that you can get a lot out of if you pay attention to them and work on the practice when she gives time to do so. She also genuinely cares a lot about students and our learning, so if you take the time to talk with her, you will get a lot out of that. Exams are tough but definitely fair if you study.

The most frustrating part of this class was the rubrics for assignments and tests — they felt over penalizing for small things. Some HW was too long. Good lectures, the course structure / content was overall enjoyable and well taught. There was good access to support like office hours. Professor Ritz is nice if you talk to her, overall good class.

Whatever happened in past semesters Prof Ritz turned it around. Lectures where amazing. Web work was eh, didn't feel like I got a lot out of it but also not much work. I liked the checkoff system a lot. Felt way less stress over the course of the semester. Focusing on a specific topic without worrying about many others made them easier to master.

This was my first math class where I didn't teach myself from the textbook. Lectures are pretty. It helps to "clear" LOs so that you don't have to worry about them later in the course but sometimes their timing and order fo testing was weird. Slightly frustrating near the end when no practice questions were given on non-homo PDEs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is not honestly as bad as most people claim -- the course has improved. The lectures were somewhat confusing and were paced oddly, so I often used the published notes. Professor was quite nice and helpful during office hours for revisions. Preparing for later LOs (Heat etc.) was annoying as pset problems did not align with exam problems.
I don't know what the hate for Ritz is. She gives amazing lectures, and really cares about her students. Sure the tests are hard; just study well.

Do not understand the hate towards this professor. The LO grading system is okay if you put in consistent effort across the entire semester and all quizzes and exams. This professor was wonderful in her office hours and her lectures were quite informative even if you don't read the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Ritz is able to teach course content with clarity, providing students with plenty of opportunities to ask questions in lecture and review material. She uses interesting demonstrations during lecture (i.e., MATLAB scripts) to describe the physical behavior of differential equations. Overall, I really enjoyed this class with Prof. Ritz.

Ritz isn't the worst, but her grading with Learning Objectives (LO) is. You could be doing good all year, getting 3/3s on LOs on all 4 graded quizzes, and going into the final with 14/21 graded LOs as 3/3s and then bam. If you don't get the answer almost perfectly right you get a 1/3 and your grade is ruined. It's perfection or nothing with grades.

I think her teaching is fine, but most of her responses to questions on Ed Discussion are snarky and unfriendly. She will refuse to give actual answers to genuine questions and respond with things along the lines of "I will not entertain this" or "Why are you asking this?". It just makes me lose respect for her as a person.

For statics ritz has always been very transparent about all of the resources and the criteria to do well in her class. She is more than willing to help you in any way you need to succeed, if only you reach out to her. It's a hard class so make use of the resources.

I will not understand the hate against Ritz, she is mega caring and extremely accessible outside of class. You can tell she cares a lot about her students. For context, her canvas home page has a pep talk for the students. I truly enjoy the grading for this class and it is not as terrible as everyone says: just make sure to not fall behind.

Ritz is the best lecturer I have had at Cornell, for both ENGRD 2020 and MATH 2930. Her classes are definitely tough, but she is always there to support her students and wants to see them all succeed.
This is the worst grading system of any class I've ever had the misfortune of taking. You could do the entire course perfectly up to the final, miss two questions, and get an A-.
What can I say that hasn't already been said? Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Atrocious grading rubrics with no thought behind them. Consistently took off 20-40% from total homework grades for tiny errors like not writing dimensions on a Free Body Diagram or not writing "Given: Find: Plan" above the solution to a problem, even when all final answers were correct. Partial credit wasn't given on prelims, which weren't curved.

Says we get multiple attempts-not true. Gave no advice about approach to prelim 1, making prelim 2 a sprint through 9 questions. 2 problems drop a whole letter grade, we got 1 try for them, how this even makes sense when the whole point of this grading system is to have multiple chances. Class material is not bad but just ridiculous grading.
Some people have good karma coming their way. This is not one of those people

Not one to ever use this site, but wanted to publish a review for Professor Ritz.

I truly enjoyed my time in MATH2930 with Hadas Ritz, and I truly believe that this is the most that I have ever learned from a math class. Her lectures are incredibly understandable, and while the grading system may seem odd, she is very fair and it helped me learn.

Disrespectful/snarky on Ed, restricts posting to reduce criticism, doesn't respond to complaints, changes the rules every single day based on mood swings, revokes opportunities, contradicts her syllabus, imposes a draconian grading scheme no one asked for to try to prove research paper she wrote, targeted student who called her out

The new grading system is... interesting. I (and many others) did not like Ritz's course (the lectures move painfully slow), and it covers shockingly little material (no transforms??). The grading scheme doesn't aid with "learn at your own pace" and instead obfuscates what should be a pretty simple class. The material's easy, but grading isn't.

Ritz's grading system where your final grade is determined by mastery is awful. While her lectures were ok, she's got an attitude outside of class and on Ed discussion. Students tried to address some of these concerns and her solution was to set all threads to approval only and tries to silence students in class.

This class was awful; wouldn't recommend it. Uncertain grading scheme caused stress, with assignments delayed throughout the semester. She changed syllabus multiple times, leading to excessive work over holidays. Office hours were chaotic, and criticisms were dismissed as disrespectful. Students unfairly faced consequences due to her shortcomings.
Hadas Ritz is the GOAT when it comes to teaching Differential Equations! She's super chill and makes complex topics feel like a breeze. Love her teaching style!

Ritz is a great lecturer, but the grading scheme she tried to implement this semester was poorly organized and incredibly ineffective. Some things on the syllabus were changed in the last week of class, and there is little/no partial credit.

The class is graded by mastery which is an interesting adjustment to make. However, I enjoyed this grading style. While some of the assignments were very difficult the overall stress around exams was lessened and I believe I performed better on them because of this. Dr.Ritz is also very kind and super willing to help in office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: really easy class, easy grading scheme
grading system makes no sense

I have never learned as much as I did in this class. The homework and material IS very difficult. Ritz asked for feedback multiple times throughout the class and actually applied what she received; it's obvious she cares about students' learning. She is amazing at summarizing the material in approachable ways. Does a good job mixing in examples.

The material itself is not that difficult; she is.
A group of my friends went to find her for help because the exam average was a 70 (and we knew she was not going to give a good curve) -> professor said our year is just dumb. She doesn't understand how COVID exams are easier.

The class was curved to a low B- (she called it a generous curve).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Ritz tried a new grading scheme that was too good to be true. While it intended to give us lots of opportunities to succeed, it ended up doing the opposite. There was a lack of transparency with the grading scheme, and students were left confused for the majority of the semester, with a huge workload at the end of the semester.

Took ENGRD 2020 in FA 22. Prof. Ritz tries her best to lecture well and convey the necessary material; however the homework sets were pretty long/convoluted and exams usually had a fair share of curveballs. Class was curved to low B- (super annoying) ... be ready for a lot of work for this class with her.

dumb grading system dumb; there were so many important quizzes due during the study period that it was hard to do work for other courses. Missing a single quiz can knock you down a +/- for the overall grade.

The psets are tough but doable for the most part. The content starts out alright but suddenly gets difficult toward the end. There's a harsh curve (median B-) for the overall course grade, and I literally did one std above the mean for prelim 2 and the final and still got a B+. There is "online homework" in addition to the pset, which are annoying.

Grading scheme had a cool concept but basically made all assignments either not worth the time or worth the same as an exam. Every assessment demands perfection or you won't get any credit at all, which makes it way harder to prove understanding than it needs to be. Make sure your TA likes you & be persistent with regrade requests.

The grading was inconsistent/inaccurate. Grading was either full points or no points: no partial credit. There were many times when I got full points on an assignment, and someone with the same answer and work got no points. Or I got no points, put in a regrade request, and then was told my answer was perfectly correct. Disappointing class.

Worst grading system of all time. Does not to partial credit at all. I did not receive credit for several things that I know how to do, because any small algebra mistake means you get no credit for an entire problem. That policy applies to exams, homework, quizes, and everything we do. It is the most awful system I have ever seen
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: very stupid and unclear grading system that requires perfection. First two months we didn't know exactly how grading worked. It caused so much unnecessary stress and anxiety because they didn't communicate with students and assignments were graded very late. There were 6 assignments during study week and some of them were due after the final exam.

Very tough grader. She claimed that the course is graded on a curve and in the end, she said it is not exactly curved which doesn't make sense since the medians for all exams were in the mid 60s. They only slightly adjusted grade boundaries and still, the median grade was low B-. Don't take this course if you don't have to or you will only suffer.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Absolutely confusing grading scheme. Good idea but poor implementation. Students were not informed enough until the end of semester where every assignment piles up and become very stressful.
Her courses traumatize me to the fullest

Avoid at all costs. horrible woman with zero empathy for students. Had her for both ENGRD2020 and MATH2930 in the same semester, would strongly advise against taking either course from her, but especially recommend not taking both from her at the same time unless you're willing to sacrifice both your gpa and many nights of sleep.

Assignments are graded late, no partial credit or mercy. Even going to office hours and getting your work personally checked is not enough, staff might still say it is wrong. Grading scheme felt unfair and does not reflect students mastery of concepts. Is a good lecturer when compared to the rest of the math department.

The grading system seemed appealing at first but it was not executed well at all. Students got drastically different levels of difficulty for the questions. The course was not planned well in that we had 2 checkpoints before prelim 2 and there were 8 due during the study period before finals. Does not address student concerns very well.

I took diff. eq. with Ritz under her new grading system, and unlike the majority of the class thought it was awesome! The grading scheme not only made it extremely easy to do well in the class, it also helped with learning and retaining the material. Ritz is a great lecturer who explains concepts well and addresses any and all question in lecture.

horrible new grading scheme that left students scrambling during finals week. students have no idea how they are doing in the course due to grades not being returned in a timely manner. she assigned ridiculous amounts of work during finals, doubt it'll be graded on time. she's causing stress to students already under lots of stress as engineers

Literally the worst Cornell class I have ever taken. I did well in this class and it still has inspired me to never take a class with professor Ritz ever again. If you see that Ritz is teaching a class that you need to graduate, you're better off taking a 5th year to get there.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was a completely awful experience. I still have no clue what my grade is going to be and she owes me like ten grades. A total failure on her part. I do not know how a mandatory course can be taught this badly.

Professor Ritz fails to organize a half-decent, organized class. Students have little clue how well they are performing in the class until they recieve their final exam. The grading is lazy, as partial credit is simply not awarded, including for computation and algebra-heavy problems. 
Lectures are dull. Online course components are buggy. bad.

Bruuuuuuhhhhhh. Staff cannot keep up with new grading scheme. This has lead to a disorganized mess with feedback coming weeks after its relevant. We also have multiple assignments due 4 days after the last class - which the results of dictate what we need to study for on the final. Absolutey embarassing, and ridiculously stressful on students.

Her new grading scheme is too idealistic and disorganized. Her vision was good (student assessed based on general performance instead of test grades) , but as one of the guinea pig students I can say the disorganization of it all makes it only counterproductive. Turns out we are even more harshly penalized by any mistakes. Run.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Remarkably and unacceptably poor at explaining concepts. Learned through textbook/other resources for the whole semester. Frequently makes errors in lecture, and often changes course structure in detrimental ways. If you can, try not to take this class with Prof. Ritz.
Worst professor I have ever had.

extremely disappointed with this classes policies, especially regarding the hw. Problem sets are excessively long + assigned every week, even on weeks with an exam/break. She also refuses to grade the 10+ page assignments unless they follow her insane formatting to a T. otherwise decent lecturer, just wish staff was even remotely empathetic.

Lectures were fine, not too hard to follow but some rough days on harder concepts. Homework was atrociously hard and took a whole day per assignment, covering more than what was on the prelims or in class. Prelims were terrible for covid semester as they were open book/entirely conceptual, with little actual math done on the exam. Discussions suck.
I was often confused during the semester because the material was difficult, but the lectures were so organized and help was so available that it was not difficult to catch up when I fell behind.
Moves too slowly through material in an uninteresting manner.

She is terrifying. But go to office hours for the homework (it's basically impossible without OH or some other kind of help). She has very high but clear expectations and posts good videos to help with difficult concepts. The exams are hard but straightforward so do the practice problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof. Ritz was the best engineering professor I had at Cornell. She is VERY knowledgeable, very organized, and was using digital resources effectively even before the pandemic. She doesn't take nonsense from students, but is also not abrasive or hostile to students. She will simply teach you the subject matter clearly and effectively.
Great professor
Just not a good lecturer. Spends lots of time in silence just writing stuff, which makes it very hard to focus. Doesn't help that her handwriting is really hard to read either.

One of my favorites at Cornell! She really cares about teaching, and is great at explaining things, both in lecture at office hours. She was very approachable and made lectures interesting. The class is undoubtedly hard, and you'll have to work for your grade, but there's a high level of support, and expectations are clear. Highly recommend!
Doesn't understand that there's a pandemic going on. Literally so frustrated and office hours were not helpful for this course at all. worst engineering class i've ever taken.

Incredibly off-putting personality, made me hate the subject from the very start of class. On top of this seems to assign work with some sort of vendetta in mind, intentionally confusing students with the mere selection of problems (not to mention the ridiculous format in which homework must be submitted) and then penalizing the confused class.

She doesn't understand that a lot of people do not care about mechanical engineering and how diff eq applies mostly to physics/mechE stuff. We just need the math requirement and will never use that material again
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Assigns huge amounts of work even during weeks with exams
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Decent professor. Online homeworks are very difficult. Homeworks are usually manageable. Exams are hard, but fair
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Class seems to be going well at the start then all of the sudden she throws a bunch of material and assignment at us at a time that we were supposed to be on break. The material that she threw at us was not easy and was not explained at all in lecture, she simply just clicked through the slides without a care in the world for her students.

Great lectures, definitely worth getting up before 8am for. Could actually do the hw on my own. Unfortunately, the exams were written by a different professor so that wasn't too great. Very good at explaining complicated topics in an understandable way and very patient.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I was wary of Statics, but Ritz was a fantastic professor who really made me interested in the material. The class is hard but not unmanageable if you put in the work - OH are very helpful! Lectures were above average and the exams were fair (although difficult). Homework sometimes seemed like a lot but the problems were worthwhile.

She is a great professor for freshman intro classes, but for junior/senior standing courses she expects more from her students to the point where it's almost too demanding. She gives a lot of difficult work across multiple categories (iClickers, lab quizzes and reports, hws, hit-or-miss exams) which makes it hard to maintain a consistent grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Lots of good reviews for 1000 level classes, but MAE3260 (Systems)  is a totally different animal. She got criticism last year for the sheer length of problem sets, cut them down for this year, and they are still three times longer than those in any other class. The class material is hard, yes, but her grading policies make it brutal. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Good lecturer. Lecture included participation which is unusual and helpful. She would give example problems in class and have you solve them, and give you time to work as she walked around the room to make sure people understood on an individual basis. Was glad to go over things that students didn't understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She cares  about her students but often struggles to get a hold of their attention. Not a lot of work with the exception of the final project which takes way too much time for the course's level.

Class super easy except the final design project takes up way too much time fore a 1000 level engineering course. Doesn't really lecture and just goes over problems in class, which is really a better class structure.

Really enjoyed this class. Lectures were usually enjoyable and the material was interesting but not too difficult. Labs can be very frustrating but the final project is a lot of fun. Good overview of mechanical engineering.

She likes doing examples on the board,  always pay attention to it. Doing them yourself helps you really learn the material. Also, don't be scared to ask questions in class, she'll answer and help you learn. Especially if you sit in the front like me. 1910 isn't always easy, going to her lectures will help. So please, don't skip, even if an 8 am!
Prof Ritz is an excellent lecturer - very clear and concise. She moves a bit quickly sometimes, and can seem intimidating, but overall a great professor. The tests for 1910 are very difficult.

Amazing teacher with a genuine concern for her students. She Encourages participation in class, is open to many different views, and facilitates engaging discussions in her classes. Count getting her as a professor as a christmas present.

She is an amazing teacher! Humorous and also absolutely nice! Her lectures are very organized and clear. Although sometimes the materials are difficult, if you go to lectures and study hard, you will be fine! Prelims are fair (although prelims are not written by her). She gives me a good start in engineering math in college!

I would say that Ritz is a great math professor. She is very helpful and open in office hours. However, the class is definitely a challenge... as are many of the first engineering math classes. Tests were written by the other professor, who was definitely a lot worse than Ritz. She also coined the term "Math Happens"!

Ritz is a pretty decent teacher. She's really helpful. She'll answer anything you have trouble with and she loves it when students come to her office hours. She's a really fair teacher. She tests her students on their knowledge, doesn't really seem to try to trick us. I really liked her! Take this class!

Ritz is a great math teacher! She is really clear and helpful when explaining topics and is really funny too! Great teacher, and from what I've heard, the best professor if you are taking 1910. The prelims are fair (I don't think she makes them though..) and the content is about what you would expect from an engineering calc class.
AMAZING!! Funny, clear, helpful!!! Great class, great professor!
A bit strict for a freshman class, but overall very straightforward and helpful.  A good lecturer, plus has very generous "quizzes instead of prelims" policy.

Overall, Ritz is a clear, her class difficulty is fair, and she is a pretty good lecturer.  Instead of giving prelims, she gives ~10 (relatively easy) pop quizzes over the semester (I liked this policy).  She does give a final.  The final project was a lot of fun. My TA (Anoop) was the best TA I have ever had.  Labs were fun.
Regretted this. Poor communication and coordination. The contents of the class were fun, unfortunately, the person teaching it was not.
Quite disrespectful to students. Had a disappointing experience similar with others.
There really isn't a lot of work for this class and the midterm was fairly easy. A big chunk of your grade comes from participation and projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Stay away.
I've heard poor things about this professor and how little effort she puts into making the class fair. It is definitely true. Do not take class.
Does not listen to students, very selfish professor. You will see.

Group projects are fun and engaging. The lecture itself is also interesting. Very respectful and open to students' opinions and thoughts. Assignments are not too heavy. If you at least read and pay attention, no problem at all. Highly recommended class!

GREAT TEACHER!! So passionate and knows so much about Dante's inferno. This is not an easy class, but great for improving writing and analysis. is based off of effort/improvement and you can get an A (not based off of individual grades)
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very nice professor. Grading are based on your commitment.Homeworks are basically journals (200 words ish) and Assignments (1000 words ish). The professor is quite flexibile on ddls. Assignments are not graded, but instead you have to sign up individual meetings with her, and she gives really helpful feedback.

IEA very clearly cares a lot about her class and her role as a teacher. She is there to help you improve in your writing and will NOT give an easy A for FWS. She will give a lot of feedback and help you get better. If you put in the work and clearly try to improve, you'll get good grade and you'll learn a fair amount. Def more work than other FWS.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of, if not the, best first-year writing seminar professors. Her feedback is incredibly detailed. Instead of simply giving out letter grades and due dates, she expects you to improve your essays as much as possible through office hours. All grades in her course are based on the final drafts at the end of the semester: she focuses on improvement!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I love this prof, the topics were so interesting and we read/watching things about love so most of our assignments were a response to them. The final project was ab a topic of your choosing, it was so helpful to have meetings with her ab the essays and she's super understanding. My new fws doesn't compare-also the community in the class was on top

ROMS 1108: Took her FWS and almost everybody got a B+. AVOID THIS CLASS. If you turn in assignments on time and do work well the default is a B+, which is lower than other writing seminars, which usually give As.

Alvisi was great and taught me a lot about Italian literature. I really enjoyed her classes, and I definitely would have enjoyed them more if they were in person. Just be sure to participate a ton and always come prepared, she respects that a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Definitely gives extremely harsh feedback on essays but is a lovely break from high school English classes. She managed to make learning about Dante's Inferno fun, with a superb mastery of the text and frequent humor. Does not grade individual essays, but requires multiple meetings for feedback.

She's a great lecturer and is very knowledgeable about the text. Also, I learned how to organize my thoughts in writing properly thanks to her. At first, I thought she gave me excessively harsh feedback on my papers, but her concete and thoughtful criticism ultimately improved my writing skills.

reviews.comment: Funny in class. Get ready to do a lot of assignments.

Took both his Ancient Iran and Modern Iran History. Probably easiest classes I've taken. No outside readings. His lectures do not require attendance but they are very interesting. Even if it was graded harder I would still recommend I think he is a great prof.
Iago is a great professor all around. Super accommodating of students. Taught largely from his own experience in Iran, which made the course feel very real.

reviews.comment: THE BEST PROFESSOR AT CORNELL. PERIOD!!!!
best teacher ever at cornell he is so nice and caring

super kind and helpful professor despite my lack of knowledge in Persian. Really patient in teaching and never shames anyone for their less-than-perfect participation or attentiveness. Strives to create an equal learning opportunity and doesn't exclusively pick up good students.

Such an amazing instructor and just simply a wonderful human being. His attentiveness and thoughtfulness towards the students was inspiring, his kindness and humbleness was heartwarming and provided such a unique and comfortable learning environment. Witnessing his knowledge and how easily he talked about such complex topics was really impressive.

Iago was one of the best professors I've had at Cornell. He cares so much about his students and shows genuine passion and interest for the subject he's teaching. Be wary of the TA because he was an extremely harsh grader at times. However, if you participate and keep up with the material you should be fine in the end.
if you speak persian this class is easy, if you dont it is hard but manageable. absolutely love him!! not too much homework and a flexible grader, super kind

He is such a sweetheart! He made sure his class was a comfortable space for everyone. I loved coming to class everyday. His lectures are fun and engaging. Farsi was so easy to learn with him because he adds fun activities to make you more interested. He doesnt fault you if you have absolutely no experience in the language.

Extremely nice professor. Lectures are some of the most interesting and well taught Ive had at Cornell. TA was a very harsh grader, but extra credit makes it so that you do better than you thought in the end.
Iago is superb! One of the nicest, kindest, most caring instructors at Cornell. You will not regret taking his class.

Iago was by far the best professor I had at Cornell. He is kind, understanding, and truly wants his students to enjoy his class and learn a ton. I took three classes with him and loved every single one. Would recommend 100% to anyone even vaguely interested in the language - his classes will inspire you to keep learning!!
By far one of the best professors I've had at Cornell. I've taken three classes with him and he teaches them all incredibly well. My Farsi has greatly improved thanks to him. Can't recommend enough

Great teacher! Amazing lecturer, teaches fast though, so you have to keep up and do your homework every day. If you do that, you'll learn farsi very quickly! He is always willing to help as well, whether it be outside of class, or in the middle of class!

Best professor I've had at Cornell. Not only is he extremely willing to help whenever you need, he's so knowledgable and interesting. If you put in the work, you will learn Persian very well, in just one semester.

Definitely one of the best professors I have ever had. Classes are interesting, thought provoking, and well-conceptualized. His class inspired me to learn Persian.  Take his classes if you get a chance--by far the best decision I made this semester!
One of the best teachers at Cornell.  Exceptionally kind, passionate about NES and has lived all over the middle east.  Take the time to ask him about his life, he has an amazing background.

Unbelievably gifted professor.  Not only is his class easy, but also effective.  I feel quite confident in my Persian abilities after only one year of studying with him.  On top of that, he's nice, smart, engaging, and willing to help.  Basically everything one could possibly want in a professor.

His are the only lectures which have never bored me out of any class I've ever taken. His energy, clarity, and knowledge make the material very interesting and I managed to learn a lot. In his own words the texts are unnecessary and I did almost no reading, but the course is extremely easy. Trivial A+ and absolutely worth it for the enjoyment.

I took this course in fall and loved it. It was never boring. I liked that material was planed the way that it wasn't overwhelming but I learned a lot. Professor is knowledgeable about the topic and teahcing. He is very donw to earth, approachable and helpful. Awsome course.I recommend it.

I took this course in fall and loved it. It was never boring. I liked that material was planed the way that it wasn't overwhelming but I learned a lot. Professor is knowledgeable about the topic and teahcing. He is very donw to earth, approachable and helpful. Awsome course.I recommend it.

i took the course for distribution requirements and loved the course. it became one of my favorites at cornell. lectures were interesting and involving. because it was about one specific country it wasn't overwhelming, but because professor put everything in broader context you learn about the region and world history. highly recommend.
incredibly knowledgeable and helpful.  cares about his students and wants you to learn. i loved his lectures. overall a very nice person person.
He's very knowledgeable, not only about the material, but also about how to teach. He makes the class fun and knows how to involve students. He's also a very nice and cool person. Highly recommended.

great course. phenomenal professor,  extremely knowledgeable and great at explaining material. very passionate about his field, enthusiastic and helpful,  approachable.lectures were great-helpful slides and videos, interacrtiveness.probably most interetsing lectures i've attended.  make sure to ask for help if you need-you'll get.

one of my favorite courses at cornell. wasn't overwhelming and learned a ton.Professor is approachable, gives extra office hrs if you ask. it helps to speak up in class. we had a quiz,  2  take-home exams with essay questions, a paper.   The lecture slides and videos were fun+ very helpful for exams. i looked forward to every class. take it!
great course

History of iran course, very interesting material. Kinda boring powerpoints, almost no work required. Just a couple quizzes, 2 tests, 1 paper, and an easy final test before exam week. Honestly, if you don't get an A, it's your fault. The tests involve no essay writing, just fact memorization, it was like I was back in high school. Take this class!

The professor is smart and excellent in his field. However, the teaching is hard, and office hours, or even after class inquires, are almost impossible. The professor is always busy with things and doesn't even have a minute to answer students' questions. Exam questions are vague, and there are dozens of formulas you have to memorize, all tough
The two reviews on Jan 20 are very likely his own ratings, given the name-calling "Dyson kids" and the clarifications. Decided to drop as the office hour policy discourages us from seeking help.
A great professor that is very engaging. Lectures are very interesting, so interesting that you want to go to class.

He's obviously a brilliant guy, but he needs to do a better job of making sure everyone in the class understands what he's talking about. He's not great at going over the basics, and the pre-reqs for the class underestimate the course content. If you're working on an S&T/Fixed Income desk, this is the class for you. If not, you're out of luck.

Pretty straightforward with his class, and he aims to help you understand the content if you have questions. However, his office hours can sometimes be inconvenient, so it can be hard to reach out to him. He doesn't really publish anything on canvas, and his lecture notes are pretty disorganized. It can start to get confusing if you skip lectures.

He is terrible at breaking things down and he expects you to understand the content well. You cannot stay to work through a problem set in his office hours because "it's not his job to guide you through it" but rather answer very specific questions. The assignments and exams were very vague as he is more focused on his research and academic drama.

While this professor's German accent can be a bit strong at times, Professor Stoye is clearly passionate about teaching, and this becomes especiallg evident as we learn more material applicable to the frontier of research. What I appreciated the most is his continual presentation of current/past papers that would tie course material very well.

reviews.comment: Professor Stoye really cares about teaching. His lectures and notes are enough for exams if you study and understand them thoroughly. He inspired my interests in Econometrics. Too bad he is not teaching undergraduate courses anymore :(

Econometrics is not an easy class, but Stoye is definitely one of those professors that cares about teaching his students. To do well in the class, you have to read the book carefully - a task which is made a lot easier by the fact that Stoye is a very meticulous lecturer. Exams can be tricky, but they are fair since they are based on the material.

Professor Stoye will not be teaching undergrads post-Spring 2014 for a few years. He is extremely enthusiastic about econometrics and lectures relatively clearly. Very willing to answer questions. Exams can have trick questions but are fair if you have read the textbook and attended lecture. Emphasizes conceptual understanding.

Clear lectures. Could be a little hard, but becomes much easier if you come with no pre conceived notions. He does a good job in presenting material in a concise useful way. Exams not the easiest, but not hard to score in if you study a reasonable amount.

Econ 3200 is tough no matter who you take it with.  Stoye is knowledgeable.  I only wish that tests better reflected homeworks and that homeworks better reflected the textbook. Clear speaker, clear presentation (as clear as it's gonna get) and good in office hours.

Class is nuts hard, Stoye lectures ad nauseum about incomprehensible theoretical concepts at the expense of both teaching the material and preparing you for his capricious tests. They guy does have great fashion sense though

Honestly, Jiachen Wang is like the ultimate professor, yo! I'm telling you, this guy is on a whole 'nother level! Not only does he know his stuff, but he's got this magical way of teaching that just sucks you in.

Jiachen Wang is seriously the best professor ever! His class is like a literary dream come true. He knows how to bring out the best in you as a writer, just like the masterpieces of Hemingway, Carver, Lu Xun, Munro, and Kafka. Taking his class is an absolute joy and I feel blessed to have him as my professor.

Jiachen Wang is hands down the best professor I've ever had. Their teaching style is like a literary dream come true, perfectly blending the wit of Hemingway, the raw emotions of Carver, the social criticism of Lu Xun, the nuanced storytelling of Munro, and the mind-bending narratives of Kafka.

Dude, let me tell you, Jiachen Wang is legit the GOAT of professors! Taking his class feels like diving into a literary paradise, with a mix of Hemingway's concise storytelling, Carver's raw emotions, Lu Xun's deep social commentary, Munro's captivating narratives, and Kafka's mind-bending twists.

Jiachen Wang is hands down the best professor I've ever had! His class is like a perfect mix of Hemingway's concise storytelling, Carver's raw emotion, Lu Xun's social critique, Munro's intricate character development, and Kafka's surreal vibes. I absolutely love and enjoy every moment in his class, and he truly deserves the title of the GOAT!
Okay, so let me just say, Professor Jiachen Wang is legit the ultimate GOAT of professors! His class is my absolute fave because he really knows how to make the material come alive.

He's a good lecturer. The material was actually so hard and abstract that I kept falling behind in lecture. Definitely read the textbook (it's extremely boring) before. Prelim2 and the final were outrageously more difficult than the practice. I dropped my math major after this. My review isn't representative of the whole class's experience, though.

Solid lecturer, if sometimes a little disorganized. Very kind and willing to answer questions. I strongly recommend that you ALWAYS read the textbook before lecture, and at least write down the key definitions/theorems/equations. The grading is pretty tough, but I got a lot out of the class.

Some of the best lectures I've had in the math department; the lectures are clear, and cover a lot of content. The examinations for the class are challenging, but fair. Homework assignments will take a long time, but they are rewarding once you understand the concepts, and will help on exams. Lastly, Moore is very helpful in office hours.
great, attentive professor. explains concepts well. very organized. a lot of homework, but not overwhelming. material is tough, but he teaches it well.
A solid professor- taught the material clearly and the homeworks were all do-able.

reviews.comment: Go to his office hour, especially before exams - it helps A LOT ( he holds many office hours before tests). He's really nice and helpful and the way he explains the concepts makes them easer to understand than the textbook. Tests can be tricky but if you do put effort to go through all the recitation and workshop materials you should be fine.

reviews.comment: He cares about what he teaches. Tries to make sure that students fully understand how to solve the example problems that he does on the lectures. Tests can be hard sometimes but the curve is always reasonable so it doesn't (most of the time) hurt the students.

He's an all around great professor. He shows that he actually wants to be teaching even if the class is an intro class. Sometimes his lectures aren't the easiest, but he is more than willing to explain concepts to you one-on-one if you just ask.
Sometimes lectures are difficult to understand, but he seems to want to help.

Problem sets were often needlessly difficult. He also has a habit of lecturing on things he likes that are kind of related to multi but not tested on the final. He definitely knows the material and can explain how to do problems well, but that's when he chooses to stay on topic. My recommendation is to just do problems from the book and ignore pset
Difficult course. A lot of blackboard notetaking, but helpful.
Taught directly from the textbook. The textbook was not very good. Presented the material in a way that was way more technical than it should have been. Would not recommend.

Professor DeVault is one of my favorite professors in ILR. She is extremely knowledgeable and cares a lot about your learning. The readings were worth it and she always has her door open to students if you ever want to discuss essays, ideas or topics covered in class. Attend lecture for good grades!

Devault was the most biased Prof I had at Cornell. Teaches 'historical facts' but implies clear political ideology. Grading scheme (letter grade averaged out at the end based on the lowest range of that letter) doesn't make sense. Lectures dull, didn't encourage diverse discussion. Decently easy class though.

No clear grading criteria. Essay grade ranges were insane and many students had conflicting thoughts. Slides have pictures not actual content. Of you don't go to lecture, you're done for. We also had a final which is unnecessary. Also, did I mention the class was electronic free?  If I had to do it again, I probably wouldn't take it with her.

plz avoid this class its so unclear

She assigns 100-250 pages of reading per week with weekly quizzes in discussion. Slides are pictures with a title and she just speaks about it. Attendance not mandatory but she tracks engagement and office hour attendance, and slides not helpful. Harsh grader on essays and final. OH not rlly helpful she laughs at questions (me and others)

reviews.comment: Professor Devault is very passionate about labor history and it shows. She assigns a TON of reading, but you should just skim.
