reviews.comment: DeVault clearly cares about the subject and the class. Go to office hours for help on the essays and you will do well.

Professor DeVault is clearly passionate about her subject matter. However, her class had excess work as well as a final exam that other labor history classes did not have. She graded harshly and the clear expectations were not laid out prior to paper assignments.

reviews.comment: Interesting professor who presents interesting material, but lectures had the tendency to be very dry. Weekly reading quizzes during discussion section, not so bad.

reviews.comment: DeVault is one of the nicest people I have ever met. She genuinely cares about her students. I had a class during her office hours, so she regularly scheduled other times to meet. I struggled a lot with the first essay assignment, but DeVault helped me and taught me what I did wrong. Her lectures can be dry, but the information is interesting.

Awesome professor, super passionate and nice.  Lots of weekly reading with reading quizzes in discussion, but you can definitely "skim" main concepts and do extremely well. Two papers, go to TA office hours and you will do well on them. Extremely fair final. Some find the subject boring overall but DeVault makes it as painless as possible.
Excellent professor! Clear and learned a lot, definitely not an easy grader but she is very helpful and sweet and a fair grader. Love her!
Nice and helpful.

Not a bad course..very dry though. make sure you suck up in section to your TA and dont worry about the weekly quizzes too much. most imporant thing about this class would be to meet with both the TA and DeVault before both of the papers to talk about your thesis and make sure youre on the right track... they will tell you what to write basically

Unfree Labor: Slaves, Servants, Wives.  Great Teacher, learned alot, ALOT of reading, one book per week, sometimes half a book, seminar style, classes tend to be very large.  Attendance is not required but necessary for class participation points.  She really knows her stuff and goes a long way to ensure your understanding.

Comparative History of Women at Work.  Best seminar class I've ever been in, attendance is not mandatory, but necessary to get class participation points.  Reading is tough, one book per week+short paper, but well worth the effort, learned alot, seminar style allowed for greater understanding of others opinions on women's issues

Intro to Labor History, lots of reading, but if you keep  up your set, class participation counts for alot, you'll definitely learn something.  I liked her so much, I've taken 2 more of her classes. (IC636 and CB388)

DeVault is very passionate about labor history and is a good lecturer; she gave us weekly ‘reading quizzes’ which were annoying but I guess it made us read the many books we were assigned...  A pretty interesting class if you’re into the subject. 2 papers, final exam was 2 essay questions; DeVault is a tough grader but a good teacher overall.

Wonderful teacher.  She is very interested in the subject and conveys it.  She is also very helpful, friendly, and pleasant to talk to if you see her in office hours.  Probably my favorite teacher this semester.

Excellent professor. I have heard that other CB100 profs are more dynamic lecturers, but I never had a problem staying engaged or awake in her class. She's definitely a professional, and I respect her tremendously. She has very high standards for your work, but that definitely motivates you to do well.
Boring and dry, but very clear and organized.  Go to lecture and get the gist of the readings, and you'll be fine.  Was also very understanding and accommodating when I had a conflict.

I have taken three classes with her,and I would take more if they were offered! Show up to class and you're set. Being interested in history helps a lot, but overall she is extremely nice and cares about how you do.

Good lectures, make the material as interesting as it can be. Ton of reading, nobody expects you to do it all though. For papers, make sure you hav a good thesis and you will do fine. She is very interested in women's issues, clearly. Overall, great prof.

An excellent professor and lecturer.  She made a very dry topic into something interesting. She assigns a lot of reading, however she doesn't intend for you to do it all, but rather gather general concepts.  Overall it was a pretty easy course if you went to lectures.
Incredibly boring.  Her many random examples are irrelevant and a waste of time.  She also refuses to change a grade no matter how unfair it may be.

One of the best professors you will have.  Lectures were clear, easy to follow and interesting.  Take good notes in lecture and you're guarenteed good grades.  Papers are a decent amount of work but very fairly graded.  The best prof. for the class by far.

Great professor- very clear and helpful. There is a lot of reading which is useful when it comes to doing papers. Papers can be tough...it helps to run your ideas by her first. Very nice and approachable and her lectures are very clear. No complaints here!
very clear and informative lectures, requires work (esp for the reading) but you'll learn a lot about US labor history

My favorite prof so far. I wasn't expecting labor history to be fun, but it's the only class I'm never inclined to skip. She's a really nice lady, very knowledgable, makes the class interesting w/o compromising depth or clarity of material. Papers aren't bad; reading can be a bit much, but doable.
Ileen is a goddess
Excellent professor; Papers require work, but if you try you can do well; Very clear lectures

This is a very interesting course on immigration. Devault does a great job at putting the history of immigration into context with work related stuff.  She is a very nice person who is very honest and fair.
very nice and helpful if you ask.  papers aren't that bad.  very good lectures and decent amount of reading for a cb class.
Tons of respect for this professor. DeVault is organized, clear, and strives to be as accessible to her students as time allows. No complaints!
very knowledgeable, great lectures. Papers requre some work though.
No Comments

Made the midterm extraordinarily and unnecesarilly long and difficult. Completely unfair exam, and strolled into lecture the very next day and bragged about the exam being so difficult. Professor took it like a joke. Zero accountability.

A lot of people left bad reviews after the prelim, but it was sorted out in grading, so I'm giving a 5 to offset the non updated low ratings. Realistically, he was a 4, but you shouldn't fear Prof Sridharan in higher level classes; he just expected more than some students could deliver. If he ever teachers 1110 or smt tho…good luck.

Karthik isn't the best professor for intro to ML especially if you have no prior knowledge of machine learning nor good at linear algebra. I thought I was failing the class, but Karthik put lots of effort into adjusting grading scheme and also creating extra credit opportunities towards the end of the semester to make up for the horrible midterm.

Incredibly boring lectures; highly disorganized class structure with a lot changing on the fly; final grading scheme heavily benefited those who performed better on the heinous midterm compared to the final despite them trying to adjust the scheme mid semester to mitigate this. The content is cool but please take 3780 with anyone else.
I lowkey thought I failed the midterm but bro saved my grade with the lenient grading.

I also thought the midterm was super hard, but it seems obvious based on edstem that he will make the grading account for the difficulty of the test. Recent reviews are overplaying how much this test will hurt them (bc it will surely be curved), and he is definitely a genuinely kind professor even if a bit boring at times.
don't, just don't.
Never take his class please.
Worst professor at cornell
Prelim is insanely hard, lectures are insanely boring.
DONT EVER TAKE HIS CLASS UNLESS YOU ARE A GENIUS AND ALREADY KNOWS EVERYTHING

WORST PROFESSOR EVER! His exams are unreasonably hard and nothing like the exams from previous year. I only did like half of the problems on the exam and cannot even get to the last ones. His lectures are AWFUL. So boring and I cannot follow at all.
the prelim is nothing like the previous prelims. much harder and weir wording, uses concepts not included in previous classes. AVOID!!!

Even though I can understand his accent I still dont follow in the lectures. Had to go to youtube and watch Killian's lecture instead. The other instructor (a grad student?) is so much better in terms of lecturing.

This class is not for the faint of heart. Plan to go to office hours for the majority if not all of the assignments. With that being said, Karthik is a good lecturer and the class is a thorough introduction to learning theory. The class was also curved, but I am not sure by how much.

He was absolutely amazing in cs 4780 this semester! Hands down the best professor I've ever gotten at Cornell. He breathes new life into the content. We looked forward to his lectures every other week because we have never been that locked in to demolish ML. I worship his teaching style, must take class, especially with him.

Karthik was a kind sub professor for CS 4780 but the way he teaches was dull and boring. He tried to explain concepts but they weren't intuitive. I just started watching videos online to understand concepts. One thing I can say though is eager to help students but you would have to wait after class. Any case, I just started to watch videos online.

Karthik was a sub professor for CS 4780 and OHH GRACIOUS GOD, HE was so dull. I expected Killian to teach but to my surprise, Karthik taught most of the time.  He is a nice guy but the way he teaches is so confusing and dull. He attempts to explain concepts but the examples are not intuitive. I started skipping unless Killian taught the class

The Mathematical Foundations of Machine Learning course CS4783/CS5783 was very difficult but he explained the concepts fairly well. After prelims, gave me good feedback on my projected grade (B+) and suggested that I work on the project to improve it. Finally gave me an A grade. Get ready to work very hard but it would be worth it if motivated.

reviews.comment: A good teacher
It looks like he spends little effort in preparing the lectures. He was not able to explain the course material clearly.

CS 4786 is a rather theoretical class that requires you to be somewhat self-driven. The course will not spoon-feed you material. You need to be able to do some independent reading / review. However, most importantly, Karthik is always patient and will help you understand the material if you visit him during office hours.

Subjective grading - deductions handed out whimsically in write-ups and given far more weight than the correctness of the technical work. Also, if the majority of students do well, then the professor will arbitrarily deflate all scores such that your final grade can end up being seriously hurt even if you do consistent A work throughout the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: The professor is a good guy. The problem is that he doesn't structure his class too well. He has zero exams. While this sounds great and all, this results in a lot of groups cheating on assignments and projects. Take this class only if you have a solid group, otherwise you risk getting crushed by the curve.

I strongly disliked this professor and this class. Up until the last 2.5 weeks of class things were not that bad. Lectures were dry (most people did not show up), professor often made mistakes in lecture, and he was unclear. Fortunately, hw was easy up until this point. Then in the last 2 weeks everything went to hell and things became impossible.
The worst Professor I've ever had in my life. AVOID.
Homework is utterly irrelevant the the lectures. Lectures are dry.

This was by far the worst class I have taken at Cornell. Karthik is a very nice guy but my god are his lectures dull. 75% of the class doesn't show to lecture and the ones that do are put to sleep by his droning. Assignments are more or less not correlated with the material taught, and the TAs are the least caring bunch I've ever seen. What a shame
just don't.

reviews.comment: Definitely don't take if a STEM major

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS. She was a nice lady but oh my god is her grading criteria absolute bull. I had to withdraw from the course because she was not clear about what my final grade would be. Too much work for a 3 credit course. Save yourself the energy and do not take her class as an FWS.

reviews.comment: This class was difficult. I learned a lot from it, but the workload was unreasonable compared to other FWS classes. However, Professor King-O'Brien is very nice and cares a lot about her work, but it was difficult to balance this class' workload with my four other classes.
DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS!!!!!!!!!!

reviews.comment: Do not take her class!! Absurd workload
Her teaching style is rather counterproductive to the learning of students so I would not recommend at all.

Prof. K is a sweet person at heart and wants her students to learn something. But the workload is just tooo much. She expects us to whip up two research papers (with more than 20 sources) and a revision of every paper written by the end of the sem. Which, compared to other FWSs out there, is just absurd for a 3 credit course. No A+ btw. Pray for A.

reviews.comment:
100s of pages a week plus need to annotate another three sources weekly. All this reading and annotation ends up being only 7% of the grade

There is no point taking this when you could get an easy A in another FWS

reviews.comment: Professor Kelly's negative reviews are understandable, but do not easily write her off as the worst professor at Cornell. If you put in your best, she recognizes and rewards dedication and hard work. This class TREMENDOUSLY helped improve my writing skills but this course will not be for everyone. Professor Kelly set me up for success at Cornell.

reviews.comment: A-lot of work!

reviews.comment: Would not take her class again, please be aware of her ridiculous workload.

She wasn't THAT bad lol. You do A LOT of reading for classes and for papers she makes everyone write multiple drafts. I never had troubles with her grading so the class for me was just an FWS with a lot of work, but a lot of my classmates understandably hated the class. If you're not really into US history, there are easier fWS's and chiller profs

reviews.comment: Terrible professor. NEVER take her class. Grading is unreasonable and work load is ridiculous. Had a horrible time in her class. I should have dropped while I had the chance.

Terribly boring lectures and strange discussion based class. Weekly writing assignments amounted to well above 5,000 words per week. Several longer essays were 15+ pages. Tough grader and has unrealistic expectations in terms of the time assignments should take. Definitely do not take if you're a stem major. Even it you're not, wouldn't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: This course is not difficult conceptually. But it becomes the worst class I have ever taken at Cornell because of her. She is such a tough grader and never says things clear about her criteria. She also demands a lot from her students without doing much on her own.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I dont know why this class would exist. There are so much extra works, and they are not helpful at all. I don't think my writing qualities improved through her class. Instead, I was so stressed, and I wished I could drop this class earlier. I think my college life would be much better without this class.

She is the worst professor Ive ever met at Cornell. Her assignments are heavy and tedious. Even the essay rubrics do not make any sense. There are so many extra weekly individual meetings - so intense and time-consuming. As a student who suffered in her class, I suggest you guys not take her class. Good luck!

The worst professor ever. NEVER EVER WANNA TAKE HER CLASS AGAIN!!! Her assignments do not make sense at all and are so fk time consuming. I did not learn anything from this class. Just don't take her class then you will have a wonderful college experience!

King-O'Brien was an incredible professor, you will learn SO much with her. Yes, this course was insanely difficult, so only take it if you're up for the challenge, but she will give you the grade you deserve based on the work you put in. She's also such a fun teacher when you have a good group of students. Be ready to participate!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Every class has a quiz regarding the reading previously assigned. Each reading is between 60-150 pages between a 2 day period. Multiple papers are due throughout the semester including one up to 15 pages. She is not easily accessible outside of class and difficult to reach by email. She'll make you work to pass and does not let you miss class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Taking this class was the worst decision I made last semester. Very vague with the feedback, not likable, and all around a tough grader. Every paper will be at least five pages ( one was over ten) and the take home essay required us to write eight pages in 24 hours in response to a prompt she posts online. Way too hard for an FWS. Do not take!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Easily the best professor I've had at Cornell.  You definitely have to work hard to get anything out of her class but it is so worth it in the long run.  She is incredibly helpful in one-on-one meetings.
I was excited to take this class. But this prof. is horrible. Major chip on her shoulder - i always felt like she was mad at me when I asked her anything.

She is probably one of the worst teacher's I've had at Cornell. While her assignments make no sense, she grades harshly and would rather fail you than help. You can tell that she doesn't care about students; she treats every student as if they've wronged her in some way. I highly recommend against a class with her.

If you love literature DO NOT take this class. This teacher really knows how to dampen interest and enthusiasm. Loves to be authoritarian. This teacher will treat you like a middle schooler, so if you want to be treated like an adult her class is not for you. She is intentionally intimidating. Does NOT create a comfortable atmosphere in her class

I learned a lot from this course. It's two semesters of biochemistry in one and self-taught, so it's naturally very fast paced and comprehensive. At times, the amount of material can be daunting. Kevin is very responsive to emails and was always cordial to me. Resources are plentiful and help is easily accessible in this course. Exams were fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This course is 2 semesters of biochemistry in 1, so of course it is a lot for 1 semester. I learned a lot from this course. At times it felt daunting and overwhelming, but pushing through was worth it. Kevin is very responsive to emails and shares useful review videos. This is an autodidactic course, but resources are plentiful. I felt supported.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I liked the course, hated the professor.  Professor does not care about students and is not involved.  You primarily work with the TAs (who are great) but he will NOT be accommodating and there is way too much work for one semester
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Auto biochem is very time consuming, but totally doable if you're willing to show up to the study center and engage with TAs. Quizzes aren't bad, prelims are hard. If you're premed TAKE THIS CLASS. It prepared me so well for the MCAT, both in terms of content and building independent study habits.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Obviously a weed-out course.. fast-paced, jam-packed, but it is NOT an unfair one. Professor is really kind if you meet with him in the study center

Kevin was fine as an instructor. The course itself was awful, super boring, and a ridiculous amount of work to expect people to do in one semester. All memorization, no actual thinking whatsoever, just cram hundreds of terms and figures into you head each week. Worst class I've ever taken at Cornell; as a non-premed, made me regret majoring in bio.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Kevin is the GOAT. Responds to emails within minutes, is super patient, and never makes you feel dumb. There are weekly pass/fail quizzes, but he mainly just wants to save the procrastinators a mountain of trouble later on with these. Prelims are fair, proportional to the amount of effort you put in.

Best option for biochem for pre-meds, esp since it is one semester. 13 unit quizzes (pass/fail, gives slip days) and 3 prelims, so its definitely a heavy workload but worth it in the end if you put in effort :) Prof is so kind and accessible outside of the study center!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: What a bad person. Will go out of his way to make sure student's lives are harder than they need to be. Everything is at his discretion, and he decides to impose all these arbitrary rules that no admin cares about just to make our lives difficult. I also get the sense that he is immensely sad outside of lecture. No need to make us miserable too!

This is an auto-tutorial class...the course is extremely fast-paced and the material is super difficult. You have to do 13 Unit quizzes during the semester, and prelims on top of that. But the prof is super good at explaining concepts and I wish I saw him in the learning center more often!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: BEST BIO CLASS @ CORNELL
Extremely fair exams, always happy to answer any questions, love the course so much!!
Roberts is a really kind and caring professor. He is very approachable, but his lectures can be daunting and a little unorganized at times. He is a very seasoned prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Great professor who is so incredibly knowledgeable about Latin American political economy. His focus on democracy is also fascinating and very applicable to the current political climate. Best part of lectures are his insane anecdotes — he's experienced everything! Totally take the class

If you've taken 1313, it's pretty much just like that format and difficulty-wise. Very chill hands-off prof. Grading isn't harsh, grades on a variety of mediums (like tests,papers,etc). Lectures just repeat whats on the readings so you can skip, but his lecture style is honestly super engaging and I love his anecdotes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: Roberts is no doubt one of my favorite GOVT professors at Cornell! He always made time for students in and out of class, added some of his crazy stories to the lectures, and was very enthusiastic to teach students about Latin America. The class is very well organized and very interesting, all thanks to Roberts!

Prof is super great and chill. Very knowledgable in his field, especially on latam politics. Class isn't hard overall; 2 short quizzes, 2 papers 3 pages each, 1 short final. Concepts aren't hard to understand and relatively basic. Readings may be a lot, but you can just skim to get the main points. It truly does feel like an intro-level class.

Roberts is awesome. Sometimes he'll be describing a coup or rebellion and be like "yeah I was down there talking with the president when it happened." The book was actually really interesting. Posts all lecture slides online. The weekly 1-pagers are an easy grade anchor, research paper and final are not bad if you use notes and put in effort

professor roberts is by and above one of my favorite professors at cornell. incredibly insightful and experiencedexpect some wild anecdotes. also, make a point to go to his office hours. he has a wealth of knowledge that he's willing to share, and is amazing for book recommendations or if you just want to chat. couldn't recommend him enough!

While I agree that Roberts did a good job of explaining concepts, I think his lectures were incredibly boring. He basically repeated what was on the slides (which, as I said, were very good), and I found it hard to stay focused. There was also way too much reading for a 3-credit course. That being said, the TAs were pretty good, and I learned alot.
He is very helpful and approachable. He knows a lot about Latin America, and he succeeded at making his lectures interesting and relatively easy to get through - not boring.
The lectures were pretty interesting if you are naive to the subject; His personal experiences really aid the context of the class.
Great Professor.  Really knows his stuff on Latin America, and facilitates nice discussion.
Awesome prof. Lectures are interesting and very clear. Readings arent bad. He does a really good job of putting the readings into context and explaining diffcult concepts clearly.
No Comments
No Comments
My favorite professor. So kind and passionate. SUCH a fun class, best class I have taken at Cornell.
Lovely professor

This is a tough class to teach--it's hard to lecture the entirety of two years of ECE studies. Because of this, lectures feel optional--but they are interesting, and generally worth going to. There's a lot of lab work. No task alone is horrible, but combined, I spent a ridiculous amount of time in lab--still, Petersen deserves a lot of respect.

Roebuck is a great professor - clearly loves Japanese history and wants you to be engaged in the content. Extremely reading-heavy class (1-200 pages/week, which is a lot for non-humanities majors), but assignments are 100% writing and graded generously. Focuses on broad historical developments and connections instead of memorization, which I liked.

Absolutely amazing professor and person in general! Super funny and although lectures can be a bit boring sometimes, only sometimes, she has tons of amazing knowledge and really knows her stuff. Reading is a lot, between 100-200 pages a week. Def lots of memorizing but that's normal for history. Great fashion and person in general.

Great prof overall and excellent at running seminar. Super caring and chill overall. Readings are a bit dense but not as bad as other history seminars. Professor isn't a harsh grader, but gives minimal feedback and isn't the clearest on expectations. Not really a Marxist tho, just a traditional critical theorist (yes, there is a difference).

Incredible, engaging, and charming lecturer. She likes to use visuals to draw you into the historical context. Readings are dense, and you memorize lots of facts to do well on the exams. No extra credit. 
Also, the historical narrative she offers is conspicuously feminist and Marxist (but not communist).

Professor Roebuck is an incredibly engaging lecturer. She is very clearly an expert on the subjects that she teaches, and responds to tangential student questions with evidenced, precise knowledge. She is very nice to students and very friendly during office hours. The course grade is one prelim, one final, and discussion participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great and consistently interesting lecturer. Get ready to take a lot of notes because the way she makes slides but honestly she's really good at lecturing so if you're not taking notes on them you are wasting your time
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you go to the discussions, participate, and do the readings, you will be fine. Prof. Roebuck is amazing and is always helpful when you need help. The lectures are always engaging and she always stays after class to answer questions despite how late it is. Also gave a lot of grading accommodations that made the students' lives a lot easier
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: DO NOT take this class. I am a hard working, respectful student who showed up to each class prepared to work hard. While she may understand Japanese History, she has no understanding of how to teach, be compassionate, and return the respect to her students. Rudest Cornell Professor. Never have I been more disappointed and offended.

so the TAs for the class were kind of rough (really pretentious grad students) but prof roebuck is amazing. she's such a good lecturer and the course material is really good. would highly recommend taking her class.

My favorite course I took freshman year was her "World of Modern Japan" course. Her lectures flow perfectly, and she makes information very accessible (even to people like me who had never studied East Asia before). Readings and section participation are ESSENTIAL, but every reading is helpful to understanding (no extra material). Would take again.
very knowledgeable; expects a lot out of you; makes you work for it
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lecture is really boring, but you should go because there's 5 pop quizzes that are SUPER easy. Tests are easy because they follow the study guide. Easy A+.
Class course for ILR/Gov students. 40% midterm 60% final so very high stakes. Didn't pay attention at all in class but still did well because of the study guides.

Great professor who is very knowledgeable of the topic. Reading intensive but he summarizes everything during lecture. Test heavy, graded on only 2 tests but he provides study guide and reviews beforehand. Extra credit 5 times through semester in class. Is unintentionally funny, and overall very kind. Lessons can be kind of boring sometimes tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Super boring lectures but the entire class is graded by two exams that he gives you review sheets for and spends a class before the examing going over. Going to class is helpful, and he gives extra credit quizzes a few times throughout the semester, but it's really not necessary. A median.
All you need to do is write down all of his reading summaries and you'll be fine. Only two lectures you need to show up for are the 2 review sessions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The Prof is very nice and knowledgeable and the subject matter is very interesting but can get a little repetitive (unions!). The class itself is an easy A without even having to go to lecture, as the prof gives detailed study guides and attendance is merely a bonus. Overall great class.

Turner is a super nice professor whose class carries the typical workload for a Cornell gov class. The readings are not too bad and if you show up and take notes youll be fine. Class grading is 40% midterm 60% final, so dont mess either of those up. He also gives pop quizzes which are for extra credit and can only boost your grade.

Class mostly consists of the professor lecturing and the students getting down notes without many lecture slides. However, he does give a detailed study guide that is everything you need to know for the test, so you really don't have to read as long as you prepare well for the test. Midterm is 40% and final is 60%. Solid class, not too difficult.

Taken online. This class has interesting material but the lectures are honestly very boring. The Prof knows his stuff but is pretty left-leaning. However, he doesn't ignore conservative viewpoints. The tests have short answer and can be tricky but overall are not too difficult. Don't remember doing any work besides tests.

Politics of the Global North SP2018. The class is super interesting and not hard at all. Turner is really nice. The reading for this class is a few chapters from a few books, and there are no essays only tests. He gives you a detailed study guide before each test. He's just retired too (except for teaching), so things are probably even more chill.

Professor Turner is clearly an expert in his field, and integrates a lot of insights and examples into his lectures. The exams are very fair, and readings are engaging and relevant to what we learned in class. Would definitely recommend taking his class before you graduate!

Sweet guy. Bad lecturer & professor. Says he wants to give everyone a good grade but the tests are nit-picky & graded unfairly (I got a 90 but was counted as a B+ because everyone else did well; not afraid to curves down). He gives the cumulative grades by just looking at your 3 grades and sees if there's improvement. No calculation involved
Do not take this course. The professor just read the materials. Disorganized. Destroy your GPA even if you spend a lot of time preparing prelims

Professor Lowell Turner is an excellent professor who is an expert in his field and an even better teacher. You will learn a lot taking this course and will enjoy doing so. One of the best courses I've taken at Cornell.
Lowell is a legendary professor and brings a huge depth of real world experience to his classes. Inspiring and vital.

Professor Turner is an excellent lecturer since he integrates class material with current news and he is also able to propose viable solutions to current socio-economic issues. I believe that the class should be a requirement for all Cornellians since it presents an issue that has now become a major concern for developed societies (aka inequality).
Awesome class

Do not take this class. Turner presents no information other than what you already know from the readings. I am inclined to agree with his views, but he provides no evidence to support them. If you value your time and are interested in learning, avoid any of turners Classes. On the other hand, his research is great!

One of the best classes I took at Cornell. Prof. Turner is a great teacher, relates well to his students, and keeps the class material interesting and relevant to current affairs and global politics. He has real world experience as a labor activist plus he has some of the best TAs at ILR. Highly recommended!
Great professor interesting course and incredibly helpful when approached.  Definitely has his own opinions on the subject, but so does every other decent political economy professor.
Great professor! One of the best classes I took at Cornell!

Barely payed attention in class but learned so much doing the readings to prepare for the prelim/final. It was one of the best classes I have ever taken because the course material is so relevant to what is going on in current politics. But I have to say that his lectures were not hugely helpful. The class is simply too large for this kind of study

Terrible and biased. All readings of relative complexity were ignored or dumbed down. This class was easier than some classes I have taken in high school. I was frustrated by his personal bias, especially that he chose to inject so much of it into lecture. I actually agreed with what his stance, but his paltry analysis of issues was frustrating.
Amazing professor, one of the best I have ever had at Cornell!! Great sense of humor and he really cares about his students.

Global North is a great class, but not one to take if you really want to be pushed or challenged. That having been said, I learned quite a bit about current events and conflicts - Turner does an excellent job of putting it all into context and injecting his own experience into lecture.  Absolutely take it, but don't expect to have your mind blown.

This prof. is awesome. He is by far my favorite professor. He got me so excited about politics of the Global North, which, to be honest, I wasn't that interested in before. He seems like he really knows what he's talking about too.

This professor is pretty much the most amazing professor I've ever had. He is enthusiastic, intelligent and is obviously very dedicated to teaching. His class was definitely not easy, but it was 100% worth it. I've probably learned more in this class than in 5 of my other classes combined. Take this class before you graduate!!!
Excellent professor. For summer session, it was two 3-page papers. The final was to answer one of  questions which we were given previously.

It's easy compared to any government class and you actually learn something about international institutions and the foundations of many modern conflicts. Prof is nice and responsive to student input. Not one of the most mind-blowing classes you'll ever take, but worth it.
Great Professor! Professor Turner is very helpful and also has a great deal of knowledge and experience in the international relations field.
This class is incredibly easy but his lectures are so boring because he doesn't really teach anything mind-blowing. Luckily, there was takenote :)

Lowell Turner is very easy-- yes, and it is evidence of what little work he actually puts into his teaching.  His lectures are ill-prepared and boring.  He relies on old material to teach and he uses stupidly simple concepts.  Excruciatingly boring class bc of what little I learned.  Steer away.
No Comments
Very easy A, crazy not to take this class in the summer with him.
No Comments
Best professor ever! Really wants to see students succeed. Very fair grader and interesting classes.  Up to date of current affairs.
Doesn't listen to students' needs at all, even tho she makes it seem like she will. Hard weekly quizzes based on lectures from weeks before. Boring lectures where she rambles about nothing.

Larissa Shepherd shows little concern for her students. The class is unnecessarily hard, and she's strict about attendance—even with a doctor's note. Lectures are dry and don't match the quizzes, which are given every single week. Overall, it feels disorganized and unfair.

Quizzes every week that do not prepare you for the final exam. Intense homework every week. Incredibly picky about attendance, and will become upset even if you have an excuse. Dry lectures. Avoid if you can!!

Boy oh boy where do I even begin my glorious 5'7 blue eyed king Killian Wineburger. It's not just the way you have the whole crowd laughing at your jokes that makes you the GOAT, Killian pookie, it's your utmost passion and love of the game that truly shines through. Your unparalleled talent makes you alone are the honored one of cornell CS

such a great guy, one of my absolute fav profs at cornell because he makes lectures so exciting not to mention he's drop dead hilarious. very in tune with explaining difficult concepts and reading the audience to know when students aren't following along. would recommend x100!

Fantastic professor. Taught a topic I knew very little about and left me knowledgeable and inspired. Also great at juggling, great jokes and knows how to keep a class entertained. Mandates that students don't take notes on their computers, which made life harder for me, but delivered handwritten and typed lecture notes.

A great professor with excellent juggling skills! I had no prior ML experience before this class, and Kilian explained so many tough concepts in ways that just made sense. He is a master at finding helpful analogies and has a great sense of humor. I would highly recommend this class if you are someone that wants to learn the foundations of ML.
the goat. if he's teaching something while you're enrolled, take it.
Good professor. Don't hesitate to take this class when it is Killian teaching.
Best professor I have had. Very informative and fun lectures. Lots of material posted online

You will not find a better ML professor. The man knows his stuff soooo well and is really good at explaining it to people who know nothing about it. He also juggled in class one time which was hilarious. I did not miss a single lecture this semester and it's so worth my time. I do not understand how anyone can rate him low.
really good
great professor of a great class

Funny and engaging professor. CS 4780 is definitely a little overhyped, but taking it with Weinberger made it pretty enjoyable. Definitely re-watch the 2017 lectures on youtube if you're confused. Programming assignments and mathematical psets kinda sucked, but workload still wasn't as bad as some other CS courses. Can't really ask for much more
Fantastic professor (one of the best here!), I have no clue why there are any bad ratings at all.
Incredibly engaging lecturer and explains the concepts so clearly! Best CS professor I've had at Cornell
Easy class filled with lots of regurgitation and little problem solving
Most enthusiastic professors I have ever seen in my life. Answers every question with patience and is very funny

Fantastic lecturer who's really passionate about the material. Despite the high number of students, he interacts with students as much as he can. He comes from the industry and since becoming a professor has built around the world a great academic reputation. Couldn't have asked for a better professor. Lots of projects and hard exams, be prepared.
Extraordinary lectures!

Best lectures i have ever heard in machine learning. The way he sets the intuition is simply out of this world. Thank you so much Dr. Weinberger to break these complex algorithms down and make them super easy to understand
This class was so tedious

Context: I've taken most of the Machine Learning classes Cornell has to offer, and this is the very best class Cornell has to offer on the subject. If you *ever* want to do machine learning for a tech company, or even your side project/hustle, then this is the class you should take. No idea why there are so many bad ratings for such a good class.
Take 4786 to get some real design experience instead of this waste of time.
I recommend a more rigorous ML class.
Kilian brushes over all the material we need to know for tests and for projects and spends excessive amounts of time on proofs that ultimately teach us nothing.
BAD CLASS! BAD PROF!
Praise the department for putting a different prof in charge of 4780 next year. This was an unbearable class.
Tests check how many equations you can memorize rather than a fundamental understanding of machine learning. Disorganized lectures. Tedious, buggy assignments. Useless HW assignments.
Great lecturer, fair tests, and makes the subject seem interesting.
Really bad class
Professor Weinberger was an entertainer first and a lecturer second. In the end, I forgot all the material the second the final exam ended.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Prof. Weinberger is an expert on the material and covers a broad field with sufficient depth. There are growing pains to having such a large class size due to the growing popularity of the topic but I learned a lot regardless. Well prepared lecture notes and entertaining, effective demos.
The worst part of the class is feeling intimidated by how hard Kilian says the course is when, in fact, it isn't.
ML with Prof. Kilian was the worst 4000 level CS class I have taken.

The best class I have taken at Cornell! An excellent class to develop a strong intuition of ML. Prof Weinberger is an outstanding lecturer; the best I have had in three years at Cornell. He really cares about students understanding the content and he asks students' feedback. More time on DL can make the class even better. Or a separate DL class!
Ugh this class was so boring.

One of my favorite courses in Cornell. Professor is very funny but teaches the material in a very clear and effective manner. Be prepared for a lot of work, but projects and homework helped with my understanding in ML. Exams are not hard as long as you spend time going through lecture notes. Definitely would love to take another class with Kilian!
Pretty awesome course

One of the best classes I have ever taken. The material is challenging but relevant and Kilian teaches in a way that is both comprehensive and captivating. I learned most of the content by reviewing the online lecture recordings (class moves pretty fast and I really benefitted from being able to pause/rewind videos). Come ready to work and learn!

He covers the core of ML with good intuition and the necessary math rigor. If you want to learn ML, this is a great starting point. As someone with previous ML exposure, I still learned useful ideas in areas I hadn't focused on much (e.g. boosting). Some reviews hype too much tho - very inaccessible prof & altho clear + funny, not very engaging.
This was a disastereous course where I learned more about overfitting than machine learning.

I had Professor Weinberger for CS 4780 and he is the best CS professor Ive had at Cornell. His lectures are funny and the material is interesting. The only downside is the course is really challenging. Its hard to keep up unless you do the extea credit as well

Just an amazing, terrific class. We were genuinely so excited to come to class every week knowing that we would be learning and laughing. It's a feat to take Machine Learning and make it digestible and exciting, but he has taken the time to develop clever and funny analogies and demos and we all really appreciated that! Very sad that it's over!

I thoroughly enjoyed the course and made it to almost all of his lectures. It was fun. Though i got scared with placement test, the math content turned out to be too easy. I should have worried about my programming instead ... a few of the projects were tough nut( Dual SVM, trees etc.) If you put in expected work, exams are straight forward btw.

I have been studying Machine Learning from last 3 years, still, I found his class really useful in getting clarity about the subject. He is one of the funniest people I have ever encountered. To sum up, this is one of the best class that I have ever attended.
The best course I have taken in Cornell. Though it is somehow too easy for me.

ML is truly as great as it is at Cornell due to the instruction of Prof. Kilian. He tries really hard to improve the class which is why it was offered at a later time and for so many students this semester. He always encourages feedback and is very organized. If you put time into the class and enjoy the material you'll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Definitely a tough class with lots of partner projects. I won't lie and say it was easy but Kilian did a great job with the material. I really enjoyed the energy he brought to his lectures. Make sure to brush up on your linear algebra, multivariable calc, and stats before you take this class!!
An extremely tedious class with long, rambling lectures.

A terrible professor who cares more about telling jokes than teaching content. If Kilian spent more time teaching than he did talking about how hard his exams were, maybe we would have learned something useful.

Amazing lecture! Prof. Weinberge is so hilarious, but he can explain every point clearly and he also spends a lot of time answering questions. Quite many projects, but if you enjoy transfering the knowledge that you learned into code, you will definitely love this course.
Kilian apparently knows his topics very well so he can talk about them like a champ. If he is not one of the best ML professors then who else?
good lecturer is he a truly good professor? :(
fantastic lecturer, with just the right mix of humor and brilliance. A must take class for any CS student!!!!

The class itself was difficult, but interesting.  There are a lot of assignments, but they have never been too long and are really fair.  What makes this class one of my favorites instead of least favorites though is definitely Kilian.  He is a great professor and an entertaining lecturer.  This is not an easy class, but it is a fun and fair one!
just so annoying and a grating voice in your ear at 9am. does the quiet coyote on us like we're kindergarteners and shushes us "ch-ch-ch" every second

the attendance is based off the amount of iclickers you do, not the amount of lectures you attend. there's only 2 iclickers a class and the first is always right as class begins so you cannot be late or you'll get a 50% on attendance. NOTE THAT the only lecture time is 9 am and in statler, when most of her students live on north.
being very strict in a basic level course.

Leah teaches college students like an elementary school teacher. She will wait till everyone stops talking, spends most of the lecture talking about inclusivity, and rushes through the overall material. Avoid her at all costs.

My first time sleeping in lecture after 20 minutes. She is not always organized and the quality of presentation is sometimes unprepared.
Be ready to self study or go to ask TAs.
Lectures were really disorganized, hard to follow, and unprepared. Exams were mostly easy enough to compensate. Homeworks took a lot of work and didn't really feel that beneficial for learning.

You can tell she's really trying her best, but her lectures are harder to follow and feel less content-dense compared to Professor Eichhorn. Went on tangents sometimes about non-related course material when there wasn't even enough time allotted to cover the actual course content. Hope she's able to hit her stride and shoutout Xi'an street food!

Great lectures and great lecture notes. Really supportive professor who is very willing to help outside of class. Provides practice prelims very similar to real ones. However, homework assignments are long and very harshly graded.

I felt like whenever she did lectures instead of Matt I always would have to review notes since the lectures were harder to follow. Although she was very engaging, I felt like she tried to hard to bring it outside topics into the course that made us run out of time to focus on what were expected to actually learn

Ruth is a phenomenal lecturer, academic, and professor in every regard.  As my advisor for the History major, she has been a kind and caring guiding figure during my time at Cornell that I have never had trouble asking for help when needed.  I've taken multiple courses with her, and she is an excellent authority on the history of war & the U.S.

She was an informative and clearly well-versed teacher, gave interesting lectures and gave reasonable tests. Very few students actually did the readings for this course; most emphasis was given to the lecture, and the only paper is a ten-pager near the end of the course that has yet to be fully assigned/ discussed. All in all, she's pretty great!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Really amazing lecturer, very engaging and knowledgable. Lots of reading, but all of it supplements the content pretty well. Grading is fair and there were a few opportunities for extra credit. Overall, great class, great professor, would take her again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very interesting class and lectures that offers new perspectives on WW2. Graded on 3 papers and a 10-12 page final paper. Lectures not necessary to jot down but can be helpful. The papers were very open-ended and require heavy critical thinking, but they're also very intellectually demanding/stimulating as a result. Good feedback and good grading.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Lawlor is the best professor I've had. She is passionate, enthusiastic and has a great sense of humor. Despite longer readings, as expected in history, her discussions in seminar are thought provoking and she's not afraid to follow the interests of students in what they read. I want to be an academic and she is no small reason why.

By far, Prof. Lawlor was my favorite professor while at Cornell. She is truly an inspiration for those who aspire to remain in academia as a career, as Prof. Lawlor is the kind of scholar one hopes to emulate. Her classes are very reading-heavy, but Prof Lawlor is very empathetic and does her best to ensure her students' success.

Her Gender & Sexuality seminar was one of the best courses I've taken at Cornell. Readings and discussions were varied, relevant, and interesting. She's extremely knowledgable, caring, and a fair grader. However, readings are long and if you're confused about a concept she may ramble. Papers are tailored to personal interests. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor is so passionate, it radiates into the lectures and discussions. Grading scale is unique (85 is an A-) and it's writing-based but overall a solid course. She is just overall a very nice person who's accessible to students and has tons of knowledge. Lecture heavy but participation is encouraged. Final project/paper worth 40%.
Literally cannot teach to save her life. No curve in the class and brutal exams.
doesn't want to help her students
Reading the textbook is better.

Teaching style hard. She doesn't explain many answers if a student was able to get it right in class. Many students never attend lecture bc they think reading textbook is better. Grading unclear. doesn't curve but grade cutoffs are made more generous? so you never know where you stand. I barely learned anything in lecture

We had MacDonald for half the semester when other prof was out. I found myself to understand the content MUCH better when MacDonald taught. She explained both how to do the math and the significance of it. She attempted to learn everyone's name in lecture and interacted with everyone individually. Lecture notes were amazing.

The class itself was fine but Prof Kelly was amazing, she was a great lecturer and really cared about the students, but Prof MacDonald really showed no care and empathy to students and made it very difficult to communicate or ever ask her questions due to her rudeness. I would recommend kelly instead.

Class is not hard, and she's nice so fine if you need this for a req. She does walk around and stop to ask the class questions like middle school often, so it can get really frustrating. However, the class content is interesting and Marie is a nice lady who is accessible outside of lecture, so though I don't love the teaching style, I'd recommend.

Also confused by all the negative reviews. Don't listen to those people - they likely didn't ever go to class or OH. Seriously, Marie is so caring and loves what she does and wants her students to succeed. Go to OH with her for HW answers! Go to class and you'll do great! Marie is there to help you, put in the work and you'll get a good grade.

Also confused with the bad ratings. Marie is such a kind and caring prof, & walks through all the hw with you during office hours. The course content itself seemed unrelated to calculus and a bit nebulous at times, and TAs are picky with HW, but the prof is great (and this class is certainly better than MATH 1110 from what I've heard).

So confused about the negative reviews. She's actually a godsend. The class moves slowly at first, but I wasn't complaining. Workload is more than reasonable. She will help you through any homework/practice problem. She actually cares about teaching and wants you to succeed. She's so sweet.

This class is notoriously known as the "easy calc 1" but I wouldn't even call this a calculus class. You don't look at derivatives/integrals until prelim 2. Beyond that, they teach the most useless topics and they do a horrible job. Marie isn't great at explaining new concepts and relies on students reading the textbook to get by. TAs also suck...

The only class I've ever taken where the instructors actually want you to fail. They take off unnecessary points on pretty much every assignment, and they will literally ignore regrades if it isn't in the exact format they require, even if you deserve a regrade. Stay very consistent with the class materials if you want to survive.

She's terrible at explaining any concept above the second grade level. Teaches college students like they're in elementary school and disregards any nuance in math and science. Also ironic how little she knows about biology, considering this is a life sciences class. Also Jonathan Lafler is miserable, and has 0 empathy for students in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The most unnecessarily difficult class ever. Points taken off for the tiniest mistakes in HW + exams and the class is so disengaging, I've never felt more defeated in a class. They give the hardest examples during class for no reason and then explain things so vaguely it's a miracle I got through this class at all, feels like they want you to fail.

Wickham is a terrible prof. Her lectures are incomprehensible slides filled with equations with random formatting and colors, making them hard to follow. Her homeworks and exams are riddles where it's sometimes harder to understand a question than to solve it. She's very nice, but that doesn't make up for everything else being atrocious.

Wickam is a great person, but easily the worst professor I've had at Cornell. Her lectures don't make any sense, and the problem sets are somehow worse. I honestly cannot believe she is still employed.

Classical mechanics and its mathematical framework and very important, but Wickham does not do them justice. She communicates ideas incoherently, in part because of her strange and unnecessary notion. It feels like a high school physics class. She is very kind and supportive, but, to be honest, I would have rather learned the material.

Horribly taught class. The class isn't difficult because the material is hard, it is difficult because Professor wickham doesn't understand how to conevy her ideas over paper, and thus the homeworks become excessively cumbersome. Honestly half the students in the class could probably teach the class better than her.

Dr. Wickham might just be the absolute worst professor I have ever taken a class with at Cornell. She writes essays to describe the most simple problems that could be stated in 1 to 2 sentences, thus making simple physics incomprehensible. Additionally, ever since Covid hit, she just lectures from text heavy slides (atrocious lectures).

Whilst doing her problem sets/ exams, I sometimes wondered if I was in English class, except the professor stopped taking English after 3rd grade. Her lecture slides are densely compacted with useless jargon. The textbook is a little elementary, but then again so is she. I don't know how this lady still has a job. She is nice though, I suppose.

Her lectures are a mess, her homework is often 5-6 pages long where each question is 5-8 parts and each part is a long rant that goes nowhere. One of the only professors who can take an easy concept and make it completely incomprehensible to anyone. Her grasp on written English is tenuous at best. By far the worst professor in the department.

At first, I didn't like her. She was too hyper, her notes and homeworks were poorly formatted. But my opinion changed when I actually interacted with her. She's EXTREMELY sweet and genuinely cares about you, the material, and making sure you get it. Pay attention, work hard and you'll do awesomely.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Loved this class, Dr. Wickham is great. Although she covers a lot of material, you will benefit from matching Dr. Wickham's enthusiasm for the subject. Show up and take good notes and you'll be on your way to mastering the subject and a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Wickham cares a lot about getting the material across and is genuinely a very good person. For that reason alone she is one of my favorite professors. Her lectures are a bit fast, and she clearly drinks A LOT of caffeine, but many people find her style exciting/refreshing. Assignments are very thorough and help a lot. Lots of work but worth it

Professor Wickham is a really good professor, but she suffers from a lack of clarity sometimes. It's tough to tell when she's moving on to a new topic.  That said, she knows the material really well and the problem sets prepare you well for the exams. Wickham reminds me of the principal from School of Rock.

Disorganized and confusing lecture format. She just throws information at you for 55 minutes nonstop, constantly running out of breath. The class and material could've been taught in a much better way.

The lectures are extremely quick. However, if you put in the time and attend all of her lectures, the class is reasonable and fair. To be honest, she's one of my favorite professor's at Cornell because she is so upbeat about all of our lectures.

Definitely one of the more responsible professors at Cornell. Her classes are very difficult, no doubt, but she does cover materials in great detail. She reviews the previous lecture briefly so people shouldn't have trouble following her. She is also extremely helpful outside of the classroom. The classes are difficult, but very rewarding!

By far the worst professor I've had at Cornell. Unable to express herself clearly (or concisely), stutters through lectures, consistently poor choices of notation, and generally terrible presentation of otherwise interesting material. I can't believe she will be the only professor I'll have for more than one class here.
Lectures very unclear. Problem sets unclear and long.

Definitely the worst professor I have had at Cornell. Lectures are way too fast, and she doesn't stop to explain anything. Exams and problem sets are hard, and I came away from the class feeling like I hadn't learned anything. Terrible class.

She's a very organized and knows her stuff, but lectures WAYYYY too fast. Course covered twice as much material as it should have. Students were frequently clueless when it came to the lengthy, time-consuming homeworks. I would have much rather done two-thirds of the material and learned it five times better.
Extremely helpful and very nice. Very enthusiastic about the material
Well organized
Very clear and enthusiastic
No Comments
She's very enthusiastic about the subject.

I took his Bioethics FWS and had a great time. Readings were very reasonable in length, and I generally found them interesting. Matt gave very insightful essay feedback and encouraged multifaceted discussion in class. Essay directions were clear, so grading seemed to correlate with what you expected. Was a great intro to the Cornell Philosphy dept!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He's awesome. I took him last semester for bioethics and he made the class really enjoyable. Creates a great environment for discussion of arguments and objections, too, which is helpful for a philosophy course. Just make sure you do the readings (there are occasional pop quizzes) and ask questions when necessary. Would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Good FWS professor! Had him for Bioethics and he was very chill and made discussions engaging. Super down-to-earth and nice. Gives good feedbacks on essays and readings are minimal. Beware of occasional popquizzes in class, but they're not hard and worth very little. Not a harsh grader--do the readings, participate, and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Paskell was a pretty chill professor. Five essays in total, with each being weighted more as the semester progresses. Attendance in lectures and discussions were mandatory, but going is helpful just to gain further clarification on the readings and insights to write the essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: I had Professor Paskell for my FWS Bioethics. Super interesting class, and he always made discussions very interesting! There were usually readings for each class, but most of the time very short (and very minimal compared to other writing seminars). Also gave very good essay feedback (although he is a slow grader). Overall great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This was for an FWS on Luck and Morality. There were a lot of readings, quizzes, and small assignments, and attendance was mandatory, so the class took a decent amount of time. However, he made the class discussions pretty interesting and gave really helpful feedback on the essays, so the class was worth taking.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Trottier is a genuine and passionate professor, who actually cares about her students. I have taken two of the her courses and she was consistently clear about expectations, flexible, and knowledgeable. She creates her exams from the slides that she presents in lecture, and not from other sources.

Wonderful human being!! Wants to make learning fun and doesn't want you to just regurgitate facts. She deeply cares about the well-being of her students and will work with you to make sure you understand the topics. Not sure what the poor reviews are about, the class is very organized, and all the tools to succeed are laid out for you.

Dr. Trottier is so caring and knowledgeable! Important to go to lecture, there are open note quizzes almost every lecture and some concepts are not written down but is verbally explained. Exams are doable if you answer learning objectives detailedly/ask for help, also extra credit on exams. Grading scale is lenient (A= 90+, A- = 85+ etc).
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Trottier is an amazing professor. She takes the time to explain things thoroughly and is very receptive to questions. Her slides are organized and she provides clear learning objectives for every lecture. I would 100% take a class with her again.

The most amazing professor I have had at Cornell. Cares deeply about her students and does a great job teaching the material. She is so passionate about the content as well, she really wants her students to learn. Nice grading scale as well.

Dr. Trottier is an amazing professor with great passion for teaching! As long as you work hard and participate in class you will do good. She has a deep knowledge in what she teaches, the bad reviews on here are from students who must've not gotten the grade they wanted and are unfairly rating her poorly. Take this course!

I regret taking ANSC1500! Worst course I've taken! She appears engaged, but her knowledge seems limited (always reads off slides) When seeking clarification, she would say I'm not sure or it's in the reading, giving no guidance but expects us to know EVERYTHING though she claims that it's for non-majors. She takes points off without explaining why.

This class was more difficult than it needed to be. The content itself was not difficult overall, but the way the instructor taught the material was odd. She expects you to put in a lot of work outside of class before each lecture, which just is not realistic especially mid to late semester as this isn't the only class most people are taking.

This class is a waste. It's a flipped classroom, but with in person quizzes/exams and 3 hours of pre-lecture material due each night. There's a semester long group project that is split into 4 milestones. The project and material learned doesn't make any sense with how she teaches. If you ask for help she just says that it was in the notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Waste of time. It's basically a flipped classroom. She rambles in class and asks us questions that are impossible to answer because she doesn't teach any material. No idea what I'm supposed to know for the prelims. When I asked a question she said: "If you think about it more critically, you will find the answer in your heart." Avoid at all costs.

On several occasions she will assign 3+ hours of Pre-Lecture Homework the day before class, and her lectures are extremely dry and unhelpful. It's basically a flipped classroom. Over 80% of the questions on the first prelim were solely random facts from the readings we did. This wasn't hard, but makes no sense. She gave the same lecture 4 times.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: great professor, super super knowledgeable in his field, lots of fascinating experiences and overall a great guy, genuinely wants to talk about class topics and help you with assignments. lots and lots of readings but definitely manageable.

Fall 23' - I enjoyed the class content; can be engaging. He provides outlines (used for notes). He shares a bit of his research which is also interesting. It can be heavy on the reading but as long as you skim or get the gist, you should be fine. The papers are pretty good; enjoyed writing my final paper! The discussion sections were nice!
Lecture can be tedious but also some interesting parts. He mainly reads his lecture notes so it is easy to get lost, however he is very accomodating and the workload for the class is manageable.

Nadasdy has a very questionable lecture style to say the least.  For a course on Indigenous history, he does not choose many readings from Indigenous authors, often depicting a very Euro-centric view on Indigenous people. Even further, he references his research with a specific group as his claim to knowledge while blatantly spewing misconceptions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures run really long and cover very broad topics. Mettler is clearly passionate and kind, and TAs are helpful. Exams are straightforward, readings are extremely long, and the textbook isn't very necessary. Projects are interesting. Overall, strong professor but weak course structure.

It took a hot minute for this class to gain momentum because in the beginning it was extremely boring but in November it got good. Professor Mettler clearly cares for her students and definitely appreciates participation, she remembers students who do which is nice. The TA's are awesome and the assignments are fun to do and exams are pretty easy!

The readings for homework are pretty hefty, but you can slide by since they are discussed in class and in discussions. The papers aren't hard, nor is the tests. A little hard to get above a 95 in some aspects, but if you try, you can easily get a 90+.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very passionate and knowledgeable on the subject. Exams were a bit difficult and relied heavily on readings (of which there were a ton) so be ready for a good amount of work.
Took this class freshman fall, was such a good class and introduction. She gave clear lectures with good notes and the papers and exams were not hard at all.

Amazing professor. Really organized + engaging lectures. There's a manageable amount of readings per week plus textbook chapters, however you don't actually need to read the textbook in order to do well in the class. The assignments are tedious but doable and are graded pretty fairly.

An interesting and engaging lecturer who deeply cares about her students. A genuine wealth of knowledge. Grades will largely be dependent on TAs, but they were lenient for me. Would recommend to anyone.
loved her!

Prof. Mettler is a very nice person. She knew almost two thirds of the class(which was around 200 students). The grading is done mostly by TAs, and is done rather fairly. The lectures are very interesting. The textbook is huge though, and the readings can be boring, but you can survive on the summary/glossary at the end of each chapter.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This is my second semester taking a class with Professor Mettler, and I can confidently say her class was the most engaging and well-presented one I've taken in the government department. Exams are 1-1 reflections of class material and are very fair, if not generous. Always available to discuss content or review. Would 100% recommend, a must have!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Mettler is an amazing lecturer. I came away from her course every day with renewed interest in Government. She works super hard to make the class relevant and inspiring and mostly succeeds. There is a decent amount of reading but it's manageable in the grand scheme of things, and the assignments are not too hard.

Professor Mettler's lectures effectively covered course content, although it often didn't reflect a lot of what was covered in tests. Assignments and exams were reasonable, and readings weren't the most challenging. Overall, class is a great intro to US government and I would recommend to take this class.
Great, great professor that truly cares about her students. Interesting lectures and always responds positively to students. A lot of writing, no doubt, but it is well worth it.

She's a decent lecturer who knows what she's talking about. Can be a little dry and repetitive at times, but overall interesting subject. Textbook isn't necessary per se but probably I'd try to read it as much as reasonably possible. TAs can be hit or miss.
Great lectures that were engaging and gave time for feedback on questions from students to make lectures more interactive. Easily accessible and great feedback during office hours.
Mettler is very engaging in lectures and does so by walking around the room and encouraging students to share their answers with the lecture class. Easy to stay engaged and focused.

Professor Mettler is an excellent professor who is very clear with her expectations and one of the most engaging lecturers that I have had at Cornell. She takes her job very seriously and is very dedicated. I liked that she broke up the monotony of lecture with questions to the class and I thought that the course readings were really interesting.

A great professor that conveys ideas clearly and powerfully. Great introductory course to Government. The materials and concepts will challenge your thoughts and increase your interests in politics. lecture is organised with clear flow.

Professor Mettler is such a kind person who absolutely loves what she does.  She is always more than happy to talk to people outside of class and makes an effort to keep class interesting, even in a large intro class.  I sincerely am glad that I was able to take the class, which is relatively easy, and get to know her.

Listen, unless you LOVE government she won't be your favorite teacher; but she is more than fine. Lectures are dry and you don't have to pay attention; but do know the terms she emphasizes (you'll know).  The homework and essays aren't hard, they just take time.  Overall, a pretty enjoyable class, especially everything going on in the world.

Professor Mettler does a really good job for a broad intro course. She is organized, clear, and very helpful if you go to office hours. Readings are helpful but not totally necessary if you pay attention in class. Would take again!

As a person, she is  good-natured, and genuinely cares about getting to know her students on a personal level as much as she can. She also really allowed for a discussion of current events to dominate, and made herself available to students seeking help or advice (not just with the course. Lectures can be a bit dry/dull at times though.

I wouldn't say she's terrible. She is really sweet and really passionate about her work. However, the papers were quite vague at times and there was a lot of reading  (tbh you can sort of bs it unless you want discussion to be awkward). Also, it's hard to determine what grade you have till the end (the median grade is an A- though!)

Terrible beyond words. Rambling, unclear lectures combined with vague essay prompts not even remotely related to the material in the readings and lectures. It was so bad that the TA even apologized to our section for her lack of effort. Condescending and rude during office hours-- basically told me to go away when I asked for clarification on essay
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Although attendance grade does not take up a significant portion, you would need to attend her classes to see what are highlighted.  Skipping the discussion sessions is also fatal. It is almost 20% of your grade. The course has some small homework assignments but they are based on participation not quality.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She was a good lecturer although sometimes it did get rather dull. She's very data oriented so that can get tedious to listen to at times. Overall she is very passionate about the subject and open to discussion and questions. There is a heavier load of outside reading to do between classes
The lectures tend to be a bit vague, and it is incredibly obvious what her political views tend to be.  Other than that, she is a sweet person who has passion for what she teaches.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: I'm surprised to hear negative feedback about Mettler's Obama seminar. I really enjoyed the class. Although I do think Mettler admired Obama, I didn't think she was biased, or that she discouraged criticism of him. I personally wrote a final research paper criticizing Obama's expansion of the NSA, and I got a great grade. Lots of reading, though.
reviews.rating_tags: CARES ABOUT STUDENTS--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Mettler isn't exactly the most interesting professor but she is a solid choice... Clear expectations and well-developed lectures and assignments.  If you have a basic understanding of American politics, it shouldn't be too hard to pull of an A.
Terrible. Avoid at all costs. Abysmal lecturer, condescending, unclear expectations.

Mettler is the single worst professor in the entire Government department. Her entire seminar was dedicated to talking about how great Obama is, with no room for criticism from either the right or left of him. Called on the same student literally 10+ times in each two hour seminar. Grading was based on how well you regurgitated her political views.

Lectures are amazing! Clear, concise, and helpful. She doesn't go on tangents and focuses on the material. Presents it in a very interesting, thought-provocative way. Truly cares about her class and her students (remembers people's names and what they've said). The textbook & almost all the summaries of all readings can be found online ;)))
