I really enjoyed this class. A lot of the material overlapped with AP Gov, which was nice. The lectures were interesting, very organized and easy to understand. The essays are a little harder and are graded based on how closely you answer the prompt. You can also get a lot of participation credit if you're up to date on current events.

An example of a research- focused professor that will give you a B- on an A+ essay. Grades subjectively based on how your arguments are aligned with her beliefs. Generally takes away from the educational experience with short-sightedness and one-sidedness. All we learn is her opinions on government and that is a true shame.
Glorious Goat

Professor ning the goat . Very nice guy, lectures are very good. he clearly wants the very best for his students and is very passionate about statistics - He continues answering questions in office hours even 30 minutes after they ended. Also he said about 65% of the class gets an A- or above and he curves grades lower than that up.
pookie bear
Definitely the best professor I had at Cornell - his lectures are amazing, makes the concepts very easy to understand. Super nice person as well!
amazing professor! super smart, nice, chill, and understanding. you can tell he wants his students to succeed. would definitely recommend taking this class.

very smart, nice, and accommodating professor, but not very responsive to students' questions on piazza. takes a while to get assignments graded, so you don't really know where your grade stands in the class. exams are 50% of grade. also wish he taught R in class, rather than have us learn it ourselves. overall, interesting class and nice prof

Amazing and informative lectures. Very accessible outside classroom. He assigns homework that are actually useful and thought-provoking. The exams are fair and well represent what we learned in class. You cannot ask for more than that.
The best professor I have ever seen. Believe it or not, he is the only reason I want to stay in Ithaca. I love him.

very nice professor who is accomodating of different kinds of learning styles. lecture slides are useful, the assignments and exams are reasonable reflections of the course content. very accessible in terms of emails and office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Focuses on key-concepts and applying material rather than memorization or details. Very straight-forward and fairly easy class is you listen to lectures and look briefly through the textbook. Pretty good professor with strong insight into machine learning applications.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: He's probably the first professor I've ever met who still voluntarily ask you "do you have any more questions?" when his OH has already finished by half an hour... Very clear, very patient, very detailed. Definitely take it if you want to be more clear about the foundation of machine learning. He also has a great personality!!!
The nicest professor I've ever seen
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I have never met a professor that is as nice as him.

Took his class at University of Waterloo in 2013, I was from other session and his class was in the morning session. Nothing could wake me up in the morning but his class(NOT MY SESSION). That's all because his crystal clear explanation. I think it was truly worth my time writing a comment for him after a long time his name came up from my head.

I have never regretted to take Professor Ning's course at Cornell, i.e. clear lectures, acceptable workload, personal charm. He towers above so many so called reputable professors I've ever met.  You do deserve the course and don't be shy to ask him questions, you'll be agreeable to have chances to talk with him, trust me )

Really a great professor,  very helpful and explains the concepts of machine learning  in details. Makes the subject more interesting to read. Always accessible and ready to help. One of the best professor!

Dr. Ning is the best lecturer and advisor you could have in your life!!!!!!!!!!!!!! He's super clear in lectures, good at breaking down complex ideas into simple concepts. He made the course really interesting. You can tell everyone loves him by how many people are still coming to class the day before Thanksgiving and even after the last exam. LOVE
YOU MUST TAKE THIS CLASS if you are interested in statistical learning and want to be exposed to some of the basic machine learning concepts.
Great professor for this EXTREMELY popular course. Clear teaching points with explanation.

This is the best class I have taken at Cornell and I always look forward to it. I love the seminar style where students and the professor sit around a table conversing for the entire period. Conversations are always enlightening and engaged and Mulder helps students understand the topic by participating in the conversation and asking questions.
Mulder's lectures made less sense than Trump's speech.
He makes a vivid example of himself by teaching this class.
He really doesn't know how to explain things and his office hours are such a waste of time. Highly recommend having ChatGPT replace him.
worst prof in my 4 yrs of undergrad
Even Donald Trump is more agreeable than this guy.
if you like to go to a zoo and observe the monkeys, this is the right class for you
There is no such thing as trash, only materials in the wrong place. Obviously, Nick is in a wrong place.
I won't give Mulder 1 if negative scores are available

Attending Nick's class is like watching a flop movie. You fall asleep in 5 minutes and wake up 1 hour later just to realize that you are still able to catch the plot seamlessly. 
Then you fall asleep again after 2 minutes.

Don't be fooled by the negative reviews! Professor Mulder is easily one of the best professors at Cornell. His lectures are easy to follow, his exams are straightforward and he is always willing to share his knowledge to students wanting to know more about Europe as whole. Even if you don't like history, Mulder's course is must take at Cornell!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: you can hardly find a worse instructor in the entire department
trust me, you will learn more by going to a zoo and watching monkeys eat bananas then attending this man's class
terrible.
chose this class to fill requirements. deeply regretted it. don't do it if you have a choice.
disorganized

Mulder never delves deep into his materials and he does not entertain questions that require thorough thinking or rigorous logic. He will happily answer questions such as "what is the year of the French revolution" but not ones like "how did the economy of X contribute to Y". I even learned more in my AP Europen History class.
If you are really passionate about the subject and want to learn things, better choose another professor or just watch youtube videos. This man is not good at teaching at all.

Had to take this class for the distribution requirement and was not a fan of European history but ended up loving this class. He gives good lectures and the workload is small (one reading question per week). He is the best-dressed male professor in the history department, period.

Amazing professor, cannot recommend him enough. He is extremely knowledgeable about the content and is able to talk at length about even the most obscure topics. I had his discussion section and he was very engaging and did a wonderful job explaining the material. Office hours are also very good! Literally one of the best professors I've had here.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Avoid this man at all cost

This class covered a wide range of materials. But sometimes Professor Mulder went over topics too quick to give enough explanations, and I was under the impression that he was throwing out isolated events without elaborating more on their inherent connections. He also spoke too fast and his voice was too low. Hard to hear if not sit in the front.

He didn't seem to know his material very well. Many times when students asked about the identity of the people in or the context of the pictures he used in his slides, he would say "em I wish I would know more info about it". Honestly I think the TA did a better teaching job than him. He was also very bad at responding to emails.

Professor Mulder is an amazing lecturer and extremely knowledgeable. He's very good at imparting knowledge through his lectures and is extremely approachable outside of lecture. The only grades were a midterm essay, participation, and the final, and he's a very easy grader. Cannot recommend him and this class enough

Excellent professor and great course. Highly recommend to anyone looking to take a history class. Grade based only on participation, weekly discussion posts, and a final paper. Super interesting material and the way Prof Mulder runs the class makes it all the more enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Sam goes above and beyond to teach students the value of advocacy and debate. He set up 1-on-1 meetings when he could have graded virtually instead because he wants to learn new and interesting things from each student. He naturally gains student respect thanks to his gentle, dedicated, and prudent style of instruction.

This is the easiest A of your life if you go to the main lecture weekly and study vocab twice the semester. Professor genuinely cares about you and will tell you in main lecture that a specific question may be on the exam and how it will be asked. Half of class doesn't attend lecture but its interesting and you guarantee yourself a good grade

lecture attendance wasn't mandatory but discussion attendance was. but you should go to class. exams are based on the textbook and things he talks about in class. he does round up a grade. shoutout to ta amalia she's really good
go to class and review/study for the exams. you will also have some other assignments to do. good class

The class itself was ok; the material was not hard to understand. However, be aware that the TA (Nazmun) who helped conduct the class is extremely passive-aggressive, undermines your work, is super unhelpful, is very open-ended when answering questions, and is very unresponsive. Also, the professor was ok, not my fav, but ok.

Absolutely hilarious & a pleasure to get to know! Weekly night lectures felt more like a comedy hour to look forward to. Actively engages students with concepts using memorable (sometimes preposterous!) examples. Very knowledgeable & personable. Gets to know students. Exams = vocab quiz + short answers based directly on lectures (discussed prior)

Does not deserve the negative reviews. As long as you go to class/get notes from someone who does, this class is light. MC questions are based on textbook vocab, so just memorize. Short-answer questions are based on lecture topics. Writing assignments are chill if you listen to his explanations. Raises your grade a letter higher at the end of sem

I took this class for the “easy A.” I genuinely believe that previously this class used to be easy, but now the tests are so hard, the essays are completely unintuitive, and half the class dropped the course after the midterm. I don't know who angered him last semester, but this professor has a bone to pick with the Cornell student body.

Don't trust these reviews. The average on the first exam was genuinely a 60, and the first paper was around an 80. He doesn't use lecture slides and does not post any information from class afterwards. The exam is 50% textbook terms (237, and no, he doesn't narrow them down for you) and 50% lecture material, which could be anything he said in class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures were very chill, and most of the knowledge comes from the textbook. For the 2 exams: 25 MCQ from the textbook, worth 50% of the test, and 5 questions from lectures, also worth 50% with no partial credits. However, the section staff Ibe often interrupts students when asking questions during the debate POI. Very rude and mean.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: after the first 3 weeks it was literally just students giving presentations for 2-3 hours and him watching from the back. Free A though which is cool.
Super easy A. Chill class.

He makes it clear from the start of the course that he resents competence. Everyone receives an A, but no one receives an A+ unless he subjectively believes you deserve one. Take for an easy A, but avoid if you are meaningfully attempting to boost your grade or if you care about your grade reflecting your ability. Complete bore, not worth the time.

Prof. Nelson is an amazing, hillarious teacher who genuinely cares about all his students. The class is easy to succeed in IF you show up to lectures and discussion!! He goes through exactly what to expect on the exam during lectures (especially when there are less students who show up). He is super understanding and accessible outside of class.

Great professor and great class. Professor Nelson is a genuinely kind man that enjoys his students and what he teaches. Meets with each student 1-on-1 at least once a semester. This is the easiest 4 credit class Cornell offers, and I would recommend to anyone. You will also probably enjoy it and do well if you manage to make the night lectures.

Sam Nelson is a delight. Though his class seems unorthodox, he really cares about debate and loves to see his students engaged and excited. Taking this class improved my public speaking skills and it was a very easy, low pressure 4 credit class. The essays seem like a lot but they really aren't, and always lets you out early.

Day 1, there was a scenario about if he brought in beagle babies and started stomping on their heads, what would you do? He makes you think. Sometimes in crazy ways but the class makes you think about where your values lie through a lot of topics. I learned a lot about debate and getting my opinions across. Go to lecture and you'll do great.
One of the goofiest professors Ive had at this university. Would absolutely recommend him

So so easy. The class can be interesting but sometimes drags on. People do very poorly on the first exam in general, and often not great on the first paper (which he lets you resubmit), but the median is still an A. Cares about students and meets with all of them during the semester.
One of the nicest and most genuine professors at Cornell. He cares about his students and tries to make sure each and every student is set up for success.
Easiest class ever. Only like 2 projects and paper and Sam is a super easy grader. Lets us leave lecture after like an hour.

Sam is a great professor. Just like advocacy and debate, rhetoric is also a very easy class. The class is 2.5 hours once a week but often finishes over an hour early. The few assignments he gives are easy and the grading is light. Definitely take this class for a free 4 credits.

For each 2.5 hour lecture, there is maybe 15-20 minutes of actual content, and the rest of it is just Sam chatting with the students in a pseudo-forum. You *have* to read the textbook (or study the quizlets made by past students) for exams. The canvas is never updated and paper expectations are only explained in lecture. It's fun though- would rec.

Sam is a great professor. He is very nice, accommodating, and makes a somewhat boring topic enjoyable. Class is only once a week and there isn't much work except for a few papers. The class is easy even if you have no prior knowledge, he will cut you slack if you simply ask, and the average grade was an A. Take this class.
His debate class is easy and he is just such an amazing human being. I would definitely recommend anyone to take the class!

Sam is a great person and is easy to talk to but I didn't actually enjoy this class like I expected to. I don't feel that I learned much or that my debate skills improved. Lectures were full of tangents and stories, so some classes will be more important than others. Tests were definitely curved.

Nelson is a weird professor and you will need to adapt to his interesting style. You HAVE to read the textbook. A lot of students made the mistake of glossing over it and not performing well. Also, make sure you go over EVERYTHING from the lectures. He asked for quotes on the final without warning. Everything is fair game.
He is an entertaining lecturer, and highly recommend taking the debate class if it satisfies requirements. This class will also make you a better public speaker.

Sam is a really funny and caring guy; favorite professor I've had so far. Made lectures really interesting and worth going to, despite it being a night class. Tests are 50% lecture, 50% book details, so lectures are definitely necessary, as is the book. Discussion is kinda boring; don't take early in the morning. Overall, great class. 9.8/10.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Sam is an amazing professor. His teaching style is very nontraditional but I still learned a lot from his class. Discussion sections were really interesting because that is where you actually debate and they were on interesting topics. Super easy A and you become a better public speaker after this class. HIGHLY RECOMMEND HIM IF YOU WANT AN A.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Easy A from a mediocre professor. If you are even the slightest bit interested in rhetorical criticism, prepare to be disappointed. Sam is so lazy, he manages not to give a single lecture. NOT ONE. Your FELLOW CLASSMATES will be teaching each class. Hopefully they read the textbook. You will learn nothing. You will get an A.

Very easy A, "alternative" teaching style. Engaging lecturer for a night class, always has interesting stories. Gives exact test questions in class, but if you have a friend give you the notes, you'll be fine. Still worth going to lecture for the stories though.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Sam is great. But I wish he was more clear about what would be covered on the exams! The only thing I had to go on was that he could ask us anything about anything from all of his lectures and the assigned text (that he NEVER went over). I failed the first test because of this, but aced the second exam because I knew what to expect that time!

What an inspiration!  I wish more professors mimicked his style.  He is very down to earth and has the best lectures I've ever attended!  The first test is all about definitions (they'll tell you this) that can be found in the text.  Much of the grade is based on debate participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Sam is, by far, the best teacher I've ever had. I had him for my ILRLR 3300 3-week summer program and it was undoubtedly the highlight of my summer. He's super funny, super friendly, and super knowledgeable. He gives lots of lectures but they're always fantastic.  I visited him a lot during my course and even met with him at CTB. He's a true gem.
BEST TEACHER I EVER HAD

Hands down one of the most influential classes in my Cornell experience. You'll learn to articulate your opinions and argue effectively. Sam's great in lecture. He always presents great hypothetical scenarios when trying to illustrate a point. The lectures are 3 hours long, which sucks, but there is a break halfway through.

Awesome Professor. I cant even sit through a 3 hour movie, let alone a lecture. But he made it fly by and it was so interesting, I actually LOOKED FORWARD to his class!! Definitely Should take this class while youre at Cornell.
Very easy and entertaining class. You'll become a better debater and public speaker just by virtue of attending lecture.
You must take Argumentation & Debate with Sam Nelson.  He is hilarious and genuinely wants his students to learn.  As long as you show that you're trying, you'll get an A.

half the time no one, as in him or the TA, knows what's going on. 2 tests, 1 final, which was all true or false this year, papers, and 3 debates.  he's extremely funny and it's an entertaining class, and you do learn some stuff but mainly the questions for the test are stuff you read in the book.
The class can be kind of dysfunctional at times, but Sam is hilarious (if he wasn't a debate professor, he could have a successful career as a stand-up comedian) and it is an easy A.

GREAT PROFESSOR!!!! Lectures were extremely interesting! His laugh and his jokes kept me laughing the entire class time! You must take this class, it is not too hard if you put the effort. Read the book, you MUST go to lecture to do well on his tests, and do the assignments given...

Sam is mad funny, by far one of the better professors at Cornell. He is always cracking jokes and loves to hold class discussions on interesting debate topics. I was always awake when Sam taught Great course. Great Professor. Easy A

Sam is mad funny, by far one of the better professors at Cornell. He is always cracking jokes and loves to hold class discussions on interesting debate topics. I was always awake when Sam taught until his asst came to teach. Great course. Great Professor. Easy A
Definitely the funniest professor I have ever had. As stated before he makes the 3 hr class fly by. It was the best 3 hours of my week hands down.
GREAT Professor!! Although I can't stay awake in a 45 minute course, Sam can keep my attention in a 3 hour course. Take his class! It's an easy A.
agreed with above. awesome professor.

Quite possibly one of the ONLY professors that can keep my interest in a three hour lecture. His lectures consist of a joke every five or so minutes at the very least, and the material he teaches you is interesting. Tests are easy if you skim the book, and as long sa you have an interest, it's an easy A/A-. A+ is somewhat hard to get, though.

Impossible to enjoy this class with how monotonous and disinterested she is, it's time to pass the torch to a different professor. Overwhelming amount of info on slides, prelims test arbitrary information. No point in going to lecture besides clinical correlates and the weekly quiz. Class is not curved for whatever reason.

NS 3410 is a tough class; each lecture is a little longer in size to that of 1350 and 1440, and there are 4 lectures a week here instead of 2, so it's literally at least double the content. However, I think Prof. O'Brien does an excellent job of making it clear what exactly you need to know to do well. Just study consistently and you will do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class is hard, though I think that its structure keeps you on pace as best as possible. O'Brien can be monotonous at times but it is very clear precisely what you need to know - the slides are really well made. NS 3410 with her is not for the faint of heart but it is absolutely possible to do well in it as long as you study consistently.

The course is dense, and lectures have a lot of information packed in them, but she explains topics very well and makes sure to repeat information to enforce it. She responds well to feedback (started including review slides mid-semester to help study for quizzes). No doubt, this course is HARD, but Dr. O'Brien does what she can to help students.
avoid this class like the plague. This woman has no remorse.

Lecture was boring but fine. The course is disorganized. Assessments always have errors and are graded slowly. The "midterm" clinical correlate grades were returned with only 2 weeks of class left. Exam questions often test incredibly niche information, rather than important concepts. Professor doesn't take student feedback when they have concerns.
The most disorganized professor I've ever had.

Prof O'Brien was very nice an overall an ok lecturer. I thought discussions were fun and material was engaging. However, grading was horrible. My grades were changed so many times on canvas and it made things so confusing. If they make mistakes in grading, you have to FIGHT to get those points back, which really left me frustrated. Overall ok.

Dr. O'Brien's lectures are mind-numbingly boring. Though the content has the potential to be interesting her approach left me disinterested in the material. The class was poorly organized with frequent grading errors and poor communication with the students. Be prepared to study 100s of slides and be tested on niche content.
She's actually the worst professor I've ever had, no exaggeration.

she stands in the front of the lecture hall and just talks in a monotone. you need to work every single day. there are substantial quizzes every Wednesday along with prelims, a midterm, case studies, a "clinical correlate" on Tuesday (requires lots of prep and participation) and a final. Really awful prof and not very nice or helpful either

Youll learn a lot from this class. It will prepare you well for anatomy content on mcat and even freshmen anatomy class in med school. Shell teach you Latin roots that are helpful to figure out unfamiliar medical terms. This class was very interesting and shes very passionate about what she teaches. It is a time consuming class tho.

This class involves A LOT of memorizing. Theres a quiz every wednesday and those are extremely stressful to prepare for. Slides have way too much info and the prelim tests you on very small info that's at the corner of the slide that a lot of people look pass. Regret taking this class and I'm way too scared to find out what my grade is. uncurved

if you decide to take this class BE PREPARED TO MEMORIZE SIGNIFICANT AMOUNTS OF INFO. The exams are solely based on lecture material (there is no textbook & the lectures are EXTREMELY DETAILED). The exams are also very detailed! The class is very time-consuming and you will spend hours studying every week. THERE IS NO CURVE!
Not any easy class at all. So many mindless details that are impossible to remember. She's an awful professor and the class should be curved. Everyone I know got a C

do NOT take this class, i was duped by the reviews. o'brien has no deeper understanding of the material, she just robotically reads her ppts & freezes up if anyone asks a question. there is no common thread or logical flow that would exist if the prof knew the content. she stuffs nonsense into her slides & tests on insignificant details. GPA killer
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Kim was fantastic! From my understanding, the Honors section of PSY 379 is much easier, but regardless, she's a great professor and very knowledgeable about everything health-related. She's one of those professors you could go to with serious problems and she'd help you out anyway possible. Definitely take her.

Great professor. She is very straightforward and makes it very clear what is expected of you from the class. Tests you on what is on her powerpoints and has weekly quizzes so that you keep up with the class. Definitely a lot of memorization required but she makes it manageable!

I met with her outside class and she may be the kindest professor at Cornell. I don't know why every one is complaining that it's to easy, she genuinely wants us all to do well, and really what lecture of 400 kids isn't boring? People need to stop finding things to complain about, I loved Dr. O'Brien.

Class is based entirely on memorizing what's written on her powerpoint slides, so there's no educational reason for attending class.  However, she does try to make you come by having weekly quizzes and daily clicker questions.  It's a good class for pre-meds, but it's definitely dull and only for those who can handle lots of memorization.

Easiest science class I have taken.  A lot of memorization involved, but if you do the work the quizzes and tests are really easy.  Lecture is pretty boring and unneccesary because she reads straight from slides.  Don't need to read the book.  Be aware, she makes some mistakes on slides and in lectures! Class helps a lot for the MCAT

She is not the most exciting lecturer but she provides the info that she needs to in a big lecture format. You can print out the lectures. Her quiz questions & most the exam questions are straight forward. GUEST LECTURES SUCK. If you have taken A&P before this, it is a breeze. If she is unclear, she is very willing to go over/clarify.

Professor makes the nutrition department seem like a joke.  She should be prohibited from ever teaching again.  I agree with the person below; she uses Wikipedia for EVERYTHING!  This illustrates the true competency of this monotone robot.
This professor is like a talking wikipedia with the capacity to generate quizzes and exams out of her a**.

Professor O'Brien was great. I do agree that there were times when she was not as clear as she could have been but if you needed help she would have gone over it with you. I thought the weekly quizzes helped alot, they were made so that we'd keep up with chapters. Please take this class if you can, alot of memorization but so worth it O'Brien ROCKS

class has a lot of potential to be really good but the prof makes everything so dumbed down and boring i felt like she inhibited my learning. once a week quizzes and lectures with clicker questions make it worse. take the lab too if you can, it makes it more interesting.

The most painful 50 minutes of my life. I wish she would read this and stop being so boring. We learned 1/2 the stuff in 115. I don't think anyone in lecture pays attention long enough to hear the end of her run-on pointless repetitive sentences. Should stick to research and far away from students

Not the brightest crayon in the box...besides being a ppt drone, she says the dumbest things sometimes...the quizes are about 7th grade level...not that i'm complaining at cornell, but she could step it up and curve the class instead. and emphasizes the most bizarre disorders/tangents. completely ruins the course.

First class taught here(?)...and powerpoint drone. Some professors can work the powerpoint without making you want to gouge your eyes out, but this 3x week lecture plus weekly quizzes, lab practicals, prelabs, postlabs and prelims sucks. The prof is nice, but just a REALLY POOR LECTURER.

Super nice. class is graded on completion. Very good lectures and makes me excited to show up to a class in my least favorite subject. would definitely reccomend, although there's a lot of reading and watching films.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: She leads discussions that are very in depth and insightful. The pieces are all very interesting! Your whole grade is on completion, and the format of the reading reflections makes it very flexible to fit in your schedule. Also gives a LOT of feedback on everything and cares about you as a student.

One of the few classes I've felt fully immersed into when going to class. Participation is a large part of class which became very productive over time helping me learn how to look at material differently. Grading based on criteria and improving, so it becomes a class you can enjoy material for instead of stressing your grade. Great teacher!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She is very nice, who encourages you to answer questions and participate in class discussions. The class atmosphere is chill and respectful. She grades you based on completion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: She's really nice and grades based on personal improvement and completion. Classes include a lot of close reading, working with peers, and discussion.

Prelims and final are just like the practices, content is easy but sometimes explained more complicated than it needs to be. HW is online and very easy. A bit of a boring lecturer and pollev attendance, everything you need to know is on the slides so lecture is not really helpful

Caring and kind professor. Funny and exciting lectures with a focus on applications. Very active, lots of polling questions. Group project with randomly assigned peers is very important to grade. Psets and quizzes are light; exams are not. Make sure you have a good cheat sheet and know how to use the stats function on your calculator.

Orlov is very disorganized as a professor - materials were posted late and exams were graded extremely slowly. This made the class a headache. He also created a weird testing scheme when the prelim grades came in really low - blamed the students instead of his teaching/organization. Would not recommend.
Great professor! Taught well and posted slides. Attendance is mandatory but not really (pollev). Don't need to read textbook ever. Tests very similar to practice prelim.

PollEv was kinda annoying, but other than that, he was a super chill prof who had some fun references in his exams. His lectures really told you everything you needed to know about the exams, and the slides were my best friend. One or two things seemed subjective on exams, however.

Horrible lecturer, overcomplicates very simple topics to the point where you have no idea what he's talking about. Posts slides onto canvas but they do not help. Get ready to read the entire textbook if you want to know what's going on. Also assigns way too many useless homework assignments a week (50+ questions), and the prelims are difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I think his a good lecturer. Sometimes in class he overcomplicates simple concepts, which I think bars him from being an outstanding and great one, but overall he is a good professor and person overall.

It can be a confusing course, and in Orlov's lectures, you need to pay attention to little things and the interaction between topics. You can miss up to 6 classes without losing attendance points, but sometimes it takes a while for lecture/discussion slides and lecture recordings to be uploaded. Two midterms and a final based on practice prelims.

He was my lab instructor and miscalculated my total grade back in 2015, which became a source of long-lasting frustration for me. 

I still remember how proud he seemed of himself, and how he carried that unnecessary arrogance during lab sessions. 

I feel justified making this comment now because I am currently a PhD candidate.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Orlov isn't a bad person but he's not the best lecturer. He tends to overcomplicate every topic and for someone who doesn't know anything about economics this was a really hard course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Funniest professor I've had, he literally turned office hours into stand-up. But his tests? Pure evil. Compared to other profs, it felt like we were prepping for the MCAT. I went to almost every office hour, gave it my all, and still somehow got wrecked. 10/10 for vibes, 2/10 for my GPA.

Has the greatest slides to help study-- literally just read them through and review and you will do fine on exams. He also provides great practice materials before exams they are pretty much exactly like the real thing.

Orlov gets a lot of unjustified hate. As long as you actually go to class, the material is super understandable. He genuinely cares about making sure students know the content and his slides are very thorough. He also provides plenty of extra resources and ample help hours for extra practice. The tests are exactly like the practice exams.

Orlov is a good lecturer and has very clear slides. If you go to lecture and pay attention, you'll know the material. He provides practice exams that are basically exactly what's on the actual exam and are super helpful for studying. The median grades on exams tend to be pretty high as well.

Professor Orlov's class is slightly difficult and does require some level of attention. If you actually read the textbook and read the slides, you should not have much of an issue with this class. Additionally Professor Orlov, is always willing to answer questions if any confusion arises.

Professor Orlov's class is honestly not very difficult if you go to the lectures, or even if you just look at the notes. He also makes himself very available and wants to help you learn. I took AP Macro in high school and found that the class was very similar to that, and I honestly just studied the slides and did well on the exams

Bro's slides might be the best slides I've ever seen in my life. His lectures are pretty good, but if you're still confused by something his slides literally go over everything step by step. Even though the upper level Econs get way harder, this class made me want to be an Econ major and I don't regret it.

Professor Orlov is one of two microeconomics professors in the semester I took this class. After hearing about the other class (which was primarily online), I feel as though my foundation in microeconomics is a lot stronger than my peers who took the other professor. He also curves each exam to make the median a B. Extra credit at end.

Professor Orlov is an amazing educator as long as you attend lectures/discussions and study for the prelims using his practice exams (they are very similar to the real prelims). Also, he takes attendance using pollev for every class so be aware (but he allows 6 absences).

His lectures are extremely organized and concise. His lecture slides contain everything he discusses almost for verbatim. As long as you go to class or read through the slides before the prelims you are going to do well. People who say he is a bad Prof or the class is hard probably put in almost zero effort because I did basically the bare minimum.
Very disorganized class, difficult to understand, test-heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good slides that are easy to learn from outside of class, and so helpful for studying for exams so you don't have to take notes. His prelims were fair and representative of the practice prelims. Only issue is that in my experience Ed Stem is not a good way to reach him, if you have questions go to office hours or ask right after lecture.
Good lecturer and engaging. I left with a good understanding of microeconomics and helpful slides to look back on. I also really liked the textbook he used.

He is definitely a very nice/caring person, but the exams (which makes up a large percentage of your grade) can be tough if you don't study the right things. Textbook was sort of helpful, but I would say the practice exams were the best way to learn.

Pros: caring/respectful, wants students to succeed + gain a thorough understanding, extra credit, several top-notch TAs, useful/challenging practice prelims

Cons: HWs r good GPA boosters but long/not super useful 4 prelims, provides confusing/long-winded explanations in OH, can't go into the class w/out knowing Econ, some terrible TAs

Orlov is actually very nice AND I do think I have an extremely thorough knowledge of micro econ after taking the class. So if learning is important to you, then you'll like this class. But it's graded off of very few things and prelims took an extremely long amount of time to grade. Ur gonna be stressed about the final regardless of current grade
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Can definitely do well in this class if you have a baseline knowledge of microeconomics and study the lectures/practice tests very well. I would say it was one of the harder classes, but it is very doable. He's an extremely nice person and very excited about what he teaches, but maybe look elsewhere if you are focused on getting a good grade.

You'll have to study and know his materials well. he offers tons of out of class opportunities for you to study though. Literally every day of the week before the final there was office hours. hard class but afterwards I really feel like I understand the material significantly better, and he did a great job. for an easy A, take a different prof.

Receives more hate than necessary. Prelims and Finals were very similar to practice tests, and everyone could definitely get an A if they prepared well for them. Annoying amount of homework and required participation, but really not bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Orlov is amazing!!! I don't know why people have so many complaints. He provides accessible resources to succeed on the prelim and finals. He doesn't do open note exams so students are forced to learn the material. Thank god professors like him still exist. 100% recommend this class if you want a solid foundation in Microeconomics.

Professor Orlov is okay. If you have to take him, take him. But beware of a stringent attendance policy and lectures that can be likened most closely to sonic Xanax. He is not too strict gradewise, but his sections are led by soulless PhD candidates and he can never seem to settle on OH timing, making accessing help harder. Overall, not worth $44k

Orlov is nice, but that's it. For 1 thing, the other micro class has all online exams which makes Orlov's class so frustrating. 2 prelim + 1 finals = 80% of grade, course assistants are clueless, and the prelims take MONTHS to grade. Writing this on Christmas Eve and still don't know my final grade! Orlov is ok but get Thomas if possible

He is not as bad a lot of ppl say he is. He's a nice guy, very accessible and he explains stuff ok; he could be a little more clear sometimes. The class is not that hard; the exams are pretty similar to the practice ones. His voice did make me want to fall asleep sometimes since it was a 9am. This is coming from an engineer.

Orlov is a great guy, and very willing to answer questions if you approach him after lecture. Class is very organized/slides are posted regularly. Little HW, so 80% of the grade is based on exams, which were moderately challenging but similar to the practice ones. Class size is ~600, so if you want support you have to go out of your way to get it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Graded based off lecture participation because he knew that if he didn't, nobody would show up to those crappy lectures. Spoke as if it's middle school, would get super pissed at people for getting up and leaving the lecture hall early. "The bell doesn't dismiss you, I do" type of guy.
Nice professor with extremely clear slides. Didn't like how attendance was mandatory, enjoyed the pop cultures references on exams.

This man's lectures make 0 sense but are mandatory to attend. You have to teach yourself the entire course and there's always something on the tests he only went over one time or not at all. Never take this class.
Lectures don't help and the whole grade is based on exams and final. Hard exams and hard final because he struggles to teach.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Orlov has incredibly clear lecture slides and seems to generally be a nice person. However, he is not great at teaching the material and he assigns a ridiculous amount of homework. The homework is also very different to what is tested on the prelim. Avoid taking him as an instructor if at all possible.

Little homework, 6 absences allowed before your grade drops- but even then it barely takes any percentage off. Exams are exactly like practice prelim and are not that hard. Lecture slides are clear. Passionate lecturer too

Orlov is a nice guy who cares about his students. The only complaint I have for his class is that attendance is tracked and pre lim two was so hard. Considering Thomas has open note exams I would take her

Take with caution. Prof. is nice but he doesn't teach the material well. His slides are long & not everything is on the exams. He doesn't take extra time to teach the most important problems. He should show us how to construct the graphs step-by-step, but he doesn't, and instead just shows pictures on slides. Students need guidance- he lacks this.

No cheat sheet on exam is really really really annoying............
Mandatory attendance is also really really really annoying........
One practice prelim is not enough as well

Take Sanders or Thomas-- I've heard from other students that they allow cheat sheets and you can take exams online. We had no cheat sheets and IRL exams. 

He was enthusiastic and knowledgeable but could not convey information well. Lovely guy, terrible lecturer.

He was fine. Not the best lecturer but not bad. Exams were a little harder than I thought they should be but not terrible. Homeworks were fine. Attendance policy was annoying. He's really nice and enthusiastic about the content just not the best at explaining things sometimes.

Pretty clear in his lectures, only 2 prelims & 1 final so exams are 85% of your grade but he gives 2 options. Class avg is a B+ I think, he gives practice final pdfs, & lots of office hours. Lowest 3 hws are dropped, pollev for participation each class. Exams are fair but can be tricky so study the slides. At the end, he offers extra credit

bro is kinda the goat, go to office hours if you're struggling since the class does move fast. offers extra credit questions on every test that're easy if you go to lecture as well as a 5% ish curve, class median was a B+ I think
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
I've loved Orlov as a professor.
I've taken his micro & macro intro classes, and I loved the way he structured the course. He always gave a review class day and a class off before a prelim, which I appreciated. Tbh his lectures were not super helpful for me, especially at 9am, but the HW helped reinforce the topics I'd need for the prelims.

By far, the most difficult economics course I have taken this far. The content itself is not terribly difficult, but he moves through it at a rapid pace. He does have an accent which makes certain things difficult to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Okay so Professor Orlov is a really nice guy who is clearly trying his best to provide a good experience for his students. Despite this effort, he teaches introductory macroeconomics like it's a 6000 level graduate course. Difficult subject matter that goes beyond basic Econ, tests are ridiculous, homework is overwhelming, and the list goes on.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The prelims are horrendous; 20 questions valued at 5 points each. You miss two and that is a whole letter grade down. He is a nice person but terrible professor. He goes through 10 slides in a matter of seconds. Worst professor I have had, not even Stephanie Thomas was this bad. His class will make you wish you never enrolled.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Orlov is a great human being, and he is one of the kindest Professors I have ever had. With that being said, the prelims were ridiculous. The median is far below other macro professors, and the lectures can be quite hard to follow. I never left class understanding what I was doing. Best of luck.

Orlov is a great lecturer. While many say otherwise, the way he treats lectures is more of a supplement to the textbook. Light workload and a lot of practice tests. Orlov even cares about keeping the same grade distribution from previous years. Man is trying his best.

Unstructured and not engaging. extremely low median exam score for prelims (which make up most of your grade in the class). I did better on the exams when I read the textbook on my own and stopped caring for the lecture. Discouraging class to take, but it's an intro class and requirement for so many people so you just have to bear with it.
If you want to take a class where you are given absolutely no guidance and have to teach all of the material to yourself, Orlov is the professor for you to take.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While the class doesn't have a ridiculous workload, he's a terrible professor and his lectures are painful to sit through. Theres weekly hw with large textbook readings, and I'd be ok with this if I felt it prepared me for the prelims, yet the class average on our first prelim was a 71, a ridiculous grade for an introduction class with 400 people.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Smart guy who was super nice. If you struggle in Econ I suggest you take this class because he is always willing to help. Also gives out chips and snacks during the late night class. Graded on attendance so super easy A

I'd definitely recommend taking Prof. Orlov's class. Be aware that ECON 1120 is lecture heavy and there will be mandatory attendance as well as hefty homeworks 1x week. 

That being said, it's pretty obvious he wants his students to succeed. He makes himself extremely available and will go over material in class to ensure a thorough understanding.
Extremely tough grader, but funny and engaging lectures.

Professor Reed is an outstanding professor. She is very knowledgeable in her field. Be willing to put in the work. Show effort, commitment, and discipline. Don't be afraid of making mistake.  Get out of your comfort zone and take initiative. I highly recommend Professor Reed to anyone.
Rate my professor scared me but she is amazing
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

I would rather take my chances in hand to hand combat with a grizzly bear than ever have to deal with her unsufferable attitude towards her students again. She is part of the reason the hotel school's applicants are decreasing, get rid of her and her latex gloves immediately.

One of the worst professors I have ever had. She has such an unorganized canvas she contradicts herself almost every day. Really great professor. Has a bad rep but cares a lot about teaching. If you go to class and do the homework you will do well in her course. Great lecturer
Great teacher. Going in, I thought she was going to be horrible and I was very scared but it was the complete opposite. Very caring professor who wants her students to succeed.

Not sure if she has changed or what happened but just took her course and had a great experience. Really cares a lot about her students, very reasonable, and very passionate about teaching. Overall, great professor and great course. If you do the homework, show up to class, and participate you will do well in this course.
she was so bad, i want to give her a 0, but that's not possible, so i give her a 1.

She is the WORST teacher I've had in my entire life. Lectures are absolutely idiotic, I learned nothing in this class. She grades like a mad woman. reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is impossible to do well in. Only take it if you like to cry. Prepare to have your spirit decimated, your motivation demolished, and your will to live diminished. I genuinely wonder if she is aware that we take multiple other classes. Atrocious, merciless, insufferable, mental-breakdown-inducing, brutal, cruel, unrelenting, unendurable, overwhelming. HEINOUS&distressing. Makes me need to double up on my antidepressants. I would rather dry swallow a handful of nails than ever take a class with her again. She believes this is your only commitment. Assignment grading is crazy, impossible to get a good grade. Turnaround time for assignments is deeply unreasonable.

This professor is one of the worst professors in the hotel school. She lacks any empathy for her students and expects them to treat this one class as their only priority. reviews.comment: She is the literal worst. Required in-person meetings on the weekends, even though she can't be bothered to come to class in person herself. Cruel!

Peggy is the WORST professor in the hotel school. She has made multiple people cry in class and seems to go out of her way to make her students depressed. This woman made me cry 3 times in one week. She is unrelenting. reviews.comment: not the best

I really enjoyed doing this class with Professor Ozanne. She is very kind, caring considerate and teaches well. i truly learnt a lot from this class that is not just restaurant or F&B related but for life.  There are 2 prelims in class which are failry straightforward but the calcutions and math part of class gets very tricky
Great professor, very approachable, she is truly passionate about the subject and classes are engaging.
Great person, great teacher. I was not interested in food and beverage when I came into this class. Left the class somewhat interested in it. Nothing but great things to say about her

I had her at 8:40 a.m. in Spring '25. Honestly, she has so much more energy in the morning compared to her students. If you have any concerns, like problems with a groupmate or something you do not understand, she will take the time to help and explain. The prelim is straightforward if you read carefully and do the practice test.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: she cares about her students and she really likes the subject. however, she's french...

Prof Ozanne cares about what she teaches and makes every class interesting, even at 8:40 in the morning. The grading is fair, and the prelims are pretty straightforward if you put in the time to study. She's also super approachable and helped me figure out what kind of internships to look for. Would definitely take her again.

You can tell that she is very passionate about F&B. Her prelims were all really fair. Everything she told us to study for (during our review lecture) was on the prelim and nothing more. There was a slight problem with wording in a few of her questions but other than that her class is very doable.
Incredibly boring lectures. Would not take again

I had her in Spring 24. She is very approchable, and she gave me great advice for my intership during office hours. Lectures may be heavy, lots of content, but a great prof and a useful course if you want to work in the F&B industry.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Ozanne is a TOUGH grader, with a lot of content expected per assignment and a large amount of time dedicated to her work. However, she is incredibly clear with what she wants and is very good at explaining the breadth of topics in her class. Be prepared to read, as every lecture has a reading and quiz associated with it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Ozanne was great. While this was only the second semester HADM 1361 was taught and the first taught by Professor Ozanne there was not a lot of feelings about being guinea pigs. Overall Professor Ozanne was great and would be happy to have her again.

Prof Ozanne shows that she truly cares about her students and their learning. I honestly learned a lot this semester and I am already applying some of the concepts seen in class at work. There is some work to put in but nothing unmanageable.
She is a nice lady but a terrible professor. Lectures aren't engaging and are incredibly boring, get prepared for knowledge quizzes every class.

Easy class, great professor, provides extra credit and tests are fair. I had her during the coronavirus when things switched online. The first half of the year there was barely homework besides readings, she does clicker questions, and the prelims are straightforward. During corona she gave a lot of work but it was easy

Professor O'Donoghue is an outstanding professor, and his lectures were always engaging. Homework and exams were challenging, but if you focus on understanding the intuition behind the concepts, you should be fine. Lastly, his passion for the material clearly comes across in class, which made learning the material enjoyable and thought-provoking.

This is one of the most interesting and rewarding classes I have taken in the econ major. O'Donoghue is truly at the forefront of this field and often cites his own research which is fascinating. Very difficult course, but lectures are amazing and p-sets and exams are fair if you are keeping up. Would highly recommend for all majors.

O'Donoghue is kind, knowledgeable, and engaging. Behavioral economics is not an easy course, but O'Donoghue articulates concepts clearly and provides lots of materials to help. Highly recommend! Just make sure your schedule isn't too overwhelming when you add 4660 - there's a lot of material.

Took in Fall 2020. Best econ class I took at Cornell. Best mix of interesting content, fair hws and tests, and great teaching. Class is more "mathematical/theoretical", but Ted is fantastic at explaining it all. He's also very approachable and caring, and I appreciated that he put in extra effort to deal with the circumstances at the time. GOAT.
Loved this class. Really interesting material and the math/econ basis isn't difficult. Cool concepts and a great lecturer.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. AEM 2020/PSYCH 2940 was so difficult for no reason. Prelims and the final are 100% of your grade and the tests are extremely hard. For a class that does not even count towards your major, it is not worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are extremely clear and is very willing to engage with students and answer questions. Despite his ability to explain the concepts very thoroughly and make the content look easy, the material itself is pretty challenging. Tests are challenging but not unreasonable. Definitely take a course with prof OD if you get the chance.

By far the best prof I have had at Cornell! Behavioral Economics was amazing, and his lectures were fascinating. I wish more professors were like him. The class is exactly the right amount of work, and Prof Odonoghue is very accessible during office hours.

Despite the difficulty of the course, Professor O'Donoghue makes his slides very clear and concise. He explains everything in plain language and gives constant reminders on previous materials/terms/equations to jog your memory unlike other professors who just put a bunch symbols without clearly explaining. He is the definition of a good professor.

Literally defines what a professor should be like. I'm doing better in this class than other "easier" classes I'm taking, largely due to how thorough and clear his (actually pretty difficult) lectures are.

The best professor I've had at Cornell so faramazing and engaging lecturer, super accommodating and really organized, makes complicated topics seem easy, and literally one of the top academics in the field of behavioral economics. Definitely take one of his classes if you're an Econ major, he's so great :)

Extremely organized and handled the logistics of this 5-professor course. Super clear in explaining concepts and satisfyingly concise slides. I had no prior econ education but still managed to understand everything. Also helpful during office hours: an incredibly intelligent professor!

Professor O'Donoghue is a pretty good lecturer. When speaking about the material he makes it seem so simple. Only thing is, it's not. This class requires a lot of intuition thinking. Nothing like you've probably learned about in your intro econ courses. Problem sets are fairly short but office hours are key to doing well on them.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The course was really interesting, the exams are challenging though and grades are curved such that the median is a B+. The prof was quite engaging, sections are optional

Awesome professor, again, probably the best I have had in all my econ classes. His lectures are exceptionally clear, which is great, but also kinda makes other professors' lectures seem really not-on-par. The materials are definitely not easy, and going to lectures actually help you learn better.
Awesome! Awesome! Awesome!

Probably the best Econ prof. at Cornell. The class is def. not easy, but if you pay attention in class, work hard on the PSets, and go to office hours, you should be fine. Sections were pointless though, and there is no textbook, but his crystal clear lectures are enough to do well. Would def. recommend this for econ majors

Love this class! Lots of interesting subjects covered, and he certainly knows his material. Even though he posts the slides online, it's recommended to go to class because he shows you how to set up problems (which does not end up the powerpoint). He's also a fairly engaging lecturer. Try your best to do the problem sets without help.

Lecture stuff is online, though lecture will help you understand the slides better than just reading them online. He tests hard, but it's possible to do well if you assimilate to his testing style. PSets i dunno, didn't go to section

I thought the class was a bit boring, but others think it's really interesting.  The professor is very clear.  No textbook, his notes are online, and he gives you a number of problem sets that help you learn the material.  Tests are a bit difficult, but he'll scale grades upwards, so no worries there.

Solid professor and a really nice guy but a few points of caution about the course: the class is curved to a fairly low grade making it difficult to exceed an A- for anything but exceptional performance and possible to achieve a B or lower for decent work; the subject matter is inherently interesting but better dealt with in the realm of psychology

crystal clear lecture notes, posted on blackboard but you have to attend class to get his important additions - no textbook, so you have to go. interesting lecturer, not boring at all and the subject is interesting. good class for fulfilling econ major .

Great lecturer. Very clear and willing to help, the subject material is incredibly interesting. There's no textbook for the class, however, and section was optional and not very helpful. Hence, going to every lecture was inherently mandatory and extremely vital to doing well. Just go to the twice-a-week lecture and you'll be fine.
I love this professor. IMO he is the best econ prof. I have had yet. Keep up the good work prof!

No, seriously, he is the best teacher in the econ department. VERY clear lectures. Light reading, hard problem sets that were graded harshly. Tests seemed fair. Overall grading policy is more than fair. EXTREMELY helpful in office hours - use them. Learned a lot. Must take!!
Best Professor in econ department. Very interesting topics, clear teaching, fair in assessing students' learning
Maybe the best instructor of economics at Cornell. Brilliant, helpful and great to talk to.
No Comments
Great professor. Difficult topics in Econ 302.
Pretty good professor. He gave a very clear teaching!!!
No Comments

He is pretty nice. Quizzes after every class can be rough at the beginning. The guest speakers are interesting, and there is barely HW. There are 2 time-consuming prelims, and quite a lot of reading & understanding for prelim prep. He's a fast email replier. Harsh grading, the final project brought my grade from A to B.
not understanding at all, very abrasive

He doesn't teach the class. Loved the guest lectures but if he's gonna have prelims in this class, they need to be based off guest lectures, not an external reading that makes no sense. Grading is so vague. Got a 60 on the first prelim and 80 on the 2nd one. This class should go back to being pass/fail. Students skipped anyway and chatted prelim.
This is the first time I've been motivated enough to write a review on a professor. Harsh grader, barely teaches, drove the whole freshman class insane. Just make sure you glaze him.

Preszler believes in learning through guest speakers who share experiences in the business world. The course is centered on the UN Sustainable Development Goals and wicked problems, forcing critical thinking about complex, real-world challenges. Prelims are based on out-of-class readings, and short quizzes follow each guest speaker for engagement.

reviews.comment: Bad professor, harsh grading and very unclear grading criteria. Professor does not teach himself, and relies solely on guest lectures. Prelims are based on material not covered during lectures. Reviews are accurate.

Professor is a narsacist. Very hypocritical when it comes to grading. Most people chatted his prelims. Does not curve at all. Final reflection assignments matters a ton (took me from an A to a B). This class should go back to being S/U.
Not good AT ALL. Intentionally grades harshly to get the class median grade down. Good luck all freshmen who have him.
Bald man. Bad man. Hurt my grade man. Bad tests man. Bad grading man.

Let me put in caveperson speak so clear. Much read. Professor talk many word, say nothing. Sassy. Condescending. Self-center. Grade tough for fun. TA ridiculous. Guest speaker come. Worst class. Grades without clear guidelines and a clear curve down. Doesn't even teach as he relies solely on guest speakers.
Subjective grading without clear guidelines in the instructions.

His foundations class is an absolute joke. All Dyson freshmen are required to take this course and he grades way too harshly for someone who doesn't even teach. The class is just guest speakers who come in every class (aside from prelim days).

Professor appears nice. Speakers brought to class are all interesting and unique. Prelims are definitely rough, and readings can be challenging to understand. The small quizzes are difficult, depending on the speaker. The final presentation has strict guidelines, so make sure to meet every expectation.

Very caring person who is passionate about the course. Some guest lectures were more on the boring side but most were great. The prelims aren't too bad as long as you're a decent writer. The final presentation is easy and he seemed proud of everyone's work. He's also flexible with any conflicts that athletes or anyone have with the class.

Trent and Lennox taught this when I took it (Fall 2024), though it's changed since. The class had guest speakers (UN SDGs focused), and you could volunteer to host one (join their dinner). Easy course with reflection writing and mandatory attendance. Lectures were boring & people started to skip, so they added Poll Everywhere with location tracker.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The new 1101 is really hard, this was the first year attendance was mandatory. Quiz after each guest speaker, prelims are a little rough unless you study a ton for them. Do the readings ahead of time (but he doesn't assign it til a week before the prelim). He's a nice person but isn't the best teacher I've had.
Preszler is a narcissistic a-hole to some, or a great resource to others. participate and be engaged and you will have the latter relationship.

Preszler is a very nice guy who takes an active interest in student's work and puts a lot of effort into each lecture. For the class you have to write several essays which are graded very harshly and require lots of revision. This class does make you a better writer and you learn a lot, but only take if you have an interest in the subject matter.

Trent is a nice guy, but his Grand Challenges Writing course is incredibly hard. For the love of God, do not take his class. Compared to other grand writing courses, this is so much more work. Please do not do what I did. Save yourself and take another class.
I enjoy his classes but they are too theory-based. he doesn't ask students to remember historical events/examples but only definitions
He is my dad so like he is the best and everyone who said 1 star is lying and failed the class

Honestly, Pepinsky is pretty rude towards his students. I felt it was highly inappropriate when he screamed at students in front of a large lecture hall. (Stop taking my reviews down Pepinsky)
Class was not hard, did well. Just many better government teachers who are far more engaging and kind.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pepinsky is the goat, and this was probably my favorite class taken so far. Lectures are very engaging and well structured, and the content is interesting. You can easily tell Pepinsky loves what he teaches and is very welcoming in class and office hours. A lot of readings but not any more than most other govt classes. Highly recommend :)

Professor Pepinsky is an excellent lecturer, and one of the best in the government department here at Cornell. His lectures are clear and organized, focusing on a particular theme or subject. Just be aware that he doesn't post his lecture slides on Canvas. Exams are fair, and students are allowed to bring a cheat sheet the size of an index card.

GOVT 3443 is not an "easy" class to put on your schedule. It covers a lot of content and comes down to basically two prelims and a final paper. Attendance is "not mandatory," but slides are not posted, so if you don't show up you will not do good in this class. If you find this topic interesting, go for it. It's fun, deep, and very interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely knowledgable about his area of expertise

Professor Pepinsky clearly cares about the subject and ensuring that his students succeed. VERY knowledgeable. Fair warning, he is extremely lecture-heavy, and slides are not posted after class. Though attendance is not required, it is necessary if you want an A range grade. Lecture, reading, and section material are all fair game on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not take this class. Professor is rude and inconsiderate of his students. Felt like he had a superiority complex over Cornell kids because he went to Harvard. No text on the slides and refused to post them online- hard to take notes. And then exam content was solely based on lecture. Overall lectures were extremely boring and hard to follow.

Lectures can be pretty boring, but definitely do attend them because there are no online versions. He's pretty funny and has a great personality though. Tests aren't that bad, just review well, especially focus on lectures in my opinion. Haven't gone to office hours, but he seems like he really cares about his students. Good personality and nice.

Lectures matter quite a bit. They can be difficult to understand or boring because of the content, but Pepinsky makes things as clear as possible, and has great energy. Maybe my favorite lecturer I've had at Cornell.

Prof. Pepinsky is a great lecturer, he is clearly very passionate about the subject and is very prepared and organized for his lecture. He also knows a great deal about SE Asia. I also like how he deliberately gives examples from all parts of the world for concepts.

Though, his grading is really tough, and the readings can be overwhelming.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Essays graded too heavily

Professor Pepinsky is amazing! Even as a STEM major, I found the material super engaging. Attendance is not mandatory but you HAVE to show up. Prelim and final MCQs are 98% lecture-based. The two papers are easy and your TA grades them. Cons are the heavy reading (60 pgs/week) and little grade flexibility (missing one check-in can tank your grade).

Difficult tests that make it impossible to come back from a single mediocre score and lectures that you have to fight to stay awake for. Very little content is even covered in the mandatory lectures and most of the interesting material is in the readings.
an extremely boring class

Pepinsky as a lecturer is near perfect. He is incredibly knowledgable, doesn't go off on tangents (too often at least), and passionate. Also, I'm leaving the class feeling like I learned lots. Grades depend on TAs and try to follow formats asked. You'll be graded harshly. Make sure to come to class every time or have a friend who takes great notes.

Professor Pepsinky is great professor and probably the best I've had at Cornell. The class is not easy, but it is very fair and rewarding to people who show up to class and put in effort. Great lecture style and he is very engaging, I never got bored in class. Highly recommend
very hard dont take

Before Pepinsky, GOVT 1313 was supposed to be an incredibly easy introductory class for the major. Now it's quite difficult, tests/papers graded harshly, dense lectures(if you miss lecture it is near impossible to make up the material). That being said, Pepinsky himself is a great lecturer/professor. But take any other required intro GOVT class.

Professor Pepinsky is AWESOME. I learned a ton about Southeast Asia despite being from there myself, and even with the abundance of information I still felt like I had agency in forming my own thoughts. I looked forward to every lecture despite them being held during sleepy afternoons because they are that good, and I'm not even a government major!

The two classes I've done with Pepinsky are hands-down the best I've taken at Cornell over three years. He is so superb that his recalcitrance to give flat A's can and should be overlooked. Clearly one of the best Profs at Cornell and I would sign up for any class he teaches, regardless of subject. He is that good.
Probably one of the best professors at Cornell. He is very knowledgeable and makes the classes very interesting and clear. This is one of the classes where Ive learned the most, would take it again!

Lectures can get heavy on history, but are always relevant as knowledge to use to analyse political situations. There is a strong emphasis on comparative method and he sells the class well to people uninterested in Southeast Asia. Does a great job at being neutral during lecture.

The professor is smart and approachable. He apparently knows his stuff very well and tries to involve students in discussions during lectures. But overall it is a hard class especially if you do not have an economic background.

Recommended: take Intro Micro before taking this class - it will make the more technical readings in this class a lot more clear, but Prof Pepinsky does a great job of walking you through the most important takeaway points. A great lecturer, and brilliant mind.

Class was Politics and Markets. Good professor, can come off a bit full of himself but not in a terrible way. Definitely will learn a lot. Does not ever post lecture slides so basically have to attend class.
One of the best lecturers I've had. Interesting and clear. But a hard class...

He's a very good lecturer.  Even for people who have no general knowledge about Southeast Asia, this class is still exciting and interesting.  Definitely take his class!  As for grading - I believe it was rather fair.  But then again, I took this class in 09.

Great professor who is very willing to help students and improve the class experience. Class discussions are always interesting. Workload is definitely managable. Very reasonable grader-ask him for advice if necessary, he is very approachable. You will learn a lot from this class!

Very clear and easy to follow. Leads interesting classes. He's very into Southeast Asia and Economics, so even though you don't need to have any background, its good to know some stuff on economics. If you don't, it'll be a little tougher, but he explains things very well, and you'll be able to follow. If you do the work, you'll do well.
Pepinsky knows and loves Southeast Asia. Lectures were organized and interesting, and assignments were straightforward and fair. A bit of a hard grader, but study and you can do fine.

I was hesitant to take SPAN 2205 at first, but the lively discussions Pr. Pinet facilitated made it my favorite class this spring. She grades fairly, and while there is a lot of reading, the overall course load is still pretty light (3 in-class mini-essays + 1 presentation). Pr. Pinet, if you're reading this, ¡gracias por un semestre increíble!

I didn't enjoy any second I spent in this class. TA wasn't good at all; he was honestly pretty rude and didn't listen to students' opinions ever. Felt neglected the entire semester, happy to walk out of there with an A.

How fascinating. According to our favorite AI tool, "there are some red flags in the positive reviews that suggest possible self-representation: repeated phrasing across multiple top reviews, highly balanced and polished tone, and specific mentions of course code and warnings about others' negative reviews." Simone isn't fooling us.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Anyone who has had Simone would know that she never goes over readings. You are required to memorize tiny, insignificant details of 300+ pages for each lecture and she proceeds to ask questions (in a severe patronizing tone). Simone regularly makes inappropriate jokes that reflect her complete lack of professionalism & even basic academic decorum.

I was scared when I first saw her RMP reviews but after taking her class I couldn't disagree more. She knows her stuff but would allow the class to have great discussions and also giving us her input. The class is very reading-heavy but she goes over readings during class. Be sure to participate and do the readings and you'll be good!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's rude to the class and acts like teaching is a waste of her time. She does not seem to like her job and will take it out on the class. Stay away.

Where does one even begin? Simone's tantrums would make a screaming five-year old seem perfectly well-behaved. Her directions are often vague and she gets annoyed if you ask for simple clarifications. One time, she screamed at the entire class and then threw us out because she was not happy with the way we were answering her overly obtuse question.

My roommate got COVID and I was a couple minutes late to a scheduled meeting I had with Simone. She immediately insulted me and proceeded to tell me how she is "very, very good at [her] job" and doesn't need to be "wasting [her] time" meeting with me. Well, she gets a 0/5 rating for that!
If you're a minority student, run away.

What a waste of my tuition money. Lectures were torture because S Pinet cannot build strong classroom discussions other than her letting her minions say really banal things. Will fulfill my requirements with other professors who can at least make lectures insightful.
This professor is a potential Title IX field of land mines. Be aware.
Simone was vindictive and petty towards her students of color. Almost unhinged at times.
