Was the comment that students saw professor Pinet write her own positive reviews during office hours removed?
I dropped her class. I was very uncomfortable how she talked to some of the students.

Takes attendance in every lecture. Then Simone asks the same: "Leyeron?" Bad question considering that it doesn't really matter because she only wants to hear you basically quoting her. Simone doesn't want to hear any original ideas. AVOID HER... a hyena would do a better job teaching SPAN2170 and without being so hostile.

Literally my favorite Spanish teacher and my favorite Spanish class that I have ever taken. She is so passionate. The homework is super light, and we have weekly reflection papers. That is it! I loved the class with my whole heart and plan on taking her senior seminar last year.
I can talk all day of the profound contempt this professor has for all her students of color.
Not a particularly nice person or teacher

I love how even the supposedly positive comments here have a crap ton of dislikes because NO ONE believes this professor is remotely capable of teaching a decent class where ever single one of us felt the tiniest bit comfortable

Her class was a very disappointing experience. Definitely left a bitter taste in my mouth. Honestly, to succeed in this class youll have to be a grIng@. It's very obvious to all of us students. She doesnt hide it. Would not recommend any P0C to take a class with her.

It was a mediocre class. The lectures were very discussion-focused, so make sure to read the assignments before then in order to not be embarrassed by Simone. Also, avoid office hours at all costs. You'll regret it if you dont.
The reading material was sometimes boring, sometimes interesting. But Simone herself did not create an inclusive learning environment. I recommend taking the class with a TA
Simone is a pretty okay teacher. The class was fine and she's knowledgeable, but working with her on getting clarify for assignments was torturous.
Simone was great, I was timid in my speaking skills and had difficulty understanding so she checked in with me through office hours often and helped me understand the course curriculum.
Awful professor. Never disagree with her on anything. Her way or the highway!
Her teaching skills are questionable at best. Some of the readings contain very disturbing details.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I had. She is easy to approach and class with her is very enjoyable!

Simone is not only one of the smartest people I've ever met, but she is engaging, funny, and open to the ideas of her students. Out of all the Spanish courses I've taken, she's created the most comfortable environment for participation. I'm shocked by all these bad reviews; she's inspiring and down to earth despite her impressive qualifications.

If you want to learn something, take this class with Maria Antonia or another professor. Even if Simone spent 100 years on a remedial teaching journey, her hatred for students would prevent her from actually evolving into a somewhat decent instructor. She knows it too, hence all the self comments she is writing due to low enrollment in her courses.

Without a doubt one of the most memorable professors that I have had here at Cornell. Her background as a medievalist gives her a unique perspective and this, among other things, allowed me to connect the medieval period of Spanish history to that of contemporary Spain. In terms of the class, she gives a lot of creative freedom as well.

Simone is literally a bully in every sense of the word. She preys on young students.  Her relentless efforts to write positive reviews herself won't change every day reality. She lacks the respect of both students and faculty.
Simone is literally the best. She is a professor you will look back on 30 years from now and remember what she taught you.
Simone, aside from having written five books in different languages, is a passionate and caring professor. I love her and her classes!
Almost poked my eyes out! Simone's insecurity is only matched by her infinite hostility for her own students. Her lack of scholarly publications compared to other professors speaks for itself.

One of the best classes and professors at the university! Professor Pinet was always willing to help me improve my writing or just discuss class content. She made me think of certain ideas in such mind-blowing and new ways. Overall I really enjoyed this class.

Lectures aren't interactive as Simone only wants her favorites to talk in class even when they say things that lack basic analysis. Essays are fine and quite short in general. Simone does take attendance in every class, though.

She's an amazing teacher who is beyond nice and laid back. Of course, you need to try to some degree and a clear comprehension of Spanish is required. However, she makes the course enjoyable regardless of your skill level.

Simone is willing to help as long as you care and are passionate about the subject.  She is fair in her criteria and gives you the chance to succeed as long as you put in the effort.  As long as you participate the class should be fine!  One of my favorites so far at Cornell.
Simone may be hostile at times. Papers are simple and quite short. Just participate and you are guaranteed a decent grade.

Unsure as to what would be more painful... another twice-a-week class with Simone or or being eaten alive by a bull shark. Lectures are endless and she mocks you if you don't say exactly what she thinks is right. Write down everything she incoherently speaks and give it back on every essay. Forget other options if you want to pass.
Just awful. The worst professor I have had in my entire life. Mean, unclear and a total nightmare. Any interest I had in pursuing a minor was crushed by this class and this woman.

I loved Simone's perspectives class.  She taught a ton, and, as we were all interested in Spain as a country, it was fascinating.  We were always asking questions and getting amazing, thoughtful answers.  She set the tone for my time abroad, and I'm glad that I took her class.

Simone is the worst professor I have ever had. The only opinion that seems to matter to Simone is her own. If you do not agree with her, she will tear you apart. Although she is smart, this is clearly the wrong career for her.  Once you get on her bad side, it is impossible to get a good grade.

This is a required survey course for majors and not many professors teach it. I have fixed feelings about Simone. As a rule, it is best not to ever contradict her and to stay on her good side. Grades are entirely subjective but if you keep that in mind and don't argue with her, it's easy to get great marks.
No organization. No coherent style. No feedback. Simple assignments. Not many options for Spanish majors.

Simone takes Spanish Golden Age literature and introduces new and unexpected ways to view and interpret the texts. She understands the fact that this is only a survey course and doesn't expect gratuitous analysis of literary minutiae. Instead, she sets the groundwork for a working knowledge and appreciation of the texts covered in class.

The Spanish Golden Age is one of the most fascinating periods in literature. Simone, however, manages to bring to life the worst aspects of this period, as you feel that you are experiencing Cervantes' struggle--being kidnapped and hoping desperately that someone rescues you. In the end, it is not Simone's fault that she isn't professor material.

Simone took a class on a period of literature that has the potential to be really boring and makes it interesting and relatable. We even did trips to the Johnson museum and Rare Books library to look at manuscripts from the time period we were studying and art from that period. Very fair grading and overall a very good class.

this professor cursed me out in her office, saying that I was stupid, yelled at me, and told me to get out of her office (because I yawned). she is outright nasty, insecure, and got the job because of her husband, who once said in class, "as far as human ignorance is concerned", perhaps I will include myself". Need I say more?
Relies too much on weak classroom discussions based on whether she agrees or not. Be ready to hear the equivalent of "What do you guys think, what do you guys think?" all the time, which is annoying.
Painful elective. Simone imbues the worst of everyone in the class; however, if you write down everything she says and reproduce it on the essays, one can pull of an A or A- easily.
A tyrant like Simone will always find a pretext for her tyranny

Crazy woman. Loves to say: "I'm very, very good at what I do." Unfortunately, if that were true, everyone would know it and she wouldn't have to say it all the time. Her class is not that hard if you are on her good side.
Professor was out of control. She assumed we knew tons about Medieval Spanish Literature even before the class. Stay away at all costs.

Just finished her "Theater of Early Modern Spain" elective. Simone fails as a professor because she is teaching something she lacks passion for. Add to that her creepy personality and it's the longest 75-min lecture in which the best thing to do is to bring a bodyguard and pray for night fall.
I dropped this class after attending the third session yesterday. Can't imagine having someone so moody and dictatorial for a full semester.

Threw everyone out of class once because according to her no one read that day. Translation: if you get assigned over 100 pages a night, make sure you are able to recall every tiny detail. Otherwise, prepare to be thrown out of class after hearing a huge lecture on how you are not taking education seriously.

Don't try to learn anything. Bottom line, if you want to do well and not get harassed, tell her exactly what she wants to hear. Not too difficult if you pretend to agree with everything she spills outs.
this professor is terrible. she should get a different job.

Professor Pinet is too abrasive. SPANL 217 with her is similar to being on the Wizard of Oz and hearing "I'll get you, me pretty, and your little dog, too!" Like the previous poster mentioned, the books were plain gross, e.g. imagine reading about thieves who****innocent women and then cut their throats.

Simone's class is for anyone who enjoys reading books about pirates who make their victims eat fecal matter. Yes, really. The name of that book is "Naufragios" and it happens to be Simone's favourite. Appalling.

By its nature, Spanish literature is subjective! Come on. Leaving aside the previous poster's error--"to much," medieval Spanish lit with Simone is not demanding b/c she says the important things about each book. yes, it's true she only talked about Mexico a few times. Her major flaw was being too cocky and not having enough office hrs. OK overall.
To summarize the experience: "Give me another professor or give me death!"
No Comments
Pay attention to do well. AVOID creativity on essays. For the final exam, review notes. And, try to show interest in Mexican culture. That's all it takes. Eeeeaaaassssyyyy A.
Run away or pray for another person to teach this class
Never met such an insecure human being. The semester was wasted on bogus books... Probably the most boring stuff I have read. Ahhhhhhhhhhh!!!!!!

Expected grad level work even though it was SPANL 319. The less you ask, the better off you are. Anyone who comes across as intelligent is penalized. It is unacceptable for Cornell to hire such unprofessional staff.

One word: CHAOS. Simone made what was supposed to be an interesting course feel like you were burning within four walls. If you do not have a strong Spanish grammar background, forget about doing well, this prof didn't really have many office hours.
This woman is obnoxious. Don't ever contradict her. Avoid at all costs.
A moderately intelligent prof who seems to dislike most students

Funny how the previous student hit the nail right on its head. SPANL 319 had a distinct emphasis on Mexican works/culture. Not sure I would say Simone is "evil." In my experience other profs from the span lit dept have been nicer. Of course this doesnt mean she is terrible.

Had this professor for medieval spanish literature. Simone does not listen to a word you say. She was determined to prove her intelligence to the class, nothing else. good luck to her future students.

The class provides a biased point of view--Simone's; no other is tolerated. Most of us never understood why she became a college professor at Cornell when she kept talking about Harvard all semester long. The title for SPANL 319 should have been "From Bad to Worse to Hell."

Like most students, I experienced a terrible semester with Simone last spring. The only reason I ended up with an A- in the class was due to the endless hours I spent working on each essay. Hard classes do not scare me, but Simone is probably the rudest and most unpleasant professor I have had at Cornell. DO NOT enroll in any of her courses!

On average all 400-level courses at Cornell are pretty difficult, but Simone made the course a living hell that only got worse throughout the semester. She offered no help with the papers, and constantly reminded us that this was an advanced course and it was our responsibility. I pity anyone who takes a class with her, including myself.
Takes attendance on a daily basis, you cannot afford to miss class. Prof. Pinet talks way too fast sometimes. It's almost impossible to get a decent grade.
dont know anyone who likes her. class was a waste of my time. avoid

Grrr... surviving this class was a concern I had. Unfortunately, for SPANL 319 there aren't many options. Lectures seemed endless. The material itself was challenging, well maybe for me-- Spanish is not my native language. I did not ask Simone for help many times, but when I did, she was not very nice about it.
Ok class. Some of the novels were very interesting. Simone may not be the nicest professor in the department, but at least she has some original, capturing ideas from time to time. I have had worse.

Lots of banal books to read, none worth one's time. Simone is not very good following a complex idea, so she often attempts to mock her own students as the result of her lack of understanding. I'm happy that the class is over.

Granted, 16th and 17th-century spanish lit is hard to understand, but this class was just too much. Simone expects you to read at least 70 pages a night and be able to recall the most insignificant details from the novels. She knows her stuff, yet her animosity toward her own students creates an uncomfortable learning environment for everyone.

Well, I loved magical realism until I took this class. The instructor expects you to agree with all her ideas and if you don't, she will attempt to ridicule you. This class had no room for one's personal interpretation and theory. To make matters worse the class ended with a dull final paper assignment.

Glad to hear I'm not the only one who did not enjoy this class. As others mentioned, it's not the fact that papers are graded harshly as much as unfairly. Class itself was painful, and I actually like spanish lit.
Painful class & instructor
This class was a true nightmare, mostly due to the professor.

I haven't taken that many Spanish literature classes at Cornell, but I sure did not enjoy this one. The class lacks structure. The professor was never nice to us. The entire class had a very negative feeling. After 3 absences, your grade in the class will suffer.
Simone never offers any help to her students. Her essays are graded harshly. I should have taken this class with someone else.

In my three years at Cornell, this was the worst class and professor I have encountered. The readings were never interesting, class time was brutal. I wish I would have taken this class with another professor.
Worst professor ever. She is never available during office hours and one can never approach her. Avoid at all costs.
In one word, awful. She is highly disorganized and does not offer much help during office hours. Stay away from her SPANL 319 course.

Did not learn a single thing. Never taught in class, not once. Misinformed me about when the last day of class would be and made me miss a crucial assignment. Then when asked about it, her response was that she believed it didn't matter since I "wouldn't have done well on it anyway". None of my peers nor I took a single thing away from this class.
It was very hard to learn from her because of her language barrier, bad explanations in videos, and structure of class.

For how ever many supposed "degrees" she has, she actually might be one of the least competent profs I've ever met. She has zero common sense. She makes tests intentionally hard, tricky, & unfair. Just know that email-her and in-person-her are two completely separate personalities. Email version chooses violence. IRL version is sweet as pie.

Conniving. Her flipped classroom method is very ineffective. Class starts really easy and gets unimaginably complex very fast. She seems nice but don't be fooled, she's not. She doesn't know how to teach because she herself just finished school. Sections get treated differently, you'll see why. Just try to keep up and work with others

BS from Tsinghua; PhD from UC Berkeley. She's “nice,” but the flipped classroom feels like buz 💻, which is expected. No rubric, so assignments are unclear and feedback is vague (“minus 1 point for blah”). Individual and class assignments are tough; the curve spans all sections—think twice before sharing what's on the exam 🫵🫵🫵 no partial credit

Did not like the class structure. Professor Meng is very nice and accommodating, but you learn nothing from the class, even if you get a great grade. Sometimes the grading criteria are also a bit confusing, but overall not hard to get a good grade.

Flipped-classroom. You copy videos for homework, then do a harder version of the content in class. No explanation of the material. In-class TAs do not grade and cannot provide clear feedback or help, and the grading criteria is unclear. Students submit identical work and receive different scores. Assignments due @ the end of class. A waste of time.
You genuinely learn nothing
she's a nice person, but i genuinely learned nothing from her classes.

The class is flipped and you have to come to class with the model prepared. If you watch the video and/or read the notes before class you will do well in the class. The quizzes/prelims are open internet and are similar to the models used for the regular assignments. If you come prepared and do the bonus you will do very well.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Terrible teacher. Flipped class. All you need to do is copy what she does in the videos and you don't have to learn anything about statistics. She doesn't make her grading guidelines clear either.

Ernesto was the most laid back professor I've ever had and this was probably the most chill class I've ever taken. Also the second half of class you watch movies once a week and discuss the other day, final project is also a 5 min video on any topic you want. Goated class.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super laid-back. Classes with him are really relaxed. He points out great writing advice and tips I never knew about. He's just not too into fantasy writing and head's up: not good with remembering names. I've taken two classes with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Ernesto was my professor for True Stories (FWS). He is a great and will really work with students. He assigns few papers and gives good feedback. The class is about radical political movements in the US, and we sometimes watched movies and did light readings (less than 5 pgs). Would 10/10 recommend this class to anyone!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The fact that this is my first time giving a review here is testament to Ernesto's teaching ability. He's sharp, open-minded, funny, experimental, inspirational, and doesn't BS. He won't sugar-coat, but he will make you a better, more aware writer. And if he pulls you aside to encourage you to send your work out... you know you've made it :)
If you put in the work, you will do very well.
Friendly, but provides no useful feedback and no help improving work. Doesn't pay much attention. Easy grader but you learn nothing.

Didn't think creative writing was going to be this interesting.  Ernesto, and he never wants to be called professor, would play a film clip and then have us read a short story and lead us to see the same narrative techniques being used in fiction. Amazing!!!  He is very cute but he wears the same black shirt a lot.  Easy grader.
Interesting guy, extremely laid-back and passionate about the material he teaches. Dynamic, creative professor. Very easy grader.

Professor Qian worked with me on my doctoral thesis and is a lifesaver in every definition of the word. She was the main advisor for our research team and saved us so much time and energy on our projects. She helped us get our findings published, present at conferences, and advocated for us at every step of the way. Can't say enough about her.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: Probably the best professor at Cornell. She's a great mentor, accessible, and willing to work with you on every level. Taking her class redefined my entire life and career.
So great to have a professor that actually cares about their students. Her lectures changed my life.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment:
Dr. Qian is one of the most intellectually stimulating professors I've worked with at Cornell. She pushes us to question assumptions and find design solutions that are both elegant and ethical. She also genuinely cares about her students' growth. 

She gives tough feedback, but it's always constructive and deeply insightful.

Dr. Qian was definitely challenging, but she's incredibly supportive and always willing to talk through ideas or give thoughtful feedback.

By the end of the semester, I felt like I had leveled up as a designer and as a thinker. If you're ready to put in the work, she will absolutely meet you there and help you get the most out of the process.
She's the best professor I've ever had.

Loney is honest & funny, but MATH-1100's flipped format relies on a TERRIBLE textbook that sets students up for failure IMO. 

The real problem is grading--which is shared with Prof. Kaminski whos unbelievably harsh, inconsistent, & nitpicky. So be aware, if you take Prof. Loney in the summer, you're stuck with her grading too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Quincy has to be the worst professor I've ever had. He would often get confused by his own questions, struggle to explain basic concepts, and nitpick every HW calculation to his exact standards. Be prepared to teach yourself. He is a horrible professor, and a rude person who tries to make you feel dumb instead of helping you during class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Loney (wishes to be called Quincy) was an extremely animated professor. His course was super difficult for me, but most students seem to do just fine. A majority of the course was all about the textbook so the textbook is a MUST! He's super excusable outside of class and only wants to help the students succeed.

Very personally invested in teaching and improving every student's Chinese skills, though that sometimes means being harsh with her students and assigning large amounts of memorization-heavy homework. She takes attendance and diligent completion of homework seriously. Her grading practices are predictable; you directly get out what you put in.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Pretty strict but wants you to improve. Skilled at teaching the material and getting conversations going. In class exercises are repetitive but improved pronunciation a ton. Sizable daily HW + daily writing quizzes. When you make a mistake, she is strict with you, making you repeat until you get it correct, which can be stressful (Whiplash vibes).
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: It's a ton of work, but my Chinese did improve a lot, both over CHIN 2201 and 2202. I wasn't on her bad side, but if she doesn't like you, it gets a lot harder for you to finish out the class.
My Chinese improved a lot after taking Intermediate with her. She really wants everyone to practice as much as possible, which was encouraging.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She's very helpful and reasonable, but it is a tough class with many pop quizzes. I had to work hard, but I am now able to spend hours with my Chinese friends without speaking any English, which ultimately is the only true measure of a language teacher and course.

Took both Chin 2201 and 2202 with her, she can be really funny sometimes and make the class interesting with some fun dialogue. However, she sometimes carries the crazy high maintenance mother persona which scares me. Besides all that, shes a really great Chinese professor who will teach Chinese in a very painless way and make you laugh.

I took IMPAC over the summer with Teng Laoshi and liked her. She has her moments of snappiness and strictness but usually she's really nice and patient. She also teaches you a lot of useful vocabulary that isn't in the textbook, which is somewhat obscure. Her tests are manageable and her expectations are reasonable. Teng helps move students along.

Compared to He Laoshi in first year, Teng Laoshi gives students a much more time-consuming workload. And she expects all students to have a fairly high ability to understand conversation. Her teaching style may not be the most effective nor lucid for everyone, but students at least get a solid background in vocabulary and grammar, if nothing else.

Though I hear she's a lot harder on her 200 level class, I took 4411 with Teng Laoshi and loved every moment of it. Relative to the other chinese faculty, she's easily the most sane and reasonable, plus probably the most intelligent and driven. You'll learn Chinese with her and not hate your life doing it.
Nice, helpful, knowledgable and interested professor.  Some of her in-class review games are a little tacky, but they get the job done.

Don't know why Quan has so many haters. You can literality fup the Prelim (miss almost half of his 25 MCQ exam) and still get an A. He is THE BEST professor in hotel school. Years of experience in  Real Estate. 

YOU need to forget about what your $10000 career coach tells you. Just go to class and learn!!!

One of the worst classes I've taken at Cornell, 100% wouldn't recommend. Posts no grades, exam averages are god awful, and curve isn't published until grades are finalized on transcript. He reads off of word documents during lectures and makes them unbearable. Called guest lecturer by the wrong name and fell asleep during another guest. No good.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: tests are extremely tricky... lectures and slides do not prepare you well enough for them. all MCQs, no partial credit. answer choices include a lot of none of the above, not enough information, or all of the above. easy for him to grade but hard for us to take as test-takers.

Professor Quan tricks you the first day. He makes fun of his grades on rate my professor which makes you think that they are fake however they are real and he is one of the worst professors at Cornell. Do everything you can to avoid him.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His grading can be a bit obscure with one M/C question being worth 15% of an exam and his case studies are a headache but overall good professor. Not impossible getting a good grade. He'll give you an A if you do better than everyone else as its subjective at the end of the semester. (grad students tend to be bricks and bring grade average down)

Quan sees himself as infallible, which is ironic because he is the worst professor I have had at Cornell. He's defensive and will snark students. During lecture, he mindlessly reads off Word documents. He does not prepare you for the case studies at all - e.g. he just assumes you know how to make a 2-tier JV equity waterfall on excel lol. Good luck

Professor Quan sucks the life out of real estate. Your grade is mostly consistent of 2 exams, both only 20 multiple choice questions designed to mess with your head (lots of "not enough information"). Lectures are dry as he only reads off the same pdfs he uses every year. If you can avoid him, please do!!!

The worst class Ive taken at Cornell by FAR. The classes quite literally are just him reading the lectures and hes a horrible lecturer. Tests are nearly impossible, and he doesnt respond to emails with questions either. Should really consider retirement ASAP since it seems like while alumni from years back respect him, current students do not.

Literally just reads off of the notes. Class is miserable to try to sit through. Sasses people who participate. Your grade depends on 2 home-works and 2 exams that are only 20 multiple choice questions. Did not learn anything.
Makes no sense. Can't understand professor Quan. He rambles during class.
difficult class but one of the most rewarding! many drop out after the first prelim but should def stay around. GPA isn't everything..this class is great learning!!
GENIUS
Excellent professsor
If you don't take a class with Quan you are missing out on one of best professors not only at Cornell, but in the Ivy League

Prof. Quan is amazing.  His real estate and finance knowledge are unsurpassed, and he's got some great contacts when it comes to job hunting.  His courses aren't easy, but you'll get more out of them than 99% of other Cornell courses.

He is a great lecturer and very passionate. Most of the grade is on the in class essay exams or the out of class written assignments based on the readings, which tbh I didn't really like the readings, but they were graded quite generously. Definitely recommend.

Professor Travers is brimming with passion, which makes the lectures utterly fantastic. However, I wouldn't say this is the most organized course. You write essays based on assigned books, but it is often difficult to include anything you've gleaned from lecture (making it feel more like a literature essay). Grading is also a little pedantic.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Attendance is technically mandatory because you have to write lecture reports, which are ungraded but helpful for recalling information. All the papers will be on the books you read for your discussion section - attendance is mandatory for those. Don't take if you're looking for a class to sleep through or slack off for - worth paying attention!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took this for a distribution requirement, but Professer Travers was the first Professor to make me truly care about history. He is very approachable, and he makes large lectures feel like small group discussions, always inviting conversation and giving thoughtful responses. I'm so glad I took History of the British Empire.

Travers is an amazing lecturer and very passionate about the subject. Not very accessible outside class/by email, but the TAs are. The reading is mostly unrelated to the actual lecture content and the reading is what you write papers based on. No screens during class, and mandatory lecture summaries every week so you have to take notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Travers is superb! He will change your view of history for the better!

Prof. Travers is an engaging lecturer who seems passionate about teaching and cares about his students. Reading load was reasonable. A variety of graded assignments (papers, exams, discussion participation, etc.). Fair grader.

Great lecturer and ad very good FWS professor too! He divided time between historical lectures, reading Kipling and writing in the class. Lectures were easy to follow and he was very passionate and enthusiastic about the British Empire. Travers also took time to schedule individual meetings for papers and had very open office hours. Great guy!
Travers was great to listen to... He was SO enthusiastic and clearly loves the material (and his British accent always made things interesting).  However, be aware that his readings are VERY long.

Really enjoyable class, lectures can be kind of disorganized, but mainly because he gets excited and goes on tangent. It's clear he's very passionate about what he teaches. It's worth taking any class that he takes.
Prof Travers was so enthusiastic and engaging and it was wonderful to witness in class. Every time I hear the word "Blackpool" I think of the Blackpool Rock song.

Professor Travers is a very engaging lecturer whose passion comes across with every lecture. He is funny and relatable. The only drawbacks are that his lectures are not always easy to take notes on and he demands a lot interms of reading and papers. Expect to work if you take his class but also expect to enjoy him as a professor immensely.

Best professor so far at Cornell! Built engaging lectures based on only a few notes. Covered all the major theories about different aspects of the British Empire, in greater depth than you'd find anywhere else, and tied them together into a coherent presentation. The lectures are worth attending even if you can't take the class.

Travers is a funny guy, at times bordering on hilarious. His lectures, though, were long, somewhat disorganized, and boring. While he was very approachable, very into the material, and very very British, the class was surprisingly intense. Definitely not the easy liberal arts class I was hoping for. If you really want to learn though, it's solid.
Excellent professor. He gives engaging lectures with some good comedy thrown in here and there.  He also makes an effort to get to know his students even in a pretty large class setting.
Professor Travers is wonderfully British, and wonderfully wonderful!
A very engaging speaker, Travers has the unique ability to inspire students and draw them into what he is saying. A fair grader and solid professor

He's an outstanding lecturer. A really nice, down-to-earth, genuinely funny guy. Very passionate about what he does. Interesting class. However, though the lectures were very organized and beautifully presented, the class as a whole was a little unorganized.
Travers is pretty cool, a good lecturer. Class is disorganized but prof is very passionate about subject matter. Western civ might suck, but Travers is a good teacher and funny guy.

Travers is brilliant, engaging, and communicates a tremendous sense of the importance of the material, as well as inculcating a love for history.  Also, he teaches from different historical perspectives and allows students to compare and evaluate them for themselves.  Travers' class is fun and engaging, a rare combination.  And he's funny, too!
Very good lecture, solid understanding of the topic, overall very helpful and supportive. Taught the eye opening class that is 2240

Excellent lecture notes (probably the best lecture organizer), accessible outside of classroom. He writes very hard exam problems but curve is very generous (Median A- in 2240). Course itself is worth taking.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great math class if you want to truly understand linear algebra and multivariable calculus. Expect a LOT of work, but no busywork. For comparison, it is significantly harder than CS 2112.
Lectures are extremely informative, and explain the content even better than the textbook (and the textbook is very good)
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Pros: Good lecture notes, well-paced, good exam curves, no attendance required at all
Cons: Sometimes cannot understand student's questions, TONS of homework (10+ hrs per week)
I liked his lectures because he always goes through proofs and the "why" so conceptualizing is easier. MATH 1920 as a course was horribly hard though, but if you practice a ton you'll survive.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Respected

reviews.comment: Prof. Sjamaar always had well-organized lecture notes and I found in-class examples useful for completing homework. Some find his lectures boring, but he always explained material thoroughly. He may be a bit dry in office hours but he is helpful and understanding. Class is hard, but doing practice prelims will get you through.
Took his class for Math1920. Class was very test-heavy. Stopped going to his lectures after a couple of weeks. His lectures were boring and hard to understand.

honestly don't go to the lectures its not worth it. you will get so much more out of just reading the textbook and taking notes. the final for this class was the hardest test I've ever taken in my life (as was agreed upon by everyone I talked to after as well) but the curve made up for it I guess? Idk just try to persevere guys.

Nice and can be funny in lecture. Lectures weren't necessary to succeed, but I went to all of them (8am, very rough). A bunch of topics def could've been explained better. Def recommend using the textbook, do all practice prelims given, & learn how to do all those problems for the prelims. Didn't appreciate that the prelims were curved down.

Lectures are hard to understand unless you read the textbook beforehand. Professor often doesn't know how to explain the material in a helpful/applicable way—there seemed to be a disconnect between lectures and HW questions IMO. however very chill and nice person, recommend going to office hours and you'll be fine
The lectures are hard to understand without having read the textbook beforehand. But overall multi is a hard class and Sjamaar does a decent job at teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Hard to ask questions. Scary and Industrial Class.
Great lectures and absolute icon, great analogies. Textbook problems are similar to the quizzes, but exams are different. Practice prelims are helpful.

Very cool and calm dude. Lectures organized very clearly, amazing handwriting, and explanations are very helpful. Very patient. Just go to lectures, go to office hours, and ask questions, then you'll be fine.

Seems like a nice professor who wants you to succeed. Lectures were pretty enjoyable and even though the content was difficult at times he was pretty good at explaining things. Exams were pretty hard but not unfair, and the curve was pretty generous. Overall he was a good prof to take this course with

This class was pretty tough for me personally. I found lectures difficult and unclear and the textbook was not great at explaining certain topics. Quizzes during discussions were alright since they closely followed the homework, however, tests extremely difficult and unfair. Also ed-discussion responses were a bit mean sometimes.

Gives lecture note templates, neat and structured lectures, sometimes monotone but always makes sure he goes over every topic. Gave us one letter page, front-back, cheat sheet for exams. Just read the textbook, and attend lectures, Sjamaar is a solid professor.

Tough to sum up my 1920 experience with Sjamaar. For some reason the tests were exactly the same as 2019, and he had to change the final grading scheme to make it a little fair for those who had studied.

As others have said, the lectures are well organised and concepts are well explained. However if speaking with him after lecture (or even answering questions in lecture), his manner often makes you feel stupid. His responses on Ed are very abrupt. Overall would take again, just don't except any warmth.

Professor Sjamaar is a great professor; his analogies are funny and useful, and he has a pleasant Dutch accent.

His favorite word is orthogonal, and his office hours are always popular. I would recommend him, he's a memorable lecturer for sure!

I suppose 1920 can be difficult, but he made it enjoyable; it's always help to Read as well :)

He is very well organized and good at explaining/naturally developing concepts. His presentation of the content is at times much superior to the one given in Hubbard & Hubbard (the textbook). I'd recommend going to his office hours, he often has really interesting things to say about any question you could ask and is enthusiastic about helping out!
Very good lecture organization. Most lectures are not very compelling however. He can be intimidating outside of class. Hard to connect with.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Personally, his lectures were ok. They were extremely middle of the road. However, his review lectures were exceedingly helpful towards getting a good score on each prelim. Overall, I think my grade mainly reflected my own reading of the textbook rather than the quality of his lectures and his teaching style.

Good class, but you have to study pretty well to do well (I slacked off before the first prelim and highly regret it haha). Lots of available resources provided by the prof, just have to make use of them. Additionally, really reached out to help students especially during this weird covid era.

Some might find his lectures a bit dry, but he is such a wonderful professor. Explains things super clear and is always happy to answer all sorts of questions from students. I attended both his and another professor's class for math 1920, and Sjamaar definitely has it more organized. 10/10 recommend him.

Came back to rate him after 3 years. Best maths prof I ever had - halfway into the semester I literally gave up my original lecture session and skipped lunch to attend his. He lectures and writes on the board clearly. Also gives interesting examples every once in a while. Students are encouraged to ask and answer questions during lecture.

Lectures were useless. Just went over theorems and a couple examples. Did not help from the problem solving aspect, which I felt was most needed. Prelims were very difficult, especially the final. I wish detailed answers were given for the homework. And forget about being able to sit up close if you don't get there 20 minutes before class!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: hardest class ive taken. There is hardly any partial credit on prelims and NO continuation points. When i asked why there are no continuation points, the sjamaar simply replied that it didnt exist! this class is more about being careful (when hardly any time is given for exams) than understanding concepts i guess! glad its over.

Very good choice of a professor. Lectures can be a bit difficult if you don't sit near the front as he has a bit of an accent and a mumble - but he will throw in a little joke every once in a while. He is also willing to stop and answer questions during the lecture. Although tests were hard, it wasn't unreasonable given what was covered in lecture.

Pretty solid lecturer; his teaching is a bit dry, but he throws in the occasional joke to lighten the mood. He definitely knows his stuff, and doesn't mind taking the time to answer questions or explain in further detail. The 1920 exams are absolutely wicked, but he does a decent job preparing for them.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: His lectures are pretty useful overall, having a good mix between theory and examples. Math 1920 is a hard class overall, but he does a good job of making sure we have a grasp on the material. He really seems to look out for his students, and he's always willing to stop lectures to answer questions.

He was a solid lecturer. His lectures started with the theory and he then worked through good examples. I liked to look over the chapter summaries from the textbook before lecture (those chapter summaries were amazing). And quick note: he typically finishes class 1-5 mins late.

Very nice person. He is very passionate about math and would often include funny side comments/jokes every so often to lighten the mood. Very knowledgable. The exams were very tough, but that's not entirely his fault, the course is hard as is whether its Sjamaar teaching or anyone else.

His speaks the way a math book is written. His energy level is quite low. The homework and quizzes are easy, but the exams are unnecessarily hard. He's an excellent mathematician, not a great lecturer.

Great lecturer. Yes, he follows the textbook, but he doesn't regurgitate it - he makes the information more clear and presents examples that aren't in the book. I particularly appreciated that he organized the board in a methodical, easy to follow fashion as he went. Not all math professors are good at this.

mediocre lecturer. just regurgitates the textbook, moves really quickly. grading only depends on the tests, which really depends on which semester u take it. homework takes a while and our prelims were ridiculously hard.

Material and prelims were tough, but his lectures definitely made everything a lot clearer than what it could've been. Very responsible, answers questions quickly on Piazza, and holds extra office hours and all. Amazing professor.
Really difficult class, but Sjamaar is an excellent professor. He does all he can to help his students, and he encourages questions. Definitely would take another class with him.

An amazing professor who explains difficult theoretical concepts with great clarity. He also has a good sense of humor. His teaching reminded me of why I enjoy math so much. The class may be tough but it was worth it and I would love to take another course with this amazing professor again.

Great Professor. I even nominated him as we evaluated the faculty at the end of last semester. Crystal clear; the note on blackboard is extremely good and informative. If you want a solid grasp on linear algebra, I recommend taking his class and don't miss a single class!
No Comments
Excellent professor: very clear, and extremely knowledgeable.  Professors like Sjamaar make Cornell what it is.  Teaches not only the material but also how to think mathematically.
Great class. Very clear presentation of some very difficult concepts. Homeworks were difficult, but covered extremely popular and important ideas and concepts. Really great.
Taught his own material, very difficult to find help outside of lectures

He's not a bad person, just a bad professor for teaching freshmen chemistry. He went too much in depth and wouldn't explain the basics. He also loves to ridicule students who have the nerve to ask questions about the material. Overall the course was curved to a B so grades were okay but no one learned the material (test averages in the 40s).

Peter, while he may be entertaining, does not teach us anything. His slides are discombobulated, and he does not explain stuff well. He also insists that we not use the textbook as "they are cheap and incorrect." Organic Chemistry Tutor is your best friend. Your only saving grace is that while you may be completely lost, so is everyone else.
Caan't teach.

Wolczanski clearly doesn't want to teach freshmen and the freshmen don't want to be there. I skipped every lecture and homework, literally just showed up for labs & prelims and mostly guessed and got a C-. Class averages for prelims were all under 50% so the curve was insane. He's rude but hilarious. Engineer trauma bonding starts here.
Worst prof ever

Trying to decipher the incomprehensible babble that bubbles from this poor banal soul's mouth was the first and only sin that many new engineers have commited. The class is not hard, chemistry should not be his hard, but when you've got it out for the kids... godspeed to the next year who takes him.

Lectures were poorly organized and had little information on relevant material, yet extensive information on "bonus topics", which cluttered lectures. Despite this, it was expected to locate the rare pieces of actually relevant information, which would then appear on prelims. 
Extremely disdainful towards students, for some reason.
Does not know how to teach.

Peter's lectures were not the most interesting but he definitely knows what he is talking about. Very confusing in the beginning but it takes about 1 prelim to figure out how to do well. Study the lecture notes of course, but I did text book problems and did fine on the exams. Easy grade since averages were
put me a step further towards the ithaca gorges. should be named in his honor

The professor was funny but not a good lecturer, and it was hard to separate essential information from what is mentioned in passing. The course needs a better focus on the basics as it was very sporadic and made it hard for anything to truly stick. Mostly self studied since the course material given were hard to decipher.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Did all the work myself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I played Geometry Dash in the back of class most lectures. I think Peter was a fun guy but the lectures didn't help much and content was a little all over the place. We started with nuclear chem. I found the best way to study was to UNDERSTAND the problem sets. Most of the learning happened by referencing problem sets to posted lecture notes.
Worst class I have ever taken. Do everything to not have this professor.
6 point font, reads off the slides, and inconsistent lectures. Lectures about his research instead of the actual content. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!! Also, hard prelims with a 40 average.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The only problem with Peter is that his lecture notes are very hard to understand, rest are fine. Going to lectures don't really help to be honest, but the office hours were surprisingly helpful. Exams are fair as they ALL come from his lecture notes, but decoding his slides was the hard part. As long as you spend time studying you should be fine
Peter was a great teacher! Truly a grateful experience to be in this class.
Somehow got an A in this class. Ride the curve. OChem Tutor is your best friend.

PETER PETER PETER PETER PETER PETER PETER
DON'T TAKE THIS MAN'S CLASS

Taking Pete's class is truly an experience (a bad one). The lectures teach you about everything EXCEPT Chemistry. I've left the class knowing the same amount (if not less) about chemistry. He makes it a point to show his disdain for students every lecture, and gets mad at the class when only 5 people out of 500 score above 75% on his prelims. Bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: PTW and the administration highly discourage students from seeking accommodations for their needs protected by the government of New York State using the loophole that granted these accommodations is "high effort" and "logistically inconvenient"
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you don't need to take his class, don't take it. If you need to take his class, lock in.

reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Peter Wolcanski is a unique professor for his deep hatred of his students. He assumes you already know the basics of general chemistry and will spend majority of his lecture going over advanced topics , assuming a foundation. Exams are atrocious and based on an all or nothing approach. Youtube is your best friend, if there is any hope to be had.

He's a hard and confusing teacher in lecture. But there is not much homework. And he grades harshly but fair. The class is curved to a B so if you work hard you will be fine. On one of my prelims the average was a 39% but that got curved to a B.
Wow, don't take this class. I would HIGHLY recommend taking this class over the summer or a semester where he is NOT teaching. I should've known after seeing these reviews.
You should know already by how many reviews are here. I concur HEAVILY.

This was by far the worst professor I ever had at Cornell. Prof. Wolczanski is a terrible lecturer, runs a poorly organized course, and completely underprepares his students for his exams. It would be difficult for him to try to make his students' lives any more difficult than he already does. He lacks compassion and adds unnecessary stress.

Please do not take this class I took AP chem and I swear the prelim is so god dam hard nothing like the homework prelim questions follow each other so one wrong everything is wrong. Loves to talk about bomb although its not mandatory the lectures on the slide are most of what he says but he will add additional information outside of it. beware

Ok so here's a REAL evaluation of PTW's infamous 2090 class: it is not that bad, IF (and let me emphasize this) you have had prior Chem experience (AP or otherwise). Honestly, a lot of people here are complaining because they dont show up to lecture or dont pay attention. But if you show up, put in good effort studying, you will do fine

Not a bad person but teaching a genuinely impossible class. Admin designed it in a way to make you hate yourself and chemistry and succeeds in doing that by prelim 3. Overall, in general, not just with Peter but with any professor, CASE out of the course. You could have Newton teach it & it would still be shite. Pete: 2/5, CHEM 2090: -5/5
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Unfathomably bad
Idk what's going on in class ever and it's mostly self taught
Easily the worst prof at Cornell. Good luck
Very simple way to describe the course: doom, despair, and everything unfair
dude destroyed any love I had for chemistry.
boo tomato tomato
had to comfort crying friends after most prelims. save yourself.

BIG PETE… total disaster. People are saying he might be the WORST chemistry professor ever — maybe the worst professor of ANY subject. Lectures all over the place, nobody knows what's going on. Not a single person can believe it. Truly one of the biggest flops of all time!

ps. MY EYESs
bald LMFAO

Peter will lecture on topics way outside of the breadth of the course. Some of these topics are on the exam and others will never be heard of again and you have no way of knowing which are which. Prelims are absolutely brutal and he yelled at us and called us stupid after the class average was a 43%.

arguably the worst professor at Cornell. Run, unless you're stuck here because of 2090. Be prepared for confusing and incomprehensive lecture slides and hard tests with questions you have never seen before.

Peter somehow finds a way to crush curiosity and the will to learn in his students with his boring lectures that focus more on random bomb facts than the actual material. The slides are practically illegible, his tests are a poor reflection on the topics we learn (high weighting towards minute details that he skims over in class)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: buddy cannot teach for shi, slides are dense and barely understandable, homework is fine but prelims questions are nothing like the practice problems, its always not too clear what prelim encompasses, this class will tank your grade and your mental health (unless ur a genius) do not take this class under big pete

He really loves bombs.The slides are not organized and the topics covered in class are not sequential. A class could cover quantum physics and the next class we balance equations. The information is scattered throughout the slides and u have to find information like a puzzle for some reason. Blames students for bad scores based on his teachings.
Don't do it. Don't even think about it.

For the love of lord, never take 2090; moreover, never take it with Wolczanski. The course is designed so that students learn 4 years of chemistry material in one semester. Knowledge of quantum mechanics and thermodynamics is a prerequisite.

This professor is smart but doesn't know how to teach. I took AP Chem before and every lecture he overcomplicates the topic and in general his lectures are very unorganized. He judges people that ask questions that he thinks are easy and already in the lecture slides. Also for some reason he loves explosions.
Berates students for asking questions, blames them for not studying when exam average was 43%.

Blames students for the test average being 40%, accuses students of "laziness" for allegedly not reading his lecture slides that are borderline incoherent. Jokes and puts down intellectually curious students for asking questions. 

Please, if you can, take the CASE exam to try to skip this course. If you must, rely on your TA.
This class will obliterated your self-esteem. I genuinely believe 95% of Cornell engineering students have imposter syndrome because of him (and the other 5% are the ones who get to skip this class)

Ok lecturer but very difficult prelims. Given the amount of material that has to be taught he goes over everything quickly. However if you are prepared to put the hours in you will be fine. I haven't taken chem past a sophomore year of basic high school chem and have scored above median on both prelims thus far. Just be prepared to ride the curve.
Avoid at all costs. Professor berates students for not studying after the class averages a 43% on an impossible exam. Expects a very strong background in chemistry coming into the class.

run. do not take. the whole distribution for exam 2 was literally a uniform graph around 40% and he blamed US for not studying when the whole class failed. its clearly a him issue and he needs to have his ego checked.
just literally don't think about taking this class AT ALL please avoid him in any way possible

came into this class with very minimal chem background (just hs sophomore year), and this class did NOT help me gain confidence. it seems like everyone else already took AP chem and even they are extremely confused. the test averages reflect how lost we all are. the slides are hard to digest and I'm so cooked, this should NOT be an intro course!!!

please please please do NOT take his class for chem 2090. you will regret it, it will tank your gpa, and destroy your self esteem. i know people hear others saying that they should drop a class and ignore that advice but for this one DONT. get the credit from a community college instead, i promise you this is not worth it.
Smart guy, bad teacher
Expects you to know a lot more than you already do coming into the class. Organic Chemistry Tutor is amazing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: pray. just pray bc this class is HARD.
Goodbye America Hello Ithaca Gorges!
im cooked guys
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He didn't teach stuffs that are on the homework. 0/5 professor. Don't ask a question in his class or else you get publicly humiliated...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Genuinely seems to hate teaching; belittles even the (very) few students who have the courage to ask questions, sometimes insinuating they are on psychoactive substances.
The gorge will call you.

THE WORST chem prof i've ever seen. Ordered lectures in a very weird and unreasonable sequence. As someone who learned the entire syllabus before, even I struggled to catch up with what he was saying because more often than not, you'll see him mumbling about some random BS
If you love your life don't take his class
Slides are awful, too many irrelevant stuffs
so confusing.
never again. what was that first lecture. by slide 3, just know you have to self study..... no other prof/section, fight through it

Wolczanski is undoubtedly the worst professor I've ever had. His lectures and notes were incoherent, making it extremely difficult to learn the material. Problem sets were posted with as little as 3 days notice before the deadline and extremely time consuming. Doing well in his class requires a disproportionate amount of effort.
Him, one of his past students Devika Pokhriyal, and other students of his are cyberbullying students on facebook.

In 4 weeks of class (intro class for non chem majors btw, some of whom had no chemistry experience) he taught us practically everything that I learned from high school and AP chem classes. The work that he assigned to us and the material we had to learn was way beyond the scope of the class. Please listen to the people below: DONT TAKE HIS CLASS!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I had Prof Wolczanski during my first semester at Cornell. After completing my degree, I can say with certainty that he was the worst professor I had during my time here.

Not the best lecturer... doesn't rely so much on the textbook as on his own class notes, which are extremely confusing. Many of the topics he chooses to cover are above the level of a first-year chemistry class. That being said, the insane difficulty of his exams forces you to study the material on your own and learn a lot.
Horrible lecturer. It's clear he's smart as a whip and knows a lot about chemistry, but he has no idea how to teach it. Goes way beyond what should be taught in a general chem course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Horrible guy, unwelcoming, gives you a thousand judgements if you don't know something. Homework is wayy too hard.

Wolczanski's Inorganic class was excellent. He covered all of the basics and did a solid job simplifying the more complicated concepts. The material might be a little hard to grasp at first, but I seemed to grasp it without going to office hours. Overall, a great professor that likes to challenge his students and grades fairly.

- very bad professor . He goes in depth in what you don't really have to know and therefore has you confused the ENITRE lecture . His exams are unimaginabley long and difficult . He wants you to be able to derive hard concepts rather than understanding the concepts you actually need to know in gen Chem. Terrible !

Lectures are long, boring and meandering. He has a somnolent effect on students and expects too much prior knowledge. Self-study is essential to pass. He  made no attempt to make the lecture interesting and it was jarring compared to Professor Crane. Tests set by him are unbelievably difficult. All in all, the worst teacher I have ever had.

Smart guy, but not a very good teacher. Taught concepts well beyond the scope of the course that were largely irrelevant to the vast majority of students without a lot of outside research; then tested for how well you were able to manipulate his lecture notes as opposed to for understanding of the material. Tried WAY too hard to be funny...

Hated this class the moment he stepped in. He rambles a lot, and I think half the time he did not follow the curriculum. Instead, he discussed his own personal research and went far beyond what was necessary during lecture. Was very disappointed with his ridiculous exams, but he is occasionally funny and is truly, extraordinarily brilliant.

Chem 2090 with Prof. Wolczanski sucked.  His lectures are not worth attending; just read the lecture notes he posts online.  Tests are hard, you'll somehow be saved by the curve.  I still don't understand chemistry.  He also has a wicked sense of humor (not in a good way- think mean).

Lectures can be  long and draggy. You can tell he is really smart and really into his research, however, he is just not right to teach an introductory chemistry class. He spends a greater proportion of his lecture talking about some abstract concepts and the worst part, is you can barely find the topics in the prescribed textbooks.
Poorly organized lectures that ramble for too long on irrelevant material. Assumed much too high a level of understanding for a general chemistry course. Lectures are absolutely useless.
worst professor I have ever had avoid taking a class with him at all costs that is all you need to know.

If every TA has to say "I don't know how to explain this to you guys in the context of what you're learning since I learned this in advanced inorganic chemistry," then something is wrong. He teaches all these terms and concepts without explaining what they are, and he teaches stuff that is nowhere in the textbook, so the textbook is useless. AWFUL!
Spends half the lecture doing complex derivations, then tells you it's not important and won't be on the exam.

Professor Wolczanski is said to be a very tough teacher, but everyone should go to his office hours and actually have a conversation with him before judging. He's an absolutely amazing professor and he truly is there to help. I wish I realized this earlier, so that I could've taken advantage of the time I had with him as a professor.

Clearly very knowledgable, but he is unable to pass information to students in an effective manner. His lectures are disorganized, and he assumes far too great of a basic level of understanding for a general chemistry clas.

This guy is the worst Professor I have ever had in my life. I have had professors who don't speak English that I would take over this guy. I would rather have my right ball chopped off than have to take another one of his classes.
absolutely terrible

Worst professor I have ever had at Cornell so far. Doesn't teach relevant material to the textbooks and teaches students as if we all understand physical chemistry on his level. No one ever understands his lectures and he mumbles a lot. He killed chemistry for me. Would avoid him if possible.

Talking to TAs or peers or reading your book is the better option for this class. He makes weird (and unnecessary) references in class that don't pertain to the lecture. His content is confusing and hard to comprehend.
You're better off staying home and reading the textbook
Lectures were not useful. Tests were hard and too long for the allowed time. Homework was fair, but learn the material from the textbook because it's not covered in lecture.

Lecture was useless I couldn't understand anything, take an AEW if you can get into one it helped me a lot. Tests are really not that terrible as most people are saying, most of the questions follow directly from the non-textbook hw questions. The mean is consistently pretty low so you're not expected to know everything. Final mean was 161300
useless lectures. hard exams. textbook material seems irrelevant.

Professor Wolczanski teaches a lot of interesting things that are not really contained in the textbook. If you have a TA that knows what she is talking about and can help you with the homework, it is possible to do well in the class. He assigns extra homework problems that he writes that end up being exactly like test questions.
Easily the worst professor I have ever had
He makes a lot of drug references in my class, maybe he likes to party? But this class is no party for the students; he makes everyone regret not placing out of this class.

Prof. Wolczanski covers interesting material not found in the textbook in his lectures. So, if you tend to skip classes, chances are that you wont get good grades just by reading the book.  The pdf notes he puts up before class are super helpful.

Lectures are virtually useless, as he gives material that not only fails to appear on the test, but that the TAs don't even know how to teach because they only just learned it in grad school classes. Also has a very monotone voice and uses high-level terminology that makes lectures almost impossible to understand.
I wish he would just be more respectful to his students. No one appreciates his disdainful comments about engineers when we ask for help.
One word. Terrible.
He takes pleasure in his students failing. He relishes in the feeling of superiority and enjoys picking on his students' struggle in the class.
he's impossible to understand and lectures about everything we don't need to know but leaves out everything we do. Sometimes it's actually funny how confusing he can be
I see him at parties, what a guy. Not a guy during lectures :
8th grade math yo, actually though just CASE out

One thought comes to mind when I think of PJ: What is life? This man simultaneously does not care about his class while still enjoying his class more than anyone else in the lecture. Although his lectures are truly incomprehensible, I think we should give him a break -- he is only super ten year. I can only hope to be as cool as him one day.

His lecture is completely useless and totally ruined my interest for chemistry. If you must gain credit for chemistry, take the placement test and avoid this guy if it is possible! Prelims and final are kind of irrelavant to the course material.

Horrible. He is out to get you. He is so condescending when you ask a question too. Know the extension problems and his HWs very well. Barely uses textbook material. Tested us on ridiculous stuff that was totally irrelevant to chem 2090. Go to his lectures or else you will fail. It is hard to hear what he is saying cause he mumbles a lot too.

Here's the advice to get through.  Go to all the lectures and read his notes before class (class has more meaning this way), thoroughly do the problems.  to study make sure you know every lecture and every extension by heart.  I promise if you do this you will beat the curve on every exam.

Avoid this guy! Lectures became useless very quickly. Teaches further than the curriculum requires. Makes a attempts at joking around during class, especially when it comes to bad grades. Prelims are OK if you study extension problems on HW... however, the Final was madness. Says he is an exceptional teacher, and that's why he "gets the big bucks"

OH MY GOD!  Professor Wolczanski is freaking amazing!  This guy must know everything possible about his field.  He's the Wayne Gretsky of organometallic chemistry.  Anyone who has Professor Wolczanski is amazingly lucky
did not learn a thing. horrible lecturer. tests are impossibly long but not too difficult. using his practice hw problems helps a lot with tests.
Avoid this professor at all costs. Especially is you aren't a ChemE. If you do end up in this course, use the previous exam questions on the problem sets to study for the tests. and good luck

The tests were by far that hardest I've taken at Cornell, more so than MATH 1910 which is supposedly to weed out the under achievers. He told us it would be one of the easiest classes we would take at Cornell. So not true.

To sum up CHEM 2090 as Wolczanski taught it: useless lectures and hard exams.  I generally did ok because I had a high quality non-AP chemistry course in high school; had I the AP credit, I would not have wasted my time with this class. In general, there was nothing I learned by going to lecture that I would not have by reading the book.

I learned so much in this class. It was a lot of work and we covered much more material than we were supposed to, but I loved it in the end. Prof. Wolczanski is just brilliant. He seems a bit mean initially, but he's actually really nice and extremely helpful.

I took advanced inorganic chemistry organometallic chemistry class from PTW when I was a graduate student spode. I was initially terrorized, but broke my ass and did OK. PTW recognized and appreciated that. If you are a whiner, you are over.

The absolute worst prof I've had at Cornell. His tests were killer (and the means reflect it), his demeanor in lecture can be summed up best by his sarcastic sneers at what he believes are stupid questions or stupid students, and he has no desire to help his students. Don't count on his office hours being any better either.

Had him for Chem 216. A total disaster. I remember the day when the mean on the prelim was a 26. But I have to agree with one of the other posts here, by the time i got around to chem 410, things had definitely improved. not sure if it was teaching non-freshmen or the subject matter or just a lot of therapy, but whatever it was, it was not too bad.

It's apparent that this guy is in academia to do his research and views teaching as an unfortunate liability of his job. He is often late to class, and wouldn't lift a finger if it would help one of his students attain a successful career in chemistry. Moreover he is belligerant and heartless, and often embarrasses students who ask questions.
No Comments
WOW
Worst teacher I had at cornell. Mean on tests = 40% You don't learn anything. Its all about competition. Take 207 alternate chem course - will not affect your engineering standing at all.

Moves very quickly, doesn't stop for questions, and not much fun to listen to.  Rarely gives you any background info on WHY you're covering the material you're covering.  Looking around the room it's amusing to see so many confounded students.

Had him freshman year for 216 and thought he was pure evil.  But by the time I had him again senior year for 410, I had come to respect his intelligence and humor and stopped being so scared of him.  Plus, he's really good at drawing icosahedrons!
While demonstrating wave propagation with a long slinky: "I'm a married man, so I haven't had much practice with my hand." --Wolczanski... these are the only words I remember from his course.

It was the material that this course covers that is very difficult (take 207), not the teacher. Although the professor was not overtly enthusiastic, he was by no means Evil or sadistic, he just did his job and that is why he is only a mediocre professor.
Absolutely Evil man.  His only interest in teaching is so that he can prove he is smarter than his students.  Steer clear at all costs.  Avg test scores of 41%
When taking the final, everyone opened up to the first page and the entire room started laughing... there is no way this man should be teaching.  absolutely horrible
Steer Clear of this class at ALL costs.  Take the alternative chemistry for engineering majors (207?).  You will be happy you made the choice

MEAN MAN. He is the epitome of a Cornell professor who cares more about his research than the students. Even the TA's for the course could not do some of the exam questions. Why is it necessary to trick students when we are here to learn & graduate? W
he teaches VERY FAST and too much in one semester-- he may go into too much depth...  but hes a funny old man, and a good professor i gotta hand it to him, hes really smart and knows his stuff.
He teaches way too much material at too high a level.  I retained nothing I "learned."
No Comments
THE STUFF WAS TRANSCENDENTALLY IMPOSSIBLE TO DIGEST, MAN!
ARRRRRGHHHH!!!!!!! So... evil....
No Comments
eeeeeeeeeeeeeeevil
horrible teaching style, horrible course

I absolutely LOVE Professor Smith. He has a strict grading criteria, but after a few visits to his OH, I was able to figure out exactly what he was looking for. I learned so much, and I gained a good mentor. He's personable and has so much knowledge to share. Don't be afraid to pick his brain. He's a lot more interesting of a person than he appears

Makes a lot of time for students and gives detailed feedback on writing assignments. The course has a good amount of work that will keep you busy. He writes the quiz and exam questions himself and they can sometimes be challenging, but if you go to office hours, you'll be ok
Top professor. Very good!
Amazing professor. Extremely helpful and his class was fun.
This is one of the greatest professors I have ever had the privilege of taking
Best professor I ever had! Taught me all sort of things that I NEEDED to hear. Not useless words.
Great professor.
top guy, top professor.

Professor Smith is amazing and has personalized office hours. He is a harsh grader however, he gives feedback and is very clear. Honestly a great professor that responds quickly and care about you as a student.
KINDEST PROF IN ALL OF ILR!!! Take him!!!

Professor Smith is the most kind/accommodating/accessible professor Ive had at Cornell. On several occasions, Smith sat with me on a Zoom call for 30-45 minutes to make sure I understood the concepts well. He answers emails within minutes and cares so much about his students. He WANTS you to succeed!! and you will in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is my favorite professor in all of Cornell. His class is not difficult at all and is easy to follow along. You don't have to do all the textbook readings, they just ensure you receive an A- on every quiz but these quizzes are easy to do anyway. He offers a lot of help with the research paper and wanted you to have office hours.

Best professor I have had. He is extremely committed to his students and very passionate about his work. He is exceptional at helping students understand difficult concepts and is truly invested in his students' performance.

Best professor I will ever have. One of the most helpful people that you will ever meet. He is so interested in his students and their performance in his class. If you did not perform well in his class it is because you didn't make the effort to work with him. Amazing guy, VERY smart, insightful, and funny. TAKE HIS CLASS!!

He's awesome. He so chill and lax. Sometimes he isnt really clear about the assignments or in lecture, but he is always there to answer questions. the quizzes are kind of challenging, but if you study the review q's, they wont be. Start your paper early and meet with him regularly; he will help you so much. Tests are hard but he grades generously.

Professor Smith is one of the best teachers I've had at Cornell. His class is by no means easy, but he is extremely helpful and in fact makes office hours mandatory, which was great. Exams were fair and he wrote the book so you know what he thinks is important. He's also a great and surprisingly funny person  Also counted as ILR Advanced Writing!

Great guy.  Non-mathematical approach to labor economics is incredibly applicable to real-life scenarios.  Smith really helps students understand practical applications, rather than equations you will forget after the final.  Writing credit too!  His answers and grading are very subjective, but you'll learn what he's looking for.  Highly recommend!

Professor Smith really helps his students understand labor economics in a way thats relevant to the current economy.  If you ask questions and go to office hours you should do extremely well in the class.  He's a great person.

Professor Smith genuinely cares about his students. Not only has his class taught be a lot about economics, but by meeting one of one with Professor Smith on a number of occasions I have learned a lot about life.
