He is easily the kindest and most sympathetic professor at Cornell. You're crazy not to take him.
Ignore any negative comments. Honestly, Prof Smith has been my favorite professor at Cornell. He is helpful, kind, and sympathetic. His classes are interesting and he is very funny.

Easily the most accessible, friendly, and genuinely interested in this lives of his students that I have ever had at Cornell. His writing seminar is indeed extra work, but sure as hell beats all of the other ones. There are few people in this world that I respect more highly.

I think what has been said basically sums it up. He is an extremely smart and friendly professor who is generally and genuinely interested in helping his students learn and grow. The downside to his class is that he grades hard, and he grades based on subjective ideals that you will never understand.

Subjective, but helpful. The trick is, his help is worthless. May give you pages of feedback on your paper then a poor grade. Lectures are incredibly boring, and poorly organized. If you don't like the lectures, the book is worse since it is written by him.

Professor Smith's grading procedures are ridiculously subjective. I wouldn't recommend his class unless you like not knowing what the professor is ever looking for and enjoy re-writing your in depth term paper (compared to other professors' assignments) approx. 3 times before submission and still having it scored lower than those with other profs.

TAKE A CLASS WITH PROFESSOR SMITH. He is my favorite profesor that I've had at Cornell. He is a very good teacher and an even nicer guy. Don't be afraid to go to his office hours... he's friendly and genuinely interested in helping. Not too easy or too hard (just about average difficulty but made easier by his good teaching).

professor smith is by far my favorite prof that ive had at cornell. he is extremely nice and extremely helpful. he seems to genuinely want to help his students learn. the lectures themselves were interesting because it wasnt just straight econ, he mixed in practical applications of what we were learning. overall i would say he is the man.

He's a professor and a great guy! Very helpful and always willing to have a chat, provided he has the time. He's a pretty difficult grader and requires a lot from his students, but also practically walked me through the final paper. In short, if I didn't have a boyfriend, I'd marry him.

Prof. Smith has been very helpful and approachable in my experience.  He seems like a nice guy, but the class actually does require a little bit of work.  Once you learn the stuff, it isn't too difficult, but it does require studying his textbook.

Smith is a fantastic, down-to-earth professor.  If you're looking for a professor to give you some guidance about classes or the future, visit him in office hours-- he really cares about his students.  Solid, straightforward teacher of economics.

Smith is very entertaining in class and explains all material easily. The material is straight from the book, mainly because he wrote it with Ehrenberg. He makes all sorts of side assignments that encourages you to read outside literature.

A great guy, an even greater teacher.  If you walk out of his class not learning something new every time, you were sitting in the wrong class.  Very helpful, exams are fair, and not too much homework.  Do your reading cause he wrote the book

Shalom is a genuinely lovely man. His classes are organized and thorough and you will walk away from them having actually learned and retaining a lot of Hebrew knowledge. Don't fall behind on the short daily homeworks and you'll be fine. He's always there if you need someone to reach out to.
The undisputed goat. Kind, caring, chill, funny, easygoing, patient. Great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Shalom is incredible, probably the best teacher I have had at Cornell. If you have any interest in learning Hebrew, I 100% recommend you take his class. He is extremely understanding and plans his lessons so well to ensure you really are learning. I looked forward to his class everyday, and you can tell he also enjoys every class.
Shalom is a great professor. It's easy to do well if you just show up and do the homework.

Shalom is by far the best professor I've ever had at Cornell. He works incredibly hard to make learning Hebrew an enjoyable experience and is extremely accessible and approachable outside of class. You will get a good grade if you put effort into this class. Amazing class to fulfill A&S language requirement

Shalom was such a great teacher. I was concerned going into the class given that I have no background in Hebrew, but with the work put in, I got an A+. We had daily homework assignments, so make sure to not fall behind. Our test reviews were essentially the exam. Overall, great class to fulfill the A&S language requirement!
Shalom is such a sweet and caring teacher who genuinely cares about you and wants you to do well in his class. Best teacher I've had at Cornell so far.
Hands down, the best teacher/professor I have ever had. Genuinely cares about students learning the material. Would recommend to everyone

I never use this site, but felt the need to write a review for Shalom because he's such a quality professor. It's clear he has a passion for teaching and genuinely cares about his students. Although the class is pretty light, it's great for getting a foothold in Hebrew. Definitely take, if not for an interest in Hebrew, then for a class with Shalom

He is the nicest man in the world! He knows how to teach a language better than anyone I have ever seen and turned a 5-day-a-week language class into my favorite of the whole semester. He is also very understanding when life gets in the way (but don't get behind). If you want/need to take a language class, take Hebrew with Shalom!

Shalom is the best! He truly cares about his students and is always willing to give extensions if you need them and is very accommodating about everything. The class was pretty easy to do well in, tests were all take home this semester and Shalom did a great job trying to recreate a class environment online. 10000% recommend!

Shalom went out of his way to make me feel included,as one of the few with no Hebrew exposure. If any of us express interest in a Hebrew song/poem or need help with a specific area (e.g. script) he takes time outside class to address it. He celebrates progress and in language-learning promotes what works in a fluid way. Ask anyone, we all love him!

He loves his job and you can see it in the way he teaches. In the past, I have found it difficult to learn a language from a native speaker because they don't always understand the whys and how to make people understand, but Shalom is an incredible exception. He makes learning Hebrew fun and interesting. I wish all of my professors were like Shalom
He's the absolute best teacher I've had so far, truly cares about his students and loves his job it makes learning Hebrew that much more enjoyable.

absolutely incredible. He's the nicest man ever who really just wants everyone to succeed and get A+s (which is possible). There are quite a few tests but he schedules them around busy weeks so that you're not extra stressed. Also he's very accommodating with making assignments up. Definitely the only class worth being awake for at 9

Shalom is an amazing professor who wants you to do well. The pace of the class is really easy to follow and yet at the same time you'll learn a lot. You have to keep up with the work but it's very easily spaced out for you and won't be hard to do. If you do the work you will do well. Would 100% recommend!

Once again, Shalom was my favorite professor of the semester. He really wants each of his students to do well. He'll change test dates if you're too stressed. It's easy to do well in this class despite all of the work because Shalom helps along the way. He's also so much of a father-figure that you wouldn't want to do poorly and disappoint him.

Shalom genuinely cares about each of his students. Learning Hebrew can seem daunting at first - I came in knowing absolutely nothing - but Shalom caters the class towards the individuals in it. It's easy to do well because Shalom helps you and makes you want to work hard. He makes sure you're prepared for tests. He also sometimes brings in food.
Amazing Professor who loves to teach and watch his students learn the language.

With Shalom, it's all about the learning. Shalom is caring and kind and fair. You cannot hide in this class, but that's OK. It's good to be in a class where the teacher and students actually know each other. I am so glad Cornell offers this class and that Shalom is the teacher.

Shalom is kind, caring, loves the subject and wants students to learn. He understands that people come into class with different backgrounds but he has high expectations for everyone. Small group meets everyday which means you can't hide but the upside is Shalom knows everyone. So much better than huge lecture courses with random TAs.

I had reservations about taking a foreign language, but Shalom is one of the most caring individuals I have met at Cornell. Class is very laid back, and though it is everyday, it is not stressful at all! Do the work, and you will do very well!

Shalom is an AMAZING professor. He really wants his students to learn, and takes extra strides to make sure no one is left behind to struggle with the material. Class and homework is enough to adequately cover the material with out being burdensome. I can't sing his praises enough.
I was nervous about taking hebrew but Shalom is an amazing teacher. Class every morning was tough but I'm so glad I took this class. I highly recommend it.
LOVE HIM. five classes a week but its not bothersome at all.  homework due daily for the most part but its easy and defintely not a burden. he makes class exciting because he's just the greatest
He keeps class fun and entertaining, and wants you to learn and do well. Doing the homework and keeping up is a must, though.
Great teacher and a great guy.  If you do the HW you'll get a good grade, he's not looking to give bad grades.

A great professor, clearly very enthusiastic about his subject material.  The class was rather difficult for someone coming in with absolutely no Hebrew experience, even with a large amount of work put in.  As well, this professor has a habit of announcing tests only 1-2 days before giving them.  Great professor overall.
the best

Excellent professor, even though 5 days a week, not stressful and simply a fun class.  Not too much homework, and even though many come with prior knowledge, there really is no disadvantage if you didn't know hebrew before taking the class.  Great teaching style and very relaxed and easy to talk to.  Take it.

Shalom is a great professor - he's incredibly helpful and knows how to structure a language class.  Most people come into the class knowing how to read and write, but people without any background still do very well. (And if you take 2 hours to learn the alphabet before the semester starts, you'll be well on your way.)
Great guy, great class, but a gpa killer if you're not cut out for it.

He's a great teacher and a great guy.  I am only half way through the second semester, but I already feel like I am extremely proficient in Hebrew.  Take this class if you want an easy A.  It's very minimal work, and minimal studying.
Shalom is an amazing professor.  The class is challenging (especially for those with no Hebrew experience) but overall if you come to class and put forth effort, you will get a good grade.

Absolutely wonderful teacher and great person all around. Really fair. Always available. Go to Hebrew Lunch Tables.. they're really fun. He is very personal. He teaches with music and stories and homework doesn't take long to do. Very enjoyable. TAKE IT!

He is a very nice guy, and a pretty good teacher.  However, this class can kill your GPA.  If you don't go to class everyday and do all your work, he will personally kill your grade.  A real stickler.

If you're a****with 6 years of Hebrew background, it's an easy A.   Otherwise, this class will be a GPA drag, even if the professor is a good guy. This is an intro course, it shouldn't be that way.  His lessons tend to be haphazard.  This class is structured toward those w/ sig. experience.
Very engaging, helpful, caring teacher. Can tell he enjoys his job. VERY laid back. Class itself is flexible.
An amazing prof.  Even though i thought i could never enjoy learning a language, he proved me wrong with this class.  Study the vocab before class and you'll like the class even more.

Shalom is amazing. He is one of my favorite people in the world. It is worth taking this hard class just to see him everyday. It is quite a hard class, but he really cares, so just ask for help and it will make sense. Truly a gifted teacher.
I'm usually not into languages, but Shalom made me really love Hebrew.  He's an amazing teacher.
Best teacher I've had at cornell! Shalom is an incredibly compassionate teacher. He really cares about his students and that they enjoy learning. I would definitely recommend this class.
No Comments
I took both NES 101 and 102 (beginning hebrew). Sholom is an amazing teacher. Though learning a language can often be boring, Sholom makes you love to learn hebrew. he is a gifted educator.
really engaging teacher but extremely difficult and time consuming class.  be prepared to work
Fun class!  Worth the work!

Beginning Hebrew. WONDERFUL. Loved him. it's a 5-day a week class but you can go different times different days, and you have to do the work of course, but I couldn't ask for a better teacher or a more likable teacher.
it's not an online class but it might as well be. everything is made with ai and so everything can be done with ai. in fact, he encourages it. don't expect to learn anything meaningful. easy A though
I showed up to maybe 2 lectures and still got an A. unorganized, and kinda surface level material, but he's funny and its a good GPA boost.

Professor Ault made learning actually enjoyable by making the class manageable and fair. I would recommend this class to anyone, as it improved my understanding of the importance of mitigating climate change and showed that college is about meaningful experiences and interactions with nature, and not just grades
he is very engaging and easy to understand! makes learning about climate science fun. amazing prof

He is so unhinged and chill about assignments! Lectures are so chaotic but engaging with his style of teaching. Super easy A class as he is so random with grading and almost always gives a 100 for any assignment. Prelims/Final are online and are really easy. Live laugh love Toby

this guy is actually addicted to AI. The most basic photos will be generated by AI, and online tests would just be generated by AI, which would result in confusing and repetitive questions. Great personality, but lectures would always be my time to do my crosswords

lectures feel like he is talking to himself. painful to listen. cannot tell if he is giving trivia facts or teaching. not engaging. i know i am not the only one bc most ppl works on other class during the lecture. few hw, online mid term, final that are clearly made with ai and can be solved with ai. mandatory attendance bc surprise inspections.

This is a guy you would WANT to find outside lecture. He cares about his students' experiences just as much as the lecture material. Although he cracks jokes and likes to make students laugh a lot, his anecdotes and rambles tie into class material, creating cohesive stories that teach the material at a competent and memorable level.

I took Dr. Ault's EAS 1330 and 1310 courses. Dr. Ault explains the material in a way that's easy to understand for both majors and non-majors. He offers plenty of extra credit and is overall a great professor. Easy A, definitely take him for distributions. He was also recently nominated for the CALS Chancellor's Award for Excellence in Teaching!

This review is actually for EAS 1300. He's one of the greats at Cornell. He wants all of his students to succeed, only ones that wouldn't are who to refuse to show to class. Take a class of his not only for a requirement, but if you need to reach 120 college credits. Lectures were awesome. Not much homework either. He is the GOAT

AWESOME PROF. Prof Ault understands most people are taking this class for distribution and doesn't try to make the class too hard. Genuinely, he just wants to make people understand the threat of climate change and need for action. Rewards people who come to class with extra credit opportunities. Tries to make lectures engaging and class not hard.

For an easy A class that fufilled two of the annoying Arts & Science distributions at once, Professor Ault understood the assignment. He knew most people didn't care about it and was taking the class because they had to, so he made the lectures interesting within that context. He was fun and gave tech breaks, absolute G!
Master T-Dog was the best teacher ever! Never afraid to bark - or to call people out for barking in the back! I was so happy to take this class: I met animals that are in my lifelong pack

I LOVED Toby and this class! Learned a lot about climate and Toby is the most passionate teacher I've had at Cornell! Class was very easy, as everything is take home (including tests). Everyone was treated equally (as if we were all dogs) and there were so many unique people in the class - I met lifelong people in my pack! Would recommend 10/10!
Professor Ault is endlessly kind and always striving to make lectures engaging, accessible, and easy to comprehend.
He doesn't what he is doing, nor do students have a clear expectations of what the class aims to give. He can mess up the Canvas site a million times while nobody really understands what's happening.

Great prof and a really interesting class! Professor Ault made an attempt to get to know students, and made an effort to ask about our mental health. He is very interesting and engaging, and the class has a lot of opportunities for extra credit. Most caring prof I have had so far at Cornell!

Incredible class, with an even more caring, knowledgeable, and engaging professor. The class is really easy, and Dr. Ault makes you actually want to learn the material regardless. 200 kids in lecture and he makes an effort to get to know everyone. Best experience with a professor!

Prof. Ault is very smart and definitely means well when planning out lectures for his students, but execution is very disorganized and poor. Hopefully this is a consequence of not being super experienced with teaching undergraduates and he works on this.
great professor, cares a lot about material and students learning it, which is really nice

Funny dude - I really enjoyed his lectures. The course does not cover much content so discussions were constant review, didn't have to spend much time outside of class (please still study though). Exams were straightforward. You are set up to succeed in the class - wanted to put this review so students are deterred from taking his class, he's good.

Great lecturer excited about the material that tries to make sure that all students learn in his class. It is an interesting and enjoyable class if you stay engaged, as he also definitely cares about participation. Class doesn't have too much homework but requires paper reading. I and other friends all had positive experiences

Grading criteria never clear, terrible handwriting, poor time management, teacher doesn't care what student learn, too tough on details, recitation class misleading, encourage memorizing rather than learning.
The worst professor ever in my life.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: He is one of the worst professors I have ever had at Cornell.  The guy does not care about his students, never answers emails, barely gives any homework (which makes it impossible to study) and is so boring in lecture.  I think he really doesn't care if you do well or not and makes his tests really hard.  He also has awful handwriting.
Amazing teaching. Well organized study material and very helpful on asking questions. Lucid presentation on self assembly.

Very crappy professor. No website, not enough homeworks given, poor handwriting, and no assistance before examinations. I honestly think that he is one of the most lazy and unmotivated professors who simply does not care whether or not you learn anything. I learnt nothing and he sucks.
great professor, funny, clear, has a good understanding of material and seems very interested in what he teaches, helpful

The project has no rubric no matter how much you ask. Then you get a random grade a few peers come up with. Your project can be better than others but you will get a worse grade. learn very little in this class. Avoid this class please. Its just a shame there are not other good ML classes available. it forces people to take this class.
Her lectures are pretty interesting, and has a project-based approach.

very accomplished person but atrocious professor... put out one of the most poorly prepared prelims i have ever seen at cornell and came up with a very unfair and universally hated peer grading scheme that students abused to help themselves in terms of the curve
It is a difficult course, but if you work hard you will learn a lot. Recommend!

I find it difficult to believe that Cornell University would include this professor in its team of excellent professors. You can just skip class because the lectures are worthless. Support from TAs and Professors are also non-existent. The group projects are graded with unsupervised peer review, incentivizing people to sabotage others. Don't take.

Rarely am I compelled to post a review on Rate My Professor but this class was so horrible and utter garbage that I must insist. The class is hard for no reason at the expensive of learning, I can probably find more help from Scooby Doo than the Professor and TA team. There is no transparency in grading. Don't take any of her classes stay far away.

Udell's explanations were so unclear to the point that I had to google everything she said - the Internet did a much better job than her in teaching. Grading was not transparent - hw instructions and grading rubric were very vague. She made us do peer grading - this coupled with non-transparent grading incentivized students to sabotage their peers.

Probably one of the worst classes I've taken at Cornell. Udell is a confusing lecturer, and the TAs for the class are very focused on not giving you the answers to problem sets, even if it comes at the expense of a student's understanding. Very unclear and somewhat arbitrary grading rubrics. Avoid at all costs.

In MSE, you will probably have to take a decent amount of classes with Umbach. He is pretty not well-received as he doesn't teach well and tends to give grades arbitrarily based on personal feeling. You probably won't learn much in his classes and will def feel frustrated, but if you BS effort and try to seem nice, you'll get a better grade...

Umbach is a super nice guy and his office hours are key for the problem sets! However, the class itself is super disorganized and nanotech is such a broad topic that it sometimes seems like we're just learning random stuff. Prelims were okay, but quizzes were pretty bad
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: exactly what others talk about. He expects too much prior knowledge about chem and physics even if its engri class and the class is really boring and long.
Great professor! Definitely take as prospective ChemE or MatSci

Umbach, although tough, is an entertaining lecturer and a kind professor. Arguably, Nanotechnology is one of the hardest ENGRI classes, and as such, many people are disappointed with workload. However, the class was inspirational, and it completely changed my personal career path; as such, I highly recommend the class for motivated individuals

Decent professor. His lecture notes are extremely dense, but he posts all the power points which are very convenient for reviewing for prelims. For the most part the tests are fair. The homeworks didn't seem particularly useful but they weren't very hard. The material is often interesting, other times not so much. Overall a decent experience
horrible teacher. expects you to know too much. ridiculous tests and unfair grading policies. do not take nanotech!
He's super awesome. Love this dude.
No Comments
Long, long, boring lectures. Expects you to have prior knowledge about nano before the class. Class was very difficult.
Easy class, easy professor. Take it with Umbach.
i failed finance w another professor. ukhov makes info clear, practical, & understandable. it's almost like having a good professor can make a subject feel easy!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great professor who cares about his students, especially  if you go to class and get to know him. Loves athletes. His lectures tend to be long and a bit boring but great professor overall.

Such a cool guy. The stories/examples he uses in class are hilarious, but also teach you the material. If you go to him during his office hours he is extremely helpful! You don't have to attend class, but he may boost your grade up if you do go.
Legit professor of finance. hotel school sucks less with real finance professors like ukhov

Awesome professor/ class. Very funny and engaging lectures, often sidetracks to relevant current events. Straight-forward material, easy homework and exams. If you are looking for easy A and a practical, interesting class, this is it
Best prof in the hotel school

This guy is a boss.  Doesn't really care if you come to class but will bump your grade up if you do (not that you'll need it).  Class teaches you the basics of finance and he keeps it pretty simple.  A quality professor who knows his stuff.  Highly recommend it.
EASY TO PASS

My favorite professor at Cornell thus far. Extremely smart and knowledgable, and also willing to help his students in office hours. Go to office hours and get to know him-- he's a great guy with funny stories, and it will help you in the class. If you show up and pay attention, no reason you can't do well.
Took this class based off the rate my professor reviews and it went great. He's knowledgeable but sometimes disorganized when posting HWs/cases. Favorites blonde girls so you might be in luck.

This guy is hilarious. Has a heavy Russian accent, which makes his stories even funnier. Cares that you learn the material. Exams are much harder than the practice problems and homework he gives. But all in all, one of the best professors I've had simply for the pure entertainment value of his stories.
This guy and class are awesome.

GREAT Professor. had him for advanced corporate finance. new guy, but dont be scared, he knows what he is talking about and has a genuine interest in the students. Very helpful at office hours, and makes advanced corporate finance interesting. Oh, his random facts about the finance world are the great. All hail Buffet!

I had the privilege of taking three classes with the late Professor Uri Possen, including an independent study. He was one of my best and favorite professors at Cornell. He taught financial economics, a subject I loved. He helped me sign up for an internship, because of which I got the visa papers. Always there for his students. I miss you. RIP!

He doesn't explain the models in detail during the class, rather you should study on the textbook. However, he and his TA like to help students preparing the exams. He provides good insights on the current macroeconomic situation especially on fiscal policy and financial economics . Generous grader.
The problem sets is all that will prepare you for the tests. If you miss lecture, be sure to get the packets you missed.
His lecture is a bit tedious, but he is personally nice guy and always willing to help students. When you rely on textbook, which is the best i have ever seen, you can ace this course
Horrible teacher. Disorganized. His TA was worse than he was. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!

Good Professor. Very interesting course. Go to all lectures and take good notes; cross-reference with the book and go to office hours for whatever you don't get, he'll appreciate you all the more. Start the paper assignment EARLY!!
Very interesting class, and a professor who has a great grasp of the material.
Really interesting course. I enjoyed it. Professor very clear and helpful.

I had literally already taken finance when I took this class, so it was kind of a joke. But he's not a bad guy. Strangely though, I got a higher grade in the Johnson school finance class I took previously than I did this one. Odd.
Hard to get by on just his lectures because they're so disorganized. Tests are fun though and he's very entertaining.
Cute professor. Probably one of the easiest chem professor in Cornell and I am not complaining. Good and helpful guy

This guy is so enthusiastic about his job that he makes me want to be a professor. And he loves chemistry and his lectures are always interesting. But wow, some of the homeworks and tests are pretty hard. And the concepts. The only issue with this guy is that he doesn't actually TEACH very well...

He's a great professor in one sense - he's very kind and funny and overall a really nice person.  Open to questions etc.  He sings in class and shows us amusing videos  But I don't feel like I learn chemistry from his lectures.  he just demonstrates calculations.  As with Zax, I feel like I learn the most from the supplemental prof Dr. Johnson.

Some like him since he's funny and charming, some don't since he wastes some time singing and telling stories.  I liked him not only for his stories and jokes, but because he really does know what he's talking about.  If you follow his lectures, you'll do well.
nice guy, but is one of the worst professors here. He moves very slowly, and lectures are absolutely pointless.
He is a cute person, with his silly songs that he sings and whatnot, but he is not a very good professor. Moves at a glacial pace through the material and lectures are generally useless.

Amazing Chem teacher who makes use of class time to make sure everyone understands the concepts by going over examples and demonstrations in detail.  He makes class fun and enjoyable with his personal anecdotes and songs.  Overall, great teacher and is a class everyone should take before graduating Cornell.
really old and cute with the besttt accent and i love when he sang opera he was so good! kind of a sucky chem professor though...

Love, love, love! Usher is a great professor and an outstanding opera singer. As long as you understand the lectures, textbook chapters, and how lab demonstrates what you're learning in class, you should be fine! Do plenty of practice problems, read the textbook, and go through lecture notes! Not a bad class if you know your stuff...

Going to his class is entertaining because he's funny and sings. But he doesn't go through the material fast enough, his homework assignments and labs involve material before it is covered in class. What he says in class is easy to understand, but he goes on tangents also.

he was fun (sang opera every day at the end of class, went off on funny tangents, had a preoccupation with the blackboard erasers), but did not get through enough material each week--had to learn a lot of  it on my own just to be able to do the homeworks and labs
awesome professor. exams are very fair and very similar to practice exams (20% of it comes from homework problems). he definitely makes the class interesting with his photos from greece and opera.

105 was kinda hard.  Only because his freestyle lectures were not supplemented with a textbook, so exams were pretty tricky.  He doesn't TEACH you how to do the problems in class, just shows you what you should know, but with no textbook this is hard to deal with, though I gotta love his singing, family slide shows and random episodes of Buffy.

His exams sometimes tested things that were specific examples during lecture. There are 3 prelims, 1 final, and no homework. This saves you time, but also gives you less of a grade buffer. I hate orgo, and even though he was entertaining with singing and stories, I couldn't wait for the semester to end. His digressions got annoying after a while.
His lectures are not particularly useful in learning the material. Use them to see what material will be tested and use the book and study guide.
A great professor and a great guy.

I was a little irritated for the first month of class when it was clear that the Chem 357 people were moving faster than we were. Than, Usher's pesonality, his genuine love for students and the realization that less work in Orgo was not necesssarily a bad thing won me over.

I loved orgo.  That has to say something about the teacher.  Yes he sings and digresses, but if you take notes, do the reading and the (optional) problem sets, you should be fine.  The LSC review sessions were helpful too.
We don't learn much, but you gotta love David Usher.  He sings us Opera and tells funny stories.  His New Zealand accent is charming too!

Very good lecturer.  First half of the class is really easy, because he won't teach much.  During the second half of the class, he will start to do a lot of catch up and cover many chapters in a week.

Very engaging lecturer. Prelims were based directly from the text and lectures. True/False of DEATH were useless... He could have prepared us better for CHEM 360, but the course was nonetheless entertaining and demanding.
Classes were very engaging. I love orgo because of this man. He rocks.

Very entertaining. Will definitely keep your attention in class. But from a learning point of view, this prof doesn't really cut it. He goes off on to so many tangents that we do not learn as much. He does well on the stuff he gets to.
Usher is the best! He makes class interesting, he sings opera to us, and he has a great accent.  I wish he was my grandpa!

singing was great and entertaining, but he did not really care to teach us! 357 people learned more than we did! even their prelims were harder than ours! so 360 turned into hell, cause we did not know enough from 359.  But can't argue, he is a great guy
I came to this class to learn orgo, not to hear some guy play his guitar. Someone should fire him.
I suck at the class, but I love him anyway!
he is a funny dude, and sings opera in class sometimes!
He made orgo interesting, and his tests are fair... tricky, but fair if you know your stuff.
This guy is CrAzY!!  in a good way...
He sang to us! Charming accent.
Highly entertaining class, especially for orgo.  He even sang to us
Hilarious and quirky! Love his accent.
Best Quant finance course in Cornell
I liked how this course was designed to help introduce to engineers the concepts of various financial instruments and the role they play in market dynamics
Great professor and course discuss interesting concepts related to financial markets and their statistical mechanics. Probably the best course about financial markets in Cornell.
incredible class about financial engineering & hands down the best professor I have had at Cornell.
Lectures are hard to understand but the professor is super caring and does cool side projects. Definitely recommend going to his office hours. Prelims are super similar to the psets.

Def a weed out class. Lectures are hard to follow, took more time trying to figure out his handwriting than the actual content. Exams are very similar to the psets given though, so easy A. Seems like the professor is just too smart to know how to teach.

Varner was my professor for Intro to ChemE. The class was pretty easy although you do need to pay attention and show up since the lectures aren't recorded. The exams are pretty much the same as the review. His handwriting is a bit hard to understand but other than that the class was an easy A.

Very nice and caring professor; however, he's extremely disorganized. It's probably because he's teaching the class that he hated the most when he was an undergrad, but the format of the class is is all over the place. Most of the class has no idea what we are learning, at at this point are too afraid to ask.
Has a cool personality but do not know how to teach. The lectures are confusing. His handwriting is cool but very hard to read.

Honestly a great professor who is always willing to help his students, the prelims were take home and really easy and there was no hw in the class, however lectures were a little boring but thats because the material is basically a bunch of equations

He has such cool handwriting, but it's sometimes hard to read. The class was very fun and interesting . His lectures were pretty clear. Quizzes and tests clearly correlate to lectures and problem sets.
Awesome professor! Doesn't emphasize grades and wants you to be there so you can learn.

I took this class over the summer, so idk if Thomas is different during the school year, but overall the class was fine, the hw was time consuming and the lectures were quite boring. prelims and final were open notes but still quite difficult.
Many kids are struggling in her classes. You're only graded on 3 exams and 5 homework sets. Office hours are limited and unhelpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The only slightly redeemable quality about this professor is her lectures are moderately enjoyable things about her class. I have given her the benefit of the doubt but it is clear she does not care if her students pass or fail. She is mean and nasty, I just sent her a question I had for exam and she replied "it depends" with no other explanation.
DO NOT TAKE! I earned an A, yet I still regret choosing this course. DO NOT put yourself in this situation!
Doing the HW and going to the lectures ain't enough. Half the stuff that are on the exams don't make sense. Gets mad for no reason and she's boring.

Extremely disorganized and poorly managed course! She is very unhelpful during interactions and dismissive of student concerns. She often creates unnecessarily difficult situations for students and lacks clear communication. Final exam was a complete disaster, 40+ mins late with no organized seating plan. Ppl were literally cheating in line.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I started the year attending every lecture... I quickly realised that was foolish and a waste of time. Her slides are poorly made and horribly taught. It was far more useful to spend class time self-learning all the concepts from the textbook readings. Also, her exams are 25 MCQ with no curve. Get 2+ questions wrong, and u can kiss an A/A- goodbye.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: People who say Thomas is a 'bad teacher' or 'doesn't know what she's doing' simply don't go to lectures or do the homework. The class is extremely straightforward if you put the work into it. 1. Read the textbook, its not that bad. 2. Ask questions in lecture, she is very helpful. That's it. I never went to office hours but I'm sure they're helpful
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Disorganized + careless. Professor mishandled the final: some students seemed to start 30–40 min early, discussed questions, took photos, and bragged about ChatGPT with no enforcement. Exam was nothing like practice/MindTap. Lectures felt rushed, questions dismissed, expectations unclear all semester. Grading felt arbitrary too. Avoid at all costs.
She's a lovely person and I had several insightful conversations with her during her office hours that I really enjoyed. Economics is just not for me, unfortunately.

lecture slides, hw, and practice prelims are SO UNREPRESENTATIVE OF THE REAL EXAM!!! not enough practice problems, class is 75% graded on exams, and exams are 25 MCQ!!! NO CURVE!!!! if you take this with her, be prepared to self-teach yourself EVERYTHING.
Do not take her ever.

Avoid intro with her! Lectures are boring. Her practice exams are in no way an appropriate reflection of the actual exams, and all exams are 25 question MCQs so if you get more than 2 wrong be ready for that B! Highly ineffective and made students line up to get the final exam which wasted more than an hour.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: THIS IS A JOKEEEEEEEE. Do not take this class no matter what like seriously. The prelims and final exam was literally insane, like the questions were so hard and nobody was prepared for that level of difficulty. Also she is actually evil like she made a class of 300+ students line up and sign in for the final exam, which wasted 45 min, like what??

Avoid Econ with Thomas if you can. I left lecture every day feeling worse about the content than I had self-studying. Her slides are badly done, horribly explained, and whatever "group work" she had us do was irrelevant to the test. Prelims are 25 questions, no curve, so the difference between letter grades is often 1 question wrong. HW also sucks.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It's really hard to study for the exams—her practice prelims and homework's don't reflect the difficulty of the final exam at all. The exams basically decide your grade so they're really important, too. No one goes to lectures because she doesn't teach well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Stephanie Thomas is an ineffective, disorganized teacher. She will cover surface-level material during lectures, but you'll have to know the material on the bottom of the iceberg for exams. There were dozens of typos on the second prelim, and a question on the final had no correct answer... in a class with 15+ CAs.

Greg Mankiw is the GOAT!

Consistent exam errors and refuses to curve despite low medians. Claimed the historical median was a B, after our final, contradicting the syllabus stating that it was a B+. Extremely disorganized—made two sign-in lines for 200+ students, wasting 40 minutes of our time. Ironic for an economics professor who preaches efficiency but practices none.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE ECON 1110 WITH THOMAS! All of the exams were the weirded in the worst way possible you would probably get a better score if you guessed. Also constant typos and errors in exams.. For example she forgot to put THE ENTIRE ACTUAL QUESTION for one problem and just gave a graph and answers and then "forgot" to add a correct answer to another

ALERT: DO NOT TAKE. Lectures are useless as she just reads off the slides. Prelims and finals are only 25 multiple-choice questions, worth 75% of your grade, and she refuses to curve. Also, she drags lectures way longer than needed. Worst class I have ever taken. If she took her own class, I don't think she would pass. I would give 0/5 if I could.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The actual tests were very different from the practice tests. Also, many people were able to cheat on our final due to the way she organized it.
actual exams are so different from practice exams and only 25 questions on each gives little room for error. poor at answering student questions and dismisses concerns about exam difficulty.

Take Econ 1110 with any other professor. Her lectures are very elementary compared to exams. This class was much harder than it should've been and I did almost all my learning through youtube (DrAzevedoEcon you are the GOAT) and through the textbook. Also, do not be fooled by her open note policy as I found it was not as helpful as it seemed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pt1) This class was unequivocally the single worst organized class I have ever taken in my life. In fairness, to  Prof Thomas I never went to lectures so she might be a good lecturer, but the difficulty of the material was far from the problem in the course. 25 multiple choice questions does not work.
do not take this class

🥀Weak excuse of a Professor. She will teach an elementary topic, such as utility, for 40 minutes. This topic will then never appear on any prelim, and will barely appear on the homework. The assignments are tedious, she seems to find joy in her students' hardship, and she is so corny.

As I write this review, I find myself struggling to convey the deep anger that resides within me when I think of Econ 1110 with this sad excuse of a professor. Please do yourself and your GPA a favor and literally avoid this entity like the plague. You have been warned. Take a different class your fall semester and WAIT for a different professor.

Possibly the worst professor I have ever had. Lectures are useless, as they spend time demonstrating first-grade-level problems just so the tests are astrophysics-like. Final exam had a problem with no answer. You have to learn the whole class on your own from the textbook or YouTube. Can't really say anything good about this class or her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The exams used to be online, but she changed them this year to paper. Averages used to be over 90 (duh), but now they're in the 70s. Yet, she refuses to curve. The prelims are substantially harder than the practice exams/homeworks. Do not take this class if you want to actually learn. Take Sanders or Orlov.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The exams were much more difficult than the practice exams and lectures useless, you have to study 90% on your own from the textbook.

reviews.comment: I think that Stephanie Thomas cheated her way through school. Exams could not be designed in a way to make cheating any easier. This women has no idea what she is talking about and is so disorganized I question if she even knows that her TAs exist.
do not take her class.
lectures are mostly useless, and the 3 tests worth 75% of grade, with each only having 25 questions. she is a pretty reasonable person but the structure of grading is kinda brutal.

only ppl who excel are those who are econ majors that already understand the material

Prelims were online and problem sets were assigned (allocate more time to learn the concepts on these). If you do the practice exams and pay attention in review sessions, you'll be fine.

reviews.comment: Is extremely boring and just throws tantrums in class out of no where.

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE! While her lectures are clear and she explains concepts well, her exams—though similar to the practice exams, homework, and lectures—are extremely time-pressured. You know the material but won't have time to write the details she expects. With only five questions per exam making up 75% of your grade, scoring high is nearly impossible.

reviews.comment: Please do not take this class for your own sake.
Bad professor in general
