reviews.comment: Not only is Professor Ajunwa a great lecturer, she also cares about her students and is easy to connect with beyond class.

Went from live to online. Taken for ILR soph writing requirement. Prof is nice and pretty knowledgable about her topics. She struggles to communicate how to do assignments and when they are due but doesn't grade harshly. You may have to ask her multiple times. Not too much work and it isn't too difficult or tedious. I think participation matters.

Prof. Ajunwa has been my favorite professor at ILR to date. Shes a knowledge powerhouse and was terrific at teaching labor law in a way that would benefit non-lawyers. During the pandemic she was also very flexible with students, which is a true gem regardless. Dont miss a class with her if you can help it!

Professor Ajunwa is very smart and a great teacher. She knows a lot about law and technology, and many of the class readings were her own papers. She grades pretty lightly, and class discussions can be pretty interesting. Her one flaw is that she sometimes struggles to communicate assignment expectations and deadlines.
Standout professor at Cornell. Challenges students in a thought-provoking and respectful way, and does not take sides -- instead kindly pushes all ideas. Unique teaching message. Strongly recommend.

This was an excellent class. I truly enjoyed the class and found the material to be current. The prof. is extremely knowledgable in the subject matter. The couses leades to and to ann understanding ofthe changing nature of work as influenced both by technological advancements and changing attitudes about the role of work and work/life balance.

She is nice and willing to help students during and after the class. In the class, she will prompt you to think and discuss the real-life decision-making scenarios in a variety of ways. The reading materials, though heavy loading every week, also help a lot before in-class discussions. I am glad to have those articles and books finished.

She does a great job in leading really thought-provoking discussions and challenging our assumptions. I especially liked her efforts to help us apply business and legal concepts to real-world cases and her flexibility in adapting to the class's needs. She's a fair grader and gives clear feedback. Anyone who takes a class with her will learn a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Manages to turn extremely interesting subjects into extremely boring academic droll. Class forces liberal media and ideas down your throat. Took it to learn about Tupac and Biggie, not trans rappers from Puerto Rico that no one knows about.
She was incredibly disorganized and difficult to understand.

Fun and interesting class; you'll learn a lot about African history and culture while doing some cool music workshops. Professor clearly enjoys teaching the course  and is always available to help you improve your papers and assignments.
Good professor, always enthusiastic, and very approachable.  Clearly enjoys the subject matter, and always responds quickly to questions and concerns.

Everything about her is unprofessional. She refuses to speak audibly, she gives no trust or respect to her students, and she scans material too quickly for comprehension. Her lectures are painfully tedious, and her essays are contorted and impossible. She is an atrocious grader, and doesn't mind failing everyone. Avoid this class at all costs!

The moment the course moved into more conceptually difficult territory Apanasovich pretty much became incoherent. But she was still really helpful and often dedicated entire classes to explaining concepts about which students expressed confusion. It also doesn't hurt that she's extremely attractive...
This professor was very soft spoken, and awful in her teaching methods. Her PowerPoints were useless, and exams were extremely hard. Avoid this professor unless you want to ruin your GPA.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Prof Apanasovich is hard to follow at times. She gives good tests, not many homeworks, fair.  What really helps to get through the class are her looks, she is hot in a quirky, nerdy kind of way.
The prof is very approachable and clearly understand the material. It really helped to be comfortable with asking you questions and talking to her.
fun ...not boring at all...the material is very interesting and cutting edge...and it helped me to get a job offer, very glad I took it
Great class, the professor is very sweet and helpful. Learned a lot, would recommend  anyone who is interested in Data Mining to take it.
WORST PROFESSOR AT CORNELL EVER!
Boring class. Learning to use SAS Enterprise is cool. Learning useless mathematics is not.
Booooooring!
Professor Tanya is a very sweet, wholesome young woman. ... She is a great person and a good teacher...
HOT
this woman is not a very good teacher, all of her lectures are straight out of the book. will sometimes also test random bits of information too.

very boring professor, very monotone. i thought this class would be fun and relatively easy, but it is not interesting at all. shes not a very good lecturer. basically reads right off slides, so going to class is not needed. tests are pretty fair though

Immunology was very interesting and I learned A LOT!  Appleton is one of the nicest and fairest people at Cornell (curves test to 88%) and she is very interested in her students doing well.  Guest lectures were great.  Downside is 8:30 AM in the vet school...I fell asleep a lot so reading the text was crucial to doing well.

Basic Immunology is a demanding class:  meets for an hour and a half twice a week, and covers a lot of material.  Very interesting, though, and Dr. Appleton is a really excellent professor: fair, understanding, timely with posting material, while maintaining high standards.  Powerpoints are comprehensive study tools and expanded on in class.

There are no "tricks" to this class. The exams can be challenging on occasion, but if you can achieve a baseline understanding of the slides in her presentations you should be able to master the tests no problem, which doesn't seem like too much to ask from someone who goes to Cornell... Prof. Appleton is extremely nice and very helpful

This professor teaches Immunology.  I thought this class would be fun but unfortunately this professor is extremely boring.  It doesn't help that the class is at 8:30 in morning.  Also, the tests are ridiculously tricky for no reason and her lectures are sooooo long (about 38 slides each).  I suggest not taking this course.

Nice professor. She is really knowledgeable. She is helpful during office hours, but she asks you to think hard instead of giving you the answers straight out. Exams were tough, material is extremely tough. But a great class to take if you are interested in analog IC design.
Lectures weren't very stimulating. Basically followed the book word-for-word. Homework assignments and lab reports were a pain. As long as you study the material, the prelims aren't difficult.
No Comments
Lots of work, but overall a good class
she knows her stuffs.  And when I took this class, she is really good.  She gives lots of help and I simply choose my career path after taking her class. I want to do what she does.

She's smart, no doubt about that...but she lacks coherence, organization and enough of an intuitive approach to teach the class...she expected students to know way too much; homeworks and test are long and difficult; labs are worthless and she's very inconsiderate of students' time; don't take it

She's a smart woman, but she REALLY doesn't know how to teach. Her "lectures" are just straight out of the text. Homework takes too long, and class isn't exactly a walk in the park. She isn't that helpful either unless you hound her with questions.

Very difficult class.  Lecture consists of reciting the book... better off just reading it instead.  She has a very heartless and uncompassionate personality.  Final project expectations were ridiculous for time given to us.  I hate analog design now because of this class.
She is one of the greatest teachers that I ever had!
she's actually very nice in lab, knows her stuff and is willing to help. she's not that good at lecturing, but definitely someone who makes an attmept to help her students.
She's better that Lal at lecturing and she helps alot in lab...doesn't seem very approachable, sorta serious personality but once you ask her for help she'll be sure you understand what you're doing
I can't believe how bad the two professors for this course are.  how do they expect us to learn anything from such an important class when we don't have any good professors or ta's?

Anne Bracy is a great professor who is very clearly knowledgeable in C/C++. Her explanations clarify why and how the code functions within memory. Her grading scheme is very fair, especially for prelims. Pay attention in lecture and take notes alongside hers (filled notes are not posted). The course material builds on itself, so don't fall behind.
Amazing professor, very caring. Her lectures make difficult concepts much more intuitive and understandable.
It is very tough to feel positively about her. She makes up convention on-the-go and confuses me more than helps. I learnt best when I skipped lecture and read on my own.

Taking online online classes with this prof explains everything very well

CS 1110 was organized well—as someone who has not used a single computer program before. That being said, the assignments were sometimes a pain and some exam questions were really difficult. I took this for a distribution requirement, and while I really liked the coding, I would not go back. Remove the (HANDWRITTEN) exams and I'm on board.

Anne Bracy is definitely one of the better professors in Cornell CS (which isn't saying much, but I digress). She is a great lecturer, yet still has a strong non-teaching background. I liked how she handled 1110, but she made the labs too inconsistent in workload and made the prelims far longer than was realistic, leading many to not finish.

reviews.comment: Great, encouraging professor with clear, easy-to-follow lectures. Holds helpful office hours and review sessions. Projects in the class are a great balance of challenging and engaging. Learned a ton in the class and would recommend to anyone who is trying to get into CS!

Anne Bracy is one of the best professors I have at Cornell. I came into this class not knowing anything about CS, and I walked out of this class with an A. The materials were very interesting to me, and I enjoy them substantially.
I loved Professor Bracy- she is truly a great lecturer and has a very impressive professional background. She made me want to major in CS!
Good lectures, very accessible and caring about students. Difficult class with a lot of workload but Bracy does a good job at navigating the course.
Crazy analogies. Intense workload. Interesting content. Compassionate professor. Can't ask for much more.
Amazing professor! Very kind and inclusive. Lectures always very well organized and prepared. Engaging lectures.

CS 3410 is no joke. The projects are challenging and ridiculously time-consuming. I think Professor Bracy makes the course fair and is a great lecturer and professor. My only criticism is the exams in the course are much more difficult than they should be and are frankly really hard to study for.

Wonderful lecturer! CS3410 is a challenging and difficult class, but Prof. Bracy's lectures makes it bearable with her jokes and funny/good examples and comparisons. She is also super accessible outside of class, and is supportive of students with disabilities. I think anyone who says otherwise has to reflect on their (internalized) misogyny.

reviews.comment: Professor Bracy is great at what she does, lectures are very content-heavy but always worth going to. Do NOT procrastinate projects or you will come to regret it, office hours are available all week and very helpful. She gives lots of relevant practice materials for exams and although the tests can have hard questions, they are all graded fairly.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: (Note that she gave a textbook but literally no one used it) Very clear lectures, assignments are pretty straightforward, tests are fine if you study well. The class, in my opinion, is not meant to be a class to take "for fun." It's pretty time consuming, and Bracy expects a lot, but she made a significant effort to ensure students are prepared.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Pretty easy class, feel like I learned the fundamentals well. Lectures are not the most helpful, but the labs and assignments are great to learn.

This is more of a review of CS 1110 than of Prof Bracy, but I have zero prior coding experience and learned a lot and liked the course without being too stressed by assignments or exams. Class is heavily weighted and a few exams had very low unweighted averages (60%-70% range usually), so it's usually possible to recover from a bad test/assignment

Great class and great professor! The material could be challenging at times but she explained things amazingly clearly and often worked in fun examples to keep it engaging. The class does have a fair bit of work, specifically time consuming projects. Luckily projects are very interesting and there are lots of office hours.
Spring cs1110 is much easier than fall cs1110. Bracy didn't really impact me during the class, but I thought she was fine.

I don't have any experience with her in other classes, but in CS1110 she was great! Not perfect, but I certainly felt it necessary to attend lectures just because of how fluent she was in explaining the core concepts. The class itself was very difficult, but I think she certainly alleviated that a great deal.
A professor that forces financial hurdle on students by requiring physical iClicker.

I was a repeat cs1110 student this spring (took walker white last fall). Bracy and Lee are a great combo for teaching and I found the assignments more interesting than in the fall, and therefore I was more engaged and completed the course successfully. If possible I would wait until the spring to take this course. I feel more confident in cs now.

3410 is a tough class because material is new to most people and there's A LOT of work, even if it's mostly just busy work. Concepts usually build on top of one another so you do not want to fall behind. Class will seem overwhelming at first but gets better. Felt that Bracy makes the class doable contrary to what others might say. She's also funny

Fantastic lecturer! Makes CS clear to all, whether you are a first time learner or more experienced. Professor Lee writes tests and assignments, but Bracys lectures are super helpful for these. Would highly recommend taking!

Prof. Bracy was awesome, and I was pleasantly surprised by the way she taught CS. This class is definitely not easy, and requires a lot of effort, but if you put in the time and effort you will learn so much. Bracy was very nice, helpful, and accessible. The tests are hard but curved, the course is quick but help is given to people struggling.

Professor Bracy held all lectures for this class and ensured that all concepts were easily explained in class. While, many of the topics were extremely difficult to a first time programmer, it was clear that all topics were learned in a professional manner with clear examples that were performed in class.

Clear lecturer who's very passionate about the subject, and makes many references to Wegmans during the lectures. Went through numerous examples during class when covering more complex topics like caches, and reduced the difficulty of the assignments to accomodate for a hybrid class format. Had a reasonable slip day policy for project submissions.

Professor Bracy's class was so incredibly difficult for the sole purpose of being difficult. Lectures move so incredibly fast, projects have virtually no guidance and are difficult, and exams are not super related to projects and are still hard. I did more work for this class than any of my others classes and was miserable for each second of it.
Bracy is an excellent lecturer and really cares about her students. That doesn't mean the assignments and prelims aren't insanely hard...
Terrible person. I was hospitalized for a week and she forced me to use all of my slip days instead of just granting an extension like a human with empathy.

Bracy is a great teacher and clearly knows her subject. Her lectures are well-designed with clear language and she drops hilarious lines from time to time. This class covered a lot of highly technical details and sub-regions of CS, and not attending the lectures would make it hard to understand the slides. That said, the textbook is comprehensive.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Really I wish I could give her 0 star. Just dropped the course, and do not understand where those good comments come from.
Not intelligent in teaching at all. Confusing lectures, baffled homework... I hope someone could let her know how awful her lectures are. By the way, she is rather mean and arrogant in the same time.

I love Bracy! She's a great professor and her lectures are done in a way that is easy to understand and accessible. Assignments are always geared towards what we have already learned; if you can do the assignments, the tests should not be too difficult. There are clicker questions to log attendance, but they're only 5% of your grade.
One of the worst classes I have taken.
Unintelligible class.

Bracy is a god among men. Never have I seen such a professor so passionate about both the material and her students. She gets so excited teaching and talking with students that it makes lectures my favorite time of the week. Yes, the class is difficult and condensed, but if you pay attention in lecture, the class is very manageable. SHE IS AMAZING!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Professor Bracy is a talented and funny lecturer. Her lectures explain material extremely well while also being fairly concise. CS 3410's projects were hard (10-20 hours per project) and its exams harder, with means around a 55/90. I would highly recommend taking her classes she teaches.

Bracy is an amazing lecturer and made this class (which could have been terrible) pretty enjoyable and interesting. I really loved her classes and thought the assignments were pretty standard for a CS core class. Also, she's awesome to talk to outside of class and genuinely cares about her students. 10/10 would recommend!

Bracy is so great that I'm taking CS 2110 with her next semester. I loved her teaching style because I am a very visual learner (she's won teaching awards). She inspires great questions from her students in lecture, and the lecture material clearly laid out what was expected on exams. Beware of the tricky assignments and make use of office hours.

Her lectures were usually pretty good, but sometimes slightly disorganized. She's super nice though and has plenty of office hours! Apparently her assignments were a lot harder than the fall CS 1110 professor's, but they were doable.

Bracy is by far the best professor I've had at Cornell! She is passionate about CS and her lectures are clear and enormously helpful. The assignments were quite difficult at times but prepared you greatly for the prelims and final. I came in with zero coding experience and learned so much in a semester. Challenging but immensely rewarding class!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She is a great professor. Her lecture style was clear, and I the examples made tough concepts easy to learn. Her expectations were clear and it was easy to gage how I was doing in the class. Not an overbearing amount of work, and makes CS really fun to learn. Also, she is just an awesome human.
I really loved cs3410 with her :) I maybe only scraped past tests, but it was worth it for the interesting lecture and great content.

Best undergrad professor I've had. She turned systems from a hated subject of mine into my graduate focus. Negative comments below are reactions to unconventional teaching. Lectures focus on concepts, exams are difficult but test your grasp of concepts in terms of big picture. Not a cookie-cutter professor/lecturer - what makes her great.

Great Professor. The lectures are very clear. Attend the classes since It takes more time to figure out the lecture note than just attending the class. Not sure why are there so many very negatives comments. I took 4410 in the Fall semester. The lectures are a bit slow and repetitive and the projects are pretty difficult. But t's fine overall.
Super difficult class, but the best proffessor I've had at cornell
Awesome teaching with low scores. Think thoroughly before you enroll!!

Fun lectures that fly over topics at the speed of light. Be sure to read up before lecture begins (there's HW before every lecture to help with that) and take notes like a good student. Tests are difficult and annoying as they often test a concept that you know well but contorted so that no one knows how to answer. Still, great, fun person.

The class is harder than it has to be. Concepts in lecture are briefly touched upon, with the majority of content being self-taught. Lectures and projects have little overlap, and tests are hard to predict. Bracy is good at teaching in lecture, but little of what she teaches is actually useful for the tests and projects.

Overall, I wish there was more thought put into the course. Projects were not well planned, had too much time to complete, but little support. Having weekly problem sets would have helped students know what to focus on. Many difficult topics on the exams were covered in the book, but glossed on in lecture. Had to self-study to do well on exams.

Little to no TAs use the piazza, and some of the answers are rather rude. Tests have means in the 50s and are unrelated to anything learned. Lectures have minimal overlap with projects, and the projects are very hazily laid out. For one project, we were told to simply google any questions. It's a shame this course is mandatory.

Bracy  loves using analogy to make the material less bland, but  3410 material is something that requires accurate and technical language!!

Never take 4410 with her. She clearly knows 3410 well, but completely messed up 4410 to the point of making (the very new) Prof. Agarwal look bad. She is mean and extremely useless in her office hours. She even co-organized the office hours for the two courses she was teaching that fall. Messed up the entire course and worst part were her lectures.
Go to office hours. Nothing in lecture can even compare to the evils of Logisim and malloc.

I don't know whether my negative experience with prof bracy owes itself more to the overbearing nature of the class (and I mean this class approaches levels of work akin to 19th century industrial revolution standards of labor), or to her stone cold, stoic conveyance of the material. reviews.comment: Prof. Bracy is a great lecturer whose skill was sadly undermined by the incompetence of her co-professor.  I had her for both CS 3410 and this class, and I would say without a doubt that Prof. Bracy will go out of her way to help anyone who needs it, and is capable of much more than she was able to demonstrate in CS 4410 when I took it.

Bracy is unorganized, uncaring, and mean. Unwilling to help students and a very boring lecturer. In several instances, she would release grades for assignments 2 months after they were due. Her class organization is poor, has no accountability, and is not a good nor fair lecturer.

Despite Prof. Agarwal's messing up of the entire class, she was actually a good lecturer and you can tell from piazza and office hours that she actually cares and wants students to learn and succeed. She was organized and clear. 10/10 would recommend

I really like Anne as a lecturer but this class was just awful. 3410 was good but 4410 was by far the worst class I've taken at Cornell. I'm not a big fan of the material to begin with and the fact that this class was a logistical nightmare did not alleviate that issue. I really hope they get it together.
One of the best professor at cornell! Homeworks can be a little disorganized but her lectures are always interesting, informative, and entertaining.

Professor Bracy is one of the best professors I've had at Cornell. I took a class with her, and also was a TA for another class that she taught. Her classes definitely aren't easy, but she really cares about giving her students the best possible experiences and does everything that she can to help them succeed. Would definitely recommend her.
Nope
CS 3410 is a mandatory CS class and Bracy made it as painless as possible. As long as you make use of all the resources, you should be fine.

As Anne Bracy describes it, CS 3410 is like "trying to drink from two firehoses." This class is a TON of work, and the concepts are very hard. However, Bracy teaches them really well. She knows her stuff, and can answer any question you throw at her. This class will be near impossible, but Bracy and the TA army will help you out.

Wow, Bracy yourself for 3410 cause it's the bomb dot com. While the projects/ homework aren't too hard, they are time consuming. The 3410 TA army and Bracy is there for you though, so you are in good hands.

Shoutout profesora Alice she always brings a positive attitude and you can tell she cares about her students' learning and understanding how to read and write in Spanish. Just be ready for a good amount of work (as all language classes are) and occasional cold calling and presentations, but other than that she the goat
Really amazing teacher. One of the best I've had. You have to put in some work but really not that bad. Def recommend taking this class with Professor McAdams.

Really a great class. The professor is great and she really cares. She will introduce you to amazing new music shows movies and podcasts in Spanish. The class really improves ur Spanish with lots of speaking exercises as well as a lot of immersion with Spanish media.

I absolutely loved having Professor McAdams as a teacher! Class didn't feel like a chore, and I definitely improved my Spanish skills though the course. Her lectures were very easy to understand and in class activities were fun, engaging, and helpful. She is very kind and clearly cares about all of her students and their success in the class.

Lecturer McAdams graded harshly regarding participation and often gave unclear instructions for exams and expected attendance during office hours to understand oftentimes necessary elements. She was very rude when interacting with various students which soured the learning experience. In the future, I hope she practices more empathy.

while her class can be stressful at times (cold calling! presentations!), she does her best to make the class chill and challenge her students to become better speakers and writers. however, if you don't do your work, you will not have a fun time. 

(1230 w/ her also involves a lot of spanish music, so you can pad your spotify playlists with this.)
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor McAdams is very disrespectful and discouraging to students. She answers all questions in a snarky manner, states that any question that she does not want to answer is "stupid", and she insults students if they don't immediately understand a concept. She will destroy your interest in studying Spanish.
Well-respected and knowledgeable professor. Lots of reading, but a fair grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Allen is a super nice person and totally willing to help you. However, he is really busy (I believe) and it is hard to find him after class. Still, I highly recommend taking his course and enjoying the discussion there.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This course involves tons of reading. Interesting lecturer, just lots of work.

Carlson is a very solid and nice, if uninspiring professor. His lectures are always clear and if you're interested in China he sufficiently will stimulate it. Workload is easy too. However, he is very disorganized (not giving out assignments in time, always being late, etc)

Professor Carlson's lectures are extremely boring and he never replies any emails. But it is an easy class with easy grading.Read the materials and go to lecture regulatory will almost guarantee you an A range grade.
Ok. I dont know if he does this because he got tenure but he NEVER replies to your emails. If he does, it is after several days or weeks. I would never take his course again.

Useless powerpoint and a ridiculous amount of reading, but Carlson is a GREAT professor nonetheless. He really knows his stuff and loves what he does. Chatting with him during OH can be very intellectually stimulating

Carlson is a very good professor.  His lectures are interesting, his readings a bit much but informative, his assignments fair, and his stories funny.  He is very intelligent, dedicated to his material, and personable.  If you have interest in this material, even if you have not taken 181, I strongly recommend this course.

Carlson did a good job of presenting the material.  He's relatively funny and doesn't expect too much from the students.  He allows students to participate while not losing focus on the material.  He is easily able to tie everything together to create a cohesive course.
I find many of his lectures to lack structure; he no longer uses prepared notes and fails to substantiate his key arguments with empirical data.  I find this to be a fluffy poli sci course.
very knowledgable and will debate you at will.   a good guy and a great professort
Professor Carlson knows his stuff, is helpful (wililng to listen to student concerns) and gives fair tests. If you do the work getting an A shouldn't be a problem.

this is a guy who calls people out on BS w/o compunction--earning my respect on day #1. but he isn't self-impressed about it; he just knows his stuff (and how) and has enough respect for his students to demand they substantiate everything they say. great.
Lectures are really interesting and easy to follow because they're usually outlined well. A good speaker.

personally, i think poli. sci. is puss, and i usually don't have a lot of respect for its students or teachers.  HOWEVER, Dr. Carlson just plain dominates.  He knows both his chin. hist. and just about everything post-revolution.  take his class.

I thought this was a very accessible class for those trying to get an overview of environmental law. I had no issue with the Exams, there were cheat sheets available, and the questions were relatively straightforward. Attendance is mandatory, as it is with all law classes, but I didn't mind that. The professor is very amicable and experienced.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Chatrchyan is not a law professor, but she taught a course heavily reliant on understanding of American law. She was often unprepared for lectures, redirecting questions to undergraduate TAs or back to the student who asked for clarification. The grading rubrics for exams were unclear, leading to confusion from students and TAs.

Slides were poorly made and presented, exams were made the night before being given and contained frequent mistakes, grading was unfair and TAs could often not explain the rationale of their peers or the instructor. Readings are heavy and interesting, completely necessary to pass. Would only recommend this class if you LOVE environmental law.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Allen is truly a great professor. He is unapologetically himself, and it is so refreshing. It is not often that I come across a challenging class that I look forward to attending. I would highly recommend Dr. Allen to anyone interested in learning about biology, physiology, or life in general.

Amazing professor, made a pretty difficult class bearable. My grade was not because of the professor but my own fault, and if you put more time into learning the material than I did, you can get an A.
Don't be fooled by his jokes, toughest tests ever. You can study for a week straight and still fail, test format just doesn't work for me.

Dr. Allen is an amazing professor. He takes the time to learn everyone's name and really cares about his students. The class had an annoying amount of work (especially in lab) but I learned a lot. I would say the class is mostly busywork and memorization more than anything. Also lots of opportunities to earn points outside of prelims

Dr. Allen is awesome. His class is certaintly difficult, but he is super open to working one on one with you if you are struggling. 100% recommend this professor - he is truly hilarious and one of a kind.
yes yes yes yes Yes yes

Dr. Allen is one of the best professors I have ever had. Not only is he passionate about the subjects he teaches, he is always trying to make sure his students understand the material and is more than happy to answer questions. His lectures are hilarious and he really cares about his students.

very understanding and funny prof. his jokes in the class are to die for and actually helps rmbr info to study for for exams. exams are reflective of lecture slides (memorize slides to get a good grade). he is a very understanding and kind person and provides so many resources to do well in the class :)

Great teacher and very funny, the perfect person to teach this class. Everything you need for the tests are on the slides, and there are so many TA office hours as well as his own that you can go to if you need help. If you do poorly on tests there are plenty of other assignments that can boost your grade. Study the slides and you'll be fine.

It is impressive that Professor Allen makes everyone feel comfortable talking about reproductive biology. His lectures are fast paced but very entertaining. All the information is on the slides (no readings, hardly any homework). If you study hard for tests you'll get an A.

He is one of the kindest people on campus. He is the perfect person to teach the intro course and makes you feel like you belong immediately on campus. The course is a lot of material, but he gives enough bonus and other non-test opportunities. He makes an effort to know everyone in the class, and with a class of that size, it's amazing.

Class covers a lot of material, but everything is explained so clearly that I always felt prepared before exams. He creates in class activities that are direct reflections of exam material, very helpful for review. Very explicit course expectations, grading is very fair. He is very knowledgeable of the material, and I am glad I took this course.

You need to work hard in this class. Attend lecture + study weekly and you will do well in this class. Dr. Allen puts in 110% to every one of his classes and makes sure that every format is available to his students; lectures, lab, hands on learning, recordings, etc. etc. The TAs also try really hard too and their office hours are very helpful!

He's a “if I tell you the answer you're never going to learn” type of professor (if you get something wrong on an exam you're never going to know why unless a nice TA decides to tell you. He often says something rude and excuses it by saying it's just his humor.

He's a good teacher if you're naturally smart, and he masks his rudeness with being funny. His jokes can be funny, it does make class more interesting. If you're not naturally smart you can study for a rest for two weeks straight and answer all the questions, but still get points taken off for not being specific enough, even if you got most of it.

His teaching style definitely didn't match my learning style and there was a lot of fast paced read off the slides type lectures. That being said, his TAs were super helpful, his slides are detailed, and the lab was well paired with the lectures. If you're confused, just ask your questions and you'll be fine
Dr. Allen is a gem to behold. He is hilarious and engaging. He cares deeply about all of his students and helps them succeed, even with things that do not relate to his class.

Dr. Allen is a great lecturer and makes class interesting even when the topic is boring. the class is very difficult in my opinion but the exams reflect the class material and the grade you receive is very representative how much effort you put into the class. there is a textbook that is provided for extra help but it was not used in class.

Dr. Allen is awesome. Explains all the material well and lets you know exactly what he's looking for on tests. This class has A LOT of content, but is completely doable. Don't need the textbook at all and TAs are a great resource. The total course grade it made up of a lot of smaller things, so a bad grade on a test isn't the end of the world.
By far my favorite professor at Cornell. This class was much easier than domestic but still a challenge. Would recommend him to anyone!!!!

Dr. Allen is awesome! He loves his students and works to see you succeed. Its a very big course with lots of content. Sometimes content is skimmed and prelims can be very difficult, but he makes the class fun

Super funny and great professor, really understanding and loves to get to know his students. This is a super hard class because of how much content there is, but it is doable. Stay on top of studying and go to TA's if you need help with figuring out how to study for this class. I didn't like TA exam grading and how lab was run though.
just take him. Literally my favorite, ever.

Dr. Allen is one of the best professors in the Animal Science department. His classes are difficult but not impossible - you just need to be able to put the work in. He is super personable and really cares for his students. I cannot recommend him enough!

Yes, the course is hard. But Dr. Allen makes it 100x better and much more manageable. If you try your best, he will work with you to help your succeed. He does do random attendance checks, so just beware of that. But overall, this is one of my most favorite classes I have ever taken and most of the reason why is because of Dr. Allen

Avian Management is an easy class compared to 1100 and 2400. He makes the prelims difficult but only because he wants you to study and learn the material instead of brushing the class aside. It was a fun class, and I learned a lot. There's no final but instead a group final project that makes the last month of the semester a little easier on you.

Cornell should pay him triple his salary. His back must hurt from carrying animal science. He's the Michael Jordan of talking about reproduction. If you didn't take BIOAP1100 this class will be really hard, but if you did it will be challenging but easier than domestic. People bring friends not in the class to lecture cause he's that good.

Dr. Allen is a great professor. He is very personable and is always there as someone to talk to if times get tough. Funny guy too; he makes a lot of inappropriate jokes but makes sure to not cross lines and will apologize if he does. Overall, tough course but I learned a lot. He makes sure your education at Cornell is rigorous. Prelims suck though.

Jeremy is the goat. If you disagree you are wrong. He genuinely cares about his students more than any other teacher I've ever had. The class is difficult, but he structures it so that everybody can succeed and offers so much support. He can offer you so much help inside and outside of the class; my Cornell experience is 10x better because of him.

Best professor at Cornell hands down. Hilarious guy, makes you feel so welcome your first year. I suggest any freshman taking Domestic their first semester to get to know him. He helps you so unbelievably much. Get as close as you can to him. Fantastic guy.
Dr.Allen was a top tier professor, I literally take any class I can with him.

It's not a difficult class if you keep up with it, and he's more than fair on every assignment. His exams are extensive, but he will prepare you for every single question. He's funny, but often toes the line. If you put in a little bit of effort to build a rapport with him, you'll find he's very helpful. A mainstay in the animal science department.

Dr. Allen is understanding and caring. You can talk to him about anything. Tests are reasonable for ansc2400 and bioap1100. He is also inspirational and hilarious, incorporating memes into lectures. His lectures are clear and his mode of instruction is among the best professor I've had in cornell. Fantastic professor!

Dr. Allen is a really wonderful professor. He is there to help students who are struggling whether it be with the class itself or with problems outside of class. In both the lecture and the lab he creates an environment conducive to learning and also makes an inclusive space, in and outside of the classroom. Expect to put work into the class.

Dr. Allen is very charismatic and a favorite in the animal science department, evidently. His lectures are engaging and he makes a real effort to foster a comfortable and relaxed classroom environment. His grading is a bit questionable, as he inflates individual assignments but then deflates the class as a whole. Otherwise he is highly recommended.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This man was by far the BEST professor I have ever had. His lighthearted attitude and amazing teaching abilities have allowed me to thrive in his class. He is always SO supportive and such an amazing person to talk to

Dr. Allen is one of the best professors I had in Animal Science. He is compassionate, enthusiastic and extremely reasonable. He wants to make class accessible to everyone and is truly enthusiastic about teaching and the subject matter. He is very open to communication and has a great sense of humor, but that doesn't make his class an easy A.
Dr. Allen is an incredible professor. His classes are engaging and entertaining, and you will learn a lot, however this isn't necessarily an easy class. You have to pay attention and stay engaged.

Absolutely the best professor at Cornell hands down. Cares about his students so much but won't just give you the credit, work hard and you will be rewarded. Most respectable and down to Earth guy you'll find teaching any class. Lectures are interesting and funny. Even people that never had him know of him and think he is amazing.
Hands down my favorite professor. He makes everything fun and engaging and will do his best to make sure that you do yours. The class is not easy, but the content is very clear.

Dr. Allen is by far my favorite professor at Cornell so far. Besides his evident knowledge and passion for the material he teaches, he has a remarkable sense of humor that makes his class extremely engaging and fun. The nature of the course certainly requires lots of memorization so be ready to grind. On the bright side, Dr. A is extremely helpful

Dr. Allen is one of the nicest professors I have ever met. He truly cares about every one of his students. He makes lectures fun with jokes, memes, and stories. You definitely have to study hard to get a good grade, but he also gives out extra credit. He picks really good TAs that are also extremely helpful. I wish all my professors were like Dr. A

Dr. Allen is genuinely kind and understanding. In lectures, he takes time to thoroughly explain concepts while keeping students' attention during longer and complicated topics. He has a fantastic sense of humor but maintains respect. During office hours, he is receptive to all questions and willing to meet additionally for any reason if needed.
Dr. A is probably one of the nicest profs you'll have the luck to learn under at Cornell. He will listen to you, help whenever he can and honestly, do his darndest to make sure you don't flunk.

He's a nice guy with a great sense of humor, but don't let that fool you into believing that you can get away without studying. Prelims and quizzes require a huge amount of memorization to do well on, so try to avoid this class if you aren't ready to grind.

Dr. Allen is an amazing person who can teach very well, but expect to study very hard for this class -- lots of memorization needed. Really unavoidable as it is an ANSC requirement, if you are having trouble start meeting with him when the semester begins. He lets you retake your lowest test, and the final is usually multiple choice.

Dr. Allen is a great professor. Lectures are always organized and clear, and he is always very transparent about what material you need to know. Gives plenty of extra credit and is flexible with deadlines. He is very understanding of his students and just overall a very genuine person. Best ansci course I've taken at Cornell.
a jocular and knowledgeable professor. Never stop thinking for the students, exams are very fair as long as you study.

Hand down, this was the best class I have taken so far. He is hilarious and makes sure as long you do what you need to do he will help you pass. He cares about his students and offers many resources to make sure you understand the material before the test.

Professor Allen is the best professor I've had at Cornell thus far. He genuinely cares about his students, and it is clear that he truly wants us to learn and understand the material. His tests are never designed to be unfair or unnecessarily fastidious, but rather to fairly judge what we have learned so far. He is enthusiastic and compassionate.

Dr. Allen is by far my favorite professor at Cornell. Absolutely hilarious, makes learning really fun and easy. Course content is very manageable and exams are fair. Plenty of opportunities for extra credit. I'm going to miss this class a lot and wish I could take it again with him.
Dr. Allen is one of the best professors and individuals I've had the pleasure of receiving. He is absolutely hilarious and cares a lot about his students. I wish I could take his class over again!
Wonderful, informative class

Dr. Allen is a great person and professor. He cares about his students and gives engaging lectures. One of the best professors I've had, and repro is not my thing. He doesn't grade on a curve, but he's willing to give extra credit. If you go to class, he makes it pretty clear what kind of stuff will be on the exam, but he's a good lecturer anyway.

Dr. Allen is the best!! If you are a dairy student struggling through the ANSC required classes, don't worry he does a lot of lectures that tie into basic dairy knowledge with regard to repro. It is challenging, but only if you make it that way. Attend lecture, take notes by hand, go to review sessions, and ask questions!

I loved Dr. Allen!! He really cares about his students doing well. While he doesn't believe in curving, he gives many free points and always offers extra credit opportunities. He will always tell you exactly the topics you should study before prelims. He's hilarious and his stories related to the topic he's lecturing about are always so funny! :)
Dr. Allen is truly the best professor I've had at Cornell. The class isn't easy but the lectures are understandable and enjoyable. He's a wonderful person.

Dr. Frith is an amazing professor who genuinely cares about nutrition and her students. NS2060 is a great and low-stakes class. I really feel like I bonded with my GPHS cohort. I'm not sure that it was super helpful in finding my ELO, but I enjoyed this class and it's an easy A+. Your grade is just attendance, reflections, and a group project.

Dr. Green was one of my chillest professors this semester. The class within itself it's a chill class aimed for an easy A, so as long as you show up, participate, and work hard on the group projects and critical reflections your fine. She wants you to succeed, and its low stress in my opinion.

She is very nice and understanding and clearly cares about her work. The class was slightly unorganized but the workload was low and it was easy (mostly focused on career exploration and exploring global health to prepare for ELO). Not super useful but I enjoyed it.

This is the worst class I have taken at Cornell. The professor doesn't care about her students, the feedback on assignments is unhelpful, the class is completely unorganized, and the content is pointless. When talking to her one-on-one, her tone is very condescending. This class is a requirement for the Global Health major/minor, so beware...

She is kind, personable, & easy to reach. Encourages participation, but in small groups. Tests are easy bc they are all grammar & vocab. The hardest parts of the course were the amount of work (so much hw!!), essays (bc she is a very harsh grader), & oral presentations. Overall I found the course to be easier than AP Spanish, if that helps anyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Silvia is honestly a great professor, but her class is really hard. I had to drop it because it was taking too much time and was going to lower my GPA. Lots of work and a really tough grader. She cares about your learning deeply and wants to see you improve your Spanish. I am retaking with a different prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: VERY HARD SPANISH CLASS and she is a harsh grader. would not take it again

Silvia is a wonderful professor and an expert in the Spanish language. The course is not easy at all, but Silvia's job is to improve your Spanish, and that is exactly what she does through constant conversation and comprehensive feedback. Silvia makes herself extremely available for outside help, and it is very clear that she wants you to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Literally the worst part of Cornell by far. Spanish has actually ruined my whole semester and, in running the Intermediate Spanish program, I can see that she clearly doesn't actually care about teaching. Tbh she seems more like the type of teacher that prides herself in making her class hard even if the material doesn't help us learn anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: There are rarely instances where she is actually teaching spanish because the entire class is done in small groups. She cares more about if you do exactly what she says than if you are learning the language. It feels like there is an exam every day. Curriculum of SPAN 2090 is merciless, and she just makes it worse. Try to take it with someone else!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I was intimidated by these ratings but IRL, Silvia is great. After months without practice, she refined my Spanish and empowered me so much. Make use of office hours and make sure she gets to know you. Her feedback is super helpful on ensayos and she will go over your test errors personally. Silvia made online learning feel more doable!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The content of this class was not difficult coming out of AP Span in high school, the challenge was the workload. The class meets 3x per week, and there is at the minimum 2-3 hours of HW due the following class every single class. However, if you are struggling, she is sooo accessible in office hours and will genuinely try to help you succeed!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Silvia is one of the best professors I have ever had. She's a tough grader and the material isn't easy, but she's super helpful during office hours and I was in her office every week because I liked talking to her so much. She cares a lot about her students, so put in the work and you'll get good results!

Silvia isn't a good professor. She has single-handedly ruined my passion for Spanish. Every class of hers feels like torture. She is a super tough grader and expects you to talk, speak, read, and write like a fluent native speaker. Plus, she assigns many hours of homework per class so you can never escape. In short, don't take a class with her
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Silvia will make you work for your grade, but you will inevitably get what you put into the class. I started off really lazy and my grades reflected it, but she gave me a nudge and knew I could do better so I picked it up towards the end of the semester and my grade improved. She's a little contradictory sometimes with what she expects in homework.
Professor is a solid OK. Definitely not entertaining but bearable. A ton of busy work. Attendance is mandatory. Easy A, especially if you took AP Spanish.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The small class size facilitates interpersonal dialogue, and Silvia is AMAZING. She is caring and wants her students to succeed at Cornell and in her class. I definitely think Silvia's great teaching would allow any motivated student to succeed. Does a virtual exchange with students in Colombia, which was a great experience. Lovely person.

Silvia was my favorite professor this semester. She's caring, reasonable, and highly encouraging. The class was definitely a lot of work at times, but it was always manageable and within reason-- your Spanish WILL improve. I initially took the class just to fulfill the language req, but now I've been inspired to continue Spanish throughout college.

I was initially very intimidated by the syllabus and considered dropping the class, but she encouraged me to stay and I am so glad I did. She is the best Spanish professor I have ever had, and I learned so much more from her in just one semester than I did in all my years of high school Spanish. And she returns things promptly. Amazing professor!!

Best Spanish teacher I've had at Cornell. She's pretty strict on the Spanish-only policy, which is good I think. Gives feedback on rough drafts for every essay. Class activities are generally pretty interesting. She was very helpful in office hours.

Silvia has been one of my favorite professors at Cornell so far. She is very patient, and makes Spanish fun! I learned way more with her in one semester of Spanish than I did in 5 semesters of high school Spanish. I would definitely recommend her and her class.

Silvia is SO nice. She is super friendly, personable, and welcoming - I always felt comfortable. I always got the feeling that she really wants us to learn Spanish properly. I do have to say that it isn't an easy course. She is really tough in the essays, it's pretty impossible to get an A, BUT I cannot believe how much my Spanish improved.

I'm in a class she coordinates. I like the person who teaches me, but not the coordinator who creates the syllabus. The work that this crazy lady makes us do is just absurd. I probably learned much more with other better professors who actually engages us in Spanish, not just drown us with useless works.

Agree with her ideology to get a good grade. What happened to "ANY PERSON any study?" She dislikes wealthy people and/or americans. The whole class is about white americans discriminating against hispanics. She did equate conservatives with materialistic people and tested us on this "fact" which was ridiculous. Horrible.

Don't try to even discuss politics. She's from Spain, living in america, yet claims america sucks- really frustrating and demeaning if you try to discuss things she doesn't agree with- half the time she's wrong anyways. like the one time she said that rightists and materialistic people were the same b/c all republicans just want money. :(

Likes things done her way. Does not help with verbal skills; she will finish sentences for stumbling students, rather than letting them figure things out. Grades papers severely, and essays must be written according to her stylistic constraints, which conflict with those taught in most English departments. Neither friendly nor helpful.

This is a great class if you are all about spanish. However if you are in it for an easy grade dont take it. She doesn't offer any extra help other than her office hours which fall on class times, and is very strict on grading in regards to essays and tests. Orals saved my pathetic grade.

She's very knowledgeable and clear, but she is mean and completely surprised and  offended when you don't understand something or her class isn't your first priority. She accused me of cheating, and even though I wrote an essay in her office and proved that I hadn't, she never said anything, no apology, nothing. Don't take her unless you love Span!
Very good teacher.  Helpful with explanations and very open to giving extra help.  If you make the extra effort to meet out of class time, she will make the extra effort to help you too.

Her class was easily the most frustrating and terrible class I've ever taken.  She's nice, she's helpful, she's overly demanding and often shocked when students don't understand "easy" concepts.  I don't know how much of that is her fault and how much is how Cornell structured the course, but either way - you're in for a LOT of work.  Watch out.
She SEEMS nice but I thought she was mean!! She embarassed students when they didnt know the answer and she graded tests and essays really hard, with little option for rebuttal.

Silvia was such an amazing instructor.  I had her for 2 semesters, and I learned more spanish from her in a year than from the combined efforts of all the teachers I ever had in high school.  She's helpful, enthusiastic, positive, and awesome in general.

TERRIBLE! SOCIAL ENGINEERING CLASS! Newman feels Any challenges, failures, or misery non-white people face in life is not their fault. And, even worse, there is nothing they can do to change their circumstances. So, just stew in your bitterness and hatred for White males along with her and her like, so goes the leftist campus orthodoxy of the day!!

Prof. Newman is calm and talks slowly. Sometimes she was not able to control the class. As each class of Cornell University worth a ticket of a Broadway show, Prof. Newman's classes obviously do not worth that price. For instance, she asked students to do mock interview one by one for 3 consecutive classes while she did not give much useful feedba
She is nice and helpful, especially when you actively seek her help.
Tough grader. Very friendly.
Prof Newman is one of the best Man Comm teachers. She's about as interesting as you can get for this course, and truly a very nice person.

Man Comm is Man Comm and she is better than snow. I thought she was pretty good for Man comm, she is a good mix between Snow and Arlisse/Dahl. You actually will learn something and she won't harass you like Snow.
better than snow but still man com

Really nice lady. All the mancom teachers are hard graders so it's understandable that she is also. Assignments are reasonable and applicable for the future. However, I felt her feedback was weak. Overall, it's a good class and I'd take her over Snow anyday.
Passionate about computational biology, and tries her best to make lectures engaging. Cares about her students, and responds to both questions on Piazza or via email.

Prof Williams is a fantastic teacher who cares deeply about her students. She is passionate about the material and manages to take complicated machine learning algorithms and makes them manageable. Be warned that projects are always longer than you expect, though they tend to be graded nicely. She is extremely responsive and a great professor.

Professor Williams is very caring about every individual's success in her class. Assignments are challenging but doable if you put in the time and ask questions and they are very relevant to course material. Her lectures were often times not the most clear, but she does try her best to be engaging. Graded on five problem sets and one final project.
Mike is a tremendous leader in the dairy industry. Actually being able to know and work with him in classes is truly amazing.
great professor, very intelligent
world renowned professor. Negative comments below are because people never bothered taking classes this man actually offered.
He is so biased its ridiculous. He loves you if you're a dairy student or in agr he hates agsci students.  Overall I dislike him.

He is a really nice guy, and does a pretty good job keeping the class interesting, by telling jokes and talking about his life.  But the class is only about dairy cows, not other animals.  A lot of field trips, not much homework, no prelims, but there are 5 quizzes, 4 different professors take turns teaching.  Overall unfocused

This class has a lot of potential, but falls short. When Mike speaks, you can tell that he's both extremely intelligent and extremely biased towards dairy and Italy. You can't blame the guy since dairy is his life, but you can't help but wish he would try to show all sides of the arguments he presents.

Great class and professor. He really helped me in my ability to see both sides of an issue. Teaching style is different than most other professors, but in a great way --makes you pay attention. He also expects input from his lecture students.

Lectures are really biased towards the meat industry.  It's an easy A, but the lectures all seem random and unfocused and skewed opinions are presented as fact.  It's not a requirement for the an sci major, so if you can possibly skip it I would-- I can't imagine much of a practical application for the information presented.
he retired but im giving him a 5 for the vibes

Chill prof. Test questions can be a little vague and confusing sometimes, but overall still very easy. There's a group "community project" that's pure busy work. Graded on 3 prelims, discussion attendance, and that project. A+ is very doable, but first prelim always trips ppl up. Great way for non-STEM ppl to coast through their bio requirement.
Chip is a really cool guy. The lectures can be boring at times but the workload is very doable. I'm more interested in genetics just because of his class!

Chip was one of the kindest professors I've had at Cornell. 1290 was easy and only required a weekly discussion post and take-home prelims and finals. The lectures can be a bit boing, but attendance is used as extra credit. Easy A/A+ class except the take-home exams can be a little tedious but TAs offer a lot of help
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: fun class and kind professor.

The lectures are tedious and the take-home prelims are long and challenging. You go into them with essentially 0 understanding of how to answer and just have to sit through office hours until a TA spells out the answer for you. Ridiculous class.

BIOMG1290 is perfect for the PBS requirement, but it's not a waste of time either. Chip is caring and invested in this class, and though he makes it easy to do well, you still learn a lot. One of the nicest professors.

great class. take-home prelims and a take-home final. exams require a decent amount of thought/time but chip and his TAs will help you in office hours! go to class and discussion and you'll be fine. wish i could take this again, was really interesting and not too too hard

The best prof I've ever had here. Some of the lectures are a bit boring but Chip does a great job connecting material in class to the real world! Is always available for help, is smart, and cares deeply about his students - always says hi, checks in, and even takes time at beginning of class to congratulate student-athletes in the course on wins.
Wish I could take this class again. Such a kind person and professor who cares about his students so much. Not too hard and grading is fair

Chip is hands down one of the best profs I've ever had. Cares deeply about his students and the subject matter he teaches. Is there for you to help at any time, and exams are fair if you do the reading/pay attention in class. He goes out of his way to keep students engaged by doing DNA testing/bringing in guest lecturers. Really smart and kind.
Seemed like an easy class. Exams were unreasonably detailed. TAs were awful (except one). Discussions were pointless. It was cool to get our DNA tested. This class needs some serious tweaking.

The material is quantitative and kinda boring. HOWEVER, it has some extremely interesting applications. And Chip is a pretty good professor, always approachable with questions. He's really challanged me as a scientific thinker and I actually feel smarter thanks to his class.
He knew all our names by day 2! And cares tremendouly about his students' success.

Generally, I would only recommend to take this if you already had some tennis experience beforehand (at least JV ish level). Pretty chill guy, actually found out that he knew some of the kids who played tennis back home. Class is a little bit of a workout (definitely kept me in shape haha). Overall, definitely recommend.
I actually got better at tennis during his class, but he did extend the class to like a week after the end was supposed to be rather than just canceling classes due to inclement weather.

Well all of the previous comments certainly scream sarcasm...  For an "advanced" class, this was pretty much a joke.  We stood around and hit down the line or cross-court nearly the whole time, before playing some useless game.  Arthur is...interesting...and knows his stuff, but his own strokes are sort of odd so his examples can be kind of off...

Arthur Arthur he's the man...if he can't get low, no one can. Arthur's brilliance in taking the sport of tennis and innovating it into exciting and fun minigames (including the one where he feeds you the ball and you play the point out from the baseline)...he should win the Nobel Prize for smart people... ehh where's my curry?!

This class, most simply put, is MONDO.  Arthur is great, and as Paris Hilton would say...That's Hot.  The intermediate tennis class was an experience of a lifetime.I am ready for the advanced class, and I can hardly wait ... loves it!  Take this course for a good time ... Have fun!!

Arthur is the MAN! As long as you love to play tennis, and you don't mind "GETTIN LOW" for shots you're going to have fun in this class. Must take...highly recommended.  You can do pretty much whatever you want, and you play this cool game all the time where he feeds you the ball, and you play doubles from the base line.  THIS GAME IS GREAT!!!

A bit montone but still sweet and very knowledgeable. Lots of extra credit and quizzes were easy. The final essay was gradely very leniently. Quiz questions are a bit rough unless you take notes from the slides. Prelec recordings were a bit info heavy. Besides that really easy and straightforward class.

I mistakenly uploaded the wrong final file. Over break I sent an email, asking if the project despite missing revisions could be graded. She replied by pasting my words, said nothing could be changed, and signed off with a snarky “use this as a lesson,” which felt mocking and unhelpful. The tone left me discouraged. I could not recommend her.

I was disappointed with her quality of instruction and the course's extremely unclear grading criteria. Without any mention that the class before spring break was worth double the points for attendance students were forced to receive a lower grade. Similarly, for course assignments, grading was unclear and her answers to course questions were rude.

Cider is twice as much work as Wines and Vines in half the amount of time (seven weeks). Grade depends on weekly quizzes which may cover complex topics not mentioned in class. Two papers around sensory evaluation, apple production, cider fermentation, and/or marketing/economics graded (harshly) by peers. Very fun daily tastings and guest lectures.

As a VIEN major, I take a lot of courses and labs taught by her. She's very nice and available when you have questions. However, the lectures are difficult to follow and not structured. Most of the time she reads off the slides and adds random pieces of information. Most work are done in class with groups.

Attendance is a huge part of your grade, and specific notes in class are a must. Quizzes are based on what Kathy says in class, but may not be on slides. Points lost on quizzes add up on final grade. Extra credit final exam to bring your grade up. She knows what shes talking about, but sit in front because the acoustics in stocking hall are awful.

She knows what she's talking about when it comes to wine, and does a really good wine tasting evaluation. The lectures tended to be a little dry in terms of interaction and engagement, and it's hard to get her attention to ask a question.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took Wines and Vines with Kathy and found it to be very interesting. I took the class coupled with an online program recommended to me by another professor who also teaches for the National Wine School and that really helped me understand the lectures. Getting a sommelier certificate along with an easy A was a great result.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took VIEN 1104 because I thought it was interesting and I am taking the major, but Professor Arnink is very hard to pay attention to and the slides are impossible to follow. She's very nice and willing to take your questions, however, but this requires you to be proactive. Class is extremely easy though, but don't expect to retain much information
Professor Arnink is great. She is really well read in wines and a very interesting lecturer. Her classes are easy to pass if you care. I wish I could take more classes with her!
This class was the easiest A+ I've ever received.  There's so much extra credit available that if you show up, you will get at least an A. Definitely recommend!

I really enjoyed Wines and Vines and would take another class with Kathy in the future, as she was friendly and willing to help her students. I learned a lot about enology and had the opportunity to sample a wide variety of wines from all over the world. Highly recommend this class, not sure what the other guy is going on about.

The courses Kathy teaches are all extremely unorganized and there are lots of little assignments with unclear instructions. When you ask questions about due dates, lengths, etc she tells you to look at Blackboard, which usually doesn't help. I receive good marks on everything, but if you like organization, DO NOT take her classes.

Absolutely adore Dr. D. He made the somewhat difficult thermo material understandable, was always available for extra office hours or answering questions. 2 prelims were not too hard, final was harder than anticipated but still very doable. Super kind and awesome. GOAT

The lectures for this class were not the most straight forward, but the in class assignments and homework helps to reinforce the material. The tests are fair and generously graded. He is very accessible outside of class and corrects mistakes very quickly.

Professor D was great. The online part of the class was convenient and the lectures were very engaging. If you have any background in any physics this class will likely be way too intro level for you, but sometimes you're looking for that easy class. 5 tests felt like a lot but you end up dropping one. Material is a bit random at times but is easy.

Dr. D is a good professor all around. He is really kind and wants his students to succeed. If you need help, he will help, and his behavior will never dissuade you from going to lectures. My only issue is that the lectures were sometimes pretty confusing and required extra studying.
Oh, and there are 5 tests.  Luckily you can drop one.
Overall a manageable and comfortably paced course in thermodynamics. Course consists of quasi-weekly problem sets and two prelims which were fair.
can be disorganized on the lecture materials but otherwise cares about the class and the students.

Dr D had Interesting lectures and was knowledgeable about the subject but it was hard to go back and follow lectures without rewatching them as PowerPoint/class posted notes weren't stellar on their own. Homework and climate math (quantitative quizzes) were manageable, plus no exams during covid semester, only weekly multiple-choice quizzes w drops

My favorite professor so far! Lectures were super clear and he was very encouraging and helpful to everyone in the class. He didn't have specific office hours but was really easy to schedule a meeting with outside class. Definitely make sure to pay attention in class because he may call on you to answer a question & you'll do better on the homework

Taken online. The lecture slides are confusing but the prof does a good job explaining them. Grading was very lenient and based on weekly quizzes, take-home quizzes, and simple assignments. Not sure if he will go back to tests once online is over instead of the weekly quizzes. Take this class if you're interesting in scientific climate change stuff

A very animated and passionate lecturer - you can tell he cares about the subject. He also genuinely wants students to succeed and always answers questions. Prelims are pretty straightforward and similar to class examples, and he gives good study guides.

One of my favorite professors at Cornell. The course is challenging, but interesting. Professor DeGaetano will make you work for your grade. Great course, attendance is key; he says things in lecture that you will be tested on and they are not in the lecture notes/slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Absolutely fantastic and passionate lecturer! He's very helpful and willing to guide you thru the fairly complex psets. Exams were 50 minutes in-class which means the questions are fairly conceptual. Would recommend, great professor.
Made me find my love for physics!

The best and the most "physics" physics course I've ever had! Truly inspiring and interesting! The materials were very tough, but Prof. Arias made it engaging and thought-provoking through his clear, logical, and amazing lectures. Recommended to all who want to learn and understand physics! Very helpful for future learning!

Arias is so great and makes such an effort in his courses! I would definitely recommend taking a class with him. The material was tricky but he's always available to ask questions to and wants his students to do well and feel passionate about physics.

[Rating for honors waves] Very theoretical and math-heavy. Lectures are very clear and well-organized, with a focus on derivations, not applications. Gives very useful lecture notes. Provides loads of useful support and office hours. Exams are fair and much easier than problem sets. Problem sets are difficult and VERY time-consuming!
I didn't actually take Professor Arias's class for 3316, but I pretty much did, considering I substituted all of Jian's lectures for Arias's lectures.

Truly some of the best lectures I've experienced at Cornell. Prof. Arias' unique PSets were really long and hard, but were some of the most insightful I've ever done. Very knowledgeable professor who can also help with all sorts of physics and math problems.

Prof. Arias is the best lecturer I have ever seen. The class was at 9 AM, but each day I woke up excited to climb the slope and watch his lecture, being sad when it ended. The homeworks can long, but extremely informative and rewarding to do (arias makes his own questions). Exams are fair. Arias is a rigorous (mathematically) source of knowledge.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Arias explains things very clearly and his class is extraordinarily organized. Although Psets were hard, taking 10-15 hours (I never went to office hours bcuz of time conflicts, which may have reduced the time ), I gained a really good foundation for quantum mechanics. Exams require you to work really fast but they're fair and easier than Psets.
Arias gives fantastic lectures. Course website is well prepared. Homework are quite a lot but generally inspirational.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Arias was one of the most passionate professors I have had at Cornell. Even though I despised physics, he somehow managed to make me enjoy the class.

Arias is a nice guy, but is not very accessible to get help from. The P-Sets were incredibly difficult, covering material not taught and requiring 5-12 hours a week in office hours. The TA's often weren't sure how to do the questions (citing them as being harder than some of their grad-level P-Sets). OHs were ALWAYS packed (50-80 kids at a time).

Professor Arias is a wonderful professor that really cares about his students. The problem sets and lecture videos/pre-class exercises are a lot of work, but Professor Arias' dedication to his job makes it very enjoyable and worth it!!
Take him now - it will be a fun ride.

Good teacher, only complaint is that the tests questions were asked in very obscure and confusing ways. Many of the tests were based on randomly plugging in formulas, without the need for much physics.

Arias knows A LOT, and wants to meticulously prove things to his students. He is a GREAT lecturer, and is very open to talking to students both in and out of class. Homework was really difficult and took many hours (for me, 8-15), but I did come out of it a lot better at math.

Arias is very passionate, which makes lectures more enjoyable. Other than that the class is crap. The discussion section is not representative of the difficulty of prelims. The problem sets are WAY too hard and do not help you for the prelims. In my experience, you feel like you know your stuff and then the test rolls around and you don't.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: I liked the flipped format of the class but I found the homeworks to be unnecessarily difficult. The tests were difficult but nicely curved. The lecture videos and questions were informative, organized, and easy to complete. If you put in the time to understand everything and attend lecture as the course goes on, you can do well.

Physics E&M was a lot of work and demanded a lot of time that I sadly did not always have. Prof. Arias is a really nice guy who genuinely cares about his students and is truly happy when the median grade on exams is high. Don't sweat the problem sets too much, as long as you understand the Co-Ops you'll be okay for exams.

Arias really cares about the students. He gets very happy when people in class understand the topics in lecture, and if they don't, he does his best to clear things up.
