This course is very fast-paced, and Arias doesn't like to waste much time. The problem sets are incredibly challenging, but if you understand the COOPs you'll be fine on the prelims
He really wanted to see us succeed and seemed genuinely happy when prelim scores were high.  Probably the most likable professor I've had so far.

He kind of reminds me of a dad. He was very approachable and encouraging during office hours. I started off struggling, but he was always willing to accommodate my learning style. Some people liked the flipped classroom method, and things really started to click once we switched to videos.

Prof. Arias is a good teacher.  I learned a lot through his 'flipped classroom' method of teaching.  I would highly recommend watching the video lectures at  a faster pace, as Arias speaks kind of slowly and pauses a lot.  You can take a 45 minute video lecture and turn it into a 12 minute lecture.  Major time saver. Definitely attend lecture.

Professor Arias is the best professor that I have had in my time at Cornell. He is kind, approachable, knowledgeable,  and an all-around great guy. When students voiced concerns, may it be with format or content, he listened and acted, at one point even starting to produce hour-long video lectures to help. He is amazing, and deserves high praise.
Clearest professor I've ever had. Empathizes with what the student knows and doesn't on a intimate level. However, you'll have to do a lot of work for his class (if you want to do well, that is).

Arias is truly dedicated to making sure his students understand the material. The exams (with the exception of the multiple choice on the first one) were very fair and very straightforward. Problem sets were challenging but very doable. He also made himself available for questions and pretty much wouldn't let you leave until you understood it!

Best professor I've had in my four semesters thus far. He's extremely helpful and genuinely wants everyone to succeed. He's also very passionate about the material and teaches is better than anyone else could. If you have a chance to take a class with him, don't pass it up.
Simply the greatest

Arias is an amazing professor. If you ever have to take 2213, make sure he is teaching. Arias is so caring about students performance, and he is genuinely a nice guy. This is a really difficult course, especially if you struggled in multivariable like I did. The problem sets are hard, but they prepare you well for the exams which are pretty fair

One of my favorite professors at Cornell. His lectures are theoretical but he make tough topics extremely clear to understand with a lot of enthusiasm. He cares a lot about his students and truly wants  them to learn the material. Tests are slightly challenging but the homeworks prepare you well for exams.
Wonderful professor; however, he curved the class to a lower grade then normal, so that contributed to lower grades. Very clear and enthusiastic.

Best professor I've had at Cornell yet. If you're the type of person who just wants to memorize equations and apply them then you will probably not like this class. However, if you  find the subject interesting and want to truly understand the fundamental concepts then Arias is a spectacular professor.

Probably one of the most brilliant people I've ever met. Lectures were indeed mathematical- but in the best way possible. Contrary to what some would say- his derivations go far beyond what's written in the book. He generates his own problem sets that are tailored to what you'd expect to see on an exam. Phenomenal instructor for a phenomenal class.
HORRIBLE! do not take a class with this professor. literally did not learn a thing. makes me fail every prelim because he does not teach us how to approach the difficult problems he presents.

If you don't enjoy the derivations involved in learning physics, then you don't enjoy physics. They're the point of it. That said, this class is amazing. Arias approaches electromagnetism intuitively, and teaches all of the fundamental concepts and theories by deriving them. If you really do like math and physics, you'll love Arias.

Does a pretty good job explaining derivations during lecture.  Pay attention to these as they are pretty close to what the problem sets and tests are like.  I do admit the class is very "mathy" although it's really not bad.  The problem sets are good at bringing up old material so that you are always practicing what you've learned
He spent all of lecture going over derivations provided in the book, and just made us do math heavy problem sets. I would recommend not taking the class with him.

Absolutely brilliant. He focuses a lot on theory and mathematical calculations during lecture and doesn't really give much application and problem-solving, but he is very organized and extremely clear in his explanations. Would definitely take another course with him.

For electromagnetism this semester, the lectures were not very helpful with regard to exams, feel free to skip them and read the textbook. The problem sets were excessively time consuming and calculus heavy. He's not that bad, but I recommend taking this course with another professor in the spring semester.

This is a review for how he taught electromagnetism for engineers. He gave extremely difficult problems sets, but the prelims were fairly easy. His lecture is very easy and simple, on the conceptual side, but that will not help with the homework which all rely heavily on vector calculus. The lectures were not all that helpful for exams either.
Hes the professor now for autotutorial physics. Take this class. He's good at explaining things and a very smart man. Course is time consuming but easy grade.

Pretty much what everyone else said.  Very good teacher, knows how to explain things in a way that's easy to understand.  The class wasn't too hard in my opinion, but I think they curve the class to a pretty low mean grade, so you need to work pretty hard if you want an A.

this was one of the harder classes i've taken.  this guy really has a solid command on the subject and it able to communicate and teach very well.  i should have put more time into this class to get a better grade.  exams and homework are hard.

Best physics professor I've had, but that's probably because honors physics profs aren't that great (Veit Elser, Pollack...). Really loves physics, and does a good job explaining the stuff. Exams are pretty tough, and homework is tough! (it goes step by step though, so you'll know what to do) Go to his lectures and do the homework!

fantastic professor and course! problem sets can be a bit challenging, but they're well thought out and you really feel like you've learned a lot when you're done with them.  most helpful professor i've had at cornell.
Very Very good teacher, though HW sets were kind of hard, exams were all relevant to his homework problems. Highly recommanded!!!
Very good teacher, excellent explanations, made a tough class a little more bearable

I took this class a while back and didn't do well on it (C+). But it's not an easy class, my TA wan't that good, and the class itself was competitive (std dev is like 5 points on prelims), so it's not his fault. He's clear and helpful, and I definitely should have gone more. GO TO LECTURES!!!
Quality lectures. Exams are fair. And that time he dressed up as Morpheus from the Matrix... What more can you ask for in Cornell?

This is simply the best physics teacher I've ever had. He really loves teaching. If you are taking Physics 214, take it with him. He will challenge you, but you'll end up loving the subject beacause of him.

Great Teacher! I usually skip classes, so it doesn't mean much, but for the times I was in class, I understood what he was talking about even though I missed half the material before that class. It was also immensely enjoyable to see such an EXCITING smile on his face all the time.
His excitement is clear, but he should really drink less coffee before lecturing!!
No Comments
Prof. Arias is way too organized (prelims had tables of contents). Great teacher and nice person.

Lecture was presented clearly and orderly. He really knows the material! A little of it went over my head, but I'm an ECE major, so that's ok. He added a lab at 8AM on Friday!!!  I wouldn't have taken the class if had known!
A really great prof -- knows the material and enjoys teaching  Publishes notes online -- helpful
This guy rules.  He enjoys what he's teaching immensely, and makes physics lectures interesting.  The subject is tough, but he's more than willing to help you if you need it.
Yo... he is da man... not

Great professor. You do actually have to study for the tests but they aren't too bad. He is a fantastic lecturer and I've never enjoyed a class that doesn't allow technology so much. When he talks about chimps there's an art of storytelling there and its quite enjoyable. I look forward to class every time I have it.

Super well organized. Took the summer course, asynchronous. Everything was meticulously organized and easily understandable. Grading was fair and content was actually super interesting. He touched on real world issues, beyond just facts of biology. Highly recommend.

If you need a bio distribution requirement, especially as a humanities major, take this class! The readings are short and relatively interesting (not too much hard science) and they are not tested on the exam. While you do have to study for the exams, they are not particularly intense. The lectures are also engaging and easy to understand.

I had professor Arcadi for a FWS that turned out to be all about canoes. He is a chill and nice guy, you will write 10 essays over the course of the semester but with a guaranteed A if you do the work and come to class! You will have a solid amount of work but I am glad I was in this class

I wouldn't recommend this class if you're merely trying to fulfill the A&S bio requirement. This is an amazing class if you have strong interest in the subject matter. His office hours are very helpful. However, do not expect an "easy A" out of this class -- the medians for the exams were quite low, hitting the C+ and B- range (without a curve).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. Even if you didn't have interest in chimpanzees prior to taking the class, you will by 2 weeks in.

Such a nice guy. Super accomodating to my family member's illness. Can follow along with online lectures, but in person is much better and better for retaining knowledge. Cares so much about the topic, and is really descriptive allowing anyone to ask a question about whatever during class. Spots usually fill up so mostly seniors. Bio distribution.
makes chimpanzee science fun!
Professor Arcadi is an amazing professor. He has left a tremendous impact on me, and ultimately influenced my major.
A very reasonable teacher. This class was a decent amount of work but was manageable. Professor Arcadi is a witty teacher who inspires thought and creates a fun class environment. #superfun

Prof. Arcadi is a wonderful professor and is really passionate about the subject of biology and primates. His lectures are clear and well-crafted and the readings he assigned were also interesting. Through this class, I learned more about the lives of chimpanzees and their similarities with humans. I'd highly recommend everyone to take this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I love this man with all my heart. Caring, compassionate, thoughtful, smart, everything you want in a professor. Professor Arcadi understands what matters.

This class was really interesting and Prof Arcadi structures his lectures very well. The tests weren't difficult (24 hours, open note) but it definitely required knowing the lecture material. Prof Arcadi was super nice and loved the subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Arcadi is great online. He crafts his lectures with so much care, and they are very well-organized. The prelims are 24 hours, which hasn't been hard thus far. He knows so much, and his enthusiasm is contagious. The flexibility of the asynchronous lectures and the optional office hours are great too. He's just a nice dude

Professor Arcadi is hilarious, interesting, and very experienced in the field of anthropology/primate research. He's surprisingly approachable and likes when students go to his office hours. GO TO CLASS (on time), pay attention and don't make the fatal mistake of pulling out your phone in class. He's a great professor and gives amazing lectures!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Tests are lecture-based, no Multiple Choice, essay based. Exams are not cumulative take really good notes, you will need it for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Arcadi is a really good lecturer; he conveys the information in an interesting and engaging manner. He's funny, but if you're late or have your phone out he'll be (justifiably) pretty rude. I personally liked his tangents and occasionally subjective ways of describing things. I ended up learning a lot in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great lecturer, conveys a lot of info clearly and concisely. Read a total of 4 books with 8-10 about them at the send of the semester. No final only prelims. Lectures aren't mandatory but you will miss a lot by skipping. Section is bi-weekly and either you go or write a two page paper about the reading. I would highly recommend this class.

Professor Arcadi is engaging and passionate. His class on chimps was easily the most interesting class I've taken. It was very fun. You absolutely need to go to class and take notes. He only lectures, with no powerpoint behind him. I was surprised at how much I liked this approach.

The most appealing aspect of Intro to Anthro is its low difficulty.  Arcadi's organized and you will learn a thing or two, but he also makes the occasional rude comment or focuses more on giving his opinions than objective info.  Textbook is officially required, but you can probably do fine without one.
Discussions tend to go off on tangents but this is decidedly a good thing; one of the main reasons why class with Arcadi is interesting.  Very bright guy and very opinionated.

I took this class on a complete whim, and it was by far my favorite of the semester.  Professor Arcadi was a great lecturer who seemed to really care about the class, even though it's an intro level.  he was organized and engaging and very, very knowledgable.  take this class!!
Interesting class...Prof. Arcadi is clear and has well-organized notes...class is not really hard but exams can be pretty tough if you don't study enough
he's fun, and spent a lot of time hanging out with chimps... so he knows his stuff.

This is a good guy.  The classes are surprisingly interesting for a science class.  It's also not hard.  It's definitely a good class to fill requirements, fairly easy, and the labs are just sections (not real labs).  Definitely a reccomended course.

Prof. Arcadi has a very stern attitude and he likes to scare people during the first week of class by embarassing those who come in a couple of minutes late - but he is very clear and knowledgable, and he can be fun. I think he looks a little like a mix between Hugo Weaving and a wolf.
He's such a nice guy! His lectures are organized pretty well and he likes to engage his students. He makes his course material fun to learn.

He's a really great prof!! He wants students to do well - if you are struggling/need help/want something to be different, tell him. Super accessible outside of class. Make sure you find a friend to do the end-of-class quizzes with (it's allowed). He is so nice and enthusiastic. Applies concepts to specific examples really well.
I loved this class, the lectures were very interesting and accessible! a rare for cornell classes
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Okay class. DeGeatano clearly cares, but he's just a very poor communicator, and the class is not organized in a way that makes it engaging. Would be a lot better if it were split up into sections so that we can discuss rather than listen to lectures. Also, dense with material, yet geared toward non-science majors. Reinforced my dislike of physics.

One of the coolest profs at Cornell! Very clear, funny, personable, informative.  Excellent at explaining material, but you have to go to class. The slides he uses only have graphs and figures that you won't understand unless you actually go.  Gives a few short homework assignments that are helpful to reinforcing class material.

So this is one is coming from a meteorology major. The man is in his element with the smaller classes, like EAS 341. He's a very nice guy, more than happy to help you out in class and in his office (he never has regular office hours). Likes to call on people at random though, and gets flustered when he loses his place in his notes.

This is coming from someone who took this course to satisfy a science requirement. That being said, the course is dense with material, and no sections don't help. Take this if meteorology is your focus. Also, don't be that kid who tries to wing it w/o talking to Art. He's a good man, and very approachable.
Great class in which you learn about the cool stuff in Meteorology(Lightning, rainbows, halos, radar...)
The nicest man ever.  The tests are exactly from lecture notes, don't read the book.  Only about 6 homework assignments.  Lectures are interesting.  Would take this class several times over.

Physical Meteorology is really tough, and your notes will just be derivations, and then derivations won't be on your test. His problem sets are tough, but there are only three.  He is very approachable and a very lenient grader, although his exams will make you (want to) cry.

He went at just the right speed during class. He is very friendly and always welcomes students who need extra help and have questions. He always showed how he got equations, rather than simply writing them on the board, which was useful. An overall good guy!

Excellent lecturer... Worked through in-class examples very thoroughly, and made sure everyone understood... Always available for homework/pre-exam help...  Be aware the tests can be tricky, and he WILL call on random people during class.  Otherwise, made thermodynamics almost enjoyable!
Calm, cool, and collected Prof Attell is a hallmark figure in the English dept. Makes class enjoyable and relaxed.
I love him (I didn't read at all and never went to class, but I read SparkNotes before every test and that was enough!).

KEVIN ATTELL MY GOAT. Take ENGL 1102. This class is so much fun. It's basically just reading books written by Cornellians and talking about them with the professor. KA has so much background knowledge on the books and authors and his interpretations of the books are always so enjoyable to learn about. Exams are light. Paper is light. 11/10.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A passionate guy. Relaxed structure. Just do the reading (in 1102's case, read some fiction every night) and you'll be fine.

The lectures were minimally helpful, and Attell is at best a merely average reader of poetry. The main problem was his lack of enthusiasm. I was very excited about the course, but Attell did not make the experience worthwhile. The readings are hard (DON'T BUY the packet; ALL of it is free through the library or online) but the grading was very easy

Kevin was a great professor in Short Stories. He openly facilitated an environment where you could really explore your ideas and share them in discussion. I really enjoyed this class and the ability I had to expand my writing skills in a way that I had not had a chance to before. Would totally recommend. Also light homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Attell is one of my favorite professors at Cornell, and I enjoyed his class very much. It is challenging, but I have learned so much and gain so much confidence from his class. He is definitely an accessible person and willing to help. Its a class where you should be a perfectionist though.
Decent class. Relaxing. 3 papers, insightful, nice.
not clear at all, we can't understand what he is teaching. obviously, he doesn't prepare for it carefully.

Asis is one of the sweetest professors at the hotel school and you can tell by how personal he makes lectures. He puts in the effort to know EVERY student and don't be surprised if he knows your name first day of class without introduction. The class is hard but put in the effort to do the problems before class and you will find it a lot easier.

You have to come to lecture prepared with the problems and cannot arrive late. He is strict, but he has his reasons and is very reasonable if you communicate with him. The tests are hard, but he curves them and if you redo the problems / go to OH you'll be fine. The median grade is an A- and the tests are super curved.

Asis is one of the best professors in the hotel school and he is incredibly fair. If you follow his instructions (i.e. participate in class and try the problems beforehand) you will easily do well. These bad reviews clearly come from people who wanted to get an A without putting in any effort. Also, he's super easy to reach if you have questions.
Asis is a great professor. You will learn a lot.

Exam questions are too flexible and he didn't give us enough materials to prepare for the exam (only limited 2-4 in-class exercises can be used to review before exams). Class participation is too strict and meaningless. Accounting class should focus more on helping students understand concepts, instead of penalizing them for not being active.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: he would be a great prof if there were 48 hours in a day

He does not teach the material in a way that is productive. No one knows what is going on. The same man that has typos in nearly every assignment is in charge of grading our assessments - this is a problem when he marks a correct answer as incorrect, refusing to release an answer key after the assessment.

This class is probably one of the more difficult class that I've taken at Cornell but I definitely learned the most. Asis is the sweetest man ever. He is so accessible outside of class! You will have to grind (do hw problems over and over again for like 5 times) but if you put in the work, you'll do well. He also curves a lot.

The bad reviews come from ppl who didnt listen. We were to read and do homework before class so we could discuss in lecture. I did so and learned a ton. I participated more than anyone. It irked me that so many of my peers wanted an A handed to them when they failed to do what he asked. Do what the prof wants; they shouldnt bow to entitled hotelies

I really enjoyed taking Asis's class even though I did freak out in the beginning. His teaching style is different from many other professors as he really wants to help students to build up a critical thinking mindset. He has a lot of cool experiences and is willing to help students both academically and professionally.

I really enjoyed having Asis for Managerial Accounting. He is tough, but his class set me up for success in the rest of my classes in the Hotel School. He took the time to get to know everyone . I really appreciated how much he cared for his students, and he was always available for extra help (which really helped me succeed in this hard class).
you can tell he really cares about his students and gives tons of opportunities for OH. he wants his students to succeed past academics.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: the hw probs r different from the ones on the test bc the ones on the test require u to apply multiple topics, and many students are used to only being able to do the same types of q. however, he wants u to think like a manager, and u don't always get the same types of q irl. asis is very caring and u can tell he spends sm time on this course:)
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: I have only taken Asis for higher level classes so that's all I can speak towards, he reasonably expects preparation for class and it creates a great environment where we can go in depth. Mastering Strategy Execution is a small class and discussion based and Asis leading these discussions have been my favorite class taken at the Hotel School

Asis is a nice man, not a great professor. He puts a lot of effort into class and wants his students to understand it (e.g. asking students who are participating further questions to make them think) but this just ends up making student more confused. My best advice is read the textbook, teach it to yourself, and stop listening in class

I love Asis so much as a professor; he always took the time to hold extra office hours if you need it, and you can tell that he truly cares about his students and their future. Have an open mind!! Hes really a gem.

Was the absolute worst ... made me hate accounting so, so much. Get ready for 2 hours of homework before every class. He's also super disorganized, so you're also going to be confused throughout every class. Everybody I know complained about him. Prelim averages were 60-70 ish (he did curve, though). Would try to avoid this prof if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Great Professor. Taking care of students. It was hard at the beginning; however, when understanding his teaching style and the basic logic of the problem sets, the tests are not as terrible as I imagined. Really nice professor and will learn a lot.

Dont take his class,teaching style is such that he really doenst explain much in class. expect us to understand the concepts beforehand and he would just solve a problem based on the concept in class,says that the questions he would put in the paper would have never been seen by us before. Teach yourself the content. Only good is Curve, too many hw
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The class concepts aren't too difficult, so as long as you practice the in class assignments and make sure you understand things conceptually, you will be fine for the exams. The workload can be pretty heavy, but he's a nice person and is accessible outside of class to answer questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Verbally harasses students and pushed all exams together so we would receive your last exam grade right before the next exam. Impossible to learn and prepare yourself. He refuses to teach, and instead walks through problems while answering them completely different from the questions asks. Broad questions mean missed points and he hates critiques.

Asis does not care to help struggling students and has taken away ALL outside resources. You know he's not a good teacher when the tutors AND the TAs can't even understand what this man is teaching. He does not teach you any fundamental principles so you are completely screwed for the exams so you are left to teach everything by yourself.

His teaching style just isn't suited for this course. He adopts a Socratic style which works for Master's programs and concept-heavy classes, NOT a math-heavy class like man. acc. He fails to teach the material that ACTUALLY matters; leaving students to fend for themselves. Love him as a person, but it's very easy to dislike him as a professor.

Asiss class is a struggle. Hes a very kind and fun-loving person but he is not an effective professor. Most of the material covered in exams are never gone over in class or homework. The exams always have low averages but he curves them so everyone can do decently. The lectures are hard to follow and youll have to teach yourself the material.

Gives insane amounts of hw and has no empathy for struggling students. Assigns an average of 5 assignments/week, and praises himself for giving you a "break" every few weeks and assigning 4 assignments, all WAY longer than normal. Doesn't follow the syllabus at all and won't teach any content in class. Yells at students after cold-calling them.
Don't take the class with him. Run away.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: When I took his class, he failed to foster cohesion in our group. We eventually dropped the course because we couldn't build a rational connection with him. Although meetings were accessible, his feedback and understanding of our situation were consistently discouraging — not something I expect from a senior professor.

The GOAT. Best professor you will have in BEE. Really cares about his students. BEE 3500 is hard just by the nature of the material, but if you show up to class and his OH, everything will work out for you.

He cares about his students' learning but struggles to teach them effectively. The theory behind the course material is very relatable to real life, but the testing includes material that you may not cover in class. Attendance is graded, but you'd likely be better off (for your knowledge and achieved grade) learning the material outside of class.

Datta is a great professor who truly cares about his students and wants them to succeed. The class itself was really difficult but it was well supported by office hours and the TAs. He really emphasized problem solving and understanding the problem itself before beginning the actual solution.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Datta is by far the best engineering professor I've had at Cornell . The courses structure, the spiral bound course notes, lifesaving problem solving charts and his ability to teach, really allow you to develop a true understanding of the topics. Unlike other eng courses he actually wants you to do well in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This is overall a good class, if you struggle on the homeworks, do as many problems as you possibly can before the prelim. Also -- MEMORIZE THE PROBLEM SOLVING MAPS -- thank me later
One of the best professors I ever met in Cornell! Very considerate, and always there for his students. Love him!
He's great! Best lecturer I've had so far.

Professor Datta is extremely invested in his students and it shows.  Even though his prelims can be tricky at times, if you do a bunch of problems from the back of the book and go to office hours for homework help, you'll be in good shape.

Professor is a little condescending and often goes over the time limit for class, which is rough when it's all the way up in Riley Robb, but the class is very well-organized and he is more than willing to help people who are struggling. I highly recommend attending the discussion section.
Great professor who knows his stuff. He really wants his students to understand the material, so I recommend meeting with him personally if you need help.
Very explicit about expectations and the conceptsskills he expects you to have down. Several resources to learn by, including text and lecture notes.
Great professor. really cares about the students and takes the time to meet with students. Great organization. Class was alot of work but i learned alot too
Probably the best professor I have ever had.
Amazing prof. Genuinely cares about students, and his lectures are extremely clear and helpful. Course is also very relevant to BEE. One of the best profs in the BEE department and at Cornell.
I had Professor Datta for both 3500 and 4530 and i have to say he is the best. He really cares about his students and wants them to really learn and love the subject as he does.

He's welling to help and he wants to teach well for sure, you can tell from the enthusiasm.  However, some of the homeworks and prelim  problems are poorly worded/made.  It's just so hard to figure out what the question is asking or what the diagram is showing. You have to talk to him and after awhile you get it but there's no time on the test...
Great academic professor. You will learn a lot,and if you don't understand him he will definitely help you out. Not the coolest guy, unfortunately.

Professor Datta is one of the best professors I've had--if not the best! He sincerely wants everyone to understand the material. He makes a lot of effort to help each student who asks for help. Lectures are clear and informative, and recitation is a great way to learn how to approach problems.

Datta is awesome. He really wants everyone to understand the material, and explains things well. I feel like I may actually remember the material for some time. Homeworks and tests were fair, and he is good about reviewing for exams.
Datta is really nice and pretty good at explaining things.  Plus, the textbook is just like the lecture notes so if you miss class its not bad.

Professor Datta really likes helping people. He really encourages us to go to office hours. Although, I do admit his lectures are rather boring, he is still a really nice guy and wants his students to do well.

Quite possibly the best professor I've ever had. He explains complicated ideas clearly and easily. I've never met a professor that put so much effort into his classes. He'll definitely help you any way he can, and he wants you to do good (opposed to most engineering classes).
very helpful, he actually loses sleep when he doubts his class' understanding of the material.  plus you get your own mailbox for the class.
Very nice and always looking to help students. Grades were high.

Terrible!  His course notes (that red book) were awful--typos, unlabeled diagrams, poorly worded sentences.  I couldn't believe he called it "the best book out there on biological mass tranfer".  His "demos" also sucked! Glade air-fres

Pretty easy grader for a good writer, BUT Make sure to ask her about her grading criteria at the beginning of the semester ESPECIALLY structure. Not very engaging as a lecturerer. Overall, she's not a bad professor and nice but I would only take her if you are interested in the subject matter.She gives 2 projects and 5 6-page papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: unclear grading

Lectures were often difficult to understand and follow. Regarding papers, she would often deduct points for errors and not explain how to correct them, even if you already tried to correct it. Grading criteria was not always easy to understand.

Taken online. The lectures are honestly difficult to understand if you are not somewhat versed in the topic area already. However, there isn't any work except for the papers which aren't easy but graded very leniently and the average grade in the class was an A. Lots of discussion in class but you don't have to speak if you don't want to.
Did not enjoy this course at all. The professor assigns wayyy more work than any other 3 credit courses I have taken. Was a pretty inconsiderate professor, I don't recommend taking her course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Super nice and caring prof, put in the work and show that you care and the prof will be super nice and helpful. Accessible outside of class & loves meeting with students to talk out ideas. A LOT of work and reading, the content is interesting but the workload is extreme for a 3cred course (many indicated this in eval's so workload may be decreased)
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took this class for a distribution requirement for Arts & Sciences. Would never recommend this professor to anyone. My participation grade was completely inaccurate and we were told final grades were "non-negotiable." Instructor made me feel extremely uncomfortable when discussing grades or anything regarding this class.

Each lecture was based on a short reading from the night before of relatively few pages and a few short readings in class + discussion. The class essentially boils down to a final paper and some reading assignments.
Loved the class, Professor Van Oyen loves her work and makes learning about ancient economies very interesting
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Compassionate, caring, understanding, interesting course material, and easy grading. Really could not ask for much more. Would absolutely recommend to any major.
I took CLASS 2712 and thoroughly enjoyed it. Prof Van-Oyen is very knowledgeable, and the way she organizes the lessons and lectures is engaging and is undoubtedly conducive to learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I took Roman Archaeology with prof Van Oyen fall 2021. It was my first archaeology class and was overall very interesting, very low stress, and she presented the material in a very organized manner. Honestly, this very chill and not hard at all, just make sure to write a good final paper and participate occasionally and you will do well.
Very engaging and interesting topics, not much work at all. Professor was really nice/knowledgeable and always gave insightful feedback. Learned a lot about the romans too

I had an awesome time in her Archeology of the Roman World class. The class was taught online, and it was clear that she had spent so much time organizing it to fit an online format. Awesome lectures and interesting content too

Astrid is amazing. This class is a seminar, lots of writing and reading, but overall a great class. It is not a show up and pass, but she does give good feedback on your essays. Complete the essays, be prepared for presentations, participate, you'll be good. Take this class, you may learn something about yourself too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Ashley is the best professor I’ve had at Cornell. She’s very relaxed and class is a nice atmosphere and the time passes quickly. She also encouraged me and made me feel confident in my writing for the first time whereas teachers in high school would only criticize.

Ashley is the best teacher Ive had at Cornell. Ill never look at reading the same way after taking her class. She starts from ground zero on how to analyze stories and then shows you how to use the various narrative elements as a springboard to write your own story. The only class this semester I actually enjoyed attending.

Its early on in the semester but every class has been awesome. Im excited for the rest of the course. She breaks down the readings in a way that will sort of blow your mind. Shes also super hot and funny so that doesnt hurt either.

I absolutely loved coming to this class. Ashley is so caring and so funny. She makes you look at reading in a whole new way. She also teaches you actual strategies to get better at writing. The course isnt demanding per se but she makes you want to work hard and give her your best. I wish I could take it again!

Ive learned so much from this class. Ive liked reading and writing at a young age but at high school, English classes have been taught in a way that discourages that. Hand is caring and passionate about writing. Her class is a breath of fresh air. You will learn to become a much better writer in this class.

Ashley is one of the most caring profs at Cornell. Her prompts are broad, so you're really able to run with the assignments and do what you want with them to make it your best work. You'll get out of this class as much as you put into it. Ashley made me view literature in an entirely new and exciting way, and I'll forever have this class to thank.

Hands down the best teacher I've had at Cornell. You're lucky if you get into her section -- the class is pretty easy, but it's memorable and makes you look at the world differently. Assignments are pretty open-ended. Lots of freedom to do what you want!

She is so unbelievably kind, you can tell she actually cares about you as a person. I do find myself spending a lot of time on the assignments. The instructions can be sort of complex but she's a forgiving grader as long as you put in effort. It does take a while to get your papers back, but she gives great comments and is really encouraging.
She's charismatic and kind and keeps class interesting. Favorite prof so far.
worst professor at cornell
Most horrible teacher I've ever had. If you like a course, reconsider taking it if he's teaching.  He maybe nice to you, but when push comes to shove, he's a terrible human being from the soul.
The professor is really unhelpful and the assignments are way off the topics that are discussed during the class. Really unorganized class material.
The professors has difficulty in communicating the theory and also the home work is much more unorganized
I found the classes were not structured properly. The professor does not teaches the basics and in case you have a query , he is not able to explain the queries in a proper mathematical manner
take this class only if you have taken other ai classes before. instructor assumes you know the basics. i had hard time catching up.

Does not have the best teaching skills. But wonderful for research discussion related to class project. He comes up really quickly with examples to explain the hardest concept. Strongly recommended if interested in robotics. Best roboticist the Cornell has to offer.
I was so interested in this course prior to attending Cornell.Sad that I would not be taking this course again. The classes were vague and the professor has problems in communicating.
Classes were confusing and material used was not very relevant. Bad experience. Not going to take again

I had taken many courses in the AI vector at Cornell. This class used many algorithms and discussed applications to robotics. I really liked the way homeworks were designed that helped understand the material and how to apply it.

I really loved machine learning, and this class's applications on robots connected my theoretical understanding to reality. The lectures on Kalman Filters and Reinforcement Learning were fun, although it helped to prepare a bit in advance before the lecture.
Very helpful in class projects. Had fun!

The rant I just wrote for my course eval was double the size allowed here. Suffice to say Saxena is horrible. I had him for CS 6758 last semester and should have known better. Say away. 0/10 stars. Would not take again.
Easily, the worst professor I have ever had. He never gave a single helpful lecture or comment. He also doesn't listen to students...it's like talking to a wall.

He seems to be a good researcher, but he just cannot teach. He cracks pathetic jokes. Has problems while communicating, rather than sticking to slides, he wastes times around the blackboard. I agree with earlier reviews, probably not the best one Cornell has to offer, sadly not even average.

Jesus tap dancing Christ! I can't agree more with the previous comment. This guy is the worst professor I have had so far by a long shot. Lectures are useless, he does not know how to explain the material. He uses another prof.s notes, no textbook. HW is a huge time drain. Not helpful at all.
Worst professor at Cornell. No exceptions. Cannot lecture, test, produce homeworks, grade or use proper mathematical language well. The course is a timesink and waste.

Should take Pubpol 2301 in the spring. Prof Avery is very nice, but the lectures consisted of slides with outdated statistics and videos. She is not very involved as the undergrad TAs do essentially everything. Long and difficult group project takes up most of the semester.

A very well-respected professor, but I wouldn't necessarily recommend this class. Lectures are required for exams, but Avery sometimes goes on tangents and mixes up statistics that are on the slides. Exams are weighted very heavily and often require knowledge of specific figures and statistics, but the curves are fair. Exams are hard but manageable

Professor Avery runs the course much like a high school teacher might. She and the TAs care deeply about student success and are very particular about content and matching public policy analysis formatting. It is a Brooks intro course, after all. Classes are fairly large but the TAs are approachable and kind. It's a hard class but I recommend.

+
Interesting content 
Class Dinners 
-
TAs are clicky 
Avery had many backhanded remarks 
No leniency granted for extreme personal circumstances
Spiteful 
*
Do readings, as many example cases are on the prelims 
Understand graphs from slides 
Record prelim review sessions,slides notpost
Do not take this class if you already have a heavy work load

Amazing professor. The class is very difficult, but it is rewarding. She is also a hard grader. 

BEWARE the TAs. The tall class of ‘27 one is arrogant, full of himself, and only there to impress her.

avery is honestly one of the worst profs i've had at cornell. I took the class in 2019. I hope she's changed. discusses and examines policies in class while leaving out factors such as poverty, race, etc. I recall one time she said the reason food stamps are only for food rather than cash is b/c impoverished people would use it for drugs over food.

Professor Avery is always willing to chat in office hours and is caring . However there's a clear disconnect within her class. This class felt like a predatory weed  out class and the TA team was insufferable, egoistical, and narcissistic. Her exams also felt predatory as very minuscule details were expected. I recommend the spring class.

Prof. Avery is a brilliant, kind professor and is objectively strong in the department. But this *introductory* course felt like more a weeder for incoming Brooks students (of which only 75 exist), and was ultimately characterized by the excessively hard exams and cliquey, self-important TAs. Take the spring class if you want your money's worth.

Prof Avery is a good lecturer and the class itself is actually so interesting! Tests are ALL memorization which makes it really easy to study. There are 2 really long and grueling assignments (1 individual and 1 group) and while they are SO much work, the average is always an A. If you just do the work, your grade will be fine.

Avery is a brilliant lecturer, but sometimes moves too quickly through slides and topics. I learned a ton in the course, but it's difficult. The prelims are strangely worded and the fictional state of “New Avery” is just self-aggrandizing enough to be a little funny. 2301 takes itself way too seriously- beware of power-tripping UNDERGRAD TAs.

This class was extremely difficult/time consuming, but it was also extremely rewarding. I felt like I truly grew as a student and learned a ton about public policy. Prof. Avery is really nice and it's clear that she cares about her students. TAs put in a lot of effort and they create a great environment in section. 2 prelims + 2 research papers.

Avery is literally a perfect professor. Her work is challenging but incredibly rewarding and she is incredibly nice outside of class (even if she can be a harsh grader). However, her TAs are a completely different story. Specifically, two of her Class of '27 TAs are arrogant and egotistical and love the power trip of being a TA.

Attendance policy was completely wack, no drops and will count against you unless you tell them way in advance (even if you become sick). The course was very difficult but worth it. Professor was sweet but also biased in her content. I enjoyed the content and the flow! Discussions were boring though

This is a difficult class, but you get a lot out of it. Tests are pretty hard and require alot of studying, but they do get significant curves. Professor is nice and is very knowledgable.  TAs are also really great and gave a lot of help on assignments and test prep. But if you don't pay attention and work hard, you're definitely going to struggle
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Caring professor and gives engaging lectures. Exams are tough but rewarding. She's a lenient grader but sets her grade brackets pretty high. Felt like I did A quality work but because she does't round a 93.6% remains an A-. Definitely deflating and makes me reconsider taking a class with her again because in any other class that would be an A.

The most caring Professor I've had at Cornell! Concepts covered in class are foundational for any PAM Major, and the projects are a decent amount of work but prepare you very well for future PAM classes. Lots of resources to help you succeed (she posts 2 years of past exams, sample papers/presentations and is super accessible outside of class).
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Avery is amazing! This class is one where you get out of it what you put into it. It's definitely time consuming, but extremely relevant and interesting. Grading isn't very harsh, but you need to do the work in order to pass. Definitely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor is really organized and is a good lecturer, learned a lot about different federal policies. People say the class is a lot of work, but you're given a lot of time to actually do the assignments. Grading was very fair - if you put in the work you will get an A.

This was not an easy class, but at the end, the median was an A or A-. It was a great way to start my freshman year, I feel like I learned a ton and also learned how to study in college. The TAs are really attentive and helpful (and chill since they're undergrads). Had to study a lot for the prelims, but they got curved up by 15%.

Nice person, but I hated this class. Took it last semester and it made me drop the PAM major. She expects you to memorize random facts + statistics from lecture slides that are just almost impossible to memorize. Even though I got high A's on the homeworks, papers, and group project, I ended with a B+ just because I got mid 80s on prelims.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not take this class unless you have to, and even if you have to I would recommend against it. This class led me to drop the PAM major entirely. The lectures were so dense and she would make you recite random definitions word for word on the prelims. This is the most intense class I've ever taken and the amount of work assigned is absurd.

I would not recommend this class even to my worst enemy. There are two major papers that require you to read so many academic papers - more than what you should be reading in your whole freshman year. The TAs are condescending, forcing you to go to a library even when you are going through personal matters. This class will make you question PAM.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You can basically learn everything in this class online as the content has barely changed since she has started teaching. The assignments and exams are unnecessarily difficult and overall the class is not engaging. You have to take it to be in PAM which makes things even more stressful.

Professor Avery is super knowledgeable in her field and really cares about her students. That said, this is a work heavy class, much more than a normal entry-level class. The TAs are great, but don't expect to do well if you don't show up to class and especially do the readings, as they definitely appear on the tests. Super informative professor.

Her class was a lot of work. The individual and group papers required way too much time and effort for an introductory level class. Had to study a decent amount for the exams but they are similar compared to previous years which made things easier. Required class for PAM majors. Avoid if your are not PAM major because it is too time consuming.

Professor Avery is approachable and knowledgable! The class is a lot of work, but manageable. Prelims are memorization and she does look for specific wording in the answers. Lectures are interesting and make you think. She tests readings heavily and they've been cut down, so take notes while you read! GPP groups are hit or miss. TAs are amazing!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: She loves what she does, is a strong lecturer, and obviously cares about her students. The course itself has a LOT of information (most of it in lecture) but as long as you go to class and pay attention/take notes, you'll be fine for the tests. Grading is also fair/easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: There is a difference between hard & unfair. Avery's class is hard- intense, but rewarding. Prelims and papers require devoted studying but concepts are crucial for future coursework. She provides multiple office hours and extra credit. She cares so much for her class and students- she memorizes every students' name. 2300 affirmed why I chose PAM.

Prof Avery is fantastic! She really cares about her students and is a good lecturer. Her course does involve a lot of studying and essay writing, but it is 4 credits and most people end up with an A or B. TAs are very involved, the class is interesting and focuses on current events, and is overall a great intro to the PAM major.
gpa is based on socializing skills. tons of hw.
All of the comments below are true.
The prelims for PAM 2300 or pure memorization and the class is simply a ton of work. Prelims combined with the policy papers take up an enormous amount of time.

Professor Avery goes too fast through the slides, doesn't leave time for questions, gives Herculean projects, the tests are memorization of material you'll never use again or could look up easily, and the TA's form a cult of personality around her. Avoid this class if you can.

This class was not fun. I am definitely switching majors next semester. I don't like the way this class is run, really encourages students to kiss up to her to try to be come a ta or research assistant. Feels more connection based than merit. Most of the content from lectures was useless. she made a point to take attendance after a break or project

She's nice, but her class is the worst I've ever taken. Material isn't difficult at all, but there's an obscene amount of memorization. Prelims are killerher questions are poorly worded & ambiguous and you get points off for not phrasing things exactly how she wants, and for not including things she didn't even ask for. 0/10 wouldn't recommend.

The GPP was the worst assignment I've ever done, especially since a member of my 3-person group did nothing. Prof. Avery should have mid-semester group evals to weed out free riders. Lectures were dry and hard to follow, prelims were absurdly difficult and she took off points for not mentioning things that were not asked as part of the question.

Hated this class. Interesting material, but her teaching was terrible. Obscene amount of work outside the actual class. Not accommodating & expects u to prioritize her class over others. Narrow-minded in that she can't see how less-privileged ppl might b affected by policies. 2 other PAM majors I know switched out of the entire major b/c of her.

The actual material for this class isn't particularly difficult, but the way that it is presented in lecture is confusing and hard to follow. The group project took up a ridiculous amount of my time (easily 80+ hours over the course of 2 months) and the prelims were hard- average raw score was a D for both of them, but they're scaled to a B.

Useless readings. Killer prelims, b/c there's so much material & b/c the way she words questions makes it hard to know what she wants. No final, but a group project. Thinks her class is the most important & schedules mandatory events over ur other classes. Hardest class I've taken in two years. Lectures are 60+ slides long & convoluted. Great TAs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: This class has so much potential but Prof Avery makes it the worst course at Cornell. Her slides are poorly executed--each powerpoint is between 60 and 70 slides, lacks structure, full of text, and she flies through them. Her class is scattered with no focus, and there is endless useless and over-tested dense reading (lack focus/meaningfulness)

She's a wonderful person, but she flies through hr lecture slides that no student can actually catch up with what she's trying to teach. This class is a LOT of work. I feel like I did learn a lot, but because of the fast pace of the class, I don't think I have retained much. If you want to learn about policy (and turn cynical), I recommend taking.

I always got the sense Prof. Avery was talking down to us  while it is a freshman-heavy course, it isn't the first exposure to college work for a lot of us. Her lectures contain a lot of material. The group paper was absolutely awful and allowed for a ton of free riding, which was ironic since she taught about the negatives of that in lectures.

Best class I've taken so far at Cornell. Material was interesting and Prof. Avery was engaging. Prelims/final were tough to study for (lots of memorization) but if you put in the work and studied a few days in advance they were fine. TAs are incredibly helpful. Do the extra credit. I think class average was around A-/B+ range.

Incredible educator concerned about the practical application of her teaching and well being of her students.  There's quite a bit of group work and assignments, but it's manageable if you pace yourself.

Her lectures are pretty fast-paced. Her powerpoints are quite dense, but she flies through them. Fortunately, she does upload all of her powerpoints online. Very helpful, but the material is quite difficult and heavy.

Not as great a class as everyone says. A huge tease: seemed interesting at beginning of semester but got more and more boring. Avery is a nice person and good communicator, but has way too much text on her powerpoints and isn?t all that engaging. You?ll do fine though. Papers aren?t too bad and tests are lecture-based with huge curves. No final!

Prof. Avery is an outstanding professor. She really shows interest in her students. Even made it a point to remember everyone's name. Be sure to keep up w/ the readings to the best of your ability and go over slides for exams. She is always willing to help if needed. A very interesting class and she has amazing TAs.

Study the powerpoints. They are the majority of what's graded. The readings are too intensive...you can get by if you only do some of them. Short policy paper is hardest assignment of the year. All group projects are automatic A's. Avery is a very nice teacher and is very clear! Love that accent! TA's are great too.

Very good prof. She gets to know each student's name, which is quite impressive. She also holds plenty of office hours and picks outstanding TAs who are knowledgeable in the field. I'm not a PAM major (or anything close to it), but I found the class very informative and a good portrayal of what an ivy league course. Do the readings and go to class!

i took this class after reading all the comments here but honestly i don't really think this class is as big of a deal as some on this site has said. it was good, but not the best class ever. the professor talks very fast and very broadly about many topics so you don't feel like you learned that much. TAs bascially show films in sections.
ok
Very good teacher.

you will definitely work hard in this class but all the material is interesting.  professor avery never misses a lecture and she takes attendace.  her ta's are very well trained and helpful.  the prelims are curved a lot.
Professor Avery was really interesting and her tests were long, but curved pretty high. It was a lot of work for a PAM class, but that's not saying too much. You need to do the reading though.

Professor Avery is the best professor I have had at Cornell, and this is the most incredible class/experience I have had here as well.  She learns the name every student in the class and cares about how everyone does. Lectures are interesting and the class is just completely satisfying.
Her lectures are pretty interesting (+ mandatory) Definitely harder than spring semester PAM230. . .but it was worth all the effort

This is the best class I have ever taken. I have never worked so hard in my life, and I would do it again in a second. I learned more from Professor Avery than I have learned in all of my other classes combined. You will have to work, but it is an incredible experience.

You will work very hard in this class, but as a professor she's very nice and friendly. The tests are ridiculous, but she does this in order to curve it. Work ahead of time on your papers. Love your TAs because they can help you out a lot.

this class is a full time job. it should be a 5 credit class. it's kind of really boring and the prelims are abs. horrendous. but she's a good teacher, v. friendly, helpful, nice. she knows everybody's names which is kind of creepy.  great teacher****ty class
Great Prof, very friendly and approachable but will work you hard.
She is an amazing professor, she'll work you harder than you've ever worked in your life but you will learn so much from her. She's always willing to help you.
No Comments
No Comments
shes so nice, works you to the bone, but it prepares you for the future, really learn alot and tests your limits.
No Comments

Avery is awesome. Everyone says shes the best teacher but you don't get it till taking her class. Although you may not appear to be doing well in the class at first, she fixes that for you by the end of the semester (easier quizes come later, gives an A on every group project = 25% of your grade)
No Comments

Avery makes you work, maybe harder than you've ever worked, and her anal retentive attention to detail might buckle the weak at heart.  She is a huge fan of group projects, is a sucker for presentations requiring business attire, and has clout within CU.

Very warm and friendly.  Excellent lecturer and actually takes an interest in her students...maybe too much interest.  Her method of picking TA's is a mystery.  Some are blatantly incompetent.  Must be something going on behind closed doors.

she is AMAZING! she ask alot from her students, but it is all well worth it. i learned so much, and people tend to do well in her classes (I also took PAM 230 w/ her). Her classes always have the same format, 2 prelims, indiv. paper and group project.
No Comments
interesting class, but too much work for a 3 credit class.
She is an excellent teacher, but expects a lot from the students. Although she can be tough at times I learned so much from her class, and a lot of it was stuff I will actually use in the future.
No Comments
pretty hot for a 50 year old...can sometimes be really fake or have multiple personality disorder...very intense but dedicated to teaching.  Be wary of the ****y side.

Well organized blackboard lectures, and course content is paced really well (I can easily keep up with writting my notes, and he takes time to review concepts from the prereq classes when needed). Not too much homework outside of class, and homework¬es are very representative of content on exams. Definitely knows his stuff. Great class
Prof. Avedisian is really nice. Do your part; you get good grade.

Lectures were organized.  Subject was interesting and relevant to my summer intern job.  Avedisian is passionate about heat transfer and clearly knows the material.  Good guy - reach out to him and you won't be disappointed.

One of the most boring professors in MAE. Tries to present the material from the book, ends up over-complicating everything, and failing miserably. Just read the book, at least it makes sense. He just likes the sound of his own voice. Preach.

Lectures were example based and not too difficult though presenting a more generic solution technique could have helped the clarity a bit. The textbook was only really useful for the summary formulas. Homeworks were fine, and the best part was that tests were open book/notes.

Avedisian is a really nice guy. He kind of has a grandfatherly air about him. But he expects a lot of heat transfer students- the material is definitely really hard, but he tries to make it make sense. The prelims were atrocious, though- study your butt off beforehand!
Prof. Avedisian is a fine professor and really nice guy. He is an excellent lecturer and shows a caring attitude to his students.

This was a great class mainly because of the professor.  Prof. Avedisian is a wonderful teacher. Clearly, he is smart and communicates difficult concepts easily.  Plus, he always showed a caring attitude.

Avedisian's a rambler, that's for sure. But he "keeps it real" as he's said on more than one occation. I don't know if I would have learned any less had I never attended class, but the book is very good and he puts all his lecture slides on the web. It's worth going just to hear him talk about "getting the rust done" on his Volvo.
Avedisian cares about his students and makes a strong effort to communicate.
One of the least helpful classes I have ever had.  I get the feeling that he's real smart, but just doesn't know how to apply it towards teaching.
Cares about his students, but the class was often very boring.

Professor Avgar cares more deeply for his students than virtually any professor I've had. He takes seriously the responsibility of teaching and is fully committed to teaching undergrads and grad students alike.
Ariel Avgar is an incredibly knowledgeable and engaging Professor. He is very helpful in office hours. Labor Relations can be dry at times but he made the class worth while. Overall great guy.
One of the best professors at Cornell

I love his lecture because he try to explain why you should learn concepts, properties, and theorems in the graduate students' point of view. Especially, he tried to make connection between probability and your research area, how to adopt what you learned from this course for your research. I got A, but I heard that he had tough grading policy.

Absolutely no learning in class, lectures are same to same content from text book. Exams r hard. Tough grading policy , professor does not make clear his grading policy he will talk in terms of mean and median , normalization if yo ask for grading criteria and will make you confuse. Better not to take this class ever. Professor is in USC now.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: You won't like probability at all after taking this class. You would not learn anything in lectures, lectures are dull and boring, lecture notes are from book only (same content). Exams are very hard . Professor shows no pity even though nothing of that sort is taught in class as he ask in exams. Recommend, to avoid this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Probability is a very hard course and he made it harder. Does not give grades in exams and sets them too hard. His grading scheme is also too hard to get past - he expects you to get 85+ to get a B, which is very challenging given the nature of the subject. Not friendly at all.  Do not study under him. It is a disaster.

If you critique others you are given a grade in this course. This course is all talks, no brains. It's easy for her to talk badly about others, be it colleagues or students, but difficult for her to face feedbacks. These reviews are student's "lived experiences" with this professor. So why flag these lived experiences now?
Flagging reviews? Maybe those who flagged don't have an identity and can take whatever is thrown at them. Some have an identity and self-respect. Not everyone's lost in life.

Grades were never a problem, but her personality was the biggest issue! She carries regret, but she needs to move on and not let it impact students cause of it. There are students who supported her with selfish intent, ultimately flagging her later. Had she been good to those who were good to her, things would have gotten better instead.

I'd be cautious about sharing personal information. In my classmate's experience, some interactions felt uncomfortable, including comments about Gen that didn't seem appropriate for a professional setting. I found it best to maintain boundaries and focus on coursework.

She never apologized despite the consq. When I met her in person she said "I did what was right and I have the authority to say whatever I feel in an academic setting," which sounded as though she is venting her frustration out on us cause of her personal issues. Comments flagged below show the indiscretion of students and herself. shame!
Tbh I don't feel comfortable engaging with her beyond coursework. Most of the times, comments and interactions felt judgmental and made the environment uncomfortable.

I wish this course had matched its intent. Most discussions felt misaligned and occasionally included comments about others that made the environment uncomfortable. It was in their hands to maintain clear boundaries but they chose not to, costing them the position and job.
She was removed from her position due to misconduct involving students, but presents it as a ‘new beginning.' Important to be aware of the full context before enrolling.

Disorganized teaching and unclear expectations made this course MEANINGLESS! She added ideas on how to make a country bankrupt and JOBLESS which does not really reflect the core purpose of the program!
Imagine what would happen if she joins politics? The whole country would go BANKRUPT AND JOBLESS!
Extremely poor teaching
Dis-gust-ing!!!

She is a mis-o-gynists who can't accept the fact that students can be extremely talented and competent at public health. She would consistently berate maj- ori-ties with un-related comments in an attempt to convince the class that they are somehow less qualified than others.

Hopeless! I feel unfortunate to have chosen this course where she literally relates everything in her life as well as every single thing around her with whi-tie-s for absolutely no reason!!!! This course is at the peak of its negativity and can get no better if she continues teaching it!
Just don't!!!!!
Weird readings, dis cri miN tory articles and a ha. tred filled mind.
The course description is different compares to what actually is taught in the course. A lot of discrepancy exists and this course needs to be STOPPED for God's Sakes!!
Is she mentally stable? Maybe she needs some help. This program needs to conduct a health check-up for their faculty.
If there was a tag for differentiation, I'd add that. She spreads negativity against certain people in her weird course.

What's the ATTITUDE about? Has a major support from the program but lacks respect. She assumes she is EXCLUSIVE and has been mean to students this year. She told me you will be graduating with lesser skills. So basically she is proving that she is NOT a great instructor.
She is the first hire at this program but the worst hire. Racist mentality. Too young to be a professor, she herself is a student and needs some training.
I felt uncomfortable during office hours due to rude comments. I also did not receive support with internship recommendations, which was disappointing.

One of the best teachers I have ever had in my life, both at and outside of college. If you are interested in screenwriting or even just reading and analyzing screenplays, take this course. Amazing lectures that he puts a lot of effort into preparing, and he brings in great guests from the film world. Accessible outside of class as well.
Great Professor! He always was bringing in cool people to help give us a sense of the field. Truly awesome class, would love to take another one like it in the future. 10/10

Prof. Austin Bunn is one of the best professors at Cornell, Screen & Story is one of the best classes at Cornell, BUT he sometimes isn't that nice of a guy. He pokes fun at students in class and makes the class laugh at them. He will also mock your opinion if he disagrees with it. He's incredible at his job, but when the joke is you, it's not fun.

Lacks professionalism needed from a screenwriting professor. Rude to students and out of touch with experiences outside of his own. Condescending and inexperienced in the subject that he teaches. Inconsistent when giving notes. Unqualified.

Intimidating but brilliant. workload is alright, BUT he holds the honor of being the first cornell prof who's ever denied me an extension (I'm a rising senior)... so don't expect a lot of flexibility.  still, I learned a LOT in Screenwriting and if you're lucky enough to get into the class, you're gonna get a lot out of it.

I took Intro to Dramatic Writing and can't wait to take Screenwriting with him next semester! Bunn is an amazing teacher, very accomplished, extremely talented, and incredibly funny! Our class became super close and I was actually extremely excited to start my hw when I returned to my dorm after class.

This class was great! The structure of this class made it easy to balance with other courses, reading, writing short discussions posts, and writing essays. The short stories were enjoyable. You will not regret this class.

She is an amazing professor who genuinely cares and respects each of her students! I enjoyed taking Creative Writing with her and our class discussions were always insightful and fun. She always encouraged us to share our own thoughts, ideas, and stories, and to know that our voice matters. I've learned so much more about writing, thanks to her!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: amazing teacher. made me feel really heard and included in class; i am personally not very strong in english, but she made me want to try and want to raise my hand in class. she makes sure that everyone is engaged in class (it is not difficult to be, at all!) and is super accessible & flexible in office hours (they were over zoom, by appointment).

Ms. Ayaz was an amazing professor. She was very kind and professional and understood that students have other commitments outside of class. The feedback that she provided for each essay was extremely thorough and she truly shows how much she cares for each student.

Ms. Ayaz was a joy to have. Classes were very orderly and meaningful. She cared about us and even extended due dates when necessarily to accommodate the class. You will pass as long as we follow her reasonable grading criteria. Helped me develop as a writer. Always gave impactful and constructive feedback. Kind and always made me feel included.

Aye was the most amazing and inspirational professor I ever had. Her material is very hard - I struggled immensely with her material, but at the end of it all, I felt rewarded with a wealth of knowledge that has forever impacted the way I understand chemistry and biology. I felt that I had learned, rather than studied, organic chemistry.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Prof Aye is definitely one of the most intelligent professors that I have ever had, but she has a hard time slowing down and breaking the material down into helpful and informational pieces. She either teaches a concept in a way that is too simple or too complicated and then she tests on multiple concepts combined.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Aye is really challenging, but her lectures weren't entirely bad. There's a bit of a language barrier and she tends to focus on drugs/biological applications. SHE WILL TEST YOU ON THEM. She only gives answers to in-class practice problems during lecture, so make sure you show up ready to write really fast. Tests are rough but interesting
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: When I searched in google for one of the concepts, I realized that it was an unproven mechanisms published on NCBI that she wanted us to know. I feel like if I master all the mechanisms she wants me to know I will be able to synthesize a new cancer curing drug or something by myself.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Aye is the worst avoid at all costs, try to take Dr. Ruttledge his class is not easy by any means. But, Dr. Aye is not engaging, her test involve unnecessary reading that further complicates orgo. Her test are horrible, at least in Ruttledge's class you are clear on instructions even though the problem may be really hard.

Professor Aye is definitely a bright individual who should be teaching Organic Chemistry, but teaches this Intro to Organic Chemistry class as though we have already taken her section of the class twice. The class overall is test heavy and those are what determine your grade. Professor Aye makes Dr. Ruttledge's tests look like middle school quiz
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is amazing! An exceptionally caring man and he brings that attitude with him to class every day. Papers and the exam are graded fairly. About 30 pages of reading each night which was not bad at all, and if you didn't actually read on time you were still in good shape. Definitely would recommend.

Professor Rana is an amazing lecturer - he has no notes but still presents information in such an engaging way. Also makes an effort to be accommodating and makes it a point to learn everyone's name and asks how you are doing. Assignments are not too bad especially if you go to office hours. One of my favorite government classes at Cornell!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I've taken a few political theory courses before and none were as engaging and thought-provoking as Professor Rana's. He is an incredibly smart guy and makes the material so interesting! Essay prompts really make you think but they're fun. Attendance is mandatory, but I would've showed up to class even if it wasn't.

Following his lecture is like watching thriller movie. You think you know something, but it turns out that you don't. He teaches us a theory (or model) and its strengths very clearly, and in another session, he will open up the theory's weaknesses, and ask us to be wise in using it. A highly recommended course.

Got an A in his class and I still wouldn't take any other course with him. He is not a good professor and his concern for students is highly questioned. I wouldn't be surprised if the two previous comments were written by him since they seem identical.
