wonderful and useful for real world application
Complete waste of time. Avoid at all costs.
Rude and obnoxious
Very kind and helpful, course was very useful for real world application
The most useful class I have ever taken in my entire time at Cornell
No Comments
Bitter, unhelpful prof, a shame to the CRP department.

Horrible lecturer. Inconsistent. His lecture is ok, but gudelines of the term paper are very unpredictable, which never showed up in the syllabus. Never plan ahead of writing a term paper, since he changes his plan very easily. Bad personality. Not helpful in office hour.
Extremely disorganized and repetitive. Support are really poor as well, no responds on Ed and Hw are poorly structured. Do not recommend
Prof. Selman to open to discussing novel, out-of-the-box ideas in and outside of class. He really motivates you to think and reason the way a researcher approaches the problem.

One midterm + final, in person. Very badly organised class, TA's not great either. Class website wasn't set up for weeks & the canvas isn't properly organised. Three hw's, two right before midterm & one before finals. Dry lectures- he's very into the material and uses textbook. I dropped because I failed. Grad element: extra essay with no context

I have never taken a class this organized. First hw answers wasn't posted until a day before midterm. The midterm was basically the same as last years so half the class got 100s. Only 2 hws total, 3rd made extra credit bc it was due during finals. No practice questions for the exams after promising some. Nothing really to study from at all. A joke!

Incredibly disorganized. Boring, repetitive lectures on interesting topics. Put me to sleep every time. Lectures are vague and about the history of whatever we're discussing, but have no substance. Then the tests and homework are technical, which is unfair. Would not recommend

Lectures are a bit dry, but he is a very nice guy, helpful and very approachable outside of class. He is definitely knowledgeable in AI and I believe it would be fun for someone who is really into the material.

Somehow makes an interesting topic seem boring. Lectures were very dry. Hws and midterm were fairly easy. Don't know if I'm just stupid, but final seemed to be ridiculously hard. Like way harder than anything we had seen before. Would not recommend.
Very hard to understand.
One of the worst professors I've had at this school. Unorganized, consistently late, and somehow he manages to make everyone fall asleep while lecturing on an interesting topic.

He's really into the subject, while the students not as much.  Didn't go to lectures, didn't need to.  Problem Sets from book, only need to read the book to understand.  Midterm (only one) and final were pretty fair.
He does a pretty good job of teaching the course actually. He makes a good effort at explaining and teaching a difficult subject.
I have been in this class for four classes, and havent learned one thing.
slow and boring. better read the book yourself.

He took over the couse for 1 semester. i think he ruined the class. the stuff i knew how to do i knew it from other classes. i think skipped about 13-15 lectures, and got A+. if you just want a free A, and not learn anything and be screwed later, go for it.
Fall 1999.  One of the easiest professors I have ever had teaching a class.  I slept through almost every lecture and still got an A.  'nuff said.
hard to understand, not very interested in teaching or students
Most teachers complain about students' cell phones ringing in class.  This guy's phone goes off every day during lecture.
472 was one of the most boring classes I've ever taken. (But it was an easy A)
Selman is self-absorbed, difficult and unclear. Only take 472 if you're really interested in AI.
genuinely one of the best profs i've had in my life. he clearly knows the material and knows it well. funny and engaging, makes learning the content interesting. would take again if i could

Presents course material in a very organized way so that it builds on itself. Exams were reasonable, labs were interesting, and provided a good introduction to digital logic. Recorded lectures helped with exam reviews. Used Ed discussion actively to answer questions. Prof. Batten was a great lecturer, and I would take another class with him again.

GOAT of the ECE department. Still developing the course and it changes a lot year to year, but best lectures in the ECE department and really fair exams. Labs are a decent amount of work but interesting enough.

Batten is the GOAT. He clearly cares about his students, helps out during lab sections, is a fair grader, answers ed discussion posts 24/7, and most importantly is an engaging + comprehensive lecturer.

Professor Batten was so good at explaining things. He talks fast and has a passion for what he's teaching. I enjoyed his lectures and the class in general. The class is quite heavy though, so would not recommend taking it with a heavy workload.
You need to take this class if you are at all interested in Chip Design. Prof. Batten is a great guy. Extremely well organized and fair with grading.

The best lecturer I've had at Cornell so far! Really clear, organized, and enthusiastic, very responsive and open to questions, and while assignments/tests can be difficult it's in a way that stretches and challenges you instead of bewildering you. Wayyyy better than CS2110.

Professor Batten is hands down the best professor I've had at my time at Cornell. You can see how passionate he is about what he teaches, and he gives so much support as long as you put in just as much effort. It's easy to score well in this class but you need to put a lot of time into it. Lots of emphasis on the reports.

Professor Batten was a great professor who taught material clearly and had good organized lectures; I probably got a better understanding of data structures/algos from ECE2400 than CS2110. Also cared about his students' mental health and pushed back assignments if needed.

One of the best professors I've had at Cornell! I'm from another engineering major, took this class for fun. Great lectures, super responsive, you can tell he really enjoys teaching Coursework is reasonable, there's clear criteria for getting a good grade, and you're not curved relative to other students.

Hands down one of the best professors at Cornell. Although some of the reports are rough, you can always seek help at his office hours or his great TAs. I extremely recommend that ECEs take ECE2400 instead of CS 2110.
One of the best professors in the Engineering department, if not Cornell. If you pay attention in class, you will do well for sure. Only hard part was the long lab reports we had to write.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Amazing lectures--So many papers

reviews.comment: His lecture is great and you do need to put effort to study

Great professor who really goes in depth to make sure you understand each topic he teaches. He's always accessible outside of class and gives helpful feedback on exams/homework assignments. Pretty tough grader and assignments are challenging, but you'll learn so much from this class.
best professor of all time

Batten is simply one of the best professors at Cornell. He is well prepared before every lecture and explains concepts very well. Video-notes are still very helpful. Homework is  long and difficult but you can learn a lot. Project can be challenging, but Batten will help you find your bug. He is as dedicated a professor as they come.

One of the best professors I have ever had (I am a Master's student whose undergraduate institution is not Cornell). He is funny, he knows his stuff really well. He is extremely willing to help students learn. He explains concepts remarkably well. Very enjoyable class. He is tough on grading though.

He is an awesome Professor. He helps us in learning every concept by giving a real-time analogy. All his assignments help us in strengthening our knowledge in all of the important concepts. He makes us approach every problem from a different perspective. We are confidently able to talk about design trade-offs after attending this course.

Hands down one of the best professors in the ECE dept. Class is challenging but the effort from the prof to help out, in class, in his office or on the online forums makes you an expert in his subject. Explanations and notes are clear and always encourages constructive discussions! Labs are hard and do require time, but you'll be proud of the work!

not the nicest, expects everyone to know things from courses that are not pre-reqs. Does the socratic style of teaching but the questions he will prompt you with are not helpful and condescending. gives no examples. Rarely grades on time.

Very knowledgeable, the course definitely provides a good preview for prospective matscis. Baker has this idea that the ideal test mean is a 50, so the tests are correspondingly difficult, but the class is curved so don't be scared. Labs and homework were pretty substantial, but they did help me learn the material better.

Fantastic teacher!! Very nice and reasonable to talk to, and motivated to teach students!! A bit of memorization, but also has conceptual stuff.. i agree with the other person, the grading is definitely pretty weird. Like my friends who are smarter than me did worse than me but I'm also really organized, so being organized is key!!

Interesting class, great professor, but designed like a highschool class. Your grade has little to do with how much you know the material and can figure out, but lots to do with how well your work is organized, and how you show it. You'll get little credit if a careless arithmetic error is made. Put stuff that wasn't asked for or you lose points!

He's a great person, always friendly, and not unreasonable when his grading or teaching is questioned. He is also very thorough (but sometimes not very clear) in lecture. However, he does have some irritating habits which hurt my ability to learn in the class like starting a new topic in lecture with 2 or 3 minutes left of class.

His teaching style is absolutely dreadful. He does not explain to help you visualize the concept, his most used phrase is "it turns out that, this is equal to..." To make it more confusing, there are course notes online, textbook, and his lectures, all cover different things. He is very friendly, but going to lecture is a pain. I dropped the class.

Professor Baker is the friendliest professor I've ever had. MSE 2610 is  the hardest class I've taken thus far, but it also has taught me a lot. I would definitely recommend taking a class with Baker, but if you're not a material science major or minor, it might be too time consuming.
pretty hard class, dun take it unless it's necessary.

Teaches quickly and covers a lot. Deluge of information, only half the equations are tested (the major ones). Occasional in-class demonstrations. Group labs (3) are harder than necessary and an exercise in lab write-ups and delegation (little learned from them). Homeworks and tests are hard (but at least can make a cheat sheet). Friendly in person.

good class. His exams are open book. Most of the problems are similar to the homeworks. He is approachable and friendly. Only problem is that he teaches a bit too slowly at the semester beginning and rushes through at the end with a lot of homeworks and quizzes.
Extraordinarily well-organized, very clear notes and lecture.  Hard work, but do-able.  Baker is approachable and very good at conveying information and comprehension.  Excellent professor!
No Comments

Worst professor I've ever had. Extremely unclear notes. Randomly introduces things without much explanation. A very very terrible teacher. Especially, his notes are extremely unclear and hard to understand. Nice guy, but very bad professor. Sorry guys, but try to avoid him if you can.
Terrible notes (bad handwriting and lots of errors). Good guy though. Only assigns 1 hw half the semester and all of a sudden assigns more hw and quizzes during the exam week. Poor lecturing style.
He showed a great interest in making sure you understood material.  Went out of his way to explain things on his own time past office hours.
Taught straight from notes without explaining much. Confused the hell out of me sometimes. Can tell that he knows his stuff though. Pretty boring too.
Despised us all for our ignorance but good natured about it. Okay class

Lectures interesting but office hours w/ him were useless- he once spent 1hr teaching a group of us the WRONG way to solve a problem. Homeworks constantly being revised b/c of mistakes- tests are extremely hard! Labs/assignments disorganized
He makes you work hard, but you learn *alot*!  Easy to talk to and all around nice guy.
i loved the class, though it was hard...
One of the best classes I've taken :) Not easy, but worth it.
great lectures
Excellent Prof! Great course
Very painful class
the least organized prof ever. you will get absolutely no feedback all semester and deadlines will constantly be moved around!!
Yeah - just read the other reviews. What an unfortunate joke of a class.
Very disorganized and unprofessional
THE WORST PROFESSOR AT CORNELL UNIVERSITY ! ! !
most unorganized and difficult class in ORIE, prof needs to make exams easier and actually grade them instead of waiting till after classes...
NEVER TAKE HIS CLASS!

It is currently November 24th... here is the fact pattern:

We have had 6 HWs due throughout the semester. 5 have been graded
1 Exam on 10/16, have not gotten it back
A final he said was 12/2, then said 12/4 and is now unscheduled for next week, with no practice 
A final project with no details, no due date
A final HW with no details, no due date

The class is pretty disorganized 😅. We have one more week of classes: still need Prelim 1 back from October😅, the final date is a mystery😅, project is due same day as final.. don't 
Know what project entails😅.Lecture content jumps around😅, some (quite a few) questions on Ed go unanswered😅. Honestly, I am scared😅

He's REALLY disorganized. We have not gotten our prelim 1 back from October. We don't know the date of the final (there's only a week left of class), our project is supposedly due the day of the final (we know nothing about the project), there has not been a single lecture where he goes in order. He avoids questions on ed he cannot answer. vibes 😃

Horrible prof. Worst I have had during my time at cornell. doesn't teach properly, doesn't post proper materials for the class, is absent or irresponsive half the time. Prelims are insanely tough and he misleads students by saying they are easy.
Amazing prelim! Hope everyone can try!

Released final project details two weeks before the final exam and decided to have a it due on the day of exam (with a presentation). Also absent and very irresponsive throughout the semester like bro u good

reviews.comment: very bad professor, and not responsive AT ALL. He never cares about his students, like posting midterm grades in December and not coming to classes several times. AVOID HIM AT ALL COSTS

Bad professor. Lectures are unorganized, and you must spend tons of time completing the HW. You probably have to read the textbook for the HW completion (or use ChatGPT if you want). Have to attend recitations and complete questions assigned. The final exam was harder than expected. Not recommended.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Very bad teaching skills. Unorganized lectures. Most of the time, he got confused by his own questions. Expect a lot of homework assignments. Nothing useful/substantial taught in second half of the semester. I would recommend taking ORIE 5581 if you still want to take this course unless you want to earn extra 2 credits without any efforts.
Interesting course that turned out to be more helpful than I imagined
This whole course is an unorganized messy crap. The most unresponsive prof ever in my life ....... don't think anyone can beat him on this.
Please if you are reading this do not make the mistake of your life and take a class with this professor. That's all I'm gonna say.

Benjamin is a nice person. The PPT of the course is detailed, but has HEAVY homework that must take the time to fix all details well【many little points for deduction】All his big exams, 2 midterms & final exam were F**king DIFFICULT. He will give a curve, before curve, scores may be less than 1/2, or even 1/3. RUN AWAY PLZ.
If you are considering taking any of this guys classes, RUN the other way. Seriously, worst professor i've had at Cornell.
I am convinced that the non-1 reviews were him just reviewing himself.

This course was incredibly terse and difficult to get through. Every part (especially exams) were made unnecisarily difficult and soltoff is not easy to work with. Take 2950 in the fall, avoid this prof at all costs.
NEEDS TO BE FIRED!!!
A a senior, worst professor I have ever had at Cornell easily. Negative contributor to the Cornell community.
The man needs to be fired. Provides little to no help. Rubrics are intentionally vague. Even if you ask for clarification he just says “I'll be grading on whether I think it was a difficult project”

reviews.comment: Avoid avoid avoid

Typical Professor Soltoff behavior. Terrible rubrics that emphasize things not present in the assignment description. Gets upset with students when they fail to understand a topic quick enough, failing to realize that this is the result of his own incompetence as a teacher. I don't know why Cornell continues to allow him to teach.

reviews.comment:
Took 3312 and now 4940 (applied ML) 

Ben is extremely gifted in his craft, he is a masterful statistician and understands coding like no other. 

That said, his soft skills are so garbage. He is terrible with feedback and talks to everyone like they are an idiot. 

Application Exercises get messy and he doesn't care about overworking you.

This dude is actually a terrible person. He should not be a professor at Cornell. He should not even teach at a kindergarten level. Terrible grader. Does not give any feedback. TAs have no idea how to help students. He is extremely picky with what he wants but never tells the students how to achieve those criteria.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Did not learn as much as I wanted to in the course, first midterm was incredibly hard, lectures were often rushed and always confusing.

I believe this man should be fired. There are such a large number of students who don't enjoy his class or his personality. I waited until the last minute to take this class as a senior. I wasn't able to get my degree because of his ridiculous curriculum, unnecessary amount of overlapping work, and unfair grading for the group project.
he'll go out of his way to screw over your grade in the class, 10/10 do not recommend
Sometimes I would not wear a seatbelt driving around campus hoping I would crash so I wouldnt have to go to his classes anymore

This professor is genuinely not only the worst professor to exist but also one of the top ten worst humans ever. If you see his name under a class you are planning to take, save yourself the trouble and don't. You have have been warned.

Grading is extremely unfair & TA's are not helpful when you go to office hours. Rubric is completely made up at the end & they will dock huge amounts of points for things they never told you to do. The exams are also difficult & the medians are extremely low. Professor admits he's doing this for a paycheck & doesn't even like teaching the class.

I read the reviews, it was worse than they said. Professor was awful, bad teacher, demeaning to wrong answers, something due almost everyday, grades extremely hard. First time there were in person exams and the highest grade was a B, he then disabled grade calculation and blamed us. STAY AWAY, just take it in the fall with the other teacher.

The most impactful course I've taken at Cornell is INFO 2951, period. The content is so applicable & extensive. However, beware this was also my most workload intensive course—think three to four assignments a week for a total of 15 hours. This prof gets a lot of hate, but he is genuinely one of the best lecturers I've had, just a bit intimidating.

Talk too fast in lectures. Talk a lot, but vague most of the time without delivering a clear focus. Loads of homework (projects, in-class exercises, homework, etc.). Very bad workload/grading scheme design (i.e. too much homework and trivial exercises to the point that it loses focus of what should be more important.)
Previous ratings got deleted because of how explicit I was - that should tell u enough. Horrible professor. Do not take any courses with this menace.

The fact that this guy has a job—at Cornell or otherwise—is one of the great mysteries of the universe. He has no redeeming qualities—he is below par in every metric as a professor and as a human being. I believe the sole purpose he was hired was to demoralize enough students to debloat the InfoSci major.
Horrible professor
Never take this class by him. Would be unresponsive in help and completely unhelpful for exams. Do not recommend

In all my time at Cornell, I have never encountered a more unaccommodating, rude professor in my life. Joined the class a bit later (but still before the add deadline) and he told me "I wouldn't get credit" for any work I make up. Gave me a nasty, "I don't care" vibe. Not to mention his voice is UNBEARABLY patronizing too. Who hired this man??

let me be clear
1. INSANE WORKLOAD (hw + lab + project + ae + exam + extra credit... should be 8+ credit course)
2. AMBIGUOUS grading criteria (most TAs don't know what they mean either
3. 50% OF WORK COMPLETELY OUT OF CLASS MATERIAL 
4. DISORGANIZED PROFESSOR (speak too fast with no meaningful info)
5. 0 HELP FROM EXAM ("just review the material")

Mandatory lectures were lighting fast, yet mind-numbingly dull. Homework/project grading criteria was vague and subjective. He administered a final with no precedent of written work (hw/projects completed in R modules/Quatro documents). Tries to connect with students via pop culture references (genuinely cute), but is abrasive when approached.

Rude professor who refuses to help students. Provided 0 information for our final exam (which is structured completely different than anything we've done in class) and when students asked questions about it on the discussion board, his answers were days late and extremely vauge. Harsh grader with unnecessary workload.

Snarky individual who refuses to help his students. Snarkily answers most questions with "check the reference materials". Turns the class space into a toxic environment that is extremely hard to learn in.
Awful professor. Gives extreme amount of work and makes it a big deal when accommodations are asked for. class is also way too fast paced to truly learn the material, setting students up for failure.

I write this review at the very edge of my sanity. There is simply no rhyme or reason to how this man runs his class. Assigns an inane amount of work that takes a huge portion of time for no good reason. Grading is completely arbitrary and students are left to guess his expectations. Even the TAs are confused about how to do the assignments.

The worst class I took at Cornell, only took it because it was required. Professor wasn't terrible and at least tried to make it fun, but he was stuck teaching the worst subject, never gave the rubric for homework, didn't teach, and no one in class understood or learned anything. His voice is piercing and annoying.
dont take this course if you can. the lectures, homeworks, and exams are completely different, and you will get 0 help. he is a terrible instructor.

if someone were to ask me who the worst professor at Cornell is, I'd without skipping a beat say Benjamin Soltoff. His lectures are dull, homework penalties are arbitrary, and one of his finals took well over 16 hours to complete, on average. Avoid like the plague.

Took 3312, and everything about the graduate-level course (5001) is true. Lectures and labs do not align with what the HW's are asking us to do AT ALL. Do not take unless you took 2950 with him and have extensive R knowledge, TAs don't know what they're doing besides reading off the answer key.

Could give a 0 if I can
Homework rubric was super unclear and he said he had no obligation to tell us the rubric (???)
Instructions of assignments was unclear, grading was based on his own expectations. 
OH was not helpful at all, and TAs knew literally nothing other than comparing your work with the answers
Could give a 0 if I can
Grading is extremely tough. Grading not only based on rubric but based on his own expectations. The workload is heavy throughout the entire semester.
Low score maker. No one can even receive A
Monotone lectures, can get boring.

The course is very structured, and I learned about R having no previous knowledge. The lectures were fine but a little bit dull at times, but the projects and assignments were interesting to do. The exams were very fair and easy to prepare for. Overall he is a good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: His homework setup is not making sense as it sometime requires codes outside the class, which is not making sense to me. Expect a heavy workload.

Well-organized and interesting lectures
It is fulfilling to take his course
The professor have changed his teaching style and now it is pretty good to have his classes

The only point is that the work-load is a little huge, except for that, he is a perfect professor

not the best lecturer but i think the class was quite organized and appreciated how there were no in-person tests. the final group project was fun depending on your group (we got to choose) and open ended-- we were given quite a bit of freedom. Overall very reasonable prof and I don't get the hate.

Avoid this professor at all costs -- despite asking for feedback, he never tried to change or cares to listen for constructive criticism. Disrespectful and uninterested during lectures, and agree with all the other posts about him being a tough grader and unreasonable workload.

This was my least favorite class at Cornell so far. Despite my love for data science, this class was so disorganized and down right bad. The prof. was unbearable to listen and lectures were a mess because RStudio kept crashing. We learned from watching the prof code, and the workload was too high: prelim, homework pset, lab, and project in 1 week!

This professor is a disaster. They have no idea how to effectively teach data science and seem to be completely disengaged from their students. The assignments are unreasonably difficult and the grading is arbitrary and unfair. If you have any other options, do not take this class.

actually terrible professor. info sci department just hired him but should get rid of him immediately. least accommodating professor at cornell and very inconsistent with workload. would have weeks where there are homework assignments, lab, project, and an exam all in the same week.
Carl Bernard ruined my life. With that said, circuits was an incredibly well-run course and Carl put his heart and soul into it.

Dr. Bernard is a good lecturer who cares about his students performance. His office hours were extremely helpful in understanding class material. He is also a genuinely nice individual who helped break down complicated topics into digestible pieces. I would highly recommend taking classes with him.
Explains concepts very fluidly while weaving humor into his lectures. An excellent professor and person.
He gave very helpful lectures. He teaches straight from the book but I always understood much better when I showed up. His exams are very difficult so be prepared. He is kind and understanding.

Ehhhh, didn't get an A+, so I guess that class was a little hard. One of the more easier classes here at Cornell ECE. Prelim avgs were like 50%, but I never studied and still averaged 80%. Carl is a good lecturer and funny at some moments, but he teaches a lot in a single week, especially towards the end, so be ready.
pretty good at lecturing but homework is very time consuming. labs are not bad. all tests are extremely hard and gets upset when the class collectively does bad because it was so hard.
Great teacher, funny and engaging. Class was not to difficult and had very minimal homework. Prelims and quizzes were easy as well. A great introductory class.
Very good teacher, tough love, available during office hours, but oh boy beware the TESTS
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great lecturer, but not a great professor. The homeworks are intense, but the exams are worse. He purposefully makes the median low. For my second prelim, the median was a 46%. A typical math course should have a median of B- or B, but he makes his a C+. Please, do not take this class with him. But if you do, prepare for the worst summer ever.

Overall, Carl's lectures are chill. However, the past exams he released before prelims are ALL extremely easier than the actual ones. He could literally throw out brand new concepts at the exams and assume the students could understand. This class is useful, but it is really exhausting.

Labs are based on faulty equipment which literally prevent you from completing them on time. Tests are horrible . Homework takes forever : course is genuine hell makes passionate ece students want to never see anything circuit related again - but hey Cornell at least you torture your engineers so they can be good in the workforce !!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He's mastered the art of teaching Circuits. It's a 4 credit class with a 6 credit workload, so be prepared. If you go in with that mentality, and are willing to put in the work, you can succeed. Attend every lecture and find a study strategy that works for you. Would highly recommend some form of studying with others.
Not worth taking this class over the summer. Homeworks are long and so are the exams. Purposely makes exams longer than need be to see how students would do.

Carl cares deeply about how students perform - there are sufficient resources outside of lecture for students to learn (i.e., Ed discussion, textbook, TA office hours). However, with that said, it is easy to be discouraged in the course. Exams are extremely difficult and immense amounts of effort in the course are only met with unfair grades.

Gives AMAZING lectures, but fails to provide much support beyond that. Super nice in person. Any online contact with Carl (email, Ed) is met with passive aggressiveness that he frames as constructive feedback but more often leaves students confused than not. Class felt like students vs professor rather than students and professor working together.

Very rigorous class with weekly homeworks and labs, so having a consistent schedule is key to be able to handle the work. Great professor though, gives clear lectures and office hours are very helpful. Helps transition students from introductory classes to the real ECE major.

Carl is one of those professors who pushes you to be a better student. Workload is intense, exams are tough, and grading isn't necessarily generous -  but if you keep a positive attitude and put the work in, you'll be absolutely fine. Great lectures, very organized, and always willing to answer any questions.

Carl is one of the best profs I've ever had. He teaches the class very well and makes it very easy to understand everything. All exams were extremely easy and fair. He is super enjoyable and makes class entertaining too. He's the goat.

Took MATH 1910 with Prof Bernard in freshmen fall. Overall, lectures are very organized because he mostly follows the textbook. He answers every lecture question and tries his best to help the students by breaking problems down into simple terms. Furthermore, his lectures are always lighthearted and have a positive vibe in general. Best 1910 prof!

Carl is a very caring person. He'll answer any question during/after lecture, he also responds super fast to emails and Ed Discussion posts. For several weeks in a row he pushed back the homework deadline to accommodate for students' exam schedules. ECE 2100 is a rough class but help is very available
Has a very high work ethic. Expects the same from his students.

Carl is a great professor that cares about his students. He is very responsive on ed discussion and makes active effort to listen to student feedback by constantly adjusting assignment deadlines. However, this course is innately lab intensive and homework heavy. Having a consistent schedule of doing the psets is crucial to surviving this course.

Prof. Bernard is one of the kindest profs I've had at Cornell. I'm not an engineer, but I took the class for a minor I was receiving and he was extremely supportive along the way. The class is tough and heavy with the content (esp over the summer), but he encouraged me not to drop the class even though I felt like I was struggling. 10/10 prof.
good professor, hard class but definitely the best lecturer for 1910

I took BC in high school but didn't do too well. I'm taking 1910 as a business major so I found it very hard. I was not registered for his class but still attend his lec and saw a huge increase in grades and understanding.  He's super accessible outside of class and hosts many OH before tests and would set up individual meeting with u if needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Took for ECE 2100, not math but no option.

Great dude. weird stomps

Prof Bernard (formerly Poitras) is the best professor for MATH 1910. I took BC and found 1910 fairly straightforward, but Bernard's lectures helped me deepen my understanding. His lectures are clear, his use of the chalkboard is exemplary, and his care for us is evident. His section always scored above the class average, and I highly recommend him!

He is like khan academy irl. Very organized with his lectures and explains stuff clearly. Very good at getting the material across. Also cares about his students (rare trait). One of the better profs to take 1910 with imo. Only con might be that he follows the textbook very closely (which is a positive thing in my opinion so idk)

Dozier is a decent professor. Teaches almost directly from the textbook, but nothing negative other than the fact that lectures can get dry and the lack of slides. However, he is very articulate and attempts to make the class fun. 1920 is naturally a very difficult class so make sure to be on top of things.
Didn't like lectures at all, it felt like there was no clear direction or structure but at the same time went too slow. Ended up just reading the textbook.

Professor Dozier is a very easy to understand lecturer with neat chalkboard notes. The lectures aren't the most exciting, but I recommend going anyway because by paying attention and taking notes, you'll save yourself a lot of time on the HW. 1920 is a hard class with hard exams, but if you do the HW, you will be pretty well prepared for the tests.

Despite his approach leaning more formal and conceptual, lectures are full of valuable information and problem-solving frameworks/workflows, and clear to follow as long as you concentrate in class. Prof does a great job giving you physical intuition for concepts and is open to questions. The course textbook is great as a supplementary resource.
Lectures were boring and followed the textbook almost exactly.
Very boring

Note: I took multi at an extension school and retook it.
Lectures uninteresting and exactly follows textbook examples instead of his own material. HW not bad, but office hours necessary and carried by goat TA. Prelims + tests have some tricky problems, but overall fair if you study well. Didn't provide practice for prelims, but did so for final.

Most impressive prof at cornell so far, his resume speaks for itself. Lectures are boring, he uses heavy language that people don't use  daily which makes lectures feel like walking through an encyclopedia, but class is chill.10/10 Prof
Prof Rissing is one of the best professors in ILR. This class is both interesting and fair, and a great option for the AWS in ILR.

Preferred Wiggs's section content wise for Soc of Work
Go to lecture and pay attention and you will do well, both profs do offer a bit of extra credit for the end. Focus on the slides.
Agree with the review of him posting a lecture even though he had surgery.

I liked the content taught Wigg's section more but Rissing is way cooler. Great teacher really cared, dude had a surgery and still recorded a review for us. TAKE NOTES IN YOUR SECTIONS some stuff is only in sections and not in slides/readings, will be on the final. Memorize bold terms. Readings are not important, lotta it is covered in lecture.

Intro soc with him is pretty easy. He's a good lecturer, but you don't really need to go to lecture because his exams are based on the bold terms on the slides. For the in-class writing assignments, make sure you know definitions very well (down to each word) because the grading criteria is rly specific.

Professor Rissing is a fantastic, engaging lecturer. His lectures move at just the right speed to properly take notes and understand the content without dragging. He very clearly cares about what he teaches and about his students. That said, the in-class writing assignments for this class were absolutely dreadful with incredibly low average scores.

Prof. Rissing is truly a gem of a professor. His lectures were all super engaging, and he marked all important vocab terms in bold. His grading criteria was super clear, and it was fairly easy to get 100s on both of the papers. He is super approachable and really cares about each of his students. He is a really great professor and all around guy.

The thing I like best about Rissing is that he makes sure you know all of the content that is going to be on the exams in the class and provides comprehensive review days dedicated to that material, which was instrumentally helpful. He's also a really good person who genuinely cares about his students and wants to see them succeed. Awesome teacher!

Rissing's a nice professor, and his 1st exam was fair. But, the class is TA-dependent, and some TA's will grade way harder than others: creating an unfair grade distribution. Final was cumulative, unlike Soc 1, and harder than prelim 1; it asked many questions based off random readings or minute details off the slides. Wish the final was a bit fair
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Rissing is a great professor. Lectures and grading criteria are very clear and easy to understand. No one assignment is graded too heavily (ex. The final was 25% of the overall grade). You should be able to do well in this class even with minimal effort.

I do not have any interest in HR and find OB generally boring but I have so much respect and admiration for prof Rissing. He is incredibly organized and you can really tell he cares about his students. He is very understanding and tries very hard to make sure everyone succeeds.
Great lecturer. Made content interesting, applicable, and engaging. Doesn't make the class harder than it needs to be. Nice and funny guy too. Respected within ILR student body.

Prof. Rissing is amazing. He teaches using a mix of textbook definitions and cases he presents in class. His papers are application of course concepts, and he is very accessible if you have questions. He is a fair grader and will help if you ask! His vibes are also very nice, which doesn't hurt.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Rissing has been my favorite professor at Cornell so far. His lectures are amazing. They are very engaging and the course material is very interesting. He is a fun professor and I never tire of listening to him. Spectacular guy. Also has an unbelievable resume for his age. Even if I tried, I couldn't say one bad thing about him. Legend.
good lecturer, fair grading, is a caring professor

Rissing is honestly the GOAT. Lectures were engaging, fun material, and workload was very manageable. He makes it very clear what is on his tests, and as long as you actually study, they aren't that bad. He gives some extra credit and curves as well. Only problem with course is TA's, as they can grade papers harshly

Professor Rissing was the best professor I had in my first semester. His ILROB1220 lectures are extremely interesting and he keeps you engaged the whole time. He knows the subject extremely well and stays after class to answer any questions that people still have. Rissing is a really interesting and kind person, I recommend his class to everyone.

The absolute homie. Favorite professor I've had at Cornell. So easy to engage with the class because of how interesting he makes the material; everything is framed through real world, applicable examples. Awesome guy outside of class too: understanding, accommodating, likes to meet students. Goated

Professor Rissing is an amazing professor. Defintly take his class for ILROB. His lectures are crazy good and is a great person overall. Not much reading or work. Interesting course matieral. Will miss his class

Professor Rissing is a generally fun guy. His lectures are engrossing. They feel like TED talks at time. Course content isn't the most interesting, but I never regretted coming to class. Papers are graded by TA's which makes grading criteria not always the clearest but that's not really his fault.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Rissing is awesome, he made this course an incredible experience. He was so understanding of everything especially in a virtual format. His lectures are enjoyable and informative and he is very clear about what you need to do on tests and grading criteria for papers. All in all, awesome content with an awesome prof

Rissing is one of the best teachers I've ever had. Being incredibly well-spoken and organized, everything he presented in lecture made sense and was easily comprehensible. Very interesting subject matter as well. I can't overstate how good of a professor he is - the effectiveness of his teaching was incredible.
He is so good, especially the flow of the course during the COVID. My only prof that I would say manages time well. Designs perfectly the discussions.

BEST PROFESSOR TAKE HIS OB CLASS. He was by far by favorite professor my first semester at Cornell. He incorporates videos into his lectures and they are very very very interesting. The workload is not so heavy there is 3 exams and 2 papers. RISSING IS THE MAN!!!!!!!!!!

He is very passionate and an amazing lecturer. He is also an incredibly considerate person. The TAs were horrible and he increased one of my essay grades by over a letter grade after I talked to him. Textbook can easily be found online for free and grade is split over several large assignments. Put in a good amount of work and you will get an A.

THE BEST PROFESSOR. If you have him, make an effort to get to know him outside or class. He is very encouraging and invested in your success. Such a great lecturer, so organized, and so good at teaching. This is my favorite and most useful class I've taken so far. I learned so much that I applied to my actual life. A gem of a professor.

Amazing teacher! Lectures go fast but the slides are posted online so dont worry. Very kind teacher and willing to meet wth students. Best class i have taken at Cornell. Interesting and interactive!! Would recommend

Extremely intelligent and well spoken professor, especially for someone so young.  Makes lectures interesting and none of the assignments in the class are too difficult.  Study the slides and book for the prelims and you'll get an A

One of the best lecturers I've had during my time at Cornell. Always put together, somehow basically memorizes the slides and effortlessly relays the information. Has had an incredibly accomplished and interesting life despite being only like 30 years old. Prelims are very aligned with book material, TAs are not bad as well. Highly recommend!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Funny guy gives funny lectures. You'll learn a lot of actually helpful/useful things. Lecture can be heavy, so make sure you attend lecture even not mandatory, cuz the 2 exams are close book so requires you to memorize some stuff. I didn't like his slides when reviewing cuz they're mainly pictures. Should be fine as long as you come to lecture.

The NS 3150 curriculum is relatively interesting, and the pathways he covers are too. I do think his teaching style is not for everyone - he has dry, dad humor and you either love it or find it boring. Overall nothing in the class is overly hard and the exams are fair. He also offers extra credit for talking in class so that's nice!

honestly the first few lectures (the non-"biochem" stuff) were really interesting. but uh the other "biochem" lectures (just few pathways) were really bad... I feel like he doesnt know what hes talking about. i feel bad for him though bc i can tell a lot of ppl dont really care about his class. seems like a cool guy. easy class tho for a 3000 level

Berry is the most hilarious lecturer, and it's really what makes this class so interesting. While the lectures are common sense, he teaches us the "science" of obesity and weight loss that challenges what we already know. This class is lecture heavy, so be sure to attend every class, and he drops hints to exam questions throughout lectures.

Berry made this class much more difficult than previous years. I heard such great things until now. He asks very nitpicky questions and they don't match what he says at the review or hw. Seems funny in class, but is unapproachable otherwise. I was so excited to take this class for fun, but now I would never recommend it. Wish I took it pass fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Clear grading, prelim questions directly from assignments and lecture slides.

Great class if you simply do the work. 2 exams, 1 final paper. Studied two days prior for both exams and just followed the straight forward rubric for the exams. Posts zooms of every lecture and gives extra credit opportunities. Dr. Berry is a funny guy if you have a sense of humor. Easy class if you pay attention.

Memorization heavy class. Says you just need to know the big picture on exams but you NEED to memorize lots of details to get a good grade. (not an easy A; you need to put in the work) Very interesting material. Tries to be funny but his sense of humor got annoying after a while..

Don't know why Dr. Berry's score is so low. Prof was so funny and laid back, making class worth showing up to (attendance wasn't required). It seems all he wanted was to encourage us all to engage and participate in class, if you do that you're all set to do well and have a great time! This class exposed me to so much new and interesting material

Professor Berry really tries his best. This was his second year teaching the course, and he made adjustments because of the difficulty students had last year. His lectures are organized and his slides are clear, and he tried to engage us as much as possible during lectures! His exam was fair, and he genuinely wanted us to do well! A sweetheart!

Dr. Berry is an awesome professor. His exams really don't require specific details and you get full credit for things that can be answered with one/two words. You only need the key words/phrases!! An A is attainable. All materials are lecture-based and he's always more than happy to help students. He's very approachable, kind, and pretty funny.

He really isn't that tough a grader seriously. In all honesty, yes there is some stuff that are detailed and lecture heavy content. It's all on the lectures and the exam is SUPER do-able to finish!!! He doesn't expect super detailed responses (that would be impossible) literally I put bullets on my exam and was able to get a fair grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He would walk around all over the lecture hall while recording a Panopto video which was impossible to listen to since the mic was only at the front. He elaborates on a lot of things and never concludes his statement. His lecture was all over the place and his exam was 60 short answers in 75 minutes that had to be detailed responses.

Professor does not speak clearly and gives the most ridiculous exams. He assigned a 60q short answer exam (in 75 minutes) and deducted points on answers that he claimed did not need to go too in depth in class. The material itself is easy to learn but you have a lot of memorizing to do, he covers a lot of extraneous detail. Did not enjoy his class
does not speak clearly, comes to lecture unprepared, tends to confuse students with his unnecessary research

WHAT are these other reviewers on about. PLEASE IGNORE THEM!!! She is so awesome, good lecturer, cares very much about her students, funny, and yeah, we have to have laptops and phones away, but it's not that big a deal. Lock in y'all, she's great, easy grading for the most part too.

grading wasn't very clear. the class consists of lectures with in-class mini quizzes and group projects and a final solo project. it seems like they are trying to implement a curve on this class now. my progress in the class was on track for an a and then the final grade was decided by some arbitrary process (lower than it should be)

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS (2475). She makes attendance mandatory and there are quizzes during each lecture. Grading criteria is super unclear, I didn't receive above an a- on a single group project and some even got c's. I got an A on the final and ended up with a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Belot is not a great instructor. Unclear grading criteria. Constantly forces us to put away laptops mid class. Attendance mandatory to do daily quizzes. Intro-level economic concepts, learned nothing new. Imposed a negative curve for the final grade (70% of my average was an A-, but got a B+ in the class). DO NOT TAKE! NOT WORTH IT!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the worst classes offered at Cornell. The grading criteria on her stuff makes no sense and they try really hard to force a distribution in the class. The TAs are not helpful and the professor isn't great I honestly learned nothing all class. It's one of those classes you take thinking it's gonna be easy and it ends up being a ton of work

This course is very easy from an economics perspective. The professor obviously cares about the material, but since lectures and assignments are not related, students do not pay attention. Would recommend as an econ elective, but course got bumped down to a 2000-level. Easy, chill professor and chill class where most students get As. Little work.

Without hyperbole, the worst class in the CS department. Dry lectures, devoid of content, full of meandering anecdotes that didn't go anywhere, content at least 15 years out of date, half the semester wasted on unrelated material, and a staggering number of just factually false statements made by the professor in lecture.

Lectures are dry, hard to follow, and riddled with random tangents unrelated to the course. It seemed like Ken really didn't care much about the class and didn't enjoy teaching it. It felt like he wasn't invested in our learning and was just waiting for the semester to be over from the first day of class. He was a very poor professor overall.

He is smart and achieved many things. But he is a terrible instructor. Each lecture goes into so much details which only obfuscate the main theme of the course, if there is any. Background knowledge on several domains are assumed. He is hard to approach.

Thank god he is leaving Cornell. When he made his post on LinkedIn annoncing his leave, he ranted at the fact that only 60 out of 375 students showed up to lecture. Is it more likely that 315 students are the problem, or the common denominator, 1 professor?

Birman's lectures often went on tangents about his technical acumen and how prideful he was of his work across companies/domains. Prelims were easy, and the grading curve was extremely forgiving. The knowledge you gain from the class depends on how much work you put into understanding concepts/C++, but you can get by with an A without much work.

Ken is a brilliant scholar and kind professor. He does like to ramble and lectures are sometimes unfocused, but his stories are always insightful. He is a very generous grader, and the workload is equal to or less than other CS classes. Highly recommend this course, but only after 3410 (it's a recommended prereq, but it should be required imo).

The course is really what you make of it. You can sink a lot of time into projects and understanding the material if you want to.
However, the course is graded such that only basic knowledge is needed for 100% credit, which is not ideal.
Birman is very smart, and he'll have a good answer to any question.

Birman is super knowledgeable about the field, but his lectures just really aren't that good. The class covers a lot of super interesting content, but I think it would be much better taught by a different instructor.

lectures were challenging to follow and exams did not accurately reflect material emphasized in lecture. Homework writeups were often missing key information on output formatting and were poorly written. condescending if you aren't a top student + very unforgiving late policies. crushed any motivation I had to pursue this field further

Prof. Birman would reply to ed posts even on weekends, so very accessible outside of class. 
However, his lectures are not very friendly for students without lots of knowledge in systems and whose learning style is to comprehend fundamental materials before jumping to high-level ideas.
Was not born to be a good teacher
Server error. Please refresh and try again.Server error. Please refresh and try again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Before attending this course, it would be better to have some background in distributed systems. This course seems like a breeze at first, but it's not. In particular, it's very useful in system design interviews. The workload is reasonable, and it's doable to get A+ since there are multiple extra credits.

Cornell CS degree from engr school early-90s. Birman is a highly regarded scholar/researcher. He was either an asst or assoc prof when I was there. PRO: his research is a good thing for Cornell CS rep. Ugly truth: he was a marginal undergrad instructor, annoyed at having to waste his time teaching, condescending tone, completely unapproachable.

The most interesting in this class is that for the same homework, two TAs can make the grade very different one TA just gave 60 points but another gave 90 points which is very unfair for some students like me :) because of very unclear grading criteria and unresponsible work attitude. Moreover, the lecture content is not well organized.

The professor pretends to be approachable but he is actually not. If you ask questions that are not appropriate in his mind, he will rudely interrupt you and ask you to go back to review the material. Once, I was actually teased for being "poor" in English because I didn't understand his explanations... Well done!
kuai tao!

The lecture content is good and I did learn a lot about the field. However the lectures and slides are not well organized and he is not a very nice professor towards students. 40% of the final grade are on 1 guest lecture in discussion which makes me feel what I learned in class is a joke :)

Was extremely unclear with assignment instructions then would insult students who asked clarification questions saying they aren't smart enough to work at J.P. Morgan. Assignments had no relation to lecture material. Mandated attendance halfway through the semester; people would just sign in and not listen to anything but made prof feel important

Started deducting students 1 percentage point from the final score every time they failed to show up to class. Lectures weren't related to assignment materials. Seems to think that students are lazy for not showing up to lectures.
Good class and professor. Has plenty experience and relevant stories to share. Lectures were fairly interesting. First time course so there were only a few assignments and quizzes, but useful.

He seems like a nice guy who really wants students to learn a lot from his class. However, he comes off as very arrogant when answering questions, and is extremely unclear with assignment requirements. He changed the requirements of an assignment after many people had started it, but he blamed students for being lazy. Lots of errors in slides also.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures felt very dense sometimes. But I walked away with a strong grasp on important concepts in cloud computing. The professor was also really nice and went out of his way to help students during covid which was really nice of him.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ken is a giant of the field. He was light-years ahead of his contemporaries in the 80s and 90s, and came up with the foundational systems that run Internet services today. He's responsible for not one but two paradigm shifts (Virtual Synchrony and Gossip) in distributed computing. I am still applying things I learnt in 614 in industry years later.

The worst professor I have ever met. Not friendly helping students,  but only expect students to find solution all by themselves even suggesting you to read tough paper or try yourself for over 10 hours instead of giving you a hint or answer in 10 seconds.   Poor professor.
Not someone I would want to be friends with.  Very arrogant, not helpful.  The class is doable but projects do not relate to lecture.

He is an ok professor but it is not easy to follow his logic in lectures since he spends a lot of time talking about himself and his own research. Exam questions were somewhat unclear and it is not always easy to understand what is required from the student. In his course, prelims are very heavily weighted while assignment almost have no weight.
I really liked him. He gave most of the lectures. Seemed to genuinely care about teaching. I wish there had been more variety to the projects though.

The class overall is very interesting and can be fun if you enjoy Java and learning object-oriented programming. I found Birman's lectures quite boring and dull and ended up learning most of the material on my own time by reading the lecture notes that were put online. You probably would not need to attend class.

This class was very poorly designed.  The Exams, Lectures, and Codding assignments were three disparate entities.  There was a ton of support from TA's and lots of Office hours.  Birman had this incredibly pretentious attitude in his lecturing that evinces his arrogance.
Awesome professor. Lectures were extremely interesting; he did a great job explaining the material. You can tell he loves teaching.
Very well constructed and interesting lectures. Prof. Birman was very helpful to anyone who needed it.
If you need help beyond the lectures see the TA not Birman

He's a pretty nice guy, but only if you establish yourself early as someone who is there to learn and not simply sit in lecture bored all day. He can be arrogant at times, but his lectures are clear, at least. The TAs help out a lot. The assignments have nothing to do with what you're learning in lecture, so start early.

On the surface, Prof. Birman seems to be an excellent and engaging professor.  His lectures are fairly clear, and assignments are challenging but fair.  However, as the semester progresses, a different side of him begins to show.  He is highly condescending and egotistical.  If you're an undergraduate, HE DOES NOT CARE ABOUT YOU.  That's it.

The lectures were vague and not related to the material that we were tested on. The example code given in class or on quizzes was wrong on multiple occasions. And Birman's arrogant attitude did not help matters. While Birman was at one point a key player in his area, he has not stayed current in a changing field

The worst professor ever solely based on his condescending nature and ego.  So what if he is a major player in any field.. most professors care about their students and is not only trying to fulfill a teaching requirement.
Very caring towards students and easily approachable.  Can be vague in classes but in person great, and an important player in his field.
Best class I ever took - a guided tour through the past, present and future of distributed systems.

Extremely helpful guy. Is really a big shot in his field. Has lots of exciting stories to tell and is extremely caring. However a pre-requisite to attend his lectures is a good interest in the course else the lectures do seem vague if you don't concentrate.
Knows his stuff
No Comments

Birman dislikes assignments and grading, but his lectures are engaging and lucid.  He enjoys tooting his own horn, but this is understandable since he's a very major player in the field of distributed systems.  His disengagement from teaching tends to mean confusing assignments, but high grades.  If you can cope with him, you'll benefit from him.
His mediocrity in teaching is overshadowed by his cockiness and complete lack of respect for his students.
Easy prof. Lectures are interesting too, though they tend to be unclear at times. Exams are straightforward, from the text or from written assignments.
Always had to be right and seemd to enjoy shooting students down.  Also seemed more intent on bragging about his own past projects and accomplishments than teaching the class.
Course was disgracefully easy.  Bizarre essay-question style homeworks.  Optional final = slack teacher
Easy prof, but gives very handwavy lectures.
She really cares about her students and is incredibly passionate about the subject. Great professor and great person! Highly recommend taking her class if you care about ILR.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: My favorite part of ICL she felt the most enthusiastic about her section. Also probably the easiest test but even ignoring that, she's still my fav. The way she broke down the section felt the most informative about her given area compared to other sections and lectures felt less monotonous

The topic fluctuates between being interesting and boring. Reading is required to some extent, but you don't need to spend hours on it. There's a solid amount of writing on it, and she's not the easiest grader, but she is fair, provides thorough feedback, and typically allows you to submit early to get feedback before turning it in. Compassionate.

Professor Bishara is an extremely nice person, very knowledgeable, caring, and understanding. This review is more about the class itself. It is very boring but extremely easy. You don't need to pay attention in class but she does take attendance. As long as you know how to read and write 2-3 page essays every once in a while, you'll do fine.

Professor Bishara can be a bit shy, but she really cares about her students and gives a variety of assignments to complete. She is a fair grader and has a genuine interest in her field. She also asks the class for feedback about assignments and projects so she can adjust due dates and make changes for future classes. I highly recommend her!

Prof Bishara is the nicest person and has such a genuine interest in her topic (middle eastern revolutions) you can't help but get excited as well. Can be shy but if you talk to her during an office hours she loves helping and will tell you her experiences and will give you abundant resources to further examine.

His class is relatively easy. Participation in class lectures is graded as well as in labs (mostly field trips to surroudning ag facilities). Super chill class the exams are not hard at all as long as you study. He might not be the best at responding on emails but he genuinely cares about his student's success.

Good professor but his tests are hella difficult and u'll probably fail if you do not have prerequisite knowledge on plant sciences. His tests are super specific don't listen to him when he says that it will cover the exam broadly...he will NOT. The only good thing is that tests do not make up the majority of the grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Miller is a super kind, knowledgeable, and funny professor. He is very clear in outlining the expectations for grading criteria in the course, and gives ample time for assignment submissions. Class is entertaining, informative, and interactive; a great course for anybody with interest in plants, regardless of your major. He's a great professor!

Dr. Miller is incredibly respectful and kind. Although the 1101 class is mandatory for many of the people taking it, I'd still highly recommend it, or any other taught by him. Dr. Miller works hard to accommodate the needs of his students. Overall, Dr. Miller is a very funny and relatable guy who made learning enjoyable.

Dr. Miller is incredibly kind, caring, and intelligent. All the material in his class (PLSCI1101) is presented clearly, and as long as you attend lectures, you will do great in this course. I would recommend anyone to take this class (as long as Dr. Miller is teaching it)--even if you have zero interest in plant. He is a wonderful professor!
Great guy, interesting lectures
Prof. Miller is a great professor and a genuinely caring person. Made lectures engaging and always open to questions and re-explaining concepts.
Just a genuinely nice guy, very knowledgable, answers all questions, very chill about deadlines and gives a lot of small graded work to spread the grade out. Midterm and final were very fair.
Professor Miller is a great instructor. He's very interactive with students and makes the lecture engaging and interesting. Very approachable and humorous.

Bill Miller is an amazing professor and person. With anecdotes and other funny comments, he makes lectures interesting and engaging. The labs are very enjoyable, as we get to see firsthand different plant science research taking place at Cornell. I would highly recommend this class to anyone, even if you don't have a background in plant science.

Great professor and loves to joke around. Someone you can have an actual conversation with about a variety of topics not just tulips. The first half of the class is spent learning materials and the second half is just guest lectures. There is a group project at the end of the semester that is equal to the amount of 2 prelims but the grading is easy

I thoroughly enjoyed my time in PLSCI1101. Bill is a fantastic professor who genuinely cares about his students. He is a down to earth guy and clearly passionate about his field of work. Bill is always willing to work with students to aid in their success in the class. I experienced zero stress in this class and learned so much about plant sciences

Bill Miller is an awesome professor. Lots of anecdotes and keeps the discussion flowing throughout class. He is very knowledgeable in his field and has a lot of info and experience to offer in all things greenhouse-related. The Wednesday labs are particularly fun as you go into the greenhouses and grow your own flowers!

This was Professor Miller's first year teaching this course and it greatly showed. He was very unorganized, as the initial syllabus was completely ignored and he ended up changing all the grading percentages right before finals. The TA's were not very accessible or helpful to us either. If possible, avoid this class and professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Don't forget to proof read!

Worst class every. Course not curved. Not given a single point to extra points problems, even if you did all of them and received full credits. No response in email and failed to answer students questions during classes. Told you quiz tested on a certain chapters, but actually tested on different chapters.
She is a kind, caring person who is accessible by email. She did not curve the class at all, so many people hate her for that. Many people did not like her teaching but I found it okay.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Terrible instructor. A black box grading process and you lose points for NO explanation!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Absolutely awful. 10 minute quizzes that are worth 5% of your grade each that are hyper specific to the textbook. No drops. Lectures are very slow. Sadistic grading on exams, youll lose 10% for a mistake on a question, does not matter how big or small, minimal partial credit. Horrible communication, gives no information about means/medians.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: do not take her class period.
Do not take her class, She give bad grade.

Very disorganized and incomprehensible grading. On multiple occasions, she's randomly deducted points from my exams and when I ask her about it, she can't remember why she took off points and refuses to fix my grade. One of the worst professors I've ever had.
A nice person, but not a great lecturer.

One of my favorite professors I've had at Cornell. Math and Politics is a great class, and she taught it well. Prelims were fair and had an easy final project instead of an exam. She will sometimes wait to get to the same number of votes every time for every iClicker question, which can get annoying. Knowledgeable about game theory altogether.

Like another commenter said, she is a nice person, but her lectures are quite poor. She'll often ask the class a question, then wait about 5 minutes in silence for someone to figure it out, and when no one does, she just gives the answer. This can happen about 1-3 times per lecture.

She's a nice person but just not good at teaching... Her lecture is not well organized and her notes are very unclear. She seems to be a happy, helpful person and she tries...  I found the lectures not helpful at all and just learned most of material from the textbook. The book is very good and cover all the material fairly clearly.

I think she is a very good lecturer. Her lectures are clear and organized and summarize all the important points in the textbook. Homeworks are not always straightforward, but they are in general a lot of fun! Enjoy this class very much!
Lectures are quite useless
The worst teacher I have had at Cornell. I couldn't understand when she spoke english words let alone calculus jargon. Don't take calc with her!!!
Try to have another professor.
No Comments

It is true that you do have to go to class every lecture, but that is because attendance is 40% of your grade! Thats awesome! The material is not hard, and is actually interesting.  It is easy to get an A+ if you just do the work.

It was supposed to be an easy class, but every class you miss, you get reamed. I even wrote 3 extra credit papers, forged a dentist appointment, but she is a Nazi for grading. I was smart enough to get an easy A, I got a C+ from missed classes. If you like coming to class and listening to her babble, you are golden. If you like to party... Pass

She is a nice person and helpful when approached, but her lecturing style is just terrible... it basically consists of writing some stuff on the blackboard, stating some claim that seems obvious to her at least, and waiting ages in silence for us to get it on our own. Glad she's not the DUS anymore.
Truly the worst professor I ever had at Cornell. Math is known for abysmal teaching, but she truly stands out as a leader in her field.  And nasty  to boot.  Avoid like the plague.
Had no idea about optimization before this class. But I learned a ton and it has been really useful for upper div ML and data science.

Overall nice professor, very accessible outside of class and helpful. Cares a lot about his students and offers opportunities to improve grade. Material is difficult. Organization could be better - the timeline for the class in terms of homeworks and grades were a little confusing but other than that, I thought he was a great professor.
Fantastic professor!

Bitar's classes are super engaging because he uses the chalkboard for all his lectures. No PowerPoint slides at all! It's a nice change, but you definitely need to be on top of your note-taking game. The class is tough, with a lot of proofs, but he's really patient and explains things in a way that actually makes sense. Just be ready to work hard!
He's gives great lectures and is helpful in office hours too. Just make sure you start homework early and don't wait till the last minute. Prelim and final were fair.
One of the more challenging classes that I've taken at Cornell, but lectures are crystal clear. Also Bitar is very approachable and helpful outside of class.
Is very slow - takes too long to post things like homework solutions

Took in Spring 2016 - his first year teaching ECE 3100. I thought he was awesome, can be really blunt/quick at times, but will help you understand it esp 1-on-1. Good lectures. I had no idea what probability was before class, but left with a solid foundational knowledge that has been really helpful in later classes (ML, robotics, etc.).

Lectures were entertaining and informative. Fostered a great class dynamic, despite the difficulty. Prelims were much harder than practice materials. Told us what was on the final and stayed true to it. Labs were not bad as long as you are efficient. TA grading was harsh

Professor Musser really cares about his students. Pre-lims were tough but manageable if you are willing to put in effort. He offered extra review sessions and gave us a clear sense on what the final was going to be like. He is not the best, but he definitely deserves a higher rating.

Honestly, he seemed like a decent guy, but… Exams were way harder than anything he covered (just irrational). He did not prepare us enough for the midterms (not enough resources & did not go in enough depth). Labs were inconsistently graded & expectations were not made clear at any point in the course. Only did OK cause I knew most of it beforehand
Nice guy, difficult class. Lectures were not as in-depth as the prelims. Labs were long and TAs graded inconsistently.

Musser is a good guy and tries hard. Prelims were fair. Lectures were usually engaging. He can sometimes overcomplicate things. Ignore his overall rating; he was review-bombed. 

The class was annoying at times. Labs are really long and are graded arbitrarily. TAs often made mistakes grading prelims. Curve is nice though.

I honestly thought he was a really entertaining lecturer and really wanted us to do well; however, those prelims were so difficult. He would release practice problems that were supposed to be comparable to the difficulty of the prelims, but after getting pretty much every question right on the practice, I would get in the lower 50s on the prelims.

Too many discussions breaks in a large lecture. In class assessments were too long for the time allowed and graded quite harshly. Decent lecturer although the content was a bit boring.

Kendra was one of my favorite professors at Cornell. Her lectures were detailed, it was easy to tell that she was inspired and truly dedicated to her work, and her classes were always enjoyable. She especially was very accessible outside of class during office hours and gave really detailed feedback on paper drafts, etc.

Professor Bischoff was great even in online lectures. The weekly quizzes required that you do the readings and pay attention in lecture but were not too difficult. The readings could be quite long but it really varied from week to week. Reflection papers were simple and graded very leniently as long as you answer the prompt.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Especially for an online class, lectures were very engaging! Professor Bischoff explains concepts well and incorporated fun aspects like group polls and videos into class.

Professor Bischoff is an amazing professor! She gives interesting and easy to follow lectures that are very engaging. Definitely an easy A if you put in the time for the readings, which I found to be mostly interesting anyways (there were only a few really long/dense ones). Made me consider double majoring in sociology. Take this class if you can!!

Way too much active learning. Get ready to be in awkward and silent zoom breakout rooms for nearly half the lectures. Only take this class if you enjoy active learning and self study as most of what she wants you to know are in the readings and not in her actual teaching.

She is nice but not a great professor. Nearly half of your grade 45% will be quizzes based on long readings. It was hard to remember the details of the readings for the quizzes especially because she does not go into depth with them in lecture. She IS going to test you on very specific information that she does not include in lectures. unfair imo

Loved this class! Prof. Bischoff explained the concepts in a straightforward manner, since the majority of the students are not going to become sociology majors. Tests were only short answers, and the TAs look for precise, word-for-word answers when grading, so a bit of general memorization is helpful. Discussion sections on Fridays were mandatory

This class is easy if you show up sometimes and take good notes outside of the slides. You don't have to do the readings to get an A because she goes over them. She is super sweet, knowledgable, and tries to get to know everyone. The memos are easy 100s: pick one sentence or point made in the reading and connect it to your everyday life.

She is a very knowledgeable professor who takes the pretty straightforward subject matter and delves deep. You can skip every class and still get an A on the prelims (she posts slides online), but if you go you will get a great understanding. She will make an effort to learn your name and the weekly homework is abundant but easy. Would take again!
The readings were excessive. At least 80 pages of reading a week.

One of the best professors! Very passionate and energetic, seems like she really cares about students doing well. You don't really have to show up to get an A but I would def recommend going to lecture because shes really engaging. As long as u put a little bit of effort in, you'll get an A

The kind of professor that will learn your name if you speak up often, even in a huge class. She is an engaging lecturer and she explains all of the reading in a very comprehensible way.
