Not everyone in a science major is premed.  This class is not teaching biology for the large picture.  Lectures (I did not miss one) were not helpful, nor where the accompanying slides.  Goodloe's supplemental class is where the real learning takes place.  Shame on Turgeon, and Sarvary was even less impressive with his arrogant attitude.
Horrible, boring lectures. Extremely unfair prelims. Anti student. BAD BAD. I didnt like him and probably 90% of the class felt the same way! Sarvary and GIlbert are way better.
terrible.  should move to a retirement home.  obnoxious and old and monotone and difficult.

He is a necessary evil. He does what intro bio is designed to do- weed out those who are not cut out for the premed track. While I do not agree with his testing of such nitpicky, unimportant details, and lying to the class about fairness of exams, it does help you to see that you CAN get through this class and keep up with the "big boys" for premed

Didn't care too much for him. His lectures were pretty much incomprehensible unless you were already familiar with the material and/or read the textbook before class. Tests were difficult and not a measure of your knowledge of bio, but more of your ability to know nit-picky details. Has a nice soothing voice that will put you right to sleep!

Lectures are boring incomprehensible and tedious.  I found the best way to stay awake was to mock him to myself during lecture.  some lectureslides bordered on creepy and sketchy.  Tests werent terrible but the detail of teh questions was insane.  saving grace was interesting guest lectuerers

Lectures are excellent; doesn't just put a list of points up and expands on the diagrams from the textbook. His tests are reasonable, but definitely require students to prepare thoroughly. Very accessible during office hours, especially for help with web quizzes and questions that go beyond what the textbook explicitly explains.

Very nit picky and doesn't look at the big picture. Unlike Cole Gilbert, he is out to get you. Uses 4-5 iClicker questions per lecture (in BioG 1101, app one per day was used!) and often, the answers do not make sense. He does not put up guide questions before lectures, and rants on and on about other things not related to biology.
Did a good job teaching, made the class interesting. Loved his last lecture of the year, he was really humorous. Exams were not that tough if you studied a little bit.
This guy is a bit easier than T.Owens. But he is still pretty tough. He isn't as talkative as Owens either. You need to do the most and study hard to get just a B+/A- in this course.

Everybody said they liked Turgeon more because he was nicer than Tommy O. The fact is, Turgeon might be nice but I think he really slacked at his teaching job. He was too lazy to post lecture slides, AND there were no makeup tests because he was too lazy to write an alternate test. Tom Owens might have been a dick but he worked hard at his job.
He may not teach the big picture much, but his lack of teaching the important material is stupid. Terrible professor and insensitive.

Professor Turgeon is a great teacher. If you study well you'll do fine on his exams. He's not quite as big-picture oriented as Professor Owens is. He really does teach you the subject if you're ready to do the work and learn.
What a 360 from Owens! I hated how he tested you on stupid little details. Definitely not the think-of-the-big-picture kind of teacher.
Really great class with easy prelims for people who actually study!!!

doesnt cover the 'big picture' as well as owens, but tests are much more realistic... as in not a novel about how bio affects the universe, though sometimes asks about stupid random details. has a funny kanuk accent. i think he secretly hates bio students too.
the tests this guy throws out make me really miss tommy o because at least he tested the big picture and not just little random facts
SO much better than Tommy O! Bio is fun again!
No Comments
After Tom Owens, this man is God!!! makes biology enjoyable again!!

I think that most of the unhappy reviews are because he taught intro stats (I can see him being difficult to learn from in intro stat). But for an advanced class he was good. Taught the theory in class and gave us examples of how to use R to actually apply the theory in the real world. Met with me 1 on 1 when I was behind and helped me catch up.

Very meh professor. He seemed like he had no desire to teach this class at all as his lectures were very boring with few examples of how to do the statistics for ourselves. Additionally he went awol right before the final and students were panicking because we didn't know what was going to be on the exam and the TAs couldn't help us either.

Kind person, & extremely intelligent. However: He went through slides way too fast, & I ended up teaching myself the whole class & R programming language. Provided very few practice problems you'd see on exam. Concepts were not really explained thoroughly. 8am+kinda boring lecturehalf an auditorium of kids passed out. Would not take again :/
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is very knowledgeable and nice, but he gives his lectures either too fast or too slow, and tbh, kind of boring. Exam mean and median are lower than previous years. Part of the reason is due to his ambiguous lecturing style... Overall I learned a lot from this class, but I won't take his class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Prof. Ramshaw is an awesome lecturer and systematically breaks down hard concepts into easy to understand bits. He is also really funny and keeps everyone engaged in class.
Professor Ramshaw is an amazing lecturer and did justice to my first experience with quantum mechanics. He organized the class really well and his lectures were on point.
Nice man

It was a really hard class for me, but Professor Ramshaw was very helpful and accommodating through the entire semester. I scored around the median for every assignment and exam and still somehow ended with an A? I would strongly recommend this Professor though, super chill guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: What a caring man. Caters and accommodates to all your needs and then some. Responds well to pranks, has watched Friends, just an overall God. You can ask the same question thrice and he'll patiently answer it in clear, detailed prose. I have nothing but the highest level of respect for this man.
Excellent professor all-around. Did I learn anything? Barely, but I don't mind since it was easy and a good class to take as a senior

Prof. Brann is kind, accommodating, and always puts the needs of his students first. He even removed a required essay we were supposed to do. I took this class based on genuine interest and because of no exams (just papers), and it was definitely worth it. Lectures are great, and Prof responds really quickly to emails as well, which I appreciated.

He liked to ramble and get off topic. There was a lot of work that was graded kinda harsh by the TAs, but HE was a nice grader. He really liked to connect with students and would take them out to lunch. Great class if ur a kiss ass. DON'T USE AI! I loved him. Genuinely wanted his students to do well. Be prepared to talk about current events.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Brann is by far one of my favorite professors here at Cornell. His genuine interest in his students and what they have to say is incredible in addition to his vast knowledge on subjects. NES 3523 was almost entirely essay based with participation being important too. Participation comes in varying forms. Readings are important--could skip
Good professor with interesting lectures. Made the class easy by cancelling a prelim
Ross Brann was a very approachable professor, and he did an amazing job teaching the Israeli Palestinian conflict class. Our grade was determined by mini-papers, mini quiz, and attendance.

Took history of israeli-palestinian conflict and it was one of the most interesting classes I have taken at Cornell. Professor Brann is incredibly understanding and clearly very knowledgeable and passionate about the subject. Grading was mostly based on essays but they were graded very fairly.

One of the most engaging professors at Cornell. He's super receptive to students' needs and is super encouraging overall. There are about 5-6 mini-essays and usually 2 quizzes. All grading criteria are transparent and attendance is checked so come every day! Although you'll probably want to anyway.
Great prof.

Professor Brann is a very memorable professor. Islamophobia, Judeophobia and Racism was an incredibly interesting course that I looked forward to attending. His lectures always had different formats which kept class interesting, and he always included snippets of current, relevant news which made the content more applicable!

The only thing that made me mad was how disrespectful other kids were towards Brann. Very passionate and knowledgeable about the field, and will (quite literally) get on his knees to beg students not to stress about essays
Excellent professor. Would not change a single thing. I came to lecture every day, not because we needed to for a good grade but because it was so interesting.

Opinionated, funny, and very unique style of teaching. No exams or big papers. Responds to emails within SECONDS. He is the friendliest professor you will meet, but some students take advantage of his kindness and do the bare minimum. I kind of wish he demanded more.

Professor Brann was a great lecturer who always made content relevant and interesting to learn. He was also very caring and receptive to all students, he pushed back a deadline when we were all stressful. Overall, a great class with not too much reading, grading is left to the TA's but they are always willing to meet. Overall, very solid professor.

Pretty good class, lectures were engaging for the most part, but sometimes class was a little bit hit or miss for me. That said, Brann always does his best to make the material interesting, explain larger themes of the class, and if all else fails, crack a joke. Makes the class easy but grade ultimately depends on TAs.

Professor Brann is an extremely intelligent, wise and kind person. The US and Middle East class is taught in an objective, broad fashion and Professor Brann's anecdotes are interesting. He makes an effort to get to know his students and really respects people seeking him (OH). Grade was negotiated at the end of semester!

The class is quite reading-heavy - at least 40 pages of reading for each class. There are bi-weekly mini essays which are do-able. There are no prelims/final which is pretty nice. If you struggle, Professor Brann is incredibly helpful, and I definitely recommend going to his office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Awesome professor and easiest class at Cornell. Don't have to do the reading, don't have to show up to lecture. Overall an easy A plus.
Professor Brann is a wonderful person with great knowledge to share with his students. Take a class with him before you leave Cornell.

People disagree on whether Brann is a Zionist or pro-Palestinian, which tells you a lot about how objective he is during class. There's a lot of reading, but I was able to not do most of it, only what was required for weekly mini-essays. Easy class. Also we read an amazing textbook with Israeli and Palestinian perspectives.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Absolutely phenomenal... Was more than willing to give out As and class content was VERY interesting.  Clearly cares about students, is very easy to talk to outside of class, and is very interested in material.  I LOVED Professor Brann.

Brann is basically a rock star- he shows up to class in black jeans, combat boots, and Ray-Bans. He's great at mediating discussion and presents a tersely debated topic with levity and objectivity. He's a clear and thorough lecturer and very approachable outside of class for essays and such. Great guy and genuinely cool.

Approachable, fair, interesting, and clearly knowledgable. Just FYI: most of my discussion section and Brann himself seems to lean pro-Palestinian. BUT Prof. Brann makes a VERY admirable effort to not reveal his views. Given how heated the Israeli-Palestinian conflict is, he takes a very even-handed, informative, and scholarly approach.

This dude is chill...one of the best mediators of discussion and participation I have seen even in a large lecture class. Class isn't too difficult, and is very interesting if you are into studying different religions.

For a topic that is relatively difficult to present as unbiased, Brann did a good job in this class, especially with such a heartfelt conflict. Though I knew quite a bit of the background and material before the class, overall it was still very informative and improved my insight on the conflict. Overall, a not overly stressful, interesting class.
Brann is the best! He's classes are easy, lectures are engaging, and he is extremely approachable. I can't recommend him enough.

Terrible class, avoiding taking it if possible... Poor depiction of religions, not evenly spread over timeline either... Grading is totally objective- depends entirely on TA... Brann is nice enough and will offer extensions if necessary, but just rambles in class making it difficult to follow or take notes.
Great. Cool topic, nice guy, flexible with deadlines. Tried to present everything objectively.
Great course, great professor.  Very few assignments but a lot of studying needed for difficult exams.

brann is completely overrated. his lectures have no organization to them, and it feels like he's always mindlessly rambling. i got an a in the class, but only because i looked everything up on wikipedia before the exam. his lectures were way too confusing. he is a nice guy.

This guy is a great professor. I highly reccomend anyone to take this class. Not only was the class based on an interesting subject, but his lectures were clear, concise and fair. Great profesor. Also, exams and papers are not that difficult.

Great class; great professor! Brann really knows his stuff, and communicates the issues of today’s pluralistic, multi-religion society. He was engaging and extremely interesting (with breaks of levity also). I would recommend this class and this professor. Exams were easy, and papers were interesting to write.
Great class!  Brann is what a professor should be!  Provocative and approachable with a desire to see his students learn.  That's it!

He's a great lecturer, is understanding, easygoing, really cares about students and deals well with controversial subject matter.  Regarding other comments here, I was surprised to find someone thought he interjected his opinion too much--maybe he's changed, but I thought he tried very hard to not let his opinion be known.

One of the few professors who can lecture without lots of fancy visual aids and powerpoint and still be totally interesting. Clear, balanced views on controversial topics, sensitive to his students and fair. Lectures are like fascinating stories, and readings assigned are all relevant, interesting, and of reasonable length. My favorite professor.

I like professor Brann. He doesn't assign too much work, but his class is interesting nonetheless. Presents things coherently even though he has a tendency to generalize. Yes he's a leftie, and does tend to inject his opinion into lecture moreso than other profs. He's still recommended to anyone with even a peripheral interest in the Middle East.
No Comments
an excellent lecturer but a little too opinionated/far left for me.
No Comments

He is one of the kindest professors at Cornell. Engages every student in discussion, is flexible with deadlines and makes class interesting and is a great grader. He gives clear feedback and works to improve students where they are at. Take his class, you won't regret it.

Professor Burlew is a very relaxed professor who is more than happy to work with students both in and out of class. His take on teaching and assignments has made the semester much more manageable than it otherwise would have been. Do not be afraid to ask for help!

Best FWS! Professor Burlew is one of the funniest, caring, nicest professors I've had at Cornell so far. He is very understanding of how busy his students are and tries to tailor his class to meet their needs. His feedback on essays is detailed, and he is a very nice/fair grader.
Super understanding professor and very approachable. He understands we are college students with heavy workloads and tries his best to make things easy for us. Essays were super fun to write.

He is one of the kindest professors at Cornell. Extremely thoughtful about material, very flexible with deadlines and classwork, and grades essays very well with clear feedback and is not harsh. He creates amazing discussions. TAKE HIS CLASS, you won't regret it.

Professor Burlew is one of the kindest professors at Cornell. He is thoughtful with the material, engages every student, and is very flexible with deadlines, attendance, and classwork. There are four essays, but he's a good grader, gives a lot of feedback, and meets you at your level. TAKE HIS CLASSES, you can't regret it!
Very caring professor and lenient with attendance/deadlines. As long as you communicate concerns, he will be understanding! Super fun class too with modern applications, so it's never boring!
This professor is awesome and I would definitely recommend taking his class.
Very chill
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The professor is very approachable and understanding regarding extensions and absences. As long as you attend class, participate, and complete the assigned work, earning a grade in the A range is very achievable.
i loved professor buckley's lectures and he is very kind and helpful. i really enjoyed microbiology bc of him, his lectures were engaging and interesting
Great professor, hard class. Very approachable out of class and wants to see students do well. Tests are memorization heavy

Such a caring professor. He really wants his students to succeed and actually learn. Cornell should have more science professors like him. But, I did SO bad in the class because the exams were just ridiculously hard. But, I think the homework grades will save your grade.
Really helpful and caring guy - he reached out to me individually when I wasn't doing well and it meant a lot.

Professor Buckley is an amazing teacher, I went to his office hours every week because I didn't understand a lot of the lectures. He really took the time to help me learn and understand. With this class though you can not just memorize. You really have to apply the concepts. I think I could have gotten an B or A if I really tried. Lec is boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Great lecturer that cares a lot about his students and will do anything to help you out!

Absolutely amazing! Best professor I've ever had. Takes all the bio concepts and info and relates it back to everyday life. Lectures are extremely interesting and go at the perfect pace. Definitely take this class!

One of the greatest professors! He made me a lot more interested in biology. He respects the students a lot and as well as every silly question a student might ask, whenever in class or office hours or emails. Additionally he always smiles at you!!! If he is going to teach another higher level class, I would definitely take whatever the subject is.
One of the best biology professors! Very inspiring.
In  my opinion he gives the best lectures in all of Cornell! Absolute gem! He teaches with a style that just gets to you and makes you want to learn more about microbiology.

Ms. Happiness is genuinely one of the greatest teachers that i have ever had. She is very understanding and cares very much about building a community with the students of her classes, makes class feel like a family.

Bi Happiness is one of the best professors out there! She is so nice and caring! I took this class as a language requirement, but it ended up being my favorite class of the semester. For learning a new language, Bi Happiness makes it super enjoyable and easy. Weekly assignments help you improve both speaking and writing. 10/10 would recommend
Most of the submitted class work is online and 4 days a week short lectures mainly focus on reviewing homework and in class discussions

Happiness is the best language professor/teacher I have ever had. She is unbelievably caring and genuinely interested in her students. Swahili is a fun language to learn and Happiness creates a low-stress environment to do so. I look forward to her class every day and no Friday classes are a perk :) I highly, highly recommend!!

I love Happiness so much. I've learned a lot of Swahili from her and would encourage anyone to take her class. If you want to skim by and get an A, it's totally doable. If you really wanted to learn Swahili that's doable too. What you put into this course is what you get out of it. I love starting my day with Happiness and my Swahili class

Bulugu is, simply put, a great professor. Swahili with her is always fun and is an easy course so long as you put in just a little time going over vocab/grammar each week. Because of the small class size, you'll definitely bond with your classmates. Only good things to say.

- struggles with classroom technology to the point of wasting class time

- struggles to present coherent lectures, most are a disjointed direct reading of the slides

- never prepared for class

- lacks any clear expectations for assignments, presented various several year old rubrics and struggled to provide any clarification

Other review was definitely not accurate. She picks favorites and then is rude to those who ask questions. Grading criteria is unclear, and she gives unclear answers about it. Very few assignments, which is nice, but not worth being held hostage for an hour because she won't let you leave if theres nothing left to do or you finished the assignment
Do not take this course. Do yourself a favor and take regular oral comm.

Good communications class, especially for E&S/plant science/agsci majors. Assignments included: mock newspaper article, video, elevator talk, and final presentation. Carlyn was a riot (affectionate), and I thought the assignments were reasonably graded. Only con was that she was disorganized at times & expectations weren't always straightforward.

This professor's employment makes the school look like a joke. The most disorganized and unfair professor I've ever encountered. Our entire grade was based on a singular research paper that was given to us 2 weeks before class ended, without any instructions and a misleading rubric. The presentation we worked on for 3 months had no weight. Fire her

While Professor Burton is lovely, ILRID 1700 was among the least organized of my Cornell career. There is a ton of weight on group work, making it almost impossible to succeed if you get a bad group (speaking from experience) and lectures are generally all over the place. She obviously cares a lot about the material but the class was a real pain.
Not a great instructor. The lectures were poorly organized and the group project was arbitrarily graded.

Overall, the class was very disorganized. There were many small assignments, that were difficult to keep track of, and many difficult group assignments. Grading criteria was completely random and generally unclear. Would not take this class again.
Absolutely the worst experience I've had with a professor at Cornell. Her feedback is condescending and she will belittle you if you don't agree with her pov. Avoid at all costs

I'm disappointed to see the other reviews here. Prof. Burton is honestly a gem and I loved listening to her lectures throughout the semester. She really cares about her students and works hard to find interesting, relatable material. Unfortunately, many students jump on her in class and try to take advantage of her kindness, derailing lectures.

As a management class, this has been one of the worst-managed and least-organized classes I have ever taken at Cornell. It's great that she's so passionate about the subject matter, but vague lectures, poorly-defined grading criteria and a lack of awareness of how much work she assigns are massive detriments to her teaching style. Bad website, too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The class wasn't so bad (besides being way too much group work for my liking) but Burton was the worst lecturer I've had at Cornell. Unprepared for class, talks in circles, doesn't make any sense, etc. I wanted to like her, since she's super enthusiastic, but she was just not good at teaching.

Professor Burton is very enthusiastic about students but she speaks VERY fast and to be honest, she's not a very good teacher. She's hardly clear and very difficult to follow. Her lecture slides are also absolutely horrible. Its literally a sentence and a bunch of pictures and is impossible to comprehend after lectures. I wouldn't take her again.

Regarding his film class at DU. He refused all criticism and brought up his Playboy career, calling Hugh Hefner a “good guy.” Then he'd show films mocking lesbians. He obsessed over AI tools, pushing students to subscribe to ChatGPT and Grammarly Premium instead of actually teaching writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Byrne is the GOAT. I loved his Sports COMM class and I think any student interested in sports would too! The topics are very interesting, and it was a pleasure to attend class.

At some points, Prof. Byrne shows you what he can do as a professor but at others has you questioning why he's there. He's laid back but seems to teach the course because he's interested in random topics. Not because he necessarily cares about student growth. Unfortunately, don't take it unless you plan on going into media or have to.

Prof. Byrne is one of the best comm profs. He is knowledgeable and genuinely a good person. He gives good feedback to improve on assignments, and is generally reasonable with grades and has clear rubrics. Due dates are fairly spaced out, and overall he's just a great person and professor
Such a caring and compassionate professor who is passionate about his work. Has fantastic energy!
mean to students

Ms. Bunea is pretty good at lecturing. The exam problem is very similar to the problems she goes through in lecture or the ones she gave in recitation. The class is easy as long as you pay attention in class. She also posts all the notes on canvas which is very helpful. Recommend taking this class with her!

Mostly good. 95% of grade is three prelims, rest from an optional homework. You don't turn in the other homework for credit, but do them to do well in the class! Also do all the discussion problems. If you can do all those, then exams are not bad. But each exam is 5-6 questions. I messed up 2 questions on 2nd prelim and tanked my grade to an A-.
good lecturer, lecture notes also made for good review material. exams were straightforward especially if you pay attention to lecture and homework content
Skipped 3/4 of the lectures, didn't read any textbooks, good class

She is an AMAZING professor who teaches clearly and explains the material well. I put in effort, did my work on time, and received a good grade. She has a slight accent and uses a blackboard, but overall she's an enthusiastic and kind woman. I was confused by the negative reviews I read, anyways this is a great class and professor. 100% recommend

The class is pretty straightforward, and Bunea teaches it well. She's funny, and she's accessible through email and outside of class. She posts her lecture notes online but the lectures are still helpful as she tends to add context that is not present in her posted notes.
My favorite professor i've had at Cornell. As long as you pay attention and do the homework you should really be fine.

BTRY 3080 with Bunea was one of the lighter classes I've taken at Cornell. I came in without having taken any calculus or stats since high school but all you literally need to know is basic integration and differentiation. Bunea was chill, homework wasn't bad at all, and there was no final. Genuinely don't understand why this class has a bad rep

Bunea's class was hard for me. Definitely wouldn't recommend for someone who doesn't have background in Stats or some calc. That being said, she clearly likes the class and her students. She said some of the funniest things in lecture and was really open to helping me when I did poorly on a test. She gets a bad rep: unjustly.

Absolutely the worst course I have had. She makes the course and the material unnecessarily complicated. If it wasn't for the TA, I would have failed the class. Attending her lectures were the worst hours I spent on campus. She writes on a blackboard and her handwriting is just way too difficult to read and goes too fast. Take ECON3110 instead.

I enjoyed Prof. Bunea's lectures very much. Some people might say otherwise but honestly I think it's very difficult to teach a statistics course and keep it engaging in general. She really does a great job and I really appreciated everything I learned! Final grade is 90% prelims/exam though, so be careful if that's not your cup of tea.

The text book is so much better than her lecturing. The class is pretty cool and straightforward. Just read the textbook and go through the example problems and you will do well. A lot of students do very well. Make sure you can integrate well (double integrals too).
Lectures were always boring and unhelpful, so I learned everything on my own time to even do remotely well on exams. She can be quite funny occasionally.

She's been teaching this class for a long time so it seems like she has lost interest. Lectures are pretty boring and people usually stop showing up to class halfway through. She does post all the notes online though and the material itself isn't too difficult. The TAs are also not great. Make sure to review the discussion questions and do homework

Worst professor I've had for a statistics course. Makes it extremely difficult to understand and the course is very theorem-based when exams are not. Her notes are also very hard to decipher and the grades take forever to be posted.

Great teacher. Her lectures are easy to follow and well paced. Overall, some more difficult concepts, so would not recommend if you're looking for an easier class. However, sassy, fun, and by far my favorite prof.

Professor Bunea is always willing to help students (replies directly to students who have specific questions in class and by email), but has some really boring lectures.  She's stated that the course is more rigorous than in past years. I feel that grades  have to be earned with hard work now. 3 tests make up 90% of your grade, so study hard!
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Lectures are not engaging at all. She attempts to get people involved by asking questions, but is just greeted by awkward silence. Going to lecture/recitation is not necessary to understanding the material. Just read the textbook. Prelims are based on recitation and homework problems, so if you do those, you're set. Low effort to get an A-.

She really cares about her students and wants everyone to understand. Very approachable. I've heard this class in the spring was impossible but as an average student I thought this class was pretty easy. The tests were exactly what we did in class.
Avoid at all cost. Very distant and disorganized.

Literally gives you copies of handwritten notes at the end of each class -- so even if you didn't go to class, you're able to understand the material. She's very friendly, approachable and while she does have an accent, it's not difficult to figure out what's going on if you pay attention.
horrible

Stay away from this woman at all costs. Don't risk your grade whatsoever. If she doesn't like you it's over for you and your grade. Has no structure to her class and is honestly the worst professor I have ever taken at Cornell. Listen to this please. AVOID.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This professor is a menace. Her grading was completely unclear and she obviously gave students bad grades for no other reason than she didn't like them. Taking this course was like watching a child on a power trip every day. stay away

You have no way to figure out how to improve because there is no grading rubric and no feedback. You will be expected to read upwards to 150 pages before every class. Very arbitrary grading and excruciatingly long lectures with no breaks as promised in syllabus. Grading is a mystery even with 1 week left. Expects thesis level work with <1000 words.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Oh God please, do yourself a favor and stay away. No clear grading rubric. Impossible to please. A class where hard work doesnt pay off. Unreasonable amount of reading. Long, boring lectures. Dont, just dont.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: She really knows her stuff but definitely assigned way too much reading. I ended up skimming a lot because it was physically impossible to read everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Byfield knows her stuff! She knows a lot about the things she teaches. She  is always willing to help students out if they need extensions on papers etc. She is an engaging teacher and encourages discussion during discussion sections, otherwise she lectures in her other classes (still interesting).
Boring at times, extremely interesting otherwise. Lots of long essay writing unfortunately.

Interesting, but a LOT of material. Readings tedious at times, I ended up skimming a lot. Lectures LONG; prof mostly lectured nonstop, reading from her notes for 75 mins while students struggled to keep up with notes; no visual aids such as powerpoints. Discussions the best part of the class; fair grader. I'd give the class a B-

Literally one of the best professors at Cornell. When a classroom's desk space was too small for an in-person prelim during COVID, he immediately moved the exam online. His lectures were engaging, and some of the few recorded ones that I looked forward to watching. Honestly the best.

Professor Hwang is fantastic. The class was set up to work at your own pace, but help was always available when needed. He is fantastic at explaining things, very friendly, flexible, and approachable. Even if he taught more boring classes, I'd still take it if it were with Hwang.

Professor Hwang has been one of my favorite professors this semester and it's a shame I didn't get to take his class in person. He explains the material very well and in a way that makes it fun. Sets clear expectations and clearly cares about his students. 2240 is an easy class but I'd recommend it even if it wasn't because Prof. Hwang is great.

Prof. Hwang is there best in the business. Whether your into Fi or not, you will need to thoroughly understand the fundamentals of equities and fixed income if your going to be big in this game. Hwang is a world class Corporate Finance prof, and renown researcher in Behavioral-Fi. World class prof, in a world class program. Sit up front.
A great professor, super accessible and a wonderful guy. He is extremely helpful and wants you to succeed in his class. Would really recommend!
This professor makes intro finance super engaging and easy to understand. Doesn't take attendance but going to class is valuable. Tests are fair and he gives practice problems beforehand.

Hes a super nice and helpful guy, and a great lecturer to top it off. There is a good amount of self learning for this course but it is not too challenging. The stock trading game and portfolio projects are fun and easy. Lectures give you career insight as well as basic finance knowledge 10/10 professor
The lectures are super clear. He is a really good lecturer, super nice, and is always available for help. The class overall is easy. Little reading and the tests are easy.

Professor Byrne truly cares about her students and not just their success inside of her class, but their outside involvement as well. I was fortunate to have her for COMM 1101 in person this year and she was so understanding about all the struggles of online learning for the kids who were not on campus and pushed back assignment dates to help.
This is a chill and fun class. You won't regret it

She is so amazing. The material is not super interesting but she makes it enjoyable. She is also super understanding. Attendance is mandatory but she gives a fair amount of absences. I definitely recommend taking a class with her if you can.
She seems like a very genuine and caring person.
She is one the most inspirational prof I have ever met. She is a really nice and caring person with very good teaching skills. She is my favorite prof so far.
Fantastic professor. She gives you many opportunities to succeed in the class. She genuinely cares about her students and wants them to do well.
Sahara is truly the best professorperson at Cornell. She really cares about her students.

Great teacher. Engaging, interesting and pertinent lectures. Creates great study guides that is incredibly clear what will be on the exam. In office hours, very helpful and fun to talk to. Projects were fun and final paper was not exceedingly difficult.
Exciting lectures, interesting topics. Constant class discussion (very enlightening)

Best professor and best class I took in my 4 years at Cornell. Prof Byrne respects you as a student and person, and if you're willing to work hard and put in an honest effort, you will learn more in her class than any multiple choice/test based class. Amazing professor, even better person!

LOVE HER! Great class, very interesting, very relevant. Really knows what she's talking about since she worked in the field for so long. Probably my favorite class I've taken. FOR TESTS STUDY THE TEXTBOOK. Love her, recommend media/sahara to everyone!

Byrne's is awesome, I love her! That said, don't take the class for granted. Make an effort and THOROUGHLY read the assigned chapters in the book and pay attention. It will pay off in the end. Byrne's is such an exciting prof, and I'll miss not having her next semester. Great Personality!

Best teacher I have had at Cornell. Professor Byrne is an engaging speaker who truly cares for her students. She takes interest in what students have to say and tests are straight forward. She makes awesome study guides too, page numbers in all.. Take the class!
Sahara Byrne is the best professor I've had at Cornell so far hands down. Super nice and caring about her students, and a great teacher. Take 2200 if you can.
BEST TEACHER EVER!!!
No Comments

She is wonderful! Her lectures are well organized, concise and engaging. The exams are straight-forward - she doesn't try to trick you. If you attend lecture, at least skim the readings, and turn in the projects, you will have no problems getting an A.

Sahara Byrne is the best professor ever! Very helpful and makes the subject matter interesting. I can stare at her all day long. The exams were very fair, as long as you read the assigned readings and go to lecture, you should have no problem.

In Byron Suber's ballet class you will get an amazing work out, spiced up with tidbits of dance history. He makes you reevaluate the Ballet aesthetic and think about its socio-cultural implications. His style is based on classical ballet, however, be prepared for unusual combinations that will challenge you to ditch your habits.

This class was definitely not what I expected.  DANCE 232 (Modern Dance Technique II) was really more yoga than dance.  Sometimes we rolled around on the floor or did strange acting exercises.  If you're free-spirited and hippie-ish, you will probably enjoy the class.  If you're looking for something similar to a jazz class, this is not it.

This class can be as challenging as you want it to be, depending on how perfect you want to get with all of the exercises. They're not intricate, but they are useful for developping good form, etc. Prof has some interesting thoughts on ballet- it's not a traditional ballet class at all, but can be a great experience no matter what your preferences.
No Comments
really bright, really funny, really motivated, and really ****. just the way i like my dance teachers.

Trauma Studies was the hardest class I took at Cornell as an English major but the most rewarding. Prof. Caruth brings such a high level of scholarship to the table that it is sure to challenge but inspire as well. Additionally, she is one of the most caring, easy-going, and perfectly mannered English profs I know. She is a blessing to Cornell!

A truly special professor; I took Caruth's first year writing seminar (it should be listed as COML 2030, but I selected this one instead). Professor Caruth was very understanding with deadlines and extensions. She doesn't grade off of attendance or completion points, so participation is tantamount to success in her class.

Professor Caruth is a truly inspirational instructor. Her knowledge and dedication to teaching is second to none, and offered a diverse syllabus that covered an eclectic range of topics. I highly recommend taking one of her courses if you get the chance.
Is there anything this professor can't teach?
This is a special professor. A professor who will make your dreams come true. Don't miss out!
She is a professor for all of us.
Her name is Cathy GOAT (greatest of all time)

Awesome professor, super inspiring, top of her field. Essentially chose to become an English major after this class. readings were difficult, lectures were engaging, and grading (take-home papers) were super doable. Had a lot on my plate the semester i took the course and still was able to get an A.

Professor Caruth is one of the most caring instructors that I have ever met. If you contact her outside of class, she is very accommodating, and she wants to see all of her students succeed. The course involved a lot of reading, but it was manageable and allowed for an increase in analytical reading skills. She also brings outside relevant info in

I really learned what it means to read closely in this class. I never knew one could get so much out of a text! This is a skill that will have other applications in my life and I'a grateful to Prof. Caruth for teaching me this. I learned a lot and really enjoyed the texts we read. Plus Prof. Caruth cares about her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I thought this was a fabulous class. Not only did I love the class reading/discussion but Prof. Caruth is also very sensitive to student concerns. I have never had such good feedback on my papers. Prof. makes issues come alive. I would recommend this class to anyone. Truly great Prof!

It is clear from the moment you meet prof. Caruth that she cares about her students and all global struggles, creating a forum for open discussion. However, she tends to overly state her views on politics and religion in class, and (maybe accidentally) make those who disagree feel belittled. Also, her grading criteria is extremely confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Esteemed professor, bad course. Very elementary
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Levine is passionate about both the course material and its application towards advocacy and political change. Her lectures are very interactive, and she grades based on in-class writing, out-of-class essays, and participation.
Attendance and interaction are 40% of the grade, and there is a lot of reading before each lecture. The assignments are not difficult. The content is interesting for a humanities course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very easy 2-credit class taken for a GPA boost. Just 2 papers and a final paper. Attendance required unfortunately. Her lectures are so awfully dry. It was an easy A but probably not the most worthwhile class I could take.

I took ENG 3795 Communicating Climate Change, and I genuinely believe it was the most important class I took in Fall 22'. Caroline is personable, lenient, and a good lecturer, and I feel that I came out of the class as a much better climate communicator. There are many essays and readings, but IMO they are all worth your time- 9/10 would take again
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--So many papers

reviews.comment: COGST1101 was a mixed bag. There were times when it was very interesting and thought-provoking, and other times when there were no thoughts to be had. The format of the class is not great, as most of the time, students are giving presentations on the content and not Casasanto. If she taught more, I think her class would be more interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was one of my favorite classes. A good amount of reading but no homework, I enjoyed her lectures. I didn't like having to listen to students' presentations because most were not very good. Her tests were so easy, two short-answer exams (mostly had to argue well) and 1 MCQ. You can do a group presentation in place of an exam. Easiest A+ for me.

Professor was okay, but did not actually teach most of the class. She would only give 1 of the 5 presentations each class, with a majority of time spent listening to other students' group presentations. Her lectures were solid and covered the reading well, but beware of the class format. Exams were a bit tough, but doable if you did the readings.

She's a great professor. This class is all group projects and Socratic seminar. If you like talking about current events and are very opinionated, you'll love it. DO NOT take this class if you have a fear of public speaking. This is the kind of class where 1 super liberal & 1 super conservative kid fight the whole time. Lot of fun.

she is thorough, smart, and caring. i wish they had her teach the entire program, she is genuine and very encouraging professionally. please bring her back and make her a full time professor for cybersecurity and contract law

Dr. Nateram was in a roundtable and development chat, and she went the extra mile to show everyone principles of a good contract and also talked about cybersecurity how important it is to review data we put into AI models and how we store information. She is so sweet and smart, if you get a chance to take her class, do it!

It's an ivy league school, so expect it to be challenging and difficult. Not sure about the other ratings but i learned alot from her and the course. I really like cornell's professional development classes and all the professors they have. Celina always took the time to have a coffee chat with students after going through the materials. 10/10

I really loved her instruction on my courses at Cornell and despite my challenges between being a busy mom and having a career, she made the time to respond to all my questions and genuinely felt she cared about the well being of students. I love Cornell and having professors like her.

Celina was an OUTSTANDING instructor for the Power and Ethics in Negotiation class.Her energy, intelligence and teaching style made the live sessions both fun and informative. She provided meticulous feedback, showing genuine care for students' growth.Cornell's cert programs are pricey but worth the investment, I'd love to take more of her courses.
Amazing lecturer, caring, simply one of the best professors Cornell has to offer. Take this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class was by far one of the most interesting classes I have ever taken. Papers are peer graded and the median grade is the grade you get. There are 6 papers, 6 discussion sessions, and 12 quizzes + lectures. 6 extra credit points are offered. The lectures are quite long but are usually very interesting. Take this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The course was enjoyable and Ceci gives thought-provoking lectures. The books are actually interesting, unlike some FWS classes. There's extra credit opps and the 6 essays are peer-graded, so getting an A is totally possible! The 3-hour lectures do get a bit tedious. The class was a bit disorganized (esp. paper deadlines and PollEv quizzing).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--So many papers

reviews.comment: Nice guy, but posted wrong essay prompt to Canvas. When students pointed out the mistake, they said to answer the prompt on Canvas. 4 days before the due date, they changed their minds and said to write a different prompt. This was after many students had already completed and submitted their essays. Never taken a class that was so mismanaged.

Ceci is incredibly kind, a great teacher, and extremely well-respected in his field. I haven't met a single person who doesn't like him/his classes. He is flexible and caring and incredibly knowledgable. Get to know him if you can!

Six Pretty Good Books was co-taught by Prof. Ceci and Prof. Macy (and has been taught by Prof. Hancock before). I took it to fulfill requirements, but it turned out to be a REALLY interesting class. Authors included Duncan Watts and Malcolm Gladwell, and some visitedskyped in for Q&A. Definitely talk to Prof. Ceci after class--he is SO nice!!
Great professor and great class. My friends at other elite universities do not have classes on bees, and they wish they had
I honestly expected an easer class kind f like other non major bio major classes but i am really glad i took the class because it was super interesting
I can't believe how much I learnt in this class and it was really fun
Funny and passionate. Her exams are NOT easy and very specific.
yay bees! great class and professor :)
She's a great professor! Very friendly and very fair. If you have a genuine problem with the course you can bring it up to her and she'll probably agree with you and fix it!
great class, bees are cool!
amazing class, professor and person. Vey clear and engaging presentations, slides, and grading criteria. As long as you show up to class, you'll do well on assignments

Professor Caillaud is a great lecturer and I really enjoying learning about the fascinating biology of honeybees. It was always interesting to be in lecture and very often fun. I wish her slide shows were a bit shorter so we can get to everything in class
I swear to god just show up and get your A

Taking this course right now and really loving what I am learning. the course is super intersting and well structured with pre and post lecture quizzes that keep me on my toes and engaged. The in class activities help with that too. Definitely a great course for non majors

TAKE THIS CLASS!! Mrs Calliaud is literally the sweetest little French professor and her energy lights up the room every time she speaks. The content is also super interesting! Best class I've taken at Cornell so far

I love Professor Caillaud!She is funny, passionate, about honey bees and wild bees. I really liked the structure of the classwith the activities during lecture and the weekly online quizzes. It kept me engaged and on top of the  material covered and made prep of exams easier.
Professor Caillaud is a great lecturer; she goes the extra step to ensure her students are engaged and interested in the topics she discusses.

She was the best and a fantastic lecturer, very understanding with regrads to needs of individual student, and very responsive. The active learning material during lecture was useful even though it slowed down the pace of the lectures. Great class! We need to save the bees!

A great class about bees, really interesting, and taught with care and thoughtfully. Weekly homework involves pre-lecture videos and readings, plus an online quiz. The final project is awesome and I had a lot of fun with my partners. Loved this class! And professor Caillaud too!

Without question, the greatest professor I've ever had the pleasure of studying under ever. You guys will learn so much being in her class and the commitments for the week are minimal at most. Would definitely take again, and no, this isn't a paid review. Prof. Caillaud is an 11/10.

She has great knowledge of the subject and she is very enthusiastic which kept me very engaged during lectures. Using polleverywhere also helped me stay motivated during class, the weekly online quizzes were super helpful but she never posted the key

Professor Caillaud is so lovely, kind, and intelligent. Her lectures are engaging, and while there's a ton of information, most of the work is just busywork. Her quizzes are kind of poorly written, but she clearly cares so much about her students. Definitely would take again.

Marina Caillaud was the best professor I had in my four years at Cornell. She is caring, kind, intelligent, and she is absolutely hilarious. I took the course in 2019 and was a TA in 2021 and can honestly say graduating without taking one of her courses is a travesty! She has inspired my passion for public health advocacy and I am so so grateful!
just taking that course rn and loving it.
Super kind prof and passionate about material. Need to study for exams but questions are straight-forward if you know the content
Great professor with really interesting lectures. Professor was very accessible and accommodating when I tested positive for Covid-19. This was by far my favorite class at CU so far (i am a senior)

Lectures by professor caillaud included latest information on the topic at at hand and that was really unexpected given that this class was described as a non major, and I definitely had several friends in the class who were not biology majors yet they enjoyed being treated with latest info
amazing lecturer, and I learned so much from her course
very interesting material taught with enthusiasm and care

If you are interested in learning about diseases and epidemics, this class is great for you. The material is pretty interesting but Professor Caillaud often reads off the slides. The tests aren't so difficult, as long as you know the material, but the sections are a little unnecessary.

Great professor-- cares about your learning. This is one of the few classes where I felt like I learned a LOT but didn't feel like I was until I got to the end of the course and realized I know a lot more about the process of epidemiology. She's super nice and very helpful and accessible during OH and through emails.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: The course was really interesting. If u read the articles she sends out (there is no textbook), you should be able to get 100s on the prelims. There were some quizzes, but they were not hard at all. There is no final just a final project. Definitely an easy A. I would take it over again if I could.
Professor AI is a great person. He truly cares about his student, and has a kind heart for grades. Would like to take his class again.
Most practical classes at this university.3838
Very demanding and fair. So informative that many lazy and spoiled children whine about the difficulties that the material of his classes present.
Lectures are useless. And he's grading is really arbitrary. At the end of the semester a lot of people had issues with the grade.
He's a nice guy.  He really cares about his students.  He helps you get a job after graduation if you haven't found one.  He looks mean, but he's really a teddy bear.
Very helpful once you prove you know what you're talking about, very intimidating otherwise.
No Comments
Not a very nice person.
Not very helpful; overly sarcastic

This is NOT a stats class, it's a financial mathematics class. You will be plugging in formulas - start memorizing early. Multiple new concepts are introduced in every lecture and there is no discussion, just a three 75 minute lectures and office hours. Homeworks are not like the lecture examples but do reflect the difficulty of the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The lectures are really long and tedious, going over very simple topics for a very long time. However, the homework is nothing like the lectures and are almost impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She's a nice person, just not a great teacher. Her explanations aren't always what the student asked about. Grading is 90% 3 prelims and 10% homework and you can have a one-page formula sheet on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Homework problems are nothing like the examples done, over and over again, in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Earls is great at explaining things during office hours. I just think the nature of the course and the crammed curriculum makes it harder  to explain everything so easily, especially during a 8:40am lecture
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Her lectures are the worst. She just reads off powerpoint so fast, you have no clue which things you need to jot down (if she even stays on that slide for that long), literally my second semester with her and I only understood the first 3 or so lectures of each semester and the rest is just trying to understand her cluttered powerpoint. NoBook4Help

Dr. Earls' lectures aren't the best: she reads a lot through slides; however, during office hours, she does an amazing job to clarify each and every single point of what she explained in her lectures. The homework is based on the material covered in the lectures and the labs. Work through the homework and the exams shouldnt be too hard.

Knowledgeable, approachable, and very helpful at office hours. However, she does speak very fast and go through a ton of information each lecture, so be ready to go through lectures before/afterwards on your own time. Be ready for 40+ slide power points in 75 minutes...
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is not clear, and even some youtube videos make clear points than she did. She basically just read through slides. Morning class!! Attendance is not mandatory but there is a weekly quiz on Thursdays. Appropriate homework load. Not many practice problems. Use R to do homework but didn't require to code in exam. Allow one self-made formula sheet

I've had two classes with her and she's wonderful! Can be tough at times but is seriously dedicated to helping you learn the material and is often quite funny. You obviously have to participate a lot since its a language class so I don't suggest taking it early in the morning or you'll be too tired to want to do the exercises
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Flaminia is great; she keeps class lighthearted and fun, but also really helps to jumpstart your Italian.  She knows how to work with students at all levels and is a genuinely nice person.  She takes our work seriously but is always good for a laugh during class.  If you don't slack off, you'll really enjoy and get a lot out of this course
i love this professor!

I hear the intro (101) with her is difficult, but 109 was a blast.  Small class of 25 or so where I made some of my best friends.  Flaminia is a sweetheart and a wonderful woman who sometimes cooks at ZaZa's (it's nice to see her there).  I don't know about lower levels but she's amazing in 209!
Just because she's cute and from Italy doesn't mean that she's a good professor.  Picks favorites, pretty damn condescending, not much of an intellectual.
fantastica. if you can take a class with her, don't hesitate...if you're at least somewhat interested in italian, you'll love her and her class.

Flaminia is amazing, and I've had 3 classes with her...She is so patient, beyond helpful, and has no problem giving As if you pay attention and  keep up with the work. She also has a great sense of humor and seems to really care about her students.
Great professor, awesome classes...she makes Italian worth taking
Best professor at Cornell - brilliant and extremely fair...you have to do the work though....
Flaminia always seems bored in class.  She doesn't seem very smart, but that is probably because she hates her job. She can also take out this frustration by making fun of students in class.
awesome, smart, hilarious
No Comments
Fun, sassy, very intelligent, and good at getting discussions started. Willing to help out, fair grader. Can get testy when provoked.
She's so cute!! She can be tough, definitely hard-core for the Italian dept.
Amazing - best prof at Cornell.  If you do the work she is the greatest!

Dude hasn't taught here for a year...but in light of the below comments, wanted to say one of my better classes. Make an effort, talk to him, and you're fine. He gives a damn and a lot of people end up with crappy grades cause they can't deal with having something asked of them..

He shows up late to almost every class. But more importantly, he is perhaps one of the hardest graders at cornell. I am a great writer, and have always done well in english courses, but in his class, i struggled more than i  ever have in my life. His grading was incredibly harsh and unfair (at one point the class average was a C-).

For some reason, does not give out many A's. Teaches a very hard class, but ENGL 1108 has a high average grade, becasue the other TA's are easier. do not take this calss if you want an easy writing seminar at all - you will do a lot more and harder work than you have to.

great guy. intimidating first couple of weeks but warms up, everyone in the class ended up loving him.  knows his stuff.  put effort in and you'll do well.  shows up a little late sometimes.  more based on fiction than poetry.  great class!
Rockin' bod.  Very strict, but you learn a lot.  Very wide face.  Frequently shows up late.  Not married.  Family lives in Michigan, crazy older brother.

Cecil is challenging but at least he?s doing his job. Unconditional praise is not my idea of education. I?ve seen the stuff my classmates write in peer reviews, and it?s dribble, disrespect for a guy trying to actually teach something. You want the praise that you feel the ?Ivy League? warrants you? Take the time to write a halfway decent essay.
He is condescending and crude.  He is not helpful, in fact, on the contrary, he destroys independence, confidence, and interest levels. He is an embarrassment to the Ivy League.
No Comments
wouldn't recommend. shes pretty interesting but lecture very reliant on student participation and its her way or the highway

Professor Chang is AMAZING. Even if you are not interested in gender studies, you should take this class. Her lectures are not opinionated at all and she allows for class discussion. The TA was amazing too.

Professor Chang was great. She is extremely smart and knowledgeable about history and gender issues. She is smart, stern, and well-respected. She shows no favoritism towards any specific students which is great, and she really values all ideas. She is impartial and a great teacher. I learned so much, and think everyone should take this course.

This is the most useful class I've ever taken at Cornell and I've learned so so so much. We tried 6 wines every class in different countries. Professor Stanley is the most knowledgable, caring person ever, and she will answer your questions extremely thoroughly. Also learned a lot about Cornellians in the wine industry. Super proud!

This class is only pass fail, and the drop deadline is after one class. The 2 hour and 50 minute lectures are surprisingly manageable once wine is involved, and the professor is clearly very knowledgeable and I definitely learned a lot! Exams were harder than expected but definitely still okay (you get an index card of notes).

This course is just a disaster. I have no idea why they do not allow students to drop this course even before the deadline set by the university, which made me have no chance to drop it. Take care if you wanna take this course with this guy and the one called biondi
Take wines, just take it. This class and professor are awesome.

I love love love Professor Stanley. She is so knowledgable and kind and one of the most engaging lecturers I've ever had. She knows so much about wine and her brutal honesty and fun teaching style really kept everyone engaged. I wish I could've taken her class sooner. SHE IS AMAZING!

I absolutely adore Prof. Stanley. She is so passionate and knowledgeable about wine and cares about her students. Lectures are info heavy but she makes it very obvious what will be on exams. She is super approachable and always is happy to connect students with resources/alumni. Wines was my fav class at Cornell!!

Stanley is great at her job. It's a feat to teach this many people about wine in a way that's accessible and interesting. The lectures are long and definitely drag a bit after a glass of wine, but overall I'm glad I took the class. She tries to make it fun (not hard, it's a class where you drink wine), and I definitely learned a good amount.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It's wines, so the lectures themselves are fun (you drink wine for credit). My main issue was the prelim and final, it really covered incredibly niche things that just were not covered in lecture at any point. Theoretically, the questions came from the reading, but it's like 40 pages of reading per week to cover it all, and it's wines, like come on

Dr. Cherney is a sweet woman, but she does not lecture well and her ppts were all over the place. I had zero experience with animal care, so the messy lectures paired with no textbook to supplement made it really difficult for me to really learn anything at all, so I personally struggled a lot on the prelims

Easiest class I've taken. All the assignments are easy and you can usually fight for points back. Don't take the 1 prelim lightly though, there aren't many grades in the class so make sure you do decent on that. There's a final project that's basically graded on completion. Lecture is very unorganized so you can skip and not miss anything.

She's a nice lady and easily one of the most caring you'll meet. However, she's not the best lecturer and lecture is a snooze fest. Just review the practice tests she provides and review the slides and you should be good. Lab assignments are tedious but it's really the only thing you have to worry about. Class is pretty easy just do the work.

Nothing against the professor, just how to course is organized. Half of the grade is just menial busywork that doesn't correlate to any real life application or to the course itself. Valuable feedback is never given with little clarity offered on questions, leaving students guessing as to how to get points. Labs and lecture are peak nap time hours.
So sweet and caring, but unorganized. Assignment grading criteria is often unclear. The practice exams are very helpful for the actual exams.

Very sweet woman, but so unorganized and unfocused in lectures it makes it so difficult to follow along with anything she is saying. She is a pretty easy grader on papers and assignments and tells you what you need to know for the one prelim in the class. Overall easy course, but hard to sit through her lectures.

While I think she can be a bit disorganized, she will only test on things she lectures on. I loved writing the papers for this class and enjoyed the freedom we were allowed. She's very caring and available to answer questions. I do think that you get out of this class what you put into it so if you don't care about it, you won't gain anything.

Dr. Cherney is such a nice lady and so helpful if you ever ask her anything. The class is interesting if you actually pay attention (the first couple of lectures were kind of boring and hard to follow but it gets better). She provides notes for all her lectures that are very helpful and prelims are fine. Noncumulative final

She is so unorganized in lectures and just rambles on and on. Extremely hard to follow. I only showed up for the first few lectures and then I couldn't take it anymore. Still have an A+ so very easy class, not a great professor. She is a nice person, just not good at her job

Cherney is a very nice professor and cares about her students, but the lectures are very disorganized, and grading criteria isn't very clear. It's not entirely clear what she's going to test her students on, and lab instructions are often poorly worded and difficult to follow the specifics for. Nice and relatively easy, but not the most organized.

A very nice woman, but her teaching style leaves me so discombobulated. She's a relatively easy grader, but does not usually provide her expectations for an assignment so if you get points off, it's usually because you didn't realize something had to be included in the first place. She's also pretty inaccessible. I didn't learn much in the class.

Cherney is very nice and is willing to help students who are worried about material. Lectures are often tangential and can be hard to follow, but she posts online notes and practice exams that practically spell out the answers to test questions. While she is approachable after class and during office hours, she doesn't often respond to emails.
Shes scatterbrained and unorganized. I couldnt follow a lecture to save my life.

She is honestly a very nice prof, who will take time to discuss any worries/issues you have. But although it is clear she cares about her students, her grasp of her own material is often spotty at best. She tries hard, but her lectures are disorganized and often rambling. She will frequently go off topic which can make lecture frustrating.

Cherney is super nice and cares a lot about her students.  Knows students have a life and other classes, and she is often willing to relax a deadline  for projects/assignments. For those who think she doesn't care: simply not true. She's extremely busy (just take a look at her office & desk) and does her best to make time to help students succeed!
horrible professor, does not pay attention at all in lecture and teaches us useless information just by reading off of the powerpoints she makes
Can be confusing at times, but generally a good professor. Cherney is very fair and gives you a good idea of what to expect on tests, etc. Genuinely cares about the success of her students.

Great discussion-based class, which is hard to find in most science departments.  Workload is not terrible- just participate in class and don't save the book review and final project for the last minute.  Dr. Cherney is so nice and willing to help students.  She's a sharp tack, but isn't condescending like some professors.

Dr. Cherney is a very sweet person.  She really cares about her students and how they do.  I think she is a fast paced lecturer who likes to get a lot of info in there, which is great.  Her lectures are interesting and highly informative.  She is a great advisor too- very kind and helpful.

Possibly one of the worst classes I've taken so far at Cornell. She doesn't really explain things well, and a lot of time it comes across as if she doesn't even know what she's talking about. Class is genuinely boring. If you aren't interested in farm animals, this might not be the class for you because we spend way too much time talking about cow.

She is one of the nicest professors I have ever had.  She genuinely cares about how her students are doing in the class and will do her best to clear things up if you dont understand them.Knowledgeable, straight forward, great all around. Im looking forward to having her as a professor again.

I've had Professor Cherney for 3 classes and she is always awesome. She explains things very well and is always available to her students. She makes her classes fun and is very fair when it comes to grading. A great Professor.
quite confused and seems at times to be way in over her head.
She's really nice and very smart.  Very down to earth and willing to help. Great teacher!
Very good teacher. Could be more confident, but she is very smart....

I took INFO 4940 with him and he is an excellent professor. He comes to class well prepared and preps students for the assignments by showing lots of examples and providing lots of feedback. A great professor overall!

I had this professor for INFO 4940, and it was one of my favorite classes. Their lectures were engaging and well-structured, making complex material easy to follow. The course emphasized creative, project-based work, which challenged me both technically and artistically. I appreciated how the professor encouraged originality
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof C was a great professor who taught with passion, experience and curiosity. This class expanded my ideas of technology in relation to life and culture. He gives great feeback and comes to class exicted each week to learn along with us.
He's very smart and incredibly helpful to students. He's very interested in their progress!
Very interesting course!
Chris was very inspirational!

I've taken 4240 and 4940 with Chris and both were good classes. 4240 can be a bit of a drag sometimes but you'll notice despite lots of complaints most people in the class get a grade in the A range. Chris is more enjoyable to take in 4940 because of the individualized attention you get so don't be afraid of other reviews.

Course had good message but grading/instruction methods made it horrid. TAs are so inconsistent and grading is harsh, you can easily get under 70s. While I tried to have a coachable attitude, it was impossible because every TA would say vastly different things I honestly got lost on how to even improve. I don't think many peers liked this class.

Overall, would not recommend taking this class. Assignments are tedious and require huge leaps to come up with a (usually) speculative design. Design methods were not taught well. Grading is subjective; difficult to improve/master. Lectures were the only positive of the course; they were often interesting and I appreciated Prof. C's sense of humor.

echoing what everyone else had said except for that one 5 rating. feedback is all over the place and they stop giving it at the end of the semester. one week a TA will praise you and another will degrade you the next week for the same quality of work, so there's no point in even applying feedback from previous assignments.

In addition to everything that's been said already professor Csikszenthmihayli continues to do what he does. Still hasn't put in grades 2 days past the deadline, with ungraded assignments from like months ago. Such a bad bad class recommenced everyone to STAY AWAY

The undergrad TAs don't know what they're doing. Insanely slow grading yet feels like a lottery. One week you'll get close to full points then the next you fail with the same quality of work. Feedback all over the place and professor is so snarky it's irritating. Even for INFO, choose another concentration course. DO NOT take for fun. I regret it.

Didn't learn anything in this class. Grading totally depends on the TA, but there are many opportunities for extra credit. Attendance is 100% mandatory, scarily so (checking attendance multiple times in a given lecture, counting number of students in the room, etc.). OK I guess for a major requirement but would not take for the pursuit of knowledge

Just terrible! Grading feels like roulette depending on what TA you get / how the professor is feeling. Class has 0 structure, readings / material is laughable — for those interested in design careers, this will not help you in the slightest 

Look at how many angry students there are this is pretty indicative how peers in the class feel

GRADING IS SO SUBJECTIVE. THEY GRADE SUBJECTIVELY AND LAZILY TO JUST TAKE POINTS OFF. CHRIS DOESN'T HAVE A CLEAR STRUCTURE IN LECTURE EITHER AND JUMPS BACK AND FORTH BETWEEN TOPICS. HE ALSO OFTEN UMMS/UHHS THROUGHOUT THE LECTURE WHICH IS DISTRACTING WHEN IT'S HARD TO UNHEAR.

my least fav class ever at cornell! prof is super rude + bashes students in class / assignments. beyond the prof the class itself is awful, its all over the place and lecture is him just stuttering / umm-ing through random topics with no flow
Amazing class, amazing prof. Really gets you thinking about how technology interacts with and impacts the world around us. Assignments encourage you to be very creative.

Wordy assignments make expectations unclear. Subjective grading and dependent on TAs — you might not always get the same TA so if one gives you positive feedback, another might not especially if the professor is grading it. The professor can be funny but snarky. You can do well with effort, though what counts as “effort” seems inconsistent.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Grading is subjective and harsh, by undergrad TAs who don't give clear feedback. Projects could be approved by one TA but criticized by another so confusing. Assignment instructions are scattered, which can cause large chunks of missed points. Prof can be snarky and passive aggressive. Choose another class. My least favorite INFO prof and course.

First time writing RMP because INFO4240 was a nightmare. Attendance is strict, class activities useless, 50 pages of dull readings every week, and workbooks are graded completely subjectively. 

Grading is biased and ridiculous. The instructor even calls graders who give too many 90 grade, completely unfair. Avoid this class—you'll learn nothing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment:
He assigns a lot of readings before each class, and they feel more like long research papers than enjoyable material. It's hard to focus during lectures because he says “umm” and “uh” 30 times in one sentence. The grading is very subjective, and getting over 90 seems nearly impossible. An 80 feels like a win.

I recommend you to not take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Kao's lectures present upcoming design technologies, focusing on STEM. They are inspiring to students exploring the boundaries of design.
