Grades are easy, and the vibe is quite comfy. You learn to actually design and improve through the "learn by doing" style of this class. She brings a new face to design that I learned to appreciate.
Such an understanding and engaging prof, workload is minimal and fun. Take this class :)

So knowledgeable in the subject area, and clearly cares about her work. Class time is split evenly btwn lecture and in-person workshops, and there are weekly readings and Canvas posts. Two "big" Projects but you are given ample time and support to complete. Very tech saavy, smart, witty, and understanding. Will definitely take her again!

Content wise, Human Bonding was a spectacular class and you can sense the years of experience/research she has in her lectures. But take *really* detailed notes! It's begun to live up to its 3000 level difficulty with some rather harsh grading.

Super captivating lectures, and fun to take with friends. Never wanted to miss a lecture. Very tough grader, though. Just take good, detailed notes. Graders are looking for specific keywords in short answer questions

Not the easy A anymore that everyone claims it to be. The material is interesting but the structure is really strict and doesn't have many opportunities for improving grades. Even though the exams are online, the responses need to be super specific and the feedback from graders are unclear. I've taken many HD courses and this was the hardest one.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Interesting course content, but you're solely graded on three exams that are worth a lot and are graded very harshly with points deducted for not including a single word despite them being online. There are also not many chances to improve your grade, and you receive very little feedback. Fun course material, but no longer an easy A anymore.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I was a TA for this course so I'm biased when I say TAKE IT!! It's so much fun to bond with your friends who might not be psych/HD majors because it's truly a class for everyone. Open-note prelims and relaxing afternoon lectures in Bailey Hall make for a great class to take in your last semesters at Cornell when you can get a spot.

NOT EASY A! Lectures are boring, graded by TAs who don't want to talk to you,& it doesn't matter if you know the content; The exams are like "explain in 1 sentence," then take off points for not expanding enough. ppl like her bc she gives a FEW ppl free therapy,& it's cool for ppl who have never taken a psych class and don't know basic attachment.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: exams seem easy and are online but she takes many points off for not mentioning specific words in the open ended question. her voice puts me to sleep
Good luck. She grades based on very few things, so make sure you copy her slides word for word and regurgitate them for exams.

This class changed from the previous years. The grading is quite harsh if you don't put every detail or exact keywords. The nature of the exam doesn't allow time fro you to add to your answers from the study guide because you will run out of time. I was disappointed in how it was run this semester.
She's so wonderful! Lectures are so engaging and prelims are very fair. Very personable if you want to chat with her after class

Truly the most wonderful woman I've ever had as a professor. Extremely kind and tries to incorporate pop culture references about human bonding. She makes you want to go to class and covers such important topics about relationships. I swear she is the reason I now have a boyfriend just after taking her class.
One of the best professors!! Super captivating content, fair exams, and personable

You don't know what you did right or wrong on exams and just see your grade; you don't really learn their goal in the class is who is the best copier from slides for exams; this isn't idealistic and a good way to be tested.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: AMAZING CLASS. I think everyone should take this class!! Professor Hazan is a very clear and interesting lecturer, and the content is fascinating. There is almost no homework, just some readings for the exams, and she tells you EXACTLY what'll be tested in her study guides. I learned so much in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very engaging lectures, she does speak rather slowly, but that just give you time to write down everything she says (good for the prelims). Overall she seems to really know her stuff, have her class organized well, and enjoy teaching and working with students.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Entire grade is based on exams (which r based on the lectures). WRITE DOWN EVERYTHING SHE SAYS even if it's not in the slides (those r nuggets of gold for the test). it helped me immensely with the tests as i would write down those little details! also not everything is on her slides.
most caring cute person ever

You will not get to see your graded prelims or get to see why you lost points. They do not want you to think critically, instead they want you to copy and paste from the PowerPoints. 
Some lectures focus on single studies and are presented as if the results are absolute yet there are twice as many studies that are inconclusive or say the opposite
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hazan's lectures are very interesting and she gives great examples to apply the psych studies. Grade is dependent on prelims and final only, but there is extra credit. Taken async over zoom, so was able to watch lectures at 2x speed. Her normal talking speed is like 0.5x, so I am not sure how people would be conscious during in person lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Hazan is an amazing lecturer- extremely funny and engaging. Human Bonding is the best class I have ever taken. Beware: it is really difficult to get a spot in her class as an underclassman because it's so popular. Also, her TA's graded really harshly, but I still got an A with curving. Entire grade is based on 2 tests, but interesting material

TAKE HUMAN BONDING! Such a great class, the material is super interesting (love, relationships, etc.) Don't skip the lecturesthat's the best part of the class! Get a study group before the prelims, they're straightforward, but cover a lot of material. Really cool class and great professor.

You will walk out of this class with knowledge that you will use for the rest of your life. If you're in a relationship or ever plan on being in one, this class is incredibly insightful. Lectures feel like TED talks, they're fun and laid back. No homework, just study for the exams and do the readings (short, interesting) the night before.
Hands down the greatest professor, and greatest class, I've taken at Cornell. If you can take this course, 100% do.

Professor Hazan is loved by everyone, and for good reason. She's interesting, kind, funny, and much more. The tests can be graded harsher thank you might expect, but don't let this deter you from taking this class (there's no homework so all you have to do is study). One of my favorite lecturers--and she has a really soothing voice!
Best professor ever!

One of Cornell's most beloved classes, taught by one of its most beloved professors. Engaging lectures, fascinating material, and Hazan really values student questions and input. Also has a wonderful sense of humor and you can tell she's really passionate about her subject.
Hazan is a great professor. She is extremely helpful,  very funny and guess what, she's a matchmaker!
This class is amazing!

One of the best profs I've had in Cornell. Clearly interested in her research and unbashedly shares that enthusiasm with the class. Is very approachable and friendly so don't afraid to go up and ask her questions. TAs are also very professional. Prelims can be tricky but the final makes up for it . Take the class with prof, you wont regret it!

Straightforward but interesting subject matter, engaging lectures. Takenotes very useful for exams. Only complaint is that exams were incredibly specific on lectures and readings, i.e. sometimes not focusing on main idea of reading but more on tedious details. Nit-picky grading on exams. Not 'easy A' unless you are good at studying/ test taking

Excellent course: simply put, a must take. Hazan is a great professor and researcher with information-packed and engaging lectures. Multiple choice questions on prelims can be tough, but tests overall are very fair. Don't do the readings until the outline comes out because only certain sections are required. Also, the final was about 80% repeats!

best professor I have ever had at Cornell, and my favorite class. She knows how to give a lecture, they are very entertaining with so much useful information. Her tests are hard, make sure you do all of the readings. Given that, she is very enjoyable and you can go to her office hours and ask any question about relationships. highly recommended
A bit disorganized and scattered in some lectures. Good overall.

The best professor I've ever had at Cornell. Her class is not easy, but if you work hard it's incredibly rewarding and you learn a lot. Tests can be difficult, but her amazing teaching style definitely makes the class worth it!
Great professor in class, but can be very unfair if she doesn't like you and she is often moody.

Human Bonding is a wonderful class and Professor Hazan is an extremely competent professor. I was always really excited to go in and learn. I should note that there are certain concepts that she really beats into the ground, but she is sweet enough that it makes up for it. Go up and talk to her after class!

While the material for this class was interesting, the exams were completely unfair. The tests are ridiculously specific and the TA's do not grade the exams fairly (even though it takes them about 3 weeks to grade them anyway). Must memorize a lot of information and even if you read the entire book, there is no guarantee that you'll do well.
Amazing professor! One of my favorite classes at Cornell!!  But the tests are specific so studying and reading the assignments is a must

Amazing prof. and human being. I always left her class feeling inspired about human relationships. It's a very feel-good class, and one of the most popular. It actually has helped me in my own romantic relationship tremendously. I think all human beings should be required to take this class. On a side note, though, take time to study for the tests!
great!
Human Bonding Professor at Cornell -- the hottest class available.  She's simply the best.
Great professor. Interesting material. Fairly easy class.

Definitely one of the top 2 classes I've taken at Cornell. The material was very interesting, I learned alot about human relationships and why we do the things we do. Hazan is a good lecturer with a great warm personality. Thre are lots of extra credit opportunities. I highly recommend this class!

I wasn't as crazy as most people are about this class. The material is easy, but the tests are very specific. Not a lot of work required, but not as easy to get an A as I thought it would be. I thought the class was kind of boring, but there is no doubt that Hazan is extremely nice.

hazan, i think i am developing a deep emotional attachment to you.  i have acute onset infatuation, physiological arousal, and mood dependencies.  you are my single target. (a little human bonding humor) GREAT PROF! A+
ONE OF THE BEST PROFESSOR AT CORNELL! Extremly interesting course, very useful in real world and she is just amazing! A+
awesome professor, but can be very repetitive!

Class is boring and useless as hell, but an easy A. Take it to make fun of the dumb HD kids and marvel at the extra credit opportunities.  It's really just a question of whether or not you can tolerate the stupidity of the course just to get an A.
i love you prof hazan, will you marry me? You are the best professor on the face of this planet.  And you have a nice rack

She is an AWESOME professor! You sit in the huge classroom, but feel as if she were talking personally to you. The lectures are very, very interesting. I'm happy I took this as my elective! You've got to pre-enroll early though, it gets filled up quickly.
Best Professor at Cornell
275 should be easy, but somehow isn't.  class sometimes interesting, sometimes real boring, and often pointless.
One of the best professors I've ever come across at Cornell.
Best prof at Cornell!!IF you have to choose take HD362!!
Boring class, put me to sleep.  Tests test material which is directly from the book, final is worth 50% of you grade!
Great prof!  Excellent class, very clear on lecturing and addresses all questions!
AWESOME PROFEESOR! She is the treasure of Cornell, one of the best professor ever. Great class, very useful and a must take.
This was a great course, one of the best I've taken at Cornell.  Hazan is very lovely.
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments

Honestly, he gets a lot of trash talk but he's seriously a really nice professor. He is so enthusiastic in his subject and it's unfortunate that many people don't take his class seriously. If you feel like you are doing poorly, try and talk to him! He won't bite :). There's also a huge curve at the end so no need to stress!

Completely incomprehensible during lecture. He likes to go off on unrelated tangents and make bad jokes to himself. Hard to stay focused in his lectures, and exams are often on material completely unrelated to what was talked about in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Please do not take any of his classes. He should not be teaching because he is not capable of putting together a lecture that makes any sense. He might grade easy at the end but this class is a nightmare. You will not know what is going, regardless if you read the textbook. He seems like a nice person but he can't teach to save his life.

Horrendous. You will, without fail, fall asleep in this class. Lectures are incomprehensible. Approaches the subject in the most trite and boring fashion. Everyone should avoid, ESPECIALLY if you like the subject, because he will ruin it for you.

Even if you absolutely need a one-credit course to bring you up above the minimum number of credits to remain in good academic standing, do NOT take this class! I was pretty interesting in the material before coming to class, but Cisne just lulls you to sleep. And if you think this class is an easy A, don't take it...it's not. Studied for days! = C

Most boring man alive. Do not take this class to try to get an A. No longer puts the quiz answers up before the weekly pop quizzes, and the exercise sets are extremely unclear. You can drop the lowest 1/3 of your grades but half the tim ethe quiz averages are 60s and its a guessing game. Awful class.

This class is very, very boring. I slept through the entirety of the first three classes. Then, I stopped going to class altogether. Wouldn't recommend this unless you really need 1 science credit to graduate - avoid this class.

A very easy course that liberal arts majors terrified of hard sciences go to for a requirement. Weekly HW takes 40min max(go to office hours), quiz answer keys given beforehand on blackboard, T/F Final, and the lowest 1/3 of all grades are dropped! Take it if the topic interests you, otherwise you will zone out. A free A/A+ for engineers/scientists

Dinosaurs! This is the easiest class at Cornell.  1 credit, meets once a week, no hw, only grades are multi choice midterm + final,  median grade of A-.  Don't graduate without taking this class.  If you're not interested in the subject (what's wrong with you, it's dinosaurs?) his lectures can be boring, so just surf the web till Til TRex comes up.

The worst lecturer I have ever had.  Cisne is super nice and jolly and looks like Santa, but it is impossible to pay attention in lecture and I don't learn anything.  Disorganized, boring, irrelevant.  It's a shame because I thought the class would be fun and interesting.  Don't waste your time with this.

Honestly, I do not know if this class is worth taking unless you are really interested in dinosaurs. This past semester, only 15-20 people out of 250 enrolled showed up to lecture, and I think he realized it when final grades came out (median of a B).  Don't bother enrolling if you do not really take it seriously. It is not worth it.

EAS 170 (Evo of the Earth and Life) is the most boring class I have ever taken.  Pity because the subject actually is very interesting; it's just that it's an incredibly broad intro course that like ends up dumping an incomprehensible amount of info on the students.  Cisne himself is a very nice guy and a very easy grader at the end of the course.

Only class I have ever consistently fallen asleep in.  Make sure you show up, because you will want to take as many of his quizzes as possible.  Memorize the quizzes he gives you from the previous year. (content is in random order so don't just do the next one in line)

Hilarious guy, especially when he's not trying to be. I'm a bio major and I thought the class sounded interesting. For the most part, it's not. I really don't care about rocks. End of the class is actually about organisms, and kind of interesting. I wouldn't really recommend the class, but it wasn't that bad either.
Easy science credit.  Nice guy... but extremely odd.  He basically wants to be T-Rex.
Professor Cisne is the sweetest professor ever.  I stopped going to lectures after a while bc they were irrelevent to the exams and course.  Just study the course packets and you'll do fine.
No Comments

The subject matter is actually pretty difficult but I got an A+ despite failing a bunch of quizzes because the curve is skewed.  If you sign up for the 9am lecture, bring a cup of coffee.  It's actually pretty interesting for an intro science class (although if you want an easy science class that's more fun take ntres201).

I didnt care about dinosaurs, stil don't. Just wanted to let people know this is the goofiest SOB teaching at Cornell. Great guy, sounds like a cartoon character. Any class he teaches can't be to serious.
great guy- great lectures

SANTA!? This guy is definitly sweet and kind hearted. He does awesome impressions of dinosaurs, sings, swims like a squid...hahaha. Those times however are the only times i actually stayed awake. I learned just about nothing except for the practical which even I aced with less then a true hour of studying. Our TA John freakin' rocked! (EASY)

If you just want an "A" and don't care about learning, take this class.  But if you actually want to learn and don't want to waste your time and money, don't sign up. There is no learning involved in this class whatsoever.  Lectures are completely disorganized.  Labs make no sense at all. I actually had been interested in geology, but now I'm not.

Prof. Cisne really is a nice, helpful individual.  Much nicer than any other professor I've had but I mean it is true, he can put students to sleep with any of his lectures.  He is just so passionate about his field of expertise that you are excited but tired all at the same time,... heh.

This class was BORING. I fell asleep during every lecture. Literally. Yet, I think Dr. Cisne is great. He is helpful, friendly, and doesn't see a problem with letting the average grade rise into the A-/B+ range. His lectures are boring beyond belief (repeated for emphasis). Cisne is a good guy.

do not take this class--cisne is jolly but crazy! the class is so boring.It's easy, but you dont ever really know whats going on--instead, you spend the whole time wondering how anyone can like rocks so much. if youre a lib.arts major, take eas111 instead

class is boring as hell. dont know what to study.  TAs dont know whats going on either. Cisne is a nice, jolly guy though.  dont take eas 102 unless you love rocks.  i can honestly say as a liberal arts major, I LEARNED NOTHING in this class
Nice guy, class is somewhat too easy...
Cisne is nice, but the class is boring as all hell.  And since the class is small, he knows if your sleeping and drooling.  No work except for 1 paper at the end.
the formal definition of jolly.  great guy, good lecturer, fun teacher, engaging mind.
The looks like a cross between Santa Claus and Colonel Sanders!  Very light-hearted and enthusiastic dude...
Wonderful teacher, humorous lectures. Known to mimic the movements of dinosaurs during class. Easy quizzes, plenty of lightheartedness.
What a nice person. Brought us asparagus from his garden in the spring several times. Brings calm, cool, and collected energy to a hard subject.

I had professor Clary for SANKS 1131 and 1132 and is amazing at linguistics and the Sanskrit language. He occasionally tends to say a lot of linguistic jargon but encourages students to be participative, ask lots of questions, and is genuinely willing to spend time and support you.

He's a super cool dude. Very passionate. Extremely knowledgeable. Often there are readings and you should attend class (slides don't have to much info; he speaks a lot). Lec/OH help before exams. Exams are pretty easy (short response) and workload is not horrible especially if you like to read. Not a humanities person but the class was interesting.

Prof. Clary is a very kind, positive, and interesting professor. His clear passion for the subjects he teaches translates to engaging lectures and an approachable attitude. His upbeat teaching style makes even an ancient language relevant and captivating for students. If you engage with the material, you will do great.

Professor Clary at Cornell was exceptionally caring, prioritizing our comprehension over grades. His engaging lectures were complemented by his thoughtful gesture of sharing homegrown vegetables, creating an enjoyable learning environment.

The lectures were super enjoyable. You can do well without them but the class is much easier if you go. The tests are straightforward with the material and the final project is fun and can be very interesting if you put effort into it. Overall a fantastic class and professor that I would take again!

Super great class, I am so glad I was able to take it. He is extremely knowledgeable and explores a lot of different aspects of Greek mythology, and ties it to modern media as well. You really don't need to attend lectures to do well in the class, but they are very interesting if you want to know about the class material. Highly recommend!

Professor Clary was extremely kind and always made class very fun to come to. He was always understanding if I had extenuating circumstances that kept me from coming to class, and prioritized our learning of the material above our actual grade, offering much extra credit during the semester. I would absolutely recommend him to anyone.

To do well in the course, you do not need to attend every lecture, but I highly recommend it because his lectures were incredibly interesting. I had a lot of Greek Mythology knowledge before coming to class, but I learned so much more than I expected. The exams are manageable. If you watch and take notes at the review sessions, you'll do fine.

Professor Clary is a really awesome professor and hes very passionate about what he teaches. He loves connecting aspects of Greek to linguistics which is very cool! Definitely would recommend taking his classes.

He gives very engaging lectures. He values student input highly. He knows his field well, but is always willing to look at things another way. I highly recommend this class, it's one of the best classes I've taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took this class for a distribution requirement and I absolutely loved it. Prof Clary was interested and provided interactive polls throughout lecture to keep us engaged. Biweekly reading, weekly quizzes, two exams (both are partially group work), and a semester project. Reading drags a bit but Clary goes over it well in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Todd is great. He REALLY loves ancient languages and wants his students to have as much fun with them as he does. Going to class is an absolute must. You can't avoid participating, but if you flounder while translating something, he will help you in a very non-judgmental way. Hopefully you enjoy bad jokes and proto into-european tangents :)

Clary is a super chill professor and teaches several languages in Classics. He is very knowledgeable, and his light-hearted demeanor (can't forget the jokes and ancient Greek stories) makes learning a tough language a little more palatable.
Fun Class, Clary obviously enjoys teaching languages. lots of dumb jokes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Cindy was a great professor, one of the best so far since being here at Cornell! She is willing to work with students if they have any issues, etc. Lectures can be engaging and brain breaks are the best! The TAs for the class were also extremely helpful and understanding. GO TO OFFICE HOURS! Cindy and the TAs are both amazing when you need help.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Cindy is a very kind person and a great professor! Its clear that she cares about us, and she structures the course/discussion sections in a way that gives students nonstop preparation for exams. Exams were not too bad after reviewing HW and section material, and there was extra credit on most of them. Only downside is lectures weren't recorded.

Cindy is a fantastic lecturer who has the ability to take something traditionally boring (ie stats) and make it interesting and exciting. She is compassionate and will regrade exams if a grading mistake was made. She gives you all the tools to be successful. Great professor!

She is very passionate about what she teaches and genuinely wants you to succeed. Exams are straight forward and match the practice tests in rigour. Course content is so boring but van Es tries to keep lecture engaging. TAs for the class are awesome

Professor Van Es is like that one grandma who gives you cookies if you get 50 algebra problems right. Tough class if it's your first time with stats, but she's such a nice professor it's hard to complain.

If you've taken stats before this is a breeze. Easy to understand if you haven't with many examples and working through problems in class compared to ILR stats teachers who don't give you any. Very nice, cares about the subject.

Cindy creates and conducts lectures that are very informative and interesting, especially given the boring nature of statistics. Prelims are the correct amount of difficult, but if you study, you'll be alright. In my opinion, she is one of the best here at Cornell.

The class just feels like high school, in a way that most of the homework is like busy work that consumes my time and the lectures could be condensed down into a 5-minute summary that could be fit on a page of paper. If you want a more interesting course I recommend looking for something else. Otherwise, an easy A if you just do the work.

Cindy is a great professor. Has a very good team of TA's that are ready to support you during your discussion section and outside of it.  Participation does matter. All of the material is covered during the lectures, but you always have the TA of your section and they go through the material during the sections.

Really great lecturer! Class content itself can be kinda tricky but she and her TA's are always available during OHs to help. Homeworks can take hours to do so start them early, and also bank on the extra credit opportunities she has! Overall explains concepts really well and does examples in class to help reinforce topics.
I straight up didn't learn stats the way I wanted to dawg

Like many others have stated, fronts as being a nice and caring person when in reality is harsh and disregards students. For example, when the final was moved online, she stated that there would be no partial credit given. One arithmetic error would cause 15 points to be taken off. She also intentionally gave out the wrong grade and acts snobbish
Interesting lecturer, exams are tougher than you think they will be. She has a good staff if you need help with homework. Demands student respect (But I don't think that's a bad thing!)

This class was a rollercoaster. The beginning was great, but it just got more and more painful. Cindy is an engaging lecturer in a boring stats class. But there was unclarity during COVID, unfair grading/regrades, threatening students during class, etc. Go to office hours for HWs. Prelim 2 is a lot harder than Prelim 1. The final is brutal.
Professor makes stats harder than it is

Never took a stats class in high school before and this was easily my most challenging class. Didn't think the content was tooo hard but she likes to make content harder than it is. Don't be fooled by her bright demeanor, she secretly couldn't give a sh*t about you + threatens to use her influence against you if you get on her sh*t list. good luck
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: No bueno!

Cindy is the worst professor I've had at Cornell. She is incredibly unaccommodating and inconsiderate. She goes out of her way to kick students when they're already down and I would absolutely avoid taking any of her classes at all costs.

is extremely rude to students, especially during covid. expects us to show our hands/face on zoom during exams, which is literally impossible given that we have to type our answers into canvas, and has security in place for those that click away from canvas but literally requires us to be on zoom so if we click the zoom tab we'll be in trouble
tough grader and does not care if you pass or fail. not terribly hard if you listen to TAs but don't expect to learn anything from her or get sympathy

extremely unclear. honestly the TAs are the only plus about this class. lecture is really boring and she complains about students falling asleep or being inconsiderate, but she goes out of her way to make exams difficult, especially with everything that has happened fall semester

Pretended to be nice but showed a clear disregard for students. Gave pop participation quizzes right before break even though some people had to leave early. During code red, she was forced to move the final online but gave no clear instructions on format. Moreover, she stated that partial credit might not be offered on the online final.
the worst professor i've ever had

Fronts as being considerate but doesn't care about her students. with covid rocketing and cornell shutting down, she is extremely unaccommodating despite most other professors making exams optional/cancelling them. instead she is giving us an online exam with limited partial credit, and has provided little to no information or support

Was extremely unhelpful during Fall 2021 semester. With everything going on, Cindy showed disregard at the concern of her students. I understand that AEM2100 is a large class, but with omicron on campus, she did little to nothing to accommodate. Instead, she implemented a draconian zoom exam many other classes showed understanding with a take home.
Cindy wasn't the best and she kept getting distracted in lecture. I feel learnt everything from the assigned section and couldn't focus in class

Cindy takes all class to mess around telling stories of her life and her children, while not teaching the class. She repeatedly makes mistakes during lectures and has to get help from students and TAs to continue. Overall, it wasn't worth going to class, except she would have random participation items that were worth way too much of our grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Awesome lecturer. Tests are easy if you are willing to do the required work.

Professor van Es is an excellent lecturer for intro stats. Her class is clearly organized and follows a note packet she has compiled. The discussion sections for the class are mandatory and help supplement and reinforce the material learned in class. While exams can be challenging, ample preparation can help you excel in this class.
Good lecturer, very energetic, and fair grader. Her class is a little tough, but you will be fine if you did well in the intro stats class .

She was a great a helpful professor. Lectures aren't mandatory and you can still perform well in the class without attending lectures. The discussions were the most useful part of the class so take those seriously.

Cindy is a dynamic lecturer and a great person. She cares about her students doing well and will ensure everyone has the opportunity to succeed. Sections are super helpful. Cindy made stats enjoyable and if you study, you are guaranteed to get A's.

Cindy's class was a great introduction to the world of statistics and came into every lecture full of energy! If you put in the effort (going to office hours, properly doing the HW) you will definitely end up with a good grade. Don't bother purchasing the textbook, just go take pictures of the HW questions from the library or the OH room.

Cindy is one of the kindest and silliest professors I've had. She comes in with a great attitude every day and does not let anything get in her way of having a good day. Some of the material is hard to grasp, but there are so many resources available to you so that you can understand and succeed. Also she is good about giving points back on exams!

The sections, homework and lectures all reinforced concepts that we needed to know, and the exams were very fair and based on these assignments. Participation is recommended because a % of your grade is derived from your participation in random in-class activities. The sections are helpful, but the lectures are made extremely amusing by Cindy.

Go to lecture because 1) it's easy to understand and 2) she gives out random participation points. Also go to section because what you don't understand in lecture, you will get in section and it's free points. Also buy the course packet because it's all the notes you'll need.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great class! Would recommend taking it for anyone interested in statistics.

Probably the goofiest, nicest, & most likable professor I've had. It's difficult to learn the material as she teaches it, but the course is arranged so that you're able to master it before the exams. Lectures got a bit monotonous near the end of the semester, but her personality is always refreshing. Her course packet is insanely helpful. AWESOME!!

You will have weekly sections and discussions in this class. My TA and section saved my grade. I found her lectures hard to follow but I also normally struggle in large lectures. She randomly takes attendance so if you happen to miss a day she takes attendance it really sucks. There is almost always office hours since there are so many TAs.

Wonderful professor! She's funny and goofy but that livened things up in class. Her "brain breaks" in the middle of lectures were also a lot of fun. I didn't do great on the first prelim (nobody really did) but if you go to her office hours (or the TAs) you'll do just fine. They're all so helpful and they really want you to succeed.
Awesome! Awesome! Awesome!
SO great!! I dont even like stat that much but she's awesome

Loved her class. Didn't do so well on her first prelim, but I would recommend going to office hours and her office hours and you should be set for the course. Not hard material, she is very good about explaining it all, and if you check your homeworks in office hours, I don't know why it's not possible to get an A+.

I believe she is the best professor at Cornell! She is the rare combination of interested in her students, kind, intelligent, and great at communicating concepts. I wasn't very interested in taking statistics but because of Professor Van Es, it quickly became my favorite course. If you study and do homework you will get a good grade. Take it!

I couldn't have taken stats with any other prof. I am NOT a math person but her personality, explanation, and section layouts really help. It's a lot of work, but not more than any other 4 credit class. The homeworks are long but it really makes sure you understand, since there's a lot of material to be covered. Textbook's not necessary but helpful

Cindy is an amazing person and teacher. She uses humor and her lively personality in order to keep students' attention in lectures of otherwise dry stuff. All of the class material is in the lecture packet, and the book is literally only used for a few homework problems. The class isn't a breeze but one could get a good grade with some effort.

Cindy is a great stats instructor, but she needs serious help choosing her TAs. As other students already wrote, TAs did not know much and were even rude at times. They seemed to have been chosen randomly since their stats knowledge was shockingly deficient.

she's a hard teacher and the class is massive. her TAs were bad and there were definite favorites in the class. they didn't explain anything/weren't helpful at all. i really wish i had take ilr stats in hindsight. only plus was that i managed to sell my textbook for a decent amount $

Cindy is the best professor I have ever had at Cornell thus far! Lecture is so much fun and you learn quality material! If you hold up your end by attending lecture, paying attention and doing the hw and section work, she will help you get an A!

Cindy rules!  She is an excellent profesora, probably one of the best I've had at Cornell thus far.  Although she does a great job and makes the material approachable and easy to understand, the prelims are not easy and you have to study a lot to do well.

The textbook is such a waste of money. She gives you a 200 page course packet, and you very rarely use the textbook. Hilarious lecturer (in stats? yeah!), hot undergrad TAs, homeworks and sections were very helpful. Overall a well-organized and effective class.
Cool prof
Nice prof. Cracks me up sometimes.  Class stinks though. It's stats how fun can you make it?
Cindy is the best professor at Cornell hands down.

Prof. Van Es has been one of my best professors at Cornell. Her class really isn't harder than the other Stat classes if you keep up the work - which is very manageable. She truly wants you to succeed, and there are so many opportunities to get help. Could not have asked for a better Stat teacher.

Good professor although she seriously needs to learn how to create better support systems for students. Throughout the semester, my TA didn't seem to understand the material and could barely explain it. Going to office hours was useless.
Cindy is AWESOME!!!
I love Van Es! I had zero interest in Stat walking into this class but she makes things easy to understand even if the material itself isn't super easy. I thought the class was fair and fun.
Absolutely LOVE Van Es!!! Reminds me of Pheobe from friends!! Intro to stats was the most well run course at cornell. I felt like I learned alot!
Such a funny lady. Totally in her own stat world. The prelims were reasonably challenging but not impossible. Felt like I learned a lot.

Great professor!!  Great class!  Van Es does an excellent job organizing and teaching the material.  All concepts are reinforced well in section.  This course may be difficult if you are not profficient in math.  But if you have to take a stats class, this is a great choice!

Even though the class was easy, I still felt like I learned a good deal--not like I was wasting my time.  The professor is a bit of a nut and she actually makes stats interesting. Attendance to lectures is not mandatory, but highly recommended since the textbook is super dry and the sections are taught by undergraduate TAs not grads.

A very lively professor and sometimes gets a bit too excited, but I definitely enjoyed going to every lecture.  Material itself was somewhat easy, even though I never took a statistics course in my life.  I was able to get a good grade without being a super-intelligent person. haha
Very good teacher.  Lively, makes class fun.  But workload is not that easy.  Homeworks take time and exams can be difficult.  The project can also take time.  Still worth it in the end.
No Comments

She makes the lectures as interesting as anyone ever could. The homeworks get too numerous towards the end of the semester. The homeworks are misleading because the exam problems are so much harder. Don't take this one looking for an easy class. The exams will bury you even if you understand everything. Didn't get as much out of this as I expected.

Good class.  She makes the lectures interesting and the materials very clear.  But don't expect the hw to be very easy in term of workload.  A MUST for students interested in a career of consulting.  Great Lecturer.  Probably one of the best in AEM.
The presentation is clear.  The lecture is not borng.  Prelims are reasonabl.e    It's a good class to take.
No Comments

Van Es is a great lecturer, she has boundless energy and LOVES to teach. She actually made stats interesting, which would normally be somehwat boring. I was able to pay attention for the entire lecture. Her TAs are great as well. Sometimes she says things that make you think "O can't believe she just said that!" She's amusing.

Prof. Van Es is an all-round fantastic teacher. Her class was easy because she was so clear and made the information so accesible. She is also very nice and energetic, and has great TAs. If you need to take stats, I would strongly recommend her course.

Pretty easy class - class mean on the exams was upper 80s. Great, energetic professor who tries to keep a very boring subject semi-interesting. If you go to classes and sections and do the homework, shouldn't be too hard to get an A. Much easier than high school AP Stats.

very nice but completely cracked out.  material is hard to follow especially because of her screechy voice. prelims are really difficult. i don't dislike HER i just really dislike the course. its hard to learn stats in a huge lecture hall with 300 other people.
No Comments
Tough class but she makes the material easy to understand. Great professor!!! She loves what she does and her always amazing mood makes class fly by. A+ teacher. take a class with her if you can.

A great teacher and really energetic.  She makes Stats enjoyable.  I don't know how anyone would be able to fall asleep in her class when she's up there saying: "YAY, IT'S A BOXPLOT!!!!"  Her prelims were kinda challenging, but she was fair.
its hard to make stats interesting and fun -- she does it
Very good teacher, makes stats fun
Great prof!  Makes stats interesting.  Totally devoted to teaching.  very funny.
No Comments
she is hilarious... can actually  make the material interesting!
Good professor. A total soccer mom who is sweet to her students until prelim time. She gives pretty challenging tests.
Nice lady, makes stats somewhat interesting & gives fair tests
No Comments
A really good teacher
Probably the most helpful professor I've had in 6 semesters here.  She really cares about her students, which is rare in these parts.
No Comments
No Comments
She actually made stats funny!
Not engaging at all but a rite of passage for E&S majors

rambled and lectures didn't really make sense, but it was an incredibly easy class. they almost never take attendance, but sometimes they'll take one random example used in lecture that wasn't on the slides and make a whole test question out of it.

He hates modern technology and progressive ideology, like a primitive ancestor resenting the first human who began to walk upright. Given that he was a Cornell undergrad fifty years ago, it makes me wonder how rigid the campus culture once was.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class was so pointless. While some topics were interesting, Kraft does not have the ability to get his points across, which means that on the tests (which change in their format every other week, it felt like), everything you knew was solely based on readings or what you could manage to pick up from lectures (which no one showed up to).

Cliff Kraft gives the most incomprehensible and pointless lectures ever. You'd think a topic we spent 3 classes discussing would be on the prelim, right? Nope! The exam questions are often unfair and are based around concepts or vocab terms that were not extensively covered. The class is pretty easy but its such a rage bait.

Cliff Kraft Survival Guide: Try to find and appreciate his passion. His lectures are directionless but have purpose/connection in his head. You won't fully understand or appreciate why he's exploring a certain topic, and you can count on a tiny vocab word being the whole of an exam question.

Pretty impassioned and disorganized lectures, don't bother going. Will post the slides but there is very little text on them. However, everything can be gathered by doing the readings. The course is super easy, and I got an A+ even though I skipped every lecture after the first prelim.

He's a funny lecturer who goes on tangents sometimes. He cares about the state of the world + it's reflected in lecture (which people don't like despite it being an inherently political major?) + sometimes he crashes out which is a bit much. The lesson can get a little lost in all the blabbing. Exams + assignments are easy if U go to lectures.
Really boring lectures, tests on random topics not discussed in depth. Spends a lot of lecture complaining about technology. Overall pretty easy class, but boring.

When I saw I had to take this course for my major, I looked at rate my professor and saw his low score..."It can't be that bad, right?" I said to myself... boy was I wrong... Never have I ever met a man who rambles on and on about material that HAS NEVER BEEN ON THE EXAM. his co lecturer ginger gives us actual information thats on the prelim.
Understanding E&S (Egotism & Sermons)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This is a requirement for my major, and possibly one of the worst classes ever. If not required RUN! Kraft would always be angry during his lectures and they were not only boring but also not very informative at all. Also your grade truly depends on your TA I had Jeanne and she was such a strict grader, even nitpicking my word choice???
Too bad it's required for the major. Run if you can!

Professor Kraft rants constantly, is insanely passive aggressive, and pretty much actively discourages participation. It was hysterical. He'd get mad at the blank faces staring at him and shout about all of us being "real human beings" and then when someone would attempt to answer one of his questions he'd find a way for them to be wrong.

If you want a class where a majority of the sparsely attended lecture time is dedicated to complaints about a lack of attendance (which is not mandatory) and students using computers (which is not prohibited) where your final grade is determined by 5 essays with the most nebulous "prompts" you have ever read, NTRES 1101 is the course for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Horribly boring and unnecessary lectures that had nothing to do with the essay assignments the course was graded on. Professor Kraft spent more time complaining about attendance and phones and mocking our reasons for studying sustainability than he spent teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Imagine attending class to watch him rating about attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Do not take this class if you do not have to. The lectures were very boring and did not make much sense.

Worst class I've taken at Cornell. Easy to fulfill the arts bio requirement, although I doubt they will continue to allow it to in the future. 30% of your grade is weekly reflection, random in-class polls, and discussion section—these should be split up. 

Lectures are boring and useless. Prof. just rants the entire time and you learn absolutely 0.

His lectures did not provide any information about the topic we were supposed to be learning. Somehow, they always felt like a discussion about how he believes normal people's reactions to the changing environment are stupid. A clear bias was always present, and a lot of time was wasted on useless conversations about technology and attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: He harms the reputation of Cornell and the E&S major since half of the class are new students. This course fails to reflect the standards of an Ivy League education.

Lectures consisted of: 1) ranting about attendance to the students who did, in fact, attend class, 2) ranting about how technology is terrible and HUMAN INTERACTION IS ALL THAT WE HAVE LEFT, 3) pulling up some sustainability add and going "Oh wow!" and then changing topics, 4) giving us a tour of his camera roll instead of teaching us information.

The most boring professor I have had yet. If you can avoid this class, avoid it. PERIOD. genuinely one of the most useless lectures I have been to, yet you have to go because of Poll Everywhere. Do not take this course and pray he is not your main lecturer.
DO NOT take this class unless it's required. You won't learn anything in the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Attendance is now mandatory and lectures are boring, dull, and kinda pointless unless you want to listen to Prof Kraft rant for 55 min at 9am. There was a paper each week which aren't hard to write, but require SO MUCH READING. On numerous assignments there were over 4 readings. Weekly discussions are mandatory and use group work for activities.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Lectures are hard to pay attention. Grading is harsh but depends on TA. If you quote readings and use some thought, you can usually get an A. I got roughly a 96 but most my peers struggled. You are assigned pretty much weekly papers, sometimes with only 1-2 days of notice. An annoying class but gets better as semester progresses.

He really hates robots and emphasizes that in every lecture. Don't know how it relates to understanding 
 environment and sustainability.

Although this class is pretty boring and mostly pointless, cliff Kraft is a pretty decent dude if you talk to him one on one. He gets pretty aimlessly angry during lectures but makes more sense if you track him down to talk. Overall an interesting guy.

I took NTRES 1101 in the fall of 2022, and honestly, I did not enjoy this class. The lectures were inconsistent and only occasionally worthwhile (attendance is not mandatory though) and the frequent papers were nebulous and I overall rarely learned much. I think that's more the problem of the class than with Cliff Kraft, though, he was overall ok.
4 pages of writing almost weekly. Graded randomly. Lectures are not engaging. Talk to TAs to brainstorming ideas for writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Kevin is too smart to teach.
Speaks in riddles.

I aced Clermont's class but the one thing I'll note is that his class is very lecture focused. Random iClicker questions, previous practice problems, and off-the-cuff lecture tangents morph into exam questions so you sort of need to write down everything he says. Being old school he's also purposefully opaque. And the textbook? LMAO.

Clermont is a brilliant scholar but unable to make the material understandable for his students.  Lectures go off on irrelevant tangents, leaving less time for important material.  The exam was absolutely ridiculous and does not measure how well the students learned the semester's material.  Sorry Cornell 1Ls, you're stuck with him one semester.

The best professor I've had so far. Prepare for class and think about the material and you will get a lot out of this. So far he is the only teacher to write multiple choice questions that don't have mistakes in them that make the answers ambiguous. People see issues and know the material will do well in this class, and people who don't won't.

1 of the 2 finest professors at Cornell back in 82.  His analysis of the overlap of attorney client privilege, work product and mental impressions should be mandatory learning for all trial judges, who I find almost uniformly misunderstand the principles.
Great Prof. After you have done your work, he would lift you to a whole new level. The exam was not easy, but reasonable nonetheless.

Clermont is tough because he wants you to take the material seriously. He's "extremely helpful" only for those people that have actually struggled with answering their own questions before coming to him. He does not suffer fools lightly. If you've given your best effort, he'll give you some direction - but no free answers.
Difficult to understand, moody, bitter, hide-the-ball exam.

Teaches to the top 10% of the class, and the rest of his students are left scratching their heads. Prides himself on the fact that he gives out incredibly difficult finals.  Unfortunately, every 1L can expect to have him.

Clermont makes it near impossible to learn civil procedure, one of the hardest first year classes.  He doesn't realize his students haven't been studying it for 50 years like he has.  But too bad.  All 1Ls have to take him.

A great professor - engaging and dedicated.  For those of you there now, this man never missed a single class while going through a year of intensive chemo.  Yeah, he loves to play jedi mind tricks on students -- if you want to be spoon fed the material, get out of his classroom.

Brilliant; great fun; hard.  He does a great job explaining the second half of CivPro.  He knows what he is talking about (he did write the book, after all.  I didn't care for CivPro 1st semester, but Clermont is able to both explain the subject, and make it come alive. Wait for his Pennoyer discussion. it's hilarious and tragic at the same time.
A really fun professor but don't feel bad if you walk out of class and feel like a complete moron... In some ways, he makes the class harder than it needs to be.
Very smart, very funny.  However, he sometimes forgets that not everyone understands Civil Procedure as well as he does.  You end up taking a lot of notes in that class.
I thought I understood everything until I took the exam.  Very impressive to listen to, and he knows it.

probably the smartest professor in the law school.  but it isnt worth a damn if you are set up for failure.  what i mean is, this prof is known for making a purposefully hard multiple choice final for which the average is 30%.  Civ pro is hard as it is without some equisite scholar traping you.
Good professor, but I never understood a dam thing he said.  Has a lot to do with subject though.  Probably the smartest prof in the law school, and that is saying a lot.
Powerful intellect and classroom presence.  One of the law school's finest.

The grade for this class is primarily based on attendance. Each class, you have to submit printed copies of either three poems or three pages of prose. There is no feedback on these submissions unless you bring them to workshop classes. Prof. was often very serious during class, which made her feel unapproachable and discouraged participation.

Lyrae is one of the most incredible teachers, and inspiring people I have ever met. I came into her class hating poetry and left after every class understanding something knew about poetry, literature, and life. She cares about her students, engages the class and facilitates great discussions. Take her class. She's amazing.

Lyrae is art incarnate. She's inspirational and brings out the artist in everyone. If you don't have semi-thick skin expect some exfoliation, especially if you have little exposure to creative writing. But if you stick through it I promise she'll make you a better writer and a better human. I love her  and you'll love her. Go for it.

Lyrae is a walking inspiration. I took Advanced Poetry with her, and I can honestly say that she completely changed my perspective on writing, and transformed me from a dabbler to a poet. She has given me confidence. She is also sassy and hilarious. Take advantage of this opportunity to take a class with such an amazing human being.

S:106. Avoid if possible. More than half of the initial class dropped w/in the first week. Harsh and biased grader. Quite mean when things don't go her way. Has stated that she does not like the KIfW. Assigns "group essays". Course books are perverse &/or boring. Deceptively changed the course title. Does not use internet. Great poet, bad teacher.

If you're looking for an easy stats class to fill your distribution reqs look no further. Yes it's not very interesting or exciting but I don't really think that's his fault. He is an incredibly flexible professor, records all lectures. Attendance is never mandatory I probably only went to about half of them and have an A. And you will learn stats!

This class put me to sleep. Prof was very nice, but the content was boring and lectures were long, he spoke quietly, and sometimes his writing was impossible to read. He puts recordings of the lectures in canvas, which is super nice. Assignments are quite long, and there are weekly quizzes. Grading took a very long time. I did learn stats though.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is my favorite, super understanding guy. I love him. The course itself is digestible even if you have no knowledge in statistics. He really loves the subject and you can tell. The class is not curved at all but there are a lot of assignments and easy points, so it's not hard to do well. You get cheat sheets on the exam and they're fair exams.

Class can be quite boring so its hard to pay attention. He posts recordings and theres a bunch of HW's and open-notes quizzes so you can do well even if you have trouble on the tests (which are super conceptual).
Really inspirational

The professor teaches the content with enthusiasm, which makes the class more engaging. Getting cheat sheets is a huge plus for exams + finals, and with enough time and effort, all content is understandable, just a bit time-consuming.

He would definitely be better at lecturing to higher-level students, but the actual content is very understandable and it is very easy to succeed in this class. You get to have cheat sheet(s) on every exam and there are a lot of different components that go into your final grade. It can sometimes be time consuming but is pretty straightforward.

Pretty nice and accommodating teacher. Attendance is not mandatory so I didn't really go to lecture but reviewed recordings and crammed before tests. Allows cheatsheets for exams which was helpful. Overall material was digestible

Don't do all the readings. The lectures are adequate enough to understand the material. Dr. Cleland does a great job explaining concepts and is open to questions. Use the practice questions at the end of the textbook to study. Do the assignments and quizzes in regular weekly study groups to make them more fun.

Overall, he was generally accommodating, however this semester after finals he changed the grading percentages, and I went from getting an A+ to an A. This is extremely unfair, and he even implied that he did this to lower peoples grades. No professor of mine has completely changed the grading last minute to screw over their students so beware.

Prof. Cleland is an awesome and kindhearted professor, but he can be nit-picky about the grading. Go to OH and review your homework questions with a TA before you submit; otherwise, you can miss points even if you understood the question. Go to lecture and take detailed notes, then transcribe those onto your exam cheat sheet. You'll get an A.

Tons of homework, esp. if you do the 4-credit option. Thom (as he signs his emails) is an interesting guy teaching a *very* dry subject. Intro stats can be memorized, which makes it pretty boring. I don't go to lecture and I just read the slides so I'm not a great judge of his teaching abilities. Very easy class, however, as he grades v reasonably.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Easy class if you put in the effort to read the textbooks. Prelims are open-note, but you don't really even need the notes: the information isn't that hard. Lectures are kinda a doozy but he's a nice guy with some funny moments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The worst professor in the CS apartment. Never knew I could dislike a professor this much
bad. Not recommended

Honestly kind of mediocre. She seems nice, and she brings her dogs to class, but I dont think shes the best teacher, per se. Class is decent, moderate in difficulty (more bothersome than difficult, since there are lengthy projects that must be done in pairs as well as exams and written assignments and a pretty involved participation grade).

Prof Cardie is a leading NLP researcher, a very good instructor, and a caring person. I took the introduction to NLP class. The class itself was super interesting and the staff does a very good job at breaking down a very complex and ever changing subfield of CS. A must take!
So disorganized, unclear lectures

Professor Cardie herself is accessible and tries to be helpful. However, the rest of the course stuff was disorganized and it felt like Professor Cardie was out-of-loop regarding her own class, especially in terms of the assignments. Very interesting class but beware the projects, very open-ended, unclear and time consuming.

This class was very interesting, and the programming assignments, while long, were excellent. Professor Cardie was frequently quite unclear with concepts, and Piazza was very seldom used by the instructors, so it would take a long time to get what was quite often a less-than-helpful response. Assignments were graded easily, but the final was tough.

Lectures can be a little dry (and she sometimes seems a bit nervous?) but Prof Cardie is super nice and helpful in person. Programming projects are interesting and not too hard. Needs to hire better or more TAs, though - I've taken both IR and NLP with her and both times the TA team was sub-par wrt to responsiveness and knowing what's going on.

Information Retrieval is an interesting class. Claire is a pretty good lecturer, and bring her dog to class often.  The one major flaw for this course was the grading structure, which as fairly ambiguous. This year 60% of the grade came from 3 problem sets, which were not easy.  The pacing of the course is good, and Claire is willing to help you.

This field is very interesting and the instructor knows her stuff, so thats good. Even though there are no exams I think I learnt and understood/remember more concepts than in other subjects- because the assignments were designed very nicely. They were time-taking but interesting.
Machine Learning, Spring 2000.  Senior year.  Very difficult class, but I was interested in the material, so that helped.  She was quite accessible as far as office hours, e-mail, etc.
No Comments
She made something cool (AI) really really boring.

She gives such clear and nice lectures. The leture slides are very organized and well-written. She also gives very good homework--chanllenging enough not make you feel bored, but not too much to drive you crazy.. very nice! She is also a very helpful and understanding person.
Great teacher, but doesn't like it when you yawn. He has a pleasant side and a dark side. Proceed with caution especially if you have to yawn during a lecture
Great interesting Prof
This guy is a literal Nazi who thinks Hitler was great and the Holocaust was mostly made up. Puts his Nazi attitudes and racist comments in his class repeatedly.
David seems to know at least a little of chemistry, but spends most of the class arguing that the Holocaust was the fault of America and the Soviet Union.
He was professional and funny making difficult scientific analogies to simple life lessons. It made material more understandable.
Amazing Prof. Most honest and knowledgeable Prof or person I've ever known. If your willing to learn and have an open mind, no one will teach you more. Wish he was my Prof for every class.

The class itself isn't bad, but mostly depends on your TA. I hope I never have to take a class taught by Dave again though - offensive guy but tries to be funny. Makes students uncomfortable (check his twitter). Lectures are a mess and he goes off on tangents constantly. Not sure I learned a single thing from him. Bad at technology & no canvas.
He's a king and a bright man all around. keep on rockin Dr. C!
A complete nutjob. Check out his twitter feed. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Just dont like him or the class

Hilarious guy and the most awesome stories you'll ever hear in your entire life. Wish he spent time in class clarifying the material better than just telling stories. Exams are tough, but fair. Overall good professor.
Fun class.  Dave is hilarious and very opinionated.  Tests are tough as hell but don't count for anything.
Best lab course. Looked forward to lectures and labs. Lectures, especially. I was actually sad when he started cancelling lectures second half of the semester.
This was the first lab I ever looked forward to coming to. The work is interesting and Dave is a great lecturer, on topic or not.
Dave is so inappropriate and hilarious!  He is so hott and the class is awesome.  I'll really miss going to lecture!
No Comments
Dave is so funny!  He tells the best stories and the labs are really fun too.  Everyone should take this class.
Insightful class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof Cohn is the best! Always accessible outside of class. Class covers variety of topics and each paper has multiple options so there's something for everyone. Some readings get dull but that's moreso the state of the industry than the class itself. Go to class and office hours and ASK QUESTIONS! She'll even learn your name
Professor Cohn was wonderful, very easy to contact and was super flexible with deadlines. I loved her class so much. Highly reccommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Elisha is hands down the best prof I've had the pleasure of learning from at Cornell-- I even asked her to be my major advisor, and nominated her for a teaching award (literally wrote 3 full pages about how wonderful she is). She genuinely cares about her students and wants everyone's input. She values student readings as much as her own!

Pros: Super approachable and knowledgeable professor who makes an effort to keep class interesting and gives specific feedback, not difficult to get a good grade if you put even a little effort into essays and talking in class Cons: A LOT of reading, class participation is important to your grade  Overall, a good class that did improve my writing!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Pros: Lectures were amazing and I was always engaged. Teacher is very nice and enthusiastic about her work. Essays are easy as long as you come to class and take notes on her ideas.

Very clear, engaging and nice. Class was lively: somehow everyone used to contribute(unlike my other FWS where like 2 people ever talk). My writing improved a lot! She points out mistakes exactly so you can work on it. Don't take the class if you aren't at least mildly interested in British Lit, though(but that goes without saying,duh).

I took this class freshman year as FWS, and I immediately dropped it. The time I was in it we spent in a circle just noting random facts about the book at hand and didn't get anywhere at all, plus it was ridiculously boring with no variance in activities whatsoever. Felt like I was back in 9th grade lit. Like the topic; don't like the professor.
Class if extremely interesting and Elisha is very engaging in class. Not that hard of a grader, engaging lecturer.
Very interesting lecturer and class. Exams tended to be specific, but graded fairly. Lab portion is a lot of work with making the collection
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
very kind and funny, flexible about deadlines, and reasonable grading.

That said, this class is extremely hard if you don't already have a very strong understanding of insect bio it will take up a lot of time to memorize and learn everything.

I love this guy, but I don't love the way he teaches. Super cool guy, but his lectures are unclear and he includes material that is neither in the textbook nor lectures in his prelim. I thought BIOG 1440 was easy, but he was by far the hardest out of the four professors. Still love him though.

He's interesting and engaging, but his slides are mostly pics so you need to pay good attention. A lot of times he talks about unrelated things. The class is moderately difficult. There's videos, readings, and mandatory quizzes twice a week, 4 prelims, optional final, and attendance is not mandatory. Prelims are tricky. Don't take if not required.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: One of my favorite lecturers from this class.

Lecture notes are unclear and difficult to understand. Supplemental material don't pertain to lecture. Lecture topics random and disorganized. Lectures are repetitive and boring. Tests are on hyper-specific topics sometimes missing from lectures entirely. no curve

His lectures are a bit boring and each of his slides are just crammed with info. Pretty friendly guy tho. He makes an effort to teach but sometimes he explains concepts in a way that is more confusing than it should be. I also feel like the content on the exams are deeper than what he discusses in lecture.

He didn't get everyone falling asleep in class, but that DOESN'T MEAN he was a good professor. Lecture content was VERY different from test material, and the class WAS NOT curved. The average was supposed to be a C, but he widened the bins so everyone got a B-. Then the very last day of grading, he changed half the grades due to math error. RUN.

Dr Gilbert is by far the funniest and coolest lecturer of 1780. He teaches Animal evolutionary history and is hilarious and one of the few professors for the class that is actually engaging. Very down to earth, very meme worthy. Favorite professor of the semester by far, if only for the pure sass and sarcasm emanating from this man.
The insect collection is tough, but that's mandatory for the course and good planning will make it work. Cole is hilarious and caring.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This professor is boring and disorganized. I have not gotten lower than an "A" until this 1440 Biology class. If you think looking at slides all course and cracking silly jokes is fun great. Exams had no continuity with lectures! Should have gotten out of his course. Then half the final grades posted were wrong and the final grades reposted - WOW!

Cole is a great lecturer and cracks a lot of dumb jokes. Definitely a steep learning curve in the lab and obviously geared towards people with some background knowledge already. Be prepared to spend a lot of time on the insect collection.

The fun does not balance out the work. The first half of the semester is unreasonably hard. Lecture is interesting even though it is early in the morning. Lab and the practicals are harder than class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Terrible Class. Will never take again. Must have entire bug collection in addition to lab tests AND prelims in class. Tons of work. No reward.

He is definitely a nice guy, but I don't see how the lab and lecture correlate. In lab, you get thrown right in without any explanation. Lectures, he talks about basic, cool things, but you have to know a lot of details which he doesn't make you aware of. This should be an intro course, but I feel like I should have had a lot of prior knowledge.
Cole is an amazing lecturer and incredibly funny. He's super helpful and really does his best to make the class as informative and fun as possible.
So much better than Booker! And he's funny. He's very clear and keeps students engaged. Great professor!

Prof. Gilbert was great! He tried to be as interesting as you can with this material. His lectures were clear and simple, and he showed genuine interest in our understanding the subject and being prepared for the exams. Oh, and sometimes he'd randomly run around to make a point. Cool guy!

Cole is one of the best professors at Cornell that I've encountered. His lectures are interesting, and doesn't just lecture the reading; he goes above and beyond the reading. He is an incredibly nice guy, and extremely knowledgeable about entomology. I loved this course with him. A+

Hilarious.  The powerpoint slides he makes are very entertaining.  His material in 1780 can be hard because it's all memorization but he gives lots of interesting examples.  Possibly my favorite of the five 1780 lecturers.

Cole Gilbert is awesome.  Coming from an engineering and pre-med background, its really refreshing to have a teacher that is enthralled with what he teaches and can talk to students in a relaxed atmosphere.  As for the class, study his lectures and ask questions during lab and you'll do fine.  I just wish he'd teach more classes!
It was clear that he wanted us to do well, but he was not effective at teaching and I found the tests to be unfair compared to the material taught.

Fun class, Professor Gilbert made what would have been rather dry and straight from the text much more interesting with his anecdotes and examples but did not get sidetracked by them - lecture focused on major concepts not detail.
Great, interesting professor.
No Comments
Okay class, not a great teacher. Make sure you stay on schedule with the readings.

Dr. Gilbert is really, REALLY good. One of the best lecturers I could wish for. I wish all teachers could be so amiable yet knowledgeable. There are some profs you can't hear bc they mumble- Dr. Gilbert will never subject you to that. Crystal clear! Makes Bio accessible!!!
nice guy, sort of interesting sometimes, class needs a lot of reading and lectures can get pretty boring

Dr. Gilbert is an amazing teacher. Unlike other profs, he genuinely wants you to succeed and isn't out to get you. Tests are fair, but be prepared to put in a lot of effort. Goes through ppts and lectures very quickly, but they're all online afterwards. He also has pre lecture questions to help with the reading. Overall, an amazing teacher.

Fun lecturer.  Goes through slides a little too fast, but posts powerpoints and audio recording of lectures online, so you can catch up later and study easily.  Tests aren't easy, but they won't contain that many inordinately difficult questions.
Kool dude. Go through the powerpoint and lecture audio before the exam and ur golden.

Dr. Gilbert is not a good professor...he flies through his powerpoints without taking a breath...it's impossible to catch hardly any of what he is saying...his tests are unbearably difficult b/c of the large amount of material he inadequately covers..if you want to pass his class, be prepared to put in lot of extra work teaching yourself everything

Cole Gilbert is one of the most helpful professors at Cornell just go to his office hours. Though he zips through lecture and it can be difficult to keep up at first, as long as you actually put some effort its managable. He has a sence of humor too and truly tries to make class entertaining. Great professor to have.
Though he zipps through his lecture he tries to keep it interesting and is extremely accessable and helpfull during his office hours
No Comments

His lectures were informative but boring, he chose some really random and irrelevant things to go in depth with. Otherwise really helpful though. Good use of powerpoints and the clicker questions were actually helpful. For prelims though, your best bet is to just memorize the book. It's a challenging class, but not impossible.

His teaching style doesn't make or break the class - he's just aite. Ideally, you could look at the ppt slides (& listen to audio if you want to) & skip class & do just fine, but you gotta go for the clicker q's. Study really hard, you know the rep of intro bio...
He's very enthusiatic and willing to help anybody
I liked how he taught the class with funny jokes and whatnot

Dynamic and exciting lectures. He sometimes goes into certain topics too deep, but that's fine. Prelims can be harder than you think so be prepared. I personally didn't like his prelims because some questions seemed irrelevant. Yet, overall, Prof.Gilbert is a great guy.
I like his lectures. The diagrams are great !!

Gilbert is AMAZING!!!  I absolutely love this class.  He's a really dynamic lecturer, and he knows his stuff.  I'm pretty sad that he won't be teaching 2nd semester intro bio.  The best way I've found to study for this class is to take my textbook and highlight/take notes in it as he lectures...he tends to follow it pretty closely.  He's great!

As an intro level bio class for majors, the class is meant to be difficult and lives up to its reputation. However Cole does a great job in teaching the class. By going to lecutres, keeping up on the readings, and studying difficult material extra the class in manageable. Cole does excellent lectures, has great powerpoints, and is so knowledgeable.
No Comments

Ent 212 was the best class I have ever taken!  Dr Gilbert teaches in a fun, involved manner; he takes a deep interest in each student's progress.  Classes are interesting, field trips are fun, and the lab-work actually holds purpose!!!!!!
It was alright. I didn't learn much. It's just that I lowkey was taking this ENGRI because it was easy.
Fantastic guy

One of the best profs ive had at Cornell. Was definitely my favorite class ive had this semester, and the content taught was super interesting. very reasonable grading, and he is also so nice and obviously cares about his students!! wish all of my professors were like him, take any class you can with him!!

This was by far one of my favorite classes that I have taken at Cornell. I took it my freshman year, spring 2022 and I learned so much from the class.
