Good guy. Made exams, assignments, and classes interesting. Would definitely reccomend.

Kozen is a good guy. He really cares about helping his students, from what I can tell. I've been to his office hours a few times and he's really friendly, and he knows how to teach. The class is really easy too, as it's not graded on a curve. I got a good grade and I learned a lot. I highly recommend cs 211 with Kozen.
pretty easy class, dont like the written tests

Kozen, unlike many professors, knows how to teach.  Presentation is clear and explains concepts very well.  Prelims are quite hard but most of your grade comes from the assignments, which are straightforward.  Friendly and understanding, likes to give extensions.

This class is a lot of work, but Kozen is a pretty good teacher.  Most of your grade comes from the projects rather than tests (I failed a prelim and did pretty well in the end).  The projects are interesting which makes them easier to do, but you still must figure out a lot on your own.
pretty easy class grade-wise. i got a 57 on a test (med. 67) and still got an A. It is a good amount of work tho. also, kozen dims the lights in lecture so its real easy to fall asleep.
No Comments

The band name is "The Burning Sensations" and that's just the kind of guy Dexter is. Really smart, really fun, and the kind of person you'd like to have tea with afterwards. Good luck with the subject matter, though. Hard as hell.

I heard him say "I'm doing my time in the trenches with the undergrads this term."The class was rather hard and he didn't seem to be much help.  He was in some band I forget the name of -- I never spent time outside class but he was in a band wi
very smart. theoretical/mathematical style
He's hot for a CS prof. Amazing crarity, and his book on Automata is the best there is. Keep it under my pillow every night.
great class.

Genuinely the GOAT of hardware accelerated ML. His lectures are so tuff and often go into the math derivations behind a specific method i.e. he proved the decent lemma from the top of his head AND he can write torch code in real time (wow). A very nice guy during OH too, willing to work through examples together for clarification which is awesome.
Genuinely enjoyed almost every lecture. Covered a good range of material, and the problem sets and programming assignments did a decent job of forcing you to understand it.

Most concepts taught in this course are very very useful. If you want to pursue your career as an ML/DL engineer/researcher, this course is basically mandatory, although many concepts are indeed difficult to understand.
Hard core course but moderate exam (for the year that I'm taking).

He is very good at lecturing and clearly explaining concepts. However, CS 4787 has many assignments; I believe he managed to squeeze in 6 programming assignments, 6 problem sets, 5 paper readings, and 2 exams into a 15 week semester.
AWFULLLLLLLLLL

Great lectures, delivered with a lot of passion and vigor. Clear explanations. He is a genius so often time you have to ask him for clarification when he jumps 5 steps in a derivation, but other than that he's great. Exams are hard, but he gives a nice curve

De Sa was super nice, helpful at his OH, and gave awesome print outs of his lecture notes. The programming assignments (in python) build off each other so sometimes your just copy/pasting code and didn't take too long to complete. Overall I learned ML much better than CS4780 and used many of the concepts at my AI/ML internship, highly recommend.

The course covered a lot of interesting topics, but since there were few homeworks and no exams you'll only learn if you engage with the material yourself. Chris was exceptionally approachable and a genuinely caring/considerate person. Lectures were organized really well and not too hard to follow. I highly recommend taking any class with him.

Highly recommend 6787 w/ De Sa for anyone familiar w/ ML who wants to get acquainted with how ML research is conducted on all sides---statistical to hardware. Took away a lot of messages and ended up thinking about/reading material outside of class. He lets students lead paper review lectures, and mainly moderated/clarified things.

De Sa was excellent in Principles of Large Scale Machine Learning. His lectures were clear, organized (notes on website), and very rigorous. I came out of the class feeling like I had strong skills in supervised learning, and good intuition for any related to ML or optimization. Material is used in practice in and is cutting edge for a ugrad course
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: He's new to Cornell so, he was not well adjusted to teach CS 4780. Killian is much better and completely took over the course towards the end of the semester.
Chris de Sa is the Josh Peck of the CS department, beware you could get a newscaster incident. Also cares a lot about ML, and is invested in students learning the material.
The best prof in the whole HIST dept, if not the whole university.
I didn't like the class, but I REALLY didn't like how he stared at me while I was just trying to do my work. I don't think he thought I could see him, but it was creepy.

Funny, engaging, and lenient. Originally there were four essays, but he gave everyone an A for one of them. Would have given a 5 if he were a little more punctual; he took long to upload discussion prompts and never returned our papers (I only got the final grade). Great course overall, and great for law & society minor. Would recommend!!
Quite possibly the most fun I've had in a class freshman year, if not ever. Stress is unheard of, as long as you pitch in maybe once a week

A nice guy, engaging lectures. Very light workload, only a midterm and final paper on top of weekly discussion posts. We did not receive any grades or feedback for our work, only our final grade on Student Center.
I recommend everyone to take this class. I learned a lot about Asian American history from this brilliant and friendly professor. Manageable workload and fair grading.

Prof Chang is a super super nice guy, and you can tell that he really cares about his students. He's always willing to accommodate extensions and responds very quickly to emails. The only issue I had with the class is that we literally didn't get a single grade until our final grade, but I knew that coming in b/c of reviews on here lol.

Took a FWS with Professor Chang last semester. I gained so much from the in-class discussions & readings. Very caring and hilarious. My only issue is that we didn't get much feedback on our papers, so I don't feel like my writing skills improved that much. However, he told us that his main goal is for us to learn; he wants to give everyone A's.

Took a FWS with Prof Chang last semester. He is so adorable and he really cares about his students; this is great especially when COVID brings about many difficulties. Attention: A lot of hard history readings were assigned. They might be too abstruse for a stem guy like me.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof Chang is THE most disorganized professor I've ever had and I honestly feel I didn't even learn anything from him: learned everything from the readings. he's always behind on everything & we only received 1 singular grade the entire semester - no grade transparency at all. but I guess he is nice, friendly & willing to talk outside class
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Chang is one of the best professors that I've had at Cornell. He is really engaging and passionate about the material. He's also a very kind person and was accommodating when I needed an extension. There wasn't too much reading and only a few writing assignments. Mix of lecture and class discussion. I learned so much from him!
Lectures are interesting, but my main issue is his arbitrary grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Prof Chang is a great guy who knows a lot about this subject area and is very passionate about it. He just wants you to learn and enjoy doing so, and is more interested in fostering genuine interest and discussion than making you work really hard for a grade. This class is very manageable and not hard to do well in if you do the few things he asks.

Professor Chang is one of the best at Cornell. His class is laid back, and he genuinely cares about his students. If you have a lot of work or another prelim on any of his due dates, he will definitely give you an extension. His lectures are informational but also funny; he tries to make it fun. I did not read at all, just pay attention to lectures

Very nice guy and seems passionate about the subject material although I found the lectures a bit dry. Assigns lots of reading but you don't really have to do it for class, only if you only have an essay to do which seems to have been graded lightly which was nice.

Not quite sure what the "C" student's situation was below but my experience with Professor Chang was the complete opposite. His lectures were engaging and the workload was certainly manageable. I highly recommend visiting him for office hours for help or even just to chat. We discussed all sorts of things from affirmative action to Premier League.

Derek is definitely one of my favorite professors so far, his intro to asian american history class inspired me to minor in asian american studies! Hes genuinely passionate and knowledgeable about what he teaches & as long as you participate and work on the two major assignments (a take home midterm and final) youre set

Professor Chang was fantastic! I took him for a seminar and he was conducive to conversation, understood students' concerns, and respected all ideas. Do the readings and talk! He's definitely worth all the work!

Professor Chang was a true nightmare!  Did not know how to teach and extremely forgetful.  He actually lost one of my assignments and claimed that I never gave it to him.  I completed the course with a "C" grade, even though I have been a straight "A" student. List to me and you won't be sorry. Avoid at all cost!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's nice, understands your workload, doesn't give dry/dense material, and really cares about you. He's so likeable outside of class. His grading was a bit weird so it's kinda anxiety-inducing but overall not a tough prof.

really friendly and good guy, understanding of students' workload and generous with extensions. other than in class assignments all assessments require a reading of the assigned texts so reading and understanding those is more important than lecture. grading is done all by TA and his grading was sorta nonsensical
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: CHANG IS AMAZING. if you aren't strong in the liberal arts (e.g. reading/writing) you might struggle, but i personally found this class easy and interesting. he's very flexible and understanding, extremely generous with extensions too. a friendly, nice, intelligent professor. might even be my all-time favorite, no joke.
He's a pretty chill professor especially for an ivy league school. The only thing is that he is a bit lazy and handed the final exam to us in a week when he could've gave us more time.
Great professor and awesome person. Highly highly recommended

Great lecturer and unbelievably nice, down-to-earth person. The prelim and final questions were so engaging that I actually enjoyed writing the prelim essay. We talked about basketball and politics during office hours. Nuff said.
No Comments

Incredibly nice guy and very easy. For the exams he gives you a list of the terms from which he is going to test. THe class goes way to fast though and you come out of it not knowing too much more about American history than when you went in.

Prof. Chang is excellent!  Really nice guy who is always willing to talk to you one-on-one, even if it's just to chit-chat...intelligent guy who knows his material well...makes class fun and leads discussions well...try to take a class of his if you can!
No Comments
A great professor. Very clear, and extraordinarily nice. Leads sections very well.
Great professor - really smart, clear, engaging, and SUCH a nice guy! I would highly recommend taking one of his classes!
Great lecturer, fair grader, and a general nice guy.  I have every intention of taking more of his classes.

Great teacher--you get out what you put in, and I definitely put in mid levels of effort for an okay grade. Awesome lecturer and a total math nerd. I felt like some parts of the class were taught in a very unintuitive way that just didn't mesh with my learning style, but the assigned textbook generally explains things well.

Kelly Delp is clearly very passionate about math, but one of the issues I had is that she would focus lots of time on the conceptual aspect of problems whereas Math 1920 is more of an application class rather than a proof class. Her notes are very helpful and posts skeleton and final notes after lectures. She's great but do more practice problems.

Focused a lot more on the general idea of the math and why it was cool rather than how to actually do it. We were told why something was important before how it worked. Because of this, I ended up learning mostly from posted notes and the textbook. You could tell she was passionate about the math though, and that was not always contagious.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The class itself was hard, but Delp at least made it bearable. She was always very energetic and gave really good lectures. She was always very friendly and seemed to know the names of many students in the class and would greet people as they entered the class making it a really nice class environment.

Delp is great! The policies for her course are very clear and straightforward, and she provides skeleton notes before every class so people know what we are covering. The lectures aren't my favorite environment, and I often relied on the textbook to supplement them, but that's ultimately a skill issue: Delp teaches incredibly well.

Professor Delp was the best math professor/teacher I've ever had. She provides skeleton notes to all her lectures which make it easy to follow and understand. Prelims are generally easy and she gives 3 long quizzes in discussion throughout the course. Homework is the best way to learn in this class and also asking questions is a must if lost
The tests were graded so brutally, and barely any partial credit was given. Delp is fine, but her lectures aren't super helpful. You probably have to rely on the textbook mostly.

Amazing lectures, her notes are super organized and she explains things very well. Her lectures pair well with the textbook, honestly best professor I've had so far. She's super sweet and genuinely cares about all her students. I personally think 1920 was way easier than 1910. Would recommend Delp to anyone who can take her class.
absolute queen. her notes were very organized, making it very easy to follow. great explainer. very passionate.
Did not miss any single lecture. Professor really kind and helpful!

Delp is kind, but represents the issue of assigning senior lecturers to intro/low-level classes; they're overqualified thus don't take the low-level courses as seriously, leading to lapses in lecture quality and pertinence to exams. Read the textbook in Finite Math because you'll learn more than in lectures. She's incredibly nice, however.
Easily one of the best professors I've ever had. Her lectures were extremely well planned and organized, and the homework questions were chosen well . If you can get Delp, get Delp.

Amazing lecturer, really cares about students, and is very accessible. Entertains all questions without making anyone feel silly. Final kicked my butt but course was otherwise pretty fair if you read the textbook outside of class
go to lecture and do readings ahead of time if you dont want to grind before exams. do every homework problem at least once
Multi was very cool to understand. Delp does an excellent job in really providing a conceptual and intuitive mastery of the material. Challenging but very fruitful. Would take again.

The textbook is the saving grace of a Delp course; relying on lectures would leave you desperate, stranded and alone. You will have no choice but to take 1920 with her, but only having the previous reviews to set expectations is a sin- you will be sorely disappointed. Honestly, I am not positive that I had the same professor as other reviewers.

Loved Professor Delp she has skeleton notes for all of her lectures making them so easy to follow and fill in, and she will answer any question you have in office hours. Clearly loves math and wants us to love it too
Amazing professor who is really passionate about what she's teaching. Made a huge difference in the class despite its difficulty.

I didn't show up to 1920 lecture much, but whenever I did she was an amazing lecturer. Expectations for quizzes and tests are clear and if you do the homework and study it well you will do well. Deadlines are a little flexible. If you have the chance to get her, take her and you won't regret it.

Professor Delp is a cool dude. You'll probably get discouraged while doing the homework since some of the problems are straight-up impossible, but the questions on the quizzes and prelims always seem to be fair. She goes pretty fast in her lectures, so stay focused and don't get distracted by things such as the majesticity of her hair

Professor Delp really cares about her students, and is such an inspiring, fair, and passionate person. I thoroughly enjoyed taking multivariable calculus with her, and learned a lot from the course. I came in with no experience in the subject, and now feel confident with all the material. Quizzes and Exams(except maybe the final) are all very fair.

Heard multi can be very bad. However, I was very lucky to have Delp as my professor. I actually ended up liking multivariable. Homework is helpful and prelims/exams very fair. Discussions are helpful.

The only good thing about this class is that hw is worth 30% of grade. She adjusts grade cutoffs very fairly, but that doesn't take away from the material being hard and boring. She is a nice person in general, but her lectures are terrible. She is scatterbrained and gets distracted easily, making it difficult to follow the math problems.

The material itself is hard but going to lectures with Professor Delp and participating makes all the difference. Professor Delp is so excited about math and cares so much about her students, her lectures are great. Wish I could take another class with her.
I don't go to lectures that often since it's 9 am, but when I do go, I never regretted it. She's great at explaining difficult concepts with simpler ones. Also, the lecture note is amazing.

Professor Delp is fantastic! She is really passionate about what she teaches and brings good energy to her lectures. Her exams are really fair and are based on understanding of how everything works rather than just giving really hard questions that are meant to stump students. She is kind and understanding, as well.

Great professor! Truly cares about students, makes an effort to engage the class and keep them awake during the early morning lectures. Very passionate about the subject which comes across in her teaching. Pretty fair weight of homework/assignments, great grading scheme, very accessible especially over EdStem for doubts all semester long.
I have never met a professor as passionate about their course material as Professor Delp. Her lectures are fantastic and engaging. Truly an excellent teacher.

I dropped the class last sem because of another professor, Connelly. I was on track to get a C+ or at most a B- in the course, as Connelly's lectures didn't work for me. Delp's course organization is phenomenal. Love the "skeleton notes" Now on track to get an A/A+, and I have a solid grasp of multi now. Great lectures, textbook is a supplement.
Prof Delp is by far the most engaging and thorough math professor I've had. Multivariable calculus is a difficult, boring subject that she makes enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I actually really enjoyed math 1920 because of professor Delp. She gives very clear and engaging lectures which make the course material much simpler and more comprehensible. The homework is reasonably difficult and prepares you well for the exams.

Professor Kelly Delp is a real gem. She has a passion for teaching. Her homework questions really make you question your major. I am lucky to be in her Math 1920 class. I respect Professor Kelly Delp a lot. Sometimes she can speak in Calculus 9 during her lectures so you should know the material well

Dr. Delp is a great teacher and her passion for math really shows in lecture. She's good at explaining difficult topics and very open to questions. Makes very fair tests and wants everyone to do well.

Delp is an amazing person and professor. Extremely kind, passionate, and helpful to all her students. Though the lectures were just what the textbook says, her breaking down the topic in lecture was helpful for me. The lectures were enough for me, no crazy amount of textbook readings, but reading a bit before lecture was always solid.

Lectures didn't really help me in terms of understanding material so I just stopped attending. I basically learned everything from the textbook and did fine. Professor is really kind, caring, and makes lecture fun though. Exams were not too bad; very manageable if you did the homework in my opinion.

Professor Delp taught this class in an extraordinarily approachable manner. The lecture was fun; she may seem a bit disorganized but she is extremely knowledgeable about the material, is passionate about the content, and successfully manages to inspire students with an eager sense to learn. The textbook is a must. Restored my joy in mathematics.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: She is literally the best. She is so caring for her students and really tries to make sure you understand the material. Office hours are super useful and thats where she gets to know her students. Even on zoom she played music and made it a really fun environment. She was also really good at answering questions in the middle of lecture.
Kelly Delp is an amazing lecturer! I was intimidated by multivariable calculus but she made it quite easy to understand. It is the best class i have taken so far.
Professor Delp's office hours were extremely helpful. Don't be afraid to schedule an appointment with her as wellshe'll go above and beyond to make sure you understand a difficult topic.

Great Professor. Unlike many professors here she cared about us learning the material and having fun along the way. Dynamic lecturer, and she really goes deep into the visualization of the nitty gritty concepts, which was a lifesaver for a visual learner like myself.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Delp is a passionate, energetic, and dynamic lecturer who made me love multivariable calculus. If you have to take 1920, take it with her--the class and her exams are FAR more fair than other professors who teach the class. Lectures are essential for understanding conceptual parts of the course, which she loves to test on her prelims and final.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Gives sample past exams but doesnt give solutions. What's wrong with her brain?
Delp is a really cool person who is obviously very passionate about math. Lectures are sometimes tangential and the tests are way too hard (especially prelim 1)

She ditzes out - a lot. And her voice is annoying. And goes on tangents about graphs, and the "+, -, 0" game. For Example - she didn't know the name of the fingers. and then spent a couple minutes telling us about it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Kelly's lectures are energetic and she's enthusiastic about sharing her love for math. She also tries her best to provide visuals for a better understanding of the material. However, it is multivariable calc, and won't be easy.

Multi is notoriously a hard class; however, Professor Delp has great energy so far this spring. She's a great lecturer and seems like she really enjoys teaching multi. She has her lectures prepared before hand and does not get side tracked. I really like her so far.
Her lectures don't make any sense and don't help with homework or section. Alot of notes aren't given and the group work is stupid.
She is very energetic during lectures and is open to answering questions. Uses a lot of visual representations, which helps with understanding the 3D structures in multi.

She's really sweet and nice but the problem is she can be a little scatter-brained and she makes a lot of mistakes. She's very good about catching and correcting them but by that point you're already confused. Multi is hard enough even with good lectures.
Miller was a wonderful professor! Very interesting lectures and material. Easy class - grade was primarily based on iClicker questions (readings required)
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Miller is very nice, good lecturer, extremely knowledgeable. Always replied to e-mails really quickly & good at clearly explaining things.  This class was really interesting; one of the few I've taken that's actually useful in the real world!  Super easy--if willing to put in tiny bit of effort you will get an A. Take this class!

He's really nice, and his questions on tests are really straight forward. Easy to take notes during class.  The paper is easy points.  Dr. Gravani, who teaches the 2nd half of the class is very nitpicky though.  The class is worth taking for Miller's lectures though.
Tests are far too hard.  Class averages very low.  Avoid if possible.  Needs to be reminded that 2 credit courses shouldn't be more work than Orgo.

I used to be bored and not pay very much attention in my past math lectures, but Sanjay's engaging and clear lecturing style allowed me to pay close attention in lectures for the first time. This also deepened my interest in the course (differential equations) and made me enjoy it overall. However, the prelims were not too easy. Final was alright.

Pretty good lectures. Need to read the textbook to do the homework because sometimes the homework content wouldn't be covered in lecture until the day it was due. Grading was also fair. I think for the most part, the class isn't curved by very much and the average grade is like a B, but the tests were fair

Professor Dharmavaram is the best! I really enjoyed this class and we used the same textbook as my high school, so it wasn't too stressful. I really enjoyed the material and his presentation of it. The man really knows how to teach! It's really unfortunate that this is his last semester at Cornell. He'll be at UCLA for research soon! Godspeed. (A+)
Great Professor.
Very clear and willing to explain concepts in various ways with helpful examples.

First prelim was really hard. It got better after that though. Final was okay. Sanjay is good at teaching his stuff, but he was kinda boring sometimes. Also very helpful and always encouraged questions
good lecturer, test was really hard though
Really good instructor, I had him as a TA. His sections were probably more useful than the lectures. Also, very approachable and helpful person.
Really one of the best TAs (if not instructors) I have had at Cornell thus far. He's funny, engaging, approachable, and teaches the material incredibly well. Highly recommended
Dr. Dharia is easy as can be.  I learnt a ton in this class but didn't have to put much effort into it.  He works hard to try and make the material interesting is accent is hilarious.
Prof. Dharia is good.  He hardly use textbook.  I make A in him class and hardly homework.

Only once have I looked forward to class with such anticipation that I felt as though I was about to have a first kiss with a new love.  Dr. Dharia was the culprit.  And he was able to achieve that with a material as drab as economics.
Such a cutie. And so bright!  Not the easiest but you learn a lot.
No Comments
No Comments
Dr. Dharia is hilarious.  He tells great stories of his lady friends.  He should be the president.

AEP 3200 follows the textbook closely and moves quickly through useful math for physics with some review. Lectures present identities/theorems but few examples, so a lot of learning happens from the Psets. Exams are long, and the provided formula sheet is minimal.

Good prof. His lectures follow the textbook very closely, and his test questions are interesting (though challenging). He is better at teaching some topics than others, but you always have the textbook. HW can be challenging, but never unfair (contrary to what others said).

One of the best and most engaging lecturers in the AEP department.  He provides insight where the book lacks and creates engaging, yet challenging problem sets.  Of course there were hiccups with course management, but students have 3 drops (for 14 assignments).  Exams ranged in difficulty (1st Avg: 86, 2nd Avg:50).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: A final HW with 11 questions to do over break. Long exams and no reference sheet to complete within 2 hours. Releasing full-length problem sets only 3 days before they're due and expecting students to complete it or take a 50% hit to that grade is unreasonable and does not facilitate learning. It facilitates rushed learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: His teaching is fine, but he is a very unsympathetic professor. Many times he released a pset 3 days before it was due, then refused to give us extra time to do it. He gave hws over every single break.  For thanksgiving break, he gave us "2 weeks" to do the last problem set, except it was twice the length of a usual pset. TAs were alsoveryunhelpful
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Assigned 11-problem homework set over Thanksgiving break, gave only Three days for another problem set, required students to know material one week in advance of the actual lecture on it, homework sets on material he hadn't taught yet
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very good chalkboard lectures for class, very dry content. Worst part of class is group homework and group final project -- if you get a bad group / group member that just does not want to meet, its hard to learn the content. Learn by working with friends, group with them if possible. He does not know Python, but has great theoretical knowledge.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Diamessis is great. No matter how challenging or coding‑heavy the class can feel at the time, the ideas will only become more relevant. Definitely go to class and participate!

diamessis is a great guy once you get to talk to him, this class can be difficult and I understand why he might get a bad rep, but if you put even an ounce of effort to talking to him about needing help with the class he will help you!

I don't know what happened last year, but he literally implies he could give extra credit in return of a good review. I think he needs to focus on the quality of his course rather than finding a way around.

Very funny guy. Gives off the energy of the basketball coach who's forced to teach a class, except he's actually a decent lecturer and not actually a basketball coach. The psets are pretty long and require a solid background in coding. Idk why last years class resented him so much. People generally seemed to like him and the class this year

In most cases, Prof. Diamessis gives you a feeling that he just learnt the material a night before the lecture but not fully understood. Overall, the lack of quality in his class makes you question both his knowledge of the subject and intellectual rigor.

Prof Diamessis is a great guy and is very accommodating towards his students. However, his lectures are very difficult to follow. Psets/ Final project were difficult and TAs were unable to answer many questions in office hours, leaving students even more lost. Exams were doable but grading was extremelyyyyyy harsh on all assignments.

Prof D is a great person, but a terrible professor. He struggles to break down concepts to an understandable level, does not post lecture resources, has difficulties answering student questions, and never works through example problems. Worst of all, his TAs often don't understand the content and thus prelims and finals are graded SUBJECTIVELY.

He chooses his course time for a slot that is honestly waay too early, you'll notice that fewer students show up as a result. Problem set every week but assigned for teams of two, which makes things a little easier. Nice guy, though sometimes a little jumbled. Receives and utilizes student feedback effectively.

Probably the most down-to-earth, friendly professor I've had. Extremely helpful, responsive and pragmatic. Good with posting notes, homework, and practice exams that are relevant so missing class isn't a huge problem. He is the kind of guy you want to sit down and have a beer with.
Cool guy. Know his stuff and helps and cares his students at all times. Lots of coding for homework, but some are very conceptual as well. Exams are hard, but grading is fair.

Very organized class structure. Only thing a little strange was that assignments were due at 11:59 AM (noon), not PM. 

Do not underestimate the prelims.

Dr. Dietz was a gem. She was always willing to help and made sure rubrics were clear. Practice exams were given but only one for each. She went out of her way to make sure our questions were answered and showed patience even when me and others asked the silliest questions. It was always nice going to her office hours and chatting with her.

Nice to your face but not behind your back. Doesn't help or support students, and it doesn't understand whatsoever. If you take any classes with her, don't make mistakes, not even typos, and avoid interactions. The other professors in the courses are usually nice and understanding, so try to talk to them instead.

Took BIONB 2210 with Prof Dietz. While she doesn't give any of the lectures, she is the main organizer for this course. She's super kind and wonderful at explaining concepts. Discovered her office hours right before the final exam, and wish I had gone sooner!
Can be hard to understand, but genuinely cares about the material and gives helpful feedback
extremely confusing

do not take coml2723. i will say that the professor definitely cares about the subject and academic inquiry, however i do not recommend taking this class. there are better courses that value participation, effort, and discourse that are not stressful and punitive like this. grading is harsh and a lot is expected for only a 2000 level course.
simply a sigh

By far the best professor I have had in my (albeit short) time here. She is brilliant; she provides excellent explanation, and very clear guidelines for grading. The seminar can be a bit intense as an undergrad, but definitely worth it. I want to take as many of her classes as I can!

I loved taking her class my final semester. I wish I could have worked with her throughout my four years. She's simply amazing. I highly recommend going to office hours (but actually go!). In the beginning of the seminar, I struggled, but after office hours, I shared my voice and grew so much as a student and person, thank you for everything!

Enthusiastic, approachable, brilliant. For every point that a student makes about the readings, she has an entire day's worth of discussion questions. She structures her course in a way that you gain a strong foundation for later, more theoretical, topics. She expects her students to think critically about the texts, and is willing to help!

Professor Savransky is very engaging and well spoken during lectures. He's funny and seems to genuinely care about his students. My only issue in this course is that you need to essentially teach yourself the entire course through less engaging, content-dense videos on canvas. Overall, good professor, I wish lectures were more consistenly helpful.

Why is one of the hardest classes in the meche curriculum self taught? You have 30-50 pages of reading every week, and it's usually not helpful because students don't learn from reading a textbook! Prelim 1 was ok but Prelim 2 had people genuinely giving up and leaving half blank. When the prelims are open note, that's how you know you're cooked.
basically a self study class, why pay so much to go to university when you have to learn content on your own?

Prof. Savransky is an understanding and caring professor. He is lenient with grading at the end of the semester, allowing students to complete an extra credit problem set. With that said, it was difficult to retain much from lectures in the course, as a flipped-classroom approach was implemented. Homework assignments were also extremely long.

Horrible professor that makes a hard class harder. Tests are easier than hws but the homework's are excruciating. Extremely tough grader. ended with a 93.9 and that was an A-. Lectures were entirely unhelpful for hw or exams. primarily poll ev based. not understanding or nice

Most organized and clear class I have ever taken. Lectures are super interesting if you watch the videos ahead of time, like you are supposed to. He is a really funny guy who helps everyone make light of what is definitely a tough class. I think he lives on Ed and gives super great explanations to any questions. Had a really great experience
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Really was great to learn from as someone who never did dynamics before - everything was super clear and if anyone had a question he usually responded in less than 20 minutes online. All lecture content was online in videos/handouts which made everything super easy to reference. Homework is hard, but lectures are super engaging and interesting

He is extremely passionate and it shines through with the effort he puts into his classes. He gives very detailed & rigorous notes for his lectures; with 4060 this was incredibly helpful since it is a complex topic, however it was definitely a lot harder. Only professor I've ever had that reminded/validated us how mechE is hard & we're doing great

Great professor - definitely loves the math side of dynamics but also very knowledgeable about the material and fielding questions. Makes you work for the class but at the end of the day is forgiving about grading.

Went incredibly fast through lectures at the beginning of the class, calmed down after a few weeks. Homeworks varied, some were easy but others were really long and tough. The material covered at the end was unnecessarily difficult for the course. Was sometimes condescending in lecture but usually helpful at office hours. Open note exams.

He speeds breathlessly through lectures so it's hard enough to write anything let alone understand what he's talking about. Even worse he makes a lot of mistakes in lecture which makes you feel even more lost. Treats dynamics as if we've all been studying it for the past ten years. The textbook is just as bad. Plenty of office hrs to help though.
super fast iclicker

Dr. McBride is an incredibly supportive professor who genuinely cares about his students' success. I took his FWS and would highly recommend it. The readings are historically interesting and his grading system is fair. Overall, this is a great class with a professor who truly is passionate about what he teaches.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. McBride is a very caring and kind professor, he makes sure to make accommodations and wants every student to succeed. I took him for an FWS and I couldn't recommend enough. The readings are historical and very interesting. If you're a freshman looking for an FWS take this one, its graded on completion; if you do the work you'll get an A.
I learned a lot from him including about how to spell P-O-N-C-E and he demonstrated it to us. Thanks!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. McBride clearly loves what he does and loves to teach what he is passionate about. He is incredibly supportive and caring for his students and if a student does the reasonable amount of work he assigns on time, he/she will receive an A.

Though I meant to write this review at the end of the class, I am writing now because the most recent one is incredibly wrong.
There have been no bad reviews since February of this year.
This professor is so kind and their grading system allows for so much flexibility, as long as you put in an ounce of daily work his grading policy GUARANTEES an A.

The class is basically just reading Peter Handke's books. No one knew what was going on in the class, and he would go off on random tangents for a long time. So long as you write the number of pages he asks for in a paper, you get an A.

Professor McBride is a very reasonable professor. He can be confusing at times, especially if you go to him for outside help on essays, but he tries very hard to get to know you as a person and build a healthy student teacher relationship. I would not take Love and Death in Vienna again solely because I did not like the material much.
Great professor would definitely recommend!

An amazing professor who deeply cares about his students, if you went to his office hours he would walk through the problems, would also crack jokes in lecture as well. I hope his retirement treats him with nothing but kindness.
Prof Diciccio is very thorough, forgiving, and light-hearted. Homeworks are due at the end of the semester, if you pace yourself there will be no problem. Exams were open note, attendance optional.

Diciccio clearly actually cares about his students and reducing stress. Our exams were all online and they give half of the homework answers in section. However, he seems to be a little tired of Ithaca and teaching in general, and most people I know didn't learn anything in the class.

ABSOLUTELY GOAT. Always recommend his classes. You can learn a lot if you put in effort, but you will also be fine if you just follow the slides and assignments. Tests are not hard, and the pressure of ddl is low.
I love him. He's actually the best and deserves the world

Professor DiCiccio was definitely one of the best teachers I've had so far. He is very chill and genuinely cares about his students. We often talked with him after class since I had questions about university applications and course material
He is very interesting. Classes are honestly very clear. Really recommend you to take his class.

Homeworks are kind of difficult and really really long, but they are all due by the end of the semester. There are no practice exams provided, so taking notes on the slides will be the best bet. I avoided lectures since he spends most of the time going over impractical examples. Class is not hard, but it is TONS of boring work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: DiCiccio's lecture style is to just read off of notes he posts online. This course has the reputation of being one of the hardest in the stats major and that rep is earned. DiCiccio makes it as easy as possible, with lots of helpful office hours, and a very generous curve at the end. Probably the nicest guy at Cornell.

Diciccio is super nice, open to all questions, and accomodating. Only take 3110 in the Fall if you can. Class is straightforward. Lots of HW but it is all due at the end of the semester with recommended deadlines during the semester. Exams can are a breeze if you follow the HW

Although Professor DiCiccio was very accessible outside of class and had a good sense of humor, he delivered EXTREMELY boring lectures. If you can take a different stats class, do that. Even if it is slightly harder you will at least have a better time doing it

One of the funniest and chillest professors I've seen at Cornell. That said, not huge into the whole teaching thing. If I hadn't taken stats before class would have been infinitely harder since lectures are tough pay attention to. Overall very easy class if you know what you're doing, but not a whole lot of learning for me. Fantastic guy though

Professor Diciccio is an awesome man, he explains things clearly, although in a pretty fast pace. Overall an pretty awesome course in understanding basic concepts and notions of Statistics. Worth taking!

Many students enjoy the class due to his extra credit offerings. As a student in ECON 3120, the lack of depth/rigor in his material is punishing. I indicated difficult for the class since it was excruciating to read his paragraphs on slideshows. AVOID!!! You will not learn with him. He gives no feedback and never responds to email.

Nice enough guy, but worst class I've taken, coming from someone who considers themself fairly good at math (although I've never taken stats before). Lectures were convoluted and slideshows had full essays on each slide, but it was never clear what any of them were supposed to mean. Whole bunch of words thrown at you, never any explanations
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I love him so much. Very very fair. Very flexible with due dates. One hw per week w/ unlimited attempts to get a 100, one test (take home, more than 24 hours to take, covered half course material). Two extra credit opportunities. Responds to email fast, very helpful in office hours. Don't have to go to class, can watch the lectures asynchronously

Professor DiCiccio genuinely cares that his students are understanding the concepts without being overwhelmed with work. His assignments focus on key-concepts that are reviewed heavily during lecture. He was incredibly accommodating for online classes. If you work hard, an A/A+ is definitely attainable with him.

Undoubtedly the GOAT. The nicest professor at Cornell who, unlike most here, actually wants to see his students succeed! Seriously a gem, super understanding and his office hours were really helpful throughout the semester for someone like me who struggles with this sort of stuff. Couldn't recommend his class more.
Literally the kindest man I know. His classes are extremely well-taught and his sense of humor is awesome. Really cares about his students. By far my favorite professor at Cornell!

I love his lectures and he was definitely a sweet person. But the problem is that he wasn't so mathematically rigorous and the difficulty was low. So if you love high grades and easy things, go ahead and enjoy. But if you are into math, please turn to a stats professor that is no an ILR professor.

He's actually the sweetest professor I've ever encountered. Even after we moved online he constantly checked on us and was very considerate and caring. He has a good sense of humor and lecture isn't boring. The course is not easy but he grades very generously.
i loved his class! insanely easy, and he makes lecture fun with funny stories. 11/10

He is the best. Some would say he is a bit boring, but his dry humour is what makes his class the best. Not only that, he is very generous with grading, very hard to fail his class. I put off 4090 because it is a hard class, but he made it extremely survivable.
Best professor at Cornell! He is truly always there for his students and wants to see every single one succeed! His office hours are also helpful for the homework!

VERY amazing professor, hands down the best. He makes courses interesting and often interjects with an anecdote or stock advice to keep up entertained. I learned a lot from him! He is lenient on the homeworks and would definitely accommodate you if you have difficulties meeting deadlines. Also the tests are easier than the homework!

This is a straight forward statistics class. It's not a big deal if you have never taken stats because the only thing you need to prep for the exams is the lecture slides and homework. Going to class isn't that important but he gives funny stories and is very accommodating. Have to study even if the tests are open everything. Take 3110 with him.

Tom Diciccio is the best stats prof you'll find. Lectures are dense but he does his best to make dull material interesting and often pauses lecture for a "break" in which he'll tell stories about his past or explain the importance of investing in your future (get that roth IRA!). Extremely helpful in office hours, class is curved heavily also.
Terrible lectures. He clearly doesn't prepare them very well and does not care about the class.
Everything is take home. Doesn't necessarily mean everything is easy. Can be entertaining in class, but you don't necessarily have to go.
Hardest class I've taken at Cornell

His slides are very dense material-wise but the class isn't difficult at all. Never took stats before and did fine. Homework is an easy 100%, attendance at section is unnecessary. Tests are long w/ a lot of questions but open everything. Diciccio is good at explaining things if you go to class and pay attention and tries to keep things interesting.

tom isn't super into teaching in general but will be helpful if u reach out. homework can get really annoying cuz they sometimes don't really have anything to do with the lecture material but he makes the exams fit perfectly with the lecture slides which he makes available. discussion completely unncessary if u can do hw alone
Great professor very accommodating still learn lots of material but very lenient.

this man is truly an angel on earth. a heavenly being sent to bless cornell university with his presence. never will you meet a kinder, more accommodating and merciful math professor. he makes an effort to make his class the least stressful as possible. also his deprecating jokes give me life

Never went to class or discussion. HW is easy, you can submit online until you get 100%. Midterm+final are open everything -- do hw & just open up slides & Google as needed. Extremely nice in grading.
Tom is hilarious and clearly really smart. He's a real expert in statistics, so I feel like we're lucky to have him teaching a basic stats course!
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Being statistics, classes can get a bit dull at times, but Diciccio tries to make it more bearable by joining around a little. He is really helpful in his office hours, and is extremely approachable. His lecture notes are really useful, and in addition to the Webassign homeworks, are more than enough preparation for the exams.

Tom was a really nice professor. He knew class material was boring, but tried hard to liven it up with interesting stories about statisticians and his past at Stanford and in Canada. Pretty easy tests, a lot of self-learning, but he is really cool during office hours and he is very flexible and understanding.

Prof. DiCiccio is a super nice guy, very approachable, really wants you to succeed. The webassign HW's are kind of a pain but a guaranteed 100. Both the mid term and the final were open notes, open book. The class avg was not good but he curves to an A- I believe. Attendance is not really mandatory. All material overlaps with AP Stat.
Best professor ever. Nice guy who genuinely cares about his students. Also tells great stories to keep lecture interesting

Although information is very dull, he interjects with funny comments. Really easy course if you want to fulfill a math requirement. Didn't feel like I learned much though. Assignments include short weekly homework assignments, a take-home midterm and a take-home final. Go to lecture and office hours and you will get an A.
Easy even for those who have never learned stats before. On-line quiz and take-home mid-term and final. Good sense of humor. Generous grader. However, not l much to learn from this class.

A great class if you're looking something to fulfill your quantitative requirement but aren't the best at math. He explains well and the textbook he uses is the best math book I've ever used. If you do the reading and don't put off the assignments, you will get an A. Though you don't always need to attend class, the guy is hilarious when you do.
Pretty clear, lots of writing

T DICICCIO is the bomb. Although lectures can be dry, their loaded with great info. prof very helpful. Take home midterm and final heehee, and really overall nice guy in general. Has a funny sense of humor (u gotta listen for his jokes haha) and his complaints about classroom technology are hilarious. Recommended to take him!

Prof. Diciccio is one of the top statisticians and one of the smartest profs I have ever had.  He knows the ins and outs of the stats industry, and he knows a range of material very well.  He has a good humor (a little awkward but it lightens up the class).  There was only take-home exam which was pretty straight forward from his teachings.

Really boring subject, but if you pay attention, you can do really well. Even if you don't, you can still get a good grade because of his ultra-generous curves. Really helpful (though not always punctual) for office hours, and good about granting HW extensions. Really funny too: has a lot of bizarre anecdotes and often mutters things about Prozac.

I hated that this was a mandatory class.  The material will be useless to most people.  Not really a hard class, but it's all theory and could give some of you problems.  DiCiccio is a good guy though.
His sense of humor keeps lectures bearable while he curves his tests so that everyone does well, even though the tests can be tough.

This guy is awesome. His tests are really easy and his deadpan humor makes the class really enjoyable. All of the homework answers are given in section too. Plus he's very helpful during his office hours. Great prof.
Very tough course, but Prof. Diciccio makes it ok.
Diciccio is a great professor.  He makes stats as fun as it can be.  His funny stories and personal remarks cut the intensity of the subject material.

This prof rocks.  He makes stats seems not only doable but also entertaining.  He is an excellent lecturer; probably one of the best that I've had.  And, he is not overly horrid with grading.  The curve and his teaching style are definitely plusses to getting through this course.  If you need to take it, take it with him.
Cuts through the normal **** most stats professors put you through and gives you the straight up dope that you'll ever need in the real world. very cool, easy to work with. Highly recommend.
Curves so that over half the class gets A's and class is open-book.  Absolutely take Diciccio!
A truly amazing professor!  He makes stats so entertaining and easy.

This was my fav class ever! Prof. Kriner is funny, knowledgeable, and gives fascinating and inspiring lectures. Despite its length, the time flew by. Grading is fair and assignments manageable. Prof. Kriner is extremely helpful and supportive. The readings are great too. I learned so much in this class and had a lot of fun. Definitely recommend!

Have taken a few classes with Kriner, and they have all been amazing. The lectures are so interesting, and he loves engaging with students to hear their thoughts. If you have a decent understanding of politics, then this class will be so chill.

Great lecturer, passionate about the political system and the presidency in particular. Engaged the class in lecture and encouraged participation. Heavy on readings and grading could be a bit arbitrary but super approachable professor and really easy to work with.

Professor Kriner is a phenomenal lecturer. He's very engaging and obviously knowledgeable about his field of study.
Prelims are fairly easy if you go to lecture, participate in discussion, and review lecture notes. Important to actually do the assigned readings, as they are often recalled on prelims and the final.

Great guy, clear he loves what he does and is very passionate. Not reading off a script ever, very knowledgable. Just 3 essays throughout the semester with clear outlines. Final was online. Would take again!
Study up on readings and get on your TAs good side for papers

Really great professor! Definitely would recommend taking this class. Lectures basically repeat the textbook, but interesting information can be found in the lectures. Lecture notes can also be found online, and attendance not taken so you'll be fine missing a couple lectures. Discussions pretty important.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class is pretty easy and Kriner is a very good lecturer, often offering different perspectives on current government problems. Lectures aren't really important, but they are interesting. Make sure to do the readings and attend discussions, as a bulk of the tests are on the ideas from the readings... other topics are common sense US Govt principles
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: great professor seemed to be very knowledgeable and cares about the topics. lectures aren't that important but are pretty interesting. midterm and final are not bad at all if you go to the discussion sections.

I feel so lucky to have taken his class. He is such an intelligent person and engaging lecturer, and you will learn so much about the subject just from listening to him in class even if you already know a lot about politics. He is so chill that he made our final online since it was late in the semester and gives helpful extra credit opportunities.

Kriner is very passionate about what he teaches, and it shows. Great lectures. Wants the best for his students. Interesting material, little homework, several opportunities for extra credit. Grade is based on 3 writing assignments, 1 prelim, and 1 take home final. Would highly recommend this class for anyone who's interested in gov't/politics.

Solid class for understanding basics of U.S. government function. Assignments are time consuming but straightforward. Exams require basic memorization. It is a large class, so the lectures aren't always super engaging.
Incredibly intelligent and so open to talk with students. Really loved this class and would definitely take again.

Doug Kriner is by far one of the best Government professors at Cornell. It's clear he is passionate what he teaches and is always happen to listen what students have to say. Discussion sections matter! Make sure to do readings as they are vital for prelims and writing assignments. Overall, this was a fantastic course!
For GOVT3161: It's a fine class, but all of the writing assignments are heavily stats based (analysis and all that), so please be aware of that before signing up.

An amazing lecturer, so if you don't like the class, it probably means you don't want to study government. Participation in discussions are mandatory but graded somewhat arbitrarily. It can be tough to figure out what TAs want from writing assignments. Exams aren't bad.

Lectures weren't engaging. I just got by with my general knowledge of American politics and didn't do most of the reading. The data analyses he assigns should be super easy but take a lot longer because he wants you to use Microsoft Excel. It wasn't a bad class content-wise, but it was so complicated that I wouldn't put myself through it again

Although the content itself was interesting, it felt as though he was ranting during lecture, and not all the material that he talks about is on the slides, so if you miss a day, you will more than likely fall behind (as he doesn't even post them). Also, so much reading. There are only a few assignments, and if you don't do one, watch out!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
I loved intro to American politics with Kriner. He is passionate about the subject matter and does a great job of incorporating data to make the themes have a poignant impact for the present day. He does focus heavily on the lecture slides, but he is a really good lecturer. 

The supplemental readings are SUPER important to do well in the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Kriner was really knowledgeable about American Government, and I learned a lot in his class. What I disliked about this class were the TAs. Mine graded extremely harshly without giving good feedback and barely covered the readings during discussion.

Great class! Prof. Kriner really shines when talking about his speciality of the American Presidency. Throughout the course he provided insight and fostered interesting discussion about the American Presidency. Grading was generous and the final project (a survey) was both interesting and relatively straightforward. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Skip this class if u can, I took it for fun and it made me change my whole major. I originally came in as a govt major and immediately changed it after this class. TAs graded unfairly (some didnt read any of the papers while others never gave above a B) his lectures are BORING, it was the longest 75 min of my life and I had to do it twice a week

Kriner is one of the best lecturers at Cornell. Other intro classes barely scrape half the class to show up to lectures, while most students showed up to Kriners lectures, despite them mostly repeating the textbook readings. Kriner was an engaging lecturer and I genuinely enjoyed showing up to class, but TA discretion largely determined grades...

I have Kriner now and he does not read from a script anymore. I can tell he is passionate about what he is lecturing on, and that he cares about the students. He is charismatic and funny and I would take another class of his.
Professor Kriner's lectures sure are scripted; however, the detailed descriptions of each topic are super useful.

Although you can tell hes reading from a script, I appreciated his effort to organize lectures in a way that helped students study for exams. I loved staying after lecture to listen to him answer students questions; I could tell that Kriner loved what he was teaching and was happy to see students engage.

Readings are dense sometimes, but are always analyzed in the discussion section so you can get the main ideas. In his lectures, it was clear that he puts a lot of time and effort into considering what to talk about - he does a lot of case studies/data analysis, and he is so accessible in office hours and invites student participation always!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures were incredibly boring. I swear he was reading off a script during class. His lecture slides were disorganized and all over the place. However, we had really good discussions during class. We also only had four assignments due throughout the semester, and they were super light.
Loved prof Kriner! He puts so much effort into his lectures, and the workload is totally manageable, all while learning a tremendous amount.

Alright what.. This class has an hour and 15 minute lectures along with a 50 minute snooze discussion section that requires participation or you get points deducted from your grade. There are pre-recorded 30 minute long lectures & as someone else pointed out he reads off a script, NOT ENGAGING. Theres also sm readings, 4 essays midterm and a final.

Kriner seems like a nice guy, but in lectures all he does in ramble on. You can literally see him reading off of his screen during live lectures AND pre-recorded lectures, so it's hard to engage with the material he's reciting. He also makes you read overly-long material before class. (BEWARE if you have no background in US gov / history)

Lectures are fascinating and always involve real-world applications/examples. Trump's impeachment inquiry began a month after class started, and Kriner adjusted on the fly and dedicated a bunch of class time to the impeachment proceedings. Somewhat easy A if you engage with the material.

Prof. Kriner gives lively lectures with opportunities for student input; theres a clear rationale throughout. Course went through insightful analysis on history of and contemporary debates on American government.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: fair class and you can tell he cares, sometimes a little disorganized

The first half of the term was difficult to follow, with lectures relying heavily on slides and moving quickly. The second half improved, with more engaging lectures and clearer explanations. Since it was his first time teaching, I expect the course will improve.
Made analogy that when you go to the gym you need to push yourself and used that as justification for making his class the way that it is.
so bad. avoid dorn if you can and take it with someone else

Very caring and passionate professor and is willing to answer any questions and help out when available. Sometimes lectures got off-track, and exams tend to be partially different than the content in the lectures and problem sets. But, I'm sure the class and his lectures will be far more cohesive as he teaches more.

His lectures are fast and not always organized. However, he always tries to improve because he is new.
There are a total of 6 problem sets, 2 prelims (20% for the higher and 10% for the lower) and 1 final. 
Exams practice are hard unless you do a lot of practice from psets. I recommend must go to TA sections!
Beware of homework, but great class overall. Easy to ask questions to.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: It's an intense class you will need to study hard and go to office hours. He's clearly a kind person.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Really enjoyed the content but definitely need to put time into the class. Loved how passionate the professor was!
Prof. Dorn was an incredible professor. Definitely challenged me to think outside the box. It's a class worth taking
Professor Dorn was extremely passionate and easy to access outside of class. Material was challenging but Professor Dorn was able to explain everything very clearly.
Great professor, would take again.

Pretty nice guy who knows his stuff, but many basic concepts were explained in really long-winded ways that made it hard to follow. The material isn't extremely hard and you can def study it in your own time, and the grade cutoffs were pretty generous. TA slides were a godsend, it was just his first sem teaching so I think the quality will improve

Professor Dorn may be a nice guy but he is fresh out of graduate school and should not be teaching this level of class. His lectures are confusing and exams very difficult. I found the TA discussion section to give me better teaching than what he could give in class. I wish I had taken this class with a different professor.

Professor Dorn really grew on me throughout the semester. I am grateful to have taken his class and really learned a lot. I feel like I have a strong foundation in supply and demand side analysis in microeconomic theory, and I would recommend that everyone take his intermediate microeconomics class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: RUN!!! You can tell that Jacob wants to make a great class, but his lectures are confusing, his slides have errors, and he will contradict what he has said. DON'T take it unless no other alternatives at all.

Super nice guy and eager to teach, but he's a recent PhD grad and it shows. Often makes mistakes in class and walks back on what he says. Combined with overexplaining simple concepts, his lectures are often confusing. Going to OH may be helpful and exams are managable. Eager to improve course.
First time teaching. Fresh phd grad. Does not know how to teach. Lectures are extremely confusing and tests don't look anything like problem sets or practice tests. He tries though.

Lectures are overcomplicated and confusing, problem sets and the minimal practice problems given for each exam weren't reflective of tested content. He is a nice guy and the curve is projected to be generous, but I'd rather be taught well than rely on a subjective curve and feel impending doom going into every exam. I hope this course will improve.

Avoid if possible. Over-explains simple concepts with heaps of unnecessary mathematical notation. Doesn't communicate well with TAs and regularly struggles to keep a class running effectively. Problem sets are incoherent and messy. However, he's a nice guy and obviously eager to improve, so you can expect his class to be better-run in the future.

He explains concepts in an extremly clear way. Although some people mentioned that problem sets are long, there are only 6 in total and they are not very difficult. He also gives three practice exams before each prelim and the final, whch is super helpful.

McKee is honestly one of (if not the) best professors I have ever had at Cornell. He not only knows the material but can explain it in very simple terms, and actually cares about his students. I almost didn't take 3130 (not good at maths, never seen prob/stats before) but risked it since I'd heard he's an amazing prof, and best decision of my life!
The undisputed goat

This is probably the most useful class I've ever taken, and McKee is a chill guy. However, I didn't find the way he taught to be intuitive or helpful and I learned much more through self-studying. Problem sets do seem to be connected to the exams, but they were pretty long and repetitive which added a lot of work to an already difficult class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: To preface, he is an great person. However, lectures are unclear and hard to follow. Problem sets are long, but the bigger issue is that they are repetitive and include ideas meant to be "implied" (not mentioned) in lecture. The workload was certainly worth more than 4 credits yet the support systems did not align with what students needed help on.

[This rating is for Teaching and Learning Economics]. Amazing lecturer! Cares deeply about students and will know your name and offer to provide support if you need it. Be ready for a lot of group work.

McKee's teaching style is confusing: lectures are relaxed with frequent 10+ minute poll-EV breaks for asinine questions, but exams have medians of 70. If you've taken 3030 with him, 3120 will be much easier. Advice: when he sends out the form for what group you would like to be in, select you want the first row - it's going to help your grade.

Prof. McKee showed genuine interest in and enthusiasm for course content, and he was very accessible outside of class. He once spent over an hour in an appointment with just me to help me prep for the second prelim. The course content built up throughout the semester, so in my opinion, things got easier as you went, which helped too.
Great professor. Very charismatic and wants the best for his students.

Prof McKee is the best professor I have had at Cornell. I took ECON 3130 with him and even though it was a lot of homework, I enjoyed my time in this class. He truly cares for his students and is a nice, empathetic person. I'm a stats major, and he explains the content better than all stats profs at Cornell. Lots of hw but you can get help in OH!

This class was one of the hardest classes I've taken. But, Professor McKee was super kind and as helpful as he could have been. He also does a thing where instead of attending class you can watch the lectures and submit answers to the pollev questions which is lit.

Extremely fair grader. Very nice and funny teacher. Prof.McKee is very responsive to questions posted on Ed Discussion (he stayed up till 12am sometimes during the final week). Never curve down. Lectures cover some hard concepts and are sometimes confusing, but the exams are straightforward. Exams are curved generously if too hard.

Professor McKee is a great lecturer and professor. They always try to make the class interesting and applicable to the real world. The work can be a lot but he is always willing to help students when needed! I would absolutely take another class with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of the kindest professors I've encountered. He has great lectures, which are all recorded and posted, and is really good at explaining complex topics. Exams have a group portion at the end to boost your grade, and he is very fair overall with grading. Overall a great professor and human being.
Very accessible and understanding professor. He is willing to help in Econ3030 and is a professor economic majors should get to know.

Loved ECON 3030 with McKee though it was difficult at times to keep up paticularly as someone who took the class freshman fall. There's quite a bit of content in the course so it's important to keep up by going to office hours and to discussion sections. The TAs are really good so do take advantage of their help.

The exams were pretty tough and made sure you did all the homeworks legit and understood them. In person lectures aren't required in the sense you could make them up later. Quizzes were just tedious (but some of the questions showed up on the exams so make sure to do them). His lectures were very useful and him and a student were very active on ED.

Great professor with really great lectures. He is very active on Ed and quickly responds to emails. Very open to adapt to students' needs. Sometimes the homeworks were huge and also not the biggest fan of the PollEv's but you can do them after the class if you miss the lecture. Fair exams.

Exams aren't about how well you know the material, but about how much can he twist the material so that he can get the bell curve. 
Covers a lot of material in one class, make sure to study every week. He's a good prof, but exams just don't fairly reflect what we have studied or done in class/psets.
Best Econ professor for core classes by far. Teaches difficult material in an accessible way, but you will still have to put in the effort.

Bad comments are disappointing. He is an expert in economics education, truly the best Cornell prof. He can cover so many topics on time but also make you comprehend the important parts by giving you intuition without confusing you. GO TO THE LECTURES, they are well planned, you won't need to study much later. Very inspirational if you like econ!
Absolute goat.... this man makes a strong case for fav prof all time
Good guy

The class lacks a lot of substance relating to some very important concepts. Problem sets are nothing like the exams and are often long and repetitive, not really helping you improve much. Exams are pretty easy, but he tends to make them long for little substantive reason. Also, there is a really annoying group project that just super tedious.

Lots of econ majors love McKee. Very caring/accommodating but also fair. Teaches one of the most important core courses in econ and makes it worth your while. His "flipped classroom" technique wasn't my favorite, but it at least keeps people engaged during lecture. Class is even accessible to non-econ majors. He's just goated. Hope he sticks around

McKee is one of my favorite professors. I hadn't taken a math class in years, but he explained things clearly in class and was very accessible in office hours. The problem sets and the practice prelims were EXTREMELY helpful to learn and to study. I literally just did the practice prelims several times to study and got A's. Excellent teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Excellent professor! Long problem sets (I would definitely work with other people on these, which he encourages) but I learned a ton! I'm glad I took this class with professor mckee.

Amazing teacher! Professor McKee genuinely cares about his students & their learning. He's super helpful in office hours, especially for problem set and lecture questions. The textbook isn't necessary (I didn't even use it) but participation is VERY helpful. Also, the previous exams are a great way to study!!
Overall 10/10 great prof!
Incredible and passionate lecturer that truly stands out for his great ability at communicating the material. Would absolutely take any course with Professor McKee again!

One of the more overrated professors in the Econ department. He gives very superficial explanations for the concepts covered in the class and doesn't seem to care if students understand the underlying math and statistics. If you're looking for a class where you'll learn and be challenged, don't take this class.

McKee is a fantastic lecturer and really approachable outside of class. Go to his office hours, he's exceedingly helpful and always does his best to help the student understand. Prelims and final were very fair, problem sets were fine and he drops 1. Plenty of extra credit opportunities to boot. Definitely taking a class with him again if I can.

Prof. McKee is a real nice guy who is ready to help anytime. The positioning of the course was a bit weird as it is supposed to be a somewhat rigorous course but the target audience is a group of econ majors who have no training in higher math at all. The result is "learning" a bunch of formulae you never have to prove (or see the proof).

Nice and approachable, but class was structured badly. Required attendance at 8am lectures, where a lot of the time was spent in silent breakout rooms. Exams were all multiple choice, which is horrible for a math-heavy course!!! Problem sets were laborious, but really helpful to learn material. Overall good prof, bad class.

This man is easily the best professor I've had so far. He is a great lecturer, but more importantly he is super considerate and accommodating especially during a tough semester. Absolute goat, and this is coming from someone who took his 8am class.

Professor McKee is one of the best professors in the Econ department. He manages to make every class entertaining with games and challenges, even when course material is a bit dry. If you're someone who does better with active learning than lecture-style courses, I highly recommend ECON 3030 with McKee!
He's a really funny and interesting lecturer. Examples given in lecture are very good and help students understand the material
