It took me time to get used to Professor McKee's interactive style of teaching, but once I did, I really enjoyed the class. Professor McKee truly cares about making sure students are thinking about the material in relation to the world they are living in. Go to office hours, they're really helpful.
Overall good teacher. Interesting lectures, relatively long homework (but nothing too bad), and pretty easy exams.
Prof McKee is amazing. He really cares for his students and rewards effort. Problem sets are quite challenging, prelims are less so. Highly recommend to take 3030 with him.

McKee is a stud- never seen a professor so intentioned in structuring their class. First day of class I was in awe at his grading criteria/expectations. He tries to reward hard work and understanding, not penalize you if you're struggling. He APPLIES the stuff we are learning to the real world. Don't expect an easy class, it's still a lot of work..
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: McKee is AMAZING. He knows his stuff, cares for students, class is not an easy A, but easy B if you study a lot. He is just a great guy in general, and as a prof he is ok. Online quizzes, HW, project, exams, and group exams. He does everything he can to make sure you get at least a B for 3120, not so sure about 3030. He is passionate about teaching
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Caring

reviews.comment: Really approachable and nice professor. I put off taking this class on purpose because this class is one of the most rigorous classes one takes in the Economics major. I was fortunate enough to have this professor. Although problem sets are long, he is a great lecturer and as long as you pay attention in class he explains the material well.
The most amazing professor I've ever met. Professor McKee is super nice and a really good teacher. His office hours are valuable.

It's unfortunate that this is a required class for the Economics major at Cornell. This is a god awful class with a professor that doesn't teach clearly and gives extremely long and dumb problem sets. Be prepared to learn stata and try to work with people that may not want to work with you. WORST class I've taken so far.

Professor McKee is not only a fantastic teacher, but an awesome person. I had a bad first exam, but McKee was very easy to talk to and make sure my grade was not affected by one bad performance. When I had this meeting, I got to talk to Professor McKee as an equal and a counselor. He has been very successful; talk to him if you get the chance!

Professor Mckee is great! He is clearly passionate about the material and it really shows in his teaching. Its a hard course by its nature, but Doug does a good job of making it understandable. If you put in work, its definitely doable. Would highly recommend the class and the professor!
reviews.rating_tags: GROUP PROJECTS--Tests are tough--Would take again

reviews.comment: This professor makes Intermediate microeconomics interesting and exciting! He also really cares about teaching and uses different perspectives to engage the class. Definitely one of my favorite teachers. He made me love the econ major again and have some hope. ECON 3030 was still just as hard as I had heard though.

I had put off taking this course because I was really scared but McKee is very sweet and patient. He actually cares about teaching-even has a whole podcast and blog about it. If you go to lecture and try your best to do the p-sets and actually are able to solve them before exams you can do really well. He's very helpful during office hours too.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: WORST class I've taken at Cornell. Hands down. Purposely long and hard problem sets that no one could solve. Just resulted in students writing stuff down they didn't even understand.  Each problem set was painful, even after going to lectures and discussions. This class killed my major and cumulative GPA all on its own.

I'm not completely sure how this professor is at Cornell. I've ever met a less engaging and more annoying person in my life. I mean truly the worst experience of my academic career. I look at the clock and it doesn't move in this class. I've learned nothing. Made a course that should be interesting so incredibly boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The least engaging course I've ever sat through its a complete an utter waste of time and money. They cannot lecture whatsoever. My friend is sleeping as I write this

ICL is an easy class, no idea why the grade is this low. Her section is about Europe (particularly France/Germany), which is probably the section you'll go into with the most understanding. questions 1-5 on the final are worth 10% each. DO THE LAST QUESTION FIRST its worth 50% and takes a lotta time. Lectures were interesting readings were helpful
Solid professor.

Writing this before I get my grade back on the first exam. She assigns ~50 pgs of reading/week and isn't the best lecturer. IMO she could improve on linking examples in class to key concepts needed for exams. (this is coming from someone with a >4.0 GPA). This class would also REALLY benefit from having a discussion section (idk how it doesn't)
How does she expect students to write so much techincal explanation requried writings in such  a short span
She can't teach, the study guide could be alot better but is making the whole process a torment.
Lots of reading for this class but if you keep up and pay attention, and work on the study guide you will do well. In class, you sometimes have discussions with your peers.

The worst lecturer of the four professors in this class. Painfully boring, disengaging lectures, and a droning voice. I'm unsure how she became a professor because she has zero public speaking skills. The content is all over the place and doesn't follow a logical sequence. I managed to get an "A" by cramming the study guide.

Good lectures with a lot of reading. The professor makes the class interesting with a good balance of lectures and discussions. Tests are based on the study guide, but grading is done by TAs, which can vary. My TA was harsh and inconsistent. Beware of the final and potential grading issues, but the professor is nice, and you'll learn a bit
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Enjoyed her portion of 2350 the most. Very clear lecture slides and teaching. If you do the readings and pay attention in class it is easy to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Respected

reviews.comment: I had her for ILRIC 2350. She seemed relatively uninterested in the class, and it was her first time teaching it as far as I understand. Her lectures were confusing, and the readings were hard. I had to read over and over again to understand. She did give us a study guide though, which ended up really just being the test questions so that was nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Assigns a TON of reading, which can be annoying especially for a writing course. No exams, but there are a lot of papers. She gives pretty solid feedback. Discussion posts are due for each class, which can be annoying, but you don't have to overdo it. Participation is required, but isn't too hard due to the open ended nature of the class's content.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Don't take this class if you don't like reading or writing. TON of readings and discussion boards due b4 every class. She is a pretty nice/fair grader on the papers but omg lots of work. She expects a lot from her students. There are no tests but you will have a 15 pg research paper due at the end of the semester. You must participate in class
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Toby is the goat. He makes you genuinely interested in the material and doesn't make his exams very difficult - they just test the main broad topics, nothing too specific. This class made me switch my concentration to microbio... everyone should take it!!
Microbiology is a hard course however Professor Doerr makes this class very engaging and interesting. He cares a lot about his students, and genuinely wants them to succeed.

Doerr was such a funny and sweet professor. His lectures were always engaging, and he really is passionate about microbiology which made me enjoy it too. His lecture slides can be a little overwhelming sometimes, and he does tend to go very in-depth about topics that aren't necessarily covered on the more straightforward exams. Still great prof!
Amazing guy. Smart, funny, knowledgable.
A professor that genuinely wants you to succeed. Rare to find within the bio major. Absolutely take him if you can. Also gives you skibidi toilet freebies.
He is so amazing!!!! I was ready to give up bio but he made me fall back in love. SO GOOD AT EXPLAINING CONCEPTS. He should teach more classes.
Honestly, one of the nicest profs I've met here. He makes the material digestible and is so accommodating to anyone's situation! A real lad

Professor Campana is maybe the best professor I've taken a class with here. He's a wonderful lecturer who's extremely passionate and knowledgable about the subject, and always makes really interesting points which challenge your thinking. His grading policy is very fair and not overwhelming, and he's kind to students and always willing to listen.

easily the kindest and most understanding professor i had this semester. professor campana doesn't cold call on students, so it's sometimes upsetting because it seems like no one cares. my only regret is not putting in more effort into the class. would definitely take another one of his courses just to have him as a professor again.

Easily one of the kindest and most genuine professors I've known at Cornell. When I needed an extension, he never said no. His courses were well organized, and his lectures were always a joy to attend. I think he legitimately loves what he does and wants to share it with his students. Often went to his office hours just to chat, which was fun.

You get what you put in with Professor Campana's classes, but the content he goes over in class is so interesting it's hard not to be invested. Great lectures, great organization of course content, would highly recommend if you are interested in hearing about games and animation as a reflection of japanese popular culture!

Most professors tell you how to improve essays. Not prof. Hill. Will instead ask what you think of your essay. Seeing a fortune teller about your essay may have the same results. Take a different class.

Every office hour consisted of me asking him for feedback and him saying "But what do *you* think should be changed?" while providing nothing from his side. EXTREMELY HARSH GRADER. In a required FWS class, only 2-3 people got 90+, even though the assignment topics were really hard. I communicated to him that English is my second language, no effect

Dr. Andrew Hill is easily the best professor I had at Cornell. Intelligent and well-spoken, even among his Ivy-League peer, yet lenient, caring, and clear. While he doesn't do much to make lectures exciting, the brilliant things he has to say about the material are enough to keep anyone sincerely interested in the subject matter thoroughly engaged.

At first I did not like his class at all. There were reading responses due before every class, and the texts he gives are quite challenging. The readings were a stepping stone to the final curatorial project Overall, Dr. Hill is very approachable and VERY lenient with deadlines. His grading criteria could be more clear. Helped me improve my writing
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Genuinely one of the most inspiring and fascinating minds you can find. I had Dr. Hill for my FWS, and was so motivated by his incredibly designed class format and assignments that I took his ENGL 2690 course. Any of his courses are essential if you are looking to evolve as a writer, artist, historian, or scholar. I can't recommend enough!
Great teaching style
very good professor

Heard good things about Professor Hill although I have not taken his class. Absolutely brilliant mind and is caring but forthright. Indubiably the most incredible human. 10/10 would take his class again.

When you think of the greats, who comes to mind? Albert Einstein, Isaac Newton, Nikola Tesla, perhaps. For me, it's Andrew Hill. Hill's mind may be the most brilliant I've ever had the honor of engaging with. Every thought was so well-formed, every conclusion so clear and decisive. I was in awe in every class.
Great professor with a great teaching style. Professor Hill is one of the most well spoken individuals I have ever met, and he makes his lectures and discussions enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This guy might genuinely be the most well versed person I know. Not only that but he let me borrow his lambo when my car was in the shops. I would die for this man
not responsive at all to emails
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: no just no
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: avoid at all costs

Overall, Professor Hill teaches a solid class, one that is highly conducive to creating unique perspectives on whatever reading is being covered. He cares a lot about students' progress and makes himself easily available, though he's not very engaging as a teacher and sometimes struggles to capture a class's attention.

Professor Hill is a little bit strange, definitely quirky but a funny guy once you get to know him. He shows no mercy when grading essays, and assigns several difficult readings every class. Like why was I reading a 50 page medieval bestiary and a culty version of the bible for homework. Overall, I would just switch.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Whitmore is pretty chill and straight to the point. Some content might be difficult but the TA's and the professor himself are very helpful. There's a fair amount of work but it never gets too difficult.
Really easy class, but significant amounts of work, and the TAs grade strictly but fairly. The professor is easily accessible through emails, office hours, or in person.

Professor Whitmore's class structure is odd, but pretty easy. 1740 is a super useful course and I genuinely learned a lot from it this semester. That being said, he doesn't really know how to answer questions. He doesn't really teach in class, only from video lectures, so I spent a lot of time working on materials outside of class. TAs are helpful.

Honeslty one of my favourite professors. He doesnt waste time and is a great teacher. He teaches exactly what you need to know for exams. Before the prelims and final, we have one full class for review where he will work through a similiar practice paper to the exam and makes the assignment as similar to exam as possible. very good guy. Lots of HW
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I have taken two of his classes now and can say he is a really good professor. He is not as approachable for small talk as other professors but he does a really good job at teaching. He goes through content and explains everything in the best way possible. Everything is very easy to understand and his slides are also very concise.

I feel like Professor Whitmore is about as good a professor as you can get for biz comp. In class he's always willing to help you and his TAs are helpful as well (and hold lots of office hours). Regardless of who you get, the class has a ton of work, so just do it and you should be fine. The excel prelim and final are easy imo, only word was hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Practical class. Teacher was professional. Maybe too much coding in the lecture though.
Very useful class for internship and jobs. One of the harder core classes, but worth it at the end.

Now that we got our final grades I am much more satisfied with this class. It was a hard semester back on campus after over a year of remote learning. The situation with the final being postponed until the following semester didn't help either. That was the university, not him though. I did better than I expected and I think the grading was fair.

Pretty good. Was clear about expectations. Tough grader though. Good at explaining stuff in person, but the structure of the class didn't really facilitate much of that. I would suggest to hold more office hours and get to know students more. Other than that I learned a lot from him.
The single worst teacher I have ever had for a lectures. Disrespectful, entitled, arrogant, and self absorbed.

Professor Whitmore was 100% my worst professor this semester. His course is set up terribly so I will give him some credit for that, but he made it even worse. If someone was doing bad in the class, the other two prof. would try to help and give feedback but Whitmore did none. If you had an issue with grading or a question, he left you on your own

Andrew Whitmore is possibly the least caring professor I've ever had. He acts very passive aggressive towards students and is not accommodating towards individuals who ask questions. When students try to ask questions he usually gets angry rather than being helpful and asking a question.
Whitmore is the goat

Homework is 50% of the final grade and pretty easy, so if you do all the work you'll be fine. Be sure to format all things based on the rubric. It doesn't really matter which professor you have for this class because all content is the same (not sure if it's only because of online classes).
Simply the least understanding instructor at Cornell.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Whitmore is very professional and helpful. He will respond to your emails quickly and is responsive on discussion boards (if you have them). I highly suggest meeting with the TA's because they will be grading most of your assignments. I would definitely take this class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof Whitmore is very talented and clear in his presentations and Business Computing comes highly recommended to any Cornellian. Though he can come off as arrogant and annoyed, he displays information in an easy to understand and comprehensive manner.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Pretty awesome professor, gives great and comprehensive lectures. Homework can be long if you haven't done this before, but honestly pretty chill + easy if you have experience. Lots of room for your own direction, lots of fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Lectures are amazing, as are the course notes. There are pop quizzes that count for credit, and they're often placed at kinda evil times (such as right after thanksgiving break this year). The homework is very hard, and takes more time than you'd expect. They teach a lot of content and they teach it very well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Very demanding and time-consuming assignments, but lectures were great, and the final project was extremely rewarding.
Explains things very clearly in lecture. Moves very fast, making it easy to get lost if you miss anything. But if you're paying attention, you learn a lot.

Prof Myers is the GOAT! Clearly, he knows a lot about Java and programming logic as a whole, however, some of it may be outdated (one time he mentioned a "recent" java release and it was from 2014 😭). Lectures go by fast but not so much so that the content is overwhelming. If you're stuck on anything, office hours should be your #1 resource.
amazon lecturer
Similar to Previous years, Compilers is just as difficult and rewarding as ever. Group wrote over 15k lines of code. Well worth the grind!

His lectures are okay and he is good at answering students' questions in an enlightening manner. Perhaps things would have been different in a smaller class format, but he was just middle of the road.

Prof. Myers is a great person for people who have had experience coding in java and with the concepts taught in the course. He is clearly not, however, meant to teach 2110. The only coding experience I had before the class was CS 1112, and this was a huge step up. Lecture pace was WAY too fast and course was pretty disorganized. Exams were fair-ish

Myers lectures at a level far too abstract for 2110, and doesn't seem to understand his audience. I did well because I came in with a lot of knowledge and taught myself everythign new. He also decided to rewrite many of the projects, and released with many bugs. I once spent hours finding bugs in my code only to find out the smoketester had a bug.

Very obvious he loves Java and is very knowledgeable. However, he teaches so quickly half the times I am just scrambling to get all of the notes down in lecture. He teaches quite a bit of honors material (even though this is 2110). Java syntax is not taught at all (unlike in 1110) so Java Hypertext and googling is your best friend for assignments.

Myers is definitely incredibly knowledgeable, but his lectures were fully useless. If you have a tough time learning on your own, a course with him is not wise, and I found participation being graded to be super annoying. You can get an A if you just read the notes thoroughly and do the assignments, which are well-designed.

Great lectures, interesting material. Assignments were updated somewhat unexpectedly, but it's understandable since the assignments this past semester were new. Could have given more study material, but notes were well-organized and assignments were fun. Very knowledgeable about the subject.
Poorly run class, Professor was not helpful even a little bit.
some rocky issues with assignments (last minute corrections to design that werent publicly announced), but overall great class. easy but fun assignments

I took this class in the fall of 2020. Professor Myers completely transformed the way I viewed computer science through this course. The assignments were very involved, but they also taught me so much about principles of software engineering and how to design large-scale systems. Myers is easily one of my favorite professors I've had here so far.

Prof Myers's lectures are engaging and entertaining and he manages to make incredibly difficult concepts understandable. His courses are difficult, but are transformative and absolutely worth it if you're ready to put in the work. Do not mistake salty reviews from students not ready to make an effort to be an accurate representation of Prof Myers.

This has been one of the worst run classes I've ever taken. The assignments are very difficult and he does not teach well. Office hours are always packed and you can sometimes not get help for hours. Whenever there is an error on the staff side of things the students are left to suffer the consequences (ex. Multiple OH canceled/ last minute changes
Worst class in the history of classes, DO NOT TAKE!!

cs2110 this semester has been horribly organized. for some reason helping the student out when harmed by an error on the administration's part is always the LAST option, rarely taken. I've basically been told 'Oops! Deal with it' a dozen times when I'm the victim of admin error. lectures too fast. class is also much harder than previous iterations.
Just not a good experience in his class
Thanks for making CS 2110 like hell. I'm retaking in next semester.

Wow, what a wonderful guy. I mean, he's contributed more to Security and PL research than anyone else currently alive, and continues to have the time to welcome anyone and everyone interested into the PL community. Before taking 2112, I was going to study ML. Now I've seen the light (Professor Myers's light) and I'm going to study PL. Thank you

I came to this by chance since I saw some post about Andrew Myers and thought to myself, "that name is familiar". I took this course close a decade ago and he was a great professor.I was a senior taking this class for additional context. What added to the course was the small size instruction, which I hope is still the case
Tests are impossibly difficult and completely irrelevant with teaching materials. make simple ideas impossibly difficult. it's a joke.

Myers is very knowledgeable and you can really tell that he cares about his students through the way he carries himself in lecture. It's crazy how much work is in the assignments (200 hours total for me), but the online course notes and TA office hours are a god send. I've never learned this much from a professor and a class before.

Myers is the best prof I've ever seen. His lecture is always inspiring, and he genuinely cares for his students. TAs, classmates, and just the spirit of the class is amazing. It is a VERY heavy workload class (like a solid 10 hours per week just on coding projects on average), but it will be fun if you love programming.
Probably the best professor and class ive taken at Cornell. Also the hardest class Ive taken, but the amount you learn is well worth it. The compiler project is no joke and extremely fuffiling.

Prof. Myers' courses are extremely difficult, but his lectures are excellent and you will never learn more in such a short time as in his class. He is also friendly in Office hours, if you have any questions about the course. Take his class if you want to be challenged like never before.

He put in a special effort in remembering everyone's name, and that's really something. Extremely organized lectures. Exams were fair. Projects were hard (120 hours of coding for the whole semester). Lots of fun.

Professor Myers is knowledgeable and his lectures are amazing. He might get a bad rep because his classes are hard, but hes extremely helpful and is always willing to answer your questions either after class or during office hours. And if you cant make it to his office hours, he has a website where you can book an appointment with him.
Really hard but one of the best teachers I've ever had.

I love the guy so much. He's a genius.  Don't mix up the courses with the teacher. Let's separate the two:  Professor Myers is: Well spoken, focuses on big picture, focuses on good programming, understands everything. Nice.  The classes he teaches are: honors/heavy duty CS courses at Cornell University. HW is 10+ a week. Lube is advised.
2112 is plenty of work, but well worth it if you love CS.
Good teacher. Explains well and helpful if you ask for clarification. Assignments are long but the grading is quite generous.

Lectures were always very clear and interesting and were a good learning experience. Taking the honors course resulted in a hefty load with seemingly unreasonable projects and deadlines. In the end was worth it. Prof. Myers was always very helpful when we had questions as was the rest of the course staff. Take this course if you want a challenge!!

This class is simply way too hard.  Problem sets in this class are longer and more tedious than comparable 300 level computer science classes, and the TA's grade them in the most anal retentive unforgiving manner possible.  Myers is a pretty good lecturer, but don't let him organize the assignments.
Nice guy, tries to explain things. Projects are WAY too long!!!!!!

Don't take his course if you want an easy ride! His classes are tougher than almost anything else you'll spot in college. And yet, if you need help, he's always there to help. Plus, if you survive the course load, I got more out of his courses than any other class.
If you like to stay up nights and programming for over 30 hours at a time, have fun with this class.  personally i think he's on the crazy side of cs.
Above average teacher but not amazing.  He hates C with a passion so do not get into an argument about programming languages with him.

Likes to focus more on the logistics (comments, specifications, etc) of programming rather than the actual code itself.  Has very long complicated projects.  Class concepts are obtuse and difficult to understand.

There are a few pop quizzes and a lot of reading, but the workload is manageable if you focus on key ideas. Professor Moisey is extremely funny and makes every lecture engaging with great jokes. I would recommend this course to anyone, even just for fun. He is super patient, answers questions clearly, and really encourages interest in learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Great lecturer that keeps you engaged and makes fun jokes. Took this class just for fun and out of interest, and I was able to learn so much more about photography. Exams are not hard and the TAs are super helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Moisey is an incredible professor. I'm taking his class as a senior and wish I knew of him sooner. His lectures not only make me laugh out loud, but the way he roots the content in the broader scope of life makes every lecture incredible interesting and at times deeply moving. If you haven't had a class with him, you're missing out!
Genuinely good prof who cares about his students and their ability to learn. Entertaining in both content and presentation

Professor Moisey is an amazing lecturer, this is my favorite class at Cornell. He's genuinely interested in the material and explores it alongside you, plus is insanely entertaining which makes it easy to pay attention. The reading is a lot, but get the big ideas (skim+) and you'll be fine. Start the final paper early, and get your TA to proofread!

Lectures were always the highlight of my day. Moisey is a thoroughly interesting professor who encourages students to think outside the box and embrace somewhat abstract concepts. Very sad that I probably won't be able to take another one of his classes.

A professor that sincerely cares about what you learn and how it will impact your future life—whether that's academically or just day-to-day. He makes you think critically and creatively. He carefully curates lectures and guest speakers. Highly recommend his class and am grateful for all I learned.

Did not like Moisey. Not a difficult class but he was very full of himself and had minimal structure beyond his stream of conscience rambling. He was disrespectful to students on a few occasions as well and was not very approachable.
passionate but rude
Don't graduate without taking an Andrew Moisey class.

Moisey is an amazing lecturer. He is the funniest and most passionate professor you will ever meet. The topics for this class are very interesting and makes you think about the world in a deeper way. If you've taken Visual Studies, please take this class too. It's so worth it.
It was fine
Moisey is a great professor and he makes the course content interesting and engaging. The teaching team is very accommodating. Would definitely recommend to people even if they are non-majors.

Took this as a distribution requirement, and was definitely one of my more interesting ones. Classes at the beginning are definitely a little more boring, but second half was where I felt things got more interesting/relevant. Very easy class, Moisey also made attending lecture interesting even if the content was hit or miss for me. Funny guy

Moisey is such a funny and engaging lecturer. This class opens your eyes in ways few others do. ATTEND LECTURE, ALWAYS. Do the readings (they can be dense/long, but that's where lecture comes in). If you take diligent notes & review them before the exam so that you're familiar with the order of material, you'll do great (open-note exams).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: By far the best class I have ever taken at Cornell (and I think the best one I ever will take). He's the most engaging, enthusiastic, and humorous lecturer and he really makes you care about the material. You will leave every class with your mind blown.

Best class I have taken at Cornell. Goes beyond "Visual Studies" and explains everyday life. Moisey is an engaging lecturer and totally hilarious. Really cares about what he teaches. The first few readings are weed out but it gets more interesting after that. Definitely don't do the final paper at the last minute. Easy grading.
Fantastic professor. Fantastic class. You will never be bored in lecture, and you will leave with many things to think about.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Really great class. Do the readings, participate in lecture discussions, attend the out of class events, and put effort into the major paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: My favorite course I have taken. Highly interdisciplinary-- covers many potentially weighty theoretical and philosophical topics. The majority of the grade is a 15 page research paper, which he insists on being an intervention -- asking and answering a question that begs both. He is hilarious, and he wants you to care about the class. Approachable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Don't do it!

While lectures were interesting when he talked about the new tariffs, he basically just read off the slides. Easy problem sets, but hard prelim multiple choice Qs. His grading was unclear (besides the median and the “top 45% get an A” you don't know anything). Definitely not “bad”, just gave less effort than other Econ profs and uninspiring.

I don't like macro but this class was much better than expected. He spent some time explaining the new tariffs, which was interesting. Tests can be hard so make sure that you understand the slides well.
His accent made it difficult for me to take away much from his lectures, which consisted of reading off of slides. Not a very hard class conceptually, but be sure to study a lot outside of class!

As long as you study and understand lectures you can pass. he's generous with grading problem sets and has a good amount of office hours to help with any questions. The only bad thing is he doesn't post lecture slides after or a recording, so you have to go to class.
Mediocre lecturer but has easy tests and psets. mainly just reads off the slides

Nice dude, class was kinda forgettable though. Definitely did his best to explain the material clearly, but it could sometimes come off dry. Certainly not a hard class if you just stay on top of things and attend section, and considering it's a core course for ECON that's probably all you can ask for.

Buy the optional textbook! His lectures go extremely fast and are packed with so much information, but there are no lecture recordings. The lecture slides were often unclear/confusingly worded, so I highly recommend purchasing the optional textbook and reading the chapter summaries which do an amazing job of simplifying concepts.

Took his Intermediate Macro class this semester and I'm glad I did. Even over Zoom, he gives good lectures and his passion for the material comes through quite well. Grading is based entirely on problem sets and exams. The problem sets are simple enough but be sure to prepare well for the exams as they will probably be harder than you expect.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very interesting class and Professor. Good class to take if interested in law school. Pick 4 homeworks out of 16, final project, and participation. Light grader.

Dufresne is such a genuine professor who truly cares. There were no exams, 4 homeworks, and a final project. The class can get a little repetitive and boring because there are no lecture slides, and it is just her talking. She does tend to call on the same group of people over and over again (who are usually students in her advocacy clinic.

Professor Dufresne is amazing!! In my opinion, she gives the best lectures. If you're considering law school as a career choice, I'd highly recommend taking one of her classes. Her classes are very participation heavy, so you get out of it what you put into it.

Professor Dufresne has the amazing ability to take complex and difficult subjects like immigration and make them not only enjoyable to learn about but easy to digest. She goes out of her way to make sure both students who have a law background and those who do not are able to get the information they need.

Professor Ghosh is a wonder of a human being who is so considerate in the way she leads class discussions. Even if you don't do the readings, you will be able to contribute in class. The grading system is extremely generous if you put any effort into your essays. It is hard to get less than a B- if you are present and do the assignments.
Unbelievable professor. Easily the best lecturer at Cornell. She is a humble genius who steers the conversation in such a way as to be unimposing but also critical

Really great history class that pushes you to think of the big picture rather than just regurgitating events. Readings were all extremely interesting. A bit of a tough grader on the essays but she values improvements and gives a grade based off performance not numbers. Great class overall
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Gives complete control of grades to TA probably with instructions to grade tough because you usually do not have the right to question. Material is interesting, but you are encouraged to follow her view on the subject matters even though her class is mentioned as open to debate. Would not recommend taking it unless absolutely necessary.

TA grades the papers, very unfairly. Prof Ghosh is good but readings are boring and hard to digest. She gives the control to TA completely. Discouraged to challenge your grade in class. Grossly unfair
One of the best lecturers I've had. As an engineering student I usually don't enjoy humanities courses but Ghosh was different. I can't imagine what someone who actually likes humanities would think!

Probably my best professor at cornell.  Her lectures were very organized and helped to explain the readings.  She is very helpful and open to questions (no matter how basic).  She grades very fairly and gives good comments.  I highly recommend Hist275 (it also fulfills a LOT of the A&S requirements).
Really good professor. Engaging lectures, extremely helpful and nice. Fair grading and good workload. Lots of academic readings. Recommended

Class consisted of 2 5-page essays, a midterm examination, and a final examination. Both examinations were in-class and a choice of essay topics. Reading assignments were moderate and interesting. The class is excellently organized and Prof. Ghosh is very articulate and interesting.

She is brilliant and articulate.  She's friendly, although she can seem a little brusque and not that personable.  I'm learning a LOT in her class, although there is a lot of very difficult reading.  She cares about teaching and wants her students to be engaged.

Hard to contact him should you find yourself needing to, but his hockey class is so much fun. He's such a genuinely nice guy, and I actually looked forward to this even though it was early. He's reasonable and takes everyone where they're at (experience-wise). 100% should take this class, Dusty is awesome.
Great guy, way more understanding than he had to be, considering certain people in the class could not ice skate whatsoever. I got much better at ice skating, and had a very fun time.

Great guy, actually so funny and understanding (really put up with a lot from some students). All you really need to do is show up to class and skate. I did get better at ice hockey even if I'm still bad. Highly recommend!

He is great. He lets you pace yourself so the class is what you make of it, but he's also happy to help with advice or stretches. His attendance policy is very fair(usually just make-up) and he's an overall relaxed guy that knows his stuff.

He's really chill and nice. If you're late, he won't be mad as long as you jump in to participate. As long as you don't go over your max limit of skips, you're cool. He will answer any questions you have about working out and building muscle.

Awesome professor. Really taught me how to become a better hockey player. Taught the class how to make Hockey Stops, and just simple maneuvers to better facilitate your flow of the game. But, you have to know how to skate on ice. Although the class is an intro, but most of the students are already good at hockey.

Note: the course I took is actually HIST 2931- Making an Empire in China. 
Prof. Du is very knowledgeable, caring, and hard-working. Her lectures are information-dense but well-structured. No need to do all readings, but read papers. Go to her office hours and you'll get great book recommendations, advice on writing, and even life lessons.
Super caring professor, grade based on weekly reflections and research paper at the end. Every class is a seminar, so come to class prepared and youll be fine.

If you attend all lectures you get half a grade up. I like her passion (although her accent might be a bit difficult to understand at first). Read the syllabus carefully. It's ok to not do the weekly readings. She is very accessible outside class and it's willing to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Duffy is a true gem. It looks like a lot of work, but she's flexible and caring. She recognizes when her students are struggling with school and life in general. She's also a great lecturer and gives many opportunities to earn points through different things (essays, tests, discussions).

Turned really interesting topics into dry discussions over common sense. Both lectures and overall class schedule are very disorganized. Would avoid class like this if you don't want to waste your time and tuition.

BEST communication professor. She is so genuine and caring. Really values students' opinions of the materials and course. Her classes are very lecture-heavy and likes to throw in a few readings that she likes to discuss in class. She's very approachable! Easy course with basic syllabus structure - highly recommend all of her courses

Prof. Duffy is one of the most incredible professors at Cornell. She genuinely cares about her student, makes class expectations clear and rather reasonable. The pace of this class was a bit slow, also lectures were heavily summaries of assigned readings making them kind of redundant. But great prof and easy course.
Beers with Dwayne is such a fun class! He clearly loves teaching about beer and you can learn a lot if you pay attention during lecture.
One of my favorite professors ever
Exams (multiple choice and online) were a bit challenging but there is a lot of extra credit

He's really chill and makes the class fun. Don't buy the textbook, you'll literally never need it. There's just a couple of assignments besides the midterm and final, and he grades really easy, so it's a grade GPA booster.
Bad slides and extremely difficult exams that were out of scope.

This teacher is an incredibly difficult assignments and tough grader. 12 hr per week assignments, and just a bad teacher overall. I would not recommend this teacher for any class, let alone an actual difficult class like this one. Save yourself the bad grade and drop while you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He knows his stuff really well and cares that you learn but the class is insanely tedious. The workload is very heavy, feels like a 7 credit class with the group homework, random assignments, 2 hour calculation sessions, 3 prelims, and projects sprinkled in between. Plan wisely and make an effort to ask him questions and engage with the class.
He grades like he genuinely wants to fail you and makes the workload unbelievable undoable. Has a passive aggressive tone when speaking and you have to use the textbook he wrote.
A lot of work. Homeworks were so tedious and did not yield much. Overall a difficult class and a lot of your time commitment will be spent here. The professor gave good lectures.
Wasn't the best person but was a decent teacher. Learned a lot but he isn't the nicest.

This class was a nightmare. Insanely long homeworks with barely any course staff that could help. Exams were graded SO HARSHLY with almost close to 0 partial credit. Always rude whenever you spoke to him and lectures were always useless. Not sure what's gotten into him this semester.
Not sure if I had the same professor as other reviewers because he was always passive aggressive, declined to help you, and had a huge ego problem.

Prof Duncan cares a lot of about students learning, his lectures are very well organized and based off the textbook he wrote. TAs were cool and helpful with problem solving. Spreadsheet assignments were a pain but overall not that bad as far as ENGRD goes. I never went to the discussions but I'm pretty that's 10% grade for attendance.

Very good lecturer. Grading is spread evenly between homework, prelims and a final. Workload is fairly light. Lectures follow the textbook, but I would recommend reading the textbook before every lecture. Grading was lenient on exams and class was slightly curved. Would highly recommend this class for an engineering distribution as well.

Generally Duncan is a good professor. Can be blunt in lecture when receiving questions he thinks should be obvious. Group homeworks can be a drag. Tests require very solid conceptual understanding of the content, he will reapply concepts to completely new situations, so do lots of practice. Occasionally funny.

Prof. Duncan's lectures are AMAZING, and he provides every document on his website for easy access. We always knew what was expected of us, and office hours were well-timed throughout the week. Tests were difficult but fair, and homework was done in groups, which I personally loved. Sometimes he can be a bit sarcastic, but he is a great professor.
He was a passive-aggressive professor so it was not a welcoming environment when you wanted to talk to him. Plus, you have to buy his textbook he wrote.

A very respectable and respectful professor who genuinely cares about his students. His care takes the form of wanting the best for the student, which doesn't translate into lax standards in any way. Excellent explanations. Office hours are incredibly valuable.

While homework groups were annoying at times, they weren't terrible. All exams (3 prelims+final) were completely fair and if you took good notes in lecture and really understood homework and section problems, they were straight forward. Don't slack because it seems easier than PChem. Advice, do all problems yourself before exam so YOU actually know
Not the easiest intro course, but probably the most useful. Anyone with the slightest inclination toward pursuing ChemE should take the course.

TMD is the man! He lets you know from the start that it is not a normal intro class in the fact that you must work hard and you learn, but if you stick through it you gain a whole new perspective on your chosen major. It does stink that he wrote the textbook because lectures can seem repetitive, but he is very personable and helpful in office hours

He's an odd teacher - doesn't really teach to the style of the students, despite the fact that he says otherwise. Heavy emphasis on the textbook. Really smart guy though, but didn't seem connected to any of the students but his favorites.

He is best professor I have ever met. He always make everything clear and his class is well organized. Although it is not an easy class to get good grades, you can learn a lot in his class, not only engineering knowledge, but the attitude towards life, critical thinking and communication skills.
Professor Duncan changed my interest from "What is chemical engineering?" to "This is the coolest stuff ever!"
AMAZING

Fantastic course teacher.  Poor advisor.  Condescending if you are not confident or if you do not agree with him.  This is college; kids are supposed to find themselves, not be discouraged. His favorites get more confident while the shy ones get more shy.  This is an unfair and unstable method to students.

In a perfect situation Duncan would be a great teacher. He interacts with the class, seems friendly and is very intelligent.  But the reality is, he takes things personally, a very bad characteristic for someone in a position to educate.  Once he aligns himself against you, consider avoiding him at all costs and not depending on him for help.
He intimidates me ... oh TMD

I had him for multivariable calc and he was a great teacher. He was out of his subject matter and he did an excellent job of teaching the material. He was clear, comprehensive, and loved to interact with the class.
He's definitely someone who picks favorites. But watch out if he doesn't like you. He'll make your life miserable.

This is a very rigorous introduction to chemical engineering. It is not an easy class, but you will learn a lot if you put your earnest effort to it. A lot of skills are honed in this class. For instance, interpreting graphs, guessimating, etc. It is a critical thinking class, and this is how the professor wanted it to be.

Avoid this class at all means possible.  It requires much more work than an intro class and more time consuming than 3 credits should be. If you are thinking of being a chemical engineering, you will really rethink it after this class.

First time a teacher actually knew my name and cares how i was doing. Duncan is by far the best teacher I've had at Cornell (he was named teacher of the year in NY for 2007!) If you take this class, beware, he knows your name and whether or not you care to show up or try hard
Awesome teacher, very willing to help anyone out!!  Teaches great classes.
The best teacher that I have had so far.  He really knows what he is teaching and has a good sense of humor.  Excellent use of chalk and TAs.

He really knows his stuff, but taking notes in class is really hard because of the handouts.  Its impossible to study from the notes in class, and the text isnt much help. Best way to study is do the practice problems on the website. Office hours were overcrowded and the TA's didnt have enough time to be particularly helpful to anyone.
Great Professor in terms of knowing the material and getting it through to the students. Intro to cheme class will give you a good idea of wether chemical engineering is what you want.

The textbook is horrible and convoluted.  you basically buy it for the HW problems inside.  taking notes in class is nearly impossible and pointless since he passes out so many handouts. limited number of practice problems. studying for prelims and final are difficult because of this.
he looks like jack from lost

Helpful; tries to help us learn the material and understand different applications of topics. Lectures are disorganized and somewhat uninteresting, but he manages to teach fairly well anyway. Grades fairly and makes exams so that they really test our knowledge instead of trying to trick us. Helps you do well in the class.
No Comments

duncan is probably one of the worst teachers i have had at cornell. during pchem i had the impression that he didnt like me.  from the other posts,i can see im not the only one.  he does not act like a teacher.  by this i mean if you annoy or upset him, he takes it very personally and singles you out (ie not offering help, offering it arrogantly)

Lectures are quite disorganized.  Writes all over the board so it's hard to take organized notes without rewriting them after.  His book was the most poorly written book I've ever read (I stopped reading it).  Arrogant and moody.  Best to avoid interaction.
Awesome class and actually a lot of fun, but yes, prepare to work for your grade. I loved his lectures and the text was one of the few that I actually read.
very hard class. Duncan was an alright teacher. Need to get on his good side to do well. He was a bit patronizing.

Overall a bad professor.  His course was well-organized and clear.  But as a person he is: Arrogant, Rude, and Insulting.  If you get on his bad side - watch out; he's going to make your life difficult.  I found the best course to take with him was to avoid him.  In summary he's a decent teacher, but is a vindictive and mean-spirited person.

Quite possibly my favorite professor so far.  He goes far out of of his way to get to know his students really well - he often knows things that you never thought he would care about.  Lectures sound like you're reading from his textbook, which is clear as well.  Knows everything he teaches front and back.
No Comments
Great teacher!  One of the best at Cornell.
I love Prof. Duncan. He was really helpful during office hours. His lectures were clear, and he really cares about his students progress. He is one in a million.
i <3 T.M.D

Excellent class, very organized and straightforward. Takes time to learn the material well and to do the homework, but it's worth it. I never found him to be unpleasant or rude, nor do I know anyone that's felt that way.
Course is ok. Duncun is not. He can be is a cocky rude mood frequently. But deal-able when he's in non-hostile mode.
Designs very difficult exams, but is a very clear and straightforward teacher, if a bit impersonal.

Duncan was awful. He graded harshly (esp final), expected a lot of work, and was clearly discriminating among students. If you get on his good side, you're lucky. If he hates you, your life in ChemE is gonna be hell. I tried talking to him once, and he's really cocky and rude. God bless Mr. Duncan.

Great professor. He expects you to do a lot of work, but if you're willing to make the effort he really cares about helping you succeed. It was a relief to have a professor who treated teaching an intro class as an important job.
really gud prof...one of the best...xtremely helpful...
Very organized and clear, good professor.
Duncan proves that when you respect your students and treat them like adults, they will respect you back and give their utmost effort.
Professor Duncan is truly inspiring and I've learned more from him in the last few months than I have from any other professors!
The chalk!  the chalk!
Awesome teacher, went out of his way to give students tools for sucess
Wonderful teacher, also teaches math 192
The T. Michael Duncan was the best professor I had in the four years I took classes at Cornell.
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
Most organized person in the World!
No Comments
If he can't teach you graphical analysis, your just helpless

One of the worst classes and professors Ive ever had in my life. I honestly dont think he is In teaching to actually teach. The entire class was just pushing out as many assignment as possible. And then when I got something wrong, he would not teach and let me know why, he just said this is not correct, like gee thanks TEACHER

You have to be a fast note taker b/c tons of information on slides that are fine print. No electronics allowed in class! Be on time to every lecture! Try to ask specific or detailed questions as much as you can b/c vague ones don't get accurate answers. Go to office hours frequently to understand structure of assignments as much as possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Better communication skills needed and less words on the lecture slides, so information won't feel overwhelming when trying to take notes in a 50 min class. This class is fairly confusing when it comes to completing assignments. Overall, this class needs better structure and order to provide a more effective learning environment for students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Story time with Corey was one of my favorite experiences at Cornell -- definitely one to take in your senior year then go to Luna's Monday night trivia afterward. Really helped me develop an appreciation and gratitude for my alma mater.
amazing class! corey gives great lectures and multiple fun opportunities for extra credit, definitely recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Literally the easiest A+ you could possibly get at Cornell. Honestly, I felt a little bad throughout the course because since it was so beyond easy, nobody took the course seriously. A few extra mandatory assignments could make the course better in my opinion to keep students engaged. Lectures and professor were great otherwise.

Was an amazing professor. Took this class to lighten up my science heavy semester and boy am I glad that I did. His lectures are interesting and engaging and he gives so much opportunity for extra credit. I highly recommend this class to anyone and everyone.
Fantastic instructor. Never knew there was so much behind the history of the University!

Class is eh. Professor is passionate big whoop! 2 credits and you need to memorize 600 slides worth of content for each prelim, for 5 prelims + a comprehensive final. No structure to exams, they ask random obscure details. If you want a good grade, don't come to this class unless you have photographic memory.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Took BIOMI 3310. He's a great lecturer and really cares about his students, but the course takes a ton of studying for only 2 credits. Exams are 100% of your grade and require you to memorize an insane amount of detail from the lecture slides. He does give bonus points though. Only take this course if you are really passionate about the material.
Overall, really easy class but requires time to rote memorize. Go to class. Memorize slides cold. Get the extra credit points. Get an A+ and pat yourself on the back.

Probably the best professor I've had here. He goes through a lot of material but he makes it wildly interesting. Additionally, he really cares about his students doing well and he goes out of his way to help. Definitely the most interested, interesting, and caring professor I've seen.

Probably the best class I've taken here. Dr. Bowman is extremely interested in what he is teaching and in doing whatever he can to help his students do well. The material isn't easy, but it's wildly interesting and Dr. Bowman makes it fun. I definitely recommend giving this class a try.

Too much information on slides. Slides are poorly organized with no structure to them. Talks too quickly, glosses over topics such that lectures becomes confusing. Exams are difficult and require LOTS of memorization of detail. Final is comprehensive, ridiculous given how many parasites are covered.

Tests are very hard. Have to remember many species and specific details about life cycles, length, location. It is way too much information and detail to remember for each exam.  Too much details on slides, and need to memorize huge amounts of info. Can't cram for exams. Hard exams.

Not an easy class. He is unclear and extremely vague on his tests. Very specific and a too much info needed. Almost impossible to learn it all unless you take other easy classes (which I did not). Easy based on no work but the tests are horrible

Bowman is awesome and makes lecture really interesting and applicable.  I learned so much in this class and am super glad I took it.  Tests are very fair, even though the memorization is kind of a pain.  Study back tests and review guides on blackboard, no need to read the textbook, and you will be fine.

Dr. Bowman is an awesome professor.  He is clearly enthralled with what he teaches, and even makes class interesting with witty descriptions and side stories that pop up every lecture.  Very approachable and makes fair tests.  Study the lectures and review sheets!

Clearly fascinated by what he teaches.  Very approachable and interested in answering questions.  Tests are very fair if you study the lecture material.  Lots of extra credit.  Wants students to do well -he's a good guy.

I love Dr. Bowman!  I work in his lab, and he is the nicest prof ever.  Def come to his dinners b/c he tells the best stories, but bring a friend with you (for potential awkwardness reduction).  I made flashcards for each parasite which seemed to really help me do well on tests.
He has a very good sense of humor that makes even the subject of deadly parasites entertaining to learn.

Engaging and entertaining lecturer, interesting subject material, fair tests. The material would probably be useful for anyone planning to be involved with tropical medicine in any way, though since the best way to do well on the tests is to memorize everything, the amount of information you'll actually retain beyond the course is questionable.
mother ****ing ****....i hated his class so damn much...

Dr. Bowman was awesome!  His classes are fun and informative.  The style was very loose, and you learned a lot but it was easy to get a good grade thanks to extra credit etc.  Definitely recommend him.
No Comments
loved him! loved the class!
Dr. Bowman was one of my favorite professors during my time at Cornell. His lectures were enjoyable and he's a fun person to work with.
he's an awesome professor and very cool.

I love Dr.Bowman.  He's so cool and friendly and personal (but not in an invasive way).  You can contact him 24/7 and he'll answer your e-mails and messages really fast!  I came in 4th place in Zoology wiht him.
Dr. Bowman is a very fair and fun professor usually, though lectures were sometimes a little disorganized.  Heavy use of visuals made it interesting.  Lots of extra credit.

Class is difficult and six hours of lab a week is brutal, but far and away best Professor I've had at Cornell. Knows the entire curriculum by heart, great person with a good sense of humor, and extremely helpful. Lectures can be a bit boring, but office hours and lab are incredibly useful. The most useful class you can take for research.

Prof. Kirkland is quiet which can make staying awake hard but he's a great teacher with a good sense of humor. He's always around during labs and is friendly/non-judgemental if you need extra help. The labs for this class are tedious and grindy, though, so make sure you don't fall behind. Weekly homeworks are short.
Awesome course

Incredibly smart and kind professor. Always has a keen eye for making even the most difficult or confusing concepts understandable; he never treats any question as trivial and always takes time to give a complete answer

Prof. Flanagan taught the advanced undergrad quantum class. 4443 is a mathematically sophisticated and theoretical course. He's a caring professor and 4443 is awesome. He covers topics in graduate quantum including density matrix, tensor products, path integrals and more . Lectures are important because the content isn't encapsulated by one book.

Flanagan turned PHYS4443 into basically GradQuantum1, covering about 80% of Sakurai through his very fast paced and extremely mathematically sophisticated lectures combined with challenging problem sets. Extremely caring professor with a gargantuan brain. Amazingly insightful and interesting class, but be mentally prepared for a baptism by fire.

Flanagan did two classes worth of material, and I am glad that he did: I learned a lot. His arguments are mathematical, offering a different perspective at problems compared to the "physical intuition method". Homeworks were the focus of class (50% of grade); they were tough, but you take a lot out of them.

I LOVED THIS CLASS!!! Made me really excited about Civil Engineering. The class was easy and interesting. Earls is really passionate about the material. Very helpful in office hours. No textbook, a few short homeworks, 1 paper, and a group project in the place of a final. The project was fun and a great way to apply the material. My favorite class.

Lectures were pretty interesting compared to some other classes, but lasted a long time. The homeworks are easy if you go to office hours. I loved this class because the final project was so much fun, and there's no final.

The professor is AMAZING!!There is no textbook so pay attention to the lecture. However, the lecture is so long(over an hour) and there is no light because of the ppt, so you can fall asleep easily even though the lecture is interesting. There're no tests, only easy homework with only 2 or 3 short questions, include one group project and one paper.

Made the class fun and applicable. While he didn't teach too much into the specifics of statics, mechanics, etc, the holistic approach was beneficial to the freshman class of engineers. The final project was superb and everyone had a good time with it

Prof Earls did a good job with steel design. Lectures were very clear and well organized. Earls was always willing to help students. Homeworks really taught me about steel design. Tests were similar to homeworks, not too difficult. I recommend this course for a CEE design requirement. PS he's hot!

Professor Earls did a good job with steel design. His lectures were put together very well and he was always willing to help students. Not too hard, not really easy either. I would recommend this course.
Professor Earls did a good job teaching Steel. I would recommmend this class.
Very kind and helpful professor, happy to meet outside of class, but very easy to understand in class.

FWS: Guts, Ghosts, & Glory was a pretty good writing seminar to take.  We had one or two less essays than most others.  Professor Eaton has her positives and negatives.  While she can provide good feedback and isn't a harsh grader, she tends to think that she's the only one that's right and that writing should only be in her particular style.
No Comments

I didn't really attend a lot of the lectures (cause they were optional) but I thought I'd nevertheless leave a review for the class. The class content was extremely interesting and insightful. Just download the textbook "Networks, Crowds and Markets" and read through some parts. You'll know whether you wanna take this class.

Difficulty of this class made a 180 compared to last year. Practice problems before the two exams were useless as not even 1/3 of the problems made it onto the exam. If you're looking for easy liberal studies and have a rough workload definitely think again. You have to read the textbook and camp office hours, not what I expected for 3 credits.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: i cant believe people thought this course was easy. midterms/finals are so advanced compared to psets and practice exams it was like whiplash. every time i felt like i understood something it got flipped upside down the next chapter or on the exam. i was an office hours warrior and barely passed. genuinely saw someone cry during the final today too

Easley and Kleinberg are the original authors for the textbook and them teaching the class is ABSOLUTELY GOATED. It was extremely eye-opening to hear him share his past experiences and it is obvious that he is extremely intelligent. Also very very kind during office hours. Best class I've ever taken at Cornell -- made me change my way of thinking.
Superb class, extremely applicable, and grading was both fair and unbiased. Anybody saying otherwise has cope levels off the charts, probably because they need to reevaluate their IQ score
AMAZING AND SO CLEAR -- HE MADE THE CLASS CONTENT SO EASY TO UNDERSTAND AND INTERESTING!

Networks gets a bad rap, as I never found it to be that bad. Lectures were clear (sometimes boring), but textbook a great resource if still confused. People got mad at the weekly HWs and they are kinda annoying but I never found them to be too difficult. Easley does his best to make lecture interesting, but the class was a bit forgettable overall

Amazing class and professor! It was a super interesting class, but there is a lot of work. weekly hw assignments that take a few hours to complete, but if you take time and do them well, the tests are easy and straight forward just like the hw.
The lectures are fantastic. The class is not easy but worth taking.

Dr. Easley makes PhD microeconomics clear and easy to understand. He knows the material inside and out and knows how to present it to the class. He is just as helpful outside of class, and is incredibly helpful in office hours. The class wasn't easy, but it was all fair.

Class: Networks. Very organized class. Most people wouldn't show up. It was pretty easy overall. Professor Easley did a great job at getting the content across. The average final grade was an A I think.
He's good at explaining hard to understand concepts in an easy-to-understand manner. Silky, butter-like, rich voice. He would have been a great sports commentator.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: Networks is an easy class. Maybe it was made easy by Easley and Kleinberg's ability to teach, but truthfully I don't think teaching this material would be challenging for anyone. I would love to see what Easley could do in an intense economics course. He seems very smart and very personable.
Very good
Great lecturer and taught mostly from the textbook. The textbook is legally free to download digitally; print copies are $40.
Easley is easily one of the best profs I've had. Really nice guy and very happy to discuss material in office hours.
I prefer Kleinberg but Easley comes really close. Both great lecturers.
great + dedicated

Excellent class, highly recommended! Slow and steady coverage of material, easy, especially if you have prior experience in game theory (I did). Very good explanations of material. Better handwriting than Kleinberg. Easy tests and homework. Free electronic textbook is not necessary unless you don't understand the notes or want to go deeper.
Easley lectures to us as if we're two year olds. Networks is  boring but ridiculously easy. Class is optional because he recites what is in the textbook, verbatim.

there is not much work to do. the test is not very hard, but the grading system is kind of harsh. last year this class was a median A class, but this year I DONT THINK SO.i have pretty good GPA and i got the lowest grade on this class. the material is interesting though. if you are taking this class for GPA booster, think about it again

econ 204 / cs 285 Networks - great class, easy , interesting, little work and little reading to do . easley lectures very clearly, almost painstakingly slow over some material --- not hard to get an A.

This prof is pretty cool but his class is deceptive. It might seem easy at first but things just come like a torrent of information. Stay on top of your material you are almost guaranteed an B+/A-. His lectures are pretty interesting.

Easley is a very capable professor and definitely knows what he's talking about. His lectures were good, although I still slept through/missed a lot. But that's just me. Homeworks are doable and graded easily. Prelims are almost exactly like the example ones he gives you from the previous year.

easley is an amazing prof, one of the best at cornell.  he takes a drab subject and makes it approachable and bearable. the problem sets are hard but they are graded easily, and while the exams are tough, easley's teaching makes up for it.  i highly recommend this class.

Easley is an awesome professor. Period. He is fair. He grades without a curve so the smartasses don't hurt your grade. He tells you exactly how hard the class will be from the start. He has realistic expectations. Lecture is mandatory, but never boring. He's good at giving an intuition for econ.

Great lecturer.. you must attend class. Makes material much easier than it has to be. Willing to work with you, but is very busy (understandable with a 150 person class). Don't take Microecon with anyone other than him.

Easley is an excellent professor. His lectures are very clear and organized, and he uses interesting examples to supplement the sometimes dry material. Exams and problem sets are challening (somewhat) but you get used to it. Almost no understanding of calc is needed, he teaches it all.

This was my first econ class, and I can't praise Easley enough! He had great lectures and was always clear, organized, thoughtful, and provided many examples.  His weekly problem sets were very do-able, although it takes a little getting used to.  Same goes for the exams.  One of the best.

Teaches very well. Comes up with creative examples, and makes the dry material a bit better. As much as this is econ for engineers and calculus is expected, you barely need to understand a derivative.
Extremely helpful and clear, engaging, great professor. Very recommended.
Tough but fair, great instructor (for econ!)
Smooth lectures and fair exams.  A rarity for Cornell!!
great teacher.  great course
I admit that the course is well taught, but I suppose I just don't get economics.  Be aware that this course is DESIGNED FOR ENGINEERS!!!!
The class is deceptive. Everyone seemed to get a lower grade than their grades warranted. Only take the class if you have to, because it kinda blows.
Easley is a very good lecturer, using good examples and always making the material as interesting as it possibly can be. This is way better to take than ECON 313.  Plus, the TA's grade pretty easy.
Very dry. Methodical. Robotic, even.
He makes a difficult, boring subject somewhat easier to handle. The examples are well thought out and makes a topic simpler to grasp.
Seems like a nice guy.  The 75 minute lecture is a little long and gets boring towards the end.  However, he manages to come up with interesing/amusing examples to keep our attention.
clear and precise, great lecture.
Great Chest man!
Gotta love that open shirt!
Great guy
Amazing professor - very useful course due to its relevance to real world necessities.

Wow, Brian was probably the best professor I have ever had at Cornell. He is smart, funny, caring, and basically I could go on and on. The class is not that difficult, just make sure you read the book before the two tests, other than that, enjoy yourself and the lectures! Speeches are a breeze as well. Great job Brian, we love you!
Brian saved my bacon during my years at CU. A great teacher and better advisor and excellent friend. Far too few Brian Earless in higher ed. Highly recommended!
Prof. Earle genuinely cares about his students and his class was the most useful for post-college life!  He's wonderful!
Prof. Earle is awesome. He's funny and understanding, and you'll learn a lot in this class. A must-take before entering the business world! Per his request, I have labeled him as smokin' hot. Yowza!
Brian's the man

I was unexcited about the class at first, but it actually was very useful/valuable. A must for CALS Freshmen, taught by one of the most quality people I've ever met. He was always amazingly understanding, never giving up until he helped students to the best of his ability.

I just thought that this would be a continuation of COMM 201, but it's so much better than that.  His class is about REAL-WORLD stuff that I will never forget (i.e.: interviewing skills)  Really useful class and you enjoy talking to him just try not to mention that you like the Yankees.
the best prof i've ever had.

I was very unenthusiastic about the class at first, but it actually helped me develop study skills and learn a lot about Cornell's history. Very easy A to offset first semester Bio and Chem. Highly recommended.
Prof. Earle cares about his students and he obviously wants them to be able to take the skills and knowledge he imparts on life-long journeys.  He's a darling!
One of the best in the business. Most applicable course to the real world that Cornell offers.
I graduated in 1995, and even back then, Prof. Earle was one of the best at Cornell.  Take his class, it's easy and you'll learn a lot!!!

Not only a great teacher, but also important in the department. He's a large part of the reason I was able to transfer in, and he even eventually became my advisor. When I think about great teachers at Cornell, Brian is one of the first to come to mind.
Very reasonable guy, funny too.
unhelpful oldie
Everybody should take this class... He is very easy and will give you an A no matter what you do. Easy guy to ass kiss to get a good grade
No Comments
No Comments

Fantastic prof. Class can benefit anyone in any field where talking to groups or giving presentations is important. You even learn how to handle business dinners and lunches. Prof goes out of his way to help you if you show effort. A great asset to the Un
Great guy, interesting course.
Pretty easy class... funny guy
Highly recommend if you don't know math. Like me. Got me invested into math as a humanities person.
THE GOAT SWARTZ, I LOVE HIS MOANS

Very good professor who made content very interesting. Class got somewhat difficult after the 1st exam, but it is still a very good class to take if you are interested in higher-level math. Professor really pushes you to think about the concepts more deeply as opposed to simply applying algorithms to solve questions.
Swartz is a strong lecturer. He teaches math the right way. Would take a Math class taught by him any day of the week.
Ed Swartz is the best professor I have ever had. He was a very good lecturer, the lectures were challenging and thoughtful, although a bit scattered, they were always very engaging and interesting.

Swartz is a good professor in general. The class itself is quite easy; to do well in the class, all you have to do is read a couple textbook sections/do the homework once a week, and you can skip the lectures completely. The lectures themselves are a bit dry. The TA's for this class were fantastic - all knowledgeable grad students.
Great Proffesor!

The workload of this class is light. Prof. Swartz is rude and does not seem to care a for his students. His lectures followed a linear though process, but the writing on the board was small and disorganized. It seems, though, that he is one of the professors that I least interacted with since I would learn more the textbook than from his lectures.

Tests are 80% of grade (each prelim is 25%, final is 30%). Brilliant, funny guy, but writes small/messy on the board and talks quietly, so sometimes difficult to follow. Pretty boring too, hard to focus after 40 min. Exams are pretty difficult but doable with office hours and hw. TA's are really good and know what they're talking about.
Good professor with clear lectures and helpful Office Hours. If you didn't understand a concept he would always explain it multiple ways until you got it. I found his psets difficult though
