Never shows his work on how an equation was derived (e.g glosses over/ skips steps for a derivation but will spend 5 minutes explaining P up is V down in PV=nRT), uses unconventional signs, and reads off a script when recording his lecture videos. Overall useless.

Some students like Mueller's class but not me. Recitations/problem solving lectures/labs are unhelpful. Mueller doesn't have office hours, only TAs (few are helpful). Prelectures are surface level and Mueller isn't a good teacher if you haven't taken physics before. Demos are pointless when they could be helpful. However if you study, it's doable.

I've never taken physics before and I owe my doing well to Prof. Mueller's efforts. Read the syllabus before. If you're consistent with pre-lectures, you should be more than fine. Discussion helps a lot with applying the material. Office hours are rly helpful. Labs are easy. Attendance is by PollEv. Practice materials are very accurate/useful.

His online lectures for homework worked really well for me, and then doing problems in class was good. He allowed us to have so many notes for prelims and finals that they turned into a class where you write down the right problems, instead of knowing how to do them. We do spend a lot of time in class for the number of credits though.

Professor Mueller deserves a much higher rating. His class was well taught, and he spent hours preparing all of the pre-lecture videos for us to watch. He is very approachable and engaged us during lecture.

It was a pretty heavy workload. Mueller participated in flipped class where we had the lecture recorded before class and then in person was problem solving to practice concepts. We were allowed to bring in 5 pages of notes for each prelim which was helpful since we could write down anything we wanted on it. If you put in the work you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Had a great introductory physics course experience with Prof. Mueller. There was plenty of practice questions and office hours with the teaching staff available to help with the material. Tried his best to make accommodations as needed for the class and appreciated his effort to run the class as smoothly as possible.

May as well have taken auto tutorial physics if the only way I was gonna learn was through pre lec anyways. Did not care about the mental health of his students and rarely (if at all) made accommodations for us. I mean a man with a gun was running around campus and we still had to take the quiz? Seems cruel and unnecessary.

I loved Erich as a lecturer; he very much cared about the topics and he always had fun demos to show us from his home. He taught us everything we needed to know in lecture and the prelim I took was very fair. The final was the only reason to dislike him. It was designed to be impossible and it was. This was prob because of online format.

I took this class fall of 2020. It was his first time teaching, but it was supposed to be lecture based, but it was anything but this. We had weekly modules, including multiple videos and readings. We were going at a fast rate at almost 1.5-2 chapters of the book per week. It was so hard to keep up. The 1st prelim was easy, but the final was bad.

Would not take him ever again. The final exam was designed for you to fail and stress you out (why even study then??), class structure was just way too complicated and extra. Not receptive to student feedback, TAs even were frustrated. The class was asynchronous but at times felt like a whole full-time job. The subject wasn't terrible, but he was.

Never take this class with him. He did not listen to students when we complained and instead blamed it on us. The TAs are also overworked as hell and in the beginning, they didn't even respond to our own concerns and questions. He seems passionate about his subject but tbh he killed any interest I had in physics.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly the most awful experience I've had with a class at Cornell. He was extremely unaccommodating during the pandemic and barely listened to students who complained that the exams and grading schemes were completely unfair. They posted the (very low) final exam grades on Christmas morning with no explanation or grade distribution. Awful.

Erich is really caring. It's easy to see how much effort he puts into his teaching.  He holds extra office hours, attends both of the discussion sections, and has entertaining lectures. Talking to other people in the class, it was clear that nearly everyone loved him and the class itself.

Overall excellent guy. He clearly put a ton of effort into the class. I definitely enjoyed it, but some of the more advanced "applications" of QM went over my head because we went through them so quickly.
Mueller is a good, but not great lecturer. However, he is fantastically helpful outside of class, and clearly cares about making sure his students grasp the material he teaches.

Mueller is very sloppy at times, but overall he puts a ton of effort into the course. He really cares about his role as a teacher and is always looking to help with whatever when possible. Clarity can be an issue on occasion. This class covers a potpourri of topics in QM. Expect something different in each lecture. There are labs, HW, and handouts.

Lectures aren't terrible, but the tests are ridiculous. Roughly 70% of the exams are multiple choice, which sucks because there's no partial credit for most of the test questions. Plus, sometimes the responses aren't just A-D or whatever, they're A-Q so the answers given aren't helpful in any way.

Mueller is very enthusiastic.  He seems to really love what he does.  However, he does not do a good job in preparing students for exmas or teach them a ton about physics.  I had to do a lot of outside reading/work in order to keep up.

Lectures are very disorganized and hard to follow - read the text book and make sure you really understand the concepts.  Make sure you go to lecture too because a lot of stuff from lecture shows back up on the prelims and final.

Your standard mechanics class.  Prof overly excited about the topic, but lecutres remained tedious nonetheless.  Standard physics department style of using 3 overhead projectors for lecture, and demos are less than interesting.  Read the book, do your homework, and the class is easy.
You should probably understand physics before you take this class with him as the prof. He tried to teach and attempted to be interesting, but was not really successful. Need a good TA.

Disorganized lecture, would be better off skipping and reading the textbook, learned mostly from Tbook and HW.  Overly excited and demands class participation on elementary topics (This just makes lectures go slow).  Tests fair with some long, involved questions.  Do your HW and study, try the 012 (Lieberman is great) you will do fine on the tests

One of the worst profs I've had to date. His lectures, homework, labs, and readings had nothing to do with each other. The tests were mostly taken from the labs and the really random and pointless examples he did in class. Write them down, or at least wake up for them. Thats the only reason most people went to lecture. Avoid him if possible.

real nerdy, tests are fair, not a hard class, some of the TAs are weird. try and take notes in lecture eventho u will always think that it is pointless because he uses a lot of it on tests and its not in the book

Hated this class and this professor. She has a very heavy accent and terrible handwriting. Her lectures would be her just doing proofs but not explaining why she did any of the steps she did and she would just read out what she was writing. Lectures were completely useless and made this awful class even worse. Textbook and OH saved my grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: If you can avoid any professor at Cornell, please avoid her.

Largely incomprehensible, despite good intentions. Lecture attendance mandatory, but unhelpful. All grading was given to the TAs, turning every single assignment and exam into a game of regrade requests. Believes that if you explain a concept loudly, it will magically make more sense. 
Enjoyed discrete math in HS, will avoid it at all costs now.

Compared to Halpern, her lectures were clear and easy to understand, and PollEvs were really helpful for engagement. Exams were very fair. I didn't talk to her during office hours, but at least in lecture, her blunt attitude was not a problem.

Worst professor I've ever had. Her lectures are unintelligible and filled with errors, making it harder to follow than the material itself, total waste of time. One time I went to office hours and she was extremely rude. On the last day, she straight up insulted students who made mistakes on previous exam. I could go on. Completely unprofessional.

lectures are well done, definitely attend to make sure you understand the content. expect to spend a lot of time on the homework if you want to do well, putting in time for the homework pays off on the tests. tests are pretty fair, similar to the homework.

Does a great job explaining topics and working examples during class. Encourages feedback at the time and goes as far as to say email me for extra HW points if you correct a mistake during the lecture. Very helpful and understanding outside of class too. Accent is really not an issue as some have mentioned, definitely not a turnoff by any means.

She is well known in the community and places students well and knows her stuff. But she is kinda bitter to talk to. She isn't the most pleasant easy going person who is happy with her life. She can be acerbic and rude.

The assignments were hard at times but not unreasonably so. The textbook was written by Tardos (and others) specifically for this course, and the explanations are outstanding. The exams are manageable since the questions are similar to homework questions.

Professor Tardos is not a very clear speaker due to her heavy Hungarian accent. However, she is very willing to reexplain anything she says during lecture. Sometimes, she will gloss over material that she thinks you know, but, again, she will clarify anything needed. The homeworks are pretty easy; however, they can be poorly written and confusing.

pretty decent prof. A little confusing at times, but very approachable and willing to help. However, her Homeworks are frustrating, as many problems are vague/poorly worded. Overall decent/pretty easy class.

Worst professor at Cornell, can barely understand what she is saying and the problem sets were so terribly written and difficult to understand. I felt like it was an easy class that I just could not understand at the same time. I was much more confused after listening to lecture than before it. Terrible class, worst I have ever taken. Hate it.
Overall decent teacher. Somewhat unclear at times in lecture, but very friendly/approachable/nice person.
I really like her. She knows her material very well and she is extremely helpful during her office hours. She also seem to be very concern about students' well being as well.

Seems like she might know the material, but is very bad at teaching it. Isn't clear in lecture, and is bad at being precise a lot of the time on both homework questions and on examples, which is bad for a course that is in large part a logic course. Sounds like she's better in the higher courses.
A good teacher once you get used to her accent and handwriting.  Very willing to help students during her office hours.
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments

ENGRI1190. Weekly homework. TA office hours were helpful. Prof. Donnelly is very kind and understanding. Two prelims and a final group presentation. Prelims were very similar to practice prelims. Study sheet was permitted to take to the prelims.
The course is curved to a B+. The final is a group project. TA Eric is great, highly recommend office hours with him.

Just average. Good person, lectures were pretty boring. Grading rubrics were not straightforward, even for some prelims. Still, not difficult and final project instead of exam. Doesn't give A+ (even for students who earn 98-100), annoying for ENGRI course
Amazing and understanding professor!

He literally made up all the concepts in the class so you can't really find any additional study material online. He is an amazing lecturer though so you probably should go to class because his slides are purely images and have no text.

Gary is the kindest professor I have had so far, and he is extremely knowledgeable about the topics we learned. The class itself is easy if you just show up to lectures and study the questions that he gives in advance for the tests. He is also very helpful during office hours and has even offered to meet outside them. I wish only the best for Gary.

Great professor who excels at presenting his expertise to the general student body. Active listening and detailed notes are key to doing well; slides are not very detailed. Material is interesting and taught at an Ivy caliber, so it's very important to pay attention. Very receptive to student needs & accommodations. Really changes your thinking!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Evans is one of the best professors I have ever had the privilege of learning from. His lectures are always engaging and I am still impressed that he does them without any notes. Even if your major has nothing to do with this class you should take it because he makes it so interesting and he is such a smart and caring person.
The best professor I've met at Cornell. Take this class whatever your major is (I'm in engineering) and you'll love it. Inspiring, caring, and just have love for the human kind. God bless Gary.
Very interesting class- you must attend lecture to do well but it is very worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's very straight to the point. You are given 10 questions and 5 are on exams. Projects are very fair (abt like 2-3?) a semester. Overall very good lecturer. If you go to class and take solid notes, it's an easy A class.

100% necessary to attend class. MAKE FRIENDS! YOU NEED OTHER PPLS' NOTES TO SURVIVE. lectures are genuinely interesting and i liked attending, but u have to pay attention and take notes the whole time. really passive aggressive in emails but it's fine because it's a big class and he wont remember u. no words on slides, u might want to record class

I hated this class, but Prof. Evans was alright. The actual material is SO outdated and sometimes just blatantly wrong. The class would be so much easier if he put any words on the slides or recorded the lectures. I went to every lecture but still would have gaps in my notes. He gives you the questions that will be on the prelim, so they aren't bad
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: pretty easy, go to lectures, very nice prof who was clearly passionate and willing to clarify,
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: His lectures are interesting, but slides are only pics so you HAVE to go for notes. barely any homework, except the readings (optional). The projects are kind of annoying. For prelims, you get 10 questions ahead of time, 4 are on the prelim. The q's have part a,b,c and he looks for specific answers. Go to office hours! Its a minimal effort A.

Kinda overrated class. He doesn't put any words on the lecture slides, so you're forced to go to lecture. The content is pretty much all common sense, but you have to know his made-up vocabulary to understand what's going on. It's a very easy class though since there's barely any homework and you get the prelim questions before the test.
Very few classes at Cornell where just showing up, taking half decent notes and reviewing (verbatim) questions for exams gets you an A- at least

- attendance not mandatory but you pretty much have to come to each lecture to effectively prepare for classwork/exams
- assignments are easy points, it's very hard to do poorly
- offers extra credit
- gives the exam questions beforehand, you have to prepare before the actual exam for the questions using notes/OH
- always regrade! TAs r everywhere

if you like lecture-based classes and take good notes this class is perfect. if you like cramming right before the exam, not paying attention during lectures, and teaching yourself the material (me) this class is extremely difficult. grading is really varied too which is frustrating. just not for me
Good professor and a great person. He truly cares about his students. The prelims are short-answer based and there are a few writing/design assignments.

i did the extra credit without realizing that it didn't contribute to getting A+ but that's fine. He's very nice and holds lots of office hours which were very useful to the prelims. His presentation notes aren't very good so you pretty much have to show up for class

Great class. Would definitely recommend! Prof.Evans is very friendly, and his lectures are engaging. However, make sure you download the lecture outlines and organize your notes accordingly, because he does not always mention explicitly which section he is in so you could get lost. Grading is very fair. Go to office hours and you can surely get A!

Professor Evans is such a great professor. The material in this class is super interesting no matter what your major is. The work is very manageable. It's clear that Professor Evans loves teaching, and he is very kind person and wants his students to succeed.
Fantastic professor. Very interesting and relevant material. Always willing to help out students!
Elite... that's all.
I was genuinely interested in the topics that he covered. As long as you fill out the practice questions for the prelim ahead of time you should do well in this class.

Very interesting class. Dr. Evans is accessible and truly cares about his students. Grading is very fair, but not an "easy A" class. You have to work on things thoroughly and ahead of time to make sure you get all the points. Some people don't do this and underestimate the workload. Then they get points off and think the grading is harsh.
Professor Evans is a fantastic lecturer and you can tell he really cares about his students. Highly recommend!

I can't rave about Gary enough. He is extremely caring and accommodating to students. He has no problems with giving extensions. The class itself is pretty easy. If you went to lecture and took good notes, exams should be a breeze, but still pretty time-consuming. Assigned readings aren't necessary to get an A. The class material is also very cool.

I really enjoyed the lectures, but the exams were extremely intense and graded toughly (despite questions being released ahead of time). The TAs are tough graders too when it comes to the projects. This would have been one of my favorite classes if the exams were not as excessive/detailed. The professor is really insightful.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very straightforward and easy class. Lots of opportunity for extra credit (with SONA), and the rubric is very clear. Going to lecture is pretty important as his slides/slide summaries aren't very informative on their own. He's a very engaging and good lecturer though, and it's very clear he knows what he's talking about.

Absolutely a great class. Makes you think beyond simple principles and forces you to apply your understanding to real world, environmental examples. Prof. gives ten essay questions before the test, and the tests consists of four of the ten, randomly given. Very very fair, and the class makes sure that you understand the material. Tons of extracredt

Gary Evans is a wonderful professor. He really loves teaching and is very willing to talk to outside of class. The tests, however, are a series of incredibly specific questions that are given out a few weeks before the test. Prof. Evans does hours of prelim review, which is essential for doing well because in grading he looks for specific answers.

Evans is such a nice guy. Go to lecture, pay attention, and you will breeze by with an A. Distributes ample exam questions well before tests - answer them thoroughly, because he picks 4-5 of them of the 8-10 given to place on the exam. Don't buy readings, just take notes in class. Tests feel long, but if you answered the ?s beforehand it's easy.

I took an economics class with the allegedly distinguished professor Evans. When I had received a puzzling low mark on an assignment, I had asked him for Office Hours, where he repeatedly made clear he only takes students alone. When I had arrived, he seemed very distracted and was constantly jingling change in his pocket. Unprofessional boomer

Gary is an amazing professor and his teaching style has really contributed to making my life simpler. You have to go to lecture or make sure you know someone who takes good notes because his slides are hard to understand if he doesn't explain them. His grading system is fair and office hours are a very beneficial. Also make sure to ask questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Evans is a great lecturer - I took this for a distribution requirement and loved it. Just make sure you go to lecture and take good notes, he encourages to use group effort to prepare for all exams and all answers to 10 essay questions are covered in lecture. No need for any readings, so don't buy them! Just go to class, and listen:)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Took this class not knowing anything prior about the subject to for credit requirement. Lectures were really interesting. Pay attention during them because slides won't really help much and office hours before prelims are packed. love his prelim system, and the extra credit helps a lot. Dont be afraid to approach him before class!! fun guy
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: DO NOT buy the required textbook material. Don't need to do readings to get an A go to lecture and write down examples for exam. You get possible 10 questions on exam and 4 are actually on it. If you go to office hours he literally goes through them and gives you answers & you can do psych studies for 20 points of extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Evans is amazing! His slides are easy to understand and he makes them so applicable to our lives! The class is interdisciplinary and very interesting, and his method of preparing students for exams is really effective and shows that he cares. Definitely recommend!

Don't expect to be able to ask your TAs about making anything clearer before tests or projects; they aren't responsible for grading, and some (if not all) of them don't even go to class. Gary Evans is a fine lecturer (if he would just put some words in his slideshows instead of just pictures every now and again), but the class is disorganized.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: LOVED this class and Professor Evans. Such interesting material that changed the way I think about the world around me. The readings aren't necessary, but they're interesting. Taking thorough notes in lecture will give you everything you need to do well on tests and projects.

Professor Evans is very helpful and clear in lectures. His lectures are engaging and usually interesting. His tests are not too bad but sometimes his TAs grade a bit harshly. Professor Evans is very helpful in his office hours and very fair. He has done a lot of famous research and written several books but he is very humble in class.

This is an interesting, low-stress course that gives you a language to think about the environment in. Gary is helpful, exams are fair, and projects are relaxed. The one frustration was that many studies seemed vague or even outdated. We needed to think about fewer studies in more depth rather than brush over sketchy data.

This class is great for anyone interested in design, human behavior, or a little self-reflection. TAs grade prelims kind of harshly, but you can easily make up for it with the projects and attendance grade. DO THE EXTRA CREDIT; it will help a lot. Overall, good lecturer, VERY interesting class.

The only redeeming aspect of this course is that attendance is not required.  Gary Evans is a nice human being, but shockingly stupid.  Class is rampant with overgeneralizations, confusion of correlation and causation, and old, weak data.  If you wish to become a more critically thinking person, do not take this course.

Class is very interesting for anyone. Assignments aren't hard. Tests are doable, but sometimes the TAs grade too harshly. After one exam, I got a pretty low grade and asked the TAs why I lost certain points. They couldn't explain some to me, so I went to Evans and he offered to meet with me for 2 hours going over each little point. Recommended.

Talks about things that really make sense and can be applied to everyday life but are still unique and insightful. Great for anyone interested in design, and for anyone just interested in how people of different cultures and in different settings interact with their environments.

Gary is a great lecturer, very insightful and fun to just sit back and listen to. You can do pretty well without doing the reading, but the readings are actually pretty interesting and you end up getting a LOT more out of his lectures if you've done the readings beforehand. Also he's very approachable and great to talk to.

Tests are very lengthy and may be only 4 short essay questions, but each question has an 1a, 1b, 1c, 1d, 1e, 1f, etc, so really it's like answering 30 q's. Wish I were kidding. you really have to prepare, & even then it doesn't guarantee you'll do well. Take the WIM section. it reduces the test grades to only 25% of your grade. Much easier that way

Professor Evans is a clear lecturer, is interesting, and is very helpful in his office hours (especially in that he has many many office hours near prelim times).  The tests are short essays, but you are given a bank of essay questions (4/10 questions chosen) before hand, which is nice :).
Professor as extraordinarily unprofessional, took far too long to get back to us when asking questions, and all in all provided for an overly stressful semester. Would not recommend.

I feel like Cornell keeps the Engineering Communications requirement just to keep Rick Evans employed. This is the most useless course I've ever taken at Cornell. Makes you read and cite a simple-minded "book" written by an unknown SJW "writer". Also, a very self-important and arrogant individual, for seemingly no reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Rick means really well but the class is just so dull. He reads off of his own handouts, which have very little added value to begin with, all the time, making the classroom environment feel very dull. I would not recommend. Especially for seniors this class is an absolute waste of time.

So here's the deal. It's easy to get into the habit of being annoyed by Rick. He gives a LOT of handouts that he reads to you, and then some of his discussions are boring. But Rick wants you to learn something, through his lectures and through the project he assigns. If you put in work on the project, and participate in class, you'll get an A.

Rick is a nice guy and helpfup. However, his classes were ridiculously pointless. He spends each class giving students 2-4 handouts then reading them word for word, as if we couldn't read. He talks about genres and abstract things, then gives you assignments he has told you nothing about. The material is easy but he is BORING. Waste of my tuition.

Professor Evans is a great professor. He is extremely helpful with anything a student might need help with and always very enthusiastic. I learned a great deal in this class about project teams and communication skills that I know will be helpful for future pursuits. The grading was very easy and fair and the workload wasn't bad at all.
This class was an enormous waste of my tuition money.

Rick is a great guy who really cares about his students. The workload is really not THAT bad, and he is a very easy grader. I was originally in Sharon Ahler's technical writing course and it was far more difficult than Rick's. Full marks for this professor.

This class is the most worthless class I have ever taken in my whole life!!!!!! I completely did not learn any single thing in this class. I just took it to fulfill my major requirement. I regret taking this class.
No Comments

The class is not that much work. However you have to do an observational study of an organization that will take up a LOT of time, especially towards the end of the semester when you have to write up a thesis and do a presentation. So basically all the work is at the end. The class is pretty boring.

The best thing to happen to me during my time at Cornell was taking Cooch's classes. Honestly, he's the best thing in the E and S major, and with him retiring from teaching, there won't be a lot to recommend it.  Unless you like humanties and social science stuff. If you like strong quantitative training, look elsewhere.

Best prof ever. Unfortunately retired. Still any of his classes (NR3100, NR4100, NR4120, NR4601), are must takes for those studying ecology and conservation. Some of these classes may disappear, but the ones that stay I highly recommend taking.
Awesome. sad to see him go .

Best professor I've had at Cornell. Period. Explains things more clearly than any other instructor - truly interested in your learning the material. I can't say enough good things. Only bad thing is, I learned recently he's retiring from teaching soon. Take his classes while you can. Not sure what the major will look like when he hangs them up.

Well, I just finished my career at Cornell, and the highlight was definitely the classes I took with Evan Cooch. It is so obvious that he is here for us, lowly students, and not for his own career or research. Unfortunately, he is the exception to the usual rule. I just heard he won't be teaching much longer. Take his classes while you can.

Cooch is a model professor. His class was very well organized. It has some difficult content, but it is presented in a way that encourages learning. He has taught this subject for 20+ years and he is still on top of his teaching game.

I took all 3 of Cooch's classes (there are now 4 he teaches). Easily the best classes I took at Cornell. He can take the most complcated idea, and make it cool, and simple. He should probably win every teaching award, but because he doesn't do the Ivy League professor thing (at all...), probably never will. Too bad, because he should.

Best professor I've ever had at Cornell. None of the ivy league bs. Appears to be very tough and intimidates you in the first class, but is actually a very caring and passionate prof. Office hours very helpful. He sends you all the lecture notes, very detailed and thorough.

Thought I'd hate this class (took it to satisfy a quant requirement), but turned out to be the best class I had that term. Evan is amazing. I bombed the mid-term, but with his help (and the army of TA's he has), pulled it up to a decent A-. If you ever want to see someone teach because they want to, not because they have to, take Evan's class.

Cleares, most engaged instructor I've ever had. Had him for several classes a few years back. Takes super-complex ideas and teaches them in a way so by the time you're done, you think its the easiest stuff in the world. He pretty well gave up his big-time research to teach, because he thought that was more important than being a big star.

The best. I took 3100 first, and then about everything else Cooch teaches. Now that I've been in grad school for a while (ok, more than a while) I realize how criticall Cooch's classes were in getting me here. In fact, I still use his notes, which are clearer than the stuff I look at in my 'grad classes'.
I took his 3100 and then 4120, both were well-taught and useful.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Best professor I've had at Cornell. Best class. Evan is a master at explaining things. Has a good sense of humor also.

This guy wants you to succeed and can tell who doesn't show up to class. He can seem very intimidating but he is incredibly understanding and is open to helping you out in office hours. Honestly the best professor I took that semester and I went back to take more classes with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Best prof I ever had. Period. Here is a tip, though. Take his 3100 class early - second or third year. That sets you up to take his upper level classes, which are a straight path to grad school . If you take 3100 late, you won't have that option.

wonderful! you will learn so much! he is one of the best professors at Cornell. You will not leave his class without knowing more about ecology, population dynamics, wildlife, etc. TAKE HIS CLASSES!!!
Took a few classes with Cooch. The best. Dedicated to teaching, and to your understanding the material. Can play hard ass, but is actually very forgiving when 'real life' gets in the way.

Great class, great professor. One gripe is that he will not even consider regrading a paper or giving points back. Tough love kind of thing, but amazingly frustrating if you have answered all questions correctly and still did not receive full marks.
Amazingly clear, and the best teacher I experienced at Cornell. Cooch got me into grad school, and this class was one reason.  If Cooch teaches *any* class, take it.

Most unusual prof I've ever had. Amazingly clear, most awesome lecture notes ever (better than a textbook), and absolutely no connection to what I would have imagined for an Ivy League professor. Exams were tough, but fair. TA was a saint. One of the best profs, and best classes, I took at Cornell.

Thought I would hate this class, but turned out to be the best class I've taken in a while. I suspect real 'math geeks' will hate Evan's approach, but for me (hated calc), he was a savior. Still don't know how useful this stuff will be, but it was a fun class.

Hardest class I've ever taken. best class I've ever taken. Scariest prof I've ever had. best prof I've ever had. Now I get the rep of this class. I did really poorly on the mid-term, by Cooch prodded, cajoled, and helped me learn the material, and get an A. He is so anti-typical prof as to be unreal.

Best prof I have ever had at Cornell. Would take more classes with Evan, but they conflict with my schedule. Demanding, funny, very fair. Almost perfect evaluation system (regular assignments that are super helpful), and unlimited time exams.
Ever wonder what it would be like to take a class with someone who doesn't care what anyone thinks, so long as you learn? Evan is that kind of teacher. Cornell must hate him, but thats good for us.

Best prof I ever had. This was not an easy course, but it was so well taught, and I learned so much, it was worth the amount of time (a lot!) I spent on it. Only offered every other year. Take it if you can.
Hard to describe -- great at explaining complex and abstract ideas (really good), but can be a bit abrasive (if you're not into his style of 'humor'). Very fair grading system.

I only took this class because it was required, but I'm so glad I did. Evan is unlike any other prof (in fact, you might have trouble believing he's a professor at a snooty Ivy League school). Does the best job of explaining abstract ideas of any prof I've ever had. And he's pretty damned funny in the process.
Best. Prof. Ever. Took a subject that is abstract and a bit 'dry', and turned it into my favorite class so far at Cornell. He actually likes teaching!

Very nice and entertaining. Class is not very useful - you can just read through his crystal clear lecture notes. Exams can be somewhat challenging because he gives you problems that you've never seen before so you have to really by able to apply what you've learned. BUT gives unlimited time on the exams and is very generous with partial credit.

Co-taught with Tom Gavin when I took it. Cooch is like having a class with Henry Rollins (Gavin was Jimmy Buffet). Awesome. Who knew that matrix models could be cool? If you want to now how high-level consbio works, take this class.

Took both 310 and 410 a few years back - still the best classes I took in NTRES. Evan's lecture notes (more a text than notes) are still what I rely on as a grad student. Wasn't much interested in 'quantitative' things when I took the courses, but Cooch got me hooked (even though he makes fun of fish - my study organism). The best...
Scared me to death at first. Basically flunked the midterm, but he never stopped encouraging me, and helped whenever I asked. Ended up with a B. Evan is great.
Cooch is by far my favorite professor at Cornell. Take any class you can get with him, work hard, and you won't regret it!

I echo the last comment - Cooch is awesome. When I was a student at Cornell, I took all of his classes. He is the person who is basically responsible for getting e into grad school. He has this kack for explaining really complex things in very simple ways. It wasn't until I got to grad school that I realized (i) how much material that normally isn'

Great class - I'm not a 'math person', but Evan is pretty much a master at explaining fairly complex stuff in very accessible language (he should teach a class to the math profs here on how to do it). Even manages to be pretty funny (most of the time), which given the subject is no small feat. About the only class this term I never wanted to miss.
Class is ok. I don't see when in my life I will use anything I learned in this class. Just took it because it is mandatory. Evan is a nice guy once you get to know him and he's a fair grader.
No Comments

Everything is through Aplia, so international students need a US VPN. Every assignment was time-consuming & nothing like the test. The textbook was useless. 70% of the grade was based on 2 tests. Multiple choice questions were ok, but the essay questions were time-consuming & tough. The comments he gave on them were vague, unrelated, & confusing.

Yeah, the person who said Evans is the "best" is obviously lying because Cornell doesn't offer Economics as a minor. He's not clear at all, spends 20 minutes every class trying to impose his political views instead of teaching the material. Don't take econ with him, you'll be screwed and unprepared for harder econ courses.

Whoever wrote the comment below is in bed with this guy. He's not clear at all when he teaches and at 100mph. No one knows what's happening because he lectures WHILE writing so if you copy the notes you're screwed and if you just listen you're also screwed. He also asks a lot of annoying questions on his tests that don't really test your knowledge

CLEARLY THE BEST PROFESSOR AT CORNELL. I was lucky enough to have him twice in my college career, and I wish I could have taken more of his classes. He is CRYSTAL CLEAR and very knowledgeable. He knows how to teach. After taking his economics classes, I decided to minor in economics because I loved them so much.
Best teacher I have had at Cornell so far. Very clear, very knowledgeable, and very fair.  Overall great guy.
SUCH A GREAT TEACHER AND CLASS

Threw out the syllabus schedule after day 1, changed his attendance policy to reward EC to students with perfect attendance when there was only 1 month left of class, and reweighted completed assignments to be worth significantly more after cutting out a project that we didn't do yet. Graded VERY arbitrarily and very disorganized, don't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall, I felt the class was fair and improved my public speaking through the different assignments. Instructions can be slightly unclear, but as long as you talk the TA and the professor, and try to apply his technics into your presentations you should be good. Participation is key
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Really not bad at all, everyone is being dramatic. Definitely a good amount of busy work and not super clear grading metrics, but if you can write and speak, you will be fine I promise
He is passive aggressive in a manner that is unbefitting of a professor. Avoid him like the plague. Take any other professor.
This guy is my least favorite professor. The other comments are completely true so I won't regurgitate what they said. AVOID AVOID AVOID
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He gets mad when people use the bathroom. He gave no instructions on how to do assignments but graded extremely harshly and very subjectively. No clear grading structure. For someone whose whole teaching philosophy is being clear and concise, he is the furthest thing from that. He has no empathy and is painful to talk to, to say the very least.

Professor Estad may have been one of my least favorite teachers I have ever had. He is the least personable human I have ever encountered. Talking to him is a chore as he demonstrates no emotion. He teaches the class like we are middle schoolers, but when it comes to grading he is obscenely harsh. Whatever you do DO NOT take his class.

He is very strict with students attending lecture ON TIME WITH ICLICKER. If you show up 2min late you might as well go back to bed because you would have missed the iclicker. His lectures are extremely boring and homework are harder than what he expects in the lecture. His instructions are confusing and his jokes are lame too....
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Really enjoyed Evans lectures. Study for the tests by reviewing the homeworks closely. A lot of people say that his office hours are confusing. Always clear where you stand compared to others due to his clear grading criteria with distributions for every homework and prelim. Appreciated his organization skills.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I. hated. this. class. He took an intro level course and turned to to something way too complicated. Little to no use of the textbook, and dont bother trying to study from it. Nearly the whole grade was based on two tests. Essay questions were super confusing and feedback was even worse. A lot of hard work but it didnt matter.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: about 3/4 of the grade was on two tests. multiple choice is not bad. short answer was really tough (even though you study) and comments on answers were unrelated, vague, and still confusing as to why you got it wrong. we didnt use the textbook. graded it tough, no extra credit. a ton of work and assignments, but it was barely 1/4 of my grade.
go to class and do your homework and you will be fine

Ok, Tom knows how to teach an Intermediate Micro class. For a subject that I thought I wasn't very interested in, he managed to be extremely engaging and clear in every lecture. He starts each class in the morning by playing music and then tells a news story related to a concept we are learning about that day. Not an easy class, but enjoyable.

An interesting class. Applies a lot of models and learning to the real world. The professor is clear in his explanations- homework follows what is taught in class, but is surprisingly tougher. It's probably the most challenging part of the class, but if you can do the homework then the prelims are very manageable.

Probably one of the greatest professors ever. Great lectures, mad chill. Homeworks are pretty straightforward and they're pretty easy to finesse. Exams are straightforward. Tom Evans is a great lecturer, he constantly engages the class in thoughtful discussions and he's pretty funny too. Overall a great class, Tom Evans deserves a teaching award.
Evans is really thoughtful and caring. He goes out of his way to help students. Class is challenging but really satisfying when you understand. It takes hard work but totally manageable.

Lectures are excellent and engaging.  Material is delivered at a very quick pace.  Professor Evans was helpful, responsive and encouraged me not to quit, and I'm grateful for that.  Verbiage on exams doesn't match text verbiage, so understanding problems from the text isn't always helpful.  Exams are crazy hard, but he curves.  Survival mode.

Class is overall straight forward concepts and professor is kind and funny. He does his best to bring real world stats into class, but the big downside is that he is not good at slowing down to explain the mathematical process. This makes the tests real rough. People were crying after the first prelim. Good professor teaching a too-hard intro class

Took PAM 2000 in Spring 2014. I really liked him as a professor. He definitely will present his biases on things, but loved how we opened every class with discussion. He wrote fair exams and homework and genuinely care about students.  One of the best professors I have had here. I would recommend any course that he teaches.

Evans had interesting lectures and generated discussion, but never clearly told us what we needed to know. He graded HW for accuracy but when he went over answers in class after, he often concluded that even he didn't know the right answer. Overall, interesting lectures but poor structure
very passionate and it come through in his teaching

Evans is a good professor. He teaches everything in a clear manner, and incorporates useful real world examples. The only problem with him is that he drinks the free market limited government no taxes juice too much. His views are  short sighted and I don't think he thinks critically enough. Might just be a problem with economists in general though

Great Prof. Lectures were extremely interesting to attend. Not an easy prof though. Tests aim to see how well well you apply what you learned, not just knowledge vomit. Graded pretty fairly, and curved fairly too. I thought I was on the verge of B+ A- but got an A? This class is not easy but not too hard either.

This class was a struggle for me. It didn't help that this was Prof. Evans' first time teaching PAM Stats. Prelim 1 was ridiculous, Prelim 2 and the final were fair, and going to his office hours sort of helped. The curves were also fair, because without them a lot of us wouldn't have passed. Never again, though.

Exams can be unfair because there's no partial credit, and he makes mistakes in mathematics often. Also, going to office hours help, but only if you can withstand his condescending tone. Otherwise willing to help and his exam percentage policy is pretty fair. Exams can be long though, just pace yourself.

He is a great lecturer. You never need the textbook - his notes are fantastic as well as his problem sets. His exams are tough but he curves them a lot so everyone does ok in the end. If you study his notes and problem sets though you'll end up doing well (with the curve of course.)
A fine man. I would love to take another class with him. Engaging. Funny. He made you think critically about economics.

Very good prof. Understandable, friendly, interested that the class understands what's going on (both the subject and applicable current events). Can be a hassle that attendance is mandatory, but usually worth it
Tom is a great guy.  He is reasonable and very understanding.  Best professor I have had so far at Cornell!
awesome econ professor....clear, accessible, and curves tremendously

Tom is great guy. I thought he was funny and he always made the lectures interesting. Prelims were unreasonably hard, but the curve is generous. If you have to take introductory microeconomics, take it with him.
Clear, willing to help students learn, gives extra sessions for struggling students, will address current economic conditions.

Evans is so wonderful. His class is so interesting, he is so smart, an so excited to share his thoguhts with the class. He makes great class discussions and is the best teacher I've had yet at Cornell.

Evan's is a great lecturer. He's very entertaining and always teaches exactly what you need to know. I never read the textbook and I did well. The homework problem sets are difficult, but if you understand them, you'll do fine on the exam. Go to a discussion section or some form of office hours if you have problems and you'll get an A.

Great Prof. Insane prelims, though he finally curved them and also curved the grade distribution (i.e. an 85= A-) b/c people did so poorly on the prelims. He is understanding and more than willing to help out. Take advantage of his office hours, they are great. He is a true genius but doesn't understand not everyone else is

Tom Evans is an amazing teacher. He makes every lecture interesting on some level, and his graphs and powerpoints are always very helpful. He's also just a really funny guy who tells good stories and bizarre examples that you'll be talking about after class.
No Comments

Class is far above "intermediate economics". Evans is clearly a genius but he's not very good at getting his points across. His lectures lack direction, are confusing, and he thinks it's funny that his students do not understand the material. I'd recommend taking PAM 200 with another professor.

Dr. Esposito, or Alex as he prefers to be called is genuinely one of the best Professors I've taken in my college career. Doing research in his class was great and he is always down to talk about your work or just chat about what's going on in your life. If you get the opportunity take his class.
Professor Big Purr is very good at illegal screens
Super chill, had applied ethics FWS!
Applied Ethics FWS Fall 22. Amazing course with great in class discussions, a great, flexible, and chill guy.
was a chill guy

Super sweet guy and tries his best to put energy into the class. I never had to worry abt the class, the homeworks are straight from lecture +he even hints on half the topics on the test. Only thing in take advantage of the cheat sheet for the test! The test goes pretty in depth, but a breeze if u just put it on ur sheet. TAs were also rly helpful

Favorite class of the first year by miles. was teaching the most 'complex' topics, yet my easiest class for the reasons: Super enthusiastic guy, very clear explanations (!but only in lectures! his slides are more sparse and just explains in class), workload was very light (only 3 homeworks), and interesting material. 

would 100% recommend
chill class fun labs

Dr. Lee gave interesting lectures and is also super nice. I appreciated that he would let us know what would be on the prelims specifically in class during lectures. My only complaint about this class would be the grading as his grading outlines that the TAs had to follow were pretty strict. However, overall the class was not too difficult.

Very enthusiastic lecturer but course content was not at the level of an introductory course. Very little foundational info was given to build a basic understanding of complicated concepts. Grading guidelines for homeworks and exams were unclear, but revisions were allowed for exams for up to 50% of points back.

Dr. Lee was draconian on deadlines and massive points were taken off minor mistakes. Though engaging in his lectures, the course material was not appropriate for an introductory-level course and labs often contributed little to the understanding of the concepts except to provide additional workload.

Prof. Lee is a very smart, funny and caring guy, however he may have not been the best choice for an intro class. His exams are hard and there are few resources to help you prepare for them outside of the in class powerpoints. The TAs for this class were incredibly unhelpful, so it is difficult to seek help unless you go to his few office hours.
Pretty solid choice for an ENGRI. Dr. Lee was a good professor, and the content covered seemed very relevant to current Biomedical Engineering. It wasn't too hard either.

Fascinating and distinguished guy. Lectures are long, but he is brilliant. So long as you put in some effort for homework, you get full credit, and the final project is built into the homework and is relatively straightforward (but a long paper).

Course is essentially an extended research project. Fairly self-guided, invest a lot of time in learning about and finding a good research topic. A lot of opportunities for feedback on your writing and you learn a ton about how to conduct and present research. End up with a nice writing sample useful for internships or senior thesis apps.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--So many papers

reviews.comment: So nice

He's a distinguished professor, but should really not be teaching undergraduates. He basically leaves the students on their own to do research with very little guidance. This class is only good for students that already have a good deal of macroeconomic knowledge or field experience.

Prof Escalona Torres is amazing! Honestly he might be my favorite professor of all time. I took SPAN 1210 + 1220 with him. He's super caring, he was great at explaining the material, and he really made every class fun. Cannot praise this man enough. So sad that I can't take more classes with him, I think he's at a different university now :(

Absolutely loved this man. Funny, personable, approachable, not harsh, really helpful. Homework was pretty easy. Projects take up more time. Improved my Spanish in just one semester. Lots of oral practice in class so participate. Would recommend taking a class with him if possible.

Span 1230 was really disorganized and frustrating for me but I felt that he really did everything he could to make the course less confusing. He's a really nice guy and also very knowledgeable. He's harsh on pronunciation given his linguistics background but it was very helpful. Def would take a class with him again

Professor Escalona Torres is so charismatic and intellectual. I enjoyed the material he brought to class, which he tried to personalize and relate to real life and his own life as well. I think he tried to make Spanish practical for us, but the Spanish department at Cornell really limits what he can do.

Juan is super enthusiastic and made an effort to make class interesting and expand office hours. With that being said, SPAN 1230 is difficult and there is a lot of homework. If you have to take it I'd recommend Juan in a heartbeat, he made the material easier to understand and more interesting. But it is a lot of work -- not his fault but be ware.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Harold was a fantastic professor and I absolutely enjoyed his class. It is definitely in my top 5 classes that I've taken at Cornell. If you're interested in soil or ag, you will not be disappointed. We did have to read a short book as an assignment but it was worth the read. Overall an excellent experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is such a wonderful, thoughtful, knowledgable, and kind man. I loved his class to the moon.

Good class. The homework assignments can be tough, make sure to start them with plenty of time to spare and meet with the TA if you are confused. Exams require you to read the assigned texts, which are posted on Blackboard. Labs are long! Dr. Van Es makes an effort to keep you engaged. His passion is clear and he is always excited to teach.

BEST PROFESSOR I HAD AT CORNELL SO FAR
Great explanations, can be fast sometimes though so you have to be concentrating in class. But absolutely amazing, never wastes time but somehow still manages to not make lectures boring.
Lecture summary in the beginning of each class was pretty helpful.
Lectures weren't clear or organized, and had trouble explaining concepts in an accessible way. The final exam was quite unfair (avg was a 60), leading to low course grades.

Very clear lectures, lets people ask questions and gives effective answers. He lecture for people who care about understanding the material and for people who just want to know how to solve problems at the same time.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: DiffEqu is a hard class but Dr. Esmaily is caring and does what he can to help make difficult concepts make sense. He really cares about his students and is there to help.
Knowledgeable but sometimes cannot convey what it is hes trying to teach us. Also pretty bland, not that math is exciting but at least liven up a little.

Professor Kim is extremely passionate in physics which really shows in her teaching. She is well prepared and explains concepts clearly. She is very funny and will share anecdotes from her life to inspire us and share her love for physics. The homework is very fair, challenging but not impossible. Strongly recommended for aspiring physics majors.

My first physics professor at Cornell. She had a tendency to simply copy more complicated derivations from her notes and could not always clearly explain her derivations. The final was a lot harder than the earlier prelims.

This class was almost a disaster. Very often she would talk about a subject for an hour and then move on to something else before concluding the discussion. She made it really hard to ask questions, and even intimidated some students for that. She did not say "I don't know." even once, which is really unexpected for such an advanced level class.

Kim was my favorite physics prof. from the honors intro sequence. She provides the lecture notes in advance which makes most lectures much easier to follow. While 1116 & 2217 required more intuitive thinking to solve crazy problems, 2218 dealt more with becoming familiar with more technical problems. Uses the definite articles incorrrectly at time.

Professor Kim is very organized, and has great lecture notes. That being said, you have to put in a lot of work outside class (reading the textbook, etc) to learn the material. Homework isn't always related to lecture, but she's still organized and willing to help.
The problem sets and prelims are fair so far, and I'm learning a lot in the class. The lectures are pretty clear too and accompany the readings well.

Physics 2218 Honors Waves and Thermodynamics. Nice lady, but presentation of material is disorganized and lacks motivation. I have the feeling that I worked harder for this class than any other, but I learned very little. I recommend you avoid Professor Eun-Ah Kim.
He likes to interrupt lectures to play his trumpet and have the class "Name that Tune". Not much learning goes on, but it is nonetheless the best part of my day

He's enthusiastic and eccentric, but I remember very little of any of his lecturers. He hops around A LOT, which is very distracting. Really nice guy, but didn't seem to click as much with the class as his co-professor did.
Frequently off topic.
A very unique person, he loves to jump sporadically while lecturing. Unfortunately, struggled to hold the attention of this intro level class.
hes a cool guy, very bouncy
Definatly a professor worth getting to know. Got alot out of his class that i didn't even realize untill later.

She is a caring teacher and I've grown to love her. I went out of my way to try to take Li laoshi's next chinese class after 1109. But, the class definitely feels like 4 credits and the tests can be very difficult. Daily homework is also very important, but not surprising as the class is structured very clearly and methodically.

She's nice and engaging in class, but beware of cold-calling. LOTS of homework and she's a harsh grader--will keep you on the edge of an A to make sure you actually put effort into the class. Lots of memorization vocab wise and quizzes every week..the class keeps you busy and working. Kind of a lot of work for a language class, but it is 4 credits.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Lovely and caring professor! But you have to actually work for your final grade

Li laoshi did a great job with breakout rooms and got people to participate. The readings are based off a textbook that has quite a few mistakes, but does teach vocabulary (albeit in a weird order). The assignments and presentations do help a lot in improving Chinese skills - but to ace them you need to have spoken chinese at home/learnt before.

She's really cool! I had her for FALCON this previous semester, and she's so funny. Always draws Xs in the air when we get stuff wrong. Doesn't always speak clearly, but it's probably better for our overall Chinese language learning.

Most people think this is a hard class. you gotta memorize all poems before each test! It's graded on improvement. If you honestly try hard, you wont get below A-. But no one tries hard; they treat this like an elective. It's 4 credits not 3! Very kind teacher; teaches well
Goated professor
Always makes the class smile and makes this course entertaining. Also good at explaining the content.
🐐 the goat
prof is amazing with an added bonus of a cool french accent. so so so grateful i took statics with him. he made this notoriously hard class more enjoyable and accessible.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Royer lectures very well and is very considerate of students and student requests. I would definitely recommend going to his office hours. He is very clear on his expectations, but might occasionally miss one or two topics that you should read in the textbook or go ask about in office hours or after class.

Royer is an incredible professor. The class and material were pretty difficult as expected, but I have never seen such an adaptable lecturer. His lectures evolved over the course of the semester, becoming very helpful as he adapted and updated his lecturing style. He is very approachable and funny, and he brings that personality into his lectures.

I was surprised when this really young professor that mainly focuses on research was so effective at teaching. Thankfully, he works closely to align his course with Dr. Ritz (who has long organized this course and the exams) and the quality is about the same. Dr. Royer just takes it to the next level with his enthusiasm, care, and French accent.
Professor Fath was clear in all of his assignments and it was easy to do well in his class. I definitely recommend taking any class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. Lectures were engaging, and the topic was interesting. Highly recommend.
One of the best professors on campus by far. Helps manage stress really well. Love how all exams are open notes however you still need to study because of the time crunch. Hope he gets tenure soon.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This man is great. All of his exams are online and open note. One of my favorite professors

David is a professor who truly is interested in his subject of teaching. He's always available outside of class to speak and aims to give detailed and tailored feedback for each student. This class, however, is work heavy for an FWS and you will likely be writing more essays or spending more time than your friends. Still worth it, great experience.

classes are definitely more of a lecture than a seminar so be aware of that but i had a great experience last fall in this class. i was never stressed over deadlines, my writing improved, and i can't overstate how much dr faulkner cares about and makes time for his students. overall a great guy and a good, very chill fws
Super flexible with deadlines but lectures are useless and doesn't give much graded feedback until the very end of the semester

Prof Faulkner is a nice guy but he was very distracted this semester and he was not focused on teaching this class. A lot of classes are him talking at you for an hour. The classes with discussions are far more interesting, but far more sparse. He will not give you a grade until the very end of the semester so it is difficult to gage where you are.

He is one of the most frustrating professors I have ever had. He loves to listen to himself talk, and that is basically all that happens for 2/3 of class. We are currently writing 4 essays simultaneously, and none of them have due dates, essentially meaning we have 4 essays due finals week. He ignores any part of a text that references anything
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Convinced he talks just to hear himself speak, we didn't received a single grade until it was too late to revise or make an attempt for a better grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I didn't realize of a professor he was until I took another FWS. He truly cares about his students and will sit down and discuss with you about your paper and how to become a better writer. He is also very passionate about what he teaches. A fun class overall with great discussions.

I love Professor Faulkner!! I had him freshman year for an FWS, and despite not being a strong writer, he was really open to working with me (and all of my other classmates) to make sure we got the help we needed to do well in his class. We seemed to write more essays than the other FWS's, but he constantly gave us opportunities to improve.

Honestly this man is the best professor I could have ever asked for. He's super chill about everything, deadlines included, and he really does care about his students. He gives few grades so that you can focus on your writing instead of what grade you're going to get in the class, which I really appreciate. He's such a good man. 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Would take again

reviews.comment: Overall he is very laid back about deadlines, which could be a good or bad thing, depending on the student. No grades are given until the end and when they are they aren't necessarily final. He jumps around so its hard to concentrate on specific topics. A tad condescending in class and when critiquing work.

Amazingly clear lectures; very lucky to have been able to take this class with this professor. Difficult course and be prepared to spend significant time on material. Content is relevant and practical in ECE. Attending all lectures and discussions is critical.

Material is tough, many prerequisites are assumed, and the pace is accelerated. However, the lectures are excellent and the homeworks/exams are incredibly helpful for improving understanding. I would take any course that Prof Rana offers in any subject.

Awesome lectures and lecture notes. Prof Rana is exceptionally articulate and clear and explains things very well. Very likely the best lecturer in ECE. Homeworks can be tough if you don't attend the sections. The course 4060 starts from the basics but quickly rockets itself into advanced quantum stuff.

Rana is a very good lecturer. Maybe the best I have had at Cornell. His courses are known to be phenomenal learning experiences, and 3150 was the best course I have had so far. But his courses are not easy and if you are not interested in the subject matter, life can become hard. And don't skip classes or fall behind - there is no catching up.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Rana has clear lectures and slides as long as you pay attention and dont sleep. Don't just only go to OH. Go to rana specifically for help understanding how to apply the concepts. Hes almost always free and there. He will help you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Lectures are very clear and slides are well done. However, he makes the class revolve only around grades by always saying "this can be on the final" and publicly announcing top scorers on each assignment. Made me less interested in the subject.
Only cares about grades, he's a good lecturer but the constant focus on exams and grading instead of the actual subject ruined my enthusiasm for the subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: okay so great teacher will give 5.0 for teaching... HOWEVER, it is a tad difficult. Also how could you make the final design night lab wednesday.... This is absolutely ridiculous in terms of timing. Why do so many of the students give him a 5.0 rating when they keep repeating difficult and tough grader? let me be an actual honest reviewer.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: One of the best lecturers at Cornell. Clearly puts in a lot of effort into teaching his classes and conveys difficult subject matter lucidly. Homework assignments are difficult and time consuming, but doable, especially with his recitation sections. Exams are some of the hardest I've taken at Cornell (much harder than homework assignments).
Awesome in everything

This was by far the most difficult class I have taken at Cornell. Too much material was covered in a single course. And exams were also tough. But Rana is a super good lecturer, very sharp, clear,  and to the point. Almost scary. The course material was also organized extremely well (better than any book) and  I learnt a lot.

Rana looks mean but he is probs one of the nicest professors around. He made an otherwise difficult subject really lucid and he is super helpful with assignments. If you want a good grade, then the class would be a lot of work. Final was way easier than midterm, and grading was lenient. I recommend taking this class with him, if you can.

For the class that had so much material, Rana was really good at picking out the main points, stressing them, and without sacrificing any rigor.  The class was also structured very well, having good coverage of semiconductor physics and

Great lecturer! But extremely difficult material and even more difficult exams. If he wasn't a fairly generous grader, the median on our midterm would've been in the 30's. Through fairly generous grading, it ended up being in the low 60s.

I was impressed by the quality and clarity of the lectures,  handouts and homeworks. He exceeded my expectations. The course is rigorous and you need a broad background in physics to be able to fully appreciate the content.

This was the best class I have taken at Cornell so far. Rana is out of this world. He is the most eloquent and coherent professor in all of Cornell. Listening to him is like listening to Mozart - not a single word is out of place. Why aren't there more people like him in this world.
He is a terrific teacher, crystal clear, speaks a little too fast, but very hot!
Most awesome engineering professor. Teaches very clearly and extremely helpful. Physics-oriented solid state class. More recommended than the equivalent class in the AEP department.
He is one of the best teachers i have seen simply awesome
Extremely difficult, but I learned more in his class than any other

Tough class. Lots of his grad students.  Many students will try to take as many classes as they can.  Keep up with the mountain of work that you have to do and you'll be fine because he can explain semiconductors to a five year old perfectly.
Legendary. There is no one better than Prof. Rana in Cornell ECE. Wow.
best physics-oriented engineering professor i've ever had
Best teacher in graduate level Physics. Among the best four professors at any level I have seen so far.  Clear and Coherent. Undoubtedly ranks among the finest teachers in EE in the USA.
rana is a dream boat.
Farhan is my daddy. Fall 2005 was his first semester being the head professor for a class and it was the best one I've had at Cornell. He should always teach ECE 303 now.

Farhan Rana is an absolute genius. He is always extremely prepared for lecture. His slides are amazing and very helpful. His classes are notoriously hard, but his lectures are good enough for you to do well. Come to class and do the homework and you will do fine in his class.
Tough Teacher but amazing. Was a great combination with Lal for 315.

Straightforward lectures with slides posted online, minimal homework, tests were fairly easy to prepare for if you put in some time. Super nice professor and very knowledgeable, easy to get an A or A+ and also come away learning a lot.

Professor is chill and teaches a very interesting topic, although admittedly lectures weren't the most exciting. Consists of 1 midterm, 1 book review, 1 final. But graded pretty lightly overall. Go to lecture, read the readings/book, and you'll get an A in this class.

Prof knows a lot on the Middle East, and his classes all cover interesting stuff
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Even though attendance was not mandatory, still went to class every day. This class was thoughtful and engaging. When I read a news story about the middle east I still reference my notes from this class. Prof Fahmy is great at explaining many complicated things in ways you can understand. This is the class I recommend to everyone.

Fahmy is the goat. It's a super easy class that will teach you a lot about the Middle East. Readings are "mandatory" but not super necessary. Study Fahmy's PowerPoints and you will ace the exams. There was a midterm, paper, and final exam. The median for Spring 2023 was an A-.

The class was easy. I never did a reading and skimmed the powerpoints for our exam. Fahmy is not trying to make your life harder than it already is; show up to lectures when you can to learn some history.

Professor Fahmy is a good guy and very easy going. This class is lecture heavy, so take good notes. Discussion was my favorite part of this class. His teaching assistant/graduate student team is amazing! Amr and Ibrahim were both very knowledgable and made discussion super fun. Will be taking more of his classes!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor, great class. I learned a lot but the class wasn't too hard

Great lecturer who cares about his field and knows what he's talking about. Studying for tests is relatively easy as his lectures are very closely aligned with the textbook and the slides are all posted online and are very comprehensive. Essay grading can be a little difficult because it's a little unclear exactly what he's looking for.
Lecture can be boring, but the textbook is really interesting and he is very knowledgable on the topic. Finished the class was a lot of new information I about various cultures.

This guy's exams are super, super difficult. When he lists a key term, he ACTUALLY wants you to list EVERYTHING about that term that you have ever learned in the class. That includes the date. Ignore his 3-5 sentence limit, write at least a full page on each ID and you might have a chance on the tests.

Professor Fahmy is clearly knowledgeable about his subject - and it shows in lecture. Lectures can be a bit boring at times but Fahmy uses plenty of different medias to keep the class engaged with relevant information. Also is very open to questions and clarifications but keeps to the topic at hand. Not life-altering, but certainly a solid class.
Great class, lectures are interesting and professor keeps everything straight forward.  2 papers and 2 exams, not difficult to get an A if you put effort into each of them.

Fahmy's lecture notes are great. The reading supplements the lecture very well. Do the reading, attend classes and write your papers ahead of time and perfect them you are sure to do well in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Best class I have taken at Cornell
Made the class much harder
this is my second class with Fahmy. He's intelligent, clear with his expectations and a nice guy. Def. recommend.
The class wasn't an easy A. Focus on the lecture slides and discussion in section class. I bought the book, but it isn't necessary. Sections are great and having a good TA helps a lot.
One of the must take courses at Cornell.
Great class. Makes you think about why history matters in understanding the modern Mid East.
Lectures clear. Don't really need to do the longer readings. Concentrate on lectures.

He is a great professor who really cares about what he teaches and loves to answer questions. Readings, excluding the primary sources, are not tested on. If you can memorize Powerpoint slides and show up every week, you'll do well in this class.

Fahmy is kind and very approachable. A fair amount of textbook reading, most of the info for prelim/final is through lectures though. Easy to understand and the tests were straight forward. Keeps the class fairly interesting. Overall not demanding at all, nice guy, and good class.
If you are looking for courses that do not take much of your time in that semester, this is one of the perfect courses.

Silvia is the worst professor I have ever come across in my career. She has absolutely no respect for students or anyone else for that matter. She will never help a student in need. Course is completely useless in terms of learning outcomes. Never take this course.
Silvia does not respect students or this job, just teaches the course as a job, not motivates students to learn at all. Will never take her course again.

Silvia Ferrari is anything but a Professor. The course structure is extremely haphazard. She has no interest in student's growth. It's like she was forced to take this job and teach this course. Really feel sorry for all students who take this course. Wouldn't recommend it to anyone.
The course material is not well organized, not taught in an interesting way.
The course lectures are taught in a very dry and boring way, not worth the effort to learn it. The instructor does not respect students and the questions asked are not explained very well.
Cover too much material but easy to get a high grade.
Ferrari is awesome. I've learned more useful stuff in this course than I have in most of my Cornell courses. She is an amazing human being that is always ready to help or motivate

Such a nice Professor, I absolutely loved this class. Such a fun and great FWS. She priorities you above all else and does not punish you for taking mental health days. My favorite class I have taken in Cornell so far. I can imagine someone disliking her, such a great person. Gave us snacks for Halloween and Christmas to celebrate the holidays :)
