She is so caring, it almost makes you feel like a human again. She's always checking in and making sure the work load isn't too heavy. She's very poetic when she teaches, and highly relatable (sharing tiktoks she made in her announcement emails). I really felt like I could write papers without worrying about a grade.

I have nothing but nice things to say about her. I've enjoyed working on most of the assignments. The class is low stress, and she is definitely the most caring professor I've ever had. Wish I can take more classes with her in the future.

Briel is one of the best professors I have ever had. She is such an amazing, loving, and caring person. She truly cares about the students and is passionate about her job and writing. If you love all types of writing like poetry, nonfiction, fiction, articles, or story-telling, and many others, this is definitely the class and professor for you.
Literally the worst
She's caring and obviously enjoys teaching the subject. However, the grading guidelines are very unclear which can be frustrating.
Basically doesn't teach and expects you to know by Googling everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She doesnt know the material very well and does not do a good job of explaining especially those who dont have an understanding of the material before.

I feel like Renate has a lot of ideas about aligning practice with the behavior of the innovative art world itself. She often ends up going on in lectures about all these "ideas," but never teaches technique. As long as you know what you want, what your ideas are, and you can show her you're always a step of ahead of the game, she'll be impressed.
Terrible

Renate is the nicest instructors I've encountered at Cornell and always willing to go out of her way to help you out.  Didn't always teach the most direct way to use each computer program, but taught us that the best way to learn how to use PhotoShop and Video editing software is to simply play around with it. Very little work outside class.
Yikes.
Should not be teaching in Fine Arts. Her incompetence is a disgrace to the college. Easy A though.
so vague when she teaches... doesnt know what the heck she is talking about, sometimes even teaches wrong concepts.  BIASED when it comes to grading.

I love Falk. Funny (albeit very sarcastic), extremely knowledgeable on the subject matter and leads very interesting and engaging lectures. Leaves good, thorough, constructive feedback on papers. Lenient on extensions for assignments. He is a tough grader though. Heavy amount of readings for class which are often not discussed. Cold calls a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Falk is the worst professor I've had at Cornell. He enjoys bullying students in discussions and is also immensely passive aggressive. He refuses to answer questions and doesn't know what it means to give constructive criticism. On top of this, he is a harsh grader. If you value your time and want to be respected DO NOT take his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Not inspirational or very interesting. He killed my interested in the subject for a while. Struck me as quite a negative guy, who thinks he is smarter than he really is. Not the hard hitting scholar he thinks he is. Also suffers from overthinking and obsessions, like grade inflation.
Pretty boring
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Falk leads discussions well, however that is the only good thing about the class. The readings are long and very difficult to read. Essays are very difficult and grading is harsh with very poor feedback. He expects the work of a professional historian from a first year in college. I would avoid this class and professor if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: WORST DECISION OF THE SEMESTER. Class was on viking peoples and many readings were in Old Norse... that nobody knew how to read???? At one point he made someone cry because he misinterpreted what he/she said and then continued to insist that he was correct in his interpretation. He also compared my writing to a mental disorder...
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Falk is the best thing that happened to my undergrad career at Cornell. I did both a class and an independent study with him and he opened my eyes to a new world of history. I finally felt like I was being understood, I am forever grateful. His class was fun and interesting and as long as you cared you are going to get a good grade.

Very much a mixed bag. Assigns lots of reading but guides discussion of it very well, good at pushing a free conversation among students to useful places. Unfortunately he also gives maddeningly cryptic responses to even the most straightforward questions, especially about assignments and grading. Grading and comments are mostly unclear/unhelpful.

Clearly very smart guy. Had ridiculously high expectations based on the level of the class, and did not teach you how to conform to them. Unclear in his assignment instructions and expectations. SUPER tough grader, concerned with grade inflation. Feedback was mostly critical, not constructive. Heavy reading load. Got visibly annoyed with students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: GOD, please don't take this professor's class. Lectures are boring than hell, grading is tough (totally based on how he likes you; he's extremely obssessed with the problem of grade inflation ), readings are unbelievably huge (even if most students mentioned this and he changed the amount of readings but still the course is too time-consuming)

Oren takes a little getting used to and has a dry sense of humor but he is extremely helpful and a very fair grader (he gave me a higher grade on my final paper than I likely deserved because I was engaged with the class). He is a wealth of knowledge and one should probably actually do the work for his classes. Great teacher and scholar!

This class was demanding, but well worth the effort. The pace was fast but all of the material seemed important and interesting. To receive a high grade in this class, one must be willing to think critically, closely examine readings, and be present and attentive for all lectures.

Professor Falk is very intelligent and helpful. His criticism can be harsh, but it's always constructive. He helped me improve my writing and my ability to analyze both primary and secondary sources. More than any other professor that I've had as a History major, he's willing to go out of his way to help you improve your own work. A passionate prof

He's really really nice and helpful. Though his class may be boring, but if you have any problem, he'll always be there ready to help you. He can spend a lot of time helping you clarify any issue. I really love him! He's amazing! Though his essay requirements are sometimes vague, but just go to his office hours and ask him any necessary question!

(Hist 1510) The class was definitely hard, but it wasn't unfair either and I ended up learning a lot. Professor Falk's lectures can be snoozers at times, but he did bring in a few very interesting guest lecturers to liven things up. All in all, it was a good class that I would recommend.

Strange guy. He is smart (duh) and interesting but there is something wrong with him, just can't put my finger on it. Class was on vikings, which is boring as hell, and i'm a respectable history major. Perfect class for you if you are a dork or some risley weirdo who likes to play with fake swords.
Egotistical, couldn't understand his assignments, harsh grader, extremely unhelpful when approached with questions.

I took two classes with Professor Falk-vikings and western civ. I received C's in both of them. But to this day, they are my favorite classes that I have taken at Cornell.  There is a lot of work, and the tests and papers are difficult.  But he is enthusiastic, prepared, and engaged.  Do yourself a solid, and take one of his courses

Its weird, this guy is an AMAZING lecturer, well structured, clear, funny (without being desperate), engaging etc. But he assigns so much busy work that I actually dropped the class and audited instead. Auditing is def the way to go, dont try to actually write papers for the guy, but also dont miss the chance to hear his AMAZING lectures.

Seriously great professor. No doubt you'll have to work hard, but you will also learn a ton. Hilarious sense of humor. Some people make him out to be evil, but that's only because he's incredibly challenging. If you actually want to LEARN something while you're at Cornell, take one of his classes, any of 'em.

OOOF what a dud. this guy is bizarre. he told me a story about how he wanted to be a pilot in the Israeli army but couldn't, and tried to make an analogy for students having difficulty keeping up with his cryptic assignments and verbose, soporific lectures. This is the kind of guy who uses unnecessarily complicated words and feels proud of it.

he's great if you show any interest in the topic and he really wants students to learn something...expects a lot from students and has very high standards...great for seminars and serious students. probably not someone you'd want to have if you're fulfilling a requirement. no matter what he'll force you to learn.

Oren is very knowledgeable and he enjoys teaching. You will be expected to do lots of work and he will call on you during lecture. However, his efforts will undoubtedly surpass yours and I was continually amazed at his level of preperation. Do some work and you will learn plenty.
The best class and proffesor i've had so far.  Not so much work for this class, just one long paper, but he is very demanding and hold high standards.  Incredible class discussions.
No Comments
excellent
the best teacher iv had so far... some people hate him but thats just because he has very high standards... his courses are hard but worth it because he is such an amaizing teacher!
I find people tend to be on one side or the other - you either love Oren or hate him, but either way, he doesn't bore you.
Falk pretended to be interested in me and be nice to me but it was painfully obvious that he wasn't.  I was expecting an engaging survey of Western Civilization and that is not at all what I got.
No Comments

Smart man, knows a lot about his field, approachable. Some people don't like his teaching style, but I thought it was great. If you are interested in what he is talking about you will learn a lot from his lectures.

Consistently told me I was doing well, but graded my work extremely low. Easily put over 30 hrs/wk into this one class between readings and assignments, to the detriment of my other classes. He told me I wasn't even trying. Avoid the jackass, he doesn't k

The subject was so interesting, but the lectures were so dull. I studied like mad for the final, but I felt like I knew nothing. He also basically said that I can't write, yet I'm an English major. He's a nice guy, though.
Professor Falk is a tremendous, one man tour de force of medieval history.  He wants students to read ALL THE TIME, and he is therefore the BEST EVER.
worst teacher ever...should have dropped the class earlier but ended up withdrawing it was so bad...DO NOT take a class with him!!!

Had to drop the class after a month in- I was doing more work for the class than all my others put together (busy work mostly) and he was supremely unclear in both lectures and what he expected in assignments.  Avoid!

In addition to being the most skillful discussion leader on the planet, Falk is a very friendly & terrifically knowledgeable professor. It's true he's got high standards, but as a result he's a prof you can learn a lot from. (Dig the viking ponytail man)

He is a really great professor who absolutely loves what he's teaching and expects you to love the subject as much as he does. Very intensive readings, but you do learn a lot in the course and from his lectures. Eccentric and funny.

Of all the teachers I have met at Cornell this is by far the worst, do yourself a big favor and avoid this class. He faults your writing and then makes the same (what he calls) errors in his reviews of your work. The lectures are completely pointless.
No Comments

The Worst teacher I have ever had.  I do more work in this writing seminar than I do in my three other courses combined which are all science courses.  He is extremely confusing and does not know how to make sense of his assignments.  Never take his class

The assignments are extremly confusing. The subject material isn't difficult, but understanding what he wants is near to impossible. He contradicts himself in lectures. The class is a truely mind-numbing experience.
The comment above says it all.  Do not take this course if you want to be able to pay attention to your other classes.
No Comments
Nice pony tail.
No Comments
No Comments
He's not a bad teacher, really.  The class and readings were interesting.  He expected WAY too much out of everyone though and was NOT an easy grader.

AMAZING PROF! I can't imagine having learned biochem from anyone else. Clearly covers difficult concepts, so helpful and welcoming during office hours even just to chat about non biochem related topics. So sad he is retiring from teaching, one of the best!
The lectures and slides in this class were so confusing. They left me super frustrated and I always felt like I had to learn the material entirely by myself.
Very kind and attentive professor. Lecture guide is detailed.

Very traditional, straightforward lecturer. The lectures aren't mandatory, and basically a transcript of what he says is put on blackboard (I found studying those to be most helpful, although his lecture guide is pretty good as well). As difficult as you would expect a biochem class to be, but not unreasonable, and a very nice lecturer

This class is extremely difficult. Not only are the lectures super boring and the lecture guide extremely confusing, but the material we are expected to learn is just unreasonably specific and unnecessary. This quizzes every week are a huge pain and you don't feel like you are actually getting anything out of them. Also he's like really mean.
hes sooooo mean lmao ive written three reviews and none of them have come up. guy is a terrible guy who yells at students and other cornell faculty. disrespectful and fake nice

Professor Feigenson really cares about his students! He sent out email to students who did well on the midterm and actually congratulated them! He also held weekly optional discussion, pls go to those if you have time. They are super helpful!
Just received a pretty good grade on my midterm, and Jerry goes out of his way to send me an email tO CONGRATULATE ME FOR MY SUCCESS. What an awesome guy.

Incredible professor and individual. He genuinely cares about his students and their performance in his class. He's super clear and efficient too. I know some students who didn't go to some lectures but that's stupid. Don't skip ANY lectures. There is a LOT that you have to know for the weekly quizzes and especially the final.

The greatest professor at Cornell and probably in all of New York state in the sciences. He genuinely wants for you to succeed - if you have a suggestion for the class, he'll weigh it and do it. He holds sessions for help applying to med school weekly. He lets you decide how the class will be graded and he tells you what will be asked on each test.

Dr. Feigenson was, by far, my favorite professor at Cornell. You will not find anyone more astute, approachable, and devoted to his students . The format of BIOMG 3310 is incredibly conducive to learning. At the end of every lecture, he goes out of his way to tell you what you need to know AND what you don't.

This professor made me miserable.  I could not follow his lectures and he focused on equations and minute details rather than teaching us central concepts.  The one time I spoke to him outside of class he was very intense and kept repeating that I should have known something.  I left his office crying.  I simply stopped going to lecture.

Gerry is the only professor I have ever had that actually goes way out of his way to help his students, even long after they are taking a class with him. While the course is not a breeze, he is such a truly good human being that I would absolutely recommend taking his class and not being afraid to ask him for advice on just about anything.

feigenson is definitely for the students, as the reviewer before me said. He is very approachable and you can just tell he cares A LOT about his students. He's very helpful in office hours, not condescending, and tries really hard to get to know his students. But, i felt like I was memorizing answers more so than actually learning in his class

Feigenson is one of the best teacher at cornell. He is so approachable. He is FOR THE STUDENTS. He goes out of his way for his students. Very good lecturer, very knowledgeable about the field. His Friday sessions are really good, I recommend that everyone should go! Very nice guy. This course really stimulated my interest in Biochem.TAKE HIS CLASS!
Definitely he is the best professor i ever had. If you ever get to know him well, he is one of the most nicest people ever. He is a great help for med school application and he loves his students.
Great lecturer

Amazing professor who genuinely cares about teaching. His passion for the subject really shows during lectures and simplifies a lot of stuff so very understandable and intersting as well. Surprisingly low amount of memorization required. way to an A: master lecture notes(understanding is the key), do previous quizes. you're set and done.

Feigenson is fantastic.  You can tell he puts a ton into this class, from the separate word files he creates for the lecture notes to the silly little overheads he prepares and manipulates with forceps.  Great prof.

I would not be where I was in my life today without Dr F.  I'm now almost done medical school, and his course REALLY helped... and his extra 'seminars on life' are very worthwhile:  he gave me a sense of focus and direction again.  Very inspiring and changed my life.

Prof. Feigenson is an amazing man - very helpful! Go to his office hours because he tries hard to get to know his students. He made it very clear on what things we need to know and not for the test. The second chance policy works really sweet. Previous tests help a lot. Make use of the virtual office hours- TAs explain better that way. SWEET CLASS!

Professor Feigenson is, hands down, one of the finest professors at Cornell. I finished my first year of medical school, and my preparation for biochemistry was far superior to that of my classmates', based on what I learned in BIOBM331. On another note, he's also one of the most approachable professors I've met.
He's so clear in his lectures and it's easy to understand him.  Wish the grading was easier, though.  Too many quizzes every week.
Very good!  He tells you what you need to know, and then tests you on it.  Very straightforward.  Excellent teacher.

Wonderful man who is one of the clearest, best, and most interested lecturers I've had.  If you know stuff on old quizzes and exams, you'll do well in the class.  A billion times better than the teacher 2nd semester.

BEST SCIENCE PROFESSOR HERE.  I really can't say enough about how great Prof F was.  He's so interested in his kids--he even does these Friday sessions where he talks about issues his students are facing (like applying to med school, grad school, doing research, etc) and offers sooo many office hours.  I'm so glad I took this class.
Great professor.  He writes his notes from each lecture online which really helps since they are very comprehensive.  You don't need to read the book which is cool.
i hate biochem but he is a good prof. knows the**** and has very interesting lectures for them being about reactions in a cell.

EXCELLENT prof...way cooler than most bio profs at this university...he understands the student perspective and really helps you to do well...he def makes you work your butt off for your grade!!! (also makes you love the subject in the meantime) This was the best bio class I took at Cornell.

Challenging and informative course. It isnt easy, but he makes you want to study as much as possible, just to make him happy. He makes such an effort on your behalf that you're guilted into trying your best. AMAZING PROF, probably my best biology teacher ever.

Feigenson is one of the most genuine professors at Cornell.Talk to him!He really wants to get to know you!An added bonus:he can actually teach.You'll never fall asleep in his class and he is very fair in his grading.BioBM 331 has been the best science class I've taken at Cornell and I'm a bio major.
Feigenson is the BEST proff in the bio department. He is absolutely caring and his lectures makes you interested in the material. His exams are managable if you study. Great course and proff
Sparked a genuine interest in Biochemistry
Excellent excellent professor.
one hundred trillion times than bik tye's 332. he is a chill dude.
Very friendly and a great speaker
he cares so much about his students! his grading system with dividing your grade by the mean is a little wack tho...it makes it imposs to get a's on a lot of things!
very competent professor
No Comments
Best Professor ever!
David is amazing! Be prepared to work really hard and dedicate a ton of time to the class, but also get ready to learn SO much.

David is the Zen master. I took his Directing classes many years ago - I still refer to his lessons ALL the time in my work in theatre. He is a truly dedicated teacher - loves theatre, acting, directing - and wants everyone to excel and demands the best. A graduate level course as an undergrad. You simply cannot do better. Take his course. Listen.
He's the coolest ever! Learned so much in class about how to be a better speaker!

Professor Feldshuh is so cool! His class requires some degree of dedication and a willingness to work hard, but the reward is well worth it.  Also, if you are feeling adventurous, ask him to do the splits!
Professor Feldshuh is awesome! His class requires a lot of work and dedication, but the reward is well worth it.  Also, if you are feeling adventurous, ask him to do the splits!
Professor Feldshuh is awesome! He requires commitment and dedication but it is so worth it. Also, if you're feeling brave, ask him to do the splits!

If you want to learn to direct, David can teach you.  But this class requires a lot of outside work (it should really be 4 units instead of 3), and the grading is tough.  A tip: try to get an actor in your group, because the scenes will be much better.
He da man! Got the powers of Professor X, Captain Picard, and Patrick Stewart combined!
Dr. Fitzgerald is so passionate about what shes teaching and seems to really want to share that with her students. such a kind professor i would be surprised if anyone remotely disliked her.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She really cares and makes class genuinely interesting, you can tell she's passionate and wants us to learn, not just pass. That said, her grade cutoffs are kinda insane (a 100+ for an A+ is wild), but getting an A is totally doable. Overall, one of those professors you'll actually remember.

You can tell Dr. Fitzgerald really cares about her work and is passionate about teaching. She understands student needs but is also fair and equitable when making decisions. Her TAs were easily accessible outside of class and offered fun insights during guest lectures. The class has weekly reflections that are pretty simple and easy to keep up with

Idk what y'all are talking about but this guy has lost his spark or something. Wears a mask the whole semester that muffles his voice. The whole class is about VR. He has an infinite catalog of Youtube videos about VR and optical illusions which is kinda impressive, but he still puts the whole lecture hall to sleep by being so boring.

The class is super interesting and entertaining, and David Field does a great job of explaining concepts and topics in lectures with examples. There is no workload at all, but that means that exams make up nearly your entire grade. There are hundreds of study problems, so memorizing info can be hard, but exams tend to choose the most important ones
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Field's lectures were really interesting and actually made me want to go to class. There's a long list of sample problems given before each prelim, and if you study those you'll do well. Definitely recommend this course!

Great Class. He updates the class every year according to technology (he loves his iphone) and gives great and fun examples. Study the practice questions with 3-4 days prior test and you'll get a sure A. Very enthusiastic.

Extremely clear lecturer with a good sense of humor and a lot of enthusiasm for the material. If you like the sound of the course description, then trust me, you'll love the class! (For me it has been easily one of my favorite courses here so far - two and a half of the most fascinating hours of the week since the very beginning of the semester.)
loved the class, great enthusiastic professor! tests are easy if you study for them (he gives you all the questions) book and lecture slides are helpful, but it's a good idea to go to class.

Really enthusiastic during class but can seem distant one-on-one. Really enthusiastic about the material and always has some fun/hands-on/demonstrative way of demonstrating a concept. Presentation can sometimes skip around and be unclear (esp if you aren't physics/math oriented).

Have to go to class. Exams are straightforward - he gives you the questions, you just have to study all of them. He clearly understands, and is excited by the material, and has a strong desire to convey the information to students.

Varying opinion: his exams are very easy as long as you study the questions ahead. This class contained some VERY interestnig materials regarding contemperary tech. issues, and he was very knowledgable. Not really approachable professor, but he's intelligent and I always looked forward to this class

I wanted to learn everything I could in this class, but I found it very difficult to go to and stay awake in Prof. Field's lectures, which were an integral part of the tests.  The grade was based of 3 EXTREMELY difficult essay tests.  I found the professor to be pretty unhelpful, and unresponsive.

Idk what these awful reviews are, but she is a fantastic lecturer. For her course, just do the work. If you do the work you'll get a good grade. This is a super interesting class that will allow you to understand pre-migration, migration and post-migration stories of refugees.

I am shocked by the ratings for this class, while there were few grading criteria provided and confusing projects it was a really informative class. We got the opportunity to visit refugee resettlement centers and contribute to the real community around us. We watched a lot of movies about the refugee crisis, and there were no tests.

this course wasn't that hard, but this professorr is tough to work with. besides being biased towards students she knows, she continually undermined other students and their work. I would only recommend this professor if you want a hard time in your academic career. good luck with her!

She has no grading ideas that will have no feedback or comments. Additionally I don't think a professor without public policy experience shouldn't teach this class and it shows. Also, a lot of readings!!!! and little work on refugees. Even though the project was fun, she lack knowledge on how nonprofit work functions because the grading was harsh!
Such a waste of time
I have never seen such a racist instructor and someone who makes students' life hard-what a waste of time for students, please choose another professor.

I had a very difficult experience in this course due to what I felt was unfair grading and a lack of willingness to communicate with students.This created an overall stressful and unproductive learning environment. I would encourage future students to be aware of these issues when considering this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Please don't take his class, if you want to be happy.

Really enjoyed this class! If you do the readings and attend class you'll do very well, while learning a lot in the process. The course reviews many different genocides across the course of history and offers many details on each. I also recommend this course if you need a class for credit or to fulfill a requirement.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Took this class as an easy distribution and it did its job. Prof. is nice and very clearly cares about what he's teaching, though the lectures were painful to sit through. Almost felt bad that people weren't taking notes/paying attention. Essays were easy, skimmed readings, and final was exactly like the review sheet he gives.
Professor Fiskesjo is a nice, genuine guy who lectures well. He clearly cares about anthropology and what he talks about. He has a lot of readings, but he goes over them in class.

Prof. Fiskesjo is a great person, very genuine, and always willing to assist students with questions. However, his lectures could be improved. Just do the reading, discussion posts, and papers then you'll be fine. Class content is very thought-provoking and is great exposure to cultural anthropology.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Fiskesjo is a nice, genuine guy who lectures well. Clearly cares about anthropology and what he talks about. A lot of readings but he goes over it in class.

Chill guy. Beware of weird ppl trying to drive you out of the course. Stranger came in 1st day and called him a psy-op bc of his Uyghur advocacy. Often went on unrelated tangents that could disengage you. 2 short essays + online final. Slow feedback but lenient grading. Was willing to hear student opinions even if they didn't align with his.

Approachable and easy going. Clear on assignments and grading. However every once in a while would go off tangent from course material to share views that were unrelated (somewhat controversial & ungrounded) to the material.
In terms of content, the course was decent. Nothing to complain about. However, he would often go on long, somewhat racist tangents. Ruined the course

This is for his Study Abroad in Cambodia course for 2 and a half weeks. I can't understand the negative reviews. How could anyone not love Magnus? He is funny and LOVES what he does. I really hope he keeps doing Study Abroad in the future. It's not just that the trip was great on its own, but he made it sooo much better!

Magnus is great! His lectures were generally very interesting and he is super passionate about what he teaches. He really encouraged discussion as well. He's also just a very likeable, if quirky guy. My only criticism is that the class was graded on just a few things: a midterm, a fairly long paper, and participation.

Magnus lectures are often very interesting despite his dry tone. The class is fairly easy for the most part (very short essays), though some of that depends on the TAs. Having attended both his Zoom and in-person lectures, I can say that he is MUCH better in person than over Zoom.

Avoid at any costs. I found his assignments are ridiculous amount of reading, and yet has nothing to do with exam Id rather take other class and read what interests me. Im not attending a trading club.

The prof seemed passionate about his subject, but the class was poorly organized. The grading system was unclear to students, even though the assignments were easy. Problems occurred with zoom and canvas (i.e. not recording sessions, not publishing info on canvas, etc.). The lectures and readings were interesting though, and my TA was great.

This might be harsh, but this was the worst class I've taken. His teaching was not conducive to Zoom. The lectures were boring. I was really disappointed by the way he discussed topics I had hoped would be interesting. The grading scheme was unclear and unfair. Easy, but I would have taken a harder and more interesting class over this one.

Class was light work. But lecture's super boring. I feel bad because no one participated but he didn't really create a great atmosphere for it. He's probably better in person, but not good at zoom. We spent the whole class talking about how things aren't really objective and then the final was defining terms objectively. Nice guy tho, wish the best

Lectures are boring and he just repeats the information from the readings. Grading criteria is unclear and he is very disorganized. He told us about our midterm 2 weeks before it was going to happen and we didn't know how it was going to graded or what the format was. He didn't tell us the format of the final then people got C's on it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: super kind and caring professor. very passionate about his field. material is very interesting. workload pretty low.

Very interesting guy, engages students in the lecture asking questions and feedback, not afraid to consider and discuss other points of view. He brings a breadth of examples and approaches to a variety of topics each week, it's impressive. Always includes the most timely debates. Assigns a lot of reading, essays were short and not hard to write.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Don't be fooled by the comment below, Magnus is a great guy who really cares about his students. It's important to keep in mind he is from Sweden and so sometimes what he says can be misconstrued. More than willing to be corrected and amend his own opinions if confronted, always up for an open conversation. In no way denies his son's identity.

Magnus is such a nice professor, he obviously means well. His TAs do a lot of the work but his lectures do explain the assigned readings. Exams are not hard, just do the readings. Essays are two pages and are not too bad. I got an A and enjoyed the class. He is very friendly and approachable!!

his lectures can get really boring. section helped out a lot because i had a great TA. there are weekly essays assigned but they are very easy if you understand the readings.  that being said, the readings can be very long and if you get bored of anthro it is easy to fall behind. easy A if you do the readings and incorporate them into essays
Everything about the guy screams smug and lazy. How he manages to live with that huge ego is a mystery.

Despite the fact, his tone is really sleep inducing. But overall, he's really helpful, always there for you. It's so easy to lose attention in his class, which makes it boring then. But overall, he's so friendly that you wouldn't want to skip his class.

Magnus is really cute in a very goofy foreign way. I feel bad for him when he asks questions in class and everyone is silent. He's super nice and goofy. His lectures are a snoozefest and you NEVER need to go to class literally ever. You have way too many essays but its all about your TA.

He isn't a very clear speaker, the lectures are usually hit-or-miss with some of them being horrible and others being really insightful. Although he isn't a great lecturer, but he really cares for his students and is interesting to speak with one on one. This isn't a bad intro class although the readings are way too long! Only take if u like anthro
SO LAZY!  Just talks about himself and his own research and clearly does not care about his students. Not nearly as smart as he wants us to think.

Very confusing and into his own research. His T.A.s did all the work and the lectures were terrible. The readings themselves were interesting yet sometimes too lengthy. Sections were laid back though, and interesting. As a person though, he is a great guy who is excited about his field-- He could use some work in teaching.

Don't let the awesome course description fool you. This class was really boring. Boring lectures are mandatory. Manages to make fascinating topics dry. Monotone voice. TA's grade everything and lead the only interesting part of the class-discussions. You'll be able to pass this class with a good grade, but you'll probably be wasting your time.
Like the others said, this guy loves his work but absolutely fails at passing any of it on.  Some of the worst lectures I have ever sat through.

He definitely loves his work!  Assigns way too much reading, and its hard to know what to cover, bc he doesn't cover all of it.  His own work is really interesting, though.  I'd recommend taking this class only for fun.

Fiskesjo is one of those teachers who loves what he does SO MUCH that he's in his own little world when he lectures and tends to float off subject. He assigns a lot of reading and doesn't really highlight key points so you'll need office hours for that. Also, he will put you to sleep faster than a roofie. Nevertheless, the material is interesting!

This professor was the harshest grader I've had to date in my time at Cornell. They have no sympathy for their students and look down upon students who ask for extensions. The exams were unusually difficult for an easy material class and the lab portion was poorly run. Weekly lab reports were a long time commitment. Lab portion was fun though.

Not a bad professor for lack of ability but lack of care about anything related to the course or its students. I don't know why she's in the field, because she could make anything associated with it more boring than simply watch the clock tick on. Also, her grading system is quite honestly atrocious.

She is knowledgeable and pretty clear. However, the class is boring and usually consists of her talking directly from her slides. Class is 1/3 lectures on tissue eng, and then 1/3 journal club, and 1/3 project presentations. Class is helpful, but can easily be learned with the textbook + journal articles.
Very helpful professor.

Though the prof teaches well, can't help but feel like there is no depth. It's a lot of cell biology in the lectures and useful, interesting labs! TAs kind of had no idea about anything the whole time, so they didn't help either. Hard to study for :(

Literally the kindest professor I've ever met. Explains labor economics very clearly and he truly cares about his students and wants them to succeed. Manages to make econ interesting and not too difficult for a humanities oriented student!

Professor Fields is one of the best-loved professors for all ILR students. He is so caring for the students, not only your academic performance as a student but also your health and wellbeing. His lectures are easy to understand - he has the magic to simplify complicated theories/models into something that everybody can relate. He is so amazing!
Two tests. First one is easy. The second one is crazy hard
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Not good professor. Very unclear. Do not take if you have the chance!
Awesome prof.

Professor Gary Fields single handedly makes the study of Economics  -dare I say- enjoyable . His lecture content is organised and he his crystal clear and methodical in his delivery. He humanises the subject through personal anecdotes and real life examples. Even if you absolutely hate Economics, you MUST take his class. You're welcome.

What can I say that hasn't been said? This guy is: The Man. The best professor I've ever taken. A legend. An absolute genius when it comes to not only his field but to teaching itself. The material is not easy, even totally foreign, and he makes it crystal clear. He's also hilarious and each class is a really a pleasure.

Fields is a phenomenal educator. He's one of the most cited and well-respected economists in his field, but manages to still relate to students on a personable level. The material is extremely interesting and life-changing, and taught in an anecdotal fashion that made the class unforgettable. Grades are based on the midterm and final only.

Very hard-working, fantastic professor. Expectations for the course were very clear. Presented the material in a way that made it accessible to students with no previous econ courses. He made labor econ enjoyable! Gives out copies of previous years' exams, which pretty much mirrored which type of questions were asked. Excellent!

Great/best professor and super clear. He inspires and cares for  students.  Introductory labor economics class for mostly MILR and MPA students so different from usual econ undergrad courses, he doesn't focus on theory or math that much, which means course and exams are not so difficult:-)
Take Fields. I'm approaching my last semester at Cornell, and made sure to enroll in another of his courses before I leave. He is awesome; you won't regret taking classes with him.
Best professor for international student because he is crystal-clear and almost never uses American slang. Funny, positive, helpful and extremely organized.
Best!
Really makes you excited about the subject matter.  Extremely approachable, and very helpful.  One of the best profs at Cornell.
I just wish every professor at Cornell was like him: crystal clear, passionate, helpful, approachable.

Adore him and his teaching style. Got to be one of the most hard-working professors at Cornell. His lectures are organized, methodical, and crystal-clear. The amount and level of material he covers is the perfect balance between covering the essentials and stretching to keep it interesting. Exams are fair and straight-forward.
one word: amazing

He is absolutely an amazing teacher of economics.  Very good at explaining difficult concepts in a way that makes it seem simple. If you get the opportunity, take as many classes with him as possible. There is a reason he is a leader in the development economics field... b/c he knows his stuff.

I think this class being labeled "introductory" is deceiving. It is very homework heavy and the grading rubric is very vague in my opinion. Prelims tend to be difficult as they are in a format different from the homeworks/exercises done in class. If you don't understand why and how your code works, performing on the prelims can be difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took this class in SP24 and took away a lot from the course. As long as you put decent effort into the class and treat the assignments seriously, you will come away with a good grade. If you find climate change and global warming to be interesting, then you will enjoy this class. Nice guy and very chill class.

Would like to echo that his grading is really silly, grades off stuff that isn't taught (i.e formal scientific captioning). Also would like to add that instructions for homeworks were terrible, rubrics often don't reflect instructions. Would not recommend this class.

Weird class- apparently it was easy in the past but is no longer. The workload is light but he makes up for it by giving harsh grades based on "scientific formatting" for graph captions- a nebulous concept which he does not teach but expects us to know. Lectures are not presented in an engaging way and can be difficult to digest.

There's very little work and no exams. The lectures are a little boring but he clearly knows what he's talking about. I wouldn't consider this an "easy A" class though (median grade is B+). Most people think they can ace the quizzes without paying attention to the lecture, which isn't the case
His class is really easy. Weekly quizzes were open note/internet and were mostly fine. Homeworks were also not that bad. Overall, he's a pretty chill guy with an easy class.

Laidback professor. Course is understandable for students not from climate science-related backgrounds, and gives a good overview of climate change, as opposed to the minutia of the field. Open notes and collaborative weekly quizzes, only three questions long. No final exam, just a group project making an infographic.

A solid introduction to python using interesting meteorological examples, homework coding assignments are given after the lecture portion of class concludes to start on with the prof present and then due before the next class (usually 2 assignments per week). Accessible outside of class to help understand assignments or run thru issues in code.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Super engaging lectures and makes difficult text easier to understand. Engages with the class during his lectures

Professor Fleming's lectures were engaging and made the material interesting. He is clearly passionate about the content. I had a rough start to the semester, and he was accommodating and supportive, which I really appreciated. The exams were fair. Overall, it was one of my favorite classes so far.

Fleming gains a lot of points with people for infusing comedy in his lectures and his boisterous persona. Personally, I found him annoying. He made participation graded in a 100 person lecture, graded so hard on essays and tests, and wasn't helpful in office hours. Funny guy, but little was graded before drop deadline and grades came unexpectedly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best class, best professor, wish I could erase my memory and take the class again

Professor Fleming is the best professor I've had at Cornell, and Critical Theory is possibly the best course I've taken. His lectures are super engaging and interesting. I'm honestly just sad the class had to end. The grading on the essays wasn't very harsh, and the tests were as fair as he could make them. If you can, take a class with him!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I felt challenged but learned a lot. Definitely not a class to take if you don't want to be challenged, but better for it
The class is hard, but if you are interested in a career in real estate or finance (as most Hotelies are) then this course will prepare you very well for any internships you do.
Dropping my real estate minor. Final was the worst final I have taken in my life... It was a curveball and not content that we covered in class or our homework problem sets.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not take principles of real estate with Flynn. His exams do not cover class content and are so confusingly written. This class made me want to drop the minor singlehandedly. There is no way to prepare for the curveballs you will be thrown. There was a public debrief outside the exam hall after the final discussing how lost we all were. Run.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: HADM 4230 taught by Flynn has been my favorite class at Cornell. He cares deeply for the subject and explains it incredibly well. I gained impressive competence in the MBS industry. Great job at tying in macro news into the lectures. Although not easy, the class will prepare you well for a job in RE Finance, MBS specifically. Very impressive prof.

Professor Flynn gets a bad rap because his exams are difficult and commercial real estate itself is a hard subject. Despite this, you learn so much in the course - I found myself using a lot of what I learned in this course in my internship and impressing my bosses there. If you need help, reach out and email Flynn, he's very available.
run

Flynn has no enthusiasm in his voice when teaching and purely reads off his slides which contain a lot of intermediate/advanced information while he fails to explain the introductory topics. Overall, terrible professor for principles and insanely challenging exams that he doesn't prepare you for. Save yourself and don't take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: AVOID AVOID!!!! I seriously think he forgot he was teaching an intro level class. I have never heard so many students complain about the difficulty of an exam in my time at the hotel school. The only way to do good in this course is to have previous real estate experience because he never goes over the foundations.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: "There will be stuff on this exam that you've never seen before." He said this word for word. He purposely tries to make your life miserable and for you to get a bad grade in the class. He speeds through his lectures like it is a race, and it is impossible to understand what is going on. You need to read 2 entire textbooks or you're screwed.

I feel like he puts basic concepts on to ChatGPT with the prompt: "make this sound 100x more complicated than it is." Seriously, most of my studying consisted of going to investopedia to look stuff up I could actually understand. I think he's a really smart guy, just not meant to teach.

TERRIBLE! felt like a chore. he does not want to be teaching, has zero interest in his students, grading is impossible, does not test on anything he teaches in class, purposefully does not explain the most complicated and important concepts in class "because they r in the reading" and " we do not have time".  Also 99% for an A+ is unheard of

I have genuinely never been in such a confusing, difficult class. Flynn should absolutely not be teaching an introductory class- he has no comprehension of what students should be learning in a 101 class. The tests are near impossible. Don't take Flynn, but ESPECIALLY if you are actually interested in RE bc this class will crush your dreams

Flynn is the worst professor I have ever had the displeasure of taking a class with. He purposefully tests on material he does not teach on, does not follow the standard course curriculum, and his problem sets come through a large group of unclear, unfair instructions. 

AVOID AT ALL COSTS!!

Boring lecture, extremely difficult exams. He doesn't test on what he taught in class. He tests random things that he thinks are related to the topics but actually not. You won't be able to follow if you miss one of his classes. He literally makes real estate unattractive to most students in the hotel school.

The toughest grader on campus is Professor Flynn. Infamous for stating that an average of 75% is considered "higher than expected," most exams I've observed are uncurved, with the majority of students scoring between 75% and 80%.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Along with taking stream ecology, I worked under a grad student in his lab for a bit, and Dr. Flecker is probably the sweetest professor I've ever had. He is genuinely so kind and caring. He is very gentle. I highly recommend.
Lectures were a bit bland, but he tried to put in lots of interesting examples to better explain concepts like research cases or planet earth videos. Seems like a nice guy, though.

I really liked this professor as a person. His lectures were boring 70% of the time, and I didn't like the 3 prelims or final. I didn't feel like it was super clear what we were supposed to be learning. My TA sucked. Overall the class was alright, maybe not for non-science majors.

He dropped the lowest exam which was great; I skipped the final and went home for break early. If you study the lectures you will do well on the tests. The workload is predictable and manageable. I was afraid to take bio as a business major but ended up enjoying the class and getting an A, even though I skipped several lectures.

Fantastic professor who has an excellent grasp on the subject. Lectures filled with extremely interesting, cool examples, and although some concepts taught are complex, they are covered very lightly on exams.
You don't need the textbook. All you need to do is attend section and memorize lecture slides and you'll get a good grade on the pre-lims and final.
Not the best best teaching ability - was far from captivating. Voice hard to hear, didn't use mic well.

Not impressed with teaching ability. Lectures are boring and disorganized. He does not treat students as though they are Ivy League intellectuals. Reads every word on every slide shown in lecture, rather than using slides as a reference or tool for discussion. We can read. We know what your slide says.
Lectures are a little disorganized.
pretty good but alittle out there

If you think ecology is hard or boring with Flecker, you should have seen the guys who taught it before him.  Chabot put me to sleep every single time, and I used to really like ecology.  Trust me, Flecker was the best option the ecology department had.
nice enough guy, but he put me to sleep.  not an engaging lecturer, hard to follow
Super nice guy- but lectures and tests are hard to understand.
No Comments
No Comments
Exams are the worst

I loved Prof Chiara. She was really nice, gave good feedback, and honestly if you show up prepared, you'll have a good time in her class. She may seem a little scary and blunt, but she is really helpful and provides amazing feedback. She's understanding of last minute work and as long as you are open and honest, she'll help out.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: A clear example of how a professor can hurt a students experience at cornell. Had a situation where she bashed on essays and treated students unfairly. Not professional at all.
One of the worst professors in Cornell with a very biased grading system. Will not accommodate and willing to work with students on class matters. Unfair and ethical and would highly avoid
Yo Clara how is 95 a B+ ur grading system is messed up and even makes ur teaching worse than anyone at this institution

Brilliant scholar and educatoralways able to provide critical views of the works at question with clarity and humility. Grading schemes are clear and the course is very well organized. Always open to different opinions, cares about her students, & provides a safe space for all. Would recommend to anyone, esp. those w/ interests in Islam & Asia.

Prof Formichi is caring and approachable, willing to adjust to students' need. I don't know what happened with the other students here, but to me her grading criteria is very clear (she gives you a grading rubric of each type of assignment at the start of the semester, and if you check them carefully, you get good grades.)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Though the material is very interesting and inspirational, her unclear/harsh grading criteria renders her a terrible professor. Lectures are disorganized, points are taken off subjectively and feedback/point deduction is not fair as it doesn't reflect student effort. I wish this amazing topic and religion could be taught by a worthy professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is literally the bomb and the class is super interesting. It is very easy to do well and she is very engaging. Know the vocab and you will do fine
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Unclear grading criteria and lectures were all over the place. You basically have to teach yourself the information. Would not recommend and will not take again.

Professor Fontaine is an absolute expert. He is an innovative thinker whose lectures encourage you to really think about deep and controversial topics. I highly recommend taking 1615 (esp. Classics majors), it's a lot of fun and incredibly interesting. Probably one of the most underrated courses at Cornell. Don't take it if you won't participate.
Very terrible professor, lectures drone on and on. Very inflexible and inconsiderate.

Difficult to reach over email and sometimes passive agressive to students. The class was take online but canvas links were broken and discussions were not set up correctly, yet no extensions were given. Exam timings are rough for students in international timezones.

In class, he highlights and points out exactly what will be on the prelims and final. Although the class is called Intro to Ancient Rome, it primarily is about Roman literature, not an intro class about the civilization itself.
If you do the readings and take good notes on the lectures, very fair to do well. Super interesting content. Great person.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Amazing Professor. Always willing to help a teacher you should absolutely work with!

Dr. Fontaine is clearly passionate about his subject matter and that carries through to his lectures. As long as you do what he clearly outlines, you should get an A. Many group discussions. Material is interesting, and Fontaine won't give you all the answers in lectures; he encourages you to think critically for yourself. Overall very stimulating.
I don't know why people write such mean things about Professor Fontaine. Yes, he is a tough grader, but he is also very kind and always available if you need help. He also has a great sense of humor.
I don't know why people write such mean things about Professor Fontaine. Yes, he is a tough grader, but he is also very kind and always available if you need help. He also has a great sense of humor.

Knows his stuff, knows how to keep the class on its toes. Will call on you at random, so make sure you do the reading, but if you're up to speed on anything he'll give an insightful, funny, interesting class. One of my favorites, once I got used to his style.
he is really interesting, but uses the socratic method and calls on people randomly so it's really stressfull
His class is sooo cool but the tests are hard! Can't decide whether or not i'm glad i took the class!
Awesome prof. Great knowledge of subject matter, and definitely encourages interest.
Good class but extremely harsh grader.
No Comments
absolutely the man, whenever hes mean, its really just in a funny way, don't back down and make fun of him if he makes fun of you
ask him about stuff; he knows the answers.
Sometimes boring but great professor. 2x Fishbowl and 2x take home midterm/finals

What a gem of a professor. The class structure is nice but interesting: socratic seminar style discussions instead of lectures. 2 take home midterm/finals papers. Keep up with the readings and you'll do absolutely fine. He cares so much about the subject. If you're interested in the material, definitely take the class.

An absolute gem of a professor. If you don't do the readings you'll definitely strugglebut then again, why take a theory class if you don't want readings? Prof Makki is incredibly knowledgeable and helpfulif class discussion isn't great, go to his office hours for some super engaging conversations. 11/10

this dude is amazing! don't pass up the opportunity on the class. you learn SO MUCH altho you will read a lot (not that unreasonable though, as ILR found it less than some classes). Really interesting material that changes the way you view the world. take home exams (although hard questions and they grade hard). participation, no quizzes. excellent
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: While the class is not the most interesting of subjects, you come away knowing more than you thought you would. I use my knowledge from this class in everyday conversations. Professor Makki is a little dry, but stick with him.
As long as you go to class, this is not too hard. And prof Makki is awesome. This was my favorite course at Cornell

YAY Makki! He doesn't do powerpoints, so it's pretty much mandatory to go to class unless you can understand classical theories well. But he explains everything to a T and is more than willing to help. I loved him!

Davis was very nice and accessible, but I didn't feel like he taught well. I was much less prepared for his exam questions compared to the other lecturer. I didn't need the textbook until he started lecturing because I didn't feel he was explaining anything well. His homework was easy, though.
Davis seemed like he genuinely cared about students. The lectures were a little stale at times, but he made me enjoy 2070 more than the other lecturer.

Professor Davis seems like a nice guy but the lectures were very boring. He taught very slowly to the point where we were not able to cover enough material in each lecture. Problem sets were long but not hard. The textbook is the one thing that helped me do good.

Davis is slightly better than Hines (who taught the first half of 2070), an engaging lecturer who posts slides beforehand and is more open to questions. He teaches a bit slowly, though, and by the end we were struggling to cover everything before the final. The class is still held back by a diabolical grading system (iykyk) and borderline evil TAs.

2070 is a hard class regardless of professor, but Davis is a genuinely kind person and likes doing demonstrations and cracking jokes, which makes the lectures bearable. He uses slides and uploads them the night before lecture which is convenient. His examples can be slightly confusing sometimes so be sure to pay attention or else you'll be lost.

His lectures come straight from the textbook, but there are some engaging parts of lecture that add to understanding. Some homework questions appeared exactly on exams so understanding them is important. He's nice but the lectures are pretty boring. Read the textbook for anything you don't understand as he follows it exactly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He taught the second half of Chem2070. My biggest complaint is the homework. Hours upon hours of problem sets. The professor who taught the first half of the class gave problem sets, but Floyd gave so much more homework than she ever did.The lectures were pretty boring, but at least he made explosions to keep us engaged.

Very dependent on the textbook, everything he taught and all grading criteria came from the textbook. Often went on tangents in lectures to the point where you couldn't understand what was important and what was irrelevant. Rarely did any practice problems in class so most of us did not know how to actually apply the material.

His test questions could still be quite difficult (typical of CHEM 2070), but he seems like a very sweet and caring professor. His lectures were more slow-paced compared to Prof. Hines, and I enjoyed his in-class demonstrations.

Floyd is a lot better at teaching than M. Hines, in my opinion. He teaches at a slower pace and conducts experiments in class. He is also very caring, and he reminds me of the grandpa in UP. He's so cute and wholesome core.
They need to make the 50 min 2070 lecture  2x as long once he takes over. Half of class each time is spent watching him figure out his own computer. Painful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really nice professor. Take advantage of regrade requests; Professor Davis is very generous and understanding of circumstances that arise during prelim season. His lectures were fast paced, but all slides are posted and he listens to his students concerns and is very patient in answering questions. 100% take 2150 over 2070.

despite davis being a nice and caring guy, his lecture slides aren't helpful, examples and derivations don't correlate to hw or prelim q's. OH aren't helpful. he doesn't walk you through problems, he just talks (not great for visual learners). textbook isn't great either.

lab work for this class is hard. TAs often didn't show up to office hours.

Prof. Davis is a solid professor. Lectures can get quite dry and proof heavy with derivations (particularly with equations in thermo and quantum), but you won't be tested on 99% of it. He does post lecture slides, which is super helpful. For 2150 specifically, try to stay on top of the content and take advantage of old exams/psets.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
-willing to help (office hrs, etc)
-overestimates students knowledge
-doesn't explain overall concept/basics much: easy to get lost if you don't know content already
-posted online lecture slides aren't helpful: lack lots of explanations/content discussed in lecture
-very time consuming lab reports
-definitely caring, but not the clearest explainer

Tough class, but with the curve (average is B+) you should be okay (just try to stay around the mean for prelims. By looking at the textbook before lecture, you should be able to follow. Clearly a passionate and smart guy, just tends to gloss over the basics. If I had written this after my first prelim, which made me question taking the class, idk.

Lectures were very informative and held my attention. Did demos every class. Homework was reasonable and lecture slides are posted at least the day before lecture. Overall a great professor who is passionate about what he does.
Respectful professor. Really kind when answering questions.

Pretty great teacher all around! If you like Chemistry and you're gonna take a course with him, you're in good hands. Clearly shows he loves Chemistry and love to project that to his students. For 2150: Make sure to attend lectures and study from given HW, old PSETS and exams. Book not really necessary IMO.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: lectures are somewhat hard to follow and heavy in proofs for equations (imo like a physics course); a little boring. fun demos at the end of lecs though. labs are time-consuming (learn to use excel) but easy to get full or almost full points every time. tests are difficult. study assigned psets + old tests A LOT. course curved to B average.
Unfair in his dealings with students. Only cares about himself and how he looks to his peers and the administration. Deceptive and dirty. Plays politics a lot.

A very helpful professor who is always open to questions from students. He responds to emails quickly. Lectures are also well-organized, (almost) each time ending with an interesting demo. Exams are not that difficult once you practice past prelims and problem sets. Be prepared for the time-consuming lab reports :)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Really nice prof. You don't really need to go to class because he posts lecture notes (I didn't go 95% of the time). Just skim the notes, do some problems, and you'll do fine

I had Professor Davis for CHEM 2080. While his lectures may seem a bit dull at first, they become interesting, and they are invaluable to passing this course. He always tries to keep things interesting, and always shows cool demos. His prelims are extremely fair. If you studied well, you will have no problem. Overall, Professor Davis is a good prof

The lectures are pretty heavy. Better go prepared e.g print the lecture slides maybe. Prof D used 90% of the lecture time going through some tough practice problems which turn out to be pretty helpful when studying for prelims. Labs started out tough and get a little better toward the end, so really work on those lab reports!

Delivers introductory chemistry material slowly but in an effective way. Attending lectures helps hugely, as he goes over practice problems that are similar to required weekly homework. (Also looks like the grandpa in Up!)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: He was fine but nothing special. Tests are tricky, because he only really covers the bare minimum in class

Prof. Davis did an OK job.  His explanations were very clear and simple.  Often he ran out of time at the end of lecture and scrambled to finish demos.  The first exam was way too easy and was compensated for by a much more difficult second exam.  Overall, he was fair and did an OK job.  I stopped going to class eventually and still did well.

Came into this class as a chem major, left as NOT a chem major. His lectures are mostly useless, and it's much easier to understand if you just read the textbook. TA's office hours are hit or miss. Prof's office hours were not really helpful. FYI, do NOT take this class if you aren't confident in your previous chemistry knowledge!
He's a great teacher with a lot of passion for what he does. The demos are all really cool. My favorite class in freshman year

As most people have said, the lectures are standard and the demos are cool. The P-sets really are a reflection of what he'll put on the tests, so do those (even though they aren't for a grade). He himself is pretty reasonable when it comes to grades and advice, though he may go over your head if you ask him about other chem topics.
Good teacher. Knows his stuff and communicates it pretty well. Tests are fair. Labs are difficult but there is a curve so it's all good. Funny guy, too, and demos are awesome.

Demos ever lecture, which kept it interesting-- he's really great at making the material clear if you listen, though I can't say he's particularly exciting or funny (you may fall asleep in class). Exams are doable, and the class has a pretty big curve. Lab starts out next to impossible but gets a lot better.

Very friendly teacher. He definitely loves the demos (as everyone else here has commented). His problem sets are a very good representation of the prelims, so if you understand the psets, you're set. Although I definitely didn't do well in the course, I'd definitely recommend people to take it (especially if you've had AP chem.) You'll enjoy it!

Great lecturer! Problem sets are a very good indication of exam-type problems. Exams can be a tad bit long, but nothing unmanageable. Helpful during office hours and very enthusiastic and knowledgeable regarding the material. Awesome demos as well.

His lectures were very interesting. He always has some demos for each of the lecture sessions. He communicates the materials very well to the students. He is also very organized and the exams are reasonable.

Great demos. He is really really into kinetics so if you don't understand rate laws well you are pretty much screwed. Tries to keep the class interesting, it sort of ran out of steam at the end of the semester, but it is very obvious that his genuinely interested in his students learning and chemistry overall.

I want to know where his cartoons went! Professor Davis loves chemistry and it shows, whether he's randomly firing cannons into the lecture hall or working out the steady state approximation for the tenth time. He explains concepts thoroughly and gives fair exams, not easy, not backbreaking. He's a really nice guy too!
Cool Demos, wakes me up when I am sleeping in class. It's very easy. I got A+.
Lectures are great; partly due to his clarity and partly to his demos. Understanding and helpful. The class was tough but problem sets and labs helped prepare you for exam.
Problem sets are clear indication of what's represented on exams-- lectures are interesting enough.

Lectures are really useful for understanding the topics and different types of problems.  Always does a cool demo, like exploding gummy bears or a hydrogen balloon.  The practice prelims are pretty much on par and really help you prepare.
demos!!!

Floyd's class is by far my favorite (first semester freshman year). He loves to do demonstrations in class; any day we dont blow something up is a day wasted in his eyes. He is obviously loves the material he is teaching and the feeling transfers to his students. It is a difficult class though.
I went to all lectures because there were awesome deomos. He is funny and friendly.

Throrough and clear presentations of material in class w/ fun demonstrations thrown in.  Definitely a good teacher for an intro. chem class.  A little more difficult than 207 in terms of problem sets, labs, and tests, but manageable.
It's an easy class as long you keep up with the material and do the problem sets by yourself or else you won't learn anything.

Davis teaches from the book a lot, but is helpful and easy to understand. He seems to try not to make exams too difficult. However, he often doesn't teach something needed for a problem set or lab until just before it's due. Loves demos. Overall, makes the class fairly enjoyable and bearable.

def. better than 207!  his tests are actually possible to pass, although the problem sets can be harder and take a longer time to complete. he seems really nice too...makes class bearable with his demonstrations
i love FLOYD
Complete waste of time if you took AP or honors chem in highschool.  Textbook is verbose, but contains little useful information.  Easy class though.

Lectures were a waste. He spent 50 minutes going over about 10 minutes worth of information and the rest was  spent with examples. Also, I went to meet with this professor one-on-one and he was not helpful at all. You can tell he wants to be a good professor, though.
Not the best lecturer, but he tries. His prelims are loooooooong. He could do a better job of using class time effectively (i.e. not so much math and more examples).
Waste of time.  I would have learned more by skipping class and reading the textbook.
Boring.

He's a pretty good teacher.  Lectures are strait forward and easy to follow, an appropriate level for chem 208.  He's a p-chemist and it shows.  if you don't like math, this class might not be for you, but as a physicist I love it.
He's an alright lecturer. Explains things but doesnt really show enough examples. He tries hard to keep people interested.
No Comments
He's a really good lecturer and explains things really well. tests are very similar to homework questions. it's definitely a good class, if you like chem and physics
Really caring, understanding, and prepared. Extra credit offered. Clear on expectations for midterm and final. Good rapport with students in lecture.

Great professor and amazing class. I came into this course knowing barely anything about philosophy, but Prof. Fortier explained the topics in a manner that truly enlightened the way I think and reason about certain things. While this course is way more philosophy than psychology, I thoroughly enjoyed every lecture. Genuinely learned a great deal.

Dr. Fortier is a great professor. There is a lot of writing, but she really helps you a lot with it. There is a lot of assigned reading, but you don't need to read it. This is way more philosophy than psychology, but don't let that scare you; the readings are not that dense, & she really talks it through with you. She's interesting, kind, & smart.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Kind, supportive, engaging lectures. Only two papers, a midterm, and a final. Extra credit available. Super willing to answer questions and engage with students.

Prof. Fortier is very intelligent and kind. She is able to take dense readings by Kant or Hume and explain them in a way that is understandable and relatable to students. When students ask questions, argue or object to certain philosophical ideas, Prof. Fortier is very good at engaging with or expanding on students' ideas.
Good prof, great class, but not a spectacular lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Foster is a passionate lecturer and enjoys his discipline. I would have given him a 5 star rating if it weren't for the fact that I found him too impartial to my issues regarding group members which ghosted me multiple times and made this class hellish. Do NOT take this class alone. Tests are take home, but very technical, fair but long
Genuinely cares about students and is very fair with extensions. Had a great time in this class :)

Prof Foster is very knowledgeable and kind. He is clearly passionate about the material and his lectures are interesting and engaging -- even though attendance isn't required, show up anyways. CS 2112 is an honors course so it's obviously challenging and a lot of work, but Foster puts a lot of care into helping everyone get through.

One of the best profs I've had. Made 3110 very bearable even if in the moment I thought it was too much work. Weekly assignments at the beginning a little tough, but his lectures and textbook are good enough that you can figure it out yourself or with TAs. Would highly recommend going to class to listen to him though. Cannot recommend him enough

I would steer clear if you aren't interested in programming languages and proofs because 4110 is very much the love child of 2800+3110. The homeworks and prelims were really hard to get started on which makes it easy to get no credit. Despite hating the course content, I thought Nate was very genuine and considerate at every turn. Liked him a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: He can't possibly be a better professor than Clarkson for CS 3110, let's be real here. Something about his dull lecturing style started grating on me after a while, and I feel like he didn't do a good job structuring CS 4110 to actually be interesting. The treatment of the material seems surface level to me, not enough detail to any specific topic.

Amazing man, and amazing professor. He really cares about his students, and his lecturing style is engaging - he is clearly passionate about the subject matter, and conveys that passion to students. Grading criteria is very straightforward, but make sure you actually follow the rubric. All in all, if you can take a class with him, do it.
Best professor ever

Foster was (thus far) my favorite professor at Cornell. Engaging, friendly, and incredibly committed to the course and its students. Even with the difficult transition to online learning this spring, he took enormous initiative to rapidly convert a class designed for in-person instruction into one that worked beautifully online. Highly recommend!

The best professor I've had so far at Cornell. Foster is not only extremely knowledgeable about functional programming and PL in general, but is genuinely caring about his students and has done a really good job this semester in dealing with the pandemic while maximizing our learning. Both 3110 professors are top-notch!

Prof. Foster is extraordinarily kind and extremely intelligible, but he is also quite busy compared to other professors. Unfortunately, CS 3110 is now a pale shadow of its former self, and many formerly important topics are no longer covered in great depth
You can actually learn in this class.

Without a doubt the single most thoughtful, compassionate professor I have had in the CS department and Cornell in general.
