Definitely a very difficult class, but he genuinely cares about the learning of all of his students, and he has been working really hard to accommodate and help us in the midst of the coronavirus pandemic.

I love Nate Foster! He is so passionate about the material and he presents it in a very clear manner. After lecture on Valentine's day, he had the tas hand out OCaml pickup lines and chocolates. I'm taking this class during the coronavirus pandemic, and Foster has really shown how much he cares for the wellbeing of students. Ta's also very helpful.

Professor Foster is the nicest, most accommodating professor I have had so far. Although the class is difficult, he works hard to make sure everyone is comfortable in the class and even puts fun music and puns into lectures. Even tho im prob gnna fail the class Great guy and does his best help with understanding 10/10 love him xoxo

CS 3110 has cool material, but far too much work. Lectures are in general not too useful as concepts are presented much more simply than is necessary to get an understanding good enough for the prelims. Projects are too long, and since many of them are group projects, getting a good group is absolutely essential.
Foster believes in the potential of every student. His course is difficult, but he provides excellent resources in order to ensure that anyone can succeed. My favorite professor in the CS department.
the best professor so far at cornell
An amazing professor. The lectures are very fun, and while the course is hard his teaching style will help you do well.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: It's the same format and style as 2800, but with more advanced topics. It feels like he walks us through recent papers, and you really feel like an expert by the end.

He goes through the material in such a clear way. He goes through the experiments and then come to the principle discovered. You definitely need to go to office hours and extra quiz-style questions help though, but those are almost always the same style as the questions on the prelims/final.

Great professor, would highly recommend this class. Some students find the material dry, but everyone agrees that Fox does the best he can with the material and tends to deliver engaging lectures. Big on problem solving, not memorization: you really don't need to memorize anything. Go to the problem solving sessions!!
My favorite prof. He's a really great guy, very human and down to earth. Really good at explaining complicated genetics stuff. I would take any class with him at the helm.

This was the hardest class I've taken but it was very rewarding. Dr. Fox is so nice and his lectures are great. Btw this class is NOT memorization heavy. MY TIPS: Do all the tb practice problems! And never skip lecture bc he teaches stuff that isnt in the tb. Also OH are very helpful (Dr. Blake is great too!)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Challenging but overall very interesting class, important to go to lectures because he tests on that material, the textbook is good for supplementing lectures and practice questions. Dr. Fox is very friendly and approachable, and goes out of his way to help out.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Great professor definitely one of the more difficult courses at Cornell and hard work is necessary, but Fox is a genuinely enjoyable teacher who makes the best of it. Fox is also extremely knowledgeable and always available to talk.

Dr. Fox is probably the best professor I have had so far in my Cornell career. This class gave me my worst grade so far, but I genuinely enjoyed every bit of that class-no matter how hard it got. He is so passionate about what he does, and is such a caring person. When times got tough, he was there to listen to me. DO ALL THE TEXTBOOK QUESTIONS!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class is a real gem. I took it after enjoying my time in 2800, and it was one of my best decisions so far. Fox was hilarious as always, but in the small classroom environment he was also able to dig deep into the field of Genetics, while keeping the workload simple and accessible for everyone. Do your reading and you will get an easy A.

Professor Fox was committed to my learning. He was engaging, patient, and reasonable. His office hours were very helpful!! He was great at recognizing what material was confusing to students and allocating his time wisely. He was also great at reading my face and knowing when I was not understanding.

Great class! IF you like genetics or are a GGD concentration I highly recommend. There are no tests just take home quizzes. You learn a lot (particularly about yeast) and its really interesting and current. If you need help or have to miss class he will meet with you. Highly recommend.  One of top 5 Cornell classes!!!
Difficult class, but good professor

Fox is a great guy who makes genetics interesting by teaching beyond the book. The course is probably the most demanding one I've taken at Cornell. Do EVERY SINGLE ASSIGNED TEXTBOOK PROBLEM to prepare for exams. Exams are difficult and the partial credit is abysmal. Go to every lecture; some things he mentions are not in the book but still tested.
Take Genetics with Fox! By far the best. His lectures are not verbatum from the text which makes it way more interesting. Go to his office hours not Neros, he is way more helpful
He''s a very nice professor always ready to help or answer your questions when you need it. Class average is around 60-65  and some of the problems can be really hard on the prelims.
Dr. Fox is very willing to help and interested in helping his students. The class has a bit of a bad rap, but taking it with Dr. Fox is really not bad.
approachable and willing to answer questions, offers clear solutions, affinity for motorcycles ups cool factor, tests fair
Completely adorable and a very enjoyable lecturer. Prelims are fair but the mean tends to be around 65 (curved to a B).

He's a spectacular lecturer who kind of reminds me of a mouse or some other twitchy, furry animal. If you listen to what he has to say, he's brilliant and great at making the material understandable. And he's very witty-funny. Also, a lot more clear and easier than Goldberg, who teaches in the fall. (Prelims still hard-- averages around 60.)

One of the best professors I've had at Cornell so far!  He gives very clear lectures and is brilliant but also approachable.  Take Genetics 281 in the spring with Tom Fox and you won't regret it. It's still going to be hard regardless, but at least your lectures will be interesting and organized.

Very thorough, engaging lecturer. Concerned with what students think, encourages questions. Extremely approachable during the lecture break, before, after and during OH. Thoughtful and understanding as well. If you need to take genetics, Spring is a good time! Plus, he's a yeast dude, unlike the Fall guy which is a Drosophila dude.

First-rate professor!  Excellent lectures- great explanations with occasional humor injected. Do/understand all book problems, as those are going to comprise the  majority of prelims. Tough class, grades maybe a bit deflated, but you'll learn a lot.
BEST TEACHER AT CORNELL! Lectures are always clear, he is incredibly helpful to meet with and always available- great to talk to about stuff other than genetics too!

Lectures were interesting/engaging most of the time... toward the end of the semester they became somewhat erratic and hard to follow. Overall, a very nice guy, very helpful if you ever see him around. Definitely do the hw problems!
He is way more interesting than the dude who teaches in fall. He's real nice and lively, so you wont be too bored by the tedious material.

Excellent professor!  His lectures are well-planned and organized.  The material is complicated, but he does a good job of explaining things.  It is impressive that he can make this subject interesting!  I would definitely recommend taking genetics with Dr. Fox.  Of course, the class itself is a pain, so better to not take it at all!
amazing professor. incredibly clear. always helpful if have any questions.
Wonderful professor. Definitely wants to communicate to his students well. Looks like Mark Twain a bit, but with a nice compact body (and what a butt).
Fox is an extremely good professor.  In preparation for exams, I suggest doing all problems assigned.
Great professor! His lectures are very enjoyable and easy to follow.  Make sure to take genetics in spring with Professor Fox!
Tom Fox is an excellent professor. His lectures are very clear and interesting, and it is surprisingly easy to stay awake for the two hour lecture. The lab, however, is far from enjoyable.
He's a great lecturer. Lab is the real killer, not the lecture. Take this class in the spring not fall, the fall professor is horrible.

This class is definitely difficult, but interesting and practical. Fox is a good lecturer- a little unorganized but tons better than Macintyre. Lab is a pain, problem solving is helpful. Tests really aren't that bad but you have to put LOTS of time into this course. Don't fall behind!!!!!

Hey Guys, c'mon, FOX is a nice guy. The lectures could be a little bit more structured and follow the test more. But, wow, you really get to appreciate Fox when Macentire came in a did a lecture. Fox was like 500 times better!

Profesor is extremely out of touch with the material on the exam. If you want to do well in the lecture part of the course go to all the Problem Sovling Sessions and do those problems. You should be fine. Lab is a ton of work. If you're interested in the material great class, otherwise stay away.
This class is difficult but interesting if you like biology. Fox is a good lecturer, very clear and helpful. He is an all-around nice guy and kept me awake and interested through a long lecture.
Fly with the hippies

The course subject is difficult, but I think Fox did a good job of teaching it.  He's one of the better lecturers I've had: speaks and writes on the board at just the right pace, so I usually don't have trouble with taking notes.

Yes, it may not be the easiest class, but to be honest I had a LOT more trouble with orgo.  I find the class interesting, and Fox is a great guy-easy to talk to about anything, real down to Earth.  I like his lectures.
The professor looks like a mouse. Actually, he reminds me of the Pinocchio's woodmaker. I like the way he stares into the space after he finishes a thought. Cracks us up and wakes us up.

Lecture had nothing to do with exam content. Lab pushed me to the brink of suicide. Head TA is a psychotic B*TCH who swears too much and treats students like SH*T. This class sucks--stay the hell away!

The class is pointless. all stuff we've learned in other classes, mainly Intro Bio. Lab's the killer. a violation of our constitutional rights in how many hours and days of lab work it requires. doesn't respect the religious sabbath. write a letter!!!
I would rather stick a fork in my eye than take this class again.
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
Freund is a great professor, he made us muffins. The class sucks tho. LOTS of hw, and an emphasis on group work, which isnt my preferred way of learning. prelims and final were difficult too.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Really liked the learning objectives system. Rewarded staying on top of content and kept stress low throughout the semester. Freund has very nice lecture notes and quite good lectures. Much better experience for Diff-Eq than Lin-Alg in my opinion. Very kind and cares about students, personally helped with logistics issue.

I have heard varying things by section, but my non-mandatory section consisted of being handed a worksheet and getting no guidance. We had long problem sets due weekly that did not line up with our in-class work.The tests were 5x harder then any other work we had seen; if you had not previously done well in this course, I would not recommend.

freund was a great prof! accessible outside of class, and taught the information well. 

that said, CALC 1110 as a class was a nightmare. HW is graded on ACCURACY, textbook is useless, and prelims are 5x harder than what's taught in class. might be easier if you have taken calc before, but if you havent (like me), dont take this class

Aside from the weird grading system of 2930 that starts out great but then hits you like a truck in the last 3 weeks, Freund's lectures towards students are outstanding. His lectures are fun and engaging, but sometimes can be hard to follow. You can tell he tries to take students' thoughts into account. Sad to find out he got demoted to calc 1.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Freund's lecture are extremely clear, fun, and well-organized. He is also very helpful at office hour and never make you feel stupid. Stay on track with the LOs and you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Clear and funny lecturer, but dont fall behind on your LOs. His office hours are helpful
Great prof. Sad that he's getting demoted.
I like his funny hair
Amazing lecturer who makes great math jokes to keep the class interested. Moves in a clear logical way and also answers questions well.

lectures are very good, make sure to attend. homework ramps up in time and difficulty significantly towards the end (as does the rest of the class). very strange grading scheme that makes it easy to breeze through the course if you stay on top of things, but is very punishing if you fall behind at any point.
Amazing professor. Super kind and teaches very well. Go to lecture and you'll be fine!

Fruend was good at explaining but I found it kind of slow at times. He has many in class "discussions" where you talk with other students, but I feel like it would have been so much better if he just spent more time explained concepts instead of making the learning interactive.

Terrible lecturer, always saw people nodding off during lecture because he is just bad at teaching. The class itself is prepared fine and the materials like notes and study guides are well made. He is a very bad professor though.

Literally maybe the most KINDEST professor I've had here. Imo course was hard, esp comp to prev years, but it was DEFINETLYY doable (i'm just especially bad at math) so idk what the other reviewers were on lmaoo. Do practice and ur fine, its all textbook based.
Grade cutoffs were fair too, and grades are mainly tests/quiz, but thats normal for math

The quizzes in this class were generally quite rough (and 20% of grade all together). Tests were pretty fair, lecture notes were not always super helpful, homework was fair. I had a technical issue and Professor Freund personally fixed it, he's nice and super helpful. I've heard MATH 2930 is better with him so looking forward to that in the Spring.

David Freund is a nice guy but a bad professor for Linear Algebra. I had him for Diff Eq and he was great because there was a clear rubric and clear expectations. The curriculum for Linear Algebra was all over the place and had few concrete conceptual examples. We kept on revisiting past topics as it became apparent the class failed the T/F probs.

He's a really kind and supportive professor, and his office hours are extremely helpful. The tests were fair, but the True/False questions were quite challenging, being more conceptual and theoretical than I expected.

He's a caring and funny guy. I didn't find his lectures particularly helpful due to a lack of examples and structure, but the course has a lot of resources to help you succeed. The tests were fair, but I think the quizzes were a bit too difficult.
Just lock in and study hard. Linear might be 'considered' easy and you might want to slack off, BUT don't.
He is so nice and you can tell that he truly wants his students to succeed. However, the T/F questions were highly conceptual and difficult for most students. I had an extremely hard time with them.

Every positive review this sem must either have previous experience or is super talented. It's a rigorous version of Lin Alg and is transformed from its “reasonable” reputation it had. True-False questions conceptually are more theoretical and harder than the CAS lin alg (I compared). Conceptual rigor is extremely high- beware of the work.

David is a super nice and kind proffesor! 2940 is very exam heavy 90% of the grade comes from exams/quizzes. The discussion section + textbook readings are very helpful. Lectures are concept based, and include short applications. If you really understand major concepts and the HW then the exams are very reasonable.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Better for 2930 than 2940. Test heavy like every other math class. Very nice and accessible. Quizzes are pretty easy; exams are harder but more than reasonable. Goes a little too slow for me; he should focus going thru more practice problems in lecture. Lecture style not for everyone. Keep in mind, people often come here to rant; you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very difficult professor for LinAlg. Extremely heavy on conceptual understanding. Quizzes and exams are worth 90% of the class! Unforgiving class and punishes those who struggle with exams. The positive ratings on this professor are either extremely gifted test takers or have some sort of linear algebra experience coming into the class.

This class is awful! The professor is absolutely terrible! His lectures are run like a circus. Impossible to pay attention and jumping between random topics, the prelims are impossible with topics that have never been taught or seen on homework. Please spare yourself and do not take 2940 with this professor, absolutely terrible!
Light class, cool professor.

People in these reviews saying he is the worst lecturer they have had are actually delusional. David is an amazing professor. He is by far the kindest professor I have had at Cornell. Quizzes are not bad. Prelims are harder but still reasonable. 10/10 recommend. Great guy. Objectively (3+)/5 professor. I'm saying 5 because he is the goat.

Lectures for this class were basically useless and barely went over any example questions. Homework was long and hard and not similar to what was done in class. Tests are relatively fair. This class is not curved, which sucks. There are four hour-long "quizzes" you need to take, which are often unfairly hard. This class was fair before he taught it

save yourself and do not take Lin Alg with him. most miserable class of my entire college career and he references random Harvard problems all the time and has topics on exams that arent even in the textbook. problems are terribly hard and are heinous. I would rather take a class called how to poke your eye out with a spork than take this one

Heard this class wasn't too hard before he taught it. Lectures and notes give very little information and you have to read the textbook in order to do even remotely well. Tests are much more difficult than the content taught.

Spring 2024: He was a solid lecturer. The grading structure keeps this class rather lowkey if you're on top of it since it isn't really cumulative. I wish less time was spent on the easier topics and more on the last few topics (e.g. PDEs) but the grading system doesn't really allow that to be so. Easy class relative to the other eng. math classes.
Great lecturer

Implemented the mastery system very well, and his lectures were easy to understand. As the course progresses you get less attempts on the harder topics such as PDEs, but that's an issue that can't really be solved given the format of the course. Overall great experience.

He made the learning outcome thing much better this sem. I liked it a lot personally. His lectures were pretty solid. Kinda rushed at the end a little since content was harder. Course is generally smooth sailing until u hit Fourier Series/PDEs. Just practice PDEs a lot b4 the final and use the inner product shortcut when u can, it makes life easier

The Mastery system was a complete trainwreck last fall, and I was scared when I learned Freund would be implementing it as well. However, his version of the system was far superior to Ritz's and as long as you stay on top of things, it's honestly a nice system. Quizzes were fair, prelims were a little harder. Lectures were not great, not terrible.
Amazing lecturer!!! This class was much easier than I was led to believe

Very nice guy and seems like he is a good professor, but the way he teaches makes no sense. Students have to teach themselves new concepts, and get thrown hard questions about what we taught ourselves the next day in class. Might just be Calc 1 in general, not sure
Great professor with amazing lectures.
Not only the best math teacher I have ever had, but one of the kindest people out there. Lecturing is his second nature; participate in class and you'll get so much out of it.
Good prof. You can tell he's taught before. Not sure if he or delp made the tests this year but they were fairer than most past years.
He does aerial silks and bakes cookies for his class. 10/10 would recommend
Avoid at all cost
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: I would say she's the worst professor at Cornell. She doesn't know what she's doing, and believes she's always right, even though she doesn't know any of quant field. Many of students really don't know how this kind of person could be teaching at Cornell.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She tried to convince me that Fixed Effect does not eliminate unobserved, time-invariant effects of each entity. You know what's up... Clearly, she has no idea what she is talking about. There is no way she has taken a statistics course, and I encourage her to do so before lecturing again.

She likes to change the instruction on the same day of big paper dues. And she even tried fine students $20 who use any technology (phone/laptop) in class. And being so sarcastic to some students. Force a student turn camera on while he's driving during a zoom call that on a weekend. She likes to believe what she thoughts, no matter what truth is.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Avoid this professor at all cost if you can. She doesn't know what she is doing at all!!!

A difficult class made extremely frustrating by the professor. Unable to end a sentence with the same thought he started on, hearing him talk actively hurt my understanding of circuits. He lectured by coming in and happily rambling until we got up and left. A nice guy, and grading was okay in the end, but anything I learned was from the lab manual.

He's really nice and means well, but he can't teach. Grading scheme is unclear, tests don't always reflect the content, & lectures aren't helpful in any way. His strategy is to look at the slides he took from another teacher for the first time in class, which means he has no idea what he's doing and sometimes gets his own iClicker questions wrong.
Carl is really helpful and cares about his students (ie. meets up with individual students to discuss labs and writing reports). However, he's not particularly clear at times.
Very confusing recitation.  It would help if this instructor learned to talk more slowly, and not jump so quickly from topic to topic.
Carl is really nice, but he's an awful teacher. Basically didn't teach or spell out his expectations for anything (data analysis techniques, experimental methods, report writing...).

Prof Kozen is amazing and everyone should have the chance to take one of her classes. If you're an FSAD major or minor (or just interested in fashion or fibers) she will always make time outside of class to meet with you and be supportive. She also tells it like it is which can be hilarious. Hoping she never retires bc FSAD could not exist w/o her
The sweetest and most passionate professor ever. You HAVE to take her classes!
Good prof! for FSAD 2310 your group will make or break the class.
I took Kozen for FSAD 3200 and loved her. She is the best dean ever and is so sweet. The class was pretty easy if you did the homework. Love Kozen with all my heart.

Professoressa Fulginiti is truly a smart, caring teacher. Greatly improved my language and cultural proficiency at a high intermediate/advanced level. Would highly recommend for 2202 for students completing the Italian major or minor, or for those who plan to study abroad in Italy. Great course!

Professoressa Fulginiti is a great teacher of the language. Very knowledgeable and kind. Expectations are clear and easy to fulfill - homework doesn't take long at all if you pay attention. It's a good way to boost your grade and reinforce la lingua..
She is the absolute best - very kind and approachable. Made expectations clear and works very hard to teach, easy to learn from. Funny too.
I took my FWS (Italian Sci-Fi) with her. Great person and great teacher!

Fulginiti is such a sweetheart, and she really just wants you to learn the language easily and thoroughly. Show up, participate, and use the textbook and you will get an A, very easily. Maybe an hour of homework per week. Exams are straightforward if you study, easy to do well on.

Good professor is able to explain and break down concepts very well even in Italian as entire class is taught in Italian from day 1 even though it is the first course in the Italian sequence. She is a very fair teacher and respects effort put in.
So sweet and caring, definitely put in a lot of effort to teach the class. Easy A if you study!
My course project was very good! I appreciated Prof. Sue

Professor Fussel was the worst professor I had at Cornell. By the end of the semester, I had no idea what my standing grade in her course was because she had failed to grade even one of the three papers I wrote for the class. Furthermore, the course content was boring and trivial. There was also a terrible group paper at the end. Avoid this class.
Probably one of the best professors in CS, INFO and COMM areas hands down. She cares about their students. You in HCI area, no excuse not to take her class.

Prof Fuhrmann is a wonderful lecturer and is very knowledgeable and passionate in her field. The way this course was structured was quite interesting as a bulk of it were guest speakers within the Asian Studies department and I enjoyed learning the course materials through those different perspectives. The workload was normal and pretty manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Fuhrmann is extremely nice, and very accommodating with extensions. Always willing to talk with students after class. Extremely easy grader. Class median was an A+. I think I had a perfect 100 average in the class because she and her TA Anna, who was also great, gave me full marks on every assignment even when I thought they weren't so great.
There is a lot of reading. Prof. Fuhrmann is very accomodating if you have problems, though.
An all-around amazing guy

Don't listen to the haters. They're right that this course has way too much work, but Bert himself is great. Only a few people can truly understand his comedic genius. He can be a little boring, but what can you expect from a professor who has been teaching the same course for 50 years.
super nice when reached out to personally, engaging lectures that sometimes went fast. do your readings and youll be fine

Nice guy. Useless lectures - flipped classroom should be banned nationwide. Far too much work for 3 credits - Physics 1110 is a waste of a credit. If attendance was not mandatory for the course, there would a 0% attendance rate, as lectures are read directly from slides. It is a shame that an intro class can make so many people dislike physics.

Not a hard class material wise, but work wise it was brutal. Lectures and class are overall very disorganized and you have to self learn everything. The course covers a lot of material very fast and there are absurdly long weekly p-sets. This along with the physics lab will take up at least half of your work time in a week.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The homework was really tough at times, but the course offers a lot of resources to help, such as "study hall hours." The flipped classroom was an interesting set-up, but overall I'm not sure how effective it was in teaching us. The demos were interesting, however. The practice exams and HWs are the best way to study for prelims and the final, imo.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Bert us entirely dedicated to the success of his students.

I am not a physics person at all, but I really enjoyed this class because of Professor Fulbright. He's a great guy who gives good lectures and is easily accessible outside class. You get out of the class what you put into it, but it's not unreasonable. Probably my favorite class this semester.

Can't really say much about the professor, but the class was a well implemented flipped classroom. Lectures involved solving practice problems and some demos that helped students understand them. Homeworks were sometimes challenging, but helped me teach various physics concepts. Prelims were reasonable, unlike the ones in CHEM 2090.
Becoming a great physics "teacher" is not easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr. Fulbright is very caring and always willing to help. But it's a flipped classroom so lectures are mostly iClicker questions. Not the best lectures and reading the textbook is absolutely essential beforehand. Problem sets are quite difficult so office hours are extremely vital. Prelims are highly conceptual and have a lot of multiple choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Bert is always trying to make the material more interesting through the lectures and seems to really care about the students! However, sometimes things get confusing. HW sets are unnecessarily difficult and the tests intentionally confuse you

Prof. Fulbright cares so much about his students and surely loves the material he is teaching. He has so much passion, and his infamous demos show this. He is a great professor, and although the course itself is a decent bit of work, the material is not the most difficult. It was definitely my favorite class I took last semester.
So much homework. Exams slightly harder than homeworks. Lectures not particularly interesting but mandatory due to iClicker questions.
Bert is a southern gentleman that tickles your brain with his smooth southern drawl and most definitely Juuls during class
Physics 1112 is a lot of work, but exams are incredibly fair and do not have any surprises. Hope you get a solid TA who can clarify topics during discussion as that's where I did most of my learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's very energetic and makes really boring physics entertaining. The class is still boring and a ton of work, but his lectures are okay.
Enjoys himself a lot during lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Makes the class harder than it needs to be, with engineering concepts thrown around, while some of us barely know calculus. Some sections were taught better than others. Lecture makes it easier to get a good/passing grade, but it really does not help too much. He is willing to help, a kind man, and really well versed in physics, however.

Don't take his class if you're taking 2208. Take autotutorial, it's way easier. The tests and homeworks were really tough! The TA's were really amazing and very helpful.  The way he scales the class at the end is very generous. It's NOT a bell curve which I think is actually better.

If he is teaching 2208, DO NOT TAKE IT.  One on one he is a kind man, but he is a terrible lecturer and teaches the class like it is an engineering one. He overestimated our math background and gives really  hard tests and homework and I often felt that were not enough office hours to get help.  Take autotutorial instead.

Rigorous use of calculus in a class where the majority of students haven't taken calculus in years. The class passed around a petition to reduce the homework quantity because people were spending 15 hours a week per week on it. Very monotonous with poor explanations, refuses to post answers to anything on blackboard, and very unclear class grading.

Fulbright is pretty decent for a professor. However, his monotone voice may make you fall asleep. He always explains answers to iClicker questions and tries to crack a joke from time to time, which is a plus. His exams were slightly difficult, but if you understood the material to a decent extent, they weren't impossible at all. Overall, not bad.

Fulbright was a nice guy, that is for sure. His lectures were informative, but they were a bit of a bore, unfortunately. What's more is that that attendance was mandatory. Still, relative to LeClair's 1112 class, Fulbright's 2213 was pretty easy, though I'm probably saying that because I switched in after a stint in 2217.
I just want to point out that he is not a professor, he is a lecturer.  He shouldn't even be on this site.

He is the worst prof I have had here.  Really boring and useless lectures, but he unfortunately uses an iclicker.  Tests are way harder than hw and are all based on theory- never had to do any calculations.  This class was a huge struggle, but probably still better than auto-tutorial.  Unless you need it for premed or a major, avoid it!

His lectures are helpful and very detailed in what was a pretty difficult class.  He's a pretty funny guy, not because his jokes are that funny but because his jokes are just so nerdy.  But if you can stay awake you'll get alot  out of his lectures.
Very helpful, very nice, his jokes are hilarious (at times, but at least always entertaining)!  Recommended.

Clear lectures. Very thorough. I heard that Phys 208 is harder than 207, but for me it was more enjoyable and interesting (and easier). Do the Problem Sets, as weekly quizzes in section are based on them. TA OH are extremely helpful. Final was supposed to be cumulative, but it was really just the last third.

Bert is the best!  He is the most helpful professor I ever had.  His lectures are extremely clear and he is always ready to answer my questions.  Unlike many other professors, he makes nearly no conceptual errors.  Bert rocks!!!

Professor is really nice and friendly, cares about students. However, his prelims were terribly difficult! They were long, not enough time to finish them. The lab course was okay. Difficult concepts if no prior experience, the problems really got tedious to do! I hated the weekly in section quizzes!

Professor Fulbright was my lab TA. At first, he seems sort of apathetic towards students based on first impression, but he is not like that at all! He is so genuinely caring about his students. His lectures may be a bit boring because he has the same tone throughout, but he tries to make it interesting with great demos and dorky jokes. He's great!!

Not a great professor.  His lectures are dull and he makes no effort to engage the students.  There are few examples of practical applications of the subject.  The tests and homework demand quantitative answers, while in lecture, he NEVER works example problems.  The students have little interest in learning what he teaches.  Bad class.

I have to say that for a science professor, he's one of the best I've had. He's extremely clear. The course is very well organized. His demos are interesting. All around a good class. The only thing is that he's not too exciting, but he's the punniest man I've ever seen. No one can compare. But please laugh when he puns. It makes him smile.

Fulbright is one of the worst lecturers ever!  His lectures are so dull and simplistic, his jokes are stupid, and he expects everyone to understand the physics at a higher level than he teaches (and he doesn't teach at that level because he probably can't).  He copies the obvious equations from the textbook for his lectures.

professor fulbright is someone who really cares about his students and explains the concepts very well. his lectures might not be fun, but was helpful and well-organized. aboveall, there's none like him when it comes to being a nice, accessible professor. i'd be honored to take another class of his.

Very nice guy, but I sometimes wonder whether he understands the material.  He does not seem to be able to tie all the concepts together.  It will definitely help to seek help from other assistant professors in the course in addition to Dr. Fulbright.

Bert is a nice guy, but not a good lecturer.  He bored everyone in Physics 208.  It is hard to stay awake in that class.  The homework assignments are tough and the lectures usually don't help you in solving the homework problems...try reading the book for help.
He was so helpful!  I had him as my TA and he was the best!
This is pretty much the nicest prof you'll find who is also willing to help you. He knows his stuff and is always available to help if needed.

Of all of my professors at Cornell, Fulbright stands out above the rest. He is willing to help and will bend over backwards to make sure that you do your absolute best. No matter the circumstances, he will help you do your absolute best
No Comments
This guy was amazing. Not only did he make lecture easy to understand, but he also made it interesting! Also, he is one of the nicest guys here at Cornell-very helpful!

Actually interested in the students' learning. He can be a little nitpicky in the assignment grading sometimes, but he will drop a few assignments with the lowest scores. He appears to be very well-prepared and structured with his lectures and assignments. The work can be a little much, but it is pretty manageable.
One of the worst, just want torture students

Gary is an incredibly professor, but the class is hard. Lots of team assignments, be a good teammate, and be prepared to do the work. It is very reasonable to get an A in the class if you put enough effort and come with a good attitude, but this class is heavily based on teamwork. Not an easy A and grading scheme can be interesting, but fair class.

I took HADM 2021 with Gary this semester and really enjoyed his class. He is extremely smart, and you can tell he is passionate about all the students in his class learning and growing. He challenges you to think critically and outside of the box, something that not many professors do. I would highly recommend taking HADM 2021 with Gary.

For students who aren't looking for a hard class (most of the people who have reviewed) this class isn't for you. Gary is an amazing professor. He is brilliant (writes his own code for impressive programs) and is extremely sensitive to students. He challenges you to be a novel and bold thinker, which is strangely lacking in professors at Cornell.

I don't care what other say. Please ignore other comments. He is genuinely the nicest professor I have ever had. He actually cares about his students and is brilliant (he makes all his code himself, it's extremely impressive.) He is clearly very sensitive to student's needs and is an amazing person and professor.

He does not teach at all. He just expects you to know everything by yourself. His prelim mean is around 60. He also doesn't have any rubrics and he grade everything for what he thinks is right. If you ask him any questions, he does not answer directly to your questions nor helping you solve the problems. Don't take his class.

The only reason this class is so hard is because he's so nitpicky. For no reason, you can write your name wrong and he'll give you a 0. One of the only professors I've met in the hotel school who doesn't care at all about their students. Can't believe my tuition pays someone like him.

Past students seem to have a vendetta against Gary due to his extreme efforts to maintain Academic Integrity. There's no reason in 2010 that you can't set yourself up with a good grade going into the final if you pay attention to the prep videos before class for the in-class assignment. 

He takes a very logical approach to his style of teaching.

Lectures typically last 30 minutes and consist of three students showing their homework, a complete waste of time. The only lecturing Gary provides is videos of his code. He does not explain how the code work, he just shows it. 
Acts unprofessionally on several occasions. 
I would not recommend taking his class.

(Part 2 of the previous post) IDK why it didn't show this, but I also got an A in the class because I hustled and answered all his questions the way Gary wanted. Otherwise, I've learned nothing in this course, and he couldn't care less. I'm deeply sorry for the students he hurt.

On god, the worst professor I've ever had. He chooses a batch of kids, picks on them, and fails other kids for his joy. I even heard this man even abuses a couple of his students. Disgraceful. Frankly, I am stunned he is still employed - and his disrespect for his students indeed says a lot about SHA.

I have no problem with teachers who are tough graders that set clear expectations and are there to teach. He has no interest in teaching and cares nothing for students. He won't have office hours or take questions. He belittles students. He is one of those guys who likes to give bad grades. I think it makes him feel like he is better than everyone.
He makes me want to drop out.

Gary has one of the biggest egos at Cornell University. Instantly whenever you ask a question he turn into a uno reverse card and proceeds to ask 30 more to get you to leave. I feel like he sets students up to fail more than to succeed. I know of someone who switched out of hotel school because of this guy.

Gary doesn't understand the concept of a question because he seems unable to answer any of them. He's unclear, harsh, and stubborn. Some hard professors know that they're tough, Gary is blind to the suffering he's inflicting

never have had a worse professor before.. can not understand why he is working here because he clearly doesn't want his students to succeed and never clarifies his expectations/instructions. you ask him a question and he will ask you 5 questions back. also has the biggest ego ever. if you have him, you should immediately switch profs

My computer is short-circuiting from the puddles of tears. So confusing and lacking any future application of the material because nobody understands what he wants and he does not teach. Legit take this class with the other guy because this guy is very smart but he does not know how to teach this in a way people can understand.

This guy has the worst character of any professor I've met at the Hotel School. So unnecessarily strict and wants the worst for his students. He must have written the positive reviews on his page because there's no way anyone likes him.

Proffesor Thompson is wayyyyy too proud of his ridiculous auto grader, horrible to work with and makes me not excited about learning. Would go out of my way to not take this guy again, incredibly ego based and just an overall horrible vibe.

This teacher is so nit picky and quite honestly for the first couple assignments its almost impossible to do well. It almost feels as though Professor Thompson enjoys when his students do poorly so he can correct them- this is shown when he gives cryptic answers while your working on a problem and then grades you down after you've submitted them.
Listen closely and work hard early on and you will do well. Learned a lot.

reviews.comment: Gary runs HADM 2010 (Hospitality Quantitative Analysis/Stats) in a reverse-classroom format. You watch video lectures (<30 minutes long) before class, and come to class and do an Excel assignment with a group. There are TA's to help with any questions and the assignment criteria are clearly laid out. The grading is fair & there's extra credit too!

reviews.comment: Best professor I've ever met. Simply the best. No one can compare.
Loved this professor!  Hard but practical information.  Make sure you take Service Ops with him.

Launchpad is a waste of time and the most boring class I've ever taken. However, Professor Gaulke is really good with advice on our assignments in the Food & Bev labs, especially the final project. It's just that Launchpad is so God damn boring with strict attendance policies. At least you can scroll for 45 minutes straight.

Awful class! Reading every day, talked nonsense, wasteful assignments. Somehow, we got a paper due in one day, making us write a 5-page report (no AI and single-spaced), giving students a low grade, and not considering the effort. Students asked random questions just for the participation grade and not for the purpose of learning.

reviews.comment: Launchpad is a complete waste of time. I'm currently watching a video on how to take a multiple choice test in an Ivy League school. End this half credit class

I wish Gualke was subject to the same 350 character limit we have here on my RateMyProfessor, because BOY he needs it. Every time he opens his mouth I would set a timer to see if it would be over/under 10 minutes, and the over usually won. Very nitpicky grader, LOVES the sound of his voice. Get ready to suck up to him for anything near an A.

LaunchPad is miserable and a waste of student and faculty resources. It is vapid, filling time with  unhelpful and unnecessary info; they hold the class just because it has always existed. Prof. Gaulke is not a pleasure to have leading this course. Graded by attendance, with annoying HW taken too seriously. I'd rather watch paint dry. Or eat paint.

Really annoying tests that are so useless, purely memorization. very cocky and full of himself. grading is super tough, i studied a lot for the exam (for multiple days) and got a B-. most people don't get an A on exams, i think you would have to study for like weeks to get an A. participation grades are ridiculous.

Take all the 5 star reviews in July below with a grain of salt as they are from high school/summer class students.

Most feedback from the undergrads at the Hotel School are quite negative. He's the only lecturer for this core class so there isn't much point of reading these but keep your expectations low. Chef instructors are great though

Reads off the slides and is a horrible teacher. Stops teaching mid way and says "you guys will cover this in lab" when lab is for actually applying what we learn in lectures. Also very inconsiderate towards students' times. Cancelled class the morning of multiple times without notifying students. Too bad there aren't other professors teaching 2360.

Professor Gaulke makes sure that every question is answered and that everyone understands the content. He holds study hall sessions to help students catch up on work. He is thoughtful and understanding. I hope to take another one of his courses in the future!

For any college students, all of the HADM 1102 class was taken by pre-college students (who only took 1 course and it was done in 21 days instead of the usual semester so it may be pretty different from the normal experience). All in all the work pressure wasn't a lot because if highschoolers can do it so can you. but the course was fun.

Mr. Gaulke had a great teaching style as he incorporated a mix of interactive activities and lectures. He showed a broad knowledge of the topic, kept students engaged, and ensured that all were keeping up with the material. I had a great time in his class and highly recommend to anyone who is interested.

Mr. Gaulke was a great professor and I felt that I learned a lot from him. He lectured a lot, but also included activities to go along with with what he was lecturing about. In order to succeed in his class, you need to be willing to participate and ask a lot for questions.

I had Mr. Gaulke as my professor for the precollege program and thoroughly enjoyed his class. While his classes are lecture heavy, he does a great job answering questions and allowing us to fully absorb material. The class was not easy by any means, but still manageable.

Great professor. This class is very interactive, and the professor strives to allow everyone a chance to speak. This class does require a lot of group work, and the professor will answer any questions or concerns on the assignments and the final project.

Mr. Gaulke was a great professor! Very captivating and animated in how he spoke, and the cause of an overall great experience at Cornell SCE. Keep in mind, this course is very lecture heavy so a glass or two of caffeine is very much recommended but group projects are emphasized and the material was well presented/distributed.
Great professor all around. I loved his way of teaching. I usually doze out in class, but he found a way to keep me engaged.

Mr. Gaulke is a good professor with high ability of teaching hospitality classes. His use of language is extremely professional and concise, he explained everything clearly and willing to answer questions from the students. He sometimes will give us self-study materials and let us discover the knowledge which is super good. Overall, he just great.

Mr. Gaulke is a super nice guy. He makes all his lectures engaging and he facilities great conversations in his classroom. Additionally, he is a very fair grader and recognizes and awards people who participate in the class. Overall I had a great experience in his class and I would recommend it to anyone.

I am extremely glad to have taken this course over the summer. Not only did I find the workload just challenging enough, but the teacher is funny and always open to meeting with students to help them. I got COVID during the last few days of class, and this teacher made accommodations for me as well as checked in on me to see how I was feeling.

I had an amazing experience in this course with Mr. Gaulke. As long as you participate and pay attention to lectures, you should do well in the class. He is fair with grades and is willing to discuss them with you. I actually really enjoyed his class; I'm not sure why he got such terrible reviews from other students.

I don't understand the grading criteria, I found it to be very inconsistent and I compared scores with others with the same answer who got partial credit when I got no credit at all. He seems like a decent teacher and the information is well conveyed, but sometimes I was a bit confused and irritated and felt that he wasn't listening.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Seems to care about the students and is willing to work with you and answer questions during study hall. He's pretty clear on the criteria he needs for each assignment but sometimes there is a bit of gray area (nothing few questions can't fix). Overall a decent professor and experience, if you pick the a good group for your project.

Mr. Gaulke is a great teacher, it was interesting material but also challenging at times. Prepare to do a lot of group work so pick a group you like. Ask questions if you have them because he will answer any and all questions. The material can get a little mundane but he always made sure to engage the class every time he sensed us getting bored.

I don't understand other commenters... if you put in the work the class wasn't that hard.  The content is technical and detailed but the instructor does a good job of connecting it to real world examples.  The labs and the project were actually quite fun.  Anytime I needed assistance he was always willing to help.
Great professor. Course has a large workload. Interesting material.

Makes students feel dumb. Clearly thinks he is better than everyone else and is extremely cocky. Only goes by "policy" and is a horrible teacher as well.

He just comes across as a total A-hole. He's stubborn and self-righteous, thinking his class is the most important. He's not a very good communicator or professor, so there are no good qualities redeeming him.

As long as you do your readings and take notes, you will be fine. Yes, the projects are hell, but in the end, you will get the hang of it. This course pace is fast but I made friends :D

takes a thousand years to post zoom recordings, takes a thousand years grading quizzes/assignments, takes a thousand year to respond on ed discussion. there's one cumulative exam that's pure memorization. had weekly quizzes that with useless, specific questions -- he wouldn't unlock the quizzes after so you never know where you went wrong.

The quizzes will leave you like Kyle from Sig Chi- sweaty, shaking and a little dissatisfied. The lab grades seemed completely random. Ed discussion board was a joke; if he does respond, it takes days. The pretentiousness soared higher than the rooftop bars he has expected us to dine at and participate about. Good luck!

Gaulke is the absolute worst professor I have ever had. He is a terrible person to interact with, thinks WAY too highly of himself and speaks down to everyone else. He only knows the information on the slide and makes this topic unbearably boring and insufferable. He's a smug narcissist and I'm sorry for anyone who has him as professor.

reviews.comment: This class could have been a fun intro class but you just learn a lot of useless theories of reactions and bacteria that has no practical value in the real world. Professor Gaulke takes a class that could be very fun for any student from any major that is slightly interested in culinary and absolutely ruins it. Not fun at all. The culinary labs are straight forward. It's a 4 credit class and every point counts, so stay after and wash dishes to get full credit- you won't regret it! Lecture material is dense. Amazing at lecturing.

reviews.comment: At a recent public health conference, I spoke with a professional from Tompkins County who was familiar with the program. That conversation echoed some of the concerns I've experienced myself, particularly around inconsistencies between how things are presented by Gen Meredith, and how they actually are. Btw, the professional called her FAKE!
Learn reputation-control from her by taking selfies with 0 competent students and alumna. Like the review below, she cannot stand academically strong students. Avoid this program at all costs.
She gives more than two job positions to only one student, which looks fishy! No talent, no caliber seen in the student, so what is actually the criterion for hiring?

She has her own favorites and favors them more than anybody else. Gives TA jobs to some 2025 alumni who don't even know how to write grants or explain them. Neither the TA nor the class was helpful. Waste of money, time, and energy!

Instructions are extremely unclear, nothing important is taught in class. 82% of the class fail on the first homework, that's an instructions PROBLEM. Student went to her, brought up the problems and then never acknowledge the problem, kept emphasizing that her intentions were to "help" us, "setting us up for success"?

Jealous of students who work hard and acheive this by themselves. She is less of a teacher more of a competitor! Highly racist. Not sure who has given the good review about her saying she is easy to reach, but you have to email her a lot to get in touch with her or reach out to a staff member in the MPH suite. She and Audrey Baker are the worst.

When she sits in a group, her problem is she will entertain potty mouth students who will bully asian students. Instead of neutralizing the situation and creating a friendly environment, she will laugh and make jokes out of them. She leaves her professionalism at home and comes to work. She is a big bully!
Love Gen! She's super supportive and is easy to get into contact with. Offers great feedback and makes the grading criteria very clear on the rubric.

Horrible! Very egotistic about her experiences, flaunts it everywhere. Very biased. Rubrics -unclear! She never responds to emails. Has zero knowledge. Doesn't teach at all, and will just make students sit in teams and work on the rubric. Very insecure and jealous of ambitious students. Misleads students in career opportunities and is unsupportive.
Very clear and organized lectures. Exams require a good amount of thinking/reasoning so it is good to do practice problems yourself to familiarize yourself with thinking through such problems.

A lot of reviews have said that some material he tested on were not included in lecture. I disagree. Sure, some of the questions were difficult, but I would qualify them more as "thinking cap" questions, where we've seen a similar mechanism in lecture but on the test it was slightly different. TLDR, pay attention in lecture and you should be fine.

reviews.comment: He is pretty good at teaching but the course itself is pretty difficult. It takes a lot of practice questions to succeed in the class. The optional sections were very helpful.

It's organic chemistry that makes u wish u were deead... not Ganem. His lectures are actually really helpful. However, they DO NOT ALWAYS cover everything on the exams -- anything from the assigned textbook chapters is fair game. On that note, don't expect the exams to be fair... expect them to be hard.

His lectures are good and cover everything you need for the test. His tests were generally fair. Curve is generous and better than gen chem. If you go for 1 on 1 office hours with Dr. Ganem, he's very condescending which doesn't help so it's best to learn what you can in lecture and use the TAs for outside help. Great teacher, meh person.

I loved Dr. Ganem even though I didn't get the best grade in honors orgo. I learned so much and he is genuinely such a cool guy. Please go to office hours to learn more about him if you have the chance because he has super cool stories and a very effective one-on-one / small group teaching style as well that you don't get from lectures.
Go to lecture, and go to the practice review sessions because the test questions are not like the lectures. Difficult class but good lecturer

Dr. Ganem is easily one of the best professors at this university. His lectures are direct and inspiring, and he truly gives you all the tools you need to do well in the class, if you work hard. Weekly practice is your best friend in this course. Also, pay attention in lecture, and you will be able to predict what will be big on the exams.
Very engaged in students success, and good lecturer
He explains things clearly and is very organized. gives good analogies
Orgo has a lot of information, but if you do the assigned text book reading, and go to a lecture, the tests shouldn't be too bad. The curve helps a lot too.

Best Professor at Cornell. I've never enjoyed any lectures at Cornell until Orgo with Dr. Ganem. He's a great professor and does a great job at explaning everything simply and nicely. If you pay attention in his lecture and understand and memorize everything he says during lecture you're going to do well on the exams. Fair exams

Dr. Ganem is an amazing professor. Although his credentials can seem intimidating, he's actually quite caring and approachable. He is the only professor I know of who carves out time each week to meet with students. Although exams can be hard, the curve usually compensates. Pay attention in lecture, read the textbook, and you'll do just fine.

Orgo is a tough class, but Professor Ganem makes it bearable with his witty lectures. Stay on top of the material and use resources like the textbook and Unstuck study - it really helps offset the difficulty.

Orgo is a hard class in general, but the lectures were generally pretty clear. Exams were harder than lecture material. Take notes and READ THE TEXTBOOK! I found the textbook super helpful and did practice problems from the book after/in between lectures. It is easy to fall behind, so stay on top of studying bc it can be stressful to catch up.

Yes this course is difficult- it will be no matter where and who is teaching. Prof. Ganem makes the best of it by presenting the material in a witty way and tries to keep your attention by explaining why it is important in everyday life. I highly recommend going to every lecture as it is easy to fall behind.
The only hope you have is to guess on the test. Too much to memorize. Start early, like before the semester starts.

reviews.comment: Prof was very condescending and unapproachable, and his lectures were far below the rigor of the exams. Get ready to study for this class more than your other classes combined, only for some wild guesswork on exams

reviews.comment: I've never had a more organized professor. He carries out lectures seamlessly. That did come with some bad parts he would often brush past details that he didn't feel were that important but left me confused. He's very passionate about what he does and he wants people to get into it which is nice. It doesn't seem like he wants people to fail.

If you want to learn Organic Chemistry don't take this class. I learned more from the Organic Chemistry Tutor.  I got a B in Biochem and Orgo was way harder. Worst professor I have ever had. The average on the final was a 50 SD of 39 to give perspective on how ridiculous the class is. As a professor if your students are failing, it's your fault.

Probably one of the worst professors I've ever had. His lectures are extremely hard to follow and I pretty much learned everything from reading the textbook. Even then, the course itself is very hard but he made it 10x harder. Also, the final exam was on stuff that we hardly learned. Don't take with Gamen if you can avoid it

Professor Ganem definitely knows his stuff, but can sometimes fixate on certain topics that do not count towards much on the prelims. You definitely need to read the textbook and do practice problems outside of homework. Practice prelims are usually a good way to gauge how well you will perform & tend to be tougher than the actual exam.

reviews.comment: Orgo is always hard, but it definitely felt like he made it harder. He also makes it hard to see him directly through office hours, and when you do see him, it's only for 10 minutes, which really doesn't help that much.

Dr. Ganem is a great and organized lecturer. He took feedback into consideration during the semester about the course during the Covid-19 FA20 semester. Overall though, he was not very transparent about how he derived our grades and gave no practice questions/exams to the class to prepare for the exams.

reviews.comment: Thank you Dr. Ganem!

His prelims become progressively tougher but he is not the type of teacher to ask trick questions. I really enjoyed learning orgo because of him!

Interesting material, great delivery in lecture, tons of help from many sources out of class (himself, TAs, CHEM 1057, tutors). Make sure you do as many problems as you can get your hands on, both from the text and from the old prelims that he gives you to study from.

reviews.comment: He's definitely a nice guy and tries to learn people's names. His tests are also very fair- he doesn't test you on what he doesn't teach. reviews.comment: Ganem is easily one of the best professors I've had at Cornell. He's caring, accommodating towards the demands of college, and an incredible lecturer. reviews.comment: Prof Ganem is very clear lecturer and genuinely cares about his students. Orgo is hard because of how it's graded but the subject matter itself is not very difficult and there were no surprises on prelims. reviews.comment: Ganem is the worst professor I have had at Cornell. He is a rude and arrogant professor who only favors a select few. Very unfair and poor lecturer.

Bruce Ganem is a brilliant man who is enthusiastic about Orgo. I can appreciate him as a professor, but I truly hated this course. It's incredibly difficult and the pace is super quick. There is a very competitive nature in this class and once you stop understanding something, you get left behind.

Professor Ganem is, simply put, the best professor I've had at Cornell, period. The man is a genius, and he truly is passionate about Orgo and teaching. His lectures are crystal clear, but this is still a difficult course. Lots of studying is required to succeed. However, Professor Ganem makes it all an enjoyable experience. I recommend him fully

Ganem is by far the best chemistry professor Cornell has to offer in my view after taking Gen Chem 1 and 2 and Orgo 1. Out of all chemistry professors I've taken he is the most innately brilliant and teaches in the most organized and understandable way , but is also very personable. I say this even after receiving a lower grade in the course.

OK guys I screwed up big time in his class. I got overconfident on the first exam since I got an A-, then was putting off studying, and fell behind immensely. I don't know how I didnt get an F honestly. He's a great teacher but I made huge mistakes.
Very clear and easy to follow notes. Difficult class, but he makes it as bearable as possible. Look over his notes for the exam, they help  simplify the book

One of the most intelligent and straight-forward professors in Cornell. His lectures are always at comprehensive level. His tests are very hard if you do not spend enough time on the orgo studying. Talking with Ganem will be your most interesting experience if you get closer with him. Dr. Ganem will make Chem 3570 interesting for you.

reviews.comment: Probably one of the most straight-forward teachers I have ever had! He teaches the information at a very comprehensible level, and he is a very nice teacher.
