reviews.comment: No curve after huge standard deviations. Lectures and lecture slides are not good.are this class graded way harder than it should have been
Great professor, great class conceptually, but 4 question exams leave little room for error.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very strict professor and content in lecture does not match that of exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: not a good experience
He's very passionate about teaching. Great class. Textbook is not really important if you attend lectures and review slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Horrible handwriting during lectures and could not understand him very well so it was hand to decipher, never answered piazza, did not post solutions to practice problems. Did not seem to care for students . Overall, super poorly run class. Curved to a B during COVID while ORIE 3300 curved to an A-.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Good professor, very smart. Cares about students. Most importantly, explains things super clear and always willing to answer students' questions(he asks if anyone has questions many times during lectures). I usually don't write comments, but I would recommend take statsII with him.

Doesn't give solutions to practice tests, homeworks are much harder than the examples presented in lecture, and he mostly just reads off of the slides. Doesn't provide much help and doesn't answer questions about course logistics on Piazza. I would not recommend taking a course with him. Very unsympathetic during a global pandemic.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Read off the slides during lecture that he posted online, tests were confusing and nothing like the homework.

I'm kind of surprised by most of the reviews. I enjoyed his lectures and I liked that he had a lot of examples that were easy to follow. The exams weren't hard, and he allowed a cheat sheet which really helped. Pretty friendly guy too.

Most memorable thing is his stutters during lecture and his really tight & sexy sweaters. Also his really off-mark jokes (in his Russian accent) are pretty funny. Has powerpoints online in case you're lazy, but answers questions during class readily, so it's worth it. Prelim & finals are both ridiculously easy.
No point going to class. Literally read the powerpoint slides he puts up and you will be better prepared as he is not a good lecturer.
He is unsympathetic. I did badly on first exam and I went to personally meet with him. He simply didn't care and didn't want to help me. Was very rude. Do not recommend taking any class with him.

I usually don't write reviews, but Professor Samorodnitsky is amazing. It's a privilege to have him. Always asks if people have questions during lectures. Homeworks are very educational. I also surprisingly have a blast taking his exams, even if I'm not sure on a question.   Very likable guy. Would love to take another course with him.

Overall a very good and *FRIENDLY* professor. My one gripe is that the exams had only 4 questions each, and I feel like I got a lower grade than my level of understanding should have gotten me because I slipped up on one question on one exam.
Chill guy, FAIR tests, and very helpful with questions. much better than some of the other ORIE professors. Stats 2 could have been much worse!
The best ORIE professor I had at Cornell.  Very willing to help students and gives clear explanations.
Awesome guy.
Not an easy class, but the professor is very friendly, helpful, and caring.

Samorodnitsky can be a little difficult to understand at first,  but once you get used to his thick accent, he's pretty darn good. He's the best professor I have had in ORIE thus far. His explanations are very clear and concise and he is very willing to help his students. He's also an awesome advisor -- he cares for his students.
Great professor!  Very friendly and willing to help.  Course and lecture slides are clear and organized well.  Not an easy course but he is clear in his expectations (no pun intended).
USELESS.  Lecture was so useless that he needed an attendance quiz to make people show up.
Not only an awesome professor, but a nice and funny guy in general. Go to class and do the homeworks, and it's almost a guaranteed A.

Very horrible professor. Does not care at all about helping his students.  After not doing well on one of his exams I went in asking what I could do to improve, and his response was "I dont think you studied very hard", when i had spent the last week studying.  If possible, do not take his course.  Horrible class in general, but required for OR.
Everyone falls asleep in his class. He assigns pop quizzes to make sure students attend his boring lectures. He's also very unhelpful and does not care about his students at all.

Lousy professor...lousy course as well...full of theory and honestly, i really don't see how the stuff taught can really be applied... lousy class... better hope and pray you OR majors don't get this professor for your 360
I totally disagree with the last review, he is an awesome lecturer and I learned a lot in 360.

Terrible lecturer. Granted the material is not terribly enthralling, but he does not manage to engage anyone's attention except from his stutter. To keep awake try guessing what word he's going to say as he begins to stutter it.
He tallks too fast for the level of difficulty of the material.  Definitely a nice guy though and awarding extra credit for asking questions is a great idea.

Really amazing professors. Can tell that he's genuinely interested in teaching. He's also a very hardworking professor! :) And very helpful during office hours too. The only thing is.. I don't know why I am doing so badly in his class...

He's a great professor! He explains things very well and encourages questions (by awarding extra credit for them!). His prelims are not easy, but FAIR! He is very animate and keeps the whole class tuned in for the duration of the lecture.

He has a thick accent and stutters (though the stuttering is much less evident when he's lecturing), but explains very well nonetheless. He talks so loudly that it's impossible to zone out or fall asleep, which really does help concentration.

what a great and caring professor!!! really listened to her students and made CHIN2209 as easy as it could be for us (originally had 2 essays, class did so well she made the 2nd on optional). weekly quizzes + readings, but as long as you did the homework and studied hard, this class was 100% manageable. she is interesting and funny and cares sm.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Definitely lots of homework and tests can be difficult. Participation really does matter and so do details on tests. Lovely personality, character, and person overall. Very funny and told a lot of great personal stories. Love the environment and teacher, but definitely difficult class.

Went in with low expectations because of the reviews... but she's pretty great. She is passionate about helping you improve Chinese so it might come off as harsh. She tells funny anecdotes in class. Class is discussion based and she will call on you to answer questions and read.

Went into the class thinking it would be an easy A-- it's not and I am fairly fluent in Chinese. Much of my free time was spent writing essays, doing hw problems, and preparing for the next class. I thought the lessons were somewhat interesting. Su laoshi is a strict and harsh grader. Classes reminded me of Chinese school from my childhood
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Su is caring, but also very harsh and can seem unfair. This classes took up most of my time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I thought Chinese class could be a fun learning experience, but I am so disappointed after taking this class. Teacher Su is very sentimental in the class, and my Chinese has not improved much because her topics are not very interesting. She is not a fair grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This class is hard (be prepared to read and write a ton) but also really rewarding; I thought my Chinese skills improved a lot. I like how she gives you feedback on all your writing and only grades the second draft. Cares about her students and tried to relieve some stress through extensions, shorter exam, etc. Accessible outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Indeed this class is heavy loaded, a lot of homework and projects. I spent most of time on studying this subject and passing the exams this semester. The question in the test is not always meaningful. For example, the place of the temporary government of GuoMingDang, Chongqing or Nanjing. I don't think my Chinese is improved much from this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really love Su laoshi, she's very nice and genuinely cares about her students. Make sure to talk about politics or social justice topics if you want her to like you, don't be afraid to share your opinion. But, she does grade very harshly and all the negatives are true as well. I only did well in the class because I'm fluent (but still ABC).
This is the worst class that I am taking at Cornell right now. Contents of this class are old fashioned, and boring. Antique is the best label of this class.

Complex Chinese is being taught in this class, which it was abandoned decades ago in Mainland China. The essays taught in this class were all written in old times, and dont represent modern life and young people in China. That may be because SuLaoShi is in old generation and doesn't catch up with millennium Chinese literature.

Su Laoshi was strict but clearly laid out her expectations for the students at the beginning. Expect to spend many hours each week preparing for class. Although this course took up a lot of my week's time, it was rewarding due to Su Laoshi's engaging teaching. She truly wants us to get the most out of the class.

Su Laoshi's class challenges you to synthesize what you've learned and use it in free dialogue or conversation apart from the daily dialogues we had to remember, which I think is very important for learning a language. She gives everyone a chance to answer when introducing new words or speech patterns in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Su Laoshi assigned a lot of homework and it was hard for the ABC students who didnt live in China to complete. It was a typical Chinese teaching method by simply giving the students heavy workload with no efficiency. Your grade was decided in the first day of the class.

Loved this class so much. Dreaded taking foreign language to graduate but she was an excellent professor, really made the classroom feel welcoming and productive. You really have to put in the effort to get the grade you want but it's well worth it, I learned so much. Reading T/F quizzes each week, 6 writing hws, 2 oral presentations, 2 exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: This class was cool

Su Lao Shi really cares for her students, and wants them to do well. She can pick up on your problems very easily. and even if she seems like she's picking on you, she really just wants you to improve. Your Chinese will improve greatly if you put the effort into the class.

I had Su laoshi during the 1st half of IMPAC (summer intensive). Chinese is an incredibly tough language and luckily Su laoshi is skilled at teaching.  Tones are very difficult and she does not give up. She makes sure we get it right, & I'm grateful for that. My tones have improved dramatically. She is kind but tough!

Su Laoshi is great, but expect to work very hard and not be guaranteed an A.  If you show that you are trying and go to office hours, she may be inclined to help you out.  Her class is no walk in the park, but you will learn a lot of Chinese and retain it.  Highly recommend her class if you're interested in Chinese.
Very aware of what we needed and knows how to make the class fun and informative! Love her!

Easily the best professor I've ever had at Cornell. I took this course because it was required, and it was certainly not easy. But I worked hard and got good grade. Also the atmosphere of Su laoshi's class was always very good, and I had lots of fun while learning. I now look forward to learning more Chinese the following semester.

Easily the best professor I've ever had at Cornell! I took this course because it was required, and it was certainly not easy. But work hard and you will be fine. Also the atmosphere of Su laoshi's class was very good, and I enjoyed it so much that I look forward to learning more Mandarin Chinese the following semester.

Definitely frazzled as the other reviews have mentioned, but in the best way! Embrace it as a part of his character & you'll easily enjoy the class. Truly cares for his students & the topics discussed each week. Very invested in our 2 project assignments & does all he can to help! Not much work, especially if you have a background in envi sci.

He is a sweet guy and really nice. Be prepared to learn about the Amish. Grades were entirely determined by one massive final project worth 55% and a small assignment worth 35%. The syllabus also changed half way through the semster, but he's chill and will giving you a good grade if you put in the effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Frantz is a very talkative and great professor who is more than willing to give you help. I will definitely recommend his interesting (and not very difficult )courses!
Really funny and knowledgeable guy. I continue to take his classes because I find him so engaging. A little frazzled but in a good way! Would definitely recommend if youre into the topic!

Frantz has been a great professor. I really appreciate all the insight he has as an actual practitioner, especially since the past two CRP profs I've had were just researchers. CRP2000 has been really interesting and you can tell that Frantz not only knows his stuff, but he's passionate about it. I just wish I knew what my grade was lol

Prof. Frantz has no idea what he is doing. He has reorganized the syllabus three times, and his latest modification shows that he is completely unaware of school calendar as he scheduled classes for days when the whole university is on break. Does not know how to use Zoom and complains about it constantly. Lectures are total repetition of readings.
George is the best professor ever at CRP department
chill guy. good TAs, easy homework and exams

I agree that he's a very exciting professor and he teaches R in a very digestible way. The way you earn grades in the class is .. not the most direct? The exams are nothing like the homeworks or examples. The group project is unnecessarily difficult to combat AI use. If you're taking this class because you're interested in R - by all means.

He is so energetic about teaching that it makes the course (which is objectively heavy with work) a lot of fun. Additionally, he cares what students think about the course and adapts it to best suit learning needs. Truly a great prof.

Gerarden's a smart guy. He explains complex econ concepts in simple terms and is clearly passionate about teaching. Super accessible outside of class. It's one of the rare times I've walked out of an upper div econ class having fully understood what was presented to us. Tests are fair. OHs are very helpful for psets.

Worst business professor I had at Cornell. Problem sets include quantitative questions that depend on material not covered in class. There is no textbook and you have to rely on OHs. Exams include quantitative questions that are fairly different from problem sets and practice prelims. Class curved with Master's students to make it even worse.
I would not recommend this professor due to their teaching style.
Not good, stay away
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Avoid this professor

if you're confused by the variance in ratings, he writes the good ones himself. he is notoriously bad, and I recommend you don't take his class unless you need to for graduating/going abroad. otherwise wait.
Unreasonable, abrupt bursts and Unnecessary strict approach made it a stressful learning environment.

Prof. Jakubson's teaching style is certainly unique, but overall, his lectures, which were often at a slowed-down pace, made the material digestible. His cold-calling was intimidating, but you should be fine as long as you're clearly paying attention in class. Expectations for exams are clear, and he's a fair grader. But review slides thoroughly.

Professor Jakubson has a tough teaching style, but engaging with it can pay off. Lectures may be confusing at first, but office hours help clarify things. For study prep, try using unstuck study alongside the free textbook - it's a game-changer.
very disrespectful

He's an extremely nice guy. From the first classes, he clearly clarifies what bothers him and what doesn't. Make sure you are on his side: don't take out your cell phone in class, participate, etc. Basically, be engaged with the class and you will do well. He knows a lot about econometrics and tries to make it easy for students to understand.

To pass GJ's class go to lectures &review the problem sets, modules, &sample test materials. If you don't attend lectures you won't understand how to apply his notes to answer problems on prelims. Mostly he spoke of his EMT experiences & cautioned us to be safe during cold winters, covid, & slope day season. Put in some effort you will be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors. He teaches a difficult subject very well. He does get irked when students ask basic questions he's already gone over, which is why he gets a bad rap. But if you try, getting an A is very doable. His office hours help a lot. Don't let these lousy reviews scare you, they are likely from students who put in little effort

A friendly guy with a hard shell. You will do well if you go to office hours. His lectures can be confusing but once you get it, you get it. The other reviews are misleading-- no one goes to class and no one goes to office hours. It is hard work, but I enjoyed my class with him.

i'm sure he is a very smart economist but he simply should not be a professor. lectures are genuinely useless but attendance counts. acts personally offended if you have a question that is "too simple." extremely condescending. exams are evil (q's are purposely misleading, include "optional" content, avg in 50s vs 90s in other classes). avoid.

By far the worst Cornell professor I've ever had and I've taken every ILR core class. Jakubson genuinely ruined my semester. It's genuinely impossible to follow the lectures/slides, and there is no textbook. He complains every class about how no one comes to class as though it's anyone but his fault.

The other reviews say it all. Professor Jakubson as Economics DUS has been very rude in his communication with students. I don't understand where all this anger comes from when all a student does was asking simple questions.

So rude that I don't understand how he's still allowed to teach. It shocks me that a professor can speak to a student like this. Watching him speak to people like that made me shocked that an institution like Cornell could ever hire him. This man should not be an educator, nor exposed to most decent humans because of his unprofessionalism.
This is one of the rudest most unprofessional professors who will come across on this campus. This man should not be allowed to interact with students.

I only took Jakubson's class to avoid having an 8AM and that was the biggest mistake I've made in my entire Cornell career. If you can avoid Jakubson's class AVOID IT LIKE THE PLAGUE!!!!! He is truly a terrible teacher, if you take his class prepare to not understand anything despite studying for prelims 2 weeks in advance and attending lecture.

Lectures are very hard to follow. material unclear. The only actually helpful days are workdays. I was excited about this class but as time went on, the material taught didn't translate in PS. TA was amazing. I was able to learn the very basic stuff from them. Take it with someone else,
Super lost in this class. Could have been a cool/enjoyable subject, but every lecture makes things more unclear. Wish I had taken it in a different semester.

Professor Jakubson gets a bad rep. He teaches a technical course to students who normally hate anything quantitative, but he really does care about his students. If you do the work and consistently practice on your own outside of class, you'll be fine in this course. This is not a spectator's course - don't try to cram the material.

Professor Jakubson has some harsh reviews, and I knew that going into his class it would be tricky. However, the people writing reviews are likely the ones who didn't put in the effort. He was extremely accessible outside of class and willing to answer any questions! GO TO OFFICE HOURS and you will be fine in this course. Cannot stress it enough
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Went from live to online. Likes to waste time telling stories in class. Lecture barely makes any sense and neither do the psets or tests. He doesn't use a textbook or slides and writes messy stuff on a chalkboard. Study his pset answers hard and you'll do okay on tests thanks to the massive curve. Tests avgs are like a 50. AVOID this class.

One of the worst professors at Cornell, certainly worst in ILR. Incredibly rude to students, expects everyone to know as much as him. Gets distracted during lectures telling pointless stories and being passive aggressive - this class is the biggest waste of time. Also extremely disorganized, prelims are not easy. Avoid this class at all costs.

Jakubson is by far the least caring professor I have ever/will ever interact with at Cornell. He is extremely passive aggressive to students for no reason. I have reached out to him a few times with professional emails asking simple questions about the course of study for econ, and each time he has responded extremely rudely. AVOID AT ALL COSTS!!!!

Completely mishandled online classes. Expects students to attend online lectures but spends the first 20 minutes nagging and down-talking to students. He has a large temper and has a habit of getting upset with students during lecture. Lectures are rambly and unfocused, may be due to unfamiliarity with online format, but still bad for the student.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors at Cornell. The topic was difficult, but Professor Jakubson is incredibly willing to help outside of class. The TA was great. He really wants you to succeed, but you have to put in work. Lectures could be a little slow and tests are hard but everything is curved up.

AVOID this class. He's a nice guy, but not meant for teaching. No one knows what he talks about in class, and he doesn't use slides or a textbook. Says attendance doesn't matter but passes around a sign-in sheet every class. Psets and tests also make no sense, and means fall below 50. Don't worry, the massive curve will save you. Utilize the TA.

One of the best professors I have ever had. If you show up with respect and determination George will show you mutual respect and dedication. He makes sure that everybody in class knows what is going on and is extremely personable. Makes waking up for an early class not just worth it but ENJOYABLE! I absolutely recommend taking his class.

This class is a straight up disaster. Tests are much harder than the hw. I think I finished 2/3 of the final. He is difficult to deal with in class or in OH and gets mad when the prelim average is a 50. I would recommend avoiding him at all costs and take 3120 w/ someone else

Worst class I've taken. Condescending and very disrespectful. He literally makes students chant after him and says things like "good job, you guys finally reached grade school" He says he makes us do this to engage in "educational scaffolding" but anyone with a brain will know that he's just doing it for the sense of control. tldr:Napoleon Complex
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: AVOID him at all costs. He gave the "option" of starting the final an hour earlier with a super long exam that you would't even be able to finish in 4 hours, not to mention that it was not fair for those who chose to show up on time. Questions were tricky and LONG. He didn't provide practice exams and lectures were pointless.
It depends. If you are a normal human, avoid him.

This was the worst class I've taken at Cornell by far. The material is inherently more difficult and mathematical than any course in the Econ major but Professor Jacobson makes life harder than it needs to be. He flips if you whisper to a friend next to you or fall asleep for a second. Very demanding and has absurdly high expectations for students.

I would not recommend taking Labor Econ with Professor Jakubson. He is a nice enough guy, but he takes the structure out of the material and tries to explain it all like one big story. Grading is very arbitrary as students who got 40s and 50s on prelims ended up getting Bs in the class. Take Labor Econ with Hutchens instead.

Amazing professor, I honestly learned so much even though I basically failed every exam, and it ended up being my highest grade in the semester. Visit office hours, study the practice exams, and attend lecture. If you have an option to take him then I highly recommend it!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: AVOID Prof Jakubson at ALL costs. He is the WORST. He is nice if you approach him correctly. But, his class is SO hard. The lectures and textbooks are pretty much useless. Go to office hours and take the practice prelims until you memorize the answers (exactly what he doesn't want you to do) the class is impossible if you don't. Disrespectful Prof.

All test questions are based on practice prelims and problems sets.  There are 2 problems sets about 6 questions each throughout the course. He doesn't grade them he just checks for completion. At the end he curves generously so people who got 40 and 60ish on prelims end up getting Bs for final grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: His class is difficult, but it is fair. His lectures are really helpful and cannot be substituted by the textbook. He really gives a good understanding of basic labor economic thought and theory. I highly recommend taking his class!

Professor George was clear, engaging, and most of all cared about actually teaching econometrics to us in practical terms. He made himself available every day after class if you had any extra question. As long as you went to class, did the homework, and participated you should have no trouble getting an A. Great guy- really glad i look this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE labor economics with Jakubson. For someone who has taken Intermediate level economics courses at Cornell, Jakubson's Labor Economics course was a nightmare. He is disorganized, lectures are like story times, and the more he tries to take the "math" out of his material, more he makes the course pointless. Grading is also very arbitrary.
no, just no

Jakubson just wants his students to learn and if you put in the effort, you will absolutely get a great grade. I understood more about economics in 1 week of his class than I did from an entire semester of micro or macro econ. Do the problem sets, go to office hours, show you're making an effort, and an A+ is very possible.

Professor Jakubson was an amazing professor, definitely one of my favorites. I took the course during the summer and learned so much! I recommend going to office hours. Jakubson really cares about his students and wants them to learn the material, if you show progression throughout the course you will be fine! Thanks George!

Amazing Professor... I entered his class having failed Labor Econ already and ended with a B+.. pretty good considering I failed the first two tests. More importantly, I'm now an econ minor. Thanks Prof. Jakubson!
Great professor. Don't rely on the book. Go to lecture and you'll be fine. Expect to put in some work but he's very approachable in office hours.

Jakubson is a phenomenal lecturer. Prior to the course I had little to no understanding of the material, but he is incredibly good at simply explaining complex topics and I left the class feeling like I finally "got" it. He makes himself very available for office hours. He can be condescending, but he's a very patient teacher for those who struggle

Professor Jakubson made econometrics as painless as possible. He posts solid practice prelims and made himself available every morning for office hours to help struggling students. He grades based on improvement so he won't kill your grade if you bomb one of the exams. His exams are typically very long though.

George's class is intimidating. Prelims are hard. However, if you go to office hours and show progression throughout the course its an easy A-. I almost dropped the class, but decided to stay and I couldn't be happier with the decision. Hes a great guy, quirky but runs a great class. PS  no need to buy the book, just use his hand outs

During office hours, Jakubson is very helpful. During class, however, it seems as if he doesn't care at all. You either know it or you don't, and too bad for you if you don't. Additionally, his exams are ridiculously hard, and we are expected to know the material as well as he does. If you are able to, take ILRLE 2400 with a different professor.

Class is absolutely boring! He uses the same sayings and "explanations" constantly.  Answers questions with questions and useless tangents that have no relation to what the student wanted to figure out. Miserable excuse for a teacher, since he does not like to teach. Talked badly about TA too. Perfect example of the cons of tenure.

This man helped me so much, beyond the classroom included. He is a genuinely caring person who wants to help his students if they come to him for help. As  teacher, he is a little loopy and can be a little frazzled-seeming, but he makes his points relatively clear. Of course, I had him over the summer so I don't know what he's like usually.

Lectures arent exactly clear but they are fairly interesting. He gives out solid practice prelims for the test and curves it generously if need be. Take ILRLE 2400 with Jakubson if you actually want to learn something. The class is curved to a B+/A-.

He really wants to be the professor who gets you into statistics, but his glaring mental instability prevents him from achieving this.  His class is like a gauntlet, be ready to be verbally taunted and treated with zero tolerance if you make the slightly faux pas. Take at own risk

Had him for summer. His notes in his lectures make you wonder why you copied them down in the first place when you review them, but then the magic appears when you go to his office hours because he does a WAY better job explaining than during class. Btw, do NOT do anything distracting such as and even asking your TA a question, or you'll regret it.

Liked the graphs and comparisons and approach of prof. Not a bad guy. Needs to get over his Napoleon complex. He's too much about power and control. Gets in the way of enjoyment of class and the material. Needs to take some vicodin and chill out. Has too much tendency towards anger.
Great professor! Super helpful, one of the nicest I've had at Cornell. Makes econometrics as clear as possible!
Worst professor I've ever had. Avoid this guy if at all possible. He is the devil's reincarnate. You have been warned. That is all.

Is not easy, although, if you do all the homeworks and keep notes in class it is totally do-able! Sessions are extremely important in order to pass the exams and completely understand. The material is great since all are real life/applied cases and that gives the class a great point of view.

Man, everyone's being so mean about this guy. He was really nice to me. Admittedly, he doesn't dress for class and he does kind of swagger, but he's still a great prof. Haters hate because they didn't get a good grade!

Took the course over the Summer.  Definitely a great professor.  Knew what he was teaching and used real world data for the course.  Just go to class, do what Jakubson tells you to do for hw, etc, and there should be no reason why any student cannot ace this course.

Jakubson's an excellent professor with a sense of humor and a passion for economics. Admittedly, he hates it when students don't show up to class or treat him as a joke -- understandably. If you do the work (don't bother with the textbook), go to class, and go to office hours, you'll get an A.

Jakubson is one of the LE department's worst (has been there for 30 years and still has very little recognition). His lectures are terrible--he spends many of them shaming his students after a poor test, then does little to prepare students for the next one. Simply inept at explaining econ concepts and stifles classroom discussion Faculty hates him

If the Devil had a name it would be Jakubson. If you are looking for the worst professor in the world... congratulations you have found him. This guy is worse than death. I generally do well in all my courses but this class i blame it 130% on this guy's mediocre teaching skills. If you are taking this class prepare your souls.

Horrible.  Lectures are incomprehensible. Related everything to "the moon is made of cream cheese." Tested and assigned homework on SAS programming without a single mention or guide. Tests are wayyyyy too long for alloted time. Without exaggeration, the worst professor ever.

He always made himself appear to be very helpful, but I'm not sure how helpful he really was. He has catchphrases which get old fast. He said he would make it a 2 1/2 hour open note final but give us 3 1/2 hours to do it. By the end of the 2 1/2 hours, I had finally arrived at the last 17-part question. Despite this, still not a bad class.

Teacher was very helpful, very approachable. Material was not easy, but he welcome you to his office hours and helped there. He gave out practice prelims and a practice final which all were very useful. His exams reflected what he taught in class. Class attendance is a must to do well!

I second the comments made by the previous commenter. The midterm was hard and the final was god-awful. The lectures were hard to follow and there was very little continuity from lecture to lecture. Not recommended.

Basically taught as an applied course.  Disorganized lectures and a lot of jumping around in the textbook.  Still, Jakubson is a really nice guy and very smart; he always makes an effort to accommodate students.  Few homeworks; tests were really long.  Wish we had gone into the more technical side of concepts.  He doesn't like math.
Publicly humiliates students in a semi-joking manner, causes permanent trauma and fear of the professor.
Totally awesome.

Rudest guy ever. He explains things to you like you're an idiot. Even more unhelpful in office hours. Definitely does NOT stick to the syllabus, he changes what you'll be graded on after every prelim. Overall, is very knowledgeable but CANNOT teach to save his life.
Garbage.  Straight garbage.  Good luck.
No outline of what is expected in class or on tests
Econometics is hard, but if you go to class and pay attention you can get a good grade.  Jakubson is tough, but his office hours are very helpful and the material is interesting.  Great class!
cares about our learning, funny guy
Avoid! Avoid! Spends the majority of the class period making students feel stupid...Does not use the text...This class has given me a huge headache. It is not worth your time.

this man called some poor kid stupid in front of the whole class. i find the way he swaggers and sways about to be greatly offensive. he also needs to stop saying "so far so good" bc its not so good, ITS NOT SO GOOD. finally, he needs to stop talking about his children, as they probably hate him just as much as the rest of the world.
AVOID. Spends the whole class time trying to find different ways to call you an idiot. Doesn't seem like he is teaching economics at all.
No Comments

Terrible teacher.  For one he dresses like a construction worker.  He is unclear and all over the place.  Seems to lecture from the top of his head.  Don't buy the book, he doesn't test from it at all.  He makes fun of ILR students to his higher level econ classes.  My suggestion is to go to the TA's office hours early on.  stay on top of it.

Oki...econometrics is a hard subject to study..there will be people who wont understand it at all...and professor's teaching style can be arguable..BUT he George is very nice person, if you use his office hours, and he is THE easiest grader in economics department. And if metics make sense to you,...you will easily get A+ on this class..

He is actually really nice and only rude when someone deserves it.  HOWEVER, I agree that the question of what to study is extremely unclear:  you don't want to waste your time druding through that boring textbook, but at the same time his class lectures are scattered in their material and it's impossible to to tell which concepts are important.

Office Hours: Gets annoyed when visited, actually called one girl an "idiot" for coming to office hours. She cried. Classes: Also says things like "shut up" and "sick of you" to a certain person in front of the whole class without reservation. Book: totally irrelevant and he just teaches whatever the heck he wants, not necessarily following the boo

He is very knowledgable and a very engagin lecturer. Give him a chance and ignore the silly ratings left by the few unfortunates who are too retarded to understanted basic economic concepts. He gives you solid practice exams and throws a nice curve on the grades if need be. Utilyze office hours if you are confused...he likes explaining things

Jakubson is an outstanding professor and knows his economics.  You must utilize your time well and actually put some effort into this class in order to do well.  The concepts aren't too hard to grasp and he is always willing to help you out if you don't understand the content.  I recommend taking Jakubson although you must know your basic algebra.

I dont know what these negative comments are about. He is amazing. So smart, Jakubson, teaches to the common person. His analogy of picking up chicks in the bar and applying economic theory to it made my semester complete. TAKE LE WITH HIM!

uggggghhhh what a HARD class.  he somehow managed to inject soooo much math into a class that really didn't require it.  Spent much of the class talking about the theories but would expect students to magically know how to do the math on the test. Avoid if at all possible.
Jakubson = Satan. Anyone who says otherwise is an engineer crying tears of joy to have a break from their miserable engineering curriculum.

What a pompous prick. His lectures are jumbled, he removes the projector sheets after 30 seconds, and the textbook is completely useless. His tests are marathons that are challenges to complete. It doesn’t reward knowledge, but how fast you can work. In office hours he says u r either stupid or lazy
worst professor, worst class, avoid at all costs

The worst Econ professor I have ever had. He is arrogant, has an annoying lecture format, and makes his exams unreasonably long. He seems to know his stuff, but he has a really hard time passing any knowledge on to his students.
I thought his class was very fair.  He is very approchable if you give him a chance.  Also he is hot. With that beautiful facial hair.
No Comments
very unhelpful
He is a great teacher and always helpful during office hours.  You just have to go to lecture and take advantage of office hours. Not easy, but you learn a lot.

DON'T BELIEVE THE LIES! Excellent, challenging Economics course - you learn a LOT. Professor Jakubson is super nice and super helpful, and rewards students for exceptional progress. Our TA, Jing Liu was absolutely awesome! HIGHLY RECOMMENDENDED COURSE!
I agree with someone down there. This man is Satan. Every rumor you have heard is absolutely true. This man and this class are two of the WORST things about this school.
His lectures are clear, but the problem sets basically REQUIRE you to show up to every office hours for help.  Tests are exactly like the practice exam.
Straight up awful.
The hardest class I ever took in Cornell...I can still remember the pain of the problem sets after 3+ years...
not a bad lecturer, but unhelpful and arrogant.  thinks he's god's gift to statistics.  smirks a lot and is very short.

Jakubson actually isn't a bad lecturer. Unfortunately, he doesn't convey the material particularly well and his tests are unreasonably difficult. He also was not particularly helpful and when I voiced a concern about the class he kind of blew up.
He thinks that he is an amazing teacher and that his methods will help everybody see the light.  This couldn't be further from the truth.
Yuck.

This man is the devil. He will do whatever he can to make your experience as harsh and terrible as possible. Do not take 321. It is worth it to take 319 and 320 just to not have to deal with Jakubson.

Shes not for everybody, as you can see by the sharp divide on reviews. Shes very strict with deadlines and making sure you are in class and engaged, which rubs many people the wrong way. But she truly does care about the students and will go out of her way to make sure you are doing well.

Likes student questions but will ask them to shelve the discussion til after class if time's an issue. Requires airtight logicexplanation on HW. "Harsh" bc she doesn't allow laziness, rudeness, or excuses from the students - expects people to read posted announcements, doesn't accept the "I forgot" and "I'm really busy" excuses for late work, etc

You will do matching markets of basically everything you could ever think of. She was unclear most of the time; don't expect much of an explanation on concepts beyond what's already on the slides. You also don't have much in the way of other sources to consult for help on HWs since 1) there's no textbook and 2) the subject matter is hard to Google.

She is awful. Subjective grading, not based on any real evidence. Condescending. Will not listen. Try not to argue with her. Material gets old really quickly as she spends 8 weeks covering matching algorithms. Boring after a while and it gets hard to pay attention in class. Do not take just because you liked Networks I (which is an amazing class).

Nicest professor I've had at Cornell by a long shot. People who complained about her "arrogance" and "harshness" are simply those who went into her class with the intention of getting an easy A but ultimately failed. She's extremely fair to her students and she is constantly trying to improve her lecture style by asking for feedback.

amazingly unclear. half of students get what shes talking about and she tells the anyone who's confused to learn it on their own, do extra reading, or see her outside of class which happens 5-10 times per class.  i'll also echo the arrogance statement - seems she feels insecure and tries to make up for it by being condescending to students

She is very clear in lectures and consistently goes over material several times to make sure that students have a firm grasp on it. However, her grading can be a bit arbitrary and you could end losing many points for one mistake (i.e. very little partial credit).
Extremely unfriendly and arrogant during her office hours. Do not try to argue with her or you're doomed. Overall the worst professor in CS/IS department.

This was Prof. Ghosh's first ever course and I thought she did a very good job. Unfortunately, the students came from very diverse backgrounds so some found it easy and others found it more difficult. In all I enjoyed the class alot
Prof. Ghosh was the worst professor I've had at Cornell. Not very helpful, subtly arrogant, and does not present/lecture well. A class with her is most likely not worth your time.

Not the best lecturer. Can harshly grade. We spent 8 whole weeks on matching markets, which got old way too quickly. If you were interested by Networks I, do not take this class. It's not as interesting, nor is the class as good. Avoid if possible.

Prof. Gilbert is great-- he cares about teaching poetry and wants to spark ideas. The seminar class(3525) felt like a small discussion among friends. While there is little work involved, it's beneficial to do the readings and put effort into understanding. Many drop bc they don't find the work worth it- but it is a rewarding + fair A if you attend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Overall a pretty chill class, very open discussion and no real expectation of participation but he will lead you to participate. You're graded on only a few papers and it takes weeks-months to get the grades back, so you'll never really know how you're doing in the class. Gilbert's a very kind person and really cares about the content.

I was really grateful for this class and am glad I found out about Roger. I was so busy this last sem and his class allowed me to get so much done! There really are no expectations. Just take it and get your A. The benefit for you is extra breathing room in your schedule to focus on actual subjects and a free Gpa boost. Works for me!
This class saved me. Roger is a blessing. I would've never graduated without his class. It allowed me to accomplish so much.
Roger is the perfect professor. He is selfless and only wants to educate you. He is so so helpful!!

Roger is my favorite professor because of the way he engages me in the classroom and the way he facilitates a safe space for discussion. He makes me feel like I'm doing well and improving. His feedback on my essays is generous and helpful. The poetry he assigns is fantastic and rich. I only wish he assigned a little more reading.

Amazing! I loved his style of teaching. He allows students to really develop their ideas about the content through open discussion. 

We even met his dog! and discussed our book outside on the grass. What I loved most was the chosen material. I found myself laughing and weirded out sometimes but it was difficult to put the material down.

Professor Gilbert is clear with instructions and deadlines. The assignments required a good amount of reading, but he does not ask for too much from students and gives thorough and helpful feedback. The reading assignments were pretty interesting but could have been a bit more varied regarding themes. Easy to reach and quick to respond.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very boring and probably not the best value. The prof added little the conversation, and most of the students weren't taking it seriously. It reminded me of my high school study hall. E-Z way to get credit if you're just looking to zone out, get other hw done, or hide in the bathroom.

He's very similar to Tom Hill. You won't learn anything at all, and you can count on getting an A without doing any reading, ever participating, or even attending class. Intellectually, his class is terrible. If you're just looking for credit, however, it's fine. He's too anxious to talk back to or correct students. He mostly just keeps quiet
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Gilbert is great. You can tell how much he loves what he studies and he gets so excited teaching it. He assigns a lot of readings but I thought they were all interesting at least. Definitely graded the papers harder than I expected but gave enough feedback to be constructive.
Not the most animated, but still clear and fair. I have much more appreciation for poetry now that I have the patience to understand it. I've even tried writing my own...
Overall a good teacher, especially considering all the trouble I made him put up with last semester, being the wild/rowdy freshmen of the bunch.
I love his sweaters.  And what can I say--he is hot, hot, HOT.
belittles poets by finding them "cute"or "funny"; seems unprepared for class and claims not to understand john berryman as if that is berryman's fault

Professor Vidan is one of the most thoughtful and engaging professors I have across. The lecture materials are super well curated and she puts in a lot of work tying threads together during the lectures. Her office hours are amazing! If one's attentive and puts in the work, it will give you a great footing in tech policy and science studies.

Lectures are dry, but content is super interesting. 

READING QUIZZES every lecture, 1 question based on reading assigned. This is a huge part of your grade but very easy and straightforward.

Prelim format is outlined very clearly and it is easy to study. Structured exactly like an AP test, in a good way. Discussion sections are so helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Okay class but you genuinely can't reason with her.

The class is pretty interesting and I like how it evolves each year with current events. Most of it was busy work but definitely easy, and they told us the exact format to expect for the prelims. There are two policy memos which also weren't too bad. They have a clear grading point standard which is nice.

She is clearly very passionate, however not the most interesting professor I've had. The subject material is usually really interesting though, including up-to-date assignments that require actual creative thought to try to pose solutions to modern day policy problems. Overall I'd say the class and material was more interesting than the lectures.

She is very knowledgeable and eager to help students. Her lecture slides are well-organized, but her lectures themselves often didn't add to the slides that much. Highly recommend going to office hours - she is happy to talk about the subjects, and much more helpful one-on-one! Also - strict about talking in class, don't try and get away with it.

The lectures are easy to follow and exams are quite straightforward. Weekly write-ups are not bad and help guide the main points of the upcoming lectures. My only gripe is that the grades on the two policy memos (a huge part of your final grade!) heavily depend on who your TA is; some TAs seem to grade way tougher than others.
She's very caring, explains systems very clearly, easy to understand, good class structure, has dogs :)
good class
great class
Great class!

Guidi is a great lecturer. She occasionally stumbles or makes slight mistakes, but she's also a pretty new lecturer and those really don't get in the way. When there rare mistakes, she fixes them. Course organization was excellent, even considering the course had just been redesigned. Grading was fair as well. Definitely recommend!
The class is very applied, covers a wide range of topics, and introduces you to numerous tools. The homework can be long but is always rewarding. The lectures are good.

got me interested in microbiology. surprisingly his slides are great if you use a book to supplement with and tho his lecture may be boring many times, he actually explain things well if you pay attention. I had the other professor who teaches in spring for a week, but Ghiorse is much better. He doesn't trick you, and he is willing to help always!

got me interested in microbiology. surprisingly his slides are great if you use a book to supplement with and tho his lecture may be boring many times, he actually explain things well if you pay attention. I had the other professor who teaches in spring for a week, but Ghiorse is much better. He doesn't trick you, and he is willing to help always!!
Good Professor. He is overall a really nice guy. The grading for class was very inconsistent and harsh though.

Engaging at first but he quickly becomes boring. He yells a lot during class and emphasizes things that seem trivial. He's great if you want to learn about life on Mars, but otherwise not very interesting. About half the class stopped showing up to lecture. Killed my interest in the subject.

Very enthusiastic and thorough. He got me very excited about learning microbiology. If you prepare well for the lectures before hand they have a lot of clarifying information as long and you pay attention.

Ghiorse seems to care about students' doing well in this course. However, he is quite soft-spoken and is hard to hear in lecture. The Powerpoint presentation he makes are pretty awful; most slides have far too much information and distracting colors. Otherwise, Ghiorse is fair and knowledgable. Plus, there are plenty of extra credit opportunities.
Lecture is useless. Everything you need is on blackboard. Just go during quizzes. His quizzes are a lot harder than his exams.

This guy's theatrics will keep even the most unenthusiastic person awake in class. He tells you what he wants you to know and then tests you on it- can't get more fair than that. Reading the textbook is unnecessary- just go to lecture and study the ppt slides (posted online.)  Loved the class, can't wait to take the lab this spring.

His lectures are lively, but kinda pointless. He ends up getting stuck on some dumb detail and repeating it instead of getting through the material. He's very enthusiastic and nice though. Quizes are tough. Exams are fair. Read the book. I didn't and did bad. Going to lecture is hardly helpful. As far as advanced bio courses go, this one is good.

Most enthusiastic professor I've had.  Wow!  The concepts are pretty interesting too, but I recommend the lab BioMi 291 to go along with it.  The lab made the information in class a lot more relevant and it was really fun.  The class is kind of far (by the dairy bar) but it wasn't that bad of a walk (or bus ride).

The yelling during lecture is really annoying; you can get by just fine with the takenote if you're willing to pay for it. The tests and quizzes are easy as long as you've studied, and the other assignments are just a matter of putting the necessary time in (which isn't too much anyway). Good class.

Aaahhh, Dr. Ghiorse. Love him. The best thing about him is his incredible enthusiasm for teaching. He seems to genuinely like it & he even got some sort of award for it. He's head of the department, so he knows his stuff. Also, this isn't like the boring science classes you took freshman year. By the end, you'll actually like bacteria.

As has been said, Ghirose's lectures involve lots of yelling and gesticulating.  The problem is, he yells unimportant words like "WATER!" and "AND!"  His powerpoints look like collages, and he is terribly unorganized.  It's an easy A, but don't bother going to lecture - you won't learn anything. Just study the powerpoints.

Dr. Ghiorse is enthusiastic and extremely loud, by his lectures are not very effective. You'll end up learning everything yourself using the book. Quizzes are often very tricky, but manageable. Exams are very easy. The curve was generous, so it was not too difficult to earn an A- or B+ (the median grade). The subject material is very interesting.
Quizes are tricky, hard to do well in class overall cause it is based on a limited point system. Lecture are hard to follow at times.

Dr. Ghiorse is very energetic but he still doesn't teach much. I dont feel like I learned anything. And all the yelling kinda takes away from the real lecture info. Ppt slides are really cluttered and hard to follow.
this class has taught me zero. he likes to scream and smack things with his pointer and tell us about mars. If I cared about mars I would be in another department.
What a lecturer! He's enthusiastic and clearly loves what he's teaching. His nickname among many of his students, Gandalf, is definitely indicative of his vibrant personality.
Very clear with his expectations, and an incredible amount of enthusiasm for microbiology.  He loves his "pet" microscope.  He wants people to learn, and do well.
Good Stuff. Enjoyed Class and teaching.

Very clear, and VERY enthusiastic professor.  Yells frequently to emphasize points, stomps the ground, points pointer at students.  Powerpoint-based lectures but they are extremely colorful and cluttered.  Exams and quizzes are usually easy.
No Comments
Cool lecturer, but not a nice guy in person. But you don't really need to see him for help cuz the course is so easy anyway.
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
not terribly friendly outside of class; very good prof; take ALL the quizzes
DID NOT RESONATE AT ALL with this teacher had her twice got C's for both. It was freshman year too though.
Course is pretty fast paced. I did not resonate with her teaching style.
Super tough grader and very picky with what she wants
I had Prof. Andreoni for my montserrat so I don't know what she's like in a language class but she was always trying to be available outside of class and offers great advice for writing assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Andreoni is so sweet and an incredible Italian teacher. Literally one of the nicest people ever and makes an effort to have everyone participate each class. If you get something wrong she is so sweet about it and never makes you feel uncomfortable or embarrassed. Textbook HW is also super quick. 11/10 would take class with her again!

Professor Gleeson is a full-on baddie. Idk how ppl complain—do you know what you're skipping?? She goes HARD in her research + teaching. You just gotta be ready to be humbled + have a growth mindset. Once you're in, you level up FAST. She's brilliant and solid and ready to support students that show up with fervor. 10/10.

Save yourself. DO NOT take even if you think this is your last resort for a requirement. There were 3 papers and an exam. Even if you hit everything on the rubric, the TA says you have to go "above and beyond" for full points. There are also reading responses every week that you have a 500 min word count but this takes time. RUN.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Had professor Shannon for a PHIL2990 module. Lectures are content HEAVY but have very few things written on slides and readings are lenghty. We didn't have a prelim only the final in her module so I cannot speak to her normal tests. She is passionate about what he teaches, especially sociology, but I would not take her unless you like the content
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are dry and historical (but mandatory). Take notes during theory lectures because you need them for the assignments. She is knowledgeable and does important work in immigration, but assignments are very vague and she can be condescending when asked about them. The TA grades everything, so go to their office hours to ask about assignments.

The grading in this class was really not too bad, but I would only recommend it if you are DEADSET on immigration studies. Gleeson is knowledgeable and kind, but her lectures were kind of a drag. Readings for the course were great (but change every year). The assignments, however, were AWFUL—overly vague and directionless—in my opinion. Overall, eh

Professor Gleeson is incredibly knowledgable about the topics she presents. She provides many guest lecturers to give real insight on the topics and events she speaks about. Her lectures are pretty helpful, but half the class doesn't pay enough attention, or reads anything at all to realize that. If you do the work, and don't bs you can learn a lot
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment:
Professor Gleeson is a wonderful human being and a kind professor.
She is accessible in and out of class, and is more than happy to help you with any concerns and issues you may have. 
This class has MANY assignments, but the class is structured extremely well. Take advantage of office hours and go talk to her! All in all, great professor.

Professor Gleeson is awesome! If you don't have a problem with writing, this is the course for you! Easy A if you submit things on time and follow all her directions. Well outlined course and lots of freedom to write about what you want. Just go to class, talk once in a while, and do some good writing and you will pass with flying colors.

Does not post slides, is VERY one sided in her arguments of what she is teaching.  Grading is fair and not too difficult, biggest challenges are the two mentioned already and the mass amount of material.

The first few classes were intimidating.  She's fast-paced during lectures.  She is very "by the book" regarding submitting papers on time, class attendance, and her expectations, but if you ask questions and go to office hours she will tell you everything you need to do to get a good grade.  Overall, I'd love to have her again.  I learned so much!

Talks SO fast and does not post her slides so write EVERYTHING down. She doesn't respond to emails quickly, so email her days in advance. The readings are the most helpful part of the class, but have a lot of irrelevant information, so learn how to decide what is and is not important.

Missed an exam due to the passing of my father while in college! Glenn was as mean as it gets. Didn't give a passing grade. He is very mean spirited and I can't imagine how and why he is revered, except that he presents a different image to Cornell administration while students have a pretty good read on him. Do not take his courses. Mean spirit.

Altschuler comes across as a very nice guy in class.  However, talking with him 1 on 1 he appears to be a really self-center SOB.  I think only his arrogant peers respect him.  All the other ones pretty much agree and talk about him behind his back.
He's very funny, interesting, & smart. Highly recommend any class with him.
By far the best professor I have ever had in my four years at Cornell. Hilarious, interesting, and fair. I loved his class even though it had nothing to do with my major.

OMG.  Where did this guy come from?? He seems like the nicest guy in lecture and then you talk to him in person and he is a self-centered jerk.  His ego is a mile long and why is that?  Why are the less famous always the arrogant ones!!  It's a powerhouse dept and he is a lightweight.
this is the most fun class ive ever taken

Generally enjoyed the class; found humor and insight in the lectures.  Only reading is the novels involved in the section.  Most were good... Got really sick of reading Jewish perspective books, though.
The most hilarious teacher ever, an incredibly fun and entertaining class.

Absolutely the best prof. at Cornell.  The coolest dude ever.  You really need to pay attention in class to do well on the tests, but the material is so legit that you wont mind taking notes.  If you like woody allen or larry david you will love glenn.

Knowledgable on what HE thought was interesting.  When asked about matters not directly related to his lectures, he is evasive and uninterested.  Takes personal offense if one of the readings is unanimously rated as boring.  Puts on airs...a wannabe intellectual.
cute man
enthusiastic guy
Very engaging lecturer.  Opinionated, but open to debate; a good thing if you're well-informed and a very bad thing if you haven't through things through fully.
A very unethical person. Also writes books about Cornell...bootlicker.
Fabulous teacher - one of the best I've ever had!

Brilliant lecturer...He really forces you to absorb the material just because he speaks with so much conviction. Great command of the language...Tries to incoporate his opinion sometimes, which you should watch out for, but still highly recommended.
interesting professor...lectures started to repeat by the end of the semester. had some moments of humor, but seemed to just stay with general ideas and never moved past them
Should integrate more multimedia into his lectures.
Able to mingle in stories with history..Fun class and is one of the few that youll wake up for at Cornell
Was good at tying individual vingettes together, but rarely seemed to build into anything larger.
A great lecturer, he can be preachy but the his real skill as a teacher is in his choice of topic...he is able to distill interesting stuff into educational material which makes for a fun class.
No Comments
fantastic course!
Funny guy with entertaining lectures, but tries to pass his opinions off as fact.
No Comments
No Comments
Provided a different view of pop culture.  Always willing to help a student.
filters all information through his own perspective before  informing  the class
No Comments
No Comments
Totally agree. And he tries to pass off his opinion as fact.
Altschuler's lectures are very funny, but he can be arrogant.

Very nice. However his lectures were very hard to follow and I felt like a lot of the examples we did in class lacked justification. Expectedly very difficult. All exams were take home and very long I would have preferred in person. Overall an ok professor and a bad class so not much to be done about it

Avoid at all costs.

Time-consuming PSETs, with 3 assigned in the last two weeks, even over break. Lectures are too fast-paced and hard to follow, leaving you to teach yourself most of the material. Not worth the stress.

I'll be honest, I didn't learn much E&M. His lectures are math-heavy and I often got lost. But in my time at Cornell, as my mental health & class grades tanked, Gibbons was the ONLY person to ever reach out and ask if I was okay, and he put me in contact with resources that saved my life. His class is tough, but he truly cares about your wellbeing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: I think other students on here are too hard on Professor Gibbons. He did a solid job of walking us through this class's abundant material. His handwritten notes are very informative, and his assignments are excellent. However, he often seems to have trouble engaging with students' questions, so it's hard to learn from him directly beyond lectures.

Professor Gibbons did a fabulous job with the course. His homework was interesting, his tests were consistently middle-of-the-road fair, and he did a fabulous job making his lectures engaging and interesting. As with any physics class, expect to spend time reading the textbook. This course was a joy.

Professor Gibbons was a very engaged professor. Presenting from a theoretical framework, he started with force laws and derived the rest yet also had cool demos. He was even humorous with relevant Batman quotes. In short, the class was very enjoyable.  Gibbons provided ample assistance outside class with office hours and time to help with homework.
I had no idea what he was talking about during most of the lectures, I tried to talk to him but he refused to help me.

He does a lot of demonstrations which is nice but the lectures are otherwise unorganized and not helpful. The homework is challenging as expected, but the tests are comparatively very easy. Course did not feel indicative of other honors physics courses.
Doesn't seem to understand the material, and no help. Gives the entire department a bad name.
Easiest A of all my physics classes - just don't expect to learn anything from this prof.

Professor Gibbons made his class my favorite of the semester. His knowledge of physics is very deep and insightful, and his explanations are generally very clear. If you ask him for help, he can be a bit vague, but definitely  cares for his students. Also appreciates their feedback. In short, a wonderful mentor!
Useless prof. Avoid if at all possible. Thank god for the TA.

I found Professor Gibbons to be a very good lecturer.  It was challenging because it is honors level, but he did a great job of showing how and when concepts would be relevant. The assigned problem sets were very useful in solidifying knowledge and providing practice, and he is a very easy grader, as long as you show a basic understanding.

Professor Gibbons is so far the best professor i've had at Cornell.  He always made himself available and really cared that you do well in his class.  Yes, the material was very challenging and i spent many hours studying and preparing for exams, but it is an honors level class.  He made it interesting and encouraged you to do your best.

Yeah, this class was ridiculously hard, but its an honors level at an ivy.  While his lectures weren't the absolute best, he was really helpful and when I went in to visit him during his office hours, he was beyond helpful and he even took an active role in giving me ideas for extra practice.
he doesnt teach you anything.. the class is very challenging.. VERY challenging. if you take this class be prepared to self teach !!

Horrible, horrible professor. If you have any option other then his class, take it! Better off taking the class independent study because his lecture adds nothing to the textbook. The homework takes an absurd amount of time and the tests are confusing and come out of nowhere.
Worst teacher ever!!! Do not take a class with him. It will be a huge mistake! No redeeming qualities!
This class is really hard. Go to every section you can. He is a pretty boring lecturer, and fairly tough. Approachable most of the time for help.
His lectures are a waste of time.  I learned everything from section.  A good lab TA will make labs a pain, but you will ultimately learn much more.
Sections are useful, Lectures are completely useless.  Get a good TA.
The TA's make his class understandable.  Thank your TA every day.

attention cornell administration: GET BETTER PHYSICS PROFS. phyiscs department hands down has the worst professors in the school. tests are harder than anything covered in hw or class. this joker doesnt even give all the formulas and expects you to derive them....
bad, but not quite as bad as everybody says.

VERY boring. I skipped lectures because I knew I would end up sleeping. He also curved everything to a C+. I recommend reading the textbook, learning from the TA, and attending those 0013 classes (led by a really cool prof).
Horrible. Puts you to sleep in a second. Would not recommend but isn't that bad if you don't have any other options.

Almost every professor I've had has at least one redeeming quality. Unfortunately, this one has none.  He's boring, confusing, monotonous, and worst of all does not seem to care about his students.  He cares enough to assign large amounts of work, but not enough to explain concepts or give extra help when you ask.  Only passed thanks to awesome TAs
It's all true...all of it.  Avoid him like the black death.
No Comments

Yes, this class is painfully dull. Gibbons is very monotonic, and is not helpful when u go to talk to him. I suggest being nice to your TA, and go to the 013's... they're relatively fun, i learned all the material there, skipped lecture, and did well in the class.

Gibbons sucks at life. Worst professor I have ever had...boring, useless, oversimplified lectures. Hard, long, homework on topics we had to 'teach' ourselves. Hard tests, especiallly the nearly impossible final! very unrepresentative of what we were supposedly taught. bad bad teacher.

Worst professor I've had at Cornell.  I'd rather have my head slammed against the side of Rockefeller for 50 minutes than attend one of his lecures.  He cannot teach to save his life (don't bother with lecture), homework assignments are long and tedious, warmups and quizzes can only hurt you. Acts like his is the only class.  Avoid him at all cost!

one of the worst profs at cornell. Lectures were oversimplified, hws were painfully long/hard, warm ups are annoying as hell, and his monotone voice makes me want to gorge my eyes out. final was the hardest test i have EVER taken in my life (mean was about at 44). lectures are useless, all the material is right from the book, dont take class w/ him

I suggest reading the textbook closely, but skipping lecture altogether. Prelims and final were very detailed, and mostly focused on material not well-covered on the problem sets. Lecture was therefore useless, as he only outlined very basic concepts covered in the text. Also didn't give a complete formula sheet on exams, what was up with that?

I agree with everyone else, this man cannot teach. It's very boring. Do the reading and you can skip lecture. His prelims weren't too bad, but the final was the hardest test I've taken in my life. I expect the mean to be below 50 (from what I've heard from others and how I did myself).  He ruins a potentially good class. Hard, meaningless homework.

Gibbons wants to teach his students, but he can't, he lacks the ability to keep his students involved, entertained and even interested in the material. he tries and cares, to an extent, but is just a very poorlecturer, and very boring.  You can do alright in the class if you read and do everything on your own and have a good TA. Still a lot of work

Might as well not wake up at 9 am to go to class, sleep in, and then just study on your own or in a group later.  Good suggestion, go to the physics 013 class, now that guy, although old, he can teach and is interesting

Gibbons is boring. He genuinely cares about the students- he wants you to be involved. You can tell, because he tries to involve the class through voting, discussing, and "warm-up" exercises. Problem is, it doesn't work. He can't teach himself out of a paper bag. He's boring, and that's incurable.
SO BORING and cannot teach to save his life. Once he tried to do an example in class - emphasis on TRIED. SO BORING. Lecture was nap time.
No Comments
This man does not know how to teach, which is a shame because I really looked forward to taking this course.  I'm teaching myself the course at this point.

He came to lectures half-asleep and talked in a monotone with lots of um's and uh's. He didn't say a word that was not in the textbook, so I just stopped coming to class. The warm-ups questions were ridiculous and unscientific. He didn't even know the right time for the final.

You can either go to lecture or sleep through it. I vote sleep through it. He has some interesting demos and he does some interesting derivations. The textbook sucks, but we don't cover anything outside of it. I got a B and I attended roughly a dozen classes. The daily warm-ups he gives suck.

The lectures are boring and hard to follow with his mircoscopic handwriting on the projector slides.  I def learned more by reading the book than by going to lecture.  It's a teach yourself class. You learn a lot from hw and the TAs are gernally very helpful.  Tests arent too bad though.

Terrible lecturer. You're better off printing off the slides from lecture and learning them on your own then going to the Physics Support Cener for any help. His tests are impossible and his problem sets are unecessarily long.

Class is a waste of time. He outlines the book, without adding anything useful.  The tests and hw are both challenging, but barely any partial credit and no calculators-long division takes up more time than the actual work if you know the material.
He goes over really oversimplified stuff in lecture and the problem sets he gives are impossible, but the exams are very fair, and a lot easier than the homework

Jane was the best professor I have had at Cornell. She is incredibly understanding and caring for her students and provides a welcoming environment for all. If you take her class, watch the movies and go to office hours - you won't regret it!

Jane takes FWS too seriously. Papers are not only marked harshly, she gives them later than the subsequent paper is due which doesn't allow students to improve on their papers effectively. Lectures are boring and films are VERY long.

5 essays + a presentation (ungraded). Average workload except Essay 5 is 4000 words.... why? Avoid her.
