reviews.comment: Lectures were boring, didn't give back essays in adequate time, expected us to watch hours of documentary in one week, and had anger issues: called out specific kids in class and compared the poor performance of the afternoon class to her "better" morning class, didn't learn how to improve my writing and did not receive critical feedback each time

Larry is great, he does make it obvious that 1585 is meant to lure people into taking more history classes so if you think of it like a baby history class it makes more sense. Lots of reading, but if you do them and show interest in sports history you'll probably get an A

I took Sports & Politics with Glickman -- had some interesting topics but overall grading ruined my experience. Not a terrible lecturer but exam content is minimally focused on big picture ideas and themes taught in lecture but more on specifics (dates, obscure people, listing athlete DOBs first to last). some interesting content, poor class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: He is an absolutely amazing professor, I took this course as a distribution but it ended up becoming my favorite course of the semester. The homework was light, the research paper final project was not stressful but extremely interesting to do. Super amazing class!

Great class here at Cornell, Professor Glickman is a passionate teacher who ensures that topics are interesting. Readings are manageable and I felt that tests were reflective of course content. Finally, final research project was allowed to be creative, overall great class, with an interesting topic, and a really caring professor. Would recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great Professor teaching a very interesting class. He is clearly both passionate and knowledgeable about the subject matter which makes listening to him actually interesting. Readings every week but they are really not bad at all if you are interested in sports
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great professor and great class. He's obviously an expert on 20th century American political history and his class taught me so much about the subject and gave me a greater appreciation for the study of history of a whole. He's also super nice and extremely approachable. Overall an amazing class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Very approachable, kind professor that knows his field extremely well. Hes written pieces for the Washington Post and the Atlantic among others which I thought was cool. My only criticism would be that he lectures too much toward the end of the semester (its a seminar). Great class that I learned a lot from.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Glickman is a nice guy and a good professor. The content of Sports and politics class at Cornell gets REALLY REALLYH BORING. It is a LOT of reading and the TA's are so harsh with grading they leave little to no room for improvement. There is a weekly assignment everyweek due THURS 7 am which isn't hard at all. MY POINT IS THE GRADING IS UNFAIR!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof Glickman is one of the best professors. He is passionate about the subject (which is really interesting), and is just an overall amazing human. He responds to emails quickly. He also cancels sections during exam weeks and before breaks. The research paper is only 5-7 pages and the readings are required, but interesting. 15/10 class
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof. Glickman is amazing. Gives interesting lectures and responds to emails quickly. A decent amount of reading and a research paper, but the readings are interesting and the paper is only 5-7 pgs. Take this class if you love sports, I would take it again in a heartbeat.
Great class, interesting and supportive professor.

Easy class. 1 take home midterm and a final paper. Everything is TA graded. Most of the grade for the course comes from section participation. Go to section, participate every once in a while and do the readings. Very reading intensive course, weekly writing responses that are not graded but are just for participation credit.
Extremely helpful one-on-one. Knows the material inside and out. Skip the TA's office hours and go to his instead.
No Comments

People rating low is weird I loved this class it was so incredibly easy (info major so i think maybe aem kids are struggling with the intro level coding) but gomes is so kind and funny, attendance not required, and there's an optional final that no one takes because we were doing fine. simple final project too with no in person presentation

Took this class out of curiosity. At the end, I was filled with nothing but deep regret.
The prelims are designed to ensure you make mistakes. The problems you have to solve in prelims do reflect examples from psets, but are intentionally made more convoluted & tricky. On top of that, you get very little time to solve them. DO NOT TAKE!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Difficult to understand during lecture. Problem sets are filled with busy work with no substance. Prelims are rife with trick questions that aren't meant to teach you anything but to make you try to catch extreme edge cases. I gained nothing from this class except for a stronger dislike for environmentalists.
she's a gem. such a nice prof - sleeper class (no attendance, optional final, easy psets)

Prof. Gomes is a very intelligent woman who does research in very cool areas. However, I thought that her lectures were not engaging and hard to follow. The material wasn't hard but I don't think she explained things properly. She is a very considerate teacher who is very helpful outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Very engaging and explained complex content very thoroughly. You can tell he is passionate about what he teaches!
charismatic, easy to follow, makes u wanna go to lecture, super passionate, simplifies complex concepts, explicitly says what he'd ask on a test
Very charismatic lecturer; made me excited to go to class
Amazing, passionate professor. Does a great job at explaining difficult concepts. I learned a lot from him. Also clear about what material will be tested on. Really enjoyed his lectures!!
Very good explanations and teaching
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Griffitgh

Professor Griffith made this class very enjoyable and interesting. Unlike other sections of labor law though, class was not mandatory (outside of 2 lectures where you are "on-call") and there were daily/weekly write-ups. The class was graded on a midterm, final, and writing assignment and although the tests were dense, they were fine if you studied
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Nice professor who goes over everything in class. She doesn't post the notes though, so make sure you take good notes and review them. Office hours and TA review sessions were helpful. There was a lot of content covered even though she encourages students to ask questions to slow down the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very unclear grading criteria. Disorganized class and do not recommend. Way too harsh on her grading. Don't recommend

reviews.comment: pretty straightforward class and professor. do readings, understand readings, tested on readings. grading was a little vague but whatever
Definitely the best labor law professor. You won't regret taking labor law with Griffith!

Griffith was an amazing professor (definitely the best for labor law). The class is not easy but an A not impossible. You have to be on top of your work. Exams are based on class discussions; pay attention to your classmates not just Griffith.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Such an amazing lecturer. She explains everything so well and clearly. Definitely recommend her for labor law!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Griffith grades based on a prelim, legal writing assignment, and a final. She is very clear in class on how to approach the prelim and the TA is very helpful for questions about cases. Make your life easy and start the legal writing assignment when she tells you to. You don't need to read every case, but be sure you have each brief.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: All you need to know is... that she does her job well.

Prof Griffith is a spectacular teacher. She clarified all of the course material and clearly explained the expectations for the course. 2 tests and 1 legal research assignment. You need to be in every class because EVERYTHING is fair game for tests. Tests are pretty difficult, but she does give the course a curve and that worked to my benefit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Griffith is amazing - always makes sure her students are clear and understand the material. 2 exams one paper. Make sure you take really good notes in class, study, and you'll do great. But, if you miss something or are unclear, make sure you ask questions!! Would recommend wish I could take anther class with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Would take again

reviews.comment: She is overrated on here because the other professors teaching labor law are unbearable. Her class is significantly more work than other labor law professors due to the in class tests. She is a fair and reasonable person and doesn't have the elitist superiority many other professors do. There are pros and cons to her course, weigh them and decide.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: really boring before the 1st midterm but it gets better.  She takes specific notes about your exam so you really know what to improve/understand your grade.  very friendly and helpful and brings in amazing guest speakers. def reccommend for labor law
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great professor. I didn't have any interest in labor law but this class was one of best classes I've taken. It was also the toughest class but you'll be fine if you pay attention in class, take good notes and work for it. Go to office hours if you have questions and show your efforts to the professor and TA. Recommend taking any of her class.

A really awesome professor who knows her stuff, and knows how to get students to learn. Made the class clear and rewarding even though i previously had no interest in law.  The research paper is pretty straight forward, and shouldn't give you trouble unless you wait until the end. And the tests are really clear, she doesn't give trick questions.

Best ILR law professor. There's a ton to study and some of the stuff you think wont be on the exams will be on there. The 1st exam is tougher and the paper is tough, but i think her final curve is strong. she's a great teacher and really sweet. do yourself a favor and take her.
What a great gal, she will answer any and every question you have during class and will slow down and review certain cases if the class seems to have trouble with it.

Excellent. Highly recommend any of her courses. Not the easiest grader, but expectations are made clear and if you put in the work, you'll have no trouble getting a good grade. She does not try to trick or cheat you out of points; everything is straightforward and if you know your information you'll be set.

Best Teacher I have had in the ILR school,  Hands Down. She is very fair and interesting. Great job engaging the class. Tests are extremely fair. Awesome. Definitely take this class with this professor.

I've taken a number of Professor Griffith's classes.  She is always fair and engaging.  She is very willing to help anyone who goes to her office hours.  Definitely the best professor I have had in ILR; probably the best I have had at Cornell.

Professor Griffith was a great teacher. She was very helpful during office hours and always asked students if they had questions during class. She was always willing to further explain cases discussed in class or details went over about specific cases. I definitely reccommend her course!

Clear, accessible, and fair. Anyone who takes the time to see her in OHs knows that she genuinely cares for her students. Presents all sides of policy debates. IMO, the best labor law prof.  Griffith strikes the perfect balance between Gold and Lieberwitz--her classes are not overbearing, but still rewarding and educational.
She's very clear and precise. make sure you pay attention in class. The cases are pretty interesting, and I thought I would hate the class but I actually enjoyed it.

she does a great job at introducing students to law and learning how to apply it. she gives exams for which you can cram but you must have gone to class and have done the reading. you will leave her class with the ability to read and pull out legal principles from cases, but with gold you will know much more but suffer more.

She is so helpful if you go to office hours. You have to do the reading to even think about passing her class. The exam questions are fair. The paper you have to write was a bit unclear but it was graded fairly. You really learn a lot in class...better than Gold (his students leave class depressed and tired).

The class isn't easy and you will have A LOT of reading and the final paper if done properly will be A LOT of work.  However, the exams are fair and Griffith is extremely helpful, especially for those who take the time to see her in office hours.  And in the end it is still less work than Gold, but you learn just as much.

The final paper and midterm/final are fair. She is helpful in office hours. Class can be difficult if you don't do the reading. She teaches the class in the Socratic method so there's a lot of class discussion. I wouldn't buy the text book. She gives you a lot of handouts and you can either borrow a book or photocopy from the library when needed.

Fair grader, nice lady. She and the TA were willing to help if you needed it.  My only real complaint is that she relied heavily on the class to produce the answers to our own questions, and it was sometimes hard to tell which answers were so-so, which were spot-on, etc. Not to mention that a quarter of the time you couldn't even hear the student.

Griffith knows what she is talking about. You learn a lot in the class. It is very straight forward. The tests and paper are very fair. Required reading every class (if you don't do it, the class is can difficult). She encourages everyone to speak.  Recommended.

An overall great professor. He explains concepts clearly and is very kind and approachable. I took him for an upper-level biology course, and exams were mostly based on lecture slides and recorded lectures. If you keep up with the material, the tests were very fair. Office hours were extremely helpful, even though not many students attended.

Martin really cares about the students' learning and success. He is passionate about his research and cell biology in general. The exams were very fair, and the questions were directly from the lectures.
Martin's lectures were very interesting and had a good pace. Exams were based directly off what he said in lecture.

Martin was an excellent professor, clearly very knowledgeable and approachable during office hours. Lectures are fast-paced if you take handwritten notes, but still very engaging and fascinating. Grading is extremely fair, as exams are all MCQs and directly relate to lecture content. TAs are wonderful - take BIOMG1350 even if bio isn't your thing.

He is clearly passionate about Biology, but lectures can be fast-paced if taking handwritten notes, and kind of monotonous. Nevertheless, always accessible by OH and super knowledgable. Prelims are probably the fairest you can get--straight from lectures/slides, MCQ, do well on them and maybe skip the final. Easy class, memorization heavy!

Uninspiring to say the least. One of those classes that you take to get it over with. Nothing wrong with him but just reads off the slides. Voice could put me to sleep. Do well on the prelims and you can skip the final though.
Martin is one of the best professors at Cornell. The grading is really weird and impossible to calculate your grade, but he really is passionate about biology.

I love Martin. He is so wholesome core, and it is so obvious that he cares so deeply about what he teaches. The prelims are solely based on the lectures and the section, so they are fair. He is such a king, and I love his accent.

Dr. Graef was an excellent lecturer. He was passionate and clear. Lectures were densely packed and covered lots of material but are recorded. Exams covered information directly from lecture and were all MCQ style. The grading system for final grades is really weird and impossible to calculate your grade.

I really enjoyed Martin's lectures in BIOMG 1350. He's clearly passionate about the content and explains it in a clear way that is easy to follow. Lectures are the most important part to this class (much more so than the textbook) and I rarely read the full suggested text, only skimmed for pre-class assignments.+lectures are recorded which is great

Dr. Graef's lectures were dense and quick but the prelims were very fair in my opinion. It is a lot of memorization but that is just how biology usually is. If you review the slides and do the practice problems you will most likely do well.

This class is overall just a grind. Martin is passionate about what he teaches but the class is just so much stuff. Sometimes you'll see something on a prelim that was literally the last slide on a lecture, but that's just the nature of the class. Commitment to the class is very minimal; its the studying outside of class which takes A LOT of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: he recorded the lectures so you actually don't fail the class by missing something from the lectures.
Clearly cares about the students, knows his stuff. Make sure to take the notes on the slides before lectures because he goes very fast.

Dr. Graef emphasizes active student participation, with transparent grading criteria. Success relies on attentive engagement during lectures, and Dr. Graef fosters a caring atmosphere, contributing to a positive learning environment. Despite challenges, the course offers valuable insights for dedicated students.

I had him for BIOMG 1350. He definitely cares about making sure his students understand the material but he FLIES through the slides. Just soak it in because taking notes is basically impossible. The class is really well organized. Exams definitely require some studying- basically everything is memorization based.

Michael Gold is a great professor that really gets one interested in ethics. The class is graded by few things but it is not hard if you actually do the readings, which he gives you multiple classes to finish. Would highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: great prof, very informative. Very tough grader, I hate his quizzes. Grades them right-wrong/total so an 8/10 gets you a 60%. Leave the answers you do not know blank, don't try and guess you'll just get it wrong. read the "common ways to lose points" for the research paper, be very conservative w/ word count. Its stressful but grades get curved.

I avoided this class because of the reviews, but it turned out to be one of the most informative classes I have taken in college. Gold knows his tough, and his toughness while grading pushes you to put the effort needed. Your grade will suck, but his curve makes it all worth it. Had a 76 curve to an A
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: Gold has been my favorite professor at Cornell. This class taught me how to read dense information critically to create a case brief, which is an invaluable skill for law school. The course might've been changed to make grading more lenient, since my 82 curved to an A+. If you're considering law school (and even if you're not) take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: YOU WILL BE OK and ask the TA Lisa for help, she's amazing! There is weekly group work, but I never did an assigned reading and ended up ok. I had a 10% raw score my first essay and got a 90% on the revised version. The curve is insanely good at the end, I went from a 75% to an A-, so there is hope. Go to every class cause those points add up.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: ILRGL 4820 He's a nice professor, but he grades extremely harshly and uses archaic methods to teach his students. Extremely difficult to understand what you're being graded on, as the questions for the exams and papers are vague and there is no real rubric. Grades are based on whim. Do not expect feedback on exams or ways to improve for next time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very hard class. First paper had a median of around a 25%. If you want to do well on the two papers, you basically have to spend two straight weeks in the library before you submit them. If you don't want to do that, and you care a lot about your grades, try to avoid this class. Curve saves you; upper 80s turns into A+.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I had Professor Gold for Labor Law many years ago and, because the class was so exceptional, I then selected him to be my advisor for my ILR honors thesis. Professor Gold was excellent as a thesis advisor and helped me develop much better writing and analytical skills. I have always been grateful for his wisdom and patience. He will make you think!

Gold is a class act and a wonderful professor. I was definitely apprehensive coming into this class, considering all of the folklore surrounding both him and the course, but he is a brilliant teacher who really pushes for you to actually learn. I would genuinely take any class he taught.
This dude is terrible do not take this professor he will make you want to go to Cornells bridge

Gold randomly assigns you two partners to always work with for exercises. Pray you have some good partners who do the reading. I got a 27% on the 1st writing assignment that I worked my butt off on. I dedicated an entire week to the final essay and got a 92%. I averaged 56% throughout the semester and got a 69% total after the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Great class to get exposure to law school, but I learned nothing in this class. However, Gold is a great professor nonetheless who will call you out on your bs in class and in papers. also is just a nice and respectable dude overall. I was way below the medians on all the papers (50% weight) and still got a b+.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The pop quizzes are graded right minus wrong answers. Annoying, especially when it is later in the semester and you feel pressured to earn more points to improve your grade. The final paper is incredibly hard, so start early. You can do ok in this class. Participate and you will learn a lot. More than labor law, you are taught critical thinking.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: okay so basically class grade is based off homeworks/pop quizzes abt homework and TWO big papers (+ a rewrite of the paper for final essay.) You can do well in this class but you have to go to office hours with prof and start papers weeks in advance (to have enough time to change it). not very accessible + super unclear criteria for essays.

Gold's instructions for assignment seem clear at first. Ultimately, you realize you did not and he pulls a "gotcha" and you fail the exam. Ex: I spent 20+ hours first assignment, I got a 50%. I spent another 20+ on another assignment and worked with 5 other people, I got the highest grade and it was still below average. Avoid him.

Very knowledgeable, but extremely tough course. If you are going into law, take this class. If not, you will learn a lot but put in an insane amount of time and effort. If I had the option to take a different professor, I would've because I don't want to go into law, but still glad I had this experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Easy to relate with and very understanding
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Yeah, Gold is the hardest professor in ILR for the most difficult course; however, he is one of the most knowledgable professors in the school. This class will not be easy, and will require a lot of work. If you take this class, I promise you will leave it a better student. Gold is unique!
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Gold is a gem. You will truly learn and get your money's worth. Everyone exaggerates over how hard this class is. If you put in the work, you will succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Hardest class I have taken so much at ILR. The material was very dry and the pop quizzes are really difficult. Don't plan on sleeping because there are often 3+ readings due every class plus homework. Papers are graded very harshly. Gold starts every class off with a joke, but someone needs to tell him that he isn't funny.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Most difficult class I've ever taken in the ILR School. Labor Law took up at least 70% of my time this semester, with my other classes crammed into the other 30%. Because most of the cases are antiquated, they're a pain to read and understand. He distances himself from students and I felt intimidated to talk to him most of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: If you value sleep, I wouldn't recommend this prof, but if you have any interest in law you have to take it with him.  Unbelievable amount of hard work, but it pays off in the end.

Professor Gold's class was not easy. But it was my favorite class at Cornell. You learn  a TON. He is inspiring and really dedicated to his students; I was assigned a group and we got along super well so it took some of the pressure off. He wrote my recommendation for law school and now I'm a labor and employment lawyer, if that tells you anything.

worst professor in ILR. Least clear assignments, but has very specific expectations. He doesn't realize that students have other classes besides his, and you will leave each class with no idea of what to do/how to apply the information from class.  Very smart man but awful instructor. Avoid his class at all costs.

if you want to go to law school this is life affirming. otherwise, get a different professor for labor law.  I spent all my time on this class and got an 80% which curved  to an A. Lots of group work but you can't choose your group which sucks sometimes. The Law school TA is SUPER HELPFUL, you'll learn a ton about labor law/your writing. MeanB+

Prof. Gold is great. His class had  a reputation for being hard as hell, but it really isn't all that bad. There is a lot of required reading and pop quizzes just about every class. Most of the homework is group work. Don't worry about his tough grading;  I had a 45% raw score at the end of the semester that got curved to a B. Learned a TON.

For Ethics at Work (sophomore writing seminar), he values more quality than quantity. You don't write that much, but you need to summarize complicated philosophical concepts and theories in 2 pages. Take notes; they help a little. Reading helps a little. Office hours help more.

If you take this class, make sure your footnotes are on the correct side of the period at the end of the sentence--I had 1% taken of my final paper for each incorrectly placed footnote (about 34 in all). If thats the kind of class you like, then go for it. If its not, then you will regret taking it and you probably wont get above a B-.

Professor Gold is the professor who lets you challenge him and doesn't dismiss your ideas when they're different.  My class with Professor Gold is the highlight of my semester. His comments on your papers are longer than the papers themselves; I learn so much about my writing style, my strengths, and my weaknesses. It's  such a pleasure.

His Labor Law course is by far my favorite class. While the work is extensive it is all extremely relevant to the lectures. He starts off each class with a joke or a funny story. He also asks if there are any questions from the previous lecture. In the end, the curve will help you a ton so don't freak about the low grades throughout the semester.

Gold is incredibly intense and intimidating & labor law is undeniably demanding. But he is a fascinating lecturer, a fair teacher, and incredibly knowledgeable. The workload is very heavy but classmates bond over essays & seemingly impossible assignments. The difficulty is worth it; I learned so much in this class. Attendance- basically mandatory.

Probably the most demanding professor at Cornell and the teacher of ILR's most demanding class. He's incredibly smart and experienced.  You will learn TONS about labor law (and time management). Workload is insane, but his lectures and your knowledge at the end of the course make up for it. 2010 is great for bonding with others over lack of sleep.

Professor Gold's course has been by far the best course I have ever taken at Cornell University.  He is a very fair professor which views students as equals, no matter their backgrounds, and challenges every student in the same manner.  I highly recommend this course.
he is a great guy and amazing teacher. don't be scared to take his class. there's work, but it's definitely worth it in the end.
The material is not easy for sure. Luckily, Professor Gold makes it interesting and he is fair.

Probably the best class I've taken at Cornell.  I dreaded the course and Professor Gold before taking his class, and ended up loving them both.  Plan your other classes around this one though -- incredible amount of nightly work.  Gold stimulates creative thinking unlike any professor I've had, and in the end, I view the world differently.

So I figured I would kick off 2009 by reiterating that Professor Gold still is, in fact, moderately deranged. With that said, he is a brilliant professor and a leader in his field. I would not discourage any ILRee from taking his class. His work is tough and time consuming, but I can not criticize Gold for demanding a lot from his students.
Amazing teacher. If you get a chance, chat with him outside of class about something besides class, you'll be suprised.

As a current law school student and former labor relations specialist, I can fully appreciate Gold's teaching style.  I'm sure that I learned more in his class than the other CB201 professors taught their students.  Do not shy away from this class if you really want to learn labor law.

Not to belabor the point, but Prof. Gold definitely is intelligent, knows labor law well, and teaches the topic well. However, unless you have a major interest in (labor) law, it is truly senseless to work exponentially harder in this class than in the other labor law classes. The grading is fair, it's just that the amount of work is excessive.

While he might be a good professor, there is way too much work compared to the other labor law class, and the grades end up being the same.  If you want to learn and dont care about grades, then take him, if however care about your gpa and or time, think twice before signing up

What can you say about Gold? Yes, it's a very demanding & grueling class & you will learn a lot. And yes, nothing that you could ever read or say will prepare you for the amount of work required for this class. He can be insensitive & a harsh grader, but you will walk away w/more knowledge than you ever thought possible. Take him & enjoy the ride.
If you want to go to Law School...take GOLD! He is one of ILR's most knowledgable professors and you are truly missing out if you choose not to take him at least once.

This class is worth at least 6 credits and not the 3 they claim, you WILL be doing hmwk for this class EVERY night and it WILL keep you up to the early hours in the morning for research papers and homework alike- Gold isn't a bad guy, but he doesn't seem to understand that students are taking more than just his class- that or he doesn't care
Gold is pretty interesting in lecture, but this class has waaaaaaaaaay to much work invovled for a mere 3 credits.... avoid if possible

Take Intro Labor Law with Gold if you actually want an introduction to labor law. Yeah this class is hard but if you put in effort you do well, and thats how a class should be taught. You'll learn more here than in any other class I've taken at the ILR school. If you can afford to, do it.
Great Professor, but this class is not for the faint of heart...

most of the positive comments that i've seen and heard about him have been about his wardrobe; i think that should say enough, shouldnt it? this class is very very very hard. there is  online homework every day, and he gives pop quizzes in class. avoid gold if you can.
No Comments

A dapper gentleman indeed, finer cloths could not be weaved by angels.  A symphony of colors await the eyes as he bedazzles the room with his latest vest's of splendor.  Oh what a sight it is to glare upon Michael Evan Gold in all of his splendor, yes a class worth taking if only for the aesthetics

Prof. Gold is one of the most handsomely dressed men at Cornell.  A throwback to a gone era when professors never wore jeans and and always wore a tie.  He classes it up with an array of argiles, sweater vests, and bow ties.  He also has the academic prowess of no one i've had at Cornell

Surviving this class is quite an accomplishment.  A typical week consisted on 3-4 homework assignments and 2-3 quizzes.  Plus, he is also the type of professor who takes advantage of the fact that Cornell schedules breaks to start at 1 in the afternoon.  Also, don't plan on sleeping come paper time.

He requires a lot of work, if you stay on top of it you should be fine.  No final or midterm, but you will take 50-60 online quizes throughout the semester.  He also requires a three part final paper, talk to someone who took the class before to find out how to do well on the paper.

Not that bad of a class.  A lot of work, but when it's over and you don't have to take a final it feels worth it.  You learn a lot, but work hard to learn it.  Prof Gold is intimidating at first, but if you ask him for help he's very receptive and willing.

Somewhat helpful in OH; extreeeeemley hard class, take it only if you really want to go to law school of like the law.  Sometimes can be a real jerk, but sometimes can be nice.  Not a very interesting person
Tons of work. But overall, well worth it. You will get the most out of his classes than you would anywhere else. If you are considering law school, you must take him.
He is one of the smartest profs in cornell, but the class requires a lot of work. He'll "force" you to learn stuff
The mean on a paper was a 30%, enough said. So difficult, you feel so stupid in the class.
tons of work. very difficult. stay away.
Lots of work, but if you do it and do it well, you will be fine
Impossible assignments, but great class. He is a genius and is good at providing help to those who seek it. A must for anyone considering law school, ILR or otherwise.
Tough, but if you stick with Gold's classes you will learn a ton.  He's a great guy if you prove to him that you want to succeed.  Not a professor to take if you are lazy.
You will learn more about the law than you would ever imagine.  He's extremely smart.  He talks down to you.  The assignments are impossible.  Amazing class!
No Comments
You Learn So Much...He will help you if you ask!
Had this guy as professor-- get ready to work hard and fail!
Avoid!
impossible
Demanding, but a great guy if you know him
The worst--degrading to students.

I really enjoyed Professor Greg Londe's class. It was discussion-based and focused on readings from books, which we talked about in class. The essays were based on topics from those readings, and the course was engaging throughout the semester. The class had a very manageable workload and a great learning environment. Really recommend this class!

One of the best and nicest professors I've ever had in my life. He has such a kind and caring soul, and his friendliness is contagious. He is always very understanding toward his students, and tries his best to teach the materials and make sure the students understand everything. He also gives extensions to HW,  this is an easy and fun class.

Professor Londe truly cares about his students. If you need an extension he allows it! He has been very helpful and his discussions are very fun! I took his Comics FWS and absolutely loved it! I originally had no idea how fun comics could be until I took his class! I would 10/10 take his class again if given the opportunity!

Professor Londe is a great teacher. His lectures were engaging and fun. The grading criteria were as clear as can be, and if there was any confusion, he is attentative to anybody with any questions. Readings were enjoyable, and the amount was reasonable. Take this class if it seems interesting, and you won't be dissapointed.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Took Prof. Londe's FWS ENGL1168 (Comics and Graphic Medicine). Easily the best class of my first semester. He made a flexible syllabus and allowed us to submit activities of our own choice. He was very sweet and caring in and out of class. Highly recommend.

I absolutely loved Professor Londe! He is very passionate about what he does and is very accommodating to his students. Lectures mostly consist of discussions from the reading assigned; it's nothing too crazy and is 100% manageable. Definitely take one of his classes if you have the opportunity!

HE IS THE BEST ENGLISH TEACHER I've EVER HAD!!!!!!
He is an angel, so caring and respectful. He listens to all your perspectives and provides you with inspiring feedback.
Class discussions are extremely interesting. He always brings comic books to share with us (some are very interesting).
Take his class--u won't regret!
ENGL 1168. great professor. easy A class. valuable feedback. lectures centered around reading but you could probably get away without reading a few.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Amazing Professor! Had him for FWS and it is imminent that he cares about students and is flexible with syllabi or course structure.
Took FWS class with him not the course what i put. He is a great caring professor.

Took his math & poetry class. Amazing professor. Lectures are really interesting and it's clear that he knows a lot about the subject he was teaching. He was super accommodating during this COVID semester and I'm very grateful for it.

Greg is a great professor and person. His passion for the subject (taken classes with him on poetry and comics) is infectious and you really start to appreciate the material more after his lectures. Helpful outside class too and always willing to chat about things. Would definitely recommend a class with him.

Absolutely incredible professor who truly loves his subject area (poetry) and does everything to pass that on to his students. He cares for his students deeplyand gave some of the best office hours I've personally ever been to, as well and encourages the students to aid and educate each other. Side note, he always seems to have a great book rec.
This professor is angel.
By far the best professor I had my freshman year. I learned a lot about writing as well as broadly disability studies. Would and 100% will be taking again.
Amazing professor, incredibly engaging and very welcoming to students. Would 100% take another class with Dr. Green.

This was such a good FWS to take my first semester of Cornell. Dr. Green cares very much about both the content of the course and his students. He also takes feedback and makes changes to the course based on that. Grading was very clear and based on effort and improvement over the course. He also offered extra assignments for extra credit. 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Green was such a nice and encouraging professor. Course demanded a decent amount of work, but grades are labor-based and not quality-based. Aka your grade is an actual reflection of how much effort you put in. Chose interesting books and he tried really hard to make the material interesting. Participation matters. Would recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Turkish is cool :)
Goat. Just the Goat.
She is a really good and understanding teacher. Usually a very small class (mine only had 4 people). One of the easiest languages in the school... highly recommend.
take turkish!!

Do not be intimidated by Frau Phelps. She is phenomenal at improving your german skills and effectively teaches without making you feel stressed. She made me feel extremely comfortable in class and very casually corrects mistakes. Frau Phelps really is a kind and caring professor. I highly recommend her if you are struggling to pick up german.

Grit is an incredible professor for intermediate German. She balances creating a challenging learning environment with making sure everyone is on the same page very well, and incorporates students at varying German levels. End of the class is a bit project heavy, but they are all manageable if you prep time for them.

I didn't like Phelps as much as others did, but she was definitely not bad. I just think the environment was a little too intense for me, maybe because I missed the "elementary" time of 1210 and 1220. Assignments were not bad at all, but I would probably take a different professor instead. Again, she was not a bad professor, just not my cup of tea.
We covered interesting topics, and the assignments were easy, just a couple vocab quizzes and some short presentations.

Grit is a fantastic professor, especially for beginners. She made all of us in the class feel comfortable speaking, writing, and making mistakes, and was patient with our learning. The class is based heavily on effort and participation. The German studies department is very down to earth and makes you actually want to learn the language.

This FWS is 2x the work of others, but you emerge with a very solid grasp on expository writing and maybe even a new worldview. You also get helpful advice from your TA--most FWS's lack one. Dr. G himself is an acquired taste. To some, he is refreshingly blunt; to others, he seems self-important. To the former camp (me), he's pretty fun to talk to.

This class gives you what you put in.. or so I thought. Take this class if you need to fulfill FWS and don't mind getting a high B or low A. Professor is caring and the class lectures are extremely surface-level. The real education is when you do the readings and write on your own. I recommend just reading John Berger's "Ways of Seeing" instead.

Awesome Professor! His class improved my writing significantly. He was especially helpful in individual meetings and always gave insightful feedback on my work. I believe, however, that this class grades harsher relative to other FWS. If you want an easy A, this is not the class for you. If you want to improve your writing, then I highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Fun and Engaging! Great Professor if your main goal is to improve your writing capabilities, Otherwise it isn't worth it to take the class as a freshman, grading is comparatively harsh compared to other offerings, with courses offering B's just by showing up to class, choose those if you are just trying to fulfill your FWS requirement.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Most challenging class I've taken but I learned & grew a lot with hands-on skills in Arduino, 3D printing, laser cutting. Prof is passionate, knowledgeable, supportive/understanding in group conflicts, and has many office hours. Going to office hours helped a ton. Can seem distant at first but is genuinely kind and helpful if you get to know him.
disorganized, doesn't know how to reach students or engage properly, class was generally unclear, proof not all scholars in a field will be good teachers

The way he communicates is very condescending and just spills criticism leaving you with feeling no way to improve the situation. Not responsive, not helpful at all. He often fails to remember names and pronouns correctly and is disrespectful of people. I honestly don't think he should be a professor

The class selection process is the MOST DISGUSTING experience I've ever had. You have to do all the team matching and work without knowing if he will have the mercy to let you in. It took him more than 1 week to decide it, which left you with very limited choice for alternative courses when you found that you were doomed. Don't step into this hell!

Professor Guimbretière is clearly passionate about hardware and design, but he does not do a very good job of translating that passion into effective or impactful teaching. In-class instruction was not well paced. Grading criteria were also unclear. Note, I hear a different professor will be teaching this course from now on.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: arbitrary and highly subjective grading, zero direction with the semester long project, rushed timeline, dismissive, no help whatsoever
Very helpful and passionate!   Most hands-on prof I've ever seen.
The course is chiefly self-driven. The professor does not add value to the course at all. It is difficult to follow him due to his accent.

Francois gives you a lot of room to really apply the material in class, and is ready to sit down with your group to work out the kinks if you take the time. I think it's pretty clear that he's passionate about design and that helps make the lectures more interesting to me. If you just make sure to follow the bookblackboard, it's easy to do well.

Prof is very nice and willing to answer questions. The pace of the course is quite manageable. While there is daily homework, they are usually easy to complete. The grading is very fair, and the practice exams are very good preparation for the actual exams.

THE German professor. The other German professors are really good and still pale in comparison. Can I have this professor for every class? You literally can't go wrong with this one. As someone who was not looking forward to the language requirement, I couldn't have made a better decision.
Loved her lectures, very interactive and helpful!

The German department at Cornell is the best! Frau Lischke is super friendly and it is clear that she wants her students to succeed and gets excited when she sees students who are interested. How well you do in the class also depends on the TA you get, but overall I thought the class was very enjoyable. Also participation matters a lot.

One of the most enthusiastic professors I have had so far at Cornell; you can really tell she cares about your progress in the language. Her grading wasn't the most lenient I've seen, yet she tacks off enough points so that you are both satisfied with your grade and want to improve for the future. I would love to have another class with her!

Professor Lischke is outstanding and has sparked a interest in the German language and culture in me. I initially took German to fill a language requirement, but after a semester under Lischke and her phenomenal TAs (shoutout Spencer and Jason), I'll likely be taking German the rest of college. Classes are engaging, fun, and not too challenging.
She's very nice, but assigns a lot of pointless busywork.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The class itself is relatively easy, that said you'd still have to put a bit of effort. But I'd definitely recommend her classes

Intro to German is a difficult class no matter how you spin it, Professor Lischke does a very good job at engaging students and making content digestible. That being said, your success is hinged upon getting a good TA, which I did not. The majority of learning is done outside of class and without a solid TA to reinforce concepts, its a nightmare.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: She's very German: straightforward, organized, and a little tough. Each class had a clear theme (this was a business German class). Her feedback was always very helpful and never overwhelming. I have heard that for lower-level German classes she can be a bit strict, but for a 2000+ level I would definitely recommend her.

I love Frau Lischke as an instructor! I had my first two semesters with her then one with a TA and then 2040 with her. I can safely say she really cares about her students' progress. She is like an Oma. BUT: She doesn't seem to enjoy those who do not put in effort or make progress. She will correct your speech and can seem reserved but she cares.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Want to learn German? Take a class with Frau Lischke! The entire course is taught in German but she is very understandable- I learned more German in one semester than I learned Spanish in three years of HS. Class was always fun and interactive, and she is so funny! I wish I could have taken more classes with her; one of my favorite professors.
She is just the best.  The class isn't hard, but attendance really does matter.  She is extremely helpful and easily one of the best professors at Cornell.

Frau Lischke is an excellent professor. That being said, the class itself is not the best. It is 100% dependent on your TA, who almost never speaks English in class, making it difficult for a zero-previous-knowledge person to do well. If you are someone that typically does well with languages, then this class will work for you because of its pacing

Best language professor I've had. Always well prepared, personable, and cares about her students' education. Enthusiasm is great. Anybody complaining probably didn't put any effort in - she's not so strict that you can't get away with things any many students (in the intro sections) take advantage.
Very good teacher who loves her job.  I highly recommend her class.
She explains things very well and has a great sense of physical humor. Charlie Chaplin-worthy.

One of the best german professors that I've ever had. Always very prepared for class and very knowledgeable in many areas. Business German is a great class. She's very accessible and ready to help if you approach her. Take her class!!

She's a great person, and knows her material well.  Very professional and always willing to help you if you show interest.  For those of you who didn't like her class, you probably did not participate very much.

Frau Lischke is not exactly warm and cuddly, but she's really professional and obviously cares about her students and wants them to do well. I can't believe  this person called her mean spirited, she's too professional for that. She's tough, though. You'll have to work hard, but you learn a ton.

I came here so excited to begin my German Studies, something I have wanted to do for many years now.  I am going to drop the program because of Frau Lischke.  I cannot believe Cornell employs such an unprofessional, mean-spirited woman who dances and hides behind a thin veil of a smile.  Stay Away.
she is terrible. just terrible.
She is an excellent teacher and very professional. She loves her job and does it very well. I highly recommend her classes.
An all around bad teacher.  The germ. dpt. here has a rep for being bad, she's no exception

She picks favorites and hardly tries to hide the preferential treatment she gives those students.  She frequently seems to be carried away to the point of mania.  Unfortunately, this is the rule--not the exception--of the german department here.  I am a german studies major, and would have opted to not attend cornell, had i know about the deprtmnt.

Frau Lischke is a great professor.  She really cares about student progress and manages to make boring subjects sound interesting.  She is always willing to help and provides students with a lot of say in course material.
Frau Lischke is one of the best teachers I have met. She teaches clearly and is able to create a rapport with students to bring out their best. I highly recommend her classes to everyone.
Frau Lischke is a great teacher.  She cares about student progress and is extremely helpful.

Came into lecture day 1 talking German (scary). It is really funny when she acts out german words.  She climbed up on a table once and walked on the very edge of it to act out a word once. The novel we had to read in 122 was really boring.
She is an excellent teacher.  She is always available for extra help if you need it and truly cares about the students learning.

BAR NONE the best German teacher here.  Designs her teaching technique so that everyone is learning, regardless of ability.  Most caring, flexible, and understanding.  Makes learning German a pleasure.
Really nice and always there when you need help. Very good teacher.
She is such a great teacher; really wants you to learn the material and is very understanding and super-super fun!
No Comments

Okay class and fair Prof. In person lectures are pointless because the class is flipped with video lectures, which were convenient. Weekly quizzes were a fair way to test learning but unfairly graded on R syntax for paper quiz.  Learned more about R which made me like R less, niche, and redundant material if you've taken other programming classes.

Guinness was fine. The lectures are on YouTube. The weekly exercises are fun and challenging at times, but there were weekly quizzes that required coding with pen and paper and they're not great. The final project was hard but really rewarding. You will for sure come out a better R programmer. Grading was okay, but can sometimes be nitpicky.

My favorite professor at Cornell! His class was pretty difficult but definitely worthwhile, and I'm a much better R programmer now. I see that old ratings are complaining about the final project, but he was always transparent about the expectations. Overall fair. I wish the classroom had windows, but that is probably out of his control.
i would say definitely a bad way of handling the final

Assigned lectures and lab time are office hours, so you teach yourself. Homework grading is fine, cuz it is done by TAs (no feedback no answer key though). You won't know how ridiculous your grades for the final project will be. NO CLUE. and no feedback or comment either.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Grade unreasonably harsh on final projects to curve people down. Lectures are just looking at previous recordings.

You don't get the points for your understanding of the course or any of the effort. You write 2 question on final project they give you 60 and you receive 70 with all questions completed, just like a random int generator between 60 70 80, no feedback for the final project nor the homework.
Prepare for your final project, insane grading
I hate this professor. He assigned unnecessary work to us. Meaningless and useless. Never choose him as a professor to "help" you 5999 project.

Fairly tough assignments that really test the depth of your knowledge (ie: requires lots of studying and genuine understanding of the topics). However, the curve is fairly generous and medians for his class are usually B+/A-. Good professor, it's just a lot of work even for a 4-credit class.

Good professor that genuinely cares that students are understanding key-concepts covered during lecture. Clearly has a strong understanding of what he's teaching and teaches content well. Exams are quite difficult and requires intense review to gain a genuine understanding of statistics- prepare to work hard for your grade.
Good guy

Professor Gu is one of the best professors I have had at Cornell. He really makes the material engaging and interesting, which I am sure was difficult considering the class was taught through Zoom this semester. Great class and great professor!

Prof. Gu is a very caring and hilarious guy. Very strong accent makes lectures hard to understand at time. Content in lecture and discussion are interesting. Class is not nearly as easy as I was told it was. Class is pretty genetics heavy, and prelims require a decent amount of studying. Not an easy A, definitely makes you work for it.
Class was decently interesting, and you could skip a few and still do well. Not the hardest course and pretty interesting.
He's the bomb .com

Professor Gu wants his students to do well and works hard to make sure they do. He is an incredibly accommodating professor, possibly even too much. The course material is very manageable and do-able. There are amble opportunities to get help.  The class taught me a lot without stressing me out, which is a rare combination in a science class.
Dr. Gu obviously care a lot about teaching and really puts effort into the class.

Took this class with Dr. Gu in the Fall of 2013. First, an extremely nice guy that cares about students and about improving the course. However, he is not the best lecturer and can sometimes be unclear.  This class is not too much work with just readings and discussion HW.
Very good.

Really helpful if you go to her office hours. Probably a bit more lenient than the professor or TA's that teach this course. Don't fall behind on the book problems and don't be afraid to get help if you're not getting the material. It's very theory-based, not so much applications

Sometimes gets lost in the theory. If you're not a theory person, maybe this course isn't so good. Helpful during OH. If you really need help, go to the math support sessions or math help sessions. THey help a lot better than the class itself

Before I graduate, I just need to come here and give a shoutout to my favorite person at Cornell, Hayden Pelliccia. He's understated, knowledgeable, kind, caring, and gracious. You may think taking intro level Greek from an older, esteemed professor would be scary–quite the contrary! He's simply the best

Pelliccia was one of the most accessible professors I had. He was more than willing to meet with me and help me in this class. That being said, this class was hard. I really struggled with it. Homework every night, and lots and lots of quizzes and tests.

Loved taking Intro to Greek from Professor Pelliccia. He's passionate about the language, which comes through in his lectures and tangents. Make sure you come prepared to class with forms and homework, memorize principal parts, and you're good. Reasonable homework for an intro-level language course. Extremely accessible via email for questions.

Pelliccia is a god when it comes to greek. Though the subject matter has got to be one of the most difficult out there, he teaches greek with such passion & is so knowledgeable . He explains everything thoroughly, his expectations are clear, & his feedback on homework is so helpful. There were very few quizzes/tests, but the ones we had were fair.

The class was just the right combination of unbearably stressful and downright fun. The attention to detail was overwhelming, but the discussion was always informative-- we certainly came to appreciate the approach. The class convinced me to be a classics major. I will try to take as many Greek courses with him as I can, and can recommend the same.
Favors female students. Good at raising interesting questions. Not great at encouraging discussion.

tests are sooooooooo difficult, he'll put the most obscure material on them and then laugh as he leaves his students to struggle with the test in a room proctored by a grad student...but nonetheless he is a great professor and a teacher in the most basic senses of the words...he liberally shares his knowledge and will do his best to help a student
I love himmm!!!  He is super cool and smart and is actually really approachable and helpful, interesting to talk to as well.
What a great professor!  One of the most interesting and stimulating classes I have taken.  Difficult class but well worth it!

Professor Pelliccia has a knack for making learning unappealing.  He always finds the hardest things to put on tests, like exceptions to the rule, etc., to make sure you mess up if you are not in complete command of the material.  Very discouraging!!
Even as a TA for Kyle I can confirm his grading rubric is so unnecessarily convoluted. He is difficult to work with and just a generally unpleasant person.

Harms is an incredible professor who cares deeply about students' learning. He explains things in a way that anybody can understand how websites are designed and built. His grading criteria are extremely clear — you can get an A+ if you do what's expected. If you use Gen AI and miss the req that's on you. Genuinely the best coding prof at Cornell
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He manages to make simple things so convoluted with all of his extra steps and procedures. He also is just a very unforgiving and genuinely does not seem to care about his students.

The worst professor and worst class I've taken at Cornell. Don't take his course if u have any other options. Taking his class was the most regrettable choice I ever made. learned nothing from this course, having too much homework and projects, and a bad grade

This class was the most tedious class I have ever taken at Cornell because of the professor. He failed to communicate what he wanted for us on milestones for final projects and graded harshly on exams. His grading rubrics were harsh and lacked consistency.

Exams are annoying, he pulls random things from lecture so you have to basically memorize everything from the slides. No practice materials or study guides either (even for final), practice quizzes only sightly overlap the content on the exams. Tests on things HE thinks is important, not in actual web design or industry. Final was difficult.
Mean professor

Never had such a devious professor in my life. Extremely condescending and frustrating to talk to. Many times the TA confirmed that my work is right, but still got graded as wrong, and there's no room for negotiation. Doesn't accommodate any situation. The class content is easy, but you won't learn anything new that you couldn't have self-learned.

This is an Intro level class, and yet it is harder than most of the classes I've taken at Cornell. Tonnes of homework and projects without clear rubrics so you will have to guess how to avoid any points reduction. Lots of exams as well while this is a project based class. Most of the times TA can't help you at all. Lots of redundant work.

TA's have no clue how to help in office hours because he changes what he wants from the project milestones each semester. TA office hours weren't even worth it bc TA's were guessing the whole time. I asked one if a part of my homework was correct, which they told me was correct, and I proceeded to get no credit on that portion after it was graded

No tests, but also no re-dos on projects so you have to be careful on each project. Group project is not bad at all. Gave extra credit. I went to office hours for help from undergrad grad and Harms and rarely found help. Online resources are allowed as long as cited which is the best option. Skipped lectures so much my advisor reached out...

Prof. Harms can give long assignments, but I did learn a lot from his classes. I think that his classes are worth taking if you are interested in their content. He is also a nice person and does truly care for his students.

Flexible with giving more slip days and canceled lectures in lieu of office hours during class time. Grading could have been more clear but just read the milestone instructions. It is all there. 
Noticed a lot of complaints and confusion during office hours fall from attendance. go to class, it is early but it helps.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: grading criteria is so confusing.
loads of homework

Incredibily tedious in terms of project requirements. The content itself is not difficult,  but when it comes to project directions, there are so many little things that you have to account for and grading is arbitrary and tough. He doesn't provide you a rubric so you have to guess and imagine all the things that he could dock points off for.
he is mean

Definitely the worst class I've taken at Cornell so far. Filled with boring, busy work. Get ready to spend 3 hours writing actual HTML and 4 hours writing your design journey and hand drawing sketches of each page. Everything about the class including assignment design, is very condescending. Do not take this class unless you have to.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Loved his class! The assignments are easy if you pay attention in lecture, his demos and online documentation are basically answer keys. The group project was really interesting. He's super accommodating when it comes to the group project, too, and would push back deadlines and change requirements based on student feedback.

This class is rough, BUT, if you really put in the work and grind office hours, you can get by pretty well without attending lectures. This was 100% the most time consuming class I took this semester, but if you just attend labs and OH (can't stress how important this is) you can end up with an A+.
not a fan of him, unfortunately he teaches nearly every single info sci class at cornell

I have had a horrible experience with Kyle Harms. He has been my professor for 2 semesters, for info 1300 (got an A) & info 2300 right now. He is abrasive, condescending, unapproachable, and overall I cannot stress enough how horrific it has been. There are truly not enough words in the English language to express how terrible my experience was.

Had him for 1300 last semester, now taking 2300. There is a lot of project work for both classes but if you go to class, pay attention, and try, its an easy A. Courses are designed so well for beginner programmers. I do not understand all the hate!!
This professor is terrible. I will definitely not take his course again.

Generally reasonable and tries his best for students to understand how to code. Sometimes felt like I was being spoon-fed information. Lots of tedious homework. Energetic, which may be hard to endure for an 8:40am class.

Having the class at 8:40 am every Monday and Wednesday is torture. Not to mention his course style of taking attendance at this point in the day. Assignments were fine and doable but very tedious. The design journeys I get the point but it gets a little too much when done multiple times.

If you take a "Web Design Course" taught by Kyle Harms, just know that you are in for a rough semester. Harms is super un-approachable and rude when you go ask him for help.  He is snarky and pretentious. I do not recommend!

If you take a "Web Design Course" taught by Kyle Harms, you will not be learning "Web Design". Rather, you will be learning "Kyle Harms Web Design". Prof Harms is super un-approachable, and designs his rubrics to grade deflate. If you ask for help, he is snarky and pretentious. He is not accommodating at all; yet he makes mistakes constantly.

Kyle Harms is a fine lecturer, but he is genuinely abrasive and needlessly rude one-on-one. Harms scolded me during his office hours for "wasting [his] time" and that I "was not a priority." No professor of mine has ever come close to his level of unpleasantness. Yes, the class was informative, but the assignments were needlessly tedious.

his classes are project based, so how much effort you put into the projects sort of determines how much time you'll be spending on top of basic website functionality reqs. required participation helps you not fall behind in class, and his teaching style really emphasizes learning objectives and good practices which is pretty valuable imo

Great professor that knows the material he is teaching very well. He wants to make sure we develop good practices, even if the work seems a bit tedious. Listens to student feedback and adjusts accordingly, providing lots of leniency. What he expects is pretty straightforward, you just have to read/watch lectures and project write-up well.
Would recommend, really clear grading criteria

Man was bad, but man has CHANGED.Was struggling in INFO1300 but this time 2300 he has obviously improved so much. He genuinely cared about the students and adjusted the courses based on the feedback. The final project was heavy but he was very understanding. Keep it up KYLE!!

Took his class two years ago and this semester again. I genuinely admire how much he has improved and how willing he is to take in feedback. Never thought I would say this but he truly cares about his students and anyone who doesn't see this should give it time. 10/10 KYLE.

This was one of the classes in that I spent most of my time working on the projects: it was challenging and time-consuming, but after all, I learned a lot and had qualified content for my portfolio. I could see that the professor was trying a lot to figure out how to communicate with the students and organize the class content.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment:
He's one of those people you can tell is not only a terrible instructor but also a person you wouldn't want to ever be friends with. Stuck up, condescending, rude, overly critical.

The class concept is simple but he drags things out so painfully, teaches them in weird roundabout ways and just makes everything harder than it needs to be.
man was bad in the past, but MAN IS IMPROVING. This 5 is a recognition for being more accommodating this semester, kyle i know you have been trying and i appreciate it!

If there's a class that significantly decreased my will to keep on going, it'd be INFO 1300. The amount of repetitive work that Harms expects of you, which simply doesn't facilitate learning, no matter what Harms might repeat. An absolute waste of time and a horrendous introduction into the information science major.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: professor is quite condescending and doesn't listen to anyone but himself

Both professors seem genuinely enthusiastic for this class, but they talk to students as if they are children, and assign an insane amount of busywork graded only for completion. Mandatory 9 am lectures make this class even worse.

A 3-credit course with a 12-credit workload. A project milestone once a week which takes at least 12 hours to complete and mandatory attendance at 9 am with WATERMARKED attendance sheet. Coding was not hard, but it only consisted 35% of the class. The rest was basically bullshting the design. It was the biggest source of pain for me that semester.

At surface, Kyle Harms seems like a nice approachable guy based off the way he teaches his lectures. However, when you go to ask a question after lectures, he gives you bitter looks and answers. He also does not care for his students. He is not willing to accommodate regardless of your situation; he only wants to do whats convenient for himself.

Grading is literally ridiculous. They are unclear w/ expectations and untimely w/ grading, and take off so many points for the smallest things. And the workload is astronomical as someone mentioned; all my friends know how this class consumed my life this semester. Do not take unless your life depended on it

Truly the worst professor I've ever had, I can't fit everything in this word limit. 

Workload: Unbelievably tedious, repetitive, useless

Harms: SO inflexible, annoying, does not care for students. I asked for an extension bc I had to literally fly home for my grandma's funeral, but he just made me use half my slip days. 

DO NOT take this class

Do not take INFO 1300 unless you are required to. Lectures are very engaging and slow paced, I can actually pay attention at the crack of dawn. However workload is astronomical. Grading is disorganized and "gotchas" that cause students to lose points are NOT made clear. Students are not told how they are graded and don't receive timely feedback

Course material itself is incredibly easy but the professor has made this the most painfully tedious course. I would rather listen to nails on a chalkboard. Professor is also very condescending and teaches as if you were in primary school. If you want to design websites, self-learn the material in several weeks and avoid the mind-numbing busy work
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment:
You can learn the semester-long material in the span of 2-3 weeks using the Odin Project. He literally makes you write bullshit and then grades you for not having written good bullshit.

This is a coding class for web design but the actual web design part is like 10% of time invested. The rest is following his stupid curriculum made for 1st graders

This was the hardest class I've ever taken at Cornell. The workload during the first two assignments was somewhat manageable -- 20 hours/week, but the workload during the last assignment was around 40 hours/week. The class feels like it should be at least 6-7 credits, and is insane for 3 credits. 

NEVER TAKE THIS CLASS!!!

The main issue: it's a 3 credit class that should be an 8 - from weekly lab homeworks, prelecture assignments, lecture assignments, weekly project deadlines and weekly lab attendance grades. It's a lot. I would recommend not taking this to learn sql/web dev when you could just learn it on your own. He's extremely strict on grading for no reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: too much work, not considerate at all
Honestly just an all-around bad professor. The assignments in the class are extremely boring and require a lot of repetitive work. I would never take another class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I'm actually surprised by the negative reviews. The writeups could be tedious, but they did help me learn to justify my designs and plan my projects. Professor Harms was a great lecturer and his project instructions were always detailed and clear. Wouldn't recommend if you already know web dev and you're not interested in learning about design.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Group projects

reviews.comment: Kyle seems to get more flack than he deserves. Having been in 3 of his classes, it's clear that he wants the best for his students. He puts time/care into planning lectures, answering questions (only getting "mean" when repeatedly asked the same thing), and giving feedback. As long as you're attentive and follow instructions, you'll do just fine.

Would be very tough if you have no prior experience. Harsh grader and takes away lots of points for very small and minor details. I liked the way his lectures were set up but he was very hard to communicate with and every conversation seemed like he felt I was wasting his time. The topic was exciting but he took the fun out of the subject
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I'm a non-major, and took this class thinking it would be a fun introduction to web design. I was wrong. The majority of projects are spent on write-ups, and they feel like a waste of time. Professor Harms is extremely passive aggressive and condescending, and hides "gotchas" in projects to make you lose points. Do not take if you don't need to.

This class is unbelievably easy, I think you would have to try to get a grade lower than an A. However, Kyle absolutely ruins this class, he has a terrible condescending attitude, and this class one of the worst at Cornell. I genuinely think he is one of the worst professors at Cornell, and i would NEVER even consider taking one of his classes.

I had Professor Harms for INFO 1300, 2300, and I'll have him next semester for 4340. He's a really nice guy, and he genuinely cares for his students- it was obvious, even over Zoom. There was a lot of tedious work in his web design courses, but all the complaints about that probably come from coders who've never had to justify their designs.
Redundant easy work. I hate the way he talks to students, sounds like dripping in passive aggression.

The majority of my friend group dropped this class, and I should have followed suit. The write-ups for the projects are genuinely unbearable and seem infinite. The course is listed as a web design course, but it feels like an essay-based class. Good luck getting help on Ed, where Prof. Harms response with the vaguest answers on earth. Do not take.

Kyle Harms' class has been my worst experience at Cornell by far. This introductory level course is unreasonable hard, with multiple extremely difficult deadlines each week. The amount of stress that this class causes is unbearable. Because of this class, I have started to attend mental health counseling and therapy sessions almost every day.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: There are 4-5 deadlines each week with an insane amount of writing and he's unreasonable and inflexible with grading and deadlines. It's my second year pursuing the InfoSci major but I'm convinced to drop my major because of this man.

Without a doubt, this is by far the worst class and professor I've ever had at Cornell. He treats his students like children (not in a caring way but a patronizing one) and acts like a toddler whenever you try to talk to him. He may appear nice and act as if he cares but he's inflexible and will forsake your wellbeing for his own. Be warned.
