This class is abysmal, honestly one of the worst classes I have taken at Cornell. While it may seem like a web dev class at first, the class is much more focused on unnecessary, busy-work writing than actual coding. For the first project in this class, I coded around 1-200 lines, but had to write over 3000 words to describe my "design process."

I was excited to learn about web dev at an esteemed institution such as Cornell. Kyle deserves no esteem, nor is his class a worthwhile use of time, unless you like doing arts and crafts, since all projects incorporate endless design drawing portions, which kill both trees and students' sanity. I also wrote more in this class than I did for my FWS.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Only responds to questions with "Yes" on Ed. For example, "Do I use this method or this other method" "Yes".

Honestly, one of the best professors at Cornell. He takes our mental health and well-being very seriously and has been one of the only professors this semester to be accommodating during this pandemic. Also, the lectures, labs, and projects are pretty straightforward and easy to implement if you pay attention.

should be a garbage easy class, and it is, but harms adds all this extra junk with the design journeys and user testing. content is easy but every single task is wrapped around a convoluted menial thing like interviewing users among other garbage that makes this class and its assignments unbearable
ONE MORE THE MOST CHEERING PROFESSORS I HAVE EVER MET! REALLY SAVE ME THROUGH THE CLASSES UNDER COVID TIME!
Fun projects! Kyle does care about students' success and offers a loooot of help if you request for them in class. He tried to make his class a warm community.
One of the best lecturers at Cornell. Lectures were straight forward and I enjoyed the projects as well.

I've taken INFO 1300, 2300, and 4340 with Kyle. He is extremely knowledgable, and is very dedicated to making sure his students learn the material. This dedication informs all of his course policies and teaching methods  but as a consequence he is strict with the rules. Follow his rules to the letter and you will do well and learn a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Kyle is an easy professor grading-wise, which is great. Despite this, the class holds your hand way too much. Design journeys are brutal. Easy A though.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Kyle cares profoundly about making sure his students understand the material fully. He is always very energetic considering it was a morning lecture and you have 4 unexcused absences to use throughout the semester to miss lecture. The grading criteria was very clear, thus making it easy to do well in his class.

Honestly, I really enjoy Professor Harms' lectures and try to attend as often as possible, even though it's an early class. He uses a lot of graphics/models when describing certain concepts, which really helps me as a visual learner. It is very clear that he is an expert in his field and he does a really good job breaking down the material.

INFO 2300 is a very easy class, but the thing is that Harms is just really not understanding of any extraneous situation and is really inflexible. I do not recommend this class if you have some kind of coding experience and it's not required because the web design contents covered in INFO 2300 can easily be learned over just one or two days.

Kyle is a very motivated and focused professor, it's clear that he cares a lot about his students learning the skills behind the material that he teaches. However, as a result, there ends up being a large amount of work with strict grading guidelines with minimal leeway. But if you stay on top of everything you will gain practical skills.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He is a stickler about attendance (takes it every lecture) which sucks for an early morning class, but you can tell he wants us to actually learn the material he teaches. The projects are straightforward and you really get a good grasp of the material. Plus he was super understanding of a personal situation of mine and that meant a lot to me.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Kyle Harms did really well for his first semester at Cornell. He really spends time explaining concepts to students and does not skip over steps. He did a lot of live demos at class. He also had the class do engaging activities. Maybe use clickers next semester for attendance.

Easy easy class. Projects can be frustratingly tedious but not difficult. Final exam tested basics and nothing more. Attendance is taken at both lecture and section but you're given a good amount of slip days. Harms is good at explaining things and very willing to help. Class meant for beginners so it can feel a bit slow if you have cs experience.
He has the strictest attendance policy, but you shouldn't miss class. Great at explaining things further. Loves people who ask questions and are generally interested in the topic.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment:
Professor Heinemann's course was excellent. What a warm person.

The workload's daunting, but she'd been forthcoming about expectations and afforded students endless opportunities to access help or supplemental materials. And notwithstanding this course occupying more time than all my others combined, Heinemann clears all other ILR professors.

If you want to learn about disability studies would definitely recommend her. Overall, it is a lot of work but she gives great feedback and really helps you become a better writer. Only graded on participation and a 25-page essay with checkpoints along the way.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I love this professor. She is perfect. I am not gonna lie: This class is a lot of work. I got a great grade, but these assignments take hours and hours. There are three big assignments all writing-based. But her feedback is amazing. She makes you improve so much in writing. She is so kind and helpful, answers all questions, and is very accessible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If Professor Heinemann has a million fans, then I am one of them. If Professor Heinemann has ten fans, then I am one of them. If Professor Heinemann has only one fan, then that is me. If Professor Heinemann has no fans, then that means I am no longer on earth. If the world is against Professor Heinemann, then I am against the world.

Professor Weiner Heinemann is the best professor I have had at Cornell. She is incredibly knowledgeable about disability studies, is very accommodating, and makes her students better at research and writing. While the length of the final paper may seem daunting, she breaks it up very well and is there for you every step of the way.

Professor Heinemann is honestly one of the best people (let alone professors) I've gotten to interact with at Cornell. She is such a knowledgeable, caring person, and the class is super interesting and relevant! Super sweet and VERY helpful, so even though the course papers are not easy she makes them A LOT more manageable.

Professor Weiner Heinemann is one of the most flexible, understanding, and caring teachers I've ever had. She truly cares about the subject and her engaging teaching style makes students care as well. I've learned so much  in her class, and my writing skills have improved so much.

Professor Weiner Heinemann is the kindest professor I have ever had the pleasure of having. She is understanding of student struggles and helps to find the best solutions for any issues students may have. She is knowledgeable in the subject and is a fantastic lecturer. I would jump on the opportunity to take a class with her again in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amazing class and professor! There are weekly reflection papers, a take-home exam, and a major group project (Covid-19 breakdown). One of the best professors I have had at Cornell. Really cares about her students and will give more feedback on your papers than you write. Take a class with her!!

Professor Weiner Heinemann was one of the most influential professors I had during college, and I still think about her class and her teaching even though I've already graduated. The class was informative and relevant to current events, and discussions were impactful. I highly recommend taking a class with Professor Weiner Heinemann.
Incredibly caring and helpful professor. One of the best classes I have taken at ILR. I learned so much about disability studies and my writing improved a ton. Definitely take her writing seminar!

Her disability law writing seminar only has two papers. She will provide line by line feedback from your draft on both papers, and you are required to meet with her at least once for each paper. Seems like a tough grader but grades are forgiving in the end.

I can say unequivocally say that Professor Heinemann is the best professor I have ever had. Her lectures are always so interesting and helpful in understanding disability studies. I specifically took her Writing Seminar in Law class about disability studies which was wonderful. She gives a lot of feedback on rough drafts, it's great!

Professor Weiner is absolutely incredible. Her class is hard, but the work is meaningful and useful. She provides extremely helpful feedback - line by line feedback in the writing seminar. There is no textbook, just readings from articles. However, there is still a decent amount of reading. Also learned sm about disability studies. Take her class!

Professor Weiner is an absolute gem of a human. She is so kind and really cares about improving her students writing abilities. She gives really detailed feedback on each draft of your essay. I highly recommend taking a writing seminar with her.

Professor Weiner is by far the best professor I have ever had at Cornell and in ILR. I loved this class and am trying to take another one of her classes again. My writing improved so much because of all of her detailed feedback.

Incredible, tremendously thoughtful and helpful professor. I grew as a writer and a thinker from this class. I have never encountered anyone so invested in the students. I will admit the material was difficult, but she is always willing to help. It was a delight to take a class with Professor Weiner Heinemann and I highly recommend it.
Amazing professor. She truly cares about your growth as a writer and a thinker. Best professor I've had at ILR.

Although the class is long (2.5hrs), the lectures were always interesting. There were 3 reading quizzes (only 2 counted), a midterm & final. Otherwise, u write a quick 5 sentence reflection at the end of each class. Grading is clear cut and class is reasonably easy. There is a lot of readings (go to office hours and she will give you tools to help)

Professor Weiner Heinemann is easily one of the best professors at ILR. While her course is definitely not the easiest way to fulfill the sophomore writing requirement, it is definitely among the ones that will teach you the most. She will challenge you and you will leave her classroom a better writer. Needless to say, her grading is also very fair

This professor is one of the best I have had while in the ILR school at Cornell University! Though her paper assignments are difficult, she is extremely helpful and will go out of her way to assist you. My writing has improved exponentially and I am so glad I took this class.

Hands down one of the best professors that I have had at Cornell. She’s brilliant, funny, approachable, and (genuinely) interested in her students. She is always willing to go above and beyond to make sure that you understand the material.

Professor Weiner is an exceptional instructor. My writing skills improved dramatically from taking her writing seminar. She expects A LOT of work, but is very willing to offer help if you ask for it.I would recommend her class, but am willing to admit that it was not an easy way to fulfill the advanced writing requirement.

Professor Weiner is a brilliant person who cares deeply for her students. She gives extremely clear lectures and is willing to provide all the help you may need to do well in her class. If you have the chance to take a class with her, definitely do it.

I was very uncomfortable learning from Prof Segal because of the way he talked about Freud's theories and the women in his life. There was definitely a level of professionalism that was not met. I was uncomfortable, too, with the derogatory way he talked about people of color.

Prof. Segal is awesome! His lectures are great, and this was a very interesting topic to learn about. The exams were chill and straightforward, and I enjoyed that the class was really more intuitive and something we could apply to our own lives as students and young adults. Prof is also really caring and accommodating. Really enjoyed this class!
Professor Segal is the most caring professor I have ever had. He is lenient and tests were pretty easy. Take any opportunity to be taught by him.

I just know Dr. Segal is one of the best instructors I will ever have the pleasure of having in my entire life. This man is a gem and will be sorely missed by the Cornell community. I hope he enjoys a well-deserved retirement. His classes were interesting, engaging, and thought-provoking. He could have a 700-person lecture go pin-drop quiet.
extremely caring and easy grading
Possibly the most caring Prof at Cornell. Great lecturer as well. Very easy to do well in this course.
I LOVE THIS GUY!!!! so sweet so cute. interesting lectures and so caring! he does prelim reviews too
So kind and caring and sweet. Taken 3250 and 2450 with him and both had basically no work except for exams, which were all multiple choice and very easy.

Very fun class!! Prof Segal brings literal joy to my day. Talks less about clinical psychology and more about life lessons. His stories are endearing and the exams are very easy. Records his lectures and holds reviews before exams.

Such a wise, caring, inspirational professor. I learned so much about life from this class and highly recommend to every college student (no matter your major or if you have academic effort to spare in your schedule). The class is very easy to get a good grade in if you show up to lecture.

Cares deeply about cornell students. Made it clear and easy to do very well in the course, and it honestly did not feel hard at all. I enjoyed coming to his lectures and just listening to him talk/tell stories, but the course could definitely be summed up as "want to be happy? Do what you like to do".

I switched my college to become a psychology major because of him and the class. everyone should take this class or at least attend his class. i would pay to go see one of his lectures if he ever performed or something. kind of hard to attend his office hours but that reflects what kind of professor he is. just mind blowing lectures. love love him.

great lecturer with years of real-world experience as a clinical psychologist. Good lectures, a lot of reading not busy work; worth it. Only small issues with him are he seems to not really understand the content in the neurobiology section of the course (still teaches it fine) and tests on specific Hamlet quotes, so just make sure you've read it.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Segal is a humorous and adorable teacher. Probably one of the most approachable professors at Cornell. He always managed to make everyone laugh at least once during lecture and was good at telling us what to study for prelims. Sometimes he would go on a tangent, but I didn't mind, it was engaging. Definitely a fun class, just pay attention!
Great professor and an easy class if you put in a little effort before the prelims. I found lectures to be very entertaining and Segal was very engaging. Would take again
I love Professor Segal. He is incredibly charming and hilarious, makes lectures really fun. Highly recommend attending office hours, even just to chat with him about life. Very sweet.

Nice guy, and can be a fairly engaging lecturer, but is sometimes underprepared. Also, as the year goes on, his lectures become more and more of him just reading us verbatim the readings we had already been assigned to read. Nice guy though, and often funny.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great guy, exceptional class

Ok he is funny but also weird. His lectures are interesting. When it comes to Freud and psychoanalysis he is the man. But, when it comes to the brain he kind of just reads off PPT slides. He assigns a lot of reading from his textbook, Freud's book, Hamlet, and a book about Schizophrenia. BUT he makes up for it with his charm.

Harry is by far the best professor I've had thus far at Cornell. He's funny, engaging, and his class teaches really interesting/important material. There are a lot of readings, but if you get the general idea you'll be fine and he tells you what you need from the readings in lecture. Highly recommend if you are in any way interested in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I really love this professor. You can tell he genuinely cares about every student. I just showed up to class everyday and paid attention. I read the spark notes of the assigned reading and skimmed the slides the day before the exam and aced it. The class is actually interesting and not stressful. He goes on a lot of tangents but still worth taking.

Segal is by far the most inspiring prof I've had at Cornell. His lectures are captivating, hilarious, and mind-blowing. Enjoyed every minute of his class, it felt more like free therapy. Segal is empathetic and accommodating and really wants his students to be healthy, happy, and successful. 100% recommend if you're at all interested in psych.
He's sweet and makes the lectures really interesting. I really enjoyed this class.

Harry Segal is an absolute gem. Cares deeply about what he does and makes the material easy to understand. Don't bother doing the dense textbook readings (all available online) because Segal highlights in lecture what you actually need to know. Read the case studies. Listen when he talks Hamlet. Review lecture slides before exams. You'll do great!

Harry Segal is the best professor that I've had during my time at Cornell. He really makes the lecture material come to life and you can tell that he has the respect of everyone in the room. He genuinely cares about his students and I hope that I can take another class with him in the future. I've recommended this class to all my friends!

Amazing lecturer. He genuinely cares about his students and makes every lecture fun and the time fly by. Tests aren't bad as long as you actually do the readings! Even if you're not a psych/human development major, you should definitely take this class
A very good person who made the lectures entertaining and fun. Not much information covered in lecture but such a nice and genuine guy.

Best lecturer ever. He really loves teaching Freud and the mind. But I really couldn't follow his lectures about the biological side of things. Reading can get overwhelming. Overall though he is funny, adorable, and not too tough on tests. If you read everything with time then the A is possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: So nice, truly cares about his students.  His lectures are usually funny, and relatiely interesting.  There is Hamlet in this class, which I personally don't like, but it is not too bad.  Overall he is a great professor!

Wonderful person - funny, lively, intelligent, caring, and extremely helpful if you're interested in clinical psych. However, I didn't love his teaching style - lots of words packed onto slides that he blows through in between anecdotes/rants and Hamlet performances - and his tests varied between joke questions and extremely nitpicky ones.

One of the best profs at Cornell by far. He's super kind and approachable, has very interesting lectures, tests are very fair and the readings are sometimes long but not detrimentally so. Although I'm a pre-med and not necessary looking at a career in clinical psych I've taken his courses just because of how great of a prof he is.

Professor Segal is one of the very few Clinical professors on staff. He's very caring about his students and his lectures are interesting. Tests are fair and the final was actually incredibly fun. Another rater commented on email, it's much better to go to office hours, he gets a ton of emails and isn't quick to respond but he definitely cares!

by FAR my favorite professor at Cornell.  he is laid back, smart, direct, helpful, and really cares about his students. exams are fair and easy to do well on as long as you prepare. bonus: he usually makes his multiple choice questions have 1 choice that is clearly a joke, simultaneously making it easier and entertaining
Definitely one of my favorite professors/classes at Cornell. Professor Segal is funny, interesting, and down-to-earth. The tests are fair and as long as you study you will do fine.

Segal is nice enough, but his lectures don't really have any substance. Him reading hundreds of words off slides and acting out Hamlet are annoying. But course is simple, only two prelims and final. Readings are fairly light and you can probably do well just by going to class and review sessions. Easy A and all in all worth the occasional headache.

Dr. Segal is an interesting teacher. He wasn't particularly well suited to be a lecturer for such a large class but he kept things interesting with personal anecdotes. However, his tests were at times unclear and relied heavily on insignificant details aimed to see if you attended class (not if you actually knew basic psych).

By far the best professor I've had at Cornell so far. I learned so much from him. The course challenges you to think about yourself and the people around you in a different way. Absolutely loved it, and him.

This professor is ridiculously boring. I fell asleep every class 5 minutes in. I had an urgent issue during the semester, sent all my professors an e-mail and he was the only one who didn't respond. I e-mailed him 6 more times in the next week or so and he ignored every one. He obviously doesn't care about his students.

He's really nice but it is hard to get a lecture of 900+ interested in intro to psych. The tests are very fair if not a little easy. If you are interested in the material, take it with him--also visit his office hours he is SO SWEET.

Loved this class and Professor Segal.  The tests are extremely easy, if you study.  If you do not study, people say they are hard.  Studying really pays off in this class and if you put in the effort you will get at least an A-.
Test wasn't the most clear but the gives you 10 free points a test.
Overall good very fair test but questions are sometimes not related to psych

Harry's ability to tie anecdotes to subject matter is uncanny. Unfortunately he consumes too much time reading his own lecture slides and acting out scenes from Hamlet. As such, class was very hit-or-miss. Psychopathology was not the best psych course I've taken, but it was still worthwhile.

Professor Segal is so entertaining and makes the material interesting! Although lectures can be a bit scatter brained, he tells really great personal anecdotes from his therapy career and cares for the success of his students! One of my favorite professors at Cornell for sure.

Harry Segal is AMAZING. There's a reason Adult Psychopathology fills up in less than 5 mins during CoursEnroll. He brings the material to life w/ anecdotes about previous patients, etc., and soothes the class with his "therapist voice." He's the same way in office hours, and truly cares about students. A little eccentric, but a great prof.

The class can be hard to get into for sophomores since it is so popular, but definitely take it if you can and if you have any interest in clinical psych or are premed. The workload is not bad, and he is such a fun, easy-going lecturer. A tad disorganized but he really cares about his students.

Segal is the BEST. I've had the pleasure of getting to kno him thru many classes, & the more I learn from him the better my life is. He is genuine, wicked smart, and humble. Not even kidding, I'm naming a kid after this man. He will require you to work and really engage yourself, but you owe it to URSELF to take all his classes! Def changed my life

its only the second week of class and is probably my favorite professor in four years. absolutely hilarious, able to inject humor into his lectures to keep things interesting. HIGHLY recommend prof and class

Entertaining and fun class, going to lecture was the highlight of my day.  Yeah he doesn't really know the neuroscience and isn't totally organized...but still a great class.  He tells lots of anecdotes about patients which makes the material come to life.

hands down the best class i've taken at cornell in 3 years. prof may not be the best at teaching the science parts of the class, but he chooses good textbooks that explain it & everything else about the class makes up for it. amazing professor who's really nice, really likes teaching, does it well & wants to help his students learn the material.
great guy and excellent, engaging lecture.
absolutely wonderful! could not have survived my undergraduate years without him
interesting material but very poorly organized which makes it difficult to fully understand
Segal is not at his best in this class. The readings are great, but lecture is simply rehash and is not worth the time. An easy A, meets only once a week. Always late.

Segal brings a wealth of clinical experience into the classroom; it's not about memorizing diagnostics but really coming to know what it is like to be mentally ill. He genuinely cares about students and remembers names from a 300+ lecture. Can't teach the neurobio worth anything but is incredible for everything else!

segal's awesome, very funny and understanding, interesting topics with even more interesting case reviews. exams are fair, verging on easy if you go to lecture. really good with psychological aspects of class, not so much with science (slides are copies of textbook material) but TAs covered that. really wants you to do well in his class!
Starts class late EVERY lecture then often runs over.  We took a prelim 5 weeks ago and still have not received grades. Its unacceptable.
the most wonderful professor i've ever met. i would be lost if it was not for his encouragement throughout my undergrad years

What a lovable guy! The girls go nuts for him because he is such a sweetheart. Gives you practical pointers for life. Lectures are ridiculously interesting because they feature case studies, readings are interesting as well. Tests are very fair. Exam reviews pointless because they are disorganized.
This was a great class, comes highly recommended. Not only is the material interesting, but the tests are extremely fair. Go to office hours if you can. Segal's a lot of fun!

He was one of the most incompetent teacher I've had at Cornell. I don't know why there are so many good reviews of him. While he may be a good "person," his credibility in teaching this class is dubious. You'd come out of the class learning very little and many useless accounts in his lectures.
No Comments

this man is amazing. he's the cutest thing i've ever seen my life. you can tell he really likes what he's doing and cares about people. he's got an adorable way about him and a great sense of humor. he's emotional and sweet and generally a great guy. he uses a lot of stories and examples. i look forward to his class all week. he just makes me smile

I was very disappointed by this class. Readings were assigned that were later "unassigned" right before an exam after some people who tried to keep up with the work might have done them.  Don't buy the books. Professor Segal has a hard time keeping his mind on the lecture and makes many tedious digressions.  Prepare to be bored or angered.

Prof Segal is a great pedagogue in many ways, but know this: he teaches using examples and emotionally connecting with the students. This is great for about 80% of the course. However, he is NOT great at teaching "systems", which is the other 20%. He reverts to his use of examples, but the mechanisms often go unexplained at the fundamental level.
Best professor ever
Wonderful professor, and one of my favorite at Cornell. Excellent class, and I highly recommend taking a course with him! Very understanding and good at interacting at a personal level

3 years out of Cornell, and I still think back to the days of senior year psych field practicum with Harry. I highly recommend Harry and his classes. He is a great person, a great teacher, and a great academic. (try to get him for your advisor too!)

Prof. Segal is great! I looked forward to his lectures every day. Often tells stories and anecdotes to illustrate the point. I enjoyed his lectures so much that I went to office hours just to be able to talk to him. Great, funny guy! One of the best profs I've had, and the class was very interesting.

Prof Segal is awesome. His lectures are engaging and informative. The tests are incredibly fair. You will do as well as you want to in this course. I wish there were more profs like Segal, who actually loves teaching.

Harry is one of the greatest people you will ever meet in your life, and one of the most respected profs at Cornell. Standing in line for office hours is very much worth the wait. He has a quirky sense of humor, and he is brilliant... and effectively covers very interesting material! Plus he's the cutest person ever who simply makes you smile!
One of the best lecturers I've ever had. Very interesting material and an amazin teacher. Grading; not too hard...he'll make it easy on you if you study.
I know!he is such a cutie.  /the most attractive prof i've had in 3 years!  and the best teacher too. :)
He's in over his head.  He gets his feeling of worth from the students around him.  But he's a total sweetie, a teddybear, and a great lecturer.  C'mon guys, give him some hotness points!
One of the BEST in Cornell, period.

dr. segal is very warm and cares a lot about his students. i have had a lot of contact with him over my time at cornell, and he has helped me out with many things. sometimes he is frazzled, yes, but his interest in his subject matter and students is genuine!

Segal is charismatic, but anyone who has worked closely with him will find out he's VERY insecure & needs admiration from EVERYONE. He is always overbooked and cares first and foremost about his ego. Academically he is not helpful: he only wants to lavish praise bc he needs it so badly in return.

Segal is one of the greatest professors Cornell has.  He's the sweetest guy around, and he really makes sure you know the material.  The man has his own cappuccino machine in his office.  Gotta love him.
A must take class with a must have professor! Don't miss out on this great opportunity to learn and be entertained while doing it.

One of the best professor at Cornell ever! He is so smart, caring, funny and inspring!!! Cornell is luck to have him. He tells some amazing stories to illustrate his concept and broaden your perspectives. Amazing TAs, very dedicated.(especially Bernie).

Professor segal made my semester, always looked forward to his 10:10 class.  Amazing lecturer, very engaging and caring.  Presented interesting stories and illustrated his concepts very well. Amazing professor, we need to get him tenored.
Absolutly wonderful. He is funny, intersting, informative, and -- nice! This is the best class I've ever had.
FunFUnFun.EasyEasyEAsy.
SO easy!!!!!! very very informal and scatterbrained!!!

A compassionate scatterbrain.  Hints of pretension, but that’s relative.  He may be the most empathetic professor Cornell has, but is alas cursed with a capricious lecturing/grading ethic.  Not to worry.  He’ll make it easy on you.
The best professor I've ever had.
Harry Segal is amazing.  Great Lecturer. Captivating.  A bit disheveled...but who cares?
the most awesome prof EVER!

He's an amazing lecturer. Because he's a clinical psychologist, he knows how to talk TO you, not AT you. Tells the funniest stories! He could be a little bit more organized and clear with what we need to know, but Segal is amazing!!
Tells interesting stories and brings a sword to class.  Very friendly, interesting guy.  Likes to talk about his daughter too much, and gets many guest lecturers when he doesn't know the material.
No Comments
Best prof at Cornell
Most incompetent professor ever, No organization, Give no indications or false indications of what is expected, Completely arbitrary grading
No Comments
No Comments

He was definitely my favorite of the 3 profs for this class. He did a great job explaining all of the complex ideas, and I thought his prelim was the easiest one. For the overall course, there are textbook readings, pre-lecture videos, 2 weekly quizzes, short pre- and post-lab activities, 4 prelims, a mandatory final, and an optional prelim retake.

Love him, his prelim scared the life out of me during it but I actually did very well. Very clear lecture slides and is great at breaking down difficult topics. The class was VERY lecture heavy. Flipped classroom which sucks. Cool guy though

He's very good at explaining complex concepts. He breaks everything down to a T. There will be a lot of info thrown at you, so be prepared! The class is moderately difficult. There's videos, readings, and mandatory quizzes twice a week, 4 prelims, optional final, and attendance is not mandatory. Prelims are tricky. Don't take if not required.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Viramontes is a kind, caring person, positive even in the toughest of times. Her office hours were of the best quality—she really cares for her students, and made sure that I had the best experience possible in class despite issues that arose. I love her enthusiasm for writing—never let anyone stop you from telling a story. Take her class
One of the best professors I have ever had. Take her class if you have the chance!

Intermediate Narrative Writing with Professor Viramontes has been on of my favorite classes at Cornell so far. Not only does she have great knowledge in the subject as an accredited novelist and short story writer, but she also takes the time to connect and impart this knowledge on her students. I know have improved as a writer with her guidance.

Took her creative writing course at Scripps College. She builds a great community in the classroom. Might be a little New Agey for some, but I appreciate her approach compared to more cynical profs I've had. Love the "passion presentations" as a way to learn from classmates.

Viramontes is a phenomenal teacher and writer. If you EVER have the chance of taking her class, you must. She really cares about each and every one of her students and is willing to spend quality office hour time with them. The diction she employs even when she speaks will make you have goosebumps! VIRAMONTES IS AMAZING!

Wonderful professor. Genuinely cares about her students and is willing to put in quite the amount of time in office hours. Each time I come out of her class, I just want to go write more. Definitely a professor every English major should encounter.
Lovely woman, great writer and professor
Helena Viramontes is a genius!
Prof. Viramontes is great!--Interested and interesting, and quirky. Take her for creative writing.
am a senior and this is one of the best classes i have taken because it intersects microbiology, marine biology, and eeb. very very interesting course

Prof. Hewson is amazing! I was nervous going into this class because I have no background in oceanography, but it's been super interesting and not stressful. Learn a lot of content but no tests/quizzes. He often ties his own research/field work into class content and you can tell he just wants to get students excited to learn!

This class was really interesting. The prof went above and beyond to make the class accessible and flexible in the online learning environment. While the lectures were dense, learning goals were clearly identified and the assessments were firmly focused around these. Also assessment was flexible and tailored to each student's preferred method.

Prof. Hewson is clearly very knowledgeable&passionate about his field, but the lectures are very dense and got to be a bit monotonous at the end of the semester Luckily there was no exams on the detailed lecture content, rather theres weekly literature/writing HW, group proj, and final proj. This was nice but made it too easy to tune out lecture
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Hewson is a fantastic individual who really knows his stuff! Such a pleasure to have him as a teacher.
This was a great introduction to marine biology. Some of the labs were a little disorganized but at least there were labs!

Dr. Ian's Hewson class is more suited for people with no familiarity with biology than anyone who has even taken intro biology.  It is overall disorganized and presented in a distinctly anthropocentric and unscientific manner

Not a difficult class, but the canvas is a bit disorganized. Much of the slides is just pictures, and the exams sometimes included content not in the slides. Many extra credit opportunities are available, and the weekly quizzes were online and simple. A sweet lady, but a bit of a boring lecturer.
Very light class, as soon as I saw the bros, I knew I was good to go

Hefferon is such a sweet women that wants you to succeed. She has review sessions and even shows up to the TA one's with snacks. She is a little monotone tho. Everything you need to know for the exams are on the slides or mentioned in class.

Professor Hefferon is great and I enjoyed taking this course. There were a several weekly quizzes and a few exams, but they were pretty straightforward and were heavily based on lectures. She is always responsive with emails, accessible outside of class, and cares a lot for her students. Definitely recommend this course!
Boring lectures- just reads off slides. Cares about student learning and is willing to help anyone. Class overall is memorization heavy but discussion sections are clutch.
Seems like a nice person. Her lectures a bit boring and hard to understand. The exams are hard. Did not do well.

She's a very kind woman, but often seemed confused by what she was teaching. Her lectures consisted of her reading off the slides verbatim and then repeating the exact same thing in a slightly different way. The class often felt discombobulated. She's nice and understanding, but not a particularly helpful instructor.

If you are interested in archaeology in Latin America, this would be the class for you! Lectures can feel a little long, he provides great visuals and thoughts on different small and large archaeological sites. Stay on track with readings since there are only 3-4 essays throughout the class. Ask questions and discuss during class or office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Incredibly brilliant, caring, and underrated professor. He fundamentally shaped the way I perceive history (while still encouraging me to pursue my own opinions) and I will never regret taking a class with such an intelligent and fascinating scholar.

Essay based that's graded by him and the ta. He's a little monotone but is super nice, lectures definitely help with writing out essays and as long as you go to discussion and put effort into your papers, you'll get an A.

Professor Henderson is a good lecturer and seems to be really passionate and knowledgeable with his field. However, sometimes, his lectures can get a bit boring and it can also be difficult to hear him. I'd still recommend this class, but make sure to go to discussions, keep up with the readings, and plan out well for all of the essays!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would avoid this class if you are not interested in archaeology as you will likely find lectures very boring. For those with a genuine interest in archaeology, specifically New World archaeology, Henderson is your guy. He can answer any question you throw at him. His subject knowledge is frankly incredible.

John has a particularly soft and low voice that can sometimes put you to sleep and he knows it. But he is an incredibly well intention and reasonable professor that is extremely knowledgeable about the subject areas. He simply asks that his students show interest and put effort in the material. Great professor!
literally the most boring thing i've every done. I hate archaeology now. Almost not worth it for the arts distribution requirements. He seems nice, but he bored me to tears.

Very boring lecturer and very hard to follow in class. Creates easy study guides for prelims so you don't have to attend lecture and can just use the study guides. Section classes are much harder with mandatory attendance, participation and papers. Have to read a lot for this course (especially for section) and borrow/buy multiple textbooks.

He's a funny guy and of course knows the material very well. As some others have said, the hardest part about his class is showing up and paying attention. There was a lot of assigned reading as well. Major focus on the Americas in terms of subject matter, which was fine by me. Exams are curved generously.

Impossible to pay attention the whole lecture, very boring and monotone. Sections help a lot in understanding the material you miss in lecture. Whole textbooks expected to be read in 2 week time frame. Good class for Arts and Sciences distribution requirements.

He gave lots of very long readings. His voice can also sound a little monotone. However, he is a great guy who knows tons about the subject matter. If you listen you will learn a lot. He also has a fantastic, dry sense of humor. At first I wasn't into the subject matter or class, but then I really began to enjoy it. Listen to him, it's worthwhile.
Would definitely not recommend this class unless you're just looking for a grade.  Bad lectures surprisingly manage to make intriguing material incomprehensible.
Super boring. Save yourself $200 and don't buy the books.

Lectures usually very boring and not well organized, hard to know what to take notes on. Occasional jokes are really funny though. Tests are half very easy (ID questions) and half totally unpredictable. Focus is on the americas only, would have been nice to get some stuff from other continents.

I was very disappointed by this class and professor. I would have been interested in the material had the professor shown any interest in teaching it. Lectures are incredibly slow and boring - very hard to pay attention to even when you try really hard to. I do not recommend the class, unless you are looking for an easy breadth credit for graduatio
Great guy, knows exactly what he's talking about. Not that difficult to pay attention to his lectures. Eager to answer any and all questions. Very friendly with all his students.
Nice guy. the smaller books are more important than the textbook.

After taking two classes with this professor (120 and his Cent. America one), I have found him to be extremely knowledgeable on his areas of interest.  His lectures can be rather boring, although he does have a dry sense of humor that can lighten up his speech if one is paying attention.  Easy classes overall, great for distribution reqs.

Professor Henderson is very knowledgeable on the topic.  His lectures can be boring at times, but he knows that students are taking this class for reqs so he doesn't make it very hard.  If you have to fulfill the breadth requirements, it's not a bad way to go.
This guy's monotone belies the enthusiasm he has for what he teaches. He tells you everything you need for prelims in lecture- just pay attention (I know, it's hard not to fall asleep sometimes).
Henderson is so boring. The class would be interesting if his voice didn't put me to sleep.
This guy is THE worst lecturer at cornell. seriously, this guy's monotone just goes on and on and on and on. Dont ****ing listen to him.
No Comments

I LOVE Prof. Henderson, although his voice does put me to sleep.  Look at the class notes most for tests,and you'll be fine.  However, his upper level courses (Mexico, Andes) are more interesting and still teach you about archaeology (and are still easy).
Boring, boring, boring.  Cannt stay awake in that class for the life of me.  He talks like William Shatner and the exams are too hard for a class which everyone takes for distribution anyways

I fell asleep 10 min into the first day of class. His lectures are impossible to follow: no structure, many digressions, and a monotonic voice. However, he does have good slides and interesting guest lecturers...kinda sad huh?
unclear grading rubric with weekly quizzes
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She is super nice and smart! I enjoyed her class. Thank you, Prof. Hinrichs!

Very down-to-earth and genuinely cares about her students. Sit-down discussions are very interesting but slide lectures can be a little dull. She is super supportive outside of class for a STEM student like me who is not familiar with college history courses. Would definitely take again.
Inspiring lectures! I like her. She cares about the students!
A brilliant professor who is also considerate! I like engaging in the class.

She doesn't really lecture and I couldn't really get a straight answer out of her whenever I asked a question. That being said, she does genuinely care. In terms of grading, she's not going to give you anything higher or lower than an A-, so as long as you show up to class and put in an average amount of effort it doesn't matter.

Professor Hinrichs is super nice and an amazing person, but her class is super reading heavy (the readings are usually very boring and super long) and the prompts for her papers were super confusing. The essay grading is pretty relaxed, I turned in a few papers that didn't correctly answer the prompt but always got Bs.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: TJ is really nice and she definitely cares about her students. But, her class has a unique structure that is really difficult to get used to. There is a large amount of reading to do. You discuss the readings and questions in groups and then present to everyone. Very confusing and hard essay questions. She asks you to define everything. Participate
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: TJ is a kind professor who understands the difficulty that comes with dense historical primary sources. Very discussion heavy and participation matters. She's a fair grader but being an active participant can boost your grade. She's is flexible with deadlines and is available to meet.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Course was heavily based on Historiography, not History. Lectures are optional after the 2 in-class quizzes, but section is mandatory. Very essay heavy, with some kind of paper being due weekly. Reading everything assigned would kill you; just read Lewis and Sima Qian and you'll survive. Professor seems to care about students, which is a plus.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Bad, bad lecturer, but seems to care about students. Discussion sections aren't productive. But she's an easy grader, the class average was an A-

She is a great professor. I absolutely enjoyed taking her class. I improved tremendously as a write (better than my FWS). She is really understanding of the competitive culture that exists at Cornell, and will sometimes end class early because she knows we need a break. Readings of about 80-100+ pages a week. Density of the readings fluctuate.
I didn't do any of the readings and got an A+. If you are trying to get nice grades and gtfo this is def the class!
Course is relatively easy but graded on only essentially 4 assignments. Prof is accessible outside of class. Readings are interesting and not necessary to pass the class.

This class is very dependent on in-class exercises (that are not only graded on completion), so attendance is mandatory in some sense. Lectures had interesting content but were occasionally a little dry. Many extra credit opportunities through talks on campus that were a great grade boost. Exams were extremely fair.

Great guy, clearly knows his stuff. Not an easy class and you have to attend as a lot of your grade is in class activities (which is impossible to get 100s on even if they're great). He stumbles through lectures a bit but I learned a ton from them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Hilgartner is excellent! cCass was very interesting and made me rethink science and technology's impact on society. Attendance is mandatory as there are in-class activities, and he doesn't post slides on Canvas. Also, quizzes and exams cover material in readings that aren't covered in class, so make sure to read and review those.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great course that encouraged thinking and discussion on the role of science and technology in society. He uploaded fun and engaging lecture videos each week in the online course. There were many papers but they were easy to write and we got timely feedback on how to improve from him and his TAs. Would take again for another course.
He is a great lecturer and does really interesting research. This class helped me decide on a major.
This was an easy class. Show up, pay attention, and you will do just fine. He is quite engaging and has interesting material. I would definitely take this class again. I learned a lot from it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Class was a breeze. Show up to lectures and discussion for participation, which is a big part of your grade. 3 easy quizzes are the only sit-downs you'll take. 2 papers take the place of prelims and finals. As long as you write them semi-coherently, you'll get A's. Hilgartner is a dynamic lecturer and a great guy.

He stumbles through his lectures  some of which are more interesting than others  and sometimes explains things in a really roundabout way. But overall he's a nice and approachable guy; I'm not one to typically ask questions in class but he wasn't too intimidating and made himself accessible. Exams were also pretty straightforward.
Interesting information but non engaging lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Nice professor- nervous and rambling, but sincere
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Sweet guy who loves to teach
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof H never responded to my emails, had an odd grading system which was not defined in the syllabus, and his lectures slides are barely sufficient for prelims. Prelim scores took up to 3 weeks to get posted, and my TA googled answers when I went to her office hours. Final term paper, notebook and section grades were never posted - 55% of the grade

Professor Hilgartner is very knowledgable and skilled at conveying the information to students. In lecture, he introduces theory and concepts but always ties it to examples. The exams are very fair in terms of questions and grading. We have journal assignments this semester, which can be annoying. Not much reading
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Hilgartner is very knowledgable and skilled at conveying the information to students. In lecture, he introduces theory and concepts but always ties it to examples. The exams are very fair in terms of questions and grading. We have journal assignments this semester, which can be annoying. Overall good class and good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Hilgartner gives interesting lectures which you will need to attend and take notes. His lecture slides are mostly just pictures. That said, he doesn't cover much in a lecture and the readings are much of the course material so the course really isn't too bad. It's a good class with a good professor.

Lecture is REALLY boring and useless.  Best days were when there were guest lecturers.  A lot of reading assigned and very specific questions asked on tests.  Some of the readings are pretty interesting.  Grading is really easy, but there is a lot of busy work in this class.  Average class, average professor.  Only take it if you need ethics.

This year he changed the exams to be all multiple choice so they're pretty easy and the class is no longer curved. There are a ton of articles to read though. This class isn't hard but its incredibly time consuming if you do all the work. Also, his voice is super annoying to listen to.

Leads very interesting discussions. Expects everyone to do the readings. Will not call on people but will hint strongly for participation. Provokes interesting thoughts in terms of science and technology. Easily one of the most knowledgeable professors in the field. Extremely brilliant.

Good lecturer, interesting and very worthwhile material, decent readings, fairly interesting discussion section. Papers were fairly graded for the most part, but grading on the exams and discussion sections was excessively subjective. Definitely a worthwhile class for anyone planning to go into healthcare - excellent overview of current issues.

Very good class about science and how it relates to american politics. It is a must for any either or both of those topics. The professor is very clear, the lectures are never too dull, and the work load very acceptable. Take this class!

He's a nice guy and his class is easy but boring as hell. You will literally want to fall asleep every day because the man CANNOT lead a discussion. He preplans his jokes, which usually get little more than a chuckle. The tests involve spitting back his bullet points from lecture, and the TA entirely determines your grade. Not bad, but not worth it
Prof is friendly and overall a nice person but lectures are on the boring side. depending on the ta, you may enjoy or hate the class. the grading was fair.
Very interesting lectures that were clearly presented, interested in helping students, great class if you put in a little work

Ethics in Healthcare was a class that had the potential to be interesting. Hilgartner's speech style just made the class dreadful. His grading system needs to be changed; the class is curved on very few points. Class should be way less than 4 credits.
Class was interesting and fairly easy, but he does have the annoying habit of using a lot of  uhms  and  y'knows  when he talks.  Couple that with his lisp and he can be a little hard to listen to.
What is science?  Easy as sunday morning that's what.
No Comments
No Comments

I took Tom's SOC 2202 class my freshman year at Cornell and I was pleasantly surprised. There are short "reading summaries" due every Sunday which are up to 125 words and thus very easy to complete. The quizzes are worth a good chunk of your grade, but if you listen during the lecture and take notes you'll be fine. 10/10 class. PARTICIPATE

I did not like this class at all. He was all over the place most of the time and he made zero sense the majority of classes. I went to every class and had no idea what was going on. He grades super weird like I had no idea what was going on. Also hes really bad with tech and that just made it worse.

Very opinionated and teaches based off his thoughts. Lectures can be all over the place. Be prepared to write essays on agreeing with his political views. Class was easy if you do the essays and readings, but would not take this professor again.

So I took this as a requirement. Definitely had to put work into it. I recommend doing the readings, then you don't have to come to class. The TAs were super helpful, otherwise, I went to each and every class, and just spent my time on the internet, because it's extremely hard to focus, and I don't know why. Readings=interesting. Prof=not.

Worked with him as a undergrad researcher and took FSAD 4660. 

As a researcher, he was an absolutely awful mentor. He rebuked me for switching from chem into FS and said it was a waste of time. Real rich coming from the chair. 

His teaching is lazy. Asks you to write questions as a semi-final to be used for the final. Easy grader though.

Prof Hinestroza is honestly amazing! He genuinely cares about his students and their learning and appreciates hard work. Sure, there is a lot of work in this course, but he specifies time and again that if you're not up for the work, the course isn't meant for you. Learnt a lot of new, cool things in the class.

Assigns an immense amount of work. A lot of FSAD Management students have opted for later years' tracks just to avoid this class. I'm not sure if it's even allowed to assign semi-finals, independent project, group project, and a final exam at the same time, but this Prof has the audacity to do it. Easy grader. There's only a few real lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Hirschl is disorganized and he presents his theories like they are facts. While he claims to be objective, his lectures and essays are anything but. Easy class though.

Hirschl's class was easy, but he rarely presents opposing views fairly and talks about politics far too often. The lectures after the first few weeks were almost all rants about Trump and right-wing politics, and it often felt like being at a progressive political rally. If you can regurgitate progressive themes and shut your brain off, easy A.

Hirschl was knowledgeable and interesting which made the lectures not too difficult to sit through. He was a little unorganized but I'll give him the benefit of the doubt knowing technology is his Achilles' heel. There were some communication issues but other than that decent class.

Honestly a bit unorganized, but still a solid professor that knows his stuff. You have to be a bit patient because he can sometimes jump around topics, but you'll learn a lot of interesting things. Very easy grader, really just wants you all to understand the primary points (which he'll emphasize and review during lecture).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Pretty chill and easy class. Grading is done by TAs so it can be pretty hit/miss. Lectures are unnecessary, just show up the day there's a quiz. Discussion is mandatory but it's pretty chill and mostly opinion based. Reading summaries are due every week, and there are three essays. It's a lot of work but it's well structured and a pretty easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Great professor, had him for DSOC 1101. Go to lecture once a week when the weekly quizzes are, if no quiz don't bother going to lecture. The class was not bad and I learned a lot!

I'll try to be objective and critical, something that this professor is not. The most BS class I've ever taken. His lectures are tangental, without evidence and leaves you thinking that only 85% of what he said is true. His exam questions are his interpretations of the readings, not the author's actual points. Any answer could be correct.

he's a terrible lecturer, goes on tangents so often. he also sometimes confuses himself; sitting in class I hear a lot of snickering from the classmates when he says something that doesn't make sense (which is a lot). my TA is respectful but even he knew that the lecturers didn't help much. MC tests are vague; prelim averages were 80-82%.

Actually the worst professor I've had at Cornell -- I don't care if he is a brilliant researcher. He had no investment in the class, terrible lectures and had no care whatsoever what students took away from his class - truly terrible.

I remember that in the first lecture Prof. Hirschl was making his powerpoint slides in class. Yes, in class, while he was lecturing. His lectures were so random. He started off talking about the reading, made a few completely unrelated points, and he started criticizing some other sociologist, and then another sociologist, and then another.

Hirschl's lectures are scattered, and his explanations of concepts are very vague. I did not know what "developmental sociology" was until our TA explained it halfway through the semester. He uses examples that are not thought out, and you could argue that all choices on his multiple choice questions are correct. Even so, the class is super easy.
First two readings were hard, rest was pretty easy.  Actually pretty interesting.

Hirschl was an okay professor. Your success in the class really depends on the quality of your TA. If you have a bad TA who doesn't hand back assignments and doesn't cover all of the required material for the week because s/he runs out of time, then your grades will likely suffer. There are weekly assignments but the workload isn't too bad.

If you want to be constantly indoctrinated with socialst ideas, take this course.  Hirschl legitimately spends most of his time in lecture pushing an agenda.  It's infuriating when the garbage he's spewing is coming out of the mouth of a bumbling idiot.  That said, this class is an absolute joke and if you have a functioning brain it's an easy A.

This class was useless but I took it for the easy A. Literally rarely came to class but came to all of the sections and did the readings. Take it for the diversity distribution requirement. You won't regret it.
Take it for the diversity credit and just get out with an A.

I actually learned a lot about things of social importance in this class and it opened my eyes to the world after taking only science classes prior to it. I hardly went to lecture, but the material was interesting and it was an easy A. In section we had one paper that wasn't even graded. Exams were somewhat tough but curved high

Prof Hirschl is awful. DSOC 1101 is awful. If you do the work, you will get a good grade, but the amount of work is obscene for such a stupid class. Hirschl tests you on his own material and his own views. I didnt know what sociology was until I looked it up three weeks into class. He makes you buy books for two chapters. AVOID if you enjoy sanit y

If you try, you'll get a good grade.  Hirschl hates economics and spends most of the time explaining his own views and supporting himself with questionable evidence.  Whenever he uses scientific evidence as support, he looks foolish to the science majors.  All correct answers on exams are variations of: "Whites & men are oppressing blacks & women."

These other ratings are bogus. This was one of the best classes I took at Cornell. Didn't learn too much, busy easy A, engaging lecture, and he's such a really nice guy. 2 prelims, final, section attendance, and discussion is all. Would def take again.

This is the worst class I've ever taken at Cornell. Hirschl  hates economics as a science(and consequently economics majors like myself) and is the most boring lecturer ever. Even the books he chose were biased. (Perrucci and Wysong thought D.A.R.E was a conspiracy to distract the masses from social inequality) I got an A+ but didn't learn much.

I am an Applied Engineering Physics major and I had a 4.0  until I took Dsoc.I had to pull all-nighters every other day to keep up with the work.This class ruined my GPA,but more importantly, my life.The triple integrals he puts on the exam are ridiculously hard to solve.Bring a graphing calculator to the exams,and some extra batteries just in case

This guy is amazing, but if you become his friend, his class will become even more amazing and he will fascinate you to no end.  He is a great person who knows a lot and is willing to share, but only if he likes you and you get to know him.  So get to know him, and it will be a great experience.  Class was pretty easy; not about the grade with him.

If you are a legitimate student, this will be cake.  It's so easy!  But I hated myself for taking it.  He is biased, and the worst thing was that the pre-med/science types couldn't even see through his garbage enough to be outraged.  Unless you need a GPA boost badly, don't take this class- it was the worst one i've taken since middle school.
Really easy class and the topics are interesting, but he presents it in a way that doesn't really hold your interest. Don't really need to go to class to do well.
Easy class. Sweet professor. No studying necessary.

The stereotypical crazy college professor. This is the reason they're called "professors" - he just stands up there and professes about why cars are evil, why black people are sociologically inferior, and why religion is a waste of time. But I studied for about 30 seconds for the prelim and got a 91, so I'm not complaining!
Not too difficult, interesting topics

Easy class!! I had a great TA who made the class worthwhile. However, the professor is a horrible lecturer. He is extremely biased and does not paint an accurate picture of both points of view. Basically the whole class is set up to convince you of his point of view on every issue. However, if you want an easy A you can easily get one in this class

This guy HATES Protestants.  He just talks about things he has NO idea about.  Often, students will correct him.  HE doesn't know what Gallileo did OR what his thoughts were.  He also has an extreme obsession with his bike and HATES cars.  The class is pretty freaking easy so like take it though....

The class is easy, and Hirschl goes into the readings with a good amount of depth. The only thing is, the guy can come off as a complete idiot. He pulls examples from history and science without doing the proper research and doesn't know what he's talking about. He's also a communist which I find entertaining.

he twists the students' comments so they'll fit his thoughts, all he ever talks about is how cars are ruining the world, and he is ABSOLUTELY NOT objective... keep that in mind... you don't need to do the reading cuz he'll explain them well in the class and is pretty clear, but his personal thoughts get in the way of teaching
easy but a little boring - not incredibly enthusiatic or personable

Lectures are relevant and comprehensive. Hirschl welcomes students to interject and ask questions. Ties the whole course together quite well. He's not all caught up in himself like too many other Cornell profs. Good guy.
No Comments

Rather than inspire his students to do better and aim higher, this professor will actually make you want to not care about the subject material and simply not bother. You will find that the reading is not at all worth your time, since the professor will mostly just ask you to read aloud in class, and he will not encourage you to do much thinking.

Incredible professor who cares about his subject and making students lives manageable. If you engage with the material and take the time to read you will enjoy the course and do well. One of my favorite classes so far and will be taking him again!

Prof Hill's classes are as difficult as you make them. You can really engage with the text, or you can never do the reading- as long as you show up and say a little something during class (you can comment on what someone else said if you didn't do the reading), you will get an A. Really nice guy. A lot like Dumbledore in Harry Potter. Fun class

His section of scottish lit was awesome. I had so much fun. He's a little crazy, but has great jokes, is totally approachable, engaging and loves the subject, totally non-judgmental and just awesome in every way.

I couldn't understand a word he said and his feedback on papers was atrocious. Each time I went to office hours to discuss my essays, he'd give me contradictory advice. Loves the brown-nosers. Easy class, but I didn't learn a thing and it was painful to sit through 50 minutes of his mumbling.

Very laidback, approachable, and so sweet. Prof. Hill always has some bad/morbid jokes to keep class interesting! If I ever had a bad day, his class always put a smile back on my face. :) His love of the material is infectious! Class works best if you come with questions. He'll lecture otherwise, which is interesting but not as fun as discussion.
Professor Hill is like Dumbledore mixed with your favorite grandfather mixed with an Oxford professor. Interesting, hilarious, laidback, and brilliant. I love him!

The best professor I've ever had--witty, helpful, fun in and out of class. You will get a lot out of his classes that you don't expect, especially if you also see him in office hours. Self-motivated people will do very well; those who do only the bare minimum will pass, but will miss out. Look into the Norse reading group he advises; it's fantastic

What an amazing teacher.  I've never learned so much in any of my classes than I did from Prof Hill.  Charming, funny, completely accessible, and genuinely interested in getting to know his students.  Took us to lunch ever week and drove us to book sales in Ithaca.  Medieval Romance was great, as was Scottish Lit. I recommend any class he teaches!

On the day of finals, he invited the class to come watch a punk concert on his farm.  He is great; bearded like a norseman (very appropriate to the class).  Jolly like Santa.  He has some funny stories and bad jokes.  The class is as hard as you make it, I think.

Hill is this wild, rambling guy, passing out packets while just bursting with information. Funny, kinda disorganized, really nice...the epitome of an English prof. Grades easy, sets very clear standards for papers, not too much reading. I LOVE HIM!!!
tom is a trip. fun course and easy to pass, but it's as rigorous as you want it to be. do all the work and you'll learn a lot. this guy knows everything--go talk to him in office hours.
not much work, he definitely has favorites, class is not helpful at all... not a good course to choose if you want to improve writing/analysis of reading skills
nuts
Scottish Literature is the best humanities course that I have taken at Cornell. No doubt about it.
Great professor! Is my advisor now. Very funny, laid back, and nice. Wants you to learn and have a good time. No midterms or tests, minimal homework.

Scottish Lit w Prof Shaw...  Prof Hill is a marvelous professor.  He's dedicated, loves to teach, and truly makes the works come alive.  Take his classes!  Don't think it's offered anymore, but ENG 308 rocked as well (Icelandic Sagas).

old english is superawesome. tom's more concerned with people getting the overall concept and the feel of something than the nitpicky details. he's very approachable, and rather insane, and just generally a superduperspiffy prof
Absolutely fantastic teacher.  Focuses on the subject rather than being finicky about deadlines, will never hand you trick questions.  Very approachable, lots of fun!
Course content itself was very interesting, but lectures can be boring sometimes. Overall, she is very kind, and still teaches decently even when 90% of the class are on their phones.

Almost weekly, long assignments that are not explained in class. You need to figure a lot of stuff on your own. They have near nothing to do with the exam, and are a lot of busywork that doesn't guarantee an A. The slides contain most of the information which is nice but lectures are somewhat disorganized and uninteresting.
Lectures are not very engaging, she doesn't seem to understand her own content. She is willing to curve the class possibly to make sure people get decent grades though.
I don't understand why some people here say she's sweet, she's “sweet” but fake, unfortunately:(

Very sweet professor, she teaches well too considering the fact that 3/4 of her lecture is uninterested/treats it like an easy A. which ngl, it wasn't an easy A, but it wasn't terribly difficult either. psets could be tricky, but going to office hours made it easy
She's really sweet and she's trying to make the class easy and digestible, but she has dry lectures and isn't super familiar/vastly oversimplifies with the material.
very sweet prof, always helpful and kind to her students. lectures were a little dry to me but that's probably bc i'm not big on science

She's super kind and understanding. The assignments were sometimes very hard but office hours were helpful. Lectures were also recorded bc it can be very hard to follow along in class (a lot of content). But exams were fair.
I feel bad that no one listens to her in lect
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amazing and passionate lecturer who cares about her students. The lectures are easy to understand and interesting. The daily quizzes and lab were easy. The staff who help with this course are also super nice. As a non-STEM student, this is the first bio course I have ever truly enjoyed.

Amazing and passionate lecturer who cares about her students. The materials are easy to understand and interesting. The daily quizzes and labs are easy. The other staff in this course are also super nice. This is the first bio class I have ever truly enjoyed.

Course is very reasonable and exams are also fair. I would recommend taking the lab since it makes the exams weigh less. Overall you get to learn a lot and this is one of the most interesting classes you will take at Cornell, alongside the other ones like Honeybees, etc.

Her passion for fungi is truly contagious. I legitimately look at the world through a different lens after taking her class. Attendance is tracked through iclicker quizzes every class. Group quizzes become a nice way to get to know the people around you. Exams are purely a game of memorization and require that you get down nitty gritty details.

This class was not an easy A if you do not have a bio background. The prelims are oddly specific and difficult with a lot of memorization. Would not recommend it as a grade booster. Professor Hodge cares a lot though and teaches great. Quiz heavy class

Prof. Hodge is an excellent professor - so passionate and excited about mushrooms. Her enthusiasm made me look forward to class. Work outside of lecture is light, but you do need to attend class as there are always quizzes. The tests are specific and harder than you might expect - lots of memorization. I recommend taking the class with lab

everybody say mushroom easy A but its not. Easier if u take 3 credit cuz lab boosts ur grade. lecture only grading is

Individual quizzes	15%
Group Quizzes	10%
Thursday Qs	10%
Midterm 1	20%
Midterm 2	20%
Final	25%

That means u gotta go to every class, take a quiz (2x wk) for half ur grade and other 65% of ur grade is prelims that are mad specific

Professor was incredibly happy, enthusiastic, and entertaining. The class didn't go into much depth but was practical for most people in the class as a surface understanding of fungi. However, I wouldn't recommend it for people who want a course that uses more technical biology.

Great class! Highly recommend it. Not much work, just be prepared for short & easy multiple-choice quizzes after every lecture. The quizzes are pretty easy though and the material can usually be found in the lecture slides. 

Prof Hodge was super fun, engaging, and her excitement about her field of study is infectious! Take it!

Dr. Hodge is one of the most compassionate and kind human beings I have ever come across. She truly makes you feel as though you are not a student in a class where she is talking down to you, but rather uses her vast array of knowledge on fungi in a manner that makes you feel like you are two friends chatting about the interesting world we live in.

The SWEETEST professor at Cornell. Super understanding and caring, lectures are genuinely interesting. You do have to study a little for prelims, but nothing crazy. The only prof I've felt like I could actually connect with. I'm going to miss this class so much next semester. #shroomsquad

Professor Hodge is outstanding. Be sure however to prepare for the prelims and final. I didn't end up doing the best in her mushrooms class because I didn't study so much. If you put in the work you definitely will do well and the lectures are interesting.
Loved this class. Great prof who seems genuinely passionate about teaching. Incredibly accommodating and accessible.
One of the best profs at Cornell. Really funny and engaging, not a lot of work. She genuinely cares about her students and is flexible with her exams. Also, she feeds you a lot which is nice.

She is by far one of the best professors I've had at Cornell, and I don't even study in a science discipline (just for distribution). She is super funny and relates the subject to everyone. Unlike other teachers, she actually runs her own review sessions and extra credit sections. Honestly is everything you'd expect from a professor. SOOOO FRIENDLY

Honestly super nice! the topics were very interesting even though the readings could be much at times. Super accessible outside of the classroom and genuinely wants her students to learn about social justice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: wonderful discussions and intersectional curriculum. incorporated the struggle for justice into everything we read and learned.

I loved this class! Hodzic is a good professor - her lectures are always about readings for homework (if you want a good grade, you need to talk in the class). They're usually really cool though. Discussion section helps with your grade, and the papers are actually interesting, not boring. Very manageable to do well in if you do the bare minimum.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: I took a her course a few years back. She's great! Very smart and very helpful. Definitely knows her stuff.

Fantastic professor, her office hours are extremely helpful and is always willing to work with a student. Discussions are always interesting, open, and stimulating. Highly recommended if interested in FGSS
Terrible teacher. She's very unclear in the classroom, rambling, and just overall incompetent.
