HW grades relatively fair - she is nice and helpful, but she often lacks as an undergrad professor

Dr.Hunter is extremely smart and nice.  She's probably the nicest person you will find.  However, her lectures are very confusing and her exams are extremely difficult. Students generally complained a lot during the course, but satisfied with the grades.
The exams are a bit on the tough side and the mean for one of the exams was below 50%.  Homeworks are annoyingly long and the material really isn't all that interesting.
No Comments
The worst class I've ever taken in the department.  I dread going to class every day.
My God, words do not describe the stupidity that is 464. Do not take this class. You will spend all your time simply trying to parse the unclear, poorly thought out, useless homeworks.

worst professor ever, she doesnt teach anything that she gives on the assignments, the workload is unbelievable and a waste of time. i dont even know how to convey how terrible she is. she doesnt belong here. dont take any class with her.
homework was never covered in class, prelims were too hard, work load was too much for a 3 credit class.
No Comments

Of the 8 projects we had to do, Hunter only bothered to grade and return one.  Also lied about getting our class approved for the technical writing requirement, which made everyone very angry.  One of the most irresponsible professors I ever had.
not very interesting

Prof. Hurd is the greatest. He has decades of experience with unions. He appears strict and has expectations, but if you work hard it'll pay off. His banter with Prof. Sherwyn is not just entertaining and educational - it is arguably the most productive dialogue between labor/management in the country. Shoutout his TA's, you have to take this class

Amazing class. Both Prof Hurd and Prof Sherwyn offer excellent insight into labor relations, law, and the hospitality industry. Should be a required course for all ILR/Hotel students. Loved seeing both perspectives of union and management. Could not recommend any more highly.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Nice guy but not a good professor. Tests are fair but you have to memorize details for some questions. Attendance isn't mandatory but you should attend lectures to do well on tests as things he says that are not on textbook are tested. Pay attention during guest lectures - what they talk about is tested as well. The grade is curved and go to OH

I have taken a number of classes with Prof Hurd and I can say he is the best professor I've had at Cornell. Extremely down to earth, fair, and willing to explain things until students understand. His lectures can be a bit dry at times, but this class was also taught with Prof. Wagner who was very charismatic and knowledgeable. Reasonable work load

Hurd is an extremely nice guy and an expert in the collective bargaining field. His lectures won't wow you but the class is fairly interesting. A lot of annoying 1-page papers were my only problem with this class. The tests are fair and the bargaining simulation was a surprisingly beneficial experience. Got an A
good teacher very knowledgable doesnt grade papers very hard.
Great professor. Knows everything about unions. Fair grader. If you go to class, you can do well.
Great Professor, knows absolutely everything about unions; if you put the effort into going to class and doing the work, you will be rewarded with a good grade
Cool guy.  Sometimes he is all over the place, but he knows a lot.  He assigns a lot of reading but they actually are interesting.  All take home tests and some group work.

by far the worst math teacher i have ever had. it was often better to tune out his teaching because it would confuse me with everything i learned from the textbook. he is still a really nice guy...but a nice guy is useless as a teacher if he can't teach.

he is a genuinely nice guy and cares about/wants to help his students, but unfortunately his accent and unfamiliarity with english gets in the way of his lectures too much--he is incredibly unclear in lecture, and is not helpful during office hours. a great guy, but unfortunately i can't recommend him as a professor.
He's a very friendly, approachable professor. He has a moderate accent, but he is definitely understandable. He makes a lot of jokes in class.

If you can get past his accent, Hwang knows his stuff. If you need help DO go to office hours. He may not seem like the approachable type, but he IS willing to help. He writes a tough prelim, very "apply the concept in a new way." Extra credit for attendance.
Really sweet, genuinely nice guy, but possibly the worst math teacher I have ever had. Mumbles a lot and I can't understand anything. Basically... great mathematician, horrible teacher.

Great teacher, involves entire class in fun (but sometimes cheesy) excersizes, is reasonable and understanding, explains thoroughly and teaches "shortcuts" and "tricks" that come in really handy during homework and exams.Some may call him boring, but if you have any sense of humor at all, you'll realize he's the funniest guy ever.GIVES BONUS PTS =)
very boring
Really makes sure everyone understands the stuff. Always willing to help with stuff out of class.
he's hilarious, not a terribly good teacher, but i definitely enjoyed math 171 because of him
very softspoken, but funny in his own way.  Knows the material well and makes sure the class understands it before he moves on.  Very nice man.  Made stats interesting.
Very nice and intelligent professor.  He is always willing to help and appears to really teaching.
Although he has a very thick accent, he geniunely likes teaching (a rarity at Cornell) and cares about his students.  He makes sure that everyone understands the material.

Very simple format; grade is made up of attendance, weekly reflections (graded on completion), a midterm essay, and a take home final essay. Kind professor, really cares about the material. Not much to prepare for class other than doing the readings. Interesting and low-stakes class

Prof was so kind and cared so much about the material. Class was a mix of lecture and discussion, he really wants people to participate. Lectures basically reiterate the readings, which aren't too heavy. Not many assignments in the class, and prompts are given in advance so you can prepare your essays ahead of time.

In an hour and a half, Prof. Joo's lectures accomplish what could otherwise be achieved in three sentences. He has good intentions and the readings are interesting, but the class itself mostly consisted of him reading excerpts of what we were already expected to read.

One of the most frustrating classes I've taken. Complete lack of rubric for the 3 essays that comprise your grade. You can fix every mistake the TA cites and then get the exact same grade on the next essay. Professor is arrogant and condescending when you reach out for help.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: The worst class taken. Horrible teaching style also.
Professor is arrogant and pretends as if he cares about students. Horrible grading criteria.

Taken online asynchronous. Whole grade is based on 3 papers so I never did class or readings. The papers are difficult, allow no outside sources, and are subject to arbitrary TA grades. Leave yourself a lot of time for them. Rlly hated doing the papers but the class may still be worth it if you don't have time for daily/weekly stuff.

The worst class ever taken at Cornell. The grade is completely determined by three papers, which have very broad and confusing topics. The TAs do not respond to emails and do not leave any comment for a low grade assigned. The professor is indifferent to students' concerns. Papers were also regraded and assigned a lower grade. Horrible class!

This class was awful. Graded only by three papers with very broad questions and unclear grading criteria. They care more about details then anything else, if you don't write the paper exactly how they want it your grade will plummet. My friends and I dreaded this class. Lowest grade I've gotten in three years at Cornell for no reason at all. Avoid!

I would not recommend this class to someone I hate. The essay prompts are very broad yet the TAs all have one set approach in mind. If you don't write to their standards, it will show. They don't allow outside sources and the readings are not interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: As the leading professor in his field, lectures/topics covered were great. Can get dry at times, but you will come out having learned many new things. On the flip side, he can be super witty and fun to watch lecture. He seems to care about students' learning outcomes and makes it clear what expects on prelims.

Professor Hyman is truly amazing. I had him for class this past fall and he has clear expectations/grading and as long you put in the effort, you will do well. Assigns a good amount of reading but doesn't expect you to read everything word for word. Definitely worth taking his classes: he is funny, kind, and genuinely cares about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Um, what?  He lectures from his book.  Literally, his lectures are just him reading from his book most of the time, with side comments here and there.  The class in general is a little dry and boring.  At times, it does get interesting though.  He tries to push his political agenda too much and depending on which TA you have it's hit or miss.
Louis R. Hyman has 'It'  That's all you need to know.
Not at all helpful in office hours. Avoid!!!!

The course was interesting, but I found Professor Hyman to be a less than mediocre professor. He does none of his own grading, instead leaving you at the mercy of TA's. He doesn't even review it. If you want to contest the grade you may get worse. He's too full of himself to be an assistant professor. I'd pass on this class.
Wonderful Professor!  Very engaging and clear lectures.  Two Exams and a Paper.  Very clear expectations and not too difficult.  Makes class fun!

I'm truly going to miss his class. His lectures takes a very dry subject and makes the time captivating. 2 test and and a paper. Very clear on all aspects of the class. His knowledge of the subject is second to none. If you don't take a class with him while you're here, you're truly missing out. See ya at Wedgwood Hyman.

To date, he is my favorite professor at Cornell.  Straightforward, he tells you what he's expecting on examinations and on the paper.  A man whose vivid animation is arresting, he makes dynamic use of the lecture hall,  And if you're considering taking 2070, his teaching style is as good, if not better, than his lecture.  He's also brilliant.

Professor Hyman is amazing. Labor History seems like a dull subject but he never fails to find a way to make it interesting. His lectures can be dense but will keep you on your toes. He tells you want he wants on your exam and is really fair. Plus, he is a genius.

His lectures can be hard to understand because he moves quickly. The trick is to write down what he has on his opening slide and use it as an outline. Once you do this, the class should be easy, and he is a really nice guy. I def recommend anyone who has to take the class to take it with him.
Very fun, super engaging to listen to, clearly cares about students and always has amazing puzzles at the ready. Covers the material in an accessible and entertaining way.

Will you probably have to read the textbook outside of class? Yes. Is he incredibly cool and genuinely fun to listen to? Also yes. Class is doing wonders for my intellectual curiosity about math and otherwise.

Pretty nice guy but absolutely terrible lecturer. Struggles to explain concepts clearly and leaves entire class further confused; lecture slides also extremely difficult to follow. I only did well by using the textbook very heavily for notes + stopped going to lecture. Requires a good amount of work to do well, but much better than calc

He is a nice guy but he glazes over most concepts. I really did not benefit much from going to his lectures and often had to return to the material in the textbook to reteach myself the basic concepts. Nice guy just not effective as an instructor in my opinion.

Prof. Kim was good, but he occasionally went off on tangents where he would cover the chalkboard with equations and graphs and no one could follow his train of thought. Even though it's not a prereq, basic calc knowledge would be helpful in this course. Kim tried to explain the calc parts but didn't do a great job of it. Course median was a B+.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He was okay, sometimes his lectures were a bit hard to follow and he would include a lot of irrelevant information in them. Tests were slightly difficult but reasonable for the most part. His TA was not helpful and discussions were a huge waste of time.

He glazes over most concepts, I often had to return to the material in the textbook to reteach myself. The exams are inconsistent in their format and the homework assigned was varying in its helpfulness. It was his first time teaching the class, but his lectures did not help me understand the material. Sometimes funny though
Professor Kim is really nice and reasonable. His tests reflect the homework. If you go to class and do your homework, you'll do fine on the exams.

Professor Kim's class was great! The first half is based on econometrics, which is boring and difficult, but Professor Kim makes an effort to make it as interesting as possible. The 2nd half is based on the students presenting papers they read.

The class is divided into two sections. The first is econometrics and is mainly a review of what is learned in a typical econometrics course (like ECON 3120 or 3140). The second is a review of various research papers. There is not a second prelim and the final is before Thanksgiving break. Although the material is difficult, the professor is fair.
Professor Kim offers a strong and interesting course in econometric studies. A multiple regression background is required.

PAM 4140 is definitely a must-take course if you are interested in global health and international development. Prof. Kim's class covers wide range of health related issues and his first hand experience on the field is always inspiring. He is enthusiastic about the topic and truly cares about his students. And don't worry about the pre-reqs.
Great FWS and great professor. He was always available to help us with our writing and he did a great job of explaining the lecture concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Super interesting class, one of my favorites! Wish he was a full-time Professor!

Ian is an amazing professor, and I thoroughly enjoyed taking the class. I learned so much about Brazil, and he has inspired me to take more Latin American Studies courses. He is a very fair grader and included helpful and constructive criticism. My writing has definitely improved after taking the course.

Unique FWS subject. Lots of reading and writing-like any history class-but maybe more than other FWSs. Ian has high expectations, but a challenge is better in the long run than an easy grade. I am a more confident writer and researcher because of his class. There are few papers I have been very proud of-my term paper for this class is one of those.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Just the absolute worst of what the FWS program has to offer. Besides making coups and counterrevolutions seem boring this guy is super harsh about attendance grading. Only plus is that he loves hearing himself talk so much that you barely have to participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great course.
V. laid back teacher, and is willing to give you time outside of the classroom to help you one-on-one. Learnt a lot.

Hilarious teacher, willing to take the time outside class to give you specific feedback on your writing. Funny guy and tells interesting stories about his ethnographic study in Finland on nuclear researchers. Vincent is really cool and I definitely recommend his class: Nuclear Imagination.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Merwin is awesome. he is so willing to help students, and is very flexible in terms of deadlines and due dates.  He obviously really loves teaching and is very knowledgeable.  I'm sad to be out of classes to take with him!
Merwin's the man.
An awesome teacher and a great human being. I enjoyed his lectures a lot and learn even more than what I expected! he is genuinely a great prof!!
He presents the data clearly.  THe use of the powerpoints and photos makes concepts more tangible.  He gives you print-outs of the slides and brings FOOD to EVERY class.
Great professor, great class! The lectures are interesting and the labs are field trips. Professor Merwin is pretty easygoing. Hort 101 isn't an "easy A" but it's not heinously difficult either.
Loves apples and wines, pomology in general. Great man. Feels the land; down to earth. Loved the class. Easily apporachable and knows what he's talking about, but doesn't seem vain.
Great and easy classes...Nice guy...Definately leftover from the 60's but so incredible awesome and chill. Minimal work for good grades
Merwin is fantastic. One of the most interesting profs I've had at Cornell.
Great guy... leftover from the late sixties, all around cool guy.  Class is great!

The course content is not for the weak, but Dr. Lorey explains it in a way that makes it easy to understand. I dreaded missing his class because one lecture could mean missing important details not explained deeply in the textbook. The exams reflected the prelim reviews, and his lectures really helped make sense of the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took this class for the CALS requirement, as did most students likely. It was not a class to sleep on (lots of memorization required) but material is just above that of an advanced high school class. Prof. Lorey has thorough slides and breaks down concepts in class with on-the-fly notes. Attendance optional, but I'd go. Class is curved at the end
THE MOST BORING LECTURES EVER YOU WILL FALL ASLEEP,  The way he teaches is so boring and make you go to sleep. Every time I'm there I fall asleep, not only me but many students
Profesor Dan Lorey is a bit boring, but the class itself is easy.
His lectures are decently engaging and he thoroughly covers the material students are tested on.
Dry lectures but his videos are fun. Topics are broken down to be understandable.
Great lecturer. Posted slides, homework on achieve were very helpful and fair. Chemistry is hard, and that's not his fault.
Chemistry was hard, but an amazing lecturer, super nice, funny, and wrote fair exams.

Don't fall into the habit of skipping class - if you go and pay attention, you'll be much more prepared. Go to office hours!! He is really nice and wants to help you understand; if you ask for help, he will help until you actually get it. Read the lab report guidelines. He provides prelims from previous year. Class is curved at end. He's also funny

I love this man. Lectures are fast but slideshows are posted. This class built a community. Labs tend to be dull but thats only because they are taught by random TA's not King Dan. 1560 is challenging but VERY FAIR. I go to Dan's office hours twice a week and he is incredibly helpful with HW Labs and explanations. If you study a lot you can do well

Dr. Dan is the best! Super nice and fun lecturer. Although the class is really boring and difficult at points, Dr. Dan keeps it light with his humor and general caring personality. I would definitely recommend 1560 as an alternative to 2070 if its not a requirement.
Loved prof. Lorey. Never a dull moment in his class.

Dr. Lorey is a great professor. This is one of the most challenging courses I had to take but he makes sure that there are lots of opportunities to get help and he is accessible outside/after class. I have almost no chem background and was still able to understand his lectures, he does a great job at making them engaging.

Dr. Lorey is an amazing teacher as well as an amazing person. Although I did terribly in this class, it was in no way his fault. His office hours are inviting, and he provides lots of resources for people like me who struggle with this kind of class to at least have a halfway decent chance at passing.

Truly amazing dude, and that means a lot considering I despise chemistry. Get help after hours from Prof! Didnt get an A because didnt have time to devote to this one class. Labs are crucial; pre-lab quiz irrelevant for finals; practice exams almost exactly like real exam!! Dont take too many STEM classes in one semester and youll be g:)

Lab reports are super important! You don't have a ton of grades in this class so make sure your reports are good! Dr. Lorey is great and loves talking to his students but make sure you keep up with the work. The exams are pretty difficult so make sure you study a lot and apply problems from the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I am so bad at chemistry but Dr. Lorey really helped me grasp the concepts that were challenging. The class requires work to be put in but if you complete the assignments and come to lecture, youll do just fine. 2090 in the summer is a great class to take for those struggling with gen chem in the fall or spring
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Experiments were pretty interesting and not too difficult. The lab practical at the end of the semester was challenging, but Dr. Lorey doesn't make it worth too much. Weekly lab reports were laborious, but easy to do well on as long as you were thorough. Overall, very fair class that was a very appropriate difficulty.

The class starts out pretty easy, but after the first prelim, picks up speed pretty quickly. Dr. Lorey is a great professor, if something isn't clear to you during class, hes good for in class questions and provides plenty of office hours for you to get help.
Clear, consistent, and actually cares for his students. Dr. Lorey will get you through Chem1560 as long as you are willing to put in the work.
Simply wonderful

It's been over 25 years since I took her class, and it still stands out as one of my best college experiences. Zulma engages everyone and sincerely wants you to succeed. She is the yardstick I now use when I teach my students. Does she still wear Chucks to class? To this amazing lady, a big heart-felt grrrrrracias!

One of 5 or so best teachers in >200 credits earned in BS,MS,PhD. Co-wrote terrific text. Dedicated, enthusiastic. Awesome grasp of teaching language. Class focus on identifying & correcting mistakes that you make by analyzing everything you write. Very effective method.  Wherever she is, I hope she knows she made a huge positive impact!
Great teacher, kinda crazy, but definetly fun!
Zulma is easily one of the best teachers I've ever had.  Passionate, zany, and fun.  Teaches the subject very well and cares about the students.  The students bond a lot in the class also.
1) Tareas are often long and tedious! 2) Participation is necessary (large portion of grade) 3) Exams are fairly simple.
very structured class.  a ton of work.  A TON.  but zulma is very enthusiastic and into the class.

Estoy de acuerdo- ¡Zulma es la jefa! The class itself is a bit of work, but Zulma is really interested in everyone's progress, and really makes you want to improve. She's honestly nuts, it's great. Absolutely recommended.
AMAZING. I LOVE ZULMA. Friendliest, craziest, most amazing teacher ever. One of the teachers I know I'll stay in touch with. Zulma's the jefe.

i heart zulma. you will have a fun time in this class. zulma cares about her students and genuinely loves teaching. by far the most effective teacher i've ever had. she's very organized. i could go on forever. yea, the class is a little hard, but it doesnt matter.
Zulma is a lot of fun. The class is hard- its a lot of homework- especially in the beggining of the semster but if you stick with it it's a great class.

Zulma is classic.  Everyone loves her-- she is by far the professor with the most energy and enthusiasm at Cornell.  Her class is always fun to go to, and what's best is that she makes her students get to know each other.  Zulma is excellent!
Shes a really fun, nice lady.  The class is a lot of work, but most of it is busy work and the tests were challenging but gradewise it wasn't too bad

zulma is amazing, shes a littel crazy, but its refreshing because she is soooo enthusiastic. you have to do homework every night and it does take some time, but she is  incredible and you cant do badly in the class if you go everyday and do the homework.
very enthusiastic

Zulma is awesome! She is so excited about spanish and the class is incredibly fun. It's a lot of work but all worth it because your spanish will improve so much.  She is always eager to help students and treats you like colleagues rather than pupils.
Great Professor.
Entertaining, informative, helpful. Explains his proofs in loving intuitive detail. Gives easy homework and exams that nonetheless improve your understanding greatly.

Very helpful and likable. Good lecturer. Clearly an expert in the subject. Class was fast paced and sometimes difficult, but generous grading. Note: he often recalled theorems from lin alg and real analysis NOT in the prereqs, enabling a more complete treatment of DEs...but if you aren't done with core classes yet, be ready for a little self study!
Probably the best professor I have had in the Math department.  Crystal clear and well organized lectures, good hand writing.  Takes something of a challenging subject and makes it quite enjoyable.

One of the best teachers I've ever had. Crystal-clear expositor of math, cares deeply about pedagogy. Caring, well-prepared, clear, meticulous, and incidentally very funny. Even though I wasn't a top student, his class was superb! I give him my highest recommendation.

Sin duda, Prof. Troconis is the BEST professor I've had at Cornell. Besides being an unquestionably brilliant intellectual, every class she teaches is filled with energy, enthusiasm, and humor. She truly cares about her students' well-being and is flexible and adaptable to their needs. If you don't take her class, you're missing out!
Professor Troconis is seriously amazing! She breaks down tough topics, and her classes are basically the highlight of my semester.
Great class with a lot of interesting topics.
Take this class!!! Irina is a great Professor. She's extremely knowledgeable and gives great feedback.
Professor Troconis is absolutely amazing. Her lectures are extremely engaging. Would recommend.
Take if you want a real, engaging, brilliant professor, take this class.

Irina is an amazing professor. She comes to class brimming with energy and is extremely enthusiastic about what she teaches. She loves helping students. She has high expectations but wants overall progress over product. I have loved all my Spanish teachers at Cornell but her class is so fun and she is the best! Will be taking more classes with her!

One of the better professors I have had here at F&M. Relatively easy grader, but forces you to seriously engage with the material and to participate in class.  If you do that, you will thrive in her class.
She is amazing, these negative reviews are bologna. One of a kind, brilliant. Learned more than expected.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She was confusing and did not speak clearly and not very well into the microphone. While the material was interesting her lectures were not. The prelims and final were graded very harshly.

She's a very disorganized lecturer. I can tell that she wants to engage her students, but from what I observed, she didn't do very well. The prelims are pretty straightforward, you get the SA questions ahead of time. The final was really easy, I got a 95 without studying too much. If you can't bear the lectures (I couldn't), get the take note.

She's still trying to figure out how exactly to structure the class, but is definitely interested in what she is teaching. Although she can be a bit unclear sometimes, she is excited about what she is teaching and it's not hard to do well if you pay attention and outline the questions that she gives you prior to the prelims.
She is a terrible lecturer. She reads off her slides, mumbles, rambles, and is not very clear.

Overall good. Sometimes boring. I would say average professor. He used guest lecturers a lot, which I liked. But it also sometimes felt like he wasn't putting that much effort into the class itself. Which fair enough, he does a lot of other really interesting work outside of the class.
Cool content and super knowledgeable, but very monotonous and sometimes boring.
One of the best and most respected professors at Cornell.
Wonderful professor!  He really cares about his students and is readily available to give help or advice.  I would definitely recommend taking any class that he teaches.

I loved Professor Lovette! Though sometimes his voice is a little sleep-inducing, he really  knows his stuff. He loves birds and he always says it. Just make sure you really listen in class as well as study the book because the class takes a lot of dedication. Also, I think he is pretty hot, but that's just me.
Love this professor! He is honestly invested in his students and wants each of them to succeed. Great sense of humour and makes every class if not fun, then at least tolerable.

Professor Lovette is not only one of the best professors at Cornell, he is one of the kindest people out there. He cares so much for his students and is excited about what he teaches. He keeps class fun with jokes and examples. I would recommend him as a professor, advisor, or anything else! Definitely take this class or any class he teaches!

Professor Lovette is great! He cares so much about his students and really puts the time in to help out any student that needs it. He is such a nice guy also and someone that you would look forward to visiting in office hours. Since taking this class, my interest in evo has grown a lot! I definitely recommend this class or any class he teaches!
Really cares about his students and if they are learning the material. I learned a lot from his class.

Very nice and interested in the success of his students.  You can tell he makes an effort for people to be able to learn everything and do well, unlike professors of premed weed-out courses.  Note that some of the things other reviewers are saying on this page don't refer to him directly - e.g., the museum issue is the course director's fault.

Mandatory "field trip" to a crappy ithaca museum that you have to go on your own. The ithaca buses come at the worst ours so you'll risk being stranded in the middle of nowhere or miss an entire day of class. The worst possible design of an assignment for an already subpar class. This man is one of the worst professors at Cornell.

Class isn't curved, but you won't need it. Read the book or attend lecture, you don't need to do both. Lectures weren't THAT exciting, but if you pay attention, you'll learn. The exams were actually pretty easy (tests concepts), and you can study way less than for genetics or chem or a host of other bio major classes. Don't sign up for study group.

Class has an incredibly small workload for a 4-credit bio course.  I only read the textbook once or twice.  Grading isn't very predictable since you get to drop an exam, and within each exam, the questions aren't assigned fair point values.  For example, a 3 sentence short answer could be worth 10-15 points.  It's not an accurate grade assessment.

Purposely makes a should be simple course extremely difficult by distorting information. Diversity quiz answers are frequently erroneous and poorly worded. He only lets you drop one prelim and there is no curve in this class, in fact, he has the TAs make sure that their average class grade is an 80 (so if everyone in the class is smart, all of thei
Writes most convoluted questions imaginable, difficult to answer only because you never really know what he wants.  Writes literally incomprehensible questions commonly despite easy material.

Prof. Lovette is a actually a cool guy who made me slightly more interested in a subject (evo bio) I previously had no interest at all in. Tests are fair, homeworks are just annoying, gives you tons of chances to do well:  100 clicker points possible (worth the same as a prelim), drops your lowest prelim, and online open book quizzes.
Funny and engaging

The grading is ridiculous. He lets you drop so many prelims, that you wonder why you should even take the course. Dropping prelims is misleading, it shoots the average grade up. The tests consist of essay and multiple answer- not multiple choice. It's easy to do well if you're interested and you study hard. Don't buy the book, just go to class!

The ideas presented are all very simple. Do not need to buy the textbook. Section activities are a lot of fun, awesome TA's. The grading is very unusual and it causes everyone in the class to get the same grade.

Do not read the textbook, it is a complete waste.  Go to lecture and take really good notes.  Study for the prelims a week in advance - best method is to recopy the lecture notes and study them.  He let us drop two out of three prelims, or the final, but this grading method threw people off because they did not study enough for the prelims.
Best and easiest of the teachers for this course.  Prelims are not bad, workload is low.  Take this class after 281 and you'll appreciate how easy it is.
You have no way of determining how you're doing in the course, until you get that final grade...
Grading is extremely unfair.  Beware!
No Comments

Peeva is generally a good lecturer and is not only clear on the course material, but also on what we need to know for exams. Lectures could be a bit dry and I had trouble relating the topic material to outside topics, but all in all I learned a lot.

Professor Peeva was definitely a clear professor who taught the concepts of Linear Algebra in an understandable way. However, the course structure made it extremely stressful. They recently changed the curriculum and we had no idea what to expect. The TA's were awful and made the class so much worse. One of the hardest class I have ever taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: great professor, really clear in her lecture slides which is often lacking in upper-level math classes. tests are very fair and if you come to class and take good notes, you'll do great. 3 prelims with an optional exam at the end that lets you replace your grade on of them .  take her if you want a  4000 lvl math without the pain and suffering.

Besides her slight Slavic accent, she is the clearest math prof I have ever had. Clear writing, lecture was always prepared ahead of time, and I had to never ask her to repeat something or go over something slower. The class did feel a bit slow, but everything was clear. Class was easy considering it was an upper level maths course.

Although she talked directly into the board (which inhibited me from hearing her properly, even when sitting in the front row), her notes were exceptionally clear. Overall, she's pretty good and knows what she's talking about.

Good prof. Lectures were very clear and organized. Homework and exams were not very difficult. Proofs were emphasized before applications. My only complaint is that sometimes Prof. Peeva didn't seem very enthusiastic or passionate...maybe she's just not a morning person!

Professor Perera was an awesome professor. She explained tough concepts well and was always willing to answer questions after class or in office hours. The class was a little challenging, but the amount I learned made up for it. She will be one of the nicest professors you will have, and I highly recommend this class.

Weekly quizzes could be pretty hard, and the TAs were harsh graders. The content was mostly jargon-heavy academic research with no clarification in class. Quiz questions are written to be tricky, not to test understanding of readings. Perera was very nice and was a great lecturer, gave extra credit opportunities, and handed out candy often.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Graded on 3 short 4-6 page essays, 10 in class quizzes drop lowest one, and final group paper. Professor is chill, grades fairly, doesn't assign busy work or busy readings. Easy to ask TA and Professors for help and feedback for your assignments, grading criteria is all very clear. Would be nicer if prof discussed case studies outside of Europe.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: she is nice, no busywork which is nice, accessible outside of class, my only issues were the 10 minute quizzes which gave you like 2 minutes to answer each question and how strict grading short response answers was in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Most compassionate professor I've ever had! Assignments have a purpose behind them as the content builds off each other, so there isn't any busy work. Make sure you thoroughly read the readings and pay attention in lectures because there are in-class quizzes. The lectures were pretty engaging, and she really wants you to learn!

I went out of my way to take a second class with Professor Hutchinson. He helped me elevate my poetry and was more than willing to meet one on one with anyone to discuss his comments in greater detail. He wants to see his students succeed. I asked him to be my advisor because of this dedication he has to his students.

He is insanely nit-picky about everything, and most of his assignments are due by email at the most random times. He complains about how/what you submit.  And he doesn't teach. We do "workshops" where we give subjective feedback about each others' writing. But his feedback is not helpful. And he doesn't give you any idea of your grade. Bad teacher

Prof Hutchinson is a really nice guy.  He is a great creative writing teacher.  He writes poetry, so expect to work with a lot of poetry in his class.  We had something due every week in his class.  We did a lot of writing and a lot of peer review.   The only downside is a lack of an accurate syllabus.  It wasn't always clear what was due when.

Although I would not necessarily call the class easy, I absolutely loved it.  Professor Hull is one of a kind, and the class is one I will never forget.  She has an incredible knowledge of German History, and the class (Post-War German History) is a great one.  If you have the opportunity, take her class!  You will not regret it.

Had I.V. Hull in '81-'83.  Demanding professor who cares about quality.  Best professor I had at Cornell.  Glad to see she is still true to form.  She made me understand that history is a product of interacting groups in society, not just the actions of one leader; not just the program of one ruling party or government.

Hull is probably the best professor at Cornell. She will actually take time and proof your essays before you turn them in (she actually encourages it). She is clear, intelligent, and caring. Idiots beware, she will call you out. Come to class prepared, or get chewed out. If you are prepared to work, definitely take a class with Hull.
Course is a lot of work. Come prepared to sections, go to lecture. Tough grader but not unreasonable; she does have a serious attitude problem, however.

great lecturer- clear concise and a great discussion leader, but her personality leaves something to be desired. If you don't like profanities and hostility directed towards you for no good reason - don't take her.
One of the best profs at Cornell. Take whatever class she is offering--it will be worth it.

Awesome! She is incredible. If you want to become a more critical reader and writer, take her course. Her class is a lot of work but definately worth all the effort. She is the best professor I have ever had!
Really sharp and great discussion leader. Hard grader but completely worthwhile.

Krishna seems to be well prepared for every lecture he gives, which is good but expects the class to remember some small details learned earlier in semester for almost every question he asks the class. Which reminds me, he is one of those professors that waits for students to answer a question he asks towards the class. Does that make sense??
The class is lacking substance. No feedback on tests or homework. No suggested textbook problems to study. Little partial credit is ever given.
dude looks like he's chillin hard and honestly hes a bro
This class is just us teaching our peers the whole semester
lot of group projects with vague instructions that she then harshly critiques when giving feedback. 50% of this class is just listening to classmates present their work
Interesting content; manageable assignments

Funny and always accessible. A lot of readings but only the parts discussed during class are covered. Clearly cares about his students and always available for unscheduled office hours. Unfortunately, he's sometimes unprepared and can't answer some basic questions. Midterm graded very reasonably.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Genuinely one of the laziest professors I have had. Every class was exactly the same and he just liked to listen to himself talk. He was often condescending and grading was completely arbitrary.

Every day in class, you do the same boring activity. He is a lazy unmotivated faculty member who created the curriculum years ago and has never once revised it. He would come to class having not reviewed anything related to the material. Additionally, he provides 0 feedback on your work and doesn't explain why he takes points off.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is fascinating, and even students with a Jewish education background will learn a ton. There's a lot of reading and writing involved, which can hit hard in the middle of the semester when it's 10 degrees outside. He is accessible outside of class and encourages students to participate.

Professor Mokhtarian is an incredible professor who cares deeply about seeing his students learn and succeed. The assignments are beneficial to your understanding of the information and never feel unnecessary. He will push you and your writing skills, but it is 100% worth it and you will be proud of your assignments by the end of the semester.

really passionate prof, u can tell he really loves finance. 
the course itself is hard but hes very lenient on grading, and some of the expectations are a bit unclear.
Amazing professor who cares for his students. Lectures are very important if you want to get a good grade for the exams and practice exams & materials matter.

they try hard to make this subject accessible to students, but the material isn't easy. sometimes assignment/grading feedback would be promised on a certain day only for it to be posted days later. there is a formula sheet provided for exams. just try to do practice problems/hw to prep for prelims
Good professor but gives too much information that is not needed for exams/introductory finance. Exams are heavily curved.

It is an absolute privilege to get taught by Prof. Janosi. He is an incredibly well-organized and methodical teacher, who could as easily teach you a course in quant, derivatives, or machine learning as he could the fundamentals of finance. Given this, he intends to include extra material that can sometimes confuse students. Go to OHs.
Get ready to wait 1 month to receive a grade for an online multiple choice exam.

Janosi is a very structured man who is always quick to crack a joke. Finance itself is a lecture-heavy subject and requires that you attend class and not zone out or the topics will fly past you and you will feel lost. If you pay attention, you will be entirely fine. 
I got a 100 on prelim 1 no sweat. Take his class.

Don't take it unless you have to. If going for business minor, take the hotel one instead. Bro takes 2.5 weeks to give back an online test that's 95% multiple choice. No clarity in lecture slides and spends most of the time in class going over technical things you won't use in the exam (formulas and such that are built into the course calculator.

Great professor for the finance requirement of the business minor. It helps a lot if you have some prior knowledge about time value of money(present/future values), DCF's and some portfolio construction(alpha/beta). Attendance isn't really required, and for the tests just know how to solve every practice question and you'll be money.

Tibor is a very interesting man...his lectures are a bit all over the place and his handwriting is hard to keep up with. Nevertheless, if you cut through his dry jokes and somewhat unstructured lectures, you are left with a man who is a true finance nerd who loves his profession. I personally adored his class - exams were fair and curved generously
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor is extremely monotone and lectures can get very boring. However, they want to see students succeed and are willing to assist outside the classroom.

This was one of the most painful courses I've ever taken. Every lecture was incredibly monotone and poorly organized while he regularly made calculation mistakes in class. Prelims are 40% of your grade and the final is 45% though he didn't teach half of the final material. Would also be condescending to students asking questions pretty regularly.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice guy, but terribly boring. Lectures were extremely painful to sit through and he explained things very poorly.
The homie

One of the biggest assets of the ORIE department. The professor is an expert in the credit risk area and his explanations are very good. Enjoyed his class a lot. And, he's not a tough grader either. About 50% of the class got A- or above.

One of the worst professor ever.  If you are looking to learn anything practical this is not the class for you.  You will be fighting to stay awake as he spends the 1st 3 weeks to tell you what calls/puts are in a robotic monotone voice.  Take his class at your own risk.  This material may be interesting for financial engineers but its bad.
He presents the material very clearly and lectures are organized and interesting.

Even though Kramnick is retiring, I have to leave a review because he's just that amazing. He's the epitome of a brilliant professor in need of a hair stylist. His lectures are mind-blowing: his ability to make anything interesting made me look forward to every lecture and motivated me to really put effort into his class. Highly recommended!
An incredible professor who is world renowned.  I absolutely loved Kramnick.
Excellent class, really interesting
Amazing professor that managed to engage me with a subject I had little interest in. Clear, accessible, and not unnecessarily difficult I recommend everyone take a class with him.

Kramnick is the epitome of an old school, laid back, brilliant professor with wild gray hair. 1 assignment for our grad seminar (a paper) that doesn't have a due date. He said we could hand it in next spring if we wanted. Lots and lots of reading but he's realistic in that he realizes we have other courses and it's hard to read everything. Take him

I am currently taking a online Winter session with Kramnick and must say he is a genius. As a Senior, I have worked with many Professors and Kramnick is in my opinion, the best professor in the Government department. Cornell is lucky to have him! If you are a Gov major you must take his Intro to Political Philosophy course.

Fascinating, old-school professor who is always on his game. Lecturers are interesting and detailed. Would have liked for him to let the class participate and ask questions, but overall, good professor.

Kramnick was a fantastic professor! Got me excited about American Political thought. Lectures could get a little boring by the end, but overall, they were great. I've never felt so connected with a professor in a large lecture class.

Kramnick lived up to the reputation. He is brilliant and it shows. He may be getting old, but he hasn't lost his touch (like Lowi has). I highly recommend anyone interested in government, philosophy, or history to take American Political Thought.
He's really helpful

Kramnick is an award winning professor who really knows his stuff. If you do the reading, you should have no problem.  I didn't and still managed a B+. TA's tend to be very knowledgeable also although they teach in completely different styles and are a little tough on papers

He was very clear in his lectures, but also painfully boring. Many people (myself included) found it extremely difficult to stay awake in class. He's very knowledgeable about what he teaches, but he tends to repeat himself over and over and lectures became monotonouse and uninteresting. On top of that, there is a lot of reading. easy to get behind.

Kramnick is very interesting and enthusiastic about his teaching subject. However there is a TON of reading and TA grading is pretty hard. There is a midterm and a final as well as a term paper so there isn't a ton of work but it also makes it easy to get behind on the reading.

The lectures make the class super easy. If you pay attention, the readings will only become supplements to your essay. The TA's grade harshly, but that is how it is with all Gov TA's at Cornell. Kramnicks passionate, and it really makes the lectures better. He would save a whole lot of time by not repeating the same point over and over again though

Has an incredible love for the material and is a great lecturer. Someone you'd want to be your grandfather! Not too difficult a workload, with 2 essays and a final exam, but the lack of assessment kind of encourages you not to read...and you don't exactly need to know the readings until the final.
Amazing class, as was expected having taken 161 with Prof. K.
Entertaining lectures, highly approachable and will review your essays favorably if you feel your TA didn't quite get it.
Excellent readings, but Kramnick refuses to go into any depth with them. It's a shame, seeing that this is his specialty...

Kramnik was an excellent lecturer, but if you are not a govt major, be wary.  There are only three graded items (midterm, papre, and final), and if you can not express your ideas well and have any understanding about your topic, you will do poorly.  The TA sections are kind of a waste of time, but unfortunately, those are mandatory.

You could probably not do a single reading and get by just on the lectures (although if you are interested in taking this class, these are readings you'll enjoy).  Prof. K is the man, but the TAs vary from exceptional to mediocre at best.  Try to get a good TA then get on her good side.

Although you won't learn anything incredibly profound, this is still a solid intro class. Kramnick is a class-act guy who is  to schmooze with students and help them out. The course itself was pretty straightforward, and is not difficult at all if you go to lecture and see what he emphasizes.
I actually took Prof. Kramnick's intro and upper level political philosophy classes. I loved both classes. I never wanted to miss a class because his lectures are amazing.

Two requirements for a great professor: infectious love of the material, and gets along well with students. Kramnick excels at both (and many more). Has great interest in making Cornell a better place. "And now we come to the most INCREDIBLE SENTENCE!!!..." And yeah, he does act like Woody Allen, but in a good way.

Kramnick is the quintessential friendly grandfather figure with a side of academic know-how and rainbow sprinkles on top. Despite the large size of the lecture, he tries to get to know students personally, which I found really likable. As for the class, the real source of info is him. You can get away with skipping a few readings, and still learn.

Though he acts a little bit like Woody Allan, kramnick is my favorite teacher this semester. He is interesting, intelligent, and insightful. Sometimes the lectures can get a little boring, but I think its more the material than him. Very down to earth, try and have lunch with him and you'll see what I mean.

Amazing lecturer! His lectures always connect with the readings. There's no sections, but there is a lot of reading. Just remember one thing when you go to his class, "the race for life."  You'll know what I mean when you take the class :D. Grading for papers are subjective and varies by TAs.  Go to class b/c prelims require class notes!

Take it if you can, and you're not one of the idiots that thinks there's a war on Christmas.  It's not hard, it's straightforward, and it's better than most other classes.  Kramnick is funny and smart, and even if you disagree with him, you have to acknowledge that he's not making things up or distorting facts.

Kramnick's egotistical, but most celebrated profs are. The material is interesting, but a little boring. It kind of sucked that we never had a test all semester (only take homes) and then had a final exam that was worth 40% of our grade. Eek. I probably did fine though. Oh yeah, and we only talked about Malcolm X for 4 minutes. Learned a lot though
No Comments

I took a few with him.  I am a government major, who focused on political philosophy, so I may be a bit biased. But I think Kramnick is amazing.  Engaging, intelligent, funny, very good.  I would recommend at least 161 with him.
He's a funny guy at times.. but he condescends fairly easily.. that and I see him as a bit ****.
I loved this class.  I'm not a government major, but I though the lectures were intersting, (even if he does go off topic a lot) and there was practically no work involved.  Easy and fun.
amazing teacher, smart, very clear, brings up some really interesting issues
It's kind of a silly class.  You don't really learn anything...  you just hop along tiny excerpts of texts throughout history until you get to his pet philosophers.  It's easy though.
Course coordinator for GOV 210 - good guy.
Fun and eye opening class

Kramnick is clearly a smart man.  His lectures are very clear, but up to a point where they become redundant.  He'll try to drill the same point home for an entire lecture.  Fair grading.  Reading not too taxing, some of it's optional
Good lecturer despite crazy ideas.  Hardcore liberal.  Class organization is questionable.  Grading seems arbitrary.  Overall fair class.  ***WARNING*** Possible ****.
Kramnick is the God of American History.  'Nuf said.
Great organization and ability to give spellbinding lectures.  Not so helpful, but he has TAs for that.
i agree with the other comments- smart but pompous. grading is tough as well. the course is am polit theory (161) on steroids (366)
amazing speaker and amazing person
Kramnick is an incredible, insightful, learned teacher. He is also a caring mentor who expects the best from his students. Cornell is lucky to have him.
Entertaining lectures most of the time but stiff grading policy!
Great survey of intellectual history
No Comments
Nice guy, interesting lectures...usually.
entertaining lecturer
too into himself, lecture course not designed to be lecture
Brilliant guy

The guy is super chill and clearly very smart but he just isn't the greatest teacher. Clearly too smart for his job but course is manageable without attending lecture (lab section taught better than him). Make sure to put effort into the problem sets since they mirror the test pretty well.
Professor Chestnut was clear and values professionalism, so just make sure to be respectful with communication.

This is the easiest stats class you can take. No R coding that other stats classes do and fair exams. There is only 1 prelim and a final, with the prelim average being 90%. The professor has a HUGE ego and overshares everything. The class is really disorganized and no one knew what was going on sometimes. Also it took 1 month to grade our prelim.

A word that can be used to describe Professor Chestnut is actually in his own last name; he is a nut. Although his raw intelligence is high, his emotional intelligence is quite low (poor people skills). He often spends a good portion of class boasting about himself and is extremely unapproachable (unless you plan to glaze him in your interaction).

As others said, extremely pretentious and has incredibly low capacity to understand other's perception of himself–it's consensus that no one really likes him. He will blabber on and on about himself and his accolades for as long as time allows. 

Otherwise, very easy class. I stopped attending lectures very early on for aforementioned reasons.

embarrassingly inflated self-image, and extremely short-tempered if you contact him over email and ask questions that can be answered elsewhere. 
the class isnt terrible hard, but the weekly homeworks are graded harshly and there are only 1 prelim before the final.

One of the worst professors at Cornell. Shows no concern for students and makes the class miserable. Constantly rude, dismissive, and unhelpful. Creates a hostile learning environment and makes you regret taking the course. Avoid if you can.

Jacob gets much praise from me. Definitely look back fondly on this course despite it being a lot of work in the moment. Jacob honestly has so much wisdom to provide his students. I think I would rather be his friend than his student though.

Terrible professor, he tanked my GPA. He just doesnt care about his students, doesnt teach and expects you to know everything. If you have taken stats before you should be fine, but dont take his course as your first stats course.

Professor is the only one I had so far who yelled to students. The TA provided some incorrect information about the problem, so she asked for clarification. Professor yelled at her and said he doesn't care what the TA said. Not patient and literally the first professor I met so far that are this rude to students.

I thought that Jacob taught Intro Stats very well, just make sure you are on his good side! The lectures were clear &  homework didn't take that long. There was only one prelim and final, both of which were straightforward and we were allowed a cheat sheet, ,also curves your grade at the end. I failed both exams and ended with a B!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I thought that Jacob taught Intro Stats well. The lectures were pretty clear. The homework didn't take that long and TA office hours were really helpful with the problem sets. There was only one pre-lim and a final, both of which were straightforward and we were allowed a cheat sheet. Overall a solid class.
The comments are so laughable lol

Probably the worst professor in the world that you can ever get - narcissistic, self obsessed, and not focused on the learning or teaching that is required for this class. Truly, anyone else that you can possibly get would be better, don't sign up for his class and go for any other professor that would truly be behind you and your learning instead

Honestly one of the worst professors I have ever had. He yells at students and sent my friend a three-paragraph nasty email asking why she didn't read his 120-page syllabus when she asked a question about the final. He talks about himself in every class, and you have to teach yourself the entire course. I don't understand how people like him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: I did really well in his class so I have no complaints about his teaching style. However, I have never met such a rude, entitled, and narcissistic person before. I've worked in the hospitality industry for over 3 years, and he is still by far the rudest person I've ever met. If you have a choice, please choose another professor.

lenient and wants you to do well. you will be surprised with how well you do in the course and also what you are capable of doing by the end. students who complain about this class are the ones who are incapable of doing the bare minimum which is watching a video and doing exactly what the video does for the assignments. also, the exams are doable

Professor Chestnut definitely has some personality to him. Due to the "flipped" structure of the class, you essentially teach yourself everything, but thankfully the content isn't too hard. He clearly has some narcissism/ego problems, as he boasts about himself in almost every class, but realistically he's fine as a teacher.
By far the best professor I've had at Cornell. If you can take a class with him please do so.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Decent professor. 85% exams, 15% project. Difficult course. Exams varied in difficulty. No attendance necessary, lectures recorded and shared live on Zoom. EC worth up to 3%.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor! Very engaging lectures and I felt that I learned a lot.

Amazing lectures! Class is very straightforward and has a pretty light workload, just read the slides before prelims and you will do well. Prof. Mendle is very clearly an expert in the content but knows how to convey the material in an informative, accessible, and fun way. Really not much more you could ask for from a class!

shes a great professor and really does care about what she teaches. Her tests are super easy as long as you actually know the stuff on the slides. Everything is super fair; lectures aren't necessary as long as you go through the slides yourself and actually digest everything. she has readings, but you lwk don't need to do them. also no hw btw.

Professor Mendle deeply cares about the material and puts a huge effort into helping students digest and process the content. Top-tier professor, and I highly recommend taking a course taught by Dr.Mendle.

Dr. Mendle is my favorite professor at Cornell, but you do have to work for the A. I have taken two classes with her (Developmental Psychopathology and Advanced Seminar in Psychopathology) and both required dedication to the topic matter. That said, she is highly intelligent, and a great resource if you are interested in psychopathology.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors, she is a great lecturer. If you are interested in psych you will gain a lot from her course. Extremely organized and knowledgable.

Best psych/hd course I've taken at Cornell. Mendle is a little closed-minded regarding psychodynamic therapy, but was willing to discuss the merits of different approaches. The class itself was fantastic. Lectures were engaging and we covered all of the major disorders. I retained more knowledge from this class than from any others.

When she sits in a group, her problem is she will entertain potty mouth students who will bully asian students. Instead of neutralizing the situation and creating a friendly environment, she will laugh and make jokes out of them. She leaves her professionalism at home and comes to work. She is a big bully!
The worst and most insecure professor! She envies students. It is very unfair toward hardworking students. Unclear rubrics. Uninterested in solving doubts.

Closed-minded, passive aggressive, dismissive, unhelpful, and condescending. Made me feel like all of my effort amounted to nothing. I did not find her approachable or willing to account for students' personal issues. Felt defeated, unheard and not respected. Wholeheartedly would not recommend.
Overall disappointed. She made me lose my love for the field.

She has a very one-track mind, and it is extremely difficult to have a conversation with her because she is condescending. Comes off as nice, but extremely disappointing when it comes to class overall.

HORRENDOUS!!!! She and her TA team want you to think in one way and if you do not YOU ARE PUNISHED! Unprofessional emails, passive aggressive behavior, she is VILE! Think Mrs. Dodds from Percy Jackson. Unclear grading standards, random conversation takeovers, cultural appropriation with her outfits, just she should not be teaching!
Professor Moseley was alright, but the grading on tests was pretty unfair in my experience. The grad TA grading was insanely rough and it was almost impossible to go straight to Dr. Moseley
She ain't it
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Arguably one of the kindest, fairest, and well intentioned professors at Cornell. NS 2600 is manageable and it is very possible to get an A. Work hard on the group project and follow the rubric and you'll do well
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Main issue w/ this class is that there is tons of assignments to keep track of. All the small assignments add up. Getting an A is doable, but you have the put the work in. Remember the smallest things for quizzes and exams. Interesting content and lectures though, even though it's mostly guests. Make sure your group does well on final project!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Although Jeanne is the professor, this class is taught more by guest lecturers. The content was okay but it only mainly covers HIV, maternal mortality & water sanitation. It is also very unclear on what you're suppose to know for the tests/pop quizzes. A lot of students just don't like the structure of this course at all. Would not recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: It's hard to truly grade Jeanne as a lecturer because almost 60% of her lectures were outsourced to other people who knew a lot more than she did, (which isn't difficult.) She is a nice individual, but she treats this class more like than English class than the science class it is. The writing skills were worth more than the actual ideas in essays.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--EXTRA CREDIT--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: This class is super overrated. It wasn't terrible, but not something I would strongly recommend. Lots of guest lectures which vary in quality, writing assignments are annoying and the exams were weirdly difficult. Jeanne is really nice but the class just wasn't that great.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: nice professor, but class is mainly taught but a ton of guest lectures, do the work and you will get decent grade, I never read the readings or book and i manage to fully participate in lecture and breakout. beware of the group project grading is kinda tricky for that. a lot of the information is review if you are familiar with public health
one of the sweetest professors you'll meet at cornell

Jeanne's energy and excitement for global health is contagious.  Most of the class is an array of guest lectures. But overall, Jeanne and her team do a wonderful job of presenting the class and I enjoyed every minute of it.

Jeanne is an excellent teacher who really cares about her students. She is super approachable and always willing to help a student in need. The class has a few assignments, a prelim, a group project and a final, all of which are pretty easy to do well on. She gives an outline for the prelim and lets you use a 'cheat sheet' for the final.
One of the best

Great professor! Had him for Calc I which is a pretty difficult class, so the difficulty isn't reflective of the professor. However, he was very good at giving in-depth lectures that taught the material well. Grading is very fair (from what he can control), overall had a good experience in the class.

Great person and genuinely cares for you as a human. He always guided you to a solution and wanted his students to succeed. His office hours were accessible and he was always willing to help. I recommend!

He shows that he's willing to support his students! Don't hesitate to reach out to him for help, feedback, or really anything. He's a very chill, relatable, awkwardly funny guy. The lectures are very helpful, with clear class notes, and step-by-step solutions to the worksheets. Highly recommend this professor!
Favorite professor, funny in class. I haven't used his office hour before but he gives off very comfortable vibes and I will not be afraid to ask him any questions.

Goated professor. 
Explains things in a way that intuitively makes sense. 
I was trying to have this class waived, but I'm glad I didn't. 
Goes above and beyond, and is always ready to help you when you don't understand something.
Unlike many, he does not assume you already know something, and does not make you feel stupid.

AMAZING PROF... fav class. His lectures are so engaging and I am always excited to come to class. Make sure to do the readings to fully understand lectures and cold calls, but reading is actually rlly interesting and not difficult. His lecs are always funny and his dad jokes make class more exciting. Overall, I HIGHLY recommend taking his classes
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Rachlinski displays his expertise in both law and pedagogy through his question-answer teaching style that is both friendly to encourage participation and thought-provoking. Expect a decent amount of readings and learning to think differently than you're used to if you aren't pre-law. Regardless of your major, this class is very rewarding.

Rachlinski is very funny and engaging. As long as you do the readings and show up you will do well. This class was SO interesting but wish it was a little more of the professors talking instead of calling on students. The professors would let the students say some pretty racist/sexist takes. Loved the class though, def recommend if prelaw

Rachlinski is a funny guy, but his lectures are confusing. I found myself having to lean heavily on the readings to understand concepts because of this. I think that he needs to slow down and keep focused. He also seemed to be a more intense question-maker for the tests than Chatrchyan (co-prof), treating undergrads like actual law students.
Love this man. Class is easy if you do the reading and don't get flustered by his playfully sassy cold call style.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of the most interesting classes Ive taken at Cornell. It is essential that you thoroughly do all reading homework because he cold calls students in class. This can be stressful at first but is honestly not a huge deal. I honestly never felt bored, and as long as you show up to every class (attendance is huge) and take good notes you'll do well
Really great professor but not great on Zoom. Be prepared to do a lot of readings and there are cold calls in class as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Generally good prof but not great for zoom classes... Lots of cold calls. Lots of reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Rachlinski is a very passionate and knowledgable professor. He goes off on tangents sometimes, but they're related and very interesting!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: His lectures were really interesting.

Professor Rachlinski is very passionate and well-prepared for every class. He makes materials really interesting. He would pick several students to answer all the questions tho, so just read before classes and enjoy his amazing lectures.

The professor is so good and humorous about the corporate law. You can't stop laughing when he is making a joke accidentally during his dealing with a serious corporate problem. His answer to the course questions and past exams (with suggested answers) are very helpful for preparing my final exam. Highly recommended!

Professor Pender is really kind and extremely knowledgable. My biggest recommendation is to go to class and to go to his office hours. He will help you if you are willing to put in the work and if you talk to him. It is a test heavy class but the curve at the end is extremely generous. Overall, really appreciated the perspective he gave.

Prelim & final were the main stressers. I did really bad for both tests but the outcome was okay... Was really shooting in the dark with this course cause it's so test heavy and I genuinely thought I failed. For the final, write EVERYTHING on your cheat sheet cause he will test on the most random stuff and you would need the formulas

His lectures can be engaging but aren't super helpful with the content. The bigger issue is the exam design. Both exams had questions on series that he didn't give any prep for and he doesn't really ingrain the concepts well enough to justify the problems he puts on the test. TIP: his favorite distribution is Beta with a = b = 1/2. It's arcsin
Worst Class I've taken. Don't know how he got this job

The single worst professor I've takne a class from. Does not know how to teach, does not know how to make good lecture slides. You know the class is bad when the finals has been consistently 50%. Avoid at all cost. A shame that it's such an important class in the engineering department

I never want to touch statistics again. 

Homework is lengthy, unenjoyable, and often times irrelevant. Lectures and test prep material is some of the worst I have ever seen, both made me feel more confused on material that I already knew. Absolute nightmare. I have taken courses at five universities in three countries, this one is the worst.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This guy does not know how to teach. He just reads his slides and expects us to understand everything, and I honestly don't think he knows what everything is. He yaps a lot about himself, and the lectures are somehow boring. Since lectures are not mandatory and boring, no one goes to his lecture, but he puts a question on the prelim about himself.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He yaps too much and makes it unclear what the course is about.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Made lectures relatable and interactive. Tests were difficult but curved so the bar wasn't super high. Homework didn't consume that much time, but you still had to focus at the very least. Would definetely take again.
Avoid this man and ENGRD 2700 at all costs if you care about enjoying your educational journey.

Make sure to join lectures, he provides hints for the exams. However, his lectures sometimes are slow and the material is difficult. Hes a chill dude, but doesn't focus enough on academics in my opinion.

Honestly surprised by the level of teaching. Absolute rubbish. He's a good guy but goes on tangents in lectures, slides are pretty much useless for exams, and is not fit to be a professor at any university - especially not at a prestigious one such as Cornell. He was shooting imaginary 3-pointers during the finals as people cried towards the end.

This class was the cause of all my stress for this semester. The homeworks were returned a month late and didn't reflect lectures. Asking questions on ed discussion led to passive-aggressive responses that can make you feel sorry for asking a question. The final and prelim were extremely difficult and the median for the final was a failing grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Pender honestly is a really cool guy; he talks to students during lecture and I personally liked the stories he told during lecture. Unfortunately the course is quite rough. The p-sets and tests are insanely above the difficulty level of lectures or what an intro stats class reasonably should teach. Tells extra credit ans during lecture.

The exams are needlessly difficult. The homework's (to start at least) are needlessly long. The lectures are uninteresting. It seemed pretty clear to me that Prof Pender doesn't care about students actually learning the material. Pender acts like he is better than everyone, and I'm sure he is, but it doesn't help to make the students feel that way.

Took ENGRD 2700 with Pender, course homework's were hard and long towards the beginning but smoothed out after fall break. Prof often gives hints of info for exams for the few students who actually come to lecture. Course was not stressful and well paced I think this prof was pretty good.

Don't take this if want to skip class. He says small facts that were the extra credit questions. Psets took me 5-15 hours, but near the end of the semester he cut it down to 2-4 problems that were very easy. He's a hilarious, smart, and kind person if you go to his OH, though they were at 9 AM on Wed/Fri. Lectures and slides were very useful.

Lectured really well, kept things interesting and relatable. Made exams really difficult but that's just how university is in general, don't know why people complain about that. Slides were pretty good, homework was fair. Would take again

I don't know if Pender used to be better, but at least now, he is the TERRIBLE. Stay away at all costs. Monotone droning lectures with tangents, no clear grading scheme, no feedback…Minutes before the final, he came into the room to brag that he expects 90% of us to fail. He also bragged about a kid crying during a final during the last lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Absolutely worst professor of my entire life. How does one make the final worth 50%+ itself and gives a final with an average of 50.? His lectures are horrible and all he cares about is his pride for beating Stephen Curry in basketball. When you email him or post a question on ED, he will give u a passive aggressive message. Dont take this class.

He is genuinely the worst professor i have ever had. He does not care about teaching or students and that is apparent with never telling when a homework will be released, not given a single rubric or test returned. and above that, he will not answer questions or emails without snarky replys. do not take this class.
