Homeworks and exams are barely related to whats covered in lectures, homework can take up to a month to be graded with no feedback, and don't ask him any questions unless you want a snarky answer. Pender does not care about his students actually learning material and seems to enjoy watching his students suffer with unreasonably difficult exams.

His lectures consist of ppts that barely cover anything and in class he spends most of his time going off on non-stats side tangents. His tests are exponentially more difficult than the hw and the ppts, and do not align at all with the practice tests given. My best advice is to not take this class and if you need to, just take notes at home

Going to his lectures is like digging for diamonds in the nether. Asking a question on ed feels illegal, as if  you might overstep his boundaries. No amount of money could convince me to ever take this class again, or any under his professorship and I never want to see his face again. I hope that the other side of his pillow stays warm tonight.

Jamol Pender is a terrible teacher, you learn nothing and the tests are nothing like the material. This class and him specifically are notorious for being one of the worst Cornell Engineering class they have. 

I have to take this because i have no other choice, spare yourself

I genuinely don't understand why he became a professor, he doesn't like helping students understand the material in class or online. On Ed Discussion he answers every question with "answered this already in lecture" or some sh*t, but then the lectures themselves are fundamentally unhelpful and are more philosophical than equation/proof based.

I would rather walk on nails than take this class again. I would rather be dragged by a car driving at 400MPH over gravel than take this class again. I would rather have each individual hair plucked out of my head than take this class again. Don't do it. Trust.

Actually the worst class I've ever taken. The tests are extremely difficult and weighed way too much. He is so unhelpful and flat out rude to students on ed discussion and seems like he doesn't care about his students' wellbeing or concerns at all. Do not take this class if you want to live/have a decent GPA.
You need to put in consistent work to do well, but the effort is worth it because you gain foundational knowledge. Prof. Pender is one of my favorite professors despite the difficult tests.

The class was 75% tests (1 prelim and 1 final)
I got a 60% on the prelim, a 45% on the final, and a 100% on homework/group project, and ended the semester with a B. I understand nothing about statistics and am still unsure what the goal of the course was.
Poorly designed class with questionable exams. Bad lecturer as well making it tough to sit through 75 minutes of his slides.
Easy Class
He's an amazing loveable guy, but can't teach the material properly, I got an A+ and do not know anything in the class. Formula sheets come in CLUTCH though

Prof. Pender is in ORIE, Is a queuing theorist, loves probability and sports, and claims to have a three point percentage higher than Steph Curry. Pender is a character and a lot of the hate he gets are people that just need to step up their game.  This class isn't that hard and you can coast and get a good grade if you have any brain cells.
Awful lecturer that makes stats and prob way harder than they're supposed to be. Course material and exams are not related at all.
Very clearly does not care about the students or their success in the course.  Acts like he is being forced to be there and if you can't get the incredibly difficult questions than too bad

While the lectures were boring, the worst part by far was no schedule at all for when the next homework would be released.  Basically, you would submit the current one and then hold your breath until the next one came out one, two, or even sometimes three days later.  It was completely random, inconvenient, and inconsiderate of students' schedules

Honestly, this is the worst professor I have ever had. The lectures are vague and rarely help you on the actual homework he gives so you have to teach yourself how to do the problems. Additionally, I have never seen such cold and heartless responses to students' questions and it discourages me to get help on my work.
Not good at all, expect to put more work than what is necessary for an entry level stats class
Doesn't really have any regard for student interests and makes the problem sets hard and lengthy with short time to do it.
Homeworks take a while to complete. Exams are all cumulative, even though there is so much material.

Pender definitely makes this class harder than it needs to be.  His lectures are not good so expect to teach yourself from the textbook.  The problem sets are needlessly challenging considering he doesn't teach well.  On the bright side, the class complained about it and he did make some revisions to the course mid-semester.
Long psets with little information to be learned

For a three credit class, it has ridiculously long problems sets due every week, and a both a final exam and a final project. Professor Pender is a pretty good lecturer, but between the amount of work and time required, and the fact that his ed responses read like they come from a magic 8 ball, I can't say I enjoyed the class.
I'd rather take 2800 and algo all over again then have to suffer this class. I wake up with nightmares of its 10pg psets I have to finish every week. help.
AVOID AT ALL COSTS. The absolute worst. 10+ pages of PSETs every week. And a final project. +Midterm +Final. Take this if you want to make ur life miserable and learn nothing.

For a tough semester, Professor Pender was surprisingly understanding of individual circumstances. However, he is still strict on the leniency he doles out so I would not take advantage too much. Grading, tests, and assignments were very clearly laid out in the syllabus and I appreciate that there were no surprises in the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: A genuinely cruel and cold-hearted person. What type of soulless person gives a 24 hour take home final exam that is designed to take the entire 24 hours during a pandemic? A semester long root canal would be preferable to taking this course. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I only took this class because it worked for one of my requirements but I ended up loving this class so much. Professor Pender is really passionate about what he does and he genuinely cares about teaching this class. The class is not hard at all if you do everything he asks which again, is not much. Just pay attention to lectures and do the hw. <3
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Pender is a great professor. Engages with students outside of class, incorporates fun examples into lecture. ORIE 4130 - content was difficult, but he made it very tangible and was not a harsh grader. Genuinely feel like I learned in that class. Wish I had taken a pender class sooner.

Jamol is an engaging professor who expects an honest effort from every student. He is very intelligent, but is patient with students who take longer to understand difficult concepts. While he challenges students, his class made me want to put in a lot of effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Dai emphasizes intuitive understanding of the material and you can see the reflected in his teaching style and exam questions.
My favorite professor at Cornell! Professor Dai really cares about students and gives amazing lectures.
Professor Dai really cares about students and his lectures are extremely clear. The assignments are sometimes difficult but all the TAs are super helpful.
Prof. Dai is one of the best professors during my college life.

The worst professor I have ever experienced in my life. The class was very disorganized and communication with Professor Dai and the course staff was difficult. This made it very confusing to know what I was expected to do. Also, he was pretty difficult to understand and rarely took questions in class. Avoid taking any class with him at all costs.

Impossible to understand what he's saying at first but it gets better over time. Cares about students even if it doesn't seem like it during lecture. Prof Dai really wants everyone to understand the material and will do his best during lecture to clear up any misconceptions if you ask questions.
Cannot understand anything he is trying to explain ever. Not great learning experience
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: His lectures builds on course materials extermely well. Don't miss out his lectures so that you get to know all the examples and his wisdom about life.
Best history professor at nyush, he basically knows everything
Best history class I've ever had

Well, he told us he used to be harsh but now he's old and all he wants is a group of students listening to him talking about history and his life. He's teaching style is like ask-me-anything-in-class-because-I-literally-know-anything-about-history. Great professor, strongly recommended.

I would definitely recommend his class, but it's a lot of reading. His lectures are helpful and interesting, especially when he includes relevant personal experiences.  However, he doesn't discuss most of the material covered in the readings, so you can't rely on only his lectures.

I really enjoy his lectures, although he goes off topic sometimes. He is truly intelligent and knows a lot in his field. A lot of reading, but as long as you listen to his lectures you're fine. Reading quizes are not hard.

Thought his lectures were very interesting! He's a great teacher and I enjoyed his class very much. The in class quizzes and tests weren't that hard. You don't really have to do the reading if you pay attention in class.

Lectures are long and ambiguous. Prof. Chen goes on random tangents for a good portion of the class before he even mentions something that relates to the reading. You learn more from the reading than from his lecture. Lecture are intended to guide you but his lectures lag far behind the reading and rarely say anything of substance about the history

Prof. Chen is extremely knowledgeable. I only fully read the two books he wrote, and I suffered a bit on the final take-home essay. Overall, he assigned relevant reading and was an engaging lecturers. Even if he repeats himself - it's interesting and helps you remember.

you probably don't have to go to class, because he assigns an astronomical amount of reading. if you do the readings (especially the 2 he wrote- he repeats himself SOOO MUCH in them) you can pass the class. reading quizzes are REALLY general and broad- you dont have to memorize any dates. gives 5 extra credit opportunities. good class.

Professor Chen is the man. Intense lecturer, lots and lots of reading, and not particularly easy. But he's a great guy, interesting to listen to, and very, very bright. I knew nothing about China and didn't even care that much and he made it a rewarding experience. I had to work my butt off to do well, but it was worth it. Great professor.

I think this is a guy who will become a "must take" prof at Cornell.  However, only take him once.  He repeats himself every semester.  Also, express (even if feigned) interest in China.  If you know anything about China, or just ask him questions about China, he will give you a way better grade.

Waaaaaay too China centered for a class on East Asia (which includes Japan)... well, in all fairness the first half of the century according to Chen can be summed up as "China Good, Japan Bad". Lectures are intense (to say the least) and he does assign way too much reading. Not an easy class but quite enjoyable.

Chen is very knowledgeable about the subject, a true expert.  He assigns far too much reading, but other than that the requirements are not too bad.  His presentation of the material can be confusing at times as his lectures get a bit disorganized.
Obviously a very passionate lecturer. I do not dislike him, although he can make some really cruel comments when grading papers.

Professor Tantillo is a great lecturer who covers interesting topics and subjects. He always has a ton of energy, which brightens our mornings. He is also very hilarious and gracious. Definitely recommend taking his class!

he's a charismatic lecturer & knows his stuff, but this class is odee for a 2000-level humanities class. hard to keep up w/ numerous readings. midterm/final involve multiple in-class essays that could be on an obscure topic (worth 33% of grade each). he never posts lecture slides online, so you better be in lecture, or else you might get screwed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Tantillo is such an awesome dude, really cares about his students. His class is very heavy on reading with up to 100 pages/week sometimes. But it isn't really mandatory, but HIGHLY recommended. He has a midterm and final which are on the topics of the course and you really can answer the questions however you feel necessary. Great teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I started this class pretty nervous because of Professor Tantillo's reputation of giving a lot of readings and grading so few assignments. All of that is true, but like others say, you can get away with skimming a lot of it. The lectures are pretty interesting and I left the class having learned a lot. I would recommend him
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Worst professor I have ever had the misfortune of having at Cornell. His "lectures" (I use that term very loosely) are very disorganized and consist of him basically rambling random quotes. Course reading is HEAVY, easily over 100 pgs/wk for most of the semester. Take-home midterm (avg 25-30pgs), term paper, nightmare in-class final. Stay away!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: don't take this class. this guy is the worst.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Tantillo was one of the worst professors I have ever had at Cornell. In lecture, he does NOT use powerpoints and simply just talks at the class, goes on random rants and reads quotes from books. Outside reading is VERY heavy. Despite telling you to "skim," he expects you to know tiny details on the essay final exam and take-home midterm. AVOID!!!
Enjoyable, great depth of knowledge

Dr Tantillo is knowledgable in his field and a good lecturer. Ntres 3320 is heavy in philosophy and lighter in environmentalism, however there is both. His lectures are really just him talking but he emphasizes important things that are reiterated in readings and discussion. Not the easiest class, but I didn't read much and still got a B+

Tantillo is absolutely my all time favorite professor at cornell.  he is completely brilliant and knowledgeable.  be warned, however, that he expects his students to participate and know the material.
The most hysterical man. Had him for summer college and we still act like best friends.

Very smart and humble. He is extremely well-read and knows what he is talking about. He is an excellent speaker, and he won't tell you this, but he is often invited to speak at colleges/events about aesthetics/hunting. A very hard class, but manageable if you are a fast reader. I read a lot of books that every college student should read.

Unquestionably, Tantillo is a great speaker and an interesting person. Sadly, his teaching skills are extremely lacking, and his expectations greatly outweigh the quality of his lectures and efforts (his TA grades everything!). The readings he assigns are difficult to keep up with, assigning a 400 page book for two weeks. I would not this class!!

One of the hardest classes I've taken. The reading is rather impossible, by his own admission. First reading assignment is on how to skim. Books run from "sublime" (Cronon!) to idiotic. Lectures poorly attended. Has own agenda, have of which you'll agree with. Final exam is graded easily but truly a nightmarish encompassing of all reading.

He is a very smart guy.  His speech is so eloquent that he is fascinating to listen to.  I really enjoyed the class before the midterm because we were reading one book at a rate of about 40 pgs. per week.  The book was by Kagan and was interesting.  After the midterm, he started to assign a new book to read every week- almost impossible to keep up.

He is a charismatic lecturer, but irresponsible.  BEWARE! The readings are so numerous and tilted towards his own viewpoint that it becomes difficult to recognize his agenda.  He attacks certain environmental movements and writers without ever examining them.  He's easy to like, but actually listen to what he says and attack him on it.
the class seemed interesting at first, but the amount of reading and the lack of discussion about what we read made it impossible to enjoy

Wow, this guy has to be one of best lecturers. He knows his material and is eloquent. The drawback...too much reading! Be prepared to stay on track or forever be behind for the semester. Best advice, take his class s/u... Definitely worth going to class and not much effort required
Very appreciative of creative thought.No boundaries teaching.Bring something of your own to the table:he'll slice it,dice it,put it on a platter,and mark it with a "B".

Wow, can this guy talk. He's a very good lecturer and will keep your attention. Very demanding course though. Lots of reading. Exams are tough to study for because of so much information that is valid for each exam. Just hope you are lucky...
Jim is extremely knowledgable. He's down to earth and fun. I learned alot from this class.
I enjoyed Tantillo's class immensely.  Although it was a lot of reading, it was very much worth it, and he made you want to come to lecture.
Jim is an awesome person and teacher. he was extremely helpful and his class was interesting, but a bit of work. i recommend taking a class with him, and getting to know him as a person.
He is extremely well-read and I like the course

Prof. Sullivan teaches a very interesting subject that he clearly cares a lot about. He is very strict on things like attendance, calling people out for leaving the lecture hall or sitting in the wrong place, which caught me off guard during lecture. The class is very easy, tests based mostly on memorization (use quizlet).
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall a very easy A just look at the study guide questions. The lectures are kinda boring and attendance is mandatory. The discussion TA was easy on grading the presentation too (there's only 1 presentation to do and its not much work).
genuinely so boring during lecture

Professor Sullivan is very helpful during office hours, and the review sheets are very similar to all three prelims. He was very knowledgeable about everything covered, and you could tell how passionate he was. This class was very lecture-heavy, and the discussion part was also very engaging. I could not recommend this class more.

Very easy class. Prelim questions exactly same as the study guide. But lecture lacks structure and feels like yapping. Would be fine without attending lectures at all but attendance is mandatory with only 3 absences allowed.

Professor Sullivan is beyond knowledgable in his field and really cares about his students. Though this class is very reading heavy, every reading is meaningful and value to this class and the outside world. The exams are very fair and he prepares you very well. As long as you do the study guide you will succeed. I highly recommend Prof. Sullivan

Prof Sullivan is the best professor I have had so far during my time at Cornell. He is so knowledgeable and an expert on sociology. He encourages his students to think with a sociological perspective and apply all these extraordinary ideas/frameworks to society. I knew nothing about sociology before Cornell, but it has become my favorite subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: If you want an easy class, take this in the fall semester. I enjoyed most of the readings, but it got boring near the end. Tests are mostly memorization and completing his study guides are enough to get a good grade. Essays and the class itself don't require much thinking, you just need to follow his guidelines. TAs are helpful and quick to respond
I LOVED THIS CLASS. he doesn't deserve the low rating. This class is an easy A+ if you put in the effort. Tons of bonus points on the exam. Discussions were interesting and entertaining.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Sullivan was a very good teacher. In SOC1101, he definitely designs the class for first semester college students. Occasionally the lectures were a bit dry, but overall I would say they were pretty informative and interesting. There is a lot of reading, but it is manageable. He encourages students to engage with the material as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took SOC1101, he was fantastic. Take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Easy class but requires no thought, very disappointing.
One of the worst courses I have ever taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: SUPER interesting course material, and a caring professor, but I didn't like how the class was structured. He basically spends classes recapping the readings, and I disliked the format of the papers too as they're also basically recaps of the readings. The structure of the readings was really good and again, really interesting, but class was eh

Prof Sullivan is a really great Professor: one of my favorites at Cornell! His class "High Tech Regions in Comparative Perspectives" was one of the most interesting courses I have taken, and I genuinely learned so much about a topic I knew nothing about. He really cares about his students and about the material he teaches. I would really recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: I have no qualms against his manner– he's kind and enthusiastic. The grading is bad though. You will be thrown off the deep end only for expectations to be clearly communicated after you receive a poor grade. The final project is simply too much work. Take this class Pass/fail if you don't want to be worried
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super class that changed how I think about the education system and my role in it. Sipple prioritizes flexibility over rigid criteria, which makes feedback scattered. Inspiring lecturer - access him during office hours for most value-add. Best for people who prioritize learning and are willing to stretch themselves. Challenging but rewarding!

Professor prioritizes use of his “course language” (overly dense academic vocabulary) over substance. Most assignments receive no feedback, as only a few are randomly graded; any received feedback is minimal. The course is largely historical, with little quantitative work or modern policy analysis.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Entirely changed my view of the education system, but the class itself was SO poorly run. A lot of the grading is not properly communicated (believe grade cutoffs were changed at the end of the semester), and overall support for this class was not great. I really wish this class was more accessible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Great professor. Very caring. Meet with him in office hours and go the extra mile. Scattered at times but if you show him you care about the content you will do well. Lots of weekly homework but I found all the content interesting. Prob wouldn't have been worth the trouble if this wasn't my major/interest, but honestly still think it's worth it.

Really cares and knows his stuff. The workload is heavy but manageable if you keep up. Fair prelims, open-note and long paper due at the end, but you have all semester to work on it. Wants students to succeed, but values participation a lot. Great TA's.

I love-hated this course. Sipple and his lectures were really engaging, and the readings were fine, but that was ruined by the weekly reading responses. They were unnecessarily stressful and overbearing (please do a normal discussion post!). Final was OK, and I thoroughly enjoyed the big project we did. Overall: good professor, frustrating course.

Professor Sipple can be a bit scattered at times, but he was always super attentive and went out of his way to show he cared about his students. He was easily accessible outside of class and even held extra office hours before big projects. Instructions were sometimes vague however, it's because he did not want to restrict/limit exploration.

Professor Sipple is incredibly knowledgable about his course material. Almost too knowledgeable, as he talks on and on without stopping sometimes. He's very expressive as well, and he clearly cares about his students.

Very good professor. The class starts out a little slow, but gets really good. Lots of reading, and you really should do it. You should also go to lecture, but discussion section is not as necessary (but still pretty good). Annotations are quiet annoying, but the class is still worth it.

Even before the pandemic, the instruction team was woefully disorganized and expectations regarding numerous aspects of the course remained muddled throughout. Lectures were sometimes engaging, but more often than not overly preachy and scattered. Weekly annotations touted as useful for the final exam proved to be little more than busy work.

Professor Sipple is a very knowledgeable professor who enjoys what he does. There is a lot of work expected but it shouldnt be an issue as long as you keep up with the readings and engage in the discussions/lectures. The class is tough but rewarding, providing students with the knowledge of how politics, social issues, and education intertwine.

Sipple is very knowledgeable and respected in his field but beware that he is very unorganized, hard to reach outside of class, and his lectures are convoluted and ramble-y. The workload is heavy so except to spend a lot of time on this class outside of lecture. Lastly, his undergrad TA's can have a superiority complex and be overbearing at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dont take this class if its not required. The class discussion are lectures with little opportunity to truly discuss. The amount of work required with stringent yet unclear guidelines paired with Sipples disorganization and overzealous undergraduate TA's means your grade is dependent on your ability to self-motivate and go the extra mile.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Sipple is a great professor; knowledgable and unbiased. The course makes students think and tries to get you to view education outside the box. But he is unorganized; he often misses his own OH without telling students and forgets student meetings. Great professor, just needs more organization.

BEWARE: Hands down the worst professor I have had in college. I came into the class wanting to be an education major, but he singlehandedly changed my mind. He made material that should have been fascinating deadly dull, assigned ridiculously pointless weekly assignments, and was impossible to get in touch with.

Really interesting class. I usually don't enjoy reading for classes (who does?) but the assigned readings are interesting and captivating. Fun professor, and his TA's are awesome. Pre-class question every day so attendance counts. Lectures are long but he keeps them interesting. All quizzes are online, out of class (woot woot!)

This class is easy but a lot of (not difficult) work. I had heard great things and it didn't live up. Sipple is not very clear on expectations and undergrad TAs are a big part of the course. It's a fine class for people who aren't used to policy/social sciences classes but any history, gov, sociology majors will be disappointed at how basic it is.
Takes a montessori schooling method to a stats course. Useless.

If you're looking for an easy class, don't take this one. If you're looking for one of the most interesting classes from one of the best teachers you'll ever have, this is your class. You will WORK your butt off with tons of readings and annotations to write each week, but you will walk away learning from the best teacher you will ever have.
It was a lot of work but very rewarding and the quizzes/final weren't graded too harshly.

Really enjoyed the course.ALOT OF WORK!! A lot of readings and papers however if you are able to grasp the main idea of the course it can alot of things into perspective.Enjoyed the teacher,class and readings.Make sure you keep up with the work from the beginning its difficult to do 5 sets of annotationa over thanksgiving break.

This professor is a very nice and knowledgeable man.  However, he seems to forget that the students in his 271 class are undergraduates who DO take other classes at Cornell.  Very interesting subject matter is discussed, but whatever enjoyment could be taken out of the class is lost in the exorbitant work load.  Good class to sit in on but thats it
Although the man is very nice the amount of work required does not match the credits for the course. This class had the potential to be my favorite but the work has made me loathe it.

Sipple gives way too much reading and expects you to master an enormous amount of dense sociological material. It was too boring for me, which sucks because it had the potential to be an interesting course. He is a very nice guy though.
My favorite professor in my 3.5 years here. He's absolutely amazing!
Jon is a good guy, super wacky, but class wasn't bad. He talks a lot during class, which can be distracting, but as long as you come to class and do the work, you will be fine.

He's an interesting professor and classes are chill. But after class there's lots of work, long essays and making our own comics. He also only gives out a few As and more Bs for each work. Good thing is that I think his comment every time is pretty accurate and helpful. Thus I won't take this class next time but he is a good person.
He literally never told me what I got on certain things and just made up grades... Everything he does is only decided by whether or not he likes you lmao. terrible.

Like the above rating said, the info comics class is not helpful at all for academic writing. He had us write research papers for literally anything yet provides not enough guidance. It's all about philosophical stuff.

Means well but lectures degrade into conceptual nonsense. FWS is very philosophy heavy and class is not based on traditional graphic novels but on informational graphic novels. It is hard to decipher what he wants in class at first, but become clear that you have to roll with his opinions. If you want an easy or interesting FWS this is not it.
Very poor teaching and unclear instructions. Super boring contents.

As a tenured professor, it is clear that she no longer enjoys teaching. No devices in class, frequent reprimanding of the entire class for individual's mistakes. Her lectures are extremely boring and slow-paced. Do not take this class if you do not have to. It may be easy, but it comes at the cost of extreme disrespect to your time.

Professor Rickard tends to go on lecture tangents that are unrelated to class and not particularly interesting. All presented ideas seem partially unfinished or unclear. The prompts for papers and vague and the grading criteria similarly vague.

The professor was very knowledgeable and the lectures were generally interesting. However, the course structure could sometimes be disorganized and instructions for assignments were unclear. What you get out of the course is what you put in.
The content was interesting and discussions definitely helped make the ideas cohesive.  Pretty straightforward to get a good grade.

As someone who was not really interested in visual studies, this course helped me to gain a true appreciation for things that I otherwise take for granted. I'm not sure if any of my other classes have influenced me in this way yet. Overall, I learned a lot!!

The class was disorganized and the professor would ramble about unrelated topics during lectures. The readings and content were fascinating, but never related to what we discussed in the lecture. Very easy A, though.

This is one of the best classes that I've taken thus far! My eyes were opened in lecture. Usually profs just make us learn on our own, but prof. Rickard actually teaches the content. I would enroll in another class taught by her in a heartbeat!
The class felt unorganized. She rambled on during lecture about nothing specific, and gave vague assignments. Disappointing class.
Life-changing course! If you put the work into the course, you will reap the benefits.

This class really opened my eyes to an amazing area of art. Professor Rickard is very knowledgable about so many issues outside of art that entered cultural studies because of her. You would be lucky to take a class with her!

I found the class to be very informative even though it was a lot of work. Professor Rickard is very knowledgable on the theory behind Native issues, but students without any background knowledge (attended American schools) may have found the class difficult to grasp. And in reality she was a fair grader, hard word was rewarded.

Jolene took time out of her insanely busy schedule as interim director of the Arts dept to work with me on an independent study project on settler colonialism, imaging & resistance. I found her to be, in contrast with most of these comments, a dynamic & challenging teacher who genuinely cares for students-their development but also well-being.

I learned absolutely nothing in this class and feel asleep everyday for at least 30 mins. Prof. Rickard is REALLY boring and talks in the most uncomprehensible roundabout way. Also, she is a harsh grader for no reason. The assignments were stupid, not hard.

This class was horrible!! She didn't follow the syllabus at all and assigned random papers with no prompts. It took her several weeks to return anything graded, and her grading system was very ambiguous. Impossible for her to stay on topic and lectures felt like they lasted foreverrr. DO NOT take this class if you can avoid it!!

Tobin's class is the most unorganized class I've ever attended. His assignments have no rubric or direction whatosever, he encourages and grades participation but never lets students get a word in, and TA Rostad is a super harsh grader and grades entirely on subjectivity. Its such a shame since this subject area really interested me - def avoid!!!

Overall, the class was fine and structured well. However, Tobin's lectures were unorganized and very difficult to sit through. Entire classes were set aside for "group discussions," but it was nearly impossible to get a word in since he took up the whole time with lecturing.

Strange class. Probably unnecessary. Covers basics of finance, very little on sustainability. Papers graded harshly by TA Branham, who is very nitpicky and does not offer constructive feedback. Final group project to develop financial instrument highly dependent on assigned group, some of which are carried by MBAs while others don't even have MBAs
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Tobin really knows his stuff and has an incredible resume. Engaging lecture and highly recommend if interested in sustainable business. However, grades are dependent on papers with weak prompts and TA Branham's awful arbitrary grading criteria . Likely less writing intensive than AEM2055, the writing in the majors course, but still writing heavy.

The most boring class ever... class is all about sustainable investing, but the homework reflects nothing we learned in class. It is basically a writing class, with all of the grades reflected through "the number of typos" and "clarify in your argument", without actually commenting on the argument. The TAs were so bad, no reply or grading comment

Weirdest class at Dyson ever... they have a very weird QR code attendance policy. With that said, the class was the most boring class ever, with a professor sharing experiences in an investment bank that is already bankrupt, and continuing to share those knowledge as if nothing happened to the bank.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professors Tobin and Sudip are exceptional, offering great content with genuine care for students. Both have impressive backgrounds as Managing Directors at Credit Suisse. However, the TA, Branham Culpepper, was the worst TA ever. The TA falls short in support, grading and clarity, often cancelling office hours and struggling with tech assistance.

Does truly know what he's talking about... cool, but you'll never get a word in unless you REALLY make an effort. Has snapped at students before. 4 papers every 3 weeks graded by TAs that lead weekly discussion sections. Get your stuff in on time and it's no problem.

Knows A LOT about his subject area; excellent resource for career advice. LOTS of diverse case studies and articles to read to prepare for lecture. Hard to make appointments with because he's really busy with his other job as an administrator; but if you talk with him about setting up a meeting, especially if it's class-related, he'll make it happe
THE best prof and class I've taken at Cornell. His lectures are interesting and he prioritizes our learning rather than a strict grading criteria. Would take every class he teaches, highly recommend.

Managing Talent ILRHR 2600 was the easiest class ever. 3 quizzes, some short assignments, and a very easy final. Very easy class but still interesting. JR Keller is very qualified and his lectures actually cover important and helpful content. He also brings in HR professionals from top organizations to talk to us.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: JR is by far the best professor I've had at Cornell. The only one who actually prioritzes the learning of his students rather than strict grading criteria, and is the essence of what college and college lectures should be. I couldn't recommend him more.

JR is the best professor I've had. I once went to office hours and he already knew my name (out of 100+ people). My advice would be to put in the effort to get to know him cause he is an amazing professor. Guest speakers are interesting. He always has a smile on his face. Made management and human resources really engaging. Everyone loves him!

Prof Keller is an amazing teacher who made HR such an interesting topic. This class has 3 assignments, 3 take-home quizzes, and a final assignment. Attendance is mandatory but 3 skips are allowed. The class is very enjoyable and Prof Keller is one of the best professors at Cornell.
Best Prof in ILR. Super super easy class and you learn so much. Such a good person.

Free A if you do all the work and come to class. Guest speak were very interesting and he is a great lecturer. Lots of small grades that make up the class and the writing "assignments" are all graded 100% if you do them

Prof. Keller is so nice and very knowledgeable. He is clearly passionate about what he teaches. My one pet peeve of this class was that no A+s are awarded so in a way it can drop your GPA. However, it's super easy and lots of cool information. Guest lectures provide great insight.

Super easy class. Can be a bit boring sometimes but you'll also learn some cool stuff. He's very laid back. There's almost no assignments, and the ones that exist are easy and graded leniently. Absolute king.
Super fun and energetic professor!

Professor Keller is one of the best professors here at Cornell. His HR class was extremely informative and interested. He is extremely easy to talk to and makes a genuine effort to connect with students and get to know them. This class was extremely easy and any work you had to do was largely opinion based.

nice guy, makes human resources class actually engaging and interesting. doesn't make the class harder than it should be, and I think he does a great job in teaching it. class is academically very easy, but personally rewarding.

best professor at cornell. truly one of a kind human being, so dedicated to his students, the material and makes lectures engaging and fun. 

seriously do not pass the opportunity to take his class.

Simply a wonderful human-being and teacher. So accommodating, professional yet relatable, and a fun teacher overall! I am always excited to attend his class and would recommend it to anyone -- regardless of their course of study -- to take any class he teaches. This man deserves a raise

One of my favorite professors in ILR. Keller creates engaging lectures and assignments that expand your perspective on how a business operates. He also goes out of his way to bring in interesting guest lecturers. Would recommend this class to everyone in ILR!

Amazing professor!! Really works hard to ensure there is hands on learning and that every student understands everything. Take a class with this professor, well worth your time. Will learn a ton about consulting and how to analyze a business and give a presentation.

Great lectures, great personality. Definitely a course you want to take if you're interested in consulting. Makes the class interesting, fun, and applied which is difficult considering it's a theory class. Presentation to a consulting firm at the end of the semester was an extremely valuable experience.

This is a great class. Professor Keller is extremely clear and helpful. No tests, just two case analyses and two group case presentations. Reading is honestly not required, but you should do it if you actually want to take something from the course. I highly recommend it!

Proff. Hairston is a genuinely good standard professor. He teaches exactly why you SHOULD know for the exam. It's probably not his fault that whoever writes the exams has issues with constructing a clear question. It seems like they give a group of grad students shots of tequila and then make them write the exam from memory, and then no one revises
One of the best professors I have ever come across while earning a degree. Friendly, honest, respectful, knowledgeable Great guy and made for a great experience in Limnology

Nelson is awesome- he really cares about his students and wants you to get excited about lakes! He studies zooplankton so he focuses his teaching on that but you'll learn a lot about limnology in general. Take the lab if you can- you'll learn applicable skills and Nelson teaches the labs himself- not just a TA. One of my favorite professors!
Very nice, clear instructor. Interesting and kind. I wish he had taught more of my class!
Great professor, one of my favorites at Cornell.  Nelson speaks very clearly and the way he taught the class allows you to follow the material very well and stay engaged.  Lakes are awesome!
Nelson is a great prof and a nice guy. He really really knows his stuff about lakes and makes the subject extremely interesting.
So sassy and unforgiving. If this isnt requirement, DONT TAKE THIS CLASS. Lab reports were the worst part of my days, weeks, months, and overall life. You have been warned.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: makes the chem lab rubrics and makes sure TAs don't give student points or any leeway. lab grade is dragging down my grade.

Currently taking 3570. She doesn't go by the textbook order unlike every other professor and just jumps around, so the support class is unhelpful. She denies every regrade request and doesn't post any notes. How is it possible that the prelim 1 avg is a 67% when the past semesters the averages have been around 90.
actually insane. There's no way

Hardest part about 2070. No rubrics provided, so students are left guessing about what info they need to include in lab reports. Harsh grading and regrade requests are often denied without proper reasoning. Grading is inconsistent between TAs, so just hope you get lucky. Instructions are not explicit and even one bad lab is hard to recover from.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There is no rubric for lab reports and they are graded strictly. The regrade system has many holes that bar students from receiving the points they actually made on assignments. The lab section is the hardest part of the class, and the one you're least able to progress in due to the set up of the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Impossible to do well

She makes the lab reports difficult because we are not allowed to see a rubric, and her grading is very inconsistent. She grades super strictly and somehow expects you to read her mind. Also, if too many students submit regrade requests, she will go into lecture and yells at everyone. She genuinely prays on every student's downfall.
Don't take a class with her

She is the lab director for General Chemistry. The TAs for CHEM 2071 are expected to deduct a set number of points (with quotas), and students have been discouraged from requesting regrades. Rubrics are not provided before lab reports are due and are instead created afterward, with TAs instructed to grade very harshly. Nice person, however.

She makes it unnecessarily difficult to do well on labs by changing the grading rubric each time and taking off points for the smallest things. She expects students to read her mind and know exactly what to include in lab reports (e.g. which outside sources to cite in the introduction). This course was honestly more difficult than CHEM 2070 lecture

Does not provide rubric for labs to students or TAs, so there is no way to improve performance. Grades on things never mentioned before, then tells students not to submit regrades. Leaves comments on reports that is not constructive, but critical and unsupportive.

Does not respond to emails and will not release rubrics so students are left guessing what they did right and what they should keep on doing for following labs. Lab TA's are don't have them either and are left confused with grading as they also don't know rubrics till after we submit. Graded on things that were never asked of us in instructions.
lab instructor who did anything to ensure you didn't succeed.
I enjoyed his lectures and passion for the subject, but it's actually one of the hardest classes I've ever taken. Please don't take this bio class, for your own health.
Just don't take this class. I struggled dearly

This is a bad course. Exams are unnecessarily difficult and graded in an extremely rigid way ,Communication is poor. Emails go unanswered, questions are discouraged, and the instructor often comes across as unapproachable. Grading mistakes were frequent and added even more stress. Honestly, if you can avoid this class. Just take BIOEE 1440 instead.

He went through lecture material quite quickly, and sometimes refused to take questions. Sometimes he came off as rude when talking to students. The test questions are very specific and are made to trick you with wording. Attending lectures is important to understand what he will test on.
Lots of ambiguity in test questions as well as unreasonable amounts of specificity. Quite a rude person as well.

Avoid St. Juliana and 1610 at all costs. St. Juliana's class is hands down the most tedious class that I have ever taken in my life. He runs through lecture content super fast, rarely takes questions, and writes exams and quizzes that demand SPECIFIC answers to POORLY WRITTEN trick questions. I would not recommend St. Juliana's class to anyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I loved the class content, and both Sparks and St. Juliana were great instructors. However, the tests were extremely difficult and felt subjective. Despite studying a lot, many questions had multiple valid answers, yet only one was accepted as “best,” which made grading feel unfair. He used the phrase "what is the BEST answer" in his questions.
Tests are hard for no reason, st juliana is a bad professor, moves way too fast and puts questions on the test that we didnt learn at all in lecture.

His questions are really ambiguous, and two answers could be correct, but the answer has to be the one he believes in more. It's very subjective, and even the TAs hate his questions. He's also quite rude when someone asks questions. Do not recommend.

One of the worst professors I've ever had. Lectures are fast-paced and you're expected to review slides outside of lecture as there isn't enough time to take notes. Tests are absurdly difficult, questions are written to trick you so you get the wrong answer. Stubborn & rude, blames class for low average below a 60, rather than his teaching ability.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: St. Juliana was probably one of the worst professors I've ever had. Half of the questions on the midterm were impossible trick questions that actively tried to get you to choose the wrong answer. He was also generally incredibly rude outside of lecture, and seemed annoyed whenever I asked him a question despite the fact that answering is his job.

His lectures were pretty clear but always fast-paced and hard to keep up. There was an expectation to review the slides after lecture because there wasn't enough time to understand/take notes during class. The lectures were split between two professors and I always enjoyed the other lecturer more. That being said, I did enjoy the course material.

I took this class as a requirement for my major, and had so much hope for this class because it is what I want to pursue as a career. However this class was much harder than you would expect and pay super close attention in lectures because he will ask the smallest little detail on the prelims...

Fall 23' - Lectures aren't bad but are fast-paced. He sticks to his grading policy and particular answers for prelims. If you want a practice test, he will NOT give you one. It would be helpful for the class, but he does not provide any information on past exams. I took the class for credit, but I would not take it again.

Pretty good prof. Is engaging in lectures, but moves a bit fast, and is not the clearest. His prelim question are bs and are often subjective, and he can be a bit stubborn about it. Prelims really do comedown just to how good of a guesser you are, and not how well you know the content. It is what it is.
Amazing Professor! Slides were very clear, and she had an amazing way of relaying information. Put in effort and you'll be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She has a lot on the lecture slides and expects everyone to be familiar with what's on the slide and in the readings. The hardest part is that she doesn't make it clear what will realistically come up again in the course; best piece of advice is go to office hours as she tends to be a lot more clear there.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Modica genuinely cares about you and the class isn't an easy A, but you will learn a lot about labor history; she's a kind and knowledgeable woman so you should get to know her and go to office hours. The final is difficult, but she did her best to alleviate stress around it/ accomodate us.

regularly asks for student feedback and is willing to reduce certain required readings (however the readings were still excessive), weekly reading checks, had a couple easy grade booster assignments, professor is very knowledgeable, final is very difficult
Simply amazing!
She knows her stuff, exams are tough, and she cares a lot. She's super pretty, so it's a bonus if u get bored with the lecture. Findley the TA is the goat.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really nice person. Only a couple of assignments, 2 Exams. 30% of the class is participation. Very long readings and a very hard final exam. Class will require a lot of studying, but you will learn a ton of labor history. What I appreciate most about Dr. Modica is that she's open to change in how she formats readings, assignments, and exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: People are being harsh. Lectures are informative, she's very passionate about the course/her students. Definitely a difficult course but also the readings can be easily skimmed, and the writing assignments like Kheel Center/Film review are interesting/grade boosters. TA is super chill. Final seems really difficult though, may change in future.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Modica is genuinely kind and energetic. However, she is an impossible professor to have. She is obviously an expert in her field, but I think she carries a mindset that her students are equally expert, assigning 200+ pages of reading at times. Her Final Exam is essentially impossible unless you study 12+ hours/day. TA Findley is very cool tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Just really made the class a lot more difficult then it should have been

Modica is a fantastic person, but has unrealistic expectations of students. You were expected to read 200+ pages, review 80+ slides (each slide was a block of text), and complete a reading assessment each week. Her grading metrics were unclear. Super kind and understanding of her students, but her definition of "light" work is 200 pages vs. 250.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Peraino showed not just a clear understanding for the music, but a deep care for it as well. She had seen the artists she presented perform live, written about them, and was truly excited to show us their music. The way the content tied into the theory behind it made this my favorite class ive taken at cornell. Mad props to Peraino.
Great professor, interesting class. Would absolulely recommend if you enjoy rock music, just make sure to thoroughly study for tests (is a fair amount of memorization, but is fun)

Really enjoyed this class! If you have no interest in music, then this class prob isn't for you; but if you have an interest in music, pay attention in lectures, and put effort into your papers, you do decent. Think people are misled to think it's a "no-effort A" - there's a fair bit work, but if you put in some effort, you should do well.

Worst professor I've ever had. Incredibly disrespectful, ignorant, and arrogant. Teaches material through a single lens and downright refuses (or maybe even doesn't know how) to try to look at material from a different perspective. Wants you to fit in a box. Overall, I'm disappointed in her.
I have taken her punk class and history of rock class and it is the best thing I have done at Cornell. Take a class with her if you like history and music! Every class gets better
This was not my favorite class taken at Cornell. D-.

This was my favorite class taken at Cornell BY FAR. Even if you aren't a huge Beatles fan but enjoy their music, this class is extremely interesting and informative. I not only learned some very interesting facts about the Beatles, but I also learned a lot about history/culture of the 1960s. Dr. Peraino is a great lecturer, and the class is a must!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class is for everyone from the ultimate Beatles fangirl to anyone needing an interesting elective. Professor Peraino gives great lectures and teaches a very thorough history of The Beatles and the 60's. She sometimes brings out an electric guitar to show how The Beatles (or Rolling Stones) made their music. Peraino teaches the coolest classes.

The class was entirely discussion based.  Prof. Peraino did a great job facilitating discussions, while still allowing students to direct them.  The workload was fair.  Sometimes the reading was a lot, but the essays were fun and not terribly long.  I took the class for its first semester.  It was an unusual combination of topics, but interesting.
Awesome

Assuming you come into the course with some familiarity with rock music, all you need to do to get a good grade is review your lecture notes and copy down powerpoints from section.  You also need to memorize random song info.  Course is interesting but it gets boring when covering an artist or style you don't enjoy listening to.

Parts of the class, such as analyzing song influences that was interesting. Being able to identify specific musical elements was very difficult. For each test, required to memorize 50 song titles, authors, dates, and unique musical characteristics. Lecture-optional, section-mandatory. Take it pass/fail as senior. Not worth the headache as a grade.

Excellent class, definitely take it.  Section is required, lecture is not, but notes from each are verbatim on tests.  Very easy to do well if you go to class and take notes and memorize, but not if you blow it off.  Very interesting.  Best class I took in 4 years

fantastic professor. i took history of rock and loved it. easy and interesting. i had absolutely no musical background and didnt even like classic rock before peraino's class, but that didn't matter, and i gained an appreciation for it because of the class btw, while lecture isnt mandatory, section is and the material covered in section is separate
Super Schwet Class.
Excellent class, fun prof.  The tests were not very challenging and the material was really interesting.  Highly recommended--if you can get into the class!
She is awesome.  Great class, learned a tremendous amount, very fair tests, very clear lecturer.  Great TA's.  A lot of fun.  She is one of the authorities in the field as well.  Recommended to all.
Very helpful professor. She was always available and enjoyed teaching. Highly recommend her.
No Comments

Professor Markovits is very conscientious and considerate. 

Pros of Ethics
- Good introduction to moral philosophy
- Low-stakes familiarization with philosophical ideas
Cons
- The lecture format, rather than seminar, dulls discussion - few students pay attention
- If you've already taken some moral philosophy, this class will feel like busy work
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Markovits is an extremely caring and considerate professor who was very flexible with deadlines and extensions and was very easy to reach out to for office hours, which I highly recommend doing If you want to succeed in her class.
really nice and flexible with deadlines. lectures are super boring though
boring

Prof Markovits is a caring & considerate professor, and is genuinely interested in what she teaches. Lectures are required but quite interesting. It is easy to get helpful feedback on papers by attending office hours w/ TAs & Markovits. Not difficult to succeed in this course, biggest time investment is the three papers.

Great ability to explain concepts comprehensibly without over-simplifying. I added the class late and she was very accommodating and helpful. Class structure flows very well from one topic to the next and the total course content feels quite cohesive by the end. Taking argument-focused notes in lecture and on readings is important.

Professor Markovits is fantastic and I took another class with her after taking ethics. Her lectures are great and her grading is very fair. She has lots of opportunities to get easy credit, such as attendance/ participation and short weekly posts which are graded only on completion. She also has flexible deadlines for papers. Great professor!

Great lecturer, you have to respond to the readings before every class but she always gives a reasonable amount of reading (no more than 20 pages but usually pretty dense). She then explains the readings in class and gives you her notes on them! You basically don't have to take notes in class at all and can just think about the topic/ follow along.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Material and readings were interesting. Only thing I didn't like was the attendance/participation component.

My main complaint is she often seemed unprepared and didn't do a good job explaining the material. While doing research for a paper I came across MIT's Open Course Ware and to my surprise, the contents of her slides were lifted whole from the MIT site. Literally word for word including the typos! This explained why she so often seemed unprepared.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof. Kalas is amazing. So passionate about the material that she makes you feel passionate about it. She's open to every single comment from every student and willing to take the discussion in whatever area the students want. The papers aren't heavy, but the reading is. She's a fair grader and super accessible in office hours.

Rollercoaster of a class. Everything was disorganized from assignments to lectures. There is never a clear thread or guideline. Grading ultimately is okay, but definitely not worth the effort taking this class. Content is interesting, but it sucks because of how it is delivered. 

Also, GOOD luck carrying around a 2k page textbook 3 times a week.

Prof. Kalas is AMAZING. She gives interesting lectures, great feedback, and genuinely cares about her students. She always made time to meet with students outside of class and was very flexible with deadlines/responsive to the needs of the class. Can't recommend Prof. Kalas enough for an FWS, or any class you're lucky enough to take with her.

Your ideal FWS teacher - caring, knowledgeable, well-spoken, and engaging. There were times where some lectures could get a tad long-winded, but you won't need to listen to every word in order to succeed in the class.

Kalas is an amazing lecturer, and she really makes an effort to get to know her students. She's very passionate about the material, which makes a world of difference in a class that can get pretty dry at times. If you're worried about your grade, go and talk to her. She will help you and will likely offer extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Prof. Kalas is a great professor! She taught my FWS (Technologies of Writing). Her expectations are clear and the workload is manageable compared to other FWS's. Our in-class discussions were always productive and enormously helpful in writing papers. She is a caring and passionate professor. Her feedback on essays is enormously valuable.

Brilliant poetic analyst. She is excellent in a small, seminar-type class, not an amazing lecturer. Her critique on papers was always helpful, and she comes up with some fun creative assignments too. If many students are having trouble keeping up with readings, she will listen and adjust the schedule some to help.

Rayna is tough but fair and she grades according to your ability. If you can swallow your pride long enough to watch her eviscerate your papers you can learn more from this one woman than you can imagine. Her comments are illuminating and she really tries to understand what YOU wanted to say and help you say it better.
Eh, alright class.  My positive impressions probably flow more from the interesting subject matter though.

Kalas is a hard grader, and she destroyed any interest I had in medieval lit after taking her class-otherwise a nice woman. She only likes you if you repeat what she says. No matter how much I tried to make office hours and meet with her, she was always late. Her final exam was one of the worst English finals I'd ever taken at Cornell.

I dreaded a class on Milton; but by the time the class was done, I could honestly say it was one of the best at Cornell. Dynamic, passionate professor with a profound knowledge of both Milton and the period in which he wrote. Pretty difficult class. But definitely recommend taking it just for the professor.
If you talk in class, help with the discussions etc, she will give you an A on your paper regardless of whether it was well-written.
Kalas knows her stuff and she's a dynamic lecturer.  really hard topics but they make you think. if you get bored by a challenge then don't take her.

Definitely one of the most challenging classes I have ever taken here.  She has a great style of lecturing, although sometimes they go off too long, but for the most part, if one is as enthused in the subject matter as she, then it's all good.
Passionate about Shakespeare and nice woman, but discussions are boring, paper topics are obscure, and grading is very arbitrary. Definitely one of the hardest writing seminars in terms of work load.
Perfectly fine. Reading the textbook covers 90% of what you'll need to know for the tests. Lectures don't tend to add all that much, but can be interesting at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Wonderful!

Definitely ruined my experiences in philosophy classes. She is a very poor lecturer and could not synthesize an idea and explain it to us concretely. 
Went to office hours several times and she was either a: not there or b: makes me come across as dumb without offering advice. Do not take her classes!

I came to this class with a more-or-less pessimistic attitude toward most  ancient philosophy. Now, I find myself regularly thinking about Plato. Professor explained things in an energetic way, and for any lover of philosophy it was undoubtedly interesting. I won't comment too much on the difficulty as I have a lot of philosophy experience.
Very hard to understand, very disorganized
Amazing professor for Greek & Roman Philosophy! Easy to talk to outside of class, readings are dense but interesting, and papers are graded fairly.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Overall, she was an unnecessarily harsh grader. Even basic discussion posts are sharply critiqued, which makes it very difficult to get above a B in the class. This also makes it very hard to do well on the main essays, where the feedback was confusing but still harsh. She was a very nice professor, but she was difficult, boring, and inaccessible.

Discussion posts are graded, making it hard to get full credit. She assigns over 150 pages a week. She is very bad at responding to emails. Her lectures are very dry. The papers are graded harshly, much stricter than other philosophy classes. Definitely one of the worst philosophy classes I've taken. Such a shame, given the interesting content.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: She was just ok literally nothing special. For the final paper she did not give clear, concise or accurate feedback, that resulted in a lower grade than I should've gotten.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She really put a lot in to the class and I think that those who wanted to got a lot out of it. Of course, she's a tougher grader than the grad students who don't care but I found the class interesting and appreciated the effort she put into it. She also fairly lenient with dates -- so long as you're not consistently late.

She is probably the nicest and best prof I've had at Cornell. She is passionate and knowledgeable about the subject matter, but is also relatable and down to earth. She truly cares about her students and wants them to learn and succeed. Highly recommend this class. Exams were online and collaborative and there were only 2 assignments required.

Pretty chill and funny sometimes. Course material is actually pretty interesting. Sometimes, she wouldn't release assignment details until a week before the deadline, so things got a little disorganized. She gives the option to do the assignments in class, which has fewer requirements than the online version. All the exams were online and open-book

Love her! She is such an amazing professor who cares deeply about her students and their well-being. All concepts in her pop health class are so engaging and relevant to healthcare. She is very understanding and provides great support for students on top of very clear and doable assignments and prelims. I plan to take more of her courses!

Professor Carmalt is so sweet, and you can see she genuinely cares about the content she teaches. I liked going to class to hear her perspective, but the tests are based completely off the slides so no problem if you miss. I liked the course content, but could get repetitive at times. Super easy and interesting if you like medicine/healthcare.

I've never written a review before, but Dr. Carmalt is that amazing. She cares deeply about her students - hosted a discussion after the 24 Election, lenient extensions, very accessible outside of class. 

She speaks about healthcare in a candid way, highlighting its injustices, but also offers a positive light that is deeply inspiring.

Julie Carmalt is very kind! Grants extensions freely without you begging and she is very open to knowing her students. The flow of the course content started out strong, but it started getting confusing and disorganizing after the first topic. The projects had some unclear grading (talk to TAs), and tests were just annoying as well.

not as easy or enjoyable as made out to be in the past...lectures were eh and projects were interesting but prelims were stupid. professor is nice most of the time but not really fair in terms of grading
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She's comes across as nice, but the class has definitely changed from the past. The grading criteria on some of the projects was unfair and the incorporation of prelims was an interesting switch. Didnt really enjoy a lot of the class content either
Gave extensions without questions, lovely lady, cared for her students and their mental health. DEF RECOMMEND

I think Carmalt is one of the sweetest profs i have had! Some of her lectures were really enjoyable, and some were super boring. Full disclosure, the boring lectures def discouraged me from coming to class a little bc attendance wasn't mandatory. But overall i feel like this class is super important and pretty easy, would highly recommend taking it
Awesome lecturer. Had a few easy projects that meaningful in helping students achieve the class's learning objectives.
Just an amazing professor :)
Professor Carmalt is my all-time favorite professor at Cornell!! She is the most understanding professor and loves to keep students engaged. Workload was minimal and fun. Content was so interesting!

Just great. If you care about social justice, take her class, even if you are not interested in public health or such you will learn a lot and her clear grading criteria will for sure help u get an A. She is so sweet. Her lectures were pretty fun. It is hard to ignore her lectures because she is so charming and witty.
My favorite professor at Cornell so far! She is super inspiring and so kind. Is always there for help or just to chat. I highly recommend intro to pop health - she really makes the class amazing

Dr. Carmalt is one of the best professors I've ever encountered at Cornell. She genuinely cares that you are learning something meaningful, and this is apparent in her teaching style and lectures. I highly recommend trying to take the class in the spring if possible - it's a much smaller class and literally everyone in the class got an A+

Julie Carmalt!! As a lecturer just ok. I dropped this class and readded when the class I dropped into was horrible, and it's been fine, definitely easy to get an A, but lectures aren't super stimulating and I haven't learned that much that was new (maybe this is just better taken as a frosh or soph). As a person? Aspirational. Amazing. Adorable.
One of the best professors at this university, take her class
great teacher and so nice she loves her students. so knowledgeable about health disparities and pop health management.

Extremely Rude. She picks favorites who are all blonde or red haired and treats the others as dirt. I have numerous complaints about her attitude towards me and her snappy behavior. Not a great role model or human. But her class is good and she teaches it well.

Julie Carmalt is one of the best professors at Cornell. Full stop. This class had nothing to do with my intended career plans at the time, and it essentially changed my outlook on my future goals and the world in general. She's hilarious and truly cares about each of her students. I would take her class every semester if I could.
Dope dope dope!!! She's such a refreshing human and so inspiring ! If you do the work she'll reward you -- she wants all of her students to succeed! TAKE THIS CLASS

Only two exams, prelim 1 which is very fair and Final. She's very interesting and although the class isn't really intro, it isn't too hard. She's also a great mentor and person in general, highly suggest emailing her or meeting with her to introduce yourself! 3 or so projects, they take a while but overall good class, and not too hard.

Dr. Carmalt is incredible. Engaging and fun and just an awesome lady. The population health class is not super in depth but it's interesting and could be challenging if you wanted to make it so, but it's not hard to get an A. I highly recommend the class. and do the readings, they are great!
Enthusiastic professor. Classes are very lecture-based except a group project at the end of the semester. Grading and tests are very fair, although the final is not easy.

Hard to understand. His lectures were difficult to follow, especially for first year students. He can be helpful for one on one help. First two prelims weren't bad but final was diabolical. Discussion was helpful

It is hard to hear or understand what he is saying at times due to his accent. Lectures are mostly spent solving examples. However, his work is hard to follow, as he jumps into solving the problem without explaining his thought process. It is much easier to read the textbook. 
He may be better in higher level non-engineering math courses.

Does a great job answering questions, but his accent is difficult to understand most of the time. Lectures are spent completing long (very long) example problems, with a lot of time spent on performing tedious basic computations.

Hard take home exams that take a long time. He is a decent lecturer, but at many times will skip many steps, and it is unclear how he got the the answer. On the positive side, he is very lenient on late homeworks, and quizzes.

I'd only take a class with this guy again if I got hit with a shovel and forgot about the first time, but I learned a ton. By far hardest class I've ever taken and likely ever will take. He's super nice, very easygoing about late submissions, and wants you to succeed. He just really likes math. He may be unaware if everyone is struggling, TELL HIM.
If you can handle it definitely take this course. Very intense but worth it. All tests were long and take home. Most Ive learned in a semester by far. Bettered my math skills significantly.

He is a lecturer that only clicks with certain people. His teaching style was definitely confusing at first, but it got better. One of the hardest classes I've ever taken at Cornell, but also the most rewarding.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: exams are too hard
Had him for 4310, textbook was terrible, lectures were hard to understand, and tests were very difficult. One of the worst classes I have ever taken
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The lectures were confusing sometimes but he generally did a good job. The most accessible and easy to talk to professor I've had here. Explains things very thoroughly one-on-one.
Avoid at all costs. Worst math professor I've had at Cornell. Handwriting is illegible, prelims are nearly impossible, and does not teach the concepts well at all.
Alright professor
1. incomprehensible handwriting 2. bad pronunciation 3. not good voice 4. exam questions exceedingly difficult 5. low textbook usage. I dont think he is a bad person but he is the worst as a teacher.

Yes, yes, a nightmare of a class. But I feel really really really bad that he's so bad. He is a genius, but not in terms of teaching math. If your smart, i still recommend going to his lectures. Yes, you will have to read the book. Best thing is to go to his office hours, he does the homework for yo
Bright guy, but just can't speak english or teach math. He doesn't understand your questions, and his lectures have no structure or logic.
Very unclear, skips steps in proofs, hard to follow, in general difficult to understand.
nice man but can't teach for crap, speaks Bulgarian with English accent, speaks too fast, can't write, homeworks and exams are way too difficult, the curve is unfair, homeworks are harshly graded.

He's a nice guy, and he tries, but the lectures are very disorganized and hard to follow.  The book isn't much better.  Thankfully the TA was pretty good and managed to explain more of the things that the prof. couldn't. Don't take unless you are really prepared to teach yourself the material.

People hate on Tarantino too much. Yeah, the flipped classroom style of the class sucks, and the homework is lots of work and the grading is nitpicky, but if you ask the TAs or Tarantino for help in class, they'll pretty much give you the answers. Beware of the prelims, my grade never recovered after the first prelim, final is cake compared to them

This was my least favourite class of the semester. Most of the content is taught by videos, and we weren't even taught everything for the final MOS Excel exam. Attendance is mandatory despite the lecture having negligible content and consisting solely of completing an assignment. I would not recommend this class in any circumstance.
