Tarantino barely teaches with the excuse of using a "flipped style" and relies on videos she made so many years ago. She doesn't prepare you well for prelims and instructions are very unclear. She's also extremely strict about attendance, and after you miss 3 classes every absence after that your grade drops half a letter.

Kasey is hands-down, the most unsympathetic professor I have ever had. She enforces mandatory attendance, even if you have interviews or have to go to a funeral. Also doesn't teach in-class; instead, she has videos from 5 years ago and have students watch before class. If you have to go to the bathroom, she would give you an absence.
Make sure u study really well for prelims. She is the most unforgiving teacher

Ppl are rlly overdramatic about this class. The flipped style isn't fun & watching the vids def takes time, but if you actually take notes you will understand and it won't be hard. MOS final is super easy in comparison to the prelims. Def a lot of assignments and the project mid-way thru was stressful, but not at all as bad as people make it out.

work in this class was doable -- directions were super unclear and even when asking her/TAs, would be no help. OH did not help at all. You really have to rely on yourself for this class. Flipped style is super annoying.

Mrs Tarantino is super kind, smart, and overall a lovely person! The class, however, is disastrous. Since it's "flipped" every class is anxiety-inducing. Each class you, work on the assignment of the day. Prelims are hard, but the MOS exam at the end of the semester is easy.

For this class, she had a teaching style where she gave videos to learn the material, and then she did a short lecture in class on new (sometimes more challenging) material and then gave the rest of the time to work on the homework assignment. I enjoyed the class because it was professionally applicable and easy to handle. Grading very harshly tho.

The class isn't the most engaging, but you learn a lot of valuable skills. Most people are happy they took it. The flipped classroom isn't ideal, but you have to learn how to live with it. Exams aren't difficult if you practice. MAKE SURE YOU GO TO OFFICE HOURS FOR EXCEL! Doing well on the homework assignments is a great way to cushion your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: The videos assigned are extremely boring and redundant which makes the mandatory aspect of the class very irritating. However, she cares about her students and their well being. Watch the videos and ask questions and you should be fine.

Content is valuable, but the structure could be a lot more student-friendly. Grading is petty and inconsistent, with hidden criteria. "Nothing a TA or professor tells you is guaranteed correct". Relies heavily on pre-recorded videos, actual class time is redundant. Weird 9 P.M. deadlines. Prof's lack of enthusiasm affects learning atmosphere.

I would reccomend taking this class with Professor Whitmore. Tarantino makes her prelims very tough and provides no review or resources for her prelims. The average was below a 70% and she blamed the class on not studying hard enough. All the assignments are graded by the TAs and the rubric is always so vague and unclear. Good luck if you have her.

Not a fan of the inverse course structure HADM1740 (we learn 95% through pre-recorded videos, and in-class is just basically study hall and asking questions to TAs). Professor Tarantino barely teaches anything in person, yet attendance is mandatory. Class average for the excel midterm was lower than 60%, and instructions on prelim are unclear

Terrible prof. Doesn't teach, just has you watch her videos which are hard to listen to because she ends every sentence like it was a question. She isn't very knowledgeable in her field either. She has a hard time answering questions she doesn't expect. I could have learned more by watching somebody else's YouTube videos. Take someone else.

Such an interesting class and the professor is clearly well informed (rambles a bit too much). Only issue is she barely gives out As and doesn't give proper feedback. Super nice during office hours and overall a great teacher.

Her grading criteria was very unclear and she didn't give us good feedback on how to improve our writing. I would say that my AP Lit/Comp class taught me like 5x more about how to write well, than this class did. It's unfortunate because it means that we are not making good use of our tuition/time/energy here at Cornell.
Do not take this class.

If you choose to take a class by this professor... don't. If you have to take a class from this professor... good luck. She is hard to listen to and rants for ages. The class has no clear rubrics or standards for writing. She grades harshly with little to no room for improvement no matter how much time you may spend. Save yourself, please.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Very comprehensible

Kelly was a really great professor. She regularly takes the time to stop and check if we have questions about the material instead of just steaming ahead. She also gave us a short break in the middle of lecture to go over logistics like deadlines and tests. This helped us to stay organized and refresh us in the middle of class.

Overcomplicates simple calc 2 concepts. Homework also gets longer and complicated for no reason. She also isn't transparent about class mean and median which makes it difficult to gauge how you're doing. There are quizzes in every discussion so it's mandatory to attend.

If her class is open, then take it. She is an amazing lecturer. As a student who did not take BC in high school, she was very thorough in teaching new concepts. She is also very accessible during OHs.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Pohland was really nice in this class was just sometimes unnecessarily difficult. Homework is pretty hard but doable. The discussion was not helpful because the TA was going through a worksheet really fast. Everything is graded very picky.

I took Math 2930 Differential Equations over the summer with Prof. Pohland. Honestly, she's the best professor I've had at Cornell. Very caring and accessible for students, always willing to help you out if you have questions, etc.

Professor Pohland is an awesome professor and cares about the academic and holistic success of her students. While MATH1110 posed to be a huge struggle for me, she truly went above and beyond to give me leeway in order to succeed in the course. She is the best out of all the Calc 1 Professors.

She was very nice and a great lecturer. Her analogies in class were very easy to follow and her explanations of the material was helpful in better grasping the content. She often spent 5-10 minutes explaining/answering one person's question that she could have just answered after class. The exams were much harder than hw problems

Professor Pohland gives solid lectures and is willing to answer questions before, during, and after class. After a disastrous midterm performance, she was willing to meet with me individually to better strategize for the final exam, and I brought myself back from the brink with her help. Approachable and kind.
Lectures were alright. Would often spend way too much time answering one person's questions. Tests were hard, and they never gave practice representative of the actual test.

Professor Pohland is very caring and considerate. Her lectures are clear and easy to understand. Her office hours are fantastic and I cannot recommend them enough- she always took questions and never judged for questions. Excellent professor.

HIGHLY recommend Prof. Pohland for Calc I. If you see her section, take it!! I dropped this class before because of a bad professor but because of her I excelled this time. Always willing to help, she gives mini lectures and encourages questions during class instead of only making you do group work, and is easy to meet with outside of class.

Eddy is the clearest and most articulate lecturer I've ever had. He never stutters, never goes overboard, but every explanation has a lot of value and is very understandable for students, almost like he's reading off a script. Upperclassmen say he used to be strict, but I guess that's a thing of the past, because he is honestly very accomodating.

The class teaches a variety of media, and as long as you follow the rubric and attend class, earning an A is very achievable. The emphasis on technique reduced the pressure to be creative while still leaving plenty of room for creative exploration. Professor Kim also deserves five stars—he is kind, supportive, open-minded, and very professional.

Professor Kim is a serious but fair and considerate professor. He is well respected in the field of design and architecture and is a valuable resource for students like me who want to become better designers/creatives. His Principles of Design Computing class helped me develop my technical toolbelt and my professional/academic portfolio.

Professor Kim is a passionate professor and designer, but he doesn't tolerate slow students or "bad" questions. Make sure to pay attention in lecture. There's no wiggle room for mistakes, so read the guidelines. The lecture recordings are a lifesaver. He is very passionate and constructive for people who both pay attention and are open to learning.

This class is ver manageable, that being said it really depend on how tech savvy you are. Additionally this class is very important to pay attention to. Instructions are vital for all assignments, if the basic criteria isn't followed its an automatic fail. Sit in the front or a spot where you can see the board. Eddy is nice though and funny.

professor kim cares about his students in that he is mostly nice in class and one time even brought snacks, but when you mess up he is very passive aggressive which i found unsettling. you can bounce back from mistakes grade wise but i thought his passive aggressiveness was really rude and unnecessary and the environment wasnt welcoming

professor kim was passive aggressive and rude when students had difficulty keeping up or felt confused about the classwork, which felt especially unwarranted since it was an introductory level course. he also discouraged creative takes on the assignments, and instead emphasized simply following directions, which was upsetting in a design class.

You definitely have to ask the TAs questions to succeed - however, they are super accessible during class and there are a lot of office hours so it's easy to get them to help you. Projects are designed to help you learn useful, practical software applications. Professor Kim cares about his students and gives 1-on-1 help when possible.

reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Kim is a highly respectable professor who is very knowledgable on the information he presents. If you pay close attention to his expectations and the rubric then grading should not be too stressful, and instead the projects allow you to creatively express what you learn during his lectures.

Professor Kim is incredibly caring and thoughtful. He often brings snacks to class, which is especially appreciated since it's a night class and many of us are tired. The snacks help keep us energized and focused. On the last day, he even bought us pizza, showing how much he values his students. It's such a kind gesture!

The techniques I learned here have been so helpful for both current projects and future professional goals. I gained valuable skills in Adobe software, Revit, and Rhino, which I've applied to other courses. My professors even complimented the quality of my work, which wouldn't have been possible without Professor Kim's detailed and expert teaching.

Professor Kim goes above and beyond for his students, recording hour-long tutorials to guide us through software so we never feel stuck. He's considerate, respecting our time and well-being—like holding Zoom sessions during Thanksgiving break for those who left early. He also shares internships— he truly cares about his students and their success!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: If you want to learn how to use Adobe and useful FSAD modeling technology - this is not the course for you. There are only a few major assignments and your grade hinges entirely on what TAs you get and what mood they're in that day. Be prepared to get blindsided by a B- or lower if you make a single mistake on an assignment.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would rather fall into the needle pit from Saw II than take this class again. Grading is heavily determined by who is assigned to grade your work and how they are feeling that day. Very few graded assignments were given and if you mess one up..... well too bad I guess. It seems like nobody knows what this course is actually supposed to be.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Wow, what an interesting man. I'm pretty sure he is a robot, but really enjoyed his class. He teaches really fast so be warned, but everything he does he does for a reason. J pay attention during lecture and you will be fine.

He's good at explaining things in lecture. He's caring and always willing to answer questions during class and after. It's a tough class and problem sets are long but the work is helpful for exam prep. If you have to take this class, I would recommend taking his!

His class IS difficult. the PSs are pretty long but good practice for the tests. He really cares for his students and WILL try his best to help you if you reach out, and he's genuinely passionate about what he teaches. To get good grades, make sure you understand the concepts and do the sections and really listen to the lectures.

Such a difficult class BECAUSE HE MAKES IT THAT WAY! Get your ECON 3030 credit somewhere else because this class genuinely is so difficult for no reason. If you care about your GPA, don't take this class. He has extremely difficult content in problem sets (6 a semester), after lecture quizzes, and most of the time he couldn't finish his lecture.
Engaging, yet informative lectures. The material is difficult but the criteria for success are clear cut so it's not impossible to do well.

This class is genuinely brutal. Just one of those classes you need to get through for Econ major but it's frustrating the entire time. P-sets are actually absurd and the entire course is multi variable calculus despite half the class not having taken that class. Prof seems like a good dude but it doesn't really matter when the class is unreasonable
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: immediate no. Can't fit his lectures into class time so he always posts a video of what he didn't cover in class. Usually these videos are posted NEXT DAY.ew

Sweet professor who cares about course and students, but very difficult course. P-sets would take upwards of 8 hours each (6 p-sets for the course and one drop). Exams are much easier than p-sets. Lectures are difficult to follow, but posts lecture slides. Accessible for OH. Would recommend, but be ready to put in a lot of work outside of lectures

Pretty nice guy but could not make any sense out of his lectures. Talks about how content is easy but likes to jump from one thing to the next without a ton of conceptual explanation; slides aren't the best either. I learned the most from this class by just figuring things while doing the psets, but felt like exams questions were a lot different.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good lecturer, but sometimes struggles with pacing content. Make sure to do the reading (BEFORE you take the quizzes) and go to class. Not too many p-sets, but they take forever. Exams are very fair--if you understand the problem sets, you will do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Very sweet man and tries to be accommodating, but oh boy he does not lecture well. Tries his best, but exams are crazy hard too. Annoying part is that he just keeps talking about how easy the exam was, and just doesn't explain well. Better off just self studying tbh

A good lecturer, but the slides can be a bit lacking, with a bit too heavy an emphasis on theory at times. Tests can be difficult but graded fairly, and if you study you will do well. Problem sets are difficult but definitely reasonable. Overall he is a caring professor who takes feedback well and is willing to accommodate his students
Don't listen to the past reviews!! She has definitely taken feedback to make her lectures more organized and is a very kind teacher :) Give her a chance!

She is a bit disorganized in her lectures and it can be hard to follow. Her tests mainly surround the slideshows but I would use the textbook as extra information. She does test you on the location of parts of the brain that can be challenging. It is possible to do well. You would just have to do most of the learning on your own and extra credit!

Awful organization of lectures, topics just jump all around the place with no defined progression
Too many small details about the brain that don't make sense together
Tests are too hard, you have to memorize everything even though she says you don't necessarily need to 
DO NOT RECOMMEND
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very nice person who seems to care, but a horrible lecturer. Her lectures are just empty words, cannot answer questions, and an unorganized method to the order of topics. She means well, but I can't say I learned much at all.

She makes it nearly impossible to succeed in her class... even though the lowest prelim grade gets dropped, her lectures don't correlate well to tests and often don't make sense. She is also terrible at answering students' questions in class and even if you attend office hours.

Khenas lectures may be a little dry, but she is knowledgeable about the material and exams are straightforward, mostly from lecture. She genuinely cares about our wellbeing - removed short answer questions from the exams to make it easier for us. 4 prelims (+ optional final) was a little too much, but it made studying for each exam less stressful.

Professor Swallow seems like a genuinely nice person, but unfortunately is such a bad professor. It is so hard to understand, very long and monotonous lectures, and the class is entirely disorganized. Tests have questions that are never mentioned in class or the readings. Overall: DO NOT TAKE.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Swallow is passionate and wants students to succeed. Her tests were pretty straight forward and easy. Unfortunately, she is a bit disorganized which was frustrating and getting back test grades took weeks, despite having many TAs.

2 prelims and a final, drop lowest one. Some tricky questions, but mostly from power points. Final is cumulative. Three homework assignments, some parts can be tricky but if you go to TA office hours they will help and book will help. Only need to go to class for clicker points. Find book online. Readings help clarify material

Honestly had no idea what was going on in lectures most of the time. They were barely relevant and pretty poorly executed. Course material was very interesting though, and tests are relatively easy to study for since she posts slides online to look over (you'll get more looking at them yourself with the textbook than going to lecture).
Dont take her classes ever. Very dull and dry lectures. Her TAs did a better job lecturing and getting the class engaged.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Overall, I enjoyed this class. Cognitive science can get deep and technical rather quickly, bleeding into computer science, philosophy, and linguistics. So, developing and teaching an introductory-level cognitive science course is no trivial matter, but I believe that Professor Swallow and her staff did a great job.

The course itself is interesting if not for the professor. She is extremely unprofessional and not careful with grading. Warning: go see your test after you take it there will be errors. This year a "computing" error dropped everyone's grades a week later because she couldn't be bothered to grade the tests right the first time.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Probably the most boring professor I have ever listened to. Complete and total waste of 27.5 hours of my life that I would do anything to get back. First lecture she mentions how taking notes by hand is more useful but she doesn't even give enough time to type half of the slide down. Asks what you think, talks about everyone's answer and goes on.

This teacher is the absolute worst. She is so boring and just lectures about why the human brain is a computer. Unless you are CS and interested in psych, you will find this class boring. The material is interesting but the teacher makes it boring. DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are extremely dry, and you cannot skip due to mandatory GRADED iClicker questions. Majority of lectures are disorganized and she often comes unprepared for class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Horrible class with busy work and a horrible, disorganized professor
Very dry professor with a very disorganized course

*** Textbook may be needed for those select few clicker quiz questions*** Material could be much more interesting if presented in a different way, but overall she's a pretty good lecturer. Participation plays a heavy role because every lecture, we have graded iclicker questions based on the previous lecture's material/reading. Memorization mostly.
Super boring lectures which you are unfortunately required to attend. Easy class with minimal work.
Hardest class I've taken, may not even pass.
The class is an easy A if you go to class and actually study the lecture slides (you really don't need to purchase the book).

Swallow's class has potential to be much more interesting than it actually is; she's passionate about the material but lacks any enthusiasm in teaching resulting in boring lectures. Class is very easy though since 1 prelim gets dropped completely, and you can make up participation on piazza. Overall recommend.

No tests, just case studies and a final project (all group work).  Truly wants you to do your best.  Was willing to meet at any time to answer questions because I could never attend office hours.  Tip: you can answer the case study question any way you want, just USE EVIDENCE to back up your claim and you'll get As.  Great professor, great class.
Final, group project and paper are all do at the same time. Great professor and class though. Doesn't round grades up.
Other than the huge final project required, everything else was good. Professor Khessina tries hard to make it interactive.

Without a doubt the best of the Johnson School. She is highly intelligent but is still super nice and down to earth. The class moves fast and you have to read because as any other business course, there is a mandatory curve so you are constantly competing against your peers. Fun discussions, I actually looked forward to a 5 p.m. class.
Amazing professor with a great sense of humor

I took CS 6820 with Professor Kleinberg (graduate version of CS 4820), and it has been my favorite course at Cornell thus far. Bobby is an amazing lecturer and answers questions very clearly and concisely. I would take every class at Cornell with him if I could. He is very fun, and even outside of the classroom, is always full of great advice.
Super engaging lectures, explains complex topics well. Makes proofs a conversation and motivates each step

Really good class but super challenging, def got a lot out of the class. In class quizzes were fairly easy as long as you paid attention in class, and the final was fair. Would recommend starting HWs later as he often makes edits because he realized problems are way too hard.

Professor is amazing, and the workload is light with only 6 homework and 4 small quizzes. Homeworks sometimes require a bit of thinking. Overall, although not too hard, this is a decent course to take if you want to satisfy the probability requirement but don't want to waste credits on trivialities like MATH 4710.

Kleinberg's are amazing and funny. He is extremely good at explaining complex subjects, and will let you see ideas in a new light. The price you pay is that the course is quite difficult and time-consuming. It is definitely worth it though.

Really nice, kind of funny, uber nerdy guy. I find him charming and easy to talk to. Also have him as my faculty advisor. But, hardest class I've ever taken. Could put hours and hours into HW and OH and still get <20% on it, HW/exam medians were about 50%. Maybe worse because it was online. Also I just suck at algo, which is not his fault.

Prof. Kleinberg is one of those professors that, the more complicated the concept, the better he is at explaining it. His lectures on max flow, NP-Completeness, and Turing Machines were very helpful, while I mostly learned about greedy algorithms and DP from the book. His homeworks are definitely very challenging, with HW / Exam medians 50-60%

Prof. Kleinberg is an excellent instructor who is very good at explaining deep concepts, from NP Reductions to Turing Machines to Network Flow problems. His homeworks are quite difficult (some have had medians close to 50%), but I have learned so much in his class.

He basically gives the answers to students he likes and students who have no shame when asking directly for the answers to problem sets. He is also not useful in lecture. The textbook was the only way someone could learn in that class. He just tried to show off and act cool during lecture.
great lecturer. fascinating course material. challenging weekly homework. super useful class.

Bobby is, no lie, a genius and is well-respected. Lectures can be slow, but are very intuitive. #3 on problem sets can be very difficult sometimes. Exams are pretty easy. Advice: start psets the day they get released and rEAD the TEXTBOOK!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: He is extremely intelligent and very committed in helping his students learn the material. He can be a little brash when dealing with administrative issues in the course, but seems genuinely interested in his teaching duties. Would highly recommend taking 4820 under him if you want to seriously test your understanding of algorithms.

Professor R. Kleinberg was excellent for Algorithms, Spring 2014. He is very open to student questions and attempts to make a sometimes-challenging subject clear. Not an easy professor by any means, but assessments fair. Relies on the textbook a good amount, but also references outside research.
His lecturing style as well as his mastery of the subject matter are both top-notch. He also seems like a great person. It's an absolute privilege to have him as a lecturer.

Had him for both 4820 and 6820. Great lecturer (he writes a lot, so it is hard sometimes to keep up with both listening and writing down nots). Amazing personality (will go overtime to answer your question). In OH, he will insightfully lead you to think rather than just giving answer away. HW can be super challenging.

R. Kleinberg is an amazing teacher and super smart. His lectures are organized, exciting and the material is super fun and challenging. The HWs are super super challenging. Every HW has a question which is so  hard that sometimes the TAs arent sure on how to solve them. But it is fun to solve the HWS. I really improved my problem solving skills.

Nick is a fantastic professor who clearly cares very deeply about the transit planning. Lectures are well made and informative especially when coupled with readings (which are tracked on Perusall). Assignments are engaging and supplement the course content well. Be prepared to reach out if you want to know your grade before the end of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Klein orchestrates a wonderful introduction to the URS major. If you do the reading, along with putting in good effort on the assignments and final, you'll be totally fine. Will definitely be taking CRP 3860 in the future!

He genuinely cares about his students and is highly professional. As long as you keep up with the readings (and essays), you'll do just fine. I'm truly grateful to have met a professor like him, and I highly recommend taking his class — it will change your perspective on American planning. :)

Nick Klein is awesome! He is a really engaging lecturer who is clearly passionate about making public transportation work for everyone. The assignments he gives out are really helpful for understanding the topic and I loved the flexibility he gave us in what we did for our final projects. He definitely encouraged creativity and helped when asked.

Levy teaches the law/history part of the course, Jon teaches the stats. Math is not my forte but he still was able to explain it well enough for me to do well. Whenever you have trouble, there's Toooons of TAs to help. Mostly graded on homework which you can ask TAs help with. If you want an A+ and put in the work, very achievable.
great class, great professor (along with Karen Levy) - workload is super light (6 problem sets throughout the year) and the material is pretty interesting/pertinent to modern times

Jon is too smart to be teaching this class. His brain runs at a billion gigahertz, so I feel like he's malfunctioning when he has to explain introductory statistics in INFO 1260. The way he speaks is so robotic it's hard to pay attention. I think he could build an AI model that teaches this class better than him.
hated the course but loved the professor and the way he taught. definitely would never take the course again or any of the network classes but he was cool
Best professor I've had so far! Enthusiastic lectures and a lot of food related topics. Really knowledgeable and helps students understand the material well. Absolute GOAT.
The most brilliant professor. Clearly a genius and he is so accommodating and nice.

Kleinberg is the best! I've never had a professor that can explain concepts so thoroughly and so well. He makes everything so easy to understand, no matter what a student's background knowledge is. He is also so kind in office hours and truly feels like my Cornell dad after taking INFO 1260 last sem and INFO 2040 this semester. Highly recommend!

Professor Kleinberg's lectures, while dry, are very efficient and informative. He always posts slides prior to class, so attendance is optional in every sense. The psets for INFO 1260 took a good amount of time but were never outrageously difficult by any standard. Professor Kleinberg and his army of TAs will help out with any difficulties.
Very caring prof. His lectures were a bit dry for me at times, but I'm not a very mathy person. Overall though, this is an easy A.
Excellent professor with some really interesting material. Material isn't too hard but can be dry. Class is generally not very interactive.

Kleinberg is so smart. Too bad I didn't get to see his true genius in a course as easy as networks. It's still neat that he and Easley pioneered the field though, and the theory could have been challenging (the textbook goes into this). That said, networks was exactly on par with what I was expecting. Still hopeful I will see Kleinberg's brilliance
great class, interesting topics,  easy to understand
One of the best professors I have had.
Amazing, clear, amazing, clear and amazing.

Professor Kleinberg is always very clear with his explanations of topics. He evidently knows his material very well and has no problems with anyone asking questions in the middle of lecture. The homeworks are easy; however, take the class seriously as a lot of material is covered.

Excellent class, highly recommended! Slow and steady coverage of material, easy, especially if you have prior experience in game theory (I did). Very good explanations of material. Handwriting could use some work. Easy tests and homework. Free electronic textbook is not necessary unless you don't understand the notes or want to go deeper.

Kleinberg is fabulously brilliant, and an incredible teacher too. Networks is honestly a waste of his teaching talent though, since the material is so easy and so useless. I really wish I had him for a real CS class such as discrete math or algorithms instead.

Best CS professor I've had, period. Very, very smart, and very good at explaining the material (I tried taking the same course when Tardos was teaching it...had to drop it), which made the class pretty straightforward and fun. He's funny, too :) If you have any interest in a class he teaches, TAKE IT!
No Comments

Kleinberg made 280 my favorite CS class.  Previous classes complained that work was impossible and the material was far too difficult - not my semester.  Problem sets are not a piece of cake, but he explains enough in the problem set to teach you how to do it.
By far the best CS Professor I have had so far, with Pingali in a somewhat distant second, hes very clear and answers questions right away without confusion
one of the best CS professors at Cornell
Brilliant Professor! One of the best I had at Cornell.

He really is a genius.  He always has an answer to any question immediately but he explains things very well and it makes sense.  Even though the material is hard he is very helpful and a great lecturer.
He's a genius, MacArthur style (look it up). Willing to go back over any logic and try and make it more intuitive for you. Great lecturer.
Kleinberg is rebel king!
why is he called the rebel king?
ping Kleinberg .... The Rebel King is alive
He genuinely tries hard, and likes to make sure students understand the material.  Unfortunately, CS 482 is boring stuff that no one ever uses.
The rebel king is alive and well!
Long live the rebel king!
All hail the Rebel King!
A great professor.  Long live the rebel king.
This guy is the CS GOD!!!
Long live the Rebel King!

Very average professor. uses lecture slides way too much. but also all the questions from exams come right from the slides, and they are all posted which is helpful. Otherwise really boring class, but super easy. Only reason I got A- and not an A was because I took pass/fail since I thought it would be harder. I never studied. Wish I took graded.

Honestly, the class wasn't too bad and Kling moves through the content slowly and carefully. Getting an A is not difficult. Lectures were boring and oversimplified but the class is management, low workload, and not busy work, which I appreciated.
Cathy Kling is a great person, however, for anyone interested in environmental economics this class is a let down. Lectures are trivial at best and do not prepare at all for homework and exams.

I took this class because a friend asked me to and I thought it would be an interesting liberal arts class to take. Prof lectured from infographics she found online, talked about pictures of dogs and cats for 20 minutes every class, made up the rules as she went. Not a good time. Have taken STEM classes with less turbulence.

I love environmental economics and was excited to take this class. What started out well quickly spiraled into a disaster as the professor changed up her syllabus unexpectedly and gave minimal preparation for prelims. Make sure to go to office hours and hope the TAs can teach you the course...

The professor wasted half of lecture either talking about people's pets or playing MOBLAB games which is great until the prelim shows up and its nothing like the homework and requires luck and guessing...

Besides the fact that she was annoying to begin with, her class is just as, if not worse. Attendance is tracked by MobLab games (there are makeups) but if you skip lecture, the slides don't make much sense because they're just graphs tbh. Psets are given sporadically and due that week, and poorly worded (jargon heavy). Exams are easier than Psets.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Disorganized but Prelims/Problem sets are pretty easy if you study the slideshow she makes for lecture
0 Flexibility
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor is not very accommodating of students; changes up the syllabus randomly. Minimal exam preparation is given, so good luck on the prelims.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
DOES NOT HONOR HER SYLLABUS. DISREGARDS SDS ACCOMMODATIONS.
Moved a test up an entire week, 3 days before the start of the new test date. Called it a "typo" in the course calendar. Syllabus states that students can drop 1 of the (only) 5 homeworks from the semester. Kids in class asked her about it and she said "Yep, we're not following that".
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: nice professor, but lectures are a total waste of time. homework is relatively easy as long as you just read the slides over. problem sets and exams frequently had typos that made doing the work difficult.

There are a few random attendance checks and writing assignments (for completion) = easy points. All info is on the slides. Exams are virtually identical to problem sets. Super straightforward class. Cathy is super slay. She's so funny and wants students to have fun (will spend 1/2 of class looking at pictures of pets). Also super understanding!
all questions on tests and problem sets are open-ended so you straight up have to know or memorize everything, literally. lectures were boring and hard to comprehend
Lectures were a waste of time. Not worth it

One of the worst professors I have taken at Cornell. She barely showed up to lectures many of the times, and when she did she spent more time talking with the class about random stuff than actual econ. Class was easy and then made a ridiculously hard final. I went to every class only to realize I was not learning anything. Quite disappointing

Class is not very hard but I also feel like I learned nothing. Prof Kling is very nice and tries to make class fun but I wish she taught better. For example, the questions on the problem sets left us to fend for ourselves a bit because she didn't teach us how to solve those kinds of problems. Fun person, disorganized class.

Cody is fabulous. I took intro to creative writing to fulfill my fine arts requirement and had a great time. Everything was graded on completion, which was a relief as a mediocre writer. She always had something good to say about your work.

Hip, young and cool teacher. She is approachable and incredibly insightful which is why I think many students respect her. My only thing is that she made us print 20 copies of our papers every time an essay was due, when we very well could sent each other our essays instead of wasting money and killing trees. Otherwise, highly recommend.

I took her not very serious class Creative Writing, she barely lectured (that I remember). When she did, it was pretty insightful and short. The class was mostly discussions/workshops about each student's story, so she wasn't too involved. A tad bit awkward during discussions because no one wants to talk. A very good writer though, fun personality.

Cody is an excellent professor. I had her Great New Books FWS--she chose amazing works to study, and the reading was never too much. Her essay prompts are creative and really make you think. On top of all that, she's VERY understanding if you need extensions or are going through a hard time. She's approachable and super hip and cool.

I took intro to creative writing with Ms. Klippenstein. She was lovely- very understanding and encouraging, and led thoughtful discussions in class. I went into her class complaining that I had to take it as a requirement, but Cody made it stimulating and inspirational. I highly recommend taking a class with her.

She's awesome and super understanding about all circumstances. The most important part of your grade is just showing up. The conversation is always interesting and the books are hit or miss in terms of preference. If you have the opportunity to take her class, do it.

Bias towards atheletes, changes answers on a whim if athletes said so, doesn't like to use Mic, can't hear him, can't listen to recordings, doesn't have concrete reasonings as to why his quiz answers are correct, multiple correct answers to one question. Trick questions.

He mentioned a right answer in the quiz, Q 2- A, but marked C as the right answer, but then when one of his favorite people mentioned D as the right answer, he just accepted it and changed that answer. He wouldn't accept any reasoning to give credit for A even though he mentioned that A is correct. He doesn't like to speak on mic, his voice is low

Adam Klausner placed many trick questions on his exams and as a result, had to heavily curve. He did not allow students to keep their exams, and did not hand back or go over the second exam. Lastly, despite graduating from Cornell Law, he was wrong on several legal concepts and was combative when students tried to challenge him. Very disappointed.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor is well versed in material and class goes over basics of law. No law experience nor interest required. Only 2 prelims make up my grade this semester - no complaints there (optional final).
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The readings were helpful but not really necessary, and I still learned so much in this class. Show up, study for the prelims, and you will get an A. On top of that, Klausner is a great guy. 10/10, my favorite course I've taken at Cornell thus far.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: Great guy. Very clear and interesting. Only 3 non-cumulative tests, and you know what will be tested on. Everything is from lecture and cases, but you by no means have to memorize individual cases, just the reasoning behind law stuff. Not hard. Take it if you can.
Adam Klausner is the best thing to happen at Cornell in a long time. Great prof, great attorney and really, really funny!
HE teaches RE Law..while using Batman, Alfred and Robin as example, how cool is that?!
Good prof but needs to speak more slowly and give better reviews for prelims
One of the best classes at Cornell. So much info and Klausner makes it fun and interesting. He's one of the best professors I've had and cares about his students. Take all of his classes!
Most of his prelim questions came straight from the examples discussed in class. So his exams are easy if you go to class, and hard if you don't. I learned the hard way after my first prelim.

Klausner is a terrific professor. He made the material as interesting as possible (come on...it's real estate law!) and supplemented with real-life stories. Be sure to take good notes and go to class, because getting notes from others will not help you during the exam. His jokes are sometimes only half-funny, but at least he tries!
cool professor, clear and interesting lecture
I'm really interested in real estate and decided to try H ADM 4487. Adam was an outstanding professor. Definitely take all his classes.
Loved this class. I highly recommend Adam. He makes real estate law fun.

Probably the most useful undergrad course I have taken. However, I didn't appreciate the long exams and lack of time to answer each question. I like Professor Klausner, but he isn't kind with grades. He basically thinks that as long as a decent percentage of the class gets As, there is no need to curve even if the mean is low.
Passionate lecturer; useful case studies.
Alright

Both my roommate and I had Adam for Real Estate Law. We feel he makes the semester more difficult than it needs to be, yet at the same time he makes it extremely interesting. Studying for the final exam should be done carefully.
Not as bad as others describe him.

During lecture, Klausner is funny and engaging. In person however, he is a typical lawyer: not overly friendly, but very, very efficient. He doesn't put up with bs. Not bad at all, you just have to study hard.
People, he is a lawyer, not your personal psychologist. Yes, it's hard to get a hold of him outside of class, but the TA was usually available during office hours. Certainly not terrible.

Unclear. I was doing well on my prelims until the final, which my grade collapse because very little information was covered, BUT questions were unfairly specific. On the positive side, he let us leave early many times.

Could never follow what he meant at times. Not sure he realized how general his lectures were and yet we were expected to know the material in-depth. His reviews are the worst, don't even bother to attend them.
Tough...

Exams contain questions pertaining to several topics not covered in class. Also, each exam has way too many questions  and you only get about an hour. I think Klausner definitely knows his stuff, though.
Interesting course but awful exams--dont waste your time

Had him for Real Estate Law. Overall, he is a good, funny prof, but the class is very difficult if you haven't taken a previous law course. About 70% of the final exam came from material that he only lectured on for literally 15 minutes and there was no curve even though many students received Ds. However, it is still an interesting class to take.
Favorite class/prof at Cornell.  That says alot.  Interesting material, and the prof likes to tell stories about law cases, as well as stories about his children and family.  Highly recommended!
Clear, funny, and cool professor.  Makes subject matter interesting.
The Man, Plain and Simple!  He helped me with an open container ticket once!
best teacher at cornell. period.
really cool guy, interesting material, definitely recommend.

The Live Sessions helped me understand the course better but it was still very hard. Make sure you have enough time to watch the videos and comment on the posts or you'll fall behind. I know I did but somehow still managed to complete.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: lots of work but easy to approach the professor. would take a course with him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Helpful! I was confused but was able to get additional assistance from him and passed the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Difficult class! The course material and projects are a lot to learn and juggle alongside work. Professor Kavall helped consistently until I had the Project completed. I'd take another course with him but don't recommend the class unless you're proficient in both Excel and Statistics.

Took the Optimizing Digital Advertising with Analytics with Professor Kavall and learned a ton! He was very helpful to the point of even having a Zoom chat after normal hours to go into detail regarding the assignment since my 9-5 was creating difficulties for me. I'd highly recommend taking the course!
Fun class. Great topic.
Thanks Professor Kavall! Your class was great and thank you for helping me.
Good conversation and was helpful after class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor Klosin was amazing! This class is really enjoyable and he teaches a lot of modern mathematics that is very interesting! There is only one project and a final but that shouldn't scare you because he is a very fair and easy grader! You can tell that he loves teaching and is always open for you to ask questions in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Awesome teacher.  Lectures always clear, extremely willing to help.  Fair tests and grading.  Made me like a topic I thought I'd hate.  Lighten up and laugh at his jokes :)
No Comments

Kniffin is one of my favourite professors with engaging lectures. He asks you to do a lot of readings which you build on in class, so there will be a lot of reading. In class, he calls on people to share their opinions which makes classes interactive. Overall, he covers relevant and interesting topics that the students are interested in a fun way!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Kevin is my favorite professor at Cornell. His lectures are engaging and he is super passionate about encouraging his students' academic growth.
Kevin is the best. Cares deeply about his students and the material. I cannot recommend him enough!
The most boring class I have ever taken. Mandatory attendance taken but no takeaway at all. The professor makes you want to sleep in every session.

Such an awesome, engaging professor! Made student anecdotes a big part of class, which kept things interesting and relevant since we always compared ideas we learned about to the real world. If you do the work, you'll do well. Must take!

8AM class on Saturday and Sunday, 6 Hour of monologue stuffed with personal anecdote or his own research that most students could not relate, everyone's lost and just ended up doing their own thing. Insufficient break time, lectures 2 hours and gives 10 minute assignment within our 15 minute break.

Class has weekly readings and reflection papers, but nothing too difficult. Professor Kniffin is very knowledgeable and passionate about the topics covered, and tries to engage the class as much as possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Course material can be a bit dry at times due to dense academic readings. That being said, its a class on sports, so its pretty cool nonetheless. All assignments are due on the last day of the semester, so you have absolutely no idea where your grade stands until you see it in Student Center. Overall solid class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Loved his class-- he has the experience and loves telling stories, which are always interesting. Lectures are kind of dry because of the nature of the ppt slides, but if you really listen to what he has to say, you'll realize just how sarcastic and witty he is. And he acts like he's cantankerous, but he'll do anything to help you if you ask.

I LOVED this class! It's awesome and the instructor really knows his stuff. He also likes to make fun of people in a while but very genuine. Our class was small so it made the atmosphere even better-- we had so many inside jokes :) You learn more than you bargain for

Classes are long and clinical time is required, but the course material is definitely easy to comprehend and interesting.  Kniffen has a lot of experience, so he can tell you not only what the state recommends, but also what realistically happens in the field.  This is a great class and I'd recommend it for anyone, particularly if you're pre-med.
Rich is pretty laid back and has a dry, self deprecating sense of humor. Tests are completely taken from the book so make sure you read and use the CD that comes with the book.

Lectures were very good. Straightforward, content-heavy but reasonably paced, and content organized in a sensible manner. Personally, he wasn't very engaging or relatable. It was easy to zone out, and even missing one lecture meant it was difficult to catch back up on content. Homework was also FAR more difficult and I just ended up chatGPT-ing it
As others have noted, his lectures were good, but I found him to be highly inflexible and condescending when approached after class or during office hours.
He treats you like you are 4 years old in office hours. Grading critera seemed to change like the wind. Would not reccomend taking the course
This testing brought benefit to me. Examinations were of the easiest, require no study.

Dr. Kowal was a nice prof, and I believe he made BTRY 4030 as interesting as he could. It's not a very applied course by nature, but he tried hard to give us homework and exam problems which were applied  to the real world, which I enjoyed. The work load in this class was manageable, but exams were hard in my opinion.
Good personality, good lecture style! The exams are pretty easy and his notes are good for reviewing. Asking questions after class is always welcome.

Basically no curve. Which he said he would. Like my raw grade was a B+ and I end with a B+. IDK maybe I was not scoring meaningfully more to get a A-. But he is so unbelievably rude. Like his lectures are good and easy to follow but he is insanely rude. Like talking to him feels insulting at times and he grades really hard.

Yes, he can be boring with dry lectures. BUT, incredibly approachable, very helpful when asking questions, gives few homeworks and they're easy, gives easy exams, and will often take your side when you have regrade requests. Exams are basically the same as practice exams and there are no trick questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is incredibly confident (to put it nicely). He believes it is the world's greatest inconvenience when you have to ask him a question. He is a decent lecturer but completely unreasonable to work with as an instructor. Fair exams. Would recommend waiting to take it with another professor.

He was very dry and seemed pretty unapproachable and uninterested in the class. He was EXTREMELY unclear about grading policies (although i will recognize it was his first time teaching the course) and just overall vague and uncommunicative. The class is a major requirement but didn't even feel useful. Don't really recommend

He was not communicative at all, rude and dismissive to those who wanted to talk about grades, and was not transparent about grading (no curve). TAs graded your assignments twice, often resulting in lower grades. Cheating on exams was rampant. If he teaches this again, don't take it. For the stats major, you are probably better off in ECON 3140.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Koenecke is extremely knowledgeable and always willing to clarify any questions. Class was pretty difficult, especially if you don't have much prior technical experience, but manageable as there's a lot of support for students.
Best prof ever, hw were a bit long, but office hours was always helpful and they gave you plenty of time. Lectures are 10/10

Great lecturer, goes through topics so so fast. HW are open note/internet and midterm/final get 1 page cheat sheet which saved me. This class is just a beast, she's a great professer that really wants to get you through it. Go to class & especially lab, there's extra credit for HW every other week. Deserved a B ty curve + extra credit + attendance

One of the best professors I have had at Cornell. Professor Koenecke is extremely knowledgeable and always willing to clarify information during lectures, office hours, and Ed Discussion. Gained a lot from her data science class and has inspired me to pursue a career in data science, especially as the material taught is so practical!
Prof is very very knowledgable. Her lectures are usually 100+ slides long and have a lot of information which made it difficult to study for exams because there was so much content.

Professor Koenecke is very caring and has a lot of knowledge from her experiences in the industry. Her lectures are awesome and her guest lectures are great as well. The final project is cool and you learn a lot in INFO 4390. Everyone who is interested in ML or data science should take the course with prof Koenecke.

One of the best profs I've had at Cornell so far. Lectures are so interesting and have genuinely inspired me to pursue data science as a career. I enjoyed this class so much -- you learn so much technical skill while understanding the theory behind it. Loved the projects in this class, too!

This class is one of the more time-consuming intro infosci courses, but as someone coming in with zero data science experience, I really learned a lot. Professor Koenecke does a great job clearly packaging this information in lectures and is great at accommodations (e.g., slip days, sending lecture recordings for excused absences).
the best professor I have had at Cornell. take 2950 with her if you can. makes concepts super clear and made coming to class worth it

This is for the course HE 2000: Social Justice, Thriving, and the Human Experience. I would recommend anyone even marginally interested in taking their careers in a public interest orientation to take this class. Dr. Korfine and Dr. Alexander both, will encourage you to consider the immediate impact you and your career can have on your environment.
Lauren is one of my favorite profs around Cornell! She is so kind and flexible, and the class material is interesing.

If you're a psych major that needs to take this class, please do it early in your degree. Made the mistake of having many different lab experiences before this class, which made it feel so slow and the group project awkward. I wish I'd taken it early, I'm sure it prepares you wonderfully. Korfine is nice, willing to help, and receptive of feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Most caring professor I've ever had and a really useful class if interested in research!
Professor Korfine really goes above and beyond to inspire and care for her students. I can't emphasise enough how great of a professor she is.
One of the best professors Cornell has! I loved her courses!! Highly recommend

Lauren Korfine is an amazing lecturer and one of the most caring professors I have had. I took her class on a whim after reading her great Rate My Professors reviews. I enjoyed her class so much that I'm taking another one with her. The grading is based on take-home, open note prelims, chapter annotations, and one term paper, so very manageable.

Prof. Korfine is by far one of the sweetest professors at Cornell and it's very clear that she cares about her students. She will make you feel so comfortable while also ensuring that you understand everything that is being presented to you and making herself accessible outside of class when needed. Overall an AMAZING prof and person altogether.

Professor Korfine is the sweetest person you'll ever meet. Assignments are graded by TA, and grades depend on which TA you are assigned. TAs are picky and grade hard. Go to TA and Korfine's office hours. Overall, the course was fun. I would recommend it, especially if you want to do something with research in the future.

Prof. Korfine is defintiely very nice and caring. I thought the grading of prelims and papers was biased and unfair, especially because the course matters are so subjective. The course content also didn't appeal to me, but others may have a better time :)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is SO incredibly kind. Incredibly understanding, openminded, and catering to her students.

Korfine is one of the nicest professors you will ever meet. Go to office hours and talk to her. But her lectures are too easy. She often just repeats what you read over the week and the class as a whole is too easy as well.

Definitely the kindest professor at Cornell. I didn't really like the class because of the subject matter, but the professor taught it well nonetheless. Very sweet, knowledgeable, and on top of things.
the most caring professor I've every met

I love prof korfine SO much. She really cares about her students and succeeds at making the class extremely interesting & challenging, but not stressful. She is by far the best teacher I've had in my entire life, and the information is very important. She also considers many perspectives & includes sufficient intersectional research! Take her class

Lauren is my favorite professor at Cornell. I've taken two classes with her and she is the sweetest person! She makes it very clear that she cares about her students, beyond supporting them in the class. She responds quickly to emails, is always willing to work with students, is friendly and approachable. Definitely recommend both of her classes!

I'm a senior, and Professor Korfine is the best professor I've ever had at Cornell, and both of her classes are AMAZING and so interesting. She is one of the kindest, smartest people I have come across in my life. I wish she taught all my classes LOL

Professor Korfine cares about her students in a way I haven't experienced from most professors at Cornell. She consistently checks up on us and creates assignments that are more about learning than difficulty. You don't have to do the textbook readings, but you'll need the textbook for quizzes and prelims. She is awesome- highly recommend!

Course had an interesting syllabus, but lectures and discussions were very confusing. Explanations are not clear. The professor is not too organized. Classes feel stale and rigid. Lots of reading as is true with other PHIL classes.

Theo seems like a very strict teacher, however, he is very lenient on submission time and attendance. As long as you do the work, you should be fine. He does talk a lot in class and get off tracked, but his lectures are very interesting and thought provoking. When you ask questions though, he will question your thoughts harsly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He is quite a nice guy, despite his constant mumbling in class. Yet once you get used to it, he is an insightful and very interesting professor to be with.

At first he is a bit of pain and not extremely pleasant. Consequently, people do drop his class. However, once he becomes comfortable and he is actually kinda funny and nice. The readings are sometimes painful and the essays are few but tough. He prepares you well for them, if you can understand his occasional mumbling, and always likes to help.

Korzukhin is nice guy, but he is genuinely incomprehensible during lectures. He mumbles constantly and talks to the blackboard. Problem sets were ludicrously difficult. Nearly the entire PHIL 2830 class needed to collaborate for around 14 hours per pset. Avoid at all costs.
Very honest, but very interesting

Lectures can be boring, but are also often very interesting. Grades are only based on discussions, participation, and essays. The essays can be difficult to write and he is a very difficult grader, but his feedback usually helps. He's overall a funny and nice guy when he opens up.

This professor made you feel like you were an idiot just for asking questions. Additionally, there is a great deal of software you must pay for and use consistently, but there is zero instruction from the professor on how to use it. His lectures are confusing and difficult to hear. Definitely do not recommend.

Took a very convoluted route to explaining basic concepts in deductive logic, will make you feel silly for asking questions. Overall avoid him if you can help it, a lot of software involved for homework and not much guidance on how to use it.
felt like this class was a complete afterthought to him. slides were never posted online consistently. also was stingy about sharing readings online. hard to hear in lecture as well. overall, not fun

Theo is an incoherent lecturer and his quizzes have very little to do with lectures. He quizzes very niche topics that are barely covered in the readings. His grading scale is generous and papers aren't graded harshly, but it will be hard to get an A in this class unless you know a lot of philosophy going in. TAs are super helpful but not enough.

She's a very nice, professor, but the class itself is so boring and the content is not interesting. Also the prelims are hard. SO much content to memorise. And I literally sit and wait for the class to end. But its not her fault. As a teacher, i really love her. She is kind, funny, passionate. the content is a lot and exams hard. Hard class. ugh
Worst class I have taken at Cornell. Never taught, read directly off the slides. Showed consistent favoritism, and material never connected to work or the exams.

If you show her that you're motivated to learn the material, she will be very caring and helpful in learning the material and receiving a good grade, she does not like slackers though. Tests were lecture-heavy and projects had clear rubrics. Very fair grader. Put in the work and you will get a good grade. Participate in lectures for extra credit.

Workman's lectures can sometimes be dreadful because feel very long, content is dry, and honestly her voice is a little annoying (sorry queen). BUT, she is fair and pretty nice. Class is soooo memorization and lots common sense (name of the concept often tells what it is). This class taught me to use flashcards.. great for this type of class.

This is my least favorite class I've taken at Cornell. The content is not engaging, and the tests are overly complicated. The professor isn't communicative and is not a great lecturer. I dreaded this class. No matter how hard I studied, I would do mediocre.

Never taught during the entire semester, only read off slides. Very uncommunicative about assignments, readings, exams, etc. Expects you to know everything and to do everything yourself. Always had an attitude when I asked questions or had concerns. Wouldn't take this class again if my life depended on it. Teaching style was rude and dismissive.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I did not enjoy her class. Participation matters a lot, and she talks a lot during lectures, so there is a lot to remember for the prelim 😒. I also disliked the group project. Working with six people made communication hard. Some group members ghost you, then act like kind, smart people in class. It felt really two-faced.

Proof that a Ph.D does not mean anything. It would be nice to have Professor's with real industry experience. Big difference from reading off slides and sharing your career experiences. Not engaging either unfortunately.
She's awesome.
Unfortunate to have a professor read off slides the entire time and not go in depth to specific topics. Cookie cutter format. Does not really care to be there.

Content is overwhelmingly in lecture, you MUST go to almost every class. Her exams are weird in format, be prepared to do a lot of studying. Too large of a portion of your grade is determined by an unfair and needlessly difficult group project, and she absolutely plays favorites.
I really enjoyed this class. She did a great job. The class was serious but reasonable. This isn't a topic that I found fascinating, but she did a good job trying to make it relatable.

I took Professor Workman for Organizational Behavior. This class is very intensive and requires you to write ALOT and never skip. Professor Workman has no office hours and she was sometimes very rude in class. She also often acted passive-aggressive to some people's questions, rarely gave feedback on projects, and grades very hard, even on grammar.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Fantastic professor. Really cares about the students. The students that are complaining about difficulty are just poor students and probably shouldn't be at Cornell.

This is a mandatory freshmen class; therefore (no offense) many of the students are new to college standards and expectations. Workman is a very good professor and is very easy; for tests you just have to look over online slides. People who think she is hard aren't used to college. She is sweet, smart, and cares a lot. Great lectures & 1 easy paper

Every lecture is extremely long and boring. No one ever learns anything as she covers an insane amount of material per class. Her tests are also insanely difficult as there is just too much information to possibly memorize. She mentions every theory or term ever written about Organizational Behavior instead of going into depth about specific topics
seriously the worst lecturer i have ever had. trails off at the end of every sentence and barely looks up from his screen. also very reluctant to answer questions

Content presented in a boring, uninspiring way. Good 4000 level econ class if you don't want to overwork yourself - no required attendance, exam material can be found on the slides. His teaching methods reflects that he doesn't think having a super difficult class is necessary - which can be seen as time-wasting to some and low-stress to others.

I was very excited about the material but became very frustrated. Professor Nimark was a very harsh grader on the exams and never gave us any feedback. Grading was very inconsistent across different students. No incentive to attend class as he brought 0 enthusiasm and effort to his lectures. Said he'd “curve the class” and yet there was no curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The slides are very boring and inefficient. The professor basically just copies what's in the textbook into the slides, so they're full of text. Exams are just pure memorization but require a lot of time.
Terrible experience, one of the worst econ class i have ever taken throughout my entire econ major career. Very useless slides.
One of the worst economics professors I've ever had at Cornell, the most monotone lectures & reads straight off slides. Prelims and finals are pure memorization. Do not take.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I personally had a good experience with this class. If you are responsible and keep up, and don't take advantage of the leniency of Professor Nimark by getting lazy (ie, attendance isn't mandatory, won't quiz you, etc.) you will excel. Also, he is by far the most caring professor and clearly cares and understands that life is more than just a class

pretty much the intermediate macro content all over again. the test is literally about how well you memorize his text heavy slides. any minor deviation from rubric results in points deduction. think twice before you enroll; there should be better places to waste your time

Probably the worst professor I have ever had at Cornell. The content isn't too hard but Nimark sure knew how to confuse his students. I stopped going to class after the first few lectures and just read the textbook instead. Only reason why I got an A- was because the TA was lenient with the grading. Overall bad class.

Easily the worst professor I have ever had at Cornell. While the class itself is not the most difficult, it is impossible to know what you need to know for the exam. Office hours for the TA and professor are horrible and I do not learn anything. Often times, the professor shows up and it feels like he is reading the slides for the first time.
Most irresponsible and poorest professor I have ever met at Cornell. Simply don't care since he's already full professor and won't be fired.

He's a little monotone and uninspiring, but he knows the subject and he's a very generous/fair grader. I don't get the frustration from others, he may be kinda boring but he explains stuff well and answer questions. Better on zoom maybe?
Good class for non-economics majors. Economists usually miss the graphs and math. TA is helpful for hws.

This guy straight up doesnt care. Very uninspiring lecturer, shows up late from time to time and doesnt help at all. This is a very easy class from a material stand point, so I would only take it if you want an easy 4000-level course. However, I have never met someone who cares less about teaching in my time at Cornell.

The TA grades the exam, class curves to a B+, grading is arbitrary. He is not all that passionate about teaching, he reads from the PowerPoints, which are taken from the textbook. READ the Textbook, and DO the review questions, as for HW talk to the TA, not an easy A, but doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I love the Cornell physics department! Dr. Krasicky is a great lecturer who wants his students to succeed. He uses demos to illustrate the concepts and provides detailed note packets for each lecture. Overall, if you pay attention during lecture and complete all the co-ops in discussion, you will do well as the exams are very fair and balanced.
Physics GOAT
I am willing to fail this class to take it again!
He's the goat
Great teacher

I wish I had paid more attention in class but sometimes it just gets kinda boring. We can all tell Krasicky and the rest of the phys 1112 staff really cares about making sure students understand concepts!! He made it so the last two exams was worth more (if you have an upward trend) so you can redeem yourself if the first prelim didnt go well!!

The lectures aren't gonna teach you anything but rather help you prepare for the exams. So be ready to do most of the work yourself and read a lot. The TAs will be the most help, especially the ones that have been TAing for a long time. The demonstrations in lectures are the most fun, the Co-ops are a little tedious though .
He's definitely the GOAT! Lectures are really interesting! Homework is a little hard but only take 5%in the final grade and mostly base on completion.

Krasicky is amazing! His lectures are very engaging. The exams are extremely fair and pretty easy to prepare for if you do all the coops, homework, and review lectures. I hated physics in high school, but this class absolutely flipped my opinion on the subject. Absolute GOAT professor
Came in with a bad physics background but wasn't an issue bc Krasicky is AMAZING. Prelims/final were difficult but we were extremely well prepared. I LOVE THE PHYSICS DEPT AT CORNELL.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Krasicky is a great lecturer. It's a flipped classroom, so the textbook readings are mandatory and a decent amount of work. P-sets can take up to 6-8 hours, but office hours and the TAs are really helpful. Prelims were fair in their difficulty and content. Overall, you will learn a lot and the grading is fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Class is uncurved and homework is lengthy and difficult. Lots of studying is required, but the lectures (and provided note packets!!) are very well done. Demonstrations in lectures are also engaging. TA wise, SOROUSH IS THE GOAT (don't be scared off during add-drop).
Amazing lecture and cool demonstrations. Also very helpful during office hour.
I have never had a bad lecture in his class

Amazing prof. Went in hating physics but he completely changed my mind. Flipped classroom structure was a good amount of work but ultimately beneficial, with lectures clearing up confusion and including relevant demonstrations. Exams are fair and plenty of outside resources (office hours, etc) provided. Krasicky wants you to succeed, loved him.

Professor Krasicky is funny, passionate, and overall a great guy who gives incredible lectures. The class is a bit time-consuming (with 3 lectures, 2 discussions, reading quizzes, and psets every week) but it is extremely well-organized and is rather "beginner-friendly" to first-semester freshmen. He is also great outside of class.

Taken FA23. This course was really laid out nicely. I also had a wonderful TA (shout out to Steve). Prof explained stuff very clearly in class, was quite enthusiastic with nice demonstrations and was accessible for questions after class. Most of my learning came from lecture, COOPs (Disc.), and the HW. You also get familiar with Curious Cat.

Very passionate professor with engaging lectures and demonstrations. Moderate, sometimes heavy workload, but the course is extremely well-organized with plenty of resources available outside of class time. Best class I took freshman year

Took FA21. Awesome Prof! Along with entire PHYS1112 teaching staff, made class super enjoyable. Already took Physics C-M in high school so material was easy. P-sets could be long, but not hard if you went to study hall. Exams were very fair (ave 75-85). Great lecturer and overall awesome person.
His lectures were very well done. The course is outlined extremeley clearley and everything is easy to follow. If you remember High School physics you will do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Phil's lectures always have so much infectious energy and enthusiasm. His demonstrations are clear and he always tries to explain common mistakes that students may make. There is reading before each class ("flipped classroom") and the content is as difficult as any intro physics class.
Really great at performing demos in class and explaining the concepts well. Also very passionate about the material.

Professor Krasicky is a phenomenal lecturer. He consistently packs his lectures full of interesting and intuitive demonstrations, and you can sense his immense passion for teaching during every lecture. The iClicker questions can get a bit rough at times, so try to establish a group of friends around you to work through them together.

The class is structured fairly straightforward and there are no surprises since everything is laid out for you to understand. The homework might take a significant chunk of time, but the hard work will pay off in the form of test questions. He is a great professor, if not dry at times, and will sometimes speed through lectures, so come prepared.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: All around good, fun guy. Tries his best to make lectures interesting and engaging (sometimes through iClicker questions though). He often starts lectures a few minutes early/exactly on time and goes through some things quickly, but in general I think his lectures are good and useful to attend. Course is very fairly and clearly graded.

Amazing professor, really makes an effort to make lectures fun and memorable with his experiment demonstrations. Class is organized really well so that the homeworks, reading quizzes, and discussions really help you learn the material. It is time consuming but the time spent helps to do good on the exams.
Phil and Bert did their best to make the lectures worthwhile. Great guy but the lectures were kinda monotonous. The tests were very fair and class is curved well at the end.
