This class is truly challenging but rewarding. Definitely expect a lot of readings but I learned how to skim by the end of the semester. PK is very knowledgeable and the classes is very organized. One of the best classes I took at Cornell.

Professor Katzenstein is truly an incredible professor, deserving his fame. Lectures can be dense at times, just like the readings, however, they are still incredibly insightful. The course is an insane undertaking, but if you put in the time, the gains are incredible. PK is also extremely accessible, and office hours are extremely fun and valuable

A lot of hype around PK. As you see by other ratings, people view him as an amazing professor although most all of the teaching happens with your TA. PK even says he's the last resort when you have inquiries, consult every TA first. Lectures lack structure and connection to readings is extremely weak. Readings unreasonably hard for an intro level.

PK made the lectures very interesting and helpful. I found that discussion led by the TA's was the most helpful part of the course and helped explain the readings. The lectures are amazing, but be prepared to read like crazy. If you are willing to put in the work this class will reward you.

Great teacher, great class. If you get the chance, take it, because I learned a lot (but be ready to read a lot for homework). If you do the readings, the class isn't that difficult, definitely not too stressful. You can get away with not buying/reading the Drezner book, but it may help you understand the concepts a little better.

PK is one of the most respected professors in the Government Department. Although he tries to make class fun and wants his students to be engaged, his lectures are often extremely difficult to follow and notes (for readings or class) are indecipherable. Be prepared for this class to take over your life as the readings are lengthy and abundant.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Katzenstein is a wonderful professor, and I greatly enjoyed the time I had taking Intro to IR. The course itself is a very difficult course without question, but it does a good job of paving new ways for you to think and analyze the world. Katzenstein has a great approach of placing students first and being a guide through this course.

PK is the someone I'd want as an interesting grandpa, but not really as a professor. This class is completely different from what I expected of the title (Making Sense of World Politics) I almost feel more confused. It is without a doubt that I've learned a huge amount of material, but how I actually feel about the material is hard to answer :/
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: PK is a gem. He is a master conversationalist and a gifted speaker. He cares about what you think and isn't afraid to say what he feels. He is biased toward his school of theory, but can provide explanations in many. I can't recommend him enough.
I wish I attended the lectures more, but when I did I learned a lot. Everyone at Cornell should take his class
One of the greatest professors I have ever seen, deserve any admiration. Anyone who has a chance should take his courses.
It's my honor to take his class. Although reading is alot, his class is really inspirational. Humorous and nice guy. Accessible. Will take his class again.
He is good, but his lectures have little to do with the material read outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Tests? Not many--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Best part of the course -- great lectures Worst part of the course -- irrelevant readings

The case-based approach is unique and incredibly rewarding. Teaches you to analyse a country by understanding macroeconomic indicators in combination with political/historical considerations. PK is strict, kind, hilarious and seems to know something about everything. He pushes students to be the best version of themselves - demanding, but worth it!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Would take again

reviews.comment: Katzenstein is probably the most famous professor in Cornell's Government department, and there's a reason for that. He is a really interesting lecturer and learning during his classes happens naturally. Sometimes he shows his age but not worse than any other professor over 30. Not particularly hard but lots of reading and writing.

Professor Katzenstein is the best professor and person. Unbelievably knowledgeable, unbelievably strict and unbelievably kind. His class is well worth the effort. The TAs are also great and allow for a class like AEM3547 to be possible. I feel grateful and inspired by this class. I have learned a lot about the world and I want to learn much more.

Professor Katzenstein's class is one of the best I've taken. lectures are organized & thought provoking; class discussions are well moderated and interesting. He encourages you to think & grow critical skills rather than memorize info The research paper is daunting at first but bc its broken down its manageable. TAs are great & key to doing well
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very informative, gives an overall sense of whats happening in the global political economy by reading interesting cases from different countries around the world. if you have no economics background you need to put too much effort, but it is worth it and you will have a good background of the current global economic and political situation.
PK is the best professor I met, and this course is the most impressive course I took in Cornell. This course changed my mind to pursue my political journalist dream.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: PK is a real gem. I've taken multiple classes with him and wish I wasn't graduating just so I could keep taking his classes. Requires hard work but is substantive and engaging (HBS case+research paper). Definitely take 3547/3557 before graduating. If you're in the social sciences, your Cornell experience will be incomplete without PK.
Prof Katzenstein did a really great job with my course. He's an interesting speaker and knows how to create dialogue. Definitely would take the course again.

Best professor at Cornell it's not even close. One of the smartest minds in his field and the country, you should be required to take his class. I will do everything I can to take more PK classes in the future.
The combination of the lecture, and the discussion section with the TA's was invaluable!

PK is incredible! Highly invested in not only his research, but the world around him. He is very nuanced and inspires students to take responsibility for the world around them w/o inserting political bias. Lectures are dense, and you definitely get the most out of them if you read assigned articles before. Sections are too large, but TAs are great!

This course with professor Katzenstein lacked signifgant structure, papers / policy memos while easy to write are irrelevant to lecture and reading material. Lectures were very dull, but the TA sections and discussion were fantastic. Overall, what I learned from this class was insignifigant despite engaging with readings and lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Truly an amazing class with very engaging lectures. He wants this class to be fun and enjoyable for his students. This was the first time he taught this class, so I project that it will be even better going forward. His political biases did not affect the course material. Highly recommend to anybody interested in learning more about IR

I took PK's class "America Confronts the World." The class was incredibly interesting, but very difficult. Get ready to engage a lot of abstract conceptual theories and do a lot of reading. The work is worth it, though - if you are willing to engage, you will learn a lot. Not to mention that PK himself is esteemed, funny, and incredibly smart.

PK is probably the most renowned and highly esteemed prof in the govt department, and it's true that his lectures are captivating. He is brilliant. Take his class for the inspiration and to hear his words of wisdom. But don't expect an A, and expect to read your butt off. This was probably the hardest class I've ever taken. Very bittersweet.

Best class I've ever taken! Both Katzenstein and his TAs want you to succeed and think critically. He really wants you to engage with an care about international relations in any context. The open mic sessions really help you and your friends engage in debates and informal presentations. He is also very funny and interjects this humor in slides.

GOVT 3557  makes you think critically about the intersections of politics, economics, and history in novel ways. It's also one of the very few classes that allows you to write a research paper on any subject of your choice. I am forever grateful to PK for giving us the opportunity to think critically and to produce my first serious academic writing

PK is one of the most inspiring professors I've had at Cornell, and taking GOVT 3557 was a privilege and transformative experience. This course will enable you to think more critically, challenge existing ideas and build your own arguments through a research paper. Do not graduate Cornell without having taken at least one of PKs classes.
This class is what distinguishes an Ivy League institution from colleges. PK is super well-prepared for each lecture. Be prepared for a lot of reading and writing, but totally worth it.

By far the most memorable and worthwhile course I've taken at Cornell. It really gives you a new perspective on world affairs and history through the HBS-case method with absolute awe inspiring lectures by Professor Katzenstein. Cannot stress enough how rewarding taking 3557 has been. Do not graduate without taking at least one PK course.

Professor Katzenstein reminded me exactly what I was looking for when I applied to Cornell. His lectures are outstanding and, although the workload is heavy, he manages to keep you interested and keen to work and read more. I feel privileged to have had the opportunity to be part of his class. I would recommend this course in a heartbeat.

Hands down the best class and best professor. Learned more in this one course than in my three years here. Class structure (HBS cases + real research paper) makes you think, work, and speak. Workload is a fair amount for how much you gain from this class. Very inspirational professor. Courses like this make the tuition $$$ & Cornell name worth it.

PK's latest class is indispensable to the education of anyone interested in politics, economics, international relations, monetary policy or financial markets. The interdisciplinary nature of the course, and the case study method through which we study and discuss, are incredibly valuable. It is precisely what I wanted out of my Cornell education.
Amazing course. Amazing Professor

Amazing class. By far the hardest class I took this semester, but also the most rewarding. Currently suffering while studying for his final but Professor Katzenstein makes you WANT to work this hard. Keep up with the readings, or at least have a google doc with reliable people to make summaries of all of them.

Wonderful class. Admittedly quite hard, but it is worth it beyond belief. Prof. Katzenstein will give you some of the best lectures of your time in college, along with unexpected humor and insightful discussions. Would recommend to any Cornellian.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Best class I have taken at Cornell bar none. Amazing orator who challenges his students while providing an ample support structure for when they need help. Very rewarding.

I absolutely loved this class. It's definitely not an easy class, but it's an important class. Professor Katzenstein is knowledgable and an amazing lecturer. I will definitely be taking more classes from him in the future.
Hard class with lots of reading material, but lectures are very interesting, and the professor is brilliant and funny. TA's may vary but mine was helpful and nice.
One of the best professors I've had at Cornell. Genuinely cares SO much about his students and the material. Lots of reading though!

Introduction to International Relations is a difficult class. It was also the best class I took this semester. This is a professor who truly cares about teaching us to think and who knows the value of a liberal arts education. Through open mic, open forums, and engaging lectures, he creates a lecture hall that feels like a community.
He's amazing. Best class ever!

Professor Katzenstein's intro to IR class is probably one of the most interesting and involved classes I will ever take at Cornell. There is a ton of reading, but by clearly summarizing and understanding the most important parts of each reading and the paradigms they cover, you will do very well in his class.

PK's course was on a level all its own. Case studies, daily debates, a research project, and a crash course on political economy rolled into one class. If you put in the work, it can be one of your most rewarding experiences at Cornell. Essential for any serious IR student.

Lectures were amazing . The discussion based nature of the course was one of a kind for a lecture of that size. The length and time given to the research paper  allowed students to do in depth research on their topic. The professor was  unbiased in his lectures, but would never hesitate to challenge students on their assertions.

PK is the best professor I have ever had, and his class on American Primacy was the most beneficial and enriching academic experience I've ever taken part in. He lives and breathes for teaching and will do anything possible to help his students. Head and shoulders above other professors.
I was told that this class would be  memorable and it was for many positive reasons.

This class enlightened me in my understanding of the complicated relationship between politics and economics, both at an international and regional level. The HBS case study method was challenging, requiring consistent in-class participation, which led to thorough engagement with assignments. TAs helped tremendously with the long research paper.

This class was hands down the best course I have taken at Cornell. I recommend it to anyone who is remotely interested in international affairs - any aspect of it! We had a very diverse class in terms of academic interests and that's what made the class great. PARTICIPATION is important!!! Besides, one research paper, which is not TOO tedious.

This was one of the best classes that I've taken b/c of how much it pushed me. But, if you are not interested in stepping outside your comfort zone, do not take this class. The TAs were a huge asset helping us learn the nuts and bolts of int'l finance, case study analysis and how to structure our large 25-30 pg paper.

Professor Katzenstein is an inspirational professor. GOVT 3547 was a demanding class as far as participation, but PK is a fair grader. As long as you prepare for class you will be able to succeed. For anyone with a genuine interest in international relations and achieving a global perspective, this is a great class and fantastic professor.
Great course with a unique setup. You must come to class prepared and ready to talk. The 25-30 page paper at first was very daunting but the TA's are extremely helpful and great. Learned so much.

Great course. One of the best I've taken at Cornell. Loved the setup with the case method. The 25-30 page paper at first was very daunting but the TA's are extremely helpful and great. Learned so much.

PK is my favorite professor at Cornell so far. I took GOVT 3547 with him during the Fall 2015. For the course we wrote a 25-30 research paper, read several economics/finance books, and read and debated many Harvard Business School case studies. I gained a lot from the course and feel more prepared to apply to MBA programs after graduation.

PK is a fantastic professor! I took GOVT 3547 with him this fall, having heard so much about his lecturing style and insights into world politics. Though I think he's still working out some of the kinks with the course's unusual style (case study-based, with a heavy emphasis on class participation), I learned so much from his lectures.

I took Gov 3547 with PK this summer. Having taken his Gov 1817 class as a freshman, I had high expectations. I wasn't disappointed. The lectures were wonderful, the class discussions valuable, and the TAs incredibly helpful. I would recommend this class to anyone with even a remote interest global politics/economics.

Took Govt 3547 in Fall 2015 with PK. Easily the best class and professor that I have had at Cornell!  I loved the combination of HBS Case Discussions along with amazing lectures by PK. I learned immensely and it really stoked an interest in the field of international political economy. Take a class with PK (esp HBS case method) before you graduate!

PK is as amazing in GOVT3547 as in his other courses! One part to highlight in this course, besides its HBD case method, is the requirement to write a full-length research paper, which you choose your own topic. The weekly TA session really helps to let you make step-by-step progress finishing the paper from literature review to the conclusion!!!

PK is finally back from Harvard. Actually, he brought back HBS case study method. Although an experimental course, GOVT 3547 run extremely smoothly during the semester and student participation rate, as I noticed, reached almost 80% at last, quite abnormal at Cornell, even at Hotel School. The course is really for every major!

GOVT3547 was the second course I took with PK. Similar to GOVT1817, US Primacy Challenged was one of the most inspirational courses I took during my time at Cornell; different from lecture style courses, GOVT3547 used HBS case method to study political economy of regional powers around the world. Full length research paper was assigned but no exam!

Katzenstein is amazing. Not only is he a funny lecturer, he also clearly cares about the students. Govt 1817 was a difficult class, because of the many readings. grades depend on TA. do readings or die
Will definitely not take his class again.
Tough class. Prof is brilliant in the classroom, possibly some of the most interesting lectures at Cornell. However, grades are at the hands of the TA who are often quite unfair.

Great Class, Great Professor - There's ALOT of readings but its totally worth it in the end. Took it as a freshman and it was overwhelming but I don't regret it at all. Got an A at the end of the course because I put in so much effort. It's do-able. You just need to care enough
Brilliant professor, delights with wit and knowledge in equal measure. Busy, but still willing to help outside of class.

The class is worth taking just to be in the same room with the guy. The readings, however, are unnecessarily long, and international relations theory sometimes has painfully little to do with practical events. But Katzenstein is truly an amazing professor. OK class, brilliant mind. Expect a B / B + with an average amount of work put in.
So much reading it was difficult to keep up. The lectures were interesting, but the tests are based off of your ability to memorize over a thousand pages of reading.
Tough class, difficult readings, brilliant professor

This is a very difficult class, although amazing in terms of how much you learn. The readings can be extremely overwhelming. Katzenstein himself stated at the end of the course that it was by far one of the hardest classes an undergraduate could take at Cornell. Save this amazing course for junior/senior year.

I loved this class! Professor Katzenstein is truly an expert in the field of international relations, and he is an amazing lecturer. The TAs are also very helpful. It is a difficult, and there are a lot of readings, but it is worth all the work. Just study super hard for the final!
Amazing professor. Interesting lectures. Difficult class and lots of reading, but it is worth it. Take this class.
GOVT 1817 is an amazing class.  If you take this class and really pay attention, you will not regret it.  Katzenstein is simply one of the brightest minds in International Relations.

Professor Katzenstein is an amazing professor. He is an expert in his field, and a great lecturer.  I sincerely enjoyed going to his class.  Yes, the material is tough and there is a lot of work, but the TAs are very helpful and knowledgeable. Professor Katzenstein challenges his students immensely, but you will learn a lot.

KATZENSTEIN IS THE MAN!!! This class is very difficult, but worth it. Even if you don't do extremely well, the material is fascinating (and I am not a Govt/ILR major). Tons of dense readings, but mainly INCREDIBLE TAs that help immensely dissecting them. Go to office hours. Study hard for the brutal final. This class is WORTH IT

One of the few professors I have had who takes the teaching part of his profession seriously. He expects a lot of reading, but the work load is completely worth it. He is extremely smart, a great lecturer who has perfected teaching this subject at the introductory level. High emphasis on critical thinking.
The discussions were really interesting but the lectures were always boring by the end because he was just talking (albeit about interesting topics) for an hour and a half straight
best IR professor, his class is intensive but the TA (nicole) made it clear. this class is less difficult than labor law with gold.
Hardest class I've ever taken at Cornell with the hardest prof, but the material I learned was all worth it... even the decrease in my GPA.

A great prof.  I was lucky enough to take his Senior Govt. Major Seminar and it was a real challenge but being in such an intimate setting really helped us think on a higher level, one fit for an Ivy League school.  He was rude with his comments via e-mail, and the workload was a challenge, but i'm glad I took his class.  He is an expert.

The readings are extremely hard. Katz is very interesting, but he can be confusing. He is unavailable out of class, and a lot of what you get from his classes depends on the TAs, who will practically determine your grade/whether you understand the readings. Lecture is for your interest, not the tests - which are totally based on the readings.

Insanely difficult, but no other class will measure up.  Tons of reading, you need a study group, but Katzenstein is such a good professor that you show up for lecture 10 minutes early.  Changes your whole perspective on the world.  Get to know your TA's preferences because they grade the essays and care about different things.
Hard class, grades not very fair

Though called an 'Introductory Class' this is by no means introductory. Katzenstein said so himself in his final lecture. This is the most amount of work I have ever had to do for a single class. Expect A LOT of readings, and expect them to be very hard. Katzenstein knows his material very well, but his lectures are not straightforward. VERY HARD.

There's no question that this class is a lot of work.  Nonetheless, Katzenstein does an amazing job teaching the material, and the class is well worth taking.  It is possibly the most eye-opening class I have ever taken.  It really gives you a whole new perspective on world events.
god-like. that's all i have to say about that.

absolutely brilliant. i can't stress enough HOW interesting this class is and how much of my hero prof katzenstein has become. no doubt it's very very tough, the readings are insanely intense and large in number, but it's worth it. this guy is unbelievable. TAKE HIS CLASS.

This class is a bit of a shock. There is an unmanagable amount of readings (which I still mangaged to complete before, but now have a study group for). It is, however a very interesting and informative class. Professor Katzenstein is one of the most brilliant professors at Cornell and is highly regarded in the government field.

Interesting lecturer, going at a comfortable pace; interacts with students. Spends beginning of each lecture going over current events and emails from students. Knows his subject well; one of the best in field. Readings fairly interesting, though WAY too much for 3 credits. Concepts learnt, though, will last you well beyond this class.

One of the hardest classes i've taken, but also the most interesting. He's a brilliant teacher who really knows the material and makes an hour+ lecture very interesting. The only thing that took away from his class was the horrible section. However, a good TA would only help improve his class bc the material can be very difficult. I RECOMMEND IT

TAKE THIS CLASS! It's a difficult course (lots of reading, abstract/theoretical concepts) but Katzenstein is a brilliant, engaging lecturer, and actually not that difficult to follow. Absolutely worth the work. Best class I've taken at Cornell by far.

An incredible lecturer.  I looked forward to his lectures, he knows a lot and makes the information interesting and accessible.  That said, it is a very hard class with a lot of reading, but it is all worth it.

He is usually a funny engaging prof. Yet, the amount of reading given was extreme. I have not seen more reading in 300-level government classes here that are even in the same field. He is an expert in IR, unfortunately his brilliance does not shine through in this intro-level course. Try one of his upper-level courses if you really want to take him
Great guy, fun lectures, but often confusing. The reading were good, but there were far too many for a 100 level class.
Take this class! Very hard and lots of reading (all on the exams) but SO worth it. Katzenstein is an amazing intellectual and professor at the top of his field.  He's my hero!

Best class ever- not easy, a lot of reading... but very interesting... almost nothing on the exams are from lecture- but it's worth it to show up, to do the readings, etc. Very relevant. The prof really connects otherwise abstract material to what is going on in the world.
Take this class... it will make you think hard, a lot of reading, but gives a new perspective on the world.  Especially important for this era we're in.
He was ranked by the economist as the most influential scholar in international political economy. His lectures are great, but you have to come prepared. Not an easy class

best class at Cornell. DO the readings. you cheat yourself if you don't. there is a lot to read but unlike other gov classes, this is all great. his lectures are extremely informative. he's also a genius. this is a MUST take. clear your schedule. this class taught me how the world really works.
Interesting, but had trouble staying awake during lecture.  Also, A LOT of reading.

Without a doubt, the best class I have taken at Cornell -- and also the hardest.  Seek out the TA's for help, and be sure to do most of the readings at some point.  In all honesty, this is the type of class makes Cornell a legitimate Ivy League school.  He expects a lot, but you'll learn so much about the world and be forever grateful you took 354.

He's very smart and has a lot of knowledge. Can be arrogant, but overall a nice guy (read lyrics of Sunscreen song on last day of class). A ton of reading, much of which you have to do. Exams are comprehensive and to do well you have to prepare far in advance. Also some basic economics knowledge is helpful for this course, though not necessary.
An amazing professor.  Katzenstein is brilliant and funny.  He's the best professor I've ever had and thanks to him I'm now a government major.  Be prepared to work a lot, but it'll pay off.
Lecture notes are a bit confusing but the man is a genius.

Best class I have ever taken.  Seriously.  Also perhaps the hardest class I've ever taken, but it's well worth it.  Katzenstein is absolutely amazing and now I'm gonna have to take every class he teaches.

If you have come to Cornell to learn how to think clearly and sharpen your mind, then don't waste your time on **** easy courses.  This course is life-changing and it is rare to find such a gem.  I hate to end on a cliche, but nothing really good comes without hard work.
He is one of the most pointless convolluted teachers I've ever had, what a waste of time
almost 2000pages of readings!  readings have no correlation to the lectures, though lectures are interesting.  he is very liberal.

Its a real shame this guy's not teaching this semester. Really smart and ties themes to current events very well. Class is not easy, lots of reading, but you can manage. Sometimes puts very personal, liberal opinions into lectures.
One of the most intelligent people I've ever met. Extremely friendly and helpful. A fantastic teacher.
nice man. bad lecturer.

Professor Katzenstein's grasp on political economy is amazing.  He is intelligent, articulate, and a great lecturer.  He adds current events into the class, making comprehension of the material very simple.  It's not a cakewalk, but not too hard either.

At risk of hyperbole, I'll just say he's the best professor I've had. period. His IR seminar is four hours at a stretch, and the class just never drags. What a fascinating mind, and as available as anyone would ever need outside of class. He is a gift.
Great Prof!  But it's a hard intro class.  He is one of the most brilliant professors you'll find at Cornell.  Make sure your in a good section that will help you handle all the reading.

Interesting course.  Nice teacher who listens to students.  Not always clear how the lectures tie in with the readings.  Never-ending reading. Still, good class.  Learned a lot.  Nice teacher--really knows his stuff--almost intimidating.

Goes well with the course, he knows his stuff. He, however, continuously bashes America too much. We understand he's a citizen now, but that does not mean he should force his negative personal views of America on his students. Overall, though, not bad.

Absolutely brilliant professor. You can't miss a course with him if you have any interest in Politics. The course is hard: lotsa reading. But you'll find him quoted on your readings! He's very knowleadgable.
Accent kinda rocks, even though it makes him harder to understand
Very interesting lectures. Great class

This is def. one of the best courses I've taken. The reading load is close to crazy but they're discussed in section so I wouldn't worry about it. The exams are not difficult and the lecture is very enjoyable!
Great professor... Great Guy... Great Lecturer.. Funny...and Hot as hell   If you do the readings (there is alot), the class is easy

This was probably the best class I ever took at Cornell. He is an amazing lecturer and absolutely brilliant. There's no doubt that it's tough, but you don't have to do absolutely all of the reading (as with any government class).
Lectures and course material are really interesting, but be prepared to read more than you probably will in most 300 and 400 classes.
This was the first government class that I took at Cornell.  He's a great lecturer but the amount of reading for the course was ridiculous.  Make him do the Terminator voice
Far too much reading for a 300 level course.  Interesting topic, however overt liberal bias evident in some lectures.

Had him as the third prof for WLC. Absolutely no indication of what was going to be on the final whatsoever. However the final was straightforward and easy and consisted of short answer definitions and two essays. Grading criteria was strict. As a lecturer he is okay but his module was by far the most interesting and was worth going to class for.
Third module in WLC. Prof Kuruvilla was very passionate about the subject matter and gave a straight-forward and fair test. Would recommend in either ILRGL 2350 or for other classes he teaches.

2nd most informative ICL lecturer (out of 4 so pretty good). gives a good history/background about economic systems in Asia, not as much about labor as I would have liked. Gives the hardest test but curves it. Test wasn't as bad as people are making it out to be, was a significant jump from the other sections. Also set up in a very annoying way
The worst among the four professors. Doesn't care about his students, everyone in the class think they failed. My A+ will turn into a B cause of him

The wildest approach to multiple choice I have ever seen. The test structure sets you up for failure as it makes you question your confidence and second-guess everything. Lectures are boring. The test focuses on little details you will never remember, without memorizing every slide and reading. TAs even warned us about the difficulty.

Craziest test I've ever taken at ILR. specific to the maximum. If u skip class u legit will not get above a 70 as the test was entirely based on his readings and his verbal lectures. Everyone thinks they failed
Do the readings, go to his office hours, take good notes and you will do well

So incredibly knowledgeable. Like other sections his final is the only grade youll get for his section but he will tell you the structure and criteria (DO THE READINGS!!!). He is so cool to talk to and incredibly caring, experienced, and smart. Watch out for a bad TA because they will be the one grading your exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Kuruvilla is the best. His phenomenal lectures make a very complex subject fascinating. If you work hard and seek out his guidance, he will help you succeed. One of the most deeply passionate and genuine professors I've encountered in the ILR School. Highly recommend taking his course!

He was the best out of the four professors and really seemed to care. His lectures were interesting, and the test was clear and very fair. He can appear a little obnoxious when answering questions, but it's clear he genuinely cares about his students. I wish I had talked to him outside of class and developed more of a relationship with him.
too much material for one exam
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Kuruvilla knows his stuff and has a ton of real world experience to back it up. He's really smart and no nonsense, which I appreciated. His lectures were always thought-provoking and interesting.
Test is tough, but I really enjoyed listening to lectures.  Has a ton of experience and knowledge about this topic, which makes his class more interesting.
really good at lectures, he engages you with his wealth of knowledge and experience, but has to speak more loudly
Good lecturer, has a hard-to-understand accent but his power points usually contain all of the necessary information and they are posted online.  Great class to satisfy international ILR requirement
One of the best!  Knowledgeable, passionate about the subject, brings his  practical work experience to make it really useful to students. Does a lot of research and shares it with his students.
A legend in his own mind, but only in his own mind.
clear, professional, great stories and experiences, global view...really opened my mind.
learnt a lot
great

grandiose facade is right. would rather dwell on consulting experiences rather than your dreams in office hours and before/after class. we need more ilr profs in asian labor relations, who care about teaching, who are able to connect with students. until then we're stuck with the alternative.

Kuruvilla has no interest in teaching or in his students-- seems like all he cares about is his research.  I went into his office hours to ask him about his past experience and he gave me indignant 1-word responses, obviously annoyed that a student was "bothering" him.  Boring lectures.  Avoid him.

My peers found him discouraging. Not a good mentor. Avoid his course. Negative attitude towards students. Students want professors that can encourage them, and strive towards achieving their dreams. If you are ambitious, avoid discussing your dreams with this prof. He puts up a huge grandiose facade

Mistakenly rated him 1 Very Unclear in previous review.  Meant to rate him 1 Very Hard (which isn't necessarily bad, as long as he's fair, which he is), 4 Helpful, 5 Very Clear.  So am rerating him in attempt to rectify that and fix his average score.

Neema Kudva-openly racist. Made remarks about my skin color and ethnicity out of nowhere which was not only inappropriate but felt rooted in racial stereotyping. Communication was dismissive, condescending, and driven by power rather than pedagogy. She is a poor representative of what academic leadership, or ethical scholarship, should look like.

She is very rude, and her mannerisms reflect this. She comes off as someone you wouldn't want to engage with. I don't understand why she resorts to such power plays. She uses foul language to draw attention to herself. Her response to many questions show that she is very insecure about things in general.
very unpleasant person
Guest lecturers were great. Sadly though, Neema's rudeness kept getting in the way.
Can't say I learned anything interesting, Neema was useless, and I'm so happy that the course is over and I fulfilled my requirement.

Neema is a great person with an interesting background. She only gives As to people who work very hard, and her readings and assignments are challenging, but if you put in he work, it will be one of the most rewarding, eye-opening classes you will take. Do the readings, show up, put in effort, and you will love it!

Challenging but rewarding. Attendance to sections is mandatory make sure you attend. Long interesting readings. She may not seem like it but is approachable and is very knowledgeable. Prelims weren't hard but grading was confusing. Overall a brilliant course, very interdisciplinary and broad but grounded by group assignment.

Though this class might have a pretty heavy workload, it definitely pays off in the end. Neema isn't about babying students through the course--you're really on your own to interpret what is said in lecture and apply it to the essays and the midterm. Overall, I highly recommend the course to anyone who has the time and energy that it requires.

Yes, this class is tough but you will learn a lot if you put in the effort. I enjoyed the material and Neema's enthusiasm and knowledge of the topics.  I probably wouldn't recommend it as an elective because of the workload though.

No notes on slides so you have to pay attention to every word she says, and she always goes after class is over. It feels like she just regurgitates the readings outloud and you can't skip class because attendence counts. The TAs grade harshly but they're on your side and will try to help, but Neema expects everyone to be studying all the time.
Incomprehensible, lacking substance lectures. The tests aren't bad while the essays are graded by TAs who are instructed to not give many As and Bs.
Decent Prof, but doles out way too much work and takes attendance WAY too seriously.  Cool accent too.

Only take this class if you have to/if it's relevant to what you're studying. It is way too much work--both in terms of reading and essays if you're just looking for an elective. Neema is fine, but lectures can be confusing/scattered, while the TAs act like her loyal minions.
Uninspiring

Neema did not seem to care about improving her teaching methods or organizing herself to levels that don't drive students crazy. Can't recommend her knowing that there are better instructors in the department. CRP 3201 was completely useless despite its potential.
Loves to argue about silly stuff and as a result the class never gets to discuss key planning issues
Decent prof, but you gotta break your back to do well in the class.
Simply a bad teacher, intellectualy confused, and often ignorant of imporant books. But at least she knows how to hide it.

Minus whiney students and HORRIBLE TAs, her classes are wonderful but challenging. You learn so much if you actually do the readings (of which there are A LOT). She is VERY sharp, VERY engaging, and assigns fasinating material. I left CRP after that semester, but to me, she exemplified what a professor should be like- sharp and no nonsense.
Looking back on Neema's course, I realize that it is one of the best that I have taken at Cornell.  Lots of work, but worth it in the end!

i don't understand people who complain about a class being hard. what are you paying all that money for?  neema responds to students who put in the effort, and has little respect for those who don't -- i'd be the same way!

Not good. She explains everything unclearly. Whenever someone asks a question, she doesn't really answer the right thing... and she is very mean... The course itself is very interesting, but the TAs hate her...... The workload is definitely not  3-credit like.

Neema makes this class harder than it needs to be, but nevertheless, she is awesome. Despite the horrible TAs I had and the difficulty of the class, everything else was fine. I feel I learned quite a bit.

I initially struggled in Neema's class, but she helped me all throughout the semester. Do all the work and attend lectures, and you will be fine. As others have said, she is easily available and a very nice professor.

I disagree with the previous comment. Professor Kudva is always willing to help. If you are struggling with your papers, write a rough draft and take it to her. She might be very strict and indeed does not easily give away A's, but she is not unfair. The main problem is that most students expect to get an A in this 100-level class.

Arbitrary paper grading standards that were "beyond articulation", would berate the class at any given point for a number of reasons, generally cranky, took an interesting subject and removed any kind of scientific or academic grounding. Worst class I have taken at cornell.
Excellent professor. Not an easy class, but Neema is very fair. Great class overall.

Kurt is knowledgeable and respectful - especially as a non-Indigenous scholar. He is receptive to feedback and brings in guest lecturers on things that he knows are not his strengths. Lectures can be dull, and he rambles, but everything is fascinating. Warning - quite reading-heavy (~150 pg/week). But, great people, great vibes all around!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Kurt is awesome. Indigenous North America is a class everyone should take and he tackles an incredibly tough topic very well. I've learned so much from this professor and can't recommend him enough. The books and readings are interesting and lecture enjoyable. He is also very kind and really cares about his students and the subject.

Very good professor! Lectures were engaging, readings were useful and interesting, and the workload wasn't too bad. Essay feedback was very helpful, grading was very fair. Genuinely interested in what the students think about the issues discussed in the class.
Great Professor. Class was super interesting and cool topics. Dude is super chill and fun. Highly recommend.
He is extremely boring and everyone is asleep. He talks forever in a monotone voice.

Super easy fws about a really interesting topic. Professor Jordan likes people to participate but if you do the readings its easy enough. Nice grader who truly wants to see improvement, will give a good grade if you show curiosity

Very nice, sensitive professor with humor, you are graded by 3 papers and participation alone. Class topic was interesting and we had numerous guest lectures that added to what we were discussing nicely.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Excellent lecturer; really brings material to life as he's lecturing, loves to make funny self-deprecating jokes. Grade for class is almost entirely 2 essays and 2 tests so no room for error, and for the tests you really need to study because the class covers SO MUCH material. Grading standards are high, but he curves at the end of the term
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Jordan's lectures were easy to follow and thoughtful and this made the material understandable for someone like me who had literally zero knowledge of archaeology/anthropology. He is caring and kind and easy to approach: he wants to help! Pro tip for class: take notes on the readings as you go along--will make the papers so much easier.

He is genuinely a nice guy and very passionate about the class. Lectures were clear, although his PowerPoints were too wordy and the class would get boring sometimes. He would occasionally crack a few jokes which I appreciate. The exams were fair, although his additional assigned readings could make the in class essays easier.
Kurt is passionate and knowledgeable. I'd recommend ANYONE take his Indigenous Ingenuities class if he's still teaching that with Jolene Rickard. Very interdisciplinary, creative, and fascinating.

Good lecturer and a great guy. He really cares about archaeology and Native American culture. Extremely approachable and will work with you to help you do well in the class. Readings aren't totally necessary (no discussion) but they benefit you a lot on the exams and papers. Tests are pretty hard and very specific. Highly recommend.
Good writing seminar in my opinion. He expects a lot from the essays, but grades fairly and has a lot of interest in the subject, which makes the class more enjoyable. Would recommend.
An extremely dedicated professor who really wants to help his students. You WILL improve your writing if you take this class. Be prepared to put in the work, but it's definitely worth it.

I can easily say one of the best professors at Cornell. Very clear, comprehensible, very fair grader, if you put the time into the essays he will give you an A or A-. Very dedicated and approachable and always willing to help. His lectures are never boring. I would very highly recommend this writing seminar. Absolutely amazing guy.

He's a great guy, extremely helpful and knowledgeable, and takes his classes seriously.  He'll do anything for you if you show interest and dedication.  He expects what college professors should of their students.  I would recommend him to anyone

What a nice guy. He may be a tad bit shy/nervous and not the best public speaker but he's knowledgeable about the subject and passionate about it, and if you go to him for help he is always there and very understanding and kind. Only negative is that he expects REALLY good papers and really detailed, hard grader. Good class overall, learned a lot.
This class was not very difficult, and tests were very fair. The readings outside of class were often boring and tedious, but the lectures were pretty good.

If you do your work, the class isn't that hard.  It's just that people think this is an easy A class where you get an A just for showing up.  I didn't do really well, but I definitely got what I put into the course.  Lectures are sometimes boring, but you NEED to go to know what's going on (unless you buy takenote).
Class readings are pretty good, a few dense books though, lecture is interesting, tests are VERY straightforward, you'll know exactly what to study for.
He is very boring to listen too. Of all his lectures I don't think I stayed awake for any of them. He has a monotone voice what tends to put people to sleep.
No Comments
"I wish I could make you sorry."

Had him for statistical mechanics and math phys. Lectures are generally good and he's nice (underneath boomerisms) but I found his tests are frustratingly difficult (and were 80% of the grade...) I did well on the HW's but particularly for statistical mechanics the exams felt more like a test on how fast you can do math rather than testing physics.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great guy. He doesn't even make us add. He knows what he's talking about.
Looks like Adam West, but he's still my favorite all time professor!  You better know your math though!

This is the only professor I didn't like that I would recommend. He doesn't sound like he is speaking to the class when he is teaching, which is weird. He wrote the textbook and teaches word for word from the book. The class covers chapters 10-15, which are totally unrelated. He is a very serious person, but intends to be helpful I think.
Best math class ever. I am a practicing engineer and constantly go back to the book/notes. Kisses rocks.

Kusse is one of the most iconic professors you will ever have. Students will fear him and love him at the same time. He knows his material, but isn't the most willing to look at problems another way or admit he is wrong. In any case, he's a cornerstone to the AEP degree, so you might as well learn to love him.
The best professor I had at Cornell. He can make one understand just about anything. Wherther you remember it the following week is up to you
Probably my favorite professor I've had at Cornell.  He's very clear and says some pretty hilarious things.

Kusse is a strange guy.  Sometimes if you see him in the hallway and he'd look like he doesn't want to talk to you, but he's actually helpful and nice if you approach him with questions.  His classes are tough -no questions about that.  The problem sets take a long time to do, but everyone should get a decent grade if you put enough effort into it.
Knows the subject inside and out. Very clear and well-prepared lectures. He's also guaranteed to make a few hilarious remarks throughout the semester. 321 and Kusse are unique to the AEP experience.
Very clear and thorough.  Teaches very closely to the text.  Homeworks can be very challenging.

One of the few professors who really cares about the students.  He, unlike most professors, shows his respect for you as an intellectual.  He is definitely well-liked by most students.  Also, his book is very clear.  Tied with Tomas Arias as best professor I've had at Cornell.

haha, what can you say? he wrote the book on mathematical physics. no, really, he did. his lectures are good, but homework takes like 3 hours per problem. It's a class worth taking, but if you're aep you don't really have a choice so you might as well enjoy it. be warned: sometimes he eats students for lunch.

One of the best professors in the engineering college.  He knows the material intimately and he literally wrote the book. Witty and patiently helpful with the rather difficult problem sets. Almost always an extremely lucid lecturer.  Although repeated questions that fluster him are met with sarcasm, his style is pretty much lighthearted teasing.

He knows the material very very well and can explain anything. Extremely helpful - whenever problem sets are due he will walk into u-grad lounge where people are working on them and ask if anyone is stuck or needs help. Will spend as much time as you need with you personally to help you understand it. Best Professor at Cornell.

As a instructor, Kusse does not present any material not mentioned in the text book he wrote.  He is very helpful and clear and knows the material very well.  Also very funny and witty; some students may not like his sarcasm, but I always find it funny.  First professor in Cornell who actually seems like a teacher and not just a lecturer.

Best professor I have had so far.  Though students like to give him a bad reputation, and he likes to pretend to live up to it, he knows the material cold, is very helpful, and really cares about your education.  He's a genuinely nice guy if you give him a chance.
yea, he will eat ppl who ask questions.
Possibly one of the best teachers at Cornell.  He is very good at helping students out when they don't understand something.
Not bad.
Extremely clear and witty. Kusse grows on you throughout the semester, and he does a great job at making a difficult course as painless as possible.
pretty rough, attacks anyone who asks questions. not ethusiastic in teaching, mistakes often.
Difficult course, but he did a pretty good job teaching it.  Problem sets and exams are hard though.
soo patient
A good teacher, very clear and usually patient.  Funny too.
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments

Really like to dramatize and escalate even minor issues. Frequently uses so-called “humor” that is distracting rather than engaging. Consistently avoids giving direct answers to students' questions. Fails to provide clear, constructive, or developmental feedback on coursework. What a waste of oxygen. How tragic.

Professor Rob Kwortnik clearly has solid industry experience. That said, he tends to play favorites and makes a lot of jokes that miss the mark, especially the more inappropriate ones. He does not know where the line is.

He is pretty self-focused, and it can make his classes tough to sit through. The overall class experience is not great
Condescending communication instead of constructive. If you value an open discussion, his class can be your worst experience ever.

while the content is interesting the homework is intended to be answered by a 4th grader. there is just too many works where he asks the same questions time and time again 
i would not take this course again nor would i recommend it

Course content is quite limited to a superficial theoretical level, and so refuse to extend the content to practical.  Kwort himself refuses to update his knowledge and scope to current business model. You can feel condescending tone with an empty core all through his guides. He won't be articulating any vague comments he made to your assignment.
If you don't have any expectations on learning updated marketing skills and, more importantly, on your grades/gpa, feel free to take his course. : D
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Frankly, if you have the choice to NOT take this course, don't. Totally not worth your time and energy. No clear instructions and subjective grading system.

The best strategies to achieve high grades in this course:
1. Avoid if possible at all costs.
2. Only quote concepts and interpret models from the professor and the professor alone to make him happy.
3. Participate in this class and make him happy.
4. Schedule as many office hours as possible to showcase your dedication to higher grades in projects

Tough grader, yes! High level required in the class, yes! However, this class was one of the best marketing class I ever had. The teacher will give you extensive knowledge about service marketing. The project was really interesting and applied to real life problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Kwortnik is a memorable instructor for better of for worse. He is extremely knowledgeable of the subject and earnestly cares about teaching. There is A LOT of material thrown at you but if you act mature, pay attention, do the readings and you'll do OK! I wouldn't pay too much mind to the criticism he gets from other students.

I enjoyed both Marketing Management for Services and Introduction to the Global Leisure Cruise Industry classes that I took with Professor Kwortnik. Despite having a BBA degree prior to coming to this program, I still learnt new concepts from the marketing class. His constructive feedback allowed me to learn from my mistakes and resubmit.

Professor Kwortnik cares deeply about the success of his students and strives to deliver an active, engaging classroom experience. His course does contain a lot of work, but the frameworks he provides are useful and highly applicable for professional work. He gives students opportunities to resubmit major projects, which is fair & praise-worthy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Kwortnik is dedicated to his job and cares deeply that every single student who walks out of the classroom understands the material conceptually and is able to apply it in real life situations. His thorough feedback helps you grow as a thinker and writer. Put in some effort (read, participate, spell check) and you will thrive. Best prof!

Extremely opinionated! He would not acknowledge concepts from outside his own slides. He doesn't believe or trust students would read course material without testing them on it. Very nosy when it comes to issues in group projects.

This guy has no consistency in grading. Kwortnik will give you a bad grade if you write about things that aren't aligned with his personal beliefs even though the answer is correct. He gives very unclear instructions. Kwortnik takes his class too seriously when it is an introductory course. Do not take him if you want an open minded professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Kwortnik greatly cares for his students and their education. He never fails to answer any question and takes a great deal of time to get to know every single student. He is always up to date on industry trends and presents relevant information. Very engaging class.
Unprofessional (singled out students in a public manner), material was vague and feedback on graded materials was subpar at best.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He is the best professor I have had at Cornell.  His lectures are well prepared and entertaining (class is mandatory). He has a lot of real life experience in marketing for the service industry and shares great examples.  He is so funny but also really cares about his students. 2 exams and 1 group project make up your grade, not hard

I actually enjoyed his class and felt like I learned a lot. I got As or above for all my essays but was given a B in the class. When I asked to discuss my grade, he said it was because I had low participation. I never received any feedback during the class about my participation, and there was no objective grading policy for participation.

Phil 1112: American philosophy. Took this for FWS. Discussion-based class, but sometimes Kwiatek steps in to guide us in the discussion. 4-5 Papers, weekly 500 word annotations on readings. Gives good feedback and grades generously. Went through Emerson, William James, Du Bois, Jane Addams. Very nice guy, genuinely interested in philosophy.
Cares about his students and is passionate about philosophy. Would absolutely recommend.

Best philosophy professor I've had by a long shot. Actually took 2 classes because of how good the first one was. His Buddhist philosophy intro class changed my life irreversibly. I would recommend taking his classes that involve Buddhism for this reason, but otherwise he runs outstanding discussions, so I have no doubts about any classes.

Pretty good professor. She says things like "come visit me in office hours, I'd love to meet all of you", but then she doesn't ever seem particularly friendly or interested. Overall though it's a fun class, the textbook is good, and prof Kushnir is solid.

Very understanding of the stress that comes with a global pandemic, and TA's are very lenient. I took this as a science requirement and loved it (I usually hate science). There are weekly quizzes but they are easy if you watch all lectures and skim the textbook. There is a large final project but it is broken up so it's not overwhelming.

Prelims are factual and very doable, lecture slides provide most of the information you need, and the baby videos are absolutely adorable!! Prof. Kushnir cracks a joke from time to time, so make sure to laugh.
This class is really fun with tons of videos of babies. The grading policy is really nice- lowest of 4 test grades is dropped. Easy and interesting class.
Great and caring professor with lots of extra credit opportunities. If you are a good test-taker, you will succeed in this class, as it is all memorization.

She is very nice and funny. Clear lectures and lots of extra credits. Tests are okay - not too hard but include couple short answer questions. Tests materials are mostly from lecture. Would definitely take her class again if possible

Professor Kushnir's lectures are clear and she does a good job keeping the material interesting by including debates and podcasts. There is plenty of room for extra credit, which is very helpful, because although the tests aren't hard, you really need to know the material well to do well.

The class itself is doable. Just read the textbook alongside attending class and the extra credit can boost your grade. The professor seems really nice in class, but outside of class, she can be very dismissive. I decided it wasn't worth going to office hours after she kept asking why I didn't check w/a friend. Wouldn't recommend unless necessary.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She's really nice and encourages questions. There are four tests, and the lowest grade gets dropped. Tests are all multiple-choice, and take more from the lectures than the textbook. A good amount of reading is assigned, but it's really fine to just look at the vocabulary and charts. Each extra credit usually asks for a paragraph or two.

Professor Kushnir is a great person! She is very friendly and approachable. BUT the way she taught this class made it so difficult for me to actually enjoy the subject. If you are an HD major (Human Development), you're required to take a discussion class which focuses mostly on research methods.
Really nice person, loved this class

By far my favorite class so far at Cornell, and I'm not even an HD major. The material was super easy to understand to begin with, but Kushnir made me enjoy it that much more. Some tricky questions on tests, but the extra credit can pull you up a whole letter grade if you do it. Would definitely recommend as a fun elective!

Sweet professor. Always looking for the class to answer questions & talk, but no one does. Class is based on 3 prelims, lowest grade dropped. and 6 points of extra credit are provided that go right on your raw average. Several helpful TAs. Really interesting & easy class if you like psych or babies! Highly recommend. She loves talking to students

Professor Kushnir is the best.  She is super enthusiastic and cares about her students more than any other professor I've had at Cornell.  Go talk to her during her office hours and she will talk with you about anything, even if it has nothing to do with the course.  She might also be the smartest professor in HD.

Dr. Kushnir is fantastic! Very smart, knowledgeable, fun, and passionate about her field. She likes to challenge, and be challenged by students, but does so in a way that is inspirational and constructive. She really believes in her students and wants them to succeed.

Professor Kushnir is the best science professor I've ever had.  She is wicked smart, funny, and a bit of a goof.  Behind it all is one of the most amazing minds I've ever seen at Cornell.  She is like a science robot with the soul of an angel.
Interesting class, easy enough

Awful! Took her class as an intro level Human Development to fill a social science requirement and saw that all we do in class is watch youtube videos. Tests were written by TAs. Not a good prof at all.

Took this after Goldstein's psych 2090 - what a mistake! Kushnir teaches outdated studies and refuses to debate "controversial" topics (isn't that the point of critical thinking?). Grading is easy: agree with her simplistic take on HD. Got an A- by gritting my teeth and writing papers supporting material I knew was questionable or proven false.

Professor Kushnir is one of the best teachers I ever had at Cornell.  I graduated last year, and have spent a lot of time thinking about who really made a difference to me -- and Kushnir is one of the few.  She's a truly great prof!

I've taken HD2300 and HD 4490 with Prof Kushnir.  I like the way she teaches.  In 2300 she showed up to almost all of the discussion sections, but let the TA's do their thing, and for 4490 she does a good job of letting people talk about what they're interested in while staying roughly on topic.

Professor Kushnir is young, enthusiastic, and knowledgeable. She's very approachable if you ever need help. I learned so much about critical thinking and taking different approaches to examining the social sciences in her course. I highly recommend taking any of her classes!

Great lectures! Young and relates well with her students. Her courses are interesting, and difficult, but necessary if you came to Cornell to actually learn something. These other comments MUST have been posted by students who received a bad grade due to poor work. Prof Kushnir is fair, and passionate about what she teaches.
Tamar is frank and friendly. Her ideas are inspiring. Recommanded if you have lots of ideas and what to organize or theorize them.
I took "Children's Learning in Social Context" (HD 4990) with this professor. She is so cocky and is full of herself. I think she would keep talking if there was no one in the room.

Kyle Shen, while an accomplished researcher, can show immaturity when students ask him for help in his class. He has told students they should drop the physics major because they asked a question he didn't like. His lectures are clear and you will learn a lot, but he could be a lot more accommodating in helping students in his course.

Extremely insightful and entertaining lectures and problem sets. Material can be challenging but the class is structured and graded in a way that doesn't punish students for taking the harder option. I'd recommend sticking around for an extra 10 minutes after lecture to listen in on Prof. Shen's Q&A which cover many subtleties of the subject

Professor Shen's class was probably the most engaging online class I took. His explanations were clear and understandable. Expect to spend considerable time trying the psets and going to office hours for help on them. He is also considerate if you have any issues with the course and is willing to help you achieve a good grade in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Shen is a great and engaging professor perhaps the best I've had yet. The content is HARD (coming from a literal physics major) but put in the work and you will get a lot out of it. The workload is on the heavier end for time but it does really enrich the understanding of the material. Clear he cares about students too.

Shen was quite a figure on the tongue of people in the class. Many things and many stories you will hear of him and people will fantasize about him.... The class is hard and might be a shock to many of the students (including me) coming into a physics degree. But you get out of the class with a lot of new skills that is necessary for any physicist.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Extremely hard class, but Professor Shen definitely made it bearable. He offered a lot of options for you to get help when needed. Lectures were very clear and precise, and he clearly had the best grasp of how to do a zoom lecture out of all my professors. If you're a phys major, def take the class. If not, probably want to stay away.
A rude awakening to the life of the physics major. Work very hard and go to every office hours and you might be able to pull an A-. He's so cool and one of the best teachers I've ever had
He is a very understanding professor and very accessible, is willing to help you and accommodate as much as he can. Very good lecturer. Clearly cares about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: The best lecturer I've ever had. I already enjoyed physics but I've never been challenged to understand it more than in Shen's lectures and in the homework he gave. You really shouldn't miss lectures, the notes get posted but you miss LOTS of detail. Plus he makes them fun to be in.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Probably the best teacher I have ever had, although I am only a freshman. Not only does he know what he's talking about, he also is able to convey it in a clear way. If you're taking 1116, do it in the fall so you can have Shen.
His class is really hard, but he is a great teacher. Very enthusiastic. He is much more interesting if you talk to him outside of class, he gets kind of nervous in lectures. He is soo attractive.

Great professor, really makes lectures lucid. The homeworks are leagues more difficult than the lectures however, which can be frustrating. Also, lectures are carried out in a group fashion; students are assigned to random groups of 3-4 and take in-lecture quizzes together.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very good professor. For 2213, he does a great job in dealing with huge lectures and a huge amount of material. He makes lectures interesting. The only thing is the lecture material is hard to relate to the hw and discussion stuff. Get the textbook even if it is not required. It's hard to know what goes with what between the lec, dis, and hw.
He records video lectures before class, and uses learning catalytic in lecture and sections. Videos are very clear and helpful. He's very enthusiastic about physics .
great class

Prof. Shen is a great professor. First physics class I have ever taken, and he sparked my interest in it. The class was not even close to easy if you have never taken AP physics, but he makes it worth it. So glad I took his course.
Excellent professor.
Professor Shen is a boss.

Amazing prof. He is extremely helpful, clear, and possesses a frightening amount of knowledge about physics. If you take his class be prepared to work your ass off. The problem sets are very tough: they require exceptional ingenuity and conceptual skills. This class makes you earn every point of your grade. Every point earned, however, will feel amazing. If you dare take this honors level course at an ivy league noted for its tough curriculum, by all means go for this one. Just be prepared.

This professor is AMAZING. He is extremely clear, has a brilliant sense of humor, and is very caring. He makes the course very very intellectually rigorous however.. but you learn so much about physics that the hard work pays off. One of the best professors at Cornell, without a doubt!!
BEST physics teacher ever! He really makes you think, and also makes you love physics! Awesome guy.
I love professor shen!!!

Awesome teacher.. very very helpful and great lecturer.. but this class is VERY hard. the class goes into very advanced math covered in sophomore level classes. ONLY take if youre an AEP or Physics major.
Best. Physics. Prof. Ever.

AWESOME teacher and amazing person as well. Very interesting, and goes out of the way to help students (ie - posts Pset solutions / lecture notes online). Very tough course though. Prepare to work hard.
absolutely amazing - very very clear and organized. very very cool / awesome guy as well. class is VERY tough - be prepared to work hard.
great prof, really shows that he cares.  Does a great job making the class organized
GREAT professor. Very enthusiastic and knowledgeable, very willing to help.

Quizzes, homework and exams will really make you think. Hard. This course is not an easy one, but Kyle Shen attempts to make it as enjoyable as humanly possible. A man with great teaching skills and an even greater character.

Awesome professor. Really helpful. Goes out of his way to make sure you understand the material. Always answers e-mails quickly, knows everyone's names, has field trips, gives out candy. Class is very difficult. Exams are awful and the problem sets will take over your life. take this class if you dare

Amazing professor, one of the best here at Cornell. Works hard, cares about students, and always does more than anyone would demand from a professor. Lectures were amazing, entertaining and never really dull.

An absolutely wonderful professor and a great introduction to college level physics. If, like me, you have never had a serious physics course, Shen will make you work. But he is a great teacher and truly cares about his students. He is definitely one of the greatest professors at Cornell.

Kyle Shen is a great professor!  His lectures are clear and prepared.  He cares alot about the class and will go the extra mile to make sure everyone is happy.  Only downside is his prelims and final are VERY hard.  I enjoyed this class very much

Kyle Shen was an awesome professor. He was a very enthusiastic teacher and eager to help. His quizzes were sometimes hard and tricky, but they helped us learn the material for the prelims. He really went beyond the call of duty in making extra handouts and example problems. Plus, Kyle is a genius and a rock star too!

Kyle Shen is an amazing professor!!  He puts so much of himself into helping his students because he really cares and wants us to learn.  He explains things very clearly, thereby helping us actually make sense of physics in the real world.  Highly recommended.  :)

The GOAT of all Gen Chem Classes. Lancaster was funny, and understood how much students typically dislike the subject, so he tried to make it as enjoyable as possible. His exams were tough, but his final compensated for that heavily. Would take his class again just to experience his in-class demonstrations for the first time. Definitely tenured.

If there is one class I could retake at Cornell, it is CHEM 2070: General Chemistry I with Dr. Lancaster. Not only is he hilarious and a chemistry legend, but he also has deep respect for his students. He actually wants to know his students and help them achieve their goals. I couldn't have had a better intro to Cornell and chemistry thanks to him.

My favorite professor that I've had at Cornell so far! He was very clear on how to succeed in his class. Office hours were always helpful just to get a greater understanding of the material. As long as you did the practice problem sets he posted and the practice prelims you should do well.

Lancaster is the goat fr. He is an amazing lecturer, and incorporates just enough conceptual explanation and interesting details to keep the otherwise fairly dull gen chem course content interesting. However, he still finds the time to do examples which are helpful. He definitely has the most joie de vivre of all the chem profs. love love love him

He is one of the better general chem professors. He is genuinely hilarious and if it were not for that factor I would not have shown up to class. Class felt entirely useless as his style of lecturing is fast paced and focuses on the theory behind chemical concepts rather than how to solve problems. The book does a much better job. curve is a B-
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: A very hard class and the way to get a good grade is to study and redo all the exam practice problems that he makes and provides for the class along with the practice prelims. I can tell Dr. Lancaster is a smart person but sometimes it is difficult to understand what he is saying because he says it so fast or assumes we know what he's talking about
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I have nothing against Professor Lancaster, he's genuinely a good guy and evidently very knowledgeable and passionate about chemistry. That being said, he isn't the best lecturer and has a tendency to present too much information too quickly. Beware of the lab reports as they are graded very strictly.

Kyle Lancaster obviously enjoys his job and does his best to share his love for chemistry with his students. The material is difficult and it is important to show up to lecture and do as many practice problems as possible. Take advantage of the resources available, like chem 1008, LSC tutoring hours, and lab office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Lancaster is an amazing professor. He is clearly very passionate about chemistry and wants others to feel that same passion. He brought energy and some fun to lectures and is a great guy. Lectures are pretty dense but I found the textbook helped a lot. He's also incredibly available during office hours and I found that time extremely helpful.

Dr. Lancaster cares about his students and wants you to succeed. Gen Chem at Cornell will always be one of the biggest "weed-out" classes, but Lancaster makes it interesting and more manageable. Don't skip lecture... 90% of them help you stay up to date and on topic with the class. If you have Dr. L for 2070, consider yourself lucky.

2070 overall is just a grind but it was a decent time. The class is very hard if you have no chemistry experience but that just comes with the class. Prepare to spend a lot of time outside of class understanding concepts. Lancaster himself is a nice guy and is clearly passionate about what he does. Cracks some fun jokes in lecture but is a grind

Very energetic lectures, though are hard to follow if you haven't read the textbook beforehand. However lectures are not always super relevant to the knowledge you really need for HW/prelims, rely on psets for practice w that. Prelim problems are monstrous but not completely unfair, do lots of practice prelims to prepare.

Lancaster is very passionate about chemistry, and hes a great guy. But, lectures do move really fast. DO NOT miss a lecture, you will be chronically behind and very stressed. He also sometimes rambles about info that isn't necessary. The tests are designed to be impossible, but don't worry the curve will save you, as it did me.

Very kind, very passionate, but not very good at ensuring understanding of those new to the concepts he teaches (most students). Lectures move VERY fast, and he sometimes dances around topics to teach things that aren't relevant which can collude the actual content being tested on. However, it's clear he's just passionate about teaching.

dont give this guy celsius and flammable fluids. a friend and I found it hilarious that he plays Rust (I'd love to play w/ him). 
He's obviously very knowledgable not only in chem but bio and as many premeds are in this class, it's very useful. His "this is not on exam" lectures are the best. 

Btw, this is my first in-person chem class ever. pain.
PAIN PAIN PAIN PAIN PAIN PAIN PAIN

Dr. Lancaster is a great professor, and his passion for chemistry is evident. He is very engaging and entertaining, and his lectures are easy to follow as well. His exams are very fair, and he provides all the resources for every student to succeed. The labs for the course are boring and annoying, but they are only 20% of the grade.

Dr. Lancaster is a really engaging and entertaining lecturer but lectures could be confusing at times. Labs really depend on what TA you get so hope you get a good one. Exams were very fair and he genuinely wants everyone to do good in the class. Overall, a good professor just a difficult class.

Prof. Lancaster is the best chemistry professor in the department and the best I've had at Cornell. Lecture is pretty much mandatory since the class moves fast and if you miss a class, it's impossible to catch up.
