Office hours & undergrad study sessions were also super helpful, and if you understand the homework thoroughly, you will get an A.

This class covers incredibly difficult content but there are a lot of resources available. OH not mandatory but I don't think I would've passed the class without attending every week. Lectures move incredibly quickly so be ready - I don't recommend ever skipping lecture as not a lot of materials are posted online, it would be hard to catch up
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Although his lectures were great and explained the matter in a clear way, he can be dismissive of questions in office hours. There were however a lot of TAs that could also be used, so you just have to find one you like. The labs were slow and annoying.

He's very knowledgeable and funny at times. However, grading is tough and those PSETs are brutal. While lectures and office hours are technically not mandatory, they are almost pseudo-mandatory because he doesn't really post everything he teaches and PSETs are borderline impossible without them.

He was very understanding of the struggle of this year for students and curved the class to a B+ instead of a B for us. Tried to make zoom as fun as he could and dressed up with his TA every so often. Material is pretty standard chem matieral but was a lot of material bc gen chem. Taught the material pretty well too.
You have to work for a good grade
Enthusiastic about material, but he teaches really fast and his test questions are lengthy and require quick critical thinking... definitely recommend taking 1070 if it is available.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Kyle is a funny man, but gives off an aura commanding respect. Clearly very intelligent, and likes to throw in memes and references to lectures. Course is very structured and rigid, in both grading and material. You *can* skip class if need be, but material makes much more sense in lecture than in book. Labs suck, but not terrible. Beware prelims!!

Good professor who really tries to keep students engaged in class but moves very quickly in lecture and it's hard to keep up/learn the material from lecture alone. Class/tests are graded fairly. Class takes a lot of time and has a lot of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: You can tell he loves teaching chemistry to students and tries to make lecture as entertaining as possible. He always tries to joke around during lecture and actually wants you to learn the material, rather than memorize it. His office hours are great too and he really takes the time to teach you a concept you're really confused about.

Professor Lancaster is not only an engaging lecturer, but he is also incredibly knowledgeable and is truly concerned with helping students find an interest in chemistry. His jokes are genuinely funny and lighten up the lectures on days when the topic feels like its over your head. I would definitely recommend this class for a rewarding challenge.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's the best. He loves to blow things up and is the best and most entertaining teacher! His explosive personality really makes the class interesting and bearable. 15/10 would recommend.
Tried to be funny/entertaining
funny guy, but hard to keep up with his lectures. If you have some chemistry background you should be fine for the first half of the course. no practice prelims :(
Dr. Lancaster is absolutely incredible. Great lecturer. Easy to learn from. Reasonable prelims and labs. Class was moderately difficult, easy A if you put in the work and time.

Dr. Lancaster is, hands down, one of the best professors you'll ever have in any Chemistry class at Cornell. He is always clear and explains complicated concepts in a simple way while managing to entertain the class at the same time. Always willing to help students in office hours and was a DJ at one point in time.

Brilliant professor who plans his classes amazingly. Everything in his lecture is important and the textbook is only helpful for practice problems. The best way to study is to do the book's practice problems right before the exam and review notes. Amazing guy.

Kyle's brilliant, and has the ability to make difficult concepts seem clearer; the times he had a sub because he was off giving lectures elsewhere, everyone just wanted him back. His test questions aren't that difficult, but sometimes, there's just too many. The curve will then either save or ruin you. Definitely recommend 1007 along with this.

Although I did not enjoy Dr. Lancaster's course due to my dislike for chemistry, his enthusiasm for his field and his ability to explain concepts made the class bearable. He's a great professor, and although his class may be tough, if you work you can learn.

Lancaster is truly amazed by chemistry and wants each of his students to feel that same passion. He's a clear lecturer and hilarious. His test are fair but challenging, and make for good opportunity to score above the mean. Take CHEM1070 & you won't regret it (will definitely help your grade). Would definitely take another class taught by him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Lancaster truly cares about his students and wants them to care about chemistry. Tests are difficult but fair. In lecture, he is clear in his explanations and writes important notes on the board. I recommend going to office hours to get help (not just before tests). He is inspirational and can make complex concepts of chemistry fun. Great guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Such a funny, passionate, and overall great professor! He genuinely cares about his students and wants them to succeed and enjoy chemistry. If you've taken chemistry before, this class shouldn't be that bad for you, but you will definitely have to put in the work.

Dr. Lancaster is an amazing professor who makes fair tests and really makes a subject I thought was boring much, much more interesting. I didn't take AP Chemistry but would recommend taking CHEM1070 in addition to this class to help keep up with the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Kyle is an INCREDIBLE professor-- hilarious, dynamic, and brilliant all around. I went into the class with really weak foundations in chemistry, but Kyle is such a clear explainer and has such an effective teaching style (writing all essential notes on the blackboard) that it's manageable to keep up and do well if you put in the time.

Lancaster was a great lecturer! His tests were completely fair, and if you took AP chemistry in high school and understood it, then you'll do pretty well in his class. Can't speak for those who didn't.

Great professor: teaches well, knows what he's talking about, personable guy. Go to office hours at least once to get to know him (and perhaps more than once because it's not an easy class!). You should go to class because he teaches the material well and it's hard to get it from the book. Speaking of the book, no need to buy anything but Sapling.
Great teacher. Talks so fast and super easy to get behind.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Even though attendance isn't mandatory, you really won't be able to get the material anywhere else. He's pretty young (33?) so he still has enthusiasm for the subject and he's able to convey that enthusiasm in lectures. While some of the material is hard (prelim 2 average was 89/150), he knows it's hard and curves the class accordingly.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Lancaster is an all around great guy, in and out of the classroom. You can definitely tell that he genuinely wants his students to be interested in chemistry. However, just because he wants everyone to love chemistry as much as he does, does not mean that the class is easy. The average grade on prelim 2 was around a 55% so don't expect an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Exams are difficult but plenty of help is available if you are willing to take it. Lancaster keeps lectures interesting for the most part and brings humor to what can be a more dull subject.

Prof Lancaster definitely expects a lot, but gives a lot too. Chemistry has never been my strongest subject but he made me love it and was always available for extra help. His lectures are hilarious and he knows how to relate to students. Definitely a gem.
Probably one of the best professors that you will ever have at Cornell. He makes difficult topics so easy to understand!
Lecture was actually enjoyable with Lancaster. Made chemistry accessible. Also in Forbes Top 30 under 30, so cool guy.
Really great teacher. You can tell he actually cares about and enjoys teaching. Exams are tough but fair.

Professor Lancaster is simply brilliant. He is one of those professors that truly and absolutely has a passion for his subject and has a blast teaching it. Students look forward to his lectures and truly cares about them, always accessible to ask questions. I would recommend anyone reading this to take a course taught by him. You won't regret it

Super knowledgable guy, very engaging lectures. Homework assignments are long and challenging but very well-written and overall enjoyable. Available both during stated office hours and at other times, and by email.

Prof Shuster is patient if you don't understand a topic. He will take the time to thoroughly review theory concepts. In my experience, if you really want to understand music theory, both 2101 and 2102 are essentials at Cornell. My musicianship has greatly improved since taking these classes. Puts the fun in fundamentals in my personal opinion.

Not to invalidate anyone else's experience, but I personally didn't see any of the concerning behaviors reported in the other reviews. He seemed like just a well-intentioned guy, perhaps with a strange fascination on Chinese martial arts (and some concerning YouTube recommended videos). Lectures were a bit unclear at times, but grading was lenient.

Extremely disrespectful - especially towards women. Made a joke that a student who was majoring in Philosophy and Music had parents who were disappointed by her. She cried. Passive aggressive in email as well as in person.

prof shuster loves to cold call and make targeted and passive aggressive comments when students are struggling with the material. he seems to insist it's all very easy even though it is in fact quite difficult at times and he doesn't really explain most of the material. he's also very disorganized and made some weird comments about autism and women

This class was incredibly disorganized (no syllabus) and fast-paced. Students weren't given adequate materials to be successful; there are no class notes, instead he writes on a chalkboard and cold calls with questions about information that has not yet been taught. The professor picks on students who do and don't know the answer.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Excellent professor -- she is kinda monotone though so I dozed off sometimes. Study slides and you will do fine on the tests. Final group project is easy if your group members are competent and share work evenly. Nothing was harshly graded. Most interesting class I took here and would recommend to any premed. Would take her again!

Plagues and people is a great class to take, especially if you are pre-med. I really enjoyed the small group work on Fridays and this was the only class at Cornell that I have genuinely been excited to attend. I would take this class with friends if you can as 30% of your grade is a group project. 2 midterms, use anki.
She runs a great course and seems to genuinely care about her students.

Excellent and passionate professor. Super knowledgeable about disease and disease vectors. Wonderful mentor, excellent lab to join as well. Could not ask for a better teacher. It is no exaggeration to say that getting to know Professor Harrington has completely changed my academic career for the better. Take ANY class by her. She's the best ever.
Very interesting class! Professor Harrington really wants her students to succeed. If you go to the lecture, you will do well!
Great professor and very engaging!

Prof Harrington is really sweet and very knowledgable on the topic of disease vectors. The class is only two years old, but as of right now the grading scheme is generous. You're graded on participation, a midterm, a presentation, and a final project (no final exam). It's a really interesting class (and I'm speaking as someone outside of entom)!
Super helpful

Very good professor, I look forward to taking her medical and veterinary entomology course next fall.  Really stimulated my interest in the subject.  Classes were really well organized and well taught overall.  Very approachable and knowledgeable.  I would highly suggest her as a professor.

Interesting material presented clearly. Lecture gets a little awkward when she tries to engage class by asking review questions... :/ Exams are fair; case studies are a nightmare. TONS of information- really need to keep current with studying.
very direct in terms of teaching.
Very good teacher. Interactive classes. Provides concepts first, then examples.
No Comments

There was 8 papers, each had a rough draft, peer review, and final. Gives you the questions to the papers ahead of time so you can begin writing as you please. The final is an in class essay that he gives you the questions for. He knows his stuff and can be interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Do the reading and you will do well. Tests can be difficult, but the class is curved in the end. Kyle is very intelligent, helpful, and down to earth. If you have to take Macro, I would take it with him.

Professor Kyle might be the best professor on the Cornell Campus. Lots of impressing experience combined with humor and academical honesty. He´s lectures are 100% easy to follow if you just listen to what he says. Tests are pretty easy and he follows the textbook chapter to chapter so its easy to look stuff up after class. Recommended course!

Kyle is smart and funny. He knows a lot about Econ. However, his lectures have a loose structure, and often ends up glazing over things that aren't in the textbook but are important. EVERYthing is fair game for final, even abstract and trivial things. If you love Econ, go for it, if not, it may be worth waiting someone else.
He's a great teacher and quite funny too. He always answers questions and makes the material seem not too difficult.

Kyle is a great professor. His lectures are always engaging (he makes fun corny jokes too), and he is always willing to take questions. The tests are a bit challenging-but just go to lecture and do the readings and you should be fine.

Teaching a class with nearly 300 people can be difficult, but not for Kyle. He has a booming voice & personality and sort of reminds me of Santa Claus. He makes a lot of stupid economist jokes in lecture to keep people awake. Some are funny. This class is very easy if you just do the readings, which are not long. Section & lecture are optional.

Kyle is a great professor. He is a genuine guy, he is funny in his own self-deprecating way, and he makes it all seem interesting. The test aren't too bad but some of the questions are a little misleading. Overall, take it!

Kyle hands out an agenda at the beginning of every class but rarely sticks with it. Lecture is solely him talking, no Powerpoint, and he can go off topic. In the end he winds up covering the most important things. Keep up with the textbook, do old exams online, and you'll be fine in the class.
Really nice and funny guy. His class isn't easy but he curves. You need to read the textbook to do well, and he requires you to read about 1 chapter for every class.

Prof Kyle is a pretty good lecturer and is clearly enthusiastic about the material. He's willing to help you if you talk to him after class.  He could sometimes be unclear and hard to understand, and he got off-topic a little too much.  He's really into real-world applications of concepts, which makes the class somewhat challenging.

I really couldn't ask for a better professor. He doesn't use notes or powerpoints when lecturing - doesn't need 'em. Regularly makes jokes, most of which aren't funny, but they keep you awake which is more important. He interacts with the class, not doing any Socratic method BS, but just asking easy questions to keep you active. Just awesome!
Tries to keep you engaged during lectures. My TA was probably the best one available and that helped a LOT. Do the past prelims and finals, they prep you quite well. The grading is fairly easy.

Prof Kyle does an excellent job of incorporating current events and issues into his lectures and exams. It makes the class both more interesting and relevant. I would recommend him to anyone. If you study and do the problem sets, you'll be fine.
Fairly funny and does a good job appealing to a lot of people. The lectures can drag a bit but the tests are very easy.
THe lectures are very clear and interesting. The problem sets have nothing to do with the prelims. He does not give out A+s unless u get 100%. Pretty mad at him ~

Professor Kyle is a professor who is very interested in his subject and this is conveyed in his teaching.  I had never taken economics before but was surprised at how clear and relevant professor Kyle's lecture were.  The average is a B or B+, which is easy to obtain if you pay attention in lecture and go to section.  Section answer hw questions.

easy class... just make sure you read the textbook. you can get away with not going to lectures but make sure you go to sections-- the TA's actually cover useful material that will be on the exams. one final paper that is pretty easy
ECON 102: This class is listed as 3 credits, but don't kid yourself; if you do all of the reading and all of the BUSYWORK problem sets on Aplia, it should be worth much more than 3.

Very interesting class, especially if you know nothing about ECON coming in to it.  Lectures not too structured, but prof very knowledgeable about material and always excited about teaching it.  Sections review material and do actual computation.  Great course no matter what major.
COTA wasn't as bad as others say.  Take it if you can, no final, but a paper, which was very easy.  Tests not too hard.

His lectures are not quite as structured as Wissink.  I wished the information was presented in a more definitive nature. The tests were okay. Not easy; but not hard.   Your TA helps you to understand the information alot, so choose a good section.
Take 102 from him. His lectures are okay, and you will learn from him. He is a very nice guy and really helpful. So long as you pay attention and do the readings, this class is very easy.

I am less inclined to think highly of Prof. Kyle, simply because his head TA cannnot get her act together. He should have been more thoughtful in his selection, she brings the whole cidate.ourse down, is unclear, and can't get anything right in her first email. Kyle should have used his Harvard education to pick a more suitable cand
TAKE THIS COURSE!!!!

Take 102 from him if he's teaching it.  Very clear lecturer and usually has funny jokes.  Problem sets may not correspond that well to the book or lectures but they're still fairly easy to figure out.
Very good at lecturing.  Very clear, uses diagrams well.  Not great in office hours.  Exams are medium, but final paper takes a while.  Good class overall.
Willing to help at any second, professor Kyle is perhaps one of the best econ prof's in the dept. I'd strongly recommend his 102 over any other.

Much more interesting lectures than I got in Econ 102.  Lectures explain the readings, so go to class (it'll help your grade a lot).  Fair tests, but not exceptionally easy. TA's vary, so section can be very helpful or awful
Kyle is pretty much what you would expect from a Harvard Ph.D. economist-- mustache, gray hair, really knows what he's doing; great lecturer.
easy tests, easy (weekly) problem sets, but they don't really correspond with what's being taught in class.  seems like a nice guy who tries hard to be funny, and sometimes can be.  knows his stuff
Very straightforward lectures. Find a good TA and go to their sections. Problem sets don't really correspond to the material. Fair, predictable tests.
A very distinguished-looking prof.  Much better than Wissink- good lectures, easy problem sets, and fair prelims
love that mustache
13 years ago, he was producing work that was truly futuristic and mind-blowing. (A phd well earned)  Nowadays, he just produces mediocre cardboard junk.  How has he regressed so much?
I'm glad he decided to start being a father to his kid. Lost all respect for this guy when he was out in Colorado.
I think its cute that he sounds like Arnold Schwarzenegger if he never got into steroids.  Class was ok.

His work you can find by Googling him is vastly different in quality & depth compared to what he teaches in classroom on the same subject matter. As such, Daniel Leithinger's class is profoundly underwhelming. He truly doesnt live up to his own reputation.

Don't be deceived by those ppl who give 5 - the average for this course is B+. Don't let this course ruin ur life. Spent a substantial amount of time on this course, but the grading criteria were unclear, making it hard to understand expectations. The final grade is disproportionate to the work required.

Underrated prof. Lectures are very clear and easy to understand. Attendance is optional but make sure to go because there are so many concepts that make sense once he explains them in class. Definitely the harder man econ professor but there is a generous curve applied at the end of the course. Dedicate ample time and effort into psets and studying

Leyden was a great professor. His lectures were clear and engaging, and he was very easy to reach outside of class. TAs had office hours frequently and were very helpful for problem sets. The exams were difficult but fair, and going to all lectures and reviewing problem sets helped. Leyden is also very understanding and clarifies any confusion.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Most students who do not do well typically don't show up to class. The prelims can be difficult, but the class is curved. Also, the prelims have parts that are very similar to some problem-set questions. If you show up to class, do the problem sets, and study or go to review sessions, then it is reasonable to get an A/A-

Leyden is an amazing professor. He cares for his students, and if you talk to him he is very understanding. His class is very difficult and I felt like I wasn't going to pass it, however, it is designed for you to understand it and to think outside the box. If you like econ, take him, if not, take Terry. Curve is very helpful for his class.

One of the worst professors in Dyson. Leyden tries as hard as possible to make his students fail; incorrect/vague lectures, dry, and (very) arbitrary grading. Lectures are useless and mostly irrelevant to exams. Going to TA OHs and learning concepts on your own is enough to get an A. Huge mistake to take his class over Terry's, who is much better!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Leyden has a dry humor and a fair sense of grading. To do well in this class you have to understand the material and not memorize it. The TAs and professor give plenty of opportunity for 1-on-1 sessions and office hours. Although some people find this class hard, it is one of the most straightforward classes in Dyson. Recommended!

Some people love Leyden some people hate him. I personally thought his class was extremely interesting, but it is definitely geared towards people who are very naturally smart/good test takers (I believe tests are 70% of your grade). The class rewards students who don't work that hard but are very naturally intelligent
If you go to OH, you will ace the class. He is clear about what is on the prelim. Very patient with students.

Ngl, hard class. Relatively tough material, but definitely work-thru-able. Leyden has tons of office hours and is flexible about meeting. Lectures can be boring but you learn cool stuff occasionally. Prelims are much harder than problem sets and limited practice questions given. Take advantage of OHs and ask questions. Super patient guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Made the class harder than it needed to be. And graded super hard. Would not recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: she teaches everything really well, and the quizzes help you keep up with studying. grades pretty fairly.

This class covers a lot of content, but is not hard if you memorize. Unfortunately, Dr. Nicholson is one of the worst lecturers I've ever had. Her slides are so unorganized: she attempts to fit the entire lecture in like three slides, jumps around from material to material with no clear organization and her lectures are too fast to take notes

Professor Nicholson is one of my favorite professor at Cornell. Her biochem lecture is manageable if you attend lecture and spend some time to study after class. No tough questions on exams and she's very fair on grading. 

She is approachable, kind, and caring for her students. Definitely recommend her lectures

Prof. Nicholson is super caring and wants to see students learn. There's a lot of content to memorize but that's just how biochemistry is. The TA study sessions are life savers and will probably teach you more than lecture. Class is not curved and average is A-. Something like 25% of your grade is essentially participation.
great professor wants to genuinely see you succeed. one of the classes that many premeds take, class is uncurved. you will get what you put in from this course, and you can get a lot.

Prof Nicholson is extremely nice and approachable. she is willing to help answering the most basic questions and always make fun jokes in class to bring more joy to the students. we have weekly quizzes, a midterm and a final, which are all fair questions.  in general, she is so great to work with

Prof. Nicholson has been by-far, one of my favorite professors here at Cornell. There are so many resources in the course, including the undergrad-led study sessions (which were so good), and if you go to everything, do all the practice (esp the prelims), and study ~30 min every day outside of class, it's pretty much guaranteed A.

nicholson was so kind and reasonable-- while biochem can be a lot, nicholson was super clear on what to expect for the weekly quizzes and exams (1 midterm + final). plus, we got 4 drops for quizzes and had other straightforward assignments that made exams weigh a little less
overall i actually really enjoyed the class and biochem as a whole now :-)

Professor was extremely clear cut on what you should know and be able to do. Her slides were a little crowded, but she still conveyed concepts well. Quizzes were helpful and not stressful and exams were very fair.

Linda is a genuinely kind person who wants students to succeed and provides clear learning expectations and objectives. However, she is not good at conveying information or explaining concepts in biochemistry. Although this course isn't autotutorial, it might as well be. You will be teaching yourself everything in this class, and it will be tedious

Her slides were kinda bad but she explained the concepts fine. It was very memorization heavy so attending lecture was necessary. We had weekly quizzes that helped me stay on top of material. The final was worth 40% of our grade with one prelim being worth 35% and the quizzes worth 25%. She also gave some practice problems which was helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Linda an incredible lecturer. She clearly put tons of time into her lectures and she provides a large number of resources like recorded lectures and written out notes. She is also very engaging, funny, and cares. She emphasizes exactly what you need to know for exams and practice exams are exactly like exams. Best professor Ive ever had.
She explain concepts pretty well and only test things that have been covered in lectures. This class has little homework, but is VERY test-heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Very understanding and lenient. Coursework is challenging

Excellent professor! Linda cares so much about her teaching , was very respectful of students' questions, and presented the material in a very clear manner. Prior to the class I had little knowledge of proteins and didn't like protein chemistry. I learned so much and now really enjoy protein chemistry!

Great professor, very in-depth and comprehensive coverage of the material. Over 1/3 of the grade is a group project. Unfortunately, she leaves all the assignments to be graded by her TA, which made the grading somewhat inconsistent with the lectures.

Grad level course in protein folding and dynamics.  Intense coverage of material, but more math than most people will probably use, and not enough coverage of software tools available.  Lecture slides disorganized.
I learned mostly on my own from doing her homework that lined up well with the exams. Her lectures were...interesting to say the least. Beware the final was harder than the prelims.

Super funny and caring professor, very willing to help even outside of class. Her homework is harder than her actual prelims, and sometimes you wonder in the middle of the exams how the questions can be so simple. Just go to class, do the homework, and do the most basic studying, and you can get at least an A-. Lots of partial credit in exams.
One of the best Professor at Cornell!

Canina is perhaps one of the best professors at Cornell! She cares deeply for your understanding of the principles and will take time to go over the material before pre-lims. Speak with her early, let her get to know you and she will help you along. Also very involved in the entrepreneurship community at Cornell. AMAZING PROF!
Professor Canina is great! She cares a lot about her students learning the material. She also wants students to get comfortable speaking up in class.
Tough but direct and cares enormously about her students. I learned more in this class than any other last semster.

Horrible professor. Her class is completely unorganized. You feel like the class content just get thrown at you from no where. There is no slides available, everything is just talked about and written down. Even the readings, she just says to read them once in class, and then would cold call random student and expect you have done everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Linda Canina was one of my most memorable professors at Cornell. Her unique sense of humor and lecture style kept me engaged throughout the hour-plus lecture, and I felt I learned a lot from her class. She LOVES to call on students- it kept everyone on their toes and definitely made class more interesting. Would highly recommend this course.

Attendance not mandatory, but GO TO CLASS. Book is not as important as her lecture slides. All the concepts on the test are on the slides. Take notes of her explanations in class. Copy everything she writes in class. Redo the problems. Understand the concepts behind each step. Problems on prelims and final  problems from lecture. I learned a lot.

Pr. Canina's lectures are interesting, and should be treated as a supplement to the book. Tests are usually drawn from the book, but by going to the lecture it is possible to determine on what they are going to focus. She obviously cares about the class and students, sometimes to the point of making  disinterested students care about the class.

Fantastic teacher. Smart, funny, and extremely helpful. Class was challenging, but not impossibly hard. Grading is fair, lectures are interesting, and I've learnt a tremendous amount more about Finance. Would definitely take another class with her. One of my favorite classes this semester.
Very Harsh grader. The lectures were very tedious and not overly helpful. Even the most studious will find success in this class to be challenging. I would avoid.

Really great class. One of my favorites if not most favorite one. Material is interesting and teacher is engaging. Class is mainly comprised of case studies and quizzes, none were easy but she explains the material very well so it's easy to follow. Very open for questions/concerns after class ends. Not an easy A class but highly recommend it.
Although this class is not easy, I definitely learned a lot.  Prof was clear and prepared for every class.  She keeps you alert and thinking about the material by calling on everyone!

This is an advanced level class, and consequently is not easy. However, she is very organized and presents the material in a very logic and comprehensive way, which makes it easy to understand. Case studies used are interesting and supplement her lectures very well. Exams are fairly difficult but manageable. Overall, awesome class & great Professor

If you're looking to take an easy class this is not the class for you. However, if you want to learn finance through a challenging yet rewarding course this may be the class you're looking for. Professor Canina is a wonderful person who cares about her students and will go the extra mile in trying to make you succeed. I highly recommend this course
Assumes prior subject knowledge and doesn't prepare students for exams

This is a great class.  If you have any math experience whatsoever, you shouldn't have a problem doing well in this class... although doing the practice homework problems is pretty essential.  Prof. Canina is funny, helpful, and amazingly kind and will work with you to make sure you understand the material well.
My favorite stats professor of all time. Russ' lectures are hilarious, and he gives you a great impression of what it's like to be a statistician in the real world. Office hours were really helpful.

The course itself is fine but it was taught in such an unorganized way that the material seemed harder than it really way. Those who did well attended multiple TA hours to get help on the problem sets. He also did not follow syllabus. I would not recommend taking any course with him.

As a stats major, this man is the worst stats professor I've ever had. He posts no lectures online and often gets sassy with students when they ask for help. He goes on random rants about his life in the middle of class and awkwardly calls on people for no reason. Avoid this class.

I mean I get it, he's a good guy, but there's always a but. He never answers questions on piazza, refuses to post notes online, requests you to spend money printing out lecture notes, and wouldn't admit that there is error on final formula sheet (yeah someone asked this and he was like "all are correct). I learned a lot through hw, but not from him
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: -runs over lectures-need to print out notes almost every lecture-need to come to class to write notes because not put online-started prelim 45 min late-only offered makeup for second prelim at one time because TA's wanted to leave for spring break and it was during day so had to miss class-syllabus not up to date-put incorrect solutions out to lab

One of the worst lecturer I've had for a biostat class at Cornell. No record videos and filled lecture notes. What he explains in lecture is really unclear and difficult to follow. Really unhelpful in Piazza. Avoid if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: very very good prof. hard subject, but he makes it understandable. people who complain that it's pointless don't understand business from a broader view. business is not just talk, but many hotelies don't get it.
really enjoyed this class

Russ tries really hard but his class can be painful and it's hard to ask questions. The homeworks are really hard and time consuming (I spent 5 hours on them a piece and there are 10). You really need to go to section and office hours to get the full benefit of this class unless you are just good at stats. The class is frustrating bc is only 2 cred
funny guy

Russ is a very intelligent guy, particularly in his field of study. He is approachable and encouraging to all his students (poor performers included).  Not only is his grading fair but he also offers a great deal of additional assistance via personal OH. While Stats is difficult for some, Russ tries to make the subject as applicable as possible.

This class is the worst. Why do hotelies need to know paired t-test beats me. He is probably one of the worst profs at the Hotel school. Unfortunately the course is a requirement but try to avoid him if possible.

are you guys on something?  russ is definitely enthusiastic, but by no means on the top of his game.  he still has a LOT to do to get used to the hotel school and his teaching methods left most of my class confused. his class has too much work compared to other 3 credit courses. & he still hasn't worked out the balance between math and theory...

Undoubtedly the best professor I have ever had.  When I came to Cornell, I was not interested in math.  After several weeks of biometry with Russ, he convinced me to switch over to his graduate class.  3 years later, I am now a biometry major.  Russ, your teaching has changed my life.  Thank you.

Russ is terrific. He took some getting used to, coming from the Ag school and all, and I gotta say our class didn't make him feel that welcome initially. However once we got into the material, it was smooth sailing. We can talk like statisticians now.. kind of.
AMAZING, demanding, energetic--all things a top professor is. Russ: you rule! Welcome to SHA. Russ Llyod--the newest hotelie.
excellent professor; makes complex concepts understandable and fun.
Russ is the best! He makes data analysis fun. His examples of lampricide and fish are very entertaining. The lecture time just flies by without you even knowing, and believe it or not, you want more.
i love russ !!!!  even in a huge (200+) class he remembers everyone's name and he's funny and really nice and knows how to teach!

ASTRO 3334 is a great chance to get hands-on experience with Python techniques in Astronomy. Lloyd is helpful in class, although difficult to reach outside of it. The class consisted of 8 projects that ranged from the very easy (apply to research programs online) to finding exoplanets and other difficult tasks. You need Python experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: If you have any interest in astronomy, this class is an easy way to satisfy distribution requirements.  Lloyd is a good teacher and he cares about teaching astronomy but a lot of the students don't show any interest in the class and just want an easy A, so some of the students complain about it, but all you need to do is just do the work.
Lloyd's lectures are mostly good.  He does lots of demos that are really entertaining.  The class is pretty easy, but there are homeworks and you need to study for the exams.

Lloyd has his ups and downs. Some of the lectures - especially those with demos - are pretty interesting. Others are fairly dull. He also isn't very good at answering questions and will often brush off a student's inquiry as ignorant. It's easier if you're interested in astronomy. Pretty easy to do well if you study before the exams.

Insanely lecture heavy. He would just yap and yap, in lab too - often about something loosely related but unclear whether or not it was important. Problem set and exam questions were confusing and graded confusingly. No set office hours. Course jumped all over the place, which was annoying. Would not take again. he just yaps and is confusing.

This guy talks a lot but it's because he's interested in his work. Great lecturer, but if you don't show up to class good luck surviving. Despite this, very accessible and understanding outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Louis does talk a lot, but he's a great guy. If you make an effort to learn you will surely enjoy this class. Very unique professor at Cornell where he genuinely enjoys and understands his field, hard not to learn here.
If you get Lou going, he won't stop talking. The guy clearly loves his field, but can be monotonous after 2hrs of lecture in lab. Great guy though.

Loved every second of this class. Challenging and has a lot of readings but the readings are extremely interesting and force you to develop your perspective on a wide and diverse variety of subjects. The TA's are extremely kind and helpful and Professor Loos is extremely friendly. Highly Recommend!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Fantastic professor. Every lecture was a joy, and I personally preferred her over Craib in this course. Readings were also great—I think I liked them more than Craib's because they were less poetic/artistic and more to the point. That's nitpicking, though. Lots of work, but if you are in any way interested in US foreign policy, take the course!!
So so so nice and smart. Remembered peoples' names and really cares about the content and the students. Lectures and readings are daunting but Loos makes them more approachable
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She remembered everyone's name, even those who didn't really go to class (and it wasn't a small lecture, either). She's kind and really only assigns readings...and while you have to go to discussions, attendance isn't taken at lectures and the slides are posted. It's a good intro course and she's great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class itself is not hard and I would it's an easy A if you put in the work (which is a lot). However, there's a lot of reading so if you don't want to read a LOT, do not take this class. Attendance is mandatory for lecture and discussion sections. Lecture is incredibly annoying because the assigned readings tell you the same stuff in more detail.

Professor Loos ensured that all lectures were interesting while also engaging with the class and frequently asking questions regarding course content. In addition, feedback to essays was substantial and allowed for the student to grow. Overall a great, interesting class and professor always made enough time to schedule meetings and go over content.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Loos is clearly very well learned and knowledgeable in the subject areas of the class. She often engages with the class with questions, ranging from "Raise your hand if..." to "What are your thoughts?". Cares about her students (i.e. extended an already-generous deadline). Lectures are heavy, but the slides do not contain any information.
Amazing

I LOVE professor Loos, she is so genuine about teaching and really cared about what students have to offer. We learned about more than romantic love, but got an exposure to a variety of different cultures. You know exactly what you have to do to succeed, participate and don't slack off in assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Fantastic professor and fantastic course. TA's were also great. Global History of Love was not only interesting, but also enlightening. Would highly recommend anybody to take a course under Professor Loos. Her lectures are engaging and she made extra time to help with essays and revisions, showing she truly wants her students to do well.

The content of the course was interesting, and her lectures were very informative. However, she talks kind of fast so u really need to be a good note taker. There is a ton of reading and you are expected to DO ALL OF IT, because participation is a big part of the grade. But in general, a decent class.

She was very helpful with any questions on the subject that you had. I had the good fortune to have both Loos and Sherman Cochran as professors for this class and it was by far my favorite class in my first semester.

I've had her twice, and she's been great both times. Once in a lecture and once in a seminar. Laid back, genuine, and thought-provoking, and really knows her stuff. Easy to work with and wants to make sure everyone does well
Loos rules!  One of the best profs around...funny, energetic, helpful, and really cares about students. Highly recommend.

Her class was one of the funnest I've had in this school. She is genuinely cheerful and has a great sense of humor, which makes class something to look forward to. Her lectures and discussions make the material as well as the reading much more interesting.

Professor Loos is the ideal prof: laid back, genuinely interested in getting to know each student, full of insightful comments, and a natural at provoking discussions. Her grading is slow but pretty lax and the readings are generally interesting. My favorite class by far.

Prof Loos is very nice and always helpful.  Her discussions in the seminar were thought provoking, and the assignments were usually interesting.  Grading is a bit slow, but she apologizes for that.  There is a decent amount of reading, but its not necessarily too much.  It was my favorite class.
Great to talk to in office hours, wants everyone to do well, very helpful
No Comments
Her lectures are clear, well-organized, and fascinating. Grading is somewhat easy. She has a great sense of humor and really makes an effort to get to know every one of the students in her class.
Professor Lorenz is such a smart person and always fosters amazing in class discussions. If you have the opportunity to take his FWS I would highly recommend it.

I took ENGL 3240 with Lorenz (I don't know why it isn't an option for the course code), and I liked his class enough to review him on RMP (this is my first review) -- so hopefully that says something! I found his insights interesting throughout the course, and he's surprisingly funny. Lean into the class, it'll make the experience much better!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: disorganized for sure, but lenient enough to make up for it.
A g
He's not as bad as other people suggest

Professor Lorenz was awesome! He made seemingly mundane texts, such as Othello, seem so vibrant and thought-provoking. The entire class grade pretty much depends on 2 essays ( a midterm and final), which are each 7 pages double spaced. There are also weekly discussion based writing assignment.

Took the FWS with him, the class honestly sucked. However Lorenz was such a nice guy and so passionate that he made it bearable. He is horribly disorganized and does not know how technology works, but I liked him. Def has favorites though. I would never suggest anyone take an english fws.

I didn't turn in my final and I got an A. I think he assumed that he'd lost it and didn't bother asking. 

He is the best professor I've ever had at Cornell.

He's brilliant: he prioritizes the most salient readings, presents complex theory in accessible ways and somehow encourages participation/helps you not feel stupid doing so. I love how accessibly he positions the texts. He's sensitive to our needs,links texts to contemporary issues and goes out of his way to enrich text-based interests out-of-class
End heavy course. First bit you can fly by but pages on pages on pages towards the end. Still though, makes you really think about what you are reading and I honestly enjoyed writing his essays.

Prof Lorenz was friendly to his students and supportive of their ideas. Grading consisted of weekly short reading responses, class participation, and two larger essays. Yes, he was disorganized, but it's fine as long as you are on top of things yourself. He takes a more historical approach to literary analysis, so avoid if this is not your thing.

If you can manage to listen to him for even 60 seconds, you'll be able to count at least five tangents. Luckily he's a nice guy, so if you contribute twice per class, he'll like you well enough. Your papers don't need to be top-notch, they just have to be mildly interesting. His take-home final was a piece of cake.

VERY disorganized. By the end of the semester, you'll be writing a paper every week because in the beginning you did absolutely nothing. However, this can work to your advantage as his grading of papers is quite easy and you can essentially hand in things late with no consequence. Plus, he can be quite engaging.

He's brilliant! Yes, slightly disorganized but this is irrelevant in the long run- lovely teaching, very helpful and very vibrant. He will engage you in a text that you otherwise hated. Would love to have him again!

I had this professor for my FWS: Question of Tragedy. The readings were very interesting, but the professor was incredibly disorganized. He was often late, would sometimes lose papers, and by the end of the semester we ran out of time to cover the material properly. As long as you defend your arguments with "text-based" evidence you'll be fine.

Literally one of the worst fws professors ever. Incredible disorganized (both mentally and physically), manages time poorly, and expects a lot out of you. Do not take his class - you will seriously hate it.
Great professor. Keeps class interesting, and is always willing to help.

He made me enjoy writing thoughtful and creative essays again after high school hade made me hate them. The plays we read were great but Lorenz was tragically dissorganized. We spent a month on Oedipus in the beginning of the semester but by the end we were handing in a final draft of a paper each week. Overall he's great though.

His grading is quite harsh. Oftentimes with homeworks and exams, he is looking for a specific phrase and will give little/no partial credit otherwise. Labs are basically sum to multihour debug sessions. TAs are largely unhelpful and as it seemed like only 1 TA had actually done the labs. The rest had answer keys and would say "try print statements"
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lorenzo is a great lecturer and wants to help students. The concept taught in class is a bit abstract and takes time to understand. The project is time-consuming and prelims are difficult. If you are really interested in distributed systems, highly recommend taking this course. If you only want to get good grades, you probably shouldn't take it.

Held my attention throughout 75 minute lectures.
The course does a good job of covering theoretical and applied topics, and the homework and projects are rewarding. The exams are also a fair assessment.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Assignments require a lot of time to solve but are rewarding. Exams are very tough and partial credits often not rewarded. Furthermore, detail and content mentioned once in class or research papers are also fair game. Lecture is a pain to sit through as the focus is not clear and professor gets sidetracked.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The relevance of the assignments to the exams was relatively low. The practice exams didn't really match the real exams, I feel like that the exams shouldn't have been as nitpicky as they were, but nonetheless he was a funny guy and tried his best. I heard Professor RVR in the spring is much easier if you want to just take this class to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Incredibly frustrating when content of lectures is not tested on the exam. Not many assignments that will help you prepare for the exam. Problems are all random and nitpicky, and test details/content mentioned once in class, and aren't on the slides or aren't clear on the slides either. Lecture is a pain to sit through.

Professor Alvisi runs his courses in a ridiculously difficult manner. The content he teaches is extremely difficult, and it is hard to find external resources for help since the content is relatively recent-research-based. However, Alvisi's content is very useful and important to know if you plan on going into systems programming or PhD. Also funny

Alvisi clearly cares about his students deeply. The content itself is challenging and a bit hard to engage with but Alvisi tries his best. Lectures are hard to pay attention since the content is fairly dense. Assignment workload is pretty manageable but the prelims are quite challenging.
Absolutely abysmal
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Found myself very often asking myself "what the hell is going on" in lecture.

Professor Alvisi is a fantastic lecturer and genuinely cares for his students. He was available for office hours *hours* after they were technically over, and takes great care in trying to explain concepts through multiple analogies (which he loves) for different learning styles. The class is tough and prelims are hard, but grades are curved

The class was rough but it did feel like Alvisi was trying his best and actually cared about students. Programming assignments were not long or that difficult. Prelims were pretty hard and they basically accounted for your entire grade though. Light in terms of workload but there's a lot of confusing and boring material to know

Lorenzo is an anomaly of a professor. Easily one of the most close-minded, confidently unfair teachers I've ever had throughout my educational career. Please rethink every teaching strategy you've wasted your time learning over the years.
Exam was ludicrously unfair
good professor but class is often disorganized. grading and exams aren't representative of the content covered in lectures.

hws & exams don't accurately measure your understanding of the material. You're better off leaving questions blank than answering them in a way that differs from the solution but shows some understanding of the material bc you won't get any credit either way. Encourages TAs to give advice like 5 year olds which is super unprofessional.

The course content was really interesting and I loved alvisi as a person/lecturer! The projects however were absolutely not worth the time spent on them, and they quickly devolved into mindless debugging. Their grading system felt super unfair and soured what was otherwise a really great class. Showed absolutely no respect for the student's time.

Distributed Systems is the hardest yet the most fun CS class I took at Cornell. Professor Alvisi delivers it so well that the abstract ideas come so natural and vivid. Would definitely recommend it to anyone who wants to take a challenge and has a solid programming foundation. The workload is heavy; have to be a strong coder to endure the hardship.

Professor Alvisi is one of my favorite professors at Cornell. He makes difficult material digestible during lecture and even though he's quite busy, he always has weekly office hours. Undoubtedly, this was also the hardest class I've taken. The material is difficult so read the papers before lecture!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Not good lecturer. Makes random analogies and slides are difficult to decipher. Exams are very difficult. I love the textbook though. He is a cool guy (has 4 motorcycles) but not an effective teacher.
Not care about students at all
Poor lectures, poor slides, few opportunities to practice and learn much of the material, unclear project specifications, and devilish exams.

Prof Alvisi is really caring - prelims are tough, but he makes sure to adjust it according to the curve. Learnt a lot on operating system from his lectures, and would take more classes from him! Also shares interesting stories in lectures.
Does not care about his students.

the tests were rough and the curve didn't come through like I hoped, but the course was pretty enjoyable given that I hated 3410. the professor was an amazing lecturer and explained concepts well. he held review sessions every few weeks and cared a lot about the course. the tests were brutal and hard to study for but I would still recommend taking.
Do not take his 4410 class. If I have to regret ever taking one class in Cornell, it will have to be this. Honestly abysmal. Tests were not demonstrative of the lecture material.

Constantly rambles during lecture instead of sticking to explaining the course material. Is a bad explainer of concepts and makes content harder than it actually is. Tests are only slightly based on lecture material. Mean on one test was less than 45%. Unfair tests with bad grading criteria.
One of my favorite CS class at Cornell. Lectures are engaging. The class is very organized. l learnt a lot from all the material, lectures, papers, projects and even exams.

This is easily one of my favorite classes at Cornell. Prof. Alvisi delivers such engaging lectures and he is capable of conveying even the most difficult concepts in Distributed Systems using relatable analogies. Overall, an amazing class that I learned a ton from it!

Prof. Alvisi is one of the nicest, most passionate guys you'll meet, but unfortunately this doesn't translate to clear lectures. I left many classes more confused than when I came in. Not to mention, most of the taught material isn't even helpful for the test problems, which all seem arbitrary and unrelated to the course material.
What he taught can always make you confused, won't take his courses again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: OS is very important, but obviouly he can hardly teach it well.
He can make easy concepts hard to understand. Strong accent with unclear thought.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Poor spoken English with terrible slides. And he will never answer your questions on Piazza.

Professor Alvisi really is what makes distributed systems one of the best classes I have taken at Cornell. The class is extremely challenging but well worth the effort. Lorenzo's lectures are both informative and hilarious and the course is overall run really well.
Awful slides along with worse teaching, and yeah very tough tests.
Very poor teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: The Professor make the exam too hard to handle (with mean 64/120 and median 62/120), alone with unclear lecture notes. Though I tried my best to review anything in the lecture, many problems seem like mysteries in the exam. I along with many of my friends decide not to take any course taught by this professor anymore!

Easily one of the best professors I've ever had at Cornell.  The course itself was extremely difficult, but the lectures were fantastic and he really made himself available to help students.  The course was well-organized, tightly designed, and left me with a strong foundation in a very difficult area of study.  Highly recommend!
this guy doesn't like emails. he also does not like when desperate high school students are in need.

Logevall is by far the best professor I have taken a class with at Cornell.  Unfortunately, he will not be teaching next semester because he is being appointed the head of the IR minor.  He is a real softy at heart. Questions are on readings and films, probably doesn't give below a B, and gives extra credit through optional sections.

Fantastic, in depth, knowledgeable lecturer. Really knows a lot about foreign policy esp Vietnam (his book won the Pulitzer). Optional discussion section for extra points. Lots of paperback reading that isn't really required until the prelim/final, where it plays a heavy part. Takes lots of questions in class. Highly recommended, interesting prof
He is a wonderful professor. Very engaging in lecture and always takes questions if something was unclear. The tests are tough but fair. The only caveat is that the TAs are extremely unhelpful.

I've taken a lot of history classes and Logevall is the best lecturer I've ever had. Tests aren't easy, but very manageable. Not a ton of reading either and some of the books he assigned were really interesting. Take this professor.

by far the best lecturer i've had in my three years at cornell. i had no interest in the subject, but his lectures are engaging as he's not simply giving information, but rather telling a great story. only one paper and 2 exams which was nice, but there was quite a bit of reading. i definitely recommend any history majors this professor!

History of early American foreign policy. He's pretty good at lecturing (though his sentences always start out loudly and quickly trail off) and has a funny, quirky personality. But not very inspiring, often runs out of time, and only rarely discusses the readings in class (no sections). Not very good readings at that. Pretty easy. Overall- 2.5/5
Really good professor, always willing to help, leads very interesting and thought-provoking discussions for the history honors seminar.

Great guy, very nice. Really enjoys history a lot, you can tell. Always runs out of time but is so passionate. Get him as your section leader. Nice dude, exams pretty easy. A lot of reading but it's worth it.

Logevall is a nice guy.  Good discussion leader. Class wasn't very heavy in requirements.  My only gripe with him is that he gets through so little information in lecture, making the class end up fairly limited in depth of material covered.
He is very clear and concise...lectures are interesting and well-organized.  He is always willing to meet with students.  Definitely one of the best profs I've had at Cornell!!
Great teacher.  He is clear, concise, and articulate.  He keeps the class interesting (be sure you get him for section).  The reading gets dense at times but is generally manageable.
Her lectures are always dense, but filled with important information. She was one of three professors I had for this class and was definitely the hardest grader out of them.

I had the pleasure of being a student of Professor Lujan for NS 1400 Intro to HBHS; her lectures are very interesting and she is great at explaining biological processes; there were 3 lecturers for this course and I liked her the best! She's also very nice
Lab component was great, very hands-on.  It is a lot of material, but manageable if you plan well.  Go to class.
She's great, knows her anatomy cold!  Really enjoyed this class, she was a big reason for that.
Can't go wrong with Dr. Lujan.

Just took this course this past spring - wasn't too keen on anatomy but Prof Lujan made it fun and interesting.  Thinking of pursuing graduate work in anatomy as a result of her class.  She was great, very dedicated.
Friendly, organized, helpful and knowledgeable.
Really doesn't understand the material at all - Best bet for understanding and learning is the lab coordinator Dr Solomon

She's very clear with what she wants you to know in the lab lectures.  The labs themselves can be unexciting, but you definitely learn a lot.  Overall, she's a pretty good instructor, but how much you enjoy the class is based more heavily on the performance of the TAs.
Very fun to listen to. Interested in topic, and very knowledgeable about Anatomy. The class is more difficult than in past years, but if you spend time in office hours you will be fine
Amazing! Loved it.
OB is interesting but Professor Lucas was an average lecturer

This is an amazing class. I thought the content was so interesting that I didn't even mind memorizing it all for the tests, which is, in fact, all you have to do to get a good grade. Lucas won't inspire you in his delivery, but he teaches the material well. Study the lecture slides and skim the textbook.
Read the textbook to do well. Exams are 50% lecture 50% textbook things not covered in class. Lectures are worth attending and Professor Lucas is interesting.

Professor Lucas was a good professor with interesting lectures. His tests were for the most part reasonable and a fair concentration of lecture and textbook material. The only downside is he isn't approachable at all and clearly doesn't want to be approached by students despite his friendly demeanor in lecture.

Lucas is a very good teacher who has very engaging lectures. Going to lectures is helpful as the tests lean more on stuff in class than reading. The course content is extremely interesting. Lucas also allows for a lot of extra credit opportunities. One note is that the tests are more conceptual and situational questions not just straight facts
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Prof. Lucas is a great professor. Clear instructions on class assessments and cares about students. He tries to relate to student experiences which is appreciated.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She is beyond sweet and this class is so easy! If you're looking for a Professor that understands that life happens it is definitely her. She is truly an amazing person and the class is easy. Weekly discussions, midterm and a final. There is one project.

Prof. Munguia is awesome! Some of the readings are difficult but her lectures help A LOT! Pay attention, take detailed notes. She gives all that you need for reading reflections and exams. Challenging but if you put in the work, you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She is lovely

She really inspired an interest in the topic. I enjoyed all of the references to real court cases and medical cases that made us think. She also always has excellent feedback on papers. My writing really improved with her.
Excellent class! It was very tough, but my other FWS had the same course load. My writing really improved after her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She's very flexible and super willing to grant extensions if you talk to her ahead of time. There's a lot of reading, but if you miss the reading you can still participate. She is a very slow grader, however. Lucia is a great teacher, and I improved a lot as a writer. This was the most rewarding class I took this semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Would take again

reviews.comment: So. many. readings. She is very sweet though. Tough grader.
Tough material, but she really gets you thinking. Gets the class talking a lot.

Love him!! Always happy to teach and answer questions. The content is very challenging but you have access to lots of help from TAs. The prelims are pretty hard (kinda similar difficulty to hw questions), but grades them VERY generously and curves them too.
Goated prof, explains examples and concepts clearly. Too smart to realize how hard he makes prelims, they'd put concepts together in ways I didnt know were possible. Very generous grader though.

His lectures are very clear and he lectures at a very digestible pace. He's really good about answering questions, don't be afraid to go up to him after lecture. The course grading is quite transparent and very fair. Exams are easier than homework, and there are weekly homework quizzes that give you a free grade boost.

I absolutely loved Perelstein! He always walked in with a smile on his face and greeted students every morning. He is super passionate about all things physics and it shows through his teachings. The lectures were interesting and had just the right amount of rigour for an introductory honors course.
Awesome teaching!

Compassionate and brilliant lecturer; be sure to hit up office hours, wish I would have more often. 2218 was a bit rough around the edges because it was his first time teaching it, but for a pilot class he handled it fairly.
I found his lectures to not just copy out of the book, even though the lectures were structured around the book. Lots of homework but it really helps you learn the material.

He's a good professor and lecturer. My only complaint is that I wish we spent more time on the more interesting stuff (relativistic EM) instead of spending weeks on radiation, waves at boundaries, etc. (much of which we already covered in 2217 and 2218...)
Maxim is fantastic. He's an excellent lecturer, and clear very smart. He made me twice as interested in the material as I was before taking the class.

The best physics professor I have had at Cornell thus far. Very clear in lecture. Knows what parts of the material to focus on when teaching and giving homework. Very knowledgable on the subject. Always wants to help if someone needs it. Studying previous years' exams is a big help since the format is similar year to year. Highly recommend!
Intelligent and Compassionate
Very clear and concise lectures. Was very helpful in office hours.  Homework was sometimes a little algebra heavy esp. during angular momentum part of course.
Hard to focus in class, also difficult to keep up with the homeworks because they are never collected. Difficult course, but doable

Perelstein is great. He passes out pretty thorough lecture notes at the beginning of class with all of his iClicker questions on them, plus other general notes and some conceptual things. He's not super exciting, but he's clear.
He's my best teacher this semester. Even as a freshman, I understand his class. It's easy to fall asleep to his voice though.
Hilarious guy (though he may not intend to be at times); pretty great at explaining things.
I have no idea why people love this guy, but he was not on my good professors list last semester.
He is a solid teacher. Explains well, tough HWs but doable if you put the effort. Prelims are fair
Nice guy. Teaches well. Brilliant mind.
Nice smile

I came to school with a dream of becoming an accountant, I can thank this course and MacAusland for destroying that dream. I did not learn a single thing about accounting, and never helped during office hours and made it incredibly difficult to succeed in this course. Worst class I have ever taken.

One of the best classes at Nolan. Just do all your homework, participate in class, and go to OHs. Very clear and easy tests, as long as you know EVERY account type, and understand EVERY relationship between the account types.
Slides are not that helpful, says she'll give you a boost in your grade if you go to office hours, didn't even help.

No partial credit on written portion on the prelims and final exam, doesn't curve much
Even if you have a religious event or interview, attendance is strictly enforced. You can miss up to 4 classes. Loves students who glaze her
Unclear grading criteria and never explained in syllabus. Lots of HW that must be turned in in-class, or receive 0

It's a pretty difficult course with a lot of homework, but there are lots of provided resources to study and all of the homework and textbook materials are useful. Stay on top of your work and manage your time and you'll be fine. If you fall behind, you'll probably have a difficult time catching up.

Initially intimidating but honeslty one of best teachers i have ever had. She teaches SO SO WELL. fr. all you need to do is listen to her lecture and make notes and you will understand and do good on exam. She is very straight to the point and helpful and caring and wants her students to do well. BUT Exams HARD, but bec accouting hard overall.

She can be strict but she's also very encouraging. She wants all students to do well.
There is a lot of work, but it prepares you for exams.
She is very organized; I love that she posts the slides and outlines to print (lectures are tough to follow).

No laptop of phones allowed though, which I'm not a big fan of. I like having notes on my laptop.

Prof. MacAusland is amazing! The class can get difficult, but she is super organized and structured, making it easier to learn. People get intimidated by her, but it's clear that she really wants all her students to succeed.

HW is very routine -- 3 different types of homework a week including textbook, online, and paper. Quizzes and exams are very formulaic so easier to study for as semester goes on. Go to office hours because she tracks that. Honestly not a bad class, and can be interesting -- just have to work hard to understand it. She likes people who participate!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Explain accounting that won't be confusing. Short, simple, and concise words are necessary.

This woman is an icon. She moves through content RAPIDLY⚡! In class, she'll introduce something confusing, then ask, "Any questions?", give people 0.01 seconds to raise their hands and then say, "Great! If not, then let's move on to our next topic!" ... Some people don't like her, but they just need to open their mind to how comical she is🎾🎾🎾🎾
SO hard, but she's a wonderful prof who genuinely cared about her field and her students

Let me be real w/ u. ppl r gonna have diff opinions abt her depending on their mindset, relationship w/ her and how well they did in the class. But she is someone who rlly wants u to succeed and believes in u (despite being a tuff grader), she tells u exactly what she wants from you, is organized, lots of office hours throughout the week, etc.

Love her. Accountant boss lady. The class is definitely the hardest of the semester. But, it was my favorite class because it was the most stimulating. Didn't even get a great grade in the class, but it still seemed valuable and she cares about students. Gave pep talks and made you feel awesome about being a hotelie.. real world connections drawn.

go to office hours. if you dont understand one chapter, you wont understand the next ones. the tests and quizzes are cumulative so you have to understand EVERYTHING in this class if you wanna do rlly well
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: WORSE TEACHER EVER

She is very cognizant of her content and is very willing to help students pass the class. Her teaching style is very good as well. Definitely go for office hours and be willing to put in the work (not so much tho) outside of clas.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor MacAusland is a very tough professor especially for first year students. However, even as she is a very tough professor she is caring of all her students and want all of them to do well. I feel that her being a tough professor it emphasis real learning and allows for students to really understand the concepts of Accounting in business.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: You either hate Professor MacAusland or you love her. She is a tough professor, but she is very organized and everything is very straightforward. She's not very approachable outside the classroom, so go to the office hours with the TA because that is the only way you'll do well in her class. Again, go to office hours trust me.

Prof. MacAusland is tough but caring, emphasizing real learning. She's knowledgeable and passionate, though her personal office hours could be more accessible. Tons of unfortunately helpful homework, emphasis on paper. Strict deadlines. Exams are quite fair with a few bonus points. Great teacher, no-nonsense, knows what works for students' success.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Took the class last year. Attendance was mandatory even though it was easier just to teach yourself the material which also defeats the purpose of paying for a class...
Fun interesting financial accounting class but unfortunately a not so stellar teacher. Not sure what else you'd expect. A simple class.

MacAusland could go either way for me. She honestly is a fair and pretty good teacher, but she gives a lot of work. Her exams are often tough, but with proper studying, you can do well in the class. Just know, her class is something you definitely can't bs your way through.

Professor MacAusland is a truly amazing professor! When I first joined the Hotel School, I dreaded college, but quickly adapted to my environment through her class. I fell in love with accounting and while she may have strict policies, they are all designed to help you learn the material. The TAs are also very helpful for this course.

Absolutely ZERO late work is accepted in this class, be prepared to turn in every single assignment on time or not at all. Lectures are very helpful (although attendance is mandatory so you'll be in them either way). Prelims and the Final were tough but all grades are relatively clear. GO TO TA OFFICE HOURS, she tracks attendance!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She is an amazing professor at the Hotel School. I took her course in Spring 2022 and she was one of the best professors at Cornell that was really caring of students and took the time out of her busy day to help us all. A truly caring and inspirational professor that knows her content of accounting and is a master.
Professor MacAusland is a nice lady but this is not a class that you can just take. Study consistently, pay attention to the textbook and do the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Everyone is very scared of her. Just try to get on her good side and you'll be fine. You kind of have to learn it yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor MacAusland is an acquired taste. She comes off at first as being harsh and cold, but that's mostly because she has to be in order to teach accounting. Once you get to know her, you'll surely realize that she really cares about her students and (somehow) has a passion for her subject. She is very fair and helps form complete understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor MacAusland is an excellent professor. She is obviously an accounting expert, but she is equally good at making financial accounting understandable to students. She is patient with questions in class and encourages students to attend office hours. Even though attendance isn't graded, each class is so valuable that you really shouldn't skip
