reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The worst teaching environment I've ever been apart of. The class is taught outside of actual class time and class time is spent by one kid asking all the questions which slows down the class and doesn't let anyone else learn. Don't be this kid. The professor doesn't actually teach she just answers questions all class and leaves students clueless.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lots of homework but they are very helpful for me to keep up on the materials, and you can drop some of the homework (I forgot how many of them). Prelims make up a large portion of the grade so be sure not to fall behind. Very helpful professor.
Instructions are not so clear
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Really cares about her students- go to office hours! Paces her class well and has quizzes to ensure that you're understanding the material. DON'T FALL BEHIND- very hard to catch up bc concepts build off each other. Be proactive and participate, and you should be good. Not forgiving to students who don't seek help when she has so many opportunities
Really nice lady and accessible outside of class but she gives A LOT of homework, tests are difficult and extremely conceptual so if you aren't an expert you will not do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: AMAAAAAAZZZINNNGGGG professor. I hated accounting before I started. I still hate accounting, but she was really so willing to help and tried to make it as easy as possible to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Took both his American Econ History Courses (3310 & 3320). Classes are full of info and Lyons is a great lecturer. You ABSOLUTELY HAVE TO GO TO CLASS and TAKE GOOD NOTES, if you skip lectures you will be screwed since there are no powerpoint slides and the class is graded on two prelims+final with pretty much all the questions coming from lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This guy is hands-down the best professor I've ever had. He's almost unbelievably relaxed and his classes are fascinating. Tips: 1. Go to class, do readings. 2. Nothing phases this guy. He will happily answer questions like "which readings actually matter?" in office hours. 3. The "Mechanical cotton harvester" is a trick question.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Get ready for a throwback to high school history class, just with more material to rote-memorize and regurgitate on the tests. Which by the way are graded by a grad student who doesn't even attend lecture. Tom Lyons is the archetype for checked-out, tenured professor who genuinely doesn't care. Go to every lecture, take copious notes and memorize.

He's a living textbook. I've taken his American Economic History course before, but the Chinese Economy course was a completely different beast. Just go to class, take down notes, and you'll be good to go. An advice I received is to think about what the core concepts are and study that. Sujan is also an amazing TA!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Going to class is a must in addition you must take very detailed notes. the exams will cover very obscure things but his office hours are helpful, readings not necessary at all. Overall is a tough teacher, study the handouts, and study in a group. Not flexible on grades and almost all the class gets a B+
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Definitely lots of information in a 75 minute class. Use a laptop, because you're gonna be jotting for a while. Some people may consider him to be a bit boring, but he uses subtle humor about Frank Sinatra and other stuff that no one really understands b/c they're about old stuff. Really smart guy with lots to say. Lecture and reading   mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: - Super clear lecturer, TONS of info given in class - Readings are not very important; much much more important to attend class - Tests are straightforward but will fully test your knowledge. Pretty much all short answer. Fair grading but will take points off without much hesitation - Moderately interesting class; NOT MUCH MATH which was great
Great Prof

Mostly lecture-based. No powerpoint slides and readings are useless so if you miss one class its a big deal. Tests were generally fair but there is a lot of information and classes are very boringearlymonotonous. Only take him if you are planning on going to every single class and taking very elaborate notes.
Great Professor with crystal clear lectures.  Helpful as long as you attend his office hours.

great professor! lectures are clear useful and full of information so notes are necessary. readings are pretty useful too. only thing is that outside of the readings and lectures there isn't much else to help you through the course. generally a good challenge of a course but not impossible. again great prof though definitely recommend him

Gives out tons of information in class. In the syllabus it says the readings are mandatory, but just skim them. Exams are straightforward but not easy. Overall, not too bad but I wouldn't go out and tell people to take this class. Take this class only if you are a morning person and/or don't mind note-taking.

He is one of the most knowledgeable and helpful professors in the entire department.  I took two of his classes before, and was totally impressed by the plethora of information this guy possesses.  He does, as some reviews suggest, become a bit monotonous from time to time, but his subtle humor nevertheless gets the class's full attention.  Bravo.
Great teacher, so long as you like tons of information.
Very clear about his information. He might be monotonous sometimes but he has an underlying wit that keeps people from falling asleep. The man is a faunt of historical information.
No Comments
Completely unreliable.  Says one thing and does another.
No Comments

His lecture style is to mostly just talk. It can be a good or bad thing depending on the person. For me, his style makes me pay attention in class. He's pretty clear too. And as long as you have good notes from class you'll do fine on exams. The assigned readings are just extra.
Tough Course, but Awesome Professor. Archer really knows his fluids and is kind. I do not like Denn's Book. Let me repeat, I do not Like Denn's Book. I hope this causes Archer to choose another text.

Good professor. However the homeworks were long and hard. Prelims were open-notes and very doable. However, the TAs tend to be not useful in office hours. Better off going straight to Archer for Office hours

Hmm..Hmm more than month after finals and still arguing about fluids. In agree with some of these posts - archer is a great prof. one of the best ones in cheme at cornell. I also think he is fair, cool, and yes hot!
Hands down the best course I have had at Cornell! Archer has very high standards, but is fair. Horrible text, notes helped a lot.

Terrible class, the material is very interesting, but Archer completely ruins it. He's completely disorganized and arrogant, and his tests are very poorly designed, not necessarily hard, just poorly thought out.
Difficult course, awesome professor. Archer is thorough and rigorous. His fluids course demands a butt load of effort, but I can say I've learned alot. He is very helpful and a master of his subject.
Worst class I ever took. Worst teaching style I've ever encountered.

Archer is a great professor. The material is really tough, but he is always willing to help and is really friendly.  If you attend his office hours, he essentially tells you what is going to be covered on the exam.  Exams are fair but problem sets are VERY long.  I'm not the biggest fan of fluids, but if you have to take it, take it with Archer.

No one wrote a fluids review? At least I'M trying to help out my future chemE underclassmen.  Anyways, Archer gives you a crap load of notes throughout the semester and blazes through them at light speed.  However, his tests were FAIR (unlike the Hws) and office hours helpful, good teacher more or less, just too much material..

Professor Archer is an extremely friendly and helpful teacher. Although fluid mechanics was tough, he made it easier to handle and definitely wants his students to do well. He is extremely fair and devotes much of his time to office hours. He is a really great teacher.

Interesting material in the class, but the professor was extremely boring and the 1:15 lectures were painful. 1-2 page and a half response papers are due every week after a lot of reading, so if you're looking for a class with little work this isn't it. They also grade the papers and exams pretty hard - I studied a lot and got B+s...Not an easy A.

BORING BORING BORING. Crowded lecture + monotone professor= snoozefest. I thought it would be a really great course but he made everything sound so tedious. I'll never take another class from this professor

His lectures are pretty flat. He assigns a lot of articles, some of which are interesting, but mostly they're just time consuming. Grading system is really annoying: every point you lose is 1% of your final grade. Miss a few questions on the midterm and you're already stuck at a B.

This teacher was horrible. I was very interested in the subject but he assigns inordinate amounts of work and grades very harshly. The experience was a negative one and my interest in the subject is now shot.

Sounded like it could be interesting from course description but Lynch is just a really flat lecturer. I couldnt help falling asleep.  Its just power point after power point, and the prelims cant really be studied for...

Great course... very repetitive of 301 tho, but new material is introdued. HW assignment dur every lecture, but counts towards final grade and keeps you up-to-date with reading. Profis really nice, and willing to offer extra help and explainant of anything. Took 30 1 and 407- i loved them both!
the course is very interesting, puts common ideas/concepts into different perspectives, exams are fair, straight forward, i'd recommend
Lynch is a good, friendly prof. His lectures do tend to make you rather sleepy, but his chosen material was interesting. Grading is fair, class wasn't too hard, but lots of reading.
spare me the lecture, i used it to catch up on my sleep....a lot of writing
he's really really nice but lecture is like having your sweet old uncle tell you a bedtime story...  just wanders off and voice drops off...  which is prolly why i just slept thru lecture.
Tom Lyson was the best professor Cornell has ever had. He was dedicated, dynamic and brilliant.We will never see the likes of him again. He's in Professor Heaven! Look down on us kindly!

This professor is deceased after fighting a courageous battle with cancer.  He cared deeply for people and the world around him and was devoted to the creation of a sustainable food system.  His concept of "civic agriculture" will reshape the way people view the food system.  He will be remembered with love and respect by all who worked with him.
VERY easy grader.  Class was boring though - very repititive and pedantic.  Rather arrogant and not nearly as bright as he thinks he is.
Course = Social Inequality.  Best course ever, read interesting books and then discuss.

He is the bottom of the barrel in every sense of the phrase. Material is based solely on his own beliefs and never presents counterarguments. When students question the material, he belittles them, even though he is the one who's definitively demented. Rude and pretentious. Blatantly sexist. Complete disgrace to the Hotel School. Do not enroll.
do not take. will ruin your Cornell experience
I have never had a professor that hates his students this much. He is extremely stubborn and will not help you when you need. Worst professor I've ever had.

Avoid if you can. The lectures are hyper-specific, obscure, and contradictory. The only way to prep for the exams - memorize (despite what the prof says).

The prof himself is very rude to students. I don't understand why be a prof if you don't like or know how to teach.

Save your tuition money.

reviews.comment: Worst professor at Cornell by far. 1) teaches outdated material 2) entire class is graded on t/f questions 3) insults the class for getting questions wrong 4) extremely rude and racist to students. DO NOT TAKE!

reviews.comment: He needs to go to anger management
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: (2)- attendance completely mandatory with I-Clicker grades for ACCURACY in the first minute of class. Offers no exceptions to missing class you just get a 0 which heavily effects your grade, even if you have legit doctors note or real conflict. Nothing he teaches is applicable to 2025 and argues with students if they ask questions. AVOID.

Despite success in the class, worst professor I have had at Cornell. Exams are all T/F about random and obscure concept from lecture/book. Is very rude and makes inappropriate comments in class about race / gender. Contradictory. rude when students reach out and rude when score low or students are confused. Outdated concepts. Offers 0 assistance.

DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE! Grades rely heavily on confusing iClicker quizzes starting at the first minute of class, often tricky with wording. The professor changes the schedule arbitrarily — he switched the final from online to in-person at the last minute, disrupting students' travel plans.

A lot of the prelims questions have nothing to do with what he talked about in class and he chose the most random thing ever from the book to quiz. IT's also all true and false and doesn't release the answers of iclicker and previous exams. Also no electronic devices allowed.

Please DO NOT TAKE ANY CLASS TAUGHT BY MIKE LYNN. Attendance is mandatory, based on ACCURACY iclicker at the moment the class starts. All of his slides are OUTDATED by 20-30 years (he provides sources, most are wikipedia). All of his exams are True/False, with subjective answers. I studied for 8+ hrs and I didn't even recognize HALF of the exam!!

reviews.comment: I wouldnt wish this on my worst enemy. Never take a class with professor lynn, he is the worst teacher I have ever had in my entire life and marketing is going to be my worst grade at Cornell. he only grades you based off of true or false exams that are all about over 10 year old data so you are bound to fail. never take this class with him.

Do not take Lynn's class. Confusing and cluttered lectures with WAY too much specific content that contradicts other things he says. Exams are true/false which is the only redeeming quality. Daily I-clicker quizzes, NO technology whatsoever, required textbook readings.

Changed a grade worth 25% of final grade for "finding a mistake in calculating" despite posting the grade already??? also admitted to saying incorrect information during lecture but still expects the class to know it
lecture videos and content are all prehistoric and outdated. often argues with students who ask questions...avoid avoid avoid

(pt. 3) Also iclicker quizzes are done within the first minute of class and if you're even 2 minutes late one day due to any extenuating circumstances he won't let you make up the quiz and you get a zero. Also no technology in class so you have to handwrite notes. Goes out of his way to be mean and aggressive towards students for no reason.

(pt 1) DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS. He's incredibly rude to students for simply asking him to reexplain things, makes sexist/inappropriate comments, and is the most boring lecturer. I'm practically falling asleep in every lecture and half the time he doesn't even teach he just plays long videos and expects us to memorize the information from them.

Plays videos and reads off of powerpoint slides the entire class. Expects everyone to remember the content of the videos despite saying "do not memorize" for exams. Insults the class for getting a t/f question wrong for no reason

every exam is entirely true/false with statements that have one word altered. makes racist comments in class, highly inappropriate examples. major ego and often yells back at students for asking questions. says not to memorize material but has questions on literally remembering random statistics from the textbook

First of all, this guy shouldn't be here at Cornell, but stay in his medieval times generation. Lectures="good old days info".The videos in class are older than us.Major takeaway-never become a marketing prof after psych major.his confidence level is higher than the accuracy of his class. He can continue his google scholar research papers instead.
Makes inappropriate comments in his lectures. Lecture participation is graded based on impossibly hard iclicker quizzes.

Doesn't allow electronic devices in his class, similar to a high school classroom. Reads off a PowerPoint for the whole class, similar to a high school class. Professor Lynn may be an expert in hospitality marketing but in my opinion is not a great college educator.

All exams are True/False and are very subjective and up to professor's interpretation. Not interested in returning points even if you prove him wrong, "that's what the curve is for". All lecture materials are old and half the time he just plays videos instead of teaching. Avoid at all costs.

reviews.comment:
Your grade is basically the average of prelims and iClicker attendance quizzes (which are still very hard - so even if you go to every class you might still end with a 75-85% on the "attendance")

Prelims are 70-90 "True or False" questions, let me give you an example: "T/F - The starting salary of a marketing assistant is $27,000" Obscene

reviews.comment: His (true/false) exam questions are so subjective and have no definitive answer. Therefore, the exams are almost impossible and are curved very little....

reviews.comment: Worst professor at Cornell, uses old research, yells at students when asked questions, course material is contradictory, doesn't say hi when seen outside of class, did not deserve the grade that I got, unfair grading

reviews.comment: Everything he presents/teaches is from 20+ years ago. Nothing he teaches is remotely relevant anymore. Also, his massive ego is so insufferable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst professor I have ever had. His canvas is blank and unhelpful; he has no TAs or mandatory I-Clicker exams in every single class (that count for 33% of your grade), and just uninteresting. After our first exam, he sent us all an email telling us how poorly we had done, in a very aggressive tone. Do everything you can to avoid this teacher...
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is one of the worst professors I've had at Cornell. Everything people are saying here is true. He has a huge ego and goes out of his way to be condescending to students. He can't answer questions about things he hasn't prepared in class and if you email and ask him to clarify something, he refuses to do so, telling you to figure it out.

He's nice, but this is the worst class I've taken. I've not met one person who actually likes this class/him. He uses studies from the late 1900's and uses them as "proof" that all the modern marketing classes we've taken are wrong. He has a big ego and wants to be right with everything. His class is boring and uses videos instead of teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Shows videos instead of teaching, and tells us it's time for him to rest, but not us. Would not post his slides prior to class, not allowing students to preview the course materials. Exams are entirely T/F questions. Very subjective, no review material, ONLY MEMORIZATION works. Don't provide answer to practice questions, expect us to guess answers.

Lynn is very defensive and somewhat aggressive towards students. He posts announcements with wording like "I have already told you, but here it is again" and "apparently, some of you interpreted my previous email as saying I do not want to meet with you. Not true." He borderline yells when you ask questions he doesn't have a concrete answer to.

Most research presented in lecture is from the 80s or 90s, and Prof. Lynn often resorts to showing the class videos instead of lecturing himself. Additionally, on the homework, Prof. Lynn expects groups to write the answers exactly how he wants and will severely punish groups who do not. Very tough grader and not very understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
I'll describe Prof Lynn's class: "Here's your next assignment. It counts for 5% of your grade and you have eight of these. If you don't do every little part of it EXACTLY how I want you get an F. And I won't tell you how I want you to do it. Figure it out"

He does not care about his students and gives very tough grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He's very passionate about Marketing but the course is outdated and textbook and lecture heavy. The course content is supposed to be very easy but he has the most vague wordings, making the exams and the project unnecessarily confusing. Grading's also very harsh and the curves make no sense, I think the class average for final exam was in 70s.

Lynn is a very sweet man but he is very outdated. He often shows videos during class from late 90s and early 2000s. If you ask him for clarification on anything you likely won't get it. Exams are T/F and matching, which is much harder than you'd think. He barely has any other grades so if you do poorly on an exam you won't do well overall. Mediocre
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: he doesnt even know how to organize his Blackboard website and slides... man has to learn his alphabet and simple math if he plans on still teaching here.

reviews.comment: It seems like he has been living under a rock for the last decade because he has no idea about technology or social media marketing. We watch videos from the 80s and pretend like theyre still relevant. Doesnt know simple math. No point in going to lecture except for iclicker because he just reads verbatim off his Comic Sans PowerPoint
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof. Lynn is a good guy and the class is pretty interesting. I would recommend to anyone who cares about learning things and who isn't there for a free A. The material is pretty straightforward, but the nature of his tests (TF, some matching) make it easy to do decent but hard to do really well. Go to class and you should have at least a BB+

Definitely my favorite class that I've taken at Cornell.  Don't know why there are some many negative reviews - he's a great professor and the material is extremely interesting.  I recommend it to everyone
He sucks. Lynn only cares about "tipping"! Did you know that he's an expert?!?! If you don't he will let you know.

A pretty good prof. Great material and lots of movie clips and demos etc that make the class very interesting. His tests involve quite a bit of memory-type questions that require reading of the book. Frankly not very good at fielding questions and not very helpful in person. Overall, I thought the class was great and he taught reasonably well.
very interesting lectures and material.  pop quizzes are easy as long as you go to class.

What a terrible teacher! The only reason this guy teaches is so he could do research on "tipping"... he is not interested in his students, he is not clear or fair at all, he is not very knowledgeable on the subject, and he is EXTREMELY BORING! almost no one came to class... what a waste of my hard-earned tuition dollars!
Interesting course material-- shame about the professor who manages to bore you to tears. Confused about concepts and has to correct himself through email. This class was NOT worth it whatsoever.

Fell asleep almost everysingle class. he confuses people on purpose. I WISH I NEVER TOOK THIS COURSE.  Bored to tears. Repeatedly asked myself, "What the hell are you talking about, this stuff is freaking obvious!"  Lynn has no real experience in the industry..he's only been "an assistant professor". go take a real class, like finance or yield mgmt
One of my favorite professors at Cornell.  If you are the least bit interested in Marketing you should definitely take this class.
Horrible Professor!  Never had class, graded very hard, no feedback whatsoever

Horrendous professor. Canceled over 50% of classes because she was "sick" and e-mailed unnecessary assignments with arbitrary guidelines to try and make it look like she was doing her job. Learned almost nothing over the entire semester and could have taken the class online. Easy class with very strange paper grading but Bogel should be fired.

Great, great, professor. She clearly loves what she does and wants to share it with you. Easygoing about deadlines and such, very understanding. Definitely a worthwhile class, especially if you have to take a FWS.

Best FWS ever. Very nice lady, has free, fun, and insightful discussions about the interesting films she picks out. Short papers (2-3 pages) about each of the 6~7 movies watched, no long papers. Pretty easy and interesting class.

Amazing professor. I have never met someone with such interest in her field as well as interest in helping students understand her world of film. Didn't require any reading, watched great films, cancelled class a lot, and was very flexible with due dates. Best professor thus far.
good class, cancels class a lot, understanding with deadlines
This FWS rocks!  Despite haveing to go watch the movie once in a while, I don't think I have written a paper over 5 pages!  Also the material is actually interesting... and hey free movies!
Bogel is just cool; she cancels class all the time.  I heard all the other FWS profs sucked, so take Bogel.  She's easy, fun, and CANCELS class often.
Excellent professor. Flexible with deadlines, not too harsh on papers, and very knowledgeable about the subject. A class act.
Very nice and cool teacher who def enjoys cancelling class. Difficult grader but ultimately very fair. Movies are fun and Bogel is both funny and mad chill.
Prepare to get your mind bogeled.
Cancels ALL the time.  But the time spent not in class is made up by the time the movie screenings take up.  The class is great, but she's such a strict grader!!
Canceled half of her classes, wish I had known in advance, great discussion when there actually is class.

Very good discussion in class, but cancels many classes.  Enjoyable at first, but when you start getting poor grades for leaving out material that was never covered (because no classes were held) it gets annoying and unfair.  Fickle on grading.

Intelligent and interested in the material. Stretches meanings in the movies. The semester I had her she cancelled 25% of classes for some unknown reason. She's okay, but the writing seminar was good.
Hitchcock class is great.  Sometimes Prof. Bogel seems a bit unorganized, but she is extremely intelligent and makes the class interesting and fun.
She's very easy going and interested in the material. She is also a pretty fair grader.

She seems to have two personalities...one is the warm, easy going person you experience in class...the other is a very harsh grader that you only experience via email as all the assignments are done this way...

Though I really liked watching all the cool films, I'm not a fan of the course. Writing about movies, or even writing about literature/fiction, seems pointless to me. You often have to find meaning where there is none.Movies/books are meant to be enjoyed.
I took a movies FWS from Lynda. She's an awesome person and a great teacher. I also liked watching movies instead of reading books. :-)

Her lectures were very fast-paced. She tells students to focus on big picture ideas but then tests on small details from her slideshows (and does not curve). Exams are very memorization-based and can have confusing wording. The content of this course was very interesting, but her exams were way too difficult for an intro course.
Everyday, I wake up trying to transfer out of my major due to this woman.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I've had Medina for both NS 1150 and 3310, and my opinion on her as a professor has not changed. She is rude, her content is very heavy, and she brags that people don't do well in her courses. Ask a genuine question and she will make you feel stupid. Why teach challenging courses if you are just going to discourage students who are trying?

I am sorry, but this class was genuinely worse than orgo, so the worst class I have taken here at Cornell, thus far as a junior. The wording of the exam questions was absolutely ridiculous, and the lecture slides were very compact. She made it unclear in terms of what we actually had to know and take away from the lectures.

reviews.comment: She expects you to memorize the exact wording of the slides and tests brute memorization over understanding of concepts.  It's not impossible to do well, but do not expect an easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The material is interesting, what really ruins this class are the exams.The exams are purposefully confusing and overall it feels like they are trying to trick you more than actually test knowledge.I wouldn't take this class unless you have to.If you are taking this class memorize everything and at the end of the class there is a very small curve.

reviews.comment: I took this class out of curiosity as I'm not in NS but thought it would be interesting. I regret my decision. There's no homework and you grade is 75% based on exams. Unfortunately her exams require you to memorize the slides and readings. Each lesson is a slide deck of +50 slides. It's impossible to do well if you are not a nutri sci major.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Medina-Rivera comes across as sweet, but I really disliked the class. She lacks empathy for her students and is only available for OH on zoom. TAs also lack empathy. Class is good for students who enjoy memorizing extremely specific content that is largely useless for non-majors, but I struggled with that pedagogy. Felt like a waste of time.

She gives good lectures generally, but her tests are absolutely ridiculous for an intro class. You pretty much need to know every single detail on the lecture slides. The answer choices are very tricky. You could "defend your answer" but you need to give her a very very detailed explanation. She seems like a sweet and caring professor though.

The test content are all in the slides. She tries somewhat hard and the slides aren't that bad, but she isn't that good at answering questions. 

The most annoying thing is that she tests you on the smallest details on the slides so no matter how hard you study you're bound to get at least a few questions wrong.
lectures were unorganized + her handwriting was hard to read. exams aren't the easiest + nothing like past practice exams. AVOID unless meche ofc (goodluck)
Overhated. Meredith's not an eloquent lecturer, but thermo was manageable if you had reasonable focus.
Lectures were not helpful, neither were the practice prelims. Good luck mech-es and if you don't have to take this class, don't take it. Expect alot of self teaching.

Silberstein is pretty difficult with lectures, they are hard to follow and disorganized. The assumption based focus of this class is a good idea, but executed imperfectly. Grading is decently lenient.
Avoid at all costs

I found the grading in this class to be surprisingly lenient. You can get partial credit on exams just for writing a formula from the six-page cheat sheet you get to make for the final. Participation points are very easy to get. Even though the lectures aren't great, the class is forgiving enough that it's manageable.

This class used to be an easy A and Silberstein has made it... not. Lecs are boring, hard to follow, disorganized, and full of mistakes, even though she precalculates everything (and doesn't show you where numbers come from). HW is chill only bc she posts solutions before they're due, but exams are impossible. You do get to make cheat sheets though
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Expects a lot from her first group of students taking her course, with little leniency built into grading. Lectures are incredibly hard to follow, and after stumbling through examples for 45 ungodly min in horrid formatting, I just couldn't stay engaged. Beyond that, she makes significant errors in class. Should try imitating PHYS 2213 and 1112.

Everyone says that she is a terrible lecturer, but she is genuinely a very nice person. The exams aren't particularly difficult, it's just very textbook based and graded harshly (the medians ~70s). It would be helpful if the quizzes or material were more indicative of the content of the exams. But overall she's a great person if you talk to her.

Truly the WOAT. The lectures are physically painful to get through because of her voice and lack of knowledge on her own content. Her typical response to questions in class is "that's a good point" *uncomfortable laugh*. Study material has too many mistakes to be useful. If you have the misfortune of dealing with meredih I wish you luck.

genuinely the worst professor I have ever had here. thermo is supposed to be an easy class with straightforward tests. not only did she make the tests impossibly confusing and hard, but she's an awful lecturer! good luck looking at her lecture slides, because they are riddled with errors spanning from conceptual to arithmetic to spelling!

Silberstein is the only professor I have met here that I cannot fathom pass her own class. Sometimes I think the medians are so low because her answer key is just wrong and she refuses to fix it. TA's are covering content they haven't learned in the semester before and every time she responds to you, you get this sense of sheer hostility.
If i had a loaded firearm in her office hours, I would use it on myself because even with her gone, I cannot live anymore with the damage she has caused to my thinking ability.
jesus christ

Zoom options make it easy to review after lectures (especially with 2x speed). However, most of the lecture time is focused on examples, which are good for individual practice, but in lecture, it causes people to lose focus... Homework solutions are always posted before the due date. The workload is not heavy, but the lectures are not very useful.
My patient gramps listened for all of 23 seconds before exclaiming "This is worse than Vietnam" before putting a screwdriver through my car stereo. (continued in review below)
No thank you to prof for making my wallet 200 USD short and causing gramps to end up in the forbidden asylum.
Ridiculously hard exams, disorganized lectures, tough grading
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: From the bottom of my heart, I must thank professor Silberstein, for she pulled off a max-mog miracle. I brought my ILR friend who is unfortunately a life-long cripple to one of the thermodynamics lectures. Lo and Behold, he magically stood up and ran out of lecture. Thank you professor for giving my friend the ability to stand up for himself!

Lectures were very unengaging and not helpful at all. She often got problems wrong in lecture. Exams were nothing like the given practice exams and were ridiculously hard. I don't usually ever skip class but I would skip this one because she was just that bad.
She's lowkey a nice person. Sometimes struggles explaining complex topics and expects a lot out of students.
just not a nice person. Also cannot teach and gets things wrong in her lecture notes?? At least her TA's are good with partial credit.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOO

If you're an atheist, pick a religion and pray. I dread waking up because of this class. I've stopped looking both ways before crossing the street in the hopes that I won't have to take this class anymore. Hell is empty because Meredith is here.
Ridiculously hard content with very little explanation. Inhuman amount of homework and tough grading.

Professor Silberstein, while good intentioned, comes to class wildly unprepared for lecture. Would often do problems and realize (after students called her out) that she had done them completely wrong. I got through this class solely by reading the textbook and learning on my own. Not approachable, kind of mean.
She is so mean and rude and just an awful teacher. I would give her a negative rating.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: My only complaint is that her handwriting is really bad and can sometimes make it hard to follow her notes. Otherwise, she is great and I enjoyed the class

She has an aggressive, condescending attitude towards students which makes her lectures very calculations-oriented rather than focused on introducing and explaining concepts to the class. So if you walk in 5 mins late, you'll see a bunch of numbers scrawled on the board and have no idea what they are. She mocks students for asking questions.

I had Professor Silberstein in Spring of 2016. Right from the get-go I knew that the class (statics) would be horrible, and by the end my initial impressions were confirmed. The grading policy was horrendous and is essential set up so that students are not successful. I wish ratemyprofessor had a rating lower than 1. I do not recommend her.
Uncurved class.. mean on the final was a 62. Makes it incredibly hard to do well. Prof Silberstein succeeds in making an intuitive and interesting class for engineers into a complete nightmare.
Least favorite professor I've had at Cornell. The class isn't that hard but she's not a good teacher and is especially unhelpful when you ask questions.
Handwriting is messy and the lectures are disjointed. Lectures consisted mostly of her going through example problems without explaining how she was solving them.

Silberstein is alright. The expectations for the course are pretty straightforward, and all the info you need to know for the homework and exams is in lecture. She doesn't curve the class, but the prelims weren't that bad and the averages were 83 or 84. The iClicker quizzes are the worst though, they're 20% of your grade which is insane.
Please take this class with Sachse. Nothing else to say.

So far my least favorite professor I've had my three years here. Lectures were frustrating because her handwriting was messy and her hand always blocked her notes. She was extremely condescending at office hours and didn't even know how to solve the problems. Not helpful at all and only laughed/scoffed at me when I would ask her for help.
She aight

It's her first time teaching, and yes, you can tell. But I think that her lectures were all right, and the discussion classes were very helpful as well. I learned enough in lecture and discussion to be able to do the homework without much problem. I'd say she's doing all right for her first time teaching.
worst professor i have had in my undergraduate career thus far. too bad i have to pass this class.

First time she's ever taught a class. You can tell. She really doesn't seem to have any interest in helping her students do well and sometimes I feel like she actually wants to fail half the class. Her I-clicker questions and quizzes are useless.
Silberstein is an alright Prof. she teaches the material that's on her tests, and her tests aren't that hard. Annoying laugh though.

Agreed. If this is not a requirement course for you, DO NOT TAKE IT. I've had my fair share of good/bad professors but she is definitely the worst I've had. Lectures are one of the most boring and unorganized I've ever seen (very few pp slides, almost all handwritten notes)

Just run. She might be the single most condescending professor I have ever encountered. She thinks we're all stupid and she just laughs at everything. Her lecture is an enormous waste of time, unfortunately she takes I-clicker attendance. Her handwriting is both illegible and tiny. Effectively curves the class to a C which is just grand.

Dr. Smith is the kindest and best professor I had at Cornell. She teaches statistics in a far more applied way than most other stats/math profs, which makes her class more engaging and enjoyable than other statistics classes I've taken. The take home exam was hard, but the other two exams are very fair.

Dr. Smith is one of the best professors I've ever had! She is so knowledgeable about the subject matter, and her exams are based off the homework. The open-ended project was a lot of work, but super helpful in learning the content. Best stats elective I've taken so far!

Dr. Smith is very accommodating to students without prior statistics experience. I found the lectures easy to follow despite not having taken statistics in high school or college. The material was presented in a way that was both straightforward and thorough.

Dr. Smith was a very effective teacher. I never had to open the textbook, taking notes during lectures and one night of studying before exams is sufficient to doing very well. Her lectures are great, but homework can be unclear. This class does barely cover any content so if you actually want to learn more than median and mean, take a harder class

She seems to only be capable of ending a sentence with the word "ok."  I counted, and in one lecture she said okay 400 times, for an average of one ok per 7.5 seconds.  One sample isn't the best statistical practice, but trust me when one ok per 7.5 seconds isn't unusual for her lectures.  It's extremely annoying, but otherwise she's good.

Professor Smith has to be hands down my favorite professor thus far at Cornell. Her lectures are so engaging, and she makes boring content seem so fun! The only downside I see to this class is the slow grading of exams. Other than that, 100% recommend taking the course for anybody interested in statistics as a whole!
professor is super knowledgeable about the subject matter and gives good lectures with real-world examples - workload is manageable and exams are pretty fair
amazing prof, very knowledgeable abt the material and gives lectures well. exams questions are straight from class content, so very fair

She made me want to consider minoring in statistics. Made stats fun and engaging. GO TO TA OFFICE HOURS because they will give you (or check) answers. She is also very sweet and approachable. Tests are very similar to the practice tests, so def go over them and ask questions. The review sessions are ACTUALLY helpful.

Professor Smith is one of my favorite professors I have ever had at Cornell. She is a wonderful lecturer and loves to get to know her students. She makes you interested about statistics. I looked forward to her classes every week.

Super kind + caring professor, course was highly accessible. It is designed so that you can come in with no stats knowledge and leave with a decent foundation. Felt disorganized at times, and pacing (ie labs and content) was a bit slow. But Dr. Smith is one of the nicest and most caring teachers I have met. Put in the work, and you will be fine!
The best! She is hilarious and makes the material interesting.

Dr. Smith is an actual angel. Have never seen a more fun and loving prof who cares so much for her students. Listen to lectures/read slides and you'll be golden, she has no intention of failing you. She is passionate about math, and just wants to foster the same passion amongst her students. A literal saint.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Agree with some of the comments saying that she is disorganized... and oh god what a procrastinator she is. Homework submission links are often posted a few hours before deadline, a ton of last-minute revisions are made, and she doesn't post any answers to homework which makes studying for exams so so difficult. The course itself is not hard tough.

A delight! She strives to make the class interesting and relatable. She wore a costume for Halloween and went WILD with it. She's truly a treasure and wants to make statistics intuitive. Personally found that the class material went slowly, but I have relatively strong math and statistics exposure.

She is a good teacher but the class felt very disorganized. She grades attendance despite the syllabus saying attendance is not required and the timing of grading is also very vague. There were barely any materials to study for the prelim.
I love her. She genuinely makes lectures so interesting and she learns all the students' names. Respect.

Dr. Smith was very nice and used interesting examples during lecture. However, the class felt kind of disorganized (and expectations for exams were sometimes unclear) and there's a lot of exams (3 prelims and a final). The homework was pretty easy but time consuming. She held a review session before each exam, which was nice.
She's great! She explained the concepts really well, and had plenty of time in class to help review concepts. A lot of my time was spent learning R, but that helped a lot too.

Amazing professor! HW assignments were helpful and helped me understand the material and prelims weren't too hard. Only problem was the TAs. They took days to answer questions about the HW on Ed Discussion and if they did decide to answer, it would be AFTER the HW assignments were due. Also haven't graded labs that we turned in almost a month ago.

Dr. Smith is the best! She uses real life examples so statistics can make sense to us in the real world.  Go to office hours with the TA's if you need help with the labs. I only needed to read the textbook for clarification to get a second explanation.

I actually really like Dr. Smith but my problem is with the labs. The TA in my lab section sleeps every single time so there is no one to ask for help. Also the TA presenting the lab is monotoned and half of the class doesn't pay attention. I like the way the Python labs are set up where they give you an assignment and then walk around to help you.
Dr. Smith makes lectures interesting by using fun examples. The labs help a lot with the prelims and there are lots of office hours. Great class!
Cool proffesor

Dr. Smith is great and she is super passionate about statistics which makes lectures engaging and interesting. She also loves class participation and cracking jokes! You definitely need to read the textbook to keep up with lectures and make sure to attend lectures! They aren't mandatory but they are super useful.

Great professor and super accommodating towards the pandemic issue. She teaches clearly and personally, I didn't find the textbook helpful but it's good for reinforcing material. Tests were fair but do require some studying. Lab times weren't that useful but I went to a lot of office hours with UTAs and they were super helpful.

Great prof! Very caring and tries to make the class as fun as possible. She prepared us well for exams, and I really ended up learning a lot. She's also very easy to talk to, and really tries to help us with our questions.

She's very sweet and really tries to get to know her students. I am not a huge fan of math classes, but she made this class very engaging. Her lectures are clear, and she explains concepts very well. Her exams are challenging but fair, and she gives us a lot of information about them and tons of practice. Love her!

definitely one of the best instructors in cornell. lecture isn't mandatory but a lot of board work. homeworks take a while. melissa is very helpful and understanding and even has lunch with her students.

Most of these reviews are from her big intro stats class. I had her for a 40 person Categorical Data lecture. After 1 week she knew every persons name. Every class she brought a lot of energy and used real life examples to teach stats. My favorite stats professor so far. I am taking her Survival Analysis class next semester.

Dr. Smith is one of the few professors who are willing to get up close and personal with her students. Her class is VERY interactive and as enjoyable as a stats class can be. Exams are very fair and manageable. Going to lab is VERY useful for completing the problem sets, as TAs give pointers/answer questions on how to go about problems/R code.

If you've taken stats before, this class will be a breeze, but if you haven't, prof Smith will guide you through it every step of the way. She really cares about each student, and takes the time to get to know you personally during class. Lectures can be a bit disorganized at times, but you WILL understand the material by the time the exam comes.

Dr. Smith is amazing! She takes the time to get to know her students and makes an effort to to engage us in discussions during lectures. She explains things very well, and makes her exams challenging but fair. She is also very caring and approachable, and one of the few professors I've been able to become friends with outside of class!

By far the most disorganized course I've taken. The homeworks and lecture notes, particularly by the end of the semester, made no sense and were rife with grammar errors that caused the problems to be confusing. The textbook was okay, but supplemental readings were not helpful at all. You also don't get to see answer keys which is problematic.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Dr. Smith is a real gem of a professor. She takes the time to get to know her students, and is passionate about her subject. She really goes the distance to make sure Stats is easily graspable, and there is never a dull lecture. She is one of the best professors I have had here at Cornell, and I recommend her fully.

Dr. Smith uses lots of real life examples or experiments to explain the material, and she teaches better than the textbook. There are lots of opportunities to practice newly learned material in class. She is funny, engaging, and even memorizes all her student's names. She also gives out extra credit (as long as you attend the lectures).

my best friend. well at least i feel like it. she actually tries to learn names which is cool. tbh i would listen to her podcast if she had one. shes a great speaker and good at explaining difficult topics. very engaging in class participation.
Really amazing professor. She is very clear and fun and makes a huge effort to get to know her students. The class isn't easy but if you stay on top of your work it is definitely manageable.

I was really unprepared for this class when I took it. Melissa was very helpful and really cared about her students. The homeworks follow what we did in lecture pretty carefully. I think it was important to have good lecture notes. Most people thought this class was fairly average in terms of difficulty. We did fun activities and she is an amazing
Amazing person and teacher

Shes a really great professor, I go to lectures because shes a great speaker, even though you could get the same stuff from the textbook. She talks fast but is engaging. Labs are really hard and the TAs not so good but the content is practical. I have a bit of a crush.
Professor McCarthy is the best. I love this man!
this man will go out of his way to help you. he'll zoom on weekends. he'll help you get an internship. favorite prof at Cornell by far. thanks prof

goated prof. really cares about students and goes above and beyond. I know he helped connect a few students to help them get internships. smart and funny. knows a lot about ai. def look forward to taking again.
Prof Mccarthy was really funny and caring and made lectures engaging. Also easy to look at (just saying)

Chillest Prof at ILR. He wont teach you the most detailed or intricate things but he is very dedicated to helping you and will try to bring in guest speakers he wants to give you internships with. He truly cares and it is clear in his teaching. He is very kind and wants to help students. A fun guy all around.

My favorite professor. Really cares about you. Only rated a 5 difficulty because he joked in class about being annoyed about having an easy rating. Great teacher, explains everything well and has funny anecdotes to keep class interesting. Also, very easy class
By far my favorite professor that I've had while here at Cornell. A down-to-earth, amazing guy that clearly cares about his students as much as he does for their education.
John McCarthy is a really nice guy with a lot of heart. He made exams open book and made review sheets with everything that was going to be covered on the exam listed. He deserves the world!

Down to earth and very realistic. Good guy who cares about his students and the subject matter. Mostly graded by a prelim and final where he gives a study rubric outlining the questions. Easy A if you pay attention in class.

[Labor, Work, and Employment in Public Education] Good class overall, interesting lectures, readings, and guest speakers. He is a great prof, an interesting guy, and easy to talk to when you need help.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: McCarthy is great! He is incredibly sweet and easy to talk to outside of class. I had him during the pandemic which makes it difficult to accurately judge his teaching style. But the class was interesting!

the best thing i can say to describe class is "meh". took the class during the pandemic and lectures were pre-recorded for some reason . . not sure why they weren't delivered live... classes were cancelled a lot.

Professor McKinley demonstrates a lack of professionalism in his interactions with students. He constantly talked to students while reclining in his chair in an overly dismissive manner, which conveys disrespect and undermines the seriousness of the academic environment.
Best professor at Cornell. Not just good at teaching, but a great person as well, goes out of his way to hold extra office hours before exams. And he's funny
Easy A/A+. Makes accounting enjoyable. Caring and willing to work with students outside of class. If you are looking for an easy A for accounting, his class is best to take.

Really funny and caring guy, knew my name despite the fact that I rarely attended or participated in class, very understanding, and tries his best to keep his students engaged so they can learn the material.

Hilarious and knows everything about Tax. Does NOT like people missing lectures or arriving late. Really does care about his students. Very important to pay attention in lecture; he emphasizes the things he's going to be testing on, so if you go to lecture you'll know what to focus on when studying and what you can just skim.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Makes accounting interesting and enjoyable to learn, and has sparked my personal interest in the subject

Course isn't that bad. McKinley uses real-life examples and calls on students often which are effective. He teaches to the material and audit concepts and not to the test which is good. Genuinely cares about students and doesn't want to fail anyone. Door is always open for students to ask questions. Highly recommend taking a class with McKinley

Hard class. But McKinley really cares about his students and knows the material inside and out. Definition of a great professor who wants to see students actually learn and succeed. Great rapport with students and very approachable for help and review of exams and assignments. Get ready to be called on though because he does stress participation.
He went on to ramble about how proud he became senior lecturer because of his wife, he is a p-on-ce.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: McBride is a great prof! Always kind, caring, and understanding. He makes sure his class isn't conflicting with any other classes and is very flexible with extensions. Make sure to stay in communication with him if you can't meet a deadline - communication is key! The syllabus guarantees an A if all work is turned in (regardless of quality).
Very kind and generous on deadlines. Wants everyone to succeed in writing and gives great feedback. Clearly passionate about his subject and gives everyone an A as long as they participate

McBride is a jolly fellow. He is very sincere and genuine and is extraordinarily generous with absences and extensions. 100% recommend taking his class if you can because it will be an enriching and joyful experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: McBride is truly THE sweetest professor  unbelievably understanding with extensions, super approachable both in and outside of class, and really knowledgable about historical context of the texts we read. He makes sure everyone feels comfortable speaking up or asking for help, which is so kind and supportive. Could not recommend him enough, truly!

He's very personable and overall just a very kind person. Absolutely willing to work with you individually, very understanding of individual situations, and super flexible with deadlines. He's also very easy to get off topic and he'll talk for 10 minutes on something tangentially related. Also pretty funny.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Mcbride is a wonderful professor! He can be a little confusing at first but once you get to know his style of teaching, the in-class discussions become so deep and interesting. He tells you exactly what to fix with your essays, and everyone is guaranteed a B so long as you show up and make deadlines. Very manageable workload for a writing seminar.

I thoroughly enjoyed this course. The material was intriguing and fun (fairytales and a sci-fi novel) and the course-load was not overwhelming like in other writing classes. McBride can be a little hard to follow sometimes, but he is extremely passionate about this course and he presents interesting ideas. This is a fun & thought-provoking course!
Terrible prof, terrible class. You can do better, prospective student, trust me.

Very interesting professor, cares a lot about what he is teaching and the students.  Nice to have the "guaranteed B" but very difficult to get anything above that.  If you're happy with doing minimal work and getting a B, take him because he is interesting, but avoid if you want a higher grade.

GERST 1109 used to be an easy class, but the grading policy has changed. Be prepared to receive a solid B in the class, while 2-3 other people get A's. Everyone is guaranteed a B in the class as long as you do the minimal work, but achieving an A is hard. Thought passionate about Romanticism, McBride often rambles on, leaving students confused.

He is a fantastic teacher who is incredibly motivating and interesting in class. Every section is well prepared and ready to engage students. He takes time to get an understanding of every student's fluency in the language so that grading reflects effort, growth, and participation fairly.
Great Professor, always willing to help and always showed interest. He may sometimes lose focus and jump between topics but his ideas and teaching methods are interesting and effective.

A very good professor overall and an interesting FWS. He is clearly enthusiastic about the subject, but sometimes, his explanations can get confusing if you have questions. Other than that, he'll try to get the students involved a lot so expect some failed attempts at humor on his part (in a good way) to get his students comfortable.
He was an extremely nice professor and was always extremely willing to help. I overall really liked him.

Professor McLeod is a great teacher and she makes learning engaging and interesting. However you have to do the readings to grasp the Theory. Sometimes the readings are a bit technical. Attendance is the bread and butter of this one, don't skip the activities. However she knows her stuff. One of the best classes in CALs.

Could really tell she cared about her students. A lot of reading/discussion posts and mandatory attendance was a pain but ultimately worth it because the take-home exams and essays were bearable. Hated the group project, but that wasn't her fault. She took student feedback to heart and tried to make lectures more engaging.
Great class, unique experiential format, although the grading rubrics can be vague. Prelim and final are easy if you study the review questions. Would recommend!

Class is incredibly boring so its a hike and a half just to make it there in the morning even though attendance is mandatory. The TAs feedback for prelim essays was confusing and not helpful. The professor did nothing to make this better. She doesnt give clear directions and was rude when asked to clarify further on instructions for help.

I loved Professor McLeod as a person! She was a great teacher and I enjoyed her lectures. Her textbook was BORING and she did have a lot of reading. The quizzes for the year were fairly easy. The 4 Take Home Exams are hit and miss for me. I got great grades on most of them, but the grading was hard and confusing. TA's were absolutely the worst.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: This class was okay. She knows what she is talking about, but considering it's an intro class, it's not very interesting. iClickers are used and she is insanely strict about attendance - we literally had assigned seats at one point. In a 100+ person college lecture. Not too difficult and TAs are very helpful.

I respect the way she teaches. COMM 1101 has very boring and dull material (expected form an intro class) and she tries to make it interesting for her students. Reading the textbook is a must if you want to get at least a B on the quizzes. If you suck at multiple choice then you'll like her prelims because it's all essay format.

Prof McLeod is great! She's fun, upbeat, and a brilliant speaker. The course is nowhere near as difficult as previous ratings state; if you apply both lecture and book material on the exams (and make connections), you'll do very well.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. The professor sucks and the class is so boring. It's literally been a nightmare taking this class. If this is a required class for you because of your major, switch majors to avoid hell. The trouble of switching majors is worth not taking this class.

This is one of the worst classes I've ever taken. The lectures are so incredibly boring. Attendance is mandatory and she's really strict if you miss a class no matter what the reason is. The professor isn't available that much and was very rude. She comes off very nice, but she's deceptively terrible. I would never wish this teacher upon anyone.

The lectures were uninteresting (I think the source material, not Prof. McLeod is at fault here). The textbook is HORRENDOUS. The expectations for the exams are unclear and grades can fluctuate greatly. The in-class tests are stupid difficult. I took two upper-level COMM courses at the same time and got A's. I got a B in 1101.

Horrible class. Terrible organization structure. No in-class exams. You think you're getting off easier with the 4 take-home exams? Think again. They are horrible. Neither her or her TA's tell you what they want. You answer the questions correctly, but they may not like how you worded somethingWRONG. I hated this class. Would never recommend.

Dense and uninteresting material with harsh grading. I've taken upper-level COMM classes and had no problem with them, but you have to work unnecessarily hard to get a good grade here. Test material doesn't match the lectures at all. Prof is hard to approach and condescending. Don't take this class if it isn't a requirement.

She is absolutely amazing: nice, classy, entertaining, knowledgeable of subject matter, engaging...I could go on and on. I would recommend her or her classes to anyone! She is one of the best professors at Cornell!
She makes every class fun, and communicates her expectations clearly!

Lectures were all directed and useful for exams, and she's very personable and helpful. She has lots of spunk and sometimes likes to start class by playing the goo-goo dolls. Exams were fair, she was fair.
was very unavailable and rude. very difficult to approach. at first I thought she looked cool but now I would not recommend this teacher for any kind of adviser.

This was by far the best class I have ever taken. Teacher is incredible- REALLY love teaching. Not only is she interesting but her classes are fun. I can honestly say we had a couple classes where everyone stayed late because they were so into the exercise that they lost track of time- DON'T MISS THIS CLASS
would call on you and pick you out of the crowd also tests and class work didn't always match

Prof. Poppy McLeod is awesome! Interesting, engaging, and exciting professor who is knowledgable and really cares about teaching her students.  Unique approach to class.  Gets students involved by doing hands-on learning rather than just lecturing. Such a nice and fun person.  And entertaining! Does have car problems.  Def a chili.

What a unique personallity!  Starting the class each day with a little taste of her, Poppy has a great way of making class feel like a conversation rather than a lecture.  The one thing she needs to get a grip on is her car!  haha.  Wonderful person.
very cool woman.  she plays music in the morning to wake people up.  she has lots of energy.  inspiring too!  and she definitely likes her chili peppers.
Wish I could have taken this class sooner!  Awesome!
Best prof of my life!
Great class - combines theoretical learning with hands-on exercises and group tasks.  Everyone should take this class!

Michael Sheehan is a great professor and lecturer, super knowledgeable about his field. The course title may be misleading as it does have some challenging biology material, but is well worth if you are interested in learning about animal behavior.

professor is very knowledgeable about the subject matter and makes lectures pretty engaging (incorporates interesting animal videos into his slides); i found all of the assignments and exams to be pretty fair (from a non-science major perspective) as long as you paid attention during lectures

Lectures and homework are super easy and then out of nowhere the tests are super hard. Humanities majors, be wary of taking this for the distribution expecting an easy A unless you want to take it S/U. I did that and the class ended up being fine. Sheehan is a good lecturer and makes it fun.

Took this class for an easy A distribution requirement, and it sucked. The class is way too difficult for what it should be, exams are hard, the grading is harsh, and there are too many tacky assignments. Not an easy grade, and not worth taking.
Looks like an easy A but his animal behavior class sucked and the grading was brutal. If you're looking for a class for the bio requirement spare yourself here.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: An INCREDIBLE lecturer! Class was easy and so interesting!
Robin is awesome. His class is interesting and inspiring! Strongly recommend!!!!

Loved the class. 6 quizzes, participation, and one final translation project make up the whole grade. The quizzes are all covered in class. If you studied those well and attended classes regularly, it is an easy A+. Professor McNeal is very understanding and flexible to accommodate students' scenarios. He genuinely cares about the students.

Robin is the best! His lectures are engaging, interesting, and informative. The assignments are well balanced and fun. This guy truly cares about his students and he knows his stuff! I can't recommend this class enough.
Just randomly assign grades to students. Students who work hard and participate actively in class ended up getting lower grades

Doesn't allow for your own interpretation of the theories and readings. It's his way or the highway. Class has a separate clique of people who defend everything he says and therefore succeed in his class.

Had good impression at first, but then realized he gives preferential treatment to a select few and grades are completely based on his opinion. Even if your paper is well-written, if he doesn't agree with you said, expect to get a much lower grade than what you deserve. If you manage to get on his good side, then all is well. Would not take again.

McNeal is my fav prof at Cornell. He's incredibly passionate about his field and is very flexible and considerate. He makes the material interesting and so long as you attend lectures, read most readings, take your time on the essays, and study your notes you'll get a good grade. It was 100% worth getting up early to attend his lectures every week.

Really enthusiastic and knowledgeable of his subject. That being said, he goes off on tangents really easily. Fun to listen to still. As long as you go to lecture, quizzes and papers are really easy. Don't think he gave below an 86 on first paper. Subject material mostly analysis of myth, and only ancient ancient Chinese myth.

He doesn't have a particular format to the quizzes, and grading takes him far longer than it should. He is not that funny, though he tries to be, and some days he doesn't even say anything important to lecture because he goes off on tangents. This course is more literary theory than actual myth but if you want an easy course than this is it.
Lectures are very interesting. Quizes are relatively easy/fair as long as you attend most of the lectures and do some of the readings. I have to say, he is a funny man
He is really great! He is tending and understand the urgent situations. Grading is good too. Really love his course!!!!!
He's a really good teacher and you can tell he loves his subject. He comes in to teach every section for a day. Very easy class, and Wikipedia will be your best friend.
Great guy- funny, realistic expectations. Brought a whole new perspective on China to light. TA's are easy graders; class is really easy to get a good grade in.
Professor McNeal makes learning about Chinese mythology fun and accessible. Awesome teacher, easy class!

take his class ! the best prof in asian dept. very interesting topic and GREAT lectures. like original ideas and discussion. asks questions that make you think. great connection with students! remembers everyone's name and willing to talk to spend time to talk to students. grading is easy too.
Very nice professor and patient. His materials are not too difficult as long as paying attention in class and prepare for quizzes a bit. He explains things well and you know he knows his stuff.
Very good Professor who makes everything he teaches interesting.  Sometimes he oversimplifies more complicated material, but this is an intro class...

This prof has known me for a while. I liked his course a lot. It was an easy course and being Chinese myself I actually learned things. The sections were not that helpful. The essays and quizzes are graded easily, and the homework is almost guaranteed full credit if you just put the effort into them.

An excellent intro to the culture and history of China.  Fun and easy to stomach.  The tests and quizzes aren't hard, and I don't remember reading a lot of the assigned reading (though the reading he assigned was interesting).  The TA can make the class work, like any class here, though, so get in good w/ him/her.
so so easy. SO EASY. he is a good professor. the class is even better if you have a awesome TA like i did.

McNeal is by far the most interesting and helpful teacher out there.  His brilliance is only reiterated by the fact that some of the documents used were translated by him.  He's also incredibly helpful and caring; he will meet with you if you're busy during his office hours.
The prof is HOT, fun, and funny...what else do you want from a class that you're taking to fulfill distribution requirements? Remember gals: eye candy.
Thought 2nd grade multiplication tables were easy? You haven't seen nothing yet. This class will blow your mind. If you don't get an A, you probably should be going to Ithaca College.

Incredibly passionate about ancient Chinese military texts, and can make even a dull reading come to life. Funny, liberal, and an easy grader. That said, not one of the most brilliant minds in the department, and at times you will wonder if the class is worth your time. Great prof if you need distribution requirements; for substance, go elsewhere.
His "Art of War" class is just pure AMAZING...he is a very energetic professor and makes you love the material as much as he does. I absolutely recommend taking the class!!!
I agree that he spends too time on the bronze age.  So he has to rush at the end.   This may because of the reasons why the later part of the course is boring compared to the first half.
Great class, my favorite professor in all my time at Cornell, geniunely interested in the subject, and speaks fluent Mandarin!

Pretty easy class... prof is clear but as he is specialist on bronze age, i think he dwells too much on that period then rushes through the class and then makes the final based on the rushed through portion. That being said, his lectures are clear and he is a nice guy.
Great professor, and very nice guy. Very knowledgable in his field. If you live in Dickson, get to know him, he's your FIR!
Amazing teacher, funny guy. Lectures are super interesting. Cares a lot about the students.

Minawi is a great professor and extremely knowledgeable but the course felt far too intense for me. We had pop quizzes on the readings which were always easy but really stressed me out the night before classes. Participation seemed a little cutthroat as well, and he was pretty exacting on the final paper. Take it only if you love Ottoman history.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: THIS MAN IS PERFECT!!! i was slightly scared of him.. but he was so cool and good at his job

I took Ottoman Empire 1800-1922 with Minawi. Really cool guy, passionate, inspired speaker who enjoys making his students think, ask questions, and engage. His classes are very reading-heavy and attendance is mandatory. His lectures are more a formality and discussion forum tbh. Exams are extremely reading materials-based. No papers but book report

Minawi will really make you think and unlearn what you think you know. Very eye opening course relevant to current events and a lot of 19/20th century history. No papers except a book reflection. Lots of reading that you definitely have to do. Fair grader. Super passionate and knowledgable. Funny and fun to talk to.
Great!

really cool, i look forward to his lectures tues/thurs. very passionate about the subject and teaches in a very engaging way. goes on tangents sometimes which can get a bit confusing. heavy emphasis on reading and participation. he'll train your historical analysis skills.

i recommend hist1561! i am taking his higher level course next sem too :)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Incredible professor. Take one of his courses before you graduate

I spent every waking minute that semester doing his tedious, long assignments. He is a very harsh grader with zero flexibility or feedback. He gave quizzes almost every class - which were more like actual tests with the amount of reading required. His lectures are dry and boring and hard to follow. He cold calls nonstop and is condescending. Awful
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Best professor I've had at Cornell. Literally made me want to become a historian

This man will fill you full of Ottoman propaganda and I loved every second of it. I exaggerate, but also nothing bad happened in 1453. He has some insightful perspectives on history in general, too. He assigns a lot of reading, but I found that I usually only needed to do the textbook reading to be prepared for class. Take his courses!

Take this guy's class. Professor Minawi is fantastic at actually teaching, so you'll learn a lot. He has interesting perspectives and I love when he goes on these passionate 10-minute tangents about history. His classes aren't hard if you put in effort. He is a very, very reasonable, down-to-earth person IF you put in some semblance of effort.

I've taken three classes with Professor Minawi because I love him so much! He is extremely engaging and makes you excited about the material. He is also very approachable, helpful, and overall a reasonable professor. Definitely recommend any of his classes!

Prof. Minawi expects a lot but definitely gives you what you need in order to meet his expectations, and is always very helpful if you are getting lost. His lectures are very engaging, and coming to class prepared is a must because he does ask a lot of questions to keep you interested and make sure you are understanding the material.

In both his Intro Ottoman History class and his upper level classes, Prof. Minawi is dynamic and fascinating. He expects a high level of analysis and participation, but does not ask too much and is always flexible when asked for an extension.  The readings are long but great. He really gets his students, and always offers to help.
great guy super chill, interesting lectures. Lots of assigned reading but it's easy to make do without reading everything. Graded on lots of things, nice grade boost from attendance
Lectures were fun and engaging, Cole was very relatable and chill. The tests did cover a substantial amount of content but were reasonable and aligned well with lecture content. Highly recommend.

So knowledgeable and passionate about course material. Obviously super intelligent. Lectures off the dome no slides but totally coherent, digestible, and engaging. Attendance is a large portion of the grade but lectures are 100% worth going to. Clear guidelines for assignments and exams. TAs were great. Review sessions were really helpful.

Fantastic professor - his class on epistemology (Knowledge and Belief) was fantastic, with an eclectic, interesting reading list. He grades very reasonably, with clear expectations outlined in the paper assignments and the (comprehensive and helpful) review. Just do the readings, pay attention in class, and study with his guide, and you'll get an A
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Moghimi is the GOAT. His lectures are so easy to follow and his instructions are always clear. Grading is super clear and super easy. Best AEM professor of all time!!!
