Moghimi is a great professor for spreadsheet modeling! His prelims were fair and straight to the point. One weekly homework assignment which isn't too time consuming. Only thing which requires a good amount of time is the final project, but other than that, super easy class!

Moghimi is a super knowledgeable and easy-going professor and teaches you exactly what you need to know for any intro level Excel internship, etc. So many profs here just do too much, so it's refreshing to have a class with no surprises--his lectures are super straightforward and he's perfected his pace and the assignments over the years.

One of the best profs I've had at Cornell. His lectures are super clear, and the course structure is one of the best I've seen in Dyson. Definitely recommend taking his classes, he's incredibly nice and genuinely cares about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very clear with his lectures, and if you pay attention and actually watch the lectures thoroughly, the class should be really easy

Professor Moghimi is quite good. His explanations about the concept and code is super clear. It is a nice course for business students who want to get more knowledge about python programming, especially its application in finance related field.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Could not teach spreadsheets any better than he did.

An amazing professor. His lectures + his videos are the ultimate combination to passing this class. His prelims are extremely fair and as long as you pay attention in class and do the homework assignments, the prelims and group project are both fair and a bit challenging. He is my favorite professor ever.

Very easy class just follow the instructions. Or watch the videos he posts. The end of the class group project is also quite okay but just be sure to choose ur teammates well. overall, just an easy class.
Very kind and easy. He is extremely chill and wants his students to learn Excel. One of the easiest and most useful classes in Dyson. Definitely take it in the spring with Moghimi!

Moghimi is my favorite professor I've had at Cornell. His lectures are so straightforward, he's always willing to help, and assignments are fair and easy. I learned so much in this class in such an effective time period. He is incredibly friendly, approachable, and a great teacher for quantitative classes!
Super organized professor. Attendance is mandatory but grading curriculum is fair and every class provides a lot of value. Really nice and understanding guy

Professors like this are what makes the ivy league the ivy league. Easily the best professor I've ever had. Lectures are super clear, concise and exams are quite fair. Also genuinely one of the nicest and understanding people I've met, he goes out of his way to help you if you really want it.

There are assignments in every class but they're relatively easy and super fast, especially if you read the book. Excel is super practical and Reza makes it easy to understand. He's also a super nice and understanding prof if you approach him with any concerns and makes some fun jokes during class. This was one of my favorite classes/
hard but rewarding. my favorite professor at Cornell University
Prof. was pretty good

One of the lowest grades I received in an ECE course at Cornell yet I felt like I learned so much more in this class then any other. Professor Molnar is truly a genius. His homecooked homework problems are very difficult, and the labs are harshly grades, but if you apply yourself through and don't worry about your grade here you will learn so much.

Took 4450, 5540, and 5790 with Molnar. Hardest classes I took at Cornell, especially 5540, but learned more from them than pretty much everything else combined. Amazing lectures, you walk away from his classes with an understanding and not just a knowledge of the material. Best Prof. in ECE in my opinion. There is no learning without pain!!!
Super hard but worth it

Amazing lectures, lots of problem sets and labs, but ultimately worth it. He and the TAs put a lot of time into the course to ensure a full understanding of analog circuits. Also really interesting uy to talk to outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Expect lots of work and a lot of learning! Go to office hours and become friends with him! He puts in a lot of effort.

Despite the overwhelming amount of work we were assigned, most of it was not worth much. It was a very leniently graded class and the professors and TAs spent well more than the required amount of time to ensure a high level of understanding.
Challenging but very dedicated to his course.  Excellent selection of TAs.  Attends every discussion and some labs to help out.

One of the best professors I've ever had. He really cares about his students/teaching, is very understanding, and is always willing to help. However, this was also the hardest class I have taken (prelims were pretty rough, labs and homework sets were long/difficult). This class will teach you to care more about learning than your grade

Professor Molnar is a fantastic guy. He's an absolute genius, super nice, and always willing to help his students. You will learn so much if you take ECE 2100 and try your hardest to understand the material being thrown at you. That being said, do not expect this class to be a breeze. Homework sets take forever and labs are tedious. Come prepared.

Prof. Molnar's 2100 will consume your life with coursework if you let it. Overall, it was very educational and worthwhile. And he's a really nice guy. Many students suspect he has (not so) secret superhuman ECE powers.

Prof. Molnar is many things, easy is not one of them. His problem sets/labs are positively sadistic, but he holds himself to the same high standards he holds you to. He is incredibly dedicated (teaches his own discussions, writes own labs) and is super-helpful when you talk to him in person. Overall, a great guy/teacher who will teach you  a ton.
A nice and interesting guy. Seems to care about his students and is willing to help them when they ask for help. Lectures are very good, but problem sets are difficult.
talks extremely fast, ridiculously long and hard problem sets

Professor Saikia is one of the best BME professors at Cornell! She is an engaging lecturer and sets clear expectations of the class. There are frequent in-class assignments (like pop quizzes) that count for attendance so make sure to go to classes! Prelims and homeworks are similar and are tedious but come directly from lectures

The lectures are very clear and this course covers interesting content. Saikia does a good job of explaining her slides, making them interesting and applicable, and making materials very accessible to students. She tries to make your life easier as a student and is very reasonable.

I really like Prof Saikia's lectures. She has a great and clear lecture format that is easy to understand and is interesting. She is also nice. Her exams are super straightforward, so if you read the lectures and understand the material, you will not be confused on the exams. There are really no curve balls.
I would definitely recommend Professor Saikia for this course. She has deep knowledge of the subject and a passion to connect it to biomedical engineering at large regardless of your concentration.

Saikia is such a passionate teacher in her field. She cares so much about getting the information across and having a genuine discussion about biomaterials and how they will shape the future of medicine. I would highly recommend her.
Not good professor at all.
Nice professor with an excellent memory. To achieve good grades you might need to memorize every detail in the lecture slides.

She's a decent professor, and her grading has gotten a lot clearer. However, the way she runs her class makes it very difficult to get an A if you screw up on one assignment or you're having a bad day. On the other hand, I suppose that is how many classes are.....

Prof. Saikia is VERY unclear in her grading policies. She gives you a small word/page count and then takes off points for not elaborating enough (not enough room). She seems to take off points almost arbitrarily at times and rarely provides a rubric. She is dismissive of student concerns and is very vague in answering questions about grading.
let me write about my own interest and was low stress but you shouldn't expect much feedback on your work

In my experience, the freshman writing seminar offered little opportunity for improvement. Many classes were canceled, and essay feedback was minimal, making skill development difficult. While the professor is clearly experienced and well published, that did not translate well to this format. I would only consider an upper-level course with him.

An excellent lecturer who pulls from a wide range of personal and professional experiences to make this class a cohesive picture, alongside Prof. Diaz and her work. He has written across may genres and provides great insight and feedback. He is someone you want to impress!

Professor Musick is super nice and cares a lot about student learning. The lectures can be pretty dry at times. I think this may be because it was her first semester teaching the class as the professor that created the class handed it off to her this year. I took the class pass/fail and it was very easy, but I did learn a lot from the class.

Course load isn't bad at all and the prelim + final aren't too hard. Dr. Musick isn't the best lecturer and she reads directly from the slides. She inherited the class from a different professor and you can really tell. Nice lady but when you talk to her you get the impression she doesn't really know the material.

Only 4 assignments throughout the entire semester, a prelim and a final that is the exact same format as the prelim, daily in-class polls that are taken to be used as attendance and also daily reading reflections about a prompt about a reading that we had to do for that day. Mostly just lectures which could sometimes be a bit dry, but she is great!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures were boring. Grading was a little tougher than expected (but that was done by the TAs, not the prof). Easy A-, had to put in a little extra work for that A.

Families and Social Inequality is pretty easy but there are 2 decent sized papers that will take a little while and 3 homework assignments that are quick. The content is pretty interesting and I'd definitely recommend the class

Musick is a great professor that very pleasant and really loves her lectures.She does a great job of engaging people, even in large classes.Attendance was required (iClicker q's) and there was way too much reading to finish for each class, but if you skim and pick up the highlights in class, it's not all necessary to do well.Very organized material

Musick is one of the nicest teachers you will ever have. She is also very approachable and enjoys helping her students. The only problem is that she is a little unclear on what she wants from the assignments sometimes. The assignments aren't that difficult if you come to class and pay attention though. And she gives you the exam questions.

Prof is very kind and chill, lectures are rlly boring but easy class. Attendance is not mandatory, but U NEED TO SHOW UP TO DISC SECTIONS-- that's where attendance actually counts. Overall super chill labor history class, highly recommend as he is the best option to fulfill this requirement
Great guy, boring lectures. your grade relies on your TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: super chill guy

Honestly, this is an amazing class. Take it. It has a pretty simple format: one midterm, two essays, and some in-class assignments/ quizzes. He also gave an option for extra credit. Every assignment allows you to explore what YOU are interested in. He is so flexible,open to connecting with students beyond the classroom, so passionate. Trust me-TAKE
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Honestly he is amazing. This course you get to explore so much of what you are interested in. I wish he explored more Latin history. But he is so much fun, love the music he plays in class and the topics we discuss. Really dynamic format. Super great. Easy if you try on assignments. Trust!.

Lectures were all over the place, he YAPPS about irrelevant information 80% of the class. We had 6-7 different books to read almost at random across the semester. Papers are extremely long for an intro class, and even longer readings. Extremely boring lectures, only survived because of my TA! (They are 100% responsible for all the grading).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Nagaraja is one of the sweetest professors in ILR. We had several papers in the class that TAs would grade, but Nagaraja was always willing to review your paper and answer any questions you have.
Professor Nagaraja is great. He's really passionate and knowledgeable, and is always willing to meet with you.

He is very nice and approachable practically begging students to ask him questions and go to office hours. Slides are way too text-heavy, but he posts them making attending is unnecessary. The TA does all the grading so I can't comment on that.
Very nice person. Approachable outside of class. Does not grade harshly. Lectures are confusing and not particularly helpful.

Very nice and passionate professor but his lectures were confusing and hard to follow. Attendance is mandatory but I did not learn much within those lectures. I found doing the readings and going to office hours much more useful. Overall, he is a generous grader if you do the necessary work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Boring lectures, but he's a chill guy and doesn't grade too hard.

All papers. Your grade lives and dies by the TA. This semester, there was a probably a 1.5 gpa spread between the two TAs and nothing was done about it. Your grade is about as meritocratic as a roulette table. Lectures are circular, directionless, and unnecessary. Just read the pertinent readings a week before the papers are due.

I kinda disagree with comments for Professor Nagaraja. I first thought he was not good at teaching. However, as I started to listen carefully what he was talking about in class, I learnt a lot. He was very informative and knowledgable. Moreover, he also gave me the freedom to explore my interests under the course framework. Very nice guy.

He's a really nice guy, but an AWFUL professor. Lectures are incredibly disorganized. Very little correlation between readings, lectures, and assignments. TAs do all the work and were pretty short staffed. Do not take him if you do not have to.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nagaraja seems like a good dude who is interested in the subject matter. However, it is clear that he is uninterested in teaching. His lectures are long, boring, and confusing, and his communication outside of class is terrible(cannot use canvas to save his life). Really disappointed becasuse I thought this would be my favorite class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Simply not a good professor
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Would REALLY not recommend

Lectures are boring and unnecessary -- read and take good notes from the books and participate in discussion and you'll be fine. Grade can really depend on your TA but go to office hours and have them look at your essays at multiple steps in the process to make sure you're doing what they want to. He's not a bad guy he's just not a good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Not a great lecturer, His powerpoint slides were really hard to follow and chaotic. He was a really easy grader though, so that was nice. There was lots of assigned reading that you didn't really have to do, and his content was very one-sided. Overall okay experience but I wouldn't recommend if you want to get a lot out of the class.

Professor is clearly very smart, but his classroom management isn't great. He assigned a lot of reading for this class and didn't get assignments back to us for a very long time. The three essays he did assign were essentially the same prompt each time? Interesting class to take if you're invested in the books but hard to get a lot of out of him.

Professor Kate is super caring and attentive with her students. She is very accessible outside of class, and it's easy to tell she wants all her students to succeed and become better writers. While this class was relatively difficult for an FWS, it was very rewarding, and I learned a lot. Highly recommend to anyone interested in future research.

I took Writ1380 and Dr. Navickas was a great professor. She has labor based grading so if you do the work and show up to class you will get a good grade. You have to conference with her between every draft and final essay, but she gives amazing feedback and if you revise based on her feedback you will do well. Honestly a great FWS!

Kate is incredible!!! Very kind, cares deeply about her students and gives very useful feedback about writing. The way she's laid out this class allows students to research, write, and share about things that are personally fulfilling to them, making the class feel like a celebration of personal interests.

Kate Navickas is an incredible professor and a caring teacher. She allows students to pursue topics of their choice, inspiring engagement with course content. Kate is very approachable, and her self-grading philosophy encourages students to find passion while writing about their research topic. I highly recommend Kate to students in any field.

Professor Kate is amazing! She takes the time to engage with each student and is very accommodating. I have tremendously improved my writing skills because of her and would highly recommend to take her class.

I took FWS 1380 (the only course code choice was 1420, so I had to choose that) with Professor Navickas, and it was really amazing. The discussions were always super interesting, with not a lot of reading and a very doable workload. It was my favorite class of the semester.
Take care of yourself and don't take this class, or any of her classes.

Professor Holmes is passionate and cares about her students, but unfortunately, the class she teaches is so unbearably boring and feels like a waste of time. 1110 doesn't relate to 1112 at all. The only thing that made this class worth taking was that we got 5 free skips for lecture and a couple for lab as well. Use them!
Boring class made bearable by an amazing professor.

Prof. Holmes makes the lectures for an otherwise somewhat uninteresting class as engaging as possible. She is also clearly very passionate about the subject matter. It seemed like she did actually care about her students and understood that they had lives outside of physics. Only thing is grad TA grading somewhat inconsistent.

The class is very easy and felt like a waste of time week-to-week. That said, Prof. Holmes tries her best to make the class engaging. She is kind and approachable. There's no way around a boring required class, but she'll make it bearable. You usually have many lecture+lab drops. Use lab drops early on (can't skip final project labs).

She made an absolutely terrible class (content wise) bearable. She is super passionate about physics, and even though the content of the lectures are pretty much useless, she tried her best to make it engaging. Very easy A if you show up and put a nonzero amount of effort into the labs.

The professor is very sweet. But as a required class, the lab and lecture felt like a waste of time. Labs are graded on a 1-5 scale with 4's as A's and 5's as almost uncovetable A+'s. The final is a presentation.
He really cares about what he is talking about and it's a great class to take.
great prof, cares about what hes teaching. class is graded by 6 short essays and 3 tests that were all online (incl the final)

This course is not meant to be difficult and I thought the content was very interesting. As long as you understand the key terms, complete the discussion posts, and follow the rubric for essays, this is an easy A/A+ class. Take this course if needed for major/minor, distribution, or if you are interested in the material and want a lighter course.
Boring lecturer. I feel like i did not learn much. Whole class felt like busy-work. But hey, easy A.

This class was so boring that I felt like I was aging 5 years every lecture—by finals, I was practically collecting Social Security. Professor Matias's monotone voice had the magical ability to put me in a coma by 10:10am sharp every weekday. Fittingly, as of Dec 2024, he's still wearing a mask—it's almost as if time hasn't caught up with him yet

This class was so boring that I felt like I was aging 5 years every lecture—by finals, I was practically collecting Social Security. Professor Matias's monotone voice had the magical ability to put me in a coma by 10:10 a.m. sharp every weekday. Fittingly, as of Dec 2024 he's still wearing a mask—it's almost as if time hasn't caught up with him yet

Extremely easy, didn't even have to show up to class, but I still showed up most of the time because the topic was interesting. He 100% knows what he's talking about and is very well reserached, but isn't the MOST interesting professor and kinda tends to drag things out to be a bit boring. Not an exciting class or professor but still was happy.

Super easy class with Prof Matias. Great guy, cares so much about what he is teaching, actually makes lectures engaging. Tests are a bit tricky but he gives lots of points back if many students got certain questions wrong.

If you're okay with writing some papers, this class is very easy and enjoyable. Lectures are interesting and relevant, and he usually ties in current events at the beginning. Papers are not too bad, and exams are all online. You can tell he really cares about what he is teaching.

Lecture is very clear, and exams are very easy to study because he basically follows a script in the speaker notes. This is very helpful when studying but also comes to show how the class can be studied without needing to go to lecture at all. Assignments are very straightforward and of reasonable workload, content was interesting not dense.

Pretty easy but interesting class. There's a design, psychology, and sociology unit each with two short papers and one prelim. Everything is open note and lectures are not mandatory. He was a nice person and was very lenient. We had reading and needed to post to a discussion board, but it wasn't graded harshly. The exams were kinda tricky though.

It takes a special type of arrogance to believe you deserve the undivided attention of 50+ people from 8-10AM. He practices what he preaches, seems to care about students. A bajillion assignments going on at all times. In a huge group all sem, felt ridiculous begging adults to study for a test because my grade depended on theirs (group average).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He is so strict about attendance, but it's actually not worth it. I've never seen a professor take attendance like that. I remember in the first class, he asked the students if they knew how many assignments there were. He said there were hundreds... I felt like all the assignments were meaningless, and I even made up things to complete them.

I had the worst professor during my first semester at Cornell. We had to take an emotion quiz every day. You could complete a few very simple questions, like "How are you feeling today?" and still not get a perfect score. I hadn't bought an iClicker in my four years of undergraduate studies, but I did for this class.
Undoubtedly the worst lecturer I've ever had at Cornell!

He may come off as intimidating at first but as you go along, you realize how much of a good teacher he is. He really loves helping students. Reach out and schedule OH whenever, you wont be disappointed.

Would not recommend! The amount of work assigned is going to be way more compared to other classes with similar credit levels, and the lectures are not engaging enough for how early they are.  Slides and homework have typos, and you don't need to take this class to learn what is taught.

Self-centered and arrogant and treats his students like children while rarely offering insightful answers to genuinely meaningful questions. For a class so centered on emotional intelligence, I think he could benefit more from taking this course himself than any student enrolled currently. This course is a waste of time and money.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class is a joke. You drag yourself to an 8am for zero useful info—just nonsense rants and breakdowns. He warns against "amdalga breakdowns" but literally has them himself. Tests are garbage and make no sense. Haven't learned a single thing. Absolute waste of time.

If you expect to learn real-world project management skills, you won't find them here. Prelims are bizarre and harsh. You must show up before 8 AM for every lecture, phones and laptops banned, or this jerk will destroy your grades. This is the worst instructor I've had since middle school and I strongly recommend him resign from this position.
boring, useless with lots of hw, prelim, final

He's definitely the worst lecturer I've ever had throughout the past five years! Avoid his class if you can, otherwise you'll have to show up at 8 am in the classroom and your electronic devices will be banned. He assigns tons of useless HWs and you won't learn anything helpful but he brags how impactful his classes to students from time to time.

Would NOT recommend. He treats students like little kids. He should understand students only pay attention in classes because professors talk about interesting things, not because phones and computers are banned. For a class that repeats industry leadership jargons and outdated concepts, 2 cumulative prelims and 1 final are more than excessive.
His classes are fun and insightful
Despite being at 8am, I really enjoyed the lectures. Learned a lot of applicable skills and Prof Newman is a great lecturer. Can get stressful when group project work picks up.
The workload can be a lot, but is doable as he gives plenty of in-class time to work on it. Appreciated the team learning environment. Great lecturer and participation is encouraged.

Having taken other 4 credit STEM courses here, I can say Newman gives an unreasonable amount of work for a 4-credit class. He gives us limited time (e.g. 48 hours) do a decent amount of work over the weekend. He often doesn't even create the content for us to work on until right before the weekends yet tells us not to procrastinate - hypocritical!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Group projects did not provide much learning and too focused on who was considered the best. Too much reliance on participation grade. Feedback received was elementary and hardly focused on descriptive content, rather on length of presentation or minor, irrelevant details. The discussions allowed for critical thinking. Disorganized at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Thinks that a 4-credit course is valid for giving hours of work for participation homework. Not even including the other individual homework, team project, team project homework, quizzes, final project, and a final exam we also have to complete for this class alone.
amazing guy loved his class

Took this class in Fall 2024. Prof. Monger is a great lecturer, and the exams are pretty straightforward, though very memorization-based. They're also based on the lecture slides, which tends to have a lot of information, but he does upload lecture recordings. It's not a purely low-effort class, but it's manageable to do well in it overall.

Lecture were a bit boring, that being I usually reviewed slides afterward if I wasn't following along. Tests sometimes required memorization of certain statistics but questions are relatively straightforward and some are repeated from past prelims. I took the lab (BIOEE 1560) and I would recommend even for nonsci majors, it was a grade boost.

haven't been to a single lecture and still did decent. just study old exams and look at review slides before the test for an hour and you'll get above a 90 almost guaranteed
free ahh class lock in bro
not a esay a

Overall, the material is engaging, and it is clear that the professor is passionate about climate change and ensuring students understand its severity. The course is harder than people say, as the exams require substantial studying and memorization. However, it's nice that attendance isn't required, and the review slides cover most of exam content.

Does a great job of informing you of the state of climate change. Also made scientific concepts very accessible. Intro Oceanography is a very easy A/A+ if you just put in a little bit of effort; all MCQs, and he gives you condensed review slides that probably cover 90-95% of the content on the exam.

Professor Monger is a great lecturer and very passionate about climate change and the state of our oceans but the class is not as easy as people say it is, especially if you're not good at memorizing things. The prelims and final are almost purely memorization based with a heavy emphasis on statistics and charts/graphs so beware.

I actually thought his lectures we're quite hard to follow because even though the content is generally easy, he goes through the slides so fast you don't have time to write them down. there's also SO MUCH content and he never clarifies which ones to focus on so you're just stuck trying to study lecture slides when there are like 40 per class.

Take oceanography, Bruce is great and it's really not a lot of work. Don't underestimate the tests though, they can end up being harder than you'd expect if you don't put in the work to study for them. Bruce cares a ton about climate change especially so the class will focus on that a good amount.

This was a great class. He cares so much about climate change and his passion for these topics really makes you want to start speaking up for our planet. All the information you need to know are in the lecture slides and take the practice tests in preparation for the exams.

Definitely take this class for the distribution requirement. Basically no homework & fair chances for EC. Lectures aren't mandatory, but GO TO THE REVIEW LECTURES!! He'll tell you what'll be on the test and sometimes covers things that aren't on the review slides.

While lectures are not required, they are enjoyable to sit in and are very inspiring. The class itself is not difficult, as long as you write the weekly 200-word (completion) responses. To study for exams, go over the practices and cover all the red text on slides. One of Cornell's best classes for a reason! Highly reccomend.

Prof Monger is a caring and inspirational person. He really cares about climate change. Just make sure you know EVERYTHING on the review slides for the tests. Also, write as close to 200 words for the weekly responses to get the EC.
He is so inspirational, kind, and I respect him so much as a human being. He makes you feel hopeful about the future and ready to take action for sustainability!

AMAZING lectures, mainly thanks to our great teacher. Lectures had the right amount of complexity and random facts/stories, made the course feel kind of like a history lesson with science, which is way better in my opinion. Also had very helpful "All you need to know" moments, as sometimes it can get detail heavy.  Tests are easy, fair assigments.

Professor Monger is incredibly passionate about the topic, and this course is an easy overview of interesting material. If you review the slides before the exams, you will be fine. His lectures can sometimes feel dry and repetitive sometimes. Overall would recommend.
Great class with an even better professor! Really passionate about the subject and caring about all students! All around great person!

Go to class, and pay attention, even just taking it for fun! Bruce is very inspiring and so engaging. Cool guest speakers too! There's a reason this class is on the list of 161 Things to Do. He wants students to learn and succeed - as long as they put in the effort. He will tell you ~1/4 of the questions on the exam. Such a memorable professor

Bruce Monger is an amazing lecturer who's passionate about oceanography and climate change. Just make sure to review slides and watch the prelim review videos and associated review slides and you will do well in the class.

Class is a bit overhyped. While VERY passionate about climate change (2/3s of the final is about it), lectures are a little boring. An A takes effort and lots of memorizing, but a good grade without going to lectures is viable if you study the review slides a few days before. The content overall is interesting, it's just presented in a boring way.

Oceanography is a great choice for all (humanities majors who are bad at STEM like me, and those who are interested in the Earth sciences). Bruce is absolutely adorable. He has so much passion and joy for what he teaches, and it is delightful to see. If you attend lecture and study the review slides well, you will get a good grade :)
Best professor ever. Don't miss out on taking a class with him while you're at Cornell.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Monger is a kind-hearted professor who clearly cares about the subject and his students. However, his lectures are extremely dry and difficult to pay attention to. I think it's partially due to his monotone voice and the content itself which I found to be uninteresting. Nevertheless, it is a good class to take for an easy credit.

Professor Monger is so inspiring. Though I took his classes online, his passion for environmentalism is still radiating. The Introductory Oceanography course was very easy, as test material is primarily based off PowerPoint contents. Would take again
Great professor, enjoyed his class. Class isn't too difficult, just study the lecture slides thoroughly.

Many think it's an easy A and put in no work. It is an actual physical science class with content to be memorized. However, exam questions were 60% from last year's exam (which he gave us). Attendance wasn't mandatory and he was extremely fair on the test questions. Basically no homework every week. It's an easy A class with some effort!

He is a nice guy and cares a lot about the subject (and the class is clearly popular). Despite this, I found a lot of his lecturing quite dry. Weekly questions are extremely easy, but tests can be fairly challenging. While I respect and agree with his messaging on climate change, his style of motivation felt lacking, corny, and somewhat dated.
Bro man is confusing af

As close to a must-take class at Cornell as you can get. Not all lectures are amazing but you can learn about important things without being worried about hard tests or hw. He clearly cares about making the class accessible to everyone and even though it's nothing crazy I couldn't recommend the class and him more.

really nice guy. lectures were only 50 minutes, which prevented them from dragging, but full of interesting content. prof monger was super inspirational, and I learned a lot about climate change/science that has been very useful.
Absolutely amazing class, professor, and person. Lectures were genuinely inspiring and super easy to follow. As long as you show up to class, you'll do really well on the assignments and exams

Professor Monger always ensured that every lecture was filled with interesting material. He always emphasized the importance of all students in the fight against climate change and really left a mark among all students in the class. Even with Covid restrictions, every lecture with hundreds of students felt special and really resonated within me.
Great class, accessible to nonscience majors, his passion for the future of the climate and world is infectious.
wonderful professor. one of my favorite classes.

Bruce is the best, no needs to tell you that twice. This class is super light and as long as you do the necessary work, you're guaranteed an A. Enjoy his expertise, it is so interesting to hear him speak. The class will blow your mind at times too. Overall amazing professor and cares so much about what he's teaching.

The course is extremely easy, yet quite inspirational. It is also very well-organized and the professor makes clear exactly what will be covered on the exams. This is definitely a class that you will remember for years to come.

Excellent lecturer that cares very deeply for environmental and oceanographic issues. Teaches you exactly what you need to know for quizzes/exams (and even highlights "exam-content" on his lecture slides). Stay on top of small-weekly assignments and do a thorough review before exams, and you'll get an good grade.

love bruce!! didnt really think about the ocean much now all of a sudden i want to be an environmentalist lol. this class really is an easy A (disregard my grade) and even despite things being online and different he makes the lectures fun and easy, and even the longer lectures arent hard to follow. the assignments are easy and personal

Professor Monger is one of the most passionate professors you'll have. His goal to inspire his students to make a change in the world is certainly admirable and makes the assignments seem meaningful. While the lectures were very information-heavy, nothing was too challenging. I'd definitely recommend for distribution requirement fulfillment.
So kind, really great lecturer, and so passionate about the material! He was very understanding and made the online class accessible and simple with just a few quizzes and an easy final paper.
Bruce is legendary.

Oceanography and Bruce truly changed me as a person and my entire perspective. The class is super easy, but the real takeaway is becoming more aware and active the current crises of climate change our planet is facing. Bruce is hilarious and this class is a must take for anyone at Cornell, can not recommend enough!!!

Prof Monger will change your life. He really cares about his students and making sure they learn instead of regurgitating info for a test. The lecture slides highlight exam material and a night of rewatching lectures will secure an A. Don't worry about your grade, seriously. Take this class if you want to be inspired to change the world.
Great class, important and interesting material. Dont underestimate oceans though, theres a lot to memorize for the exams.

Not only is this class easy, but it is amazing. Bruce is so inspiring and delivers the content really well (designed for everyone, not just science kids). I want to spend the rest of my professional career working in sustainability because of this class. Everyone should take this class before they graduate.

NOTE: 1560 has become more difficult compared to previous terms (as compared to comments by student who took it before). The course still holds very high value in oceanography, climate change and natural science knowledge for both major and non-majors. Bruce's stance and passion have not changed. Still amazing lectures. Beware of lab component.

Oceanography with Professor Monger changed my career aspirations entirely. I am now going to pursue a master's in environmental policy because of how his class inspired me to help protect our Earth from climate change. Even if you just watch the lectures online before the tests (I didn't attend a single class in person) you will learn something.
Bruce is the BEST. Incredibly passionate and inspirational.
Professor Monger is one of the top 3 professors I've had at Cornell. He's the man.

Great class except his pronounciation of "height" as "heighth" and "across" as "acrost" makes much of his lectures unlistenable. Paired with the many typos in his slides make for a frustrated lecture. "Cold tong"

Professor Monger is one of the most passionate professors I've had at Cornell; I've heard many stories of students who've taken his class and afterwards claim he changed their lives. Easy class with some memorization. Pay attention in class (or watch them online) & study lecture slides and you'll do really well. Great science for non-science people

One of the best professors Ive ever had at Cornell. Beyond the material, his grading criteria is super clear, he posts lecture videos online, and he literally highlights what you should know for exams in red. Watch the videos and take notes at 2x speed, youll be set. Not to mention he is phenomenal at inspiring you re: climate change

Prof. Monger's class was the best. Attendance is not mandatory, but you should always show up for your own good! At first, the class felt super technical and somewhat of a drag. Looking back, however, I'm so thankful for how much I've learned in regard to climate change. Very inspiring, and overall super rewarding as a "life lessons" class.
Bruce Monger is an exceptional professor. He is truly inspirational. Put in a little bit of work and you will get an A!
He got preachy in the second half, but, if you can stomach that, really easy way to boost GPA and fulfill distribution requirement.

Hands down best professor I've ever had at Cornell. He genuinely wants you to do well. His class is truly inspirational, and he does an amazing job at teaching and informing you about current issues and makes you want to be a proactive person. Class was very enriching. Definitely take it.

Literally the best teacher ever. He is so passionate about oceanography and so caring about his students. His interest in the subject and the fact that he is such a nice person makes your day so much better.

Wow. What an amazing passionate professor. The class is an easy A if you keep up with the work, but you honestly should just take the class for the professor. He's extremely passionate and makes learning oceanography entertaining and manageable.

Oceanography is an interesting topic, but the class wouldn't have been nearly as interesting if it was taught by someone else. Prof. Monger is passionate about climate change and wants people to make an impact outside of class. Class is definitely not mandatory but Prof. Monger gives such good lectures that it's worth it to go.

One of the most inspirational profs. Least amount of work required. Homework was one journal entry a week about your feelings on the topic (170 words). The tests are detailed but all on the slides and highlighted. you dont have to go to lecture but make sure to memorize the slides before the test or watch the lectures online.

I highly recommend taking Oceanography to anyone looking for an interesting and inspirational class (that is easy with minimal work!) Many of the lectures left me with a changed perspective of the world. Lectures are not mandatory(notes are posted)but I recommend attending to get the most out of the class! The only "HW" was a short weekly question.
Lot of info to memorize, but easy class otherwise

Lectures are super inspiring and the class material isn't too difficult. All prelims are multiple choice and were difficult for me at least since the material was so cursory it was difficult to gauge what would appear on exams and some questions felt somewhat trivial.

genuinely inspiring guy who made me care a lot more about the environment. tests are not particularly difficult but can get very trivial. great class for science requirement. bruce really designs his class to help students out a lot.
An amazing professor! Inspirational and easy A. Attending lecture is necessary but the lectures are recorded. If you want to be inspired as well as know more about the ocean, take his class.

This is by far, one of the best classes you could take at Cornell and Bruce is absolutely fantastic. In such a simple way he introduces concepts of the ocean and then transforms the class into an unsettling yet awing awareness of the greatest threat to HUMANITY: climate change. If you are looking for an easy A and stroke of inspiration--take it.

Bruce is the BEST. He is so passionate about what he teaches and truly inspires his students. Show up to his class- he really appreciates seeing students engaged in his class. He changed my view completely about climate change and the ocean in general. He is one of the best professors I've had at Cornell. TAKE HIS CLASS!! you will not regret it.

Bruce is the man. He genuinely cares about the environment and student learning. The class isn't difficult but you do need to put in some effort for the exams since it does require a good amount of memorization. He really cares about environmental activism and about his students actually learning rather than just grades.

I took this class because I heard it was easy, but I got so much more out of it than that. Monger is actually such an inspirational guy and whether you like it or not you'll walk out of there with a MUCH deeper appreciation for the environment. He cares more about students learning than grades. More professors should be like Bruce, he's the best!
Compelling lectures. Can sometimes get opinionated but it doesn't get in the way of course content. Passionate about subject manner, makes it very easy to understand.

Bruce is really amazing. Makes it really easy to do well even if you struggled on the first prelim (or two). Really cares about the topics and wants the class to care too. His class is a must take for all Cornell students and one of the only classes that you'll actually come out of knowing something.

Bruce is really amazing. Makes it really easy to do well even if you struggled on the first prelim (or two). Really cares about the topics and wants the class to care too. His class is a must take for all Cornell students and one of the only classes that you'll actually come out of knowing something.
"Easiest class at Cornell". Honestly, if you're not a science mayor and/or don't like science, this will be a challenging class.

This class is worth the hype. Passionate professor who really cares about the subject. Exams are straight forward. Weekly assignments are easy and helps you gain perspective on what is going on in the world climate wise. Best class I've taken at Cornell.
Best professor I've had at Cornell
some strong parts, some poor. really wants to be the students friend for some reason.

One thing I loved about this professor is that he actually cares about what he is teaching. He urges students to care about the environment and instills a will to make a positive change in the world. I am not a science major but this class broadened my perspective on the world greatly. I struggled with some of the memorization but not too hard.
One generously-graded essay was the only homework assignment of the year. Attendance is not necessary if you're not interested in the material, although you'll have to study a bit more for the exams.
Awesome Professor. Nice guy and overall cares a lot for the oceans. Would take the class again if I could.

I did not really enjoy this lecture. I'm not a science person in general, so I was not really looking forward to this class. People call this class an easy A, but it is a lot of memorizing. I'm not good at memorizing, so I did not do as well as I had hoped. However, it is pretty easy for a science class, and you get extra credit for attendance.

Bruce is the best professor at Cornell. He genuinely cares about mobilizing his students and informing them about climate change.  He wants everyone to do well, and if you study, you can easily get an A. He is the kindest, funniest, greatest professor out there. No other professor can make such a large class so interesting. Everyone loves him.

This guy is a great professor and extremely passionate about oceanography, but the class isn't really a gut anymore. Definitely study for exams because he recycles less than half the questions now and topics mentioned in lecture will be specifically asked. Take this class because it's a classic, but also take it seriously.

Bruce is incredibly passionate about his field. He really just wants you to develop somewhat of a passion for the ocean; he's not looking to make the course hard. Pre-lims are actually difficult if you don't study. I didn't attend lecture regularly, because the lectures are recorded and posted online, and I really regret it. Go to lecture.

I got 5 past exams (coursehero) - gave my iclicker to a friend - ended up with A+. Don't you think there's something wrong? Now that Maas (psych 101) has retired, this has become the most popular class - only because this class is so easy. Lecture hall is 1/3 full, yet almost 800 clicker clicks. This professor must be dumb, or simply doesn't care.
Great Class to fulfill your science requirement
Monger is the man; Oceanography is the best; no regrets

Bruce is awesome. His lectures are very clear, and he highlights what you need to know in a different color. Overall a great guy. When he realized Bailey Hall didn't have desks to take our prelims on, he ordered 900 clipboards for us. Also answers emails pretty quickly. His stories are legendary, and come up randomly. #BruceForPresident
I LOVEEE Bruce. In a strictly plutonic way of course. Nevertheless, you MUST take this course before you leave cornell. I am graduating this year and I have not had a better professor than him.

Ok Bruce is an amazinggg professor. My favorite professor yet at Cornell. I had minimal interest in the subject area before and he made me fall in love with it. He's such a nice guy and is so considerate of his students. You DEFINITELY need to take this class. No wonder there are almost 800 students in the class. I'm there everyday.

Bruce is the man. Very enthusiastic, great lecturer, makes stuff about the ocean/environment actually interesting although attendance is not mandatory at all. Prelims and final exam are very crammable the night before, don't graduate without taking oceanography
Very fair, very clear, very enthusiastic.
An amazing idealist. Best professor at cornell, TAKE THIS CLASS BEFORE GRADUATING! He should be the president of Cornell! VOTE FOR BRUCE
Bruce should be running this university.
Bruce is the man. Fun and easy to follow classes and tests, he even worked with me to let me take a midterm early so I could entertain family that flew in.
Bruce is the best professor at Cornell, period.

Bruce is a great professor, he made the boring parts of the material interesting and easy to understand. If you have the slightest interest in the workings of the ocean and the issues surrounding it, take this class.

Bruce is an interesting and amusing man. At times, he can be repetitive (either when it's a tough concept or an idea that he deems "super important"). He's very, caring and laid-back. If you take advantage of the study materials he provides the tests are very fair. This unexpectedly turned out to be one of the most inspiring class I've ever taken.

soo in love with bruce!! he's hilarious and his lectures are very straightforward.  all lecture slides are online and what's going to be on the test is even in red on the slides.  he's also a great help during office hours if guest lectures get confusing. took it for my science credit and so glad i did!  bruce for eva!

I took Intro to Oceanography in the fall with him, and the guy basically rules in every way possible. Interesting class with a surprising amount of practical knowledge (and I had little interest in the subject beforehand); no sections; 3 nonmandatory lectures(he posts all the ppts online and the tests are all MC and from the ppts). Take this class.
Intro to oceanography: A great class.  Easy to follow, accessible, Monger is terrific, save the oceans.
Bruce is the man
bruce is the man.  also his satellite class rules.

I only had Monger for the second half of EAS250 and here's his deal: he cares SOOOO much about oceanography, but doesn't really understand that no one else does. His lectures were very boring and I didn't learn anything, but he helps you so much with the labs and other material. He really cares about his students.

I took his intro to oceanography class, and it was great! Bruce was very friendly and helpful. Some memorization, but its relatively easy and not intense at all. The the labs are interesting and not that hard either!
Subjective grading. Pop quiz change to writing assignment
Grading is very subjective. Course is discussion based and felt not very useful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: he is not fair, avoid.

Most of the grading occurs at the end of the semester, so it is difficult to gauge your performance in the class. There are interesting concepts taught in this course and it is heavily discussion based, so participation matters. The professor believes his opinion is fact most of the time, so be careful with disputing.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best Professor I had at Cornell!

Neil was the best professor I had at Cornell. His expertise really shined in everything he said. It's refreshing to have a professor with heavy real-world entrepreneurial experience and didn't just "learn it" in a classroom. He always makes himself available and goes out of his way to help students with class and even starting their own company.

This class is a lot of work due to weekly presentations and team meetings but you learn a lot about entrepreneurship. It is also a class that you can mention in interviews since it is so unique. Even with the workload, the grades turn out fine and there are opportunities for extra credit at the end of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Employ the Business Model Canvas approach to developing a business concept.
Great Professor!  Really wants his students to learn.

Neil is a great guy who will always take the time to speak with and assist his students.  Entrepreneurism is not a straightforward "If this, then that" type of subject, but Neil ties in a number of real-world scenarious combined with his personal experiences to help students understand the holistic approach to launching a successful venture.
Tarallo was great. Really cares about students and always available in his office. Be prepared to be inspired.

Great professor! Class was very simple, and prof Newman understands that we all have our own stuff going on, so she is very understanding and caring. Her background is super interesting, and the topics discussed are enjoyable. Greatly appreciate the fact that there was minimal work for this class. I would love to take a class with her again!

She is genuinely AWESOME. The best energy ever and really interesting to be in a classroom with. The TA is a tough grader but it willing to help with office hours at any point for utilize that. Just wish the class was more woman-centric instead of other identifiers woman have besides female but still amazing to learn about.

i truly enjoyed her class, and it broadened my perspective of the world. but her classes felt like a long rant—like she found faults with every aspect of society, granted, and just yapped about it for the entire class. she is truly knowledgeable about her field, but it felt like she was constantly trying to argue with us to take her side on issues

Professor Newman is very very knowledgeable about feminist theory and does a great job of teaching it to growing feminists. The majority of your class will be spent reading. These readings do matter as they are how you are tested. That being said, there is only 1 short quiz and one final, so not a lot of exams. I recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I think that some of these ratings are harsh. If you are genuinely interested in the course material, you will do will and enjoy her company. I took PLSCI 3030

Rudest professor I've met here, made me quit my project team because she didn't support any students. Always loved hearing herself talk and brainstorm, and bored me every meeting. I don't know how she is in class, but she's an insufferable person

Pretty tough on grading and a bit hard to meet with, but I'd recommend discussing projects with her beforehand to work out any issues, since she's really experienced in her field and will easily identify holes in your projects. Pretty nice to talk with face to face. Will randomly call on students during class. Interesting but disengaging lectures.
Very critical. Not one for constructive criticism just pure criticism. You have to say and reproduce exactly what she wants to hear.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Nelson is kind of intimidating. She will shut your ideas down if she doesn't agree with them. She also will not hold back on tearing apart your work. She is very hard to please.

Professor Nelson is amazing and one of the best professors I've had. He's very respectful to his students and also values participation heavily in the course. This course is tough due to the subjects nature, however Nelson's lectures are very informative and if you truly work hard you'll definitely have a grade that showcases it
Absolutely fantastic. He is an expert in the area (wrote a textbook). Very clear delivery in lecture. The course involves a lot of work, so make sure to attend lectures and do practice exams.

He is regarded as an expert in the accounting profession and his teaching and knowledge exemplify that. The course can be challenging -- you have to work hard for a good grade, but Nelson is the best lecturer and uses actual financial statements and real-world cases to supplement learning the concepts. Would highly recommend this course with Nelson

Professor Nee is an ok guy and attempts to bring humor to his lectures, but ultimately his lecture style is extremely boring and unorganized. He changed the class structure and test structure twice and ultimately utilized extremely esoteric language without really explaining what he was trying to teach. I would avoid him if you have a better option
Everything was pretty easy, except for the fact that he assigned us 15 page paper to do in 10 days at the end of the semester.

Professor Nee is a very nice guy, but his lectures can be very boring. There was only one prelim, and you basically just had to show up to class and discussions to get participation credit. Overall, he does really want to see you succeed.

Prof. Nee's class is a great intro to sociology, and you don't need any prior knowledge. He loves his work and connects the big ideas to examples at Cornell, which is helpful. Not the most engaging discussion leader and the readings can be a bit dry. If you keep up and participate passing should be no problem.

Nee is an incredibly nice guy who loves what he's teaching and wants kids to do well. That being said, the material is pretty dry and some of the readings can be confusing. Section is VERY important. Prelims are both essays and you have to do the readings to do well. Yet despite all that, he bumps up the grades and its really not hard to get an A.

Professor Nee's mastery of and enthusiasm for the subject material was evident from day one. The class is extremely useful and highly applicable to any path in life. Grading was fair and reasonable. Follow along in class and interact with the ideas, and you will do well. The class is definitely worthwhile and highly recommended.

Easy A if you follow lectures and skim through readings. I loved the material studied but the lectures admittedly were a little dry and monotonic. Not generally helpful but if you sit in front/ask questions/go to office hours, he will help you like no other. He loves to talk about what he does, which I thought was just passion, not arrogance.
He's a smart guy, does not lecture that well, but at least he is very clear and the tests are easy.
He's a pretty cool professor.  A little dry during some lectures, and the slides not incredibly helpful, but I'd still say that he can be very engaging.
Though he is very intelligent, he has a boring teaching style.  Incredibly difficult to stay awake in class.
boring but important lectures.  material is interesting to study, but can be dry.  Edges on common sense.  class is pretty good though
Awesome prof. Helpful and very amiable as well. One of the better classes in the sociology department.

Even though Professor Nee is a genius in his field, he is always willing to help and guide his students through the exciting field of economic sociology. His lectures and discussion sections are very informative, and I would recommend any course with him.

This professor is by far the most knowledgeable on South African law and constittuion. His first hand accounts working in South Africa during the transition with Mandela, Joe Slovo, Chris Hani and others is extraordinary.  he is very humble, modest and a great professor.
Totally teh best .  Intelligent, extremely knowledgable, very helpful.  Totally above the extraordinary.

Prof. Ndulo was awarded one of three recipients of the first annual Awards for Excellence in the Teaching, Advising and Mentoring of Graduate and Professional Students. This is an excellent professor and engages his students in practical application of the law.

The kindest professor you'll ever meet; so approachable, helpful and easy to talk to. His classes were really interesting and he was very engaging. I highly recommend his International Criminal Law seminar!

Professor Ndulo is an awesome professor.  He has travelled to some hot spots  (Kosovo, East Timor, Afghanistan, South Africa)and brings his experience into his classroom which rocks!  PhD from Oxford, LLM from Harvard, knows his stuff!  Very helpful, strict but very approachable.His International Law and Foreign Direct Investment is the best !
Excellent and highly intelligent lecturer.

Prof. Nerode has a wealth of knowledge that he has accumulated over 60+ years at Cornell. Moreover, he is more than willing to share this knowledge with any student that has interest.

It is rare in this world to find a human being that genuinely loves to teach, and Nerode is without a doubt one of them.

Would not recommend taking this class with him. I took it when COVID first started but think about it to this day. He's nice and it's an easy A, but I learned the literal bare minimum of linear algebra. I occasionally am embarrassed that I don't know linear algebra concepts I need in my STEM classes now. If I could go back I would take ENGI linalg.

Professor Nerode is a fine mathematician, and a very interesting person to listen to, but I unfortunately learned next to nothing in his class. He gave us an overview of the subject matter more than an explanation of it. The main ideas seemed to be there, but we never got any real practice in order to assimilate them.

While his lectures were often confusing, he was always open to meet outside of class. He is clearly extremely well read. He doesn't care about grades, but is interested in students getting the most they can out of the class and their investment. If you can show that you are interested and care about the material, the grades should follow.
Don't take his class if you want to learn the material. Literally didn't learn anything. Got an A in the class. What he teaches and what's on the tests are completely different.

He is a legend in the Math world, but he is old and lacks clarity during his lectures. However, discussion sections are helpful, and as long as you hand in all of your homework assignments, you should do well. Also, there were two in-class exams and no prelims nor finals. Get to know him though; he is a very interesting man.

Prof Nerode is an excellent person, and always ready to help. His lectures can be slightly unclear at times but if you study the material, its almost fine and the Prof is always there to spend time with you to help you understand. Willing to help out beyond his class. Homeworks are sometimes long and hard, but fairly graded and exams are quite easy

Nerode is a really nice guy. His lectures are pretty pointless since he mostly reads from his notes that are online anyway. However, those notes (which he wrote) are pretty good. Tests are pretty easy. Homeworks are a bit harder and kind of long but not terrible.

Prof. Nerode is kind, approachable, understanding, and overall just a great man! The fact that he's still teaching at the age of 81 explains why his lectures can at times be a bit difficult to follow. But he was very understanding when it came to prelim conflicts so he has my utmost respect. Would definitely take any other class with him!

Took linear algebra with Prof. Nerode in Spring 2013. Professor Nerode is a very kindhearted and caring man. He's a great person, but unfortunately not mumbles to himself in lecture, but that's totally understandable since he is 81. Problem sets were mostly all proof-based (great for math majors) while prelims only had computation-based questions.

Nerode is an amazing mathematician but it's just very hard to understand him because he lectures on such a high level.  He is getting older and he can be very impatient and incompetent at times.  The class was hell, the assignments were very tedious and people at the support center even said he is odd, to say the least.

He has decided to no longer use a textbook so he has his long printed lectures that he just reads in class so there is no point in going to lecture.  Homework is difficult and for me, going to TAs office hours were a must- his were useless.  He is a nice grader though.  I got a 33% on the first exam and I still got an A in the course.
No textbook for course. No need to attend lectures. Homework is hard but workable. Extremely easy exams.
He's nice in grading and test. Useless lectures.
Greatest professor ever! His tests are just like the sample tests. The first quintile on a prelim was 118...out of 120. Take any of his classes.

I think he's better at teaching history of mathematics/logic than analysis. Classes are usually unclear and it doesn't seem to make much of a difference if you go or not since reading the book by yourself gives pretty much the same result. Plus you won't have to decipher his handwriting if you just read the book.
I know this guy is brilliant, but he can't teach for his life.  Very unclear, rambles and cannot answer questions.  The class isn't so hard, though.
Lectures were absolutely useless the entire semester.  Learned jack.  Doesn't seem to work his own problems for exams so doesn't know exactly how doable (or not) his own exam is.

Prof. Nerode is a really nice guy.  Unfortunately, he doesn't even understand his notes.  All he does is read them off and get himself confused. Class is 100% useless and the homework is really hard to do with no teacher. ALWAYS go to SECTION. Tests are so easy.
The class was pretty easy but I still felt like I learned something.

The class is ridiculously easy in that you hardly have to do anything to do well on the tests. Even so, his lectures are useless and I could not understand a single thing he tried to explain. It doesn't help that it is also impossible to read his handwriting on the board.

I took a "math in perspective" class with him and one other student.  I didn't get a whole lot out of the class content wise, but he told fascinating and funny stories and anecdotes about the history of math and his associations with other famous mathematicians.

The most kind and compassionate professor on this campus!  You will all do well in his class because he doesnt care about grades as much as he cares about teaching you how to logic, reason, and think.

He's a brilliant man, I wish I could understand all he tried to teach us. I think that was the biggest problem - teaching on a level that most undergraduate students could understand. Fascinating and intelligent.

Lectures consisted of him reading to us off overheads (which usually had errors).  Never looked up during lectures and mumbled a lot.  Nice person, but lectures were useless.  Only 25% of the class came to the lectures.
Easy assignments, useless lectures
Sometimes attending her class is like getting bullied.
very disorganized

I was studying THAI 3303 - Thai Literature I, THAI 3304 - Thai Literature II, THAI 4431 - Directed Study, THAI 4432 - Directed Study. (Not THAI2202, my classes were not in the checkbox.)
The professor very professionally teaches me about reading interpretation and analysis. She explained unequivocally and was very attentive. Never moody.

I cried three times because of the class. Has no problem humiliating you in front of the class and even though I did try my hardest, she didn't care. Expects you to understand her even though the instructions are unclear. After the many times I was yelled at, I lost motivation to do good in the class but other than that she's nice.
Very unclear expectations. Zero guidance in learning the language. Unresponsive with emails. Moody. Dont bother taking this course.

The most caring professor that you'll ever meet. She cares about your grades, your well being, and your time at Cornell. Get to know her and go with the flow. Her classes may seem a bit different than the usual classes but they prepare you so well in the future.

Best teacher and adviser I've had at Cornell so far. Not only teaches is her method brilliant but she is great to talk to outside of the classroom and cares more about her students than any teacher I've ever met. If you want to take an Asian language, Cornell Thai is the best program you can find. No textbook, simple homework, lots of fun!

Absolutely brilliant way of teaching and way of engaging students in class. Truly an amazing class to be able to take. But also must be something you are truly passionate about, and something that you are willing to just go along with. Amazingly nice teacher, but also very rigid line between teacher and students, although the class size is small.

There is no need to study, very little homework, and much less class time (especially compared to Chinese). Yet you learn the language far better than any other program I've ever experienced. You will learn the language the same you learned your native language, naturally, yet at a much quicker pace. Not a class to miss!

Her method is brilliant. There is no need to study, very little homework, and much less class time (especially compared to Chinese). Yet you learn the language far better than any other program I've ever experienced. You will learn the language the same you learned your native language, naturally, yet at a much quicker pace. Not a class to miss!

Class may seem disorganized, but it's part of her style. Her way of teaching is almost brilliant.. no need for memorization. If you pay attention and do the work, you don't even need to study. It's all about absorption of the language. She understands personal pacing and difficulties... just go with the flow and be friendly and you'll be ok.

Great class if you have extra sensory perception. No text, no structure, no syllabus, unclear, unfocussed expectations. Sometimes encouraging, and generous, but sometimes you'll come to class with no idea what to expect, or what on earth she'll do.

Made an already difficult class even more uneccesarily difficult during covid. Hard to understand his lectures even though it seems that he tries his best. Tests are brutal, quizes are gambles, said hed curve the final grade and then just didnt. This is a tough class, find a prof that doesnt make things any tougher than they already are.

It is hard to tell why and how this person became a professor here. Sometimes it seemed like he is hardly mentally suitable to be a part of a normal society, not to mention teaching someone. One of the worst professors I've had a chance to take a class from. If you have a choice - look elsewhere!

Professor Ng was very unclear to me. I had previously taken the course in high school and still had difficulty following in class what he was saying. The homework he assigned online was little help in preparing us for what was on the tests. I found the tests to be more difficult and he seemed to insert concepts we hadn't covered in class.
Ng is a good professor, he is clear in lecture, but if you don't understand the concept fully, when going to office hours he is unclear. Would recommend Professor Ritz instead.
Lena is great! I love her!
Lena is such an amazing teacher! The class is easy, organized, and SO interesting. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!!

Took FWS: Monsters in Fiction. Interesting class and class itself is also fun. The amount of reading assignment can be overwhelmed especially during prelim and final seasons.  But the books are interesting since it's related to monsters. Use the office hour, since she is very willing to help and give feedback. READ A BOOK AND PARTICIPATE.

Great teacher. Her discussions were really informative and fun, making it more than just a class. She does focus more on the reading side of things than the writing side but she still gives really good feedbacks on essay to help you improve.

Good teacher, really funny. She focuses more on the reading and analysis side and not AS much on teaching writing side, but I personally loved that. Class discussions was always interesting and I learned a lot about how to think critically. Gives great and thorough feedback on essays. Be aware that your grade goes down if you miss class.
He was one of the best professor I could have asked for to introduce me to the PMA department.

Professor Salvato is one of the most compassionate professors I have encountered at Cornell. He is a great lecturer and passionate about PMA, which makes his class very enjoyable. He also pays great attention to how his students are doing as a whole, making constant efforts to check in. If the opportunity presents itself, take one of his classes!

I took Television with him (AMST 2160) and he was such a great teacher, the class clapped for him after the first and last lecture. We watched films throughout the lectures and talked about them. We were also assigned to watch these for homework and sometimes they'd be a little long. Essay grading was a little tough but doable if you put in effort

Lectures were fine, but he likes to hear himself talk, I'd reccomend going and paying attention, but this class didn't require that much work. It just wasn't as interesting as I hoped it would be. Essays are fairly light and the HW isn't bad, just keep up with it and put a little more effort than you might expect.

He is an excellent lecturer and is highly knowledgeable. With that said, there is a lot of material that is not covered that I wish was, though I can understand that there are time constraints. I also struggled to reach him outside of class. Homework consists of readings/viewings that are often entertaining and a handful of easy papers.

Professor Salvato is a very kind professor who knows a ton about PMA studies and his passion is felt in every lecture. The assignments are a good time if you enjoy writing about TV/movies. There are readings/things to watch for each class, but it's not unmanageable. Long readings can be skimmed. The class is heavily discussion based, in a good way.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Salvato is brilliant, I learned so much, workload totally manageable, loved almost everything we watched

Advertises it as a discussion-based class but there were more than 80 students. He sold this class as teaching cultural and economic impacts of television. This is an analytical televisual class where you look at mise-en-scene, angles, etc. Wanted to be taught the visible impacts of television. By week 3 only about 30-40 started showing up.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nick is perhaps the best lecturer at Cornell - he doesn't hesitate, break, or stutter through entire classes. He also remembers students' names within weeks in large lectures. He's also one of the clearest critical thinkers on campus. Not an easy grader, but definitely fair

Nick's worst trait is that his genius can be intimidating, but if you don't let that get to you, then his class is very rewarding. He blows your mind every class period, and if you put in the work, it's not hard to get good grades. He's exceptionally accommodating about missing classes and getting extensions as long as you talk to him about it.

Really great professor who is both helpful and approachable. Good discussions but readings are incredibly long and often difficult to get through. Always a heavy bent on FGSS issues in Nick's classes even if not cross-listed as such.

Amazing professor. Not easy, but perhaps the best lecturer at Cornell. No ums, likes, or breaks. It's as if he reads from a teleprompter, but has the enthusiasm of an unplanned conversation. Incredible knowledge about television and film theory. Highly recommended!

Nick Salvato is an excellent professor - a brilliant person with a genuine interest in teaching. Be warned: the texts are often difficult, but he has a very straightforward and accessible teaching style. If you put forth the effort, you will learn a lot. Grading is fair. He is very patient and willing to help if you don't understand something.

Nick is a really laid-back, smart guy who loves theatre.  Class is just a discussion, so attendance is important (but he also is very understanding).  A lot of plays to read, but all interesting.  Very fair grader and easy to please.

Professor Silins is very laid back, flexible, and knowledgeable. For the Phil of Arts class, the typical week was 1-3 hours of reading, 2.5 hours of lectures, 1 hours on 2 weekly discussion posts. There are 2 essays and 1 final exam, all of which was manageable. My only issue was with the course content itself - it was at times a bit dull.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Silins is invested in the course material and carries that joy into classes - the classroom atmosphere is fun and laid back, which makes the complex concepts a lot easier to get through. Really enjoyed his class!

Silins is a really cool dude who is super knowledgable on aesthetics. An interest in aesthetics is paramount to making it a good class. I felt that the material was super interesting but was spread thin by a lot of different ideas. Aesthetics is a huge topic to cover; splitting it into a part 1 and part 2 by a semester system would be helpful.
He didn't show up. Cad.
