I was really disapointed by this class.  I thought that the lectures weren't very organized and he would pace back and forth way too much, it got distracting.  It took to long to get papers back and would only get assignments a week or less before they were due.

Great guy, extremely helpful, very fair grader. If you've never taken a philosophy class before, know this: you basically just copy what the book says for  all your papers. You are not meant to be original at all. I would have gotten an A in this course but for that knowledge.

Yes he's a little repetitive, but when it comes to philosophy, being repetitive is a plus. I found the lectures to be quite clear and Dr. Silins was quite accessible during office hours. He's a really friendly guy, and I highly recommend him. The only bad thing? The lectures always ran a couple of minutes late.

The lectures are repetitive, but given some of the ideas you're working with, it can be helpful. And he's quite funny at times; frequently works in popular culture references to make the ideas a little less banal. DO the reading.

Intensely repetitive in class which makes lectures very boring. It's an interesting subject though and the readings are good so if you're interested in philosophy of the mind you might as well take it. Niko is decent in private office hours but the lectures are soooooooo boooooring. Niko's a cool guy but get ready to daydream.

Took him for Philosophy of the Mind. Very interesting, hot, couldn't take my eyes off of him! He is way chill and laid back with his students and can be really funny too! Kind of nerdy but in a cute way, definitely a keeper!

Great Instructor. Once you get past the accent you can really learn a lot from him. His lectures were very organized and he focused much more on the theory behind organic reations rather than simply listing them like in 358

Overall he's a decent professor. Perhaps he could be a bit more clear on some of the subjects, but if you do the problem sets and take notes you should be able to hit the mean of the class. He is better than 3580 (Prof. Sogah) at least. On a side note, he wears orange crocs and has two dogs (one is butt ugly) which he sometimes shows during exams.
An authentic character.

Jon has a habit of speeding through the basics of the concepts he teaches, and then spending the rest of the time going over example questions that are beyond the difficulty of what is needed for this class.  If you're in his class, attend office hours with the TAs often and always do the problem sets.  (Problem sets are similar to test questions.)

He presents material in an unclear way and is not helpful in OH. I found myself often times very confused coming out of lecture than reading the book. The psets are good because they force you to think. Just do the psets and you'll be fine. Go to TA OH and 1057 and you'll be set. I hate his crocs and his stupid Icelandic accent.

Best prof in the dept. Of course that's not saying much, but he is certainly a great guy. Orgo will be miserable no matter who teaches it, but I'm glad we at least had him along the way. Gives you a solid bg and the concepts will stay with you semesters after you're done. Plus he wears orange crocs. Can't beat that.
Great professor. Textbook is useless, just use lecture information and problem sets. Course is not hard, not that much information, just about your problem solving ability
Jon is the man. his class is easy if you go to lectures and the supplements. he is quite positively the boss. only lazy people will complain about him.

tests are VERY fair if you study hard for them. he's almost impossible to understand if you aren't sitting in the first few rows of the class. book is a great supplement to the lectures. go back to lecture notes after learning the material and they really seem to make sense

This class was AWFUL. Jon tries to make things seem so basic and simple in class, and swears that he will never deviate from what he teaches for his exams...Explain how the mean on our 2nd exam was a 50!! His exams are unfair and do not accurately convey the students' understanding of the concepts, instead they make us feel stupid. Horrible prof.

Favorite professor I've had so far!  He presented the material in a really clear, understandable, and (believe it or not) entertaining way.  The tests were very fair; if you take the time to practice what's taught in class on your own, you can score way above the mean because everyone goes into the class with the attitude that it's impossible.
Good prof; easy to understand; tests are fair; bring interesting things to exams

I wouldn't go as far as [below], but, he did say the only way to get orgo was "practice practice practice" and then gave us 359 p.sets. this will be fixed if he teaches 357 again (he'll use ours). lectures were helpful b/c he covered stuff that wasn't emphasized in the textbook (sterics). Catch on to what he's looking for and you'll be fine.

Brilliant chemist, worthless teacher. Has no control over voice, which is incoherent and inaudible. Fails to gauge students' progress. Is too lazy to make new problem sets and chooses to use old problem sets...from a different level class. Clearly does not like to teach or take the time to help individual students.  Insincere and crass in person.
I really enjoyed his teaching style and the class.  He was always available to help.

Messy organisation of materials, illegible handwriting such that i spent most of my time figuring out what he's writing instead of paying attention to his mumbling words. I once asked to arrange an appointment with him becuz his office hr clashed with my other class but he told me to look for my TA instead. How helpful is that!

His lectures are a great supplement to the book, which not only teaches a lot but has great personality too :) If you must take Orgo, take this one--fewer people, greater attention, cuter prof. Take the people in the class with a grain of salt though.

I have to disagree with the previous comments. His lectures were unclear and useless. He does not want to or care about lecturing, often telling us to just read it in the textbook. He underestimated our abilities in the beginning of the semester and greatly overestimated them towards the end. I pretty much taught myself orgo.
Brilliant professor, knows stuff really well.  Covers material at a quick clip and makes prelims that are very challenging and comprehensive.  Difficult but rewarding.

Knows Orgo material very well. Presents the material in a very engaging way that really wraps you into the lecture, unlike most other lectures where you are just left staring at the board. Very attentive to needs of students and will always provide help or assistance.  Highly Recommended Cornell Professor
Jón rules.
Orgo is a dull subject but Jón is a great lecturer and makes it bearable.  By far the coolest Icelandic professor at Cornell!
No Comments

Professor Siena gave fun, enjoyable, and clear lectures which made the course very easy. Although the course itself has a lot of tests, we were always very well prepared. 100% recommend taking ITAL 1201 with her!

Had such an amazing time with Professoressa Nora! Not only did I have her for ITAL 1202, but 1201 as well, and she is one of the most easygoing, approachable professors I've ever had. She will grant extensions when asked for them, will meet with you outside of class whenever you need to if something needs to be discussed, and is a fair grader!

Prof. Siena has a very clear teaching style and a strong ability to convey the material clearly. She is compassionate and understanding and while she pushes students to do their best, her primary concern is to make students improve and fell confident about their skills!

Definitely one of the better professors in his department. Lectures were a little dry, but he is a thoughful professor who explains concepts comprehensively and gives lots of extra credit. If you attend lectures and study for exams, you will do well.
Best professor ive had at cornell so far. Genuinely makes class so intresting and made me fall in love with economics.

Professor Sanders is a great teacher and person. He actively looks for ways to make the class better for the students in it. The two different grading methods provided a lot of flexibility. The two midterms were definitely a lot easier than the final but overall they were all manageable.
Great lecturer and teacher and gives you a lot of opportunities to do well. Honestly should've gotten an A but sold. Don't rly need to go to class since he posts the slides.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: what everyone else says is pretty accurate. his first 2 prelims are easy as long as you do the bare minimum studying. maybe it was just me but the final was not it even though i spent a good amount of time studying for it. definitely make sure you know your stuff for that but outside of that this class is light and much better than 1120
He's honestly the goat. Easy class if u pay attention. So many resources like office hours and the microecon help center. 2 dif grading methods to help u get a better score in the class.

Very good professor with multiple grading schemes; even if you bomb one of the prelims, a higher grade is possible if you do well on final. Great lecturer and is helpful in office hours. He's the GOAT ;)

Grading is very clear, just don't underestimate the class like I did before the first prelim. Don't fall behind even though it seems very easy and chill, the professor is amazing and you have lots of resources but you do actually need to put some work in. Wonderful professor though, super fun and chill, made econ fun and interesting.

I knew he was going to be a great professor when his pollev question in the first lecture was about his son's favorite song in kpdh. He explains concepts well, is extremely responsive and gives detailed explanations on ed discussion especially before exams. He also gives 5 practice tests for each exam. Exams are very fair and even fun sometimes.

Great professor, includes real world examples in lectures to make economics topics easy to understand for beginners. Tests are extremely fair and modeled after previous years prelim/final exams so not difficult to prepare with effort. Beware that exams are 80% of your score in this class though.
Very clear lecturer, makes Econ easy to understand if you've never taken it before. Kind, flexible, and organized. Not too much HW, but definitely put in effort to study for the tests.

definitely the best professor for taking intro economics courses by a long shot. Such a nice, caring guy and also a really good professor. you can tell he really cares about teaching and explains things in super effective ways. also has cute stories about his family and supports women. hes him

Super passionate, cares about his students. It's a big lecture class but he is a great lecturer and I'm rarely falling asleep (even during an 8am class). Exams are fair, you're able to have a sheet of notes. He gives a lot of practice exams that prepare you well for the exam.
No complaints, amazing professor
Great Professor for Microeconomics! Highly recommended
Great Professor. Very accommodating and understanding of personal circumstances.

While lectures are not required, they are very fun and easy to follow. Would recommend reading textbook although not required. HW is not too frequent and pretty easy. Plenty of review offered for each exam. Reccomend participate in extra credit throughout semester. Very nice professor and hosts lots of OH

As others have said Prof. Sanders genuinely wants you to succeed. I highly recommend going to lecture as he is very good at explaining concepts in ways that are easy to understand, and his deadpan humor keeps it interesting. Discussions are optional. Very willing to meet outside of class for help. Exams are very fair and match the practice tests

My opinion of Sanders is mixed. He is definitely the easiest 1110 prof. He gave up to around 2% extra credit (depending on grading method). Unfortunately he mismanaged online exams, which led him to make a cheat sheet only final, despite 1110 not really being a course you could fit into a single sheet of paper. Sucked up tons of finals week for me.
Literally the best professor here. He is so kind and helpful. He also gives so many extra credit opportunities. If you put in the effort you will get a great grade.

I was expecting to be bored out of my mind in my econ class. Professor Sanders ended up making the class much more interesting than I thought an econ class could be. He had fun interactive things. The class wasn't a walk in the park but he does want you to succeed in it.

Extremely energetic at 9:05 in the morning, cracks jokes that I thought were funny during lecture, responds pretty quickly on the discussion board (especially before an exam). Sometimes went a little too quickly in lecture. There's a textbook but it's not necessary. Exams were online and entirely multiple choice, and very fair.

Professor Sanders is SUPER nice. Really really like him. Just seems like a good guy. He doesn't want you to fail. He really works to make sure you can get the best grade possible in the class. Totally respect him and would be more than happy to take another class with him. Super helpful as well.
Great professor! Smart, good lectures, interesting class.
Such a good lecturer. He is exceptionally kind and helpful during office hours. Overall, a fantastic teacher!

Took his class a while ago but couldn't ask for a better intro micro teacher. Was pretty organized and always tried to make the class material relevant and interesting, which is hard for a 400+ person intro class. Class isn't hard if you at least pay attention, but even if you don't he's very approachable for help.

Such a great professor, he released every prior test he has ever given to study off of. His lectures were well organized and fun to listen to. He was very accommodating during the shooting and bomb scares that happened in fall 21. You can tell he wants the best for his students. GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS! They help so much!

Sanders was a good lecturer for an introductory econ class. His classes always started by briefing recent research related to topics being covered in class at the time. The homework is not a great representative of the exams, but the exams themselves are very easy and he provides plenty of past exams to review.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Sanders is an amazing lecturer. Hes charismatic, funny, and is soooo passionate about economics. Would definitely recommend him. He comes up with his own exam questions and they always have a whole theme to it; its so funny. Our final this year was Animal Crossing themed!
Very good prof. Extremely good lectures and helpful in office hours. Exams reflect content well.

lectures werent helpful in terms of calculations, didnt always best explain the material. He records his lectures though so you can go back and listen to them. Makes himself available , great explaining in office hours. If youre good at math you'll be okay. If math isn't your forte it's going to require alot of work. Do all the practice prelims!
Amazing. Incredible. Phenomenal. Best professor at Cornell. Give this guy tenure.

Professor Sanders is the best professor I have had at Cornell University. He is always extremely caring as well as being an excellent lecturer. Professor Sanders is quick responder on ed discussion and you never need to be scared to ask questions in class or online. I would take definitely take a class just because it was taught by him!

Professor Sanders is one of my favorite professors in Cornell, he is very caring and respects every students. He cares about student's mental health and try his best accommodating with students needs. Lectures are mandatory but I strongly recommend people to attend lecture because it's very useful and he is a great lecturer.

Amazing lecturer and is really great at explaining concepts. Puts in a ton of effort to help his students. Overall stand up guy. The class isn't too hard if you have at least a bit of background in Econ, but the tests and assessments are doable through doing the past practice exams and asking questions.

Easily the best lecturer I have ever had. You can watch the recorded lectures later so attendance isn't necessary but if you do not watch the lectures you will not pass the class. The tests are fairly simple and very straightforward and he provides plenty of practice prelims. The homework is easy but of no help on the tests. Textbook is useless.

ECON 1110 had a light workload. Only attended a couple of lectures all semester and still had a solid grasp of the course material. The exams were similar to previous years so you knew what to expect. The required homework was not helpful to prepare. Median was a B+ but if you have any background in economics it is a stress-free and easy class.

Such a passionate professor and really cares about his students. Lectures were really clear and he spends a lot of time explaining concepts and graphs. DO THE PRACTICE PRELIMS, though. The questions are extremely similar and the homework is often too easy to be that helpful. I honestly never read the textbook, just pay attention in class.

Professor Sanders is such a positive guy. He makes class stress free and truly cares more about your understanding of the material than just a grade. Lecture is very important, as long as you pay attention to the concepts he explains, you will do very well. I highly suggest taking any course you can with him, I definitely would take another!
Amazing class! Lectures are very engaging. I found the tests to be challenging but fair.

HW - multiple choice, 3 tries for every Q, easy 100% on HW. Lectures - quality slides, but sometimes skips calculation examples that could be helpful. Discussion - optional, not rly helpful. Exams - fair. Make you think, but easy Qs too. Grading - gives different % breakdown options and assigns the best one for u, this semester could drop a prelim
I loved Econ 111 with Sanders. He made lectures exciting and interesting. There was a fair amount of HW, but he gave us three tries on each question so it was easy. Highly recommend Sanders!!

The best professor and the best course I have ever had I have been crying for hours after taking his last lecture. Nick is really awesome! I even want to take ECON1110 again next semester. He is incredibly good at teaching and bring students warmth during such a crazy pandemic period. The homework is sometimes easy, but prelims are moderate.

I had Professor Sanders for intro Micro and Economics and Environmental Policy. It is obvious that he loves what he teaches. He backs up all his statements with engaging research papers. Also, he has a deep respect for the students that can be hard to come by in a professor. Econ3850 was easier than micro.

Prof Sanders is a really great guy! You can tell that he is passionate about economics and the well-being of his students. Piece of advice: make sure you study past prelims/finals in order to do well on that year's exam. Definitely loved having him as a professor because of how engaging he was and how concisely he was able to explain concepts.

Sanders is a great person to introduce you to econ but he does tend to run behind schedule so he gets a less thorough as the semesters go by. You don't really need to show up, the textbook is decent. My TA was terrible and so were a lot of others so don't bank on that. Do a couple of his past tests, his testing is quite different from the hw.

Moves quickly through lecture slides and doesn't always explain the quantitative/calculation parts, but is great for the most part. Posts the slides online so you can skip lecture if you want. Discussions were useless. HW is easy. Exams were straightforward and similar in structure to previous years' exams. Nice guy, makes jokes during lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great professor. As long as you go to class and pay attention even though not required, exams are easy. Use previous exams he provides to study. He keeps lectures interesting also
Great lecturer. Makes class very interesting. Very accessible outside of class, with tons of extra office hours before prelims and finals. Not an easy class, but if you do the work, you can do well.

Professor Sanders is a great professor that has interesting real-world examples that make me look forward to class. His tests are very fair and make you learn the material. If you do the previous prelims and read the book you'll be fine, but I suggest showing up to the lectures to learn about the world.

good professor. he tries to be really interesting so the material actually becomes more confusing (ik lol). He will provide examples for topics without providing a framework to apply that example onto. The textbook is a must if you have never taken econ. His tests are fair, but short, so you need to be very accurate to do well. Nice guy.

Sanders is a great professor everybody loves him. However go to his lectures and spend time actually learning the homework or you won't do well. The class is fairly easy if you put in the time. The office hours are great too. Discussions are pointless and very optional.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Super easy class. I went to 2 lectures (I should have gone to more as he is a good lecturer), did not study for any of the prelims and did not go to my section a single time. I think if you just go to lectures and section and pay attention an A is pretty much guaranteed. I had two other friends who actually did the work and they both got A+'s

Not a hard class, but not an easy A bc it is SUPER easy to underestimate it. HW takes 5 minutes & isn't helpful for studying. I got a C+ on Prelim 1 bc I thought it'd be like the HW and that messed up my final grade even tho I A+'s on Prelim 2 & the final. Focus on practice problems + lecture slides. Super nice guy, & willing to help.

Interesting and engaging lecturer who clearly is passionate about the material. Presents material in a clear, understandable way. First two thirds or so of the class the material was pretty easy; got difficult near the end. I especially appreciated that he had lots of extra office hours at convenient times prior to prelims and especially the final.

Sanders is unbelievably dedicated to his job. His lectures have everything you need to know conceptually. His love for econ is contagious and his office hours are fantastic. Don't bother reading the textbook--use it as a supplement if needed. The class is not a lot of work but also not an easy A. Do lots of practice problems to study for prelims.

The most passionate instructor I've ever had at Cornell. He deeply cares about Cryptography and he wants you to learn more than anything else in the class. The emphasis is on your learning and not grades and he does this by giving lots of extra credit opportunities.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: 4830 is an awesome class. Noah is definitely passionate about and great at explaining cryptography. Lectures were engaging, and lecture notes are super useful. Homeworks are difficult, but graded quite leniently. 10/10 no notes.

Clearly passionate about cryptography and happy to share it. All his lecture notes are typed up online and he even playfully asks students why we bother to show up to lecture when we can just read the lecture notes. Decently difficult homework.
He will push you, but he's cool and calm after class, will probably nerd you out with math crypto and thereoms

Exams are graded harshly with no partial credit. Very strict grader and very condescending in Ed discussions. Always has to tell the class to be quiet and pay attention due to not being able to get the class active.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures were fast-paced and hard to understand due to messy handwriting, plus unnecessary as the online notes were 10x better, and he'd tell us to read those whenever he failed to finish all the content for the day anyway. Serially failed to engage the class and blamed everyone but himself for it. Gave 0 partial credit on very difficult tests.

Hes honestly not that bad! All lecture slides posted online which is super helpful and the content is very interesting. He may not be the most lively professor but its clear he loves communication and cares about students doing well. I would recommend him.

His class is the problem, not him. Introverted, caring guy who tries his best, but the subject matter is horrifically awful. If you hate abstract theory and are turned off by group discussions during lecture, steer clear. Norman himself is fine though. Fair, accessible and reasonable.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Norman speaks in a monotone voice and seems genuinely bored by teaching. However, the material was extremely interesting and his projects and papers are surprisingly interesting to complete. I actually looked forward to the class even though he very clearly does not want to be there teaching it. And if you study, you'll do well on the test.

Very boring teacher. Lectures and slides are very helpful in understanding the material. Lectures could be more clear and quizzes can be a tad specific. Overall, if you do the work, read the book and show up to class, you shouldn't have a hard time doing well
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Extremely boring and monotonous. Manages to turn exciting material into confusing, unimaginative, sleepy lectures. Asks self-defeating questions, loves platitudes and crams his course with meaningless group activities that are neither enjoyable nor rewarding.
One of the worst professors at Cornell. Doesn't know how to lecture so class was focused around group discussions.

Lectures can be long/boring but he's a nice guy that is there for you/will help you if need be. Sections are way too long in my opinion, and somewhat unnecessary. Papers aren't too hard but require a lot of thought. Put in some effort and you will be fine.
The professor is really boring and doesn't know what he's talking about half the time.

Brutally boring. Readings are long and put you to sleep and professor is very soft spoken and monotone, so falling asleep in lecture is definitely common too. I want to go into Advertising so Visual Comm sounds like something enjoyable but his curriculum makes it dreadful, in my opinion. But essay topics are well thought out and make you think.

She is a model of scholarly dedication.  The life of the mind is a calling, not a job, and Norton models the passion, stamina, and excitement of living for ideas.  I was her teaching assistant decades ago, and I still cherish the memory of that semester.

I wouldn't take this class again if someone paid me to do it. Lectures are long and insanely boring. She talks WAY too fast and put me to sleep probably once a week. The readings are long and boring and the tests are easy but apparently graded harshly. I did every single reading and spent hours on the paper and still got a C+. My first non-A grade.

She is a great professor who definitely knows her stuff. She is one of the most knowledgeable people I know. I have taken a few of her courses. For those of you who don't like to read, well then her classes are not for you. She talks WAY too fast, but she admits it. If you need help, she is very helpful and willing to work with you outside of class

I took this 25 years ago. I was the only man in the class and was treated with respect by Norton and my fellow students. She is tough, articulate and does not tolerate sloppiness. If you work hard, you'll gain tremendosly both intellectually and as a person. I took 3 classes with here and consider them a highlight  of my time at Cornell.
super super boring, talks too fast, grades too hard

This class was unnecessarily difficult.  All she wanted you to do was memorize what she said (which was a lot), and made the exams too general (which enabled the TA to knock off points at every end).  Terrible, boring readings, do not take this unless you actually really care about women's studies.
An intimidating professor who can be less than tactful and very arrogant.  However, she is a brilliant woman who clearly wants her students to learn.
This class is EXTREMELY difficult. The grading is unfair and the prof. talks way too fast (not to mention talking a lot about herself).  Take this class at your own risk.

Scared me to death the first day of class, but wonderful when I got used to her.  Really articulate, engaging, funny, sarcastic, shares great stories from her own research, and doesn't put up with crap-- perfect.
No Comments
Norton is obviously very very smart...as she we will let you repeatedly know throughout the semester.  Lecture could be very good but she talks way too fast...

Mostly lectures and tended to go over the time of the class by like 10 minutes consistently. Somewhat easy but lowkey didn't complete the amount we were supposed to finish the semester so the next semester we had to do more to make up for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A very enjoyable professor, very knowledgeable and open to questions. All material is on printed notes handed out each class, but not much of it will make sense if you don't go to lecture. I did have his class in the late afternoon and his voice put me to sleep several times, but not for lack of interesting content.

Great professor. Really laid back, doesn't give many homework assignments or tests. Essentially, he'll teach the amount you're willing to learn. We read Ovid--about as interesting as Nussbaum himself, but it's not like classes are dreadfully boring.Very nice, funny man. Looks like he's headed towards retirement, take a class of his while you can.

Professor Nyrop was my favorite professor during my first semester. He is an amazing lecturer and truly cares about his students. Honestly, the class is super easy, but he makes it interesting and makes you care about the class in terms of other things beyond just an easy A or A+.

My favorite professor I've had at Cornell so far. He is the nicest guy and very understanding. His lectures are very clear and tests and quizzes are fair. He likes to do interactive examples that always involve food. Labs are entertaining. Take this class!

One of the best teachers I've had at Cornell. Although he is a  busy person he is very willing to make time for students. His lectures are clear and engaging and he gets the whole class involved in discussions.
Helpful and available professor. Chair of a department, but still made sure to make time to help out students. I highly recommend the class
Worse class and Professor. Never care about well student learn.
Great intro class for polymers!
Really really bad. Clearly doesnt care about teaching/students. Boring, bad class notes, uninspinring. DO NOT take a class from this guy.
Totally lost interest after taking his class, but still a great class nonetheless because I got an A+
Great class. Never attended a single lesson and still got an A.
Great professor. I don't know why people are talking smack about him, but I am extremely lazy and somehow I got an A.
Really bad substitute for the real professor that's supposed to teach this class.  Oh well, I guess I'm stuck learning from other students and the textbook...
Ober was excellent professor. Taught subject as well as anybody else and actually seemed very interested in the subject, unlike other professors I've seen.
He is the biggest loser professor out there. If I were the dean, and I knew his TEACHING abilities, I'd have to fire him right away. I hope he learns soon how to teach and not mess around with us.

Worst professor. He posts files online that only works on his computer and nowhere else and he doesn't care about it. Doesn't care about students. Worst lectures. Very unorganized. Crappy handwriting and makes excuses. Never helpful. Dont ruin your interest with him.
Extremely unclear, unorganized and terrible handwriting, horrible professor, very very unhelpful, terrible notes, overall my worst experience at Cornell.

Interesting guy, but incredibly boring teaching style. Expect to spend the semester yawning while he explains black-and-white diagrams. The information communicated is only useful if you have previous hands-on knowledge of agriculture. Those who grew up on a farm should have no problem, but those who don't havethat background will find it hard.

Nice guy, but I didn't like his teaching style. Too many stories and not enough info. I could've learned all that material in half a semester. Lab was really poorly organized and explained; TAs weren't given instructions and Ralph wouldn't help even if asked. Learned a lot but spent half of class doing crosswords.

Excellent teacher and great guy. Makes you understand not only the course curriculum, but also how it fits into a greater academic and social realm. An awesome old-time profs who actually grew up on a grain farm in the midwest and has both the practical background and academic knowledge to be a great source of info on agronomy and life in general.
No Comments

Definitely don't take unless you've taken a stats course before. If you remember AP content, it's literally the same so as long as you do practice you're guaranteed a good grade. Lectures are boring and mostly useless. I just did my homework while he talked. Homework was graded on accuracy and it dropped my grade so be careful with your effort.

This class is definitely not enjoyable if math isn't your thing, but you can make it through with TA and Prof help. If you're kind and confident in approaching Prof. Nussbaum, he will help you in office hours and will accomodate you very fairly. Don't be afraid to reach out just due to his seriousness in lecture. He's a nice person.

This professor reads straight out of the textbook and has illegible handwriting so going to lecture is pretty much pointless. He is a very strict grader and has almost no leniency when it comes to technical mistakes. I was surprised to get a B because i flunked the first prelim and did meh on the second one. Curve must have been okay on the final

I would strongly advise you only take this course if you did well in high school AP stats or dual enrollment stats; it's essentially the same material. Learning this as brand new information is definitely extremely challenging with him as the professor. He is good at explaining specific questions if you ask him personally and the TA was great.

i'm traumatized by this class. he went so fast through lectures that we would finish like half an hour early each time but i wouldn't understand anything. homeworks take so long and he is a really tough grader. strongly discourage.
Do not take this class. His lectures consist of projecting the textbook onto the screen and reading word for word. Also no barley any curve on tests even though median was 50%.
This professor is literally the worst. Save yourself.

lectures weren't super helpful so I taught myself everything outside of class with textbook, overall not a bad experience though. I learned a lot of statistics because the class format made it possible.

Listen to me, save yourself and take ILR stats (Introductory Statistics). Wish I would have listen to the previous reviews. My biggest mistake this semester was definitely taking this class. Do not recommend.

Made the mistake of ignoring his reviews and taking the class for distribution requirements. Learned literally nothing in his lecture -- had to self-learn for every exam. He's not a terrible person, just a bad lecturer. Do not take if you have other options.

NEVER take this man's class!!! Talk to his blackboard all the time. Can't get an A even you ranked second in the whole class. Not showing up in his office hour. Never respond to email.
Better off just reading the textbook. His lecture is basically writing and reading everything from the textbook.

Every Zoom lecture consisted of him pulling up pre-written notes and reading them off for an hour and fifteen minutes. It was truly the most boring class I've ever taken. I went to office hours three times and the professor did not notify the class that he would not be showing up. The tests were much more difficult than homework/review.

Most monotone and boring lecturer I've ever had. He just reads off of his past notes, which you have to listen to because his handwriting isn't legible. I ended up teaching myself most of the material. The exams are nothing like the practice and he doesn't give partial credit.

He is very unbiased and logical. But he is strict, if you would come late to class he would deduct 1% of your grade. So, I rarely went to lecture and essentially taught myself. But lectures are v well organised. HW and labs are easy!! During corona the test was multiplechoice instead of subjective, but he made the rest much easier during the crisis

I was extremely hesitant to take math 1710 mostly because of my complete incompetency in statistics. However, this class was absolutely painless, and professor nussbaum is a very fair grader. Because of covid 19, he even pre recorded a separate set of lectures outside of his live lectures. Lenient and understanding as well as unbiased, a good prof.

He has an interesting way of lecturing. Have to really think about the concepts and I honestly get confused with the way he talks about things. These concepts should be much clearly taught. Assigns lots of articles and research papers that he actually thinks people read. Tests aren't easy either. Just overall not a fun class and harder than needed.

The professor seems dry and strict at first but if you visit him during office hours he is actually very understanding and helpful. He happily walked me through problems I didn't understand and gave me partial credit for a prelim question. He's a nice professor. Class material is harder than I expected. Tests are even harder. Utilize office hours

Please do not take math 1710, professor is awful at teaching. He talks to the board and it is very difficult to understand him. If you haven't taken stats before you are basically going to have to teach yourself a brand new subject. Prelims and exams are also ridiculous. I found going to the class useless.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Lectures weren't helpful at all.
Take any other class

Awful professor and person in general. Not only are his lectures boring, unhelpful, and tedious, he's also one of the least understanding professors I've ever had. On the bright side, the class is super easy, especially if you took stats in high school.

Awful Professor. Neither the Professor nor the TA  seem to have a good grasp on the english language which makes it difficult to understand lectures and ask for help. You're better off taking ILR stats if you're looking to fulfill a requirement. This was the most painfully dull, challenging classes I have taken.

Hard to understand in lecture, but the class itself was easy as long as you stayed on top of your work. I stopped going to lecture and found reading the textbook more beneficial, and wound up doing very well... class average was a B- according to transcripts. If you study a normal amount you'll do very well.

Is not the most charismatic prof., but is actually a really nice guy when you talk to him. He is actually pretty good about answering questions and seems to care about the students. Either way, STATS is a ridiculously easy class.

Professor Nussbaum is terrible. Get very acquainted with the textbook because everything you need to know will be in there. He teaches from the book anyway. No one went to class unless an assignment was due (Wednesdays). Labs are somewhat helpful though so attend those! The prelims and final are around 6-8 questions. Not very hard, but study.
I can't even begin to explain why this professor is so bad. He takes points off for visiting office hours. He talks to the chalkboard. You're better off learning by yourself than from this man.

Completely ignores students when they ask for help - if you go and ask him a question during office hours, he will tell you he is busy and to come back later... every time. Unhelpful. Reads out of the text book. You might as well not go to lecture and read out of the book.
really easy.....i mean honestly it is stats i guess he does an alright job of teaching the material but most of it is just common sense

Worst professor at Cornell. Completely useless lecturer. Biased. Don't go to office hours because apparently he has the right to curve your grade down if you get help. does not follow syllabus grading scheme - basically just makes up your grade based on office hour attendance / your major.
i u want nap time go to class otherwise take another stat class -- not worth it

The prof knows his material but he talks to the chalkboard. He is extremely boring during lecture but if you go to his OH he is pretty helpful. The course is not that tough. His lectures are a grind to get through because he is dull.

She is extremely nice and is great at explaining concepts and answering questions well! She is also very understanding when it comes to assignments, attendance, etc. She always makes sure students understand concepts. Go to her office hours!
She will make biology so easy to grasp.  Amazing lecturer and caring professor.
Super kind and caring

Shambhu is an excellent professor who really cares about his students and wants them to do well. I took four semesters of Nepali and loved it! It's a challenging language to learn, but Shambhu is very patient and good at breaking down concepts.

I took 4 years of Nepali and did a semester in Nepal, graduated in 98.  I loved Shambhu, and have so many great memories of his classes, hanging out at his house, etc. His classes were the best I took at Cornell.  Intro classes were super, and it was even better in the advanced classes just hanging out and chatting with Shambhu.  He is AWESOME!

BEST PROFESSOR AT CORNELL, HANDS DOWN. The language isn't the easiest but he makes it super fun and exciting. This was the BEST class I've ever taken at Cornell. Shambhu is probably the only professor at Cornell who is passionate about what he teaches and really cares for his students. TAKE TAKE!!
The best professor you could possibly have. He is clear, concise, and actually cares about his students. Take his class.

Shambhu is fantastic.  I've studied spanish and german; but was worried about Nepali and its Sanskrit-derived srcipt.  I felt really comfortable in his classes, and picked up the language quicker than I thought I would.  Would definately recommend Shambhu to anyone interested in Nepal or Nepali.

put simply, the best teacher I've ever had. Shambhu is the man, and you should consider yourself lucky if you find yourself in his class. Secondly, nepali is an extremely beautiful language, and Nepal is possibly the most fascinating place on earth.
VERY helpful, fun, knowledgeable.
Absolutely fantastic instructor.  This is a tough language and he makes it fun and interesting to learn.  Very supportive and helpful.  Strongly recommend.
Great man and a great teacher.  Agree with all that his vocabulary is above average and sometimes incomprehensible, but always helped when asked.  Very respectable
there is no difficulty in understanding him.  he teaches at an ivy league institution and expects people to have an ivy league vocabulary.  what's wrong with that??

He is a hard professor. While his projects cause students to lose sleep, he tries his best to help. Sadly, his intelligence gets in the way with his clarity. You won't understand how great the projects are until you're done with the course, but work hard and it will be recognized.
not recommended

i agree fully with the review below: very challenging, demanding, opens up creative doors. however, he has some serious personality flaws in his expectations and communication with students. be warned! the pseudo-professionalism is only a guise for a beast.
excellent. demanding and professional.  opens up the possibilities for creative exchange/exploration.

He talks a LOT and is very articulate. He can't stop talking and talking and talking. His three hour studio is basically a three hour lecture. and the thing is... I have no idea what he is talking about.
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments

This class was well-structured. I enjoyed the weekly reflections we did and it was a great way to interact with the course material and think about how it applies in our own daily lives. The exams are multiple choice, and as long as you study for them, they are very straightforward. Extra credit helped boost my grade as well. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of my favorite classes I have taken. Ong is a wonderful lecturer with extremely interesting lectures and truly cares about his students. Have to work for an A, but it is very much doable if you study and do the readings. Would recommend this class to everyone, It teaches you such valuable lessons about life and human behavior

AMAZING. The exams are fair but you have to study both lecture material and assigned readings. I love Professor Ong - I highly recommend. I have learned so much from this class it is crazy how relative and applicable material is to real life.

I took positive psychology 4 yrs ago. What I loved about Prof. Ong was that he never made me feel stupid when I had a question in class or when I went to his office hours....I recently graduated from med school and I am now an MD! Thank you Prof. Ong.

I've been waiting 2 yrs to take this class and looked forward to it after reading the comments. He is sometimes late and often has trouble working the audio visual system in the room. However, several of his lectures really hit home for me and made me reconsider my premed major. Take this class before you graduate!
He was a great professor, easy readings, the papers were good, very interesting class. You can get an A there are 3 prelims a final and 2 papers which are about urself, take the class its worth it
What you learn in this class is extremely relevant to life. Professor Ong actually "practices what he preaches" about positive psych-- rare find!
His voice is so soothing that he sometimes puts you to sleep (in a good way). He is a great professor. I would take this class again if I could.
I laughed, I cried, and I was inspired every Monday and Wed during Prof. Ong's lecture. He's truly one of kind! Take his class, you won't regret it!

I'm a psych major, and I've taken a couple of HD classes, and they're are a joke, but Prof. Ong's class was the most engaging and inspiring class I've taken in all of my four years at Cornell. And that voice...wow...he's the bomb.
Ong is chronically late due to coffee runs (a little annoying). That said, when he walks in to the room, you can hear a pin drop. He's THAT good!
I'm gaga over Prof. Ong. His lectures lift, inspire, and challenge you to be the change you want to see in world!!
I second the previous two reviews. Whatever you do, before you graduate from Cornell, you must take Prof. Ong's Positive Psychology class. And when you do, prepare to be dazzled!!
Professor Ong's Positive Psychology changed my life. He is simply brilliant!
I took Dr. Olson's online Sustainable Preservation series but that's not an option to select. She was great, very approachable, knowledgeable and provided substantive feedback.

Took the Sustain Preservation certificate series though eCornell and Katelin was so supportive and encouraging. I haven't been in the classroom for a long time, and she cheered me on and helped me work through my analysis of a passion project. Wish she taught more courses! Highly recommend
Fair and knowledgeable.

I recently took Katelin's Sustainable Preservation certificate series through eCornell and it was fantastic. She is so supportive and encouraging and the other people in the class were amazing to connect with through her online zoom weekly sessions. Wish she would offer another class so I could take that too!
Positive and enthusiastic; great class
Required course for first years in CRP. Provided a lot of information and was excited about the work. Helped me out of class improve my writing. Always available for an appointment.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took a very long time to grade. Lectures were not engaging or adaptive and she was a very strict grader on top of that. Gave contradictory advice for writing and tests were not as advertised. Worst prof I have worked with in the department as well. Not sure why Cornell admin assigned her this class as it's her first year and this is a req class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Worst Professor I have had by far in the CRP department. Grading was unfair, never returned in a timely manner, and harsh. Lectures were profusely dense with the containment of far too much information, as well as extremely fast-paced because she writes down a script of what to say. Exams and papers were difficult, lengthy, and lacked correlation.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are hasty and it feels like they rush through some parts while wasting time on unhelpful derivations one could find in the textbook. Prelims + final quite straightforward with non-strict rubric, but no practice exams provided which is annoying. Problem sets a bit lengthy, but not too bad. Would want better lectures, but not bad overall

The professor tries hard to help people understand the very complicated material and is a great person. However, the course material remains difficult to absorb, partly because the material itself is very dense. Problem sets take substantial time (go to TA office hours for help) and exams are fairly difficult. Median was a B+.

This professor is an awful lecturer and the classes are extremely monotone and hard to follow. There are no practice exams and they simply say to practice off problem sets and the textbook. Would not take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Not a very explicit teacher and the homework and exams didn't always cover and follow what was taught in lectures. The book is terribly structured and difficult to go through, which made learning the material more difficult than it should have been. Quite difficult for someone without previous exposure to game theory or a good fine math background.

Professor Rarytska is a very professional yet approachable professor. Lectures were a bit unclear since her handwriting was small and she didn't really seem to project her voice, but she was excellent in office hours - always willing to go concepts or past exams; however, was reluctant to give any guidance with problem sets at all. Very fair exams.

extremely caring professor who is very passionate about the topic. probably the 'easiest' professor for ILRGL 1100 because you don't really have to do the side readings, though you *should* read the main books that the essays are based on. sometimes went on tangents during lecture that were hard to follow, but overall choose ortiz for labor history

My least favorite class I have taken, awful class !!! Incredibly biased and one-sided view of history, if anything it's pseudo-history. Besides that, an awful workload, reading multiple books for each paper. 
He has the longest most leading essay prompts, basically telling you what view you can take. AWFUL DO NOT TAKE !!!

Definitely the "easier" professor for Labor History, class is clearly outlined, 4 essays each 25%, amazing TA and Professor is very accessible, passionate, and has insightful office hours. Honestly, don't need to keep up with class readings, just read the book the essay is based on and you should be good. Lectures can be boring but nice guy overall

This is the most difficult class that requires so much reading. the lectures are not very clear and his grading and the TA's is inconsistent. The essay prompt have so many parts and he has you read several books in a short period of time. This class requires 10x more time and effort than most classes this level
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He is the best professor at Cornell. He cares about his students and is very passionate. Heavy reading so it can be boring.

Professor Ortiz has an amazing depth of experience and is super knowledgeable about the class' subject. A genuinely nice man who cares about his students, but lectures varied in how helpful they were as he often tends to get off track. Assigned reading was a lot but grading on essays was generous. Definitely recommend taking this class with him.

Prof Ortiz was very knowledgable on his topic, sometimes his passion did overtake his lectures though and got boring real fast but overall very nice and empathetic human who is open for students to help and very understanding with grading. Loved this professor and class consisted of four take home papers, read four books throughout the semester
Smart Sexy Vampire.  I could listen to what he says anytime.  I really did learn things too.
Sexy vampire. Enough said.
If you want a C or lower grade, then take this class. If you didnt take any Macro related class before, then you would probably failed. This prof never teaches any meaningful things and has accent..
Amazing class and amazing lecturer
One of the most inspiring, funny, and passionate professors I've ever had! He made us read and watch a lot of material, but his insights were always very revealing and stimulating.

I took this class last semester and wasn't doing too well so i dropped it. I retook it with professor Oritz and i couldn't have been happier. The class is somewhat hard, but he has no control over it, the dept. does. He does however help out when he can. Hes so friendly, it was a pleasure to be in his class.
Too hard to get a good grade
Very helpful and engaging. Approachable and nice. Really gets you interested in the material. Love her!
Serious and professional

Great professor overall. You do need to do the readings and outline every week if you want to do well on the final as he is a tough grader. The lectures are amazing so make sure you come well prepared and caffeinated so you don't miss anything!

He is such an energetic and fun professor and does his best to make the subject memorable. Always prepared, really funny and very respectful. Whoever said he is always late for class, this is the third week of classes and he was never once late so I really don't get it.
Always late for class. Terrible organization.

Well, honestly, I am not sure whether it is because I am not doing well in the final exam or I ask too many tough questions, I didn't get a good grade even though I worked hard, finished all my readings, and doing several past exams. Some of my friends have the same situation so I am not alone. I wrote him twice asking Qs and received no response.
He's so yummy.
great teacher, easy grader in comparison to other spanish TAs
Great Professor.  Pretty generous grader. Fun class
A arch history teacher that will temper and refine your architectural knowledge from merely fashionable and abstract into reasoned and articulate.
dude knows his stuff. he's very approachable and is a nice guy to boot.
No Comments
No Comments

This class is the most favorite and inspirational class I've ever taken. Carl is so chill, and he is also a genius with his mindset and lectures. Working in this course healed me a lot, and it helped me go through the first tough and struggling semester. I highly recommend taking this class.
This is a horrendous class! Do not take it!
Worst person I have ever met. Likes to destroy young artist dreams and take his failure out on others.

Took an intro painting class due to my love for art despite the fact that I'm in a completely unrelated major. While he will give feedback and is usually clear, originality is not rewarded and you will not get a good grade if you deviate from his strictly defined personal preferences. Ironic that creativity isn't rewarded in an art class, esp intro

A quirky man, but an amazing teacher and a painter who's work is to be admired.  He will teach you so much if you listen, but he tends to favor work that is similar to his own, so stick to your guns and don't let him change your style.
If you care he cares. If you don't he doesn't. The smartest person I know.

Knowledgeable about art. Very inflexible about what work he thinks is good. He doesn't encourage experimentation at all, so if you have to take his classes stick to one thing and make sure to talk about how it relates to other artists. Originality is not rewarded.
Be prepared because he's a strange guy, but he will teach you about painting pretty well. When he's in a good mood, you'll love him. beware his bad days.

He sucks. No help, a complete jerk, and plays favorites. Also likes to tear down gifted artists for no apparent reason. Ruins paintings by painting over them. Loser. Cornell should fire him. Guy doesn't understand what constructive criticism means. His art sucks, too.

i think he was famous for two seconds in the 80s but blew it by being rude and nasty to mary boone, now his fellow yale grads (john currin) have eclipsed him and hes taking out all that anger by asking his students to treat him like hes single handedly responsible for reviving paitning. his grading is subjective, he plays favorites, waste of time.

pshh, i dont know what all these people are talking about!  carl is amazing! he can be difficult and scary at first- his methods are definitley... different, but you will learn to love him. he's very smart, and the more you talk with him, the more you're inspired.  ask him about his own artwork. his no nonsense attitude can sometimes be a facade.

Carl may not be the most hands-on professor, nor the clearest with his instruction (yes, he pretty much makes you figure things out for yourself), but he's incredibly entertaining even his insults amuse me ("god that looks like the bogman").  Most of his lectures can be summed up by sex, drugs, or life is ****.  Anyway, good fun.
good teacher

if you have a high tolerance for annoyance, curses, and ego, and if you don't mind early morning classes, this is okay. he's not always the most helpful person, he often just tells us to "Make it good." many times he will fingerpaint or squiggle over existing painting.
good teacher

For thesis: good grade for those who know their track. Terrible grade for those who were hoping to find their way. Make quick deciscions and stick to them, and also make sure they make A LOT of sense. It's tricky. He's helpful with technical questions, like where to buy things, what brush to use. Overall: Better than Buzz, worse than everyone else

i didn't think it possible for my deep love of painting to be squashed,but apparently mr. ostendarp is good at the impossible.  for example: he can make abstract art even more horrible than it already is.  he can claim that a pumpkin must be neon orange in order for you to pass.don't take his class!
if you can tolerate his ego he does a good job of making you think about painting differently, but after that task is accomplished he's not much help
No Comments
No Comments
One of the toughest, but best, teachers I have ever had.
you are a genius.

She's nice and the class is interesting, but her lectures are a bit dry and her power points aren't great. There were prelims that were memorization heavy and two essays that were graded generously, along with a completion paper that was easy. The discussion sections were interesting and I liked the discussion that was had.

Dr. Overby is by far one of the greatest professors at Cornell. She is incredibly educated and uses her knowledge to teach her students about the real world and values the importance of class discussions. She never cuts students off and makes everyone feel respected. 100/10 would recommend any of her classes.

Kim Overby has been my favorite professor at Cornell by far. Her lectures are interesting and applicable to anyone who is striving for a career in healthcare. As an MD and a clinical ethicist, she is incredibly knowledgable and frequently talks about real cases she encountered when she was practicing. Median grade for 2051 was an A in Fall 2019.
Probably the greatest person I ever met

Arthur Ovaska is one of the most thoughtful and dedicated design professors at Cornell. His enthusiasm for Architecture is contagious. Years later I can still hear his voice encouraging us to really LOOK at the world around us.
He's the greatest professor that ever lived.

He can sniff out chow-worthy Huevos Rancheros from 120 miles away. And if you are reading these reviews thinking you'll learn something about the profs, do the alumnus a favor and go enroll in another school. Cheers.
experienced, great listener, helfpful feedback, good studio professor overall.
Amazing professor. Best I've ever had.
He just sits there and scares students...
Very laid back and understanding. He was willing to work around our studio class and was very approachable.
Very easy going for drawing and allowed flexibility on work based on how much would be required for design. Easy to talk to and understanding. He made the class interesting.
No Comments

Very smart guy, but inconsistent--could be inspiring but seems distracted or remote some of the time, and other times is dead "on"...More of an artist than a teacher--not enough communication, you're not sure where you stand or what his stand is
So so. Talented but inconsistent prof. Doesn't communicate as well as he could. Creative ideas, but passive-agressive personality makes it hard to approach him

She has trouble with actually giving specific advice to people. When I was confused about a topic, all she did was send me word for word the assignment details again. Also, a lot of her examples just straight up don't follow the guidelines at all and make the assignments more confusing.
Great, best teacher in the department.
In Professor Owen's class, you get what you put in; her class requires a lot of work, but you do learn something.
Avoid if possible.

I will still take a class with Stephanie instead of Renée. Looking back I have been a very terrible mistake. Stephanie is not bad teacher, but if you are going to take her clasS, I advice you listen to every single one of the critiques. She hates it when you don't do what she tells you to do. So even if you think you did good and she doesn't (((

She's a bit disorganized and would be late to most classes, but she had warned us about that (the lateness) so it was expected. Overall, I thought it was a fun class. We didn't learn as much as I hoped, but it was a laid-back course. Just do your work and show your effort you'll be fine! You don't have to be an artist to get a good grade.

She requires a lot of work & reading, but you'll actually learn something. Don't get frustrated just because the assignments require work - She's nice and relatively patient, so you'll probably like her if you keep cool. Going into her class, I wasn't particularly fond of the subject matter & she knew it, but I worked hard & she recognized that.
She is in her own world and doesn't seem to care. Ms. Owens seems very insecure with herself and ability to teach students. I don't recommend taking any class with her.
pointless and unfocused discussions, seemed to have anger issues in general and also directed towards the students. if there was an actual topic, it was concealed from us.
Truly knowledgeable professor. Only place in the department you will learn to do something new, besides in intro printmaking.

Kadhim is an incredible instructor. As other reviewers have mentioned, he genuinely cares about his students and works hard to create a friendly classroom environment. His Arabic class was the best hour of my day, because he strongly encourages students to work together outside class. Also, he has a great sense of humor.

Kadhim is a really nice teacher and made every day pretty fun with his personality. Also, he encouraged a sense of friendship within the classroom which made it easier to study outside of class. He tries to warn for quizzes ahead of time too, which is helpful.
He is a superb teacher. I can't wait to take his next class. He is genuinely committed to helping his students both in and outside the class.

He is so nice to his students. Arabic is not easy though, and it is very easy to fall behind. You need to keep up on the daily-missing one or two days in a week will leave you struggling for the quizzes/exams. If you work hard, an A is achievable, but expect a B if you can't put in an hour/two a night. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great guy. He takes each of his students' success personally and shows up to class with a great attitude. If you're interested in Arabic Kadhim makes it accessible and fun.

Great guy who really wants to see all his students participate and do well. Professor Owayez fosters a supportive learning environment, which creates a tight-knit and capable class. Overall he's a genuine, caring, and awesome Arabic teacher.

I believe he visited my school(UC Riverside).Homework is online (Webwork) with unlimited tries. He is more than willing to stay after class or extend office hours to clarify anything. Very good professor
Probably one of the most spastic professors I've ever had. Since it's Calc, use the extra study sessions and the math dept. to your advantage to help you do well.

He's really nice and always willing to help. His lectures aren't really helpful and sometimes it actually makes the material more confusing. He tries very hard though. He doesn't grade the homework. There are graders that do this and usually homework is annoying and tedious, but it's manageable.

One of the harder PAM classes. She's actually nicer than she seems during lecture. What she says during class in terms of current policy reforms, data, etc. are very accurate. Doesn't conform to one political ideology. Maybe sounds like a libertarian but maybe that's because the course is focused on utilitarianism, efficiency, opp. to paternalism

Prelim means are always D- or lower (probably b/c they are graded solely by undergrad TA's and not examined by Owens), but the course has an official A median grade the past 2 semesters. Good old Ivy League inflation! Very unclear course content, misguided study materials, and ambiguous exams questions. Both Prof and TA's shockingly unhelpful.
Great class. Super interesting.  Easy as long as you put in the time.  I would highly recommend it

She is definitely a MASTER at this topic. Decent amount of work. Tests are mostly long answer, fair and straight-forward. U work in groups EVERY SINGLE DAY (You finish Questions together). Take if you like criminal studies, don't if you don't though not a class to just take for the PAM credits b/c material is way 2 small of a niche 2 "try to enjoy"

Whoever commented on her last was right- she seems PO'd, like she's being forced to teach this?? or something?? IDK, but Take it with Evans, even if he's boring he's super helpful. Her HWs take SO long.. every week. By amt. of work this should be a 400 level class.

I think she's a pretty good lecturer, but it seemed like she didn't really enjoy teaching us? Maybe bc most of the class zoned out since it's a core/mandatory PAM class. Our TA was SUPER HELPFUL & helped us with hw/tests a LOT. Prof may seem unapproachable but if you have specific questions she's willing to answer them@ office hrs. Tests are curved

Really disappointing class. Topics and class description seem so interesting, but in the end the entire class is just about crime and isn't very interesting.  The first assignment will literally make you want to blow your brains out it's so tedious. OK lecturer, but going to lecture is VERY optional. Not recommended at all.
No Comments
Awful. Test and homework questions ONLY about crime, even though there are so many other statistical topics.  Most boring teacher.  Couldn't get anything out of lecture.
Prof Owens really knows her stuff and the subject matter of this class is fascinating.  I highly recommend this class
SO SO SO amazing. Would recommend this class to anyone interested in painting.

Prof. Park's classes are not that difficult whatsoever. It's what you make of it. Her critiques of my works were always helpful and insightful, though she can be quite theoretical in her wording. She also isn't a tough grader at all... Needless to say, if your work is clearly lacking effort or if you don't participate, you get the grade you deserve
Maria is as caring and experienced as Stan Taft, and provides significantly more usable feedback. Her grading is lenient and she provides more materials than any other teacher I've had in AAP.

Interesting projects but very time consuming. Participation in critiques is crucial in receiving a good grade. Maria is always there for her students and gives lots and lots of constructive feedbacks. She does give out readings that can be somewhat confusing/complex in concept.

Shocked the ratings are so bad I think he's the best professor I've had . Made me want to major in stats after hating ap stats, super nice guy , always willing to help and put in extra time for you to succeed , tests are exactly like the practice ones and test the content in the presentations and nothing more. very nice guy, makes the lectures fun

The in class notes were a bit hard to digest but he gives what you need to review before the exams which makes it much better. The material itself isn't hard but you will have to engage with it. Overall, he's a really nice person and shows up to lecture with a smile!

He does not know how to teach, but it is easy to teach yourself if you just read over the lecture notes on your own. The coding part is easy so don't be intimidated by that, you can put everything on a cheat sheet for the prelims and final. HW is graded on accuracy and attendance is tracked by worksheets you hand in

Content for the class is straightforward, and tests are similar to the material from review/practice tests.
The workload during the semester is not too bad.
Lectures are hard to follow because he writes at a fast pace on paper and concepts are often not explained in an accessible way. TAs mostly ignore Ed discussion so it can be hard to get help.

If you show up, pay attention and try you'll be fine. The class isn't bad at all. He's understanding and always willing to work with you. I'm not good at math, and he took the time to help me break things down in a way I could understand. He's a great professor, and more students should take his class instead of being scared off by what they hear.

It was really hard to focus on what he was talking about and he went over content so fast...Did not explain a lot of concept well so need to self learn.? But overall he is a nice person and tries to give students good grading. The curve was nice. Wouldn't take it again.

Nice guy who wants you to succeed, but makes that incredibly hard. He moves very fast and explains nothing. Median on the two prelims: 62% and 74%. The curve makes it doable to get a decent grade, but raw scores so low really speak to his poor lectures.

The one-two punch of him and Enter teaching ILR stats makes the entire department questionable.

Lectures are very clear but also quite boring and rarely applied. Lecture attendance is VERY important--his follow along notes often contain word-for-word exam answers. Exams are fair--if you do the homework/practice test and make sure everything in the review sheet is on your cheat sheet, you'll be fine. He's a nice guy who wants you to do well.
very very bad
Best prof! Legit cares abt the students as long as you make the effort. His office hours were fun and helpful! And he is funny during lecture. Idk why he gets sm hate

ILRies steer away from this class. You need much more math background than Calc 1 to feel comfortable with the material. Packard wastes so much class time doing practice problems, and then rushes through the rest of the material. Curve is very good however, I would not have passed if it were not for that.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Listening to a lecture is just a string of jokes and half-explanations of actual material. Less comedy, more teaching

Lectures are overcomplicated making content way harder than it should be. TA's are undergrads that are also lost. For this class get ready to fend for yourself and use a useless software that makes the class all the more annoying. I enjoyed statistics before this class and now I just don't.

I want to preface this by saying that he is extremely nice and tries to make himself available to students. However, he makes simple concepts seem very complicated, which confuses everyone. I spent more time studying for this class than for my technically more difficult classes. I did not find this class particularly interesting.

Prof Packard is definitely underrated. He is a very nice and supportive person. While this class isn't an easy A, staying on top of homework, actively engaging in class, and making good use of his office hours (incredibly helpful) will set you up for success. However, he does not provide annotated class note, so attendance is truly important.

The class was tough for an infosci major with no stats background. I bombed the first two exams but ended with a B- after grinding 16-hour study days. The forgiving grading scale helped, but take psych stats instead. Office hours were helpful, and packard is fine one-on-one.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Between the quizzes that are based on readings that test niche details, the lecture notes that aren't posted, and the exams that aren't reflective of homeworks quizzes or readings, avoid him at all costs. As other people have said, it feels like he is intentionally out to get you. As a mechanical engineer, this class is bringing down my gpa…

Like what other comments said, the professor tends to ramble during lectures, and then the tests end up focusing on things that don't feel like the main point of the course. There are no review sessions or after-class notes, so it's hard to keep up or know what to focus on.

exams were not reflective of past prelims or homeworks. literally cannot understand what is going on every single class as he speaks so fast and rambles. need to spend lots of time understanding material outside of class.

No review sessions, learning content the week of the test, material that has been mentioned briefly being tested, this class has it all. Although I enjoy the content of the course, it took a lot of effort and studying in order to make sense of what was going on during lectures and overall not a good experience in general.
Just took the final. Im so cooked. Bro puts stuff on the test that he mentioned for one nanosecond in class. Super advanced math knowledge required, way more than Calc 1 as the course reccomends.

Worst professor ever at Cornell, do not take unless you want to be confused the entire time. Failling grades throughout the whole semester, everyone was lost. Would go to office hours and he would continuously state "this class is supposed to be hard" don't expect things to be easy. Attendance was randomly taken at different points, not fair.

This man is utterly awful. The class average for the prelim was a 58% and has been for years. I talked to my friends last year, their class average was in the low 50s. Instead of changing his exams, teaching methodology, or grading - Packard allows students to continuously struggle and fend for themselves. Take a diff ILR stats path & save your GPA
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Without a doubt the worse professor for econ stats. This guy is literally out to get you. Doesn't post lecture notes, overcomplicates simple concepts. Exams are way harder than homeworks and completely different from the practice exam. Overall, if you're an econ major, try to take 3110 with Diccicio! Don't make the same mistake as me.

Very nice guy, probably acoustic. hosted 0 review sessions, tests nothing like hw no way to practice. TA is useless/ notunderstandable. Unless you are a math/quantitative leaning Econ/Math/Stats/Eng major, you will slog in this class, and even then it will be a struggle. U need well above average math intuition to comfotably get A-/A
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Packard is the worst professor I have had at Cornell. He overcomplicates content to the extreme. He did not have a single review session all semester before the prelim or final (despite promising one). Exam content is not at all similar to homework or class material. The median on the final was a 58% for context. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a very nice teacher and is also understanding during office hours. However, this class is beyond impossible. The material is way too much, goes too fast, and nothing makes sense. I got lost after a month into the class. Packard should not be teaching undergraduate students and instead teach PhD students. Not sure what the curve will look like

Professor Packard deserves the praise for being caring and accessible in and out of class. His class is definitely NOT the easy A type of class, but if you do want to get a solid foundation of stats, this is the one with biweekly quizzes+weekly homework+2 exams (you get cheat sheet tho). Attend discussions cuz those are super useful.

Professor Packard is not a nice person and is generally a very bad lecturer. He expects you to memorize everything he said in lecture, even if it was just briefly mentioned in passing, and is very passive aggressive to students for no reason. His lecturing style is also not great to follow, so usually the textbook is more helpful.

While I did well on the midterm, it was because of the textbook rather than the lectures. I'm oftentimes lost in the lectures. He is a nice person, but his lectures are overcomplicated. Lack of annotated lecture notes is also painful for people without iPad to annotate on a pdf of unannotated notes. Quizzes are definition-heavy. Read the textbook.

Professor Packard is genuinely underrated. He is a really nice and inspirational teacher. While I have to say he makes the class difficult, but it does push students to understand the materials better. I would definitely recommend taking it.
