reviews.comment: She can be a bit arrogant and tends to silence voices that aren't in line with her own thought process. Forget about any form of discussion in class. A lot of work is busy work without any substance. I'd recommend you take this class with another teacher.

Favorite class I've taken so far. Discussions were really lively and interesting and Prof Pritchard definitely knew how to keep things moving without controlling the conversations too much. Readings were sometimes long but the discussions made them worth it. I'd recommend this class for sure!
Amazing, interesting class. She is a great professor for small seminars. She is sweet, fun, funny, and interesting. I highly reccommend taking her gender and technology seminar!
Grades too hard for such a BS class!

Math 1910 was tough for me honestly. Carl was a great professor however do not rely on the lectures. I made that mistake and realized to really undertand this course read the textbook along w attending lectures. Class is not impossible but exams were not easy. If you can do textbook problems you should be fine but you need a good understanding.

Took his ECE2100 years ago and it was good. Lectures were really clear and Carl cared about his students. I agree that he literally taught the book from word to word so you can skip all the classes and still get a good grade by reading books yourself, but overall a good class - reasonable grading, clear materials, and nice professor

He literally JUST taught the book word for word and exact problem for problem. I never felt like he provided extra insight. I knew many people that never went to lectures because they could read the textbook and learn the same. His only OH was zoom, which was unfortunate because he could've been helpful but nobody learns on zoom.

The professor's averages on prelims and the final were extremely concerning because of how low they were - between the 20-32 percent range. I will admit the exams were not impossible but almost no partial credit was ever given. The professor often seemed to express concerns within the class performance being the student's faults and not his own.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great and easy to follow lectures, to succeed dont just rely on the lectures but know how to do the examples and homework problems if they were a bit more challenging.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: 2100 with Poitras was good. Overall a very caring professor who is accessible and responsive. The class content was difficult but aided by clear lectures. Had Wednesday deadlines for HW which are pretty pressing at times but manageable. Prelims were very scattered in difficulty, it's his first time teaching 2100 so he is still getting his footing.

Carl was my professor for MATH1910. He is really nice, and from what I heard was the best lecturer for this course. He teaches strictly from the textbook so I would recommend going through the example problems for each chapter before the exams(this really helped me). He cares for the students and tries to make sure everyone understands the material

Carl himself is an amazing professor, however, he didn't get much say on the exams since he's not the head of math 1910, it was Yuri Berest, and let me tell you, Yuri Berest is evil. The exams were unfair, but they weren't Poitras' fault at all, Poitras is sweet, genuine, caring, puts himself out there for office hours. Definitely take Poitras.

Poitras is an extremely competent lecture/teacher. The class was tough for me because of my skill level in the subject but I truly enjoyed attending his lectures. The material taught was conceptually stimulating and enjoyable to attempt to master. I would definitely take one of his courses again.

Best 1910 lecturer this year. I switched into his class after attending a few of his lectures. He truly cares about his students and portrays the information in a learnable way. He is the type of teacher that wants all his students to be successful and is by far the best STEM teacher I have had at Cornell. Definitely focus on textbook practice.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Carl is a really great professor and definitely the best lecturer for 1910. He gives it to you straight and doesn't have unreasonable exam expectations (even if he's not the one writing it). He is a very compassionate guy and will take the time to answer questions in class or have extra office hours if necessary. Take his class!!

Carl is a great professor. It is clear he cares about the students in his class as he makes sure everyone understands a given concept before he moves on. He jokes around a lot and uses real life comparisons to keep the class engaged. Would take again 100%

Carl is the best! He gives very clear lectures that are easy to follow. He cares for his students and even gives us hints about certain topics that may show up on the prelim. He is an approachable man that is willing to answer questions in class and during office hours.
Carl genuinely cares for his students. Before prelim 2, he hosted extra office hours 3 days in a row. He was the only professor that added extra office hours. Lectures are clear and easy to follow.
Carl is awesome. He genuinely cares about his students and is just a very good-hearted professor with a lot of compassion. He's an amazing lecturer and the best.
Just a great class. This one was online and I was afraid to see what would happen. Just awesome.

I started 3400 this spring not sure what to expect given its history. Professor Poitras was just amazing teaching it, the labs were fun yet not straightforward, and the course was at the perfect level. I worked with microcontrollers before, I still learned a lot from the class. Teach more classes Prof. Poitras! Thank you ECE!

I took MAT 2930 with Professor Poitras and I was so happy that he was teaching this course. Math was never easy for me and he made the material easy to get and actually fun! Great great lectures, he understands the students point of view, answers questions clearly. Thank you!!!

I am taking MAT1910 this semester, online. It's a large class and we have many sections taught by different professors. Prof. Poitras' lecture is by far the best, clear, fun, makes me love math and i didn't really before. Thank you. Teach more classes Prof. Poitras!

Poitras is by far the best professor for 1910. He clearly is very passionate about teaching and explains difficult concepts very simply. Many CoE students in lectures with other professors have started watching Poitras instead. He is clear and concise, while still explaining everything fully. He is kind and caring, as well as very engaging.

I really struggle with calc but Carl is amazing at explaining things, he's always in a good mood, he's always down to help and answer questions. Even the CoE students who aren't in his class watch his lectures. We changed the GroupMe name to Carl Appreciation GC. If you have to take 1910, take it with him!
Awesome awesome awesome. Teach more classes Prof. Poitras! Get to his lecture even if it messes up your schedule.

What a good professor. Cornell needs more instructors like Prof. Poitras. Clear, fun, really talented instructor. The material isn't easy but you leave every lecture having understood the material so well that it makes reviewing my notes and doing the problems a breeze (with some work... lol). Thank you Prof. Poitras! Teach more classes!
Not caring. Did not bother to help us with the labs.

He seems like a nice guy, but he was a terrible professor for this class. He cancelled lectures 5 minutes before they were supposed to happen multiple times, the lecture material he presented had almost no relevance to the project we were working on, and he never seemed to know what was going on

Not the first class I have with Professor Poitras. Cornell needs more like him. He knows his stuff, is available, actually cares about his students. The course is a little heavy, we covered a lot of material, but thats why Im at Cornell. The material is current, the final project great.

Carl is a super nice dude, great lecturer and cares about his students. Go to his office hours as much as possible because they are incredibly helpful!! I wouldn't have passed this course without Carl

As a freshman, I was intimidated joining Cornell. Prof. Poitras is an awesome lecturer: clear classes, easy to follow, inspirational. His office hours are also super helpful and he makes himself available outside office hours too. Compared to my other classes, Cornell professors need to follow his example!
Great professor with good lectures. Very clear and easy to understnand

I really suffered in this class. It was a hard class with too much material and too little class time. His lectures were unclear, the textbook was expensive and little used, but the exam material was more of his own stuff. He was misleading about exam material. Although he took pity gradewise, I really hated this class and it caused immense stress
The course content is very poorly presented. Furthermore, the exams and homework are heavily based on number crunching into long formulas, which do not test for understanding.

Carl is incredible and hillarious! He makes difficult concepts understandable. Reading the textbook sections after lecture will help make everything click even more. Prelims are challenging but manageable. He cares immensely about each person and his office hours are so helpful. The class is not an easy A but if you work hard, you can do very well.

Professor Poitras is great. This was my first semester in ECE at Cornell and with that comes a lot of insecurity and nervousness. He is an awesome teacher, cares about us and our success. He masters this math class and has an amazing ability to make us learn the material which can be hard at times. Thank you thank you!

Carl is a fantastic professor with tons of experience in the subject matter and gives excellent lectures. He made me understand what was tougher easily. I love him. Cornell needs more profs like him. He is very approachable and takes the time to answer my questions. Love him.
One of the top very best in ECE. Why can't other professors teach like that??? He's clear, patient, funny, engaging, totally masters the material. I want to study this field! Thanks Carl!!!
Organizes the class well and always does his best of letting the students know of a myriad of deadlines. Put effort into this class and you will do well, but make sure not to slack.
I love this class. The project is awesome, Prof. Poitras does a great job motivating us and explaining concepts. I want him in other classes!

This is it my first class with Poitras and I hope it won't be the last. He's got great energy, knows his stuff, patient, motivating, funny. He cares when something personal happens (as it did to me), unlike many other profs. Awesome.
Prof. Poitras is motivating and dedicated to have you learn and succeed. We work hard but the class is great.

I have had Dr. Poitras for several classes at Cornell, and would take more of them with him. He is extremely well versed and well learned in many fields. ECE 3400 was fun, interesting and also complex (in the sense that we see and learn many things). He is patient, makes time for you when you need it.
Carl Is a great professor. He is very lenient with grading. He is always there for the students

Carl is the man. He is probably one of the most lenient and helpful professors I have ever had. He'll even help you out with your work in other ECE classes if you ask. His assignments can be kind of vague until you go to him in person.

Difficult class, although the expected student product is well advertised. Open book exam, but this only slows you down. Lab quizzes are a nuisance. Very helpful in office hours, and make sure you do the "challenge" problem for the hw if you want to be in his good graces.

Overall, I would say 3260 was my favorite MAE course so far. I went in expecting ridiculous homework, but it seems like Psiaki read the comments here and made his homework more manageable. The only things I didn't like was how much lab manual reading I had to do and the fact that prelim 2 was the disaster it was, with its bimodal distribution.

Lectures were well organized and clear, with good examples. Lots of material covered. High standards for the class's learning. Sometimes a bit dry presentation. ~5 hrs. of homework/week, of higher difficulty. Challenges for ex.C. Exams were also of higher difficulty, especially the final. ~4 hrs. of out-of-lab reading & write-up per each of 7 labs.

He knows his stuff and presents material well in class, but he is not an understanding or particularly helpful individual outside of lecture. I found him to be borderline demeaning at times. I also found it really intimidating how he picked students to answer questions in lecture and then had the class vote whether the person answered correctly.

Mark Psiaki knows his stuff incredibly well, is very well-prepared for all of his lectures, and has a very high set of expectations for students. Homeworks are extremely time-consuming and difficult for a group, nigh impossible to do alone. Find a good group and work with them on everything. You'll need it.

Psiaki is good at teaching and really knows his stuff. Class was hard and a lot of work. Like someone already said, problem sets at the end of the semester take 20+ hours, no joke. Homeworks should so count for more of your grade. Final exam was ridiculous; I thought I had A- going in but ended up with a B+ *tear*.

Professor Psiaki gives very clear explanations, but has laughably no sense of how long homework should take or any sympathy towards his students.  The first problem sets took ~3 hours, the last few more than 20.  He told the class he would curve it, but did not despite a 64% mean on the final.  He is not there to teach, and he is not your friend.

Super charismatic guy, but I wouldn't take another one of his classes. He sets students up to fail with no lecture notes, no real textbook, and a vague outline of topics. His handwriting makes it hard to follow in class, and with no notes to reference, studying for his unfair tests is nearly impossible. He also subtracts points for wrong answers.

Engaging class for those interested in drug formulation or delivery. Dr. Putnam has extensive academic and industry experience, made the material relatable. Lectures weren't mandatory but key for exams, which were straightforward. No homework, but “Literature Discussions” required participation. Class curved to ~B/B+.

Dr. Putnam's class was tough but also my favorite. The literature discussions were the low point of the class, but he's not out to humiliate anyone by calling on them. My best advice would be to study hard for the exams and put in the work to write the term paper at the end of the semester, and you'll learn a ton!
He's a good professor.

Professor Pulsoni's emphasis on participation may shy people away from the class, but he is definitely an amazing instructor and ensures that you understand the material to the fullest capacity. He always establishes that if any extra help is desired, he is available whenever we need it. He's also a funny guy and will treat you like an equal.
Pulsoni was a very engaging teacher, making sure students learned through participation. Class was always fun and interactive. Would definitely take again.

He teaches in a very unorthodox way - doesn't really follow lesson plans, but he cares about your learning. Will grade leniently if you put in the effort. Very funny, very sarcastic (in a good way), and helpful. I enjoyed learning Italian from him very much and had a great time in class.

Professor Pulsoni really cares about teaching his students Italian. He encourages students to have conversations with each other and wants them to speak as a true Italian would. He fosters an environment where it's ok to make mistakes without being ridiculed.

Clearly a knowledgeable prof who constantly pointed out various interesting themes in the readings, which were truly fascinating. You knew that he was truly reading our assignments closely as he gave detailed comments on all our answers. On the minus side, no clear grading system was provided, and his thick accent is sometimes hard to understand.

Initiation to Greek Culture is one of the best humanities classes at Cornell. Prof. Pucci is beyond wise and will make your mind literally stretch over the couse of his class. You are going to have to be extremely dedicated to the subject matter, but Prof. Pucci is very accessible and willing to talk. Get ready for a crash course in Derrida as well

Professor Pucci is an outstanding scholar, and it is a privilege take a class with him.  He has the most brilliant ideas about Greek Drama, and life in general, both of which he expresses in some of the most beautifully spoken prose one can hear.  His class was one of the high points of my undergraduate career at Cornell.

Extremely knowledgeable about everything. This class is an enormous amount of reading and writing, but he provides helpful feedback and is very welcoming in office hours. He is a generous grader, especially if he likes you. I have learned SO much in this class.

Obviously an eminent scholar, making it hard to say anything in class that won't be shot down with specific quotations from dozens of texts. Very nice man, but thick accent and boring, useless subject matter. No one speaks in class, and the syllabus very unclear.

Pucci is very knowledgeable but didn't communicate any sense of excitement for the texts. He'll put you to sleep. For the final presentation he told us we would all be "professors for the day," but he rudely interrupted my group and mocked what we were saying. Very wise, but dry, boring, and highly biased.

Under Professor Pucci’s tutelage, the familiar text will gain new fascinating depths and colors. Take professor Pucci’s class if you want to understand what “close reading” truly means and how revealing it can be. If you prepare for class work and follow discussion closely, tests will be very easy.

there was no course outline, so we didn't know when we would be tested, or how much the tests were worth (& never found out). We were tested anyway, with barely any notification and no idea about criteria. Expectations were high and the class uninspiring.
So smart...it's kind of humbling...
Not interesting, not fun, and highly biased grading.
No Comments

Qi Li is the goat! There are quite a few homeworks but they are reasonable in length and are done in groups. Exams were fair and she would always provide a comprehensive review beforehand. Qi Li cares a lot about her students and her office hours were always helpful.

The material is challenging but it is clear that she really cares and wants to help you understand the material. The problem sets can be difficult but she is super helpful if you go to her office hours and the tests were very fair.

She is a great lecturer and cares about the class content. You will however have a lot of homework each week, but her office hours are a great resource. Pay attention to her review lecture before prelims because she tells you exactly what kind of questions are on the exam. Labs are pretty easy and not technical at all but they are outside of class.

This was Professor Li's first time teaching 3310, so it was a bit scattered at times but you can tell she really cared. I think this course will get better as she teaches it more. Lectures are a bit dry, but it's easy to do well. Homeworks could be a bit long, but prelims/assessments are very reasonable.

Obviously biochem is going to be hard, no matter who teaches it. I thought Prof. Qian did a good job of presenting the material in as accessible of a way as possible. He was also really kind and somehow kind of funny. I appreciated him even more compared to next professor who switched in halfway through the semester.

He is a demanding professor and covers a lot of very important content. That being said he does move fast and it is hard to keep up at certain times in the semester. I spent about 10-15 hours a week fully digesting the material and it was a course I will remember because it reminded me why I love biology. Would take it again in an instant.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Honestly, I felt like he went pretty fast through the slides during lectures, and he wasn't very helpful during office hours. Make sure you go to class because he will test you on things he says, but are not explicitly in the slides. He did throw in a few jokes though. Not the most understanding prof. The TAs will be your best friend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He throws a lot of information at you at once so be ready to record his lectures. He also is hard to understand sometimes. The test questions are based on minor details so when you study make sure to throughly look through your notes.

Professor Qian is one of the worst professors I've had. Hard to understand lectures. Prelims are ridiculous true/false questions that don't test actual understanding of material. Very rude! Makes fun of questions in lecture. Doesn't accommodate students needs. But! It's easier than the other biochem classes and is more pre-med/vet focused.
Good professor in general! But the material covered is more like cell biology and I am a bit disappointed by that... Would love to see more chemistry.

Professor Qian definitely challenges you. If you want to do above average in his class you need to put in the work for it, but he's extremely helpful if you utilize his office hours. He wants to see you succeed and definitely believes in you.

Took NS 3200 in Fall 14.  Did not like this class and would not recommend. Professor Qian taught 34 of the class and he was not very clear due to his accent.  Also, by cramming it all into one semester, you do not go very much in depth. Fell more like a Cell bio than biochemistry. Easier than 3310 but I would recommend  3310-3320 to learn the most

Avoid if possible. He is not easy to understand and his lectures are so lackluster.  Even though I found the material interesting, I only understood the slides by studying them on my own... basically, Khan Academy was my best friend taking this class.  He is terrible at answering questions.  His exams are manageable, but nonetheless difficult.
He's very fair and organized. As long as you follow the class materials, it is not difficult to do well. All about effort.
Really nice professor. Make sure to do the homeworks and you'll be ready for the exams.  Class is not super easy, but he is very fair and his tests are based on material he covers in class.
Really nice guy but lectures (and exams) are very difficult to understand.
Great prof with a quirky sense of humor.  The concepts are well explained and he actually makes finance classes relatively entertaining!
No Comments
good guy, decent class.  exams are hard
No Comments
Best class ever at Cornell. Too bad he is leaving Cornell for Michigan. It's a big loss for Cornell.
Can't understand anything he says. Unhelpful, stern, and not very knowledgable.
Great professor and lectures so far.  Look forward to a great semester.

Professor Qi is extremely enthusiastic! The lecture material was dense, but he made it very enjoyable. He is very concerned with the student's ability to learn. A great integration of all the science courses at Cornell. Just respond to the previous comment where he/she made several factual mistakes on the iClicker and graphs. Prof English is great!

iclicker, purposefully puts a lot of ?s on days students like to miss (fri before sp break), speaks very poor english yet expects you to spell terms not in his ppt on tests, doesnt always teach the slides, just says "highlight this! you need to know this! memorize this!" and you are stuck with a long msrble pathway full of abbrev you don't undrstnd

The professor, Dr. Qi, is very funny and genuinely seems like he wants us to succeed.  I LOVE most of the material that was covered and I can see it being very useful in medical school.  As someone who is doing well in the class so far, I really felt that the amount of time I put in reflected in my grade; thus, was very rewarding in this respect.
The most helpful and cheerful instructor I've ever had! The class is well organized and the information is really interesting and relevant to real life.
Not easy. But the professor and TAs are very willing to help. One of the best classes HUMEC offers!
best teacher i have had at cornell. really cares.

He is the best professor I have ever had at Cornell.  Overall the class was a great class with lifestyle implications, the content of the lectures and the topics of the discussions were interesting, although there were a lot of information. The professor is clearly very passionate about the subject.  I really enjoyed the class and learned a lot.

One of the best professors I have had at Cornell. Not sure if he just changed everything about his teaching style and personality since last year, but he made a lot of sense, the audio recorded lectures were very helpful, he was hilarious, and he genuinely tried to have us learn the material. It was a difficult amount of info but he taught it well.

Thick accent. Not very clear teaching or organized. He works hard to take suggestions for improvement but he is still not even up to par with other mediocre profs. If you ask him a question, he tells you to look it up. Quizzes/Tests pretty difficult. Nice guy but needs a lot of work to be a decent teacher.
As if this man needed an accent to be unclear...Cornell should give up trying to look like they  care about teaching if this joker gets tenured. Far and away the WORST PROFESSOR AT CORNELL
Dr. Quirk ignores email purposefully(one of her teaching assistants told me), often makes disrespectful comments about students and other animal science staff + professors, and rambles during class

The course itself was not as bad. But I personally had a lot of medical issues throughout the semester and she was not very accommodating. It was difficult to for me since she was not very understanding of my issues. She seems like a nice lady but not a great professor

Dr Quirk is one of my favorite professors within the animal science department. If you take the time to get to know her she is truly an amazing person who cares about her students. She truly appreciates students who attend lecture and consistently ask questions within lecture.
I think while she means well, her lectures are quite disorganized and difficult to follow and the grading is extremely haphazardly done. I like the subject she is teaching but not her style.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Super boring lecturer, moderately difficult class, her grading is inconsistent. You'll do fine if you study and try hard but I wouldn't take a class with her again.

He is one of the best professor in Cornell! I enjoyed his class! Very organized, very interesting, and he is simply just a great guy! I would highly recommend taking his class :) He is very very helpful outside of class so ask for help if you need it! He will definitely more than happy to help you!

Sweet Milanese with a great accent!  His lectures are clear, though some complicated names are lost in his muddled English.  Occasional funny jokes.  Interesting and complex material that he outlines in class thoroughly and clearly, and in his handouts.  Textbook is rarely required.  Tests are straightforward.  Overall, and awesome professor!

This guy is great! His knowledge of the field is ridiculously impressive; he took many of the electron microscopy shots used in lecture himself, and can easily talk through complex processes without the use of notes or anything. Complex subject matter, but if you pay attention in class and try to learn, you can do fine. He's a boss.

Quaroni is great-- fantastic accent, brain so stuffed full of knowledge you'll be wowed on a class by class basis.  Go to lecture; he tells you most of what you need to know.  If you take detailed notes it's no problem.  Tests are straightforward and sometimes even contain cutesie jokes.
Way too much highly detailed and disorganized information gets thrown into these lectures. I had no idea what I was supposed to know for exams or how to study for this course.
There is too much information presented in this course without enough cohesiveness. I was never sure of the big picture or what I was responsible to know.
No Comments
Best and funniest prof at Cornell. Milan soccer holla
No Comments
amazing lectures.

Challenging but fair and practically useful class if you attend the lectures and actively engage with the material. Exams were easy in terms of the questions but difficult if you're unclear on any of the concepts (which is why you should attend the lectures and ask questions). Very clear slides and delivery. The TA team was awesome and available.
Exams were incredibly unfair and not reflective of the minimal content taught. Unresponsive and overall apathetic. Grades were weirdly curved down.
tests do not reflect what was taught, grading is harsh

I took her networks course in Spring 2023, the became a teaching assistant for her in Spring 2024.
She is a very inspirational person who is extraordinarily compassionate and knowledgeable in her field. I highly recommend her class and to visit her office to speak with her on class material!
Good Prof with interesting projects. Occasional class quizzes.

I feel spoiled because I dont think any other FWS can parallel this one. Truly a highlight of my day. Ryan was so cool, so iconic, and so funny that work didn't even feel like work. The content was so interesting and Ryan's passion was infectious. Loved every second and wouldn't recommend any other FWS over this one!! She's the best!

My favorite class at Cornell so far. Lectures were very engaging and just a ton of fun. Essay prompts were enjoyable and the research process was straightforward. Ryan is understanding and clearly cares for her students very much. Just show up and try your best, and your efforts will be recognized.

Ryan is so iconic and she genuinely makes her class my favorite part of the day. The essay prompts were enjoyable to write about and they were not very strenuous. The readings were also interesting and were not too long. Attendance is mandatory but the class discussions were always fun so overall I would 100% take a class with her.

Ryan is an absolute icon, and I am incredibly upset that the semester is almost over because I can't imagine how another freshman writing seminar could top this one. Ryan is passionate about the subject matter to the point where she could go on tangents for hours, and genuinely wants all of her students to succeed. This class is so fun. Take it!!

Excellent and lovely professor. I took the Asian-American Food Writing and loved it! A great way to talk about the challenges Asian Americans face and the cultures enjoyed through food. She is very understanding and receptive to the mental health of her students. The grading is effort-based (not based on capabilities), too!  Would recommend!

Alice is an awesome professor. She is very caring, kind, and understandable. Because her class is seminar/discussion like, it helps to be an active participant in the class. Helps everyone make class enjoyable. She offers feedback and is helpful to students. Professor Alice is also lenient on extensions

Alice is very nice and respectful towards her students. She explains very well and gives time to students to respond. The readings were very intriguing and were relatively straightforward. She gives very good feedback on both essays and participation. If you put effort, your grade will speak for yourself.

Alice is very nice and caring about her students. Throughout the semester, she extended deadlines numerous times to accommodate our hectic schedules. The readings were relatively light and the essays were very open-ended. 5/5 prof.
Alice is super nice and friendly, the readings for the class werent hard and shes really flexible.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof. Rickard is an amazing professor. He puts in a genuine effort to remember students and take their feedback. His lectures are great and interactive and his exams are pretty straightforward if you pay attention in lecture and do the homework. The quizzes at the end of each lecture have TAs helping you so most students easily get full credit.

Prof Rickard is very passionate about subject matter and always very engaging lectures. Somehow knows everyone's name by end of first week and encourages active participation. Omits certain slides and info from lectures posted online so attendance is mandatory to do well on exams (as well as daily pop quizzes). Lengthy homeworks once a month.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Pretty friendly prof to talk to and chill during lectures. Attendance technically not mandatory but quizzes can only be done if you attend. Quizzes are open note so you can discuss with peers. Homework isn't too difficult, and office hours are helpful. The long answer questions in the HW are a bit time consuming but are graded pretty leniently.

This man shouldn't be allowed to be teaching. He doesn't do research ahead of class and relays false information in class about various topics. He is a terrible lecturer. He gives pop quizzes at the end of class about materials that he has just taught that are worth 10 points. Then gives us these very difficult homeworks that are worth 2 points.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: TAs make or break this class. Content is very dry. Professor does a lot of examples during class which are worth doing in the long run, as they give you extra practice. They are also what is tested. Recommend learning LaTeX notation for this class. Assignments were a pain and not helpful usually, but ZyBook HW was. Final was ridiculously long.

Lectures were dry and heavy on theoretical information. Recitations were somewhat helpful but the many assignments were extremely difficult and required asking questions or stumbling through searching for specific coding functions. The class felt like it was preparing students for a PhD rather than just a masters level course. High expecations.

Daziano is a good lecturer, but outside of lecture the course was really disorganized. The recitations felt useless, and the online homework portal was really frustrating. If you studied the slides and did the homework, it was fairly easy to do well enough. Also, some lectures were way too R/Stata/Minitab heavy to be engaging.

great guy. ok professor. very disorganized, went overtime on a couple of labs. and not labs that are on campus. labs in the middle of the woods... overtime. lectures disorganized. and flipped class where you watch hours of video lectures every week and he js talks scattered-mindedly in class. he is rly great person and knowledgeable tho

He's a really sweet guy, but is super disorganized with the way he runs things. His directions are never very clear, but he is a pretty fair/easy grader. He is also super passionate about this class and is overall, a great guy.
Amazing lectures, caring and respected instructor

Flipped class- lectures were online (1-3 hr per week) but they didn't always make sense. Class was meant to be used for homework, but half the time it was more lecturing. Bad class to take if you don't have friends taking it. Everything turned in on paper and he lost our first prelims. Goes over time on labs. However, really cares about students.

He is an incredibly unorganized professor that teaches a flipped class. On the first day of the year he said, "the biggest complaint about this class is that its a flipped class, but I'm gonna try it again." It did not work this year either, and overall he is a very unorganized and dysfunctional professor as well as grader.

The man is awesome and passionate about what he teaches. However, not posting ANY grades on Canvas even after final grades are released put me off a bit altho we received our grades back from every assignment and tests. Also, beware that all assignments/reports are expected to be turned in in-person on PAPER. Instructions were often unclear.

Was taught as a "flipped class," meaning the lectures would be watched at home and activities in class. Instead, we ended up watching 3 recorded lectures a week (from 2012, public on YouTube) AND each class was a lecture, aka 6+ lectures a week. The labs were pretty cool but the lab reports were difficult and the exams were overly complicated.

He has passion but seems like he doesn't want to teach. He attempts to radiate positivity ("Go be awesome!") yet comes across as irritated. Class was flipped with about 3-6 hours/week of videos. Monday is a lecture on lab, and the other two days are either a sloppy representation of the videos or busywork. Lots of extra effort with little return.

Such a great professor- makes sure you understand (doesn't mind re-explaining concepts) and has a sense of humor. He's the perfect guy to teach an intro soil class since he's so enthusiastic. The lab reports were sometimes a pain to write but they were graded easily (might depend on the TA, though). I highly recommend taking a class with him!

Jonathan LOVES soil. I mean he LOVES it. Super passionate about what he does and really wants students to understand the material. Tests are simple if you attend the lectures and do the reading. Labs every week are straight forward. A B is pretty easy to get in the class, but an A would require some serious effort and/or a hard science background.

He is very helpful and nice.  The subject (soil science) is a very complex one and he did a good job of teaching this intro class.  My only complaint would probably be a slight lack of explanation on what he wanted lab reports to contain.  However, I'm sure he'd elaborate if one were to just ask him.  Great teacher!
very unclear with what was expected for lab reports
Very good professor, tries hard to make sure students understand and is willing to work with them to make things clear.  This class was challenging but fascinating!
Every single class has 100 pages of slides, every page full of theorems to be tested with no explanation in class.

1. the lecture covers a wide range of topics but does not go quite deeper, and some of the slides are not well-structured, making it hard to follow.
2. prelims are challenging and goes much deeper than both the lectures and the homework, it is difficult to review every topic while also preparing for the level of depth.
The course covers important materials in financial statistics, which is very useful for interviews. Professor Ruppert definitely knows a lot, but his lectures are quite dry.

Lectures are boring and I feel like sometimes the Prof. only reads the lecture to finish tasks given by the school but doesn't care about teach us anything at all. Disorganized lecture notes. The Prof. cannot even explain his own notes clearly. Financial background is not required but if you don't have any financial knowledge, you will SUFFER a lot

4 prelims but u can drop one. Attend lectures at all costs. The homeworks are hard but office hour and collaboration between classmates help. As for the exam, you have to find resources to help you ace(doing past prelims help). Financial Engineering is a very useful class and it will benefit you outside Cornell

Homeworks are especially hard. However, the prelims that count much are extremely easy to score A. Overall lecture was instructive and helpful. Very kind and moderate. Patient for any follow up questions. Highly recommend.
Very boring and uninspiring. Lecture content is disorganized. Difficult to learn. Coursework poorly prepared.

Rupper's lectures are quite monotonous and boring.  They are poorly worded and very disorganized.  The material he teaches during his portion of the course is difficult to learn and he does not make it any easier by providing a textbook, only his lecture slides.  The final is a huge surprise because it is nothing like the homework.

Rickford was my favorite professor I've ever had at Cornell. Amazing lecturer, so funny and knowledgable. It's clear he really cares about the material, and he made it enjoyable to go to class! Very few assignments, all of which were easy to succeed in if you put in any effort (Actually for HIST 3590)

Passionate about the subject matter, answered questions, good explanations for different terms, readings were heavy but informative, somewhat of a hard grader, notetaking is by hand, sit closer to get more out of the class. Always READ THE RULEBRICK.  

He advocates for students to use their critical thinking, and cares about being a good teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Guy comes to class and is really rude and obnoxious to the students. He also is known for having bigoted views and still participates in rally's where he spews hateful violent rhetoric even after being exposed by the media. Hasn't learned his lesson and has an awful arrogant attitude towards his students. As for his class it's medium difficult
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment:
An excerpt from the syllabus: 

"You are expected to attend every class and to arrive promptly. Each unexcused absence will result
in a penalty of one-third of a grade. (For example, B to B-.) Upon returning to class, students with
excused absences will submit a three-page response paper on the readings assigned while they were away"
Horrible professor, the worst professor I have ever had. Do not take his class, avoid at all costs.
The worst professor at Cornell which is saying a lot since half of them are awful to begin with. Bigoted, participed in a violent rally yesterday. Spreads hatred on campus. Avoid.
Class subjects are interesting, unfortunately he is exhilarated by the deaths of innocent civilians.
If he could simply stick to teaching and not being so antisemitic maybe I would re consider taking the class again.

What Rickford said about Israel was sad. However, as a lecturer, Rickford was amazing! He was so passionate about and had a lot of wisdom on AA history. He graded fairly, I'd say it was a pretty easy A (gov major here). 2 papers, 5 discussion posts, and a final made up the course. I would take his class again. Made us take hand-written notes tho.

Disappointing Exp.: I recently took a course taught by Rickford, and I have to say it was a rather underwhelming experience. While I respect the professor's qualifications and knowledge in the subject matter, their teaching style left much to be desired. I would recommend considering other options if you have the choice. 350 characters not enuf
Horrible.  Always felt like he was yelling at me.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Passionate and engaging teacher, decent amount of reading but worth it.
Engaging lecturer, favorite professor

I've taken 3 classes with Professor Rickford (HIST 1595 , HIST 2955 and HIST 3590). In class you can expect to read a lot so take good notes. Discussion is crucial. His personality is pretty easy going. Attendance is not mandatory but encouraged. There is a group aspect where one week your assigned group has to present on that week's reading.

Lots of reading as I would expect in graduate course (note: course code listed here is incorrect). He is intelligent, can be funny, is pretty chill about attendance, is demanding that you participate in every class, so don't think you can get away without doing readings. Generally unavailable and unhelpful. I did not enjoy his class.

Professor Rickford's class was so great because he taught such an essential topic in a way that made it easy to understand. He goes a bit fast during his lectures, but he is hilarious, and you will definitely learn a lot.
he's a tough grader when it comes to essays.

The only work is an essay, the midterm, the final, and paragraph journal entries on the readings for every class. The readings supplement the lectures, so if you miss something in class, just do the reading. He is an amazing lecturer, super funny, and although he talks fast, you don't have to write down everything he says.

Liu Laoshi cares for her students, and wants to make sure that your Chinese improves. Getting an A is difficult, but possible if you really put in the effort. The class is intense but she tries her best to make it less stressful. Take Chinese with her!

I had her for 1123 and 1124. Favorite teacher at Cornell. Super helpful and chill and really wants the best for her students. Tough class but if you put in the effort she cares. My Chinese got so much better and she intentionally sets aside free time in class to speak about random stuff which I think is the best way to learn the language.

I took Chinese 1123. Liu Lao Shi is amazing. One of my favorite professors at Cornell. Really cares and helps you improve your Chinese. You need to make sure you learn your tones and proper pronouciation but she is extremely helpful.

Liu Laoshi is really likable and easy to reach outside of class. You'll probably spend at least 5 hours a week outside of class preparing for weekly quizzes, preview homework, and journals. But overall, her classes are really enjoyable; if you put in the effort, you should be able to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: to be very honest, he does not have enough insight about his research. too vague in his comments.

Exceedingly close minded to student questions or concerns, has a "my way or the highway" type of attitude, which is natural to academia, but which he espouses particularly intensely. Also will happily encourage you to drop the class or seek a way to not have to deal with you. Will quickly discourage students seeking 1 on 1 guidance. Smart+awful.

Literlaly one of the worst professors--expectations are not clear for deliverables. He can be rude and refuse to answer questions from students for no reason. I would avoid taking any of his classes at all costs

He does not teach. Rushes through everything as if you already went through his course website and knows what it all means. Might as well just teach yourself. Slides are not posted on time. TAs end up being the slaves answering all the questions. You're just a number to him. Just know that's what you're getting.
One of my favorite professors at Cornell! The workload and expectations for this class are reasonable.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: 3510 mostly reviews the material of 2510 but in greater depth, which is helpful due to how horrible 2510 is. Richardson is overall very helpful, fair, and sets reasonable expectations. The course is a bit disorganized, and not always the most interesting, but overall pretty solid.
Professor Richardson makes herself very accessible and approachable. Definitely one of my favorite professors!
very nice and passionate about her work. The class is a lot of memorization

I don't quite understand why a Cornell professor could teach a course without even preparing it. The lab equipment we used were very oftenly broken, which could be avoided by a easy check before class. Her teaching style directly leads to learning nothing, as said by many students in her class.
Great Professor, very clear and friendly.
Engaging and friendly. Wish I could take her again...
Class is clear and interesting! I personally had a lot of fun taking this class with Prof. Richardson. Highly recommendable!
Professor rocks! Highly intelligent, very helpful, down to earth and friendly. Her passion for the subject she teaches is unparalleled.
Very good professor. I liked her a lot. Sometimes expected too much of students.
the best.
Best teacher I ever had at Cornell. Changed my life.
Beware........
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Ryan is a great instructor, genuinely cares about his students and is always open to questions. Labs were the highlight of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of the easiest classes at Cornell if you just show up. Minimal studying is needed if you go to lectures, and pay close attention during labs. Field Trips are engaging and tie back into exams. Lots of small projects, reading, and quizzes throughout the semester so just keep up with all the work. Watch the syllabus and you'll be fine.

The class is pretty easy, lots of different assignment styles, which break up the rigidness unlike other Cornell Science classes. Each lecture is pretty boring, and Prof Ryan is not the most well spoken. There are farm field trips instead of traditional labs that are fun and inspiring. Midterm and Final were both straight forward.

Professor Ryan is a great guy and is very accessible. The TA's were very nice and helpful as well. The class is easy as long as you turn things in on time. The only downside was the 3 hour labs outside on farms during freezing rain or snow.

Took for both Intermediate macro(3040) and International finance(4545) and not sure why his reviews here are so negative. I didn't attend most lectures and crammed before each test for ~15hrs and did well in both classes. Most of the grade is based on tests, which are all material from the slides so just know the slides VERY well and it's cake.
Don't do it
just a mid dude that shouldn't be teaching

He has little supplementary materials for exams. There is no practice. Fails to respond to Ed discussions in a timely fashion. Averages on exams are in the fifties, and the homework grades are in the 70s. Class is curved, though—very bland speaker. The slides don't help. You have to read the textbook to understand any of the material. Don't take.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: very kind & great lecturer. one of the best profs i've ever had.

Professor Rz. is definitely one of the best professors at Cornell. His lectures are engaging (in large part due to his wit/humor), and he's an extremely personable teacher. It's clear that he genuinely cares about student outcomes, and is also very nice during OH. The HW for 3300 is very manageable and he gives you all the tools you need + more.

Professor Rzeszotarski is the best professor I've had at Cornell so far. He is witty, and cares a lot about certain things, but is a great professor that cares for students. I would take any course with him again

Great at explaining concepts and very caring prof overall.  The homework accurately reflects what is learned but is still very interesting and rewarding.  You do have to pay attention and keep up to do well.
well-organized and well-explained material. He uploads recordings so easy to review. Assignments echo w class material so easy to work on. nice class!
I love Electro-cat and Magneto-cat
Fantastic Prof! Made physics fun and engaging. Very cool in class demos + always available to students after class and in office hours. Super reasonable guy- if you need anything just ask him!
Amazing lecturer. Loved taking E&M with it and the grading is very fair.
He is such a cool guy. You can tell he's really passionate about the material. His prelims were fair and the workload was on the lighter side.

Tapping is the kindest and fairest professor you can get at Cornell. Lectures are easy to follow along, and he makes every class enjoyable. You will LOVE this class. It's not too hard to get a B in the class, but DO NOT slack off.

Super sweet and enthusiastic guy. You can genuinely tell teaching is a passion, and he does it well! Always receptive to feedback and willing to help everyone. Class isn't as easy as everyones making it out to be though, its still pretty difficulty, ESPECIALLY when magnetism is introduced. So participate in ur COOPs and stay on top of it :-)

Ryan Tapping is by far my favorite professor at Cornell. He cares so much about all of his students, and is truly enthusiastic about what he teaches. It is easy to do well in his class, because 45% of your grade is participation/homework. The exams are very doable. I hope Cornell recognises professor Tapping for his exceptional teaching.

He is a really nice guy and puts in the effort to make a nice learning environment. He seems to really care about his students and goes out of his way to try to make his lectures more enjoyable. The work is not light though its a physics course so you do get a bunch of homework and everything else that comes with a physics course.
chill dude. A little overrated in my opinion (people act like he is the best prof at the entire school which I don't think is true) but still deserves the five.
The single best professor I've ever had at Cornell. Go to lectures and sections and you'll do well.
Amazing dude, genuinely cares about student feedback and makes needed changes.
Teaches E&M in a very good and easy to understand way, fair exams, and is literally always happy and enthusiastic. the goat of E&M for sure
Goat of physics
Great lectures and honestly just an amazing person as well. He clearly cares about his students and tests are pretty fair. This class is very well taught. OH are very useful as well.

Dr. Tapping is one of the best lecturers I've had at Cornell. He puts a lot of effort into making the lecture material easily understandable and engaging despite it being inherently difficult to understand. I love the jokes and the enthusiasm he brings to each class. Exams are super fair, and lots of practice material is provided beforehand.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Absolutely amazing person and professor. He was always genuinely excited about the content he taught. Now that I am in PHYS2214, I've never appreciated him more. Hes the GOAT.

I loved the in-class demos. Prof Tapping is so good at explaining concepts and demonstrating them. He genuinely cares for his students and helps anyone to understand. He is positive, and very passionate about what he's teaching. I enjoyed every single lecture and discussion.
Tapping is the GOAT!! He is super kind and will make surprise appearances at the LSC and TA office hours because he loves his students. The most iconic professor at Cornell.

Tapping is engaging and wants to help all of his students. He made a large lecture class interesting, even in a subject I wasn't that interested in. Tests were on par with material, but do the homework and practice problems.

Great professor!! He genuinely cares about teaching and engaging his students. I also liked how he had paper handouts of the lecture notes available as well. Exams were slightly difficult but fair. Problem sets were harder than the actual exams, but many office hours were offered.

Not only does this professor deliver amazing and engaging lectures, this professor is amicable, accommodating, and approachable. Exam content and homework grading is very fair. Supportive TAs. The class is structured very well and content is well reinforced. Pacing is the right balance to cover enough topics and have deep content understanding.

Tappings is one of the best proffesors I've had at Cornell! Super joyful and teaching engaging lectures. This class has discussion 2 days a week which is super helpful, exams are reasonable and similar to COOPs, PSets, and Lecture coverage. They also have office hours like 6 hours everyday of the week
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Tapping is unlike any other, he is so great. He is an amazing lecturer and actually seems like he enjoys teaching us. He is very approachable and responds great to student feedback. He makes learning E&M fun and his lectures are my favorite. I will miss the cat memes and the way he says hello each day.
DJ Ryan is the undisputed goat. In all seriousness, he is a great lecturer, very understanding, and the class is fair and super well organized.
Best professor I've ever had. Super understanding. Very reasonable work. Dr. Tapping, we love you and are lucky to have you!

Taken Spring 2024. Textbook is optional, he teaches so that you don't need it, it's just a reference. He teaches very concisely. Office hours are great. He even hosts office hours in between lectures. He puts in a lot of effort to help students and you can easily tell. Easy to talk to, open to feedback, and very humble. Thank you Ryan Tapping.
Extremely hard course but Ryan Tapping does his best to help all students. Make sure you attend all co-ops bc that's so much of your grade it will help makeup for the inevitably difficult exams
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Best professor I've had so far at Cornell. Very patient, encourages questions and makes sure you really understand the content in office hours. I loved attending office hours and thought they were extremely helpful. E&M itself is a hard subject but he explains it well in bare terms. He's very humble and open to feedback. Overall great guy.
Fun guy. Made an effort to go through many example problems in lecture which helped understand so much more than bullet point notes. E&M sounded very scary but this guy made it not that bad

Professor Tapping is one of my favorite professors so far at Cornell. I came into Cornell with a weak Physics background and have struggled at times because of it, but Tapping's excellent lectures and being extremely well-organized overall have made E&M so much more bearable for me.

Professor Tapping always makes sure lecture will be interesting and never comes to class without a demo prepared. I do not love physics but he makes it much more enjoyable, and also has a very fair grading system. The tests are not too difficult if you understand the homwwork assignments, and he always ensures you can get help if you need it

Prof. Tapping is wonderful. The class is very well organized, his lectures are clear, his homeworks and exams are all very fair. Tapping very clearly just wants everyone to do well and have a good time with the content. He's also just an all around really nice guy. He makes a historically hard subject accessible, even enjoyable.
I cry every night reminiscing about PHYS 2213. I will miss Ryan Tapping so so so much :'(

Ryan Tapping IS THE MAN. Best prof I've had thus far. Lectures and demos are awesome, COOPs are engaging, and I've learnt a ton. The best thing about Ryan, without a doubt, is his ability to listen and respond to student feedback - be it regarding a specific HW deadline, or even regarding the course structure as a whole, he is always on top of it!

Professor Tapping is the best STEM teacher I have ever had. He is so funny and an incredible lecturer. This is coming from someone who made a C in mechanics and is looking like they are going to make an A in this class. Beyond thankful to Ryan who made me feel like I can actually do this again. If you want to learn something, take this class!!!

Dr. Tapping is an amazing professor. He is truly one of a kind. I have so much respect for him. He made phys2213 enjoyable even though it was a hard class. His office hours were very helpful, and he is very patient with students. Thank you for everything Dr. Tapping and to all students taking his class in the future, please be nice to him.

Ryan Tapping is one of the best professors that I have had so far at Cornell. He completely turned around the Phys 2213 program, making a notoriously difficult class into something fun and interesting. His tests were fair and lectures engaging. Tapping is probably the most genuine and considerate professor I've seen.

literally the kindest and most amazing human being! i went to OH after our first prelim and it was completely empty. mans literally came in and talked with me for 3 HOURS; he came back at 11pm to see if i was still there, saying he felt bad for distracting me. he didnt leave till we finished the coop i originally came to OH to do.

Prof. Tapping did an excellent job with 2213, and it was clear from the start how important the class was to him and how much he cared about the students. Lectures and demos were engaging and fun. Though work was intensive, everything was fair.

Fantastic lectures, genuinely caring. His class is involving, and the material is difficult. But unlike others with the same description, he also makes you feel like you are respected, and there is a high level of tolerance.

Tappings is a very caring professor. It is very intentional that he makes 2213 an incredibly chill class. Compared to previous semester, the psets are very relaxed. The prelim is reflective of the psets and coops. Lecture wise, the demos are very cool and aids in conceptual understanding of the concepts. Honestly, no bad comments about 2213.

Dr. Ryan Tapping made sure that students were heard, advocated for, and made active efforts to make PHYS 2213 a better experience. I was originally scared because I heard horror stories about 2213 being tough, but he seriously made lectures enjoyable to attend. I would really recommend his course!

this prof is truly just looking for any red flags she can make up in the writing. Im an intl student so I use the "english" spelling of words (like colour instead of color) and she marked me as AI. also prof says diff. things to all her students, she told specific students she would give them a bigger curve/boost on the midterm
Difficult class, but one of the most interesting classes I have taken thus far. Class material can be used across many industries.
Very fair professor who prioritizes learning and a good class environment. This is a class where you get what you put in. If you participate frequently and attend office hours, you will do great.

For the first few weeks of this c(o)urse, I kept hoping things would get better. She cackles all the time. She dislikes women, especially when they are both from wealthy parents and smart (and also good-looking or Asian). She is either not well or unable to deal with people in general. Do not take this course while she is teaching it.

I would never take this class but I had to in order to stay in public policy. i tried to switch majors because of this class. it is impossible to do well. no matter what you do the TAs/professor will find a way to take 20% off your grade for no reason. stay away.

Don't be fooled by the reviews, she's a fantastic professor. TAs can be inconsistent on grading, but I found that by going to office hours and showing interest in the material, the class was completely manageable. PAM2030 was one of my favorite classes at Cornell so far simply because of how interesting and useful the class was.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I did relatively well in one of her classes but I felt that no matter how much effort and care I put into the class it wasn't enough to meet her standards. I also felt like she violated my boundaries and made me uncomfortable and hesitant to communicate with her outside of classes. I would not recommend her teaching to anyone.

reviews.comment: Impossible, she grades you off the smallest things and shit talks students she dislikes

reviews.comment: Impossible
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Literally the worst professor I've had the misfortune of coming across.

Do yourself and your GPA a favor and stay away. Participation grades are extremely unfair, assignments are graded unfairly and inconsistently, little-to-no test prep in class, and condescending TA's... there is a reason why this class has a B average every semester. So done with all of this quite useless work.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Actually, the reviews on this page are entirely accurate. I went to office hours every single assignment, and put in the feedback required, and yet my grade depended on how Professor Sassler felt on a given day. "Put in the work and you'll do fine." Well, obviously not, since the average for this class is a B.

I think that a lot of the feedback that's on this page isn't 100% accurate. PAM 2030 was one of the most informative policy classes I've taken. I don't think that a lot of the flack that Sassler is getting on this page is accurate--she's just as dedicated as any other professor at Cornell, and if you listen and put work into class, you'll do fine.

This is the first time I've ever rated a professor below 4 stars. AVOID. Being a good student won't save you. The professor will deduct points from your write-ups based on metrics that are NOT in the assignment instructions- and will not provide clear reasons as to why. The TA's aren't helpful, and are very rude and condescending.

Among the worst classes I have taken at Cornell. She does not answer students questions well, rambles continuously, the five exercises are grades so harshly and very weirdly, very unhelpful feedback, no rubric given for exercises. If it is not a requirement for anything, do not take it!!!!

Can Pam move her to research or something? There is absolutely no reason why Professor Sassler needs to be a professor teaching students. Despite negative reviews for years, her class hasn't changed. OBVIOUSLY something is not working if your class is making everyone miserable

By far the worst class I've taken at Cornell. Sassler has no idea how to effectively teach. She is unable to answer any student questions and rambles on endlessly. There are five tedious, confusing exercises (essentially essays) that are graded both harshly and subjectively. TAs are rude and unhelpful and form a cult of condescension around her.

Professor Sassler looks like a really nice professional from the beginning, however as soon as you get your first assignment back your opinion changes. Be ready to die with her assignments, because her's or TA's comments do not help at all. They instead make you feel worser than you felt before.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Pathetic excuse of a class. Rambling lectures are padded by incoherent jokes from Sassler and her crew of TA's who you'll grow to hate. Grading is all but incomprehensible with little to no guidance given before and after the assignment. The comments from TA's seem more like they are trying to get you to drop.
Definitely has a bias towards students that are not white jewish girls. She has a hard time liking or engaging with students that don't immediately remind her of herself.

Just checked the roster and saw Sassler is the only person teaching Pam 2030. Yikes. Good luck kiddos. This was definitely the most boring, difficult, tedious and annoying class I've ever taken at Cornell.

One of the worst professors I've had at Cornell. Showed absolutely no leniency or understanding during a pandemic. Cannot really handle criticism and can act annoyed when students ask questions or question something she says. Also, very tough and subjective grader. Only social science class I will not get an A in.
Lol. Pam 2030, Sassler had a regrade and didnt give anyone in her lecture of 200 points back. What even was that, Sharon?
Useless class. Too broad to garner any real information. Grading is impossible unless you spend thousands to go to Denmark. Worst class Ive taken at Cornell (Pam 2030, not a listed option)

This professor is amazing because you truly do learn in this course. She is a thorough grader, and you do need to work for your grade, but through this process you learn so much and grow as a student. She cares and she is in all ways willing to work with you as a student and get to know you personally. I would highly recommend this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class has the same grade distribution as intro engineering classes. That should tell you everything you need to know
Never thought a class could have such easy material and be graded so harshly

Class is graded completely based on Sharon's feelings. Yes, I got an A+ but I practically had to sell my left kidney to her to avoid getting literal Cs, which would happen if you didn't harass her and go to every office hour she held

Didnt hate this class as much as others did. There is only one midterm and one final and the final threw everyone for a loop because it was much harder than the midterm. For the papers, you MUST go to office hours. Expectations arent clear and TAs will take off points for stuff the prof expected, but wasnt made clear in the packet of directions.

2030 was not enjoyable. Extremely inconsistent grading based on which TA got your paper. Horrible guidelines, and you would get a different unconfident answer from each TA you would ask about a certain aspect of an assignment. Favoritism is real with this one, too. Beware

Professor Sassler was very clearly overwhelmed by the number of students she had. It was too much for her and she couldn't handle it, or be an effective educator or grader. She should teach smaller classes or stick to research.
Sassler was by far the worst Professor Ive ever had. Take Pam 2030 with anyone but her.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: An embarrassment to the PAM department. Pleasant individual, hellish grader/professor.

Widely held as the worst professor in the PAM department. Class is dreadful. She totally picks favorites, which affects your grade. Her name tells part of the story because she is quite "sassy," as in rude. The grading of her assignments makes no sense, yet the assignments will be graded harshly. Good luck figuring out how not to lose points.
A nice lady, bad professor.
Agonizing lol
You can spend entire weeks on an assignment with extensive office hours help, and think you completely perfected it, only to receive a poor grade with little/confusing feedback.
It seems like rate my professor is being flooded because Sassler gave us her horribly graded assignments back. This class made me drop from PAM.
Impossible to figure out how class is structured. Avoid.
Doesnt understand her own class or grading and its very obvious.

Sassler basically uses her class as a way to gather data for her research--you're part of the experiment. Her opinions are rather judgemental and lectures are boring. Don't take this class for an easy A / interesting class. Her assignments are invasive.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Unhelpful class with an unhelpful professor.
I took Pam 2030 with Sassler. Her guidelines were incredibly vague making short assignments very difficult. Avoid Pam 2030 with Sassler if you can.

Passionate about demography and makes it legitimately interesting in her lectures. Prelims were in-class and easy if you can remember terms easily. Out-of-class projects/assignments were interesting and honestly fun. For the questions that I did have for assignments she was helpful.

For a class named "Modern Romance", you would assume the class to be of average difficulty. The amount of work required for the papers and exams is, for lack of a better word, absurd. There were 3 papers, and two exams (prelim, final), and undoubtedly not worth 3 credits. The material is interesting, but she somehow lulls me to sleep every lecture
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: If 20+ people show up to a lecture every day just to click in and then leave immediately, something is wrong. Sassler is the worst prof I've had in the PAM department, and if this class had been my first exposure to the major I probably would have switched out of it. Painful, useless class that was torture to sit through twice a week.

Only an easy A class if you actually put in the work that she expects, which is reasonable. By far the best and most engaging professor I've had at Cornell. Uses iClicker for attendance. Go to office hours for feedback on papers and your grade will thank you. Participate in class so she knows your name, your grade will thank you again.

Oh my god this was the most painful lecture I've sat through in my three years of college. The exercises are graded unreasonably harshly and the class is graded just by exercises and the two exams. Sassler makes awkward jokes and laughs at herself all the time and it's just irritating. Unless you have to take this class for PAM, avoid it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--SO MANY PAPERS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: While some of Sassler's lectures were interesting and well-organized, a lot of the time it felt like she herself was disorganized. She had a hard time correctly understanding students' questions, often interpreted charts and graphs incorrectly, and assignment instructions were almost always confusing. She's a tough grader but gives little feedback.
Easy curriculum, but homework's are graded unreasonably. She doesn't help you out if you are struggling.

Very personable and engaging teacher.  Material was interesting, although it got repetitive since the class really only addresses about 5 topics.  Not an easy A, but it's pretty tough to get anything below a B+ if you do minimal work.

I strongly disagree that this class was an easy A. However, Sassler is a good professor. She challenges you in assignments, and for the most part keeps you engaged in lecture. Exams weren't easy either, but the readings are interesting. I did the most work in this class than I did in all my other classes. I'm glad I took this class; very relevant.

I like Sassler.  She's friendly - and not just professor-friendly either - and fair.  I wouldn't impugn her teaching skills by any stretch.  Lectures were organized, complete, thoughtful, and almost always engrossing.  The tests were multiple choice-heavy, which was disappointing.  But it's an undergrad PAM class; what else can you expect?

Sassler is very accommodating and understanding of student life. She is funny and lectures are worthwhile but not mandatory. She essentially gives you the prompts to the essay questions on exams. Interesting subject matter and easy A

I love Prof. Sassler! She is seriously one of the smartest people I have ever met, and truly knows her topics. I would love to do research with her in family or race policy. Her exams a very hard, but fair, and she is probably the most helpful and flexible professor I've encountered in my college career and especially at Cornell. Take her.

Instructions for assignments are vague, slides are a rambling wall of text, lectures are confusing at best.  Poor pedegogy skills.  Out of touch with students.  Presummes all who take her class are interest in pursuing a career in policy analysis and data writing.

Super easygoing guy. This class is definitely a good FWS/intro course, and he does a good job of explaining abstract concepts. Theres a total of 5 essays, little to no reading, and mostly mandatory attendance. Only advice i have is to participate during class (otherwise its kinda awkward)
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: really nice professor and the workload is not heavy. definitely a really enjoyable class with really nice prof
Pretty good and easy professor, definitely will take again
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Best professor you'll have. He is the nicest person and truly cares about his students' well being. He makes sure his class does not become another burden for students, he is fun! 10/10!!

Scott is a very good writing teacher, and his classes are always interesting and well prepared. We can learn a lot of knowledge in the weekly meeting. He can guide us to think well and write better articles. He is very approachable and encourages us to think.

Professor Sorrell is a fantastic professor! He sets up individual meeting with each of us once a week to answer our questions and check our progress, which helps me a lot! He emphasizes on students' progress a lot and is always super willing to help you whenever you reach out to him. The workload is pretty doable and suitable for freshman!

He teaches pointless information in 9am lectures which is later covered during 3-hour, unskippable labs. Getting an A+ in his class is just about impossible, and lecture attendance can be done remotely(most days). When the course is helpful, it's not directly due to his teaching, but because of the lab TAs. His teaching needs more direction.

The class itself is quite trivial if you have any experience in biology, but an easy A. Sarvary's lectures are quite fun, just make sure to do the PollEv for attendance. The labs (and getting out of them early) heavily depend on the TA, but generally really straightforward and easy. Very flexible assignment schedule.

These other reviews must be lying because BIOG1500 is not a great course. It insists upon itself and is a tad bit pretentious. Nothing against the professor, it's just that the course is a lot of busy work and not very informative.

Mark was passionate about the class, but the class has a lot of busy work and seems kinda pointless. It's pretty easy, but unfortunately, the class is not formatted in a way that is very exciting or intellectually stimulating.

Sarvary is really nice and his lectures are chill and enjoyable, but ultimately the lab TAs are a lot more important in shaping your experience with the class. Grading is annoying, as an A+ is nearly impossible (99.00+), and my grad TA was really stingy with points. Sarvary is great and deadlines are flexible, but be ready for boring 3-hour labs.

The class really really serves no educational purpose whatsoever. The lectures are sometimes engaging but again there is no point in attending apart from answering polling questions. The labs are needlessly long and do not need to take up 3 hours.

He seems like a sweet person, but I truly didn't learn much from his lectures. The three-hour labs were really tedious and painful to sit through. Definitely an easy A class, but it's virtually impossible to get an A+ (the minimum grade is 99.00%)
Useless morning lectures, extremely boring lab sessions. I don't know why the lab is 3 hours long. Please make a test-out option for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Don't really learn much in lecture and things are mainly taught by the lab TA, but his lectures were easy to follow and he seems like a nice guy.
This class is horrible. Mandatory course for my major and it's just busy work and dry content that I already know. There needs to be a system to test out of this garbage.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers
