reviews.comment: This course is required, but in the end I was glad I took it as I feel much more prepared for my summer internship and advanced courses next semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Extremely boring class and kind of useless. You think you'd learn real lab techniques but it's just simple things like micropipetting and how to use a microscope. He's a nice guy but the class is just boring to sit through. It is a requirement for any pre-health majors, but it's 2 credits and an easy A so just get through it.

Worst class ever. He is sneaky when it comes to justifying the material. This class is literally middle school level and so boring to sit through, even the lab TAs agree. His assignments are set up to confuse people and lower their grades to keep everyone from getting an A. DO NOT TAKE IT UNLESS YOU HAVE TO.

This is an extremely boring class. Grades mostly depend on your GTA, which is annoying if you get a bad one. The assignments are annoying and tedious and some are pointless. There's one exam, a research paper, and bunch of other trivial assignments like presentations and stats work. If you put in the bare minimum, you'll get an A or B+.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Extremely boring and excruciating class. Sarvary and the other professor did virtually nothing the entire semester. I got stuck with the worst GTA who graded as harsh as she could for good work. GTA was on a power play the entire time and used that to be threatening and harm students grade. Easy class but a horrible class structure

It's very easy to get an A. Professor Sarvary and his TAs take feedback very seriously. The class was interesting but a bit long. However my graduate TA let us leave earlier if we finished early so it wasn't that big of an issue for me. Overall I recommend the class and the assignments we did helped me in other lab settings.

It is an unnecessarily long class for the amount of content covered. You're expected to pay $80 for a lab manual that isn't used often. He's the author and advises against reusing old versions so you'll buy a new copy even though the maybe 5 useful pages could be on Canvas. You'll get a (not so) free A though.

Most boring class i have ever taken. Labs are 3 hours long, unnecessary, & unhelpful. The grading scheme is completely unfair. It's def an easy A, but an A+ is basically impossible because he increased the cutoff (99.000+). The only thing i like about this class is the extended deadlines without penalty. DO NOT take unless u have to.

Most boring three hours of my week were spent sitting in this lab. You don't even do labs, the class includes learning how to email professors about research opportunities, using R coding software, and reading scientific journals. The one lab that we were supposed to do ended up being cancelled and they gave us fake data to use instead. Easy A tho.

The labs are incredibly annoying, you have to sit there for all three hours, but all of it could be covered in an hour if they wanted to. He doesn't do much during the lectures each week, so it seems like he mostly is the class coordinator.

Most boring class I've ever taken. Grading scheme makes completely no sense - I forgot to add a picture of something to a single assignment and got a 100% on everything else and I got a B. Labs are uselessly long and the textbook is a scam.

Only take biog1500 if you have to, or if you want to do research. Otherwise, it is boring and useless. The lectures were all recorded videos which was nice, but the labs are three hours and we barely did anything Luckily there was not a ton of HW. Expensive textbook. I rarely saw Prof. Sarvary except for lecture vids and popping in and out of lab.

Labs are the most boring thing ever and always take 3 hours long. Class does teach some useful skills, but the required 70$ textbook is a scam!!! We barely use the textbook and they require it. Lectures were recorded and we only had to show up in person for one lecture. This class is an easy A if you do all the work but it's so annoying.

I took this course over the winter session and it was great! Mark is a wonderful teacher and really cares about his students. It is not a very difficult class but it is a great resume builder and a great introduction to scicomm, if you're interested. The zoom calls were long but we took breaks. Not bad at all for 3 credits in 3 weeks.
This class is easy, but it is very boring because the labs are just very long. The workload is average, but I would not want to sit through this class again.

Super easy A but one of the most boring classes I've ever taken. The material is extremely simple, but it takes so much time to get through. Prof Sarvary himself is kind, lenient when you need an extension and overall cares about the course.

Literally you could learn the entire semester's material in a day on your own. The labs are stretched with ridiculous questions for material that could be covered in 15 minutes but actually take 3 hours. Take it for the free A and move on.
Go to lecture to answer questions to receive credit. Lab is not difficult. Prepare for lab practicals. Take class with people you know because lab gets boring and there is a group project.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Lectures used clickers when I took it, and I had a night lab taught by a grad student. The lab usually was let out early, thankfully. Basically the course was fine and taught basic scientific design and literacy through a biological lens. The prof also helped me land a spot despite the course being full.

The lectures were early and mandatory; I would get breakfast and eat it during lecture because there was nothing of value being spoken most of the time. However, there were clicker questions to make sure we were there. The labs were slow and were very easy, so just show up, stay for 3 hours a week, and you'll get an A.

Sarvary is a quality guy, but lectures are useless (but mandatory) and labs are unnecessarily long and tedious. The lab skills are relevant and applicable to research, but the course is paced at 1 mph. Overall, the workload is negligible and the course is an easy A so long as you put in minimal effort.
BIOG 1500 was an excellent foundational course. Dr. Sarvary is a great adviser!

BIO 1500 is an insult to everyone required to take it. Lectures are mandatory, but don't teach anything useful. Labs are three hours long, and you aren't allowed to leave early, even though the material takes 15 minutes. The only upside is how easy this course is- if you passed 5th grade math, you will get an A. Avoid this course if you can.
Take caution because Savary has an accent like Tommy Wiseau from The Room. Take this class freshman year because it is taught at a snail's pace.

If you have ever taken a biology course before, you will pass. If not, this is a good way to get hands on experience with lab techniques. definitely take this your freshman year, you'll hate yourself otherwise.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Don't buy the online textbook, as everyone else said. Get the free trial. Overall, this is a fairly easy class; it was my favorite, because the labs were pretty interesting and there was a light course load. Definitely answer poll everywhere questions, and find some good people for lab partners since you'll be stuck with them for most classes!

This class is incredibly dull. It is taught at a Kindergarten pace and your experience really relies on your TA. Sarvary himself is boring, arrogant, and patronizing. I hated this class and the only reason I ever went was for participation points.
You don't need to buy the online textbook or go to lecture other than for Poll Questions.
Good lecturer genuinely enthusiastic about the class, but labs are long and boring. Tests are easy and papers and projects are clearly outlined/understood.

This class is super easy. The material is easy to understand and the lectures are straight forward. Don't even really need to go to lecture to do well in the course. Dr. Sarvary is a great guy. Does have an accent so can be a little hard to understand sometimes. The online book is worthless.
I would second the disorganized comment. Lectures too seem useless.
This class is easy but disorganized.

The online book is fairly useless as a study tool. However, you will need it for prelecture and during lecture questions. Expect the TAs to have different approaches to grading and handing out studymaterial that is allowed and not allowed. The course staff decided not to hand out study guides, practice prelims, and answer keys to homework problems.
Sarvary is a great lecturer; he almost makes going to a 9am bearable.

This man is amazing. He's brilliant, really approachable, sweet, and always willing to help. If you think your TA is unfairly grading he's willing to look over anything for you. Highly recommend this professor in any course.
Sarvary's lectures are easy to understand, and the material is really simple. If you have a good TA, this class is a piece of cake.

The class is super easy and even if you can't understand his lectures (which I totally could anyway), very little of the material is new as long as you had decent bio in high school. He's funny and friendly, even though some find him intimidating. Also I love his accent.

He teaches about half of the lectures.  His accent is horrible and can sometimes make it hard to understand him.  He isn't the clearest professor in the world either.  All in all, the class is fairly easy and straightforward (if you have a good TA).
good guy. But hated his tests and hated his lab course. His lectures are clear tho.
He seems like a good professor overall.  The class, on the other hand....
Very helpful man, lectures were clear and entertaining. Really nice guy if you ever go to office hours.
Sarvary was a clear lecturer and I enjoyed his teaching more than any of the other guest lecturers.

Assistant Prof to Dr. Turgeon- I love him and his accent. His way of presenting material is very interesting and he's a funny guy. I kinda hope he replaces Turgeon because he is a much better lecturer

One of my favorite classes so far. Prof. Schwarz is an engaging lecturer who ensures the success of every student in her class. The curriculum she designed consisted of readings that altered the way I view my life on small and large scales and taught me how to think critically about contrasting viewpoints. Her classes are inspirational.
Awesome Anette!!! Took her seminar at Yale.

The class felt a little disorganized, but overall was still really enjoyable. We covered a lot of stuff that was genuinely funny, and then class was just discussing it. I also took it during the start of the pandemic, and she was genuinely concerned for all of our wellbeing, and that felt really nice to have at that time.

She is a lot of fun and really knows her material. The class is definitely disorganized though, and there never is a syllabus/canvas site (although she does always promise there will be one soon). We only had readings and discussion in class up until the end of the semester, when we then had two short essays.

I took GERST 2700 under Professor Schwarz. Fantastic teacher. Very compassionate with the workload and assessments. Do the readings, show up to class, and participate. Those are the only expectations, they're clear and achievable.

I took this course during my high school summer and I am a freshman at Cornell rn. Among all the courses I have been taken so far, Prof. Schwarz's GERST 2250 is my favorite. I began to LOVE reading because of the course. A very inspirational, life-changing course to me.

This class was incredible, it was very informitive on German culture and the small number discussion format was both enjoyable and an awesome way to engage course readings. Dr. Schwarz is a very good professor very versed in her field, who truly cares about the well being of her students and will tailor course readings to class interests.

I just finished Prof Schwarz's summer college program--Genius and Madness in Literature. The course is fascinating, and her feedbacks to our discussions are very inspiring. I'll always remember her wisdom and humor.

Prof Schwarz is obviously a very intelligent, warm, and funny person. I loved being in her class, but i had wished there was more structure to the course (granted this was the first time this course was being taught*). We were only graded on two essays over the entirety of the semester. Super cool person and interesting readings tho. Love her.
Very nice and helpful. I highly recommend her summer college class!

I also had the pleasure of taking a summer course with Professor Schwarz two years ago. What can I say? She's incredibly sweet, able to stimulate deep discussions of the text without dictating unnecessarily, and completely approachable for help. Class is always interesting. Take a course with her, you won't regret it.
I took her class for high school students in summer college and loved it.  She's incredibly interesting and entertaining.  I feel lucky to have had her.
I love this woman.  She is one of the most grounded professors I've met at Cornell.  Genuinely interested in the material and in students' interpretations, and very approachable.  Class is wonderful.

I was actually in HIST 1690. Genuinely one of the best professors I've ever had, so funny, intelligent, and caring. Her lectures were incredibly fascinated and I could listen to her talk all day. She really pushed for in-depth analysis of seemingly simple examples, which created a good cultural snapshot of that case. Absolutely amazing.

I really enjoyed Professor Schmitt's class; it is one of my favorite courses I have taken at Cornell. She is an engaging lecturer who packs a lot of information into each class, yet keeps it fascinating and makes history genuinely fun. She's also incredibly knowledgeable, approachable, and encouraging of students' ideas and questions.

Professor Schmitt rocks. Take detailed notes because her lectures are packed with info that is useful for the exams (two prelims during the semester and a cumulative final). Make sure you do the readings in advance of discussion sections (try not to fall behind on readings). Take advantage of extra credit opportunities. Highly recommend!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Content overall was very interesting (in readings and in lectures), but I can't help but say that the lectures were way too dense. Again, the actual content was great, but there were ample moments to get confused and turned around. Honestly the course could have had half of the content. Still really engaging though—just felt a little overwhelmed
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Really good prof, she gives a manageable amount of reading but her grading is a bit tougher. All of her expectations are reasonable, explains content in the lecture very well, and is super helpful during office hours.

Lectures are great as Prof. Schmitt stops were any questions or comments. Material overall is really interesting! The readings can be a bit heavy but nothing too bad. Discussion sections are great and interactive. Papers/prelims were not bad but make sure you know what you are talking about. Either way, Prof. Schmitt and the TA gave great feedback!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Unstructured, and follows his own path. Poor communication between students and professor, and will ignore emails sent to him, then pretend as if he never saw them.
Just try it

Dave Schneider is by far the most incompetent professor I have ever had. Loads of meaningless homework, arbitrary grades. But these are fundamentally problems with the class, which is terrible and would be painful regardless of the instructor, but Dave made it significantly worse. Smug, unapproachable, and flat out rude, do not take this class !!!!
Professor was difficult to deal with and graded based on arbitrary criteria.

The professor assigns heavy workloads, including a time-wasting LEGO competition. Feedback is delayed for weeks despite late penalties. Compared to Professor Wes's SYSML course, this class feels shallow and poorly organized. The unclear objectives, trivial tasks, and weak teaching fail to provide meaningful skills or value to the program.
Terrible learning experience in his lectures. His instructions of HWs are vague and sometimes you have to guess what he wants you to do. And tons of pointless HWs will be assigned to you weekly.

Changes his hw content and requirements all the time.  Have you earn hw/group project percentages in 1%s  with all efforts and all spare time but final hw taks 50% of total grade.  Luck determines if you get a good grader, not able to change. Tons of hw, max 7 dues in 1 day. Mandatory course so don't think of this program.
There are too many homework, and the grading criteria for the homework are not clear
Lectures are poorly organized. Lots of meaningless homework. Presume all students are able to understand what he means but be irresponsible for the clarity.
There was a lot of homework and the lecture was very confusing. You don't know what you're supposed to do.
David is a cool guy, but not the best professor. His teaching style is very messy and it is easy to get lost. The class is so obnoxiously easy, however, that it doesn't end up mattering.

His assignments are very troublesome, and similarly, his courses are extremely boring. You can't learn anything useful, you can only learn how to quickly complete his tons of the useless and troublesome homework. He will specifically choose the day of the career fair to record whether you attended his lecture and then grade you.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: He tried to train his engineering students like god. In his 5100 he need students to build lego robots with all kinds of functions and required programming to complete the challenge. While he also required student to be able to draw sketch well and perfectly explain everything.

I'm very surprised to see so many negative reviews. This course works best if you apply it to your MEng project and teaches all the essential tools for systems engineers. I don't know what the other people were were expecting from the course. It does get tedious so be prepared for long homeworks, but you'll enjoy the lectures thoroughly.
lots of hw

If you want to waste your precious time, go take his course. He doesn't know about his stuff. I would prefer the TA to lecture the course. I would strongly recommend him to resign from his teaching position.

Disorganized lectures, unclear grading criteria, the professor seems to be a nice person at first but does not care about students AT ALL. The class itself is not hard though, and some of the materials are indeed interesting, it's just lots of works, and the professor makes it even worse. All the TAs are really nice and helpful tho
David is a nice person outside of the class, but over 80% of my unhappy memories in Cornell are more or less related to SYSEN 5100.
A third Very bad class, disorganized, and unhelpful. But it is super easy
Another Very bad class, disorganized, and unhelpful. But it is super easy
Very bad class, disorganized, and unhelpful. But it is super easy

Very poor organization and I don't understand why he is able to become a senior lecturer. He speaks like machine guns and sometimes his brain can't follow his mouth. So much work and can't grade accordingly. Run away from System Engineering program!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Awful. Talks a big game about understanding customers but doesn't listen to students enough to understand what they're even asking. Grading criteria clear as mud - I lost 10 points on an assignment for not having enough of something he said to my face there was no minimum for. Condescending and presumptuous. I expect better from Cornell.
Lecture slides and course in general are extremely disorganized.

Can not teach to save his life!!! Very disorganized. Seems to be an introvert but don't know how to transfer knowledge to students. Sometimes makes mistakes himself and loves to just read off of the slides. Take him if you want to spend X4 hours learning everything yourself. Very pissed at myself for taking his class. Arggghhh
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: I have had so many courses at Cornell and his course is absolutely the worst. His lecture is just a waste of your time. Tons of homework and strict requirements of your format but his slides are below even a kid's performance. If you want to learn how to waste someone else's time, go take it!
EXTREMTELY disorganized. very inconsistent grading and homework did not have any value.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He really cares about his work and empowering student. He does pile on work at certain points though. I really liked him.
Disorganized. Cares more about selling student projects to sponsors than students' learning.
Can be confusing, but will always strive to answer your questions. Fun lectures, but lots of homework.
Such an awesome guy and professor, loved going to lab each week.

discontinued PLBIO 2490 after this semester but Scanlon is a great professor. Def seems a little rough and impersonable at first but throughout the semester he gets better. Class paper grading criteria was super unclear until grades came out which was annoying but he is light on grading for quizzes and the exams.
If you get the opportunity to be a part of Mike's lab, consider yourself lucky. Really cares about undergrads and their work. Fun professor and mentor.

He is so dull; class material is dull; he does not plan tests in sync with material on theme (tends to be random), overall terrible experience. Doesnt grade tests and has each TA grade own which leads to massive differences in grades (over 10 points differences in mean). Doing fine in class, but takes up a lot of time. DULL
Lectures can be dry, but he seemed really happy to help in office hours.
Not a very hard class but by no means is super easy. Helpful to have a pretty ok background in bio

He's a really nice guy, but his lectures were incredibly boring- everyone had trouble staying awake! You didn't need to go to lecture b/c he posted detailed PP online. Sections weren't relevant to lecture, but they were easy. His quizzes/test were a bit tricky, especially with multiple choice wording. Class wasn't bad, just boringgg!
Prof. Scanlon is amazing! His lectures are as easy to understand as biology lectures can be, and really wants his students to succeed.
Teacher is a cool guy and the class is pretty straight forward. Study from the power points and the book and you'll be fine.

Prof. Scanlon makes this a straightforward class for nonmajors but he won't dumb anything down. He'll make sure you understand concepts and answer any questions you have. The lectures were all very interesting.

Such an awesome class! Scanlon is the most likable professor I've ever had, I actually looked forward to lectures. The material was really interesting and the lectures and movies were super entertaining. A great class to take just for fun.

Prof. Scanlon is the man!  This was a great class for non-science majors. We learned a new topic every week and all the information was VERY relevant to everyday life. Prof Sanlon's slides are very well done/interesting with lots of pictures.  Instead of lab, we watched movies on our own and then we would have a quiz once a week and discuss the mov

I took Prof Schrader's winter course - she was a excellent professor, and although ethics was not my fav topic, she made sure to make the class very engaging - half of time was her recapping ethical frameworks, and the other half was completely dedicated to discussing with your peers how these frameworks are relevant to current events. Recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Best prof ever!!! This was my favorite class this entire semester, and she's so personable & well spoken! Yes the seminar once a week was long, but she baked us brownies & bought snacks every week :') The course was also extremely interesting and helped us imagine what a world would look like when technology gets more predominant. Take her class!
Awful class! bad teaching

Lectures can be a bit long at times, but Prof. Schrader is one of the best professors at Cornell. Unlike most professors, she will readily make changes to the syllabus based on student input, and makes herself incredibly available to students - especially for the group project. It's a 4-credit course and people underestimate the work it requires.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Awful class... didn't learn anything. Quizzes are very difficult and cover way too much material. Even if you do the readings, you will not do well on the quizzes. Quizzes are only open from Thursday to Friday night so if you have a job good luck completing them. Lectures are confusing and long and attendance is required.

Prelims consist of a 10-12 page essay with extremely unclear prompts. Discussion sections are a waste of time, but are required. Lecturesection setup presents an extreme disadvantage to introvertspassive learners. At 10 weeks into this course we still don't have a single grade, though the drop date passed more than a week ago. Annoyed  :(

Prelims and final were 10-12 page take-home essays.  Lectures were boring and pretty useless for exams.  Course centers around class readings which are actually interesting although they can be dense at times.  She can be a tough grader on exams, but attendence and section points help boost your grade a lot.

This class was absolutely the worst. Lectures are unclear and powerpoint slides are absolutely unhelpful. Grading is very arbitrary and essay prompts doesn't really help students think and utilize their resources. I would not recommend to anyone in the future.

I've never been bothered enough to rate a professor or class before, but this one really bothered me. Don't be fooled, there's nothing psychological about this class. Also, the professor makes you do assignments designed for middle schoolers during the sections and the 'papers' never had a clear prompt. Truly pointless class.

i think the person below me must be on something, because this class was the opposite of interesting. her powerpoints were all over the place and she rambled. the class went by SO slowly. she tried though
Love this class. Definitely fun and interesting. Time flies by because she keeps thing interesting! Take it if you can.

Her classes were great, and she was always interested in getting student feedback to adapt to their learning styles. Lots of readings, which barely came on the tests, BUT were really good to understand the material. Awesome TA's. Interesting class. Be careful about skipping lecture: if you don't get good notes, you're screwed.
I liked this class, it was a lot of reading and the reading's didn't always show up on the exams, but we would talk about them in section.

If you want a class where you: spend most of your time reading boring, easy books and articles about arbitrary models, can get an easy A, and can skip lectures without worrying, this class is for you. Should be called 'philosophical models of morality and children,' not 'educ psych.' Few applications, boring, not useful or challenging. Great TAs.

her lectures are really interesting. though she has powerpoints, she never reads off them and the material is great. she's so passionate about the subject she teaches class is super intersting and the ta's amazing!

One of the most caring and constructive professors at Cornell. Seminars were great; even if you are not extroverted, you'll likely still feel super comfortable sharing your perspectives, questions, and insights. Projects are focused more on quality than quantity, and you get to choose your own path/topic. Top of the list for a 3000 SOC course.

Hearing people's complaints about other 1101 professors, I'm so glad I took it with Schnabel. Three micro-essays graded leniently and weekly home quizzes (answers are often word-for-word from the text). If you need to take 1101, take it with Schnabel, no question. He made an INTRO course an INTRO course, and I have stuck with sociology bc of it.

Overall chill class as long as you keep up with it. Weekly quizzes are open note but it helps to be familiar with readings ahead of time. TAs are super generous graders. Landon is super accomodating, but as others have said he does have a limit. He makes lecture content relevant and interesting

Interesting guy, but the material in SOC 1101 is pretty common sense. His lectures were funny and engaging. The TAs are the ones giving feedback, but they're super lenient graders. The answers for the reading quizzes are word-for-word in the readings, and they're open-note.

The class was easy very straight forward, no exams instead 2 weekly quizzez and memos (1 page papers) were assigned. Grading wasn't hard on memos and quizzes were easy can get away with skimming the readings

Professor Schnabel's lectures were always well organized and detail oriented. He posted the lecture slides with notes on them before lecture so students could really listen during lecture and take their additional notes. Very flexible in terms of grading and due dates but if he begins to feel taken advantage of, privileges will be lost.

An actually helpful teacher. Like, the grade reflects whether you tried on it, and the feedback is what you can actually improve. On top of that, the lectures aren't really related to academic writing, but literally just good writing, so if you pay attention, you can become a better writer in a real sense. Also, he's just funny and charismatic!

Sean Sam is by far the best teacher I have had this semester. He doesn't make his class excessively difficult and gives really helpful and detailed feedback. Instead of feeling stressed out about grades, we have the opportunity to focus on genuinely improving our writing. This is one of the rare teachers who actually want their students to succeed.

Genuinely the goatiest of all goats. Could not have asked for a better prof. Super responsive, laid back, and kind. We do ~1 reading a week, and 3/4 essays across the entire class. A very light workload overall. Plus, he just so happened to save a bunch of children from that burning orphanage one time, so that's a plus

Sean is the GOAT. Literally so chill. Made my first semester at Cornell so much easier. He does not care if you are a good writer or not; it is all on your own ability. Workload is super manageable, and class is fun because he is a chill guy. I'll miss you, Sean. - D

Professor Sam has a really chill, laid-back teaching style that makes the class feel low-pressure and easy to enjoy. He assigns 10-20 pages of reading every week, and very chill essay assignments. He's very nonchalant and handsome. Easiest A if you show up to class.
Great, fun class. Sean is kind and actually about his students. I got a lot out of this class.
goat, replies to emails quickly, take this class

Sean is so friendly. He is really understanding of students' writing abilities and schedules overall. He doesn't assign too much work at all (only three essays) and gives excellent feedback that improves your writing.
he is literally da goat. Thank you for letting me borrow your Lamborghini yesterday
Professor Sam is the GOAT. best english class i've ever taken
He is a nice and experienced coach, and he also cares about his students and want to make sure that students master the skills. Classes get more fun as time goes on.

Coach Seaman is a great teacher and seems to really know what he's doing. He approaches boxing with a scientific/quantitative view which helps students understand the reason behind all of the movements. He often relates the current topic to his innumerable past experiences. Really interesting guy!
Boxing is fun, Seaman is interesting, a little hard on you. Early time sucked though. I suggest taking his Filipino martial arts class instead, it looked alot cooler.

Don't read the textbook as you can more or less guess the True/False questions on prelims. Also, he reuses 80% of short answer questions, so get ahold of past prelims if you can. Prelims and final are weighted equally, each 28%. Great lecturer

Brilliant economist and wonderful lecturer. Professor Nicholson genuinely has a talent at delivering such complex information in a digestible, and even entertaining way. Great class to take to accompany a heavy STEM class  because it balances out the workload excellently. However, prelims are hard and TAs can't grade so prepare to request regrades

Dr. Nicholson is kind, passionate about his work, and a good and clear lecturer. The class offers very valuable info for any pre-health student. There's 3 assignments, 2 prelims, and a non-cumulative final. The exams can be difficult, but if you are interested in the content, it shouldn't be hard to study for them. I highly recommend the class!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was by far one of the most interesting classes I have ever taken. My only critique is that the tests were HARD. If you have a photographic memory you will do amazing on them because you need to memorize all the slides word for word. Homeworks were very easy but tests were very difficult.

Must-take class for anyone interested in healthcare!!! Very informative class and has a nice curve which helps since tests can be tricky. It's also not very much work if you don't do the readings (only one or two true or false questions per test about them).

Professor Nicholson is a pretty decent prof but lacks some empathy for students' situations. The exams are harshly graded, but you can submit regards. Overall, pretty decent class if you show up to lecture and do the readings, but small details matter.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing professor, tests could be hard but understanding the lecture material and demonstrating that knowledge gets you a good grade. Was super close to getting an A but final messed me up. Anyways though prof is really caring and always willing to meet outside class! Highly recommend

Prof. Nicholson is extremely knowledgable and I found it easy to get questions answered in office hours, assuming there weren't too many other students there. Tests are graded very harshly, however, and even if you have a suitable answer, you may not get credit because you don't use the correct stats or you may not have the correct wording.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing lecturer and a great class overall. Prelims are quite tough though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: TAKE THIS COURSE! I don't know how he does it, but Dr. Nicholson somehow condenses the material in a way that makes this Byzantine system understandable. If you go to class, pay attention, and think critically, you'll come out with more than a good grade; you'll come out with lessons you'll take with you for years to come. Best professor ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really nice and engaging lecturer, but the prelims are pretty tough. Otherwise, the homework assignments were relatively easy and you can tell Sean really cares about his students!

Incredible lecturer, easily one of my favorite classes I've taken at Cornell. Class is very lecture heavy, you basically cannot miss one or else you will miss a lot of important info. You have to WORK for tests but they're fairly graded. Rewarding class.

Solid professor. Well-versed in his field, & keeps contact even after semester is over. Curves final grade, not individual prelims. Generous on point-back system, and always wants to get to know his students more. Would definitely take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Nicholson is a great guy and all, the content of the class is super interesting, but hes just a really bad lecturer. All he does it just ramble on and on during class. Prelims are really strictly graded, you have to hit the keywords in the answer key and literally pull straight from the lecture slides to get full credit.

One of the BEST lecturers I have ever met at Cornell. The content is super interesting and understandable. Tests are open-book and mainly based on lecture slides. Sean is great at explaining things so don't worry if you are confused about anything anytime. Course design is related to current events and very inspirational. 100% recommend!

One of the best classes I've taken at Cornell. Professor Nicholson is not only an excellent, engaging lecturer, but he's also just an amazing person. He was extremely accommodating during Covid/online learning, and made sure we all had the resources the succeed in the class. Assignments were easy and prelims were primarily memorization-based.

One of the best classes Ive taken so far. Exams are memorization heavy, but online it was open note which made them very easy and straightforward. Homework assignments were easy and took little time. Prof Nicholson is super caring and answered many questions despite a huge class. Also got us cinnamon rolls and brought his dogs to office hours!
He is the best prof I have ever met at Cornell. He is chill and gives really good lectures. He really understands his students. You will learn a lot from him seriously. He knows what he's doing.

Such a good professor. Made us cinnamon rolls, includes funny clips during lecture that reinforce points but also are a break up the lectures really well, very understanding with deadlines and timing, willing to adapt the course to covid circumstances, so many good things to say

Prof. Nicholson is a really great guy, very knowledgable, and a fantastic lecturer. The content he teaches is interesting for anyone interested in healthcare. I hear a lot of people say this is an easy class. Don't be fooled, exams can be tricky and the class is curved because of it. You will need to put in some work to do well.

Professor Nicholson is a great lecturer. Everything you need to know is on the slides if you miss anything that he says, because he does go through the material pretty quickly. He includes funny videos from time to time in class that make the class more interesting. He truly wishes to connect with students, which I really like.

Hands down, an amazing professor. His tests can be a little overly specific at times, but they are easy to study for - nothing out of left field - and his teaching style is engaging. He is a professor that is truly excited about what he teaches and you can feel that when he speaks.

Biggest lecture I've ever taken at Cornell, yet Nicholson still made every class engaging, relevant, and interesting. Powerpoints posted online contain all the necessary information, but I went to class anyway because he was that good of a lecturer. Stay on top of lectures and memorize everything for the tests (including graphs) and you'll get an A
reviews.rating_tags: Inspirational--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Absolutely amazing class. Favorite class of my entire life's academic career. He knows his stuff (he's the director of the MHA program!) and this class actually made me want a career in health admin/policy. It's fun, invigorating, and inspiring. He also takes students to Banfi because he's just a cool, normal dude like that!

Very respected and very good lecturer. Disperses fun yet very relevant videos in his lectures that keep them interesting. But he also basically reads off his slides, and he posts them online, so no need to go. Tests are fairly hard, but the class is curved crazily nicely, so not difficult at all. The 3 assignments are easy 100s as well.

Prof. Nicholson is a great lecturer. He can get side-tracked sometimes, but everything he says always ends up relating back to the material. The exams are almost entirely based off the slides, which is good because the slides are well-organized. He knows what he's talking about and takes time to answer individual questions despite the huge class.

Most people would say this class was "easy," but, for me, I didn't do so well on the exams. You learn A LOT about the U.S. healthcare system overall and little things no one ever knows. Prof. Nicholson shows HILARIOUS videos in class and he is a good lecturer. Would I recommend this class: UM, YES!

Nicholson is the best professor I have ever had. He truly cares about the students and is a brilliant economist. The class is fairly easy, with only three fairly straightforward assignments and three prelims that are very fair in grading. I looked forward to going to class--he makes the dry material very interesting.

Very interesting lectures, unbiased analyses of current events. Easy homework assignments and tests, however TA grading of these can fall short sometimes but Professor Nicholson is very reasonable if you take the time to talk to him.

Everything you need to know are on the slides. The key to doing well in this class is 1) study objectives that he lists in every PPT 2) remember trends 3) memorize ratios. I think his prelims are getting trickier. I took another class of his, and they were straightforward. Questions more thought-provoking now. Write down what he wants to see.

Nicholson is one of the best professors at Cornell. SO precise and clear. Definitely go to lectures. You don't need the books, you don't need to read any of the articles at all. You have 3 Assignments all year, not too bad. And the prelims are very similar to past ones! He's great in office hours too.

Took in the Fall of 2013. He is absolutely fantastic, delivers lecture material in a very clear manner and really wants to get to know students!  The prelims could be a little tricky but overall not too hard of a class. Definitely recommend because this class was one of my favorite classes at Cornell!

He was a really sweet guy, and if you go to the lectures and pay attention you will learn a lot. He always prepares notes for the lecture and they are very useful to learn the material/have examples along with the textbook.

Very very difficult course, but Prof Chaves is able to break things down in lecture in a way that makes sense and focused on improving our understanding over anything else. He cares about his students and often hosted extra office hours for his lecture sections. This class is far from a cakewalk, but this is the professor to take it with!
Professor Chaves was a well-versed lecturer and cared a lot about our learning. He gave us nice lecture notes that made it easy to follow along in class, and he had lots of office hours.

An outstanding instructor, academically brilliant, yet humble, kind, very approachable. He creates welcoming environment that encourages interaction, uploads his own detailed lecture notes spring semester with space to fill during lecture, makes learning engaging and effective. He truly cares about students' overall experience. Highly recommended.

Explains concepts clearly, though it was sometimes difficult to hear him during lecture. The course was well structured, grading criteria was clear, and exams were fair. He was very responsive to student feedback, especially regarding exam length and course attendance policies. More practice problems on last 1/3 of material would have been helpful.

Honestly he's the definition of “fine”. He didn't project very well in lecture but his teaching was adequate. Class was well-structured and exams were fair enough. I think people struggled because they didn't focus on the theoretical concepts enough. TIP: Understand DUALITY as well as humanly possible.
Bad. Did not work well with co-professor she was teaching with. Over-indexed on silly quizzes, not much classroom discussion and very little case-based lectures.

It's a very lecture heavy class so be sure to pay attention or at least look back on the slides, the prof is pretty chill and nice. The class is very group based so choose your teammates well for sure.

Shu is the kindest teacher I have had at Dyson yet. She is very passionate about marketing and tries to make sure her students are interested as well. Classes can be slightly boring but that is just because marketing is not necessarily the most interesting. All exams get a cheat sheet, easy A.
The exams were very difficult for no reason. There was barely enough time to complete them.

Resourceful and patient prof who is willing to listen to students' ideas. Gives many real-life examples during a lecture to help students grasp consumer behavior concepts. The course is light on workload (two individual assignments and one big final project). Prelim can be tricky but Prof Shu curves the grade. Have extra credit opportunities.

Shu is a sweet professor who knows a lot about marketing, but her tests are insanely hard. They cover obscure/minute details in cases, have tough marketing math questions, and her practice tests are not helpful at all because they are way easier compared to the exam. The class is light in work until you have a case or presentation due the next day.

Prof Shu is really an amazing professor and is so passionate about what she teaches. Her tests are a mix between concepts and specific stuff - you literally need to take notes on everything she says. Otherwise, the content itself isn't difficult and the workload is manageable. Grading is so slow though.
The class is not that bad. However, Suzanne She is condescending. Good luck!

Shu is eloquent and thorough. She does teach the concepts of marketing quite well but she is not engaging at all. Her tests are difficult but there is end-of-course EC. Class is neither heavy nor light on work or material.

Professor Shu is so sweet and has a really interesting background that fuels her teaching. The class is a lot of work and can be difficult if you don't put detail into things but Shu makes lectures engaging, is understanding when issues arise and is always available to help. She explains things clearly and is an enthusiastic teacher!

Participation is key to doing well in this class. hw is easy, a couple of straight forward group presentations, and no prelims. final was open notes/internet, but still difficult. overall, chill class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Participation is heavily important in this class. Grade is not given until finals week, important to contribute to class discussions and perform well in presentations. Gives great feedback and is a fantastic lecturer. Also brings in great guest speakers.
Very nice professor but you never know what your grade is until the end of the semester. Participation really matters. Only one final and hard to study for.
Participate as much as possible. Prof Tang is very nice, brilliant, and professional.
super dedicated to the craft and knowledgable. best class of my semester by far-- everyone loves Prof Tang. Exams were hard, but paper and group projects were reasonable. Highly recommend

The class is very discussion-based, and participation matters. Aim to participate once a week (every two classes) to get an A (A+ if your average is above this). The class only has one final, so make sure to do well, but it is reasonably easy since it's open-note. She is a great professor, is very smart, and makes the lectures very interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Tang is awesome. She is an engaging lecturer. She is also cares about her students. The class is participation-heavy (participation is a large part of your grade), so make sure to speak 1-2 times per class. The final exam is difficult, but if you actually understand the concepts and know how to apply them, you should be fine.

Professor Tang's lectures are decent at best, but her grading system is unclear and terrible. She does not make it clear how much participation/attendance counts for a grade, and your grade can be SEVERELY deflated at the end of the semester.

Professor Tang is sneaky. She led me on the entire semester, had me think I had one grade, then suddenly dropped me a full letter grade due to class participation. I would say I participated an average amount for people in the class, maybe even slightly above average. Lectures were interesting and engaging and exams/papers were difficult but fair.

Professor Tang is amazing!!! She makes the course interesting and engaging. She is definitely my favorite professor this semester. She is very caring and accommodating. Participation in class is very important. There are many works in this class, including exams, reading responses and papers, but she grades very generously.

Tang is my favorite professor this semester. The class is very chill and discussion-heavy. Her exams are a little challenging, but she will curve the exams. She also gives out extra credit for movie nights and participation in researches. Very accommodating during covid.

Interesting course providing basic knowledge and skills related to Raspberry Pi. However, it is not particularly deep nor highly practical for job searching. I would recommend it to ugrads looking for a fun and educational experience. But if your goal is to strengthen your CV and expand your knowledge for job opportunities, this course may not fit.
He is a really great professor and told us a lot on how to use assemble the Raspberry Pi to build an autonomous vehicle. He is so nice to help us about programming problems.

Shouldn't even be called a professor, taught classes in a messy way that nobody will listen. Act like a "good lab-guy" and pretended to be nice to students, talk arrogantly regarding people's backgrounds in a "smart" way. Really cheap regarding 5725 lab materials. Taught me nothing beyond suffering and end my dreams regarding anything at Cornell.

Joe is super nice, approachable, caring, and knowledgable. Lectures and labs are very clear and organized. The class itself is relatively chill comparing to most upper-level ECE classes, but you can learn a lot. Highly recommend his class, the best class I've ever taken as an undergrad in Cornell.
Great, fun and chill class but I learned a lot. Hes super caring and accommodating to students during COVID. Hes really helpful and passionate about what hes teaching too. Highly recommend.
Amazing class.
Very kind and helpful professor. Class is super easy and has a fun group project at the end that serves as an excellent element in your resume.

Took the class online during the winter term, and it was an easy A+. As long as you submit the work on time and keep up with the due dates, you are good. The only downside is that you have to pay extra to take the class during winter break.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: the best professor you will ever have at cornell
Awesome guy who genuinely makes sure all of his students succeed. If Cornell had more professors like him, kids wouldn't be so depressed. Genuinely the GOAT.

Very flexible in options for taking the exams. Very recommended to do the oral exam. The content is actually kind of interesting, and minimal effort is needed to do well on the prelims. There is a decent amount of writing, and discussion attendance is mandatory. To be honest, you have to be super lazy to not get an A+ in this class.

Professor Silva is the nicest guy. This semester, I TA'ed for him for credit, which involved reviewing articles for his PLBIO 2400 course. Very very little work, but he wants all his TAs to register for 3 credits regardless. Easy A+ and he's nice to talk to. Take PLBIO 2400 with him, and then TA it for him the following semesters, nice GPA boosts.

amazing human being. truly cares about your mental health and general well being. classes are interesting. take oral exam --> you guys talk for a bit he asks 1-3q and ur done. discussion are mandatory but so chill.

Professor Silva is the nicest man. The class is a piece of cake with interesting topics. He cares far more about you doing well and engaging with the material than anything else. Lectures are good and well-organized. Exams are oral or multiple choice. Oral exams are just a conversation and it's worth getting to know him.
Literally the best. He is so chill, the exams are ridiculously easy. I love this guy
Tom is a G!!!
literally the nicest professor at Cornell and the easiest class at Cornell. do your discussion posts, write decent essays once a month, and do the verbal exams and you will walk out with a 100% clean

Great and easy class. Everyone pretty much gets an A or better. Topics are all interesting: genetic engineering, climate change, and biodiversity. Barely any work and the tests are nothing to worry about. Would definitely recommend this class. You do not need a science background.

PLBIO 2400 is one of THE BEST CLASSES at Cornell! really great STEM class for Humanities/Social Science majors. material isn't hard at all & Dr. Silva truly cares about students just learning the material. literally the SWEETEST guy in the world & is so so so accomodating. he's SO CHILL & is willing to give A+. wish every prof could be like him!!!!

Professor Silva is such a sweet man and an amazing teacher. He was especially understanding this year due to Covid and online classes. He even offers his students a way to reach out to him if they need someone to talk to. Great guy. Hilarious even. Def recommend.
Professor Silva is a great guy. I recommend taking oral exams with him. Very easy class.

Silva is a saint and is the. reason why my GPA hasn't completely plummeted this semester. He is such a sweet guy, very understanding, and is willing to work with you. If you read through the slides you will pass with flying colors. My TAs were pretty chill too. 10/10 would recommend.

class wasn't organized well, material seemed scattered, and tests were largely ambiguous multiple choice. i still came out okay, but not because of silva. honestly seems like he's focused more on stand up than on teaching when he lectures. but outside of class he seems like a pretty fun guy. just not a great teacher

Dr. Silva is the the most compassionate professor; he really cares about each and every one of his students. He really is passionate about plant biology, and tends to give the more plant based lectures of this class. A lot of bio intro classes ignore plant biology all together, so this class really tried to stress it. Would definitely take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Good professor. Occasionally his speech is boring because he tends to talk slowly, but he's passionate and compassionate. I enjoyed taking 1440. Also, learning about plants helped me understand the physiology of life better. No need to buy the text.

Really cares about his students, whether they're his advisees or not. His class is pretty big and impersonal, but if you talk to him during his office hours or take the oral exam, you should take the chance to get to know him. Great guy.
Genuinely a great guy. Get to know him during office hours.

This is one professor who actually seems like a genuinely nice guy who cares about the students. Encourages everyone to get to know him in office hours. Doesn't set you up to fail like many other professors

Really fair, chill professor. He really does want the students to succeed and doesn't care about giving out a limiting number of A's or setting up a curve to hurt students. Easy to talk to and approach.
Easy. All the material is in both the textbook and lectures. Go to office hours and he will basically tell you the questions and answers on exams.

Expect to memorize lecture slides. Silva is a good guy, and will be there for you, so GO TO OFFICE HOURS! Try and attend lectures, even if you feel like they aren't mandatory. Having the info come to you more than once will help.

Nice guy,but if you are not that interesting in comparative physiology or bio- this is not the class for you. teaches class w another professor; he loves plants and is very helpful. YOU NEED TO SHOW up to class because the book over explains. the tests are hard, but easier than they were in past years. lots of TF & multiple choice. record lectures!
One of the best professors at Cornell. He is willing to work with you if you want to do well in the class. He pays attentions to the little things so go to class! Say way to get your GPA a boost!

Prof Silva is a great professor. Definitely rewards those who actually try (e.g. ask questions, actually goes to lecture, etc.). Definitely cares about his students. Material is also not challenging but also interesting and relevant, so definitely a great course for non-bio majors to take, especially to fulfill a science req.

Do not buy the textbook, as you will never use it.  This class was very easy, but even if you do not do well on examinations, Professor Silva understands. He does a good job in lecture, and if you talk to him, he will work with you so that you can get an A in the class, by doing reports, studies, etc. to compensate for your exam grades.

He is a great professor who truly cares about his students. You can go to his office anytime to ask questions and he is very helpful. He's definitely one of the best professors I've had at Cornell. I went from being completely lost in class to getting an A.
Crystal clear lectures and exams. He is a great professor and very enjoyable to talk with. A very good mentor to have at Cornell.
he is the man and a very knowledgeable guy
Dr. Silva is awesome. He is crystal clear in his lectures and will go over the material from the previous lecture. He is one of the best teachers I have had in all my schooling.
Great teacher. He has real passion in what he's teaching.

Dr. Silva is very clear in what he expects from you.  He is very approachable and always willing to help you out if you don't understand something.  He gets straight to the point when he's teaching.  He might look a little intimidating initially but he's a great guy.

Professor Slaugh is one of the most caring and respectful professors I have ever met. He is not trying to trick you, and he genuinely wants to see you succeed. The reverse classroom can be tough and his explanations are sometimes hard to understand. I would recommend Slaugh to anyone. He is a great person and is very passionate about his work.
The class is flipped style and the assignments are reasonably done in class. The exams can be difficult but Professor Slaugh added some opportunities for re-weighting which helped grades a lot.

Although the 3010 material can be a bit dry, Professor Slaugh does a great job of engaging students and displays significant expertise in his field. The class is straightforward and easy to succeed in. It is clear that Professor Slaugh cares about his students, going above and beyond to engage with and get to know you.

Service Ops is a boring topic to many, but Prof. Slaugh is probably the nicest professor I have ever had. He is really passionate about what he teaches, and that makes the class fun. This course would likely be my least favorite if it wasn't Prof. Slaugh teaching it. His energy and passion is the reason I didn't groan when doing work or attending

Take Service Operations with Professor Slaugh! Cannot recommend him enough. I really appreciate his teaching style (flipped classroom). The class is tough, but he makes it enjoyable. He's very caring, accommodating, humorous, and just an all around happy guy. It's clear he wants everyone to succeed in the class.

Greg Sloan is one of my favorite professors I've ever had. It was obvious that he really cared about the content and made a point to share his passion with the class. He intentionally made the tests pretty difficult, but mostly so those who were going on to ASTR 102 were adequately prepared. Overall though the class was fun and super interesting.
Greg is great, he is funny and explains all the concepts well, but he opens his powerpoints through the command line and that's a little weird.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He very rarely addressed the content we needed to know
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Doesn't understand that his anecdotes during class are unwanted and unneeded, especially when they take up 70% of class time. Also doesn't keep silent when his colleagues are teaching.

She makes lectures as interesting as possible and always makes sure to answer students' questions throughout class, thoughtfully. She grades with mildly high expectations of what students will submit (specifically final paper draft and other materials). Readings discussion posts twice a week are assigned.

Professor Slayton was amazing. She was engaging as a professor, cared about my success, and kept the lectures and readings interesting. The readings are long and are assigned for each class but are very important for success.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: Professor Slayton is great! Her slides are detailed and informative. Her quizzes are very fair and she tells you exactly what she expects, and everything comes from the slides. The readings were a little challenging, but before quizzes, she reviews concepts from them that she wants you to know. Her paper assignments are graded fairly as well.

I don't really write reviews, but Prof Slayton is someone that deserves the recognition for her work and care for her students. Readings can be technical, but she really breaks them down to help you understand. Can get kind of boring, but the concepts are still interesting. Grading is very clear, and she gives A LOT of help and feedback on essays.

Definitely a gem. One of the most passionate people I've ever met. Not a professor to take if you're expecting a lot of concrete, foundational skill teaching. But a great one to take if you want inspiration, artistic insight, laughs, interesting discussion and critique. Overall, leagues beyond anyone else in the department that I've had. HE CARES.
Inspirational. Wish every professor could be like David.  He made me love art even more.
A young, friendly, passionate professor. You will never regret taking his course, for he is an amazing professor with open-mindedness and respect for students.
J.P. cares deeply for his students. If you don't love film when you enter his class, you will by the time you exit.

JP is truly passionate about his field. As a filmmaker himself (who travels frequently) and with a PhD in Media Anthropology from Harvard, he brings perspectives to the table that not only revolutionizes your mindset of what filmmaking can encapsulate, but rather, how it provokes. The films he shows you are mind-blowing, mostly experimental.

One of the best at Cornell. You have to be prepared to watch a lot of experimental films, the semester picks up at the end but also becomes extremely busy as the two biggest projects we had were done so close together. Very long afternoon class. 4 credit class, but should be 5 or 6 based on workload and the amount of time in class.

JP is one of the most amazing teachers I have experienced in my life - he gives you the tools to unleash your creative energy with vengeance. If you are considering taking a class by him I recommend watching one of his own filmic creations prior if you want to get a full taste of what this man is about before you commit to a class.
very interesting class and interesting projects. highly recommended!! excellent professor!
Amazing professor. Always helpful. Made me become a CS Major.

It was a very easy class grade wise (don't let high grades fool you: the average will be high, too, and that's really what matters). The TAs were almost always in the lab and willing to answer questions, even when it wasn't office hours (more so when it was). Made me want to be  TA for the class, though I have no interest in CS as a major.
Awesome prof. Very helpful, good explainer. Made me decide to major in CS.

Snow is the best professor I've ever taken for at least three reasons, but his high standards are difficult for some students.  1. Great content: Snow developed and honed his content over 30 years. Great stuff. 2. Detailed, frequent feedback: He provides detailed written feedback & one-on-one tutorials. 3. Accountability: He holds us to standards.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: The best teacher I ever had: what I learned from him solidified my career.  As another poster said, "he will make a genius of you, if you let him."  And yes, he is not always a very nice guy.  Just suck it up and learn.
I really don't think his class is that difficult.. as long as you pay attention in class and do whatever he tells you to do.. you should be fine...
Craig is Great.  He will force you to learn a lot; he will teach you to be concise. You will learn to write 3 word sentences, and one sentence paragraphs.  And they will have impact!

He's the best professor I've ever had. Sure-- he's tough, but he teaches you everything he knows. Many "Snow Survivors" (including myself) have received job/internship offers becuase of the way he taught us to write. I tell everyone I know, from A&S undergrads to Johnson School of Business students, to take his class.
Fantastic teacher. Wont be easy but you will learn a great deal
If you want a low GPA take this class.  Snow is extremely difficult

OMG. never had to do so much work in my life. Because of him, I slept 6 hours everyday. One thing (and probably the only thing) I learned from his class is do not procrastinate. OR YOU WILL HAVE A BIG MONKEY ON YOUR SHOUlDER

Snow is hard. He will make you work your butt off with prelims and a final report that other communication classes don't have to do. In addition, he will make you attend an "optional" morning class at 8:30am.
You will acquire better communication skills. But also, be prepared to learn how to overcome "redtape" all semester. Also, Snow likes to pick his favorites;this class can get "political."

The only thing really "clear" in Professor Snow's class is his ego. A good teacher does not spend 60 minutes describing tasks and only 15 teaching material. A good teacher does not (noticeably) pick favorites or play mind games. You can learn just as much with the other HA-165 professors. Case in point, avoid Snow at all costs.

The Snowman is truly an awesome professor--probably the best in the Hotel School. The skills that I acquired in his class are the most useful skills I've gained in Hotel School classes so far. It's easy to tell who took Snow's class and who didn't. His class is hard, but if the Snowman sees that you're working hard, you'll do fine.Take the class!
Great teacher.  Big pain in the rear.  I'll never forget bad 80's music because of him... HIT ME WITH YOUR BEST SHOT!
Snow's course will change your writing and thinking. (Note: I was not close to an A in his course). If you get an F, take him again.  He's worth as many Fs as it takes.
Shouldn't these comments have more structure, clarity, and content? 'Nuff said.

Class with snowman is no walk in the park. So if you're looking for an easy A don't get him! but if you're willing to work hard and put effort into the class, you will be fine and get so much value from it. Just remember that snow doesnt give out grades - you have to earn them!

The professor knows the subject like nobodys business but he is subjective in grading. If you are a girl with pretty smile, and you know english grammar well you are lucky. If you are a guy the battle is lost, dont even try...

Prof. Snow is an unbelievably inspiring person: he can help you identify and further strengthen your writing and speaking talents.  If you do poorly in his class, it is strictly a reflection of your lack of effort because Prof. Snow not only makes every writing tool and skill clear and available but he also reinforces what he's taught you daily.

i agree...although snowman does deliver value and has changed my writing abiltities, his arrogance and unnecessarily tough personality get in the way of his teaching. he could be just as effective, if not more, if he considered changing his tone. its about learning, not grades...but with him, be prepared for the worst!

He is a JERK, why does he think that the only way to reach students is to talk down to them and make them feel like crap. He's more worried about his reputation of being a tough professor than he is about teaching his students. I agree that the course content is very helpful, but I think his teaching style is a huge detraction!
No Comments

He's awesome.  Having this class first semester made me realize that it's not always about the grade (especially in the Hotel School), because I did poorly but learned a lot.  He changed my writing style for the better, and I keep in touch with the Snowman to this day.

He is unfair and a liar. He has a lot of pull in the school so don't think you can ever stand up for yourself and get away with it. He will teach you a lot but you will do very poorly in the class. Go to his resume writing seminar at the end of the semester...you will be set for life!!!
Makes writing the paper so hard. The guideline for writing this final paper is 100000 times longer than the actual paper.

VERY HARD class... he's a very nice but intimidating guy that prides himself on having one of the most annoyingly hard classes in the hotel school.  LOTS of personal attention, including mandatory one on one sessions reviewing papers.  Students pride themselves on having survived his class.
He made me cry, but I learned a lot.

love/hate relationship. strikes fear in the hearts of all students.  his standards are frustratingly and impossibly high, but he'll make a genius out of you if you'll let him.  tons of personal attention.  intimidating as hell
Hard as****.  If you have the chance to get out of his class.  Do it ASAP!!  Please do not think this is a joke.  He's an ****.
tough class - tough guy - pray you don't have him
No Comments
Very difficult class, he will expect nothing other than perfect from every student.
snowman rulz yo. but a tough mofo
He is horrible....;(
No Comments

Adam and Lori taught Heritage Forensics- caring, seriously knowledgeable and the lectures were super interesting. They were also approachable despite me being a little intimidated by their expertise. I actually didn't like the class because of the coding (bad tutorials) and the main project (my fault, ran into dead ends too late to change sites).

Professor Smith's lectures were very informative and followed the assigned readings very closely. The readings were a must since every class began with a series of (sometimes overly specific) iClicker questions that were graded for accuracy. The few projects in the class were fun and really helped understand the importance of the material!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Almost impossible to pay attention in class and lectures are the audio equivalent of reading a dry textbook. The amount of reading required is massive with reading quizzes every class. The way the material is presented might be interesting to those very interested in the topics, but otherwise you'll find yourself falling asleep.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Smith is super engaging and very knowledgable in his field of work. The lectures were all very interesting and heavily based on the readings assigned. The readings along the lectures worked really well together in getting you to understand the concepts. Heavy on discussion but a really good overall experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: *BIONB 3240 & PSYCH 4230. David is a very laid back prof- sometimes to a fault when he's late sending things out, etc, but it's def worth it bc it makes his classes v not stressful. He grades easy. In the lab course the grade was based off 3 papers, a short test, and participation, all graded reasonably as long as you can write a scientific paper.

David is exactly the kind of prof. I have been looking for. He's smart, interested, engaging, knowledgable, loves answering questions (we didn't get to some lecture material at the end of the text because we asked so many questions). The text is great and I read every page, I recommend doing the same. Definitely learned a lot from him and the text

Good teacher and class if you are interested in the subject, otherwise you'll probably go nuts because it moves fast and is challenging. He is a good lecturer though. Major downside: he tests on little things from the reading (like factoids in the side boxes). Don't worry about detailed descriptions from the textbook though.

This class was pretty challenging. The professor did a good job of explaining things in lecture, but it was still hard to know what to learn for the exams. I took the class pass/fail, but going into the final, I wasn't confident that I would pass. The writing assignments are easy and help your grade. I would recommend the class, but expect to work.

Interesting lecturer. Some material was pretty dry, but for the most part, classes were interesting. His tests are pretty easy (if you study a little, you'll be fine, and he drops the lowest one anyways). The few short papers we had to write were also graded very leniently. Good professor.

I thought he was an excellent professor. He made material which I often found confusing in the textbook crystal clear. Tests are hard though, so you definitely have to read the book and study, but he's always willing to clarify things you don't understand.
Awesome professor. Really nice and approachable.

Awesome professor. His lectures are extremely organized and easy to follow. He makes somewhat tedious material very interesting. Most of the material on exams are from lectures, but he does require that you read the book. He drops the lowest exam grade which helped me a lot. Definitely recommended.

Very good professor and great course. Smith is clear and makes a de facto neurobiology course unintimidating without dumbing it down. He knows you are absorbing a ton of specific information and writes fair tests. The simple formula works: read and go to class, which gets increasingly interesting. A nice enough man who entertains (common) regrades.
Very good explanations. Follows the book closely. Lecture slides are very useful, and the diagrams really help. Good class, learned a ton.

He's a great professor. Definitely the best I have. The lectures are fairly interesting, but definitely read the textbook. He lectures well and tries to keep things interesting. He's also good about reminding of assignments and tests and telling what will be on the test.
Great prof, great class.  Lots of rats.

If you do attend the lectures, take notes while you read, and actually study, the exams aren't too bad. Smith's lectures are really good. He is great at clarifying complicated topics, an is an engaging lecturer. Easy grades on papers, EC opportunities, can drop one prelim. 2 papers about 3 pages, 3 prelims (drop 1), plus a final
This is not a Psych class its a neurobiology class. He is a great lecturer but his tests are hard and he has quite the ego.
good guy. he's very smart but fair. he wants students to learn, He's very very enthusiastic about biopsych.

Instructor Smith is an extremely thoughtful lecturer, generous with his time with students and very approachable. His lectures are well organized and takes students' input and surveys very seriously. His class examples and tests are challenging yet stimulating and has excellent comand of the subject.
Mr. Smith was an excellent lecturer, he made fairly complicated concepts easy to understand. You could tell he was really putting time and effort into the course.

Man, Prof. Smith is so poor at communicating the message across that it makes the class way harder than it really is. Having taken AP stats in high school, I know most of the topics are exactly the same and yet I learned more from my high school

I had no idea what to expect when signing up for this class, but I can honestly say that it completely changed my outlook on the idea of parenting. She's brilliant, and yet still seems happy to be teaching us. The 4 quizzes shouldn't be a problem if you go to class and take notes. Take this class, it will change your views on everything.

Small is an excellent teacher. She goes over the material slowly, and honestly seems to enjoy talking with us. However if you don't come to class or don't speak during discussions she tends to get exasperated.

Small gets great enjoyment out of having the power in the student-professor relationship and is convinced that she is always right. The information in the course is interesting, but her attitude ruins everything. She also grades harshly. Do not take this class.

Anthro of parenting was the best class I've ever taken. Meredith is HYSTERICAL, and the whole class consists of drawing from your own lives & her stories. You read a ton but it's fascinating and she ties it all together. Write down her every word during lectures; she makes it clear what's important. The final paper is actually a blast.

Anthropology of Parenting was one of my favorite classes at Cornell. Very interesting and low stress. Seems like a lot of reading, but as long as you skim and can discuss, you'll be fine. Only 5 quizzes and a final ethnography project. Prof. Small is amazing!

Anthropology of Parenting is a wonderful class- the readings are fun and not too stressful, and your grade is based on 5 quizzes and a term paper.  Prof. Small structures the class this way because she wants you to do well and learn something; she's not out to kill anyone's GPA, unlike many profs at this school.  Highly recommended.

Had her for both intro to human evolution and anthro of parenting and she was awesome! I wish I was more interested in biological anthropology because I would love to take more of her classes. Tests/quizzes are easy, straight forward, and there's not BS. Great book, interesting lectures, great classes!

I took Human Evolution (Anthro 101), and it's one of the most interesting classes. She just lectures and shows slides, but the material is really interesting. If you go to lecture every day, you'll get an A. No prelims/finals/papers. Only 5 quizzes - 10 min each! (Quiz every 2 weeks) Very low stress. :)

i took anthro of human mating - INTERESTING CLASS!!
