She's a really good lecturer (just talks and writes on chalkboard), but her tests can be nitty-gritty at times. the books to read were incredibly interesting. i will most likely be taking anthro of parenting because i love her so much - but p/f because she's hard

One of the best at Cornell. Excellent teaching skills, friendly and dedicated to her students. Passionate in her views...and I think this is a great thing! Rocked my socks...and I would take 10 more classes from her if I could Get into a class taught by this Prof...not to be missed.

Small had a large chip on her shoulder.  I remember a statement she made on the first day of class regarding pre-med students (I was not one): " I will NEVER change your grades!"  Professor Small, It's really about learning and understanding of the information.  Right?
The answers she looks for on tests don't have much to do with the questions she asks and in her lectures she contradicts the books we read. Kinda hard to get a good grade, but I learned a lot.

Small is an excellent teacher.  She does a great job of tying an understanding of humanity into how we can go about living our lives in such a screwed up world.  There is nothing hard about this class but it is very interesting and informative.

She's not a great teacher. I don't know how someone so average as her is so established in her field. Anthro is an interesting class but the grading of her tests is VERY subjective on the essay parts.
Very thorough. Friendly. Exams are not terribly difficult or detailed, which is nice.
No Comments
Uses her professorship as a podium for left-wing pontifications.

One of my favorite professors.  She takes these incredibly complex philosophy writings and explains them so simply, yet so fully.  She doesn't water down the philosophers, she explains their points better.  She's liberal , and she felicitously attacks conservatism.  You will never be discriminated against for being a conservative. She loves debate

I'm not sure what everyone's talking about, she didn't push her agenda and made sure that the lone conservative in our class felt comfortable. I think she's an amazing professor, and I've learned the most in her class thus far at Cornell. She's not an easy grader and she expects a lot but we're at an Ivy league school. She made me feel like it.
Tough material but a good prof
Pushes her political agenda in class, stubborn and narrow-minded.  Avoid if at all possible!
Pretty good class.  Apparently A's are possible. :)
An incredible professor, but "stubborn" is understating it! "Stalina Marie Smith" on some issues, but definitely take her classes!

Smith is difficult and occasionally stubborn, but she really knows her stuff and wants to help the students.  She's received an undeservedly bad reputation becuase of people who are too sensitive and grade-obsessed.

refuses to admit a mistake. too concerned with form over content. stone cold heartless prof with no people skills and completely unrealistic expectations. don't take her class if you can help it. will never give an A.

Shes passionate about the course content, but she mocks student and has no clear criteria for greading. Oh, she doesnt grade, her TA does. Avoid the TA Xiaoyue L, very unfair grader, you'll get many 0s. Can't speak english, and refused to explain anything clearly. RUN if shes your TA!!! not a hard class if you have better TA. Readings are boring.

I really enjoyed this class a lot! Prof. Son is very caring and approachable, and she does a nice job keeping everyone engaged. There's not too many assignments for this class- 1 short writing most weeks, a midterm, and a final project + short essay. The class is pretty discussion heavy. I feel like all the topics are super interesting though!
Absolutely unfair. Mocks students for taking class for an S/U option. Unfair and fickle grading criteria; does not know what she's talking about. Thick accent makes her lectures difficult to follow.

Prof. Son is great!!! She is caring and always very patient. Students in class had good discussions and connections, and we felt being respected. I enjoyed the class with her. Definitely one of the best professors at cornell!
can only get A- if you dont do extra credit assignments

She changed everything! In-person daily vocab quizzes to study for on top of the daily HW assignments, weekly in-person lesson quizzes (these take up the entire lecture time and should count as prelims and follow that structure tbh), and additional HWs due on Saturdays.... 1102's content is already harder than 1101, but to triple the work is a lot.

Prof. Song is still a great professor. KOREA 1102 is a little harder than 1101 though. You have to learn a lot more grammatical structures and vocabulary words. An A is still achievable, but you will have to put more work in. Attendance policy is the same. The final project is a group skit.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof. Song is a kind teacher who cares about her students. Daily discussion is primarily taught by 3-4 TAs and attendance is mandatory (absence for 2+ weeks = grade drop). Lectures are taught in English 2x a week. NO PRELIMS/FINALS! Just a final project! Remote biweekly lesson quizzes. Daily homework. I went in knowing NOTHING and learned so much!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The most structured and organized class I have ever taken. You will learn Korean extremely well if you complete everything on time and show up to discussion. If you want to pick up the Korean language fast and are willing to put in the work, this is the best class ever and Song ssn is the best professor out there.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very helpful and clear. Is "strict" about attendance and homeworks etc, but if you put in the work, you will learn the language

She is awesome! She's always willing to help out with any question, will incorporate Korean Drama clips into the syllabus to show examples of people using certain expressions. The only annoying side (as is with all language courses, is the daily WAL at Noyes, but oh well...). The homework is not bad either! Definitely recommend her! 재&#48120

She teaches Korean for people who have absolutely no knowledge of the language. Really nice, funny teacher. Will try to be "strict" but that just means she wants you to attend section...which is part of your grade, haha. Very helpful, highly recommended!

She thinks very highly of herself and doesn't take the time to know her students or ensure they understand the assignments. I highly recommend Emily because you'll learn more.

On the other side, she'll just give you an A if she likes you.
Very kind and always willing to meet outside of class. Obviously cared about her students and wanted us to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She was amazing. Really kind, and please please take the section led by her if you are worried about introductory spanish. Don't take Emilia's section (I've heard bad things from friends who did)
Fantastic professor.

Prof. Yoon is nice, but she rambles through incomplete topics and vague grading deadlines. She harshly critiques work using concepts just barely taught in class. She forgot the name of her own class during a critique session. She rejected a proposal to install a subtle but objectively effective safety feature in a product designed for the elderly.

I took 1150 & 3301 with her, even though her feedback is sometimes savage (she will ask you to redo your thing) but prof. yoon really cares about her students a lot. Plus she is very lenient with deadlines.

It may not seem like it at first but she really cares about her students and wants them to become good professionals. She's pretty funny but gives tough,realistic critiques/feedback. Even though its a four hour studio she usually leaves within the first two hours for meetings so a lot of the time is just work time. Lenient with deadlines.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Lectures are crazy fast and confusing, and probably won't teach you design skills--get ready for Lynda. Projects take a lot of time and may cause crying/binge-eating pizza. "Mama S-Y" is really there to help you develop yourself as a designer. She'll work with you individually, give (savage) feedback, and serve as a very patient, caring mentor.
If you pay attention and take notes you'll probably do well. They try their best to make the content digestable. Go to the prof's and TA's office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Profesor Sockin is a kind passionate teacher who wants to see us succeed. That said, he is intense and has high expectations. First test average was a 50/75 with only a 4 point curve. Provides review sessions for all tests, including practice exams. The content is hard and he has no intention to make it easy, if you don't like econ run away now.
He'll get better at this with experience, but at this point he is way too harsh and expects more than people can give

Based on three psets, three exams, one essay. If you attend class, pay attention, and take good notes,  the psets are easy. 
Both prof & TA are super accessible in office hours and by email. can ask them about pset questions too.
The exams are fair. Put in effort, do practice problems consistently throughout the semester, and it'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Terrible. I can't even go into how bad this class was. Do NOT take it with Sockin or else you'll be miserable
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hands down the worst professor I have ever had at Cornell. His tests are so much harder than every other professor for labor econ, he flies through the lectures way too fast, and he grades everything so harshly. Worst professor, and the TA was TERRIBLE.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a funny guy and sorta personable but his tests are very hard (averages

Professor Sockin ate down in his first semester teaching this course. He was very kind and was always willing to help during lectures and office hours. His lectures were pretty dense, but he was very aware of that and clearly differentiated what would be on prelims and what concepts were solely there for our comprehension of economics. Recommend!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very impressed with Professor Sockin for his first semester teaching labor econ. He was extremely knowledgable on the subject, accessible outside of class, and the tests were fair. My only complaints were that the lectures were extremely dense and the tests/problem sets were mostly definition based rather than solving problems.

Dr. Sockin is a great professor and I enjoyed his classes very much. The thing I would say is that the workload for his class and difficulty appeared to be much more compared to other ILRLE2400 classes, however, he knows this and at the end of the semester, he curves the grades to be on distribution curve relative to other ILRLE2400 classes.

I'm currently taking his class--lectures are heavy, and there is lots of content he somewhat flies through. P sets are fair and he is very good at explaining questions. You must go to office hours to succeed in the class, but he is very accessible and walks you through the problem step my step. Would recommend him for the requirement!

Very overrated professor. While he was better than Juliana, he did nothing to help with making the tests reasonable. Instead, it was all subjective and vague. Also, he can't be accessed outside of class at all. His lectures were fine, but he would mention something once that would appear on tests but never on the lecture/learning objectives.
Very funny, engaging. The course required lots of reading from the textbook which sometimes didn't show up in lectures.

Seemed a little bit egotistic when talking about his personal affairs; did not reply to a single one of my emails. Also did not step up when the tyrant Juliana gave us unreasonable test after unreasonable test.

His lectures were really engaging. He's funny and you can tell he really wants students to understand the material. In lecture participation is very important for the course and he often stops to answer questions. If the option is available and you're interested in a scientific career, take the Writing in the Majors discussion option.

Professor Daryl Spurlock is an amazing and inspirational educator. His genuine care for students and passion are contagious. While there's a lot of homework, it's all relevant and valuable. This course is five-star quality. The workload makes it challenging, but the knowledge gained is worth it. I highly recommend it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: While he has sadly moved on to Tufts, Spurlock was one of the best professors I've ever had for Spanish! He went beyond teaching and really tried to connect with each and everyone of his students. His OH were very helpful and he'd always explain things in an easy to understand way. I have no doubt that you'll learn great things from him.

Professor Spurlock made lectures engaging and interesting. Although the class was horribly structured by the Spanish department, Spurlock kept students interested in the subject and provided us with great feedback in class and in office hours. It is sad to see the corrupted Spanish department push such a dedicated professor away.

Exceptionally kind and caring professor, a real gem in the department! Great at breaking down grammar concepts while making classes interesting with lessons on culture, history, and current events. Extremely accessible, so take advantage of OHs especially to talk about the essays and oral presentations. 10/10 professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Extremely caring. Accessible outside of class and is willing to meet and discuss anything, whether it be how to get better at grammar, get better at essay writing, or the oral. You'll never fall asleep in his lectures; literally the most animated lecturer ever and genuinely passionate about his material. Content is a lot but he adapts it.

One of the best Spanish instructors I have ever had. Enthusiastic, caring, prepared. He is so deeply understanding of his students and understands what it's like to be an undergraduate with other responsibilities. There is a lot of homework associated with 2090, but that is not his doing; it is the nature of the course and the coordinator.

enthusiastic, compassionate, patient, knowledgeable. welcoming environment. includes info about dialects, history, current events, culture. cares ab student wellbeing & learning more than grades. 2090 is a lot of work w/ frivolous rules but Spurlock didnt care if we followed them. tests were hard. learned a lot & attribute it to Spurlock, not 2090

I have never had a Spanish teacher/professor who is so accessible and understanding toward his students. Highly, highly recommend--he rekindled my love for Spanish! That being said, 2090 does have a lot of homework involved, but it is assigned by the language department not the professor himself, so there's nothing you can do to get out of that.

2200 was one of my favorite classes I have taken at Cornell. Not saying it's an easy A by any means, I put a lot of work into this class. The exams are very specific and you have to pay attention in class to get everything out of it. The two papers are graded pretty leniently though, so it is definitely doable. I would definitely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: In my personal experience, I found myself working extremely hard without improving over the semester. I did not find it clear what we were expected to learn for the test despite going over the lectures and the textbook rigorously. The lectures are incredibly dense and boring and the amount of information that we are expected to know is unrealistic.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: If you don't have a solid background in the brain, this class will be more on the difficult side because it is a lot to know and it is not always clear what we should know. The tests can be hard and the lectures boring, but they grade the two term papers fairly and somewhat leniently. Going to lecture is very helpful but not completely necessary.

I definitely recommend. He is very intelligent and shares some great information. The 75 minute classes can get boring and he tends to mumble, but hes a really cool guy and knows his stuff! Very approachable too. Exams are fair and he curves if need be.

Very intelligent and approachable. Takes his lab seriously, but always wanted to make sure the RAs were happy.  Research is very interesting. Definitely talk to him if you're interested in his research.
Squyres is LEGENDARY. Awesome lecturer, hilarious, AND he worked on the flippin' Mars Rovers. What's not to love????? Definitely one of my favorite professors here.
You'll not regret it. This man is LEGEND.

I enrolled in 1700 not knowing who this dude was. Holy crap thank goodness I took it on a whim! Favorite class so far. There is a crap ton of reading, but you only have to read enough so you can participate in discussion (it's not on exams). I got a C- on the midterm and cried, then I got it together and received an A-! TA Nick is very helpful
I hate this subject I love this man  Tests aren't that easy if you're taking an intro class to fulfill a requirement, but it's worth it to hear this man talk. Love him
Amazing professor. He is so passionate about astronomy and well respected in his field. This class is definitely worth taking.

Hands down one of the most interesting men I've ever met. Great lecturer (took two courses with him, history & astronomy), and it is very obvious that he has a strong passion and great enthusiasm for both his fields of study and teaching in general. Also, holding an important position on the Mars Rover Program, he gives interesting updates on them.

Only one word describes this guy: incredible. He's so passionate about everything he teaches, but especially in this class because he is an explorer. Whether or not you grew up following Squyres' Mars Rover missions, you will love this class. It's truly one of a kind, and so is he. Best professor ever.

Possibly the best class I've taken at Cornell so far.  Lectures were fascinating and readings in the second half of the course were especially fun.  Probably the only time I'll be able to read about an explorer and then have a Q&A with that explorer the next day.

Class is fairly easy. Tests are based entirely off powerpoints; not necessary to read the text. You do not necessarily need to attend lecture; but you must review the powerpoints before the test! I urge you to attend though, because Squyres is a very interesting guy. The Mars Rovers reviews are very fascinating.

This class was by far the most amazing class I have ever taken! There were a lot of guest lecturers which were interesting, but when Professor Squyres taught on the NW Passage, North & South Pole Exploration, Space Exploration, and the Mars Rovers, the lectures were incredible and un-missable. I'm so glad this class was a part of my education!!!
Lots of people fall asleep in lectures, mars updates are cool but useless for exams. the class is boring and sections you just do math worksheets or other useless information.
Riveting.  He makes the science exciting and the whole thing comprehensible.  Conveys the big picture and then brings details of his own work into class.  Challenging but boy, is it worth it.
Great course.  Graded on a few writing assignments that require research... but the essay topics are certainly interesting.  Squyres is definitely dedicated to teaching his students.
This guy is a genius. You learn a lot from him. The big BUT is that his exams are beyond difficult.

This class has been my favorite by far at Cornell. His lectures are always interesting, his Mars Rover updates are awesome, and he's just a really great guy. I'm taking ASTRO 280 in the fall with him and I cannot wait. He's the best professor at Cornell in my opinion. Take this class, you won't regret it!
He is a good professor but is not clear about what information is important for tests.
one of the best classes I have ever taken.  Squyres is amazing and i HIGHLY recommend
AMAZING class. I suggest you take it. Squyres incredible.

Incredible Professor.  Engaging, articulate, and very excited about what he's teaching.  I could've gotten the same grade in the class by not attending a single lecture - but instead didn't miss a single one.  Sadly enough it was what I looked forward to throughout the day.
Astro 104 was great because of his lectures. I looked forward to his mars updates everyday. He helps make Cornell world class by bringing his expertise to the class.

Cool Guy. Loves what he teaches and gets very excieted about Astronomy. Being a Lead Investigator on a really really big space mission such as MER is beyond awesome. Good Luck in your future endeavours Dr. Squyres.

His lectures made the class worthwhile.  I wish he hadn't been splitting the lectures with the other prof.  A bit harder than normal for an intro class, but again I think that was the other prof.  Overall brilliant guy, great at lecturing.
Excellent lecturer.

Squyres is amazing, great guy and great teacher, who loves teaching. He saved this class from the other prof, Margot. Take whatever class you can get into that Squyres teacher, as long as J-L Margot doesn't make up your tests.

Great guy.  Really knowledgable and practically experienced (he is the lead scientist for the Mars Rover Expedition).  Great lecturer - clear, makes the material intresting purely based on the science, not on lame gimmicks.

Mike is one of the most underrated professors in the university. He might not be good presenting a material for the first time, but he wants the students to learn and is ready to help at any time. He is really flexible with deadlines , PSets and homeworks. As long as you show him that you are putting effort into the course, you are in a safe place.
He hates his job, it is not the students fault

This man is a disgrace tot he Cornell campus. Michael Spencer was the worst professor I had during my 5 years of undergrad and graduate education. His grasp of the material in his compound semiconductors class is poor, rendering him incapable of writing a comprehensible test. His LAZINESS is truly epic.  His class is an utter waste of time.

Terrible lectures, unorganized notes, forgets to assign/return homework, shows up to tests late, told us there was no time limit and then wrote "30 MIN LEFT" on the board an hour into the prelim, worthless labs requiring individual reports separate from your partner, answers questions with "I don't know," doesn't respond to emails, etc.  Awful.
This is a hard course both to take and to teach, but this was just awful.  He tries, but it just doesn't work.  Be prepared for a very disorganized course.

Horrible. Worst professor I have ever had. Avoid at all costs. Very unprepared. Very unclear. Doesn't know what he is doing. He wrote the worst midterm of all time. It was full or spelling errors and typos. He probably hadn't even solved the problems himself. In a class like 315 where the book is notoriously poor, you need better than Prof Spencer!
This guy definately acts like he doesn't want to be teaching the course, he is very unorganized, homework was not returned until after the drop date.
No Comments

The content and assignment of this course are in no way helping an attendant. The way to determine the date for presentation is unreasonable, the content in class is boring, the assignment is pointless……I can still go on but I think I've made my point.

Prof makes up imaginary projects with no real details, so you end up inventing everything yourself. Nothing is grounded in actual knowledge or practice, and assignments feel completely pointless. Feels like prof has 0 teaching experience or doing real projects. My condolences to everyone coz you can't even avoid this class.

Professor Das is a great and caring person who really wants to help students understand content from a industry perspective. While the content of this specific course might sometimes be either boring or difficult depending on if you come from a background where you already know about statistics or not, professor Das does her best to help everyone.

Her class was by far the most disorganized class I have taken at Cornell. She has no rubric or grading scheme, so she just assigns you whatever grade she feels. Her classes also have no structure. She doesn't each anything in class, yet she expects you to know all the complexities of presenting and consulting in her unnecessarily long projects.

Avoid her. She made the class unreasonably intense. I completely agree with all the points mentioned in the 1-star previous posts, especially regarding her overwhelming sense of self-righteousness. I found her unbearable. It seems likely that she rated the 5-star reviews herself.

BTRY 3090 not 5954- I'm not sure how to add another course. I took this class as a statistics major elective and I was close to dropping it before the first prelim but I'm SO glad I didn't. This class was possibly the most useful and applicable class I've taken so far, and Professor Das was so caring and invested in us. It was hard but so worth it!
strict criteria and non-sensical grading expectations. The workload is not reasonable and the instruction is vague for all the assignments. AVOID this professor
too many useless group projects. heavy workload. do not take this class if possible!!!!

She is just sharing her working experience when she was working at a consulting company, which may not be suitable for everyone. Also, she likes to make everything as a group assignment, even if a 1-2 page assignment, which is extremely meaningless. So much homework. Not sure why Cornell hires her and gives this course. Nitpicky and troublemaking.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Took this course in fall 2022. New added core course, no idea why it exists and why she is here to teach. Totally useless.

I took BTRY 3090 with her and I really enjoyed it. The class content is not easy, but she's an excellent lecturer, and she really cares about her students, although it did not seem that way the first month of class. It took a little while to warm up but I would definitely take another class with her again. The prelims are hard but manageable.

I gave one point because RMF couldn't receive a negative score. She is an exceptionally unkind instructor with a strong sense of self-righteousness. Often, she would provide advance questions to speakers, creating the illusion of an enhanced presentation, and she frequently resorted to publicly criticizing students.
too intense. RUN don't take please

she has to be the most disorganized person of all time. her lectures are scattered, tangential, and non-structured. she'd be better off using verb lists and other language resources, with grammatical practice. the lack of rigor and precision on her part leads to an even greater sense of disorder. she also makes you do more work than syllabus says.

2204 was significantly less work than 2203. As usual, Sreematidi was very helpful and enthusiastic. Since there were only 2 students in the class, she worked class times and office hours around our schedules. I also got extensions whenever I asked. Sreematidi is a great storyteller, so class was always enjoyable.

This class was WAY more work than just 2 credits' worth, but I learned a lot. The writing assignments are very time-consuming. However, Sreematidi is often willing to extend due dates, so it's not too bad. She also gives very helpful feedback. Classes are a lot of fun. My Bengali reading, writing, and speaking skills improved tremendously.

122 is considerably more work than 121, but it's always very useful work. Sreematidi's assignments are challenging enough to accelerate learning without being too difficult. Sreematidi also gives extensive (in a helpful way) feedback on assignments. The class generally felt pretty relaxed and fun. And Sreematidi brought in some great food, too!

She is quite possibly the most helpful professor that I have encountered at Cornell. She is so passionate about teaching language and culture. Not only does her passion shine through, it rubs off and makes you want to put extra work in!

Sreematidi puts a lot work into her Bengali classes. She's willing to spend hours at a time helping a student. Genuinely cares about her students and knows how to teach. Assignments are pretty easy but really help to learn the material. The small class (about 12 people) made things more fun than my other classes.
You HAVE to really study for his exams and the lecture is not clear. He tends to go off topic ALL the time. Be prepared to be confused,
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's awesome! Extremely clear, endlessly energetic, really bright, and hilarious. His exams are pretty in-depth, but if you study and do the readings you ought to be fine. Cognitive Science 101 was easily one of my favorite classes at Cornell; it's such a pity to have lost Spivey to UC Merced.
Great professor! He inspired my world. Its a shame he's leaving next year to California. Funny and enthusiastic. Also easy A.

The sheer boredom of the class is only matched by Spivey's inexplicable energy in teaching this awful subject. Do NOT be fooled by the first few lectures, which are indeed interesting, but then the "fun" drops dramatically. Do not buy the main text book (Mindware) either, it will not be tested on and you will likely not understand it anyway.
Very funny. He doesn't currently use swords, but lectures are still entertaining. I learned a lot, and, yeah, he does look like Jesus.
Fun class to attend!

He looks like Jesus and he knows it! He brings robot toys into class, shows cool videos, and makes demonstrations. Sometimes gets technical, but the tests are always fair. Classes are fun. Workload easy.

spivey has great enthusiasm which is contagious... i now intend to major in cognitive science or some related subject. he is funny, obviously very intellegent and an all around swell guy. take this class! i love going to lecture, no other 1 hr 40 minute class has ever flown so fast
i love his enthuaism! the subjrct is really fun too

Very light workload and entertaining class, a break from the usual ECE stuff I took. I can't understand why other reviewers say he's unclear- he's explains things very well, and the material is pretty simple to begin with. Subject matter was interesting. Or maybe just compared to engineering?

Very boring class.  Readings are pretty much worthless.  Not recommended unless fullfills requirement.  Not an easy A either.  Just worthless.  Teacher's nice enough and occasionally funny, but why does that matter?  I'd rather do less work and get better grades.
The class is okay, but I'm already sick of his sword.  I also tend to think that I wouldn't like him too much if I knew him outside of class.
the sword thing was a bit theatrical and didn't exactly compensate for his lack of clarity but the material in this class is really interesting

The class is interesting however the lectures are not as entralling enough to truly appreciate the material.  It is an introductory class, but Spivey could work on the lecutres. On the other hand, his sword is cool, and you can tell he has a lot of enthusiasm for the course.
Great prof, great sense of humor, and very easy grader. Lectures are very interesting. Oh yes, he also looks like Jesus and uses a variety of swords instead of laser pointers. Recommended.
BORING class... Spivey is a nice guy, definitely entertaining, but as a lecturer, he could use some improvement in clarity...
The man looks and acts like a pirate. All teachers should take not of this and try as hard as they can to mimic it.
No Comments
Spivey is such a nice man!! Great sense of humor/brilliant/very kind and understanding!

His lectures are excellent and clear, and in this particular course he covers an incredibly diverse array of topics while maintaining a clear idea of what they all have in common.  He is also the only professor I've ever seen who uses PowerPoint well.
His lectures are great although they move really fast.  My one piece of advice...get takenotes and then just sit and enjoy the class.

Take one of the writing sections, if you have a little extra time, because you'll do more work in total, but you're almost guaranteed an A (at least in my section we were).  Spivey's lectures are very entertaining and you will learn a lot.

His lectures go by pretty fast, so you have to pay attention and write fast.  On the other hand, his tests are very easy if you study from your notes. It's worthwhile to get the takenotes for this class.  And then there are the swords, of course. :)
No Comments

Spivey is the man for the following reasons: (1)He doesn't like pointers, so he uses swords instead. (2) His long hair makes him vaguely resemble Jesus, at least from the back of Uris Aud. (3) Each lecture ends with a trippy "Moment of Zen.
Really charismatic and extremely competent in complex mathematics.
Good amount of homework with the lecture modules, but literally the best professor and class ever. I had 0 background in anything stats, and he made it so easy and made me actually enjoy it.

Great guy, decent class. Basu tells good, interesting, content-relevant stories during lecture. Homework and tests tended to differ a fair amount, but he is explicit about what you need to know for exams. He's fairly receptive to student concerns, this is a good class to take.

LOVED PROF. BASU!!!! Take his class he was a wonderful professor who actually carried about his students. If you go to his office hours he is super helpful and ensure that you thoroughly understand the content. Intro to R was so great too! TAKE THIS CLASS

King. He is so funny, caring, and just a great professor. His lectures can be a little boring if you're not interested in data science, but he finds ways to keep you engaged. The quizzes and homework were easy and the group project would have been if I had better partners (choose wisely). I looked forward to going to lecture every day.
the class was light (very fair grading and easy exams). he was lowkey funny too

Great teacher, paced the class extremely well in a combination of in-class lectures and out of class Canvas modules. There is a participation grade with occasional in class/in lab polls, but is explained clearly in the syllabus. As someone who took Stats during high school, Professor Basu brought back familiar material in an easy to understand way.
Really nice and funny. It was his first semester teaching but class was really easy as a non-STEM person. Def take for requirement
very easy class and not mandatory to listen to lectures, and great caring professor who checked if students felt stressed or not!

Professor Basu is funny and caring and makes an intro STATS class easy! He teaches in R, and assumes you do not have experience. The class contains 3 prelims, a final group project, weekly homeworks, and preparation videos. The work is very doable, and there are a lot of resources if you need help! A great professor, and even better person!

Financial Markets and Sustainability with Professor Thakor was my favorite class of the semester. Both professors have experience in that industry and that really adds to the quality of the lectures. He's a fun guy and the lectures are extremely interesting, though I will say there is less of a sustainability focus. Complex topics but chill assignm

If you only go to class and don't make an effort to see him otherwise, you may miss a lot of value -- some of the most interesting conversations I've had with him were talking after class or in office hours.

Funniest professor I've had in any class - hands down. If you're interested in either finance or sustainability, you'll get a lot out of this course. You don't need to be an expert in both; just having curiosity in one area makes the class engaging and worthwhile. Highly recommend! Best course I've taken.

Great professor! The lecturers have real experience from working through the financial crisis and have seen so many developments in the financial markets realtime. Lots of realistic insights that make the lectures super engaging. Great guest speakers. Assignments aren't too hard. Highly recommend.
One of the best lecturers I have had the pleasure of listening to.
One of the best lecturers I have ever had the pleasure of listening to.
Such a good professor! Funniest lectures and very knowledgeable, he does go on and on sometimes but its all very informative.

Professors Sudip and Tobin are exceptional, offering great content with genuine care for students. Both have impressive backgrounds as Managing Directors at Credit Suisse. However, the TA, Branham Culpepper, was the worst TA ever. The TA falls short in support, grading and clarity, often cancelling office hours and struggling with tech assistance.

Genuinely funny guy, lectures are long, but he makes sure to make it worth your while. There are books required, but I just checked them out from the library instead of buying, they were pretty easy find since they're all classics.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: It's obvious he knows what he's talking about, but I sometimes had a hard time staying interested because class is basically him talking at you the whole time. I thought he was pretty good at explaining difficult concepts clearly, though.

Swedberg means well, he's just sort of 'aloof.' And not gonna lie, his lectures bored me to tears. However, if you pay enough attention to get the gist of what is going on in class and write in a clear, organized manner, you will do well.
Very entertaining lectures, clearly knows a great deal about the subject, and enjoys including anecdotes about the authors' lives and about life in Sweden.

I don't think this class was boring at all. it is very easy to relate the material to your life. I think Swedberg is the best sociology professor in the department. He livens classical theory by relating it to art history, for goodness sake!
As long as you go to class you will do well. His lectures can be boring but they're better than doing the readings. I didn't read anything and went to half the lectures and did fine

Swedberg is extremely intelligent and really cares about his students.  Soc 395 is interesting and he really wants to make sure that his students learn. Definitely take a class with him if you are a soc major!

I agree with the other reviews: the professor is good, it's just that the material is shove-pencils-in-your-eye dull. Poor, poor soc majors. What makes it tolerable is that he's a nice, soft-spoken, pleasantly old-school kind of guy with a sly sense of humor. But don't take this class unless you have to.

Professor Swedberg was a good professor. He knew his stuff and seemed really interested in teaching. His accent is entertaining as is his humor. Unfortunately, my dislike for the material made me hate the class with a passion. Incredibly boring and pointless, but easy. Swedberg makes the class bearable.

His style takes a bit of getting used to, once you do you can learn a hell of a lot from this guy. He's a very frank and objective academic which is often hard to find in a field of big egos (Nee, anyone?) . His slightly self-depricating humor combined with the heavy swedish accent sometimes had me laughing out loud. Mandatory attendance is a pain.

Classical Theory (of soc.) is required for Soc majors, and is a large lecture with not a whole lot of interaction available throughout the class.  Swedberg really knew his stuff, and would have been extremely if I was even remotely into the topic.  He attempts to make some jokes. I did really well on the tests but lost pts due to attendance factor.

Prof. Swedberg's apparent enthusiasm for what he teaches really makes you want to listen to him.  He is one of the most ernest I've had at Cornell.  Though the reading can be dry, the class is not hard at all.  Swedberg is, in general, a really likable, inteligent guy.
he is really smart and nice though sometimes the class is boring (but at least it's easy)
He's really nice and obviously really loves what he does, though he hates big classes.  The material is so incredibly boring though.
Easiest class Ive taken.  20% of ur grade is signing in to lectures.  However, you'd better leave after you sign in unless you want a nap.
No Comments

He's a really nice guy. A little wierd when he waits at the end of class for questions. He's a bit hard to understand at first and lectures are a bit boring. You'll get an A if you do the readings and sign into class. It's worth it to take.
while his swedish accent and mild manner are at first a turnoff, prof. swedberg proves to be one of the most clear, organized, intelligent, and knowledgeable profs around.
Had him for classical theory; funny in class and very knowledgeable. It was a privilege being in his class.
While I understand why some people feel uncomfortable with her fickle style but she is a good person and is underrated here.

Prof Sun cares extremely deeply about her students and their learning. Took her for 3525 last fall and couldn't recommend it more - everyone complaining seems to be overreacting. Be proactive and show up in her class and it will be fantastic. She really cares and I will absolutely be taking her classes again.
Nah, trust you'll be saving your academic career and sanity by not taking this class.

To clarify the amount of reviews for 2435 are higher than the amount of 2435 students in the spring lol. The class was definitely extremely difficult but the reviews are a bit harsh. It's a history class: participate and do the readings. 
I agree that background knowledge was required for the presentations/interviews--we go to an ivy league though.

Stop the hate lmao, she was a bit harsh but learnt way more to account for it. These reviews are taken over by a select few who decided to review multiple times. Coursework was rough, but I came in the class to learn and got what I wanted. You have to learn to deal with it.
ok i lowkey had to learn a bunch in this class and got treated a bit harshly, but yall gotta realize that sometimes it has to be hard to learn... like??
idk why people are being so rude for no reason??

Worst history class I've ever taken. Expectations/criteria unclear and changed syllabus as late as March;as a result, grading is based on vibes. Graded on an interview+presentation; you aren't taught how to do any of these things. Expects high amount of background knowledge on subject matter. Very disorganized class, with no clear direction. Avoid.
I have honestly never received such a poor and unfair grade in my entire academic career.

If the course really sparked so much resentment among so many students, they should collectively report it to the administration - the professor's tenure is unlikely to be revoked, but the history department could ask her to teach fewer courses and do more research. There's not much point in commenting here.

She dumped the course load on students with zero guidance, then acted like giving actual feedback was beneath her. I went to office hours and somehow ended up in a therapy session about me, because she refused to talk about the class. Then she handed out grades like she was drawing numbers from a hat. And let's not forget the unprovoked yelling,
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Disappointed in the history department. If you decide to take her course, just hope she read these reviews and learned to do better. Else, unless you're really insightful and can politely talk over her interruptions, you might get on her nice list. Any student any study? She'll tell you off if you don't know everything before taking the class.

should've dropped this class instead of hoping it'd get better.agree w previous reviews+anecdote abt her disorganization:each class,1student presents on the reading due.there's no tracker on who presents so we had classes where two students presented or where she rambled bs for an hour(doubt she read).the 5 was probably written by her phd student.

Add on: she will give you NO indication of grades, bullies students who are presenting, and bases grading on whether she likes you. I have an above 4.0 GPA and this class single-handedly ruined my prospects of summa cum laude. She does not teach whatsoever, instead relying on students to give presentations on articles written by other scholars.

I'm pretty sure the 5 below was written by her! Worst professor I've ever had at Cornell. Once in class, students asked clarifying questions, she responded, "I don't care, I am tenured." As a student who has taken many history classes, I'm shocked at the administration for allowing such an unqualified, rude, and vague professor into the department.
these past reviews are all outrageous! Prof. Sun was a great teacher, she taught me a lot.

absolutely avoid... the content may be interesting but the professor is so rude and disorganized that it takes away from any enjoyment at all. she doesn't communicate her expectations and then lets students' grades take the hit for it. always interrupting people, making vague and irrelevant metaphors.. and god forbid you ask her a question!

If you like your GPA, avoid this class. Professor does not communicate grading standards at all, and your end of semester grade is seemingly random. She likes to bully students in class, and teaches nothing but expects students to already know everything. If you like Maoism, borrow a book from the library. Do not take this class.

Add on pt2: I was SO excited to take this course to learn about Maoism as it's been an ongoing interest of mine. Was most excited for THIS class this semester. Not only disappointed, but received an arbitrary grade after the class gave me nothing.

Add on the prev review: never had a prof that didn't teach but didn't make time to answer questions. Asked what she thought to be thought provoking questions that didn't relate to topic at all. Constantly cuts people off mid sentence to insert her -irrelevant- point. Gave feedback on arbitrary presentation flaws such as what bullet points you used.
she'll respect you by learning your name but that'll go out the window once you get up and present!

went into the class expecting to learn from her but every class is a presentation on the reading due that day from a student. already disappointed. on top of that, she interrupts student presentations so nitpick irrelevant things and go on tangents using metaphors that barely connects to the conversation. didnt learn anything from her. disappoined.
She was a very poor lecturer. Seemed to have no interest in teaching whatsoever.

mandatory attendance despite the professor themself saying that the lecture slides are "passive review" and not how you should study for the exams. not to mention BIOMG2800 is 100% problem solving and 0% memorization which is not how it is ran anywhere else in the country
Made exams hard, bad lecturing style, do not recommend

This rating is for BIOMG 2800. Her tone in delivering is plain, which can easily make someone lose track of attention. She is not very helpful during office hour as she is not good at explaining through questions.
Very interesting and great class. Highly recommend taking this class. It is not terribly difficult and half of the class is participatory discussion. Loved it!

Not a particularly hard class and very interesting material, however, her lectures are monotonous and lack any clear objectives. She does not appear to be interested in teaching the class delivering the material in an uninteresting manner supplemented by poor lecture notes. As such there is almost no point in going to class.

Lowkey she's THE baddie HR boss lady. Some days she wears a magenta blazer and she eats downnnn. I never did any of the readings, and I did just fine in her class and was able to participate every day. Her tests can be tricky, but if you actually study for them (which usually people don't because they expect HR to be easy), then you will be fine.

Amazing Professor! I took her HR class and as a shy person, she made me feel comfortable enough to speak up and get participation. She is also very caring and accommodating to individual needs and makes the content relatable and easy to digest.

Professor Lakhani is one of the most flexible and easy-to-understand professors in the Hotel school. She is clearly knowledgeable in human resources but always willing to learn and be open-minded. HR has a very light workload and easy/fair exams, making the learning experience enjoyable and stress-free.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Lakhani is one of the best professors in the hotel school. She cares a lot about her students and is accessible outside of class. Classes are largely discussion based with chances to do discussion posts instead of speaking in class. Prelims and group projects are graded fairly.
Super easy professor - would definitely take this Intro to Public Policy class in the spring semester instead of the fall.

Professor Tach was one of the best professors I've had at Cornell. Through the semester, it was abundantly clear that she genuinely cares about her students and wants them to succeed. Plus, the lectures are super engaging and really interesting - if you're even kind of interested in policy, absolutely take this class!
great lectures and incredibly fair grading - light workload for a 4 credit class

Prof. Tach is the sweetest. TAs grade all of the essays and pretty fairly. Quizzes were very easy and took 15 minutes max. Very light workload for a 4 credit class and a great introduction for kids interested in policy; not intended to weed out kids at all. However, can be redundant for policy majors taking second semester freshman year.

She is so nice and helpful, and also very knowledgeable. Quizzes are extremely fair and reflect exactly what we learned in class (plus there are study guides). The project and papers give you a lot of freedom to research something you're interested in which makes this intro class more engaging.
Literally all you have to do is do your papers and do well on two quizzes- very easy class

Overall a great professor. The class is quite easy. There are a couple of group projects to complete and present that are well planned out. Exams were take home online. Also there were a couple of papers to write.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Interesting class about housing, good diversity class choice. Don't really even need to take notes I just sat there and listened. Assignments were not too difficult, a few group projects that were a decent chunk of the grade. No exams but a few in-class quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Tach is such an amazing person, so understanding of external circumstances and truly accommodating. She's a great resource and so knowledgeable. This class specifically is pretty broad, so not too difficult, plus your grade is made up of a bunch of smaller pieces, so easy to bounce back from any (unlikely) setbacks! Take it!

Prof Tach is AWESOME - so knowledgeable, very friendly demeanor, just overall great vibes. she knows what she's talking about & she does a great job of engaging the class. she's VERY good about putting grades up - you will always know where you stand in this class. would definitely recommend this class - interesting topic & material!

Prof. Tach is awesome! Really enjoyed her class, despite it being online. Lectures were great and informative. There's a fair amount of work/projects, but nothing overly tough and the projects teach you more about the material. Would definitely recommend the class!
Good lectures with lot of examples. Easy to follow and get a good grade. Not much work.

Total Number of Hours attending lecture: 1 Total Number of Hours reading book: 0 Final Grade awarded in Class:  A+ Teacher Satisfaction : 100%. Student Satisfaction : 100%.  "Mickey Mouse Course" as she calls it.         Welcome to DisneyLand.
best teacher i ever had if you have this woman as your teacher, you are very fortunate. no other teacher like her at cornell.
Way beyond easy... Mickey mouse course, in her own words. Sucks that she's leaving
This is the easiest class I've taken in my entire life (including high school).  She is a great lecturer.  Don't buy the book!  You are never going to read it.
Awesome prof, best class I've had so far at Cornell. I would recommend it to everyone- not just soc majors.

Easy easy easy class. She's hot and a good speaker. The way she has her tests makes you learn a couple of things really well, but also makes it insanely easy to get an A. A great elective if you have a hard semester! Maybe 5 hours of work all semester.

Excellent class... vivid teaching style allowed for students to do well without reading primary sources.  Lecture slides give all the pertinent information for exams.  Also extremely kind and understanding.
really easy course, told us the first day of class we didn't have to go to lectures or do the reading

Szonja is the nicest professor I know. She is a great lecturer, has a very good sense of humor and simply makes the class a very enjoyable experience! To top it off, she is the most understanding and kindest professor I know! Beautiful person!
so helpful for all your sociology needs, will give you soc credits for anything, but is genuinly intersted in students.  Also a great teacher, even though not so challenging.

I actually looked forward to the trek out to Morrison Hall for her class. One of the kindest professors on campus. Just when you think that all of your professors are out to get you, take a class with Prof. Szelenyi!
Compassionate, sincere...Also easiest class you will take @ CU. Students love her! A real people's professor. Very accessible, friendly, and has entertaining anecdotes sometimes.
SOC101 is a great class where students are encouraged to do well.  The short and sweet answer to all of your questions: take it.  You will not regret it.
Sonja is absolutely wonderful. The class is entertaining and interesting. It's the only class I haven't skipped yet and I have it at 9 in the morning.

easiest class at cornell. topics are just barely introduced, not for people who really want to learn sociology. her lectures are very entertaining and she often makes jokes that are actually funny. and one of the hotter female teachers at cornell.
So hot
She's very lively and nice. Sometimes she goes too fast, but she always posts lecture notes online, so it's not a problem. I would definitely recommend taking this class with her.
great and enagaging
Great teacher, really engages students in the subjects.  The class is relaxed, which allows students to simply enjoy what they are learning.
The best class in Cornell with the bestttttt teacher.  Its a relaxed class but u learn soo much... TAKE SOC WITH HER ONLYY
She is great :)
No Comments
Simply amazing. The department IS lucky to have her!

The MOST helpful, MOST accomodating, MOST engaging, MOST wonderful professor on this campus. YOU WILL LEARN, but you will actually enjoy every minute of it! Cornell and Soc department are lucky to have her.
dA bOmB!
fun, interesting
No Comments
No Comments
Easiest course's taken at this school.  she is so great, you actually learn things in her class, while it is easy.  she also has a great accent, very sexy.
No Comments
AWESOME!!!!!
Easily EASILY the best professor at Cornell - the nicest you'll ever meet!
Super sweet

She is an amazing professor. I could feel myself getting better at Spanish throughout the semester. It is a decent amount of work but it is a very fair class and I learned so much. She made class very fun and enjoyable and I can't say enough how great she is!

She's so funny and nice and I really respect how clear the grading criteria was. As someone who isn't that good at Spanish either, I loved being able to learn the grammar before class so I felt confident about my participation (which is really important!!!) Class is def not easy though but you'll 10000% be way better at Spanish by the end

14 years of Spanish and I never looked forward to class until Brisa. One time she gave everyone the option of writing an imaginative essay or a thesis essay. Everyone was going to write a thesis, then she gave an lecture on how to use your imagination. By the end, nearly everyone was going to write an imaginative one. I got an 100 on it. She's GOAT
Something's wrong if you don't love Brisa. Sweetest professor at Cornell.

She was a great Spanish Lecturer. She really ensured that students were understanding the language. If you have the opportunity, try to get her as your discussion section instructor because it was really useful to establish a relationship with her where I was comfortable.

Amazing professor. SPAN 1120 was my first language class in college and I was very apprehensive going into it because my knowledge of Spanish was very rusty. She made it impossible for me not to learn the language. She cares about her students and wants them to do well.Attendance is very necessary but her class is fun so there's no reason not to go
Amazing teacher very clear grader one of the nicest profs I've ever had!
Great

She was my first Spanish prof at Cornell so it definitely was a rude awakening but I think she is one of the better ones because she tried not to follow the flipped classroom model (which I really dislike). I got a B but I was proud of it because I worked for it. Tests were tough but most other things just took time and energy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved Brisa's class. I took SPAN1210 last semester w Tomas Bevia and this semester was much smoother. I recommend trying to get in her section because she explained concepts really well and knows what to correct. Spanish was my favorite class this semester and I actually looked forward to coming to class. I wish Brisa taught the next class too!

Would avoid at all costs. She is inflexible (forced me to take a zero instead of moving a quiz when I could not be in town due to an interview, for example). She also claims there to be particularly correct analysis for any given piece of literature -- an obvious falsehood. Avoid.

Excellent!!! Truly cares about the student's improvement. Always offers helpful feedback and answers all questions. Clarifies any uncertainties about readings. Overall truly taught me so much amazing things and made Spanish so much fun!

I went in being very scared of her. She's a very tough grader with the pronunciation labs and definitely makes you work for your grade. She is truly a lovely person though who will do anything to help you succeed and will give you the grade you deserve. Very easy to do well if you put in the effort a 3 credit course warrants.

Very harsh in this pronunciation class. She has good and bad days, and if you present on one of her bad days she will rip you apart. I've heard she's good in lower level classes but her criticism on pronunciation in this class discouraged me from ever wanting to speak Spanish again. In general she is nice though.

She is a very clear and helpful teacher if you're set on doing Spanish. The TA (who lead the four times a week sections) quality was high as well. That being said, her tests are extremely difficult and overall the grading is really harsh. I'd recommend doing another language for the language requirement if you don't want your grades to take a hit.

Wow.... amazing woman.  I want to talk about her ability as a professor, but I can't help it--- I have such a crush on her!  Se encanto---       wonderful class, very serious about her work, very caring and encouraging.  Great TAs too in discussion groups--

She is awesome. She is funny and interesting, and her class was consistent and challenging in a good way. I learned a lot from her! She is young and relatable and is clearly on the side of the students. Loved this class!
Brisa is awesome, and the class is a lot of work but fun
really energetic, class was pretty easy. TAs were usually lenient.
Great teacher.
Great professor!

nice person and very energetic and tries to help. crazy about grammar. sometimes idk what she was taking points off for. is not forgiving if you don't have oral presentations perfect. make sure you participate a lot in class
too. much. work. brisa is funny though, and energetic.

Macarena is super sweet and funny, she has strong opinions on the subject material and a clear "right" way of interpreting texts so pay attention to what she says in class. The first half of 2095 was more grammar heavy and the second is more about comprehension - ALWAYS do the grammar reading before class and come prepared for a quiz. And go to OH!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class made me so much more confident with speaking in Spanish, even though it definitely requires going outside of your comfort zone!
Such a queen I love her. Class can be somewhat stressful cuz you have to participate a bunch but generally very doable and all the tests and formal presentations are online

I enjoyed the class + prof a lot! The seminar style made me a lot more confident in my speaking skills. We would read a short story and write a short response for hw, then discuss it for the whole class period. She does have an idea of what the "perfect essay" is and grades according to that (sometimes unclear) criteria but the class is very doable
not a great professor

EVERYONE shows up to class. Is this because its an honor's course with people who truly wish to learn? to some degree probably. However, his lectures are wildly helpful and informative - Brilliant guy who clearly knows his stuff, the enthusiasm will transfer on to you if you're open to it

really passionate professor that is very interested in the subject! the class is very proof based so attending TA office hours was super helpful- recommend taking the engineering one (easier). it is a difficult class but you do get a deep conceptual understanding of linear algebra. psets are moderately difficult but the grad TAs are so so helpful

Not a great lecturer - often spends too much time on examples and sometimes explains things weirdly. Written homework and exams are sometimes not fully reflective of the most recent topics learned. But the class is easy enough that concepts don't require extended analysis.
Tough Grader
Good, ready to help, not great.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Not a good lecturer. Went to office hours and he came across as extremely rude. Difficult to understand. Would not take again.

Obviously a professor who is very passionate about the subject material. That being said, his lectures are often unmotivating and poorly communicated/hard to follow. Doesn't finish his sentences a lot of the time or takes minutes to think of a response. I ended up learning a lot of the material primarily by myself as a result.

Prof. Tebbe is my favorite professor this semester. He makes very difficult topics much more accessible, and he does it in a fun and lighthearted way. He's also very encouraging and is the kindest professor when it comes to cold calling. All in all, 10/10.

Tebbe's class was nuanced & accessible. His discussions are politically neutral & he treated controversial issues objectively & sensitively,, making us comfortable. He posts & reviews problems that mirror test questions & responds to feedback. Leaves some cases for his amendment 1 class. Lots of us want to take it bc this one was great.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Tebbe is cool and charming as a person, but treats his class as an opportunity to pontificate his political point of view. His Con Law class for 1Ls only covered a few topics and left vast swathes of Con Law untouched. I feel unprepared for discussing constitutional law outside of school and annoyed at his closed minded teaching style.

Definitely one of the hardest classes I've taken up to this point in undergrad - regardless he was a great professor and always put a smile on my face. He's very charismatic and passionate about teaching - sit in the front. What made this class hard was understanding the homework for me. However, OHs were great. Use the abundance of past exams!

Great prof for a tough subject. I of course did not do the best in the class but still appreciated his way of teaching. He teaches well and uses analogies to make you learn better. This class 1st or 2nd hardest mandatory classes but Thompson makes it approachable and better

Amazing class and amazing Prof.! The course was brilliantly taught and Prof. Thompson is a genius; as someone here said, "he is a brilliant genius training you to his level". If you want to be challenged and grow academically and personally, take his class. Not to mention that Thermodynamics is the basis for many academic disciplines.

Thompson accepts that the subjects he teaches are difficult, and he really cares about students thoroughly learning topics. He's kind of quirky and definitely really busy, so he can be a bit scatterbrained, but he always knows what he's talking about and has always been helpful in class. Homework sets are tough, often require office hours.

Incredibly disorganized. He showed up late to class every single lecture and kept the class late every single lecture. You will never get your prelims graded and handed back and the problem sets are basically impossible. This class totally turned me off to mat-sci. I would strongly advise against this class or any class taught by Thompson.
Best teacher I have ever met!

He is extremely difficult and gives unclear questions on prelims and problem sets. However, he is also extremely knowledgeable and approachable. He is quite busy and never answers emails but if you can find him in person which is not hard to do, he is willing to work with you and help. Sum up, he is a brilliant genius training you to his level

In my opinion, one of the smartest professors at Cornell. You can ask him literally any question in his field and he will be able to answer you. Unfortunately, he sometimes overestimates the students' capacity to learn new material and goes very quickly. However, he explains concepts very well and you will definitely learn a lot in his class.
Great guy. Material is hard but the guy is helpful.
Extremely smart and humorous professor who can teach very well. Learned a lot from the class. Everyone says that problem sets and prelims do not count towards the final grade, but don't believe them.
Brilliant Professor. Material is extremely difficult but he teaches really well.

Professor Alexander is a great lecturer. He does not use slides; instead, he writes everything live using his tablet. His handwriting can be hard to read if you do not know cursive, but he will review anything you ask. There are 2 prelims and 1 final. You can skip the final if you want your prelims to weigh more, so do well on them. Pop quiz exist!
he wants his students to succeed. go to his OH and he will help you w ANYTHING. if you want an A, put in the work

Lectures are hard but rewarding. He is a great professor who really cares about his students. He hosts a ton of office hours and review sessions that are very helpful. Terry is wonderful, and I highly recommend him to anyone.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Terry is super nice and helpful outside of class. However, the actual class is really difficult, especially if you've never taken economics before. Goes super fast. Tests a vague and study materials aren't super helpful. Go see him outside of class though if you're struggling, he's more than willing to sit down with you.

Terry is a great guy, don't get me wrong. But god, his lectures are hard to follow and the course isn't the easiest. The exams are generally pretty rushed and you will walk out of them thinking you did great and then receive an 80%. If you can avoid, I'd recommend, but it's by no means a death sentence.

Professor Alexander is a good professor and cares about the course and students' learnings. Expect to work hard in the class, and learn. Tests are hard but fair. Mandatory in-class quizzes that could be annoying. Class surprisingly harder than expected. Overall 4/5.

Frequent in-class group quizzes and maybe 5 problem sets, the rest of the grade is 3 exams which are very similar to practice exams he provides. Attendance is mandatory (because of the in-class quizzes). His office hours are very helpful and he's very patient when explaining topics!

This professor is everything I dislike: mandatory attendance, quizzes, strict grading...but I loved his class. He provides abundant study material and test prep, is fair with his grading, and generally a joy to be around. OHs are super chill and helpful. Very knowledgable + clearly loves teaching and his students.

Terry was amazing. One of the few professors that I have ever had that makes sure you understand everything. The pop quiz 1 once a week gets a bit annoying, but they are easy as they ask you about a question that was taught 5 minutes before. I ended up with a 99.3% and got an A.

I really appreciate how he made things easy to understand. The professors Ive had at Cornell have made me feel lost bc they yap a whole lot abt nothing during class and then test you on material that ur not prepared for, but Terry has been one of the only professors who made me feel very confident in the material I was learning. Thank you Terry!

Professor Alexander's lectures are him writing all the information on his tablet so it's easy to get lost if you can't read his handwriting or don't like that teaching style. Although attendance isn't mandatory he does pop quizzes to make up for it. Attend his office hours as he is very willing to help his students!
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The exams are very vague and difficult.

Terry is absolutely open to suggestions and feedback from students. He is very patient with his students and makes sure that his students fully understand the content. He also makes a lot of funny jokes during class.

I love this man. He is the best. He invites his upper level class over at his house for an end of year party. And I wish he kept doing the brexit course for future students - it was one of my highlights of Cornell.
Favorite professor at Cornell. Very caring and understanding with extension and makeup requests. Just go to class, ask questions, and you will get A easily.

There's no other professor like Terry. He meticulously goes over every concept and will force them into your memory with pithy quips. At the same time, Terry is hilarious during lecture and will go on in-depth tangents about the birth of his son or WWII POW camps. He will also call you out for being on your phone. Easy class, wonderful professor.

Most grades are determined by exams, and he does pop quizzes the majority of classes as a way to "take attendance". While this may seem doable, Terry is an un-engaging professor who stands at the front of the room frantically writing notes on his tablet, with no structure or PowerPoint to keep track of his confusing subject. AVOID
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Alexander's class is doable, but A+s are essentially impossible (requires 100%) so don't take him if you're counting on that. His lectures were clear but handwriting was unreadable, exam grading was fair, and pop quizzes were slightly stress inducing but manageable (you need to show up!). Very nice guy though, always helped students out.

Terry is a great guy, and very entertaining, but when it comes to teaching, oh is he bad. He rambles and scribbles illegibly on the board, with no regard for our learning. Everyone I know taught themselves everything before every exam, thankfully the content is not too hard.

Despite what many reviews say, Professor Alexander is not a good professor. He is incredibly disengaging, his notes are impossible to read, and the course is not organized well at all. You are graded on very few things, and the practice problems are hard to find and have no solution. The class isn't that hard, just very boring.

Professor Alexander had great lectures that were very engaging and entertaining due to his occasional side stories and enthusiasm. The finals and prelims were based very heavily on lecture material. Overall, definitely recommend.

Terry is a great teacher. He cares about his students and is willing to help whenever someone needs it. He always listens and will go to lengths to make sure everyone understands the content. People complain about the quizzes but they were easy and my grade went up a lot because of them and they genuinely helped me understand the content.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Terry is one of the kindest and most caring teachers ar Cornell. He makes sure all his students who want to understand macro do. His office hours are so helpful and he makes an effort to know as many students names. There are pop quizzes, but if anything they help your grade, he always reviews the answer BEFORE THE QUIZ.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Terry was a great professor. Initially he didn't post answer keys to exams, but after receiving feedback he released not only the answer key but an entire video explaining the solutions and the point breakdowns. He is a really nice person who cares about his students. He made an effort to remember everyone's names, and it showed.

Amazing lecturer, was always engaged during his lectures. Was also funny, and very accessible through Office Hours and was always willing to discuss material with students. He could seem a little intimidating at first but was very genuine while discussing exams. Exams are representative of lectures.

Handwriting in class is illegible, concepts for exams are very unclear, quizzes almost every day, and practice exams do not have answer keys making the class very difficult to study for. Would prefer having actual PowerPoints in class with clear instructions and step-by-step instructions to do problems. Long tangents on unrelated topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Can not teach students at all,

Ignore the bad reviews. He is fun, funny, and a little bit crazy. Class is very interesting and he's a good teacher - if you come to every class and pay attention! Not much homework but tests are tricky. If you prepare well, you will find that the exam problems are JUST like the class ones.
Tough grader. Minimal curving. Prelims/Final are very hard. Confusing lecture materials.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He explained economics in such a confusing manner. Had to basically self teach myself all of the concepts. He is aware his handwriting is barely legible, but refuses to change his method of teaching.

He's very accessible outside of class (OH almost every day). Exams are okay (although the second prelim was pretty hard). However, he can also sound harsh when talking to students and he doesn't release the answers to practice prelims. There are group quizzes almost every class. Homework is easy. Discussion sessions were basically useless.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Never posted correct answers about exams or gave feedback. TA discussion sections were useless as were lectures
Frequently went off on tangents and always gave long-winded answers about concepts. Never clear or concise.
I could not read his handwriting. He also made a lot mistakes during lectures that he had to correct

love terry. had him for my hotelie micro class and loved the way he lectured (would write everything down on paper rather than have monotonous slides). incorporates stories to make the lectures more digestable. the info i learned in this class was so valuable and i def understand markets way more now. if u know ur lectures WELL, tests are easy.
horrible; no feedback on any tests or assignments
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Terry is patient to explain anything during and outside class. Extremely accomodating with deadlines. Group quizzes on every other session on average. Prelims and exams are fair. Practice with HW and previous prelims for the numerical part. True or False questions separate the A students from the herd so make sure to understand the concepts fully.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Terry is an amazing professor for a rather difficult class as I didn't come in with a good micro/macro foundation. He is great at explaining concepts and was also caring during this hectic semester (made prelim 2 optional and bought us all ice cream). Beware of his pop quizzes in class though.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Terry teaches the class material well. The issue is not with him but rather with the class setup. Tests and homework are assigned randomly, instructions are unclear, grades are stalled, etc. There were not enough TAs for my class so things were very messy. Considering the other options, this Macro class is a solid choice.

Took his class for 2600 last semester, and though my grade was not what I had hoped, I thought Prof. Alexander was one of the best people I've had as a professor. His lectures can be a bit odd sometimes, but he's genuinely trying to help you succeed. I reached out to him because I was struggling with mental health and he was so caring and helpful.

One of the best human beings I have ever met. He was so charismatic, and cares about each of his students. Made concepts very clear, and was really patient with re-explanations, reviews, and introducing material. He goes out of the way to make everyone feel valued, tells stories about his personal life, and makes his expectations clear. LOVE him.
