Terry is not only a fantastic and knowledgeable professor, he is a great person. No matter the difficulty you're having reach out and he'll be there to help. Tests are fairly written, yet cover a lot of content so you cant bs your way through the class. Again, terry is the brotha, love this dude

Terry is by far my favorite professor here at Cornell. He is kind and understanding to all of his students. I know someone who slept through their prelim, only to email Terry in a panic and find out that he would be allowed to make it up the next day. He is also funny and even though attendance is usually mandatory, it is well worth it to show up.

Terry Alexander is the best professor I ever had. He genuinely cares about his students and their success. He once wrote my name correctly on the board, and when he asked if it was correct I simply replied it doesnt matter. He promptly turned, made direct eye contact, and said of course it matters, its your name. Take his class.

Alexander is a nice and interesting person, but his teaching style is unfocused and confusing. His lectures are handwritten notes and unreadable, and many of the examples he gives are far more confusing than those provided in discussion. Tests are mostly fair but contain ambiguous short answers. Regularly goes on tangents that distract from class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Really awesome professor who gives great lectures! Would reccomend to anyone interested in analysis.

Professor Riley is a gem. I took this class to explore proof based math and was enchanted by his enthusiasm and course. Lectures are engaging and rewarding. Homework can be challenging but also rewarding. The two TAs were great. Exams were challenging but the course was curved a bit. Perfect course for intro real analysis and fair rigor.
Good professor, fun class

Relatively low workload as a 4-credit course. Tests are much easier compared to homework sets and past exams. Two lowest homework can be dropped which is great. Good professor but not an interesting class for a non-math major.

He is a funny, personable guy. He's ok as a professor. He spends a lot of time proving things instead of giving concrete examples and applications.  Always willing to help during office hours. For this class, he didn't give in class quizzes and worksheets like the other instructors did, might have been more helpful. Love his accent and hair though.
good

I don't think that Tian is the best at conveying the material, but I still highly recommend ENGRI 1170. The material is not too difficult, so it's not that hard to self-teach. It is also very useful to have an understanding of the concepts in this class for future meche classes. The grading is very generous (most people got an A I would guess)

The class is a fun application of physics to many different aspects of mechanical engineering. Labs are fun and interesting. Exams are extremely fair. More work than other ENGRIs, but super educational.

Confusing + fast AWFUL teaching + must AVOID. Once my friend asked her for help/resources outside of class (do not enroll if you don't know physics before!) and she told them to "just read a physics textbook." iClickers are based on accuracy and 10% of your grade but mostly done start of class so people 1-5 mins late suffer hard. No care at all.

She is an incredibly smart scientist/researcher who definitely has so much to teach. That said, she should not be teaching an intro level class. Her lectures were given at the speed of light and were extremely dense and confusing. Prior exposure to difficult physics concepts is assumed.

Professor Tian loves to bully her students. She gave tests with averages in the C and D range and then refused to curve the class, proceeding to bully and mock students on the class discussion website. She's insane and doesn't give half a **** about her students' well-being. Also is a terrible lecturer. Awful professor, avoid at all costs

Cares about her students a lot but lectures are sub-par imo and don't provide elaboration beyond what the textbook gives (lecture slides cover same figures, equations, explanation, and example problems as included in the readings). If you can learn from the book you're better off skipping lectures to save time. Super kind besides that.

Although I only took her intro to MechE class to fulfill my requirement, it was more informational and interesting than I expected. She has a clear lecture plan for each class, and she posts her powerpoint slides. The homework is doable if you just read the slides, and the tests are easy if you do the homework. She is chill and gives extra credit.

Great professor, really cares about his students and improving their writing. He's very passionate about semiotics but the topic can be difficult to understand. this class is less about understanding the topic and more about effectively writing. His critics are always helpful and he's truly made me a better writer.

Ti is an awesome professor who is flexible, caring, and fun. He meets students where they are, and is more than willing to help if you fall behind. Took ROMS 3210, History of Romance Language. He focused on us learning the material over simply getting the grade. You will do well in his course if you are present in lecture and doing your best work.
Such a sweet man- one of the most interesting classes I've taken at Cornell. The recorded speaking homework definitely piles up and was hard to find time to do in a quiet area, but great class!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Ti is really kind and caring. He will treat you well if you put in any amount of effort. He is also really smart and an interesting teacher but I found his course was hampered by a lack of participation and interest. I'm not sure how much of this was in his control, but perhaps he could have more strongly enforced attendance/participation.
He is very considerate and accommodating. He is very enthusiastic about what he teaches and takes care to integrate a variety of interesting activities.
Had him for FWS Fall 2021, Ti was an amazing professor. Very understanding of deadlines and gives good feedback. Discussions in class were interesting, as well.

The professor is amazing and makes the topic easy to understand. He's understanding about deadlines, which is helpful towards the end of the semester. If you ask him for feedback on a topic or on your writing, he will definitely help you.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Ti was an amazing professor. He wants his students to succeed and is a genuinely nice guy. Highly recommend!!
extremely unclear about grading but gives u rly good feedback as long as u seek it. classes are discussion-based and u rly don't need to have read the book to contribute
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Great professor and fun classes
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Just horrible... Ti has constant mood swings an is very unclear about everything.  He never seemed to know what was going on, and exams were handed back weeks late.  Ti tried to act like he was a chill guy, yet every single one of us were having panic attacks by the end of the semester (let's just say our class did not give him good course evals)
Pretty easy class. When you didn't hand in homework he would give you another opportunity to give it in, even if it was a week or two late.
Excellent professor! Great personality and makes the class comfortable. He is truly concerned with our academic success and interests.

Ti is entirely responsible for my sudden, powerful interest in French. So much that I think I might major in it now. He's sincerely enthusiastic about the material, and understandably so, because it's interesting.
Great teacher, still talk with him years after having taken his course.

Ti is great whether you're interested in italian or just trying to get rid of a requirement. His classes are fun and he'll meet with you any time to cover a lecture (even if you just skipped) He's really knowledgable, but not very tough about sticking to the syllabus. Feel free to ask questions. If you do any work you'll do well

Ti is simply amazing. He is extremely helpful and easy to get along with. I learned an incredible amount from him. The only--and I mean ONLY--frustration I had with this course was in the use of the Language Lab, which could be tedious or frustrating due to software problems.
Very enthusiastic (sometimes maybe even overly enthusiastic).  Understanding about deadlines and confusion; very responsive to student needs.  Can be boring and redundant--it was a slow class.

Ti is a very casual, nice guy.  He is VERY knowledgeable of the material (would spend several minutes of section talking about Italian culture), and, other than some very subtle frustration, he seems like he really cares about students learning.

The only reason students love Ti is because he tries so hard to be liked by them. Ti is your teacher if you are just trying to pass the language requirements cause he'll let you pass even if you do nothing.  He likes hanging out with the students who are brownosers.  He's a nice guy but not a very good teacher.  Plus, he has major mood swings.

Excellent, excellent professor.  Goes out of his way to make sure you learn.  Very interested in students who are interested.  Hilarious, easy going, a great guy.  Very understanding with deadlines and all.
ti's awesome, you're lucky if you're in his class.

Ti is so cool. He is an awesome, really easy going prof. A very fair grader if you are interested and do the work. Also very approachable and eager to make a difference for his students experience w/ foreign language
No Comments
Expected students to follow the course policies. We weren't even allowed to cheat on tests! Required students to learn. Treated us like adults. No thanks!

Stay away for your sanity. The only positive thing about him is he cares about Linguistics and puts a lot of work into his lectures. He shouldn't be a professor at Cornell he has no empathy for students who added the class late making their participation and homework grades lower. He will fully ignore and not respond to emails. He has a huge ego.

Professor Tilsen's lecture are pretty technical and sometimes confusing, but he is a chill guy. He obviously shows a passion for the subject, but the course isn't always taught to reflect that I feel. Homeworks are not too hard, prelims too. Although the homeworks aren't hard, I do feel that they don't really give you sufficient practice
he might be a good person but his lectures are kind of confusing. pop quizes are scary
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: One of the best professors at Cornell! Incredibly sweet and funny, and a very engaging lecturer. There are some annoying things (attendance required, pop quizzes from textbook readings) but exams are straightforward. I wasn't very interested in p-side linguistics before this class (I only took it as a major requirement) but Sam made it worthwhile.

He is clearly very knowledgeable about linguistics and a great lecturer. However, he never stuck around after Zoom lectures to answer questions. It felt like he was doing the bare minimum to teach us. The homework assignments were challenging but reasonable.
Not a very good teacher. Kind of technical. Cocky in a way that makes it seem like he's overcompensating for his lack of ability to teach. Lacks basic human empathy. Stay away from this guy.

Doesn't know how to teach. He has trouble explaining things that the book explains simply. A lot of times, I had trouble understanding what he was talking about, but when I read the book it was clear. He kind of expects you to read his mind.
Gives very hard tests and hard assignments as well. TA Hitomi is not helpful at all. Not considerate at all when students are facing difficulties with the pandemic. Stay away from Tilsen!

Took the class S/U. Lectures are engaging, but sometimes too technical. Weekly homework. Didn't even bother buying the textbook. Good as a very broad basic intro to the various subfields of linguistics.
I think he is new to teaching. I had a frustrating experience with him and I love phonetics. Very cocky.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He doesn't go easy on you, but you're sure to learn a lot.

Prof. Tilsen is a very solid teacher.  He teaches pretty difficult material and is a relatively harsh grader, but he is funny and usually pretty clear when teaching.  If you have a question, he is very good at finding a way to explain things a second time in a different way.

Prof. Campbell provided a great introduction to Machiavellian thought. He facilitated thoughtful discussions and challenged students to apply these Renaissance works to current times. His mind is fast and sharp. Class size was small so attendance and participation mattered. That said, valuable class + professor for students of any major.

Great professor! I decided to take another class with him because I liked the first one so much; he really tries to engage students and create thought provoking discussions. Assigns quite a bit of reading but a very chill and caring professor overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof. Campbell does make you think about the issues you'll discuss in his class, and his own knowledge of the content is well-versed (fascism/modernity is what he researches, after all). He's very laid back and helpful, though sometimes he can be a little too laid back. Be warned: there may come a day where he forgets to tell you there's no class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof. Campbell is an impressive intellectual. He's a really nice guy outside of class, but within the classroom setting he can be a bit too demanding. His classes are good, but you have to expect to participate ALOT in section and do an almost excessive amount of reading and writing.
intense

Prof. Hanrath provides an entertaining atmosphere for students while interweaving thermodynamics into everyday life. Very personable human being. Disorganized teaching style. Provides very useful real world applications of learned material during lecture.

his lectures are the least organized, most chaotic, and most irrelevant lectures at cornell. He loves AI and uses it heavily to generate course material and exams. Super interesting guy, but he does not know how to communicate clearly with students about course material, and you are basically left to teach yourself everything from the textbook

Professor Hanrath is a really nice person, but he is the most disorganized and confusing lecturer I've ever had. The lectures are confusing, he often goes on a tangent unrelated to the course material, the grading structure of the class is unclear. Prepare to read a lot of the textbook when you take this class bc you def won't be learning in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Interesting lecture but the equations that you need for homework were never mentioned in lecture, don't take this if you really need the 1 credit.
The most disorganized class structure I've ever seen.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Solid introduction to PV and thermal solar technology
Nice guy. Confusing in lectures at times, but still good overall.
Very smart professor and great one-on-one or in small groups. Lectures can be a bit confusing - oftentimes, there are just recaps and future outlooks and no material actually discussed.

This might be the worst class I've taken at Cornell. The lectures are nonsensical, unrelated, and redundant. She rarely engages with the course material and instead veers off on tangents throughout most lectures. She has little to no knowledge about AI, so anything she teaches about it are more speculative than grounded in reality

The class is very easy, but you won't learn anything.  Professor typically rambles on about random political topics, and she doesn't really understand technology.  I don't know how she got this teaching position.  Attendance is graded but it's not worth paying attention.

I really loved Professor Mitrano. Now I will acknowledge she is not everyones cup of tea. If you prefer very structured classes with strict schedules/ assignments, don't take this class. However, I thought that this class was helpful in addressing the societal impact of AI. Mitrano is so passionate and willing to meet students where they are.

Seminar-style class with a lot of readings, but is easy to do well in even if you don't read all the books. I appreciated prof bringing in guest lecturers (Google employee, other profs) to explain technical topics. Sometimes disorganized lectures but if you participate in every 2 lectures, you'll get full credit. Attending OH helped with essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
She really teaches to teach, not to get students ready for exams, and cares about your learning. 
The course is challenging. I was almost dropped since the history and constitution slavery etc lost me. But the work broadened my perspective. I think it all paid off

She means well, but her lectures are disorganized and poorly planned, with scribbles on the whiteboard and no clear connection between topics. She often goes on tangents about her personal beliefs that don't add much value to the course. Additionally, the assignment instructions are unclear and inconsistent, making it hard to know what to expect.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS.

Gives out grades without justifications. Let us debate all the time so she can do nothing and just be lazy. Talks randomly and writes down random things on board with no organization. Biased toward immigrants and minorities. Super mean and subjective. Save your time please, don't take her class.

She spends 75% of the class talking about US and Roman history and cold calling about random history facts. The remaining 25% will be cold calling on readings that she assigned. There is no structure to the class. She writes random thoughts on the white board expecting us to understand. AVOID her if you can!

I am sure the 5 rating was written by herself...
Just run, save your time. 
Very subjective, talks about nonsense in class.
I was interested in the topic of AI, but her class just really disappoints me. TAs are mean as well. There is nothing good about her class. Failed politician and worst professor.

DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS. Worst professor I had. 
Came up with the course grading in class, rubric did not exist two weeks into the semester. Grading is very subjective and dependent on whether she likes you or not.
Teach is VERY BAD. She talks about nothing relevant in class. Content is exactly the same as another class.
I LEARNED NOTHING from it.
Great Professor

Prof. Mitrano is the most passionate, caring, and interesting Professor I've had at Cornell. Her teaching combines the history, legislation, and background context surrounding technology which helps tremendously to set the scene of what is going on in our world today. Amazing professor and person.

In one class, we talked about AI, copyright,  the constitution,  American revolution, slavery , Ancient Greece/rome , Slavery , non racebased slavery , Feudalism, Ferdinand and Isabella , Christopher Columbus ,incest,  and nation states. I did not learn anything. Please save your time.

I have never met a worse and distasteful professor in all my time at this school. A FAILED politician who is out of touch with students, class expectations, and reality. Her class is a disorganized mess with no grades in. Assigns 8 books for the semester and cold calls to see if we meet here unreasonable expectations. Shouldn't teach. RUN AWAY!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He genuinely cares about his students. Really wants to grow and push people to think instead of regurgitate. Hi professor Troy your class was awesome!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Troy has a great philosophical mind which is the approach he takes in teaching this class. Very much reading heavy with weekly journal entries. Group blog project to be worked on throughout the semester. No slides to follow lecture, only reads lectures aloud and writes on chalkboard (difficult to read).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: if you want to transform your worldview and challenge yourself, take troy's classes. he's truly one of the most knowledgeable, patient, and skillful educators i've ever had the privilege of learning from. amazing human being (ask him about his life), and his classes are incredible. readings are long, but classes are transformative.

Material is really interesting but professor richardson reads his lectures which makes them hard to follow. He changes the syllabus randomly and doesn't respond to emails. I never knew where I stood with him, he gave very little feedback. I never really talked to him because he seems really unapproachable. I did well but would not take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Vague-- if you can't tolerate changes in syllabus and no-shows at office hours, don't take his class. But as with most professors, if you put in the work and communicate with them, you can do very well. He is at a premiere university, in a heady discipline for a reason. Don't think it will be an "easy" A.

HORRID! He rambled on inaudibly in a low monotone voice, using big words, no one could understand him. He does not reply to emails, and doesn't like answering questions. He was late to class sometimes and never told us when the final was, then changed the date twice at the last minute. Class was very unorganized. AVOID HIS CLASSES LIKE THE PLAGUE.

Great Class! If you actually do the work you get a lot out of it. It about current social issues and gets pretty fascinating. A lot of people fall into the trap of thinking it's easy and not worth the effort resulting in not so desirable grades. Everyone should definitely take.
Worst class ever.  Definitely do not take.  Professor tries to sound smarter by using longer words even when they don't apply.  He gave everyone random grades at the end.  The grades made no sense

Challenging class. Pay attention to classes + go to prof and TA office hours to review! Exams ask questions from what he mentions in lectures. Always go into details when answering exam questions. Very vague in saying which type of questions he will put out during exams. Tip: understand concepts rather than memorizing. (Record lectures if you can).

Such an interesting class!! Prof Devoogd is clearly very knowledgable and really cares about his students. ATTEND LECTURE. Take detailed notes in class and ask questions. Grade is only 3 tests and a paper and tests are only on the lecture slides (don't need to read textbook). Exams are all short answer and grading is subjective.

reviews.comment: Tough class but he is so kind and caring. He has been one of my favorite professors at Cornell. I am so sad he is retiring soon
Very nice professor, but the exams were difficult and a struggle to study for.

reviews.comment: Professor Devoogd class is the reason why im pursuing neuroscience as a career. His class was really interesting to me and I genuinely learned alot. The content is heavy and you need to go to class to pass as it is mostly graded by weekly quizzes. However his teaching style was very clear and he tries his best to make the class engaging

I enjoyed this class, but it is definitely challenging (lots of info and he goes quickly). However, if you attend lectures and the TA review sessions, it is manageable. Overall, he is a sweet and charismatic professor who is very knowledgeable of the subjects he teaches and he does his best to engage students with stories and personal experiences

ATTEND LECTURES!! Devoogd's lectures are super interesting, and it's essential that you go to them. Grades are heavily prelim/final based, and all of the questions will be taken from content/examples discussed in lectures (eg: experiments mentioned, how content pertains to real people/animals...). Readings aren't necessary, but supplement well.

reviews.comment: Doesn't understand how difficult is class is and doesn't respect student's effort. Scale, grading, and extra credit is very unclear

Professor DeVoogd is honestly one of my favorite teachers so far at Cornell. The class is very hard as there is a lot of information, tests are open ended and extremely specific (though you can have a cheat sheet). 78% of ur grade is made up by tests. However, prof is very knowledgeable and sweet, lectures are not too long and are very interesting.

I believe Tim doesn't understand neuropsychology but is able to pull it up so well. You can sense that in his hesitation and slides-over-reliance. Even asking him questions can easily shake him up. Nevertheless, this is a fun class and Tim is able to add his own touch to lectures (almost like any old prof here)

I thought I wouldn't like this class at all but ended up loving it. Tim's tests are entirely lecture-based and I didn't open the textbook once. Also, given that there is no homework, I recommend making some schedule for yourself to study regularly. It doesn't have to be too much but the tests can be really hard if you don't study in advance at all

Professor DeVoogd is an amazing professor. His class is difficult, but it's neuroscience, so you can't expect it to be easy. He's a very sweet professor and cares a lot about his students. You don't have to read the textbook, but attend all lectures because sometimes he puts things on the tests that weren't in the lecture slides.

Never take any class with this professor. The entire grade was determined by 3 exams and two assignments(Worth 12%). You must memorize every minute detail in the class. The averages were 57% and then 69% on the prelims however, the curve in the class is determined by the highest grade achieved, not by the average.  AVOID THIS PROFESSOR.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class grade is based solely off 3 major tests and one writing assignment. Very rarely responds to email. Promised an extra credit opportunity, students carried out with this, and he never followed up again. Dismissed major cheating violations although this is an entirely curved class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: My best recommendation: don't do all the readings. You will never have time for other things if you do. I suggest taking good lecture notes in the form of questions and studying off of those as well as the reading discussion questions posted on canvas possibly with a study buddy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really liked this class, and the textbook was interesting to read. Professor Devoogd knows his stuff. The tests required a lot of detail memorization, which was the main con, but I did enjoy the class overall.

I absolutely loved Professor DeVoogd. Extremely accommodating & the class has weekly quizzes instead of prelims. Each quiz is very detail-oriented but it is only based on the prior week's content so I didn't find it too bad. The final is a cumulative big picture understanding (not too difficult). Offers a lot of Extra Credit. Really nice professor!

I took Psych 3320 with Prof Devoogd. He's extremely knowledgeable about the course material and covers the vast majority of the quiz/final material in the content-heavy lectures. But if you ever need to talk to him, office hours or raising your hand in lecture are really your only shots as he will never acknowledge his emails

Gonna be real frank about this - one of the worst decisions of my life was taking this course. Terribly unclear lectures, incompetent professor, harsh and arbitrary grading, and extremely inconsiderate attitude towards students. Upon contemplating the fact that he is a professor at an Ivy League, I found myself close to a mental breakdown. Disgrace

All jokes aside - worst class you will take at Cornell. Unbelievably incompetent, at times self-contradicting, unclear Professor. Any remotely positive reviews are lying - do not listen to them. Very difficult tests with unanticipated questions. Multiple attempts should be made to get Professor removed from Cornell. Disgrace to Cornell.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Honest review: Hardest class Ive taken at Cornell (Senior, 4.0 GPA). Its honestly shocking to see any positive reviews of the course on here. The class wasnt so difficult because of the material - but because the Professor is extremely unclear & tests have ridiculously unanticipated, specific questions. I dont understand how he is a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This course was fairly straightforward. Tests are all short answer, and they are based almost exclusively on material covered in the lectures (though questions are occasionally ambiguous). You do not really need the textbook. Just study the slides and recordings. For some reason, DeVoogd doesnt always emails, so use office hours if needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Weekly short answer quizzes over the lecture material from the previous week, final paper, and long short answer final. Will need prior bio experience since this is a more advanced course with niche material. He cares about students and is good about replying to emails. I didn't do the readings and still did fine.
He gives no information as to what you should focus on for the prelims. The prelim questions are kind of a surprise which makes it all the more difficult since they are all short-answer questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The Behavioral Neuroscience (biopsychology) class was all lectures. There was nothing interactive about the entire class; just lectures and then the prelims. The lectures were dry and mostly stuff from the textbook. The syllabus says the textbook is mandatory, but I never had to use it. The prelims are long and many short answer questions.

He is nice person who is passionate and kind. I would not take this class again though bc the 3 exams that make up 90% of your grade are ENTIRELY short answer & he expects ridiculously specific answers without giving clear specificity in the questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: DeVoogd is an all around great guy. Cares about his students and is very helpful outside of class. You definitely need to work hard, but the resources are there and he wants to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: I personally feel that this class wasn't as hard as the reviews suggest. Exams make up 90% of final grade. He gave 5% extra credit, which I had 4. GO TO THE LECTURES, or you can in no way figure out how to answer some of the questions. Before exams, memorize his slides carefully, and study the pictures and reviews in the textbook. Median was a B+.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This is an interesting class, but the professor gives no details about what he expects and everything is a surprise. On test, each question is graded separately but no correct answers or feedback is given. He goes on tangents about animals and his research and his friends' research in lecture and tests on small details so pay attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Good, interesting and inspiring lectures, which explain the topics well. Attending the lectures is important to score well. Most of the test material is covered in class, and things he teaches in lectures are far more likely to come on the tests than the general stuff in the text, you can probably just study from his power points and do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Impossible tests. Do not take unless you have photographic memory so you can memorize the textbook. Expects essays on short response.  No multiple choice at all. Lectures are too one-dimensional and are really quite useless. His lectures, however, go over small details that somehow show up on the test.

Last sem was the first time Devoogd taught this class, and it was definitely more challenging than I expected. However, if you studied (focusing on what he covered in class and using the book to get the smaller details), you do fine. Extremely helpful at explaining concepts if you can go to his office hours. Doesn't respond to emails very quickly.

I never write reviews. However, I needed to in this case. AVOID THIS CLASS if it's taught by him. Students have no idea about what's going to be on the test. Literally studied like crazy for this class and still got a C- because tests were so random. barely learned from reading the textbook and going to lectures. All around HORRIBLE TEACHER

AVOID THIS CLASS. Does not respond to emails. Lecture slides are vague. First year teaching this class, an INTRO level course. Blackboard has nothing useful, we have 2 "writing assignments" due at our final, NO information has been posted regarding it. Ridiculous amount of content for tests; mix of book & lecture. Class avg is around C-. Miserable.
not helpful, absolutely irresponsible and NEVER responded to any emails - just plain disrespectful. I loved the subject before i took his class, HATED it after!

He is very detail-oriented in his exams.  Be sure you know ALL of the details in order to pass or else you are screwed.  He is a VERY harsh grader.  In his own words "It's easy to get partial credit, but hard to get full credit".  Don't expect full credit unless you write a novel for each question.

I took Tim's class in Biopsychology Lab years ago, and found it truly a great class which taught one about research protocols.  I also had the honor to work with Dr. DeVoogd in his bird lab, it was a great experience. His class inspired me to go on to medical school and pursue a surgical field.  Highly recommmend it.

Awesome guy...great teacher and advisor. He taught me a lot through his class, but it never felt like much work. The brain identification test is hard, though. Really easy to talk to and knows tons. This lab class requires a lot of time, but is sooo worth it.
This was a great class with a great professor.

Probably the best professor I've ever had. I don't know about his lecture course, but the lab course was my favorite class ever! The experiments were really interesting and I learned a lot. He was also very helpful and I don't know what everyone is complaining about because he always responded to my e-mails within hours of when I sent them.

Used lots of overheads which made class very boring, and didn't provide the overheads anywhere else, so if it was blurry, which it often was, or if it was only up for a moment, which was often the case, you missed it.  All of the tests were graded way too subjectively.
Never has real lesson plans...wouldn't take the class if I could do it over again! Not very reliable and doesn't reply to emails. Tests are really hard.
He was my advisor. waited for 3 hours in his office for my PIN, he never showed, then never responded to my emails after that. Hard to find.
really cares about students.  helpful if asked
more than scatterbrained. completely unable to maintain a coherent lesson plan, much less an organized and fulfilling course as a whole.

He just randomly picks a few propositions, reads the proofs from the textbook, and copies them on the blackboard. Taking his class is like being in hell. You learn nothing and have a mountain of homework. The homework questions have nothing to do with what was covered in class that week because he's fallen so far behind. It's just ridiculous!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The worst course instructor. Read textbook during the lecture,  agree with inconsistent grading among students. If you have very strong ability of self-study, then you can register his class. Otherwise, you will feel painful from the first week to the last day of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Never take his any course. Inconsistent grading, always find ways to deduct points. Also, can you imagine a math course requires students to do presentations?
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Interesting topics covered but Treven didnt effectively convey them. I admit I didn't go to office hours knowing that he had plenty. The prelims were killers. Prepare to study to at least get near the mean.
He should have never been assigned this class; he just goes too fast and expects everyone to memorize all the tiniest details about math.
Straightforward, fair, and very patient in spite of having the thankless job of teaching a bunch of total nonmajors.
Poor guy, can't  teach a thing if his life depended on it. He tried but the fact he kept making math explorations harder than it needed to be made the class dislike him. That's about it.
Calc is never fun, that's for sure. Treven is not an experienced lecturer. To his credit, he always answers your questions and stays after class.
Nice, intelligent guy, though he cannot explain problems very well. He is a hard grader, but very fair. OK class.
Sweetest professor ever
Lots of novel vocab in her speaking makes her hard to understand but good for learning. Ask nicely what stuff means and she'll explain. Wants to make class fun

Viktoria is a great teacher. Like the others in her department, she is very enthusiastic about teaching Russian. She makes a lot of jokes about the Soviet Union, and keeps the class interesting. Her grading reflects her appreciation for students who make an effort (even if they make a lot of mistakes). Intimidating at first, but approachable.

She's fairly strict about grammar, but you want that when you're learning a language. Don't be fooled by her English either, she's much more with it than you think. Her sense of humor is very dry, and some of her comments are absolutely brilliant. I used to be kind of afraid of her, but she definitely grows on you. She's great.
A really great teacher with a good sense of humor.

Agree that on the earlier levels she's a bit strict, but that's what you need to learn Russian! She has lots of fascinating stories, is really up on current events, and if you try hard and talk with her you will have a good time and do well both. Her movie class is really interesting, she will help you and be concerned about you as a person, too.

She can be a stickler on the earlier levels, but if you get to the later courses, she is laid-back and more lenient. Don't mess with her, and you will learn a lot and have a good time with the movies and other materials she uses. Listen to her stories about life in the USSR to pass class time and listen to some Russian.

Professor at Duke University for the FOCUS Program. She clearly has no idea what a university course is supposed to be and utilizes the class to make students read and talk about absolutely irrelevant topics that she probably just picked up from the whatever newspaper she reads. No guidelines at all. She should start a book club, not teach a class

Prof at Duke. Class was supposed to be about ageing and human rights, but we talked about colonialism 80% of the semester. That's fine, but the class was advertised as something very different from what it actually was. Dont take the focus class! My time has been wasted. She's not a great teacher either, but she's clearly knowledgeable and talented

This class was a bit more focussed on technical aspects of jazz than I expected. While at times it seemed to be a bit much, Tsitsi really pulls it together well with literature. Overall, the class is good and helpful with improving and expanding one's writing.

international monetary theory and policy- Has a great, sort of understated sense of humor. Can come off as a bit aloof and intimidating but actually cares about his students quite a bit. Tests are pretty tough, manages to create some difficult questions from pretty straightforward material. Lots and lots of graphs.

He knows his stuff well and is appears enthusiastic about teaching and in trying to involve students in discussion during lectures. However, he seems friendlier to some students than others. He can be blunt and appear to engage in subtle favoritism. Overall, his teaching is good and his regular references to current affairs makes the class exciting

His lectures are all over the place.  You'll have to learn most of the material from the book.  He's a nice guy and young, so maybe his teaching will improve soon.  The tests are kind of hard, but he'll scale your grades up at the end so don't worry if you don't do great on the tests.

OMGG!! If he is any indication of what ukrainian men look like,then im making a trip to ukraine ASAP!! The concept of diminishing marginal benefits for activities doesnt apply to the time one can spend gazing at his alluring lush eyelashes. I only hope he will teach teach more classes.I love econ bc of him and his manly eastern european mannerisms

First time teaching undergrads, became cynical at end of term. Course not difficult, he gets lost in his reasoning sometimes and gives up in explanation, but normally very clear. Set clears expectations for exams. No hw, willing to help. Good class.

Helen is GREAT! She is a great masseuse that really understands the stresses of being a Cornell student. She shows you step-by-step the different techniques. This class, Swedish Massage, is a fantastic class to take, it really helps relieve stress, it feels great, and it gives you some new massage techniques to impress your significant other.
Helen is a nice woman that teaches in a manner that is fun to learn.  she makes the day easier after attending her class.
a valuable life lesson - take it!

By far the most disorganized and frustrating class I've taken at Cornell. Homework is excessively long and unclear, filled with typos and errors. Even the professor's own answers during tutorials are often wrong. If you want to blindly press keys in Excel without truly learning, this class is for you. AVOID AT ALL COSTS, do yourself a favor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Grades are only based on a few problem sets. Takes around a couple of weeks to do the problem set because they are heavy in content. Never attended lectures but still did well. Very recommended that you attend the lecture right after an assignment is announced because he holds review sessions and walks through some of the problem set.
This class was not difficult but incredibly unorganized. The first assignment was assigned in October and assignments were filled with typos and incorrect vague information.

Professor Turvey seemed nice, but he's not a great professor. His syllabus promised 5 equally weighted assignments, but we only had 3 due to his lack of preparation and poor spacing. He then released course grades without releasing the final assignment grades. He also announced he wouldn't curve the class, even though all AEM classes should be.

Professor Turvey is an incredibly knowledgable and understanding professor. He's only got one grade back to us so far, which is a bit stressful, but that's really my only complaint about him. We have no exams - just homeworks - and I feel like that's allowed me to actually learn a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Turvey is a great professor, he really knows the material and is extremely helpful during office hours. The material is complicated but he's super understanding and the psets aren't bad if you ask questions!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Turvey is one of the best professors I have had! This class can seem difficult, but the HW assignments are not that bad if you go to office hours and ask him for help since they walk you through everything. No prelims. Really caring and understanding if you have other conflicts for due dates. Take this class with friends!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Prof Turvey's course is definitely challenging. With that being said, he is SUPER helpful during office hours, and as long as you start the work early, he basically tells you answers when you ask (I get 100s w/o understanding anything). TAKE THE COURSE WITH FRIENDS and collaborate!

No exams, just homework. Gave me an extension just bc I asked.
He is a very confusing professor and going to class does not even help. Just hope for the best with grading.

Lectures are unorganized and hard to follow. My GPA is 4.0 but I found 90% questions on the problem sets were insoluble to me. His lectures literally offer no insights. I learn nothing from his course.

Avoid class at all costs. Assignments are vague, missing info, and full of typos, clearly written without much effort. Only way to pass is to bug the TA for answers. Fails to teach background knowledge in upper level courses to bridge the gap for students who may not have exposure to technical-specific knowledge like statistics.
Lecture is unorganized and hard to follow. Explanations on assignments are extremely vague.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He explicitly specifies a few examples and questions which will appear on the exams and the HWs. There is no way to get these right unless you attend class. Not easy to follow lectures.

If you took Finance with Curtis, you pretty much already know 75% of the material from the class, just by knowing the options chapter. Most importantly: use last years hw/practice tests and you will get an A.

Mediocre lecturer but encourages questions (so ask them, his explanations are pretty good). Prelims have a few multiple choice questions on obscure-ish things he mentioned in lecture (but if you attend/review the PPT you're fine) + free response questions are straightforward but kind of harshly graded. You write an essay too, it was easy to write.

class is boring save for goofiness. seems to care ab students but is not a good teacher. very hard to study. he uses stuff from the textbook, but as other students have said, too many random questions that can only be gathered from going to class/reading slideshows. final: why naked mole rats get cancer at a decreased rate, why are mules infertile

It is not a very helpful class, especially if you are a science major. His lectures are all over the place and not very helpful for any of the prelims and final. Also, discussions never have anything to do with the current lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Robert Turgeon was a terrible lecturer. Seems like a smart guy, who's involved in very important research, but he could not lecture for the life of him. Extremely boring and covered zero material. Just read off of his slides. Class was not worth it, but he did say some weird stuff that could be included in prelims and the final.
Bad lecturer and exams were kind of tuff and hyper specific about random slides

There's only two prelims and a final which account for 65% of your grade, however, as long as you read the chapters and pay attention you will be fine. There is no written homework, just one writing assignment mid semester and weekly chapter readings. The professor is a sweet guy and tries his best to make lectures entertaining.

I personally find statistic an inherently boring subject to begin with having taken the AP class. That said, Turnbull did nothing to improve the subject for me. He monotoned perfectly for entire 75-minute lectures. I held out longer than most and stopped showing up to lecture for the last two weeks of the semester and I don't gong would have helped

The most oblivious man to ever teach. I think if the entire lecture was empty, he would not even notice or car. He just faces the lecture slides and reads them verbatim. I literally had to teach myself the entire course with the textbook, and I am someone who usually goes to lecture and rarely reads the book. Overall, booooooooooo.

I feel like maybe he could have been a good professor. He is just really boring and seems to teach less and read from his slides or computer more. People stop going to class after the first few weeks. The people who do go kind of sleep or play around. I will say that he seems nice and has a cute british accent; its just hard to learn from his class
kind and concerned about my special circumstances. obviously very smart yet patient in explaining material until I grasped it

He is certainly the worst professor i have come across at cornell.  Has a lot of trouble keeping thoughts clear, has yet to give a direct useful answer to a question and loves to keep his writing illegible.  Not willing to make any compromises.  combine this with stats being the subject and you will be better off never going to class.

Worst prof I've ever had so far. Boring, not helpful, anything bad you can think of in a teacher. When we first started the class, the lecture room was packed. By the end, there were maybe at most 1/3 who still went to lecture, some of whom were snoring and others were doing something else. I went to 3 lectures in the entire semester.

I always thought that prob and stat was an interesting subject. But the professor put me to sleep every single time. It is the only classes I have EVER slept in and it is the only class that I don't feel guilty skipping. You have to read the book and go to section if you want to learn anything.
I can't stay awake in his class. I finally gave up going. He just talks to his slides the entire time. and half of what he says is wrong(according to the book), well half of what I was awake for.
I've never stopped going to lecture before and just used the book until this class.

this guy is a really good teacher, well prepared, good notes online, real life examples, sexi brittish accent, sometimes throws some weird brittish humor in. but the subject is so boring!! ive never stayed awake a whole class. straightforward prelims.

This guy was great. He just wants you to succeed. Reach out to him and be interested in the content. He will be tough on you, but if your a good student you'll adapt. 

The class wasn't hard there is just a lot of work, but it can be easily managed.

Ridiculously sarcastic and he's the only one that finds his jokes funny. He frequently picks on one student at a time and makes rude jokes towards them to make fun of them. Man comm should be an easy class, but he made it as difficult as possible with his grading scale and unimportant lectures.

Weird guy (has a "loose cannon" personality), grading is harsh and arbitrary; ManCom is useless but he makes it more rigorous for no reason. Would not recommend as all ManCom lectures are curved together regardless of professor. Tyrell does not believe in giving students As. Go with Lennox for ManCom; he's the best and only good ManCom professor.
Tyrell is an amazing professor who is very personal with his students and cares a lot about them. He teachings comm classes which is fitting for him because he is an outstanding speaker.

Overall, definitely do not underestimate the class. In terms of actual course load, it is maybe an average of 2 hrs a week- but grading is tough. He is super open to coaching you to get better and definitely you should go to office hours to work on assignments. If you wait too late to get help- you will probably not be happy with your grade.

Professor Stewart-Harris is definitely a character. He always makes jokes and picks on people, sometimes a little too much. He grades very hard and does not give A's. Expect to be happy with a B-. His rubrics and criteria are very unclear and often contradict each other. Other professors grade much easier and almost always give A's.

Stewart- Harris was hilarious, engaging, and super passionate about what he teaches. Gives good feedback for speeches, but is always kind and fair, and really responsive. Such a fun teacher, but was really straightforward about what was expected in his class which was great!

He does not believe in awarding A's. You can attend his and every TA's office hours, but if your writing is not the best he has ever seen, you will not get an A in the course. Hope that you get a different professor because he will not boost your GPA in any way. He also does not round your grade and does not give out extra credit. Good luck!
Fun teacher, good biology class. Lecture heavy and boring, very hard to get an A, but a B is easy and hes a super cool dude
hottest prof at cornell.  easily!  Lots of work in this class though, but the eye candy made up for it to some extent :)

stay away from this horrible class!!!!!!!!!!! worst class at cornell that i've taken so far and i'm GRADUATING next semester. grading is not so sweet either, but this class alone will ruin your semester.. professor is "there" but not really helpful when you have tons of studying to do all on your own. i learned so much, but it comes up later anyway

WOW!... This class was extreme. Tons of studying all the time. Expect no sleep and when you do sleep, you dream of your next scary practical. The TA's were great for the most part, and Tyson was always willing to help if you asked him. I learned so much in this class, and I still love bio!

This is definitely one of those classes where you get out what you put into it- you can do it really superficially and get by with mediocre grades or put maximum effort into it and learn intense amounts of information. Extremely time consuming and pretty stressful; not much interaction with prof.

Amazing class, I learned immeasurably more than a semester of traditional lecture-style biology. Great for teaching time management. Didn't have much interaction with Tyson, but he was frequently at the Study Center helping other students.

Autotutorial Biology is like coffee and beer-an aquired taste. It is a TON of work, the labs are hard, and the quizzes are harder, but I would take it again in a heart beat. It allows you to have freedom if you have a work ethic. I didn't have much interaction with Sacco, but when I did he was helpf

This class was hard and time consuming.the deadlines keep you on track, but some of the information they test is irrelevant and highly specific.  if you fall behind, you're screwed.At first Tyson seemed helpful; other times very uninterested in students. the rare lectures are boring and pointless.

As much as this class was a real drag and source of stress, probably more than other classes, I definitely learned the material. And Tyson is incredibly nice and willing to help if you seek him out. Don't take the class if you can't manage your time though - that's one of the biggest challenges.
This class requires a huge time commitment, but you really do learn ALOT.  If you do all the work, it's not too hard to get good grades.  Sacco is cool and always willing to help

Lots of work, tests, stress. No major prelims though. Hard, in-depth labs, but not every week. RELATIVELY flexible, but really frustrating when the study center isn't always open, TA's are ****es, and it's always crowded.

OUch.  This class is painful.  I want to sleep more than 3 hours a night and not have to stress over the insanely broad tests EVERY SINGLE WEEK.  This class would be awesome if we had twice as mush time to get through each unit and lab.

Wow this class this hard. Get ready to spend 20 hours a week on this course to hit the mean. But you really DO LEARN biology and how to study independently. I spent a summer doing research at NIH and would probably have left in disgrace in 2 days if not for what I learned in this class.

This class is a real challenge no matter what your scientific background may include.  Units and deadlines can be a drag.  The text is a great read and the staff, including Sacco, is extremely helpful and fun to be around.
don't take this class...unless you really really love biology and don't mind studying 24/7
He's great but the class is definetly not equivalent to 101.  If you want to work your ass off it's perfect.

For the first 2 months, I figured Tyson sat in his office playing computer games all day.  But in the last couple weeks when I was really struggling, I sought him out and he was really helpful, understanding, and tried to calm me down when I was stressed.

He's so hot, took the class last year and flunked it, but that aside, what you put into the course is what you'll get, DON'T FALL BEHIND, and the weekly oral tests really do force you to learn the material, which is good (if you live, of course).
good course. It is autotutorial though, so you only see the professor if you want to... Or, if you are failing the course
For God's sake, don't take this unless you really, really want to retake bio AP. Oh yeah, and Sacco: talk to your students!
Bio at Cornell and easy will never go together...
Yeh...you don't really get to see him, but when you do he's nice and willing to help... he doesn't look like a prof! Students don't realise he's actually the prof. Younger than some of the grad TAs.
He doesn't really teach the course, since it's autotutorial, but he is very willing to explain stuff if you ask him.   Very hot!

Tyson Sacco?  Who is Tyson Sacco?  I've heard he is teaching this class but I haven't seen him yet.  All I've seen are a bunch of confused TAs who cannot schedule quizzes so that everyone gets to take them.
No Comments
No Comments

Literally the worst professor I've had at Cornell. Has no idea what she's talking about, reads directly off the slides with her back to you. Very rude to students would ultimately make fun of us when we did poorly on her quizzes on material she never taught. Went into her half of the class with an A+ somehow left with an A- after her final.
Good Class. Just make sure to do all the old exams and memorize her lecture slides and an A is easy

barely went to any lectures. studied the slides thoroughly and read the relevant parts in the textbook, went over 2-3 past prelims, i ended up with an A. material interesting, her prelims involve lots of lab techniques so look at those closely. she seems like a nice lady outside.

Her actual exams are VERY little like the practice exams she gives out.  Don't be lulled into a false sense of security based on them!  This is a very difficult course.  However, if you do research for her, she'll give you a FANTASTIC rec letter.  Otherwise, difficult course.  Worked my butt off for an A-.
DONOT TAKE THIS CLASS. Not hard but extremely boring. I loathed studying for this course because of how boring it was. Most of this is due to her poor lecturing skills.

Approachable however as pointed out multiple times, not the best teacher. However, if you know everything on the slideshows/read related parts in the textbook AND practice with the old prelims, getting an A is rather easy.
I think she'd rather be somewhere else than lecturing 332. Lectures were clear, exams were fair. Despite all the negative comments, I found that getting an A in this course was not impossible.

Professor Tye's lectures were so boring and I fell asleep in almost all of them, even though I went faithfully.  I never fall asleep in classes, but this class was so boring.  Prof. Tye tried, but it wasn't enough to make this material interesting.  She seems nice though.

the WORST professor at Cornell.   Her exams are all about DNA gels, which are not covered anywhere in her lectures or the book.  Her english is crap, she talks with a thick accent, she talks fast, and half the time she forgets the english word and says "uhh" instead.  Real helpful, lady.  Just buy the powerpoint packet and study old prelims.
I've always loved this subject and Bik Tye sucked a lot of that love out of me.

She is an embarassment to this university.  Easily the worst teacher I have ever encountered.  Her powerpoints are unhelpful and her lectures are incomprehensible and extraordinarily frustrating.  The book is good, but she frequently asks questions about details that do not appear in the book, nor in her lectures.  Unequivocally awful.

Absolutely abysmal.  One of, if not THE worst teacher I have ever encountered.  Her lectures are terrible, her tests are nitpicky, unclear, and trivial.  Don't go to lecture, it's a lesson in frustration.  Read the book.

I really liked Bik Tye.  It was sometimes really hard to follow her lectures, but her expectations were clear:  if you know what's on the slideshow, you get an A.  You don't need to know anything else but her slides, and she doesn't try to trick you with her questions on exams.  She's also a reall nice person.

This prof is very unclear and unhelpful. The lectures are a total waste of time. She presents slides randomly and makes very very few comments about each slide before going on to the next slide. (Most of the time, she just reads the text on a slide and moves on.) Don't bother with going to her lectures--just read the textbook at home.
This woman is amazing. Made me change my concentration to Molecular Biology!

Quite possiblt thw worst prof I have ever had, she should be banned from teaching.  On our first prelim, where everyone (almost a hundred people) but one kid had gotten one question wrong, she ridiculed us, telling us it was easy and we were stupid for not getting it
No Comments

Absolute worst professor. She is incoherent, rambles through her slides and gives the hardest exams. Says "errr" and "uhhh" a lot, annoying! Less than half the class attends lecture. Why is she still teaching??

Professor Tye is the worst professor I have had at Cornell University.  She just reads from the powerpoints, but she reads way too quickly because she assumes everyone has printed the slides.  Her notes often contradict themselves and are confusing.

She is the most dreadful prof I've ever had. Her lectures and problem sets are erratic and her exams are totally unrelated to them. Her questions are extremely ambiguous. It is a shame that a world class institution could be plagued by such an impurity. Take BBM 330!!!!
If you liked Edna Mode (or however you spell it) from The Incredibles, you'll like her.  Underrated, study the practice tests and review the slides a bit.  Keep it real.
Very easy class.  If you're interesting in biochemistry, won't put you to sleep.
skip the lectures and read the notes/book. she is unintelligible
her tests are hard and impossible to prepare for - the questions are not like any other you can find (book or problem sets) except from previous tests, which answers are not available to.
No Comments
Absolute worst prof I've ever had.

Terrible; barely speaks english, cannot run Powerpoint (though she teaches with it); Unfair test questions that everyone gets wrong and she tells the class were easy. Better off taking BioBm 330 or the summer course

The tests are the same every year, basically, but the material is still hard if you've never taken AP and if you don't keep up with lecture/reading. I found it hard to follow lecture, but that's just me. i fell asleep a lot.
Terrible professor, impossible to follow in lecture. Frustratingly useless to go to class.
The material is hard but he derives a lot of equation people take as granted. His grading curve is very nice as well, but dont expect to have an easy time-phys 214 is hard period.
He likes math very much.  Too much time in lecture was spent deriving physics equations rather than teaching us the concepts.
The class was hard but the material was covered well and at a very deep level.

Best physics professor I've had, although that may stem from the fact that this course is much easier than 213, material-wise. Go to lecture, know the math, and do the homework, and you should get a decent grade in this class.

Honestly not that bad. If you study the lecture material with the book material you can get it. Tye is nice too and wants to teach well in class even if he loves the math behind everything. Actually didn't put me to sleep. Phys 214 only hires really good TAs so that's a plus.
Eeek.
He only concentrates on the math in his lectures, and they're basically pointless.  He doesn't make the tests too difficult, though.
He ASSUMES you know a lot, and it's all about maths...
Best
I have to agree with the "cruel and unfriendly" ratings. She knows her subject but her personality is awful, awful, awful.
Very good professor. Can't complain.

I was the last person to post, and I take back everything I said. An utterly unfair rating I have to admit, because she is a great teacher, and maybe I've got to say that I was also in a very bad mood that day. In any case take her for German if you can, she's real good at what she does.
Great instructor- One of the best I've had at Cornell.  Keep up with the work, and the class is very enjoyable.

i can't say anything in response to the insanesly harsh remarks made by kids in upper level classes.  all i know is that 123 with Frau Maschke was easily the best semester of german i've ever had.  She is, to me, the prototype of Engaging!  full of bright humor and authority, great class atmosphere
She is very tough and harsh at times. Maschke does not like people who disagree with her and students must conform to her teachihng style. Harsh grader and course can be boring at times.

She is one of the best teachers and people you could come across at Cornell. always helpful and understanding. classes get boring sometimes, but even a boring class (310) is worth taking if she teaches it.
One of the most amazing faculty you will ever have.  Smart, tough but always fair.  She’ll challenge you, make you think but in the end you’ll learn more than just German.
A very laid back class - I really enjoyed and looked forward to going.  Not a lot of work for the four credits it was.
Terrible. If you don't get on her good side early on she'll screw you over. Plays games with your mind and favorites like teachers did in high school.
She's the best. Period.
very fun class, class is everyday, but you get used to it.  not a whole lot of work, but tests can be a bit hard sometimes, but they don't count for that much
Super duper easy class. Straightforward content delivered fine. Vanek is very nice and cares about students.

Some very chunky psets. The lectures were not very engaging. Vanek is a wonderful person who cares a lot about his students and is interesting to talk to. Just not a fan of the course content. Very nice guy.
Amazing professor and amazing class. The course content was very straightforward. He leads stretch breaks in the middle of lecture, which were a great way to start my day :)

I took 4210, 4640, and 3230 with P. Vanek. As long as you use his slides, you will get an A in all of his classes. He posts examples of the same questions you will get on the exams/hws on the slides so if you put in the effort you will do well. He is also the sweetest guy and genuinely cares about your academic success and interest in the subjects!

One of the first engineering classes I've taken where all the material and assigned work felt useful and applicable to real world engineering. He is a great professor who prioritizes making his class the least stressful possible. If you aren't interested in the material the lectures can be boring, but it is clear he really cares about teaching.
Really nice guy, good material for the class, explained pretty well. No complaints at all for this class

Cannot say enough good things about this class and professor. He genuinely cares about what he is teaching and his students. It is a flipped classroom, so attendance is not mandatory. Exams and homework are very fair and workload is reasonable. Overall, one of my favorite classes I have taken as a CivE major.

Vanek is extremely nice and always willing to help you. Although he is a little awkward, he's very sweet and means well. His lectures are a little boring if you aren't interested in transportation, but he knows a lot about the subject!

Another in a series of easy classes with him. All of his classes seem to blend together, probably because his teaching style is a little boring. Textbook is online. Lectures are okay. Very friendly, very helpful outside of class, very easy to pass if you're interested in the subject matter. Find yourself a good group for the term papers.

Really a great guy. Not super clear in some of his lectures, but he really likes his field and is super nice. If you ask him for help he'll be happy to give it, and he likes to give a yoga break in the middle of lectures. He's really nice and kind of awkward and it's adorable. Also, his class is super easy, all formulas and you get a formula sheet.

Far-reaching class material meant some lectures could drag on. Often based lectures too heavily on math examples. Very friendly though a little awkward. Would take another course with him, though not this one. Go to class if you can, but if you have to miss it's not a big deal. Great at bringing in cool guest lecturers. Get the free online book.

He is a nice guy, but that is the only thing in his favor. Vanek is extremely unclear and incoherent in lectures. He has a tendency to waste time with pointless stories about his life as an undergrad at Cornell, then tries to tie it to the lecture's topic. Students end up learning solely from the book and TA's. Overall, stay as far away as you can.
Horrible teacher, had to teach myself because lecture was pointless. Don't take this class!

pretty easy class. prelims were 24 questions worth 24 points. prelims, final homework added up to 100. no curve though we got a few extra problems on the final. lectures are a series of entertaining anecdotes filled with self deprecating humor. whether or not i actually learned statistics is questionable.
By far one of the best professors I have had at Cornell.  His lectures are interesting and animated and his tests are easy.

Genuinely good guy. Class was pretty easy if you took the time to study up, go over problem sets. Final exam was ridiculously hard and dropped me from a solid A to a B. His stats class, however, is a complete breeze. Great guy, has a funny walk. Use his office hours, he can be very helpful and is patient with stupidity.

The class is uncurved, 90% = A- which is really easy to not get because the exams aren't written that well/no room to mess up. There is absolutely NO work in b/t prelims, so it's totally up to you to keep up. Lecture isn't that helpful, he just bashes the Daily Sun for the first 1/2 of class.
He is the worst professor I have ever had.  Can't speak English all that well, is incredibly confusing,and completely inaccessible.  Don't take his class- take AEM stats instead.
Absolutely worthless. If he doesn't feel like teaching, he doesn't. He doesn't care at all about how well his students do and says "If you can't figure it out on your own, sucks to be you".

One of the best teacher ever. Pam200- Even if tests become hard, he adds points to maintain fairness. Really learned a lot. The key is in doing well in the problem sets because the prelims are similar to them.

One of the best at Cornell. People who are writing bad reviews are those who are indifferent to learning economics...or just learning for the matter being. Makes lecture interesting...there is no substitute for textbook or lecture. Understand the problem set...key to doing well in class.

Was an okay teacher.Lectures interesting if you got there early to catch clips from The Daily Show. Tests were kind of hard and even though I didn't do great on them, I still somehow managed to pull a B out of my a**. Sections are useful for going over problems that appear on the tests and problem sets can be taken as many times as you want online.

Everything you need to know for this class is in the book... do yourself a favor, just ignore everything that comes out of Unur's mouth and teach yourself from the book.  Unur is unclear and  spends most of your class time on a tangent of one of his previous  tangents. With the exams... while they may seem straight forward, there are many tricks
Professor Unur is one of the best professors I've had. He genuinely cares about teaching students. Lectures were entertaining and a pleasure to attend. Always helpful in Office hours.

Sinan is a great professor.  He is very helpful when you attend his office hours.  The problem sets are not that difficult and everyone in the class can get 100% on them if they put in effort.  Even if you get an F on the first exam it is still possible to get an A.  He is fun to talk to and always has some random bit of information to share.

PAM 200- the problem sets aren't bad but the tests are HARD!! The mean for the first prelim was a 60 and he DOESN'T CURVE!! He's really not a good lecturer, doesn't explain things well. Go to his office hours for prob set answers.  PAM 210- Stick to the textbook. You will learn everything you need right there. Class and section are pointless. Eas
Nicest guy ever.  May not be the most brilliant teacher, however.
Gets confused quite easily with information.  Review for Final was a 3 hour session which he emphasized a whole area to memorize only to not include it in the final at all.
Most retarded teacher at Cornell; he couldn't even solve 2x=12 to derive the eq. pt.
I love him. He's such a great, fun guy.
he's nice, okay class, nice guy
Unur is useless at life.  You do not learn a single thing in this class.  It's a joke.

decent teacher, gets confused with mathmatical examples, and for fall 2004 has choosen probubly the most useless ta ever hired, sections are NOT worth the time, tests and problem sets are simple, so if you can teach yourself the info take this guy

He teaches 200 and PAM 210. He is soooo much easier than the other teachers. The multiple choice tests are short and to the point. He also allows you to get more points than the test is worth! His problem sets are online and you can retake them as many times as you want until you like your grade.

He is extremely knowledgeable and smart, but he frequently used large words that were kind of ridiculous. He's a harsh grader, and not a very nice professor. He very obviously takes himself too seriously, and that translates to his ability to have a respectful and thoughtful conversation with his students.

Overall, pretty interesting course, would take again. A lot of reading, sometimes difficult to understand but I'd say manageable. Professor was passionate but the only downside was that the lecture slides were posted after class and it would have been helpful if it was posted before class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I feel like an outsider not giving him a 5. This was my first ANTHRO class, so idk if I'm a good source. He is very passionate on the subject, so the lectures were pretty good. He uses big words so most of the time I had no clue what he was saying. The homework readings were LONG. I lowkey felt dumb in the class ngl. Just pay attention u will be ok

I genuinely looked forward to class. His lectures were interesting and when it came to studying for the midterm/final, I felt like I already knew the material. He is also very clear with what is going to be on these 2 exams. He gives a study guide to fill out a week or 2 before
Professor Velasco is an amazing professor. He really cares about anthropology and his course, he makes it very interesting. He is very knowledgable. I would definitely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: I've taken 3 of his classes now and he's by far my favorite professor. He's really understanding, super passionate about his work, and none of his classes have been hard but they're still all really interesting. Couldn't have asked for more.

Bioarchaeology with Velasco was a great experience! I took it for distribution reqs, and every lecture he tried to make sure he was engaging the class. Doing case studies as projects felt more like investigations than work, and if you put in some solid time you're golden for them. Great teacher and great class!

Best prof. I have ever had. Knowledgeable, inspirational, fascinating. Very organized & clear, & has clear passion for his AOS & teaching. Checks off EVERY box for what a prof. should be, & I think he will be one of the most-loved professors at Cornell at this rate. Participation, group project, midterm, final are main components. TAKE HIS CLASS.

The BEST lecturer I've had in CSCE department. Notes are clear enough to get you an A without attending anything, but attending the lecture would probably inspire you to pursue more in his field. Very patient, helpful, and responsive both in and out of classroom. Well organized and developed course structure, definitely have him if you can.

He teaches Computer Science at Texas A&M now. I took him for CSCE 411 and he is the best lecturer I've ever had. Comes to lecture prepared and teaches in a clear, concise manner. Course is also structured very well. 9 HWs and 3 exams. His lectures will prepare you for everything so just show up or watch the recordings. Take Professor Veldt!

I loved Professor Veldt! He wasn't in charge of the main logistics for the course so he wasn't in total control of everything, but he did well with what he had. He has an amazing youtube channel where he posts awesome guitar videos! Just search his name on youtube.
Made the most of an online semester. Still managed to be engaging and present the complex material in a clear and concise way. 10/10, he killed it.
She is awesome.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: She moved the final exam to online because of students concerns, She actually genuinely cares about students and if you're too swamped in a given week, she's very understanding with pushing back certain assignments. She is simply an amazing person and I really enjoyed taking labor history with her. Gem of a person.

Lots of reading and history can be kind of boring, but she genuinely makes it interesting. Definitely meet with her for feedback while writing your essays, she is very helpful and cares about you doing well.
