reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Super nice professor and very empathetic. Very understanding person. make sure to read
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Prof Martinez is a great professor! extremley kind and workload is not too bad. I would highly reccomend to take labor history with her if possible
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Martinez is incredibly nice, insightful, and knowledgeable. Her lectures are presented in a way to facilitate conversation and class engagement. This would all have been wonderful if I had found any interest in the course material. There's an unrealistic amount of reading and pretty dull topics. Great teacher but boring course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Participation matters

reviews.comment: One of the kindest, most caring professors. Was extremely lenient with deadlines. Great lectures; I liked how we discussed contemporary issues like police brutality and the disproportional impact of covid on minority groups. A bit reading and writing heavy, but definitely doable and grading was fair.

Somehow takes semi-boring course content and presents it in a way that makes it the most unbearable class I've maybe ever had. Is a nice person and is lenient with due dates but the essay prompts will make you hate your life. Better read everything or know US history well already or else you're screwed

Professor Martinez Matsuda is an excellent professor. She's extremely passionate about the material, and class was extremely interesting and informative. She's also just a really great person that cares for her students deeply.

One of the most caring and friendly professors I have ever had. Made material that would otherwise be somewhat dry very interesting and engaging. I highly recommend any class taught by this professor.

There's a lot of reading and writing in the class: I remember reading (well, skimming) up to 200 pages a week. I didn't think that I was much of a historian, but she makes the material interesting. She is also open to help out if you ever need it! There's also a lot of writing for the class. I had three papers and the final was handwritten essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--So many papers

reviews.comment: great teacher; aside from the socialistic view that she preaches subtly, she was a great instructor. if your taking us labor history, she is the best teacher to take it with hands down. class is mostly essay based but in total id say its only about 16 pages the entire semester

Prof Martinez-Matsuda is AMAZING. She is super caring and passionate about her students. There is a lot of reading in this course and the discussion sections/pop quizzes are heavily based on these readings- at least skim! She is accommodating and will extend paper deadlines during intense parts of the semester. Take her!

Grade-wise:  It all depends on your TA.  She'll give you extra time if needed for assignments, especially during the heavy part of the semester.  She really loves teaching.  The readings aren't really needed- except there are pop quizzes every once in a while, so make sure to at least skim.  Overall, I'd love to take another class with her again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Caring

reviews.comment: For a class that I had no interest in, she is prob the best prof out there. The class (by definition) has a ton of reading and some medium length papers but she is reasonable in expectationsgrading. If in ILR, I would def recommend taking it with her. The TA was nice but a tougher grader than the Prof. There were a couple easy pop reading quizzes

She's super sweet, like literally the sweetest person you'll ever meet. Go to her office hours, and know her on a personal level because she's just that awesome.. Her class is definitely on the difficult side: she assigns a ton of reading and essays throughout the semester. The TA we had graded them on the tougher side, so it was a tough course.
She is absolutely incredible!  She's so energetic and passionate, it would be a mistake not to take a class with her!

i loved this class! She's so energetic and helpful. Also just an incredibly nice person. Classes incorporate video material as well as in-class debates. Very practical and insightful way to learn about immigration and labor.
Some of the information in the class is difficult to understand but Martinez is very good at explaining things and answering questions in office hours.
She's bubbly.

Rather abrasive, but a fine lecturer. You'll do well as long as you read and understand the lecture notes (the tests are purely based on the lectures). 

Edit: In retrospect, taught us how to do physics more than any other intro class. Taught us how to think and problem solve, and mathematical tricks. You learn to love him.
Takes a nonstandard approach in both teaching and evaluating his students.

Veit Elser scared off a lot of students with his famous "Do not take this course if this sounds like you" declaration at the beginning of his course. Despite this scary warning, Prof. Elser is an amazing professor. He cares about students learning a lot and provides a lot of opportunities to get help. Lectures were great, tests were fair.

I enjoyed his lectures thoroughly. He helped me gain an intuitive understanding of concepts. Homeworks were quite creative, and although sometimes oddly worded, office hours were a great resource to discuss the problems. His exams were not the most straightforward, but if you followed his lectures and applied a bit of intuition, you should be fine.
This professor does not want his students to succeed. Told us several times to drop the class. Has a bad attitude generally. Don't take his class.

Very kind and caring (brings cookies to exams!) I'm not sure why there are such poor reviews, but I had the pleasure of taking Prof. Elser's 2217 class in the Fall. Lectures are very well organized, and the structure is very intuitive. I will say, the wording on HWs and exams were sometimes confusing (I wasn't always sure of what he was asking.

Decent guy. Homework was light (but oddly worded!) for an honors course (4-10 hours per week). He only grades 1 problem per week, and doesn't have quizzes, so it was hard to self-evaluate; I went to lecture and also re-derived content from textbook + online notes. I felt unprepared for exams but did ok. 2217 labs are a joke, regardless of prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I loved this professor! Very interesting lectures. Presents material in a very accessible way, making sure everyone understands. Hope I get to take his class again.
Great teacher, interesting and easy-to-understand lectures. Makes problem sets himself and makes them related to each other. Loved his class.
Professor Elser is great. Super helpful in office hours and tests are fair.

Prof. Elser is a great guy, he has a weird sense of humor and loves physics a lot. But he's insane, like he expects that everyone in his class is a genius. This class is the hardest thing I've ever done, in my whole life. The homeworks cannot be done outside office hours, but he usually eases off for the prelims since they're in-class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Hilarious

reviews.comment: We barely learn anything in lecture - he expects that we read the lecture notes in advance, so there are rarely notes to take. He also is very hard to hear sometimes. HWs are difficult and impossible sometimes to understand what he is asking. And, even though this is "honors" E&M, the "regular" E&M (2213) has harder content and learns more than us!
If Prof. Elser is teaching a graduate level course, take it.

Elser is a genius, and I felt way smarter walking out of each of his entertaining lectures. He organized the class brilliantly and explained every topic very clearly, with negligible hand-waving. I definitely recommend taking a class with him if you have the chance.

He prints out extremely comprehensive lecture notes, but unfortunately theres no text to accompany the course. I quite liked him as a professor, he lectures well, but often assumed familiarity with material that many had not seen before. (i.e. tensors, perturbations etc.)

No book, and it's a mistake. The class is disjointed and doesn't follow a standard curriculum at all. Did not prepare me for future physics classes. It was more of a random assortment of things he decided to teach, and the tests were out of left field.
Overall excellent professor, highly recommended. It's not an easy class, but you will learn a lot and Prof. Elser makes it fun.
I think Veit did an excellent job giving us a conceptual understanding of statistical physics. He went a tad too slowly, though.

His lectures are interesting and enlightening.  Admittedly, if you do not have a really, really good basic physics background, he does not go into enough depth for you to learn physics.  The homeworks and tests can be really challenging; however, if you go to his office hours, he will walk you through everything.  He's a great guy to learn from.

Teaches a very structured way to think about the fundamentals of mechanics. I took AP C in high school so I thought this would be a breeze, but it was very challenging. Interesting problem sets.Very rewarding if you put forth the effort.Deals with vectors especially well.

This class is awesome.  Elser basically starts each lecture with 1+1=2, and by the end builds up to some ridiculously complicated concept -- but you understand it somehow.  Unlike most other professors, he constantly stops to explain things in 3-4 different ways to help you develop intuition for what he's teaching.  Homework is easy, exams are fair

Wow. I got to say, I have no idea where the other commenenters are coming from. His tests are fair, he wrote all the material himself, we talk about really interesting things in lecture, and we have learned an entirely new way of thinking! All my friends are thrilled with the class and always attend to see what new thing we will go over next.

Terrible Teacher. I used to love physics, and he has made me despise waking up 3 times a week and going to his retarded class. Absolutely the most ambiguous prof I have ever had. He is always ill prepared to give lectures and can never quite get his point across. If you can avoid him by all means do.
His class is HARD. His lectures are useless. His prelims are confusing. And his class is HARD.
this guy can't talk normal, but i guess he's pretty smart. doesn't change the fact his teaching isn't good
One word of advice: go to office hours.  He will spend a lot of time helping you work out the problems and you will pick up a lot on the way.  The class isn't easy, so don't expect free marks.

Avoid this professor: he's obnoxious and useless.  His online quizzes don't test the material--they test how well you can read his mind (for example, one question asked you to pick a random answer choice and he deducted points if you picked the wrong "random" choice).

Can't really explains his stuff, and his lecture jumps around - or maybe it's just that I'm not smart enough. Recommended for the genius students who knows almost everything about this subject already - ya, there are those of you out there, unfortunately, not for me - who did not take AP Physics

i am struggling in this class, so I can't tell if he's as horrible as everyone says or if it's just too hard for me.  i'm not sure he's quite as bad as the other ratings say.  He has some cool demos, but other than that it is kinda boring.  i've never gone to is office hours. Meade is a good TA.

a very unclear professor. his lectures are extremely unorganized and hard to follow, and his example problems never help-he never tells you what hes trying to teach you. he may have pulled off one successful experiment this year, but other than that he isnt prepared. class was only saved by the TA's

One of the worst professors.  His sadistic sense of humor and complete disregard for the success of his students make this class a struggle.  Hard to approach, lectures are disorganized and difficult to understand.  Very arrogant.

Worst professor ever.  Plauged by inexperience and stupidity, he tries to spread it to he students.  If you get this prof know that you're in for a semester of learning everything by yourself.  Our physics department SUCKS!

Horrible physics prof.  Boring, unorganized, and hardly teaches.  Stopped going to his class 2/3 of the way into the semester, should have stopped earlier.  Prelims are pretty easy, though, as they test a limited range of concepts.
Disorganized, vague, lazy, horrendous sense of humor.  Does not teach.  Online quizzes fail to appropriately test knowledge.  Do whatever you can NOT to be in his class.
No Comments

probably the worst run class ive ever seen... it took him 3 weeks to get a demonstration right.  his online quizzes are ridiculous and only serve to make you hate him and life... and this is from someone who genuinely loves physics...
Going to his lectures will not prepare you for the prelims.

If you have trouble sleeping, go his class. You're sure to fall asleep given his high degree of boredom. I was better off reading the book instead of going to lecture. Makes tons of mistakes and won't like it if you ask quesitons.
offensively bad professor.

Graded on a few two-page essay assignments and one literature review at the end. Bulk of this class is in-class discussion of academic texts on sex and gender in the sociological discipline. Maralani was genuinely impassioned about the content and about meeting students where they are at to make sure everyone gains something from the course. LOVED!

I love Professor Maralani. She is intelligent, cool, and a great lecturer. She clearly cares so much about her students and wants to get to know them individually, even in a large class. She's transparent about her process as a professor and genuinely wants feedback to improve, even with a lot of teaching experience under her belt. Great class!

Brilliant sociologist and excellent at breaking down statistical concepts in applied ways. Highly recommend this prof for taking stats. Definitely grades tough, but curves overall. You will have to work a lot - weekly assignments are time bloats, but are good learning tools.

Professor Maralani is a very intelligent stats professor and she can teach you a lot. That being said, sometimes she is a little toooo smart and will confuse the whole class, but if you talk to her one on one she'd clear it up. The tests are pretty hard, and sometimes feel like they are unrelated to class content. But, the curve is generous.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: The nicest teacher you'll have at this school. Incredibly genuine and kind. The readings are excellent, and there are many different options for each essay. Gives great feedback on all essays.

Sophia was incredible. I enjoyed her class a lot. Took this during COVID, and Sophia was super understanding if we had anything going on due to the pandemic. 100% recommend this FWS, take this class!!

She teaches her FWS: Short Stories VERY WELL. I am not even an English major but I would look forward to her class. Not because it was easy or you could sleep through it but because you feel like you can learn without major academic pressure. She ensures that if you put in enough work there isn't any need to worry about the class grade-wise.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Took in SP22. Had T. Healey but attended Prof. Vlad's lectures occasionally. Lectures were very well structured, and his notes were posted on Canvas later. Exams were very fair, homework was lengthy but not super difficult. Weekly discussion quizzes were easy. His accent can be a bid hard to understand sometimes, but great experience overall!

Vladimirsky was an excellent lecturer. As of 2022, he uses an iPad with comprehensive notes to lecture collaboratively with the students, rather than a PowerPoint. Tests were fair, homework was long but reasonable, and most students did not have an issue with the course. The class gets harder towards the final, but Vlad prepares you very well!
Loved math 3610 if you want to learn about mathematical modeling Vladimirsky knows his stuff

One of the best math professors at Cornell. Class is a lot of work but also very rewarding. Really cares about students and holds extra office hours. Has a sense of humor too. Lectures are well organized and clear. Grading is fair and the rules are clearly defined.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Terrible professor. Used powerpoint from textbook (aka written by the textbook authors), and didn't even bother reading over it before class and consistently found mistakes in it during class. Yelled at students to ask questions because as a professor, he shouldn't just speak the whole lecture, it should be run by students asking questions...
Uses Powerpoint in teaching math.. not really helpful in writing notes. Exams are tough.

Vladimirsky is great! He taught 2930 (but not other classes) using ppt slides from the textbook, but wrote out things that needed further explaining on the board. Even though there were 200+ people in this class, he took the time to answer every single question, so you have no excuses, lol. He also has a cool Russian accent. Would recommend!

Vladimirsky is very tough and expects a lot out of students.  However, he knows and can teach differential equation incredibly well.  What's great is that he forces us to think beyond the material that we were learning in class and analyze the assumptions that we make in our discussions. He actually wants people to ask questions in class.

I think I learned more calculus in Prof. Vladimirsky's class than I did in both Calc 1 in high school *and* Calc 3 at another college. You bet I had to work hard, but lecture was very informative. As an added bonus the Professor introduced the class to the beginning concepts of Analysis.
One of the best math teachers I've had. Very hard even though I have taken calc II before, but learned so much more and prof was very helpful. Exams very difficult.

Very difficult but not terrible class. Made the math more complicated than necessary, wouldn't have learned anything if I didn't take it in high school, but a great exercise in problem solving and critical thinking. Hard tests but very fair grader. Feels daunting, but not difficult to do well in.

He has high expectations, and he likes to make the class as challenging as possible.  Sometimes he knows that most people don't understand but since no one asks him to slow down, he just keeps going.  It is intimidating to raise your hand in a challenging class like that, but he is really helpful if you do ask your question.
I had previously taken calc courses but ended up coming out of his class feeling less confident in calc.  He was horrible at explaining concepts although he was willing to try and help after class.

Vladimirsky is difficult, but fair.  His tests tended to have a low average score, but the class was graded on a curve so it didn't really matter all that much.  You may not understand everything that he tries to teach in lecture, but he is EXTREMELY helpful if you go to his office hours.  Overall decent professor.
He was needlessly hard and generally unkind.
Terrible at explaining many concepts. The average of all three prelims ranged from a 45-50. He makes the material much harder and much more confusing than it really is.
Great professor, really knows his stuff and very clear. Also very funny and always availabe to help. Highly recomended.

Best course on numerical methods I've had -- the the good: better than CS 321/322 junk.  Great lecturer and likes the subject!  Coding was great -- implementing relevant algorithms and learning something about why/when they work (or fails to) is . the bad: long assignments, iffy textbook-"ANM"

I've learned more in this class than any other class at Cornell. If you're at all interested in cell biology, this class provides the context you need. Don't fall behind in lectures, the material is DENSE and plentiful. Put in the time and effort and it will pay off. First time a prof will give you helpful practice/feedback on scientific writing.

Biology like you've NEVER SEEN BEFORE. SO MUCH INFORMATION. WOW. After taking this course I have never seen biology the same way again. Honestly that's how much you learn. Reading papers is so much faster bc. of how much you learn. Great if you are considering going into biology. But it should definitely be 4 credits bc. it's LOADED. Amazing.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: People seem to be complaining about the course, but it's really not that bad. The level of detail you're expected to know is reasonable for a high-level cell biology course. Also, Dr. Vogt makes it easier with comprehensive lecture slides. Plus he really seems to care about the material and the students. It's a great cell bio class.
Avoid the class if you can because: this is a 8:40 class; he has extremely detailed lecture slides; he grades papers on how well you can write in English; he is not the most engaging lecturer.

The lecturer is not engaging in anyway while all the material is online, which is aggravated by the mandatory attendance at 8:40am. The assessments rely on you to memorise extremely specific details and punish you for not memorising them thoroughly. The material would otherwise be interesting if it weren't for the labourious memorisation required.

Professor Volman is super nice and caring. If you need an extension, he will give it to you as long as you tell him a valid reason. He's really passionate about anthropology and really does care for his students. I would take any class with him again.
Worst Professor. Lectures were completely unorganized. Didnt help with assignments. Didnt answer questions. STAY AWAY FROM HIS COURSES.
Great prof, great mentor, great advisor.  He is the main reason why I now study human origins.

Really great guy, he is really passionate about what he is teaching. Lectures can be rambling and confusing, but they didn't really matter for your grade. No tests just short papers every few weeks and two longer ones. Not an easy A but an easy B. It does take extra effort to get those final points, but average work will get you a B.

Professor Volman is fantastic when you take a small seminar with him. He cares a lot about his students, and takes pride in his subject matter. I highly recommend his courses to anyone interested in anything related to Anthro or Arkeo

Do not take this class unless you are willing to dig deep into the material and are very interested in the subject matter.  If you are still figuring out what to do, take a different course.  HOWEVER, this professor is an excellent guy to talk with.

Professor Volman is a really nice guy. His lectures are sometimes incomprehensible and rambling but his grading is fair. For this class, just make sure you know what is on the test and facts- he write a list of exam terms.

Nice guy, terrible prof.  Lecture is soooo boring and the grading makes no sense.  Seriously, the class assignments you get back have no reflection of your competency in archaeology.  I was really interested in the subject, but this class did little for me.

This is the worst class at cornell!! Do not take under any circumstances! He doesn't grade based on whether you understand what you're doing. He takes off points on essays even if you give all correct answers, just because you didn't include every single thing ever mentioned about the topic. He also believes Cornell gives out too high of grades.

He is a very nice man, and very helpful, but his lectures can be kind of boring.  I feel like with grading, you have to work hard to get a solid A, but you would also have to work hard to fail (getting Bs takes avg effort).  Environ arkeo is more watching presentations than lectures...which can get annoying bc the class seems to have no direction.

Tom Volman is one of the best profs at Cornell.  He does the most to encourage and guide his students of any prof I've ever had, especially if they show genuine interest in human origins.  Great guy to be friends with, to ask for advice, to talk about archaeology with.  If you have the chance, take a seminar with him (better than his intro course).

Good, if you are really interested in this topic. Lectures not the most spectacular, but not horrible, readings always very interesting, paper topics and grading good and reasonable. Tests detailed but not horrifying. Generally a good guy and not out to get his students or prove his own brilliance, which in this university counts as a big plus.

If you are interested in archaeology or biological anthropology, this is a great class to take. You end up learning a lot more than it feels like at first, and Volman's very easy to talk to after class. He tends to pick interesting topics for papers and his exams accurately represent what was taught in class.
Fairly easy class and easy grader.  His lectures aren't the most organized ones in the world, but his words are at least understandable.
Completely disorganized prof. Lectures are composed  of PBS videos, Gary Larson comic strips, and countless digressions. Avoid if you can help it.
if you can find organization in his lectures, please let me know!!

She is a great professor. Very knowledgeable. It is a fun class, you learn a lot of relevant things and a new perspective on examining scientific work. The midterm was graded very fairly and if you completed the study guide it was easy to do very well. The papers are more difficult. Weekly reflections are a major grade boost. I enjoyed the class.

Discussions are great- always compelling and interesting. The assignments are relevant to the class but also very useful- they are worth the time and effort and never just busy work. Grading is fair. Very helpful and willing professor. Lectures are on the dry side, but if you hang in there till discussion, all can be forgiven. She wants to help you

Vogel is a great professor when it comes to class discussions and giving relevant assignments. She is also very helpful and eager to help, just ask questions and go to her office hours-- she really does want to help and cares if you understand the material or not. Her lecture style, however, is boring. It knocks out a kid in our class every time.
smart, pleasant, hot

She was a clear speaker, although her verbal crutches (i.e. "for example") sometimes detracted from what she was trying to say. The reading consisted of articles, and the work was mostly reading responses. I did well in the class, so I'm satisfied!

A lot of reading and writing. For premeds, this class is VERY valuable. The issues and material you learn are very helpful. Professor Vogel is a really nice lady that truly cares about her students and their feedback. She really tries to help her students throughout the course. Just go to office hours.  She's really helpful.

The subject matter is really great- relevant, interesting & current. But Vogel's lecture style just doesn't match the material! She's a very monotone speaker without much passion in her expressions. This could be a phenomenal class if only she could be more lively. Sections are great if you get a good TA!
I loved Vogel. I thought she was pretty interesting if you sat up front and stayed engaged...pretty easy class as long as you go to the review sessions.
Amazingly boring...defied the laws of nature in terms of how boring she could make a lecture.  I often left lectures without the desire to learn anything ever again.
Most of the material in lecture is interesting, although she is not the most dynamic lecturer. The TAs grade the papers, but Vogel has been accomodating with midterm grades and such.
No Comments

Vogel is a waste of space.  I have never seen a more lazy, less dedicated professor.  This lady has no interest in her students whatsoever and makes completely unreasonable decisions regarding grading.  The miderm is not too bad, but papers are graded harshly.  The discussion section is extremely stimulating, lecture however is painful

All she says in um over and over.  I counted one class for 17 mins, and she said um 225 times.  She can't convey a point, she grades very hard for a class that should be medium/easy and lecture is the worst thing ever

The course has a reputation for being an easy class. Grading is unclear/delayed, but the content is easy if you show up. After the first few weeks of the semester, ~40% of students stopped showing up to lectures, which continued to decrease each week. All lectures are recorded, all slides are posted, and all quizzes are posted on the slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor is extremely rude and disorganized. My classmates and I constantly complain how responds to emails
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I chose this course based on its reputation, but the entire syllabus changed, and the class has been extremely disorganized. We're one week from the end of the semester and still don't know our grades. Rubrics for major assignments are either unclear or posted after deadlines, making it impossible to understand what the professor is looking for.

This was a new course this semester based on a grad course. The class was incredibly interesting, well taught, and had no tests. Grade comprised problem sets, peer grading, and a final group project/presentation. The teaching team was always accessible. I wish they gave A+'s, but otherwise this was my favorite class at Cornell.

Easiest class at the school (seriously, the only way it would be easier if she gave A+ grades). Half the grade is showing up. Other than the grading scale, she really is passionate about the field of Anthropology, and overall, a great person. I had a great time in the course and appreciated her lectures and think it is a must take at Cornell!

no interest in anthr and didnt expect much of the class going in but it was prob the best class ive taken at Cornell very interesting, manageable, and engaging. Prof welker is amazing and kind nothing but good things to say!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Awesome professor. Easy class. Engaging.
Professor Welker is very nice. Her lectures were very engaging. The readings provoked deep thought about global problems. The discussion sections were also very insightful.

Professor Welker always ensured that material was relevant to current issues and connected with students experiences in the real world. Class discussions always were lively and she allowed time for all students to voice their opinions throughout the class. Although some readings were on confusing topics, Professor Welker always was understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. Welker is such a knowledgeable, aware, and caring professor. She is very involved in her research and genuinely wants her students to learn as well. Talk to her about her time in Indonesia!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I felt that homework usually did not help me and was a major time sink that did not end up being worth it. Exams had too much opportunity for silly mistakes, which was annoying cus in real life, you have calculators etc. Lots of questions tho, so weak law of large numbers or whatever.
He gets a 4 for being funny but yea I didn't learn anything
DO NOT TAKE 3410 WITH WEATHERSPOON. His exams are impossible and extremely long. Horrible lecturer combined with impossible exams DO NOT TAKE
Terrible, terrible lecturer. Covers content way too fast and glosses over everything. Be prepared to learn literally all the content on your own. Avoid at all costs.

Prof. Weatherspoon is a brilliant scientist and a kind professor. He is, however, not very good at explaining concepts. So confusing and keeps talking in circles. I stopped attending lectures after the first week because I learned more from reading the slides on my own. There is a lot of content covered in this course but exams are straightforward.

I would give a 5 to the professor as a person, but a 2 or 3 to the course. UNREAL amount of workload compared to the other 4 credits CS classes, they should give this course 6 credits. However, Prof Weatherspoon is a caring and respectful person, he will listen to your concerns and advice. Really feel no pressure to stay with as in person.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Delusional workload that would easily be 10 credits if properly reflective of the amount of time necessary to succeed in this class.
Never get well-prepared for lectures. Always want to end early
Awful and unclear lectures, can only learn from textbook.

Hakim is one of the most fair and honest professors in Cornell. He wants everyone to do well and goes beyond what the majority of the rest of the faculty  would do to achieve this goal. Some people complain that his lectures are unclear, but he releases them a day early so you can skim them before class to make up for it. +1 to him.
Most boring lecturer ever. Worst prof Ive ever had here.
Course is very poorly managed. Details/busy work interfere with the course content.

Hakim is a smart guy who is very approachable. However, the class itself disinterests me, and I dont think this has anything to do with him. As a result, I didn't spend as much time on this class as it demands, therefore, I am not blaming anyone.
Textbook is your best friend in the class. Otherwise, you are all alone.

He is very knowledgeable and it seems his goal is to help his students do well.  Class might be difficult at first, but bare with him and do all the assignments and you will do well.  He also has a great personality and is very approachable.
He has no idea what he is doing!

He consistently delivered lectures as though he were seeing the slides for the first time. He was notoriously bad last semester, and this was evidenced by the consistently low scores (around 50's) of the tests. He has an excellent personality, but lectures and sections were never worth going to.
Great teacher, affable.
My queeeeen Kim! She cared about the material and made sure to organize the content in an accessible way. Easy to do well in the class and interesting.

Class is pretty heavily memorization-based, so get ready to make flashcards and mnemonic devices. But overall probably the most interesting course I've taken at Cornell with extremely engaging lectures and funny professor. Exams can be a bit tough but honestly if you study hard for the 3 total exams in the semester you'll be perfectly fine, no HW.

Professor Weeden is a knowledgeable and engaging lecturer, but this class is far from easy. The material is dense and heavily grounded in specific authors and studies, so you need to know not only the concepts but also who developed them. This is not an easy A and takes lots of studying!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Weeden is best described as "respectable." She knows her stuff, and she's also good with dry humor. However, don't expect this class to be easy. It's an information dump of a bunch of studies (making big concepts a little harder to grasp), the results of which you need to memorize for tests. Great sociologist, but not the best professor.

kim my queen!!! she's so funny + engaging! just 2 prelims and non cumulative final that are all super straightforward if you just memorize the big concepts! content is interesting and u get 5 skips for attendance (pollev)

Honestly not really any homework and most of your grade is participation/attendance, exams, and reflection memos (~2 page essays). Not really that difficult and this is a class where if you work for the grade you want you will definitely get it. You also get study guides which emphasize what will be on the exams.

Tests are short-response questions, but there's a lot. You get graded in an AP format where there's a rubric for every question (which is incredibly stupid). The SAT essay was removed for a reason, literally why is there so much subjectivity in grading? 

And don't give me the "TA aVerAgInG" spiel. It's not thorough.

Exams were kind of tough but you really just have to know the content and demonstrate understanding of how it applies to social inequality. Great professor, though, she's caring and funny and interesting in general. Really enjoyed the class especially at the last half of the semester!

Unless you have a photographic memory, don't take this class. Her exams are supposed to be easy but unless you can write word for word off the slide don't expect to do well. This is not a class where you learn its a class in which you memorize
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Absolutely amazing professor and super interesting course material! Lots of reading, but its super interesting! Lectures are riveting!

One of the most caring professors this year and absolutely cared for her students. The material is interesting and taken from the textbook but well summed up in lectures. The entire class's admin really cares for its students. This was a great overview class and definitely kept me interested.

Weeden is awesome! She is an engaging lecturer and a good teacher. The material in the textbook (found online) is very interesting and focuses on real-life phenomena rather than dry theory. The discussion sections are great. Tests are one of two essay questions chosen from several pre-provided prompts. Highly recommend this class.

Prof Weeden was absolutely incredible. She was super understanding, especially with all the tragedies occurring this semester. Not only that, but I learned extremely valuable lessons in her class. Take this course!
Her preparatory essay questions are horrible. Terribly vague and unclear and so open ended that you wouldn't understand what to expect.

Weeden is HILARIOUS. She manages to get her point across while keeping the lecture light. Her exams are essay-based, so she will give you 5-7 essay prompts in advance, 2 will be on the exam, and you write one of the 2. If you pre-write and incorporate both lecture and readings you will do fine. Amazing class-would take again!

Following an early comment, Kim is an excellent lecturer, but not the best *teacher.* She is tremendously engaging and a clear expert but she provides MANY explanations for phenomena and blows through them quickly which makes retaining material much more difficult. For exams, you're basically expected to know everything she talked about + readings.

Professor Weeden is incredible. She is engaging, thorough, funny, as nice as can be. I HIGHLY recommend taking this class, especially if it fulfills a requirement. The material taught is tremendously important and relevant, and this course will make you a more informed citizen. See previous ratings for the grading policy; it's more than fair.

Kim is a really nice professor, she sympathizes with students which is evident from the fact that she lets you take 3 out of 4 exams and gives you the test questions in advance (5-6 of them, then 2 are on the exam, you choose 1). She's one of those people you want to be friends with. I'd take the class if it fulfills a requirement for sure.

Professor Weeden is an extremely engaging lecturer, but I found the class to be poorly structured. We only met twice a week and no other examination was given other than the 3-4 prelims. Due to this, I found myself often slacking and putting other classes before this one. She assigns a lot of readings, but you can get by without doing most.

One of the best lecturers at cornell (not one of the best *teachers*, though). Her tests allow you to select 1 of 2 essay questions from a pool of 5-7 she supplies ahead of time. DL the class notes, skim the readings, make & memorize essay outlines, and you're golden. But actually going to lecture is recommended; she's very engaging.

You dont have to do the readings as long as you go to class. She gives you the essay questions before the exam. I suggest taking the class with a group of friends and writing the essays before the exams.

Gives 7 detailed essay questions in advance. Puts two on the exam and you choose one. She goes through the complex lectures REALLY fast and there is no takenote. Review sessions dont help much. She tricks you by saying she posts notes online but purposely deletes all the key concepts from the blackboard version so u'll come to class.

Actually, this semester you have to take 2 prelims/a final. She gives you about 8 possible essay questions ahead of time, but this means you have to prepare 8 detailed outlines, then remember them. Exhausting! I'm doing well in the class, but the prelim studying is terrible. Also,the TA fails at life/is in charge of grading. Weeden is great though!
Very easy you choose whether to take 3 prelims or 4 everything is really straightforward and she gives out the essay questions in advance, and gives you a choice of questions to answer.

She is a horrible lecturer who reads directly from the slides with far too much text.  She should just hand out notes and tell her students to memorize them the night before the test to do well.  Don't take this class.
This class is amazing. And she is a great lecturer as well. Grading is fair, and you will do well so long as you prepare for the exams.

Don't need to do the readings at all just go to class and the review sessions, and with some studying you'll be fine. She's a great teacher, really cares about the material and does a great job explaining some of the more dense readings. Very funny. Quite, um, "obvious" political views are sometimes injected; that would be the only negative for me
She is extremely approachable.  Professor Weeden is organized and an insightful  lecturer. I recommend her classes.
Excellent professor. Keeps the class engaged throughout. Going to class means studying is minimal, with only the relevant papers to read. Excellent teacher, and excellent class.

Very clear, an expert in her field, and approachable. Keep up with the readings and avoid last minute studying as there is a lot of material. Going to class really helps. Definitely an interesting lower level class.
No Comments
LOVE her- so funny and amazing, great class

This class is enjoyable, interesting and not that hard.  The lecture notes are all online, so there really is no reason to attend class.  The course reader (the one book for the class) is big, but don't be scared.  All the reading need only be skimmed before the exams, which are also not that hard.
Awesome prof. Great sense of humor.
No Comments

Very long homework, but not super hard. Group project takes up a lot of time so I recommend to take this course with friends. Prelim was identical to practice, but final not so much. Informative course and very applicable

Both the midterm and the final were very similar to the practice tests, so everything felt very fair. He clearly puts effort into making the course run smoothly and explains the material well. The homework was lengthy, but it helped reinforce the concepts. Overall, he is a strong instructor and I learned a lot from the class.
Homework does not relate to the test. Lectures are confusing. Final are much harder than the review. Do the test review and one page he give you. You can pass

No curve. Cares more about the TAs than the actual students. Boring lecturer. Truly the worst experience ever with a professor. The final was uncharacteristically hard and he really doesn't seem to care about the student. He shouldn't teach this course!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: good class. fun homeworks. little hard exams but very helpful TAs and very accomodating professor
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I dont know why his rating is so high. His lectures are boring and why did he yell at us saying we needed intro stat and then explain slope to us. Like everyone in the class is IS or ORIE... we do not need to relearn this. move on. Also he's not funny.

Wilkens is a good lecturer, but p-sets were long and didn't always directly connect to lectures. ChatGPT helps a lot. The course was more technical than humanities-focused, despite the title. It didn't feel terribly different from other intro data science courses. I had high hopes for this class, but it fell short for me. Not horrible though.

I do not recommend this class. Random class attendance quizzes and lectures were not useful for the problem sets. The problem sets were beyond impossible and everyone used GPT for them (and still struggled). When it was time for the final project, everyone I know did very badly bc there were no guidelines. don't take this course, the median was B-

Incredibly long and tedious psets. Could be done adequately by chatGPT, which defeats learning objectives of this course. Unclear grading criteria and bad assignment turnarounds such that we could not improve for future assignments, particularly for the final.

Unclear grading criteria. Good chance you get like a letter grade lower than you think. Not really open with us, and would often say in office hours stuff like "yeah this would be fine" and then mark off points from you. Amazing TAs (especially the head TA, who would give out help to anyone who needed it, bless her), but I don't like him.

Wilkens is an excellent professor. I took 2950 with him previously, and he never fails to explain concepts slowly and meticulously. While the psets are challenging, Wilkens and his TAs are very approachable and helpful. Clearly passionate about teaching, Wilkens definitely belongs among the best at CIS.

The lecture could only help with about 3% of the homework. I spent two nights trying to understand the codes, but the grading just proves that GPT wins the human brain. I don't understand now what is the point of going to lectures and doing the homework if eventually we are all forced by the homework to use ChatGPT to get high grades.

Surprised to see so many positive reviews. So far, everyone I know in this class has complained about how long the homework is. Questions are marginally related to what he talks about in lectures and grades take way too long to release. People who buy ChatGPT premium receive the highest grades, which says a lot about how this class is run.

Professor Wilkens is one of the best professors I've ever had. He is incredibly engaging and makes the content that he is teaching so enjoyable. He is accessible outside of class, and shows care for each and every one of his students. He wants his students to learn and enjoy learning at the same time. Without a doubt best professor at Cornell.

Professor Wilkens is indubitably the most caring and passionate professor I have met. His lectures are engaging, and he genuinely cares about students' understanding. The grade was based on a semester-long project, 8 problem sets, a midterm, and a final. The workload can be challenging, but Professor Wilkens and his TAs will help you succeed.

Wilkens is by far one of the best professors I've had at Cornell. He's a very captivating speaker, great at answering questions, charismatic, and funny. He does move slowly through content, but as someone who is relatively new to stats and data science, I appreciated the pace. I would 100% take a class with him again!
I love his classes. The level of difficulty of lectures and homework is perfectly set. I also love how he organizes the contents
My favorite professor at Cornell so far. He's extremely approachable, explains stuffs really well and genuinely cares about students.

Hands down one of the best professors I have had at Cornell, and that was in his first semester here and during the pandemic. He did a great job balancing the CIS side of the course with the implications/impact in the humanities. He was extremely caring, made sure the teaching staff was flexible, and actively sought out and implemented feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've had at Cornell! Not only is he very well read in a vast number of topics (in both Computer Science and Literature), he is also extremely approachable and well-attuned to student needs. He began every zoom class by chatting with students, frequently asked if the material made sense to everyone, and granted extensions.

Miller is a kind professor. While his class required effort it was not difficult. Would recommend studying for tests, and also try to talk to him outside of class. He has a lot of interesting experience, will be sad to see him go.

The goat. Cares so much about students and is a great teacher with fun stories. Super flexible with deadlines, and assignments are very reasonable. Interesting guest lectures and labs that cover a good variety of plant science related fields.
This guy is the man. He is hip with a capital H
Great guy!

I loved PLSCI1101 so much. Dr. Miller made it fun and is a hilarious guy. Reading is somewhat heavy in the beginning of the semester, late semester is mostly guest lectures. He is very flexible with due dates and lets you submit late assignments. Gets back to email fast. By far my favorite class this semester!

Professor Miller was kind and helpful. He took the time to meet with each student individually and gauge how we were feeling about the class. Not a lot of work and lectures + lab were very interesting especially if you don't know exactly what you want to do with a plant science degree yet.

People here needs to chill out, prob just got bad grades and came to pent. Professor Winans genuinely cares about his students and teaches pretty well, he's also an extremely lenient grader who understands the struggles of college students. Very approachable and doesn't just pretend he knows the answer when answering questions he's not sure about.
had him for microbio lab he is pretty chill. cant speak for the other courses this is just for biomi 2911

Difficult for a 2000 level class. Each slide deck takes about 2-3 lectures, so we ended up very behind compared to the schedule on the syllabus. Doesn't know how to answer questions about his own slides and doesn't even know when the prelims are. Quizzes and prelims have very specific questions that aren't important to know outside of the class.
This class was extremely disorganized.

Very disorganized lecturer. He teaches two classes that have overlapping material and often confuses the content between the two and you might be tested on material from the class you are not taking. Lectures are very surface level compared to the exams and many times would need to know outside knowledge to be able to answer the questions.

The class started out very strong, with clear lectures, quizzes, and a fair midterm. Later on, his lectures started getting more and more disorganized, his quizzes ridiculously specific (like a fine print under a picture). He was kind of unhelpful when we had logistical questions or even something about information on his slides.
Easy going and understanding

He's a very interesting lecturer that makes interaction during class very easy. He doesn't always have all the answers to questions but he will make an effort to find out the answer and get back to you. All the assessment material is really fair and everything can be found almost word for word on the slides

When I first signed up for his class, I didn't know what to expect. It was my first college experience and I was really nervous. However, once the first class began, Professor Winans blew away any expectations I had! His lectures were very easy to follow and the way he described the contents on his powerpoints instantly captured my attention!

Dr. Winans is a nice, caring guy. I sometimes skip lectures but when I do go, it's just to hear what he has to say. The material is often clear and if you do the work, you should be fine. The class was moved online halfway through the semester but I feel like it is manageable both ways. He is also responsive to students.
Really nice professor who is very knowledgeable. A bit too heavy on the lecturing for my preference but I'm sure it works for some people. Overall a great guy

Professor Winans is one of my favorite professors at Cornell! He is extremely passionate on the subject and is more than willing to help you. The material can be specific, but attending lecture is definitely useful in order to know what to study for quizzes/exams. He also adjusts grading of quizzes/exams to bump up grades. Highly recommend!

Steve was a great professor. His quizzes can be a little tough but he will adjust the curve to make sure the average is an acceptable score. His powerpoint slides are so informative and detailed that I still referred back to them even when I was taking upper level classes. He makes you work for your grade but we're at Cornell so what do you expect?

Unfortunately, Winans has been the worst Professor Ive ever had at Cornell thus far. He single handily ruined Microbiology for me. The main problem for me was how disorganized his portion of the class was. He also directly contradicts his syllabus by putting multiple correct answers MC questions on his prelims/quizzes. Dont take Microbio with him
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The course was disorganized and his half of the course was even more so. His lectures never followed the lecture schedule, and his lack of assigned readings made it hard to know what to reference for extra explanation. He wasn't incredibly pleasant when I spoke to him either. He is knowledgeable about his field, but he ruined the subject for me
I really enjoyed his classes. He has a really relaxing voice, so beware of going to class tired.

very enjoyable class because of his great personality. material may be difficult and very detailed but he is willing to explain! weekly partner quizzes (MC) based on homework (MC), prelims based on HWs and quizzes. material is only lecture based and figures can be confusing so attendance is a must!
One of the best professors I have had at Cornell! Made lectures very interesting, and it was very obvious how knowledgable he is. Definitely recommend taking this class.
Great professor!! Loved him!!! Totally recommend this class. Quizzes are sometimes very specific and annoying, and final was kinda hard too.. but overall, it was very fine!

I thought Winans was a nice guy and pretty good professor. His quizzes were pretty straightforward, but his final exam was somewhat difficult (had some short answers in addition to multiple choice). Anyways, you'll enjoy this class if you take it.

He is wryly amusing, yet his work is impeccable, his presentation thorough. Remarkably refreshing, he way he humanizes the sometimes arcane world of microbiology. My interest in science, never above middling warm, grew over the course of the term to a positive snap, crackle and pop. I won't opt into Bio as a major, but Winans is simply awesome.
he is overall very decent - very clear and highly approachable - however, he's sometimes unorganized / goes too slow.

Taught the 2nd half of general microbio. when Ghiorse took a sabbatical leave.  He wasn't quite as clear as G. but went into more depth in lecture, which I appreciated.  He's very passionate about microbio and readily answers student questions in class.  Quizzes got harder w/ him, but studying the material made you appreciate the class more.
Professor Winans was hard but a good lecturer and taught in depth. I actually learned a lot. It was very interesting.
RMP should change name to Willow Starr to reflect her new name. She should only be disrespected for poor excuse for teaching, not for her gender identity. Do not take
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Great professor who cares about subject matter. Class had daily lecture quizzes, so while the class was not lecture heavy, it was important to stay engaged during lecture; ended up being a large part of the final grade (you also got multiple drops for these). 2 papers, TAs go through it in discussion, and has multiple prompts/deadlines for students

This was so much work for a level 100 class. TAs and professors were impossible to get hold of. A professor would never respond to emails, wouldn't be at their own office hours, and would never get back to you. I asked for a regrade of something at beginning of semester and professor kept saying she will get to it (never did). do not take.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very clear grading for essays. Very clear prompts. Minds and Machines was very interesting but not sure the lectures were always great. You can take this class without any knowledge in compsci but you will most likely be putting in more effort in the first month. Only bad part, questions were never really answered in class. Idk it was weird.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Great Professor! Very humorous and knowledgable. I enjoyed the presented materials and the lectures. I would definitely recommend it!

I loved taking PHIL 1440 with Professor starr. I signed up for this class because I was really interested in the topic, and professor starr definitely made the class worth it. They showed a lot of passion in the subject and also graded the papers super clearly. Gave good feedback and made it easy to learn. The topics were super interesting too.

writing a mid-semester review because i cant wait until the end of the year to impart my thoughts. maybe it's bc of their kids, maybe it's bc of their courseload, but they were not available to talk to students. want to revise your essay? go to office hours? not there. all thtings considered, they know their stuff. pop quizzes. watch out.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Engaging and caring
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: can't say I enjoyed this class. Starr was chill but material was boring - he didn't make it interesting. came in w/ 0 knowledge of cogsci, compsci, or phil, & had hard time comprehending some material. he would lecture to us as if we already had some knowledge in compsci, which made it confusing. VERY important to do readings - random quizzes!

A good class - you don't *have* to do the readings, but it would definitely add to the understanding of the course. iClicker quizzes interspersed throughout lectures, so ya gotta go, but Prof Starr is genuine and kind and super engaged and willing to help students.
Willy is a top professor
reviews.rating_tags: Inspirational--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Easiest class I've taken here. Homeworks are super easy, and exams follow the exact same format as the practice ones. The only thing that might lower your grade is participation if you choose to skip lectures and recitation, but it won't hurt you that much.

Spends the entire time talking about minds and machines, just as advertised. However, do not be fooled by his mild, unassuming human hipster exterior.  What he does not tell you is that he is in actuality a machine himself. Beware: they are taking over.

I've taken two classes with him so far, both very interesting. He is a good lecturer, if a bit inept at rendering some material interesting. His expectations are clear and reasonable and you should have no problem doing well. He's fairly friendly and glad to take questions. His seminar was involved with cool readings and fun discussions.

The activities we do in-class definitely helped progress my understanding of R, and the HW is manageable. There are weekly readings that you have to complete. During classroom labs, Hobbs took the time to ensure that students were able to keep up and stayed behind for any questions. Hobbs also was patient in giving feedback for my final project.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I came into the class with minimal knowledge of R, and Professor Hobbs increased that knowledge like ten-fold. He's very knowledgable about R and his lectures are very helpful. Get ready to read for this class and go to office hours. It's quite technical, but very rewarding. Definitely recommend for those interested in social science research.

Professor Hobbs is very intelligent and kind, but the class doesn't necessarily feel intro level. Weekly Perusall readings (Intro to R book) w/ a lot of code examples. Must spend >1 hour on weekly reading, and add 3 comments or questions. Do the readings and show up to class. And GO TO OFFICE HOURS. ask a lot of questions, he's there to help!

No tests, just labs in class and HW that can be quite tough. Readings are required and graded on based on participation with them(like for real checks). Late penalties are quite brutal, and getting started is difficult. Decent class though, it can just can be annoying sometimes. Good dude
Easy grader. Very kind professor.

I absolutely recommend this class! He was an amazing lecturer and made the class super interesting. Super easy assignments (even let us skip one if we asked a question during a guest lecture), attendance not mandatory (but you should go he loves connecting with class), very little work, and he was super accommodating and brought in guest lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Here is a review more recent than 2018: I've taken LING2224 with Prof. Whitman this fall 2023 and I found him to be a great professor. Engaging lectures, lots of guest speakers, and enthusiasm about the topics. He is friendly and approachable. 
Might be difficult/boring if you don't enjoy the course material or aren't actively engaged with lectures
Lectures were very interesting but Prof. Whitman was not a great teacher. Did not always show up for office hours. Seemed a bit disconnected from students, but passionate about linguistics.

I took Intro with him and he's absolutely brilliant in his field. lectures were okay (very occasionally had quizzes) and as long as you do the reading the homework and prelims will be easy. Different person teaches Intro to Ling pretty much every semester tho so im sure it varies

He is a really great professor. He's very kind and extremely knowledgeable in the subject. He gives great advice on your writing, grades fairly, and has interesting lectures. He genuinely cares about his students, and he also has a good sense of humor. I would definitely take a class with him again.
Great professor: dedicated and engaging, and very interested in what you have to say. Good sense of humor too!
Excellent prof. He's great at explaining the material.  His lecture is never boring. Also, he's very helpful so def. take advantage of office hours. I highly recommend his class.
He's not only a respected linguist, but also an excellent teacher. It's great that he's got a humble heart, also. Plus, Whitman actually cares about his students! Take his class if possible.
Excellent professor.  Brings an unusual perspective to his courses.
Whitman is one of the best profs I've had.  If given the chance take a class with him!
Cornell should be very proud to have such an awesome professor!
Prof Whitman is SO nice and incredibly smart.  He's really clear as a teacher, and really easy to talk to.

Took a FWS and Language Typology with Prof. Whitman - he was wonderful for both, even though they were two completely different classes. He expects a lot from you, but is very nice and I definitely learned a lot from him.

I read some of the reviews -- Whitehead speaks quickly, but he is raising different ways to understand the same point.  If you need to scribe everything -- don't.  If you listen and take down the key points -- it was pretty clear to me.

Whitehead covers a lot of material, but it is immediately useful when you work at a firm.  The law is tough, but Whitehead makes is a lot more accessible.

Be ready for lectures, do the reading.  But you will really learn the stuff.
Yes he sometimes speaks fast but he also repeats the key points from multiple perspectives -- if you did the readings, you will do well in the class, and the lectures are great
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Does not convey information clearly. Example: I am going to give you a list of exceptions to the rule. One is .... Two is .... Three is ... Four, but let me first tell you -- while you're expecting another exception -- about what is not an exception and does not belong in this list, even though I am speaking very quickly.

First, Professor Whitehead is a highly accomplished and brilliant. Yet it's not so helpful to have him talk 90 words per minute about the law, rarely taking a pause, and having notes that, while detailed, don't include all of the important content he only communicates orally. By moving so quickly, without notes to compensate, less content sticks.
One of the best classes in law school.  Partner told me to take this class; glad I did.  The subject is difficult, but Whitehead made it a lot easier to follow.
Agree with the others.
The Best
Great Professor, engaging and entertaining lectures. Very helpful and approachable after class. Likes to call on people but is nice about it. Highly recommend his Business Organisations class!

Such such a kind and sweet professor who is also very knowledge about her profession. She also has great connects and brought such succesful Blackstone guest speakers and stuff to class. She is genuily so motherly and literlly invited us to her art exhibiton and her joyful nature makes the class enjoyable. She teaches well and NO PRELIM in this cla
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Wolfe was very inspiring in many different ways as she was exactly who I aspired to become both professionally and personally. I was really surprised and hurt at her lack of compassion when she decided to take half the credit off of my final reflections paper simply because I submitted it to the wrong folder on canvas.

Professor Wolfe is a harsh grader because she wants to push you to improve yourself. If you try and put the effort in, she will support you every step of the way because she cares about all her students. Super strict attendance and participation policy, but she just wants you to get the most from class. Learned so much from this class and her.
Tom was one of my favorite professors at Cornell. His grading and content deliver style was student centric. I have long remembered the hands-on projects we worked on.

He was one of the best I've had! He not only has interesting presentations, outings and relevant topics in class, but he is very nice, too. The class is pretty easy if you attend it regularly. He brings us coffee on lazy afternoons and gave us two manageable midterms. I love him and wish I could take more of his classes.

Professor Whitlow is an angel that walks among us. The course is incredibly informative, but it's very easy to do well. There are no real tests (The midterm and final are opinion based papers) and other grades are based on weekly ten minute quizzes at the start of class which are easy if you have been in class

This is a great class that gets you involved in real-life projects. Professor Whitlow is incredibly knowledgeable and willing to help when needed. The lectures are a little dry but he is good at explaining broad concepts with enough detail to understand. Highly recommend him as a professor. He truly cares about his students.
Tom is a very knowledgeable and patient professor! He also has a strong sense of duty.

Took for medieval food FWS - Super understanding and reasonable, with grading being very forgiving. Lots of opportunity for extra credit and will give extensions if asked. I wasn't too interested in the material initially, but she made it fun & engaging. Definitely take her if you can - I'm so glad I did!

Took Medieval writing FWS; she gave a ton of freedom for paper & presentation topics and definitely wanted everyone to do well. Also had interesting guest lecturers & multiple extra credit opportunities.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Had her for my medieval food FWS. She was very caring and would shift deadlines if we had prelims coming up. Gave extra credit. Lets you eat in class. Very reasonable, manageable workload and flexible with extensions if you need them. Always offered to read your drafts or have conferences with you. Wish I could have her again next semester!

Prof. Won was great! Her lectures were boring at times, but she was very accessible and had clear expectations. As a non-comm major, COMM 2820 was super easy - just make sure you read the textbook and make the cheat sheets for the quizzes.

BEST professor I've had at Cornell. She's very caring, and gives many good suggestions both in and outside the classroom. I also work in her lab and participate in interesting projects. 4380 is also a very interesting class - students will have their own vr set to experience different virtual worlds. Multiple opportunities for extra credit as well.
was an extremely interesting class! I loved it! It was really fun
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Being the Director for her lab, Won is an expert in immersive media. The class bestows knowledge so that students "can go out in the real world and give constructive criticism of commercial VR application" with the most up-to-date research. Fair exams with study term guide. Several projects that serve to boost grade and learn at the same time.

Prof Won seems like she genuinely cares about students doing well but the class is SO SO disorganised. Sooo many unnecessary assignments that are confusing and posted in different folders so you don't know what is due when. Also describes some content in WAY too much detail and other content in too little.

Lectures and class discussions are included on prelims. Prelims require memorization of specific terms (while some didn't seem to be). Discussion/ lab gives hands-on experience on some tech like Wix, Photoshop and tech. Prof. is helpful for office hours. Only down side- managing group activities was very hectic and disorganized.

There is so much unnecessary groupwork and can essentially ruin your grade if you get a bad group. The material is painfully dull and everytime I attended lecture I wish I hadnt. I tend to love communication class but this one was a big L in my opinion. Didnt think a class would be worse than Comm 1100 but Comm 1300 proved me wrong
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--EXTRA CREDIT--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Generally interesting material covered but Prof. Wolf has a "my way or the highway" approach to the subject matter, all while claiming that debate and discussion is an important facet of the course. Grading is fair, but be prepared to say what Prof. Wolf wants to you to hear rather than your own opinions about the subject matter.

I was really excited to take this class for my major, but Wolfs style of teaching really hurt the subject matter for me. Hes very matter of fact and actively invalidates other perspectives. He rambles on and on while making the same point 5 times in 20 minutes. Lots of papers that are arbitrarily graded. Subject has potential, but hes rough

I was first scared away from taking this class because so many people told me it's a hard class. It turned out to be a fairly straight-forward, insightful class! Professor Wolf is very good at explaining overarching governance concepts and organizing the course material. There are some group projects and weekly essays, but overall not a hard class!
One of the best professors I've had at Cornell!
Amazingly clear lecturer. Presents very interesting material. Is a very critical thinker and demands that same level of thought from the class.

Great professor. Class offers lots of opportunity for discussion and is generally interesting and well organized. That being said, there is a lot of work for a 3 credit class (weekly essays and lots of readings to keep track of)
Arrogant, pompous. Walking cliche of the 'Ivy league prof'. Smart guy, but annoying at multiple levels.
I personal did not like him but the class itself was ok. He just rubbed me the wrong way, but you do learn a lot. He is the problem not the class.

thought he was great. organized and interesting lectures...responsive to any questions. class is casual and always open for discussion. responses to readings due each week, all in all, not a lot of work.  learn a lot

Thinks he is God's gift. Grades based on whether or not he likes you, not the percentage you get. When I questioned him about my grade, he wrote back basically telling me that I wasn't capable of understanding the material. Major jerk! His class completely turned me off to the subject area.
she is awesome, the way how she is teaching and makes you remember history is very easy. quizzes are not hard. I learned a lot and understand American history without stress.
If you take good notes from lecture you will do fine - this class is an easy A if you actually go to class.

It's nice to have a professor who wants us to call them by their first name. Marge was a fantastic professor who did a magnificent job teaching us. What I like about Marge is that she didn't beat around the bush, she taught us the truly important stuff like dates and the percentage of 14th amendment cases that dealt with corporate personhood. Bravo

The class was not as intellectually stimulating as others may suggest. All material is simple, straight forward until the exams. 2 exams that are graded unfairly. 1 In class essay that is so easy and graded inconsistently with the regular exams (level of specificity). No class engagement and professor was very monotonous

Wood's class IS stimulating. It IS a GOOD class and is INTERESTING. She does a GREAT job incorporating the meaning of freedom as mentioned in the THREE RATINGS BELOW. However, she is not a FAIR teacher and is very INCONSIDERATE of her student's grades. If you want, like me, to earn a poor grade after trying so hard TAKE HER. My 2 cents.
Wood is great. Go to class and take notes. You'll be challenged but it's worth it. One of the best labor courses I've had at ILR.

Very stimulating, very intellectual. Managed to make Labor History philosophical. Instead of thinking about history of unions, I thought about the meaning of freedom. HIGHLY recommended if you want to think. Great professor, great class!

I absolutely loved Professor Wood! This was by far the best class I've ever had. Her approach to Labor History is extremely interesting and includes former slaves, women, children, and so much more. I was never bored and learned so much. I chose Ivy League because I wanted a quality education, not just an easy A. Wood is AMAZING! Take her!!

Wood is an outstanding lecturer. She is full of knowledge and really knows her stuff. However her exams were extremely challenging and very strictly graded. Directions on the midterm were not clear at all (dates). Also the "quote" section of both exams were near impossible. I learned a lot from her class but if you want a good grade don't take her.
She's not a fair teacher. I would not recommend her because her exams are inconsistent with the material she teaches in class. Take Professor Hymen instead. I wish I did before taking Professor Wood.

The material itself is really easy but she isnt clear with the directions on tests. Specific directions are needed for specific answers and she doesnt provide them. This caused the midterm average to be a B- when it should have been an A-. Take this class with professor Hyman instead.

Marj is nice. She doesnt use powerpoint, so you'll by taking notes nonstop and have too much to review for the tests. But she does give a study guide. The test contains more than what's on it though. Make sure to put dates even though the tests doesn't say to. Learned a decent amount. Not too much reading. I'd say take her.

This class was okay, it gives you a sampling of knowledge you need for future classes. She didn't really help anyone understand anything, so thankfully the material is pretty easy. Projects/HW is usually easy but time consuming.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor doesn't have much personality, but is reasonably clear and fair

Prof. Wu  is pretty boring in lecture. She also is not very clear or well organized, and often speeds through important topics. HW an case studies are graded very strictly, but that just takes some getting used to. The TAs in this class are your best friends.

I highly recommend Dr. Wu's microfluidics course. The labs were suitably challenging and the lectures were generally fun and laid-back. No exams - grades are largely determined by group lab reports and final presentation. Dr. Wu has been very kind and helpful to the students.
Incoherent, clueless - shouldn't be teaching a class. Quite simply the worst prof. ever. Threatened to give me a "C" even though my average was in the 90's.

If there is definition for an average class, this class is it.  Everything is predictable; do the homework, go to lecture, put in some work for the class and you get an A.  He's not the most exciting professor however and will talk quietly while he basically reads the textbook to you.  But the class is not overly difficult.

I had to drop the class after the first lecture since I couldn't understand (1) a word he was saying or (2) what he was writing on the board.  I guess if you already know the material you'll do fine, but after taking ap calc in hs and getting a 5 on the exam, I still found this over my head.

Prof. Wu is a decent lecturer. He is a little reticent in class but if you ask questions he always tries to help. Very helpful in office hours for homework or going over a test. Grading was 40% homework/60% three exams. If you don't enjoy math, you might find Prof. Wu's lectures a little dry; but, he is thorough and precise. Also, great textbook.
uhhh.....just ok, his lecture is not very helpful. I only copied what he wrote on the blackboard. If you don't look back and review, you will forget everything he said.

Started off with him for the first 5 weeks of the semester but did horribly on my first prelim cuz I didn't learn anything from him. Wu just mumbles as he copies his notes onto the blackboard in lecture.
