His CV says it's his first time teaching linear algebra and second time teaching overall so he doesn't seem to know what he's doing. Best avoided.
shelley is very funny as a TA and knows a lot about sociology. Very passionate about the topic and fair grader for essays.

Shelley is one of the best TA I have encountered at Cornell. She helped the professor deliverer some technical contents and is very available and helpful for research and writing projects. The grading was fair and the professor also did a great job clarifying grading criterion.
Xuewen is an amazing TA who knows a lot about the subject and would make herself accessible to students. She also organized interesting class activities for us. Very useful class and would recommend.
the worst TA i have ever had, nice and fair and all but CANNOT teach. an absolute waste of time, resources and effort for everyone involved.

My experience with professor Xu was average. His lectures had the most quantitative material, but were all very basic and easy to understand. He likes plants, numbers, and graphs about plants, so you'll like him if that's your thing.

1610 was an average intro ecology course, taught by Dr. Xu and Dr. St Juliana with a TA-led section. Dr. Xu was a decent lecturer, and the content was not particularly difficult. There is a textbook, but I rarely read it. However, the tests could be unnecessarily tricky (even TAs had trouble), and the section work was often unhelpful or pointless.

Xiangtao was a fairly engaging and entertaining lecturer, I rarely found myself bored to tears during lectures. Other than that, BIOEE 1610 was a fairly average biology/ecology course, which was worthwhile enough for me and not terribly hard. The tests were needlessly tricky in my opinion, but the content itself is not very hard and is interesting.
He was a super nice guy, but the tests were a little trickier than they should have been and sometimes he struggled to explain material very clearly.
Prof not too bad, but the exam sucks. Too "flexible" to relate to what you've learned

Overall Dr. Xu is an engaging lecturer who knows a lot about the subject and makes it interesting.He sometimes goes off topic and gives extra information that is not going to be tested which leads him to run out of time at the end of lectures. Class is very participation driven so go to lecture/section.
He scheduled a prelim on the day before Thanksgiving break... enough said

Gave good lectures but the class was very disorganized. The labs were taught by the TA's and didn't always relate back to the lectures. Homework and labs were often very confusing and required a lot of time at office hours for clarification. Tests were much too difficult for an ENGRI class. Would not recommend this class.

A great lecturer, but may go off on (very interesting) tangents and not get through all he planned, but it will still be on the test. That or it all gets repeated in the next lecture, you never know. Very accessible outside of class and I'd recommend going to every lecture and office hours to learn and because of how funnily quotable he is.
Great overall class. Tests destroy self confidence but material is very interesting. The homeworks and labs are graded generously, and there is a curve at the end.
Really helpful, clear and even humorous.
Knows his stuff and is really great at clarifying things when you ask for help. Homework was not hard and the labs were fantastic. His tests are very hard though.
class is great

Prof Xu's intro to engineering course is one of the most difficult in that category. Prelim 1 had a mean of 41%. That being said, material is interesting, labs are fun and Office Hours with him are quite useful.

Prof. Xu is very smart, but not the greatest teacher. His class was very interesting and you learn a lot from him. Tests are surprisingly hard for an intro to engineering class (on our midterm, the mean was something like 40/95). Homework doesn't take up much time. Labs are fun.

Overall excellent professor. Funny but focused. Lectures were well organized and clear. A difficult first year class (at the level of Purcell/Morin and Griffiths) but at the end I have definitely learned a lot. Grading was generous; Prof. Xu is more interested in what you learn.

He is a very good teacher. He explained the content well, and has a good sense of humor. He is willing to help if you ask for it. The tests were very hard. The problem sets were difficult,  but there is not too much homework. Overall, a good teacher and difficult content.

Chris failed to explain the subject matter in a clear way. He gave no suggestions for other helpful books, which I had to find myself with trial and error. Motivation for the topics was rare, giving the lectures the feel of a boring textbook.

Toughest class I have taken at Cornell, hands down.  Some of the material was dry, but he presented it in a clear way.  Extremely tough problem sets and exams.  They really make you think in ways outside the box.
he's SO boring and the class is SO early. the two just don't mix.
Chris' teaching is a beauty to behold, clear and crisp.  He will challenge you in ways that really highlight the subtleties, complexities, and beauty of E&M.  Extremely recommended.
Great class highly reccomend. Attend lectures and take notes on everything, no work outside class aside from studying for prelims
Clear lectures and engaging topics. He made students want to attend every class.

A solid introduction to python using interesting meteorological examples, homework coding assignments are given after the lecture portion of class concludes to start on with the prof present and then due before the next class (usually 2 assignments per week). Accessible outside of class to help understand assignments or run thru issues in code.

Wysocki is one of the funniest and most enjoyable lecturers once you get to know him. He can be intimidating and a bit condescending at first, but i guess it makes you tougher. Complaint is that he rarely posts material on canvas and grade is solely determined by somewhat harsh evaluations of 4 exams. Exams are tough, have to memorize all of unit.

Wysocki is very down to earth and if you respect him and respect what you're studying, he's a great professor to have. Some complain he's way too tough but he's only tough to a few people to set an example, don't take it too seriously because if you actually need help he's one of the best people to explain things simply.

For those with a strong science background who are not meteorology majors: His lectures are aggressive and condescending.  Answers questions by repeating his previous statement in a more patronizing tone.  Unhelpful during office hours. Answers the same question differently if asked multiple times. Grades suffer for his errors on multiple choice qs
Really funny guy who teaches a great class. Wysocki is the man!

He's funny, he's nice, and you learn a lot. But the exams are hard (you basically have to learn everything by heart and repeat it during the exam) and i felt that he wasn't really interested in doing an intro course for people who just want science credits. TAKE THE LAB, even if it's at night: it's fun, interesting and easy.
Fun professor who makes the best jokes, e.g. "If you are like me and get on a scale, it's gonna tell you: get the f*ck off of me!" HE is awesome.
He is a brilliant guy but not very helpful when you struggle in the class

Wysocki is fantastic! Clear, organized, loves meteorology. Eccentric sense of humor had me laughing every class. I didn't miss a single one even though it was a 9am.  Tests are very, very straightforward; you do need to learn everything, but the volume is manageable and he reviews at the beginning of every class.

Great guy: clear and funny. The prelims and exams for this class DO require a fair bit of preparation; however, they center on the concepts rather than on the equations. Go to class, do the readings, complete the practise exams, and you'll be just fine.

As a meteorology major, I just want to say that in the dpeartment, students unanimously love this guy. His tests are notorious for being long and minute in detail, but he's a really great guy and he's always willing to go the extra mile to help a student out. Amazing professor.
Good guy ... Bad class ... Killer Prelims ... Worst Final Ever
Wysocki is a natural teacher.  He loves it and he's great at it.  The tests are more than reasonable.  He gave one of the few lectures I actually wanted to attend, even if it was a 9am.
He is hilarious yet for an intro course, EAS 131 is intense and requires many hours of preparation just to get the mean on prelims.

Your best chance to do well is to read the textbook. Do not expect any help! The TAs are sometimes so rude that while they proctor exams, they randomly choose exams of students who have finished and start making fun of their answers. Avoid if you can.
Terrible, terrible, terrible prelims! The final exam was even worse. He loves to ask questions  that are never covered in class.
Wysocki is the man. Take this class. Take all his classes. Major in meteorology. Freakin awesome.
Nice guy, ridiculously hard tests.
funny
funny guy, no homework.  but the tests are HARD.  and there is NO CURVE.  not too helpful, either.  office hours? none.
Mark was the reason I became a teacher.  His trademark Coke can in his hand and his "verbal handwaving" made him one of my favorites.  Happy 50th Mark.
weather will never be the same anymore. the most interesting class that you can take. i highly recommend it!!!
an overall fantastic teacher.  he is very engaged in his lectures and i have no problem understanding his concepts.  very very funny, too!!!  probably among the best professors at cornell.
Passionate, caring professor. His class is always fun. However, the exams are rather hard and the TAs very rude.
This guy made me look at the sky differently!!  I learned heaps and would want anyone remotely interested in weather to take this class.  It was really enjoyable and this guy is hilarious!
Great class.  I suggest it to everybody I see.  If you go to class and pay attention, you will learn a lot about the weather and you will get a fantastic grade.
Wysocki is just a fountain of weather knowledge. He really loves what he teaches and is great at teaching it. Go to lecture and pay attention to what he says and youll do fine on the tests.
Best teacher at cornell.  Awesome guy in class and out of class. Loves what he teaches and cares for his students.  long live WYSOCKI!
Oh, the Wysocki-isms - can't get enough of 'em...  Boring class, awesome teacher!

Wysocki kicks ass!  He is such an easy-going guy who's very approachable.  I went to his office one time for ten minutes of help but ended up chatting with him about weather for over an hour.  He's AWESOME for meteorology majors and non majors alike-
Wysocki is the man. Good teacher, easy to approach, very helpful. His early classes are really easy, but his later ones can get a little tricky. Only complaint: his labs are hard to sit through.
Fun, easy going, and says "WOW!"....A LOT.

Funny Guy! Great teacher. Cares a lot about students and loves to joke. Also, very smart and knowledgeable and never scales grades. Classes border on the easy side, but much is learned. An EAS oracle!
It is a lot of fun to take his classes.

I have never met a better teacher than Mr. Wysocki.  He knows his subject inside and out, cares about his students, and is always there to help you out with work or life.  The Cornell Meteorology program would be lost without him.
Wysocki is the man!
Very effective lectures and has a solid understanding of the material. Helpful in office hours and is passionate about the topics.
The most unreasonable and harsh grading system I have known in my life. Does something called grade
The professor is partial. Grading of the course is unreasonable.

Overall, a very ncie guy. The group project makes up a substantial portion of your grade along with an online final exam (atleast was the case for Fall '24). Lectures were him creating hand written digrams of course concepts which was a ~different~ approach compared to the typical slide deck presentation for delivering lectures.

The easiest class of all time; genuinely a tragedy if you do not get an A+. All quizzes are online, asynchronous, and open notes, and attendance is not mandatory. Truly the easiest class you will ever take in the history of the universe.

Extremely Easy Class. Never went to class (neither did anyone else). Professor was extremely boring and it upset me because marketing is otherwise an interesting topic to me. If you're looking for an easy class take this but don't expect to be that engaged with the class material or lectures.
Really easy class. Nice guy, but pretty boring lectures that make it hard to pay attention

Easiest class I have ever taken at Cornell. All notes are posted and all quizzes/final draw information from the lectures. Would highly recommend for anyone to take, whether interested in business, or even just to raise GPA. Professor Yang was always ready to talk after class about technology in marketing or about other course material.

TAKE THIS CLASS!!! Professor was an awesome guy, super knowledgeable and made class fun to go to. Grading was extremely generous and assessment was all based on lecture material. I would recommend to anyone taking the business minor, and anyone at Cornell in general. In case I didn't make it clear, take this class!

Professor Yang is the goat for intro to marketing. Super nice guy, with easy quizzes/final. He also incorporates a lot of his cutting-edge research into the class as well which is really interesting. TAKE THIS CLASS!

Professor Yang is a professor for the students. His course is 7 quizzes and one final. The quizzes are all mc. Every answer is in the slides (not sure why other reviews say they are not). If a question is tricky or has bad wording, he will omit the question and give everyone credit. He truly sets the class up to be as stress-free as possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Yang is truly a gem. I had no previous experience in business classes and took his class for fun. I fell in love with the material and the professor made the material easy to understand and extremely relevant to the current digital age. If you want an easy class and an introduction to marketing I highly recommend taking this class.

DO NOT take Yang. This class was terrible and you will not learn a single thing. It was the biggest waste of time while I was at Cornell. Also, his quizzes and tests are the worst. Literally, the questions made no sense and were from neither the slides nor the textbook, and often they were trick questions. Don't take - this class will be miserable.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Yang was not the best lecturer, but so nice and understanding. Attending lecture was not necessary at all - grades were based on 5 quizzes throughout the semester and a cumulative final. Information came literally right from the slides, and everything was open note. Minimal effort for an easy A+.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Nathan Yang is the WORST professor I have ever had at Cornell. Your grade is determined by 5 quizzes, all of which are littered with trick questions (multiple possible answers for one question). Study as much as you want, it doesn't make a difference. There's a final worth 30% of your grade and it's just as bad. He ruined my GPA.

The best professor at Cornell ever! She truly cares about her students, is extremely patient in answering all questions in class, and explains everything very clearly. She always smiles, is very nice, and super friendly. She's like a genius—solving all your questions quickly and effortlessly!

Excellent 
Strongly recommend Dr.Yang!

Rarely comment on professors, but loved this one.
Had handwritten notes posted so you had time to think in class without having to copy notes all the time. The exams are not difficult and fit well with the assignments and class. Very friendly to students and the review class before exams was useful. A fulfilling learning process. Love her dog.

Lectures were just her rewriting the previous professors notes on a Goodnotes page. The YouTube videos from the previous professor taught me more than she did in class. Everything in this class was covered in Entner's 3020 and he arguably taught it better. Its disappointing that such a integral class for the major basically wasn't taught at all.

Easy, but professor doesn't know how to run a proper course at all.

Lectures were dry, boring proofs line by line with errors and brought her dog. Lectures on YT from prev prof were much better and 1/3 of the time. Ed never responded to. HW was easy but pointless. Almost no new material taught. 2 TAs for 200 students, and blatant exam cheating.

I have never felt so unsupported in a class. Dana holds one office hour per week and the TA's hold none. She created an Ed forum for us and course staff virtually never answered our questions. Homeworks are not graded quickly and we took the final with no clue where we stood. She is disorganized, but she made the final crazy easy.

There were videos of class, so you didn't have to go, but lectures were definitely mandatory to watch in some way. The homework was unreasonably difficult given the percent each problem was worth. I'd say that for ever .01% of your grade, you had to put in around an half an hour of work. That's a LOT of work. Lectures are super boring too.

There were videos of class, so you didn't have to go, but lectures were definitely mandatory to watch in some way. The homework was unreasonably difficult given the percent each problem was worth. I'd say that for ever .01% of your grade, you had to put in around an hour of work. That's a LOT of work. Lectures are super boring too.

There were videos of class, so you didn't have to go, but lectures were definitely mandatory to watch in some way. The homework was unreasonably difficult given the percent each problem was worth. I'd say that for ever .1% of your grade, you had to put in around an hour of work. That's a LOT of work. Lectures are super boring too.
Great man!

Didn't particularly like this guy; seemed rather arrogant and dogmatic in his views.  He gave the Tuesday lectures for the course; basically a standard popular science lecture, nothing you won't get out of Sagan or others...he's no Carl Sagan.
This is quite simply a great class.  Both the professors are laid back but also very good teachers.  Astronomy is a great subject -- if you have even a slight interest you will enjoy this class.

Yo f*ck this class. Literally go in, listen to her say "sigma wah wah" twenty times in a lecture,  then end up asking yourself, 'Da f*ck did I just learn?' TAs don't know the material; claim the class is messed up. Pass a prelim, do some projects, have your ears bleed two times a week, done.
Really unclear boring lectures. Pointless, overcomplicated projects. Only one prelim that's worth 30% of the grade, which means if you mess do poorly in the class.

Lecture was well organized, printable slides were very helpful. Could have covered some more content. Didn't dig into fundamentals as much as other courses. She did communicate ways to check numerical results well. Easy homework, though only 5% of grade. Exams were somewhat easy, though needed a little more time. Projects were a good intro to ANSYS

This is a pretty cool class and Prof. Gao is definitely in her element. She is clear, organized, and always prepared for lecture. She is helpful outside of class and is always willing to make time to talk to students one on one. She's also really funny!

Prof. Gao is adorable and a really kind person. She is understanding and super helpful in office hours. She really cares about teaching and always asks for feedback on how to be a better professor. She is fair in grading and her tests reflect exactly what has been covered in class and readings.

Professor Gao certainly isn't the best professor that I've ever had teaching me, but then again, the material for 325 is pretty awful to begin with. Watch out with her board work- r, gamma, and theta look very similar. She improved over the course of the semester, but she needs a few more classes to get comfortable- you could tell she was nervous.

Worst professor I've had yet here. I'm sure she knows her stuff, but tops even Max Zhang for the Incomprehensible-Chinese-Accent award. Often can't get across what she wants to, which can lead to wording on tests being vague and confusing when she tries to get clever with a question. Uses iClickers to ensure you basically have to go, too.

Terrible. Often will give examples in class that she hasn't worked out on her own or that she will not review the answer. Makes mistakes OFTEN. Admits to not having notes prepared for lecture. Will argue with students when she is wrong. More of a grad student than a professor. Has not taught in the past and it shows.

Her chinese accent and lack of good often grammar makes following lectures nearly impossible. She doesn't follow the same methods prescribed in the book. She often makes grammar mistakes in problems which completely changes the meaning of the problem. She often gets in arguments with students over the correctness of her methods.

Unsure of syllabus structure, which can be confusing for students. lecture material doesn't always correspond to prescribed textbook, which makes it doubly difficult to follow the material as there is often confusion between the material in homework and material from textbook.
This is her first time teaching undergrads, so she is a bit inexperienced. She is a nice lady with good intentions, but could use some practice communicating with students.
Very difficult to understand.  Doesn't follow 212 conventions.  Very high pitched voice.  Recommend reading the book instead of listening to lecture.  Doesn't listen to student voice.

Don't know what all the hate on this class is. Material is straight out of the book and don't need to go to lecture to learn it. Professor understands and accepts that 99% of people who take this class don't actually care about chemistry; they're only doing it because it's a college of engineering requirement. Tests are fair

PLEASE case this class if you can. She doesn't enjoy teaching this class and makes that pretty obvious. Unfamiliar with the pre-reqs of her own class (eigenvalues and triple integrals). T/F questions on her tests are pretty much impossible. Said she was going to leave during a review session because no one knew the answers.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I went to every lecture and still knew absolutely nothing for the final. There would be problems on the exams that she never even mentioned once. Her lectures weren't helpful, and she didn't explain the material well at all.

Do not take 2090 with this professor. She didn't give prelim 2 back so no chance to improve on the final. 70% of your grade is exams, but she tests concepts never taught in lecture and not in the textbook (I checked). Lectures are awful. She never solves problems completely, expects you to have taken multi, linear algebra, and AP chem before.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was a poorly structured class and often filled with her just talking to herself and skipping problems after not being able to figure out the answer.

350 characters is not enough to explain how terrible of a teacher she is, however it is enough to explain all the things related to chemistry she taught me. no actually 7 is enough: nothing. ill-conceived lectures where she writes lightly on the board in silence. dont waste time studying for her tests. legit gen chem bro hello

The class is not very fair. The exams include topics mentioned once during class (don't match the style of hw or lecture problems) and the professor discusses topics outside the scope of the class (eigenvectors, eigenvalues, integrals etc). During lectures, she often spends time facing the board and writing stuff rather than explaining the topics.

If you thought Musser was bad, she is much worse! Her topics on exams and tests are often very different from what is covered in class, and whatever is covered in class is either taught very poorly or too advanced for an intro chem course (holy eigenvalues). Every word she speaks can be used as a true/false question on the exam, so beware!

a lecturer like no other, truly a marvel here at cornell university; I'm extremely blessed to have been able to take chemistry under youn jue (eunice) bae's incredible teaching and I recommend everyone to only take this class under her guidance!

Bae does not teach clearly and the exams are extremely unfair. Lectures just consist of her writing on the board and reading it off to the class. The formula sheet given to us on the prelim had formulas that were not shown or taught in class. Asks if the class has any questions which was appreciated but will shut down students when they ask.

Tag is get ready to read because get ready to learn nothing in lecture. I should've known sooner but I knew class was doomed when she started talking about triple integrals and eigenstates with no prior explanation. Her lectures are disorganized and it's often hard to decipher her notes. I really hope she'll get an iPad for her next class.
Extremely disorganized, does not answer questions in class, gets easily annoyed when students don't understand content in an introductory course
Understanding and caring professor. She makes lectures entertaining and is accepting of student feedback. The tests are fair and the curve is generous. Take CHEM2090 with Professor Bae!

First review on rate my professor that I felt was warranted. Professor writes notes on chalkboard that often feel disorganized, most likely because she types them, prints it out with no structuring or indentation whatsoever, copies that on the board, then takes a picture of the paper she typed up and uploads that as notes for the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: disorganized lectures, illegible notes. thinks everyone took chem before. in lecture she mumbles and writes on chalkboard without explaining anything. prelim had bubble sheet and was graded with AI, avg 57%, didn't test on any of what we learned, gave us a sheet w equations we've never seen. case out if you can. she got a columbia degree too..

Where to begin... she's new to the course I hope she never teaches it again for future students. Her lectures are all over the place and writes on the chalkboard so it's kinda hard to see/read. Any little thing she mentions can be up to 3 problems on the prelims which is annoying. She's not responsive to feedback.
very difficult and doesn't get that we have other classes aside from his
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Young gives an insane amount of busy work. Don't expect to have any social life when taking his class. He gives very subjective and confusing feedback. He truly makes life miserable for his students to the point where multiple people were left in tears after getting extremely negative feedback from him. Avoid at all costs.

Be prepared to work a lot - more than other studios. It's hard. But your produced drawings and models 
 will show it. You will get a lot better and will have great portfolios to show for it. it's mainly always manageable even with a social live. Just expect to have no down time between school and social things.

While he is really difficult, he really cares to push you to be the best aspiring architect. He is passionate to teach and really wants to stretch your creativity. It is difficult and uncomfortable at times but is for sure worth it.
Gives terrible, vague and not helpful feedback. He makes an already very difficult course harder and more time consuming. He is also not understanding of other commitments or circumstances.

Prof. Mao is really nice and caring. You have to be extremely good at taking exams to succeed in this course. It's really difficult. I'm an upperclassman bio major and this is definitely one of the hardest science courses I've taken.  I would not recommend you cram for the tests since they have a lot of material and test you at a very fine detail.

The lectures are really fast-paced and required, but that is basically all there is to the class. There is 
homework for each lecture, but its only like 2 questions, and I never did the readings. There is an optional extra credit video at the end of the semester. Tests are very crammable, except the final which is worth 50% of your grade

Yuxin is a sweet guy, cares about his students. The material can be dense but not too hard to follow. Gotta show up for the attendance. The TA's are all helpful and they post a lot of review videos. Class is exam heavy but cramming is doable.

Yuxin is by far the BEST prof i've had at cornell for bio classes. He's extremely clear in the way he articulates things: his explanations are so clear and to the point. I had no problems understanding the concepts he was teaching me. He was very prepared to all his lectures - slides were great and concise and had demos when he tried to explain.

One of the best Professors I've had in the Physics department. He truly cares if the students are successful, and is willing to go over concepts and exams one-on-one with students. Also, lectures are a bit hand-wavey, but he is willing to explain the bigger picture/give resources for deeper understanding to those who ask. Overall, a great Professor

Yuval is one of a kind. He is the first professor to properly introduce how to think about physics. Intuition is what you will mainly take out of the class. Yuval's lectures were extremely entertaining with hilarious anecdotes and comments. Also an amazing person to talk to. He just kept giving me mint that he grew; it was quite a good trade.

Yuval is nice, but the class (3317) is nonsense. The technical content is all over the place with little depth, and the physics picture/intuition aspects are already well covered in other physics classes. Also the teaching staff are just being lazy at grading proper free response exam questions and instead give some T/F question which is just funny

Cares a lot about building intuition, which results in being kind of hand-wavey at times. Lectures are interesting and homeworks are the shortest I've ever had in the physics department. Would recommend.

Starts off a bit hand-wavey, but once you get the hang of his teaching style, he's absolutely incredible. He cares so much about every single person really understanding the topics. If you ever have trouble understanding something, he'll go over it with you until you really do.
Great Professor. Covers particle physics very theoretically and intuitively. Extremely friendly and funny as well! The way he covers material is impossible to find in textbooks.

He is very hand-wavey and doesn't explain the fundamental concepts. What is the action? I still don't know... He doesn't give a why; he often just gives a how. I felt like I was learning procedures rather than concepts. Also his ego is approaching critical mass.

Class gave you a very good conceptual understanding of classical mechanics.  Homework made you get into more details.  I thought the class had a nice balance.  Yuval really cares about your learning more than hearing himself talk.

Professor Yu is nice, but his class is terribly organized. Homework assignments are graded on a genuinely subjective scale consisting of a "wow factor" that is entirely dependent on how generous a TA is feeling. You may therefore never receive a 100 for completing an assignment correctly. Core concepts are hand-wavey and unfounded in data or logic.

Yu seems like a nice guy, but his class is horrible. He operates with a subjective grading schema (lost points on the "wow factor" for every assignment) and cannot be reached outside of lecture. The class is interesting, but is heavily dependent on nebulous buzzwords. Minor technicalities in definitions make this class a headache.

Not accessible after class - you have to email to book office hours even for the TAs. The content was okay-level difficulty but he made the lecture boring. The prelims are open notes but the time was very limited. Also, the example questions he gave were way easier than the actual ones. Not much to refer to when you try to study for the tests.

A mind-numbing experience. The content is interesting, but Chao delivers it in the driest and most unclear way. He somehow has a way to make easy concepts confusing, not to mention that he is the least accessible prof -- never holds any office hours or review sessions. Overall, it is an easy class, but not a good one if he teaches it.

Get ready to learn algebra, buddy. He's the goat nothing left to be said about it. If you like math (and are good at it), he's a great professor. Makes sense that all the bad reviews are from intro classes, he teaches very rigorously, but still imparts a great understanding of big picture for whatever he's talking about.

Get ready for the ride of your life! A lot of the negative reviews are for introductory classes, and that tracks: he is built to teach graduate courses, and he felt almost bored teaching the single toughest undergrad math class.  He always went 15 minutes over on lecture, we had triple the work of other classes, I wouldn't have it any other way.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I only went to class a few times, but the times that I did were always great. Oftentimes he would write something silly on the board, or if you were lucky he would make fun of a student for asking a bad question. It's also always a fun challenge to try to understand what he's saying. If you actually want to learn, however, you have to read.

He is not a bad professor, but this class can easily be passed just by doing homework and reading the textbook. I would say go to lectures if that is an easier way for you to comprehend the material. Lots of stuff on prelims and finals can be found in a textbook. Homeworks are not graded but weekly quizzes are solely based on homework.

It is a pretty tough class and the TA's are pretty bad. The professor is good at teaching, but he is very archaic. Homework is optional but you need to do it to pass this class. Textbook is your friend. This class is more learning it on your own.

The class is tough tbh. Got A in 1920, B+ in 2930. Lectures are chalk & blackboard and quite organized. Funny to me, not to everyone. 2 concerns: 1) He doesn't do examples in class, you'll only see them on HW. He only teaches theory (at least for most topics) AND 2) He will often, especially early in the semester, run overtime by ~3 minutes
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Textbook is helpful, interesting lectures, friendly
He's definitely not for everyone as his teaching style is pretty archaic but if you get used to it you'd see he's actually a very good teacher.

stopped going to lectures after the first month and fully completed the class by learning from TAs and the textbook, incomprehensible and confusing lectures.

He also put his office hours right after the weekly quizzes, likely so that no one comes to him for help.
avoid
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Escape if you can.
Lectures have a lot of info that aren't relevant for exams. Often, he would rush at the end and go over the class's time slot. Tells jokes sometimes. The textbook was much more helpful.
Lectures were interesting but largely unhelpful, you're better off teaching yourself via the textbook.
Fine professor
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Lectures were pretty unhelpful and confusing, mostly just proofs and didn't really teach how to do the problems. The textbook was definitely really important. All of the test problems (Prof. Berest wrote every test though there were two other profs) are really similar to textbook problems so do the homework and you'll be fine.

Lectures are all over the place and not even relevant to what we do for homework, quizzes, and exams. Ended up learning from the textbook and doing the homeworks, and his exams didn't even have to do with those and what we did in class. I attended a few lecturers for the other professors and the difference was huge. Do not recommend at all.

If you want to learn calc 2, youre better off watching khan videos. He is all over the place in lecture and seems to add more than needed in the small amount of class time. Even though he says a lot, you practically get nothing out of it.
Not a good teaching method
Clumsy during lecture. Unclear objectives. Makes condescending jokes. Mean and loud. Exams were graded unfairly. Test questions were about as well put together as his lectures.
Good lectures, assigns an appropriate amount of homework to teach the material. Often falls behind the lecture schedule however.

Professor is very good at explaining course material and answers any questions in-lecture. Doesn't, however, cover anything that is not in the textbook, in principle. Sometimes decides to make some jokes, which are usually pretty funny. Overall, a fine professor.
He's good. The lectures are clear and  well structured.

Professor Berest followed the textbook very closely, and if you paid attention in class, was very helpful. A lot of students don't like his lectures, but they were useful as long as you didn't slack off yourself. The exams were challenging but doable if you keep up with the homework, and this class was much better than MATH 1920.

Really didn't seem interested in teaching the course. Lectures were very dull and at times could be condescending, office hours weren't very helpful either. Tests very proof based for an engineering math class and watch out for the truefalse questions. Material seemed to repeat itself after the first prelim. Most didn't go to class mid semester

I can assure you, there's a huge chance that after the first few weeks, you stop attending this man's class. He is basically useless, and you learn everything from the textbook. He also has really mean negative grading true and false questions that mess a lot of people up. If you have a choice, take it with another professor.

Class was always packed but it was rather dull. He tried very hard to make it interesting but, we were often bored. All in all, he's a nice and enthusiastic professor but the book and other resources were essential to learning in this course because his teaching style was difficult to follow.
Nice professor. Comes late in lectures tho.. and finishes late.. kinda funny.. overall a decent professor

I dropped this course last year because I couldn't keep up, but Yuri's excellent lectures kept me going through the interminable homeworks. That being said, he usually arrives 5 minutes late for lectures and finishes 10 minutes over time (punctuality is not one of his virtues...)
I can't understand people here complain about him.. His explanation is crystal clear and very helpful.
No need to attend lecture. Just go to discussions and learn from the textbook yourself.

His lectures are very clear and sequential. Example questions are very similar to prelim problems. Homework is not difficult just tedious. TA is helpful. He tends to keep us late, which has become really annoying.
Yuri is awesome.  Learned a ton in his class.  Probably my favorite math teacher while I was at Cornell.

Funny guy.  Standard Theorem-Proof lectures.  HW was long, about 70% proofs.  Exams were fair.  Usually late to class, always in a rush, and usually kept us 10 minutes over.  Didn't like people coming to office hours without specific questions, but willing to help.

Separate graduate student as grader. He is easily sidetracked. Can sometimes be unclear (likes to give "non-examples"), but generally the material can be figured out with help from the book. Problem sets due once a week, reasonable. Entertaining person, but boring topic. Bring something else to do to class.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.  HEAVY accent, tests too difficult, unwilling to help because it will give away answers.  Sloppy on board.  TA's unhelpful.  AVOID AT ALL COSTS.  Take a different course, this one is basically useless.

I hated his class, I hated the way he taught, I hated everything about Math 213. But then I went to Office Hours during Study Week and even though I failed three out of the four tests (including the Final), I still pulled off a C. So I can't give him a really bad rating.
Nice guy, but not the most effective teacher.  He seems to confuse a somewhat easily understood topic.

Berest is a very clear lecturer, and he uses the board very well. His accent can get in the way, but overall he relays the information well. And he tries to make jokes, which work about 30% of the time. At least he tries. But an enjoyable class overall.

Berest was not a solid lecturer.  He was clumsy on the board, and not clear.  Typical of professors I've found thus far in the math department: extremely smart, and very dedicated to his work, but lacking in lecturing skills.  Math 336 itself is a joke...I taught myself and got a good grade.

The best class I've taken at Cornell by a long shot. It is very obvious Yunhao is passionate about teaching and cares about students' outcomes. I found myself often going to office hours to go beyond the course material, which Yunhao made exciting and approachable.
Take professor Zhang's cs4411 if you are serious about computer science. The course is truly a treasure of Cornell.
Yunhao was really helpful in office hours! Great professor.

Yunhao shows a clear passion for teaching and really cares about his students. The projects for the class were difficult, but I learned a lot from them. They were very well specified and made me think outside of the box to since they were very flexible, and there was no one specific way to implement them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He is goated. His projects were really fun and I learned a good deal. He is very lenient and very his explanations are great.
Always helpful and excited to teach.
Yunhao is an amazing teacher and really cares about his students!

He was a great lecturer and his projects were well designed and specified. He had great organization in the structure of the course. He also was extremely responsive on ed and had probably some of the most effective office hours I have ever been to at Cornell. Highly recommend taking 4411 or other courses he teaches.
Great class, really helpful and guides students along the way.
Yunhao is an amazing instructor. He knows his material really well, and is always super willing to take as much time as needed to answer any and all questions you have, both in class and outside.

Yunhao was a great professor, he was super willing to talk to and help students inside and outside of class. Class material was difficult at times but he would take the time to answer any questions students had.
Professor Zhang was a wonderful professor. He made the material engaging and exciting. Also, we was very helpful in office hours. You get a sense that he cares about the class and the students!

Really enjoyed practicum with Yunhao. It was clear he made a great effort to convey material clearly in lecture and dedicated a lot to improving existing course material. He was also very accessible in office hours and quickly helped debug on problems me and my partners ran into.
Very knowledgable on the topic and extremely helpful and patient in office hours. Yunhao also showed a clear passion for the topics he was teaching.

Yunhao was one of my favorite instructors at Cornell. He cared about his students and about the material he taught. He was also extremely helpful outside of class and thoroughly answered my questions about assignments.
Yunhao is a great Professor. Personally interacts with all students and is extremely helpful at Office Hours. Lectures were enjoyable and he is clearly interested in the content he teaches.
enthusiastic and engaging instructor, helped students have a thorough understanding of content beyond what was required for assignments
Yunhao went out of his way to help his students understand and complete the projects. Very helpful. Only 1 lecture a week but made them count.

Joe is a nice guy and a solid thinker. You read some interesting texts in the course but his grading of essays and participation is a bit harsh. The class isn't really about robots and is more about abstractly thinking about what makes things mechanical or humanlike.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Went into this class thinking I would be learning about Robots.... NOT WHAT YOU LEARN ABOUT AT ALL. Its like a literature class where u deeply analyze text and he expects so much out of the essays and doesn't have a rubric, arbitrarily gives grades. THE BOOKS WE WE READ ARE SOOOO WEIRD!!!!!!!

Honestly. he seems like a nice guy to be hand around with. As your lecturer? Not so much. His class is kind of bland and is hard to make interesting. Lots of awkward silence. Although this is most likely due to COVID, it doesn't feel like we are given much time to work on our essays. Class doesn't really help as we don't talk about the prompt.

Uncaring, unreasonable, sloppy exams. Despite making tons of errata on the exam, he defends himself vehemently and refuses to give any points for missing the errata. Also praises himself for pointing out all the errata he makes thinking that we appreciate it. He also decides on point allocation after grading the exam, so that's not very fair.

Medical Literacy was amazing! It got me excited about diverse medical fields. Ramin didn't lecture himself but behind the scenes, organized group of practicing physicians from Weill Cornell medicine. Every session was a case study and explored a field. The session on lung cancer made me quit smoking. So this class extended my life span by 10 years!

I did not like the lack of organization on the HWs and exams. TAs write the HWs and half of each exam. I was told the class gets harder every year. With 5 minutes left on each prelim, we got 15-30 extra minutes, but no extra time on the final, so don't expect it all the time. Overall, that made me feel a lack of trust. Do well on the final.

His first time teaching in years.  Lectures were not pertinent much and not updated online until right before final.  Problem Sets were managed solely by the TAs.  Prelims were fine.  Grade in class is almost solely based on final, as stated by email afterwards.  He's a decent person, but do try to stay away as far as class goes.
Extremely careless about classes. Lecture notes are updated 1 month later (Those for the finals haven't been updated yet).
Ramin is amazing! Extremely interesting lectures. Really knows his stuff. Enthusiastic about the subject. Best CS class I have taken. You really learn a lot about CS rather than just programming.

Incredible class. Ramin makes intro CS extremely interesting. While other CS100 classes were doing mind-numbing pointless programming assignments, we  actually learned useful CS applications and picked up the programming as we went.
Ramin is a God. Being taught by a genius like this is a true blessing.

Taking 312 with Ramin really kindled my interest in CS.  He's a dynamic and lucid lecturer, with a flair for the material.  His exams were engaging, the homework was interesting and manageable.  I hear good things about machine vision, but can't comment from personal experience.
Took class Fall 1996.  Funny guy.  Once asked the students why they took a 9AM lecture.  (um, we were freshmen, we had little choice.)  Exams and assignments were difficult but fair.
312 students should complain about the material, not the teacher.  this guy was really great in machine vision- great sense of humor and definitely one of the top 5 lecturers in the cs dept
He managed to make lectures confusing even without using PowerPoint.
Course textbook: Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy. Variable names Ford, Arthur and HHGTG were common. Lots of intel references. On a whole, really liked his teaching style. Wierd, geeky humor.
Went on personal rants all the time, and didn't really teach us much about the material. Extremely hard to get a hold of, and the grading was a constant mess. I will avoid him in the future.
Clear, thought-out lectures. Coursework can be demanding, and tedious at times. Has a strange pechant for THHGTTG.

Given that the material is difficult, Ramin is pretty good at explaining it.  He could be better; sometimes his examples too quickly, and his explanations are not always direct.  He will, however, make you understand all the major concepts.

Conceited; the class is marked by arrogant speeches that sound as if he's doing the students some kind of enormous favour by teaching them. He's very hard to get a hold of outside of class, a disorganized lecturer, and the coursework is extremely hard.
Ramin is a VERY dedicated teacher, he takes the class very seriously, and he's an interesting lecturer. He's not the best teacher ever, but he's damn, damn good.

Average grade for class was 62. Average grades for tests in the 40-50 range. Requires you show mastery of old, archaic methods for calculations. Will not accept shortcuts unless he teaches them weeks after the fact of archaic methods. Tests were nothing like class questions. MyMathLab homework was atrocious. NOT RECOMMENDED FOR NEW College STUDENTS
be ready to work. exams are tough, you will not find a better teacher than prof Zaffran. doesn't give extra credit.
Pretty good overall, though not at Cornell anymore.
Great teacher! Too bad he is in Tiawan now.
A great teacher, always ready to help!

Best math teacher I've ever had.  Makes linear algebra really interesting, nicest guy ever.  His lectures are really clear and thorough, almost word for word from the text book.  The french accent is cool too.
Overall a nice, amusing guy, a decent lecturer, and helpful if you ask.  The class wasn't that bad, especially after the first few weeks.

Zaffran was very rigorous and thorough, which made the text easier to follow. However he did not come across as extremely confident or competent during his lectures. If you have difficulty with the material, Zaffran is more than willing to help.

This is a very hard class, and Zaffran didn't make it any easier. I think he's a very nice guy, but it's hard to understand what he's saying with his accent and he doesn't make the material very understandable in lectures.
The difficulty is progressive. The final outcome is impressive. ANSYS and MATLAB in the pocket.
Really good professor. One of the only classes that will remind you that you are at Cornell University!!! It's a lot of work but its really worth it. Every single engineer should take this class!
great
One of the hardest classes I took at Cornell. That said, by far the most useful, and applicable to my life as an engineer. FEA is really worth understanding.
Intense course. Homework is not easy but extremely helpful. Lectures are really good.

Difficult course but you can succeed;attend lecture, study the lecture notes, and attend office hours. The professor was a good lecturer who wrote clear, thorough notes. This course is a great resume enhancer because of its applicability to industry. It also gives solid theoretical understanding and the professor is very willing to be a reference.

Lecture was disorganized, usually unclear, and he taught only the hardest parts of the material in class, requiring studying through the lecture slides to learn the rest. Group homeworks were exceptionally hard, and frequently not helpful. First exam was brutal, second was OK. Final project was a lot of work, though leniently graded.
A professor who's only interest is productivity. Α successful teacher, but a failed educator and leader. Students are not slaves, but critical spirits..

During a recent interview, I was asked questions related to FEM/FEA and I was able to draw my answers directly from this course. The interviewers literally started taking me much more seriously after I explained some of these things in detail. I've never been as challenged as I was in this course, but it has paid off greatly.

The course gives an all-around perception of the finite element method. The methods are basic in FEM but they are of great importance in the further study. The Professor gives excellent presentations by introducing the most core things in limited time. It's the most impressive course I've taken. Though I didn't master everything, I learned a lot!

One of the hardest classes for an undergraduate. His comments are all caustic & sarcastic which over an extent makes you feel sick & dizzy! He is good at teaching but sitting in class can be painful because of his comments. His TA's just cannot speak English - it sucks!

This class was the most valuable class I've taken for my Master's degree. The material was complex, but explained well. Zabaras had thorough slides and the material was hard at times but possible to understand. I really don't think my education would be complete without this class. It's so valuable!!!
Useful class for Graduate students.
If you don't like somebody, send him to this class. Terrible!
Studying FEM was an experience. It was not easy for sure, but I believe it is going to repay big time later. I like the way the entire program is structured...its fundamental!!

Interesting material. Professor Zabaras is one of the smartest and funniest professors I have had at Cornell. Lectures are enjoyable. Do NOT take this class if you do not plan to work very hard, but if you are looking to actually learn the material, this is THE class to take.
definitely one of my hardest classes at cornell. many hours spent and near-allnighters pulled. useful class though. the subject is really good.
This was the hardest course I have taken at Cornell.  Zabaras expects hard work and genuine quality work. He has high expectations, but he is fair.

The course was fun, lots of sleepless nights, tough mathematical slides but you get a hang of them in the end. Assignments got us all crazy & exams were not so bad! He is extremely intelligent & expects his class to perform & apply common sense!

Extremely difficult class, but if you put enough effort and time into it, it can be very rewarding. The lectures can be both impossibly confusing and extremely interesting, and I've been on both ends of the spectrum in this class. Pay attention, go to office hours, and put a lot of effort in, and it will be worth your while.

Very difficult class.  Was his first time teaching it this year but lectures were clear and slides/notes pretty complete.  You can learn a lot but you need to put in a lot of time for the homework and to understand the material.  Exams were very difficult, apparently the whole class did poorly.  Requires good understanding of previous material in h
it is a rewarding class

Dr. Zabaras is great professor. He explains complicated material in a clear manner and with real world examples and humor. In office hours he is very helpful. I recommend going to his office hours if you need something explained. To some students he come off as stand-off-ish or aloof, but he is a nice a guy.
Great class - challenging, but he's extremely helpful. Really wish more classes were structured the same.
Just...don't take his class...unless you have no choice

Zabaras's course is definitely more difficult than the other thermo lecture. However, the material is much more interesting and he really knows how to engage you with it and teach you it. You need to attend all of his lectures and make sure you spend plenty of time on all the homework, but if you do all of this the course is definitely doable.

Thermo with Prof Zabaras has been the most intellectually engaging and rewarding class I've taken. My understanding of calculus was enhanced by taking his class because the math is so tightly integrated into the thermo concepts. The professor himself has a sense of humor worth attending every lecture for. Meticulous work, but rewarding class.

Whoever said Thermo is horrible has never had Professor Zabaras, or is a real slacker ! Yes the course is challenging, but if you work you can do really well in it !  And Professor Zabaras makes lectures FUN !!! (not to mention : interesting ! ) This class was the highlight of my semester !
His section is MUCH harder than the other ones.

Great professor. He really cares that his students understand the material and is very willing to help you out if you show you are trying. You can really learn a lot from him if you pay attention.  Office hours are a must.

Zabaras understands thermo at its depths, and about once every lecture you get to have that feeling of understanding. He really shows how the math reveals the underlying concepts of the subject. Probably the first time you'll see actual chemistry (with calculus).  The course requires a good amount of work. Great professor, take this to learn.
class as described. A++++++ professor. would take again :)
Cold and unhelpful.  Not a great professor, and he doesn't seem like he cares about his students.
Helpful but gets angry
asdf

his class is "tough" but Zabaras won't let you down in the end as long as you work hard.  Also, he has an extraordinary memory.. so you better not skip his classes. Even though he doesn't know your name, he might remember your face. take this class!!!
go to section

This guy is nuts!  Be prepared to work hard and learn even more.  Don't even think of skipping lecture.  Zabaras explains things very quickly and efficiently.  In the end your grade is dependent on him knowing that you know the material - go to office hours!

His class is definitely harder, but if you go to his office hours, he is more than willing to help you out.  (I prefer his O.H.'s rather than the TA's O.H.'s)  He wants you to learn.   Also, the homeworks are hard, but they are relevant to what he tests you on.  Finally, don't let him catch you sleeping in class!

Professor Zabaras is the man. He made a potentially boring class very interesting by showing how thermodynamics was used in real life situations. His humor and honesty in class also makes his teaching very attractive. One of the best professors I've ever had. I don't know why some people didn't do well on some exams, they were just hw problems.

BEST Prof. Crazy, Sarcastic, Zany, Hilarious.  This guy single-handedly made Thermo fun.  Best memory:  He pulled out a transparency one time full of this long-winded derivation on some enthalphy property or something and just as we get done copying, he pulls it away and said in the goofiest voice- Just kidding folks u werent supposed to copy that.

Amazing teacher.  He really cares about his students and doesn't let you slack off.  He will help you (and like you a lot more) if you show that you are trying and go to office hours.  Exams are hard, but not impossible if you do the homeworks and learn the material.  Hilarious in class.  Makes an otherwise dry/challenging class interesting.
Incredible teacher, best professor i have had, but most difficult class I have taken also... Good luck, give it a shot... hes crazy
Class is tuff, but Zabaras is the man.  He's goofy and hilarious in lectures. Don't fall asleep though or he'll pick on you.  Great guy.  Take his course if your not afraid of a challenge.

He's CRAZY!  That being said, good class.  It was a LOT of work, go to office hrs for HW (makes up more of the grade than he lets on). If you understand the HW and examples in the book, should do decently in the class (that means a B+ or better).  He actually is very nice and helpful is he knows you're trying. Actually learned a lot. Good Luck!

may come out as tough prof, but if u show that u care for the subject and put work into it, he'll help u. do NOT fall asleep in his lecture if u don't wanna get picked on. exams aren't that bad if u do ur hw and do practice prelims. office hrs r "must" to understand hw tho... good luck :)

First of all crazy, but once you get past that he's alright.  Very demanding when it comes to effort put in, but he promises that we will be happy at the end of the semester.  Doesn't worry about whether you like him or not.  Responds very well to those who go to office hours seeking extra help.
Moved way too fast and way beyond what the other 221 course was teaching.  Altered the way the prelims were given and made it a lot better.

Spends a long time on derivations.  He's rushed the class so we're now covering material my TA has never seen. He's threatening to ignore the lowest 20% of the class in determing the mean and grading the class. Gets mad if you don't go to lecture.
He is on an ego-trip with his class and is leaving students behind.  We are far ahead of the other lecture section, yet we understand very little (evidenced by our last prelim score distribution).
No Comments
Hard and extremely demanding.  Comes across as kind of a jerk in class, but if you show up in his office and demonstrate you're putting effort into the class he'll respond well to you.
It was a one-to-one class, and he really cared about me as a person, and wanted me to succeed. however, he hates bell-curves, so watch out!
Funny, extremely knowledgeable, and very engaging. Assigns interesting essays, too. Very much recommended!

I love this man. He definitely knows what he's talking about, but isn't as pretentious as most musicologists and doesn't look down on you if you don't know what he's talking about. Extremely helpful and kind hearted...but he knows when you're bs-ing, so don't.
pretentious and off-putting. still informative and a genius...

Prof. Zaslaw is the most knowledgeable man I think I've met at Cornell.  The man is one of the world's foremost musicologists!  Loves what he does, isn't as old school as you would think, and really wants you to do well and love music.  Great class but memorizing symphonies/operas was challenging.
I took a Freshman Writing Seminar with him. He's a good guy and the grade was only based on 5 short papers and a final research one. I had no background in music and the class was pretty technical.
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
Very knowledgeable guy, pretty good teacher.

Lectures weren't great but you can't blame him when not even a third of the class shows up. Quick to reply to emails and Ed and helpful in office hours. Exams are fair but HW is time consuming. The final project takes a while but isn't worth much.

Dude's a legend. Takes time after class to explain anything you had problems with. Yeah the homework is a lot for sure, and he expects some basic fluency in excel/python for some assignments, but he's really good at introducing Differential Equations. Handled the online transition like a champ too (Spring 2020)

His explanations are super clear and I actually found his lectures very insightful because he brought up many interesting real-life problems and how diffeq could be applied to derive models to solve those problems. Even when the class went online, he still managed the course logistics very well. It was my most favorite class for Spring 2020.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Tough but rewarding. Some lectures are hit-or-miss. Overall not bad though. I would not dread taking the class again. If you take 2930, you might need to know how to program and graph for some homework assignments.

Assigns way too many problems for homework, get ready for over 20 pages of problems that really are just a waste of your paper. Doesn't teach well, gets most examples from Paul's Math Notes. Since moving to online (Spring 2020), the class has become a nuisance.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Tells subtle but great jokes

Good prof, explains things pretty clearly, but by no means goes in detail.  Teaches how to solve problems, but no more, so all context of problems is lost.  Not hugely interesting, either.  Nice guy though, and very understanding.
He's really boring. I usually end up sleeping in this class and read the textbook later. He makes a bunch of math mistakes too.
I went to a few of his lectures and they were clear and organized. He is great in explaining the material in office hours.
he's kinda cold in person but he knows how to teach. Well prepared and organized. 202 stuff is his specialty
Best of the three profs who teach this course (not saying much).  Clear and easy to follow, if somewhat like a robot.  Goes into long-winded example problems that no one can follow.
he's mean. super snarky. igor was rough. he was always unnecessarily vague.

Was extremely approachable throughout the course and usually available and willing to discuss any challenges/questions about lab. Vagueness in person and in handouts were sometimes confusing, but more often than not, also challenged me to learn more. His lectures went well beyond what was required for labs (apt for a class full of chemists).
Purposely makes exams impossible to finish, lecture is useless, not helpful whatsoever
Lectures were completely useless
Terrible professor
Everything I learned was from the textbook. I should have skipped 90 percent of the lectures.

I thought I used to like chemistry. His lectures are incredibly unclear unless you already solidly know the material. His tests are tough, no doubt about that. Lectures seemed to be unrelated to homework or labs--studying the homework and textbooks are the key to passing. Was fairly condescending in class.  Would not recommend.

Zax is unfortunately one of the worst teachers I have ever had. He has literally described concepts as magic and makes the simplest things confusing. His demos usually have nothing to do with the lecture of the day and he often messes them up.  I generally enjoy chemistry but this was a very poor class.

Lectures were absolutely terrible and because of that it's extremely hard to do the homeworks and tests. Impossible to pass the class without reading the book yourself and viewing Khan Academy videos. Would NOT recommend.

Prof Zax's lectures are extremely unclear and often painful to attend. His power points look similar to something a 6th grader would create, he's not concise, and he often comes across as very condescending towards his students.  Just read the textbook and do the problem sets. Labs are easy, prelims are not - "designed so no one would finish"...

His lectures don't relate to any of his homework sets and are very sporadically taught in general. His lectures are often hard to follow, even if you know what you are doing. He has also describe the reason behind some chemistry to just be "magic." Questions during lecture have been answered with quick responses that don't clarify what was asked.
He is a great professor, and makes sure that students who need help can receive it. He is informative, and he tries to make this class fun.

All of the hype about Zax is completely exaggerated. He's nowhere near as cruel or intimidating as previous ratings state. That being said, his lectures are way too complicated, and his exams are tough (but not unfair). If you're an incoming freshman worried about this class, don't fear. The material is manageable if you read the textbook.

David Zax just has a chip on his shoulders. It seems that he is not only rude to students that approach him for help, but he is also horrible to the Department's grad students and other faculty members. Unfortunately, CHEM 2070 is a "weed out" class and a common requirement for many majors; so, it's either this or summer schoolchoose summer school

Totally unapproachable and tough, but the stigma around Zax and 2070 is a bit overblown. I got an A in the class without taking AP Chem and while I worked for it, it's not necessary to go to office hours every week. Prelims are tough, but it's chemistry, so the means are gonna be low and the curve will help you.
Very confusing lectures. Does not wait for the class to understand him. Tests are extremely difficult.

Ugh... Zax. He's just a really difficult test-giver. Doesn't seem friendly although I've never actually tired going to his office hours specifically. Enjoyed his lectures for the most part. It's not his fault chem 2070 is designed to weed people out. Be prepared to work hard.

He is a worse professor than Abruna. He presents the basic concepts in class, but expect students to know things to the very detail for homework and exams. His homework was unnecessarily difficult and not good for prelim preparation. He is rude and proud. The only way to do well is to study everything yourself and do a lot of problems.
Terrible professor. He is even rude to other professors and TAs. It's so unfortunate that almost every science major has to take this course

Makes topics harder to understand than they should be. Prelim and homework questions are hard and not directly from the book and hard to study for. Material covered was not that hard but he did not teach it very clearly.

I took this course in Fall 2013 with not prior AP chem (only regents chem in sophomore year). I got an A in the class but mostly because I went to the support class every week. The concepts were simple enough but Zax doesnt always explain everything in the allotted time. His lectures are better than Abruna's and I personally liked his exams better.

I guess the people saying he wasn't so bad are the ones who took AP Chem and got a 5 or something. The last time I took regents Chem was 2009, so maybe that's my fault. Anyway, terrible class, over analyzes material 'til it makes no sense, went to all lectures, didn't help, read the book completely, tests were totally different. Worst ever.

Honestly, Zax is one of the crappiest professors I've ever come in contact with.  He's arrogant, demeaning, and expects you to fully understand ridiculously complex subjects that only the kids who got fives on the AP exam have a slight understanding of.  This class sucks, don't even waste your time going to lecture.  You rely so much on the book.

The only thing I can say is "Avoid this man like the plague." He's very arrogant, doesn't care about students, and even revels in students suffering with the unnecessary difficulty of his assignments and exams. Stay away.

Not as bad as he is rumored to be. His homework problems were really hard and took a long time but often we were not tested on the harder material. Because of this his tests seemed annoying easy because we spent a lot of time studying and learning harder things that weren't on them. I never talked to him in person or read the book and I got a B+.

Although he lacks a pleasant personality, he wasn't a bad prof. His lectures were somewhat challenging to follow but actually did explain things. I relied heavily on our book AND other chem books and did A LOT of practice problems in order to do well on the prelim and final. Hard work, but worth it.
The test questions were similar to the problem set questions... so in terms of fairness, what else needs to be said? I ended up with an A- for what it's worth.

Zax is an amazing teacher. Honestly, the rumors about him are way over exaggerated. Chem is a subject that you usually get or don't, but all in all, if you do the hw and pay attention in class you should be fine.  He may be rude in office hours, but hey, there are so many other TA's you can go to if you really need the help.
The tests were very fair. Although the final may have been difficult, if one studies they should be fine. I had not taken AP Chem in high school but still managed an A

Zax's lectures were clear, HW was helpful and tests were fair. Some test means were on the low end, but the thing with chemistry is that the lectures give you a basis of knowledge but it is up to you to apply this knowledge on practice problems. Know your stoichiometry well because it is an easy concept that they can write tricky questions on
One of the worst professors at Cornell. Dry lectures, bad at teaching, and unwilling to give clarification when asked.
His office hours and not great and he is a bit arrogant. Overall the rumors are over blown, he isn't the absolute worse.

He is a horrible professor. Most likely the worst professor at cornell. Every single person i know absolutely hates his lectures as they are utterly useless. His prelims and finals are completely unfair. The problem sets are long a ridiculous.

This man is awful. Don't ask questions in lecture unless you want him to pulverize you in front of every person in class. Don't go to office hours, he'll just do the same thing in private. In exams, he seems to delight in watching tears run slowly down students faces (true story). Labs and exams have zero to do with lecture. Even my TA hated him.

Zax isn't as bad as everyone says... yeah the final was pretty bad but it was curved, so it doesn't really matter. The prelims were very fair and easy if you were prepared. Not the greatest teacher, but the help was there if necessary.

Finds a way to 'explain' concepts in the single most confusing way. Lectures tend to wander, but can provide useful examples; sometimes will give away a test answer. He's a bit of egoist, but play into it and he'll be nicer to you.

Not a bad professor, just a bit condescending towards students. Honestly, the material was really easy and there is no reason you should do bad in the course since you have TAs and whatnot to help you.
Dry, teaches inaccurate models without indicating they are inaccurate until the very end. So, a lot of time is wasted when it could be spent focusing on things that work.

He tries to teach concepts the way they were discovered (i.e. explaining how things like orbitals are derived mathematically) when it would be clearer and easier to learn the material if he just presented facts.  Don't ask questions in class, he talks down to people a lot.  Go to TAs and tutors with problems, they are very helpful.
DAVEEEEEEEEEEE!  This man is the epitome of what a teacher should be.  He obviously loves his work, his family, and his religion.  I wish I could be Dave.
Horrible teacher. The exams were unpredictable - the means were either really high or ridiculously low. Probably one of the worst college professors I have ever had.
He is a horrible teacher. The TA's seemed to be better at teaching than he is. The final exam was a killer!

This man is a TERRIBLE professor. He doesn't really know what he is talking about and gets corrected often during lecture, especially by his superior, Prof. Lee. In order to do well, one must teach themselves. Consider this class to be "auto-tutorial". Lectures don't correlate to masterinchemistry.com work, written homework, or exams.
Horrible teacher. Horrible Experience. Unhelpful. Arrogant. Mean.
Most confusing lecture prof ever... the times that I could manage to stay awake. The material covered in lecture was not covered in the homework problems. And the final was ridiculous.

Dave Zax is possibly the most arrogant, condescending, and rude man I've ever had the misfortune to meet.  He acts as if students are appalling pieces of filth and don't deserve anything more than disdain and hatred. I wish no other student would have to endure the unfortunate circumstances that are his class.

This class was brutal. There are so many assignments due for a four credit class and there really needs to be more lecture time. Zax also was very confusing and his exams were completely off topic sometimes.
Terribly teacher. Arrogant, annoying, and overall, useless. I learned nothing from this man.

Very disappointing that almost every science related major will have to take 2070.  Tests take 2/3 of the alotted time to comprehend and have little based on what he actually lectured on.  No understanding of his students knowledge level before or after the course.  This is coming from someone who went to lecture and did pretty well in the class.
Worst professor I've ever had.  Managed to confuse the entire lecture hall almost every class.
Horrible teacher

Definitely not the best teacher, prelim means were always low, but didn't have to do much work to get above the mean on everything. Zax acts like he doesn't want to be there during class and his demonstrations NEVER worked. Didn't get much chemistry knowledge from him, but overall the class is boring, but not too hard.
He is a good teacher who is willing to answer questions.  I learned many things from the cores and it stimulated my interest in the subject greatly.
Rather useless professor.
Zax is an amazing individual. His ability to confuse is perhaps second to none.  His ability to crush the soul is also unparalleled.  Since he can't be avoided, he must be endured...

If you like lectures that go on random tangents that have nothing to do with the tests, Professor Zax is the teacher for you! Worst at Cornell thus far. If you have no chemistry experience, you will likely have a very difficult time.
Demolished my interest in chemistry.  Taught useless information that was not even related to chemistry and expected you to know the information.

Unwilling to help students during office hours. Dodges questions and acts condescendingly toward students. His tests have very low means. If you haven't taken AP Chemistry in high school, then you will have a lot of trouble passing this course.
Very helpful, great teaching style and wit. Readily available for assistance on otherwise complicated concepts. He was also voted best prof by the students for the past two years. Highly recommended!

Zax removed all of my interest in chemistry. If he spent as much time actually teaching as puffing out his chest then we would possibly learn something. And his incapability at both teaching and demonstrations degrades my perception of Cornell.
Does not care about students. Tricky exams with many application questions.
Needs to work on clarity, and making labs more relevant. Also needs to understand that no one takes chemistry by choice, everyone is there because its required.

Easily the worst professor I have ever had, and I've had my fair share of bad teachers.  This guy has no desire to hand his knowledge to his students, he's too full of himself and his previous research to even care about his students learning.  Don't bother going to lecture, reading the book and going to AEW will save you in this course.
Bad prof, clearly does not want to teach. Avoid taking this course in the fall so you can avoid this guy! Some other better prof teaches in the spring; Zax teaches in the fall

My suggestion if you are required to take this course? Wait until it gets taken over by a new professor. Being one of the few people who actually attended lecture and came in with a really good background, the prelims were still pretty tough thanks to Zax's mean-lowering exam questions that seem to have nothing to do with what we're learning
